search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Diyung (AAUDPU Dhan 06), Rice

Name note: "Diyung" is the CSC minutes name and "Diyung (AAUDPU Dhan 06)" is the Seednet name. The findings below refer to the same variety. Where a source used only one name, I say so. Four searches were run (name, breeder, research, seed availability). The Seednet portal itself did not appear in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for this variety's drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The one relevant mention is the ICAR-IIRR 2022 table row under DISEASE AND PEST below. Another Hills Times article describes disease and pest resistance for a group of RARS rice varieties in general terms; it is unclear whether the Diyung paragraph carries the same claims, so I have not attributed them to Diyung. -- https://thehillstimes.in/featured/rars-develops-organic-rice-varieties-for-rural-assam

DISEASE AND PEST
ICAR-IIRR Annual Report 2022 lists "Diyung 27680 TTBDR 103-4-4 Malbhog/Bahadur 111 IM MS 6.23 MR-SB, LF AS (AAUDPU Dhan 06)" in a table, but the column key is not in the extracted text, so the codes "MR-SB" and "LF" cannot be decoded from it. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
The Hills Times article's Diyung paragraph is a single line of the form "DIYUNG is a semi-glutinous sali rice variety suitable for organic situation of Assam." It does not name a blast, stem borer or leaf folder resistance rating for Diyung itself. -- https://thehillstimes.in/featured/rars-develops-organic-rice-varieties-for-rural-assam

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The Hills Times article reports that Diyung is the first high-yielding chakua rice variety from AAU, showed yield and maturity-duration advantages over check varieties in station trials, MLTs, OFTs and AICRP trials, and out-yielded national and zonal checks in the kharif 2018 coordinated trial. Amylose content is given as 7.55%, compared with 7.98% for local Malbhog. -- https://thehillstimes.in/featured/rars-develops-organic-rice-varieties-for-rural-assam
The AAU Directorate of Research page lists Diyung (AAUDPU Dhan 06) with release date August 31, 2022, and records that it was recommended by SVRC Assam in 2021. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: Malbhog / Bahadur (ICAR-IIRR 2022 table row, matching the parentage given in the brief). -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
Breeding-line code: TTBDR 103-4-4 (same row; the unlabelled number 27680 is probably a test or accession ID, but the row does not say so). -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
Breeding method: No evidence found.
QTL, marker and genome resources: No evidence found. A Sub1 introgression paper (ResearchGate) covers Ranjit and Bahadur, not Diyung, so I have excluded it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327731781_Phenotypic_Screening_and_Evaluation_of_Sub1_Introgressed_Lines_in_Popular_Rice_Varieties_Ranjit_and_Bahadur_of_Assam

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Assam Agricultural University (AAU), Jorhat, Directorate of Research (Agriculture). The AAU page lists AAU as the developer of Diyung (AAUDPU Dhan 06). -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127
The Hills Times article attributes the Diyung variety to Assam Agricultural University. -- https://thehillstimes.in/featured/rars-develops-organic-rice-varieties-for-rural-assam
Lead breeder or scientist name for this variety: No evidence found. The AAU page carries the name Dr. Surajit Kalita as a profile heading, but the extracted text does not link him to Diyung, so I have not attributed the variety to him.
Station: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS) is the institution named in the brief. Its specific station page did not appear in the results.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for an official email, phone or postal address for the breeding station. The AAU page gives the location as Jorhat, but no street address, phone or email appears in the extracted text. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127
Name shown on the AAU page: Dr. Surajit Kalita (role and link to this variety not stated in the extract). -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127

PUBLICATIONS
ICAR-IIRR (2022). Annual Report 2022 (author not stated; the variety appears in the DUS and variety-table section). -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
No peer-reviewed papers, theses, AICRP reports or conference papers specific to Diyung were found. The Hills Times article is a press piece, not a journal article. -- https://thehillstimes.in/featured/rars-develops-organic-rice-varieties-for-rural-assam

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Searches returned only generic Assam seed-dealer and input-supply pages, none naming Diyung. Seednet and NSC/State Seed Corporation pages for Diyung were not retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Assam. The AAU page says the variety was recommended by SVRC Assam in 2021. The Hills Times article describes it as suitable for organic conditions in Assam. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127 ; https://thehillstimes.in/featured/rars-develops-organic-rice-varieties-for-rural-assam

Open gaps: Seednet record, breeder name and contact, detailed trial data, and the column key for the IIRR table should be checked directly on seednet.gov.in, the AAU/RARS Jorhat site, and KrishiKosh.

seednet_fields.Parentage: RP 2421/VL Dhan 221 Pedigree: The material from F2 onwards was handled by pedigree method at RWRC, Malan. Unifrom line MLN 2013-B-1-1-2-1-1-1 in F9 generation was entered in station trials in 2009. From 2011 to 2013 the variety was tested in the All India Coordinated Trials.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Low & mid hills under upland conditions of Himachal Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Good, suitable for upland conditions, The yield of the proposed variety increased with increasing dose of nitrogen application from 30 kg N/ha to 90 kg N/ha. In the same trial, the variety resulted in 10.2% higher grain yield than the best check i.e., Sukardhan 1.In another trial, to determine the performanceof this variety under varying fertility levels, the highest yield was recommended fertilizers (60:30:30) and it was significantly higher than yield recorded with the application of 75% of recommended fertilizers. The variety responded well to the application of herbicides and the best results obtained with the pre-emergence application of butachlor (2-3 DAS) followed by the bispyribacsodium used at 25 DAS.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: There was no problem of lodging and shattering in this variety.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistance to blast under field conditions especially in Himachal Pradesh conditions.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Tolerant to leaf folder and rice hispa under field conditions.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): NPK 60:30:30. Entire quantity of phosphours and potash and 50% nitrogen is to be added at the time of sowing. Remaining nitrogen is to be applied in two equal spilts at tillering stage and at panicle

agronomic_details.yield: Trial grain yield: 2705 kg/ha (2020) and 2865 kg/ha (2021) at Palampur/Malan. Input record average yield given as 21-32 q/ha Kg/Ha (units as recorded in the input, not reconciled). Input record also reports 10.2% higher grain yield than the best check Sukardhan 1 in one trial.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for multi-environment stability. Results were reported from two years (2020 and 2021) at Palampur and Malan, and HPR 2656 yielded lower than HPR 2795 in both years.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Input record: low and mid hills under upland conditions of Himachal Pradesh; suitable for upland conditions. Digest ICAR kharif advisory lists it as a high-yielding variety for direct seeding, to be sown by end May or first week of June at 60 kg seed/ha.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Palampur/Malan wheat-rice trials, 2020 and 2021: HPR 2656 grain yield 2705 kg/ha (2020) and 2865 kg/ha (2021), lower than Him Palam Lal Dhan 1 (HPR 2795). Biological yield 7809 kg/ha (2020) and 8242 kg/ha (2021). Panicles/m2: 249.1 (2020) and 264.4 (2021). 1000-grain weight: 21.96 g (2020) and 22.60 g (2021). (2) MDPI study at Palampur and Malan: HPR 2656 recorded significantly lower grain yield than HPR 2795 in both years, with the lowest gross and net returns and the lowest B:C ratio. (3) Kharif 2019 tillage study at CSKHPKV Palampur: panicle density at par with Sukara Dhan (HPR 1156); grain yield lower than HPR 2795. (4) Input record nitrogen trial: yield increased with nitrogen from 30 to 90 kg N/ha; 10.2% higher grain yield than Sukardhan 1 in one trial. (5) Input record fertility trial: highest yield with recommended fertilizers (60:30:30), significantly higher than 75% of recommended fertilizers. (6) Input record herbicide response: best results with pre-emergence butachlor (2-3 DAS) followed by bispyribacsodium at 25 DAS. (7) Germination/vigour (provisional, figures ambiguous): highest fast-count germination 58.33% as reported and 100% field emergence in a paddy germplasm comparison that labels the germplasm as Him Palam Dhan-1.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Him Palam Dhan 1 (HPR 2656), Rice

Name check: The search results use "Him Palam Dhan 1 (HPR 2656)" and "Him Palam Dhan 1" for this variety, which matches the Seednet name. The CSC release-minute name was not separately found, so the evidence below applies to both names. Search dates are unreliable, so years are given only where the page shows them.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to HPR 2656. The only related finding is that it was among the common rainfed varieties farmers grew in a 2018 AICRIP production-oriented survey, which shows adoption, not tolerance. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSiteold/Production%20Oriented%20Survey%202018.pdf
Germination and vigour: in a paddy germplasm vigour comparison, HPR-2656 showed the highest fast-count germination (58.33%, as reported) and 100% field emergence. The paper reports the germplasm as "Him Palam Dhan-1" and the figures are ambiguous, so treat them as provisional. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333222708_Comparison_of_tests_for_the_analysis_of_vigor_and_viability_in_paddy_germplasm_and_their_relationship_to_field_emergence

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for disease or pest resistance in HPR 2656. Results for a pest and blast resistance profile belonged to a different variety (HPR 3201, Him Palam Dhan 4), so they were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Palampur/Malan wheat-rice trials (2020 and 2021) recorded HPR 2656 grain yield of 2705 kg/ha (2020) and 2865 kg/ha (2021), lower than Him Palam Lal Dhan 1 (HPR 2795). -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11059587/
The same trial's HPR 2656 biological yield was 7809 and 8242 kg/ha for 2020 and 2021. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11059587/
A MDPI study found HPR 2656 recorded significantly lower grain yield than HPR 2795 in both years at Palampur and Malan, with the lowest gross and net returns and the lowest B:C ratio. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0472/12/10/1678
A kharif 2019 tillage study at CSKHPKV Palampur found HPR 2656 had a panicle density at par with Sukara Dhan (HPR 1156) and lower grain yield than HPR 2795. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363263323_Growth_analysis_of_rice_hybrids_as_influenced_by_dates_of_transplanting_under_lowland_conditions
ICAR kharif advisory lists HPR 2656 as a high-yielding variety for direct seeding, to be sown by end May or the first week of June at 60 kg seed/ha. -- https://www.basu.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Kharif-Agro-2021.pdf
Yield attributes from the 2020-21 trial: HPR 2656 had 249.1 and 264.4 panicles/m² and 1000-grain weight of 21.96 g and 22.60 g in 2020 and 2021. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11059587/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage (RP 2421/VL Dhan 221), breeding-line code (MLN 2013-B-1-1-2-1-1-1) and pedigree method: No evidence found in search results. These come from the input record only and were not verified.
HPR 2656 was used as one of three testers in a combining-ability study of upland rice lines at CSKHPKV, which estimated gene action for yield traits. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362825249_Study_on_gene_action_and_combining_ability_for_yield_and_its_attributes_in_upland_rice_lines_of_Himachal_Pradesh
QTL, marker and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Breeder names: No evidence found. The Garkoti and Pandey study lists the CSK Himachal Pradesh Agricultural University and CSKHPKV Rice and Wheat Research Centre, Malan, as affiliations. This establishes the institution, not the breeder of HPR 2656. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362825249_Study_on_gene_action_and_combining_ability_for_yield_and_its_attributes_in_upland_rice_lines_of_Himachal_Pradesh
Institution: CSK Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya (CSKHPKV), Palampur; Rice and Wheat Research Centre (RWRC), Malan, per the input record and the trial papers above. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0472/12/10/1678
Breeder names for HPR 3201 (Neelam Bhardwaj, Daisy Basandrai and others) were found but belong to a different variety, so they were excluded. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/16-Him-Palam-Dhan-4-HPR-3201-A-Long-Grained-High-Yielding-Rice-Variety-for-Transplanted-Irrigated-Conditions-of-Himachal-Pradesh-and-Uttrakhand.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for an official email, phone number, postal address or institute contact page for HPR 2656 or for CSKHPKV Rice and Wheat Research Centre, Malan. A LinkedIn profile for a scientist that mentions the variety was found but is not a contact record and was not used. -- https://www.linkedin.com/in/chinmaya-sahoo-521b411b9/

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2022 inferred from journal volume 12, issue 10). Impact of Cultivation Practices and Varieties on Productivity, Profitability, and Nutrient Uptake of Rice and Wheat Cropping System in India. Agriculture -- https://doi.org/10.3390/agriculture12101678
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2024). Assessing the effect of soil cultivation methods and genotypes on crop yield components, yield and soil properties in wheat and rice cropping system. BMC Plant Biology -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12870-024-05001-y (also PMC11059587)
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Growth, yield and yield components of rice (Oryza sativa) as influenced by tillage methods and cultivars. ResearchGate preprint -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372986218_Growth_yield_and_yield_components_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_as_influenced_by_tillage_methods_and_cultivars
Ankit et al. (year not shown). Influence of tillage practices on growth and growth indices of rice varieties under mid hills of Himachal Pradesh. Biological Forum -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/75%20Influence%20of%20Tillage%20Practices%20on%20Growth%20and%20Growth%20indices%20of%20Rice%20_Oryza%20sativa%20L._%20varieties%20under%20Mid%20Hills%20of%20Himachal%20Pradesh%20Ankit.pdf
Garkoti, P. and Pandey, D. P. (year not shown). Study on gene action and combining ability for yield and its attributes in upland rice lines of Himachal Pradesh. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362825249_Study_on_gene_action_and_combining_ability_for_yield_and_its_attributes_in_upland_rice_lines_of_Himachal_Pradesh
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Comparison of tests for the analysis of vigor and viability in paddy germplasm and their relationship to field emergence. No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRIP/ICAR annual report or DOI-indexed record specific to HPR 2656 was found. An M.Sc. thesis on upland rice traits (CSKHPKV) appeared in a citation list but was not confirmed as covering this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Him Palam Dhan 2 (HPR 2880), Rice

Search note: 4 web_search calls were used. Neither "Him Palam Dhan 2" nor "HPR 2880" returned any Seednet portal page, release notification, or CSC minutes. Where a heading below relies on the seed-vigour paper or the ICAR advisory, the name used there is "HPR-2880 (Him Palam Dhan-2)" or "HPR 2880", so both names are covered by that evidence. Results about Him Palam Dhan 3 (HPR 2865), Him Palam Dhan 4 (HPR 3201), Him Palam Dhan 1 (HPR 2656), Him Palam Lal Dhan 1 (HPR 2795) and Sukara Dhan 1 (HPR 1156) were discarded as other varieties. A ResearchGate upland-rice paper listing "HPR 2884" was also discarded, since it is a different line code.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for HPR 2880. The only HPR 2880 material was seed-vigour and field-emergence data (see AGRONOMY AND TRIALS), which does not measure stress tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No blast, brown spot, gall midge, sheath blight or other resistance data for HPR 2880 were retrieved. Blast-resistance statements in the results apply to Him Palam Dhan 3 and 4 and to other entries, so they are not attributed here.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The seed-vigour paper includes HPR-2880 (Him Palam Dhan-2), with the pedigree HPU2216 × Tetap, in a germination and vigour comparison of paddy germplasm from the Himachal foothills. Germination for HPR-2880 was low in fresh seed, showing dormancy, and rose after six months of storage and after accelerated ageing. Its first-count and field-emergence values were also reported. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333222708_Comparison_of_tests_for_the_analysis_of_vigor_and_viability_in_paddy_germplasm_and_their_relationship_to_field_emergence
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The ICAR Kharif agro-advisory lists HPR 2880 among high-yielding rice varieties for timely-sown nursery sowing (20 May to the first week of June), with the note "university recommended". The advisory is addressed to the J&K region, so it is not evidence of a Himachal recommendation. -- https://www.basu.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Kharif-Agro-2021.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A PPV&FRA-linked annual report lists HIM Palam Dhan-2 (HPR-2880) with a numeric ID (1101210002) in a list of entries, with no visible column heading or test results. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/final-annual-report-2020-21.pdf
Yield, maturity, and multi-location AICRIP results for HPR 2880 -- No evidence found. The user-supplied record says HPR 2880 was tested in AICRIP hill-zone trials in 2014 and in farmer fields in 2014–2015. Those trials were not confirmed by any retrieved page.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage HPU2216 × Tetap (HPU 2216/Tetep) is confirmed for HPR-2880 by the seed-vigour paper listed under AGRONOMY AND TRIALS. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333222708_Comparison_of_tests_for_the_analysis_of_vigor_and_viability_in_paddy_germplasm_and_their_relationship_to_field_emergence
GENETICS AND QTL -- The single-seed-descent method at IARI, the RIL 4 line code, and the 2014 AICRIP hill-zone testing come only from the user-supplied record. No search result confirmed them. No QTL, marker, or genome-resource study for HPR 2880 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Chaudhary Sarwan Kumar Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya (CSKHPKV), Palampur, with the Rice and Wheat Research Centre (RWRC), Malan, as the rice station. The seed-vigour paper includes HPR-2880 among paddy germplasm; it does not name its breeder. The breeder name is not confirmed for HPR 2880. The 2011 AICRP production survey names rice breeders at RWRC Malan (Dr K. Prasad, Dr Rabindra Pd.). It predates HPR 2880's release and does not mention the variety, so it is not attributed to it. -- https://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSiteold/POS.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The user-supplied record says the variety was handled at IARI Delhi from F2 onwards. This was not verified by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact was found. Institute-level contact details that appear in retrieved pages (not specific to HPR 2880):
- Rice and Wheat Research Centre, CSK HPKV, Malan (H.P.) 176 047, India. Address as given in a Garkoti and Pandey paper. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362825249_Study_on_gene_action_and_combining_ability_for_yield_and_its_attributes_in_upland_rice_lines_of_Himachal_Pradesh
- Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, CSK Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya, Palampur-176062. Address as given in a rice-research short communication on another variety, HPR 3201. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/16-Him-Palam-Dhan-4-HPR-3201-A-Long-Grained-High-Yielding-Rice-Variety-for-Transplanted-Irrigated-Conditions-of-Himachal-Pradesh-and-Uttrakhand.pdf
- No email, phone number, or institute contact-page URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- Authors not shown in the retrieved text (2016). Comparison of tests for the analysis of vigor and viability in paddy germplasm and their relationship to field emergence. Journal not shown. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333222708_Comparison_of_tests_for_the_analysis_of_vigor_and_viability_in_paddy_germplasm_and_their_relationship_to_field_emergence
Authors not shown (2021). ICAR Kharif Agro-Advisory for Farmers. ICAR Kharif agro-advisory report. -- https://www.basu.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Kharif-Agro-2021.pdf
Authors not shown (2021). Annual Report 2020-21. Plant Authority (PPV&FRA) annual report. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/final-annual-report-2020-21.pdf
No theses, KrishiKosh records, AICRP annual-report entries with trial data, or peer-reviewed papers specific to HPR 2880 were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sales, or dealer listing for HPR 2880 was retrieved. The dealer results returned were for unrelated varieties and companies (for example DRR Dhan 48, Nuziveedu and Sri Vardhan 999), and were discarded. The CSKHPKV newsletter describes seed-multiplication agreements for other crops, not for rice. -- http://www.hillagric.ac.in/eNewsLetter/Current/Detail/23SeedMult.html (not about HPR 2880)

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Not confirmed for Himachal Pradesh. The only state-level reference found was the ICAR Kharif advisory, which lists HPR 2880 in a J&K-region context with the note "university recommended". -- https://www.basu.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Kharif-Agro-2021.pdf
The release year of 2020 and the CSC notification were not verified by any search result.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology:
For all the three subzones of Jharkhand (Zone –VII)
Zone IV – Central and North Eastern Plateau.
Subzone V – Western Plateau
Subzone VI – Southern Eastern Plateau.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: The agronomic traits such as flowering duration, plant height no. of panicles/ sqm of IR64 and the NILs IET 22836 are similar.  Entry is responsive to fertilizer dose.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
Variety : IET 22836 (RP5208-3-IR8777-445-B-B-B)
Plant height : 105cm
Panicly type : Semi-dward
No. of panicles/sq. m : 325-350
Days of 50% flowering : 85-91 days
Seed to seed duration : 120-125 days
Panicle type : Compact, heavy panicle
Panicle exertion : Well exerted
Awning : Absent
Apiculus colour : Green
Lemma palea colour : After maturity straw colour
1000-grain weight : 25.4gm
Kernel length : 6.63mm
Kernel breadth : 2.10mm
L/B ration : 3.20
Kernel appearance : very occasionally chalky grains
Milling recovery: 70%
Head rice recovery : 52.9%
Alkali spreading value (ASV) : 4.0
Amylose content (AC) : 22.96%
Gel consistency : 63mm
Grain type : Long slender
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: •	Erratic pattern of rainfall particularly during the months of Sep.-Nov. coincides with reproductive stage of the crop which is a crucial stage results in severe yield reduction.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: More tolerant than IR 64 against blast, brown spot and bacterial  leaf blight in Jharkhand.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Similar reaction to IR 64 against different pests.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 32 kg N, 16 Kg P2O, and 8 Kg K2O/ acre or 80 kg N, 40 Kg P2O5, and 20 Kg K2O/ ha is recommended.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: IR 64-Sub 1 (CSC release name) / IR 64- Sub 1 (IET 21247) (Seednet name), Rice (Paddy)

Search note: Four web_search calls ran (variety/release, breeder/institute, research, seed availability). A fifth follow-up query was blocked by the tool limit, so several headings below have thin coverage. The only page that names this variety is the NDUAT document. Everything else returned was about IR64 generally or unrelated products, and was discarded under the strict relevance rule.

STRESS TOLERANCE: The NDUAT document lists "IR 64 sub 1" as suited to complete submergence for up to 14 days -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/anduat.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The searches returned no page naming this variety with disease or pest resistance data.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The same NDUAT entry gives a maturity of 120-125 days -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/anduat.pdf. No yield, trial or multi-location data found.
GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found for this variety. The parentage and code details supplied in the brief (IR 64*3/IR 49830-7-1-2-3, backcross method, IET 21247) were not confirmed by any retrieved page. The IR64 mega-variety article (https://thericejournal.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s12284-018-0208-3) is about IR64 in general and does not name IR 64-Sub 1, so it was not used.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The NDUAT document is the only retrieved page that names this variety. It lists the variety in a Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology listing, but the snippet does not name a lead breeder or confirm that Crop Research Station, Masodha developed it -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/anduat.pdf. The same document lists the university's zonal stations (for example ZARS Kumarganj), so the Masodha attribution needs checking against the source.
CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, postal address or contact page for this variety was retrieved.
PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The submergence paper at https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0098847213002049 concerns submergence and nutrient timing, and does not name IR 64-Sub 1, so it was excluded.
SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for this variety. The only seed result was an Anil Traders (Satna) listing for "IR 64" paddy, which is not IR 64-Sub 1 and was excluded -- https://www.indiamart.com/anil-traders-satna/research-paddy-seeds.html
RECOMMENDED STATES: The NDUAT document is the only source, and it is a university listing rather than a release notification. It does not clearly confirm the release state for IR 64-Sub 1; the brief's "Uttar Pradesh" is unverified. Source: https://www.nduat.org/Doc/anduat.pdf

Suggested next checks (not run): the CSC/ICAR release notification for 2020, the Seednet portal entry for IET 21247, and the NDUAT or Masodha station pages to confirm the developer.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: INDAM 100-012 (seednet name: Indam 100-012 (IET 26999)), Rice

Search note: I ran four searches (variety, breeder/developer, research, seed availability). Only retailer and company pages named INDAM 100-012. No Seednet, CSC, ICAR, SAU, KrishiKosh or journal page named this variety. Searches on "IET 26999" returned nothing matching it. The one ICAR-IIRR proceedings hit mentioned IET 29822, a different entry, so I discarded it. Retailer statements below are unverified against an official release notification.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The retailer pages describe lodging resistance from a dwarf plant structure, not drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- https://kbtagrimau.in/product_detail.php?id=230

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. -- searched; no page names disease or pest resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Retailer listings give a maturity of about 130 days (one listing gives 130-140 days) and describe a dwarf habit with better lodging stability. -- https://kbtagrimau.in/product_detail.php?id=230 ; https://agribiz.farm/product/indam-100-012/
No yield data, multi-location trial results or AICRP entries were found. -- no evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage as supplied in the record (IAHS 25A / IASN RB30-22 (P); A, B and R lines from the company's Rice R&D farm near Hyderabad): not confirmed by any search result. Source: user-supplied record only.
No evidence found for QTL, marker, genome or breeding-line code studies for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Retailer page lists the developer as "Pradyum Kushwaha" with the company Indo-American Hybrid Seeds (IAHS). This is a single retailer-page attribution, not confirmed by an official source. -- https://kbtagrimau.in/product_detail.php?id=230
Company background: Indo-American Hybrid Seeds (INDAM) is described as a breeder and supplier, founded in 1965, with rice among its crops. This is company-level only and does not name this variety. -- https://thursd.com/breeders/indam-seeds
Company product pages describe rice hybrids, aromatic hybrids and OP varieties, but the retrieved text does not name INDAM 100-012. -- https://www.indamseeds.com/products

CONTACT DETAILS
Company website found: https://www.indamseeds.com (no email, phone or postal address was found in the retrieved text).
No breeder contact, institute contact page, or station address was found. No evidence found for official email, phone, or address.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed papers, theses, conference papers or AICRP/ICAR reports naming this variety were returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Retailer listing (KBT Agri Research) shows the variety as sold out or out of stock, pack size 3 kg, category general. -- https://kbtagrimau.in/product_detail.php?id=230
Another retailer lists the variety as "INDAM 100012" with a 3 kg and 1 kg pack and a price range of ₹500 to ₹1,600, and calls it a hybrid paddy seed. -- https://agribiz.farm/product/indam-100-012/
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet seed-availability record was found. -- no evidence found for official channels.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found in search results. The Uttar Pradesh and Punjab entries come only from the supplied record and are not verified. No Seednet, CSC or notification page was returned.

RELEASE / NOTIFICATION (2021)
No evidence found. The 2021 year of release and CSC notification are from the supplied record only and are unverified.

basic_info.institution: Assam Agricultural University (AAU), via Regional/Zonal Research Station (RARS), Diphu (digest-confirmed; original record field NOT_STATED_IN_TABLE, verify)

drought.details: Under simulated drought (PEG spray, no irrigation), Inglongkiri had the smallest grain-yield reduction (about 2.3 percent) among six upland genotypes, and the source calls it one of the drought-tolerant varieties. A related AAU Jorhat study reports the lowest drought yield reduction (1.6 percent) among tested lines, with the highest N uptake and harvest index, and suggests it as a donor for direct-seeded upland, limited-moisture breeding. A physiological study judged it the most physiologically efficient of five traditional upland genotypes under drought, with higher chlorophyll (SPAD), nitrate reductase and related traits. AAU Diphu station notes list drought tolerance for this variety group for direct-seeded ahu rice. Variety record: drought tolerant. Mechanism-level detail beyond these physiological indicators: Not found in searched sources.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest states that heat was not covered by the stress query.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest states that salinity was not covered by the stress query.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest for flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance evidence found in the digest. The Karbi Anglong contingency plan lists Inglongkiri only as an autumn-rice recommendation without resistance data. The variety record (not a digest source) describes it as moderately susceptible to blast; this is not corroborated by any digest source.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The variety record lists pest reaction as Unknown.

agronomic_details.yield: 2.8 t/ha average in the 2011 CURE-ICIMOD upland validation across six sites (versus 2.6 t/ha for Maizu Biron). DARE report table: average yield 2,800 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the six-site 2011 validation.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed upland and direct-seeded upland/jhum rice in Assam's hill zones, including Karbi Anglong and Diphu-region upland. The AAU Jorhat achievements page lists it as suitable for hill situations. The AAU Diphu page notes popularity for direct-seeded ahu rice.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Described as tall (2014 AAU ICR Farm trial page). Variety record: moderately tolerant to lodging, non-shattering, responsive to fertilizer, suitable for sloping land (variety record, not a digest source). Morphological characteristics beyond these: Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Simulated drought, PEG spray, no irrigation: about 2.3 percent grain-yield reduction, smallest among six upland genotypes. (2) AAU Jorhat drought study: 1.6 percent yield reduction, lowest among tested lines. (3) Upland validation, 2011, CURE-ICIMOD, six sites: average 2.8 t/ha versus 2.6 t/ha for Maizu Biron. (4) DARE 2017-18 table: rainfed upland, 120 days, 2,800 kg/ha. (5) Autumn 2014 direct-seeded trial at AAU ICR Farm, Jorhat, comparing Inglongkiri with Maizubiron and Rasi under weed and nutrient treatments; no yield values in the digest; the source gives release year 2011, which conflicts with 2017 in the record. (6) 2023 field study at AAU Jorhat (Inglongkiri, Maizubiron, Rasi; weed and nutrient management, direct-seeded upland autumn rice; soil and yield data); no values given in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Inglongkiri (AAUDR 9301-14-1) / rice

Name note: No search returned a Seednet portal page for "Inglongkiri (AAUDR 9301-14-1) IET 17452 IC-559417", so the Seednet name is unverified. The evidence below refers to the name "Inglongkiri" with the AAUDR 9301-14-1 code, which appears in an ICAR DARE report table and an AAU Diphu paper. The IET and IC numbers were not seen on any page. The institution is confirmed as Assam Agricultural University (AAU), via the Regional/Zonal Research Station (RARS) at Diphu.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under simulated drought (PEG spray, no irrigation), Inglongkiri had the smallest grain-yield reduction (about 2.3 percent) among six upland genotypes, and the paper calls it one of the drought-tolerant varieties -- https://ijoear.com/article-details/approaches-for-enhancing-nitrogen-use-efficiency-in-some-upland-rice-oryza-sativa-l-genotypes-under-water-stress-conditions
- A related AAU Jorhat study reports the same variety with the lowest drought yield reduction (1.6 percent), the highest N uptake and harvest index among the tested lines, and suggests it as a donor for direct-seeded upland, limited-moisture breeding -- https://independent.academia.edu/LarbeenTeronpi
- Physiological study: Inglongkiri was judged the most physiologically efficient of five traditional upland genotypes under drought, with higher chlorophyll (SPAD), nitrate reductase and related traits -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340678458_Biochemical_indicators_in_upland_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_under_physiological_drought_condition
- Drought tolerance is also listed in AAU's Diphu station notes for this variety group (Inglongkiri, Rongkhang, Dehangi) for direct-seeded ahu rice -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/116
- Flood, submergence, salinity, heat: No evidence found. Searched only drought-related topics in the stress query; other stresses were not covered.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. The Karbi Anglong contingency plan lists Inglongkiri only as an autumn-rice recommendation and gives no resistance data for this variety -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/CP/Assam/Assam5-Karbi%20Anglong.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Upland validation (2011, CURE–ICIMOD project, six sites): average yield of Inglongkiri was 2.8 t/ha, versus 2.6 t/ha for Maizu Biron -- https://cure.irri.org/stories-archive/boosting-up-upland-rice-harvest-in-northeast-india
- DARE report table: Inglongkiri (AAUDR 9301-14-1) IET 17452 listed as rainfed upland rice, maturity 120 days, average yield 2,800 kg/ha -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/DARE-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf
- Autumn 2014 direct-seeded trial at AAU ICR Farm, Jorhat, comparing Inglongkiri with Maizubiron and Rasi under weed and nutrient treatments; the page describes the variety as tall and recommended for direct-seeded rain-fed upland/jhum in Assam's hill zones. Its release year is given as 2011, which conflicts with the 2017 year in the record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/367964404_Effect_of_irrigation_and_nutrient_management_on_growth_yield_and_evapotranspiration_of_direct_seeded_autumn_rice_Oryza_Sativa_under_the_Agro-climatic_conditions_of_Assam
- 2023 field study at AAU Jorhat (Inglongkiri, Maizubiron, Rasi; weed and nutrient management, direct-seeded upland autumn rice; soil and yield data) -- https://www.iaras.org/iaras/filedownloads/ijas/2023/014-0024(2023).pdf
- Seed of Inglongkiri was handed to trainees in an AAU RARS Diphu upland training program in 2011 -- https://cure.irri.org/stories-archive/boosting-up-upland-rice-harvest-in-northeast-india

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: the Assam rice-research history table lists "Inglongkiri (AAUDR 9301-14-1)" alongside "Maibee/CRM 53" and notes drought tolerance. This matches the parentage in the record (Maibi x CRM 53), but the source does not state the cross explicitly -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- Molecular diversity: Inglongkiri is one of 100 indigenous rice genotypes genotyped with 30 SSR markers (25 polymorphic, mean PIC 0.53). It is a genotype in the set, not a QTL study -- https://www.gkvsociety.com/control/uploads/7926825.pdf
- Breeding method, pedigree details, QTL, genes, and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: AAU Zonal/Regional Research Station, Diphu, which has developed six rice varieties through its breeding programme and promotes Inglongkiri for the hill zone -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/116
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. The Diphu station page lists no staff names.
- Varietal development recognition: AAU Jorhat's salient varietal achievements page lists Inglongkiri and Rongkhang as suitable for hill situations -- https://www.sentinelassam.com/more-news/life/salient-rice-varietal-achievements-of-assam-agricultural-university

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: JK Agri. Genetics Ltd., Hyderabad (Telangana)
seednet_fields.Parentage: JKRA 1102 X JKRR 10571, both the parents were developed from propriety Germplasm source of JK Agri Genetics Limited, Hyderabad.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated condones of kharif in Northern Zone (zone-II) comprising of states New Delhi, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, J&K, Rajasthan and Eastern Zone (Zone-III) comprising of Odisha, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Resistant to lodging, responsive to fertilizer under normal planting density and non-shattering. Seed rate: 15 kg/ha for normal density 20x15 cms spacing.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: 1.	White color of stigma:  White color of stigma 2.	Days to flowering: Early (71-90 Days): Medium (91-110 days).
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Long bold grains, Well exerted panicle exertion, erect flag, Late leaf senescence.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Moderately tolerance to biotic and abiotic stresses.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JKRH 2154 (IET 24914), Rice

Search limit note: the search tool's usage cap was reached after four queries. The queries I ran were: "JKRH 2154 Rice variety", "JKRH 2154 Rice breeder institute", "JKRH 2154 Rice research", and "JKRH 2154 (IET 24914) paddy seed". A fifth query for CSC/Seednet and contact details was blocked. Searches 2 to 4 returned no breeder, contact, or publication data. Everything below comes from result snippets I could read before the cap; I could not open the full pages. Names: "variety_name" is JKRH 2154 and "seednet_variety_name" is JKRH 2154 (IET 24914). No result I saw linked the release minutes or the Seednet portal entry to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for this variety. Only a marketing listing describing general vigor was returned (https://agribegri.com/products/jk-seeds-jkrh-2154-hybrid-paddy-seeds). That listing is commercial and does not report stress tests.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No resistance data for this variety appeared in the results.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The AICRIP Hybrid Rice Kharif 2015 report lists IET 24914, named JKRH-2154, in its trial entries, nominated by JK Seeds, Hyderabad -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf . This confirms the entry was under multi-location hybrid rice testing in 2015, before its 2021 release. I could not read yield data or zone-wise performance from the snippet. The marketing listing describes the seed as high-yielding with good germination and tillering, but this is an unverified product claim -- https://agribegri.com/products/jk-seeds-jkrh-2154-hybrid-paddy-seeds

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage as supplied: JKRA 1102 x JKRR 10571, both from proprietary JK Agri Genetics germplasm (Hyderabad). The A-line by R-line pattern fits a hybrid, and the marketing listing describes it as a hybrid. No independent source confirmed the parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, or genome resources. Source for the marketing description: https://agribegri.com/products/jk-seeds-jkrh-2154-hybrid-paddy-seeds

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Nominating agency per the AICRIP 2015 report: JK Seeds, Hyderabad -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf . The supplied developer is "JK Agri. Genetics Ltd." The AICRIP report uses "JK Seeds," so the company name is inconsistent across sources. No breeder or scientist name was found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, institute email, phone, postal address, or contact page was returned. Searches should be repeated for the company's corporate site or a Seednet listing.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, or KrishiKosh record was returned. The AICRIP 2015 trial report is a trial report entry, not a publication about this variety, and it is listed under AGRONOMY AND TRIALS.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Commercial listing (JK Seeds JKRH 2154 Hybrid Paddy Seeds, marketed as a hybrid paddy seed): https://agribegri.com/products/jk-seeds-jkrh-2154-hybrid-paddy-seeds . A Hindi-language promotional video also names JKRH 2154 as a hybrid paddy seed: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XdpT6NELKyg . Neither is an NSC, state corporation, KVK, or SAU source. No Seednet or CSC record was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The supplied states are Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal. I could not verify these from any source. No CSC notification or Seednet page was returned.

Summary: The variety's existence as a JK Seeds hybrid paddy is confirmed by a 2015 AICRIP trial entry and commercial listings. Its 2021 release, recommended states, parentage, stress data, breeder, and publications remain unverified. Next steps: check the CSC/ICAR release notification for 2021, search Seednet for "JKRH 2154 (IET 24914)", and contact JK Agri Genetics Ltd. directly for breeder details.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JKRH 2354 (IET 26468), Rice
Name note: "JKRH 2354" (CSC release minutes name) and "JKRH 2354 (IET 26468)" (Seednet name) were both searched. The Seednet portal itself was not reachable in these searches, so Seednet-specific evidence is absent. Every finding below refers to the variety under the name shown in its source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Searches returned only general rice-breeding material for these traits.

DISEASE AND PEST
The JK Agri Genetics paddy listing gives JKRH2354(IET26468) as having moderate tolerance to leaf blast. -- https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/paddy/
No evidence found for BLB, BPH, or other pest resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A correlation and path analysis paper on rice includes JKRH-2354 in a comparison table with days to 50% flowering, plant height, panicles per square metre and yield. In that table the row for JKRH-2354 reads 73 days to 50% flowering, 108.3 cm plant height, 255 panicles per m², and 1766.6 kg/ha yield. The table layout is garbled in the extracted text, so treat these values as provisional and check them against the original paper. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359706304_Correlation_and_path_coeffecient_analysis_in_rice_Oryza_sativa_L
No multi-location trial, AICRP, or maturity-group data were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (JKRA 1104 x JKRR 10571; both parents from JK Agri Genetics proprietary germplasm) comes from the supplied variety record only. No web source confirmed it. -- supplied record, no URL
Breeding method, breeding-line codes beyond the variety code IET 26468, and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No breeder or scientist name was found for this variety. The developer is recorded as JK Agri Genetics Limited, Begumpet, Hyderabad. -- https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/paddy/
The Hyderabad company listing is the only institutional source found. -- https://jkagri.com/products/field-crops/

CONTACT DETAILS
Company address as listed: JK Agri Genetics Limited, 1-10-177, 4th floor, Varun Towers, Begumpet, Hyderabad – 500016. -- https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/paddy/
Email, phone, and breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Kishore NS et al. attribution is not confirmed for the paper below; the author list was not visible in the retrieved text. No authors verified. (Year not stated in source). Correlation and path coefficient analysis in rice (Oryza sativa L.). ResearchGate preprint/PDF (journal and year not identified) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359706304_Correlation_and_path_coeffecient_analysis_in_rice_Oryza_sativa_L
No KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR reports, peer-reviewed journal articles, or DOIs were found for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
JKRH2354(IET26468) is listed as a product on the JK Agri Genetics paddy page. -- https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/paddy/
No state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing specifically for JKRH 2354 was found. Results for JK Seeds JKRH 2154 and generic hybrid paddy from J. K. Seeds were discarded because they name different products.

RECOMMENDED STATES
The notified paddy list for 2011 to 2021 records JKRH 2354 (IET 26468), released in 2021 under S.O. 500(E) dated 29.01.2021, for Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
The hybrid list gives the same states and a 2021 release year but no maturity or yield values, and it lists the developer as JK Agri Genetics Limited Telangana. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/

Discarded as non-matching: the "Shobhini (RNR 2354)" entry in the IIRR newsletter, the "JKRH-401" and "KRH-2" entries in the NRRI review, and the JK Seeds JKRH 2154 listing.

seednet_fields.Parentage: MTU1010 X NLR 34449 X MTU 1010. MTU 1010 is a short duration variety with long slender grain type having tolerance to BPH and susceptibility to gall midge. NLR 34449 is a short duration variety with medium slender grain, dwarf in nature having resistance to blast and susceptibility to BPH.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigate areas of Telangana State
seednet_fields.Maturity (in days): Seed to flowering: 90-95 days in Kharif, 105 to 110 days during Rabi. Seed to seed: 120-125 days (Kharif) 135-140 days Rabi.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Due to semi dwarf in height and strong culm it is tolerant to lodging and resists shattering. Suitable for sowing from 1st June to July end. It has good yield potential under different nitrogen levels.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Enclosed morphological description including DUS  Erect, semi dwarf plant type, long bold and slightly awned grains at the tip with good panicle exertion and medium tillering habit.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Resistant to cold at seeding stage.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Tolerant to blast and brown spot.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Tolerant to BPH and gallmidge biotypes 1,3 and 5
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Basal: 15 kg N-20 kg P2O5-8 kg K2O. 1st top dressing at 20-25 DAT: 15 kg N. 2nd top dressing at panicle initiation stage: 15 kg N-8 kg K2O. During rabi season 50% additional nitrogen over recommended

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jagtiala Rice-1 (JGL 24423)

Name note: The CSC/release-minute name is "Jagtiala Rice-1" and the Seednet name is "Jagtiala Rice-1 (JGL24423) (IET 25310)." The retrieved PJTAU pages use "Jagtiala Rice 1 (JGL 24423)" and "JGL-24423 (Jagtial Rice-1)." No retrieved page was a Seednet page, so none of the evidence below is confirmed to come from Seednet. Four searches were run. The user's year (2020) conflicts with the PJTAU table (2019). I did not search Seednet directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The four searches returned no page reporting drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence reactions for this variety. -- Searches 1 and 3 (https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/ returned no stress data)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No retrieved page reports blast, BPH, gall midge or other resistance for JGL 24423. The BPH and gall-midge traits in the user's parentage note are unverified and were not found in any retrieved source. -- Searches 1 and 3

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- JGL 24423 was used as a locally popular check in a 2019 Kharif test-cross nursery of 170 F1 rice hybrids; the page reports yields for the hybrids, not for the check. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331472115_Evaluation_of_Different_Rice_Hybrids_on_Morphological_and_Traits_and_Quality_Attributes_in_Adaptability_Yield_Trials
- JGL 24423 was named as a check in a standard-heterosis study of rice hybrids; the page does not give its yield. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395230794_Assessment_of_standard_heterosis_for_yield_traits_in_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_hybrids
- A KNM 7048 variety paper cites Jagtiala Rice 1 (JGL 24423) only as a morphological comparator (1000-grain weight is reported for KNM 7048, not for this variety). This is not evidence for JGL 24423 and was not used. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/399796804_KNM_7048_-_a_high_yielding_early_maturing_long_bold_PJTAU_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_variety_suitable_for_the_states_of_Odisha_West_Bengal_Chhattisgarh_and_Maharashtra
- An unofficial LinkedIn post by a researcher reports production and sale of more than 10 million kg of JGL24423, described as long-bold and mid-early. This is not an official source. -- https://www.linkedin.com/in/ramegowda-goravale-1433871a/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME NOTE: "Kunaram Rice-1" (CSC/input name) and "Kunaram Rice-1 (KNM 733) (IET 27405)" (Seednet) were both searched. The evidence below refers to "Kunaram Rice 1 (KNM 733)" unless stated otherwise. The PJTSAU page lists release year 2019 (SVRC), but the input says 2020. Searches also returned KNM 1638 / Kunaram Vari 2 material, which was discarded as a different variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Kunaram Rice 1 / KNM 733. Searches returned only KNM 1638 material.

DISEASE AND PEST -- A ResearchGate-hosted document (Telangana State (506 007) rice research centre report, PP House 2022) lists KNM 733 among three cultures tested at ARS Kunaram, and in the same passage mentions gall midge (biotype-3) resistance, but the excerpt does not clearly attribute that resistance to KNM 733 -- unverified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre
No other disease or pest resistance evidence found for KNM 733 / Kunaram Rice 1.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Nitrogen-response field experiments (kharif 2019 and 2020, transplanted rice, 75/100/125/150% of recommended N) at ARS Kunaram compared KNM 733, KNM 1638 and RNR 15048; the excerpt is truncated and yield results were not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sreedhar-Siddi/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre/links/62fe0727ceb9764f7204ea59/Telangana-State-506-007-India-3-Rice-Research-Centre-7-Administrative-Office-8-Seed-Research-and-Technology-Centre.pdf

Maturity, yield and multi-location trial data for this variety: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY EVIDENCE DIGEST: Luna Sampad / LUNASAMPAD (IET 19470), Rice (paddy)

Name note: "Luna Sampad" is the CSC/CR name (also listed as CR Dhan 402 and CR LC2095-181-1). The seednet name is "LUNASAMPAD (IET 19470)". The notification list spells it "Luna Sanpad (IET 19470)". All findings below refer to this variety (Odisha, 2010/2011 release). Pages on "Sampada" (DRR Dhan 37, Nuziveedu, IIRR GI study) were discarded as different varieties.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerant of coastal saline/rainfed saline conditions in Odisha, 5.0 to 8.0 dS/m -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
Released for coastal saline situations; listed under coastal saline ecology, 2010 release -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/

DISEASE AND PEST
Listed as resistant to blast, tolerant of stem borer, BPH and leaf folder -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
Tolerant of stem borer (deadhearts and whiteheads), leaf folder, whorl maggot and rice hispa, per the NRRI list -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
Moderate resistance to brown plant hopper reported for Lunasampad in NRRI variety review -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
2019-20 BPH screen (99 NRRI varieties): Luna Sampad had a damage score of 3.00, among the least damaged, versus 7.00 to 9.00 for susceptible entries -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ije-83-2-016

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Medium-late duration (about 140 days), tall (about 130 cm) -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
Yield 3.6 to 4.2 t/ha -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
Duration 140 days, grain type SB (Swarna-type/slender bold classification as listed), Odisha -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391
Multi-location or field-trial data beyond the above: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Breeding-line code CR LC2095-181-1 (as CR2095-181-1 in the 2011 salinity paper) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262145028_Luna_Suvarna_CR2096-71-2_and_Luna_Sampad_CR2095-181-1_Rice_varieties_for_tolerance_to_coastal_salinity
Parentage MAHSURI X CHAKRAKANDA (from your record): not confirmed by any retrieved page
BPH resistance-gene or QTL information specific to this variety: No evidence found (the 2021 BPH paper screened it but reports no gene identity)
Breeding method, marker-assisted work, genome resources: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by ICAR-National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack; the NRRI release list places it under Orissa, 2010 -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found in any retrieved page
Release record: CVRC/notification 2011, S.O. 632(E), 25.03.2011, Odisha -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder name, email, phone or postal address for this variety was found in the retrieved pages. Institute page found (no contact details captured): https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
Institute-level contact for ICAR-NRRI (not captured by this search): No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
Sen P. et al. (2011). Luna Suvarna CR2096-71-2 and Luna Sampad (CR2095-181-1): Rice varieties for tolerance to coastal salinity. Journal/report not stated in retrieved text (ResearchGate record dated Jan 2011) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262145028_Luna_Suvarna_CR2096-71-2_and_Luna_Sampad_CR2095-181-1_Rice_varieties_for_tolerance_to_coastal_salinity
Author list for 2021 (2019-20 BPH screening paper). Authors not shown in retrieved text. (2021). Evaluation of rice genotypes for resistance to brown plant hopper (Nilaparvata lugens) including Luna Sampad. Indian Journal of Entomology 83(2) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ije-83-2-016 (DOI not retrieved)
ICAR-NRRI rice varieties review PDF (year and authors not retrieved) -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
KrishiKosh theses or AICRP annual reports on this variety: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for LUNASAMPAD / Luna Sampad: No evidence found. The notification list (global-agriculture.com, drdpat.bih.nic.in) confirms notification only, not seed sales.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Odisha (coastal saline / rainfed saline situations) -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
Odisha, notified 2011 -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MRP 5408 (seednet name: MRP 5408 (MEPH 114 (IET 24143)); CSC/notification name: MRP 5408 (MEPH 114 (IET 24143)); variety code MEPH 114 (IET 24143); crop: Rice/Paddy

Search budget: all 4 permitted web_search queries were used. Searches 1 and 2 returned mostly unrelated pages. Search 3 returned the notification list and the product page. Search 4 returned the product page and other Mahyco pages. The evidence below refers to the name "MRP 5408" and the code "MEPH 114 (IET 24143)" as they appear on the cited pages. The two names in the brief are identical, so no separate search was needed for the Seednet name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The only stress-related statement is leaf blast tolerance (see DISEASE AND PEST). Searches returned no other stress data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- The Mahyco product page lists MRP 5408 as tolerant to leaf blast. -- https://www.mahyco.com/mrp-5408.html
DISEASE AND PEST -- The same claim appears on the Mahyco paddy hybrid page, which has an MRP 5408 product heading. -- https://www.mahyco.com/paddy-hybrid.html (page confirms the name only; no trait text found there)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Product page gives duration as 130-135 days (marked with an asterisk, meaning a conditional/approximate figure). -- https://www.mahyco.com/mrp-5408.html
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Product page lists more productive tillers per plant, more grains per panicle, long and heavy panicles with good grain filling, long slender shiny grain, and high yield potential, with no numeric yield figures. -- https://www.mahyco.com/mrp-5408.html
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No field-trial or multi-location yield data for MRP 5408 were found. Mahyco's general research page says it runs a multi-location performance testing programme at 18 centres, but it names no results for this variety. -- https://www.mahyco.com/research-development.html

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage: Unknown. No pedigree, breeding method, breeding-line code beyond MEPH 114 (IET 24143), genes, or QTL data were found for this variety. The IET number appears only in the notification list (see RECOMMENDED STATES). -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing/notifying institution (per notification list): Maharashtra Hybrid Seeds Company Pvt. Ltd. (Mahyco). -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/ and https://www.mahyco.com/mrp-5408.html
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. Searches for "breeder / developed by" returned no named breeder for MRP 5408.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Mahyco describes itself as a seed company with R&D in molecular breeding and abiotic stress research, and it reports six research centres in India. This is company-level information, not variety-specific. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahyco

CONTACT DETAILS -- Mahyco Private Limited corporate office, as listed on the product page: 19, Raj Mahal, 84, Veer Nariman Road, Mumbai 400020. -- https://www.mahyco.com/mrp-5408.html
CONTACT DETAILS -- Mahyco research paddy listing gives a Jalna-Aurangabad Road address: Mahyco Private Limited, Jalna – Aurangabad Road, At. Dawalwadi, Tq. Badnapur, P.O. (institute-level address; not confirmed as MRP 5408's breeding station). -- https://www.mahyco.com/research-paddy.html
CONTACT DETAILS -- Names, roles, emails and phone numbers: No evidence found. The product page has "Call Us" and "Email Us" headings but no actual phone number or email address in the captured text.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. Searches for papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, theses or conference papers on MRP 5408 returned none. The only items were product and notification pages.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Mahyco product page for MRP 5408 exists, indicating the company markets the variety as a paddy hybrid. No dealer, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listings were found. -- https://www.mahyco.com/mrp-5408.html
SEED AVAILABILITY -- Seednet (seednet.gov.in) was not reached through these searches, so Seednet status is unverified. No Seednet URL was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Notification entry: MRP 5408 (MEPH 114 (IET 24143), year 2018, S.O. 399 (E) dated 24.01.2018, recommended for Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Puducherry. This is a Hindi-language list of notified paddy varieties for 2011 to 2021. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
RECOMMENDED STATES -- The raw input states (AP, Karnataka and Puducherry) match this notification entry. The primary gazette (egazette.gov.in or the CSC minutes) was not retrieved and should be checked before the record is finalised.

Notes for the record: The "Parentage: Unknown" value and the absence of a named breeder should be kept as is. Mahyco's product page is a marketing source, not peer-reviewed evidence, and the duration and tolerance claims there are not backed by trial data in these results.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Motigold (variety_name) / MOTI GOLD (NP 1024) (seednet_variety_name), Rice

Searches run: 4 (limit reached). Query 1 used "Motigold Rice variety"; query 2 "Motigold rice breeder developed by NuziveeduSeeds"; query 3 "Motigold NP 1024 rice research"; query 4 "Motigold rice seed availability". No query used the exact Seednet name "MOTI GOLD (NP 1024)", and no Seednet or CSC release-minute page was returned. Evidence below refers to the company's "Moti gold NP-1024" product name, which matches the variety_code, so I treat it as this variety. Pages about the unrelated Motipure/Motigold rice brand of Moti Foods (IndiaMART, a basmati and sambha rice seller) were discarded as a name resemblance.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety. The only related point is that a sister company variety (Champion NPH-207) is described as water-stress tolerant, which does not apply to Motigold -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The company's field-crop page lists blast tolerance only for a different variety (Sandhya NP-9359), not for Motigold -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Company product listing states Motigold NP-1024 matures in 135-140 days, with medium fine grains, high filled grains per panicle and higher head rice recovery -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/
Company blog (2017) gives plant height 90-95 cm, maturity 130-135 days, medium slender grain, suitability Kharif and Rabi, and claims of excellent cooking quality, fine grain and a long panicle with more grains and high yield (promotional, no trial data) -- http://nuziveedu-seeds.blogspot.com/2017/01/np-1024-moti-gold.html
Note: the two company sources disagree on maturity (130-135 vs 135-140 days). No multi-location or AICRP trial results found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The parentage PRN55/PRN14 given in the variety record was not confirmed by any search result. No QTL, marker or genome data for this variety were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found for a named breeder or scientist. The company is Nuziveedu Seeds, a Hyderabad-headquartered agribusiness; the Wikipedia entry names M. Prabhakara Rao as a key person of the company, but this is a company role, not a breeder attribution to Motigold -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuziveedu_Seeds
Company profile: the company focuses on breeding, production and marketing of cotton, hybrid field crops and vegetables, with maize and rice as main crops -- https://www.accesstoseeds.org/index/south-southeast-asia/company-scorecards/nuziveedu-seeds/

CONTACT DETAILS: No individual contact found. No email, phone or postal address for the Nuziveedu rice programme or Kandlakoya station was returned by the searches. Institute-level website only: Nuziveedu Seeds Limited homepage -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/ (company page; contact details not verified from the page text retrieved).
Address given in the variety record (not verified by search): Nuziveedu Seeds Pvt. Ltd., Kandlakoya, Ranga Reddy Dist., Andhra Pradesh.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. None of the returned papers (for example, rice salinity and nanoparticle studies, and QTL studies on other rice lines) concern Motigold or NP-1024. These were discarded under the strict relevance rule. No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer stock. The company product page lists the variety but gives no dealer or stockist details -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/
The 2017 company blog includes a price-enquiry comment, which is not a verified dealer listing -- http://nuziveedu-seeds.blogspot.com/2017/01/np-1024-moti-gold.html

RECOMMENDED STATES: Company product page lists Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Odisha, Telangana and West Bengal for Moti gold NP-1024 -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/
Company blog (2017) lists irrigated areas of AP, Telangana, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, WB, Bihar, Jharkhand, UP, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. These lists differ from each other and from the release record, which names only Andhra Pradesh -- http://nuziveedu-seeds.blogspot.com/2017/01/np-1024-moti-gold.html

GAPS TO CLOSE: No CSC release notification, Seednet entry, ICAR/SAU release record, breeder name or peer-reviewed source was found. Verifying these needs a direct search of seednet.gov.in and the CSC variety notification list for "MOTI GOLD (NP 1024)".

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NDR 2065 (IET 17476), Rice

NAME NOTE: The CSC/notification name is "NDR 2065". The Seednet name is "NDR 2065 (IET 17476)". One notification listing gives the code as IET 17475 rather than IET 17476. Every finding below was found under "NDR 2065" and cross-checked against the IET 17476 code where a source gave it.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The ICAR crop improvement report lists NDR 2065 with resistance codes "LB R-Bl, WBPH, GM" among the varieties released that year. The report does not expand the codes, so they are recorded as printed. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- The NDUAT research highlights say the variety is resistant to sheath rot. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- A 2026 seedling-stage study on PEG-induced osmotic stress scored NDR-2065 with a mid-range index sum of 4.6. This is seedling and root-architecture evidence only, not field drought tolerance. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sustainable-food-systems/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2026.1865363/full
- No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistance to sheath rot is recorded (see above). -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- Pest and disease codes "LB R-Bl, WBPH, GM" are listed (see stress section). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- No evidence found for blast, bacterial blight specifics, or brown planthopper beyond the codes above.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is given as 120-125 days, with yield potential of 50-55 q/ha, long bold grain, and suitability for early-sown conditions. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- In a direct-seeded trial, NDR-2065 gave a grain yield of 4.78 t/ha and a biological yield of 9.71 t/ha, higher than drum-seeded and direct-seeded methods compared. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346487641_DIRECT_SEEDED_RICE-FUTURE_OF_RICE_Oryza_sativa_CULTIVATION
- A 2018 Kharif trial sowed NDR-2065 on 6 July, transplanted it on 30 July, and harvested on 15 November, with 120 kg N as the fertilizer dose. -- https://hal.science/hal-05034034v1/document
- NDR-2065 was used as the test crop in a summer rice integrated nutrient management trial. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342570837_Effect_of_Integrated_Nutrient_Management_on_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Content_and_Economics_of_Summer_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- The IIRR 2022 annual report mentions NDR 2065 in a trial at Ghaghraghat, but the extracted text is truncated and gives no result. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage is recorded as (Pant Dhan-4 × Saket 4) × NDR 2018, with IET 17476, notified 2011, for UP. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382209019_Translating_Science_for_the_Benefits_of_Society_The_Direct_and_Indirect_Impacts_of_NRRI
- The parentage is consistent with the parentage supplied in the task. No breeding method, breeding-line history, QTL, marker study or genome resource was found. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The NRRI Cuttack bulletin lists the variety in its varietal portfolio entry with the parentage above. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382209019_Translating_Science_for_the_Benefits_of_Society_The_Direct_and_Indirect_Impacts_of_NRRI
- The NDUAT research highlights list NDR-2065 among varieties developed by the university. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- So the developing institution is not settled by the evidence: the NDUAT listing points to Narendra Dev University of Agriculture & Technology, while the NRRI entry shows Cuttack in the portfolio. Note that the institution field in the task ("Uttar Pradesh") is a state, not an institution.
- No lead breeder or scientist name was found for this variety. -- No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone, postal address or institute contact page was found in the search results. -- No evidence found
- The only institution names found are ICAR-National Rice Research Institute, Cuttack, and the NDUAT research network, which appear without contact details.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated (2014). Research Highlights, Research Network, NDUAT. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- ICAR (2011-12). Crop Improvement, Annual Report, AICRIP/ICAR. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- ICAR-IIRR (2022). Annual Report 2022. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
- Authors not stated (2022). Impact of breeder seed multiplication and certified quality seed distribution on rice production in India. CABI/Agriculture & Food Security journal -- https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2 (DOI 10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2)
- Authors not stated (2018 trial, published on HAL). Effect of Different Establishment and Weed Management (trial using NDR-2065). -- https://hal.science/hal-05034034v1/document
- Authors not stated. Direct Seeded Rice: Future of Rice (Oryza sativa) Cultivation. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346487641_DIRECT_SEEDED_RICE-FUTURE_OF_RICE_Oryza_sativa_CULTIVATION
- Authors not stated. Effect of Integrated Nutrient Management on Growth, Yield, Nutrient Content and Economics of Summer Rice. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342570837_Effect_of_Integrated_Nutrient_Management_on_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Content_and_Economics_of_Summer_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Authors not stated (2026). Multi-trait selection of drought tolerant rice genotypes based on seedling and root architecture responses to PEG-induced osmotic stress. Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sustainable-food-systems/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2026.1865363/full (DOI 10.3389/fsufs.2026.1865363)
- Authors not stated. Translating Science for the Benefits of Society: The Direct and Indirect Impacts of NRRI. ICAR-NRRI bulletin -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382209019_Translating_Science_for_the_Benefits_of_Society_The_Direct_and_Indirect_Impacts_of_NRRI
- KrishiKosh theses and peer-reviewed papers with QTL or marker data on this variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The variety is among those whose breeder seed was produced over a five-year period in the CABI study. -- https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2
- The IIRR 2022 report says breeder seed was produced for 305 rice varieties across 49 centres, but the text does not name NDR 2065 in that count. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
- The NDUAT highlights say the university produces breeder and foundation seed of its crops, without naming NDR 2065 in that statement. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- No Seednet listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or private dealer record was found, and the Seednet portal was not returned by any search. -- No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The ICAR report recommends the variety for irrigated areas of Uttar Pradesh. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- The notification is S.O.1661(E), dated 20.07.2011, for UP. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- The task's "recommended_states_raw" value was "Unknown", which the search has now resolved to UP.
