disease_resistance.summary: Blast: resistant and tolerant per the input CSC disease reaction record (listed as 'Resistant to blast' and 'Tolerant to blast'). The on-farm testing paper (ResearchGate) lists NDLR-7 as tolerant to blast and gives year-wise blast incidence compared with BPT in a trial table; the figures are not given in the digest. Sheath blight: tolerant, per the on-farm testing paper (ResearchGate). Leaf folder: tolerant, per the same paper. Gall midge is listed under pest resistance below. No other disease evidence was found in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Gall midge: tolerant (input CSC pest reaction; on-farm testing paper). Gall midge biotype IV: multiple resistant line, per input CSC pest reaction (the digest gives no URL for this item). Sucking pests: tolerant, per input CSC pest reaction. Brown planthopper (BPH): tolerant per the on-farm testing paper; Chittoor observations report lower BPH counts in NDLR-7 than in BPT 5204 in all three years observed; an ICAR kharif advisory 2025 lists the variety for BPH-prone areas (this is an area listing, not a resistance rating). Stem borer: multiple resistant line, per input CSC pest reaction (no URL in digest). Leaf folder: tolerant, per the on-farm testing paper.

agronomic_details.yield: 7536 kg/ha (input CSC record; KVK adaptive minikits in 30-35 farmer fields across locations, 2012-13 to 2014-15, distributed through KVK Yagantipalli), compared with 5495 kg/ha for check BPT 5204. Rice database entry gives a yield range of 65.0-70.0 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Non-lodging and non-shattering (input). Higher mean yield than BPT 5204 across multiple farmer-field locations over three seasons (input). Lower BPH counts than BPT 5204 in all three years of Chittoor observations. Stability across environments is not quantified in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for late sown conditions and scarce rainfall zones (input; rice database entry). Listed for BPH-prone areas in the ICAR kharif advisory 2025 (no state named). Short duration allows two seasons per year (Semantic Scholar success-story paper). Fertilizer responsive (input). Tested in Kurnool district and Chittoor district of Andhra Pradesh.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium slender (on-farm trial data, BIA0004934). Non-lodging, non-shattering, fertilizer responsive (input agronomic features). The input morphological_characteristics field is 'Unknown'. Note that the digest's on-farm trial duration of 130-135 days (2012-15) conflicts with the input maturity of 102-103 days.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) KVK adaptive minikits, 30-35 farmer fields, 2012-13 to 2014-15: mean yield 7536 kg/ha vs BPT 5204 at 5495 kg/ha (input). (2) Kurnool on-farm test (KVK Banavasi, 2016-17 onward): cultivation cost fell from Rs 66,050/ha to Rs 50,538/ha through reduced pesticide use (IJSR paper). (3) Chittoor on-farm trials: benefit-cost ratio 2.2 and average net returns Rs 76,808/ha over three years (BIA0004934). (4) Chittoor observations: lower BPH counts than BPT 5204 in all three years (BIA0004934). (5) Year-wise blast incidence compared with BPT in a trial table (figures not given in digest; ResearchGate paper). (6) NIVAR cyclone (2020) performance was tabulated in the IJSR paper, but the figures were not given in the excerpt. (7) On-farm testing in Kurnool district (ResearchGate paper): results summarised as NDLR-7 vs BPT-5204; quantitative details not given in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Nandyala Sona (NDLR-7), Rice

Name check: the CSC minutes name is "Nandyala Sona (NDLR-7)" and the Seednet name is "Nandyala Sona (NDLR 7) (IET No.23715)". The ANGRAU annual report uses the first form. The other sources use "NDLR-7", "NDLR 7" or "Nandyal Sona", and none mention IET 23715. Four searches were run. No KrishiKosh, Seednet or ICAR-specific page was returned, so the record is weaker on official sources than it should be.

Release status conflicts with the input. The input says "Not applicable (rejected)", but the evidence shows the variety was released and notified. The IJSR paper says it was developed and released by RARS Nandyal in 2016 and notified in 2018 (gazette 399E dated 24-1-2018) -- https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v10i7/SR21707143006.pdf. An ICAR-linked "Rice Data" table gives a release year of 2017 -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php. I could not find any rejection record, so please check the CSC minutes directly before accepting "rejected".

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Tolerant to blast, BPH (brown planthopper), sheath blight, leaf folder and gall midge, per on-farm testing papers -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346660778_On_Farm_Testing_of_Rice_Variety_NDLR-7_as_an_Alternative_to_Traditionally_Grown_BPT-5204_in_Kurnool_District_of_Andhra_Pradesh ; Tolerant to water stress and recommended for scarce rainfall zones (database entry) -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php ; Described as a drought-resistant variety in a secondary citation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346660778_On_Farm_Testing_of_Rice_Variety_NDLR-7_as_an_Alternative_to_Traditionally_Grown_BPT-5204_in_Kurnool_District_of_Andhra_Pradesh ; Reported as having a non-lodging character -- https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v10i7/SR21707143006.pdf ; Performance during the NIVAR cyclone (2020) was tabulated, but the excerpt did not give the figures -- https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v10i7/SR21707143006.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- Lower BPH counts in NDLR-7 than BPT 5204 in all three years of Chittoor observations -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0004934 ; Listed as BPH-prone-area and scarce-rainfall-zone variety by ICAR kharif advisory 2025 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/ICAR-En-Kharif-Agro-Advisories-for-Farmers-2025.pdf ; Year-wise blast incidence compared with BPT in a trial table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346660778_On_Farm_Testing_of_Rice_Variety_NDLR-7_as_an_Alternative_to_Traditionally_Grown_BPT-5204_in_Kurnool_District_of_Andhra_Pradesh

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Medium slender, short-duration variety of 130-135 days in on-farm trials (2012-15) -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0004934 ; Yield range of 65.0-70.0 q/ha listed in database entry -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php ; Kurnool on-farm test (KVK Banavasi, 2016-17 onward): cultivation cost fell from Rs 66,050/ha to Rs 50,538/ha through reduced pesticide use -- https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v10i7/SR21707143006.pdf ; Chittoor on-farm trials: benefit-cost ratio of 2.2 and average net returns of Rs 76,808/ha over three years -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0004934 ; Suitable for two seasons because of short duration -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Success-Story-of-Fine-Grain-Rice-Variety-NDLR-7-Gayathri-Reddy/29154283e7f365c5efc431e1b8b0418c87ea9d9c

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The parentage "BPT 3291 x CR 157-212" was not confirmed. BPT 3291 is Sona Mahsuri, a different variety, and its parentage is Sona/Mahsuri -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf . No breeding-line code, breeding method, QTL, marker or genome study was found for NDLR-7.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developed by Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Nandyal, Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) -- https://fpohub.com/product/paddy-ndlr-7-proddutur/ ; Developed under RARS Nandyal, ANGRAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346660778_On_Farm_Testing_of_Rice_Variety_NDLR-7_as_an_Alternative_to_Traditionally_Grown_BPT-5204_in_Kurnool_District_of_Andhra_Pradesh ; Lead breeder name not identified. A "Scientist (Genetics & Plant Breeding), Rice Breeding" credit appears in the IJSR paper, but the name is not clearly attached to NDLR-7 -- https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v10i7/SR21707143006.pdf ; Named as NDLR-7 authors on the 2021 success-story paper: N.K. Gayathri, B. Gopal Reddy, A. Vishnuvardhan Reddy. These are authors of the paper, not confirmed breeders -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Success-Story-of-Fine-Grain-Rice-Variety-NDLR-7-Gayathri-Reddy/29154283e7f365c5efc431e1b8b0418c87ea9d9c ; Named as co-authors of the 2020 on-farm paper: M.S. Jayalakshmi and G. Prasad Babu -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/On-Farm-Testing-of-Rice-Variety-NDLR-7-as-an-to-in-Jayalakshmi-Babu/414715b6c5300bbce38863628a51d6975db16cc9 ; Excluded: Kaderbad Ravindranath appears in results, but his page covers cotton breeding and is not about NDLR-7.

Stem borer: multiple resistant line, per input CSC pest reaction (no URL in digest). Leaf folder: tolerant, per the on-farm testing paper.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Nellore Siri (NLR 4001) (IET 25273), Rice

Searches run (4 of 4 allowed): "Nellore Siri rice variety"; "Nellore Siri NLR 4001 rice breeder institute"; "NLR 4001 IET 25273 rice research"; "Nellore Siri paddy seed availability". No search returned a seednet.gov.in page, an ICAR or institute page for this variety, or a KrishiKosh/AICRP record. Name note: the evidence below uses "Nellore Siri (NLR 4001)" and "NLR 4001". Neither "variety_name" nor "seednet_variety_name" appears in a Seednet record in these results.

STRESS TOLERANCE
A 2017 Deccan Chronicle report says NLR 4001 is a 145-day, fine-grain type tolerant to pests and diseases, and was then in its third year of farmer-field testing (pre-release) -- https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/170817/six-new-rice-varieties-are-under-research.html
Evidence for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
Wikipedia describes NLR 4001 as a pest-resistant fine-grain variety under research at the Rice Research Station, Nellore -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molakolukulu
The 2017 Deccan Chronicle report (above) also gives tolerance to pests and diseases; no specific pest or disease names or scores were found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A Hans India report says the state-released Nellore Siri (NLR 4001) and Sugandha are suited to organic farming that cuts nitrogen use substantially -- https://www.thehansindia.com/andhra-pradesh/andhra-pradesh-government-releases-three-new-rice-varieties-632705
A ResearchGate ANGRAU "VAR IMPACT 2024" report lists NLR 4001 among Nellore varieties in the Mega Rice Varietal Display (April 2021) and in an indent table (figures 2.2, 2.6, 0.4 in one row, column meanings not clear from the excerpt) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390283915_ANGRAU_VAR_IMPACT_2024
Yield data for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage (NLR 145 x MTU 5249) and breeding line NLR 5785-12-2-1-2-1 are from the submitted record only; no web source confirmed them. No evidence found in searches.
Breeding line code NLR 4001 is confirmed by the sources above (Hans India, Deccan Chronicle, Wikipedia).
Genes, QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found. The "NLR 4001 IET 25273" search returned unrelated papers (for example NRT1.1B and nitrogen studies) and these were discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by the Agriculture Research Station (ARS), Nellore, under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) -- https://www.thehansindia.com/andhra-pradesh/andhra-pradesh-government-releases-three-new-rice-varieties-632705
The same station's rice work is described as a sub-centre of the National Agriculture Research Project since 1985 -- https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/170817/six-new-rice-varieties-are-under-research.html
Lead breeder name for NLR 4001: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level contact only (no breeder contact found). ARS Nellore, from the ANGRAU seed availability list (as on 10.01.2022): Dr. P. Rajasekhar, Principal Scientist (Entomology) and Head, ARS Nellore, phone 9490327424, email ars.nellore@angrau.ac.in. This is listed as the ARS contact, not as NLR 4001's breeder -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Seed_Availability_in_ANGRAU_as_on_10_01_2022.pdf
Postal address of ARS Nellore: No evidence found. KVK Nellore site: https://www.kvknellore-angrau.org/index.php/technologies (no contact details captured in the excerpt).

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, thesis, or conference paper on NLR 4001 was found. The only documents were news items and a 2024 ANGRAU impact report (listed under AGRONOMY AND TRIALS), which are not publications.

SEED AVAILABILITY
ANGRAU seed availability list as on 10.01.2022 (ARS Nellore, KVK Nellore, paddy): https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Seed_Availability_in_ANGRAU_as_on_10_01_2022.pdf -- the excerpt shows ARS Nellore breeder seed for NLR 145 and NLR 30491 and KVK Nellore foundation seed for NLR 3354 and NLR 34449, but no NLR 4001 row was visible, and the excerpt was truncated. Whether NLR 4001 is listed is unconfirmed.
NSC, State Seed Corporation, or private dealer listings for NLR 4001: No evidence found. Dealer listings returned were for "Nellore sannalu" or other paddy and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Andhra Pradesh, released by the state government as one of three varieties from ARS Nellore -- https://www.thehansindia.com/andhra-pradesh/andhra-pradesh-government-releases-three-new-rice-varieties-632705
The release year (2020) is from the submitted record; the release article's date was not captured, so it is not independently confirmed.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Nellore Sugandha (NLR 40054) (IET 23194), Rice (Paddy)

Name note: variety_name is "Nellore Sugandha" (CSC minutes) and seednet_variety_name is "Nellore Sugandha (NLR 40054) (IET 23194)" (Seednet). I searched both names, plus the codes NLR 40054 and IET 23194, the parentage lines (MTU 7029, RNR 19994, NLR 5699-65-1), and "paddy seed availability." No result named this variety under either name, so every heading below is "No evidence found" for both names.

What the searches returned: four queries ("Nellore Sugandha Rice variety", "Nellore Sugandha rice breeder institute", "Nellore Sugandha NLR 40054 rice research", "Nellore Sugandha paddy seed availability"). The pages were about other rice varieties or unrelated items, including the Wikipedia article on Molakolukulu (a different Andhra Pradesh rice), a ResearchGate paper on NLR 3354 (Nellore Dhanyarasi, a different variety), and an ANGRAU seed availability PDF (angrau.ac.in/downloads/Seed_Availability_in_ANGRAU_as_on_10_01_2022.pdf). The ANGRAU PDF lists ARS Nellore paddy seed generally, but I found no entry for Sugandha, NLR 40054 or IET 23194 in its text. These were discarded under the strict relevance rule.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to neck blast, sheath rot and rice tungro virus (RTV) (NRRI Research Bulletin 39; the ResearchGate summary table lists resistance to sheath rot and rice tungro). Conflict: the same NRRI bulletin also describes the variety as tolerant to bacterial blight and sheath blight, which is not consistent with the resistance listing; bacterial blight and sheath blight status is unresolved. The original variety record (no digest URL) also lists moderate resistance to brown spot and leaf blast; this is not confirmed by a digest source. Gall midge is covered under pest resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant to stem borer (both dead hearts and white ear heads), leaf folder, whorl maggot and rice hispa (CRRI released-varieties page). Gall midge: moderate resistance per the NRRI bulletin, but the same bulletin also describes it as tolerant to gall midge, and the original variety record lists resistance to gall midge; gall midge status is unresolved. Stem borer: the original variety record lists moderate resistance to SB (yellow stem borer), which conflicts with the tolerance listing; treat as unresolved.

agronomic_details.yield: Original variety record: 3200.00 to 3500.00 kg/ha. CRRI released-variety table: about 3.5 t/ha. NRRI bulletin: 3.0 to 3.3 t/ha. Pure-line culture: 3403 kg/ha over 2003 to 2005.
agronomic_details.stability: Pure-line culture yielded 3403 kg/ha over 2003 to 2005 and was accepted in multi-location adaptive trials in Orissa. Further stability data across environments: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Shallow lowland and rainfed lowland niche in Odisha (released and notified in 2010 and 2011 for lowland and rainfed low land areas of Odisha). Original record lists adaptation as Orissa.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Conflict: original variety record states 115 to 120 days; CRRI popular-varieties page states 145 to 150 days (late maturing). The digest does not resolve this conflict. The CRRI Annual Report 2013-14 figure of 160 days is not attributed to this variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: TALL PLANT TYPE, THICK CULM, COMPACT & LONG PANICLE WITH HIGH NUMBER OF GRAINS/PANICLE AND SHORT BOLD TYPE GRAIN WITH STRAW COLOUR HUSK. Plant height about 140 cm; photosensitive; non-shattering panicles and easy threshability (original variety record); aromatic non-basmati type (CRRI popular-varieties page).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Pure-line culture yielded 3403 kg/ha over 2003 to 2005 and was accepted in multi-location adaptive trials in Orissa. (2) Organic coastal Odisha trial (Bhubaneswar, kharif 2022): reached 50% flowering at about 112 days; had the tallest plants and highest hulling percentage among the four cultivars tested. (3) NRRI bulletin: yield 3.0 to 3.3 t/ha, head rice recovery 67.7%, test grain weight 10.46 g. (4) CRRI Annual Report 2013-14 table lists the variety with 250 progeny and 201 lines; the 160-day maturity and 4.3 t/ha figures in the same passage are not attributed to this variety pending check of the report.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC release name is "Numali". The Seednet name is "Numali (IET 27405)". Searches used both names. No result from a Seednet page turned up, so every finding below refers to the name "Numali" in an AAU or secondary source. Several queries also returned pages on other varieties (Dholi, Shraboni, Bina dhan 11), which I used only as comparators, not as evidence for Numali.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The Numali-specific results did not describe drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance. The Sentinel article describes Dholi as the water-resistant flood variety, not Numali. -- https://www.sentinelassam.com/topheadlines/assam-agricultural-university-hopeful-of-exporting-products-overseas-570963

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No result described blast, bacterial leaf blight, sheath blight, brown planthopper, or other resistance for Numali.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Numali is described as a short-duration variety of about 130-135 days, which lets farmers take a second crop on the same land. -- https://www.sentinelassam.com/topheadlines/assam-agricultural-university-hopeful-of-exporting-products-overseas-570963
- In a kharif establishment-methods study at AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar, Numali (V1, against Shraboni, Dholi and BINA dhan 11) recorded higher plant height, dry matter, yield attributes and grain yield under conventional transplanting, and it was also the top performer for tillers, N uptake, and profitability in several treatments. The paper calls it a medium-duration high-yielding variety, which conflicts with the 130-135 day figure above. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390923114_Influence_of_Establishment_Methods_on_Performance_and_Energetics_of_Kharif_Rice_Varieties
- A wet direct-seeded winter rice study used Numali as its variety, and its maturation period is mentioned, but the snippet is truncated and gives no number. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/43-Evaluation%20of%20Crop%20Establishment%20Techniques%20and%20Weed%20Management%20Tactics%20on%20Weed%20Population%20Dyanamics%20and%20Crop%20Productivity%20in%20Wet%20Direct%20Seeded%20Winter%20Rice.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL:
- The establishment-methods paper states that Numali was developed by crossing APMS with another parent; the snippet cuts off before naming the second parent, so Piolee cannot be confirmed from this text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390923114_Influence_of_Establishment_Methods_on_Performance_and_Energetics_of_Kharif_Rice_Varieties
- No breeding-line code (IET 27405 or other), QTL, marker, or genome study for Numali was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- The AAU compendium "Rice Varieties Developed by Assam Agricultural University" lists Numali among the varieties and gives its release year as 2020. It does not name a breeder in the snippet. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- The same compendium states that AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar, was established in 1923 and came under Assam Agricultural University, Jorhat, in 1969. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- A lead breeder or scientist name was not found for Numali.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- Institute-level only: AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar (under Assam Agricultural University, Jorhat). No email, phone, postal address, or contact-page URL was found in the results. Please check the AAU website directly.
- No breeder contact was found.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Authors not captured (2024/2025 per ResearchGate record). Influence of Establishment Methods on Performance and Energetics of Kharif Rice Varieties. drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance under either name (OUAT Kalinga Rice 8 / Suryashree or Surya shree / IE27737) in the searched sources.

heat.details: Released in Odisha as a heat tolerant cultivar for rabi irrigated medium land; reported to tolerate heat stress above 38 C (Advances in Agricultural Technology & Plant Sciences paper). OUAT AICRP mandate page lists heat tolerance as the variety's main trait, describing it as a heat-tolerant line in the pipeline. The digest gives no quantitative heat-stress trial data, so the level rests on the qualitative statements of the variety being heat tolerant.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance under either name in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance under either name in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to sheath blight and blast (ICAR Annual Report 2023-24 and OUAT Crop Varieties Released 2022-23 report). Variety record also lists moderate resistance to sheath blight and blast. No other disease resistance found for this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to gall midge (ICAR Annual Report 2023-24; resistance to gall midge also stated in the Advances in Agricultural Technology paper). The OUAT release PDF pod borer and leaf spot entries are excluded because they sit in a block with other crops' data and are unverified for this rice variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Conflicting values across sources: 46.2 q/ha (ICAR Annual Report 2023-24); 4,257 kg/ha (OUAT release PDF); 4,276 kg/ha under rabi/Dalua conditions (Advances paper); 10,267 kg/ha (OUAT release PDF, possibly mis-assigned in a mixed block, so unverified). Yield advantage of 18.98%, 18.54% and 12.12% over national check Gontra bidhan-3, zonal check Mandakini and local check Lalat, respectively (Advances paper). Variety record lists average yield as Unknown.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Variety record lists yield stability as not stated; no multi-environment stability statistics found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Odisha; irrigated medium lands under rabi/Dalua season (ICAR Annual Report 2023-24; Advances paper). Variety record lists adaptation as Odisha. Haryana performance is reported as a yield potential of 8 t/ha in the Advances paper.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 120 To 125Days (variety record). Source conflicts: 120-125 days (ICAR); 125-130 days (OUAT release PDF); 125 days (Advances paper). Days to first picking given as 100-117 in one OUAT block.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Variety record: lodging resistance; staggered sowing followed to adjust 50% flowering; threshability good; fertilizer response good; seedling survival 90%. Grain notes: long bold grains (ICAR); good cooking and keeping quality (OUAT release PDF). Morphological characteristics listed as Unknown in variety record.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Heat-tolerant lines tested under AICRP on Rice at RRTTS Chiplima, 2014-2017. Multi-location testing in kharif 2018-19 (IVT) and kharif 2019-20 (AVT1), plus an Odisha state MLT. Yield advantages of 18.98%, 18.54% and 12.12% over national check Gontra bidhan-3, zonal check Mandakini and local check Lalat, respectively. Yield of 4,276 kg/ha under rabi condition (Dalua). Yield potential of 8 t/ha reported for Haryana in the Advances paper. Yield values from ICAR (46.2 q/ha) and OUAT PDF (4,257 kg/ha; 10,267 kg/ha, unverified) are listed under Yield.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: OUAT Kalinga Rice 8 (Suryashree) / Surya shree (IE27737) / IET 27737, Rice

Searches run: 4 web_search queries (variety, breeder/institute, research papers, seed availability). Name evidence: "OUAT Kalinga Rice 8 (Suryashree)" appears in the OUAT and Odisha sources. "Surya shree (IE27737)" appears in the Government of India notification listings. "IET 27737" and culture name "IR-12C-147" appear in the ICAR and journal sources. Parentage (IR93328-46-B-7-1-3-3) was not found under any name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Released in Odisha as a heat tolerant cultivar for rabi irrigated medium land, it can tolerate heat stress above 38°C. -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
Heat tolerance is also described as the variety's main trait in OUAT's AICRP mandate page, where it is listed as a heat-tolerant line in the pipeline. -- https://ouat.ac.in/research/aicrps/
No evidence found for drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance under either name.

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderately resistant to sheath blight, blast and gall midge (ICAR Annual Report 2023-24). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf
Moderately resistant to sheath blight and blast. -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf
Resistance to gall midge is also stated in the Advances in Agricultural Technology paper. -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
The OUAT release PDF also lists pod borer tolerance and leaf spot moderate resistance, but these lines sit in a block with other crops' data, so they are unverified for this rice variety. -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity conflicts across sources: 120-125 days (ICAR), 125-130 days (OUAT PDF), 125 days (Advances in Agricultural Technology paper). Days to first picking are given as 100-117 in one OUAT block. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf ; https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf
Yield conflicts: 46.2 q/ha (ICAR), 4,257 kg/ha (OUAT PDF), 4,276 kg/ha under rabi/Dalua conditions (Advances paper), and 10,267 kg/ha (OUAT PDF, possibly mis-assigned in a mixed block). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf ; https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
It yields 4276 kg seed per hectare under rabi condition (Dalua). -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
Yield advantage of 18.98%, 18.54% and 12.12% over national check Gontra bidhan-3, zonal check Mandakini and local check Lalat, respectively. -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
Trial history: the heat-tolerant lines were tested under AICRP on Rice at RRTTS Chiplima, 2014-2017; multi-location testing ran in kharif 2018-19 (IVT) and 2019-20 (AVT1), plus an Odisha state MLT. -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
Performance in Haryana is reported as a yield potential of 8 t/ha. -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
Grain and cooking notes: long bold grains (ICAR); good cooking and keeping quality (OUAT PDF). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf ; https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Breeding-line codes: culture name IR-12C-147 and IET No 27737 (Advances paper). -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
Variety codes: IET 27737 (ICAR); Surya shree (IE27737) (Government notification listing). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-27-new-varieties-of-paddy-for-farmers/
Breeding method: the programme was started at AICRP on Rice, RRTTS Chiplima, to meet a rabi/Dalua heat and gall midge need. -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
Parentage IR93328-46-B-7-1-3-3: No evidence found in any search result.
QTL, marker and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Release paper authors: Ranjith P, Naik BS, Mohapatra S, Pal R, Seni A, Biswas S, listed with Regional Research and Technology Transfer Station affiliation. Their roles as breeders of this variety are not stated explicitly. -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
Developing institution: Released by the State Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties for Agricultural Crops, Government of Odisha, Bhubaneswar. -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
Station: AICRP on Rice, RRTTS Chiplima, Sambalpur, Odisha. -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf ; https://ouat.ac.in/research/aicrps/
Institution: Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology, Bhubaneswar. -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf
A retired OUAT breeder's profile credits him with development of OUAT Kalinga Rice-8 (Suryashree), but the snippets do not name him, so no name is attributed here. -- https://www.nipabooks.com/info/9788119103492/cart ; https://www.scribd.com/document/928683542/9-Commercial-Production-of-Flower-Crops-1

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder name, email, phone or postal address for this variety was found.
Institute-level only: OUAT, Bhubaneswar, website ouat.ac.in. No email, phone or address was found in the results. -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
Ranjith P, Naik BS, Mohapatra S, Pal R, Seni A, Biswas S (2025). OUAT Kalinga Rice 8 (Suryashree): A New Heat Tolerant Cultivar for Odisha. Advances in Agricultural Technology & Plant Sciences 8(1): 180169 -- https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf
ICAR (2025). ICAR Annual Report 2023-24. ICAR Annual Report -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf
Directorate of Research, OUAT (2023). Crop Varieties Released 2022-23. OUAT report -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf
No KrishiKosh thesis, peer-reviewed paper with DOI, or conference paper specific to this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Searches returned Odisha seed-system reports and a 2025 decentralized seed production article, but none name this variety. -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/ag-tech-research-news/enhancing-decentralized-seed-production-of-healthier-rice-in-odisha/

RECOMMENDED STATES
Odisha: irrigated medium lands, rabi/Dalua season. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf ; https://academicstrive.com/AATPS/AATPS180169.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pandu Ranga (MCM 100) (IET 22611), Rice

SEARCH STATUS: The tool quota was exhausted after four searches, so I could not run a follow-up check on the candidate pages. Coverage is partial. Several headings have no verified evidence.

Name note: The CSC release name is "Pandu Ranga" and the Seednet name is "Pandu Ranga (MCM 100) (IET 22611)". Only the code "MCM 100" appeared in the evidence below, so any link to this variety rests on that code match.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The salt-tolerance breeding snippet (Zenodo record, "Accelerated breeding for development of salt tolerant rice varieties for coastal saline ecosystem") is topically relevant to the cross's stated aim, but the snippet did not name Pandu Ranga or MCM 100, so I have not attributed it. -- https://zenodo.org/records/10399002

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The ICAR-IIRR 55th Rice Research Group proceedings returned a result on insect and disease resistance trials, but the snippet did not name this variety, so I have excluded it. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Draft%20Proceedings%20of%2055%20ARGM%202020.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found under this heading for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage as supplied in the record: a derivative of the cross MTU 1042 x MTU 1061, made to develop saline-tolerant rice for coastal saline systems. Breeding-line code MCM 100 (also IET 22611) as supplied in the record. No independent source was found confirming the parentage or the code. The Zenodo accelerated-breeding record above is the only generic lead, and it is unverified for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- A 2013 TNAU agritech daily-events PDF reports that two new paddy varieties, MCM-100 and MCM-101, were developed for saline soils, and shows K. Nagendra Rao displaying them in the field. The snippet does not state the institution, and I could not confirm that Nagendra Rao is a breeder of this variety or that the page refers to ANGRAU. Treat this as a lead only. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/daily_events/2013/english/may/09_may_13_eng.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute email, phone, or address was retrieved. Recommended starting point: ANGRAU, Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University, Guntur, via its official website (not verified in this session), or the ANGRAU Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru, for rice-specific contacts.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The Zenodo and ICAR-IIRR results are not confirmed to cover this variety, so none is listed.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The only seed-dealer result was a generic directory of East Godavari dealers with no reference to this variety. Suggested checks: Seednet (seednet.gov.in), APSSDC (Andhra Pradesh State Seeds Development Corporation), ANGRAU/RARS seed sales, and KVKs in coastal Andhra Pradesh.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Andhra Pradesh, as supplied in the record. Not independently confirmed by any retrieved source.

Next steps for a complete record: verify the 2013 MCM-100 article and the Zenodo paper directly, check the ANGRAU rice-research and release pages, and search KrishiKosh and the CSC release minutes for "MCM 100" or "IET 22611".

RH 150025 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Searches run: 4 web_search queries (variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers, seed availability). Both names were searched: "RH 150025" (CSC release name) and "ADV 8082" (Seednet name). The searches returned almost nothing about this variety, so most headings below read "No evidence found."

Name-match note: the only page that names RH-150025 is a rice hybrid evaluation paper. The search results never tie it to ADV 8082, UPL, Advanta, or the parentage in the record, so I have not linked it to this variety beyond the name and crop.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The search returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance for RH 150025 or ADV 8082.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page on disease or pest resistance for RH 150025 or ADV 8082 was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The one page naming RH-150025 reports it among rice hybrids with high yields of 7.26 q/ha in a trial, alongside NS-6508, LP-17201, US-314 and RH-131419, which gave 8.3, 7.9, 7.1 and 7.73 q/ha. The same page lists it in a group of hybrids and gives its flowering, height and yield variation values, but the search snippet does not state the trial year, location, or season. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359706304_Correlation_and_path_coeffecient_analysis_in_rice_Oryza_sativa_L
Maturity, duration and other yield figures for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found in search results. The parentage "RH150025A x RH150025R" and the breeding-line-style codes come only from the input record and are not confirmed by any retrieved page. No QTL, marker, or genome study was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No page named a breeder or scientist for RH 150025 or ADV 8082. The institution "UPL. Ltd. (Formerly Advanta Ltd.)" comes only from the input record. An IndiaMart listing for "Advanta Hybrid Paddy Seeds" (https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/advanta-hybrid-paddy-seeds-25481416355.html) was discarded because it does not name this variety or code.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute, or division contact page was returned for this variety. No email, phone, address, or contact URL was found.

PUBLICATIONS:
Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Correlation and path coeffecient analysis in rice (Oryza sativa L.). Journal not stated (ResearchGate record) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359706304_Correlation_and_path_coeffecient_analysis_in_rice_Oryza_sativa_L
This record is the only item found that names RH-150025. It is a rice hybrid evaluation paper and does not name ADV 8082, UPL, or Advanta. No AICRP, ICAR, KrishiKosh, QTL, or conference items were found.

Note that the Seednet name is "RH 150025 (ADV 8082)" and the Seednet crop is "PADDY (DHAN)". Neither name was confirmed on Seednet; the search did not reach the portal.

salinity.details: The original variety record describes the variety as tolerant to alkalinity and inland salinity. The AICRIP 2017-2020 trials in zones VI and VII reported yield gains over alkaline, inland saline, saline-tolerant, saline-sensitive and local checks of 23.29, 18.61, 39.69, 40.12 and 12.46 percent, respectively. The IIRR 2022 annual report lists the entry under saline and alkaline reactions. The level is set to medium because the evidence is qualitative and no salinity tolerance score is given in the digest. The NLR 34449 parent is described as having salinity tolerance (parent trait, as stated in the paper).

flood.details: No evidence found for this variety in the searches. The digest states that no flood tolerance evidence was found.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: the full paper describes the variety as resistant to blast. The original variety record gives moderate resistance scores of 4.8 for leaf blast, 4.0 for neck blast and 4.8 for bacterial leaf blight. The IIRR 2022 report includes a reaction code row for this entry (MR-BLB, KA, PD, SB, BPH, WBPH, LF); the abbreviations are not expanded in the excerpt, so they are not interpreted here. Brown spot, sheath rot and grain discoloration: the full paper describes the variety as resistant to these diseases. The ResearchGate abstract that carries the same claim is titled for Rajendranagar Vari-2 (IET 26143), so it was not used as evidence for this variety. The variety's own paper (sarr.co.in) is the evidence relied on here. The original variety record gives the leaf blast, neck blast and bacterial leaf blight scores; the digest provides no URL for these scores.

pest_resistance.summary: Brown planthopper (BPH): described as resistant in the full paper (sarr.co.in). The IIRR 2022 report lists BPH and WBPH in a reaction code row without expanded interpretation. Parent trait conflict: MTU 1010 is described as tolerant to BPH, while NLR 34449 is described as susceptible to BPH, so the attribution of BPH resistance to this entry is not confirmed by the parent data. Gall midge: the MTU 1010 parent is described as susceptible to gall midge; no variety-specific gall midge score was found. Other pests: Not found in searched sources. The Telangana institute's page mentions blast resistance and multi-pest source area status in general terms only, with no variety-specific pest scores.

agronomic_details.yield: Potential about 8.0 t/ha (as stated in the paper). One trial reported grain yield 16.7 percent higher (4400 kg/ha); the trial is not named in the excerpt and the figure is unverified. Station trial and minikit yield increase figures (6.81 and 9.7 percent) were drawn from a ResearchGate page titled for Rajendranagar Vari-2 and were excluded as an attribution conflict.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The AICRIP 2017-2020 trials in zones VI and VII showed yield gains over several checks; no stability parameters were reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Nitrogen responsive; suitable for late sowing (original variety record); tolerant to alkalinity and inland salinity; seed rate 25-30 kg/acre (original variety record). Tested in zones VI and VII (AICRIP 2017-2020) and at Rajendranagar and other sites (IIRR 2022). Telangana is the recommended state.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 135-140 days (medium duration, as stated in the paper)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium slender grain; good grain quality reported in the paper; fertilizer responsive.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRIP 2017-2020, zones VI and VII: yield gains of 23.29 percent over alkaline check, 18.61 percent over inland saline check, 39.69 percent over saline-tolerant check, 40.12 percent over saline-sensitive check and 12.46 percent over local check. (2) IIRR 2022 annual report: multi-location trial with yield and disease data at Rajendranagar and other sites; trial-level yields for this entry were not extracted. (3) Unnamed trial: grain yield 16.7 percent higher (4400 kg/ha); unverified. Station and minikit trial results (6.81 and 9.7 percent) were excluded because the source page is titled for a different variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Salinity tolerance is reported for the variety, and the 2017-2020 AICRIP trials in zones VI and VII showed yield gains over alkaline, inland saline, saline-tolerant, saline-sensitive and local checks (23.29, 18.61, 39.69, 40.12 and 12.46 percent) -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Issue_2_Vol-14-chapter-11.pdf
The IIRR 2022 annual report lists the entry under saline and alkaline reactions, with the same parentage and the name Rajendranagar Vari-1 (IET 27077, RNR 11718) -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
Drought, heat, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for this variety in the searches.

DISEASE AND PEST
Described as resistant to multiple insect pests and diseases, specifically BPH, blast, brown spot, sheath rot and grain discoloration -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365738593_Rajendranagar_Vari-2_IET_26143_RNR_15435_-_An_aromatic_long_grain_rice_variety (abstract of the 2021 Journal of Rice Research paper on Vari-1, shown there)
Same claim in the full paper's text -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Issue_2_Vol-14-chapter-11.pdf
The IIRR 2022 report gives a row of disease and pest reaction codes for this entry (MR-BLB, KA, PD, SB, BPH, WBPH, LF); the abbreviations are not expanded in the excerpt, so I have not interpreted them -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
Telangana institute's own page lists this variety as a blast-resistance, multi-pest source area; no variety-specific pest scores there -- https://pjtau.edu.in/rru-rajendranagar/ (general mandate; weak evidence for this variety specifically)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Medium duration (135-140 days), medium slender grain, fertilizer-responsive, potential about 8.0 t/ha -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Issue_2_Vol-14-chapter-11.pdf
Yield increase of 6.81 percent over the check in station trials and 9.7 percent in minikits -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365738593_Rajendranagar_Vari-2_IET_26143_RNR_15435_-_An_aromatic_long_grain_rice_variety
Grain yield reported 16.7 percent higher (4400 kg/ha) in one trial; the excerpt does not name the trial, so treat as unverified -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Issue_2_Vol-14-chapter-11.pdf
Good grain quality reported in the same paper -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Issue_2_Vol-14-chapter-11.pdf
Multi-location trial with yield and disease data (2022 season, Rajendranagar and other sites) -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf (multi-location table row; trial-level yields for this entry not extracted)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage MTU 1010 x NLR 34449, cross made 2006, pedigree method, identified in F6 (2010) and promoted to replicated yield testing -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Issue_2_Vol-14-chapter-11.pdf
Breeding codes: IET 27077 and RNR 11718 -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/
Parent traits as stated in the paper: MTU 1010 (high yielding, short duration); NLR 34449 (fine grain, blast and salinity tolerance) -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Issue_2_Vol-14-chapter-11.pdf
QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Lead/corresponding author: Chandra Mohan Y (marked as corresponding author on the 2021 paper). Co-authors: Surender Raju Ch, Vanisree S, Krishna L, Damodar Raju Ch, Narasimha (et al.) -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Issue_2_Vol-14-chapter-11.pdf
Developing institution: Rice Research Centre and Agricultural Research Institute, PJTSAU, Hyderabad, as named in the CSC minutes -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356664896_Minutes_of_the_87_th_meeting_of_Central_Sub-Committee_on_Crop_Standards_Notification_and_Release_of_Varieties_for_Agricultural_Crops_held_through_Video_Conferencing_on_22
Station: ARI Rajendranagar; the station was upgraded to Institute of Rice Research in 2022 and renamed Rice Research Unit in 2025 -- https://pjtau.edu.in/rru-rajendranagar/
The institute's director-of-research table lists this variety under the Rice Research Unit, with the Principal Scientist & Head of the Institute of Rice Research named as responsible -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute: Rice Research Unit (formerly Institute of Rice Research), ARI, PJTAU, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- 500 030 -- https://pjtau.edu.in/rru-rajendranagar/
Coordinates on the same page: Latitude 17.3219; Longitude 78.3999 -- https://pjtau.edu.in/rru-rajendranagar/
Staff listing: Dr. Y. Chandra Mohan, Principal Scientist, Genetics & Plant Breeding (Rice Breeding, Hybrid Rice), email drycmohan@gmail.com -- https://pjtau.edu.in/rru-rajendranagar/ (personal-domain address as listed; not confirmed as an official PJTSAU mailbox; no phone number found)
Phone number: No evidence found.
ICAR-IIRR (separate institute, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500 030): address only, not the developing institute for this variety -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf

PUBLICATIONS

Rajendranagar Vari-1 [IET 27077 (RNR 11718)] - Multiple stress resistant, high yielding rice variety. Journal of Rice Research 14(2): 65 -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Issue_2_Vol-14-chapter-11.pdf (ResearchGate listing of the same paper, with more co-author names: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365738593_Rajendranagar_Vari-2_IET_26143_RNR_15435_-_An_aromatic_long_grain_rice_variety ; no DOI found for this item)
ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (2022). Annual Report 2022 (AICRIP multi-location table entry for Rajendranagar Vari-1). Annual report -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/II

drought.details: A 2020 on-farm study describes NDLR-7 as a drought-resistant rice variety released by ANGRAU. The digest gives no quantitative drought data or physiological mechanism, so the level is a qualitative inference. The digest's name note states that no source uses the name DLR 7 or IET 23715; these findings refer to NDLR-7 (Nandyal Sona), the seednet name for this variety.

heat.details: No heat stress evidence found in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No salinity stress evidence found in the searched sources.

flood.details: No flood stress evidence found in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Reported tolerance (not resistance) to blast, sheath blight and the brown planthopper (BPH) list, as stated in the digest. Blast tolerance is reported in the on-farm trial paper and the fpohub listing, and the same disease list is repeated in the Agricultural Science Digest on-farm study. Sheath blight is reported only in the fpohub listing. The digest does not confirm a separate resistance rating for any disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Reported tolerance to gall midge, leaf folders and BPH (brown planthopper), as stated in the digest. The fpohub listing reports leaf folder and gall midge tolerance, and the on-farm trial paper reports BPH tolerance. The digest contains no other pest resistance evidence for this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Kurnool on-farm demonstration plots: about 7,437.5 kg/ha for NDLR-7 against 5,812 kg/ha for controls. Average district productivity for Andhra Pradesh is cited as 3,350 kg/ha for context. The variety data record also gives a mean of 7,536 kg/ha from adaptive minikits in 30-35 farmer fields (2012-13 to 2014-15) against 5,495 kg/ha for check BPT 5204. That figure is not from a digest source.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources as a formal multi-environment stability analysis. The digest reports results from on-farm trials in Chittoor and Kurnool districts.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Andhra Pradesh. Trials in Kurnool (scarce rainfall zone context) and Chittoor districts. One trial report credits a Karnataka KVK (Banavasi) with introducing the variety; this is a trial location and not a recommended adaptation area.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Described as a medium slender, short-duration variety in a Chittoor on-farm trial. The digest also states the variety is suitable for two seasons because of its short duration. Lodging, shattering and other morphology: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Chittoor on-farm trial, 2012-13 to 2014-15: described as a medium slender, short-duration variety; the day range is cut off in the source snippet. (2) Kurnool on-farm trials, 2016-17 onward over three years: cultivation cost fell from Rs 66,050/ha to Rs 50,538/ha through reduced pesticide use. (3) Demonstration plots: about 7,437.5 kg/ha against 5,812 kg/ha for controls. (4) District productivity context of 3,350 kg/ha for Andhra Pradesh. (5) Karnataka KVK (Banavasi) is credited with introducing the variety in one trial report; no yield data for this location is given in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Rice Nandyala Sona (DLR 7) / seednet name Nandyala Sona (NDLR 7) (IET No.23715)
Name note: Every finding below refers to "NDLR-7 (Nandyal Sona)". Nothing I found uses "DLR 7", "IET 23715" or "BPT 3291 x CR 157-212", so the evidence is for the NDLR-7 name only.

STRESS TOLERANCE [NDLR-7 / Nandyal Sona]
- A 2020 on-farm study describes NDLR-7 as a drought-resistant rice variety released by ANGRAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346660778_On_Farm_Testing_of_Rice_Variety_NDLR-7_as_an_Alternative_to_Traditionally_Grown_BPT-5204_in_Kurnool_District_of_Andhra_Pradesh
- No heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST [NDLR-7 / Nandyal Sona]
- Reported tolerance to blast, BPH (brown planthopper), sheath blight, leaf folders and gall midge -- https://fpohub.com/product/paddy-ndlr-7-proddutur/
- Reported tolerance to BPH and blast in the on-farm trial paper -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0004934
- Same disease and pest list repeated in the Agricultural Science Digest on-farm study -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/On-Farm-Testing-of-Rice-Variety-NDLR-7-as-an-to-in-Jayalakshmi-Babu/414715b6c5300bbce38863628a51d6975db16cc9

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS [NDLR-7 / Nandyal Sona]
- Described as a medium slender, short-duration variety in a Chittoor on-farm trial, 2012-13 to 2014-15 (day range cut off in the snippet) -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0004934
- Suitable for two seasons because of its short duration -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Success-Story-of-Fine-Grain-Rice-Variety-NDLR-7-Gayathri-Reddy/29154283e7f365c5efc431e1b8b0418c87ea9d9c
- Kurnool on-farm trials (2016-17 onward, three years): cultivation cost fell from Rs 66,050/ha to Rs 50,538/ha through reduced pesticide use -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/On-Farm-Testing-of-Rice-Variety-NDLR-7-as-an-to-in-Jayalakshmi-Babu/414715b6c5300bbce38863628a51d6975db16cc9
- Demonstration plots gave about 7,437.5 kg/ha against 5,812 kg/ha for controls -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2019/vol7issue6/PartU/SP-7-6-101-883.pdf
- Average district productivity context (3,350 kg/ha, Andhra Pradesh) is in the same study -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/On-Farm-Testing-of-Rice-Variety-NDLR-7-as-an-to-in-Jayalakshmi-Babu/414715b6c5300bbce38863628a51d6975db16cc9

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage BPT 3291 x CR 157-212: No evidence found.
- Breeding-line code IET 23715 / DLR 7: No evidence found.
- Breeding method, QTL, marker or genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION [NDLR-7 / Nandyal Sona]
- Developed and released by the Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Nandyal, Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) -- https://fpohub.com/product/paddy-ndlr-7-proddutur/
- Released in 2016, notified in 2018, as an alternative to BPT 5204 -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Success-Story-of-Fine-Grain-Rice-Variety-NDLR-7-Gayathri-Reddy/29154283e7f365c5efc431e1b8b0418c87ea9d9c
- A 2022 article (IJSR) mentions a scientist who has developed NDLR-7, but the name is not in the retrieved text, so no breeder is named. -- https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v10i7/SR21707143006.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The authors of the success-story paper (N K Gayathri, B Gopal Reddy, A Vishnuvardhan Reddy) are article authors, not confirmed breeders, so they are not attributed as breeders here.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level only: RARS, Nandyal, ANGRAU. No address, email, phone or contact page URL found in the results. -- https://fpohub.com/product/paddy-ndlr-7-proddutur/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SEARCH NAME NOTE: Searched "SAVA 134" (release-minutes name) and "SAVA 134 IET 24797" (Seednet-style name). No Seednet portal page was returned. Evidence below refers to the marketed names "Sava 134" / "Sava smart rice 134" by Savannah Seeds, and I could not confirm they match the CSC/Seednet entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Marketing listing describes the product as highly tolerant to bacterial leaf blight and strongly resistant to lodging -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sava-smart-rice-134-2851302599588.html
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Same IndiaMart listing says it is protected by the company's disease package (BLB tolerance). No blast or other disease rating for SAVA 134 was found. The blast-resistance claim I saw was for Sava 127, which I discarded. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sava-smart-rice-134-2851302599588.html
- Global-agriculture product note for Sava 134 describes the disease package in general terms only. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/savannahs-high-yielding-paddy-variety-sava-smart-rice-134/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Company release describes a semi-dwarf, erect plant type with high tillering, good grain index and early-medium maturity. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/savannahs-high-yielding-paddy-variety-sava-smart-rice-134/
- Marketing listing claims 2-3 fewer irrigations, plus savings on chemicals and fertiliser, and a long slender grain. These are company claims, not independently verified. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sava-smart-rice-134-2851302599588.html
- Multi-year study by CSK Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya (Palampur) with Savannah Seeds on direct-seeded SAVA-134 FullPage: reported lower methane emissions, higher water productivity than transplanted rice. This is a press/news report, not a peer-reviewed paper. Name is "SAVA-134 FullPage", so the link to this variety is probable but not confirmed. -- https://english.punjabkesari.com/india/himachal-varsity-develops-climate-smart-direct-seeded-rice-variety
- Vajiramandravi summary: in the current kharif season Sava 134 and Sava 127 were commercially planted as non-basmati hybrids. -- https://vajiramandravi.com/current-affairs/revolutionary-weed-control-in-rice-and-wheat-new-herbicide-tolerant-varieties/
- No CSC/AICRP multi-location trial result or yield data for this variety was found. The ICRIER PDF's yield figures refer to Sava 7501, so I discarded them. -- https://icrier.org/pdf/FDI-Innovations-and-Technology-in-Rice-Cultivation.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- A review chapter describes SAVA-134 as a two-line rice hybrid developed by Savannah Private Limited for commercial cultivation. This supports a TGMS/two-line hybrid system, but the chapter gives no parental codes. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489
- Parentage F 819 (TGMS female) / Y1015 (male pollinator), the breeding-line codes, and the genealogy: No evidence found.
- QTL, marker or genome studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing firm: Savannah Seeds Pvt. Ltd. (also written Savannah Private Limited). -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489
- Individual breeder or scientist names: No evidence found.
- Institute station: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Savannah Seeds Private Limited, Raipur, Chhattisgarh (listing address on IndiaMart; no street address, email or phone shown in the captured text). -- https://www.indiamart.com/savannah-seeds-private-limited/organic-rice.html
- Official company email, phone and postal address: No evidence found.
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI for SAVA 134 was found. The sources located are press/news or company material only (listed above).
- Hybrid rice review chapter (no author names captured in the search text). Year not captured. Book chapter, IntechOpen -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Aggarwal Enterprises, Karnal, Haryana lists "Sava 134" hybrid paddy seed as in stock, about ₹450/kg. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sava-134-savannah-seed-hybrid-paddy-seed-23384986148.html
- Savannah Seeds Pvt. Ltd., Raipur, lists "Sava smart rice 134" as an organic rice / grain seed product. -- https://www.indiamart.com/savannah-seeds-private-limited/organic-rice.html
- RiceTec India lists "Sava 134FP" under its SmartRice seed products. This is a different (FullPage) product line, so treat it as a lead only. -- https://ricetec-in.com/seed-products-india/
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet listing: No evidence found (this search was not run).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found from the CSC release minutes or Seednet. The commercial dealer listing is in Karnal, Haryana, which is consistent with the Haryana entry, but this does not confirm the recommendation.

Gaps to close: the CSC release minutes, the Seednet portal entry (search "seednet SAVA 134 IET 24797"), the parent-line codes, and the breeder names. Note also that the search tool returned no sentence indices, so I could not add formal citation tags. All URLs above are the source pages.

seednet_fields.Parentage: Pusa Sugandh 3 is a fine grain aromatic type developed by IAR, New Delhi. However, the late maturity nature under the prevailing climatic situation in valley could not make it a popular variety. The pureline selection for earlines from the original stock of Pusa Sugandh 4 led to the development of new variety SKUA 494 (K416-14-3) which is 12-15 days earlier possessing aroma and other cooking quality at par with Pusa Sugandh 3.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated low land (plains basins of the valley) but not water submerged areas
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features:
1.	Among different spacing schedules, highest yield was recorded with 15x15 cm spacing.

3.	25 days older seedlings yielded significantly higher as compared to 35 days older seedlings. A 25% saving in RDF through FYM yielded at par with 100% RDF.
4.	The net profit estimated by cultivating SKUA-408 is Rs. 118000/ha and the benefit: cost ratio is 2:81:1

drought.details: No evidence found for this variety in the digest. Drought-resilience reports relate to CR Dhan 801/802, which were excluded as separate varieties.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources.

flood.details: Released as a flood-tolerant version of Swarna. Tolerant to flash flood submergence (CSC record). Under flash flooding in Odisha, Sub1 genotypes gave higher yield than non-Sub1 genotypes. Limitation: grain filling was poorer than Swarna under stagnant flooding (medium-depth stagnation). Water-stagnation tolerance per se has no separate evidence for this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: CSC record: no incidences of any major diseases were observed under field and controlled conditions. Farmers in Odisha partly adopted the variety for resistance to sheath blight (farmer feedback, not a confirmed resistance rating). Bacterial blight resistance: no evidence found for this variety (the xa5/xa13/Xa21 line is CR Dhan 800, excluded). Pest and disease incidence was reported as low in Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu demonstrations.

pest_resistance.summary: CSC record: pest reaction unknown. The CRRI table lists tolerance to stem borer, leaf folder, whorl maggot and rice hispa in a row adjacent to the Swarna Sub1 entry, but the text extraction is ambiguous, so these ratings are unconfirmed for this variety and are not attributed. Low pest incidence was reported in Nagapattinam demonstrations without naming specific pests.

agronomic_details.yield: Average about 5,500 kg/ha (ResearchGate figure). CRRI table: 5.2 t/ha. CSC record: 5000-6000 kg/ha. Nagapattinam on-farm: 5,990 kg/ha after 16 days submergence. Khurda, Odisha (6-9 days submergence): 3.66 t/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Yield advantage of 1 t/ha or more under submergence, equal to Swarna when not submerged (Odisha head-to-head). Randomised trial in 128 Orissa villages showed about 45% gain over the popular variety after 10 days submergence, with no yield penalty without flooding. Poorer grain filling under stagnant flooding. Yield stability across non-submergence environments beyond these sites: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: suitable for shallow lowland areas of coastal Odisha where Swarna is grown. Also grown in Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu (on-farm demonstrations) and Hooghly, West Bengal (management trial).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: 1. STRAW COLOUR HULL 2. DARK GREEN LEAVES. Plant height about 100 cm; medium grain (digest). Shattering of grain during harvest and transport reported by farmers in Odisha. CSC record also notes medium slender grains with good cooking quality and suitability for late planting.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Odisha head-to-head project: survived 14 days complete submergence; Sub1 genotypes out-yielded non-Sub1 under flash flooding; yield advantage of 1 t/ha or more under submergence, equal to Swarna when not submerged. (2) CRRI table: tolerates 15-17 days submergence, 5.2 t/ha, duration 145 days (MS). (3) Bihar/IRRI data: 2-day submergence 98% survival vs about 94% for Swarna; after 4 days damage 5-9% vs 20-70% for other varieties. (4) Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu on-farm: 5,990 kg/ha after 16 days submergence, 22% over BPT 5204; 50 demonstration locations in 2011-12; low pest and disease incidence; lodging tolerant. (5) Randomised trial, 128 Orissa villages: about 45% yield gain over popular variety after 10 days submergence, no penalty without flooding. (6) Management trial at Chinsurah, Hooghly, West Bengal (kharif 2011) on nursery and main-field options; results not stated in digest. (7) Khurda, Odisha, 6-9 days submergence: average 3.66 t/ha for Swarna-Sub1 vs 2.25 t/ha for non-Sub1. (8) Nature study: grain filling poorer than Swarna under stagnant flooding.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SWARANA-SUB1 is treated as the same variety as Swarna-Sub1 (Swarna x IR49830 backcross derivative, IR05F102). Searches did not return any Seednet page for "SWARANA-SUB 1 (CR 2539-1) IET-20266", so Seednet evidence is absent. CR 2539-1 and IET-20266 codes did not appear in any retrieved page. Evidence below refers to "Swarna-Sub1" unless noted. CR Dhan 801, 802, 409, 800, 909, 310/311 and CR Sugandh Dhan 910 were excluded as separate varieties.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Complete submergence tolerance for about 14-17 days, versus 4-5 days for Swarna; released as a flood-tolerant version of Swarna -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/swarna-sub1-english.pdf
Tolerates up to 15-17 days of complete submergence, 5.2 t/ha (CRRI table, row 76 "Swarna Sub1") -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
Survived 14 days of complete submergence; Sub1 genotypes gave higher yield than non-Sub1 genotypes under flash flooding in Odisha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341002513_Evaluation_of_excess_water_tolerant_rice_varieties_Swarna_sub-1_and_CR-1009_sub_-1_under_Head_to_Head_Project_in_East_and_South-_Eastern_Coastal_Plain_zone_of_Odisha
Yield advantage of 1 t/ha or more under submergence, with yield equal to Swarna when not submerged -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341002513_Evaluation_of_excess_water_tolerant_rice_varieties_Swarna_sub-1_and_CR-1009_sub_-1_under_Head_to_Head_Project_in_East_and_South-_Eastern_Coastal_Plain_zone_of_Odisha
Sub1 locus on chromosome 9 is the main contributor to flood tolerance; grain filling was poorer than Swarna under stagnant flooding (medium-depth stagnation), a limitation -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-35251-z
Under 2-day submergence Swarna-Sub1 showed 98% survival versus about 94% for Swarna; after 4 days, damage was 5-9% versus 20-70% for other varieties (Bihar/IRRI data) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/235906946_Field_Performance_Dissemination_Impact_and_Tracking_Of_Submergence_Tolerant_Sub1_Rice_Varieties_in_South_Asia
Drought, heat, salinity and water-stagnation tolerance: No evidence found for this variety (only the CR Dhan 801/802 derivatives were reported as drought-resilient, and those were excluded).

DISEASE AND PEST
Adopted partly for resistance to sheath blight (Odisha farmer feedback, Rice Today) -- https://ricetoday.irri.org/swarna-sub1-odishas-food-for-a-goddess/
Pest and disease incidence was low and the variety was lodging tolerant in Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu demonstrations -- https://kvknagapattinam.co.in/2022/03/15/large-scale-adoption-on-rice-swarna-sub-1/
CRRI table lists tolerance to stem borer, leaf folder, whorl maggot and rice hispa in a row adjacent to the Swarna Sub1 entry; the text extraction is ambiguous about which row these ratings belong to, so treat as unconfirmed for this variety -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
Bacterial blight resistance: No evidence found for this variety (the xa5/xa13/Xa21 BB-resistant line is CR Dhan 800, excluded).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity about 140-145 days; plant height about 100 cm; medium grain; average yield about 5,500 kg/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Field-view-and-panicles-of-Swarna-sub1_fig1_360962180
CRRI table: duration 145 days (MS), 5.2 t/ha -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
Nagapattinam (TN) on-farm: 5,990 kg/ha after 16 days submergence, 22% over BPT 5204; 50 demonstration locations in 2011-12 -- https://kvknagapattinam.co.in/2022/03/15/large-scale-adoption-on-rice-swarna-sub-1/
Shattering of grain during harvest and transport was reported by farmers in Odisha -- https://ricetoday.irri.org/swarna-sub1-odishas-food-for-a-goddess/
Randomised trial in 128 Orissa villages: about 45% yield gain over the popular variety when fields were submerged 10 days, with no yield penalty without flooding -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1038/srep03315
Management trial at Chinsurah, Hooghly, West Bengal (kharif 2011) on nursery and main-field options -- https://www.scirp.org/journal/paperinformation?paperid=41691
Submergence at 6-9 days in Khurda, Odisha: average 3.66 t/ha for Swarna-Sub1 versus 2.25 t/ha for non-Sub1

drought.details: CSC variety data record a high degree of tolerance to reproductive stage drought. The DARE Annual Report 2017-18 lists the variety as aerobic and medium-upland tolerant. The BAU Plant Breeding department list describes it as suitable for drought conditions. In a rain-out-shelter study it recorded the highest proline content (69.9 µg/g fresh wt) of eight genotypes and was named a promising genotype for drought yield. It was also listed among genotypes for grain yield under drought, with a drought-related trait noted for this variety (chlorophyll stability), though the digest gives no further detail on that finding. Mechanisms reported: proline accumulation and chlorophyll stability. Note: the level is assigned from the CSC record and multiple digest sources; the rain-out-shelter result is a single study.

heat.details: A four-year study examined morpho-physiological and biochemical traits under drought alone, heat alone, and combined drought plus heat. The publication Nahakpam, Kesari and Singh (2024) is titled as covering essential traits for reproductive drought and heat stress tolerance of Sabour Ardhjal rice. The digest does not report any heat-specific results, so the heat tolerance level is unknown.

Sheath blight: Not found in searched sources. Leaf folder (Cnaphalocrosis medinalis) is covered under pest_resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: Stem borer and brown planthopper (BPH): moderately tolerant according to CSC variety data. The digest found no independent evidence for stem borer or BPH. agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Rain-out-shelter study: among eight genotypes, highest proline content (69.9 µg/g fresh wt); named a promising genotype for drought yield. (2) Chlorophyll stability study: listed among genotypes for grain yield under drought; no numeric result given in the digest. (3) Four-year drought, heat and combined drought-plus-heat study (Nahakpam, Kesari and Singh, 2024): no results reported in the digest. (4) Arsenic tolerance study: among genotypes tested, considerably higher arsenic tolerance through membrane stability and antioxidant enzymes; no numeric values given. (5) Leaf folder screening at Agwanpur, Saharsa, kharif 2022: among eleven entries; score not given. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Sabour Ardhjal (BRR 0007), Rice

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Sabour Ardhjal (BRR 0007)"), so one set of searches covers both. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search. The variety code IET 24036 and the spelling "Ardhajal" also appear in some sources and were matched as the same variety. Four searches were run in total. The sources below are the ones that name this variety and crop.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- DARE Annual Report 2017-18 lists it as aerobic and medium-upland tolerant, with moderate resistance to bacterial leaf blight -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/DARE-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf
- Drought: Sabour Ardhjal is described as suitable for drought conditions in the BAU Plant Breeding department variety list -- https://bausabour.ac.in/department_details.aspx?cc=001&deptcode=Plant+Breeding+%5E+Genetics
- Drought: in a rain-out-shelter study it recorded the highest proline content (69.9 µg/g fresh wt) of eight genotypes, and was named a promising genotype for drought yield -- https://www.phytojournal.com/special-issue/2017.v6.i6S.2991/effectual-tolerant-traits-for-grain-yield-in-rice-genotypes-grown-under-drought
- Drought and chlorophyll stability: listed among genotypes for grain yield under drought, with a drought-related trait noted for this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323628212_Chlorophyll_Stability_A_Better_Trait_for_Grain_Yield_in_Rice_under_Drought
- Drought and heat: a four-year study examined morpho-physiological and biochemical traits under drought alone, heat alone, and combined drought plus heat -- https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Ravi-Kesari-2159239692
- Arsenic: among the genotypes tested, it showed considerably higher arsenic tolerance (membrane stability, antioxidant enzymes) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0098847222003069
- Water use: a news report quotes the BAU Vice Chancellor saying it needs about 50% less irrigation than other paddy varieties (press claim, not a trial report) -- https://www.theweekendleader.com/Headlines/3462/new-paddy-variety-developed-for-bihars-rain-deficient-areas.html
- Flood/submergence and salinity: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial leaf blight: moderately resistant -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/DARE-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf
- Leaf folder (Cnaphalocrosis medinalis): the variety was among eleven entries screened at Agwanpur, Saharsa in kharif 2022, but the snippet does not give its score -- https://indianjournals.com/article/apps-31-2-012
- Blast, sheath blight, brown planthopper, stem borer, and other pests: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: described as medium duration in the BAU department list -- https://bausabour.ac.in/department_details.aspx?cc=001&deptcode=Plant+Breeding+%5E+Genetics
- Yield: 4,500–5,500 kg/ha under irrigated, medium-upland and aerobic conditions -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/DARE-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf
- Direct-seeded (DSR) short-duration option for highland conditions in Bihar kharif advisory -- https://www.sgk.in/gk/advisory-for-kharif-cultivation-in-bihar
- Multi-location trial: a first trial in rain-deficient districts (Munger, Patna, Gaya, Banka, Jehanabad, Lakhisarai, Sheikhpura, Nalanda) was described as satisfactory, with no data -- https://www.theweekendleader.com/Headlines/3462/new-paddy-variety-developed-for-bihars-rain-deficient-areas.html
- AICRIP Patna centre table lists Sabour Ardhjal with a year of 2014 -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/03%20Patna.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line code BRR 0007 and variety code IET 24036 are given in the DARE report -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/DARE-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf
- Parentage (IR 87638-10-1-1-3 / Dhagaddeshi/IR78585-98-2-2): No evidence found
- Breeding method, genes, QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Bihar Agricultural University (BAU), Sabour, Bhagalpur; the Vice Chancellor (M.L. Choudhary) is quoted as the announcer, not as breeder -- https://www.theweekendleader.com/Headlines/3462/new-paddy-variety-developed-for-bihars-rain-deficient-areas.html
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. The BAU Plant Breeding page lists the variety under CVRC but names no breeder for it -- https://bausabour.ac.in/department_details.aspx?cc=001&deptcode=Plant+Breeding+%5E+Genetics
- Release-year discrepancy: BAU lists it as released in 2013 -- https://www.bausabour.ac.in/varieties-developed.aspx ; the Gazette notification is 2017 -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm ; AICRIP Patna lists 2014 -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/03%20Patna.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute postal address (from BAU varieties page): Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour, Bhagalpur, Bihar India-813210; Directorate of Research: Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour-813210 -- https://www.bausabour.ac.in/varieties-developed.aspx
- Institute website: https://bausabour.ac.in
- Breeder email, phone, or named contact for this variety: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Nahakpam, S.; Kesari, R.; Singh, S.P. (2024). Essential traits for reproductive drought and heat stress tolerance of Sabour Ardhjal rice: Implication for agricultural improvement. Journal not identified (listed as an article, September 2024) -- https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Ravi-Kesari-2159239692
- Authors not captured (2017). Effectual tolerant traits for grain yield in rice genotypes grown under drought. Phytojournal, Special Issue 6(6S) -- https://www.phytojournal.com/special-issue/2017.v6.i6S.2991/effectual-tolerant-traits-for-grain-yield-in-rice-genotypes-grown-under-drought
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Chlorophyll Stability: A Better Trait for Grain Yield in Rice under Drought. Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323628212_Chlorophyll_Stability_A_Better_Trait_for_Grain_Yield_in_Rice_under_Drought
- Authors not captured (2022). Evaluation of rice genotypes against rice leaf folder, Cnaphalocrosis medinalis Guenee in Koshi region of Bihar. Annals of Plant Protection Sciences, pp. 75–80 -- https://indianjournals.com/article/apps-31-2-012
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Effective antioxidant defense prevents nitro-oxidative stress under arsenic toxicity: A study in rice genotypes of eastern Indo-Gangetic plains. Journal not captured -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0098847222003069
- Theses (KrishiKosh) and AICRIP annual reports specific to this variety: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seed sources (NSC, Bihar State Seed Corporation, KVK, BAU seed sales, dealers): No evidence found. The BAU varieties page lists the variety but gives no seed-sale details -- https://www.bausabour.ac.in/varieties-developed.aspx
- Institute listing of rice varieties: https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-27/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Bihar: notified 30.03.2017 under S.O. 1007(E) -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Bihar, irrigated medium-upland and aerobic ecology -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/DARE-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf
- Other states: No evidence found
