drought.details: Described as a mid-early duration, high yielding variety tolerant to drought at the reproductive stage, and as a drought tolerant rice variety suitable for medium and mid-upland situations in Bihar. Listed by BAU as suitable for drought-prone conditions. The CSC record also gives 'tolerant to drought' as its stress reaction. The level is qualitative (based on the word 'tolerant' across sources); no quantitative drought score or mechanism-level data was found in the digest. Note: the ResearchGate URL 359278789 is titled with a maize hybrid name ('Maize_Hybrid_Karimnagar_Makka-1'); its drought statement is corroborated by the other ResearchGate and BAU sources, so it is retained.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance for this variety in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance for this variety in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance for this variety in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to bacterial blight (BLB), blast and brown spot under field conditions (CSC disease reaction record; the rice-garud listing gives the same three diseases). The rice-garud snippet also mentions tolerance to a stem-related trait, but the text is truncated and the trait is not named, so it is not attributed to any disease. Leaf folder screening (Annals of Plant Protection Sciences, kharif 2022, MBAC Agwanpur) included this variety, but the snippet gives no reaction score, so it is not counted as resistance evidence.

pest_resistance.summary: CSC record reports tolerance to Stem Borer, Leaf folder and Gundhi Bug (Gundhi bug) under field conditions. The digest does not contain an independent URL-sourced statement for these pests; the rice-garud snippet mentions only a truncated stem-related tolerance. The leaf folder screening (kharif 2022, Agwanpur) included this variety but provides no reaction score, so it does not confirm tolerance.

agronomic_details.yield: BAU and CSC give yield potential of 45-50 q/ha (medium to upland irrigated). The rice-garud listing gives an average yield of 57.6 q/ha. These figures conflict; both are reported. A garbled mean-yield figure ('541 3') in the ResearchGate source is probably 5413 kg/ha but is not verified.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for medium and mid-upland irrigated situations in Bihar. Zones I, II, IIIA and IIIB of Bihar are listed, with suggested replacement of MTU 1010 and Sahbhagi Dhan. Ecosystem given as irrigated.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Tested in AICRP IVT (irrigated medium, 2015) and promoted to AVT-1 IME. (2) Multi-location trials in Bihar ran 2012-2017. (3) A mean yield figure is garbled in the source ('541 3', probably 5413 kg/ha, unverified). (4) Grain yield data from the Bihar trials are not legible in the retrieved snippet. Items 1 and 3 come from the ResearchGate document 359278789, whose title names a maize hybrid, so this attribution is unverified. Nitrogen response (recommended N dose about 100 kg, from the same source) is also unverified for this reason and is not treated as confirmed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Sabour Harshit Dhan (variety_name) / Sabour Harshit Dhan (IET 25342) (seednet_variety_name), Rice

Name note: The search evidence refers to the same release under both names. The CSC/notification sources use "Sabour Harshit Dhan (IET 25342)" and the breeding code BRR 0043-IR83383-B-B-B-14 1-2. The BAU page and the IIRR-linked listings use "Sabour Harshit Dhan" alone. I found no Seednet page, so no evidence under the Seednet heading was retrieved directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
The variety was bred for mid-early duration high yielding variety tolerant to drought at reproductive stage -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359278789_Maize_Hybrid_Karimnagar_Makka-1
Described as a drought tolerant rice variety suitable for medium and mid-upland situations in Bihar -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/360485658_Sabour_Harshit_Dhan_High_yielding_and_Drought_tolerant_Rice_variety
Listed as suitable for drought-prone conditions and medium duration -- https://www.bausabour.ac.in/department_details.aspx?cc=001&deptcode=Plant+Breeding+%5E+Genetics
No evidence found for submergence, flood, heat or salinity tolerance for this variety. The submergence and drought variety pages found (Sabour Sampanna Dhan) are a different variety and were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderately resistant to bacterial blight, blast and brown spot, and reported as tolerant to a stem-related trait (text truncated in source) -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
Included as one of eleven entries screened against rice leaf folder (Cnaphalocrosis medinalis) at Agwanpur, kharif 2022, but the snippet gives no reaction score for this variety -- https://indianjournals.com/article/apps-31-2-012

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity 120-125 days, average yield 57.6 q/ha, irrigated ecosystem -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
Yield potential given by BAU as 45-50 q/ha, medium to upland irrigated -- https://www.bausabour.ac.in/varieties-developed.aspx
Nitrogen-responsive, with a recommended N dose of about 100 kg -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359278789_Maize_Hybrid_Karimnagar_Makka-1
IET 25342 was tested in AICRP IVT (irrigated medium, 2015) and promoted to AVT-1 IME; multi-location trials in Bihar ran 2012-2017 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359278789_Maize_Hybrid_Karimnagar_Makka-1 (mean yield figure in source is garbled as "541 3", likely 5413 kg/ha, not verified)
Trial results are reported in the same ResearchGate document; grain yield data from the Bihar trials are not fully legible in the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/360485658_Sabour_Harshit_Dhan_High_yielding_and_Drought_tolerant_Rice_variety

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Breeding line code: BRR 0043-IR83383-B-B-B-14 1-2 (IET 25342), selected from segregating progeny of a cross -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359278789_Maize_Hybrid_Karimnagar_Makka-1
Developed under the BAU-IRRI STRASA collaborative project -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/360485658_Sabour_Harshit_Dhan_High_yielding_and_Drought_tolerant_Rice_variety
Parentage: the parentage in the task record "IR 72022-46-2-3-3-2/IR5751-PM15-B-1-2" was not found in any retrieved source. The sources name the line only by its own code, so the parentage is unverified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Name match: "Samba sub 1" (the SAMBA-SUB1 article), not "Samba Sub-1 (IET 21248)" as written on Seednet. Described as a submergence-tolerant variety that tolerates about 15 days of standing water -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364994093_SAMBA-SUB1_IMPROVED_VARIETY_OF_RICE_AND_MANAGEMENT_OF_BLAST_OF_RICE
- Drought, salinity or heat tolerance for this variety: No evidence found. The stress-factor wording in the krishiscience PDF is generic and does not name this variety -- https://krishiscience.co.in/storage/app/finalpdf/K3toD2HFbD9NYOLUhd2T6eUkR5XCDt6KuNPAqNuI.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Article title and text refer to blast management for Samba Sub-1, but the retrieved text gives no blast resistance rating or score -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364994093_SAMBA-SUB1_IMPROVED_VARIETY_OF_RICE_AND_MANAGEMENT_OF_BLAST_OF_RICE
- Pest and other disease resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Described as a medium-plant-type, fine-grain variety; the article says it can be sown by broadcasting or by seed drill in lowlands -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364994093_SAMBA-SUB1_IMPROVED_VARIETY_OF_RICE_AND_MANAGEMENT_OF_BLAST_OF_RICE
- Yield, maturity and multi-location trial data for this variety: No evidence found. Yield and duration figures found were for Samba Mahsuri Sub-1, a different name, so they were excluded -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Production-Practices-of-Samba-Mahsuri-Sub-1-Rice-Variety-in-English.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage "Sambha Mahsuri*3/IR 49830-7-1-2-3" and IET 21248 code: No evidence found. The Samba-Sub1 article names no parents or breeding-line code.
- Sub1 locus or marker-assisted work on this variety: No evidence found. Sub1 pages found were about Samba Mahsuri-Sub1 or Swarna-Sub1, so they were excluded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/225764140_Submergence_Tolerant_Rice_SUB1's_Journey_from_Landrace_to_Modern_Cultivar

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: the article says Samba Sub-1 "was developed by" but the sentence is cut off, so no institution or breeder is named -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364994093_SAMBA-SUB1_IMPROVED_VARIETY_OF_RICE_AND_MANAGEMENT_OF_BLAST_OF_RICE
- Lead breeder name and station: No evidence found. Narendra Dev University pages found concern Swarna Sub-1 and Samba Mahsuri Sub-1, which were excluded.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact, institute email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for this variety: No evidence found. The NDUAT address in the brief was not verified by any retrieved page. Seednet portal page: not retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). SAMBA-SUB1: Improved Variety of Rice and Management of Blast of Rice. ResearchGate article (no journal or report named) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364994093_SAMBA-SUB1_IMPROVED_VARIETY_OF_RICE_AND_MANAGEMENT_OF_BLAST_OF_RICE
- Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses or QTL papers naming this variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listings: No evidence found. Seednet portal search did not return this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The Samba-Sub1 article states the variety was recommended in 2015 for Uttar Pradesh, Assam, West Bengal and Tripura -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364994093_SAMBA-SUB1_IMPROVED_VARIETY_OF_RICE_AND_MANAGEMENT_OF_BLAST_OF_RICE
- Same statement in the krishiscience PDF -- https://krishiscience.co.in/storage/app/finalpdf/K3toD2HFbD9NYOLUhd2T6eUkR5XCDt6KuNPAqNuI.pdf

NOTES
- Searches used: 4 (the maximum). Four searches returned pages on Samba Mahsuri Sub-1, Swarna Sub-1, CR1009 Sub-1 and Improved Samba Mahsuri. These were excluded because they name other varieties.
- The only page naming "Samba sub 1" with a 2015 recommendation is the SAMBA-SUB1 article. It is the only basis for linking this record to the variety. Its identity with "Samba Sub-1 (IET 21248)" and with the NDUAT release should be confirmed against the CSC minutes or the Seednet entry before use.

seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: No incidence of blast. Low incidence of sheath blight and bacterial leaf blight.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Field tolerant to Gallmidge biotype4, Low incidence of stem borer.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I ran three searches and then hit the tool's server-side use limit, so the fourth (seed availability) was not run. Most headings below have little or no evidence. Where I could not verify a point, I say so rather than fill it from memory.

Name check: The evidence below refers to "Swarna Shakti Dhan" and "IET 25640." The input variety code (RCPR-22-IR84899-B-183-20-1-1-1) differs from the Seednet code (RCPF-22-IR84899-B-183-20-1-1-1), and I could not resolve which is correct.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Only one snippet mentions a related trait. It describes Swarna Shakti Dhan as a promising genotype identified for aerobic conditions, which is adaptation to non-flooded culture rather than a tested stress rating. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351352577_Alternate_wetting_and_drying_irrigation_technology_in_rice

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The same ResearchGate page says IET 25640 is suitable for direct-seeded cultivation under water-limited irrigated areas and rainfed shallow lowland to medium upland conditions. This is a secondary, review-style mention; I did not find the underlying trial data or yield figures. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351352577_Alternate_wetting_and_drying_irrigation_technology_in_rice

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage (IR 78877-208-B-1-1 / IRRI 132, selected for drought superiority) comes only from your input record; I did not confirm it from an independent source. A QTL search returned a Nature study on GBS-based QTL mapping for reproductive-stage drought tolerance, but that page does not name this variety, so I discarded it. -- No verified URL for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution per your record: ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region (ICAR-RCER). I found no page naming a lead breeder or scientist for this variety. -- No evidence found for breeder names.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact was found. Institute-level pointer: the ICAR-RCER site, https://icarrcer.icar.gov.in/ (its variety-release page is at https://icarrcer.icar.gov.in/variety-released-2/). I did not extract a phone, email or postal address from the search results, so none is listed. The release-page snippet mentions other RCER varieties (Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 and 2, Swarna Shusk Dhan, Swarna Unnat Dhan, Swarna Sukha Dhan), and I could not confirm from it that Swarna Shakti Dhan or the 2020 release is listed.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or conference paper was confirmed for this variety. The ResearchGate item above is the only variety-specific source, and its authors and year were not captured. Nothing is listed as a citation.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Not searched. The fourth search could not be run because the tool limit was reached.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Not confirmed. The states in your record (Haryana, Odisha, Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Maharashtra) come from the input only. The release-notification page did not confirm them.

drought.details: Described as a drought-tolerant, multiple-stress-tolerant variety for direct-seeded rainfed upland conditions (ICAR-RCER Annual Report 2023). Grouped with drought-tolerant varieties in the Rice Package of Practices for Eastern India. The ICAR Annual Report 2024-25 names it, with Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 and 2, as a drought-resistant rice suitable for water-limited areas. The original variety data also records high drought tolerance. No quantitative drought trial data were found. The level is rated high on the basis of consistent qualitative descriptions across three sources, not on measured data.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. No heat-stress evidence for this variety in the digest.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. No salinity-tolerance evidence for this variety in the digest.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. The variety is described for direct-seeded rainfed upland conditions, which does not establish flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Leaf blast: moderately resistant under natural screening (IET 27962). False smut: moderately resistant under natural screening (IET 27962); the Package of Practices also lists the variety among those to select for false smut tolerance (list partly garbled). Neck blast: resistant under artificial screening. Sheath rot: resistant under artificial screening. Bacterial leaf blight and sheath blight: the IIRR AICRP table gives code MR-BL and SB for this entry. The reading as moderate reaction is the digest author's inference, since the table has no legend; the sheath blight reaction level is not stated. Overall disease reaction is based on IET 27962 screening records, which the digest equates with this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: Leaf folder: the IIRR AICRP table gives code LF for this entry. The digest reads this as a moderate reaction, but this is an unverified inference because the table has no legend and no reaction level is stated. The original variety data records pest reaction as Unknown. No other pest resistance evidence was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Original variety data gives an average yield of 4.50 to 5.50 Kg/Ha. The ICAR-RCER Annual Report 2023 gives 4.0-4.5 t/ha. These two figures differ in both range and unit, and this discrepancy is not resolved by the digest. The IIRR AICRP table gives a yield of 2.2 for this entry, with unit and column meaning not stated.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment or multi-location stability data were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Direct-seeded rainfed upland conditions and water-limited areas (drought-prone). Recommended for Uttar Pradesh per the IIRR AICRP table. The ICAR-RCER 2023 report gives release context but no state list for this variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf (ICAR-RCER Annual Report 2023). Resistant to lodging and grain shattering, and fertilizer responsive (original variety data and ICAR-RCER Annual Report 2023). Morphological characteristics beyond these are Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No dedicated trial report with multi-location yield data was found. The only quantitative entry is the IIRR AICRP on Rice table value of 2.2 (unit and meaning not stated). An IIRR scientist profile lists the variety as a direct-seeded rice variety; this is a trait listing, not a trial result. Maturity and grain-yield figures from a dedicated trial report were not found.

Grouped with drought-tolerant varieties in the Rice Package of Practices for Eastern India. The ICAR Annual Report 2024-25 names it, with Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 and 2, as a drought-resistant rice suitable for water-limited areas. The original variety data also records high drought tolerance. No quantitative drought trial data were found. The level is rated high on the basis of consistent qualitative descriptions across three sources, not on measured data.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. No heat-stress evidence for this variety in the digest.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. No salinity-tolerance evidence for this variety in the digest.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. The variety is described for direct-seeded rainfed upland conditions, which does not establish flood tolerance.

submergence.details: Submergence tolerance is not confirmed. The Rice Package of Practices lists drought-tolerant varieties clearly, but a submergence list in the same document is garbled in the extracted text. The original variety data records stress reaction as Unknown.

disease_resistance.summary: Leaf blast: moderately resistant under natural screening (IET 27962). False smut: moderately resistant under natural screening (IET 27962); the Package of Practices also lists the variety among those to select for false smut tolerance (list partly garbled). Neck blast: resistant under artificial screening. Sheath rot: resistant under artificial screening. Bacterial leaf blight and sheath blight: the IIRR AICRP table gives code MR-BL and SB for this entry. The reading as moderate reaction is the digest author's inference, since the table has no legend; the sheath blight reaction level is not stated. Overall disease reaction is based on IET 27962 screening records, which the digest equates with this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: Leaf folder: the IIRR AICRP table gives code LF for this entry. The digest reads this as a moderate reaction, but this is an unverified inference because the table has no legend and no reaction level is stated. The original variety data records pest reaction as Unknown. No other pest resistance evidence was found.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources
genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. QTL and marker studies returned no evidence for this variety; Swarna-background papers returned were for other varieties and were discarded.
genetics_and_qtl.genes_introgressed: Not found in searched sources. No named genes or alleles (e.g. Sub1A, Xa21, Pi54) are recorded for this variety. Swarna Sub1 is a different variety and was not attributed here.
genetics_and_qtl.parentage_and_pedigree: IR 81039-B-173-U3-3 / IR 81063-B-94-U3-1 (as recorded in the digest). The IIRR table cell is truncated after 'IR', so the second parent is confirmed only by the user-supplied record.
genetics_and_qtl.breeding_line_designations: RCPR 56-IR93827-29-1-1-4 with IET 27962 (variety code). The SEEDNET variety name uses RCPR 56-IR93827-29-1-14 (IET 27962); the digest treats these as the same variety, but the code strings differ.
genetics_and_qtl.genome_resources: Not found in searched sources. No genome sequence, resequencing or genotyping dataset with accession IDs was found.

agronomic_performance.yield: Original variety data gives an average yield of 4.50 to 5.50 Kg/Ha. The ICAR-RCER Annual Report 2023 gives 4.0-4.5 t/ha. These two figures differ in both range and unit, and this discrepancy is not resolved by the digest. The IIRR AICRP table gives a yield of 2.2 for this entry, with unit and column meaning not stated.
agronomic_performance.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment or multi-location stability data were found.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Direct-seeded rainfed upland conditions and water-limited areas (drought-prone). Recommended for Uttar Pradesh per the IIRR AICRP table. The ICAR-RCER 2023 report gives release context but no state list for this variety.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf (ICAR-RCER Annual Report 2023). Resistant to lodging and grain shattering, and fertilizer responsive (original variety data and ICAR-RCER Annual Report 2023). Morphological characteristics beyond these are Unknown.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: No dedicated trial report with multi-location yield data was found. The only quantitative entry is the IIRR AICRP on Rice table value of 2.2 (unit and meaning not stated). An IIRR scientist profile lists the variety as a direct-seeded rice variety; this is a trait listing, not a trial result. Maturity and grain-yield figures from a dedicated trial report were not found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SWARNA SHUSK DHAN: EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: "variety_name" (Swarna Shusk Dhan) and "seednet_variety_name" (Swarna Shusk Dhan (RCPR 56-IR93827-29-1-14) IET 27962)) refer to the same variety. Every finding below matches "Swarna Shusk Dhan" with IET 27962 or RCPR 56 codes. The Seednet portal itself was not searched, so no Seednet page is cited.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released and notified by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards as a drought-tolerant, multiple-stress-tolerant variety for direct-seeded rainfed upland conditions; the 2023 report describes it as lodging resistant -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/AnnualReport2023.pdf
- Grouped with drought-tolerant varieties in the Rice Package of Practices for Eastern India (drought lists are clear; a submergence list in the same document is garbled in the extracted text, so submergence tolerance is not confirmed) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India
- ICAR annual report 2024-25 names it, with Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 and 2, as a drought-resistant rice suitable for water-limited areas -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- The IIRR AICRP rice table lists it with disease/pest codes MR-BL, SB and LF (reading as moderate reaction to bacterial leaf blight, sheath blight and leaf folder; the table gives no legend, so this reading is my inference) -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf
- Listed among varieties to select for tolerance to false smut and related diseases in the Package of Practices (the list is partly garbled) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Semi-dwarf, early duration (110-115 days), high yielding (4.0-4.5 t/ha), multiple-stress tolerant, with fertilizer responsiveness, in the ICAR-RCER Annual Report 2023 -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/AnnualReport2023.pdf
- AICRP on Rice entry with yield 2.2 in the IIRR 2023 table (unit and column meaning not stated in the extract) -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf
- Listed as a direct-seeded rice variety in an IIRR scientist profile page (trait listing, not a trial report) -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/about-iirr/staff-iirr/iirr-technicals/88-dr-jyothi-badri-scientist
- Not found: multi-location yield data specific to this variety, or the separate maturity and grain-yield figures from a dedicated trial report.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Variety code RCPR 56-IR93827-29-1-1-4 with IET 27962; parentage recorded as IR 81039-B-173-U3-3/IR 81063-B-94-U3-1 (the IIRR table cell is truncated after "IR", so the second parent is confirmed only by the user-supplied record) -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf
- Breeding method, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found. The search returned only Swarna-background papers (Swarna Sub1, CR Dhan 800), which are different varieties and were discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region (ICAR-RCER), Patna, which released it -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/AnnualReport2023.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist names for Swarna Shusk Dhan: No evidence found. The Swarna Sukha Dhan paper (Santosh Kumar, Rakesh Kumar, Sanjeev Kumar) is a different variety, so those names are NOT attributed here -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/143280/53178/391485

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region, Patna, Bihar 800 014 (institute address as printed in a related paper's affiliation; not a divisional address for this variety) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/143280/53178/391485
- Institute website for variety releases: https://icarrcer.icar.gov.in/variety-released-2/ (also https://icarrcer.org.in/)
- Official email, phone and breeder contact for this variety: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR-RCER (2024). Annual Report 2023. ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region, Patna -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/AnnualReport2023.pdf
- Indian Council of Agricultural Research (2025). Annual Report 2024-25 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
- Indian Institute of Rice Research (2023). Annual Report 2023 (AICRP on Rice table) -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh) or DOI specific to this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for Swarna Shusk Dhan was returned. The ICAR-RCER 2021 report covers seed production of other varieties only -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/Annual%20Report%202021.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttar Pradesh, per the IIRR AICRP table -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf
- The ICAR-RCER 2023 report gives the release context but no state list for this variety -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/AnnualReport2023.pdf

Discarded as irrelevant: Swarna Sukha Dhan (IET 24692), Swarna Unnat Dhan, Swarna Shakti Dhan, Swarna Purvi Dhan 1, Swarna Sub1, and Swarna (MTU 7029). These are other varieties, and their breeders, traits and papers were not attributed to Swarna Shusk Dhan.

Searches run: 4 (variety/release; breeder/institute; research/publications; seed/Hill Rice 14-8 alias). Only one source, the Indian Farming article, names this variety. It refers to it as "ICAR-NEH Hill Rice 14-8 / TRC 2014-8". No page named IET 24197 or the Seednet portal entry was returned. Findings below are attributed to the release-minutes name TRC 2014-8 and its alias.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The search returned no stress-tolerance data for TRC 2014-8. The only other stress-related text in the source concerns other varieties (Tripura Khara Dhan-1, drought QTLs qDTY2.2 and qDTY4.1), which I have discarded. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. -- searched via query 1; no page returned for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Unattributed: the source contains a block reading "95 cm plant height, 120–125 days maturity, 3.4 t/ha yield potential in hill ecology". It sits directly after text about a different variety (parentage "Pyzum and BPT 5204"), so I cannot confirm it belongs to TRC 2014-8. Treat it as unverified. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
No field-trial or multi-location results found for TRC 2014-8.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: the source states the variety was developed from a cross involving IR 78878-208-B-1-2 (first parent only; the second parent is not visible in the retrieved text). The user-supplied parentage "IR 78878-208-B-1-2 x IR 74371-54-1-1" is consistent with this but not independently confirmed. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
Breeding method and QTL data: No evidence found for TRC 2014-8. The qDTY markers in the source belong to a different variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Recommended as developed under ICAR-NEH programmes (NICRA-linked hill rice series). Named breeder: No evidence found. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
The ICAR-CRRI "Major Achievements" page lists "INHR2014-8 (2020)" in a release list. This is a different name and institute, so I have discarded it. -- https://icar-crri.in/major-achievements/

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, address, or ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region contact page was retrieved. Institute-level contact not found in search results.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses, or conference papers naming TRC 2014-8 were returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or private dealer listing for TRC 2014-8 or IET 24197 was returned. The Seednet portal entry was not retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Released in 2021 and recommended for the lower hills of Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Tripura and other neighbouring north-eastern states. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/173999/63840/503067
Note: the source lists Tripura and the NE states as well. Your intake lists only Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka, so the record may be incomplete.

Gaps to resolve: the Seednet entry for IET 24197, the release notification, and the breeder/institute contact page. These need direct access to seednet.gov.in, the ICAR-RC NEH (Umiam) site, or the CSC minutes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Taramati (RNR 23064), rice

Name note: "Taramati" is the release name. "Taramati (RNR-23064)" is the Seednet name. My searches did not return a Seednet portal page, so every Seednet-name finding below comes from pages that use the code RNR 23064 with the same name. The institution field in the input ("Andhra Pradesh") is a state, not an institution. Four searches were run in total.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no Taramati-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. A rice-breeding page from ICAR-PJTAU describes blast-resistance work in general terms only, and I did not attribute it to this variety. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/rru-rajendranagar/

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page named Taramati together with a disease or pest reaction. -- (searched; no qualifying URL)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maturity and grain type: one IIRR table row lists Taramati (RNR 23064) with a duration of 135 (days), medium slender grain, and release year 2009. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Yield: No evidence found for Taramati. -- (searched; no qualifying URL)
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Seed demand: a 2015 Andhra Pradesh CAG audit appendix lists Taramati (RNR 23064) among varieties released in 2009-10 that had low or nil demand, with 34 quintals of breeder seed recorded. This refers to the RNR 23064 code. -- https://cag.gov.in/uploads/download_audit_report/2015/Andhra_Pradesh_Report_2_2015_Appendices.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: the input lists SAMBAMAHSURI/TELLAHAMSA. Two sources instead list the parentage as BPT-5204/Tellahamsa: the IIRR table (https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf) and an SSR purity paper table (https://www.ijsrp.org/research_paper_dec2011/ijsrp-dec-2011-13.pdf). Sambamahsuri is not confirmed for this variety. The discrepancy should be checked against the CSC or notification record.
Breeding-line code: RNR 23064 (both sources above).
Breeding method: No evidence found.
Genome resources and markers: The SSR purity paper (Aruna Kumari et al., 2011) uses SSR markers to check genetic purity of seed lots. Its variety table includes RNR 23064 with the BPT 5204/Tellahamsa parentage. The paper's main subject is Samba Mahsuri, so RNR 23064 appears only as a comparison entry. -- https://www.ijsrp.org/research_paper_dec2011/ijsrp-dec-2011-13.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The Taramati entry appears on the Rice Research Unit, Agricultural Research Institute (ARI), Rajendranagar page of the PJTAU site, which lists it with the 2009 release year. No breeder is named there. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/rru-rajendranagar/
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder name is linked to this variety. An IIRR newsletter names Dr GSV Prasad, a plant breeder who retired in 2015. That name sits near a release table, but the snippet does not connect him to Taramati, so I have not attributed the variety to him. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only. The page found names the Rice Research Unit, ARI, Rajendranagar, Southern Telangana Zone, on the PJTAU site. No email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for the unit was captured. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/rru-rajendranagar/
CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found.

PUBLICATIONS
Aruna Kumari, K., Durgarani, Ch. V., Vanisree, S., Sivaramakrishnan, S., Balachandran, S.M., & Sundaram, R.M. (2011). SSR-marker-based genetic purity assessment of seed lots of Samba Mahsuri (paper title not captured in the search result; the paper lists RNR 23064 among varieties). International Journal of Scientific and Research Publications. -- https://www.ijsrp.org/research_paper_dec2011/ijsrp-dec-2011-13.pdf
No other peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or trial result naming Taramati was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Breeder seed: 34 quintals recorded for Taramati (RNR 23064) in 2009-10, with the variety listed as having low or nil demand. -- https://cag.gov.in/uploads/download_audit_report/2015/Andhra_Pradesh_Report_2_2015_Appendices.pdf
SEED AVAILABILITY -- Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales and private dealers: No evidence found. The seed-shop results returned were for other paddy varieties (for example, Pusa Basmati and MTU types) and were discarded. -- (searched; no qualifying URL)

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The notified-varieties list gives the Taramati (RNR 23064) notification as S.O. 2187(E), dated 27.08.2009, with the scope shown as All India. This conflicts with the input value "Unknown," so the input should be updated. No state-level recommendation was found. -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm

seednet_fields.Parentage: The proposed variety has been developed from a cross between MTU 7029 and Annada.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Has been recommended for West Bengal, Odisha (Zone-III) and Tripura (Zone-IV) by 52nd Annual Meeting or All India Coordinated Rice Improvemnet Project (AICRIP) and Rice Workshop, 2017. Producation ecology: Boro (irrigated) in medium-land situation
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: (i)	Resistance to lodging and shattering. (ii)	Fertilizer responsive. (iii)	Suitable for early sown conditions. (iv)	Seed rate is 50 kg/ha (2-3 seedling per hill). (v)	Photoperiod insensitive, can be grown both in Boro and Kharif seasons.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: (i)Maturity duration: Medium group (ii)Plant height: 106.42 cm (semi-dwarf) (iii)Grain: Short bold (SB), straw color hull and white kernel (iv)Panicle: Compact panicle with high grain number. Detail morphological charcters based on “Guidelines for the Conduct of Test for Distinctiveness, Uniformity and Stability on Rice (Oryza sativa L.)” of PPV & FRA, New Delhi.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The entry resistant to leaf blast (SI=4.2), neck blast (SI=3.5), brown spot (SI=4.9), sheath blight (SI=5.4), sheath rot (SI=3.4), BLB (SI=5.4) and RTD (SI=4.0).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Tolerant to major pests like stem borer folder, gall midge biotype 1 and whorl maggot under natural screening.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Recommended doses Boro: 120:60:60 of N: P2O5 : K2O in kg/ha. Basal: ¼ N + Full P2O5 + 3/4K20. 1st topdressing: ½ N at 15-20 DAT. 2nd topdressing: ¼ N + ¼K2O at Panicle initiation stage.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VGD 1 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: "variety_name" is VGD 1 (the CSC/State release name). "seednet_variety_name" is "VGD 1 (VG 09006) (IET 24606)". The evidence below refers to VGD 1, which was released from culture VG 09006 (IET 24606 in the trial records). Seednet itself was not retrieved by these searches.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Bacterial blight resistance was added by marker-assisted introgression of xa5, xa13 and Xa21 into VGD 1 -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-4716099/v1
VG 09006 (VGD 1) was reported as moderately resistant to leaf folder in artificial screening -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352981669_A_high_yielding_Seeragasamba_variety_VGD_1
Non-lodging, high-tillering, semi-dwarf plant type is listed for VGD 1 -- https://www.covaipost.com/coimbatore/tnau-releases-new-crop-varieties-for-pongal/
A TNAU 41st CSM proceedings item mentions flood-tolerance observations in the same session, but the snippet does not clearly attribute flood tolerance to VGD 1, so it is not recorded as a VGD 1 finding -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2022/12/1.-41st-CSM-on-Rice-Proceedings-2022.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity and submergence tolerance: No evidence found in the searched pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
Bacterial blight resistance genes xa5, xa13 and Xa21 were introgressed into VGD 1 -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-4716099/v1
Moderate resistance to leaf folder (artificial screening) for VG 09006 / VGD 1 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352981669_A_high_yielding_Seeragasamba_variety_VGD_1
Other diseases and pests: No further evidence found in the searched pages.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Released in 2019 from ARS Vaigai Dam as a fine-grain, medium-duration variety for general cultivation -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ars-vaigaidam/varieties-released/
Duration of about 129 days at the station -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ars-vaigaidam/varieties-released/
Duration of about 130 days in a TNAU release announcement -- https://www.covaipost.com/coimbatore/tnau-releases-new-crop-varieties-for-pongal/
Overall mean yield of VG 09006 across trials reported as 5028 kg/ha, with station and multi-location comparisons against Seeragasamba and TKM 13 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352981669_A_high_yielding_Seeragasamba_variety_VGD_1
Farmer-level claim of up to three tonnes per acre against about two tonnes for traditional Seeragasamba -- https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/seeraga-samba-variety-released-by-tnau-finds-more-takers-849384
Front-line demonstrations of VGD 1 were conducted at farmer fields in Nagapattinam during 2019-20 -- https://kvknagapattinam.co.in/2022/03/15/rice-variety-vgd-1-a-boon-to-nagapattinam-farmers/
Seed-rate standardisation for VGD 1 is listed as a TNAU action plan item -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2022/12/1.-41st-CSM-on-Rice-Proceedings-2022.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: ADT 43 / Seeragasamba -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/VarietyRelease2019Booklet.pdf
Cross made at ARS Vaigai Dam in kharif 2007, with ADT 43 as female parent and Seeragasamba as male parent, by pedigree breeding -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/250175527_A_high_yielding_seeragasamba_rice_culture_VG_09006_and_its_medicinal_properties
Breeding line codes: VG 09006 (culture), IET 24606 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352981669_A_high_yielding_Seeragasamba_variety_VGD_1
Breeding method: pedigree selection, then marker-assisted backcrossing (true F1s backcrossed to VGD 1) for bacterial blight genes -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-4716099/v1
Amylose content recorded as intermediate for VGD 1 -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-4716099/v1
Parental polymorphism survey using microsatellite markers between VGD 1 and ADT 55 is cited in a ResearchGate reference list -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352981669_A_high_yielding_Seeragasamba_variety_VGD_1
Genome resources beyond the cited markers: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Lead breeder: M. Madhan Mohan, Professor and Head, Agricultural Research Station, Vaigai Dam -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352981669_A_high_yielding_Seeragasamba_variety_VGD_1 and https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/seeraga-samba-variety-released-by-tnau-finds-more-takers-849384
Co-authors of the 2021 VGD 1 paper: S. Jeya Hepziba, S. Utharasu, C. Ravi Kumar, K. Ganesamurthy -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-4716099/v1
Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, ARS Vaigai Dam, Theni district -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ars-vaigaidam/varieties-released/
Marker-assisted work listed under Priyanka Rajendran's profile (role not confirmed) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Priyanka-Rajendran-8

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder: M. Madhan Mohan, Professor and Head, ARS Vaigai Dam. A ResearchGate paper shows an e-mail beginning "madhanmohan." but the full address is truncated in the record, so it is not reported as confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352981669_A_high_yielding_Seeragasamba_variety_VGD_1
Institute address: Agricultural Research Station, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Vaigai Dam, Theni district, Tamil Nadu (affiliation line only; no postal code or phone found) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/250175527_A_high_yielding_seeragasamba_rice_culture_VG_09006_and_its_medicinal_properties
Institute contact page, phone, and official e-mail: No evidence found in the searched pages. Official ARS page: https://tnau.ac.in/site/ars-vaigaidam/varieties-released/

PUBLICATIONS
Mohan MM, Hepziba SJ, Utharasu S, Kumar CR, Ganesamurthy K (2021). A high yielding Seeragasamba variety: VGD 1. Journal not identified in the snippet (listed as Mar 2021 on ResearchGate) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352981669_A_high_yielding_Seeragasamba_variety_VGD_1
Mohan M. M. et al. (year not confirmed). A high yielding seeragasamba rice culture VG 09006 and its medicinal properties. Research Note / conference paper -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/250175527_A_high_yielding_seeragasamba_rice_culture_VG_09006_and_its_medicinal_properties
Authors not captured (2021 or later). Marker assisted improvement of super fine grain rice variety, VGD 1 for bacterial blight resistance. Research Square preprint, rs-4716099/v1 -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-4716099/v1
TNAU (2022). Proceedings of the 41st Crop Sciences Meeting on Rice. TNAU -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2022/12/1.-41st-CSM-on-Rice-Proceedings-2022.pdf
KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found (not searched directly).
AICRP/ICAR annual report entries: No evidence found in the searched pages.

SEED AVAILABILITY
TNAU seed stock position as on 31.07.2021 lists VGD 1 with 800 kg at a Krishi Vigyan Kendra; the centre name is cut off in the snippet -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
A Dharmapuri KVK (Papparapatty) line also lists VGD 1; the quantity field is not legible in the snippet -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
Breeder seed production of VGD 1 is a TNAU project (CPBG/VGM/PBG/RIC/2022/001) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2022/12/1.-41st-CSM-on-Rice-Proceedings-2022.pdf
Demand and seed prices are rising, per a Thanjavur news report -- https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/seeraga-samba-variety-released-by-tnau-finds-more-takers-849384
NSC, State Seed Corporation, and private dealer listings: No evidence found in the searched pages. The Seednet portal was not reached.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VNR 2355 PLUS (IET20735) (VNR-202), Rice (hybrid)

Name used in evidence: "VNR 2355 Plus" in most sources. Two sources give "IET 20735" and "VNR-202" alongside it. The Seednet name "VNR 2355 PLUS (IET20735) (VNR-202)" was not found on any Seednet page in these searches. Four searches were run: variety/notification, breeder/institution, research, and seed availability.

Discrepancies to check before use
- Release year: the user input says 2019. Sources give a 2012 notification, S.O. 456(E) dated 16.03.2012. No 2019 record was found.
- Recommended states: the input says Chhattisgarh and Odisha. The notification list and a table in the Current Scenario chapter name Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. No source found names Chhattisgarh or Odisha as recommended states.
- Code overlap: the Bihar and Hybrid Rice pages list "VNR 2245 (IET 20735) (VNR-202)" as well, so the IET 20735 / VNR-202 code appears against two different hybrids. Treat the code as unverified.
- "VNR 2355 Power" (Somani Agro, B K Krishi Kendra) was excluded because it is a differently named product, though it may be the same hybrid under another name.

STRESS TOLERANCE (name: VNR 2355 Plus)
- The hybrid is listed with tolerance to bacterial leaf blight (BLB) on the company's variety list. -- https://www.vnrseeds.com/products/variety-list/?vdb=Paddy
- An ICAR 2012-13 crop improvement report lists the hybrid with a reaction code of "MR–LBl" and "NB" for irrigated areas. The codes are not defined in the snippet, so the meaning cannot be confirmed. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-12-13.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence was found for this variety. Only the general tolerance statements in the ICAR report were found, and they do not name this hybrid.

DISEASE AND PEST (name: VNR 2355 Plus)
- Tolerance to bacterial leaf blight (BLB) is listed by the company. -- https://www.vnrseeds.com/products/variety-list/?vdb=Paddy
- The ICAR report gives "MR–LBl" for this hybrid. This is the only independent source for the BLB reaction. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-12-13.pdf
- No blast, BPH, gall midge or other pest data was found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (name: VNR 2355 Plus)
- Duration of 130-135 days, suitable for lowland, medium height and strong stems, is described in a market-strategy study. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2cac8b53-faab-405a-9736-0e3acca1c00f/content
- Duration of 130-135 days and yield of 5.9-6.0 (units not stated in the snippet) are listed in a state hybrid table. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- A retailer page gives a medium duration of 125-140 days, medium slender grain, and kharif sowing. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/vnr-2355-plus-25789468533.html
- A field day was held at Matatu village, Kanke Block, Ranchi, with a farmer's field of this hybrid shown. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2cac8b53-faab-405a-9736-0e3acca1c00f/content
- Company news reports that farmers in Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha won yield awards for this hybrid. This is company marketing and does not confirm recommendation. -- https://www.vnrseeds.com/news-events/
- No multi-location trial data or yield-trial report was found.

GENETICS AND QTL (name: VNR 2355 Plus)
- Parentage VNR-R 51/VNR-RB66 (from the user input) was not confirmed by any search result. No evidence found.
- No breeding-line code beyond IET 20735 / VNR-202 was found, and that code is not verified (see discrepancies).
- Breeding method (two-line or three-line) was not stated. The hybrid is listed in the two-line hybrid table, which does not name the method for this hybrid. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391
- No QTL, marker, or genome resource evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (name: VNR 2355 Plus)
- Developer listed as VNR Seeds Pvt. Ltd., Raipur, in a hybrid table. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391
- VNR Seeds was founded in 1993 by a farmer, Krishi Pandit Dr. Narayanbhai Chawda. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2cac8b53-faab-405a-9736-0e3acca1c00f/content
- No individual breeder or lead scientist name was found. No evidence found for a named breeder.

CONTACT DETAILS (institute level only; no breeder contact found)
- VNR Seeds Private Limited, Ground and 1st Floor Corporate Center, Ring Road No.1, Raipur-492006, Chhattisgarh, India. -- https://www.indiamart.com/vnrseedsprivatelimited-82047209/
- A state table gives the company address as Raipur-492099 (postal code differs from the above). -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Email and phone: no evidence found in the search results. The official site (vnrseeds.com) is listed as a product source but no contact page was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS (name: VNR 2355 Plus)
- Author not stated (year not stated). Market strategy and sale potential of rice variety of VNR. Krishikosh thesis or report -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2cac8b53-faab-405a-9736-0e3acca1c00f/content

- No peer-reviewed journal papers, AICRP reports, or DOI-indexed articles on this variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY (name: VNR 2355 Plus)
- VNR Agrimatrix, a wholesaler in Raipur, lists "Vnr 2355 Plus" in its product range. -- https://www.indiamart.com/vnr-agrimatrix-raipur/
- Om Satya Sai Traders, Shivli, Uttar Pradesh, lists VNR 2355 Plus as in stock. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/vnr-2355-plus-25789468533.html
- No Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sale listing was found. Seednet evidence: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES (name: VNR 2355 Plus)
- Notified under S.O. 456(E) on 16.03.2012 for UP, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- The same notification is recorded in a Bihar state list of notified varieties. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- The hybrid table lists Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu as recommended states. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391
- Chhattisgarh and Odisha as recommended states: no evidence found. Only the company's award news mentions farmers in these states.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JKRH-401 (variety_code JKRH 2000, IET 18181), Rice

Search note: four web_search calls were used (variety overview, breeder/developer, research papers, seed availability). No search targeted the Seednet portal directly, so Seednet-specific findings are absent. The name used on most sources is "JKRH 401" (with or without hyphen). One notified-variety list gives "KKRH 2000" for the same IET number, which looks like a transcription variant of JKRH 2000. Evidence below refers to the variety_name JKRH-401. Seednet name: not confirmed.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Company product page describes JKRH 401 as highly tolerant of salinity -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-401/
- Company paddy listing says JKRH 401 is tolerant to alkalinity -- https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/paddy/
- A separate company listing names "JKRH 401 SURAKSHA" as resistant to blast; it is unclear whether this is the same entry or a distinct product name, so treat as unconfirmed -- https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/paddy/page/2/
- Nitrogen-use efficiency: JKRH 401 is named among hybrids with high N-use efficiency, suitable for N-deficient soils -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356605148_ADVANCED_BREEDING_STRATEGIES_FOR_RICE_IMPROVEMENT
- Arsenic study: JKRH 401 was screened among 20 genotypes; it was grouped with high arsenic-accumulating genotypes while tolerating arsenic treatment (tolerance-index data reported) -- https://www.isca.me/rjcs/Archives/v4/i11/7.ISCA-RJCS-2014-184.pdf
- Heat tolerance, submergence, flood and drought: no evidence found for JKRH 401 specifically.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Company listing says JKRH 401 (Suraksha) is resistant to blast (same caveat as above) -- https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/paddy/page/2/
- Public-private partnership proceedings table places JKRH 401 in a pest-scoring group for disease/pest scenario in Bihar/Odisha/UP context; the table's column meaning is not clear from the extract -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281737890_Public-private_partnership_for_hybrid_rice_Proceedings_of_the_6th_International_Hybrid_Rice_SymposiumThe_disease_scenario_in_Jharkhand_Bihar_and_Uttar_Pradesh_India_with_reference_to_hybrid_rice
- Insect (BPH) or bacterial blight resistance: no evidence found for JKRH 401 specifically.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration and yield in a hybrid release table: 125 days, 6.22 t/ha, released 2006 by JK Agri Genetics -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm and https://researchgate.net/publication/263920493_HYBRID_RICE_DEVELOPMENT_TWO_LINE_AND_THREE_LINE_SYSTEM
- Company product page: medium maturity of 135-140 days, high productive tillers, long panicles, medium bold grains, excellent hulling/milling/cooking quality, wide adaptability -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-401/
- Another breeding-status table gives 140 days duration and a yield value of 6.20 t/ha (column labels unclear) -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/hybrid-rice-seed-production.pdf
- Direct-seeded rice: JKRH 401 is listed among hybrids for DSR practice -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/CRRI_Technology-Bulletin_No-250.pdf
- Multi-location trial data, AICRP/ICAR annual report entries: no evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: No evidence found (Unknown in input).
- Breeding line: restorer line JK1044R is the restorer parent described for the JKRH 401 hybrid -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12298-015-0334-y
- Breeding method: hybrid (CMS-restorer-based, as implied by the restorer line); the exact system for JKRH 401 is not stated in the sources -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12298-015-0334-y
- Genome resources: JKRH 401 (IET 18181) was used as material in Agrobacterium transformation of JK1044R, with nptII selection marker -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12298-015-0334-y
- QTL/marker studies: no evidence found for JKRH 401 specifically. A hybrid-purity microsatellite study covers hybrid parental lines generally, not confirmed for this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263920493_HYBRID_RICE_DEVELOPMENT_TWO_LINE_AND_THREE_LINE_SYSTEM

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developer: JK Agri Genetics Ltd (Hyderabad) is recorded as the developing company for JKRH 401 -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- PPV&FR registration: applicant JK Agri Genetics Ltd; registration no. 2 of 2009; certificate dated 12/02/09 -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumfinal27oct2018.pdf
- Individual lead breeder: No evidence found. Mithun Chakraborty is listed with JK Agri Genetics Ltd as an author of the transformation paper; no source names him as the breeder of JKRH 401 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/293044906_Agrobacterium-mediated_genetic_transformation_of_commercially_elite_rice_restorer_line_using_nptII_gene_as_a_plant_selection_marker
- Institutional research base: company describes in-house breeding and biotech R&D units and 3 main research stations -- https://jkagri.com/research-and-development/

CONTACT DETAILS
- JK Agri Genetics Limited, 1-10-177, 4th floor, Varun Towers, Begumpet, Hyderabad – 500016 (postal address of company head office) -- https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/paddy/page/2/
- Email: No evidence found.
- Phone: No evidence found.
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Institute contact page: https://jkagri.com/ (company site; no dedicated contact page URL was retrieved)

PUBLICATIONS
- Chakraborty M et al. (2016). Agrobacterium-mediated genetic transformation of commercially elite rice restorer line using nptII gene as a plant selection marker. Physiology and Molecular Biology of Plants 22(1): 51–60 -- DOI 10.1007/s12298-015-0334-y, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12298-015-0334-y (only the first author name was visible in the extract; the full author list should be checked on the article page)
- Singh Sanjeev (2007). Hybrid rice development: Two line and three line system. Pages 178-195; journal/book name not fully legible in extract -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263920493_HYBRID_RICE_DEVELOPMENT_TWO_LINE_AND_THREE_LINE_SYSTEM (variety appears in a release table only)
- ISCA Research Journal of Crop Science (2014). Arsenic Accumulation in Rice (Oryza sativa L.) Genotypes; authors not visible in extract. Volume 4, issue 11 -- https://www.isca.me/rjcs/Archives/v4/i11/7.ISCA-RJCS-2014-184.pdf
- KrishiKosh: a project report on market share and farmer perception of JK Agri hybrid rice mentions JKRH401 only as a product; it is about the company and is not a variety study, so it is excluded -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/4c9e2f92-b98d-4af3-be82-242a6a992005/content
- AICRP/ICAR annual reports and theses on this variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- J.K. Seeds (Hyderabad) offers hybrid paddy seed listed as JKRH-401, 50 kg sealed bags, all-India market; listed supply ability 500 per week -- https://www.tradeindia.com/products/hybrid-paddy-seed-2962104.html
- Company product listing for JKRH 401 -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-401/
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales: No evidence found.
- Seednet portal listing: not searched directly; No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified in Uttar Pradesh under a 2014 notification (S.O. 244(E), 25.01.2014) -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Earlier notification of JKRH 401 All India (S.O. 122(E), 06.02.2007) -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Hybrid release list recommends Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Other state-level recommendation tables (Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal, private sector lists): -- https://www.resear

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NPH 924-1 (IET 21255) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC notification list uses "NPH 924-1 (IET 21255)". The seednet_variety_name is "Unknown", so I did not search seednet directly. A hybrid-list page gives "PNPH 924-1 (IET 21255)", which I treat as the same entry only because the variety code matches. Crop: rice (Oryza sativa). Searches run: 4 (3 required, 1 seed-availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under a false smut (Ustilaginoidea virens) screen in Assam, NPH 924-1 was rated moderately resistant (score 3), alongside several other hybrids and landraces. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377436390_Screening_of_rice_varieties_against_Ustilaginoidea_virens_causing_rice_false_smut_in_Assam_condition
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Same false smut screen as above (moderately resistant). No evidence found for other diseases or pests (blast, BLB, BPH, GLH, stem borer, etc.) in a page that names this variety. The disease-scenario paper lists NPH 924-1 among tested hybrids but does not give its disease reactions in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281737890_Public-private_partnership_for_hybrid_rice_Proceedings_of_the_6th_International_Hybrid_Rice_SymposiumThe_disease_scenario_in_Jharkhand_Bihar_and_Uttar_Pradesh_India_with_reference_to_hybrid_rice

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Hybrid list entry: PNPH 924-1 (IET 21255), 2012, duration 125-135 days, yield listed as 6.2 to 6.7 (units not shown in the retrieved text), applicant Nuziveedu Seeds Limited. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Multi-season comparison of five tropical hybrids plus a local HYV: NPH-924-1 recorded plant height, yield-component and growth data in rainy and winter seasons. Trial location and authors are not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sukamal-Sarkar/publication/331063207_Differential_growth_and_yield_response_of_hybrid_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_to_seasonal_variability/links/5c63d76445851582c3e42882/Differential-growth-and-yield-response-of-hybrid-rice-Oryza-sativa-L-to-seasonal-variability.pdf
- The disease-scenario paper includes a days-to-50%-flowering table with NPH 924-1 values, but the column headers are not clear in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281737890_Public-private_partnership_for_hybrid_rice_Proceedings_of_the_6th_International_Hybrid_Rice_SymposiumThe_disease_scenario_in_Jharkhand_Bihar_and_Uttar_Pradesh_India_with_reference_to_hybrid_rice
- Assam Director of Agriculture letter (30 June 2020) directed ASCL to buy 1,128.60 quintals of NPH-924-1 for Kharif 2020-21. The same article reports that the variety is meant for Boro season. -- https://www.sentinelassam.com/cities/guwahati-city/strange-are-the-ways-in-which-the-agriculture-department-functions-490737

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: No evidence found.
- Breeding method (CMS three-line or other): No evidence found.
- Breeding-line code: IET 21255 appears only as the variety code in notification lists (see RECOMMENDED STATES and BREEDER AND INSTITUTION).
- Genes, QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing company: Nuziveedu Seeds Limited, Medchal Mandal, Ranga Reddy, Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- The company stated that the hybrid was released for the Boro season through the Central Sub-committee on Crop Standards (CSCSNRV) for West Bengal and Assam. -- https://www.sentinelassam.com/cities/guwahati-city/strange-are-the-ways-in-which-the-agriculture-department-functions-490737
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. Names from the NRRI hybrid review (Prakash Singh; Jawahar Lal Katara; Sanghamitra Samantaray; Ramlakhan Verma) appear in a paper that lists NPH 924-1 only as a promising hybrid. They are not attributed to this variety here. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489
- Station or research centre of the developer: No evidence found beyond the company location.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Nuziveedu Seeds Limited, Medchal Mandal, Ranga Reddy-501401 (A.P.) (institute-level address as listed for PNPH 924-1). -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Official email, phone, or contact page for Nuziveedu Seeds: No evidence found in the searches run.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Differential growth and yield response of hybrid rice (Oryza sativa L.) to seasonal variability. Journal not stated (ResearchGate record) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sukamal-Sarkar/publication/331063207_Differential_growth_and_yield_response_of_hybrid_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_to_seasonal_variability/links/5c63d76445851582c3e42882/Differential-growth-and-yield-response-of-hybrid-rice-Oryza-sativa-L-to-seasonal-variability.pdf
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Screening of rice varieties against Ustilaginoidea virens causing rice false smut in Assam condition. Journal not stated (ResearchGate record) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377436390_Screening_of_rice_varieties_against_Ustilaginoidea_virens_causing_rice_false_smut_in_Assam_condition
- Public-private partnership for hybrid rice (Proceedings of the 6th International Hybrid Rice Symposium), authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Journal/Report: proceedings -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281737890_Public-private_partnership_for_hybrid_rice_Proceedings_of_the_6th_International_Hybrid_Rice_SymposiumThe_disease_scenario_in_Jharkhand_Bihar_and_Uttar_Pradesh_India_with_reference_to_hybrid_rice
- AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses, DOI-linked trial papers: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Assam state seed corporation procurement order (ASCL) for NPH-924-1, Kharif 2020-21, as described above. -- https://www.sentinelassam.com/cities/guwahati-city/strange-are-the-ways-in-which-the-agriculture-department-functions-490737
- The company is named as the dealer of the hybrid in the same article. Current dealer, KVK, NSC, or SAU sales listings: No evidence found.
- A separate advisory lists "NPH 924-Hima" for Boro in West Bengal and Assam. I did not attribute it to this variety because the name does not match and I could not confirm it. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/paddy-cultivation-advisory-amid-covid-19/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified in 2012 under S.O. 2125(E), dated 10.09.2012, for West Bengal and Assam. -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- A CSC minutes list shows a 2007 date alongside the 10/09/2012 notification. I could not confirm what the 2007 date refers to (possibly year of identification), so the release year is recorded as 2012 (notification) with this discrepancy noted. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Recommended for the Boro season (irrigated areas) in West Bengal and Assam. -- https://www.sentinelassam.com/cities/guwahati-city/strange-are-the-ways-in-which-the-agriculture-department-functions-490737

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: US 380 (variety_name) / US 380 (IET 25728) (seednet_variety_name), Rice (PADDY (DHAN))

Search note: four web_search queries were run: "US 380 Rice variety", "US 380 (IET 25728) rice breeder developed by Seed Works", "US 380 rice IET 25728 research paper", and "US 380 paddy seed availability Chhattisgarh". Neither name, nor the code IET 25728, was linked to this rice variety in any result. The results were about other products or varieties, so they are discarded under the strict relevance rule.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The "US 380 Rice variety" search returned unrelated pages (Sri Lankan BG 380 lists, Vietnamese OM 380 rice, IR8, US rice-industry pages).

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No result named US 380 with blast, BLB, BPH, or other resistance data.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for US 380 appeared.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The parentage given in the brief (hybrid 5014A/1066R; A line 5014A; R line 1066R) did not appear in any search result, so it could not be independently verified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The breeder-query search returned a IndiaMart listing for "MS Seed Works International Pvt Ltd" (https://www.indiamart.com/ms-seed-works-international-pvt-ltd/other-products.html). That listing names other hybrid rice products, US 382 and US305, and not US 380. It is a name resemblance, so it is not attributed to this variety, and no breeder name was found. The CSC/Seednet listing was not reachable through search. A plantauthority.gov.in registered-varieties compendium (https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compediumforallcategoryuptonov-2021.pdf) was returned, but the snippet did not show a US 380 entry. It was not opened in full and should be checked directly.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute, or divisional email, phone, address, or contact-page URL was found for US 380. The IndiaMart listing above is a company trade page for a different set of products and is not used here as a contact.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper names US 380 or IET 25728. The "research paper" search returned unrelated rice papers, and the BG380-2 IRRI newsletter is a different variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The seed search returned generic Chhattisgarh paddy-seed supplier listings (TradeIndia Raigarh and Raipur, Justdial Raipur) that do not mention US 380. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for this variety was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found for Chhattisgarh or Madhya Pradesh as recommended states for US 380. The only state-level pages returned were general Chhattisgarh paddy-market articles, which do not mention this variety.

Recommended next steps: check the CSC or Seednet entry for "US 380 (IET 25728)" directly, since the search index did not return it. Confirm the release notification and recommended states from the CSC minutes. Verify the parentage with the company, Seed Works International Pvt Ltd, which is the institution named in the brief. Confirm whether this is a private hybrid with no public-sector breeder, since that would explain the absence of publications.

drought.details: The digest records no drought-tolerance evidence for VNR 2245. Down to Earth describes it as a hybrid suited to water-scarce conditions but states the article does not show drought tolerance for this variety; its drought statements refer to traditional varieties. The input variety record (CSC) states the entry has not been screened against any biotic or abiotic stresses but has performed well under terminal drought conditions. This statement has no trial data or source URL in the digest and is not independently verified, so no level is assigned.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial leaf blight: the Krishikosh project report (2021) states VNR 2245 is tolerant to bacterial leaf blight. ICAR Crop Improvement 2012-13 lists VNR 2245 (Hybrid) with a reaction code string that appears to include leaf-blight resistance, but the table text is garbled, so this is uncertain. Blast: the Krishikosh 2021 report claims 100% capability of surviving blast; the digest classes this as an unverified, company-style statement with no trial data. The input variety record (CSC) states the variety is resistant to blast and neck blast and moderately resistant to RTV, sheath rot and brown spot. The digest contains no independent evidence for these input-record disease reactions. Sheath blight and other diseases: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Brown planthopper, stem borer, gall midge, sheath blight and other pests: No evidence found in the digest. The input variety record (CSC) states the variety is moderately resistant to leaf folder, GLH (green leafhopper) and whorl maggot. The digest contains no independent source for these pest reactions.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Krishikosh project report (2021) says VNR 2245 is tolerant to bacterial leaf blight, and also claims it is 100% capable of surviving blast. The blast claim is an unverified, company-style statement with no trial data -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2cac8b53-faab-405a-9736-0e3acca1c00f/content
ICAR Crop Improvement 2012-13 lists VNR 2245 (Hybrid) as a central release for irrigated areas, with a reaction code string that appears to include leaf-blight resistance, but the table text is garbled, so this is uncertain -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-12-13.pdf
Down to Earth (Cauvery delta article) describes VNR-2245 as a hybrid of about 90-95 days suited to water-scarce conditions, but it does not show drought tolerance for this variety; the drought-tolerance statements in that article refer to traditional varieties -- https://www.downtoearth.org.in/agriculture/cauvery-delta-farmers-are-gaining-resilience-by-cultivating-indigenous-rice-varieties
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance for VNR 2245: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
Bacterial leaf blight tolerance: see Stress Tolerance (Krishikosh 2021 and ICAR 2012-13).
Blast: a Krishikosh 2021 claim only (see Stress Tolerance); no trial evidence found.
Brown planthopper, stem borer, gall midge, sheath blight, and other pests or diseases: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Krishikosh 2021 describes VNR 2245 as a mid-early hybrid of 120-125 days for midland conditions, with medium plant height, strong stem, long slender grain, medium aroma and high yield capacity -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2cac8b53-faab-405a-9736-0e3acca1c00f/content
The same Krishikosh report records a VNR field day at Boreya village, Kanke block, Ranchi, Jharkhand, for "Rice (Hybrid - 2245)" -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2cac8b53-faab-405a-9736-0e3acca1c00f/content
Note: a separate short-duration entry (105-110 days, upland, 90-100 cm, low-rainfall areas) appears on the same page, but it is not clearly tied to VNR 2245 and may refer to VNR 2228. Discarded for this record.
Duration and yield, by entry:
- VNR 2245 (IET 20716) (VNR-204), 2011: 90-95 days, 6.83 t/ha -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- VNR 2245 (IET 20716), 2012 entry: 120-125 days, 7.0-7.2 t/ha -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Nepal trial summary: 120 days, 6.00 t/ha, recommended at 60-700 m altitude -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341815196_Production_Technique_of_Hybrid_Rice_in_Nepal
- Down to Earth: 90-95 days -- https://www.downtoearth.org.in/agriculture/cauvery-delta-farmers-are-gaining-resilience-by-cultivating-indigenous-rice-varieties
The two IET 20716 entries conflict on duration (90-95 vs 120-125 days). Both are recorded as-is.
Allelopathy trial: VNR 2245 was used as a test variety against leaf extracts of Ageratina adenophora. Germination fell by 65-85% (fresh extract) and 74-88% (dry extract) at 100% concentration across both test varieties. VNR 2245 was less affected than Arize 6444, but the authors advised against growing it in areas invaded by this weed -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44372-025-00173-9 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390427793_Allelopathic_effects_of_fresh_and_dried_leaf_extracts_of_Ageratina_adenophora_on_rice_varieties

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage "VNR-F51 / VNR-RB 242": supplied in the input record only; no web evidence found.
Breeding line codes: IET 20716 (also written IET20716 and VNR-204) is listed for VNR 2245 -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
Breeding method: the source describes VNR 2245 as a two-line hybrid rice entry (IntechOpen table) -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391 (the source gives this as a two-line hybrid; the parental line details are not given).
