EVIDENCE DIGEST: Hybrid 6129 (Rice)
Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers, seed availability). Seednet was not searched by name; "seednet_variety_name" is Unknown, so no Seednet-specific evidence was gathered.
Name note: the evidence below for IET 18815 / HRI-152 names HRI-152 or Hybrid-6129 with the code IET 18815, which matches the variety_code field. Nothing found names the variety by its exact seednet name.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Hybrid 6129, HRI-152 or IET 18815.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight or insect resistance data for these names.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found for this variety. The only trial pages returned concern Arize-6129, a different name (see Notes).

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): Parentage and breeding method: No evidence found. Breeding-line code: IET 18815 is listed as the code for Hybrid-6129 in a notified-varieties list -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf ; the same code is shown for HRI-152 in the Bihar hybrid list -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm . QTL, marker and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Developer: Bayer Bio-Science, Hyderabad, listed for HRI-152 (IET 18815), released 2007, duration 120 days (mid-early), yield not available -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm . Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. Developing public institute: No evidence found; the developer above is a private company.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute or company contact details (email, phone, address or contact page) were returned for Bayer Bio-Science or for this variety.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The only paper results name Arize-6129 or P A 6129, not this variety (see Notes).

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for this variety. Trade-data pages mention Arize 6129 Gold seed exports and imports from India -- https://www.volza.com/p/hybrid-rice-seed/export/ and https://www.volza.com/p/hybrid-rice-seed/import/coo-india/ . These are a different product name, so they were not used. No NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Punjab and Tamil Nadu -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm (HRI-152 (IET 18815) row). Bihar notification: Hybrid-6129 (IET 18815), dated 05/10/2007, notification 1703(E) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf . The Bihar list gives no recommended states.

NOTES (excluded under strict relevance rule):
- PA 6129 (Bayer, 2007, 115-120 days, 6.58 t/ha, recommended for Punjab, Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry) appears in the same drdpat list -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm . It is not confirmed as the same variety because it uses a different name and no code. Treat as a candidate only; it may be a different product with the same breeder and year.
- Arize-6129 (SRI trials in NW Himalayas, grain yield about 75 q/ha in one study) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/305770285_Productivity_and_profitability_of_rice_hybrids_at_different_nutrient_management_levels_under_semi-arid_conditions_of_North_Eastern_Plains_Zone . Not linked to IET 18815 on the page itself, so excluded.
- P A 6129 in a 6th International Hybrid Rice Symposium paper, with a 36% yield advantage in early maturity trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281737890_Public-private_partnership_for_hybrid_rice_Proceedings_of_the_6th_International_Hybrid_Rice_SymposiumThe_disease_scenario_in_Jharkhand_Bihar_and_Uttar_Pradesh_India_with_reference_to_hybrid_rice . Excluded for the same reason.
- Recommended next steps: search Seednet for "IET 18815", "HRI 152" and "PA 6129"; check the Bayer Bio-Science India website; check the CSC release minutes (2007) for the official name and parentage.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page that names LG 93.01 (BLR-102) (IET 24949) or LG 93.01 with stress-tolerance data. The only related hit was an AICRIP Hybrid Rice Kharif 2015 report, which lists entry 24949 / BLR-102 but gives no labelled stress data in the extracted text. -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page linked LG 93.01 or BLR-102 / IET 24949 to disease or pest reaction.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The AICRIP Hybrid Rice Kharif 2015 report contains repeated multi-row entries for IET 24949 / BLR-102, but the extracted text has no column headings, so I cannot identify yield, maturity or height values and have not reported any. Name matched: entry code 24949 / BLR-102. -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage as supplied (A line ATPDA 0001 = IR 58025A; B line ATPDB 0002 = IR 58025B; R line ATPDG 5094, in-house) was not confirmed for LG 93.01 by any search result. The user-supplied record is the only source for these codes.
- Pages on IR 58025A and IR 58025B (CMS and maintainer lines used in many Indian hybrids) describe those parent lines in general, not LG 93.01. They are not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6062963/
- ATPDA / ATPDB / ATPDG codes: No evidence found.
- Breeding method for LG 93.01: No evidence found.
- Genome resources or QTL for LG 93.01: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Bisco Bio Sciences (listed as "Bisco Bioscience, Hyderabad" beside entry 24949 / BLR-102 in the AICRIP Hybrid Rice Kharif 2015 report). -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf
- Company description: Bisco Bio Sciences is described as a hybrid seed company (maize, sunflower, jowar, bajra, paddy) with a Hyderabad base, and as a subsidiary of Limagrain in one LinkedIn profile. This is company-level context, not evidence about LG 93.01. -- https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/bisco-bio-sciences ; https://www.linkedin.com/in/bisco-bio-sciences-limagrain-97200812a/
- Lead breeder or scientist names for LG 93.01: No evidence found. A ZoomInfo directory lists former rice breeders at Bisco Bio Sciences (Manender Singh, 2017-2021; Sharat Sonnad, 2012-2018). These are company staff entries that do not name LG 93.01, so they are not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.zoominfo.com/pic/bisco-bio-sciences-pvt-ltd/425341091
- Developing ICAR or SAU station: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level (company, not verified for this variety): headquarters given as C-39 Bharani Complex Minister Rd, Kingsway, Telangana, 500003, India. Source is a third-party directory. -- https://www.zoominfo.com/pic/bisco-bio-sciences-pvt-ltd/425341091
- Company website given as biscobiosciences.com (third-party profile, not checked). -- https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/bisco-bio-sciences
- Other location references: Hyderabad (Crunchbase, LinkedIn); Secunderabad, Telangana (TradeIndia). These conflict slightly and are unverified. -- https://www.tradeindia.com/bisco-bio-sciences-pvt-ltd-16879686/
- Official email, phone and breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Seednet portal entry: not retrieved in these searches. No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. None of the research-type results named LG 93.01 or BLR-102 / IET 24949. The results were about IR 58025A/B parent-line studies and other hybrids, which I have not attributed to this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Results were general Uttar Pradesh paddy seed listings (for example, IndiaMART, ExportersIndia, TradeIndia) and state seed-distribution reports, none naming LG 93.01. None is attributed to this variety. -- https://www.exportersindia.com/uttar-pradesh/paddy-seed.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttar Pradesh. The notification list gives LG 93.01 (BLR-102) (IET 24949), Hybrid, 2019, S.O. 3220(E) dated 05.09.2019, Uttar Pradesh. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/

NOTES ON THE SEARCH
- Four web searches were run. The name in the notification list (LG 93.01 (BLR-102) (IET 24949)) matches the Seednet name, and the CSC name is "LG 93.01" in the record. The notification and AICRIP evidence match the full name or codes; no other name was found.
- Not yet checked: the Seednet portal directly, KrishiKosh, AICRIP annual reports for trial data, and the CSC release minutes. These should be the next checks.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: US 305 (IET 21827), Rice

Name note: "US 305" (CSC minutes name) and "US 305 (IET 21827)" (Seednet name) both appear in the same listings below. The evidence refers to the same hybrid rice product under both names.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for US 305. The only trait-level claim is a general "good standability" statement on the company's product page (see AGRONOMY AND TRIALS).

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no blast, sheath blight, BPH or other resistance data for US 305.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Company product page lists US 305 as maturing in 130-135 days, with fine grain, good standability and high yield (company claims, not trial data) -- https://www.seedworks.com/product/us-305
- ICAR Annual Report 2014-15 (crop improvement section) lists US 305 (IET 21827) among released rice hybrids, with recommended region Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, and salient features of medium slender grains and 50% flowering in about 100 days (text truncated in the source) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2014-15.pdf
- Hybrid rice release table gives duration and yield as "NA" for US 305 -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- No multi-location trial or AICRP yield data found for US 305.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line code IET 21827 is given as the variety code in the release table -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Parentage F 3274-4 / M 4582 R: No evidence found. No source names the parents of US 305 or the breeding method. As a hybrid, the cross is presumably female/male lines, but no page confirms this, so it is not recorded as fact.
- No QTL, marker or genome study naming US 305 was found. The QTL papers returned (e.g., Pi68(t), grain-shape loci, milling QTL) concern other varieties or germplasm and are excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing and supplying institution: Seed Works International Pvt. Ltd. (listed as "Seed Works International Pvt. Ltd., Hyderabad-34" in the release table; company now styled SeedWorks International Ltd.) -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://www.seedworks.com/product/us-305
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. No breeder name is attached to US 305 in any retrieved source.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institution (company registered/works address from the SeedWorks product page): SeedWorks International Ltd. (formerly SeedWorks International Private Limited), Survey No. 530/A, Gowdavally Village, Medchal Mandal, Telangana - 501 403 -- https://www.seedworks.com/product/us-305
- Malkajgiri/Hyderabad address from an IndiaMART listing: Seed Works International Limited, Malkajgiri, Hyderabad, Telangana (no street address or phone given in the excerpt) -- https://www.indiamart.com/ms-seed-works-international-pvt-ltd/paddy-seeds.html
- Official email, phone and breeder contact: No evidence found. The SeedWorks page shows a "Contact us" heading without details in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report entry beyond the release table, thesis (KrishiKosh) or conference paper naming US 305 was returned. The ICAR 2014-15 report is a release listing, not a research paper; it is recorded under AGRONOMY AND TRIALS.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seed Works International sells US305 Hybrid Rice Seed (product listing; no price or stock detail in the excerpt) -- https://www.indiamart.com/ms-seed-works-international-pvt-ltd/other-products.html
- Company product page for US 305 under the Hybrid Rice range -- https://www.seedworks.com/product/us-305
- Generic paddy-seed dealers in Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra were found, but none names US 305, so they are excluded.
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU listing for US 305 was found.
- Seednet portal page for "US 305 (IET 21827)" was not retrieved by the searches; only third-party copies of the release list were found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- ICAR AR 2014-15 lists only Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu for US 305 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2014-15.pdf
- Year of release: the release table gives 2013 (the CSC minutes field was "Unknown") -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm

basic_info.institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), Oil Seeds Research Station, Tindivanam

drought.details: No drought tolerance evidence found. Rainfed and irrigated yields are reported (rainfed 850 kg/ha or 750 kg/ha depending on source; irrigated 920 kg/ha or 820 kg/ha), but no drought or water-deficit trial result was found in the searched sources.

heat.details: No heat tolerance evidence found in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance evidence found in the searched sources.

flood.details: No flood or waterlogging tolerance evidence found. No waterlogging trial result was found.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to root rot (disease not otherwise specified). Evidence: the TNAU-authored paper describes the culture as tolerant to root rot; root rot tolerance is listed among special features in a table of TNAU-released sesame varieties. A popular farm article describes it as resistant to root rot, but this is a farmer-level claim and not a trial result. No other disease resistance evidence was found. Trial-based confirmation was not found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No pest resistance evidence was found for TMV (Sv) 7. A 2015 TNAU highlights report used TMV 7 as a check for a shoot-webber-resistant entry; this does not indicate resistance in TMV 7 itself.

agronomic_details.yield: Yield figures differ by source. (1) AICRP-linked TNAU agritech page: 850 kg/ha rainfed, 920 kg/ha irrigated. (2) TNAU ORS Tindivanam table: 750 kg/ha rainfed, 820 kg/ha irrigated. (3) Intechopen table: 750 kg/ha rainfed, 820 kg/ha irrigated. (4) AICRP table: 800-900 kg/ha. Farmer-level anecdotal report: 390 kg/acre, about 33% above a traditional variety (not a controlled trial).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources, except the multi-location check: a 2015 TNAU report says a white-seeded entry gave 11.7% higher seed yield than TMV 7 in MLT, so TMV 7 was the comparison check and no stability statistic for TMV 7 itself was reported. The paper title describes it as a high-yielding cosmopolitan variety, but no supporting stability data was found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Tamil Nadu; season suitability listed across Tamil Nadu zones: anipattam, adipattam, masipattam, margazhipattam, purattasipattam, karthigaipattam, thaippattam, chithiraipattam. No agro-ecological or soil adaptation data found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 80-85 days (AICRP table and TNAU agritech page); 85 days (TNAU ORS table); 85-90 days (Intechopen table)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Branching habit; erect indeterminate growth habit (TNAU agritech page). Oil content: 50% (TNAU agritech page); 51% (TNAU ORS table); 50% (Intechopen table); 48-50% (AICRP table). A Journal of African Biotechnology entry lists TMV 7 with brown seed as a sesamin/sesamol accession; the breeding paper also describes a brown-seeded type isolated from segregating populations.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location trial (2015 TNAU report, 81st SWC): a white-seeded entry gave 11.7% higher seed yield than TMV 7; TMV 7 was the check. (2) Seed pelleting trial (2015 TNAU report): neem leaf powder, CMC, Azospirillum and phosphobacteria applied to TMV 7 seed improved seed yield and quality; numerical values not found in the digest. (3) Farmer demonstration via Primary Demonstration Field Project at Sirugamani Agricultural Science Centre: one grower reported 390 kg/acre, about 33% above a traditional variety (anecdotal, not a controlled trial). (4) ORS Tindivanam crop improvement records: breeder seed production target 0.60 ha and achievement 0.22 t/ha in 2018-19; this is a seed production record, not a yield trial.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I'll start with the first two searches, which are independent of each other.EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name scope: The record is for TMV (Sv) 7 sesame, released by Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) in 2009. The variety_code "Sv)7" appears to be a typo for "(Sv) 7". "variety_name" is "TMV"; the Seednet name is unknown and was not searched separately. Every source below names TMV (Sv) 7 or TMV 7 in sesame. Groundnut TMV entries, VRI and other sesame lines were excluded.

Search note: I used the 4-search limit. Searches 1 and 2 covered release and breeder topics. Searches 3 and 4 were run as breeder and release queries again, not as dedicated research-paper or seed-availability searches. No Seednet query was run, so Seednet evidence and seed-portal records remain unchecked.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerant to root rot disease; the TNAU-authored paper describes the culture as tolerant to root rot -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335174535_Research_Article_TMV_Sv_7_-A_high_yielding_cosmopolitan_sesame_variety
Root rot tolerance is also listed among its special features in a table of TNAU-released sesame varieties -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74180
Popular farm article describes it as resistant to root rot (farmer-level claim, not a trial result) -- https://sitemaps.pachaiboomi.com/tmv-7-sesame/
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. Rainfed and irrigated yields are reported, but no drought or waterlogging trial result was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
Root rot tolerance is the only disease trait found (see above). No pest resistance evidence found. A 2015 TNAU highlights report used TMV 7 as a check for a shoot-webber-resistant entry, which says nothing about resistance in TMV 7 itself -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/3.-81st-SWC-Research-Highlights-2015.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Season-wise recommendations and yield figures (rainfed 850 kg/ha, irrigated 920 kg/ha, 80-85 days, 50% oil, branching habit, erect indeterminate) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20tmv%207.html
Yields given elsewhere differ: 750 rainfed / 820 irrigated, 85 days, 51% oil (TNAU ORS table) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/ ; 750 / 820, 85-90 days, 50% oil (intechopen table) -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74180 ; 800-900 kg/ha, 48-50% oil, 80-85 days (AICRP table) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
Multi-location check: a 2015 TNAU report says a white-seeded entry gave 11.7% higher seed yield than TMV 7 in MLT -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/3.-81st-SWC-Research-Highlights-2015.pdf
Seed pelleting trial (neem leaf powder, CMC, Azospirillum, phosphobacteria) on TMV 7 seed improved seed yield and quality -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/3.-81st-SWC-Research-Highlights-2015.pdf
Farmer demonstration: one grower reported 390 kg/acre, about 33% above a traditional variety, via a Primary Demonstration Field Project at Sirugamani Agricultural Science Centre (anecdotal) -- https://sitemaps.pachaiboomi.com/tmv-7-sesame/
Seasons listed for TMV 7 in Tamil Nadu zones (anipattam, adipattam, masipattam, margazhipattam, purattasipattam, karthigaipattam, thaippattam, chithiraipattam) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/agri_seasonandvarieties_gingelly.html
Oilseeds Research Station Tindivanam target and achievement tables for TMV (Sv) 7 (breeder seed 0.60 ha target, 0.22 t/ha achieved, 2018-19) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/crop-improvement/

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: Si 250 x ES 22 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335174535_Research_Article_TMV_Sv_7_-A_high_yielding_cosmopolitan_sesame_variety ; https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
Breeding line code: TVS 0039 (developed culture later released as TMV (Sv) 7) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335174535_Research_Article_TMV_Sv_7_-A_high_yielding_cosmopolitan_sesame_variety
Breeding method: hybridization followed by pedigree selection; a brown-seeded type was isolated from segregating populations and tested for yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335174535_Research_Article_TMV_Sv_7_-A_high_yielding_cosmopolitan_sesame_variety
Genes, QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Paper authors (oilseeds station, TNAU, Tindivanam): V. Manoharan, M. Vaithiyalingan, M. Sudha, G. Rangaraju, R. Vishnupriya, P. Renugadevi, S. Jebaraj -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335174535_Research_Article_TMV_Sv_7_-A_high_yielding_cosmopolitan_sesame_variety
Note: the sources name these as authors of the TMV (Sv) 7 paper, not as formally recorded breeders of record. Institution: TNAU, Oil Seeds Research Station, Tindivanam -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
Released by TNAU in 2009 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/

CONTACT DETAILS
Named breeder contacts: No evidence found. The search results contain no email, phone or personal contact for the breeders listed above.
Institute-level: Oil Seeds Research Station, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Tindivanam 604 002 (postal address from the paper) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335174535_Research_Article_TMV_Sv_7_-A_high_yielding_cosmopolitan_sesame_variety
Institute page URL: https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/ (station "Varieties Released" and "Crop Improvement" pages; no phone or email found in results)
Official email and phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Manoharan, V.; Vaithiyalingan, M.; Sudha, M.; Rangaraju, G.; Vishnupriya, R.; Renugadevi, P.; Jebaraj, S. (year not stated). TMV (Sv) 7 -- A high yielding cosmopolitan sesame variety. Journal not stated -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335174535_Research_Article_TMV_Sv_7_-A_high_yielding_cosmopolitan_sesame_variety
Authors not shown in results (year not stated). Genetic Potential and Possible Improvement of Sesamum indicum L. (book chapter, TNAU variety table) -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74180
Authors not shown in results (2017). Journal of African Biotechnology, Vol. 16(23), pp. 1308-1313 -- DOI 10.5897/AJB2016.15688 (lists TMV 7, Si 250 x ES 22, Tindivanam, brown seed as a sesamin/sesamol accession; article title not in results) -- https://journal-backups.lon1.digitaloceanspaces.com/uploads/main/article/5629fc164640.pdf
TNAU Research Highlights 2015, 81st SWC (crop improvement section; authors not stated) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/3.-81st-SWC-Research-Highlights-2015.pdf
AICRP Sesame, Major Achievements (2020 DUS compendium referenced; authors not stated) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/

SEED AVAILABILITY
Breeder seed production at the TNAU Oilseeds Research Station, Tindivanam (2018-19 target and achievement) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/crop-improvement/
A farmer reported seed supplied via Sirugamani Agricultural Science Centre demonstration project; farmer also shares seed with neighbours (anecdotal) -- https://sitemaps.pachaiboomi.com/tmv-7-sesame/
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK listings, SAU seed sales and private dealer listings: No evidence found (not searched directly; Seednet not searched).

RECOMMENDED STATES
Tamil Nadu only. Listed as a Tamil Nadu variety in AICRP and Vikaspedia tables -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/ ; https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/sesame-1?lgn=en
Zone-level season suitability within Tamil Nadu -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/agri_seasonandvarieties_gingelly.html

Open gaps: release notification date and CSC minutes not found (year of release 2009 per TNAU sources); Seednet name not searched; no peer-reviewed trial paper on stress tolerance

Evidence: the TNAU-authored paper describes the culture as tolerant to root rot; root rot tolerance is listed among special features in a table of TNAU-released sesame varieties. A popular farm article describes it as resistant to root rot, but this is a farmer-level claim and not a trial result. No other disease resistance evidence was found. Trial-based confirmation was not found.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: ICAR-AICRP on Sorghum RVSKVV, College of Agriculture, Indore (Madhya Pradesh)
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Telangana, Gujarat, Punjab and Uttarakhand
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: At all the level, SPV 2714 produced (54.99 t/ha) total fresh bioimass yield which was 12.66% higher than the check CSH 22SS (48.79 t/ha) at 100% RDF. SPV 2714 produced similar total dry biomass (19.72t/ha) as the check CSH 22SS (19.91%).
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Tall, drooping leaves, semi-loose panicle. It has greyed white seed.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Tolerant
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: SPV 2714 was 28% superior to the check CSH 22SS for anthracnose resistance. For Leaf blight and grain mold SPV 2714 was at par with check.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: SPV 2714 was 5.4% superior for lower shoot fly dead heart formation against the check CSH 22SS. For stemborer tolerance it was at par to check 22SS.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha):
32 kg Nitrogen and 16 kg P2O5 per acre.
Apply half Nitrogen + full P2O5 at sowing and remaining Nitrogen at 30 (Days After Sowing) DAS.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CSV54HB (SPV 2714), Sorghum

Name note: the release-minute name is CSV54HB and the Seednet name is CSV54HB (SPV 2714). The evidence below uses "CSV 54HB" and "SPV 2714" interchangeably, and each line says which name appears. Search limit: the four-search cap was reached, so the second search batch failed and no further searches were run. Parentage is taken from the task input only; no source found confirms it.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) for CSV54HB or SPV 2714.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- SPV 2714 was promoted to AVHT-I (advanced variety trial) in the initial-cum-advanced high biomass trial for lignocellulosic biofuel traits, per the 2020 AICRP sweet and high-biomass sorghum presentation -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip19/Sorghum/presentations19/06Sweet-sorghumAGM2020.pdf
- In the AICRP sweet sorghum report, SPV 2714 is described as a sweet sorghum entry with cellulose content of 30.6%, a 14% superiority over the check CSH 22SS (26.9%). This is a trial entry, not a release-level claim -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/kh/4-Sweet-Sorghum-Report-agm22.pdf
- The same report gives a grain yield range of 801 to 1218 across entries; it does not give a yield value for SPV 2714 specifically in the text I retrieved.
- Fodder, fresh and dry biomass yield values for SPV 2714 were not visible in the retrieved text beyond the qualitative "high total fresh and dry biomass yields" statement -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/1-Millets-genetic-resources-management-agm23.pdf
- Maturity: No evidence found for CSV54HB or SPV 2714. The "113 days" maturity figure in the search results belongs to a different sweet sorghum variety and was discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage (from task input only, not verified by a search result): SPV 2714 = (112 x CSV23) x E 214) 41-6-2-2-2; I 12 = (SSV 53 x SPV 475)7-1-1-1-1; CSV 23 = (SPV 53 x 861 x SU 248); E 214 = IC 0568475 (land race).
- Breeding-line code SPV 2714 is confirmed in the AICRP sources listed above.
- No evidence found for QTL, marker, or genome-resource studies on this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The name SPV 2714 is listed among AICRP sorghum entries and releases in the AICRP on Sorghum and Small Millets 2022 proceedings, which describe it as a high-biomass kharif sorghum variety -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/AGM2022-AICRP_on_Sorghum_and_Small_millets-Proceedings.pdf
- No breeder name is tied to CSV54HB or SPV 2714 in any retrieved page. The "Dr B.R. Ranwah" breeder entry in the AT-A-GLANCE document is for a different sweet sorghum variety, so it was discarded. Likewise, the pedigree database page naming ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (former Directorate of Sorghum Research) does not mention CSV54HB, so it is not attributed to this variety.
- Developing institution, as stated in the task input: ICAR-AICRP on Sorghum, RVSKVV, College of Agriculture. No source confirmed this for the variety itself.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute-level contact, email, phone, or address for CSV54HB or SPV 2714 was retrieved. The only contact-like text was for a different variety and was discarded.

PUBLICATIONS
- Elangovan, M. and Venkatesh, K. (2023 AGM report; author line partly visible, verify before use). Millet genetic resources management, AICRP on Sorghum annual group meeting report. Contains "CSV 54HB is released for All India cultivation - Telangana, Gujarat, Punjab and Uttarakhand" and "SPV 2714 is a high biomass Sorghum variety" -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/1-Millets-genetic-resources-management-agm23.pdf
- AICRP on Sorghum and Small Millets (2022). Proceedings, 28-29 April, AGM 2022. Lists SPV 2714 as a high-biomass kharif sorghum entry -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/AGM2022-AICRP_on_Sorghum_and_Small_millets-Proceedings.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- CSV 24SS has resistance to shoot fly and stem borer, per a sweet sorghum review that cites a secondary source; I could not verify this in a primary DSR document -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5465577/
- One release-history table describes CSV 24SS as relatively tolerant to several stress factors. The sentence is fragmentary and may refer to the PPV&FRA registration entry rather than the variety's field performance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found for CSV 24SS. The searches returned only generic drought or stress rating descriptions for unrelated USPTO sorghum varieties (for example, GSV958220, GSV616359), which I discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Shoot fly and stem borer resistance: see the STRESS TOLERANCE line above, which is the only source for this claim -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5465577/
- Grain mold, charcoal rot, midge, and other disease or pest resistance: No evidence found for CSV 24SS specifically.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration and plant type: the DSR technology sheet describes the variety as tall, medium duration variety, and its performance table lists Maturity: 120 days with green cane yield of 391 q/ha and juice yield of 14833 l/ha -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/SORGHUM_VARIETAL_Technology_AT_A_GLANCE.pdf
- Yield range: a DSR review gives productivity of 40−50 t ha^-1 -- https://oar.icrisat.org/7491/7/Sweet-sorghum_sugar_tech.pdf
- Check-variety comparisons: in 2016 kharif trials, NPK 2016-2 recorded the highest biomass yield of 73 t/ha against the check CSV 24SS (51 t/ha) -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip16/reports16/AICRP_Coordinating_Team.pdf
- In 2017, (SSV F7-2)-1-3 recorded the highest fresh biomass yield of 89 t/ha and was 29% superior to the check CSV 24SS (69 t/ha) -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip17/reports/kh/3-Kharif_breeding.pdf
- Brix: 16.5% and 17.5% for CSV-24-SS and CSV-19-SS respectively (2014 report; the sentence does not state the trait explicitly, so treat as brix) -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip14/report/pc-report-agm15.pdf
- Early-flowering comparison: in 2014, SPV 2321, SPV 2270, SPV 2319 and SPV 2323 were earliest to flower among the test varieties and were significantly early (7-10%) compared to the check CSV 24SS -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip14/report/pc-report-agm15.pdf
- Trial repeat: the variety was used as a national check in 2018 sweet sorghum trials -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/reports18/rb/AICRP-Sorghum-Coordinating-Team.pdf
- Seed-grade CSV 24SS data is in the 2011 pedigree-style table; no separate yield trial for release beyond these entries was found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: CSV 24 SS (SPSSV 6) 2010 NSS 1005A × (SSV 84 ×401B) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
- Conflict: the 2011 DSR training manual lists the female-side parent as NSS 1005B, not NSS 1005A -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives
- Parent identity: the parent SSV 84 is described as the sweet sorghum variety developed using SSV 84 as one of the parent -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
- Breeding method: several improved varieties have been released by IIMR and other AICRP centers using pedigree method. These include SSV 74, SSV 84, CSV 19SS, and CSV 24SS -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5465577/
- Breeding-line codes: No evidence found for CSV 24SS in the pedigree tables.
- QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: the DSR technology sheet names the source as

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Search status: the four web_search calls were run in one batch, and the next attempt to open the full page text hit the tool-use limit. I only have the short snippets from that first batch, so most headings below have no verified evidence. Nothing was attributed beyond what the snippets name.

VARIETY NAME CHECK: "variety_name" is Jaicar Heera. The seednet name is "Jaicar Heera (CSV 36/ SPV 2301)". The AICRP report snippet below uses the name with the CSV 36/SPV 2301 code, so it refers to this variety under the seednet name. The Millets annual report snippet uses "Jaicar Heera" alone.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Search 1 returned no snippet on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. Search 1 returned no snippet on grain mold, anthracnose, downy mildew, shoot fly, stem borer or other resistance for this variety. The parentage text in the input says the NSV 13 parent was selected as grain mold tolerant, but that is an input claim, not a search finding.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found in the retrieved snippets. The Millets Annual Report 2018-19 snippet lists Jaicar Heera among three high-yielding grain sorghum varieties from ICAR-IIMR, but it gives no yield, maturity or trial data. -- https://www.millets.res.in/annual_report/ar18-19.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): The only code evidence is the breeding-line code CSV 36/SPV 2301 in the AICRP report snippet. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/reports18/rb/AICRP-Sorghum-Coordinating-Team.pdf. Parentage (SPV 1231 x NSV 13 and the SPV 1231, RS 29, SC 108 and SPV 126 pedigree) comes only from the input and was not confirmed by any search result. No QTL or marker evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The institution is supported by the Millets annual report, which is ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (https://www.millets.res.in/annual_report/ar18-19.pdf). The AICRP Sorghum report lists Jaicar Heera (CSV 36/SPV 2301) among sorghum varieties (https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/reports18/rb/AICRP-Sorghum-Coordinating-Team.pdf). No breeder name was found in any retrieved snippet.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found for a breeder email, phone or postal address. Institute-level contact details were not retrieved. The ICAR-IIMR site appears to be millets.res.in, based on the two URLs above. That domain is not confirmed as a contact page.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Annual report: ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (2019). MILLETS Annual Report 2018-19. ICAR-IIMR Annual Report -- https://www.millets.res.in/annual_report/ar18-19.pdf
- AICRP on Sorghum Coordinating Team (2018). Report of the AICRP on Sorghum Coordinating Team 2018. AICRP Sorghum Report -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/reports18/rb/AICRP-Sorghum-Coordinating-Team.pdf
- Peer-reviewed or thesis items: No evidence found. Its text was not retrieved, so I have not confirmed that it mentions Jaicar Heera and did not list it.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found from an official source (NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or ICAR seed sales). The only seed result, https://www.ekirana.nl/heera-juwari-sorghum-whole.html, is a retail product named "Heera Juwar" and is not this variety, so it was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found in the search results. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jaicar Sona (CSV 39 / SPV 2358), Sorghum

Name note: The CSC release minutes name is "Jaicar Sona" and the Seednet name is "Jaicar Sona (CSV 39/ SPV 2358)". The search results use "Jaicar Sona", "CSV 39", "SPV 2358" and "CSV 39/SPV 2358" interchangeably. I treated these as the same entry only where the page names the variety and crop. My searches did not return a seednet.gov.in page, so the Seednet entry itself is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The searches returned general sorghum pages only.

DISEASE AND PEST
An AICRP-Sorghum centre report lists SPV 2358 among entries with shoot fly and stem borer resistance targets, and among entries rated moderately resistant to sugary/ergot disease, though the pages do not say whether these ratings are final or pre-release. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip17/presentations/Centre_Presentations/9Surat.pdf
A Surat centre presentation (2016) gives SPV-2358 as an entry under anthracnose and ergot evaluation, with no explicit resistance grade in the extracted text. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip15/presentations/Day1/12Surat-.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The IIMR Annual Report 2018-19 gives Jaicar Sona grain yield as 34 q/ha, fodder yield as 115 q/ha and maturity as 102-110 days, but the table layout is ambiguous and the figures may belong to a neighbouring column. -- https://www.millets.res.in/annual_report/ar18-19.pdf
A 2017-18 AICRP kharif report records SPV 2358 at 3,362 kg/ha grain yield, more than 10% above the check CSV 20 in the trial. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip17/reports/kh/3-Kharif_breeding.pdf
A 2017-18 AICRP breeding presentation states that SPV 2358 showed more than 10% grain yield advantage over CSV 20 in AVT Zone I, and more than 20% over three years in Zone I. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip17/presentations/3_Kharif_breeding.pdf
The same presentation reports SPV 2358 as promising in Zone II over three years, with 6-7% grain yield advantage. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip17/presentations/3_Kharif_breeding.pdf
A Kerala evaluation of 20 grain sorghum varieties includes CSV 39 (SPV 772 × SPV 1754, kharif) among the entries. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/15/10/2320

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage is recorded as SPV 772 × SPV 1754 (kharif variety). -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/15/10/2320
The 50-year AICRP review lists CSV 39 (JAICAR SONA; SPV 2358), released in 2017, with parentage SPV 772 × SPV 1754 and developed by IIMR-Hyderabad. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
Note: the 2017 release year in this review conflicts with the 2019 release year in the request. The IIMR 2018-19 report says the variety was identified and then released in that period. -- https://www.millets.res.in/annual_report/ar18-19.pdf
SPV 2358 was used as an elite parent for improving popular cultivars, and an F1 cross of CSV 39 × Gundari is listed as dual/grain type. The page does not say which trait was targeted. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/reports18/rb/AICRP-Sorghum-Coordinating-Team.pdf
Another report lists a CSV-39 × SR-3019 cross as a restorer-line/donor programme cross with high yield as its target trait. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/3-Sorghum-Kharif-Grain-Breeding-Report-agm23.pdf
Breeding method, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (IIMR), Hyderabad. -- https://www.millets.res.in/annual_report/ar18-19.pdf
Station or division below IIMR: No evidence found.
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The pages name the AICRP sorghum team and authors of general reports, but none ties a named scientist to CSV 39 or SPV 2358. I have not assigned any named scientist to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No IIMR contact page URL, email, phone or postal address appeared in the results, and I did not fetch any institute site. Institution name only: ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research, Hyderabad (see BREEDER AND INSTITUTION).

PUBLICATIONS

Fifty years of research and development under All-India Coordinated Research Project on Sorghum. Golden Jubilee Publication, IIMR Hyderabad -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
Anija Hari Kumar, S., Chacko Thomas, U., Al-Salman, Y., Cano, F. J., Stephen, R., Pillai, P. S., & Ghannoum, O. (2025). Evaluation of Yield-Related Morphological, Physiological, Agronomic, and Nutrient Uptake Traits of Grain Sorghum Varieties in the Kerala Region (India). Agronomy -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/15/10/2320

AICRP on Sorghum (2017). Kharif grain sorghum trial report (SPV 2358 entries). AICRP Sorghum, Hyderabad -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip17/reports/kh/3-Kharif_breeding.pdf
Note: No DOI or journal page was found for any of these items.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Breeder seed production of CSV 39 at IIMR Hyderabad is recorded at 5.79 q in the seed production table. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/kh/9-Sorghum-NSP-BSP-MSP-DUS-IPR-PPV%20&%20FRA%20Report-agm22.pdf
Allocations for CSV 39/Jaicar Sona appear under NSAI and NDDB in the seed distribution table. The abbreviations are not expanded on the page. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/kh/9-Sorghum-NSP-BSP-MSP-DUS-IPR-PPV%20&%20FRA%20Report-agm22.pdf
Seed dealers and KVK or SAU seed sales: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
The 50-year review lists Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Telangana for CSV 39. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
The state list in the request (Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat) does not match. Andhra Pradesh does not appear in this source, and Maharashtra, Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh do. Both sources should be checked against the official notification.
The IIMR 2018-19 report gives the same recommended-state list for Jaicar Sona. -- https://www.millets.res.in/annual_report/ar18-19.pdf
Registration: Jaicar Sona (CSV 39/SPV 2358) appears in the PPV&FRA compendium of registered varieties. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compediumforallcategoryuptonov-2021.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY: Kinnerea (MJ-278), Sorghum
NAME NOTE: Evidence refers to "Kinnera (MJ 278)" and "Kinnerea (MJ-278)". The Seednet name was not searched directly. No result came from seednet.gov.in, so all evidence comes from AICSIP/ICAR and ANGRAU documents.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The four searches returned no stress-tolerance data for Kinnerea. The one page that described a sorghum variety as tolerant to foliar diseases, shoot fly and stem borer did not name Kinnerea, so I excluded it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308081683_Sorghum (searched, not used)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page named Kinnerea with disease or pest reaction data. -- (searched, no relevant page)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Kinnerea (MJ-278) appears in a 42nd Annual Sorghum Group Meeting (Pantnagar, 2012) table of ANGRAU, Madhira entries, where it is listed under Andhra Pradesh with a figure of 2.00 beside it. The table layout does not explain that figure, so I am not interpreting it. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip11/reports/kh/aicsip_proceedings_28-30_april12_pantnagar.pdf
No yield, maturity or fertilizer-response data for Kinnerea were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage "Moti x D 71258" (from the input record): No evidence found. No retrieved page stated this parentage.
Breeding-line code: The code MJ-278 is the only identifier found. It is listed in the AICSIP pedigree database of elite breeding stock (2006–2011), which records Kinnera (MJ 278) as a central and state release. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
Breeding method, QTL and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ANGRAU, Madhira is the institution listed against Kinnerea in the AICSIP nucleus/breeder-seed report. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip14/report/kh/9Nucleus-BSP-DUS-agm15.pdf
Breeder name: No breeder name was found for Kinnerea. The 2012 Pantnagar listing gives a "Sorghum Breeder" entry at Palem beside the Kinnerea row, but it names no person. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip11/reports/kh/aicsip_proceedings_28-30_april12_pantnagar.pdf
Excluded: a breeder name (Dr RB Ghorade, PDKV Akola) appears near a Kinnerea row in the 2015 report, but the layout does not clearly link it to this variety, so I did not attribute it.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for a breeder or an institute contact page specific to Kinnerea. The Directorate of Sorghum Research contact details (Dr AV Umakanth, umakanth@sorghum.res.in, office 091-40-24018651, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500030) were found, but they appear on a technology sheet for CSV 23 and CSV 29R, not Kinnerea, so I excluded them under the relevance rule. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/SORGHUM_VARIETAL_Technology_AT_A_GLANCE.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not stated in retrieved text (2006–2011 pedigree database). Pedigree database on Sorghum Elite Breeding Stock (AICSIP: 2006–2011). AICSIP/DSR report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
Authors not stated in retrieved text (2012). 42nd Annual Sorghum Group Meeting, Pantnagar, 28–30 April 2012. AICSIP proceedings -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip11/reports/kh/aicsip_proceedings_28-30_april12_pantnagar.pdf
Authors not stated in retrieved text (2015). Nucleus, Breeder Seed Production and DUS report, AGM 2015. AICSIP report -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip14/report/kh/9Nucleus-BSP-DUS-agm15.pdf
Authors not stated in retrieved text (2011–12). Sorghum nucleus, breeder seed production, IPR and DUS report. AICSIP report -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip11/reports/kh/9nucleus-BSP_IPR_DUS.pdf
No peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh) or QTL studies on Kinnerea were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Kinnerea (MJ-278) is listed in the 2011–12 AICSIP seed-production table for Andhra Pradesh, and the report says breeder, foundation and certified seed are produced in farmers' fields in Andhra Pradesh. The table does not give a seed-source contact. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip11/reports/kh/9nucleus-BSP_IPR_DUS.pdf
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing for Kinnerea was found. The seed-seller results were for unrelated US and retail products.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Andhra Pradesh. This is the only state linked to Kinnerea in the retrieved records. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip11/reports/kh/aicsip_proceedings_28-30_april12_pantnagar.pdf

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION
Notification S.O. 211(E), dated 29.01.2010, lists Kinnera (MJ 278) as a central and state release. The input record gives 2009 as the year of release. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip14/report/kh/9Nucleus-BSP-DUS-agm15.pdf

NOTES
1. The release year in the input (2009) differs from the notification date in the retrieved records (29.01.2010).
2. The parentage and breeder fields in the input are unverified. Searches did not confirm them.
3. Seednet was not searched directly. A check of seednet.gov.in for "Kinnerea (MJ-278)" is still needed.

pest_resistance.summary: Shoot fly: described as tolerant. Stem borer: described as tolerant. No quantitative pest scores were found. Original variety data also records tolerance to shoot fly and stem borer.

Original variety data: grain 2343 kg/ha (yield trial 1) and 2288 kg/ha (MLT); fodder 5845 kg/ha (yield trial 1) and 5823 kg/ha (MLT). The original data does not give a source URL.
agronomic_details.stability: Not stated in the digest. On-farm trials were conducted across several Telangana districts (kharif 2015-2018). Multi-location minikit testing ran for 3 years. Original data shows similar grain yields in yield trial 1 and MLT (2343 vs 2288 kg/ha).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Telangana; suitable for both kharif and rabi (yasangi) seasons; RARS Palem is in Nagarkurnool district (Southern Telangana Zone).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Original variety data: plants do not lodge even at a height of 2.8-3.0 m during high rainfall. Dual-purpose (grain and fodder). Yellow-pericarp grain with high protein and good roti quality (NBPGR passport). Other morphological characteristics: Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) On-farm trials under NICRA by RARS Palem, PJTSAU, kharif 2015-2018, across several Telangana districts: mean grain yield 1930.9 (units not stated). (2) On-farm study reporting PYPS-2 outperformed local yellow varieties. (3) AICSIP Kharif 2022 grain trial used 'Palem Pacha Jonna' as the yellow check: check mean grain yield 2382.4 kg/ha, with one entry 4% higher; the link to PYPS-2 rests on the digest's naming. (4) AICSIP centre report: PYPS-2 was a leading farmer variety at Palem, with variety-area share of about 25% in one year. (5) A productivity figure of 1125 kg/ha is listed for the Palem region; context unclear. (6) Original variety data: yield trial 1 grain 2343 kg/ha, fodder 5845 kg/ha; MLT grain 2288 kg/ha, fodder 5823 kg/ha.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PalemPacha Jonna 1 / Palem Pacha Jonna 1 (PYPS-2), Sorghum: EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search budget: 4 web_search calls used (the maximum). No CSC release minutes were retrieved, so "PalemPacha Jonna 1" (CSC name) has no direct evidence. All findings below refer to Palem Pacha Jonna 1 (PYPS-2), the Seednet name, unless stated otherwise.

Name and release conflicts:
- Release year: the user's input says 2020. The PJTSAU Director of Research table lists "Palem Pacha Jonna-1 (PYPS-2)" as released in 2019 by SVRC, with no CVRC entry. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/
- Parentage: the YPS-19 x YPS-72 cross is not confirmed by any retrieved source.
- Excluded: Telangana Jonna 1 / CSV 41 (SPV 2437, released 2020 for Zone I), Palem Jonna 1 (PSV 512, 2021), CSH hybrids, Tandur Jonna-1, and generic "Pacha Jonnalu" retail listings. These refer to other varieties or products, so they were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Findings refer to PYPS-2.
- Described as tolerant to grain mold, shoot fly and stem borer. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/siddipet-conducted-group-discussion-cum-field-day/
- Described in an on-farm study as an improved drought-tolerant sorghum that outperformed local yellow varieties. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372367164_Assessment_of_Yellow_Sorghum_Palem_Pacha_Jonna-1_PYPS_2_Performance_through_on_Farm_Testing_in_Telangana
- Breeding objectives at RARS Palem included dual-purpose sorghum with grain mold tolerance; PYPS-2 was listed as "dual purpose, GM tolerance." -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip17/presentations/Centre_Presentations/6Palem.pdf ; https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip18/presentations/Centre_Presentations/5Palem.pdf
- No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Findings refer to PYPS-2.
- Reported as tolerant to pests and diseases, with 12.02% protein. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety
- Tolerance to grain mold, shoot fly and stem borer (same source as above). -- https://pjtau.edu.in/siddipet-conducted-group-discussion-cum-field-day/
- No pathogen-specific resistance scores (e.g., grain mold rating scale, Striga, anthracnose) found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Dual-purpose; suitable for both kharif and rabi (yasangi) seasons; duration about 95-105 days; fodder about 50-55 q/acre and grain about 12-15 q/acre under farmer fields. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/siddipet-conducted-group-discussion-cum-field-day/
- On-farm trials under NICRA by RARS Palem, PJTSAU, kharif 2015-2018, across several Telangana districts. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety
- On-farm mean grain yield of 1930.9 reported (units not stated in the retrieved text). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372367164_Assessment_of_Yellow_Sorghum_Palem_Pacha_Jonna-1_PYPS_2_Performance_through_on_Farm_Testing_in_Telangana
- AICSIP Kharif 2022 grain trial used "Palem Pacha Jonna" as the yellow check; check mean grain yield 2382.4 kg/ha, with one entry 4% higher. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/3-Sorghum-Kharif-Grain-Breeding-Report-agm23.pdf
- AICSIP centre report: PYPS-2 was a leading farmer variety at Palem, with variety-area shares of about 25% in one year. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip17/presentations/Centre_Presentations/6Palem.pdf
- Productivity figure of 1125 kg/ha listed for the Palem region. Context unclear. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip18/presentations/Centre_Presentations/5Palem.pdf
- Quality: high-protein yellow grain, good roti quality (NBPGR passport entry). -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip12/reports/kh/1genetic_resources_management.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: No evidence found for YPS-19 x YPS-72 in any retrieved source.
- Breeding objective: improvement of yellow-pericarp sorghum for grain yield and stover quality, with multi-location minikit testing (3 years). -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip17/presentations/Centre_Presentations/6Palem.pdf
- Breeding-line code: "PYPS-2 (SPV-2293)" appears in an AICSIP 2018 Palem table, but the layout is ambiguous, so the link is unconfirmed. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip18/presentations/Centre_Presentations/5Palem.pdf
- Tester line ICSA 1013A appears alongside PYPS-2 in a 2017 Palem table, but the role is unclear. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip17/presentations/Centre_Presentations/6Palem.pdf
- Genetic resource registration: NBPGR registered PYPS-2 under RARS Palem (IC 0595529 appears in the same row), but the entry records it as a local landrace from Andhra Pradesh, which conflicts with the cross-derived parentage. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip12/reports/kh/1genetic_resources_management.pdf
- Breeding method (pedigree/SSD/backcross): No evidence found.
- QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institute: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Palem, Nagarkurnool district, Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety
- Named RARS Palem plant breeding scientist, AICSIP in-charge: Dr. S. Maheshwaramma, Scientist (Plant Breeding), in AICSIP centre reports for 2017 and 2018. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip17/presentations/Centre_Presentations/6Palem.pdf
- The 2023 IJECC paper on a different variety lists Maheshwaramma as first author, but it concerns CSV 41, so it is not attributed here to PYPS-2. -- https://journalijecc.com/index.php/IJECC/article/view/2179
- Lead breeder for PYPS-2 explicitly named by a source: only Dr. S. Maheshwaramma (role as above). Confirmation that she bred PYPS-2 is not explicit in the retrieved text.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Lavuri Krishna, Associate Director of Research, RARS Palem (Southern Telangana Zone), listed on the PJTSAU Director of Research page. Address given for the station: Palem, Nagarkurnool District, 509 215. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/
- Dr. S. Maheshwaram

drought.details: No evidence found in searched sources for drought tolerance specific to SPSSV 6 or CSV 24 SS. Search results returned only general sweet sorghum statements, and the stay-green and drought passages were not attributed to this variety. The original variety record states tolerance to moisture stress for a short period, but the digest contains no supporting evidence for this claim.

heat.details: No evidence found in searched sources for heat tolerance specific to SPSSV 6 or CSV 24 SS.

salinity.details: No evidence found in searched sources for salinity tolerance specific to SPSSV 6 or CSV 24 SS.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources for flood tolerance specific to SPSSV 6 or CSV 24 SS. The original variety record notes the variety is not prone to lodging unless there is rain and high-velocity wind after seed filling; this is a lodging trait, not evidence of flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. A leaf-disease resistance statement in the sweet sorghum status review refers to SPV 422 and ICSSH 72, not to this variety, and has been excluded. A stored-grain insect paper covering six sorghum varieties was excluded because the snippet does not show SPSSV 6 or CSV 24 SS among them.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources for pest resistance specific to SPSSV 6 or CSV 24 SS. The original variety record states moderate tolerance to shoot fly and stem borer, but the digest contains no independent evidence supporting this statement.

agronomic_details.yield: Original variety record: average yield under normal condition is 14 t/ha. Digest: release productivity for CSV 24SS (SPSSV 6) given as 40 to 50 t/ha in the sweet sorghum status review. These figures conflict and the digest does not reconcile them. In the multi-location sweet sorghum physiology trial, SPSSV6 gave about 9% more stalk yield, about 15% more juice yield and about 19% more sugar yield than the best check CSV19SS, and about 19% more ethanol yield than check SSV84. In the 2010-11 AICSIP agronomy report, SPSSV 6 grain yield was 2576 kg/ha, below SPSSV 11 (3336 kg/ha) and above SSV 84 (2252 kg/ha) and CSV 19SS.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Only single-trial and check-comparison results were located.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Original variety record: suitable for early or normal sowing in kharif or with irrigation; responds to fertilizers. The digest reports SPSSV 6 as at par with the check in a fertility-response trial and responsive to higher fertility levels in a sweet sorghum agronomy report.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Fertility-response trial: SPSSV 6 at par with the check; responded to higher fertility levels. (2) Multi-location sweet sorghum physiology trial: stalk, juice, sugar and ethanol yield advantages over checks as stated above. (3) 2010-11 AICSIP agronomy report: SPSSV 6 grain yield 2576 kg/ha, not the top entry. (4) Parbhani biomass comparison, 2010-11 AICSIP report: no entry beat check SSV84, and SPSSV 6 ranked next. (5) 2011 and 2019 AICSIP trial reports used CSV 24SS as a check: flowering about 75 days, plant height about 199 to 250 cm, with stalk and grain yield relative to newer entries. These are check values, not evaluations of the variety's own merit. Note: the release year in the request (2011) differs from the 2010 release table and the 2008 pedigree submission date in the digest; no 2011 notification record was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SPSSV 6 / CSV 24 SS (sorghum) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search note: four web_search queries were run: "SPSSV 6 sorghum variety", "SPSSV 6 sorghum breeder institute", "SPSSV 6 CSV 24 SS sorghum research", and "SPSSV6 CSV 24 SS seed availability". Evidence for this variety appears under both names. "SPSSV 6" is the AICSIP trial and pedigree code. "CSV 24 SS" / "CSV 24SS" is the sweet sorghum release name, which matches the Seednet variety code. The Seednet portal page itself was not returned by any search.

Name discrepancy: the release year is given as 2011 in the request. The sources I found list it as 2010 (Fifty Years review table) and show a "2008" submission date in the pedigree database. I found no 2011 notification record.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to SPSSV 6 or CSV 24 SS. The searches returned only general sweet sorghum statements, and the stay-green and drought passages were not attributed to this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260527271_Sweet_Sorghum_Research_and_Development_in_India_Status_and_Prospects

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to SPSSV 6 or CSV 24 SS. A leaf-disease resistance statement in the sweet sorghum status review refers to SPV 422 and ICSSH 72, not this variety -- https://oar.icrisat.org/7491/7/Sweet-sorghum_sugar_tech.pdf
A stored-grain insect paper covers six sorghum varieties, but the snippet does not show that SPSSV 6 or CSV 24 SS is among them, so it was excluded -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10625511/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
SPSSV 6 was reported as at par with the check in a fertility-response trial, and in a sweet sorghum agronomy report it responded to higher fertility levels -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip08/reports/5agronomy-physiology.pdf
In the same agronomy report, SPSSV 11 grain yield (3336 kg/ha) was significantly higher than SPSSV 6 (2576 kg/ha), SSV 84 (2252 kg/ha) and CSV 19SS, so SPSSV 6 was not the top entry -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip08/reports/5agronomy-physiology.pdf
Multi-location sweet sorghum physiology trial summary: SPSSV6 gave about 9% more stalk yield than the best check CSV19SS; juice yield was about 15% above CSV19SS; sugar yield about 19% above it; ethanol yield about 19% above check SSV84 -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip06/reports/sweetsorgumphysiolgy.pdf and https://millets.res.in/aicsip06/reports/sweetsorghumphysiolgy.pdf (both URLs were returned by the search; the first is the one that carried the figures)
Release productivity for CSV 24SS (SPSSV 6) is given as 40 to 50 t/ha in the sweet sorghum status review -- https://oar.icrisat.org/7491/7/Sweet-sorghum_sugar_tech.pdf
Trial reports from 2011 and 2019 use CSV 24SS as a check. They give its flowering (about 75 days), plant height (about 199 to 250 cm), and stalk and grain yield relative to newer entries. These are check values, not evaluations of the variety's own merit -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip11/reports/kh/4sweet_sorghum.pdf ; https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/reports18/kh/4-Sweet-Sorghum-Report-agm19.pdf ; https://millets.res.in/aicsip19/Sorghum/reports19/Kharif/4-Sweet_Sorghum.pdf
Parbhani biomass comparison in the 2010-11 AICSIP report: no entry beat check SSV84, and SPSSV 6 ranked next -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip10/reports/aicsip_coordinating_team_report_agm11.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: NSS 1005A x (SSV 84 x 401 B) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
Breeding-line code: SPSSV 6 is listed as a Sorghum Project Variety (SPV-type, sweet sorghum "SPSSV" series) in the AICSIP pedigree database -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
Breeding method: no specific evidence found beyond the pedigree record.
Genome resources, QTL, marker studies, gene annotations: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No named lead breeder or scientist specific to SPSSV 6 / CSV 24 SS was found. Evidence names the developing centre only. The 2010 release table lists the centre as NRCS (DSR), and the 2008 submission table lists DSR -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
The Directorate of Sorghum Research is described as now ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260527271_Sweet_Sorghum_Research_and_Development_in_India_Status_and_Prospects
Breeder seed production for sorghum was coordinated by Vilas A. Tonapi, N Kannababu and P.D. Khade. This is a general coordinating role, not attribution of SPSSV 6 to them -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip08/reports/8bsp_dus.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder email, phone or personal contact was found for this variety.
No institute email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL was found in the results. The only institute-level information is the name and location: ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (formerly Directorate of Sorghum Research), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260527271_Sweet_Sorghum_Research_and_Development_in_India_Status_and_Prospects
The request's address for the Directorate of Sorghum Research (Hyderabad 500 030) was not confirmed by any search result.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Palamuru Jonna (SPV-2122), sorghum

Name note: The CSC/CVRC minutes name is "Palamuru Jonna" (identified as CSV 31 in some AICRP records). The Seednet name is "Unknown," and no Seednet page was returned, so all Seednet-related findings are missing. The "variety_name" field "Sorghum" is only the crop name, so I searched "Palamuru Jonna SPV-2122" throughout. Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institution, research/trials, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bred as a high-yielding dual-purpose sorghum with grain mold tolerance; the 2014 AICRP report says it was identified for national release for that trait. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip14/report/pc-report-agm15.pdf
- Drought tolerance is listed as a breeding objective for the Palem station in general, not as a tested trait of this variety. Not counted as a finding. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/regional-agricultural-research-station-palem/
- No evidence found for salinity, flood, submergence or heat tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Grain mold tolerance is the main disease trait reported (see above). -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip14/report/pc-report-agm15.pdf
- Charcoal rot, shoot fly, stem borer and midge scores are not reported for this variety in the pages found. Midge and mite pressure in one 2014 Coimbatore trial was not attributed to a specific entry. Not counted.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pre-release national coordinated trial: grain yield 3376 kg/ha and fodder yield 14434 kg/ha. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip15/presentations/Day1/6Palem.pdf
- Zone I AVT-II yield 3389 kg/ha, with the entry noted as marginally ahead of checks. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip12/reports/kh/AICSIP_Coordinating_Team_Report.pdf (2012-13 report)
- 2013-14 AVT: 3914 kg/ha grain yield against best check CSV 20 at 3766 kg/ha (marginal superiority). -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip13/reports/pc_report.pdf
- Distinguishing DUS characters: medium plant height at maturity, yellow stigma colour present, broad leaf blade, short glume length. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvjdecember2018signed2.pdf
- Maturity days, the ideal seeding rate and spacing for this variety were not found; the FAQ spacing values are generic sorghum figures and were excluded.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: SPV 462 x SPV 1329, per the AICRP fifty-years table. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
- Breeding-line codes: SPV 2122, CSV 31 (Palamuru Jonna), and PSVGS-106 (listed as SPV2122 in one table). -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip13/reports/pc_report.pdf
- Breeding method: pedigree selection is implied by the parentage, but the method is not stated explicitly. Not counted as a finding.
- Genome resources and QTL/marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing centre: AICRP on Sorghum, Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Palem, Nagarkurnool, Telangana (PJTSAU/PJTAU). -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvjdecember2018signed2.pdf
- Named AICRP scientists at Palem in the 2016 presentation: Dr. S. Maheshwaramma, Scientist (Plant Breeding), and Ms. N. Jemimah, Scientist (Entomology). The slide does not explicitly state that Dr. Maheshwaramma bred SPV 2122, so no breeder attribution is made. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip15/presentations/Day1/6Palem.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Telangana Jonna 1 / CSV 41 / SPV 2437 (Sorghum)

Searches run: 4 (variety and release; breeder and institution; research papers; seed availability). Name used in the evidence: "Telangana Jonna 1 / CSV 41" in most sources, and "SPV 2437" in the morphology and trial sources. The Seednet name "Telangana Jonna 1 (CSV 41/SPV 2437)" did not appear in any result, and no seednet.gov.in page was returned.

Conflict to note: millets.res.in lists a "Grain Sorghum Variety, CSV 41" developed at ICAR-IIMR, Hyderabad, with different recommended areas (MP, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, AP, Telangana, TN). It does not name Telangana Jonna 1 or PJTSAU, so I have not attributed it to this variety. It may be a different CSV 41 release.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released for dual-purpose use with reported resistance to pests and diseases and good cooking quality, relative to check varieties (researchgate, 2023 paper by Maheswaramma et al.) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety
- Keywords in the same paper include grain mould and shoot fly, which are the pest and disease traits the study addresses (researchgate, 2023 paper) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for this variety in the results.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Reaction of SPV 2437 to different insect pests and anthracnose disease severity scale are listed as figures/tables in the same publication (researchgate figure page) -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Distinguishing-morphological-characters-of-sorghum-variety-SPV-2437_tbl3_371841973
- Specific pest and disease scores, grain mould ratings and shoot fly ratings: No evidence found in the text returned.
- Mystore product page describes the variety as resistant to pests and diseases (commercial listing, weak source) -- https://www.mystore.in/en/product/fodder-sorghum-csv-41-tl-1kg-pouch

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Evaluated across fifteen AICRP centres nationally before release; the paper also reports Zone I release (researchgate, 2023 paper) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety
- Reported yields for SPV 2437 in the trial results: grain 3179.8 kg/ha and fodder 15900.2 kg/ha, with grain yield +39.25% over one check, +3.86% over another and +14.88% over a third (figures as printed in the abstract of the on-farm study; the trial is attributed to this variety by the snippet, but verify against the full text) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372367164_Assessment_of_Yellow_Sorghum_Palem_Pacha_Jonna-1_PYPS_2_Performance_through_on_Farm_Testing_in_Telangana
- Identical yield text also appears on a related ResearchGate page (history of post-rainy sorghum research), so the figures may originate from the 2023 CSV 41 paper -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269397146_History_of_post-rainy_season_sorghum_research_in_India_and_strategies_for_breaking_the_yield_plateau
- Days to maturity, plant height, and fertilizer/planting recommendations for this variety: No evidence found.
- Note: the on-farm study is about PYPS 2 (Palem Pacha Jonna-1), a different variety, and is cited only for the SPV 2437 comparison line.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: crossed from SPV-86 and ICSR-89064 (commercial product page; not confirmed by a breeding publication) -- https://www.mystore.in/en/product/fodder-sorghum-csv-41-tl-1kg-pouch
- Breeding line code: SPV 2437 (researchgate 2023 paper; pjtau.edu.in and iauaindia.org list "Telangana Jonna 1 - SPV 2437") -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety ; http://www.iauaindia.org/UniversityDetails.aspx?id=37
- Breeding method (pedigree selection suggested by one snippet, not confirmed): -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety
- QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad; released under the name Telangana Jonna 1 (iauaindia.org; pjtau.edu.in) -- http://www.iauaindia.org/UniversityDetails.aspx?id=37 ; https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/
- Station: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Palem, Nagarkurnool, is named in the 2023 paper as the station for SPV 2437 (researchgate 2023 paper) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The paper's authors are listed below, but their breeding role is not stated.
- Authors of the 2023 paper: s. Maheswaramma, Nagesh Kumar, C.V. Sameer Kumar, Manthati Goverdhan -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level only (no breeder contact found). Affiliation as printed: "AICRP on IFS, PJTSAU, Rajendranagar, 500 030 Hyderabad, Telangana, India" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety
- Institute contact page: https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/ (page returned; no email or phone extracted from the snippet)
- Official email: No evidence found. Phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Maheswaramma, S., Kumar, N., Kumar, C.V.S., Goverdhan, M. (2023). Telangana Jonna 1 (CSV 41): A High Yielding, Dual Purpose, Potential Sorghum Variety. Journal not stated in the results (ResearchGate lists it as an "Original Research Article", June 2023) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety
- Maheswaramma, S., and co-authors (2023). Assessment of Yellow Sorghum Palem Pacha Jonna-1 (PYPS 2) Performance through On-Farm Testing in Telangana. Journal not stated (June 2023). This paper is about PYPS 2, but it cites the SPV 2437 comparison -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372367164_Assessment_of_Yellow_Sorghum_Palem_Pacha_Jonna-1_PYPS_2_Performance_through_on_Farm_Testing_in_Telangana
- AICRP/ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, and DOI: No evidence found for this variety in the results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Retail listing: "FODDER SORGHUM CSV-41 TL 1KG POUCH" (mystore.in), described as "also known as Telangana Jonna 1" (commercial seller, not verified) -- https://www.mystore.in/en/product/fodder-sorghum-csv-41-tl-1kg-pouch
- Telangana state seed production and seed mela (PJTSAU page): this does not name Telangana Jonna 1 specifically -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales: No evidence found for this variety.
- Seednet portal listing: No evidence found (no seednet.gov.in result returned).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Zone I (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat), released by the Central Varietal Release Committee in 2020 (researchgate 2023 paper) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371841973_Telangana_Jonna_1CSV_41_A_High_Yielding_Dual_Purpose_Potential_Sorghum_Variety ; the same release is also cited in https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372367164_Assessment_of_Yellow_Sorghum_Palem_Pacha_Jonna-1_PYPS_2_Performance_through_on_Farm_Testing_in_Telangana
