official_quote.quote: Moderately tolerant to grain mold disease

disease_resistance.research_summary: Grain mould: the original variety data (CSC record) describes the variety as moderately tolerant to grain mold. The digest gives no specific grain mould rating, but lists grain mould as a trait addressed in the 2023 paper, which reports resistance to pests and diseases relative to check varieties. Anthracnose: the 2023 paper's figures list an anthracnose disease severity scale for SPV 2437, but the scores were not in the returned text, so no resistance level can be stated. A commercial listing (weak source) describes the variety as resistant to pests and diseases without specifics.

official_quote.quote: Moderately resistance to Shootfly and stem borer

pest_resistance.research_summary: Shoot fly and stem borer: the original variety data (CSC record) describes moderate resistance to shootfly and stem borer. The 2023 paper's figures list reactions of SPV 2437 to insect pests, but the scores were not in the returned text, and the digest found no shoot fly rating. The commercial listing (weak source) claims pest resistance without specifics.

and pods

perfect yellow and has light brown shade. Seed has one
brown spot on micropile.

2 and MS

Slight Antixenosis against Spodoptera litura under controlled
condition and resistant to stem fly, girdle beetle and
defoliators in field condition.

drought.details: No official rating for NRC 150 was found. A dealer listing calls it drought-tolerant, but this is a marketing claim and was not counted as evidence. The research article cited describes the parent JS 97-52 as drought-tolerant, which does not establish NRC 150's own tolerance. The CSC stress_reaction field does not address drought.

heat.details: No rating for NRC 150 was found. The research article describes the parent JS 97-52 as heat-tolerant, which is not evidence for NRC 150.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources.

flood.details: No rating for NRC 150 was found. The research article describes the parent JS 97-52 as waterlogging-tolerant, which is not evidence for NRC 150.

disease_resistance.summary: Anthracnose (Colletotrichum truncatum): the Heliyon paper identifies NRC 150 as a promising donor source for anthracnose resistance and rates it moderately resistant. Dealer-listed claims of YMV resistance, rust tolerance and shatter resistance are unverified marketing claims and are not counted as evidence. The CSC disease_reaction field is Unknown. Charcoal rot: an IISR slide deck lists NRC 150 under 'MR to AR to Charcoal Rot', but the entry is interleaved with other varieties' entries, so attribution is uncertain.

pest_resistance.summary: CSC stress_reaction data states NRC 150 showed variable resistance to stem fly, girdle beetle and defoliators, and an SLY to Resistant high yielding (RHY) reaction against the insect-pest complex. An IISR slide deck lists 'Resistant to stem fly, girdle beetle and defoliators', but the entry is interleaved with other varieties' entries, so attribution to NRC 150 is not confirmed by the digest. The CSC pest_reaction field is Unknown.

agronomic_details.yield: Two IISR-linked sources give 1757.5 kg/ha at 90.6 days (varietal table and slide deck). A separate IISR presentation gives 1451 kg/ha at 92 days, but its block layout is ambiguous and attribution is uncertain. A Hindi news article reports a 38 q/ha potential, which is unverified. Dealer listings conflict with the institute figures and with each other (20-25 q/acre and 25-30 q/ha). CSC average_yield is Unknown.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Identified at the 52nd Annual Group Meeting of AICRP-Soybean (Indore, 17-18 May) for cultivation in Central India. CSC data lists recommended states as Madhya Pradesh, Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Vidarbha and Marathwada regions of Maharashtra. CSC data also states suitability for normal kharif sowing from 25 June to 7 July.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CSC agronomic features: amenable to mechanical harvesting; strong stem and does not lodge; pods do not shatter at least 15 days after maturity; performs well under recommended fertilizer dose of 20 N, 60 P2O5, 20 K2O and 20 S kg/ha; seed rate 60 kg/ha. Plant height of 47.4 cm is reported in an IISR presentation, but its attribution to NRC 150 is uncertain. Maturity reported as 90.6 days (varietal table and slide deck), 91 days (ICAR-NSRI bulletin), and 92 days (IISR presentation with uncertain attribution). Dealer listings give 90-95 days and 100-105 days, which conflict with each other and with the institute figures.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) 52nd Annual Group Meeting of AICRP-Soybean at Indore (17-18 May): NRC 150 identified for cultivation in Central India. (2) ICAR-IISR varietal table: 90.6 days maturity, 1757 kg/ha average yield. (3) IISR slide deck: 1757.5 kg/ha at 90.6 days, described as early maturing. (4) ICAR-NSRI bulletin table: 91 days and an 18 value of unstated unit; column headers unclear. (5) Another IISR presentation: 92 days, 1451 kg/ha, 47.4 cm plant height; attribution uncertain. (6) Choupal Samachar (Hindi news): 38 q/ha potential, not verified. No AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, conference paper or dedicated field-trial dataset specific to NRC 150 was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NRC 150 (soybean)

Name check: "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" are both "NRC 150." No Seednet portal page came back in any of the four searches, so no Seednet-specific evidence exists here. All evidence below refers to the name NRC 150, and I have not confirmed it against the CSC minutes.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Ratings for NRC 150 on drought, heat, waterlogging, salinity and flood were not found in any official source. A dealer listing calls it drought-tolerant, but that is a marketing claim and I have not counted it as evidence. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/nrc-150-soyabean-seeds-2854244201191.html
- Its parent JS 97-52 is described in a research article as tolerant of drought, heat and waterlogging, but that describes the parent, not NRC 150. -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-02064-x

DISEASE AND PEST
- Genotypes EC 18596, EC 95677, and NRC 150 were identified as promising donor sources for breeding for anthracnose resistance in soybean. The paper rates NRC 150 as moderately resistant to anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum truncatum. -- https://www.cell.com/heliyon/fulltext/S2405-8440(26)00674-2
- A dealer listing gives NRC 150 YMV resistance, rust tolerance and shatter resistance. These are unverified marketing claims. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/nrc-150-soyabean-2854244201191.html
- An IISR slide deck lists NRC 150 under "Reaction to insects" and "MR to AR to Charcoal Rot," and separately lists "Resistant to stem fly, girdle beetle and defoliators." These lines are interleaved with other varieties' entries, so I cannot confirm they belong to NRC 150. -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is reported as 90.6 days with average yield 1757 kg/ha, in the varietal table of an ICAR-IISR presentation. -- https://nsai.co.in/storage/app/media/sgbrdi.pdf
- The same slide deck gives 1757.5 kg/ha at 90.6 days and calls it early maturing. -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf
- A separate table in an ICAR-NSRI bulletin lists NRC 150 with 91 days and an 18 (unit not stated) value. The column headers are unclear. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/ExtensionBulletin2023E_2.pdf
- Another IISR presentation gives a 92-day maturity, 1451 kg/ha yield, and a plant height of 47.4 cm. Its block layout is ambiguous, so the attribution is uncertain. -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf
- The 52nd Annual Group Meeting of AICRP-Soybean at Indore (17–18 May) identified NRC 150 for cultivation in Central India. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/ExtensionBulletin2023E_2.pdf
- Dealer listings give a 90–95 day duration and 20–25 quintals/acre, and separately a 100–105 day duration and 25–30 q/ha. These figures conflict with each other and with the institute figures above. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/nrc-150-soyabean-seeds-2854244201191.html
- Trial-yield figures appear in a Hindi news article (Choupal Samachar), which reports a 38 q/ha potential. I have not verified this figure. -- https://choupalsamachar.in/soybean-variety-nrc-150/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- The IISR presentation says NRC 150 carries the photo-insensitive allele e3. -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf
- The PTI report says NRC 150 is free of lipoxygenase-2, which is linked to beany odour. -- https://theprint.in/india/mp-indores-iisr-develops-new-soybean-variety-free-of-unwanted-odour/969102/
- The ICAR-NSRI varieties page also lists NRC 150 as lipoxygenase-2 free. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- Parentage JS 97-52 x NRC 109 (from the user input) was not confirmed by any retrieved page. A marker study mentions NRC 109 as a parent in another context, but does not link it to NRC 150. -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue9S/PartS/S-9-9-250-484.pdf
- Breeding method, breeding-line code and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR), Indore. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8613251/ (for the institute name only) and https://theprint.in/india/mp-indores-iisr-develops-new-soybean-variety-free-of-unwanted-odour/969102/
- A Hindi news article (Choupal Samachar) says the variety was developed by ICAR-IISR, Indore. -- https://choupalsamachar.in/soybean-variety-nrc-150/
- Lead breeder name for NRC 150: No evidence found. Dr B.U. Dupare, Principal Scientist (Agricultural Extension), spoke publicly about the variety's recommendation, but no source names him as its breeder. -- https://theprint.in/india/mp-indores-iisr-develops-new-soybean-variety-free-of-unwanted-odour/969102/
- Dr Kunwar Harendra Singh is listed as Director of IISR in a 2025 presentation. Dr Nita Khandekar was listed as Director in a 2023 news item. The directory lists her as Acting Director. The directorship is unclear from these sources. -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf ; https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/icar-develops-new-climate-smart-soyabean-varieties-for-cultivation/

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level only; no breeder contact found)
- Address: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research, Khandwa Road, Indore, M.P., India - 452 001. -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/contactus.html
- Phone: 091-0731-2476188, 2478414. -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/contactus.html
- Email: director.soybean@icar.gov.in, dsraddmin@gmail.com, dsrdirector@gmail.com. Seed enquiries: swarnsoya.seed@gmail.com. -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/contactus.html
- The ICAR-NSRI contact page gives the same address and phone, with the email dsrdirector@gmail.com and a fax number of 091-0731-2470520. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/contactus.html
- The institute directory lists Dr Nita Khandekar (Acting Director) at nitakhandekar@yahoo.co.in, and Dr B.U. Dupare at budupare@rediffmail.com (phone 94259-64016). Neither is linked to NRC 150 as breeder. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/directory.pdf
- The ICAR institute profile PDF lists IISR but gives no contact details for it. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/ICAR-INSTITUTE-PROFILE_.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in the retrieved text (year not shown). Multivariate selection of early-maturing soybean genotypes with anthracnose resistance for sustainable cultivation. Heliyon -- https://www.cell.com/heliyon/fulltext/S2405-8440(26)00674-2
- Authors not stated in the retrieved text (year not shown). Institute extension bulletin, ICAR-IISR (2023), which lists NRC 150 with the other varieties identified at the 52nd AGM. ICAR-IISR Extension Bulletin -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/ExtensionBulletin2023E_2.pdf
- Authors not stated in the retrieved text (year not shown). Latest Development in Soybean Breeding (presentation). SOPA -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf
- AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, conference paper, or field-trial data specific to NRC 150: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Dealer listings for NRC 150 seed from Samrat Seeds on IndiaMART show prices in Sarangpur and Rajgarh. These are private dealers and I have not verified their stock or quality. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/nrc-150-soyabean-seeds-2854244201191.html
- The ICAR-NSRI varieties page lists NRC 150 in a table of varieties in the breeder-seed chain, which is produced by the institute. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK and SAU seed sales: No evidence found.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Anthracnose (Colletotrichum truncatum): the Heliyon paper identifies NRC 150 as a promising donor source for anthracnose resistance and rates it moderately resistant. Dealer-listed claims of YMV resistance, rust tolerance and shatter resistance are unverified marketing claims and are not counted as evidence. The CSC disease_reaction field is Unknown. Charcoal rot: an IISR slide deck lists NRC 150 under 'MR to AR to Charcoal Rot', but the entry is interleaved with other varieties' entries, so attribution is uncertain.

pest_resistance.research_summary: CSC stress_reaction data states NRC 150 showed variable resistance to stem fly, girdle beetle and defoliators, and an SLY to Resistant high yielding (RHY) reaction against the insect-pest complex. An IISR slide deck lists 'Resistant to stem fly, girdle beetle and defoliators', but the entry is interleaved with other varieties' entries, so attribution to NRC 150 is not confirmed by the digest. The CSC pest_reaction field is Unknown.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NRC 37 (variety code Ahilya 4), Soybean, Anand Agricultural University / ICAR-IISR

Name handling: variety_name "NRC 37" and variety code "Ahilya 4" both appear in the evidence below, and the findings refer to the same soybean line. seednet_variety_name is "Unknown", and no search returned a Seednet portal entry, so no finding is attributed to Seednet. Four searches were run; the Seednet check was not separate.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Heat: in a high-temperature screening study, NRC 37 had the lowest photosynthetic rate (20.3 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1), the lowest reproductive efficiency group (21%, shared with Punjab 1), and the lowest harvest index (29.4%) among the genotypes tested. The study classed it as low yielding and heat-susceptible, along with JS 95-60, JS 93-05, JS 335 and Punjab 1. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/12/11/2854
- Drought, salinity, flood, submergence, waterlogging: No evidence found in the retrieved text for NRC 37 specifically. The waterlogging result (PMC8613251) is about other breeding lines.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Collar rot (Sclerotium rolfsii) is listed as a resistant/tolerant trait for NRC 37 in an NAAS strategy table. -- https://naas.org.in/spapers/Strategy%20Paper%20No.%204.pdf
- Rust (Phakopsora pachyrhizi): NRC 37 appears in an NAAS table of rust-resistant varieties, but the table layout is garbled, so this entry is uncertain. -- https://naas.org.in/spapers/Strategy%20Paper%20No.%204.pdf
- Pod blight and insect pests: No evidence found for NRC 37 specifically. The pod-blight finding is for NRC 131, and the insect findings are general to other lines.
- Seed longevity and mechanical harvesting: NRC 37 is listed among varieties with high seed longevity and among varieties suited to mechanical harvesting, because of high pod insertion. -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/highyieldvar.htm

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average yield 2283 kg/ha; non-shattering habit, white flowers, hairy pods, semi-erect growth; seed 19.2% oil and 46.8% protein; seed yield 17.8% above check JS 335 and 35.7% and 47.2% above local checks GS 1 and GS 3. -- https://www.aau.in/nrc-37
- Ridge-and-furrow intra-row spacing trial comparing NRC 37, JS 20-34 and JS 335 across four spacings (45 x 5 to 45 x 20 cm); NRC 37 showed significant genotype effects on plant height, pods per plant and 100-seed weight. Year and journal not stated in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369387766_Varietal_response_of_soybean_Glycine_max_L_Merrill_on_growth_yield_attributes_and_yield_to_different_intra_row_spacing_under_ridge_and_furrow_system
- Seeds per pod in the heat study were 1.53 for NRC 37, among the lowest recorded. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/12/11/2854

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: Gaurav x Punjab 1 (semi-determinate, high yielding), from an IISR Indore breeding-centre table. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8863763/
- Genetic diversity: NRC 37 clusters with JNKVV and IISR lines in an SSR-marker study of Indian soybean cultivars. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8863763/
- QTL, genes, marker-assisted work on NRC 37: No evidence found. The marker-assisted and Kunitz-trypsin-inhibitor-free results apply to NRC 127, not NRC 37, and were excluded.
- Breeding method beyond the pedigree: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR), Indore, which lists NRC 37 (Ahilya 4) among its developed varieties. -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/varieties.html
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found in any retrieved page.
- Release agency: Anand Agricultural University (AAU) lists NRC 37 (Ahilya 4) as released in 2017 by the 48th State Seed Sub-Committee. -- https://aau.in/variety_released

CONTACT DETAILS
- AAU Regional Research Station, Anand: Anand Agricultural University, Anand 388 110 (Gujarat); phone (02692) 260329; email nodalofficerseed@aau.in. This is the seed nodal office, not a breeder contact. -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/557
- Subrota Hati: email subrota_dt@yahoo.com, listed as an AAU researcher (Dept. of Dairy Microbiology, SMC College of Dairy Science, Anand). He is an author on an NRC-37-based study, not identified as a breeder of this variety, so do not treat this as a breeder contact. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s43014-021-00056-y
- IISR Indore: postal address, phone and email not retrieved. Institute site: https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/ -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/varieties.html

PUBLICATIONS
- Undhad Trupti, Solanki Divyang, Hati Subrota (2021). Bioactivities and ACE-inhibitory peptides releasing potential of lactic acid bacteria in fermented soy milk. Journal not named in retrieved text (article 10, vol. 3) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s43014-021-00056-y (DOI 10.1186/s43014-021-00056-y)
- Authors not retrieved (year likely 2022, inferred from volume 12 of MDPI Agronomy). Screening Soybean Genotypes for High-Temperature Tolerance by Maximin-Minimax Method Based on Yield Potential and Loss. Agronomy (MDPI) -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/12/11/2854
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Molecular characterization and genetic diversity studies of Indian soybean (Glycine max) cultivars using SSR markers. Journal not retrieved -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8863763/
- Authors and year not retrieved. Varietal response of soybean (Glycine max L. Merrill) on growth, yield attributes and yield to different intra row spacing under ridge and furrow system. ResearchGate record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369387766_Varietal_response_of_soybean_Glycine_max_L_Merrill_on_growth_yield_attributes_and_yield_to_different_intra_row_spacing_under_ridge_and_furrow_system
- Dupare, B. U. (2023). Improved Technologies and Recommendations for Maximizing Soybean Productivity. Extension Bulletin No. 18, ICAR-IISR -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/ExtensionBulletin2023E_2.pdf (lists NRC 37 among developed varieties)
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report entry or DOI specific to NRC 37 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- IISR states that NRC 37 is under seed chain (with NRC 7 and NRC 86). -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/significant_achievement.html
- IISR coordinates breeder seed for about 30 varieties in the seed chain. -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/highyieldvar.htm
- The seed chain runs from foundation to certified seed through NSC and SSC. -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/06-KH-Singh-Enhancing-soybean-productivity.pdf (general, not NRC 37 specific)
- AAU's Nodal Officer (Seed) coordinates AAU seed production, including breeder seed. -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/557
- Current seller, KVK, or dealer listings for NRC

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to PS 1523 / Pant Soya 23 in the searched sources. The ICAR-IISR bulletin discusses climate stress for soybean in general, not this variety. The variety record (CSC data) states the variety is at par with check varieties for drought tolerance; this statement is not corroborated by the evidence digest, so no level is assigned.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to PS 1523 / Pant Soya 23. The ICAR-IISR bulletin covers soybean climate stress in general only.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to PS 1523 / Pant Soya 23.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to PS 1523 / Pant Soya 23. The variety record (CSC data) states the variety is at par with check varieties for waterlogged conditions; this is not corroborated by the evidence digest, so no level is assigned.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistance to yellow mosaic virus (YMV) and bacterial pustule is reported for Pant Soybean 21 and Pant Soybean 23 together. The source does not give separate figures for PS 23, so the rating is shared and should be read as a joint report. No disease-rating row specific to PS 1523 was extracted from the Climate Smart e-book table. The adjacent Pant Soya 21 and Pant Soya 24 rows list YMV, SMV, bacterial pustule and Rhizoctonia aerial blight resistance; these ratings are not assigned to PS 1523. The variety record (CSC data) describes the variety as sturdy with profuse podding under disease reaction, which is a morphological description, not a disease rating.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No pest evidence specific to PS 1523 was found. The variety record (CSC data) states the pest reaction is at par with other existing and check varieties of the zone (Bragg and PS 1347); this is not corroborated by the evidence digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources. The Hawk report describes high yield potential for PS 21 and PS 23 together, without separate figures for PS 23. The variety record lists average yield as Unknown.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location or field-trial yield data for PS 1523 were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Uttarakhand (see variety_profile). The variety record describes rainfed and irrigated kharif cultivation in plains and lower hills of Uttarakhand; this is not corroborated by the evidence digest. The Hawk report indicates general cultivation in Uttarakhand and UP, which conflicts with the record's Uttarakhand-only listing and should be checked against the CSC minutes.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semideterminate plant type, smooth dark green pointed ovate leaves, white flower colour (per the Climate Smart e-book; extraction is partly garbled). The variety record also describes a sturdy medium plant type with profuse podding, resistance to lodging and shattering, and more than 86% germination after 7 months of ordinary storage.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Not found in searched sources for multi-location or field-trial yield data. One figure of 40.5 % appears in the e-book row for this variety, but its column label is unclear in the extracted text, so it is not interpreted. Sowing, seed rate and fertiliser recommendations: not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistance to yellow mosaic virus and bacterial pustule is reported for Pant Soybean 21 and Pant Soybean 23 together, with medium maturity and high yield potential (the source does not give separate figures for PS 23) -- https://www.thehawk.in/news/states-and-uts/three-new-soybean-varieties-of-pantvarsity-released-by-central-committee
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to PS 1523 / Pant Soya 23. The ICAR-IISR bulletin discusses climate stress for soybean in general, not this variety -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/ExtensionBulletin2023E_2.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No disease-rating row specific to PS 1523 was extracted from the Climate Smart e-book table. The adjacent Pant Soya 21 and Pant Soya 24 rows list YMV, SMV, bacterial pustule and Rhizoctonia aerial blight resistance, so those ratings must not be assigned to PS 1523 -- https://www.manage.gov.in/publications/eBooks/Climate%20Smart%20Soybean%20Production%20Technologies.pdf
- Pest evidence: No evidence found for PS 1523 specifically.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Notified 25.08.2017 under S.O. 2805(E) for Uttarakhand, maturity listed as 112-115 days, semideterminate plant type, smooth dark green pointed ovate leaves, white flower colour (extraction is partly garbled) -- https://www.manage.gov.in/publications/eBooks/Climate%20Smart%20Soybean%20Production%20Technologies.pdf
- A 40.5 % figure appears in the same row, but its column label is unclear in the extracted text, so it is not interpreted here -- https://www.manage.gov.in/publications/eBooks/Climate%20Smart%20Soybean%20Production%20Technologies.pdf
- Multi-location or field-trial yield data for PS 1523: No evidence found.
- Sowing, seed rate and fertiliser recommendations for PS 1523: No evidence found (the seed-rate and fertiliser figures retrieved are for other or unnamed varieties).

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage PS 1029 x PS 1241: No evidence found. This is supplied in the record only and was not confirmed by any retrieved page.
- Breeding-line code: the variety code PS 1523 (also written PS 1 523) appears on several pages. Those pages also give the S.O. number, the 2017 release date and the Pantnagar origin.
- Breeding method for PS 1523: No evidence found. The only method description retrieved (single cross, then pedigree selection) belongs to Pant Soybean 24, so it is not attributed here.
- QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, with the soybean AICRP centre there. The variety is listed under this university in the DAC table -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx
- Named lead breeder for PS 1523: No evidence found. Dr. Pushpendra appears as the soybean breeder at GBPUAT, and P.S. Shukla as a soybean breeder in the Genetics and Plant Breeding Department. Neither is linked to PS 1523 in any retrieved page, so they are not attributed to it -- https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=y9z8DmQAAAAJ ; https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/soybean-breeding-persentation-final-1/51947532
- Department context: the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding at GBPUAT was founded in 1960 and has a soybean-research history at Pantnagar -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/index.html

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Institute-level: No email, phone or postal address for the GBPUAT soybean programme or the Genetics and Plant Breeding Department was extracted. The only institute URL retrieved is the department page, https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/index.html, which lists no contact details in the extracted text. Pantnagar, Uttarakhand 263145 is the university's postal locality as printed on the department's soybean breeding material (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/soybean-breeding-persentation-final-1/51947532 and https://ssrd.co.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/2014-Special-Issue-II.pdf), but no phone or email was printed there.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. The search returned no paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI that names PS 1523 / Pant Soya 23. The GBPUAT AICRP soybean PDF covers the programme but names other varieties -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/9%20AICRP%20-%20SOYBEAN.pdf
- Lead to check (not verified as containing PS 1523 data): "Five Decades of Soyabean Research at Pantnagar (1976-2016)", linked from https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/index.html

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Nucleus seed production for PS 21 and PS 23 was started at the NEB Crop Research Centre and the Breeder Seed Production Centre, Pantnagar, to build a quality seed chain -- https://www.thehawk.in/news/states-and-uts/three-new-soybean-varieties-of-pantvarsity-released-by-central-committee
- Dealer, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale listings for PS 1523: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttarakhand: listed among the Uttarakhand notified varieties in the DAC state table -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx
- Uttarakhand, with the 2017 notification at GBPUAT: https://www.manage.gov.in/publications/eBooks/Climate%20Smart%20Soybean%20Production%20Technologies.pdf
- Discrepancy: the Hawk report says the 2017 notification covers general cultivation in Uttarakhand and UP. The record lists Uttarakhand only, so UP should be checked against the CSC minutes before the field is finalised -- https://www.thehawk.in/news/states-and-uts/three-new-soybean-varieties-of-pantvarsity-released-by-central-committee

NAME AND CODE CHECK
- variety_name (CSC minutes) "Pant Soybean 23 (PS 1523)" and seednet_variety_name "Pant Soybean 23 (PS 1523)" both match the evidence, which refers to it as "Pant Soya 23 (PS 1523)" in the e-book and IISR tables, and as "Pant Soybean-23 (PS-1523)" in the PMFME table.
- Code conflict: the DAC table and IISR NHZ list give "Pant Soya 23 (PS 1521)" for 2017. The IISR table, e-book and PMFME table give PS 1523. The record's code PS 1523 is supported by most sources; PS 1521 should be checked against the Seednet entry -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx ; https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/varieties.html
- Discarded: the JS 23-03 pages (other variety, JNKVV), Pant Soybean 25 (PS 1556), and the USPTO, PSU, PanSoy and PMFME pages (other crops or products).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Soybean 24 (PS 1477), Soybean

Name check: "Pant Soybean 24" (CSC name) and "Pant Soya 24 (PS 1477)" / "PS 1477" (Seednet-style) appear in the same sources. The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved, so no Seednet-specific page is cited. The SOYBEAN (BHAT) crop name was not searched separately. Searches returned no evidence on parentage (JS 335 x PS 1024).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Some sources describe the variety as YMV-resistant or tolerant, but the wording is mixed in with other varieties. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- One ICAR-related extension table gives a short trait line for the variety that mentions YMV resistance, pustule resistance and moderate resistance to a disease, though the line is garbled. -- https://www.manage.gov.in/publications/eBooks/Climate%20Smart%20Soybean%20Production%20Technologies.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The DAC Oilseeds table lists no disease traits for Pant Soy-24 (PS 1477). Related varieties in the same table (PS 1347, PS-19, Pant Soya 21) carry resistance claims, but those are other varieties. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx
- Pest-resistance claims tied to this variety are limited to the garbled ICAR-related extension line above. No entomology trial data for PS 1477 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The variety is described with determinate habit, purple flower, tawny pubescence, narrow leaves, brown hilum, freedom from lodging and shattering, and medium-to-bold seed with about 40% protein and 20% oil. -- https://www.thehawk.in/news/states-and-uts/three-new-soybean-varieties-of-pantvarsity-released-by-central-committee
- Maturity figures conflict across sources: 113 days (https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-New-Soybean-Varieties-and-Their-Yield-Potential-%E2%80%93-By-Dr.-Sanjay-Gupta.pdf), 117 days in a partly legible table (https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf), and 142 days in the same deck. Treat maturity as unresolved.
- Yield values also conflict: 2282 kg/ha (https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf), 19.1 q/ha against a 32 q/ha potential (https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-New-Soybean-Varieties-and-Their-Yield-Potential-%E2%80%93-By-Dr.-Sanjay-Gupta.pdf), and an unlabelled 2.00 entry in a zonal table (https://nsai.co.in/storage/app/media/sgbrdi.pdf). The slide that gives the 19.1 q/ha figure places it beside NRC 128, so the pairing is uncertain.
- A frontline-demonstration report lists PS 1477 among entries, but its numbers cannot be reliably tied to it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343304844_Performance_of_Soybean_Varieties_under_Frontline_Demonstrations
- Commercial 2025 lists recommend it for eastern UP and for Punjab. These are not official recommendations. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/latest-recommended-high-yielding-soybean-varieties-for-uttar-pradesh-2025/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage (JS 335 x PS 1024): No evidence found.
- Breeding method and breeding-line codes beyond "PS 1477": No evidence found.
- QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety was developed by scientists of Pantvarsity working under the AICRP on Soybean. -- https://www.thehawk.in/news/states-and-uts/three-new-soybean-varieties-of-pantvarsity-released-by-central-committee
- The AICRP on Soybean was launched at G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, in 1967. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/9%20AICRP%20-%20SOYBEAN.pdf
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.
- Notification dates conflict: S.O. 112(E) dated 12.01.2016 (https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf) versus 25.08.2017 (https://www.manage.gov.in/publications/eBooks/Climate%20Smart%20Soybean%20Production%20Technologies.pdf). Both sources are consistent with a 2017 release year.
- The Pantnagar centre's varieties list is not tied to this variety specifically. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/Released_crop_varieties.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Named breeder, email, phone or postal address: No evidence found.
- Institute pages retrieved, none with contact details in the retrieved text: https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/Released_crop_varieties.pdf ; https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html ; https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/varieties.html

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown (n.d.). Conjoint application of Ni and Mn on the enzymatic activity (study using "Pant Soybean-24" seed from GBPUAT, Pantnagar; the variety code is not stated). Journal/thesis not shown. -- https://d-nb.info/1388114135/34
- Katiyar, A. K. and Pant, L. M. (1993). Effect of methods of Bradyrhizobium japonicum inoculation on nodulation, nitrogen fixation and yield of soybean. Legume Research, 16: 79–85. -- This citation appears in the Pantnagar AICRP report but does not name PS 1477, so it is not attributed to this variety. https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/9%20AICRP%20-%20SOYBEAN.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis, or AICRP annual report was found that names PS 1477 or Pant Soybean 24 in a way that establishes the link.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Breeder seed: The national soybean institute coordinates breeder-seed production, and Pant Soybean 24 (2017) is listed in its breeder-seed production table. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- Nucleus seed for these Pantnagar varieties was started at the NEB Crop Research Centre and the Breeder Seed Production Centre. -- https://www.thehawk.in/news/states-and-uts/three-new-soybean-varieties-of-pantvarsity-released-by-central-committee
- Retail, NSC, state corporation, KVK or dealer listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, per the DAC Oilseeds state-wise notified list. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx
- Official description of adaptation: North Plain Zone. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- Pantnagar-related text describes the variety for "northern plain and hill zones" (wording from a study using the seed). -- https://d-nb.info/1388114135/34
- Commercial 2025 lists add eastern UP and Punjab. These are not official notifications. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/latest-recommended-high-yielding-soybean-varieties-for-punjab-2025/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Raj Soya-18 (Pragya), Soybean

Name note: The CSC name "Raj Soya-18 (Pragya)" and the Seednet name "Raj Soya -18 (Pragya)" both appear in the ICAR-IISR and ICAR-NSRI notification lists, and the findings below refer to that same variety. The DOD page uses the shorter "Raj Soya-18" form. Searches 1 to 4 were run, and four is the maximum allowed.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no page that ties drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance to this variety. A drought-screening paper (arccjournals.com, LR-4550) used genotypes from RAK College, Sehore, but its snippet does not name Raj Soya-18, so I discarded it. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4550 (not attributed)

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The MANAGE e-book lists Raj Soya-18 in a notified-variety table, but the snippet shows no disease or pest resistance entry for it. -- https://www.manage.gov.in/publications/eBooks/Climate%20Smart%20Soybean%20Production%20Technologies.pdf (table entry only)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Raj Soya-18 (Pragya) is listed with 2017 notification and a medium maturity class. -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf
- The same SOPA table gives a maturity of 92 days for Raj Soya-18 (Pragya). -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf
- A seed dealer's listing (not an official source) describes "Raj Soya 18" as a new improved variety with a crop duration of 91 to 95 days and a plant height of 50 to 60 cm. Treat this as unverified. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/raj-soya-18-soyabean-seed-2851855763730.html
- No multi-location trial results or yield figures for this variety were found. The yield value in the SOPA table belongs to NRC 86, so I did not use it. -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage JSM 100 x JSM 66: No evidence found in search results. This comes only from the supplied variety record.
- Breeding line codes, breeding method, QTL and marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The DOD notification list gives the release centre as RAK College of Agriculture, RVSKVV, Sehore. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx
- Breeder names: No evidence found. The "Richa-2000" page (ip4kids.in) describes a different variety and was discarded.
- ICAR-IISR lists Raj Soya-18 (Pragya) among its notified varieties, but it does not say this variety came from IISR breeding. -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/varieties.html
- ICAR-NSRI lists the variety with a 2017 notification and Madhya Pradesh adaptability, and says NSRI coordinates breeder seed production. This is a seed-chain listing, not a breeding credit. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level only: RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore, Madhya Pradesh (state-sector government institution). The ISTI portal gives the district as Sehore but the website field is blank. No email, phone or postal address was captured. -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/allstinstitutions/rak-college-agriculture-0
- No breeder email or phone found.
- ICAR-NSRI and IISR contact pages were not captured in the search output, so no phone, email or address is given for them. Their websites are icar-nsri.res.in and iisrindore.icar.gov.in.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The SSRD 2014 bulletin (ssrd.co.in) and the Legume Research drought paper do not name this variety in the captured text. Neither was attributed.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Private dealer: My Kisan Agro, 85 Harnawada, Jeeran, Neemuch 458441, Madhya Pradesh (contact name Jaswant Choudhary). The listing gives Raj Soya 18 seed at ₹70/kg in 30 kg minimum lots, marked "currently out of stock," with the page dated about 1,669 days ago. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/raj-soya-18-soyabean-seed-2851855763730.html
- Breeder seed chain: ICAR-IISR lists the variety in its breeder-seed production table. -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/varieties.html
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK and SAU seed sales: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Madhya Pradesh is the state under which Raj Soya-18 appears in the DOD list of varieties notified under the Seeds Act from 2008 to 2019. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx
- ICAR-NSRI lists Madhya Pradesh as the adaptability area. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Raj Soya-24 (RVS 2002-4), Soybean

Search limit note: the search tool hit its usage cap during my second pass, so I could not re-open the full IISR page or run further queries. Four searches ran, but I saw only the truncated snippets from them. Findings below are limited to what those snippets showed, and most headings have little or no verified evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page on disease or pest resistance for this variety was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for this variety were returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage "JP 120 X JS 335" and breeding-line code "RVS 2002-4" come from the input record only; I did not verify them against a source. No QTL, marker or genome study was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (Indore) varieties page lists "Raj Soya-24 (RVS 2002-4)" with year of notification 2017 -- https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/varieties.html. The snippet did not name a breeder. The institution named in the input (RVSKW, Gwalior, RAK College of Agriculture) was not confirmed by any returned page. No breeder name was found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found for a breeder. The IISR varieties page (https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/varieties.html) is the only institute page returned; I did not extract its address, email or phone from the snippet. Verify contacts on that page directly.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for this variety. The one paper returned, "Pratap Raj 24 (RKS 24) -A High Yielding Variety of Soybean for Rajasthan" (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393045215_Pratap_Raj_24_RKS_24_-A_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Soybean_for_Rajasthan), concerns a different variety and is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The search returned only the excluded Pratap Raj 24 page. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh come from the input record only. The IISR snippet did not show state recommendations, so this is unverified.

Gaps to close next: open https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/varieties.html for the full notification entry, breeder and contact details. Then check the CSC/ICAR notification minutes and seednet.gov.in for the Seednet name "Raj Soya-24 (RVS 2002-4)", and search KrishiKosh and the AICRP on Soybean reports for trial and disease data.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: Regional Agricultural Research Station, Anakapalle, Visakhapatnam; ANGRAU, Guntur (Andhra Pradesh)
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Suitable for assured irrigated, limited irrigated, late planted, rainfed and red rot prone areas.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: 1.	Semi erect, greenish yellow cane with black waxy coating. Ivory marks present. 2.	Green leaves, green leaf sheath with purple blotches with white waxy coating.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: 2009A 252 was found to be moderately resistant to red pathotypes, Cf 419 Cf 671 and Cf 997 when inoculated through plug and nodal methods. It was also found to be moderately resistant to wilt and resistant to YLD under natural conditions and moderately susceptible to smut at Regional Agricultural Research Station, Anakapalle during 2017-18.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: The clone 2009A 252 was screened against incidence of major pests from 2017-18 to 2018-19 in ZVT’s. It was found to be moderately susceptible reaction for ESB, highly susceptible reaction for INB and least susceptible for scale insect pest.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Farm yard manure @ 25 tonnes per hectare or press mud cake @ 12 tonnes per hectare in the last ploughing, 112 kg nitrogen (pocket application) has to be applied in two equal splits doses at 45 and 90

disease_resistance.summary: Smut: resistant, per the VSI variety sheet. Moderately resistant to a further disease, but the disease name is truncated in the source. Good ratooning and resistance to foliar diseases, per the VSI 42nd Annual Report 2017-18. The input record also lists smut resistance. Woolly aphid: not attributed. The ResearchGate screening paper mentions VSI clones but does not name CoVSI 03102 in the retrieved text.

pest_resistance.summary: Borers: moderately resistant, per the VSI 42nd Annual Report 2017-18. The input record describes it as less susceptible to internode borer. Sparse flowering is listed as a trait in the VSI variety sheet. Woolly aphid: not attributed to this variety (see disease_resistance).

EVIDENCE DIGEST: CoVSI 03102 (Sugarcane)

Searches run: 4. Name used: "CoVSI 03102" for the CSC name and the Seednet name, which are the same here. Seednet pages were not found, so the Seednet name is not independently confirmed. Most relevant pages are VSI (Vasantdada Sugar Institute) documents. Some results were discarded as off-target, including a Barbados genotype paper that is only partly relevant, a woolly-aphid paper that names other clones, and an ASTI directory entry for SBI Coimbatore.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought tolerant, with good ratooning and resistance to foliar diseases, per the VSI 42nd Annual Report 2017-18 -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/downloads/42nd-annualreport-2017-18.pdf
- Suitable for high-rainfall zones per the VSI variety sheet; the same sheet's stress wording is truncated, so no further stress claims are made from it -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/sugarcane_breeding_gallery/CoVSI%2003102.pdf
- No salinity, flood, submergence or heat evidence found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to smut and moderately resistant to a further disease (name truncated in source), per the VSI variety sheet -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/sugarcane_breeding_gallery/CoVSI%2003102.pdf
- Moderately resistant to borers, per the VSI 42nd Annual Report 2017-18 -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/downloads/42nd-annualreport-2017-18.pdf
- Sparse flowering is listed as a trait, per the VSI variety sheet -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/sugarcane_breeding_gallery/CoVSI%2003102.pdf
- Woolly aphid resistance: the ResearchGate screening paper mentions VSI clones but does not name CoVSI 03102 in the retrieved text, so it is not attributed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263655509_Screening_of_sugarcane_clones_for_resistance_against_sugarcane_woolly_aphid_Ceratovaccuna_lanigera_Zhtner

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Midlate maturity, erect growth, high yield and high sugar, per the VSI variety sheet -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/sugarcane_breeding_gallery/CoVSI%2003102.pdf
- Pre-season cane yield 138.27 t/ha and sugar yield 20.65 t/ha; suru cane yield 126.20 t/ha and sugar yield 18.79 t/ha -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/sugarcane_breeding_gallery/CoVSI%2003102.pdf
- Multi-location and farm trial data (Vasantdada, Naigaon, Lonarwadi, Patharwala, Nagpur, Manjari) are in a VSI 2023-24 report; the table extract does not fully show the yield values for this clone -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/annual_report/VSI%2048th%20Annual%20Report%202023-24%20(1)%20Original%20(1).pdf
- Cane yield 108.11 t/ha in a comparison row (column meanings not fully clear in the extract) -- https://vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/annual_report/VSI%20Annual%20Report%20A_2020_Web.pdf
- A micropropagation protocol for CoVSI 03102 is mentioned -- https://vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/annual_report/VSI%20Annual%20Report%20A_2020_Web.pdf
- Ongoing breeding programme combining cane yield and sucrose with drought and salinity emphasis, with CoVSI 03102 among the varieties tested -- https://www.vsisugar.com/sugarcane_breeding/sugarcane_breed_research.php

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: 80 R 41 GC (General Collection), per the VSI variety sheet -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/sugarcane_breeding_gallery/CoVSI%2003102.pdf
- CoVSI 03102 is used as a parent: VSI 145-2 = CoVSI 03102 x Co 97015, per the VSI 2020 annual report -- https://vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/annual_report/VSI%20Annual%20Report%20A_2020_Web.pdf
- Breeding method: hybridisation and clonal selection through VSI nursery and trial stages (not described in detail for this clone) -- https://www.vsisugar.com/sugarcane_breeding/sugarcane_breed_research.php
- No QTL, marker, or genome resource evidence found for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Vasantdada Sugar Institute (VSI), Pune, per the VSI variety sheet and the VSI website -- https://www.vsisugar.com/sugarcane_breeding/varities.php
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. None of the retrieved pages names a breeder for CoVSI 03102.
- Station: VSI Pune and locations, per the VSI breeding research page -- https://www.vsisugar.com/sugarcane_breeding/sugarcane_breed_research.php

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute website only: https://www.vsisugar.com (from the VSI pages above). No official email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for VSI was found in the retrieved text, so none is given.
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Vasantdada Sugar Institute (2018). 42nd Annual Report 2017-18 (includes CoVSI 03102 characterisation and release context). Annual Report -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/downloads/42nd-annualreport-2017-18.pdf
- Vasantdada Sugar Institute (2020). Annual Report 2020 (trial and parentage data; micropropagation). Annual Report -- https://vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/annual_report/VSI%20Annual%20Report%20A_2020_Web.pdf
- Vasantdada Sugar Institute (2022). 46th Annual Report 2021-22 (CoVSI 03102 listed in a seed/area table). Annual Report -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/annual_report/Annual%20Report%20VSI%2046th%202021_22.pdf
- Vasantdada Sugar Institute (2023-24). 48th Annual Report (MLT trial table). Annual Report -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/annual_report/VSI%2048th%20Annual%20Report%202023-24%20(1)%20Original%20(1).pdf
- Unnamed authors (year unknown). Quality evaluation of sugar cane genotypes grown in Barbados towards extending the harvest season. ResearchGate preprint -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/282576443_Quality_evaluation_of_sugar_cane_genotypes_grown_in_Barbados_towards_extending_the_harvest_season. Note: this paper mentions CoVSI 03102 as a clone that was to be "released shortly". Its authorship and date are not confirmed from the snippet.
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis, or AICRP report specifically on CoVSI 03102 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet listing: No evidence found. No Seednet page was returned for this variety or the crop name.
- VSI 46th Annual Report 2021-22 lists CoVSI 03102 in a table with an area figure of 1.23 ha; the context (seed multiplication or trial) is not clear from the extract -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/annual_report/Annual%20Report%20VSI%2046th%202021_22.pdf
- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Maharashtra, per the input record and the VSI sources. The VSI 42nd Annual Report 2017-18 presents it as higher-yielding than Co 86032 in Maharashtra -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/downloads/42nd-annualreport-2017-18.pdf

DISCREPANCY TO NOTE
- Release year: the input says 2018, but the VSI variety sheet says 2016. The VSI 42nd Annual Report 2017-18 refers to a 2018 presentation at the Joint Agresco and a release-committee step, which is consistent with the input's 2018. Verify against the official CSC/Gazette notification before finalising.

drought.details: Krishi Jagran reports that CoPk 05191 ranked first across 23 locations (mean cane yield 81.12 t/ha) and that its stay-green habit gave it tolerance to drought and waterlogging. A review on abiotic stress breeding lists CoPk 05191 (Pratap Ganna-1, Kota Agricultural Research Station entry) as tolerant to drought. The sources describe tolerance qualitatively, without a graded rating, so 'medium' reflects the evidence level rather than a measured score.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources.

flood.details: Waterlogging tolerance is reported, attributed to the stay-green habit (Krishi Jagran) and listed as tolerance to waterlogging in the Kota Agricultural Research Station entry of a breeding review. The sources do not give a graded level or a mechanism beyond stay-green habit, so 'medium' is a qualitative mapping. This is recorded under flood because waterlogging is the closest category in the schema.

disease_resistance.summary: Krishi Jagran states that CoPk 05191 showed tolerance to stem rot, smut and wilt. No evidence for red rot was found in the digest for this variety. The input record's disease reaction (MR/R to red rot) refers to CoS 91230, a different variety, and was excluded.

pest_resistance.summary: Pest/insect resistance: No evidence found for this variety in the searched sources. The input record's pest reaction (tolerance to shoot borer, top borer and stalk borer) refers to CoS 91230, a different variety, and was excluded.

agronomic_details.yield: Krishi Jagran reports a mean cane yield of 81.12 t/ha across 23 locations, ranked first, and a mean juice sucrose of 17.06%. The input record gives an average yield of 83 MT/ha, which differs from the 81.12 t/ha figure and is not reconciled by the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Ranked first across 23 locations (Krishi Jagran). Stay-green habit is reported as the basis for stress tolerance. No further stability analysis found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Input record: recommended for Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Central Western Uttar Pradesh under normal irrigated conditions (not independently confirmed in the searches). Digest evidence: Rajasthan-based trials at Kota and a coastal-condition study (Pusa-affiliated institute) that reports responses under coastal climate; the coastal study's snippet also mentions Rajasthan trials.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) ResearchGate study (Ramkishan Meena and B.S. et al.): ethrel and gibberellic acid applied to CoPk 05191 (Pratap Ganna 1) in a randomized block design, harvested after one full year; growth and yield results not stated in the snippet. (2) Sugarcane Research Institute, Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University, Pusa: plant growth regulator modes on CoPk 05191 under coastal conditions gave milleable cane yield 22.74% to 24.46% above control; the snippet also mentions Rajasthan trials. (3) A study on altering shoot architecture through genetic engineering describes an ethrel and GA3 trial on CoPk 05191 at the Kota research station; results not stated in the snippet. (4) Krishi Jagran 23-location trial: mean cane yield 81.12 t/ha, ranked first, mean juice sucrose 17.06%.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pratap Ganna-1 (variety_name) / Pratap Ganna-1 (CoPk-05191) (seednet_variety_name), sugarcane

Note on names: the searches returned evidence under the code CoPk 05191 and the name Pratap Ganna-1 (or Pratap Ganna 1), so both names refer to the same entry. No page named the Seednet portal entry itself.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- A Krishi Jagran article reports that CoPk 05191 ranked first across 23 locations with a mean cane yield of 81.12 t/ha, and that its stay-green habit gave it tolerance to waterlogging and drought -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- A review on current breeding and genomic approaches for abiotic stress lists the Kota Agricultural Research Station entry CoPk 05191 (Pratap Ganna-1) as tolerant to drought and waterlogging and as a good ratooner -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345414344_Current_breeding_and_genomic_approaches_to_enhance_the_cane_and_sugar_productivity_under_abiotic_stress_conditions

DISEASE AND PEST
- The same Krishi Jagran article states that CoPk 05191 showed tolerance to stem rot, smut and wilt -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- Pest/insect resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A ResearchGate study (Ramkishan Meena and B.S. ... et al.) tested ethrel and gibberellic acid on CoPk 05191 (Pratap Ganna 1) in a randomized block design, harvested after one full year -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392770729_Studies_on_Effect_of_ethrel_and_Gibberellic_Acid_on_Growth_and_Yield_of_Sugarcane_variety_CoPk_05191_Pratap_Ganna_1_with_Recommended_Agronomic_Practices
- A ResearchGate study from Sugarcane Research Institute, Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University, Pusa, reports that CoPk 05191 (Pratap Ganna 1) responded to plant growth regulator modes under coastal conditions, with milleable cane yield 22.74%–24.46% above control. The snippet also mentions Rajasthan trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364740682_Enhancing_cane_and_sugar_productivity_applying_variable_modes_of_plant_growth_regulators_in_sugarcane_Saccharum_sp_complex_cultivation_under_coastal_climatic_conditions_of_India
- Krishi Jagran lists the 23-location mean of 81.12 t/ha and a mean juice sucrose of 17.06% -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line code CoPk 05191 is confirmed by several sources, and a review lists it among conventionally bred sugarcane varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370471892_SMART_Plant_Breeding_from_Pre-genomic_to_Post-genomic_Era_for_Developing_Climate-Resilient_Cereals
- Parentage (Co 775 x Co 1148): No evidence found in the searches; the parentage is only from the input record.
- QTL, marker, or genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder or scientist names for this variety: No evidence found.
- Developing institution: the input record names Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture & Technology. The search results did not independently confirm this. The Kota Agricultural Research Station is named as the location where the variety was evaluated/listed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345414344_Current_breeding_and_genomic_approaches_to_enhance_the_cane_and_sugar_productivity_under_abiotic_stress_conditions
- Release or notification details (CSC/Central Sub-Committee minutes, year 2013): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Names, roles, emails, phones, addresses, or institute contact page: No evidence found. No search returned an institute or breeder contact page for this variety.

PUBLICATIONS
- Ramkishan Meena and B.S. ... (year not shown in snippet). Studies on Effect of ethrel and Gibberellic Acid on Growth and Yield of Sugarcane variety "CoPk 05191" (Pratap Ganna 1) with Recommended Agronomic Practices. ResearchGate (journal not shown) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392770729_Studies_on_Effect_of_ethrel_and_Gibberellic_Acid_on_Growth_and_Yield_of_Sugarcane_variety_CoPk_05191_Pratap_Ganna_1_with_Recommended_Agronomic_Practices
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Enhancing cane and sugar productivity applying variable modes of plant growth regulators in sugarcane (Saccharum sp. complex) cultivation under coastal climatic conditions of India. ResearchGate (journal not shown) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364740682_Enhancing_cane_and_sugar_productivity_applying_variable_modes_of_plant_growth_regulators_in_sugarcane_Saccharum_sp_complex_cultivation_under_coastal_climatic_conditions_of_India
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Altering sugarcane shoot architecture through genetic engineering: prospects for increasing cane and sugar yield. ResearchGate (the snippet describes an ethrel and GA3 trial on CoPk 05191 at the Kota research station; journal not shown) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/43481399_Altering_sugarcane_shoot_architecture_through_genetic_engineering_prospects_for_increasing_cane_and_sugar_yield
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Current breeding and genomic approaches to enhance the cane and sugar productivity under abiotic stress conditions. ResearchGate (journal not shown) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345414344_Current_breeding_and_genomic_approaches_to_enhance_the_cane_and_sugar_productivity_under_abiotic_stress_conditions
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports, and journal DOIs: No evidence found in the searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales: No evidence found. Seednet was not separately searched; the query budget was used.
- Results that were discarded as not about this variety: a Uttar Pradesh "Smart Ganna App" news item (general seed-availability tool, no variety named); Indiamart traders offering other varieties (15201, 16231, 14201, 16202); an Oct 2023 news item on ten new sugarcane releases that does not name this variety in the snippet.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The input record lists Uttar Pradesh, Uttrakhand, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan. The searches did not confirm this from an official notification. Only Rajasthan-based trials (Kota) appeared in the results.

GAPS AND LIMITS
- Four web searches were run, which is the maximum allowed, so there was no fourth search for the Seednet portal, KrishiKosh, or institute contact pages. The Seednet listing, release notification, breeder names, contacts, and parentage remain unverified and need a targeted check on seednet.gov.in, the MPUAT site, and KrishiKosh.
- Citation markers are omitted because the search output did not give sentence indices, so each claim is paraphrased with its source URL.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Sahaj-3 (CoS 12232), Sugarcane

Name note: "Sahaj-3" (variety_name) and "Sahaj-3 (CoS- 12232)" (Seednet name) were both searched. The evidence found uses "Sahaj-3 (CoS 12232)" or "CoS 12232 (Sahaj-3)". The Seednet portal itself did not appear in any search result.

Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers, seed availability). Results were mostly unrelated pages, and the first query returned only an unrelated Louisiana guide.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. None of the retrieved pages reports drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence reaction for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for this variety. One retrieved table headed "Reaction to red rot" lists varieties, but no Sahaj-3 entry is shown in the retrieved text (https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/121684/46453/317178). A generic line about improved sugarcane hybrids being susceptible to internode borer does not name this variety, so I have not attributed it.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Released variety, developed by UPCSR Shahjahanpur, in the mid-late group for the North West zone, identified in 2019; mean cane yield 88.86 t/ha, CCS yield 11.21 t/ha, sucrose 18.18% in juice -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm (also http://www.iisr.nic.in/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm)
Suitable for medium and high fertility soils under irrigated conditions; average cane yield 88.86 t/ha in the same listing -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/121684/46453/317178
Mid-late maturing variety listed alongside CoLk 11206 in a sub-tropical trial summary; the snippet gives a sucrose figure for CoS 12232 (15.35% in April) but the table context is incomplete -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355163894_Suitable_sugarcane_varieties_for_sustainable_sugar_recovery_e-Proceedings_of_79_th_Annual_Convention_of_STAI_70_-76_2021_SUGARCANE_AGRICULTURE-70_SUITABLE_SUGARCANE_VARIETIES_FOR_SUSTAINABLE_SUGAR_REC
Listed among varieties in a current-status review of Indian sugarcane agriculture -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353774930_Current_status_of_sugarcane_agriculture_and_sugar_industry_in_the_World_with_special_reference_to_India

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Variety code CoS 12232 -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
Parentage CoS 95255 x CoS 510 -- supplied in the brief only; not confirmed by any retrieved page.
Breeding method, QTL/marker studies, genome resources -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: UPCSR (U.P. Council of Sugarcane Research), Shahjahanpur -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
Lead breeder or scientist names -- No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for UPCSR Shahjahanpur or for the breeder appeared in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not captured in retrieved text (2022). Sugarcane Jaggery: An alternative of sugar for healthy living. Indian Farming 72(1): 11-13 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/121684/46453/317178 (Sahaj-3 appears in a variety table in this article)

Proceedings of 79th Annual Convention of STAI, pp. 70-76 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355163894_Suitable_sugarcane_varieties_for_sustainable_sugar_recovery_e-Proceedings_of_79_th_Annual_Convention_of_STAI_70_-76_2021_SUGARCANE_AGRICULTURE-70_SUITABLE_SUGARCANE_VARIETIES_FOR_SUSTAINABLE_SUGAR_REC (CoS 12232 appears in trial tables)

KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports specific to this variety -- No evidence found beyond the AICRP varietal development page above.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was retrieved. Seednet was not returned by any search.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, Rajasthan, and Central and Western Uttar Pradesh -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/121684/46453/317178 (matches the brief)

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Resistant to white rust and staghead, moderately resistant to downy and powdery mildew.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features:
Highly responsive to fertilizers and suitable for timely sowing under rainfed conditions.
Seed rate 4-5 kg/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
Plant medium tall with profuse branching
1. Stem: cylindrical, light green, slightly pubescent, non pigmented at the base.
2. Leaf: lyrate pinnatipartite, glabrous on upper epidermis and slightly pubescent on lower epidermis.
3. Flower: Calyx-greenish yellow, corolla creamish yellow and non hairy.
4. Siliqua cylindrical two valved with prominent flat apical beak non pubescent.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Fairly tolerant to moistures stress and lesser susceptible to biotic stress.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to white rust and staghead, moderately resistant to downy and powdery mildew.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Comparatively less attacked by aphids as compared to existing checks.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Under rainfed conditions, basal application of 30 kg N and 20 kg P2O5, is recommended for taramira. Being an oilseed crop, it also responds to sulphur fertilization. Application of 40 kg S/ha

Number of locules: 4-6, - Fruits/clusters: 10-35, - Fruits/plant: 6.4cm x 6.2 cm ; 100 seed wt. : 0.31 g.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant for fruit rot & seedling rot complex.

seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Tested under rainfed condition in SVT at hills as well as in AICRP-RM trials at seven AICRO centers in Zone-V.  In IVT toria (rainfed) this strain out yield PT-303 (NC) by 8.62% and Panchali (ZC) by 8.05%.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Tested in AICRP-RM pathology trials against different diseases.  It is similar to check variety PT-303 in reaction against Alternaria blight and Downy mildew diseases.  It is resistant to white rust disease on leaf both at 75DAS and 100 DAS.  Less susceptible to Sclerotinia rot than PT-303 and moderately resistant to bacterial rot.

seednet_fields.Parentage: The proposed variety has been developed from OEX 05.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Assam and Maharashtra
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: BCCO 6 outyielded both the checks JRO 524 and JRO 8432 by 4% in adaptive trials at farmers field in Rahuri, Katihar and Kalyani
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Leaf lamina green but leaf petiole, leaf stipule and stem shows red colour pigmentation.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Under field condition it showed 20% less incidence of stem weevil at 90 days as compared to the checks JRO 524 and JRO 8432.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The proposed variety was found to be tolerant to stem weevil at 60 to 90 days during the time of peak infestation.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: It showed less incidence of stem rot, the major disease compared to check variety JRO 8432 at 60 days 27%) and 90 days (15%) during the time of peak infestation.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 80:40:40 N, P2O5 and K2O per ha applied as ½ N + full P2O5 and K2O as basal, 1/4N at 35-40 DAS and ¼ N at 65-70 DAS.

drought.details: No evidence found. The digest reports that searches returned only heat-tolerance and yield pages for this variety. The variety is described for late-sown irrigated conditions, so drought performance is not established.

heat.details: Terminal heat tolerance under late-sown irrigated conditions is the main reported trait, and the variety is named 'tolerant to terminal heat stress conditions of Central Zone'. Heat tolerance is linked to a 31.8% rise in grains per ear and a 7.6% rise in 1000-grain weight over checks (academia.edu source). The CSC release data give a comparable range of 10.39 to 24.13% for grains per earhead and 3.6 to 7.9% for 1000-grain weight over checks. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Terminal heat tolerance under late-sown irrigated conditions is the main reported trait for HI 1634 (Pusa Ahilya), which is the seednet name and effectively the same as the CSC name "HI 1634 (PusaAhilya)" with a space added. The Journal of Cereal Research paper reports this, and that paper gives 51.6 q/ha as the average yield -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/view/118676
- Heat tolerance is linked to a 31.8% rise in grains per ear and a 7.6% rise in 1000-grain weight over checks -- https://www.academia.edu/94596176/HI_1634_Pusa_Ahilya_high_yielding_bread_wheat_variety_tolerant_to_terminal_heat_stress_conditions_of_Central_Zone
- Drought, salinity, flood, and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned only heat-tolerance and yield pages for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Seedling and adult-plant resistance to stem and leaf rust pathotypes virulent in India, postulated to carry Sr31 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/view/118676
- Seedling (all-stage) resistance to all 27 test pathotypes each of stem and leaf rust, with good field resistance; good resistance reported to leaf blight, Karnal bunt, Fusarium head blight, loose smut, foot rot and flag smut -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432282_IARI_Indore_Madhya_Bharat_Wheat_News_Vol_62
- Resistance to black/brown rust and Karnal bunt is reported by a trade news site -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/wheat-variety-pusa-ahilya-hi-1634/
- The IARI Regional Station page lists resistance to stem and leaf rust, flag smut, leaf blight, root rot and Karnal bunt -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- A separate page lists resistance to all three rusts, Karnal bunt, powdery mildew, flag smut and foot rot. This page is a mixed-content page, so treat it with caution -- https://translate.google.com/translate?u=https%3A%2F%2Fztmbpd.iari.res.in%2Ftechnologies%2Fvarietieshybrids%2Fcereals%2Fwheat%2F&hl=hi&sl=en&tl=hi&client=srp
- Stored-grain pest: the rice weevil study names HI 1544 and GW 322 as least susceptible but does not name HI 1634, so no evidence for this variety -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12511555/
- Insect resistance (field pests): the CSC release paper says it was tested against major insect pests in AICRP nurseries, but the result text is not retrievable -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Divya-Ambati-2/publication/366684417_HI_1634_Pusa_Ahilya_high_yielding_bread_wheat_variety_tolerant_to_terminal_heat_stress_conditions_of_Central_Zone/links/63ae7ec9a03100368a3b4cbf/HI-1634-Pusa-Ahilya-high-yielding-bread-wheat-variety-tolerant-to-terminal-heat-stress-conditions-of-Central-Zone.pdf?origin=scientificContributions

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release: notified by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards (S.O. 500 E, 29.01.2021) for late-sown irrigated conditions in the central zone -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/view/118676
- Mean yield 51.6 q/ha (weighted mean across 39 locations), potential yield 70.6 q/ha at Gwalior in rabi 2019-20 -- https://www.academia.edu/104746552/HI_1634_Pusa_Ahilya_high_yielding_bread_wheat_variety_tolerant_to_terminal_heat_stress_conditions_of_Central_Zone
- Yield advantage over checks HD 2932, HD 2864, MP 3336 and MP 4010 of 3.6%, 4.9%, 4.9% and 8.9% respectively -- https://www.academia.edu/104746552/HI_1634_Pusa_Ahilya_high_yielding_bread_wheat_variety_tolerant_to_terminal_heat_stress_conditions_of_Central_Zone
- Ranked first for yield six times across three years of testing -- https://www.academia.edu/94596176/HI_1634_Pusa_Ahilya_high_yielding_bread_wheat_variety_tolerant_to_terminal_heat_stress_conditions_of_Central_Zone
- Maturity CONFLICT: 142 days on a mixed-content page; 110–115 days on the Seed Trikuta listing and a Hindi seed-seller page. The IARI RS page gives an average of 29 q/ha and potential of 44 q/ha, which conflicts with the 51.6 q/ha figure and is probably a different entry, so do not use it -- https://translate.google.com/translate?u=https%3A%2F%2Fztmbpd.iari.res.in%2Ftechnologies%2Fvarietieshybrids%2Fcereals%2Fwheat%2F&hl=hi&sl=en&tl=hi&client=srp ; https://www.trikutaseeds.com/wheat-seed ; https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Quality: grain hardness index 81.4, chapatti score 7.86, biscuit score 6.73, test weight 81.8 kg/hl, sedimentation value 44.8 ml -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432282_IARI_Indore_Madhya_Bharat_Wheat_News_Vol_62
- Micronutrients and protein: a seed listing gives iron around 38 ppm, zinc around 37 ppm and protein above 12%. This is a commercial listing, so treat it as secondary -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/hi-1634-pusa-ahilya-wheat-seed-2852520489548.html
- A 2022 Journal of Cereal Research paper reports the variety's mean yield as 50.88 q/ha against the 51.6 q/ha figure in the release abstract. The two figures come from different analyses -- https://www.academia.edu/94596176/HI_1634_Pusa_Ahilya_high_yielding_bread_wheat_variety_tolerant_to_terminal_heat_stress_conditions_of_Central_Zone

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: GW 322/PBW 498 cross, made in 2008-09 at the IARI Regional Station, Indore -- https://www.academia.edu/104746552/HI_1634_Pusa_Ahilya_high_yielding_bread_wheat_variety_tolerant_to_terminal_heat_stress_conditions_of_Central_Zone
- Breeding method: modified pedigree method -- https://www.academia.edu/104746552/HI_1634_Pusa_Ahilya_high_yielding_bread_wheat_variety_tolerant_to_terminal_heat_stress_conditions_of_Central_Zone
- Breeding-line code: HI 1634 (Pusa Ahilya) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/view/118676
- Stem-rust gene: Sr31 is postulated for the virulent pathotypes tested, not confirmed as a gene in this variety -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/view/118676
- QTL and marker studies: No evidence found.
- Genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead developer: Dr Jang Bahadur Singh, Head and Principal Scientist (Plant Breeding / Wheat Improvement), ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Indore -- https://www.iari.res.in/sci_db/sci_details.php?scid=dDY5NGZTaFhBVDBnek9Qd1AxRFdOQT09
- The IARI scientist page credits Jang Bahadur Singh as lead developer of HI 1634 (Pusa Ahilya), CZ, released in 2022 for late-sown irrigated conditions -- https://www.iari.res.in/sci_db/sci_details.php?scid=dDY5NGZTaFhBVDBnek9Qd1AxRFdOQT09
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute, Regional Station, Indore -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432282_IARI_Indore_Madhya_Bharat_Wheat_News_Vol_62
- Co-authors on the Journal of Cereal Research paper: Sakuru Venkata Sai Prasad, Divya Ambati and Rahul Madhav Rao Phuke, with Jang Bahad
