search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: K-1317 (Wheat)
Names checked: variety_name "K-1317" (CSC minutes) and seednet_variety_name "K-1317" are the same string. Seednet code A0104547 and parentage K0307/K9162 did not appear in any result. The Seednet portal itself was not returned by any search.
Searches run: 4 (variety/release; breeder/institute; research; seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Water-stress study: K 1317 was one of six wheat genotypes (with HI 1612, HD 2888, C 306, K 8027, HD 3171) allotted to sub-plots in a field experiment under moisture-stress main plots; the paper's title and authors were not retrieved -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-5545
- No other evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to K-1317.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. Searches returned no rust, blight, smut or insect reaction data for K-1317.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rainfed timely-sown trial (North Eastern Plain Zone): K 1317 appears as the "qualifying variety" check, with 42.87 q/ha, against HD 3171 at 35.06 q/ha. This is evidence from the HD 3171 release proposal, not a K-1317 trial report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331036676_Wheat_Variety_HD_3171_for_Rainfed_timely_sown_conditions_of_North_Eastern_Plain_Zone_comprising_of_India
- No evidence found for maturity duration, plant height, or multi-location yield trials specific to K-1317.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for parentage (K0307/K9162), breeding-line code, breeding method, QTL, markers or genome resources. The parentage in the input record was not confirmed by any retrieved source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- ICAR-IIWBR Annual Report 2017-18 lists K1317 among seven wheat varieties released by the Central Sub-Committee on Crops. This confirms the release but names no breeder and no developing institution -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sendhil-Ramadas/publication/334083251_ICAR-IIWBR_Annual_Report_2017-18/links/5d15b62e92851cf440518d6f/ICAR-IIWBR-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf
- The institution in the input record (C.S. Azad University of Agriculture & Technology) was not confirmed by any search result. No breeder name was found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found.
- Institute-level: the only institute page returned was ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal-132001, India, from the annual report header. It is not the developing institution named in the input record and I have not treated it as K-1317's contact -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sendhil-Ramadas/publication/334083251_ICAR-IIWBR_Annual_Report_2017-18/links/5d15b62e92851cf440518d6f/ICAR-IIWBR-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf
- No email, phone or postal address for CSAUAT Kanpur was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not retrieved (year not confirmed). Wheat Variety HD 3171 for Rainfed timely sown conditions of North Eastern Plain Zone comprising of India. Release proposal, which names K 1317 as qualifying check -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331036676_Wheat_Variety_HD_3171_for_Rainfed_timely_sown_conditions_of_North_Eastern_Plain_Zone_comprising_of_India
- ICAR-IIWBR (2017-18). ICAR-IIWBR Annual Report 2017-18. Institute report recording the release of K1317 -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sendhil-Ramadas/publication/334083251_ICAR-IIWBR_Annual_Report_2017-18/links/5d15b62e92851cf440518d6f/ICAR-IIWBR-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf
- Authors and title not retrieved (year not confirmed). Water-stress wheat genotype study including K 1317. Indian Journal of Agricultural Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-5545
- No KrishiKosh thesis, DOI or AICRP report found for K-1317.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Private dealer listing: Natural K 1317 Wheat Seed, sold by Mahoba Bundelkhand Herbal Agro Producer Company Limited at ₹3500/quintal, 40 kg PP bag -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/k-1317-wheat-seed-22816018673.html

drought.details: The digest reports that DBW 187 was ranked as tolerant to both heat and drought stress in a backcross-inbred-line (BIL) QTL mapping study. No quantitative drought measurement is given. The digest also states that no drought-specific evidence was found in the searches. Level is assigned as medium because the only evidence is a qualitative tolerant ranking. Under late sowing, the variety showed less yield reduction than the check DBW 39, which is consistent with a stress-adapted profile but is not a drought measurement.

heat.details: CSC record: heat sensitivity index (HSI) of 1.05, described as better tolerance to heat stress. Under late-sown conditions the variety performed better than all checks, with minimum reduction in grain yield, grain number and 1000-grain weight, indicating better adaptation to heat stress. In the 2021-22 AICRP demonstrations under heat, DBW 187 gave a 3.6% yield gain over HD-3086. It was ranked as tolerant to both heat and drought in a BIL study. The digest does not state the genetic basis of heat tolerance.

salinity.details: No evidence found for this variety in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood or waterlogging tolerance in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Foliar disease resistance (CSC record): resistant to foliar diseases under natural and artificial epiphytotic conditions. Resistance to rusts, particularly brown rust, is useful under timely-sown conditions in NEPZ. Race-specific APR responses to brown rust races 77-5, 77-9 and 104-2 were recorded across locations. Seedling resistance tests (SRT) indicated resistance to the prevalent brown rust race 77-7, and to races 77-8, 77-9, 77-10, 104-2, 104-3, 104B, 162-2 and 162A. Yellow and brown rust: listed as resistant in two commercial sources. Stripe and leaf rust: resistant, with high resistance to wheat blast, moderate resistance to Karnal bunt and loose smut tolerance in one commercial source. Wheat blast: high resistance reported in a seed-production case study. Multiple disease resistance: described in a bread-wheat evaluation paper. CONFLICT: the commercial source listing stripe and leaf rust resistance does not match the yellow and brown rust listing from the other sources; the rust type should be checked against the CSC record. The CSC record indicates resistance to brown, black and yellow rusts.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports no evidence for insect pest resistance. The CSC record lists pest reaction as Unknown.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 19.5 q/acre (the unit field also reads Kg/Ha, so the basis is unclear). Digest figures: NWPZ two-year average 61.28 q/ha, above checks HD 2967 and HD 3086. NEPZ average 48.8 q/ha. NWPZ average 61.3 q/ha. Other reported averages: 75.5 q/ha (north-western plains source) and 60.3 q/ha (Central Zone source). Potential yields reported: 64.7 q/ha (NEPZ), 96.6 q/ha (NWPZ, two sources), 75.4 q/ha (Central Zone). These figures conflict across sources.
agronomic_details.stability: Higher yielding than all checks under late-sown conditions in agronomic trials (CSC record). Under late sowing it showed less yield reduction than DBW 39 and had the smallest reduction in grain yield, grain number and 1000-grain weight among the entries compared. Under heat, a 3.6% gain over HD-3086 was recorded in the 2021-22 AICRP demonstrations. Stability across environments is not otherwise quantified in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: adapted to the North Eastern Plains Zone (NEPZ), including eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Assam and plains of other north-eastern states; timely-sown NEPZ conditions are referenced for brown rust. Recommended states in the CSC record are in the north-western and northern plains. The CSC record also states suitability for late-sown sugarcane, cotton and potato-wheat rotations. The digest's NEPZ and recommended-state references are not fully consistent, and this should be verified against the official record.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 110 To 140Days (CSC). Other digest sources: 120 days (ICAR crop profile and a commercial source), 140-145 days (commercial source), 148 days (global-agriculture source). Flowering: 77 days (ICAR crop profile) and 99 days (global-agriculture source).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf with good lodging tolerance (commercial/agri-news source, not an official record). Plant height about 100 cm (ICAR crop profile) and 105 cm (global-agriculture source). 1000-grain weight 58 g (commercial source) and 44 g (quality data in global-agriculture and Krishi Jagran sources); these conflict. Quality data: biscuit spread 8.6 cm, Fe 43.1 ppm, chapati score 7.7, protein 11.6%. Commercial agronomy: irrigated N:P:K 120:60:40 kg/ha, seed rate 100 kg/ha, 22.5 cm row spacing, sowing October-November (commercial source). ICAR demonstration (Gorakhpur): 150:60:40 kg NPK/ha and two irrigations. Early-sown high-input package: sowing 25 October to 5 November, 150% NPK, CCC and tebuconazole sprays. Morphology in the CSC record is listed as Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) 2021-22 AICRP heat demonstrations: 3.6% yield gain over HD-3086 under heat. (2) BIL study: ranked tolerant to heat and drought (no numeric result given). (3) Late sowing: less yield reduction than check DBW 39. (4) AICW&BIP coordinated trials: NIVT-1A 2015-16, AVT-I 2016-17, AVT-II 2017-18 (results are not given in the digest beyond the summaries above). (5) NWPZ two-year average 61.28 q/ha, above HD 2967 and HD 3086. (6) NEPZ average 48.8 q/ha with potential 64.7 q/ha. (7) NWPZ average 61.3 q/ha, potential 96.6 q/ha. (8) North-western plains source: average 75.5 q/ha, potential 96.6 q/ha. (9) Central Zone source: average 60.3 q/ha, potential 75.4 q/ha. (10) ICAR crop profile: flowering 77 days, maturity 120 days, height about 100 cm in NEPZ timely sowing. (11) SPL-HYPT 2018-19 performance table is cited, but its values are not included in the digest. (12) Early-sown high-input package: sowing 25 October to 5 November with 150% NPK, CCC and tebuconazole sprays (no yield result given). (13) Quality data as listed under plant_characteristics. Conflicting yield and maturity values across sources are noted above.

Potential yields reported: 64.7 q/ha (NEPZ), 96.6 q/ha (NWPZ, two sources), 75.4 q/ha (Central Zone). These figures conflict across sources.
agronomic_performance.stability: Higher yielding than all checks under late-sown conditions in agronomic trials (CSC record). Under late sowing it showed less yield reduction than DBW 39 and had the smallest reduction in grain yield, grain number and 1000-grain weight among the entries compared. Under heat, a 3.6% gain over HD-3086 was recorded in the 2021-22 AICRP demonstrations. Stability across environments is not otherwise quantified in the digest.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: CSC record: adapted to the North Eastern Plains Zone (NEPZ), including eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Assam and plains of other north-eastern states; timely-sown NEPZ conditions are referenced for brown rust. Recommended states in the CSC record are in the north-western and northern plains. The CSC record also states suitability for late-sown sugarcane, cotton and potato-wheat rotations. The digest's NEPZ and recommended-state references are not fully consistent, and this should be verified against the official record.
agronomic_performance.maturity_days: 110 To 140Days (CSC). Other digest sources: 120 days (ICAR crop profile and a commercial source), 140-145 days (commercial source), 148 days (global-agriculture source). Flowering: 77 days (ICAR crop profile) and 99 days (global-agriculture source).
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf with good lodging tolerance (commercial/agri-news source, not an official record). Plant height about 100 cm (ICAR crop profile) and 105 cm (global-agriculture source). 1000-grain weight 58 g (commercial source) and 44 g (quality data in global-agriculture and Krishi Jagran sources); these conflict. Quality data: biscuit spread 8.6 cm, Fe 43.1 ppm, chapati score 7.7, protein 11.6%. Commercial agronomy: irrigated N:P:K 120:60:40 kg/ha, seed rate 100 kg/ha, 22.5 cm row spacing, sowing October-November (commercial source). ICAR demonstration (Gorakhpur): 150:60:40 kg NPK/ha and two irrigations. Early-sown high-input package: sowing 25 October to 5 November, 150% NPK, CCC and tebuconazole sprays. Morphology in the CSC record is listed as Unknown.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) 2021-22 AICRP heat demonstrations: 3.6% yield gain over HD-3086 under heat. (2) BIL study: ranked tolerant to heat and drought (no numeric result given). (3) Late sowing: less yield reduction than check DBW 39. (4) AICW&BIP coordinated trials: NIVT-1A 2015-16, AVT-I 2016-17, AVT-II 2017-18 (results are not given in the digest beyond the summaries above). (5) NWPZ two-year average 61.28 q/ha, above HD 2967 and HD 3086. (6) NEPZ average 48.8 q/ha with potential 64.7 q/ha. (7) NWPZ average 61.3 q/ha, potential 96.6 q/ha. (8) North-western plains source: average 75.5 q/ha, potential 96.6 q/ha. (9) Central Zone source: average 60.3 q/ha, potential 75.4 q/ha. (10) ICAR crop profile: flowering 77 days, maturity 120 days, height about 100 cm in NEPZ timely sowing. (11) SPL-HYPT 2018-19 performance table is cited, but its values are not included in the digest. (12) Early-sown high-input package: sowing 25 October to 5 November with 150% NPK, CCC and tebuconazole sprays (no yield result given). (13) Quality data as listed under plant_characteristics. Conflicting yield and maturity values across sources are noted above.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Heat tolerance: in the 2021-22 AICRP demonstrations, DBW 187 (Karan Vandana) gave a 3.6% yield gain over HD-3086 under heat -- https://global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/heat-resistant-variety-of-wheat-dbw187-and-dbw222/ and https://agriculturepost.com/agri-research/india-promotes-heat-resistant-varieties-of-wheat-to-tackle-adverse-impact-of-heat-waves/
- Heat and drought: DBW187 was ranked as tolerant to both heat and drought stress in a backcross-inbred-line study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344377953_QTL_mapping_for_heat_tolerance_related_traits_using_backcross_inbred_lines_in_wheat_Triticum_aestivum_L
- Late sowing: showed less yield reduction under late sowing than the check DBW 39 -- https://researchgate.net/publication/343097264_DBW_187_Notification
- Lodging: described as semi-dwarf with good lodging tolerance (source is a commercial/agri-news page, not an official record) -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/dbw-187-karan-vandana-a-high-yielding-disease-resistant-wheat-variety-for-maximum-production-and-healthier-consumption/
- Drought, salinity, flood/waterlogging, submergence: No evidence found for this variety in the searches.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Yellow and brown rust: resistant -- https://krishakjagat.org/en/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-karan-vandana-dbw-187/ and https://realagri.in/p/dbw-187-karan-vandana/
- Stripe and leaf rust resistant; highly resistant to wheat blast; moderate resistance to Karnal bunt; loose smut tolerance -- https://global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-wheat-variety-dbw187-karan-vandana/ (note: this conflicts with the yellow/brown rust listing above; the rust type should be checked against the CSC record)
- Wheat blast: high resistance reported in a seed-production case study -- https://researchgate.net/publication/351109497_Truthful_seed_production_of_Newly_Release_Wheat_Variety_Karan_Vandana_DBW_187_A_Case_Study_of_Progressive_Farmer
- Multiple disease resistance: described in a bread-wheat evaluation paper -- https://www.academia.edu/77835559/Development_and_evaluation_of_high_yielding_multiple_disease_resistant_bread_wheat_variety_Karan_Vandana_DBW187_
- Insect pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Trials: tested in AICW&BIP coordinated trials across NIVT-1A 2015-16, AVT-I 2016-17 and AVT-II 2017-18 -- https://researchgate.net/publication/343097264_DBW_187_Notification
- NWPZ: two-year average of 61.28 q/ha, above checks HD 2967 and HD 3086 -- https://www.academia.edu/77835559/Development_and_evaluation_of_high_yielding_multiple_disease_resistant_bread_wheat_variety_Karan_Vandana_DBW187_
- NEPZ: average 48.8 q/ha, potential 64.7 q/ha -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-karan-vandana-dbw-187/ (conflict: NWPZ potential is listed as 96.6 q/ha and 75.4 q/ha in different sources; see global-agriculture.com links below)
- NWPZ average 61.3 q/ha, potential 96.6 q/ha, plant height 105 cm, flowering 99 days, maturity 148 days -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-wheat-variety-dbw187-karan-vandana/ (conflicts: other sources give 120-day maturity and 100 cm height)
- Other conflicting figures: 75.5 q/ha average, 96.6 q/ha potential -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-wheat-variety-dbw-187-karan-vandana-for-north-western-plains/; 60.3 q/ha average, 75.4 q/ha potential, Central Zone -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-biofortified-wheat-variety-dbw-187-karan-vandana/
- Crop profile: flowers at 77 days and matures at 120 days, about 100 cm tall, NEPZ timely sown -- https://icar.org.in/node/4812

- Agronomy (commercial page): irrigated N:P:K 120:60:40, seed rate 100 kg/ha, 22.5 cm row spacing, sowing October-November, 140-145 days duration, 1000-grain weight 58 g -- https://realagri.in/p/dbw-187-karan-vandana/

disease_resistance.research_summary: Foliar disease resistance (CSC record): resistant to foliar diseases under natural and artificial epiphytotic conditions. Resistance to rusts, particularly brown rust, is useful under timely-sown conditions in NEPZ. Race-specific APR responses to brown rust races 77-5, 77-9 and 104-2 were recorded across locations. Seedling resistance tests (SRT) indicated resistance to the prevalent brown rust race 77-7, and to races 77-8, 77-9, 77-10, 104-2, 104-3, 104B, 162-2 and 162A. Yellow and brown rust: listed as resistant in two commercial sources. Stripe and leaf rust: resistant, with high resistance to wheat blast, moderate resistance to Karnal bunt and loose smut tolerance in one commercial source. Wheat blast: high resistance reported in a seed-production case study. Multiple disease resistance: described in a bread-wheat evaluation paper. CONFLICT: the commercial source listing stripe and leaf rust resistance does not match the yellow and brown rust listing from the other sources; the rust type should be checked against the CSC record. The CSC record indicates resistance to brown, black and yellow rusts.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MPO (JW)1255, Wheat

Search budget note: the four permitted searches ran in one batch. A fifth call, made to re-check the stored results for "MPO" or "1255", was blocked by the tool limit, so I could not re-inspect full page text. The findings below rest only on the first ~250 characters of each result, so treat "No evidence found" as provisional.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The "MPO (JW)1255 wheat variety" search returned general wheat and barley release documents with no visible mention of MPO or JW 1255.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No returned snippet named this variety for rust, smut, or other disease or pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No returned snippet reported yield, maturity, or multi-location trial data for MPO.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. Parentage and breeding-line information for MPO were not returned. The variety code (JW)1255 is only in the record, not confirmed by any source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The JNKVV institutional homepage was returned for the query "MPO wheat JW 1255 breeder developed by JNKVV" (https://www.jnkvv.org/). Its snippet names JNKVV's wheat releases (JS 93-05, JS 95-60, JS 97-52) but not MPO. No breeder name was found for MPO. The institution in the record (Deptt. of Plant Breeding and Genetic, JNKVV) is unverified by any MPO-specific source.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. The only institute-level URL is https://www.jnkvv.org/. I did not read its contact page, so no email, phone, or postal address is recorded here.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for MPO. The "MPO wheat (JW)1255 research paper" search returned a general "Wheat Research Report 2025-26" (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/400935256_Wheat_Research_Report_2025-26). It is not known to mention MPO, so it is not listed as a publication for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed search returned only a commercial organic seed retailer (https://www.groworganic.com/collections/wheat-seeds), which is unrelated to this variety. No Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record gives "Unknown", and no source confirmed it.

NAME CHECK -- The record lists variety_name "MPO" and seednet_variety_name "Unknown". Every search used "MPO" and "(JW)1255"/"JW 1255", and no result was confirmed under either name. The Seednet portal was not searched directly, so the Seednet name remains unresolved.

Suggested next steps: check the full text of the ResearchGate release document (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318497981_Development_and_Release_of_New_Wheat_and_Barley_Varieties_for_Different_Zones_and_States) for "MPO" or "JW 1255", and check the JNKVV contact page and seednet.gov.in directly. These need a fresh session because the search budget for this one is used up.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MP (JW)1202 / MP(JW)1202(MP-1202), Wheat

Search budget note: the four allowed searches were used, and the tool limit was hit during a follow-up pass, so I could not open the pages in full. Findings below come from the search snippets. Several headings have little or no evidence. Name matching: the slideshare and indianjournals snippets use "MP-1202" or "MP 1202", and the iiwbr snippet uses "MP1202". I treat these as referring to this variety, though the pages do not give the full "MP (JW)1202" form.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Snippet describes MP-1202 as terminal heat tolerant, with bold grains and profuse tillering, suited to late-sown irrigated conditions. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/wheat-cultivation/47807540 (secondary compilation, not a primary source)
STRESS TOLERANCE: The iiwbr newsletter reports that DBW107 and MP1202 showed low canopy temperature depression values at grain filling, which is a heat-stress indicator. The snippet does not explain the test conditions. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST: A 2022 Vindhya (MP) leaf rust evaluation lists MP 1202 among varieties rated very susceptible to leaf rust. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/apps-30-2-005

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The slideshare compilation gives a yield of about 45–50 q/ha for MP-1202 under late-sown irrigated conditions. This is an unverified secondary figure. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/wheat-cultivation/47807540
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The iiwbr newsletter has a varietal table with year of release and days-to-maturity columns that may include MP1202, but the snippet did not show the row values. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The parentage POCIS/3/KAUZ82.BOW//KAUZ comes only from the input record and was not confirmed by any search result. No QTL, marker, or breeding-line code evidence was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The slideshare compilation attributes MP-1202 to JNKVV (Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya, Madhya Pradesh). No individual breeder name was found. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/wheat-cultivation/47807540

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute email, phone, address, or contact URL appeared in the results. JNKVV's official site was not retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS:
Authors not shown in snippet (2022). Evaluation of different wheat varieties for resistance against leaf rust disease of wheat in Vindhya, Madhya Pradesh. Annals of Plant Protection Sciences, 30(2) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/apps-30-2-005
Authors not shown in snippet (2022). Wheat & Barley Newsletter, V.162 (ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal; MP1202 appears in CTD data). -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
No AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI-linked peer-reviewed paper on this variety was found in these results.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The seed-related search returned only Madhya Pradesh wheat procurement news, which is about a different topic and was discarded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Madhya Pradesh (from the input record). The slideshare compilation places MP-1202 among JNKVV varieties suited to Madhya Pradesh conditions. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/wheat-cultivation/47807540 No CSC release notification text or seednet.gov.in page was retrieved, so the release year 2009 and the notification details are unverified.

Priority follow-ups, which need a new search session: seednet.gov.in entry for MP(JW)1202(MP-1202); the CSC release minutes; JNKVV wheat section and contact page; ICAR-IIWBR varietal table; KrishiKosh for MP-1202 theses.

seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
1.	NIDW 1149 is resistant to brown rust (ACI- 1.9), Black rust (ACI-4.1) and Yellow rust (ACI-3.9)
2.	NIDW 1149 has agene combinations of Lr23+, Sr11+2+ and Yr2+ which provides broad spectrum durable leaf, stem and yellow rust resistance respectively
3.	NIDW 1149 exhibited better APR response to stem rust races 117-6 (10 MR to 10S) and 40A (0 to SMS)
4.	The proposed variety NIDW 1149 is resistant to Karnal Bunt (2.15%), Powdery Mildew (4.0), Flag Smut (0.5%) and Loose Smut (3.3%)

drought.details: No variety-level drought tolerance evidence found in the retrieved pages. disease_resistance.research_summary: Yellow (stripe) rust and brown (leaf) rust: resistance reported in trial and release sources (digest states 'resistant'; no quantitative scoring given). A secondary trade blog reproducing the IARI release text reports very high resistance to stripe and leaf rust with slow-rusting adult-plant reactions against susceptible checks in field and artificial conditions (treated as secondary). A non-official extension story claims genetic resistance to all three rusts including Ug99 and to yellow rust races 78S84 and 46S119; this claim is unverified. Loose smut and flag smut resistance appears only in a retail listing (commercial claim, unverified). Karnal bunt resistance: no evidence found for HD 3086.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Mangal (HI 8713), Wheat

Search note: I ran four searches (release/notification, breeder, research, seed availability). A fifth call was rejected by the tool's usage limit, so the searches could not be repeated. Several headings are therefore thin. The search results were snippets only; I could not open the full pages.

Name check: The evidence refers to "Pusa Mangal (HI 8713)" in both the ResearchGate and ICAR pages, which covers both the CSC name "Pusa Mangal" and the Seednet name. The ICAR and ResearchGate pages describe it as a durum wheat (Triticum durum) variety, not common wheat as the input record says.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety. -- No URL (searches 1 and 3 returned no such finding)

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No rust, smut, blight or insect resistance data appeared in the results. -- No URL (searches 1 and 3 returned no such finding)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The variety is described as a high-yielding durum wheat for high-fertility, irrigated, timely-sown conditions in the Central Zone, which is India's largest durum-producing zone. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Mean-yield-q-ha-of-HI-8713-in-coordinated-trials_tbl1_358817876
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: A table of mean yields (q/ha) of HI 8713 in coordinated trials appears on the same ResearchGate page. The retrieved text did not include the numbers. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Mean-yield-q-ha-of-HI-8713-in-coordinated-trials_tbl1_358817876
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: An ICAR journal article reports farmer yields of 80 to 90 percent in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, and says Pusa Mangal gave consistently higher yields as a check variety in national wheat trials. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/121681/46450/317172

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage HD 4672/PDW 233 is supplied in the input record only. No retrieved page confirmed it. -- No URL (input record only)
GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found for breeding-line codes beyond HI 8713, breeding method, QTL, markers or genome resources. -- No URL

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The variety is attributed to the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), but the results gave no breeder names and no station details. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/121681/46450/317172
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No breeder or scientist names were found. -- No URL

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute email, phone, postal address or contact page was retrieved. The IARI institute-level contact page was not located in the results.

PUBLICATIONS:
Authors not retrieved (Year not retrieved). Pusa Mangal (HI 8713) A durum wheat variety boosting economy and nutritional security of central zone. ResearchGate publication record (journal/report not retrieved) -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Mean-yield-q-ha-of-HI-8713-in-coordinated-trials_tbl1_358817876
Authors not retrieved (Year not retrieved). Pusa Mangal (HI 8713). Indian Farming, ICAR e-pubs (journal article) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/121681/46450/317172
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report or peer-reviewed paper with authors and DOI was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY: A private dealer listing offers "Hi 8713 Pusa Mangal Wheat Seed" at ₹1,600 per quintal from Hariom Hybrid Seeds, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh. This is a commercial listing, not an official seed agency, and its availability is unverified. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/hi-8713-pusa-mangal-wheat-seed-23356317688.html
SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found from NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or Seednet for the 2013 notification. The Seednet portal was not reached.

Special feature (s)-   Lower most spikelet often sterile like PBW 343 and conferring resistance to all three rusts under field conditions occurring under Southern hill zone.

seednet_fields.Parentage:
HUW 234/ CBW 12-Sel
HUW: An old wide adaptable variety, suitable for irrigated late sown situation of Bihar and North Eastern Plain Zone of India, became susceptible to brown rust.
CBW 12-sel: A high tillering and disease resistant genotype.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated late sown situation of Bihar (15 to 31 Dec.)
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Lodging resistant, non-shattering, easy threshability, fertilizer responsive up to 120kg N/ha and suitable for irrigated late sown condition.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Semi-dwarf and erect plant with green and semi-erect flag leaf; white tapering and awned ear, bent penducle, elliptical, amber and semi-hard grain with test grain weight-34.7g.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Late heat tolerant.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to brown rust, loose smut and tolerant to leaf blight.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Resistant to stem borer and aphid.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): •	Fertilizer schedule: 120:60:40 kg N,P205&K20/ha( 1/3rd Nitrogen,full phosphorus and potash as basal and remaining 2/rd nitrogen as 1/3 rd at first irrigation and 1/3rd at second irrigation.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: G. B. Pant University of Agriculture and Tech., Pantnagar-263145, Uttarakhand.
seednet_fields.Parentage:
PYS-841 x PYS-7
PYS-841 is high yielding with multilocular upright siliqua alignment, high oil in medium bold seeds and yellow flowers.
PYS-7 is high yielding with multilocular upright siliqua, medium bold seeds, high oil content  and white flowers.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Uttarakhand Plains under timely sown irrigated conditions.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: New variety is early maturing (around 106 days).  It has tetralocular upright siliqua alignment and creamish white flowers while PPS-1 (Check) has tetralocular pendant bearing with yellow flowers.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Performs better under rainfed conditions in Uttarakhand hills as well.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Reaction against Alternaria blight, downy mildew and powdery mildew diseases was similar to Benoy.  It is resistant to white rust and moderately resistant to Bacterial rot.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Reaction against mustard aphids was similar to check Benoy.
seednet_fields.Average Yield (Kg/Ha): Mean yield: 15.22 q/ha Highest yield: 19.75 q/ha. Kg/Ha
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Apply manures & fertilizers as per the state recommendation.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MANDAKINI (OR 2077-4) (IET 17847), rice

Name note: The CSC release-minute name is "MANDAKINI (OR 2077-4)(IET 17847)" and the Seednet name is "Mandakini". Evidence below refers to the same rice variety under both names. The Seednet crop field reads "CUCUMBER", which conflicts with rice. No Seednet page for this variety was retrieved, so I could not confirm the Seednet crop entry. Other "Mandakini" entries found are a different variety, Mandakini (K-9351), released 2004, and were excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no page on disease or pest resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Mandakini is listed among early-duration varieties with a 90-115 day range, but that range is for the group, not confirmed per variety -- https://osscltd.in/cms/marketing/availability-of-seeds
Odisha seed distribution report says farmers in the state prefer Mandakini among the varieties they grow in uplands -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf
IRRI technical bulletin on rice in Odisha lists Mandakini as suited to upland kharif and irrigated rabi land -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
No multi-location or field-trial results specific to this variety were found -- searched via the research query, no page returned.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No marker, QTL or parentage page for this variety was returned. Parentage is not specified in the input and was not found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Odisha's rice breeding history is covered by the IRRI bulletin, which credits Mandakini to the state's rice breeding programme (2010 release group) but does not name a breeder -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
The same bulletin attributes Odisha's rice breeding and varietal development to the Rice Research Station, Bhubaneswar, under the university setup (OUAT). The bulletin does not explicitly say Mandakini was bred there -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
No lead breeder name was found for this variety. A ResearchGate profile of an OUAT plant breeder lists a co-author named Mandakini Kabi on an unrelated paper; this does not identify a breeder and is not attributed to the variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. Institute-level contact for seed supply (not the breeding institute):
Orissa State Seeds Corporation Ltd., Samantarapur, Bhubaneswar, Pin 751002, Odisha; Phone: 0674 - 2340573, 2340170; Email: mdosscltd456@gmail.com -- https://www.osscltd.in/cms/contact/contact-us
No email or phone for OUAT Rice Research Station or ICAR-NRRI was retrieved, so none is given.

PUBLICATIONS
Das, S.R. (2012). Rice in Odisha. IRRI Technical Bulletin No. 16 -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers specific to this variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Odisha State Seeds Corporation (OSSC Ltd.) lists Mandakini among its early-duration paddy varieties -- https://osscltd.in/cms/marketing/availability-of-seeds
OSSC is the state nodal agency for breeder, foundation and certified seed, and sources breeder and foundation paddy seed from CRRI, OUAT and ANGRAU -- https://ossc.nic.in/Production/Schemes
The Odisha seed distribution report describes shortfalls in supply of medium-land and upland paddy seed in the study period, without naming Mandakini -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf
No NSC, KVK or private dealer listing for this variety was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Notified in Odisha: the notification (S.O. 632(E), 25.03.2011) lists the recommended state as Odisha -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
The Bihar-hosted list of notified varieties also records this variety with a 2010 release year and 25/03/2011 notification -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
The input field "recommended_states_raw" (Not specified) is superseded by the Odisha notification above.

- Trait list shown for the NSCH-12 row is limited to a "resistance to BSDM" phrase, and the snippet does not clearly tie it to this row. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf

drought.details: Moderately tolerant to drought. It is considered an 'intermediate' variety in tissue-specific responses to drought stress at the seedling stage. The variety has also been a target for introgression of drought stress tolerance traits, suggesting a need for improvement in inherent tolerance.

heat.details: It is field tolerant to high temperature. While noted as 'intermediate' in some heat stress response studies at the seedling stage, overall field performance indicates tolerance to high temperatures. However, it is susceptible to low temperatures and frost.

salinity.details: It has been identified as a target for introgression of salt stress tolerance traits, implying its inherent tolerance to salinity is not high. It has been used in studies involving salt injury index.

flood.details: Tolerant to waterlogging conditions. It has also been used as a parent in breeding programs aiming to enhance waterlogging tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Cucumber Mosaic Virus (CMV) and Downy Mildew (caused by P. cubensis).

pest_resistance.summary: Not Specified

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield is about 200 (unit unspecified, as per agricultural practice guidelines). It has been found to be a good parent for fruit yield, fruit number, fruit length, fruit weight, and diameter in hybrid combinations, exhibiting high standard heterosis for yield per plant.
agronomic_details.stability: Included in All India Coordinated Trials, suggesting adaptability across various environments. It is widely cultivated, implying good overall adaptation.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation in regions like Punjab, suitable for general cucumber cultivation practices. It is tolerant to high temperatures and humidity.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plants have dark green leaves with a rough surface. Its fruit characteristics (yield, number, length, weight, diameter) are notable when used in hybridization.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Participated in All India Coordinated Trials. It is extensively used as a check variety in cucumber germplasm evaluation and has been included in numerous research experiments and hybridization programs to study traits like stress tolerance, yield components, and seed production.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The variety has been used as a recipient for trait introgression (e.g., drought and salt stress tolerance) and as a parent in crosses (e.g., for submergence and waterlogging tolerance, parthenocarpy) and genetic diversity studies.

genetic_and_molecular_profile.molecular_mechanisms: Described as gynoecious and parthenocarpic. The Frontiers/PMC paper on cytokinin, auxin and gibberellin cross-talk in parthenocarpic fruit development in cucumber used DG-8 as one of the genotypes. It was described as the second gynoecious parthenocarpic variety, after PPC-6. Parthenocarpy-related hormone pathways were studied, but the snippets give no specific gene details for DG-8.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Pickling Cucumber-8 (DG-8) is an IARI gynoecious, parthenocarpic processing/pickling cucumber released in 2022 and notified for Delhi, with a claimed yield of 80-85 t/ha. No biotic or abiotic stress tolerance evidence was found. Evidence consists of institutional reports, a Gazette notification and one genetics paper, and is moderate for identity and yield but absent for stress and Gujarat suitability.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Gynoecious parthenocarpic pickling cucumber from IARI, released in 2022. Claimed yield is 80-85 t/ha, but maturity, season and adaptation data are not specified.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No documented drought, heat, salinity, flood, disease or pest tolerance. The stress terms in the search results refer to other crops. Gujarat suitability is unverified, and local trials would be needed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Harsha (HI 1655), wheat

Name check: The variety name is "Pusa Harsha" (CSC minutes name, with code HI 1655). The Seednet name "Pusa (Barkha)" with crop CUCUMBER refers to a different crop. Every Seednet-related finding below is about the cucumber variety Pusa Barkha, not wheat HI 1655. I found no Seednet listing for the wheat variety.

Date check: The input gives a release year of 2022-10-26. The sources give a notification date of 06.03.2023. One source cites the notification as S.O. 1056(E) dated 6.3.2023 -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/ . Treat 2023 as the notification year and check the input date against the Gazette.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistance to leaf and stem rust is listed for HI 1655 in the wheat compendium table -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- A Hindi-language grower article describes the variety as water-use efficient and suited to timely sowing with restricted irrigation -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for HI 1655 specifically.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The compendium describes HI 1655 as having resistance to leaf and stem rust, with hard grain and a good chapati score of 8.4 -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Yellow rust, Karnal bunt, and other disease or pest resistance: No evidence found for HI 1655.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Recommended sowing window is 20 October to 10 November, under timely sowing with restricted irrigation in the Central Zone -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/ (general Central Zone table) and https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- A Hindi-language grower article gives a seed rate of about 108 kg/ha, 20 cm row spacing, plant height of about 90–95 cm, and NPK plus zinc at 80:40:50 -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/
- The same article gives a potential of about 60 q/ha under good conditions -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/
- The compendium lists two yield figures for HI 1655 in the Central Zone (59.8 and 38.8). The column labels are unclear in the extracted text, so treat them as unverified -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Maturity days: No evidence found for HI 1655.
- Multi-location trial data beyond the compendium entry: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: The compendium entry for HI 1655 appears to include "Pusa MACS 2496 / HI 1056(E)", but the text is garbled and not labelled as parentage -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Marker, QTL, or genomic studies for HI 1655: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Indore (MP) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- The station's principal scientist and head, K.C. Sharma, is quoted on the six new varieties notified in March 2023, including HI 1655 -- https://krishijagran.com/news/icar-iari-develops-6-new-high-yielding-disease-resistant-wheat-varieties/
- Names of the lead breeders for HI 1655 specifically: No evidence found. Station staff named in a 2025 IARI newsletter for other wheat lines include Singh JB, Sharma KC, Verma DK, Prakasha TL and Gajghate R -- https://pusakrishi.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/IARI_Newsletter_April-June_2025.pdf
- The Seednet cucumber "Pusa Barkha" was released in 2013 by the SVRC Delhi. It is a different crop and is not the wheat variety -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/vegetables/cucumber/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr K.C. Sharma, Head (Acting), IARI Regional Station Indore. Phone: 0731-2927921. Email: head_indore[at]iari[dot]res[dot]in. Alternate email listed: kc_64sharma[at]yahoo[dot]com -- https://www.iari.res.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=301&Itemid=735
- Jang Bahadur Singh, Regional Station Indore. Email: jangbsing@gmail.com -- https://pusakrishi.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/IARI_Newsletter_April-June_2025.pdf
- Institute postal address for the Indore station: No evidence found.
- Institute-level contact page URL: https://www.iari.res.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=301&Itemid=735 (page lists the station contact details)

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not listed (2024). Compendium of Wheat Varieties Notified in India During 2018-2023. ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal (RB-51) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Authors not listed (2022). Wheat & Barley Newsletter, Vol. 162. ICAR-IIWBR -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Authors not listed (2023). IARI Annual Report 2023 (lists HI 1655 as a bread wheat variety) -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- No peer-reviewed papers, theses, or KrishiKosh records specific to HI 1655 were found. The HI 8802 paper in the search results concerns a different durum variety and is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No wheat seed sales listing for HI 1655 found from NSC, a state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or a private dealer.
- The IARI Indore station reports producing breeder seed for its varieties through public-private partnership -- https://www.iari.res.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=301&Itemid=735
- Seednet and cucumber listings (Amazon "Pusa" cucumber seed) are for other crops and are not relevant to HI 1655.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Kota and Udaipur divisions of Rajasthan, and Jhansi division of Uttar Pradesh. The Central Zone table lists HI 1655 for timely sown, restricted irrigation conditions -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- The IARI Indore page lists the Central Zone states (MP, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Kota and Udaipur divisions, Jhansi division) -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search note: I ran four web searches (variety/notification, breeder/institution, research, seed availability). None returned any page about Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-1 or SKUAST-K's cucumber work. The results were generic seed-catalogue pages, a Kerala Agricultural University hybrid list for a different hybrid (KPCH-1), and a Nepali cucumber hybrid trial. I have not attributed any of those to this variety. Names used: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are the same ("Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-1"), so no separate evidence exists under either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found
DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for this variety. (A Nepali multi-location cucumber hybrid trial appeared in results, but it concerns other hybrids, not Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-1 -- https://www.nepjol.info/index.php/nh/article/download/36649/30679)
GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found naming the lead breeder, developing station, or release notification for this hybrid. Release date in the record: 2012-07-24. Institution in the record: SKUAST-K.
CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, institute email, phone, or contact page was retrieved.
PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found
SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SKUAST-K seed sales, or dealer listing for this hybrid was returned. The only seed listings were foreign retail pages (e.g., https://www.parkseed.com/products/park-seed-select-slicer-hybrid-cucumber-seeds-52605-pk-p1), which are unrelated.
RECOMMENDED STATES -- Record field states "Jammu and Kashmir", but no independent source confirming this was found.

Suggested next checks, which I could not run within the search limit: the SeedNet portal (seednet.gov.in) entry for code H0403013, the CSC/Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards minutes for 2012, the SKUAST-K Division of Vegetable Science website, and KrishiKosh for SKUAST-K vegetable theses.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-2 (cucumber, hybrid; variety code H0403014; SKUAST-K; released 2012-07-24; recommended state J&K)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-2"). No search returned a Seednet portal page, so the evidence below does not come from Seednet under either name. Four searches returned no page that describes this hybrid directly. The findings below are only tangential, and each one is labelled with the work it actually concerns.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for this hybrid's drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Context only: a Kashmir polyhouse study covers a different parthenocarpic hybrid, not this one -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue9/PartO/8-9-162-601.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for resistance ratings of Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-2. EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shrushti (variety_name) / Shruti (seednet_variety_name), maize, GH 0727

Search note: four web_search queries were run (variety, breeder/institute, research/trials, Seednet name). The Seednet name "Shruti" returned only cucumber seed-sale pages, which are discarded under the crop and variety rules. All maize findings below refer to "Shrushti" / GH 0727 and not to the Seednet crop label, which says CUCUMBER.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no page giving drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for GH 0727 (Shrushti).

DISEASE AND PEST
Shrushti is listed in a benchmarking table of Indian maize varieties with the note "resistance to BSDM" (BSDM is the abbreviation in the snippet; it is not expanded there). The table row also names UAS, ARS Arabhavi, Karnataka, Kharif, and a yellow, dent grain type. The snippet does not state a disease score for this variety, so the claim should be checked against the full document. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The benchmarking table lists GH 0727 (Shrushti) with a yield figure of 6.0 in its row, tested under Karnataka Kharif conditions. The table's column headings are not legible in the snippet, so the unit and meaning of this figure are unconfirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
The IIMR cultivar list records GH 0727 (Shrushti), developed at ARS Arabhavi, Karnataka, with status "Public," a date of 30-07-2014, a code "1919 (E)," season Kharif, and maturity "Normal." A value of 7.5 appears in the same row, with no unit or column label visible in the snippet. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
Maturity class is given as "Normal" in the IIMR list. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The searches returned no QTL, marker, or pedigree study for GH 0727 (Shrushti). Parentage is not specified in the input and was not found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The developing institution is given as UAS, ARS Arabhavi (University of Agricultural Sciences, Agricultural Research Station, Arabhavi, Karnataka), which fits the "University of Agricultural Sciences" entry in the release record. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: SNEHA (JRM-3), Mesta (kenaf)

Name note: The CSC release minutes name is SNEHA, and the Seednet name is SNEHA(JRM-3). The sources below refer to "JRM-3 (Sneha)" and "JRM 3 (Sneha)" under kenaf, which matches both names. I did not retrieve a Seednet portal page, so no evidence in this digest comes from seednet.gov.in. Four searches were run: release/traits, breeder/institute, research/QTL, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bred specifically for salt tolerance, with growth reported at EC up to 6.0 dS/m and pH up to 9.2 in alkaline soil; yield reported at about 5.1 t/ha in normal soils -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- The same ICAR report describes JRM 3 (Sneha) as performing well under salinity and moisture stress conditions, with yields of about 2.5 to 3.8 t/ha, but the passage is garbled in the extract, so treat this figure as unverified -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Described as resistant to major pests and diseases -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/Mesta.aspx
- No pathogen-specific or trial-based resistance data found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Sowing window given as mid-April to mid-May, with better fibre quality noted -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/Mesta.aspx
- Semi-dwarf plant type; flowering at 97 days and maturity at 145 days in the north-western plains zone; flowering at 91 days and maturity at 128 days in the north-eastern plains zone -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- Yield in the national list: 25-38 q/ha -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/Mesta.aspx
- Release and notification both listed as 2010 in the national table (the year 2008 in the input record is not confirmed by this source) -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/Mesta.aspx

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage MT-150 x MT-899 comes only from the input record. No source found confirming it.
- The ICAR report mentions expression of a Na+/H+ antiporter gene in the context of salt-stress rootstock responses, but it is about a different kenaf variety (JRM 5 Shrestha) and rootstocks, not SNEHA -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- No QTL or marker study naming SNEHA was found. A kenaf RAD-seq QTL map for first flower node was returned but does not name SNEHA or JRM-3 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11656747

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Source institute given as CRIJAF (Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres) -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/Mesta.aspx
- No individual breeder or scientist names were found for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No CRIJAF email, phone, or address was retrieved from the search results.
- Institute contact page not retrieved. Suggested next step: CRIJAF contact page via icar.org.in, which I did not confirm.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. Searches for SNEHA or JRM-3 in kenaf research returned no papers, theses, or AICRP reports naming this variety. The Springer Mesta seed-yield paper (14 varieties evaluated) was returned but does not name SNEHA or JRM-3 in the retrieved text -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42535-026-01723-6

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The seed search returned no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for SNEHA. The only Mesta-related result was the Springer paper above, which does not name SNEHA.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Traditional Mesta growing belt of the country -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/Mesta.aspx

heat.details: No direct evidence of heat tolerance was found. The variety was developed for arid and semi-arid agro-climates, which indicates regional adaptation but not a tested heat-tolerance trait. In farmers' fields it recorded 15.3 q/ha against a check of 9.64 q/ha, but this result is not linked to heat stress.

salinity.details: No AD-2-specific salinity evidence was found. The digest notes only that seed spices in general are reported to grow successfully under saline or alkaline water, and this statement is not tied to AD-2.

flood.details: No evidence found.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for AD-2 specifically. No pests with resistance were identified in the digest.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: AD-2 (Ajmer Dill-2), Indian dill, NRCSS Ajmer

DROUGHT: The variety is suitable for cultivation under both irrigated and rainfed conditions., with about 14.6 q/ha under irrigated conditions and 5.8 q/ha under rain-fed conditions. This shows rainfed adaptation, not a measured drought-tolerance trait. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/food-science/dill ; https://5.imimg.com/data5/OH/VP/MY-20277542/seed-spices.pdf

HEAT: No direct evidence found for heat tolerance. The variety is described as developed for arid and semi-arid agro-climate, and in farmers' fields it recorded 15.3 q/ha against a check of 9.64 q/ha. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJSS/article/view/157474

SALINITY: No AD-2-specific evidence found. Seed spices in general are reported to be grown successfully under saline/alkaline water, but this is not tied to AD-2. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329438747_Scenario_Importance_and_Prospects_of_Seed_Spices_A_Review

FLOOD / SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found.

DISEASE RESISTANCE: AD-2 recorded the lowest percent disease incidence, 5.2%, among the tested entries, and was rated tolerant. Separately, the variety possesses field tolerance to powdery mildew. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJSS/article/view/157474 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316589094_NRCSS_ACr_1_Coriander

PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found for AD-2 specifically.

QTL / MARKERS: No evidence found. A 2024 Springer review on dill breeding notes that still almost no work has been done about the breeding aspects of this important plant. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-97-9630-4_6

YIELD AND TRIALS: Station and farm trials at NRCSS: AD-2 gave 1466 kg/ha, against 1207 kg/ha for the local variety, a 21% gain. The farmers'-field result was 15.3 q/ha versus 9.64 q/ha for the check. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJSS/article/view/157474

BREEDER / INSTITUTION: NRCSS Ajmer developed the variety for arid and semi-arid agro-climate, with high dillapiole content. It was developed through mass selection based on progeny performance from Nagaur Local (selection AD-01-6). The selection was identified by the XVII All India Co-ordinated Research Project on Spices as NRCSS AD 2. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/68257

REGISTRATION / NOTIFICATION: The variety has been registered at NBPGR with IC 620541. Central notification followed: the Central Variety Release and Notification Committee accepted it for notification at its 24th meeting, held on 22 September 2016. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/68257

RELEASE DATE (input conflict): The input gives 2015-04-07. The sources instead point to a state notification dated 1.1.16, with the State Subcommittee approval noted in the same release record. The input date should be checked against the official notification. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/68257

SEED AVAILABILITY (breeder/institutional): Breeder and truthfully labeled seed of this variety is available at NRCSS, Tabiji, Ajmer-305 206

drought.details: No evidence found for GAD-1 drought tolerance. The only related data is a rainfed versus irrigated yield comparison (1561 kg/ha rainfed, 1885 kg/ha irrigated), which is not a drought stress screen and does not establish tolerance mechanisms.

disease_resistance.summary: No GAD-1-specific disease resistance evidence was found. Powdery mildew resistance with lower incidence than checks is reported only for the sister variety GAVD-1, and should not be attributed to GAD-1.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for pest resistance in GAD-1.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed: 1561 kg/ha (about 15.5% above check GD-3). Irrigated: 1885 kg/ha (about 12.0% above check GD-3). Source of yield data: AGRESCO trial evaluation.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-environment stability analysis found. The digest reports only rainfed and irrigated yields. The deferred AGRESCO proposal cited trials at Anand, Nenpur, and Sonsoli, but stability results across these sites are not reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for north and middle Gujarat.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: About 133 days, versus about 143 days for check GD-3 (the input table field reads 'Not available in table'; this value is from the AAU source).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Early maturing. Plant height 73-127 cm. More umbels and umbellets than check. Seeds smaller and less flattened than check.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Yield data came from AGRESCO trial evaluation. In April 2015, the joint AGRESCO proposal was deferred as a pre-release, pending one more year of trials at Anand, Nenpur, and Sonsoli. The proposal requested that the development method be described as 'introduction' rather than 'clonal selection'. Pollination management data (jaggery spray raising dill seed yield by about 57%) is from an ICAR-NRCSS Ajmer study and is general, not variety-specific.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
TOPIC: Identity and release status: Listed as a state-released dill seed variety from Anand Agricultural University, notified at the 46th State Seed Sub-Committee meeting in 2015 -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-released
TOPIC: Release status caveat: The April 2015 joint AGRESCO proposal was deferred as a pre-release, pending one more year of trials at Anand, Nenpur and Sonsoli, and the proposal asked that the development method be described as "introduction" rather than "clonal selection" -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Eleventh_Agresco.pdf
TOPIC: Breeder/institution: Developed by Anand Agricultural University, Anand; the AAU Seed Spices Research Station, Sanand page describes it as a dill seed release from its breeding work -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/546/236
TOPIC: Recommended area: North and middle Gujarat -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-dill-seed-1
TOPIC: Yield: 1561 kg/ha under rainfed and 1885 kg/ha under irrigated conditions, about 15.5% and 12.0% above check GD-3 respectively -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/546/236
TOPIC: Maturity and plant type: Early maturing at about 133 days versus about 143 days for GD-3; shorter plants (73-127 cm), more umbels and umbellets, and smaller, less flattened seeds -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/546/236
TOPIC: Trial basis: Yield data came from AGRESCO trial evaluation; the proposal was deferred for an additional year of data before final release -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Eleventh_Agresco.pdf
TOPIC: Disease resistance: Powdery mildew resistance is reported only for the sister variety GAVD-1, which had lower incidence than checks; no GAD-1-specific disease data found -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/546/236
TOPIC: Pest resistance: No evidence found
TOPIC: Drought tolerance: No evidence found for GAD-1 (only rainfed vs irrigated yield comparison, not a stress screen)
TOPIC: Heat tolerance: No evidence found
TOPIC: Salinity tolerance: No evidence found
TOPIC: Flood/waterlogging/submergence tolerance: No evidence found
TOPIC: QTL/markers: No evidence found (AAU Seed Science department mentions molecular characterization of released varieties generally, not GAD-1 specifically) -- https://www.aau.in/seed-science-and-technology
TOPIC: Seed availability (NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs): No evidence found
TOPIC: Pollination management (general, not variety-specific): Managed pollination with jaggery spray raised dill seed yield by about 57% in an ICAR-NRCSS Ajmer study -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9338944/
TOPIC: Recommended states other than Gujarat: No evidence found (input field "Not available in table")

basic_info.institution: RAJASTHAN AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY, BEECHAWAL FARM, BIKANER (RAJASTHAN)

agronomic_details.adaptation: Most suitable for loamy and black cotton soils with proper drainage. A dry, cool, frost-free climate is favourable. Most suitable for irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 150-160 days (official). Other sources give 130-140 (SKNAU), 140-150 (phytojournal) and 110 (RAU Bikaner notes), so maturity figures are inconsistent.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Short stature with compact umbels; long, bold seeds; a denser view of the plants when green. One source describes it as erect and medium tall, which conflicts with the official description.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not identified in the results.
commercial_info.availability_status: limited (unverified). Breeder seed is produced at SKNAU research stations (18 kg in 2018-19), but the commercial supply chain is not documented.
commercial_info.private_dealers: A spice nursery site lists RF-125 as a Rajasthan variety (spicenurseries.in), but no dealer or stock was confirmed.

variety_profile.institution: RAJASTHAN AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY, BEECHAWAL FARM, BIKANER (RAJASTHAN)
variety_profile.recommended_states: Not specified in the release record. Search results show use in Rajasthan, and a state-wise listing names Rajasthan for RF-125 (result 43).
variety_profile.state_acronyms: RJ (Rajasthan, per the sources above). GJ is not listed as a recommended state for this variety.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No direct drought-tolerance rating for RF-125 was found. The release record says it is most suitable for irrigated conditions. The slideshare snippet's 'tolerant to drought' appears to refer to a different variety, and the CRIDA snippet on drought-tolerant greengram is about another crop. The CRIDA climate-resilient technologies report says RF-125 gave the best result (23.80 q/ha) among the varieties demonstrated in Rajasthan, but the snippet does not say this was under drought stress. A Sakleshpur CVT drought trial lists RF-125 at 22.95 q/ha, but the snippet does not say how it ranked relative to other genotypes. Water stress should be avoided at flowering and seed formation.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The ICAR Crop Improvement report lists RF 125 among fennel lines identified in a screening, but the snippet is cut off and does not state the trait. It sits next to a 'terminal heat stress' passage, so this link is not confirmed. The release record says a dry, cool, frost-free climate is favourable, which suggests the variety is not specifically heat adapted.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: No salinity rating for the released RF-125 was found. A researcher profile describes gamma-irradiated M3 mutants derived from RF-125 and screened for salt tolerance. That work concerns the mutants, not the original variety. The Bharatpur station source reports RF-125 yielding 20 q/ha in a saline-affected area, but the snippet gives no comparison and no tolerance claim.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No flood-tolerance evidence was found. The adaptation note requires proper drainage, and the IPM guidance says to avoid waterlogging. This suggests the variety is sensitive to waterlogging, but this is an inference and not a tested result.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Blight and powdery mildew (moderately resistant per the AESA-IPM guide). Ramularia blight and Alternaria blight are described as resistant in secondary sources (slideshare PPT, a training manual, and a production-technology compendium). The official release record says only that disease incidence was at par with RF-101 and the local check.
disease_resistance.technical_details: The sources conflict. The NIPHM-AESA IPM package lists RF-101 and RF-125 as moderately resistant to blight and powdery mildew. The release record shows no advantage over the checks. The 'resistant' claims come from non-peer-reviewed secondary sources. No resistance genes or mechanisms are reported.

pest_resistance.specific_pests: None documented. The 'field tolerant to white fly' result (OP3.pdf) concerns a different crop and is not attributed to RF-125. The CABI note about aphid-tolerant cultivars is general and does not name RF-125.
pest_resistance.technical_details: No pest-resistance evidence for RF-125 was found.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no (not demonstrated). Only moderate disease resistance has some support. There is no verified abiotic-stress tolerance.
key_stress_attributes: Moderate resistance to blight and powdery mildew (NIPHM AESA-IPM guide)
Blight resistance claims in secondary sources conflict with the release record's 'at par with checks'
Suited to irrigated, well-drained soils; waterlogging is to be avoided
Gamma-irradiation mutants of RF-125 have been used in salt-tolerance research, but this is not a trait of the variety itself

genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_markers: None found. No QTL, SNP or SSR data were reported for RF-125.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.breeding_techniques: Conventional recurrent half-sib selection (individual plant progeny performance). RF-125 has also served as a base material for gamma-radiation mutagenesis studies, for example germination at 150 Gy.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_background: Developed through recurrent selection based on individual plant progeny (half-sib) performance in EC-243380, an exotic collection from Italy. One source (result 33) attributes development to SKN College of Agriculture (RAU), Jobner. The official record names RAU, Beechwal Farm, Bikaner.

agronomic_performance.yield_potential: 1500-1700 kg/ha (official). Secondary sources give 1600 kg/ha (phytojournal) and 17.0 q/ha (SKNAU table). Farmer demonstration and trial figures are 20 q/ha (Bharatpur), 22.95 q/ha (Sakleshpur CVT) and 23.80 q/ha (CRIDA demonstration).
agronomic_performance.yield_stability: Reported yields are consistently at or above the official range across Rajasthan demonstrations and a Karnataka trial. No formal stability analysis was found.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Most suitable for loamy and black cotton soils with proper drainage. A dry, cool, frost-free climate is favourable. Most suitable for irrigated conditions.
agronomic_performance.maturity_days: 150-160 days (official). Other sources give 130-140 (SKNAU), 140-150 (phytojournal) and 110 (RAU Bikaner notes), so maturity figures are inconsistent.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Short stature with compact umbels; long, bold seeds; a denser view of the plants when green. One source describes it as erect and medium tall, which conflicts with the official description.
agronomic_performance.field_trial_results: CRIDA Rajasthan demonstrations: RF-125 gave the best result at 23.80 q/ha, with additional farmer income of Rs 47,900-56,900/ha. Bharatpur station: 20 q/ha. Sakleshpur CVT: 22.95 q/ha. An on-farm assessment (IJCMAS 2017) compared RF-101, RF-125 and RF-145. The SKNAU document says RF-125 was released for the state by notification S.O. 597(E) on 25.04.2006.
agronomic_performance.farmer_adoption: Described as a widely adopted cultivar in Rajasthan. Breeder seed production of 18 kg was recorded at ARSS in 2018-19. It is included in DUS guidelines and the Plant Authority's registered variety lists.

breeder_and_development_info.primary_breeder_name: Not identified in the search results.
breeder_and_development_info.breeding_institution: RAJASTHAN AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY, BEECHAWAL FARM, BIKANER (RAJASTHAN). SKN College of Agriculture, Jobner (RAU/SKNAU) is cited as the developer in some sources.
breeder_and_development_info.collaborating_scientists: Not identified. Arvind Verma appears only as a researcher working on RF-125 mutants.
breeder_and_development_info.development_timeline: Recurrent half-sib selection from EC-243380 (Italy). Released in 2004. State notification S.O. 597(E) dated 25.04.2006 (per SKNAU).
breeder_and_development_info.research_publications: Secondary and review sources only: Advances in cultivation of fennel (Phytojournal 2020), Germplasm conservation in seed spices (Botany Journals 2021), Scenario, Importance and Prospects of Seed Spices (Lupine 2018), an IJCMAS 2017 on-farm assessment, and the ResearchGate review on fennel (2022) mentioning gamma radiation of RF-125. No primary paper on the variety's release or stress tolerance was found.

commercial_availability.kvk_availability: Not identified. Demonstrations were done in Rajasthan, but no KVK stock was confirmed.
commercial_availability.private_dealers: A spice nursery site lists RF-125 as a Rajasthan variety (spicenurseries.in), but no dealer or stock was confirmed.
commercial_availability.availability_status: limited (unverified). Breeder seed is produced at SKNAU research stations (18 kg in 2018-19), but the commercial supply chain is not documented.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety has several citations, including government reports (CRIDA, NIPHM) and review literature, and consistent yield evidence of 16-24 q/ha. Its stress-trait evidence is weak: moderate resistance to blight and powdery mildew is supported by one credible source (NIPHM), while claims of drought, salinity and heat tolerance are not backed by direct evidence. The score is therefore not raised above 60. It is not recommended specifically for Gujarat, and no Gujarat-specific trial data were found.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Short, compact umbels; long bold seeds; 150-160 days; 15-17 q/ha official yield (20-24 q/ha in demonstrations); moderately resistant to blight and powdery mildew; best on irrigated, well-drained loam or black cotton soil.
dashboard_data.seasons: Rabi (inferred from the dry, cool climate requirement and the 'Advanced Production Technology for Rabi Fennel' source)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: RF-125 is a short, compact-umbel fennel variety released in 2004, selected by half-sib recurrence from an Italian accession, and it yields 1500-1700 kg/ha officially and 20-24 q/ha in Rajasthan demonstrations. The best-supported stress trait is moderate resistance to blight and powdery mildew; drought, heat, salinity and flood tolerance are not demonstrated. Yield evidence is strong and stress evidence is weak, with some conflict between sources on disease reaction and maturity.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: A short fennel variety with compact umbels and bold seeds, maturing in 150-160 days and yielding 15-17 q/ha officially (20-24 q/ha in demonstrations). It suits irrigated, well-drained loam and black cotton soils in a dry, cool, frost-free climate.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: It is moderately resistant to blight and powdery mildew according to the NIPHM guide, though the release record shows disease incidence at par with the checks. No verified drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was found, and no genetic marker data exist.
