search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME NOTE: CSC name "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson-1"; Seednet name "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson-1 (KGS-32)". Evidence below names "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson 1" with no KGS-32 code unless stated. KGS-32 appears only in a DRMR table, and it is not clearly linked to this release.

STRESS TOLERANCE (evidence refers to "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson 1")
- Reported resistance to Alternaria blight and powdery mildew, with moderate resistance to aphids. -- https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638494389134564757.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found for this variety. -- No evidence found (searched)

DISEASE AND PEST (evidence refers to "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson 1")
- Resistant to Alternaria blight and powdery mildew; moderately resistant to aphids. -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638494389134564757.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (evidence refers to "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson 1")
- Early maturing and high yielding at 12.5 q/ha, about 15.40% above the check Shalimar Sarson 1. -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638494389134564757.pdf
- Seed production is comparatively easy because the crop is often cross-pollinated. -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638494389134564757.pdf
- No multi-location or AICRP trial data specific to this variety found. Trial data found for "Shalimar Sarson-1" is for brown sarson (B. rapa), a different release, and is not used here. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/283831567_Effects_of_Brassica_alba_extract_on_yield_attribute_of_Paddy

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL or marker study for this variety found. -- No evidence found (searched)
- A DRMR fatty-acid and glucosinolate study lists "KGS-32" as a B. napus entry with origin given as IPK Germany, beside Shalimar Sarson-1. This does not establish KGS-32 as this release or give its parentage. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333718099_Genetic_variability_studies_for_quality_traits_in_rapeseed-mustard
- Parentage: not specified in input, and none found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (evidence refers to "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson 1")

- Lead breeder name: No evidence found (searched). Dr. Gowhar Ali (Associate Professor, Genetics and Plant Breeding, SKUAST-K) appears in an unrelated NSP seed-distribution report and is not linked to this variety. -- https://www.jkmonitor.org/local-news/skuast-k-organises-training-seed-distribution-programme-at-kvk-bandipora

- Institution location: Shalimar, Srinagar, J&K. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sher-e-Kashmir_University_of_Agricultural_Sciences_and_Technology_of_Kashmir

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No source shows drought tolerance for Manjari Medika itself. Drought and salt tolerance in the results refers to rootstocks such as Dogridge and 140RU, not the scion. The ARI annual report mentions a 'water-stress tolerant genotype' in a separate context.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The climate-change review lists Manjari Medika among varieties in an adaptation context, but the snippets give no heat tolerance data. Other 'heat' hits concern seed oil thermal processing and wheat, which are irrelevant.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: Salinity tolerance is attributed to the rootstocks (e.g., Dogridge, Salt Creek), not to the variety. A rootstock study found Manjari Medika grafted on 140RU performed best for cane biochemical parameters, which suggests a rootstock-dependent response rather than inherent tolerance.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence found.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence found. The submergence hits refer to rice (Swarna Sub1) and appear only because they sit in the same documents.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: None confirmed. A metabolomics paper snippet says 'grapes can be said to be more disease-resistant' without specifying the variety or the disease. Anthracnose and downy mildew resistance in the Pharma Journal snippet refers to a different variety.
disease_resistance.technical_details: The metabolomics study compares Manjari Medika with its parents and links phenolic and anthocyanin content to possible disease resistance. This is an inference, not a field-tested result. A Xanthomonas study used Manjari Medika among varieties, but the snippet gives no resistance outcome.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: Many citations exist, including peer-reviewed papers (ScienceDirect, PMC, ICAR publications), but they cover nutraceutical and processing properties, seed oil, pharmacology and rootstock effects, not stress tolerance of the variety. Drought, salinity and disease tolerance in the snippets belong to rootstocks or other varieties. There is no yield value, no Gujarat-specific data and no confirmed stress trait. This fits the 60 band (at least one citation, weak on stress traits). The score is not 50 or lower because the citations are real and numerous, and not 75 because no stress trait is evidenced.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Colored juice grape from NRCG Pune (Pusa Navrang x Flame Seedless). High anthocyanins and phenolics. Seed oil rich in linoleic acid. Zero-waste use of pomace and seed. Performs well on 140RU rootstock.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Manjari Medika is an ICAR-NRCG Pune juice grape hybrid (Pusa Navrang x Flame Seedless) valued for its anthocyanin-rich colored juice, seed oil and pomace uses. The literature is substantial but concerns biochemistry, nutraceutical and pharmacological properties, and rootstock interactions. No direct evidence of drought, heat, salinity, flood, disease or pest tolerance was found for the variety, and no yield or Gujarat-specific data is available.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: A teinturier-type juice grape released by ICAR-NRCG Pune, with parentage Pusa Navrang x Flame Seedless. Yield, maturity, adaptation and recommended states are unreported, and release year conflicts (2017 vs 2022).
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Stress tolerance is unproven. The salt and drought tolerance in the results belongs to rootstocks such as Dogridge and 140RU, and the disease-resistance statements are vague or about other varieties. Stress evidence is none to low.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: Several citations or publications mention the variety: ICAR documents, a PPV&FRA registration, peer-reviewed papers (PMC, Frontiers) and a trial in Tamil Nadu. Parentage and institution are confirmed. No stress, disease or pest tolerance is documented for this variety, because the drought, salt, submergence and resistance hits refer to other crops, rootstocks or varieties. No yield data are available, and there is no Gujarat-specific evidence. This fits the 'at least one citation, but weak on stress traits' tier (60).

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Manjari Shyama is a black seedless table grape hybrid (Black Champa x Thompson Seedless) developed by ICAR-NRC for Grapes, Pune, and registered with PPV&FRA (REG/2020/101). The search results contain no variety-specific evidence for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, or for disease and pest resistance, and no yield figures. Evidence is mostly institutional listings and studies using it as a host or comparison variety, so evidence quality is low to moderate.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Black seedless table grape hybrid (Black Champa x Thompson Seedless) from ICAR-NRCG, Pune. Yield, maturity, adaptation and recommended states are not documented in the evidence. It has been evaluated in Tamil Nadu (Cumbum valley) and grown by farmers in Maharashtra.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No variety-specific stress tolerance or disease and pest resistance was found. The drought, salt, submergence and resistance hits in the results belong to rootstocks, other grape varieties or other crops. Suitability for Gujarat's stress conditions therefore cannot be established and would need local trials.

disease_resistance.summary: Official central release table lists BM 2003-2 as resistant or tolerant to several diseases; the entry names BLS, anthracnose and WB. The table text is garbled, so the exact disease list is unclear. A commercial seller listing claims 'disease resistant' but names no test and is unverified; it is not treated as evidence. No resistance to a named disease was confirmed by a test in the retrieved sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Official table reports low incidence of bean thrips (presented as resistance/tolerance-related evidence in the table). In a whitefly screen, BM-2003-2 recorded the maximum whitefly population, and in the same study it was among the highest for jassid and among the highest for pod damage. These are susceptibility rankings, not resistance claims, so no pest resistance is established for whitefly, jassid or pod damage.

agronomic_details.yield: Official central release table: 8-11 q/ha (equivalent to 800-1100 kg/ha, matching the input record). Sowing-date trial: seed yield 1508 kg/ha and biological yield 2521 kg/ha. A 1012 kg/ha figure also appears in the same PDF, but the text is partly garbled and its context is unclear. Latur kharif trial: 7.41 g pod yield per plant and 4.43 g seed yield per plant (highest among the entries in that trial).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The rainfed sowing-date and variety trial (BM 2002-1, BM 2003-2 and others) is listed, but no stability results for BM 2003-2 are given in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Kharif season per the central release table. Suitable for irrigated conditions in spring/summer seasons per the same table. The Latur kharif trial and the sowing-date trials provide site-specific performance but no broader agro-climatic fit statement.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Kharif trial at Latur, fertilizer and variety combinations: BM-2003-02 gave the highest pod yield per plant (7.41 g) and seed yield per plant (4.43 g) reported in that trial. (2) Sowing-date trial: BM 2003-2 gave seed yield of 1508 kg/ha and biological yield of 2521 kg/ha and was reported as higher-yielding than Phule Vaibhav, BM-4 and PKV Green Gold; the PDF text is partly garbled. (3) Sowing-date and variety trial with BM 2002-1, BM 2003-2 and others under rainfed conditions: the digest lists the study but gives no BM 2003-2 result values. (4) Official central release table: 65-70 days maturity and 8-11 q/ha yield.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of BM 2003-2 in the retrieved pages. The only related statement is that it is suitable for irrigated condition in spring / summer seasons -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Listed as resistant or tolerant to several diseases, with low incidence of bean thrips -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (the table text is garbled, so the exact disease list is unclear; the entry names BLS, anthracnose and WB)
- In a whitefly screen, BM-2003-2 recorded the maximum population of whitefly -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326316873_EFFICACY_OF_SOME_INSECTICIDES_AND_BIOPESTICIDES_AGAINST_WHITEFLY_BEMISIA_TABACION_GREENGRAM (this is a susceptibility ranking, not a resistance claim)
- In the same study, BM-2003-2 was among the highest for jassid -- same URL
- Pod damage ranking also places BM-2003-2 among the highest damaged entries -- same URL
- Seller claim of "disease resistant" with no named test -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/bm-2003-2-moong-green-gram-seeds-2851521094388.html (commercial listing, unverified)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity and yield in the official table: 65-70 days and 8-11 q/ha -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (yield unit as printed in the table, presumably q/ha)
- Kharif trial at Latur, fertilizer and variety combinations, where BM-2003-02 gave the highest pod yield per plant at 7.41 g and seed yield of 4.43 g per plant -- https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v3i7/MDIwMTQxMjQ5.pdf
- Sowing-date trial in which BM 2003-2 gave a seed yield of 1508 kg/ha and biological yield of 2521 kg/ha, and was reported as higher-yielding than Phule Vaibhav, BM-4 and PKV Green Gold -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue2/PartH/9-2-17-115.pdf (the PDF text is partly garbled; the 1012 kg/ha figure also appears in it)
- Sowing-date and variety trial with BM 2002-1, BM 2003-2 and others under rainfed conditions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384676279_IJFANS_INTERNATIONAL_JOURNAL_OF_FOOD_AND_NUTRITIONAL_SCIENCES_Response_of_green_gram_Vigna_radiata_L_to_varieties_and_different_dates_of_sowing

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Parentage "selection from BMG 105" was not confirmed in any retrieved page. The marker and genomic papers returned concern other cultivars (for example VBNGg 2, CO 6, CO 7).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing station per the official table: ARS, Badnapur (Maharashtra) -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- No named breeder or scientist was found for BM 2003-2 in any search result.
- Agricultural Research Station, Badnapur is the institution the variety record names; the input record's "Agril Research Station" appears to be a shortened form of this (inferred, not confirmed).

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No institute email, phone, postal address or contact page for ARS Badnapur or the breeding team was returned. The Latur paper lists the Department of Agronomy, College of Agriculture, Latur 413512, Maharashtra as an author affiliation (https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v3i7/MDIwMTQxMjQ5.pdf), but that is not a contact for this variety's breeders.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2020). Pharma Innovation Journal 9(2): 398-401, sowing date and variety trial including BM 2003-2 -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue2/PartH/9-2-17-115.pdf
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown; about 2024 by the page age). pest_resistance.research_summary: Official table reports low incidence of bean thrips (presented as resistance/tolerance-related evidence in the table). In a whitefly screen, BM-2003-2 recorded the maximum whitefly population, and in the same study it was among the highest for jassid and among the highest for pod damage. These are susceptibility rankings, not resistance claims, so no pest resistance is established for whitefly, jassid or pod damage.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
BNKR-2 / BR-2 (rice), evidence digest. Name check: "BNKR-2" in the CSC minutes matches "BNKR-2 (Dhruba)" in the Rice Research Station, Bankura overview. The Seednet name "BR-2" was not found for rice in any result. Seednet lists it under green gram, so the seed-portal evidence is not used. The variety code "DHRU BA" is consistent with "Dhruba." The search found no rice page under "BR-2" or "BNKR-2 (Dhiren)." "Dhiren" is the name of BNKR-1, a different variety, so it is excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Reported as moderately resistant to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot and sheath rot, and as moderately resistant to leaf folder, in AICRIP screening nursery trials for Kharif 2008-2010 (cited via the Bankura overview; the underlying report is the AICRIP Progress Report, Screening Nursery 2008-2010, Directorate of Rice Research, Hyderabad, no URL found) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to BNKR-2 / Dhruba. The only flood-related text found concerns folk rice in general and is not about this variety (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345063572_Indigenous_Rice_of_West_Bengal).

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderate resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot, sheath rot and leaf folder, as above -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
Caution: a ResearchGate figure page for BNKR-1 says that "Dhiren and Dhruba" both have multiple pest resistance. It describes BNKR-1 and gives no Dhruba-specific data -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Showing-the-morpho-agronomic-characteristics-of-BNKR-1-Dhiren-lET-20760_tbl1_278301784

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Released as BNKR-2 (Dhruba) by the State Variety Release Committee, West Bengal, after three years (2008-2010) of national testing under the then Directorate of Rice Research, which recommended submitting a release proposal to the State committee -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
Yield is reported as higher than other HYVs of the same late maturity group. No numeric yield, duration in days, plant height or grain-type data for BNKR-2 was found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
Release year: the Seednet record gives 2015-10-12, but no source found gives a release year for BNKR-2. The year is unverified.

GENETICS AND QTL
Pedigree: a cross between IR 42 [IR1561/IR1737//CR9413] (female parent) and Patnai-23, a coastal West Bengal landrace (male parent), followed by pedigree selection -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
CONFLICT: the variety record gives parentage as "A SELECTION FROM BHAGALPUR LOCAL," which does not match the cross above. The variety record's parentage should be checked against the source.
No QTL, marker or genotyping study for BNKR-2 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Rice Research Station, Bankura (Nutanchati), West Bengal, which developed the variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
Lead breeder for BNKR-2: no name was found attached to BNKR-2 itself. Goutam Kumar Mallick of Rice Research Station, Bankura, is named as author of the BNKR-1 and BNKR-3 papers -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/283721470_BNKR-3_SAMPRITI_-_A_NEW_LATE_DURATION_HIGH-YIELDING_RICE_VARIETY_FOR_RAINFED_SHALLOW_LOWLANDS_OF_WEST_BENGAL_INDIA
A BNKR-1 page cites "Mallick et al. 2013, 2014" in connection with BNKR-2 (snippet only), so the attribution to Mallick is inferred, not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/278376937_BNKR-I_Dhiren_-_A_newly_released_late_duration_high-yielding_rice_variety_an_alternative_to_Swarna_MTU_7029_for_West_Bengal_India

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Shade tolerance and adaptation under coconut plantations are listed as special features of CO (GG) 3, along with profuse tillering and non-lodging. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/foragecrops_guineagrass.html
- The 2009 forage list describes CO (GG) 3 as shade tolerant with high green fodder yield. -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pdf/forage%20varieties.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for CO (GG) 3. Searches returned only the shade and non-lodging features above.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for CO (GG) 3. The search returned only greengram CO 8 pages (yellow mosaic and stem necrosis resistance). These concern a different crop and were excluded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Year of release is 2009 and the variety is perennial, with green fodder yield of 340-360 t/ha/year over seven harvests, against 270 t/ha/year for CO 2. -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/10_Guinea_Grass.pdf
- First harvest is at 75-80 days after planting and later harvests come once every 40-45 days, with about 320 t/ha/year over seven harvests. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/foragecrops_guineagrass.html
- Spacing is 50 x 50 cm, with 40,000 rooted slips per hectare, basal FYM at 25 t/ha, and NPK at 50:50:40 kg/ha. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/foragecrops_guineagrass.html
- Recommended sowing season is throughout the year under irrigation, and June to September or October to November under rainfed conditions, in all districts. -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/10_Guinea_Grass.pdf
- Across multi-location trials, CO (GG) 3 gave mean green fodder yield, dry matter yield and crude protein yield of 1082.4, 229.3 and 20.5 q/ha/year, above the qualifying and national checks. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694648_High_green_fodder_yielding_new_grass_varieties
- It ranked first at All-India level for green fodder yield, dry matter yield and crude protein yield in 2010, 2011 and 2012. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694648_High_green_fodder_yielding_new_grass_varieties

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage is recorded as clonal selection from Mumbasa; the input's "Not specified" is therefore incomplete. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/foragecrops_guineagrass.html
- No QTL, marker or genetic-diversity study for CO (GG) 3 was found.

- The variety was developed at the Department of Forage Crops, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694648_High_green_fodder_yielding_new_grass_varieties

disease_resistance.summary: DGGV-2 is susceptible to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). It is explicitly used as a 'susceptible check' in studies evaluating resistance to MYMV in other breeding lines and genotypes. There is no direct evidence that DGGV-2 itself possesses resistance to bruchid (Callosobruchus maculatus); rather, a cross involving DGGV-2 (V-02-802×DGGV-2) was noted to show resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: While a cross involving DGGV-2 (V-02-802×DGGV-2) showed resistance to bruchid, DGGV-2 itself is not explicitly stated to possess resistance to bruchid or other pests in the provided information.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields for DGGV-2 vary across studies. It was observed as a 'lowest yielder' at 393 kg/ha in one analysis. Another study recorded a seed yield of 701.3 kg/ha. However, with optimal management (sowing during the first fortnight of June and foliar spray of 2% DAP), DGGV-2 demonstrated a higher seed yield of 1380 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: The varying yield performance across different studies (393 kg/ha, 701.3 kg/ha, 1380 kg/ha) suggests its yield can be influenced by environmental conditions and specific agronomic practices.
agronomic_details.adaptation: DGGV-2 is suitable for sowing up to the end of June but not suitable for late sowing. It exhibits tolerance to shattering compared to Chinamung and Sel-4 varieties. It is responsive to fertilizer application at 25 N & 50 P kg/ha. Optimal performance was noted with first fortnight of June sowing combined with 2% DAP foliar spray.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics:
- Erect and determinate growth habit
- Long pods and Leaf shape ovate
- Green and shining seeds
- bold seeded variety
agronomic_details.field_trials: DGGV-2 has been evaluated in field trials concerning yield performance under varying sowing dates and nutrition, and for reaction to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: The marker CEDG115 was found to be polymorphic between DGGV-2 and IPM-2-14. This indicates its utility in genetic studies involving DGGV-2.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GBM-1 (greengram)

Name note: CSC minutes and Seednet both use "GBM-1". The only matching source, the DPD mungbean table, writes it as "GBM 1". None of the four searches returned a seednet.gov.in page, so Seednet's own listing (variety code A0305222) is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in GBM-1 returned only other moong varieties (Gujarat Mung-4, Gujarat Mung-7, Pusa Vishal) and unrelated pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
GBM 1, released 2016 by NAU, Gujarat, is listed as moderately tolerant to MYMV -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (same table repeated at https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf, entry 34-9:10)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
GBM 1 is listed with a yield of 11-12 q/ha and 102-105 days to maturity, suited to rabi cultivation in Gujarat -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
No multi-location trial data, field-trial reports or AICRP reports naming GBM-1 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, marker or QTL study for GBM-1 was returned. The parentage field ("Not specified") was not confirmed.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The DPD table lists the originating centre as NAU, Gujarat -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
No breeder name for GBM-1 was found. The Navsari Agricultural University pages returned (https://old.nau.in/alloprtitle.php, https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676) name pulse scientists and the Pulses and Castor Research Station, but none mentions GBM-1, so they are not attributed to it.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No NAU Pulse Research Station contact page or GBM-1 breeder contact was returned. The Pulse Research Station page returned (https://www.aau.in/college-menu/507) belongs to Anand Agricultural University, Vadodara, a different institution, and was not used.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The search returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper that names GBM-1. Greengram results were about other varieties or agronomy (for example https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/102-4-6-103-107.pdf on COGG 973, and https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5417, which cites NAU theses on nutrient management rather than varieties).

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Seller pages returned (https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/research-moong-seeds-8745067873.html, https://agribee.in/agriculture-seed/greengram-seeds/greengram-gujarat-4/, https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mung-seeds-guj-4-11807325230.html) sell other moong varieties (Partech-668, Gujarat-4, Guj-4) and do not name GBM-1. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing for GBM-1 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Gujarat -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (matches the CSC input "['Gujarat']" and the 2016 release year)

agronomic_details.yield: Reported average yields typically range from 60-70 q/ha. It is a subject of studies on genetic variability parameters related to seed yield and is considered a valuable genotype for yield improvement research.
agronomic_details.stability: IPM 02-14 serves as a reference variety in comparative performance studies of green gram varieties. Its consistent performance, particularly under summer cultivation with increased irrigation facilities, contributes to its popularization.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Primarily adapted for Spring/Summer season cultivation under normal sown conditions. It is also suitable for cultivation with increased irrigation facilities during the summer.

agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been extensively evaluated in field trials for growth parameters, yield, and tolerance to various abiotic stresses including heat, drought, and salinity. drought.details: Identified as a drought-tolerant genotype. It is among the high-yielding varieties recommended for adoption by farmers under drought conditions. Studies indicate it shows low genotype x environment interaction, contributing to yield stability. Physiological mechanisms contributing to tolerance include the overaccumulation of glycine betaine and adaptive morphological traits like higher Canopy Temperature Depression (CTD) and Membrane Stability Index (MSI).

heat.details: Recognized as a heat-tolerant green gram genotype capable of setting pods at high temperatures. It is discussed among heat-tolerant mung bean cultivars and genotypes that accumulate glycine betaine, which enhances tolerance to heat stress. IPM 02-3 also exhibits higher Canopy Temperature Depression (CTD), Membrane Stability Index (MSI), and total chlorophyll content under stress, indicating adaptive physiological responses.

salinity.details: Included in studies investigating abiotic stresses like salinity affecting mungbean production. It is mentioned in contexts related to mitigating NaCl stress and examining interactive effects of sodium and calcium on proline metabolism in salt-tolerant cultivars, suggesting some level of tolerance or inclusion in salinity tolerance research.

flood.details: Listed among varieties affected by waterlogging stress and included in studies on the response of mungbean to transient waterlogging at germination and seedling stages, but its specific tolerance level is not stated.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV).

pest_resistance.summary: Screened against Meloidogyne incognita (root-knot nematode), but specific resistance level is not provided.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield of 994 kgs/ha was originally reported. Specific trials showed variations, with yields up to 1409 kg/ha (14.09 q/ha) in comparison trials, and 912 kg/ha (9.12 q/ha) in specific regional projects (Jammu, 2015-2016). It serves as a standard check variety against which newer varieties exhibit yield superiority.
agronomic_details.stability: Demonstrates low genotype x environment interaction, indicating good yield stability across different environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for normal sown conditions during the Kharif season, particularly adapted to the North West Plain Zone of India (Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan). Historically, it has been a highly preferred variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Seed are shiny green and medium seed size with high protein content.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Extensive field trials include its evaluation under different NPK doses, inclusion in State Adaptive Trials, and performance comparisons against other varieties (e.g., Pusa M 2131, MH 02-15, ML 818). Its performance has been assessed in various regions including Jammu and Central Uttar Pradesh.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: IPM 02-3 has been included in studies evaluating genetic diversity using SSR markers.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Physiological responses associated with stress tolerance in IPM 02-3 include overaccumulation of glycine betaine, higher Canopy Temperature Depression (CTD), Membrane Stability Index (MSI), and total chlorophyll content under stress conditions.

It is discussed among heat-tolerant mung bean cultivars and genotypes that accumulate glycine betaine, which enhances tolerance to heat stress. IPM 02-3 also exhibits higher Canopy Temperature Depression (CTD), Membrane Stability Index (MSI), and total chlorophyll content under stress, indicating adaptive physiological responses.

salinity.details: Included in studies investigating abiotic stresses like salinity affecting mungbean production. It is mentioned in contexts related to mitigating NaCl stress and examining interactive effects of sodium and calcium on proline metabolism in salt-tolerant cultivars, suggesting some level of tolerance or inclusion in salinity tolerance research.

flood.details: Listed among varieties affected by waterlogging stress and included in studies on the response of mungbean to transient waterlogging at germination and seedling stages, but its specific tolerance level is not stated.

submergence.details: No specific information regarding submergence tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV).

pest_resistance.summary: Screened against Meloidogyne incognita (root-knot nematode), but specific resistance level is not provided.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: IPM 02-3 has been included in studies evaluating genetic diversity using SSR markers.

genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: Physiological responses associated with stress tolerance in IPM 02-3 include overaccumulation of glycine betaine, higher Canopy Temperature Depression (CTD), Membrane Stability Index (MSI), and total chlorophyll content under stress conditions.

agronomic_performance.yield: Average yield of 994 kgs/ha was originally reported. Specific trials showed variations, with yields up to 1409 kg/ha (14.09 q/ha) in comparison trials, and 912 kg/ha (9.12 q/ha) in specific regional projects (Jammu, 2015-2016). It serves as a standard check variety against which newer varieties exhibit yield superiority.
agronomic_performance.stability: Demonstrates low genotype x environment interaction, indicating good yield stability across different environments.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Suitable for normal sown conditions during the Kharif season, particularly adapted to the North West Plain Zone of India (Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan). Historically, it has been a highly preferred variety.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Seed are shiny green and medium seed size with high protein content.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: Extensive field trials include its evaluation under different NPK doses, inclusion in State Adaptive Trials, and performance comparisons against other varieties (e.g., Pusa M 2131, MH 02-15, ML 818). Its performance has been assessed in various regions including Jammu and Central Uttar Pradesh.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): Central variety listing records IPM 312-20 as having moderate resistance to MYMV (Kharif season). The parent IPM 3-1 is described as resistant to MYMV, and the second parent SPS 5 as having high-level resistance to MYMV, which supports the MYMV resistance origin. Cercospora leaf spot: IPM-312-20 was included in a CLS resistance screening of mungbean germplasm, but the search snippet does not state its resistance rating. Host-plant resistance: a ResearchGate review of green gram and black gram diseases lists IPM 312-20 (Vasudha) among varieties cited for host-plant resistance in disease management. Anthracnose and powdery mildew: an InTechOpen listing describes a different variety as moderately resistant to these diseases, and the snippet does not attribute this to IPM 312-20.

One search snippet mentions drought-tolerant mung bean cultivars in general, but it does not clearly attribute that status to IPM 409-4. heat.details: IPM 409-4 is listed among mungbean genotypes with higher canopy temperature depression (CTD), membrane stability index (MSI), and total chlorophyll content, traits associated with heat tolerance (cited from Punia et al., 2019). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MH-125 (chickpea / green gram)

Name check: The CSC/chickpea name "MH-125" and the Seednet name "MH 125" point to the same entry. In the sources I retrieved, though, the record is a green gram (mungbean) variety, and the Seednet crop field reads GREEN GRAM. The retrieved sources give MH 125 the local name Basanti. Each line below says which name the evidence refers to. Treat the chickpea classification as unconfirmed.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistance to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV) is recorded for MH 125 / Basanti, shown as a resistance trait in the mungbean release table -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- A chickpea-listing row for "MH 125" (CCSHAU, 2010, Haryana) is marked resistant to MYMV, leaf crinkle, web blight and anthracnose, and moderately resistant to cercospora leaf spot. This row sits in a chickpea table but uses mungbean-type disease traits, so the classification is doubtful -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pest resistance specific to MH-125: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity of 64-70 days and average yield of 12-15 q/ha are listed for Basanti (MH 125) -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (also https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf)
- A grower guide gives 64 days to harvest for MH 125 and recommends a seed rate of 8-9 kg/acre for kharif and 12-15 kg/acre for summer, with seed treated with Captan or Thiram at 3 g/kg -- https://apnakhetibazar.com/green-gram-moong/
- A Tamil Nadu multi-location stability study (33 mungbean genotypes, 3 locations) includes MH-125 in its tables. The extracted table is garbled, and one seed-yield-per-plant value of 17.239 appears against MH-125 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324637241_Stability_Analysis_in_Mungbean_Vigna_radiata_L_for_Micronutrients_Fe_Zn_and_Seed_Yield (refers to MH-125 as a mungbean line)
- Chickpea trials: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: the mungbean table lists Basanti's cross as Asha x PDM 90-1, released 2010 at 12-15 q/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339424589_Breeding_Progress_and_Future_Challenges_Biotic_Stresses (refers to Basanti / MH 125, mungbean)
- A 2021 mungbean association-mapping study lists Basanti with the pedigree Asha x PDM 90-1, developed at CCS HAU, Hisar, and genotyped with 89 SSR markers -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.749439/full (refers to Basanti, mungbean)
- QTL or marker studies specific to MH-125: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCSHAU), Hisar, per the state release listing -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (refers to Basanti / MH 125, mungbean)
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.
- Station or division: The 2021 study attributes Basanti to CCS HAU, Hisar, without naming a division -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.749439/full
- A Haryana varieties list from CCS HAU is available as a PDF, but it gives no breeder names -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1550223744.pdf (refers to chickpea varieties recommended for Haryana, not confirmed for MH-125)

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Institute contact (CCS HAU, Hisar): No email, phone or postal address found in retrieved results. The only institute-linked source is the varieties PDF at https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1550223744.pdf
- Seed-company contact found, but not an institute or breeder contact: Shakti Vardhak Hybrid Seeds, Tilak Bazaar, Talaki Gate, Hisar, Haryana 125001; 80901 00540 -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/moong-seed-8981382030.html (listing reviewed as a dealer lead only; it does not confirm MH-125 stock)

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2021). Association mapping for yield-attributing traits and yellow mosaic disease resistance in mung bean [Vigna radiata (L.) Wilczek]. Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.749439/full (DOI not retrieved; DOI likely 10.3389/fpls.2021.749439)

- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Stability analysis in mungbean (Vigna radiata L.) for micronutrients (Fe and Zn) and seed yield. - Chickpea-specific publications on MH-125: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME AND CROP CHECK -- "MH 2114" (code DHBH 1397) appears only as a pearl millet hybrid, not green gram. The Seednet name "MH-1142" appears only as a green gram (moong) variety. The "millet" crop field matches MH 2114, and the Seednet crop field matches MH-1142. The two names look like different varieties, so I have kept their evidence under separate labels. The parentage "MH 421" is a green gram name, and no source links it to MH 2114. Searches: 4 of 4 used.

STRESS TOLERANCE
[MH 2114 / DHBH 1397, pearl millet] The AICPMIP release table describes the entry as highly resistant to downy mildew and tolerant to rust and insect pests, but the table text is ambiguous about which row these traits belong to -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
[MH 2114] Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.
[MH-1142, green gram] A seller page says it does not tolerate waterlogging; this is a commercial claim, not an official trial result -- https://sanjivaniseeds.com/product/moong-mh-1142

DISEASE AND PEST
[MH 2114 / DHBH 1397] Same AICPMIP table entry as above (downy mildew, rust, insect pests); row assignment uncertain -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
[MH-1142] Official-style release table lists it as moderately resistant to anthracnose and powdery mildew and resistant to MYMV -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
[MH-1142] The same claims appear in a Hindi release summary (CVRC 2020) -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-1142/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
[MH 2114 / DHBH 1397] The 52nd Annual Pearl Millet Workshop proceedings list MH 2114 among hybrids in a trial at Jamnagar, SK Nagar, Aurangabad and Dhule -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2017.pdf
[MH 2114] Yield and maturity data from a verified source: No evidence found.
[MH-1142] The release table gives 11-12 q/ha yield and 60-65 days to maturity -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
[MH-1142] Commercial pages give different figures (63-70 days; 5-6 quintals per acre), so the figures conflict -- https://market.plantix.net/en/products/seeds/fa0224bd-83b8-42ce-972d-3eb10b39329e/moong-mh1142-truthfully-labelled-seed-4-kg-cloth-bag/

GENETICS AND QTL
[MH 2114] No evidence found for markers, QTL or parentage (Muskan x BDYR 2 / MH 421).

EVIDENCE DIGEST: MH-1142 (Green gram / mung)

The first batch returned titles and short snippets, and my attempt to check the full page text for "1142" hit the limit, so I could not verify most pages. Name note: The evidence was searched under "MH-1142". No Seednet page using "MH- 1142" came up, so no evidence refers to the Seednet name specifically.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searched under the variety name; the results contained no stress-tolerance information for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. Searched under the variety name; no resistance information was returned for this variety.

The arccjournals result (Iron nutrition in green gram, semi-arid Haryana) does not name MH-1142 in the visible snippet, so I discarded it. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6408

The parentage given in the record (selection from single-plant progenies of MH 421, Muskan x BDYR 2) was not confirmed by any search result. Any verification would need the CSC release notification or the CCS HAU release record.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found for a named breeder. The institution in the record is CCS Haryana Agricultural University; no search result confirmed that institution as the developer. -- No URL.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute, or division contact was returned.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis naming MH-1142 was returned. Discarded: the arccjournals page (different topic, see above).

drought.details: No specific information provided regarding MH 1772's drought tolerance level.

heat.details: Genotype MH 1772 has been studied for its heat tolerance and anatomical modifications in response to heat stress to mitigate impact on mungbean yield under different sowing conditions. It is one of the genotypes assessed for heat tolerance.

salinity.details: MH 1772 is identified as a salt-tolerant genotype and is recommended for cultivation in salt-affected regions to enhance mungbean production. Studies have focused on its response to salinity (NaCl) on germination and seedling growth.

flood.details: No specific information provided regarding MH 1772's tolerance to flood stress.

disease_resistance.summary: MH 1772 is a high-yielding disease-resistant variety, specifically resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). It has also been included in screenings against web blight disease (Macrophomina phaseolina infection), although a specific resistance level for MH 1772 against web blight is not explicitly stated as 'resistant' in the provided results.

pest_resistance.summary: MH 1772 has been included in germplasm screening trials against major insect pests such as the gram pod borer and sucking insects. However, its specific level of resistance to these pests is not explicitly detailed as 'resistant' or 'tolerant' in the provided results.

agronomic_details.yield: MH 1772 is a high-yielding variety, with an average yield of 11-13 quintals per hectare (q/ha). Farmers have reported achieving 10-15% more yield by cultivating this variety.
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified in the provided results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The variety has been notified for cultivation during the Kharif season in the North East Plain Zones (NEPZ).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MH 318 (greengram / moong)
Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "MH 318", so every finding below refers to that one name. Seednet (seednet.gov.in) did not appear in any search result, so no Seednet record was checked.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to MYMV (mungbean yellow mosaic virus); no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Listed as resistant to yellow mosaic virus, with its main characteristics described as well under rice-wheat rotation -- https://krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/ (the search result shows the URL with "www." omitted in the source: https://www.krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to MYMV; no other disease or pest resistance recorded for MH 318 -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Dealer page says it has resistance to yellow mosaic virus; this is a commercial claim, not a trial result -- https://drseeds.in/moong/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 60-65 days -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf ; https://www.krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/
- Yield 14 q/ha in kharif and 10 q/ha in spring/summer -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf ; https://www.krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/
- Dealer page gives 8-9 quintals per acre; units differ from the official figures, so treat it as unverified -- https://drseeds.in/moong/
- Pot-trial comparison of MH 318 with other genotypes under zinc fertilisation (CCS HAU, 2010-11). Per the snippet, MH 318 had among the lowest pods per plant (5.28) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/317594571_Green_gram_Vigna_radiata_L_Productivity_and_Grain_Quality_enrichment_through_Zinc_Fertilization
- No multi-location AICRP trial result for MH 318 found

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found (no parentage, breeding method or QTL/marker study in results). The DPD record gives no parentage either.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCSHAU), Hisar, released 2015 per DPD -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Release year conflict: a 2022 Krishakjagat article gives 2016 (SVRC), while DPD gives 2015 -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found
- Institution page: https://hau.ac.in/page/achievements-11 (lists MH-318 among moong varieties with raw seed production in 2022-23; the figure's unit is not shown in the snippet)

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder: No evidence found
- Institute: CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar, Haryana, India (postal code 125004, from departmental affiliations in a ResearchGate listing) -- https://researchgate.net/institution/CCS_Haryana_Agricultural_University
- Institute website: https://hau.ac.in ; no official email or phone number for the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding appeared in any result

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in the search snippet (2010-11 pot study; year of publication not shown). Title: "Green gram (Vigna radiata L.) Productivity and Grain Quality enrichment through Zinc Fertilization", CCS HAU, Hisar -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/317594571_Green_gram_Vigna_radiata_L_Productivity_and_Grain_Quality_enrichment_through_Zinc_Fertilization
- Authors not shown in the search snippet (screen-house iron-enrichment study on seven greengram genotypes including MH 318; year and journal not shown) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/317594571_Green_gram_Vigna_radiata_L_Productivity_and_Grain_Quality_enrichment_through_Zinc_Fertilization
- KrishiKosh theses or AICRP/ICAR reports specifically on MH 318: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- CCS HAU's RDS Seed Farm produces certified/TFL moong seed for sale through university counters at Gate No. 3 (Balsamand Road) and the ATIC at Gate No. 4 (Rajgarh Road); the page does not name MH 318 -- https://hau.ac.in/page/seed-sale-information

disease_resistance.research_summary: Resistant to MYMV (mungbean yellow mosaic virus), recorded by DPD. A Krishakjagat article lists it as resistant to yellow mosaic virus, which is the same disease. A dealer page (drseeds.in) also claims yellow mosaic virus resistance, but this is a commercial claim, not a trial result. No other disease resistance is recorded for MH 318.

drought.details: MH-421 is resistant to drought stress and has been evaluated for drought tolerance under semi-arid conditions. It maintains physiological functioning under moisture-induced stresses. Differential responses to drought stress have been studied.

heat.details: MH-421 is tolerant to heat stress and terminal heat stress. It maintained high yield and physiological functioning under high temperature. It is considered an excellent heat-tolerant mungbean variety.

salinity.details: MH-421 has been used in studies evaluating the effects of salt stress on growth and biochemical changes in green gram, identified as a high yielding genotype in this context. However, its specific tolerance level to salinity is not explicitly stated as 'tolerant' or 'resistant' in the provided results.

flood.details: MH-421 is mentioned in a list of green gram varieties that include those considered for waterlogging tolerance. While studies on QTLs for anaerobic germination and tolerance to early submergence in mungbean exist, it is not explicitly stated that MH-421 itself possesses significant flood or submergence tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: MH-421 is resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV/YMV). It is also reported to be resistant to all rusts. Two dominant genes govern MYMD resistance in crosses involving MH-421.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield reported between 10-12 quintals per hectare (q/ha) and specifically 12.00 q/ha in some instances. Other reports show 17.06 q/ha or 8.65 q/ha in specific contexts.
agronomic_details.stability: MH-421 maintained high yield and physiological functioning under high temperature stress, indicating good stability under abiotic stress conditions. It has been evaluated under semi-arid conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the North Western Plains Zone (NWPZ) and Central Zone (CZ), specifically for cultivation in Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Western Uttar Pradesh during the Summer season. Also suitable for Kharif season.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium-dwarf plant type, non-shattering pods, and medium bold shining green seeds.
agronomic_details.field_trials: MH-421 has been a subject of Cluster Frontline Demonstrations (CFLD) in Sirsa District, Haryana, and disseminated through farmers' participatory approaches in Hisar district, Haryana. It is a common variety used as a test crop in various agricultural studies.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (SNP/SSR) are detailed for MH-421 in the provided results.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: While studies mention QTLs for anaerobic germination and tolerance to early submergence in mungbean generally, no specific QTLs are attributed directly to MH-421 in the provided information.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Physiological, biochemical, and antioxidant enzyme activities are studied in MH-421 under stress conditions. Biochemical changes have been observed in response to stress. Resistance to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Disease (MYMD) in MH-421 is governed by two dominant genes.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: As a 'Central released variety' from CCSHAU, it is likely available through government seed corporations and agricultural departments.
commercial_info.availability_status: Readily available, indicated by its status as a Central released variety, its presence in KVKs, and its popularity for cultivation.
commercial_info.kvk: The variety MH-421 was collected from Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) in Rajasthan, indicating KVKs as a source of availability.
commercial_info.private_dealers: Mentioned as one of the 'Popular Varieties' for summer moong cultivation, suggesting availability through private agricultural dealers.

drought.details: ML 267 has been consistently reported as drought-resistant. It was utilized in studies evaluating source leaf responses to water-deficit stresses and in experiments where drought was induced by PEG (Polyethylene glycol). Agrobacterium mediated genetic transformation attempts were made for ML 267 specifically to enhance drought stress tolerance, indicating its potential or existing tolerance. It has also been used as a test crop in drought-related experiments.

heat.details: ML 267 is identified as a heat-tolerant mungbean genotype based on morpho-physiological parameters. It has been evaluated in crosses (e.g., ML 267 × LGG 528) for heat stress tolerance and yield attributes using generation mean analysis. Studies have also evaluated stress tolerance indices to identify heat tolerance, including ML 267.

salinity.details: ML 267 is listed among varieties for developing bio-fortified mungbean lines with enhanced stress tolerance, including salinity. Specific studies have investigated salt tolerance in mungbean cultivars like ML 267 and the interactive effects of sodium and calcium on proline metabolism in salt-tolerant mungbean involving this genotype.

flood.details: Waterlogging is mentioned as a key abiotic stress for mungbean generally, but no specific information on ML 267's tolerance or susceptibility to flood or waterlogging was found.

disease_resistance.summary: ML 267 is reported to be resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). However, it is classified as Highly Susceptible (HS) to the root-knot nematode, *Meloidogyne incognita*.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance details found, apart from its susceptibility to *Meloidogyne incognita* (a nematode pest), which is listed under disease resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: While specific average yield values are not provided, ML 267 has been evaluated for yield and yield attributes in genetic crosses. Its 100-seed weight is reported as 12.0g. It is considered a popular cultivar.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly specified.
agronomic_details.adaptation: ML 267 is a popular cultivar of greengram, adaptable for cultivation during both Kharif and Summer seasons. It is particularly recommended for the North Western Plain Zone. It shows good tolerance to the post-emergence herbicide imazethapyr, which is beneficial for weed management. It is also suitable for sowing as sprouted seeds in short-duration pulse rotations.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: HAIRINESS OF STEM AND BROAD; SLIGHT TINGE OF PURPLE COLOUR. The seed size is described as small.
agronomic_details.field_trials: ML 267 has been used as a test crop in strip plot design experiments investigating different tillage methods. It has also been extensively used in generational studies (P1, P2, F1, F2, B1, and B2 generations) to analyze yield and stress tolerance traits.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (e.g., SNPs, SSRs) or QTL positions are directly reported for ML 267 in the provided results.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: ML 267 has been utilized in genetic crosses for research purposes. A cross of ML 267 × LGG 528 was used for generation mean analysis to study the inheritance of yield, yield attributes, Water Use Efficiency (WUE), and heat stress tolerance. This cross also produced transgressive segregants for traits such as harvest index, Specific Leaf Area (SLA), Specific Leaf Weight (SLW), and relative injury (stress-related traits). Additionally, a cross between ML 267 and urdbean cv. Mash 114 was made for mapping Yellow Mosaic Disease (YMD) resistance, indicating that MYMV resistance in this cross is controlled by digenic recessive genes.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: ML 267 has been included in studies aimed at identifying heat-tolerant genotypes through morpho-physiological parameters and gene expression analysis related to abiotic stress tolerance. However, specific genes or pathways linked directly to ML 267's tolerance mechanisms are not detailed.

disease_resistance.summary: (1) Yellow mosaic virus (YMV; the field guide specifically names MYMV): listed as tolerant in the Kharif field guide (ResearchGate) and in the mungbean state-release table (dpd.gov.in). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Madhira Pesara 347 (variety_name) / Madhira Pesara-347 (seednet_variety_name)

Crop check: the record says chickpea, but the Seednet crop is GREEN GRAM (MOONG BEAN/MOONG). Every source I found lists this variety under mungbean/green gram, and the chickpea-table hit is a mixed-up list. Treat the crop as green gram (Vigna radiata) unless the Seednet record shows otherwise. The Seednet portal itself was not reachable in these searches, so variety code A0305151 is unverified.

Name check: the sources use both "Madhira Pesara-347" (the dpd.gov.in mungbean sheets, which match the Seednet form) and "Madhira Pesara 347" (the other sources). The findings below refer to the same variety under both names.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Madhira Pesara-347 ... ARS, Madhira ... Moderately resistant to PM. The sheet's layout is ambiguous about which row this belongs to, so verify before relying on it. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- The mungbean list gives Madhira Pesara-347 as a Telangana/AP release with YMV and Cercospora leaf spot listed as its tolerances. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Field guide: Madhira Pesara 347 (Kharif) is tolerant to MYMV. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265793473_Field_guide_to_Mungbean_and_Urdbean
DISEASE AND PEST -- The mungbean state-release table lists tolerance to thrips and stem fly alongside YMV and Cercospora leaf spot. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- The chickpea-labelled sheet also lists tolerance to Cercospora and leaf spot, plus anthracnose, for Madhira Pesara 347; this is probably a mis-tabulated entry. -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The mungbean release table gives duration of 65-70 days and yield of 13-15 q/ha, with Kharif and Rabi suitability. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The chickpea-labelled sheet gives 12.00 q/ha and 60-70 days; this is inconsistent with the mungbean data and should be treated as unreliable. -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The station reports that five greengram varieties have been released from it. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/agricultural-research-station-madhira/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PA 9072 (MH 2082) (PB 1756), Pearl millet (bajra)

Name note: "variety_name" is PA 9072 and "seednet_variety_name" is PA 9072 (MH 2082) (PB 1756). Most evidence names PA 9072 alone, or the CSC table lists PA 9072 next to MH 2082 and PB 1756. Under each heading below I say which name the evidence uses. The 2018 AICPMIP table is garbled, so I could not reliably match some of its fields to this row. Those items are flagged.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Product page lists this hybrid as tolerant to moisture stress and lodging, and as suitable for low-rainfall areas (name used: PA 9072, "Proagro PA 9072 Hybrid Bajra") -- Tolerant to moisture stress; Resistant to Downy mildew and Tolerant to lodging; Suitable for low rainfall areas -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_PA_9072
- AICPMIP release table (name used: PA 9072 with MH 2082 and PB 1756; row alignment uncertain) lists tolerance to moisture stress and lodging -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf (http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf)
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence trial scores specific to PA 9072. The general crop-level drought statement in an ICRISAT/FAO annex is not variety-specific -- https://www.fao.org/4/w1808e/w1808e0k.htm (discarded for variety purposes)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Downy mildew resistance is claimed on the product page (name used: PA 9072) -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_PA_9072
- AICPMIP table (name used: PA 9072, row alignment uncertain) lists resistance to downy mildew, blast, smut and ergot -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- No evidence found for pest (stem borer, shoot fly, head miner) reactions specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is given as 70-72 days, early maturing, for kharif only (name used: PA 9072) -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_PA_9072
- Amazon listing repeats the early-maturing, kharif-only claim and the Western Rajasthan and parts of Haryana suitability (name used: Proagro 9072) -- https://www.amazon.in/Proagro-9072-Bayer-BioScience-Hybrid/dp/B09DPBDGFK
- Seed-treatment caution on the Amazon listing: do not treat pre-treated seed with products other than those the seed company recommends -- https://www.amazon.in/Proagro-9072-Bayer-BioScience-Hybrid/dp/B09DPBDGFK
- No evidence found for multi-location yield data, trial means or check comparisons for PA 9072. The 2021 AICPMIP-related Frontiers paper on pearl millet varieties in arid India did not name this variety in the retrieved text -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8202413/ (discarded)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: Unknown (as supplied). No retrieved source gives parentage for PA 9072. The AICPMIP table has a parentage column, but the retrieved text does not assign a parent pair to this row -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Breeding-line codes: MH 2082 and PB 1756 appear as the variety codes in the AICPMIP table (name used: MH 2082, PB 1756) -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Breeding method: No evidence found.
- Genome resources and QTL/marker studies naming PA 9072: No evidence found. The general pearl millet genome and SNP papers retrieved do not mention this variety -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28922347/ and https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9871632/ (discarded for this variety)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing or marketing company (name used: PA 9072 with institution "Bayer Bio Science Pvt. Ltd."): The AICPMIP table lists the institution as Bayer Bio Science, with Hyderabad appearing in the same row block (row alignment uncertain) -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Product literature names the brand as Proagro and the manufacturer as Bayer CropScience -- https://www.amazon.in/Proagro-9072-Bayer-BioScience-Hybrid/dp/B09DPBDGFK
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Institute-level contact (third-party directory listing, not an official Bayer page; it lists a company contact person for Bayer Bioscience Pvt. Ltd., formerly Proagro Seed Co): Jens Hartmann; Bayer House, Central Avenue, Hiranandani Gardens, Powai, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India -- https://www.exportersindia.com/bayer-bioscience-pvt-ltd-formerly-proagro/
- Official email, phone, or Bayer India contact page for this variety: No evidence found.
- Note: the Gourav Beej Bhandar phone number (08045735996) is a seller contact for a different Proagro product (9001), so it is excluded here -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/proagro-9001-bajra-seed-2854290756212.html

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. None of the retrieved papers, theses, AICRP reports or conference items names PA 9072 or MH 2082 or PB 1756 in the text I could see. The AICPMIP release table is a notification record, not a publication. Items retrieved but excluded as not about this variety: DOI 10.3389/fpls.2021.670201 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8202413/), DOI 10.1270/jsbbs.23082 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11561417/), DOI 10.3389/fpls.2022.1068883 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9871632/).
- KrishiKosh thesis search: not run; the four-search limit was used on the other topics.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Amazon.in listing for a 1.5 kg pack of Proagro 9072 (Bayer BioScience, hybrid bajra) is marked currently unavailable -- https://www.amazon.in/Proagro-9072-Bayer-BioScience-Hybrid/dp/B09DPBDGFK
- Retailer listings found (Gourav Beej Bhandar, Mahendragarh) offer Proagro 9001 and 9450, not PA 9072, so they are excluded -- https://www.indiamart.com/gouravbeejbhandar/vegetable-seeds.html
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sale listings for PA 9072: No evidence found (not searched; the four-search limit was used).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Product page and Amazon listing: Western Rajasthan and parts of Haryana -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_PA_9072
- AICPMIP release table: Rajasthan, and drier parts of a further state that the garbled layout does not let me read reliably. Gujarat is the likely reading but is not confirmed by the text -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Official ICAR/AICRP notification text for the recommended states: not retrieved. The S.O. number 1379(E), dated 27.03.2018, appears in the AICPMIP table but I could not confirm which row it belongs to.

Search coverage: 4 of 4 searches used (variety/release, breeder/institute, research, seed availability). Breeder name, official institute contact, peer-reviewed or AICRP publications, and yield data remain unverified. The next step would be to check the official AICPMIP notification PDF directly and search KrishiKosh and Bayer India's official site.

- The same review lists a second row, TM 2000-2 Pairy Mung, with 88-90 days and 10-11 q/ha. The day-count conflict between rows is unresolved.

- Central Released Varieties of Green Gram/Mungbean in India (table compiled from AICRP on MULLaRP Project Coordinator's Reports and ICAR annual reports, seednet.gov.in cited as source). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I ran four searches, but the search tool then hit its usage limit, so I could not re-query the one source that mentions Pant Mung-5. Only one result (the DPD central-release compilation) contains the variety, and I saw only its first ~600 characters. Treat the findings below as thin and unverified.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The search used "Pant Mung-5" for both the CSC release name and the Seednet name. Seednet did not appear in any result, so I could not confirm the portal name or variety code A0305153. The evidence below refers to "Pant Mung-5" as written in the DPD compilation.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Not found in the captured text. The snippet truncated before the salient-features column for this entry. No evidence on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was captured. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- Pant Mung-5 is listed in the salient-features column as resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (the text reads "Res. to mungbean yellow", truncated). The full resistance wording and rating were not captured. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The compilation lists yield of 10-12 q/ha and days to maturity of 62-79 for Pant Mung-5. The source gives these as a single row, so I cannot confirm the exact mapping of each number to each column. Season listed as Kharif and Summer. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage (VC 6370-92 x VC 6141-96, selected from VC-6368) comes from the user-supplied record only. No search result confirmed it. No QTL or marker studies were found. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The compilation attributes the variety to "GBPUAT, Pant Nagar" (G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar). No breeder or scientist name was found. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, email, phone, postal address or institute contact page appeared in the results. The institute name above is the only identifier, and its contact details still need to be verified on the university's official site.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. Searches on research papers, AICRP reports, theses and KrishiKosh returned no Pant Mung-5 items.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listings. The only "seed" results were unrelated retail mung-bean sprouting seed.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Pant Mung-5 is listed for Uttar Pradesh in the DPD compilation, not Uttarakhand as in the record. This may reflect the pre-2000 state boundaries, when Uttarakhand was part of Uttar Pradesh. Reconcile this against the CSC minutes. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

RELEASE YEAR -- The DPD compilation gives 2010, while the record says NaT. Verify against the CSC minutes or the Seednet notification before accepting either value. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

Priority follow-ups: retrieve the full DPD PDF row for Pant Mung-5, check the Seednet entry for A0305153, and check the GBPUAT Pantnagar pulses/breeding pages for the lead breeder and contact details.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
The search budget ran out after four queries, and my fifth attempt was rejected, so this digest rests on four searches. Most results were short snippets, not full pages.

Identity conflict: the evidence points to Pusa 0672 being a green gram (mungbean) variety, not chickpea. The seednet name (Pusa-0672, green gram) matches that. The chickpea-oriented searches returned nothing about Pusa 0672.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Listed as resistant to MYMV (mung bean yellow mosaic virus) in a central-release table for green gram; evidence refers to the mungbean Pusa 0672 (seednet name Pusa-0672). -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Listed as moderately resistant to powdery mildew (PM) in the same table; evidence refers to the mungbean Pusa 0672. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Table row shows bold seed and long pods; yield and days-to-maturity values are in the table but were not legible in the snippet. Evidence refers to the mungbean Pusa 0672. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Multi-location or field-trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for Pusa 0672 parentage (11/395 x ML 267) or markers.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Originating institution listed as IARI, New Delhi, in the central-release table for Pusa 0672 (year 2010); evidence refers to the mungbean Pusa 0672. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder or institute contact details found. The only institutional reference is "IARI, New Delhi" (no address, email or phone). No contact page URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found in the searches for peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses or conference papers specific to Pusa 0672.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found (no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing retrieved).

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Table entry for Pusa 0672 shows a zone code with J&K and "MN" (likely Manipur) in the "suitable for" column, and kharif season; Tripura was not visible in the snippet. Evidence refers to the mungbean Pusa 0672. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

RECORD CORRECTIONS
- Crop: the central-release table places Pusa 0672 under green gram/mungbean, not chickpea. The crop field in the record should be checked.
- Year of release: the table gives 2010, so "NaT" should be replaced with 2010 (from the central-release table; a CSC notification should be checked before finalising).
- Parentage and institution: not confirmed beyond IARI, New Delhi.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Variety name and Seednet name both match "Pusa 1641". The DPD central-release table lists it with resistance to MYMV and, in a cell cut off in the retrieved text, something related to low-level disease; the excerpt does not show the full resistance wording. -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- A farmer-facing article describes Pusa 1641 as high-yielding and disease-resistant, bred for summer sowing in the Delhi-NCR zone, with tolerance of high summer temperatures implied by its short duration. This is a press article, not a trial report, so tolerance is not quantified. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/pusa-1641-emerges-as-game-changer-for-summer-moong-cultivation-farmers-report-high-yields-and-profits/
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Pusa 1641. The searches returned only general moong variety lists.

DISEASE AND PEST -- The DPD table entry for Pusa 1641 (2021, ICAR New Delhi) records resistance to MYMV (mung bean yellow mosaic virus). The rest of the resistance cell is truncated in the retrieved text. -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- A Hindi farm article states that the variety has disease resistance as a key feature, without naming the diseases. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/pusa-1641-farmers-are-earning-lakhs-from-this-summer-moong-variety-you-should-also-know-the-method/
DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for pest resistance (for example whitefly or Cercospora) specific to Pusa 1641.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The DPD table lists 12-13 and 62-64 for Pusa 1641 under yield and duration columns; the excerpt does not show units or the column headers, so these numbers should be checked against the original PDF before use. -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The variety matures in 55–60 days and is suited to summer sowing in Delhi-NCR. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/pusa-1641-emerges-as-game-changer-for-summer-moong-cultivation-farmers-report-high-yields-and-profits/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The Hindi article recommends sowing in summer between 10 and 15 April, a seed rate of 15–20 kg per hectare, 30 cm row spacing and 10 cm plant spacing, with soil testing and zinc correction where needed. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/pusa-1641-farmers-are-earning-lakhs-from-this-summer-moong-variety-you-should-also-know-the-method/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- An IARI seed-treatment advisory recommends Rhizobium and phosphate-solubilising bacteria treatment and lists Pusa 1641 among high-yielding green gram varieties. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/farming-agriculture/high-yielding-varieties-of-green-gram-moong-iari-scientific-seed-treatment-and-sowing-guide/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No multi-location trial data for Pusa 1641 was found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for parentage, breeding-line code, breeding method, QTL, markers or genome resources for Pusa 1641. The searches returned no genetic study naming this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The variety is attributed to the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), Pusa, in a press article. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/pusa-1641-emerges-as-game-changer-for-summer-moong-cultivation-farmers-report-high-yields-and-profits/
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The DPD table attributes the 2021 release to ICAR, New Delhi. -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the lead breeder's name(s). The searches did not return a breeder list or a developing-scientist name for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found for an IARI division email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for this variety. No breeder contact was found. The Seednet portal was not returned by any search, so its entry was not checked.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The searches returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP or ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming Pusa 1641.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU or dealer listings for Pusa 1641. The only seed-related result was a general IARI advisory urging farmers to buy certified seed. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/farming-agriculture/high-yielding-varieties-of-green-gram-moong-iari-scientific-seed-treatment-and-sowing-guide/
SEED AVAILABILITY -- The Amazon.in search returned unrelated Pusa-branded seed listings (mustard, marigold, black gram) and was discarded. -- https://www.amazon.in/pusa-seed/s?k=pusa+seed
