search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: TMV 14 (groundnut)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "TMV 14", so one set of searches covered both. The Seednet portal itself was not returned by any search, so no Seednet-sourced evidence was found. Variety code A0402230 and the CSC release minutes were not found either.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The culture is completely resistant to rust disease and tolerant to late leaf spot (score 2.0), and it matures in 95-100 days. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
- Drought: No TMV 14-specific drought result was found. A PEG-6000 germination screen (Umadevi et al.) lists TMV 14 in a table, but the retrieved text does not show its classification, so I have not counted it. -- https://masujournal.org/view_journal.php?id=658

DISEASE AND PEST
- For late leaf spot and rust, TMV 14 showed moderate resistance compared with check varieties, and it showed tolerance to Spodoptera litura, thrips, Helicoverpa armigera and leaf miner. -- https://www.academia.edu/90525667/Groundnut_TMV_14_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety (also in the EJPB paper, https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00039.5)
- Leaf spot score: medium resistant reaction to leaf spot (score 6.0), against 9.0 for susceptible checks VRI 2, CO 2 and TMV 2. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9a45/4207f9b78a29dc7b42acf70e2eff76030c6b.pdf
- Note the conflict: the ORS page reports complete rust resistance, while the EJPB paper reports only moderate resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield: 2124 kg/ha in kharif, 11.5% above VRI (Gn) 6 (1904 kg/ha) and 15.2% above TMV Gn 13 (1844 kg/ha). -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-10-1-039
- Rabi yield: 2286 kg/ha under irrigation, 29.7% above VRI (Gn) 6 and 32.3% above TMV Gn 13. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-10-1-039
- Seed quality: shelling of 70.6% with 92% SMK and 38 g of 100-kernel weight. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
- Agritech gives a different maturity (105-110 days), rainfed/irrigated averages of 2222/2360 kg/ha, and oil content of 45.01%. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20TMV%2014.html
- Rainfed weed-management trial using TMV 14 in late rabi (Swetha et al., 2022). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366555054_Novel_method_to_manage_weeds_in_the_rainfed_groundnut_var_VRI_8_and_TMV_14_using_nano_encapsulated_herbicide_formulations
- Multi-location and adaptive trials: multi-location trials were run in Kharif 2013, 2014 and 2015 under rainfed conditions, and rabi 2013-14. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9a45/4207f9b78a29dc7b42acf70e2eff76030c6b.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The searches returned no QTL, marker or genetic-mapping study for TMV 14. The only marker paper retrieved (Mol Biol Rep 2024) does not name TMV 14 in the retrieved text. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-024-09633-z
- Pedigree: cross derivative of VRI 6 x R 2001-(2), developed by pedigree method of breeding. -- https://doaj.org/article/fc2c92a9a86244b39def39f3826126e9
- Parentage conflict: agritech.tnau.ac.in lists "VR12 x TVG 0004" instead. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20TMV%2014.html

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead scientist: M. Vaithiyalingan (Assistant Professor, PBG), with K. Ganesamurthy, G.V. Ramasubramanian, Sangeetha Panicker and R. Vaidyanathan. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-10-1-039
- Developing station: Oilseeds Research Station, Tindivanam-604 002. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9a45/4207f9b78a29dc7b42acf70e2eff76030c6b.pdf
- Origin: culture TVG 0856 was identified as best in station trials, tested in MLT and ART, and released as TMV 14 (2018). -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/annual-report/
- Release year conflict: 2018 (ORS, EJPB) versus 2019 (agritech). Release-minute number not found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Oilseeds Research Station, Tindivanam: postal address "Oil Seeds Research Station, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Tindivanam 604 002" -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9a45/4207f9b78a29dc7b42acf70e2eff76030c6b.pdf
- Institute e-mail as printed on the TNAU page: "ars tmv @tnau.ac.in" (the space is in the source; it is probably "arstmv@tnau.ac.in", but this is unverified) -- http://www.tnau.ac.in/tvm/
- Corresponding author: M. Vaithiyalingan, e-mail printed in the paper: mvaithiyalingan@gmail.com (a personal address, not an institutional one) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-10-1-039
- Phone: No evidence found.
- Institute contact page URL: http://www.tnau.ac.in/tvm/

PUBLICATIONS
- Vaithiyalingan, M., Ganesamurthy, K., Ramasubramanian, G.V., Panicker, S., & Vaidyanathan, R. (2019). Groundnut TMV 14 – A new high yielding Spanish bunch groundnut variety. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding, 10(1), 307–311. -- DOI 10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00039.5 (https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00039.5)
- Swetha, S. et al. (2022). Novel method to manage weeds in the rainfed groundnut (var. VRI 8 and TMV 14) using nano encapsulated herbicide formulations. Journal of Applied and Natural Science, 14(4), 1341–1350. -- DOI 10.31018/jans.v14i4.3920
- Umadevi, M., Mohammed, D., Rajeswari, R., Shanthi, P., & Kalaiyarasi, R. (year not retrieved). Screening of groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.) varieties for drought tolerance using polyethylene glycol. -- https://masujournal.org/view_journal.php?id=658 (TMV 14 appears only in a table; not confirmed as a finding)
- AICRP (Groundnut) annual reports, ICAR reports and KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Dealer listing: Maha Agro Traders (Villupuram, Tamil Nadu) lists TMV 14 among groundnut varieties, 40 kg packs at ₹95/kg. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/groundnut-seeds-2850781083933.html (unverified commercial listing)
- Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK and SAU seed-sale listings: No evidence found.
- ORS Tindivanam breeder-seed production target for 2018-19 includes TMV 14 (7 ha target, 5.40 t/ha achieved). -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/crop-improvement/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Tamil Nadu: released for Tamil Nadu groundnut cultivation; the pod and kernel traits are acceptable to farmers. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
- Season scope: the agritech page lists kharif, rabi and summer seasons across Tamil Nadu. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20TMV%2014.html

disease_resistance.research_summary: Rust: the ORS Tindivanam page reports the culture as completely resistant to rust disease; the EJPB paper reports only moderate resistance to rust compared with check varieties. These sources conflict and the conflict is unresolved. Late leaf spot (LLS): the ORS page reports tolerance with a score of 2.0; the EJPB paper reports moderate resistance compared with check varieties; a separate leaf spot score reports a medium resistant reaction (score 6.0) against 9.0 for susceptible checks VRI 2, CO 2 and TMV 2. Multiple sources agree on LLS tolerance or moderate-to-medium resistance, though the scales differ.

pest_resistance.research_summary: TMV 14 showed tolerance to Spodoptera litura, thrips, Helicoverpa armigera and leaf miner (reported in the EJPB paper and the Academia.edu copy of the same work). No quantitative pest scores were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VL Moongphali 1 (groundnut): EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: the CSC release-minute name is "VL Moongphali 1" and the Seednet name is "VL Moongphali-1". Every source found used the hyphenated form or the "VL-Moongphali-1" spelling, and none came from the Seednet portal itself. The findings below therefore refer to the same variety under both names, but no Seednet record was retrieved.

Searches run: 4 (release/traits; breeder/institute; Seednet code; research/parentage). Seednet was not reachable through search, so the variety code A0402180 is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to late leaf spot (LLS) and root rot, per the DAC notified-variety table. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The sources found name only LLS and root rot resistance.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to late leaf spot and root rot. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx ; https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
- Pest resistance: No evidence found for this variety. Pest tolerance cited for the parent ICGV 86590 is resistance to Spodoptera litura and Sclerotium rolfsii. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/538/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield potential about 1943 kg/ha, listed in the DAC table. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Recommended production system: kharif (rainy season). -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Maturity days, oil content and multi-location trial data for VL-Moongphali-1: No evidence found. The 96–123 day maturity and 48% oil figures belong to the parent ICGV 86590. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/538/
- Pod yield per hectare and oil content for ICGV 86590 in its own release, from the ICAR-DGR compendium: 1,785 kg/ha pod yield and 48% oil. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: selection from ICGV-86590 (X 14-4-B-19-8 x PI 239747), breeding method pureline selection. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- The same parentage appears in the compendium as "X14-4-B-19-8", while the ICRISAT monograph gives the parent as "X14-4-B-19-B" crossed with PI259747. Flag this discrepancy for checking. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/538/
- QTL or marker studies for this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, Uttarakhand. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1 ; https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
- Station: VPKAS Almora; the ICAR page places the institute's experimental farm at Hawalbagh. -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/node/3127
- Institute director named on the ICAR page (2021): Dr. Lakshmi Kant. This is an institutional role, not a breeder credit. -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/node/3127

CONTACT DETAILS
- Director, ICAR-VPKAS Almora: Dr. Lakshmi Kant (as named on the 2021 ICAR page). Email, phone and postal address: No evidence found in the retrieved text. -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/node/3127
- Institute contact page URL: Not retrieved. Check https://www.icar.org.in or the VPKAS site directly.
- Breeder email/phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or conference paper specifically on VL Moongphali-1 was found.
- Related (parent): ICRISAT (1992). Groundnut Variety ICGV 86590. Monograph, ICRISAT -- https://oar.icrisat.org/538/
- Related (compendium): ICAR-DGR. Groundnut: A Crop Profile and Compendium of Notified Varieties of India. ICAR Directorate of Groundnut Research -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- Related (genetic enhancement review): Genetic Enhancement of Groundnut: Current Status and Future Prospects. Journal/report and authors not confirmed from the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet (A0402180) listing: No evidence found; the portal was not retrieved.
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for this variety: No evidence found. Retail groundnut listings returned by the search were for table nuts, not this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttarakhand. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx ; https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits

disease_resistance.summary: Leaf spot: described as moderately resistant by TNAU (the TNAU entry is truncated after this point, so the full list is unverified) and as moderate resistance to late leaf spot in the 2024 on-farm trial paper. Root wilt: the 2024 on-farm trial paper reports higher tolerance to root wilt than some comparators, ranking second to TCGS 1694 (pod yield 2493 kg/ha); no quantitative resistance score is given. Rust, stem rot, peanut bud necrosis and PBND: no evidence found for VRI 10 specifically (the DAC listing of notified varieties has no VRI 10 row). A general tnbrdngo claim of built-in pest and disease defences has no quantitative data.

pest_resistance.summary: Sucking pests and defoliators: described as moderately resistant by TNAU (the entry is truncated, so the full list is unverified). No other pest-resistance evidence found for VRI 10.

agronomic_details.yield: TNAU: 2448 kg/ha rainfed and 2535 kg/ha irrigated (units as reported by TNAU; the CSC record lists average yield in Kg/Ha without a value). On-farm rainfed trial (2024 paper, trial around 2022-23): pod yield 2493 kg/ha, haulm yield 4587 kg/ha (highest haulm yield among varieties tested), BCR 2.86. Cluster frontline demonstrations in Cuddalore district (VRI 8 and VRI 10 combined, 2020-21 to 2022-23, 175 demonstrations, about 70 ha): yield gain over farmers' practice of 53.34 per cent (another version of the study reports 62.13 per cent). The gain is not separated by variety.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Season-wise recommendation across Tamil Nadu zones (kharif, rabi and summer) is reported by TNAU, naming Villupuram, Thiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Cuddalore, Perambalur/Ariyalur, Tiruchirappalli, Thanjavur and others. The digest does not explicitly confirm VRI 10 in each listed zone. tnbrdngo cites suitability for short-duration cropping. Multi-location or AICRP/ICAR trial data: not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 100 To 105Days (CSC record). Conflicting duration reported by TNAU and tnbrdngo: 90-95 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: THE PODS ARE LONG WITH MEDIUM TO DEEP CONSTRICTION, PROMINANT BEAK (CSC record). TNAU additionally reports growth habit bunch and oil content of 46-48%.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) 2024 on-farm rainfed trial: pod yield 2493 kg/ha, haulm yield 4587 kg/ha (highest among varieties tested), BCR 2.86, second-ranked for root wilt tolerance behind TCGS 1694 (pod yield 2493 kg/ha as reported). (2) Cluster frontline demonstrations, Cuddalore district, VRI 8 and VRI 10, 2020-21 to 2022-23: 175 demonstrations on about 70 ha, yield gain of 53.34 per cent (or 62.13 per cent in the other version) over farmers' practice. (3) TNAU reports rainfed 2448 kg/ha and irrigated 2535 kg/ha; the trial design behind these figures is not stated. (4) Multi-location or AICRP/ICAR trials: not found in searched sources.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. Parentage note (not a marker result): the CSC ground-truth parentage is EXTRACT OF A CROSS TMV 7 X FSB 7-2. TNAU lists the cross for VRI 10 as VRI 2 x NRCG CS 349 (derivative). The digest states that TMV 7 x FSB 7-2 is the documented pedigree of VRI 1 (released 1986, 105 days), not VRI 10, and that the brief's parentage was not confirmed for VRI 10. This conflict is unresolved.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. A combining-ability (line x tester) study uses VRI 10 as a line, but it is not genetic-marker or QTL work.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Moderately resistant to sucking pests and defoliators, and to leaf spot (the TNAU entry is truncated after this point, so the full list is unverified) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Moderate resistance to late leaf spot per the 2024 on-farm trial paper -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Showed higher tolerance to root wilt than some comparators, ranking second to TCGS 1694 (pod yield 2493 kg/ha) -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Described as having moderate resistance, with a general claim of built-in pest and disease defenses; no quantitative data -- https://tnbrdngo.org/how-the-wonder-nut-vri-10-is-elevating-farmers-standard-of-living/
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found (the rainfed/irrigated yields are listed, but no explicit stress-tolerance rating for VRI 10 was retrieved)

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderately resistant to sucking pests, defoliators and leaf spot -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Moderate resistance to late leaf spot; no in-situ germination of mature pods before harvest -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Rust, stem rot, peanut bud necrosis and PBND resistance: No evidence found for VRI 10 specifically (DAC listing of notified varieties does not include a VRI 10 row) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Parentage conflict: TNAU lists the cross as VRI 2 x NRCG CS 349 (derivative), duration 90-95 days, oil 46-48%, growth habit bunch, average yield 2448 kg/ha rainfed and 2535 kg/ha irrigated -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
The parentage given in the brief (TMV 7 x FSB 7-2) is the documented pedigree of VRI 1 (released 1986, 105 days), not VRI 10; the brief's parentage was not confirmed for VRI 10 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/ and https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Duration 90-95 days and suitability for short-duration cropping -- https://tnbrdngo.org/how-the-wonder-nut-vri-10-is-elevating-farmers-standard-of-living/
On-farm rainfed trial (2022-23 or thereabouts): pod yield 2493 kg/ha and haulm yield 4587 kg/ha, the highest haulm yield among the varieties tested; BCR 2.86 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Cluster frontline demonstrations in Cuddalore district with VRI 8 and VRI 10 (2020-21 to 2022-23, 175 demonstrations, about 70 ha) reported a yield gain over farmers' practice of 53.34 per cent (the other version of the same study reports 62.13 per cent) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/lr-47-7-016 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379741722_A_Study_on_Yield_and_Value_Sustainability_in_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_Through_Cluster_Frontline_Demonstrations_Approach_in_Cuddalore_District_of_Tamil_Nadu
Multi-location or AICRP/ICAR trial data for VRI 10: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
QTL, marker-assisted or molecular characterization studies naming VRI 10: No evidence found
Combining ability (line x tester) study using VRI 10 as a line: see PUBLICATIONS below (not genetic-marker work)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Regional Research Station, Vriddhachalam (Cuddalore district) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Lead breeder or scientist name for VRI 10: No evidence found (no page named the breeder)
Groundnut breeding program at RRS Vriddhachalam, including the production of nucleus and breeder seed -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/milestone-achievements/ and http://www.tnau.ac.in/vri/
Release year 2022 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Release notification and CSC minutes (name, notification number): No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level contact (RRS Vriddhachalam): Dr. G. Nallathambi, Professor and Head, Regional Research Station, Vriddhachalam - 606 001, Cuddalore district; Phone 04143 – 260231; Fax 04143 – 261120; E-mail arsvri@tnau.ac.in -- http://www.tnau.ac.in/vri/ (page may be out of date; the contact was listed as the institute contact, not a VRI 10 breeder contact)
Breeder email, phone or personal contact for VRI 10: No evidence found

disease_resistance.research_summary: Leaf spot: described as moderately resistant by TNAU (the TNAU entry is truncated after this point, so the full list is unverified) and as moderate resistance to late leaf spot in the 2024 on-farm trial paper. Root wilt: the 2024 on-farm trial paper reports higher tolerance to root wilt than some comparators, ranking second to TCGS 1694 (pod yield 2493 kg/ha); no quantitative resistance score is given. Rust, stem rot, peanut bud necrosis and PBND: no evidence found for VRI 10 specifically (the DAC listing of notified varieties has no VRI 10 row). A general tnbrdngo claim of built-in pest and disease defences has no quantitative data.

Plant medium tal with profuse branching

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VRI 9 / VRI-4 -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC name is "VRI 9" and the Seednet name is "VRI-4". The parentage in the record (VG 5 x NC AC 17090) matches the TNAU record for VRI 4, not VRI 9. The 2022 release year does not match the TNAU record for VRI 4, which was released in 1996 and notified in 1997. I could not confirm that VRI 9 and VRI-4 are the same variety, so the findings below are labelled by name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- VRI 9 (name match): Moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust, plus some thrips and leafhopper tolerance, is reported for VRI 9 in a 2024 trial. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for VRI 9 were found. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI 9 (name match): The same trial describes VRI 9 as showing low disease incidence and suitability for rainfed conditions, but this is a qualitative statement, not a stress-tolerance test. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI-4 (Seednet name, TNAU record): The record gives no stress-tolerance data. The Radhamani and Singh (2008) germplasm table describes VRI 4 only as high yielding and early. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322066029_Radhamani_J_and_Singh_AK_2008_Conservation_and_Utilization_of_Genetic_Resources_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_in_India_Proc_Indian_Natn_Sci_Acad_74_3131-147

DISEASE AND PEST
- VRI 9: Moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust, with thrips and leafhopper also noted. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI-4: The TNAU record lists no disease or pest resistance. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- VRI 9 (2024 on-farm/trial comparison): Pod yield 2340 kg/ha and haulm yield 4486 kg/ha, with a duration of 115 days and an average yield of 2500 kg/ha reported. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI 9 (breeding line use): VRI 9 was used as a parental line in a combining-ability study at TNAU Vridhachalam, where it had higher mean pods per plant. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5929
- VRI-4 (TNAU record): Duration 110 days, rainfed yield 1660 kg/ha, irrigated yield 2171 kg/ha, with small dark-green leaves and 1-4 seeded pods. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/

GENETICS AND QTL
- VRI-4 (pedigree): VG 5 x NcAc 17090 (Spanish Bunch), released 1996, notified 662(E)/17.9.97. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/
- VRI 9: No pedigree, marker or QTL study for VRI 9 was found. The only VRI 9 record is the CSC parentage in the input. No evidence found for QTL or marker work.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (both names): Regional Research Station, Vriddhachalam, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/
- No named lead breeder for VRI 9 or VRI-4 was found in the retrieved pages. No evidence found for a named breeder.
- Institutional mandate: The station works on groundnut, sesame and cashew breeding. -- http://www.tnau.ac.in/vri/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. G. Nallathambi, Professor and Head, Regional Research Station, Vriddhachalam, 606 001 (postcode truncated in the source). Institute-level contact only. -- http://www.tnau.ac.in/vri/
- Phone: 04143-238231 / 99943 15004. Email: arsvri@tnau.ac.in. Listed for RRS Vridhachalam. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
- Postal address (partial): Located 5 km from Vriddhachalam town on the Vriddhachalam–Cuddalore road. -- http://www.tnau.ac.in/vri/

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2024). Title not retrieved. Group paper on VRI 9 trial results. International Journal of Research in Agronomy 7(6): 224-226 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Assessment of Combining Ability Analysis for Pod Yield and its Attributing Traits in Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). Agricultural Science Digest. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5929
- Radhamani, J. and Singh, A.K. (2008). Conservation and Utilization of Genetic Resources of Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.) in India. Proceedings of the Indian National Science Academy 74(3): 131-147. Lists VRI 4 with its pedigree. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322066029_Radhamani_J_and_Singh_AK_2008_Conservation_and_Utilization_of_Genetic_Resources_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_in_India_Proc_Indian_Natn_Sci_Acad_74_3131-147
- KrishiKosh, AICRP and ICAR annual reports: searched, not retrieved within this query budget. No evidence found for VRI 9 or VRI-4.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- VRI 9 and VRI-4: No seed-stock listing naming either variety was found. No evidence found from NSC, TANSEDA, KVK or dealer listings.
- Related but not admissible: The 2021 TNAU seed stock report lists VRI 8 at RRS Vridhachalam (45,142 units). This is a different variety. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
- Contact for enquiries: RRS Vridhachalam, 04143-238231, arsvri@tnau.ac.in. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- VRI 9: No official recommendation was found. Only the input record states Tamil Nadu. No evidence found from a notification source.
- VRI-4: A TNAU seasonal table lists VRI 4 among rainfed varieties for the North Western Zone of Tamil Nadu. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/Crop-improvement%20-1.html

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VRI-4 (variety_name and seednet_variety_name both "VRI-4"; crop "sesame" per the record, but Seednet lists GROUNDNUT)

SEARCH COVERAGE NOTE: The search tool hit its usage limit. Only one search returned usable results (query "VRI-4 sesame variety"). Results from the breeder/institution and research queries were lost to a script error, and no seed-availability search was run. Treat the headings below as incomplete.

RECORD CONFLICT (read first): The TNAU Vridhachalam groundnut table lists a different VRI 4 as a groundnut variety, with pedigree VG 5 x NcAc 17090 (Spanish Bunch), released 1996, notification 662(E)/17.9.97. That pedigree matches the parentage in this record, and the Seednet crop is GROUNDNUT. The sesame-specific page gives a different parentage (VRI 2 x GT 10) and a 2022 release year. The record may therefore mix a groundnut variety with a sesame name. The groundnut findings are not attributed to sesame below; they are listed only as a conflict.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Sesame VRI 4 page lists only the 'Moderately resistant to phyllody and root rot' trait under sesame; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found for sesame VRI 4 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html
Groundnut VRI 4 (not this crop) is recorded as a special-feature line only, with no stress data -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/

DISEASE AND PEST -- Sesame VRI 4 page: 'Moderately resistant to phyllody and root rot' -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html
No pest-resistance evidence found for sesame VRI 4 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Sesame VRI 4 page: year of release 2022; duration 85-90 days; seasons Masipattam, Chithiraipattam and Thaipattam; irrigated average yield 957 kg/ha; branching growth habit; oil content 50%; semi-erect, indeterminate, profusely branching, 4-loculed, brown seeds -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html
No multi-location or rainfed trial data found for sesame VRI 4 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html

GENETICS AND QTL -- Sesame VRI 4 page gives parentage as VRI 2 x GT 10, which conflicts with the record's VG 5 x NC AC 17090 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html
No QTL or marker studies found -- (none retrieved)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Regional Research Station, Vridhachalam (institute page; sesame VRI 4 listed under the sesame VRI series) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/milestone-achievements/
The milestone page lists only sesame VRI (Sv) 1, 2 and 3, not VRI 4 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/milestone-achievements/
No lead breeder name found for sesame VRI 4 -- (none retrieved)

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact, email, phone or postal address found in retrieved content. The institute's Vridhachalam research page is the only institute source retrieved -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for sesame VRI 4. Retrieved pages were about other varieties: a mutation-study paper using VRI 1, VRI (Sv) 2 and other sesame lines -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Description-of-sesame-varieties-used-in-present-mutation-studies_tbl1_343164432 ; and TMV (Sv) 7 -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2824 (not this variety, so excluded).

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found (seed-availability search not run because the tool limit was reached).

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for sesame VRI 4 in the retrieved pages. The state list in the record (Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu) is unverified. The record also repeats Andhra Pradesh.

NEXT STEPS: Check the CSC release minutes for whether this entry is sesame or groundnut, and confirm the parentage and variety code A0402016 against Seednet. Then rerun the breeder/contact, publications and seed-availability searches once the tool quota resets.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to late leaf spot (LLS) and rust. Supporting sources: Directorate of Oilseed Development table (name VRI (Gn) 7); agrifarming.in article (moderate resistance to LLS and rust); TNAU agritech page (moderately resistant to late leaf spot and rust, name VRI Gn 7). TNAU Tindivanam germplasm list (name VRI-7) records it as a promising donor for foliar disease resistance. No evidence found for resistance to other diseases (the digest's 'Tolerant to stem rot' row was misaligned and excluded).

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to leaf miner. Supporting sources: Directorate of Oilseed Development table and TNAU agritech page (both report moderate resistance). The original variety record (CSC, no URL in digest) reports a mean leaf miner incidence of 20.67 percent against 40.5 percent for check TMV 1, and Spodoptera incidence of 5.9 against 13.5 for TMV 1. The digest found no evidence for Spodoptera, Tobacco streak virus, thrips or jassids for this variety, so the CSC Spodoptera figure is not corroborated by the searched sources and should be verified. No evidence found for resistance to thrips, jassids or Tobacco streak virus.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed average yield 1865 kg/ha (TNAU). The original variety record gives an average yield range of 1383.00 to 1865.00 kg/ha. The irrigated yield field is blank in the TNAU source. Oil content 48 percent and shelling outturn 72 percent (TNAU).

agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed condition (TNAU). Growth habit semi-spreading and suited to Anippattam, Purattasipattam and Vaigasipattam seasons. TNAU zone-wise sowing schedule includes rainfed North Western Zone Vaigasipattam sowing. Kharif season recorded for Tamil Nadu (DOD).

agronomic_details.field_trials: No field trial results under FPVS, PVS or multi-location trials were found for this variety. Reported performance is limited to the TNAU rainfed average yield (1865 kg/ha) and quality figures (72 percent shelling, 48 percent oil). The original variety record (CSC, no URL in digest) also reports aflatoxin B1 content of 4.6 ug/kg of kernel against 5.7 ug/kg for check VRI 2, and a recommended fertilizer schedule of 15:15:68 NPK kg/ha, spacing of 30 x 15 cm and seed rate of 125 kg kernel/ha. The digest does not confirm these agronomic details.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately resistant to leaf miner, late leaf spot (LLS) and rust, per the Directorate of Oilseed Development table (name: VRI (Gn) 7) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Listed as a promising donor for foliar disease resistance in TNAU's germplasm list (name: VRI-7) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/crop-improvement/
- Drought tolerance: only rainfed suitability is recorded (name: VRI Gn 7); no explicit drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence scoring was found -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate resistance to leaf miner, LLS and rust (name: VRI (Gn) 7) -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
- Moderately resistant to late leaf spot, rust and leaf miner (name: VRI Gn 7) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRIgn%207.html
- Tobacco streak virus, thrips, jassids, Spodoptera: No evidence found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 120-125 days; rainfed average yield 1865 kg/ha; 72% shelling and 48% oil; the irrigated yield field is blank (name: VRI Gn 7) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/
- Growth habit semi-spreading; suited to Anippattam, Purattasipattam and Vaigasipattam seasons -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRIgn%207.html
- Zone-wise sowing schedule, including rainfed North Western Zone Vaigasipattam sowing (name: VRIGn 7) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/Crop-improvement%20-1.html
- Field trial yield under FPVS, PVS or multi-location trials: No evidence found for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage TMV 1 x JL 24 (Virginia Bunch) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/
- Described as a hybrid derivative of TMV 1 x JL 24 -- https://www.masujournal.org/view_journal.php?id=16
- Used as a parent with ICGV 15402, ICGV 15410 and ICGV 15427 in combining-ability crosses; GCA and SCA results reported -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5929
- Breeding method for this cultivar, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: TNAU, Vridhachalam (name: VRI (Gn) 7) -- http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx
- Station: Regional Research Station, Vridhachalam, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, TNAU -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5929
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found in any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder email, phone and individual contact: No evidence found.
- Institute page found (no email, phone or postal address extracted): https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/
- Release notification reference: 2187(E)/27.8.09 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/

PUBLICATIONS
- Shobha K V, Renugadevi J, Jerlin R (2020). Studies on Seed Dormancy and Breaking Methods in Groundnut cv. VRI 7. Madras Agricultural Journal 107(4-6): 131-135 -- DOI 10.29321/MAJ.2020.000357; https://www.masujournal.org/view_journal.php?id=16
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Assessment of Combining Ability Analysis for Pod Yield and its Attributing Traits in Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). Agricultural Science Digest -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5929
- Authors not retrieved (about 2021). Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea) nodule Rhizobium and passenger endophytic bacterial cultivable diversity and their impact on plant growth promotion (semi-spreading VRI 7 used) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2452219821000057
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports, and conference papers on this variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seed from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed sales: No evidence found.
- Private dealer listings returned were for other varieties or similarly named products (e.g. a "G7" listing), so they were excluded. Search returned generic Tamil Nadu groundnut seed listings that do not name VRI (Gn) 7.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Tamil Nadu, kharif season -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Tamil Nadu, rainfed condition suitability -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/

Notes on sources and name handling:
- The CSC name "VRI (Gn) 7" and the Seednet name are identical in the input. The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved, so no Seednet-specific evidence is reported. TNAU pages use "VRI Gn 7" and "VRIGn 7"; I treated these as the same variety.
- One DOD row ("Tolerant to stem rot") is misaligned in the source table and was excluded.
- Excluded as off-target: CO 7/ICGV 00351, TMV 7, VRI 8, VRI 2, TMV 14, TMV 13 and Kadiri 7 items.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Released 2022 by AAU, Gujarat. Limited trial yield data. No stress, disease or pest data available.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: GVG 11 (Anand Bahar) is a guar variety released in 2022 and associated with Anand Agricultural University, Gujarat. The only evidence is fragmentary mentions in AAU annual reports, with ambiguous yield figures. No stress tolerance, disease or pest resistance, molecular, breeder or commercial information was found, so evidence quality is low.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Guar variety released in 2022, apparently by AAU, Anand. Maturity, parentage, adaptation and yield potential are not specified, and only unclear trial figures (106-129 q/ha) appear in an annual report.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No evidence was found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, or for disease and pest resistance. Stress tolerance is unknown, and the Gujarat score is a tentative 40.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) itself. The searches did not return any stress-tolerance record under that name or code.
- Related line, Karan Guar 14 (RGr 18-1), not Karan Guar-2: It also showed resistance/tolerance to important diseases and insects and was recommended for different states of India -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Different cultivar, HG 2-20 (CCS HAU, Hisar): suitable under rain fed situations and this variety is tolerant to drought conditions. -- https://www.agricultureinformation.com/forums/threads/officially-released-guar-varieties-details-from-agri-univerity.103226/

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3). Karan Guar 14 is reported as resistant/tolerant to disease and insects (see above, https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597).
- Different cultivar: This variety is resistant to BLB and (RGC 1066, Guar Lathi; text truncated in the snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384757778_Cluster_Bean_Cyamopsis_tetragonoloba

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) yield, maturity or trial data. Note the name and code were not matched in any record.
- Karan Guar 14 was tested at one station: its seed trials ran at RARI, Durgapura, Jaipur during the rainy (kharif) season of 2016 and 2017 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Karan Guar 14 yield comparison: The newly developed variety Karan Guar-14 has good galactomannan over the check RGC 1066 (1773 kg/ha), RGC 1033 (2110 kg/ha) and HG 2-20 (2180 kg/ha). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Zone-specific agronomy for Rajasthan (AINP on Arid Legumes, SKNAU Jobner) is available but does not name Karan Guar-2 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391521739_PRODUCTION_TECHNOLOGY_OF_GUAR_FOR_ZONE-IIIA_RAJASTHAN

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) parentage, markers or QTL. The user-supplied parentage is "Not specified", and no source confirmed it.
- Karan Guar 14 was developed from a cross: developed by crossing two genotypes, RGC 1038 (RGC 516 × HG 75) and RGC 1017 (Naveen × HG 75) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370515204_Karan_guar_14_A_new_high-yielding_and_quality_gum_content_variety
- Genome reference (RGC-936, not Karan Guar-2): a chromosome-scale assembly was reported at ICAR-NIPB New Delhi -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-33762-3

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (per the user record and the CSC/Karan Guar 14 sources): Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute, Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University (SKNAU), Durgapura, Jaipur. Verified for the sister cultivar Karan Guar 14: at Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute, (Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University, Jobner, Rajasthan) Durgapura, Jaipur, Rajasthan -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370515204_Karan_guar_14_A_new_high-yielding_and_quality_gum_content_variety
- Institute profile: Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute (RARI) is a constituent research institute under Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University, Jobner, Jaipur. -- https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm
- Breeder names for Karan Guar-2: No evidence found. The RARI variety list names Karan Guar 1 and Karan Guar 14 and Karan Guar 15 but not Karan Guar-2 -- https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder name, email and phone: No evidence found.
- Institute address as printed in a sister-cultivar paper: Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute, Durgapura, Jaipur, Rajasthan 302 018, India -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Institute web page: https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm (no email or phone was retrieved from it)

PUBLICATIONS
- Choudhury, P. R. and Singh, R. K. (year not shown in retrieved record). Growth, varietal development and cultivar diversity in seed production chain of cluster bean (Cyamopsis tetragonoloba) in India. Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences (ICAR e-pubs) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/125470 (covers the variety list 1976–2023, which includes Karan Guar 14 but was not checked for Karan Guar-2)
- Karan guar 14: A new high-yielding and quality gum content variety (authors and year not shown in retrieved record). Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences (ICAR e-pubs) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Chauhan, P. S. and Chhabra, K. (year not shown). Cluster Bean, Chapter 4, Agronomy of Leguminous Crops (regional overview) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341343072_Chapter_-4_Cluster_Bean_Agronomy_Leguminous_Crops_A_Regional_Overview_CHAPTER_-4_Cluster_Bean
- Pathak, R. (2015). Cluster Bean: Physiology, Genetics and Cultivation. Springer Singapore (book, cited in CABI chapter) -- https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/10.1079/9781800624658.0005
- No Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) specific paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, a KVK, SKNAU or a dealer. The seed listings found (eBay, Amazon, Amazing Seeds, Golden Hills Farm) are generic cluster bean or vegetable seed and do not name this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Karan Guar-2 (user-supplied record only, not verified by any retrieved source): Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
- Sister cultivar Karan Guar 14 was recommended for different states of India, including Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat and Maharashtra. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597

NAME CHECK
- Release minutes name: Karan Guar-2. Seednet name: Karan guar 2 (RGS-3). No source in this search set used either name. Every finding above relates to other cultivars unless stated otherwise.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Seednet name MARU GUAR (cluster bean/guar): No evidence found. The "MARU GUAR" search returned only a general cluster bean agronomy chapter and a guar gum review, neither of which names this variety, so I have not attributed them to it.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NRC-197 (Soybean)

Name note: The variety name in the CSC/AICRP records is "NRC 197" (the 54th AICRP Annual Group Meet listed it for notification). No Seednet name or variety code was found in any search, so the Seednet name remains "Unknown". I did not run a separate Seednet query, so that gap reflects the search budget as well as the evidence. All findings below refer to NRC 197 and soybean. Some secondary sources are trade or news sites, not official records.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Lodging tolerance and non-shattering pods are reported -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence specific to NRC 197 was found. The ICAR-NSRI page names NRC 136 as the drought-tolerant variety, which does not apply to NRC 197 -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html

DISEASE AND PEST
- Stem fly resistance: NRC 197 was classed resistant in a two-year screening at the Main Agricultural Research Station, UAS Dharwad, with lower stem fly infestation than most entries (11.26% in the mean table). The source is a research article (journal and authors not identified in the snippet) -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-LR-5312-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
- Reported high resistance to semilooper and moderate resistance to Spodoptera litura -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- No YMV, rust, pod blight or other disease ratings for NRC 197 were found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity about 113 days (one source) and 112.67 days (another), described as early duration suited to hills -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/ ; https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- Average yield 1624 kg/ha, maximum 2072 kg/ha in trials -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- Yield about 16.24 q/ha, rainfed kharif -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- Multi-location trial data, plot-level data and seed-rate details for NRC 197 were not found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Developed through marker-assisted selection -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- Kunitz trypsin inhibitor (KTi) free, described as the first KTi-free variety of the northern hill region -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- The ICAR-NSRI variety page lists NRC 197 among KTi-free varieties, but the sentence is garbled ("...are NRC 197 are Kti free"), so treat this as likely but unconfirmed -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- Parentage, pedigree and breeding-line code: No evidence found. The Dharwad screening article lists NRC 197 among genotypes with tawny trichomes, which is a phenotype note only -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-LR-5312-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
- QTL or marker studies specific to NRC 197: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR), Indore. The institute was later renamed the National Soybean Research Institute, Indore -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888 ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/latest-recommended-high-yielding-soybean-varieties-in-india-2025/
- A Hindi report says a two-member scientist team developed NRC 197, and names the lead scientist with the title "Pradhan Vaigyanik" (principal scientist). The names are cut off in the snippet, so I have not recorded them -- https://choupalsamachar.in/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- Breeder name(s) as confirmed by an official source: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute website: https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/ (cited as the institute site in the Wikipedia reference list; not opened)
- Institute website for NSRI varieties: https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- Director named in a 2025 slide deck: Dr Kunwar Harendra Singh, Director, ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research, Indore -- https://sopa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1-Latest-Development-in-Soybean-Breeding.pdf (institute-level contact only, not a breeder contact)
- Official email, phone and postal address for the institute or breeder: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR-AICRP on Soybean (2024). 54th Annual Group Meet, Dharwad, 13–14 March 2024. Identified NRC 197 for notification. ICAR -- https://icar.gov.in/en/annual-group-meet-aicrp-soybean
- Authors not identified (year not stated in snippet). Stem fly resistance screening of soybean genotypes, including NRC 197, at UAS Dharwad. Journal/report not identified (article number LR-5312) -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-LR-5312-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
- A 2021 Scientific Reports paper by Ratnaparkhe (DOI 10.1038/s41598-021-02064-x) came up, but it concerns NRC 128, so I have excluded it.
- No KrishiKosh thesis, peer-reviewed paper or conference paper about NRC 197 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The ICAR-NSRI site says the institute coordinates breeder seed for the national seed chain and that about 30 varieties are in that chain. It does not confirm NRC 197 specifically -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for NRC 197: No evidence found (no seed-availability query was run).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand (hill districts). A 2025 list places NRC 197 under the Northern Hill Region, which covers Himachal Pradesh, hilly Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/latest-recommended-high-yielding-soybean-varieties-in-india-2025/
- Official notification or state-recommendation notice: No evidence found.
- Year of release: No evidence found. The variety was identified for notification at the March 2024 AICRP meet, which is not the same as the release year.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for "Selection 1" or "Selection-1" specifically. Generic guinea grass tolerance is described for the species, not this clone: KAU's ad hoc Package of Practices says the grass tolerates drought and deep seasonal flooding, and it grows under coconut shade -- https://pop.kau.in/foddercrops.htm
- A general guinea grass review notes drought tolerance from a deep root system, again species-level, not variety-level -- https://masjaps.com/index.php/mas/article/download/12/8/8

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for Selection 1 or Selection-1 disease or pest resistance in any search result.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for Selection 1 or Selection-1 yield or trial data. KAU's Package of Practices gives species-level figures (about 80-100 t/ha green fodder per year, six to seven harvests) -- https://pop.kau.in/foddercrops.htm
- KAU Vellayani's 2021-22 ZREAC report lists guinea grass varieties under evaluation as Harithasree, Culture-2 and CO(GG)-3, with no mention of Selection 1 -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/soft_copy_of_xxxix_zreac_meeting.pdf
- Tamil Nadu's forage package lists CO(GG)3 as a clonal selection from Mombasa, with 340-360 t/ha/year green fodder, but this is a different variety -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/10_Guinea_Grass.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for the parentage "clonal selection from JHGG-96-3" or for the JHGG-96-3 accession. The JHGG prefix appears in an IGFRI-style listing for Bundel Guinea-4 (JHGG-08-1), which is a different variety; any link to Selection 1 is unverified -- https://www.leafconagro.com/guinea-grass-variety-bundel-guinea-4-jhgg-08-1/
- Background only: a 2025 GWAS of 124 guinea grass accessions from CIAT's collection (not this clone) -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41469560/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No evidence found for a breeder or developing institute for Selection 1 or Selection-1. The "Institution" field in the record is unresolved.
- The Indian guinea grass varieties found in search (Bundel Guinea series, Harithasree, Punjab Guinea grass-1) are attributed to other programmes, not to Selection 1 -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1046&context=igc
- KAU lists guinea grass varieties Haritha, Marathakom and Harithashree on its Regional Agricultural Research Station (Vellanikkara/Vellayani-region) crop page; none is Selection 1 -- https://rarsvni.kau.in/crops-0

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No email or phone number for any Selection 1 breeder was in the results.
- Institute-level fallback: Kerala Agricultural University, Thrissur (established 1971, KAU research directorate at Vellanikkara) -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/communities/f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7?spc.page=1&spc.sf=dc.date.accessioned&spc.sd=DESC&scope=f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7
- KAU Directorate of Seeds and Planting Material Production, Vellanikkara (price proceedings signed there, 2025). No phone or email shown in the extract -- https://www.kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/price_list_seeds_and_planting_materials_2025-26_website.pdf
- Regional Agricultural Research Station (Southern Zone), Vellayani, KAU: Dr. Usha C. Thomas, Professor and Head, Instructional Farm, is the PI on the fodder variety evaluation trial. This is not a Selection 1 breeder contact; no email or phone found -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/soft_copy_of_xxxix_zreac_meeting.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for any paper, report or thesis on Selection 1 or Selection-1. The KrishiKosh search returned only the KAU community page, not a Selection 1 record -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/communities/f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7?spc.page=1&spc.sf=dc.date.accessioned&spc.sd=DESC&scope=f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7

SEED AVAILABILITY
- KAU sells guinea grass fodder slips ("Guinea grass & other varieties") at 0.75 per slip under the 2025-26 price revision. The variety name is not specified, so Selection 1 availability cannot be confirmed -- https://www.kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/price_list_seeds_and_planting_materials_2025-26_website.pdf
- KAU's 2025 price order says sale is permitted only for varieties recommended by ICAR institutes or SAUs. Selection 1 is not listed as a recommended variety, which conflicts with a Seednet release record and should be checked -- https://www.kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/price_list_seeds_and_planting_materials_2025-26_website.pdf
- No NSC, state seed corporation or private dealer listing for Selection 1 was found. The search covered this only in part, as the fourth search was used for KAU sources.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The raw record says "Kerela", which I read as Kerala. KAU's package of practices calls guinea grass suited to Kerala conditions, but it names no release for Selection 1 -- https://pop.kau.in/foddercrops.htm
- Name note: the record uses "Selection 1" (CSC minutes) and "Selection-1" (Seednet). Searches returned no evidence under either name.
- Year of release is unknown ("NaT" in the record). No CSC or Seednet notification was found, so the release status is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The search for "GM-6 greengram variety" returned CO 6 greengram (a different variety, Tamil Nadu) and nothing naming GM-6 or GPM-6 for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The same searches returned only a CO 6 yellow mosaic resistance paper (https://masujournal.org/view_archive_journal.php?id=1821), which is a different variety and was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The search returned a seed biopriming study using "GM-3" greengram seed (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336513295_In_vitro_Investigation_of_Seed_biopriming_in_Green_gram). GM-3 is a different variety, so it was discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No search result mentioned QTL, marker or pedigree work for GM-6 or GPM-6.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The query on GM-6 with Navsari Agricultural University returned a ResearchGate paper with a Navsari author (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336513295_In_vitro_Investigation_of_Seed_biopriming_in_Green_gram). It does not mention GM-6 and cannot be attributed to this variety. The release metadata supplied with the request (institution: Pulses and Castor Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University; parentage: pureline selection from Bijarpur local) is input data, not search evidence, and no page confirmed it.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No institute page, email, phone or address for the Pulses and Castor Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University, was returned.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The only greengram research result was the seed biopriming paper, which concerns GM-3 and was discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The search for "GPM-6 horse gram Kulthi variety seed" returned only a Vikaspedia horse gram cultivation page (https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en). That page is about horse gram, a different crop, so it was discarded. The Seednet name "GPM-6" is listed under horse gram, which conflicts with the greengram crop in the record. No Seednet entry was retrieved to confirm this.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found in search results. The only state listed is the one supplied in the request, Gujarat (release date 2018-08-10). Neither is confirmed by any retrieved page.

Search log: 4 searches were run (the cap). Queries: "GM-6 greengram variety"; "GM-6 greengram breeder Navsari Agricultural University"; "GM-6 greengram research paper"; "GPM-6 horse gram Kulthi variety seed". Recommended next steps: search seednet.gov.in directly for GPM-6 and check its crop field, and search the Navsari Agricultural University or KrishiKosh site for the Pulses and Castor Research Station's release notification.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: TIME OF SOWING: LAST WEEK OF JUNE TO FIRST WEEK TO JULY; FERTILIZER : 20:40:0 NPK KG/HA; LODGING : RESISTANT; SHATTERING: NIL; SHOWING : TIMELY; FODDER YIELD : HIGH.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: SEMI DETERMINATE PLANT HABIT, SEMI SPREADING GROWTH HABIT, LIGHT GREEN STEM AND FOLIAGE, ATTRACTIVE BRICK RED BOLD SEED.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 52 CM; WEIGHTED MEAN : 54; RANGE OVER LOCATION : 48-60; PLANT HABIT : SEMI-DETERMINATE; PLANT: GROWTH HABIT : SEMI SPREADING; DAYS TO FLOWERING : EARLY (48 DAYS); STEM: COLOUR : LIGHT GREEN; STEM ANTHOCYANIN COLOURATION : ABSENT; FOLIAGE COLOUR : LIGHT GREEN; TERMINAL LEAFLET SHAPE : OBLONG; LEAF PUBESCENCE : HIGH AND PUBESCENT; LEAF VEIN COLOUR : LIGHT GREEN; PETIOLE COLOUR : REDDISH GREEN; PETIOLE LENGTH : 2-3 CM; LEAF SENESCENCE : PRESENT; CALYX COLOUR : LIGHT GREEN; INFLORESCENCE : RECEMOSE; RECEME POSITION : 2-3 CM; POD: CONSTRICTION : SLIGHT; POD BEAK SHAPE : POINTED AND CURVED; POD SIZE : MEDIUM; POD CURVATURE : CURVED; POD SHAPE : CYLINDRICAL; SEED: COLOUR : DARK BRICK RED; SEED SHAPE : RHOMBOID; SEED: COLOUR PATTERN : UNIFORM; LUSTURE ON SEED SURFACE : SHINY; SEED SIZE (100 SEED WEIGHT) : 3.39 G.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: THE VARIETY WAS RESISTANT TO ROOT ROT AND MODERATELY RESISTANT TO POWDERY MILDEW, COLLAR ROT, CERCOSPORA LEAF SPOT AND LEAF BLIGHT. FOR ANTHRACNOSE THE INCIDENCE WAS LESSER THAN THE CHECKS.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: THE VARIETY GHG 5 WAS FREE FROM THE ATTACK OF FEEDER AND LEAF MINOR PESTS, WHILE THE POPULATION OF APHIDS, JASSIDS AND MITES WERE AT PAR WITH CHECKS WELL BELOW ETL, LEVEL.

MOSTLY SOWN AFTER COMPLETION OF SOWING OF OTHER CROPS AND ON LOW FERTILE AS WELL AS ON MARGINAL LANDS, WHICH RESULTS IN LOWER YIELDS; SPACING : NARROW ROW SPACING (30 CM) GAVE HIGHER SEED YIELD IN COMPARISON TO BROAD SPACING (45 CM); FERTILIZER : APPLICATION OF 10 KG. N AND 30 KG. PHOSPHORUS GAVE HIGHER SEED YIELD IN COMPARISON TO 5 KG. N AND 15 KG. PHOSPHORUS APPLICATION. FURTHER IT DID NOT RESPOND SIGNIFICANTLY TO SULPHUR APPLICATION 20-25 KG/HA; SOWING TIME : KHARIF SEASON (ONSET OF MONSOON). THE VARIETY GAVE HIGHER SEED YIELD (13.9, 17.6 AND 17.3%) OVER CHECK IN EARLY, NORMAL AND LATE SOWN CONDITIONS, RESPECTIVELY IN DIFFERENT YEARS. IT SHOWS ITS SUITABILITY FOR ALL THE SOWING CONDITIONS; IRRIGATION : RAIFNED.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 30-50 CM; IT IS HAVING LUSH GREEN FOLIAGE WITH SOME WAXY DEPOSITION. IT HAS 2-12 PRIMARY BRANCHES WITH 23-65 PODS PER PLANT. SEED IS BOLD WITH BRICK RED COLOUR, WHICH IS PREFERRED BY THE CONSUMERS.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: NO SUCH STUDY WAS MADE BUT IT WAS OBSERVED THAT IT CAN GROW SUCCESSFULLY IN POOR SOILS AND MOISTURE STRESS CONDITION IN BARANI LANDS WHERE NO OTHER CROPS COULD PROFITABLY GROWN. BEING TOLERANT TO DROUGHT IT MAKES EFFICIENT UYSE OF AVAILABLE SOIL MOISTURE AND THRIVES WELL IN AREAS HAVING SCANTY RAINFALL. THIS WAS OBSERVED AT DFRS, ARJIA, BHILWARA IN THE YEAR 2002 THAT ALMOST ALL THE CROPS FAILED TO PRODUCE SEED YIELD EXCEPT HORSEGRAM, PARTICULARLY VARIETY AK-42 WHICH GAVE HIGHEST SEED YIELD (301 KG/HA.) IN COMPARISON TO CHECK AK-21 (218 KG/HA) IN COMPARISON TO CHECK AK-21 (218 KG/HA) IN COMPARISON TO CHECK AK-21 (218 KG/HA) WHICH WAS 38 PERCENT HIGHER, INDICATES ITS TOLERANCE TO STRESS CONDITION.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: NO INCIDENCE OF ANY DISEASES UNDER NATURAL CONDITIONS WAS OBSERVED.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: NO INSECT PEST ATTACK WAS OBSERVED UNDER NATURAL CONDITIONS.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pratap Kulthi-2 (AK-53), Horse gram (Macrotyloma uniflorum)

Names: variety_name "Pratap Kulthi-2" (CSC minutes) and seednet_variety_name "Pratap Kulthi-2 (AK-53)" (Seednet). Searches used: 4 web_search calls. No retrieved page names "Pratap Kulthi-2" with horse gram. The only match is the code AK-53, which appears in one genotype list. Where a finding refers to AK-53, I say so. Pages about AK-42, Pratap Kulthi-1, Indira Kulthi-1, HPK-2 and other varieties were excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for Pratap Kulthi-2 / AK-53. Searches returned only generic horse gram drought descriptions, e.g. Horsegram is extremely drought-resistant crop. That refers to the crop, not this variety. -- http://dpd.gov.in/Horse_gram.pdf (generic crop text, not variety-specific; excluded from the record)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for Pratap Kulthi-2 / AK-53. Returned pages cover seed treatment for the crop in general, not this variety. -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en (crop-level; excluded)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
AK-53 appears as one of five horse gram genotypes whose seed physicochemical properties were analysed. The source says these were obtained from AICRP on Arid Legumes at Parbhani centre. This is a quality study, not a yield or agronomy trial, and the snippet does not give the AK-53 result. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233919140_Chemical_and_physicochemical_properties_of_horse_gram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_and_its_product_formulation (name matched by code AK-53 only; attribution to this variety is provisional)

No QTL, marker, or genome study names this variety. The HPKV horse gram genome-sequencing report refers to a different accession and institution, so it is excluded. -- https://www.thestatesman.com/cities/hp-farm-varsity-breaks-new-ground-in-horse-gram-research-1502540084.html (excluded: not this variety)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. No page names a breeder or scientist for Pratap Kulthi-2 / AK-53, and no page names Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology (MPUAT) as the developer. The AK-53 seed-quality study points to AICRP on Arid Legumes, Parbhani, as the source of the genotype, which is not the same as the developing institution. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233919140_Chemical_and_physicochemical_properties_of_horse_gram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_and_its_product_formulation (AK-53 genotype source only)

PUBLICATIONS

No other publication names Pratap Kulthi-2 or AK-53. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VL GAHAT 19 (VLG-19) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name and crop notes:
- Release-minute name: "VL Gahat 19". Seednet name: "VL Gahat 10". The evidence below refers to VL Gahat 19 unless a line says otherwise.
- Crop mismatch: the input says chickpea, but every source found describes horse gram (Macrotyloma uniflorum, gahat/kulthi). Seednet also lists horse gram. No chickpea evidence was found.
- Searches run: 4 (release/agronomy, breeder/contact, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Horse gram as a crop is described as extremely drought-resistant, but no variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for VL Gahat 19 was found. -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en
- General crop note: horse gram is grown on drylands under low-to-moderate rainfall. Not variety-specific. -- https://krishipatrika.com/2021/05/21425/
- Crop is said to tolerate winter extremes. Not variety-specific. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/metabo13020165

DISEASE AND PEST
- Horse gram yellow mosaic virus (HgYMV) causes alarming yield loss in the crop. No VL Gahat 19 resistance rating was found. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/metabo13020165
- Seed treatment with fungicide is recommended against soil fungal pathogens. Not variety-specific. -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en
- No VL Gahat 19 disease or pest reaction data found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release table lists VL Gahat 19 with release/notification year 2010 (Kumar 2007 table, cited in a review). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356086546_HORSEGRAM-A_SUPREMACY_NUTRITIONAL_SOURCE_A_REVIEW
- Hill sowing advisory: VL Gahat 15 and 19 for hill Gahat, sown in the first fortnight of June. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/Extension_Edu/02.05.2020_Kharif_season_Advisory.pdf
- Improved package of practice is said to give 6–10 q grain/ha, depending on monsoon. Crop-level FLD figure, not variety-specific. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Horse_gram.PDF
- No VL Gahat 19 yield table or multi-location trial data found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker, or genetic study on VL Gahat 19 found. Parentage given in the input (VLG 1 x NIC 2659) was not verified by any source.
- Related but different material: induced mutant and multi-environment studies on TNAU lines and Paiyur 2 (not VL Gahat 19). -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-67282-5

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institute: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, Uttarakhand. Brand listed as VPKAS on the seed portal. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLGahat19_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%A419

drought_tolerance.technical_details: The snippets mention 'drought tolerant genotypes' only in the general context of the IIVR climate-resilience paper. No snippet links this to Kashi Bouni Sem-9.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: Heat tolerance is mentioned only for other crops (tomato lines such as ZT1 and transgenic tomato). No evidence for this variety.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: Salt tolerance snippets refer to transgenic tomato, not to this variety.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence. The water-logging snippet refers to other germplasm, apparently tomato and wild relatives.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Snippets mention 'Free from Dolichos yellow vein mosaic virus during cropping period' and 'tolerant to French bean golden yellow mosaic virus under field conditions'. The text order suggests these statements describe other Indian bean or French bean varieties (e.g., Kashi Sheetal) listed near Kashi Bouni Sem-9. The sentence for Kashi Bouni Sem-9 is truncated ('developed through inter-varietal...'), so no disease reaction can be confirmed for it.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety is mentioned in two 2023 publications, but only in snippets that are truncated or ambiguous. No stress trait, yield figure, or Gujarat-specific data can be attributed to it with confidence. The 'at least one stress trait' criterion for 60 or 75 is not clearly met. The possible climate-resilience association and the citations nominally place it between 40 and 60, so 50 is assigned as a conservative score. A score of 40 would be defensible if the IIVR listing is judged not to be climate evidence. Full-text verification could raise or lower the score.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Kashi Bouni Sem-9 is a 2022 Indian bean (dolichos bean) variety, apparently from ICAR-IIVR and developed through inter-varietal breeding. The 30 search results are repeats of two ResearchGate documents with truncated snippets, so no stress tolerance, yield, or commercial availability can be confirmed. Evidence quality is low and the Gujarat score is 50.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Dolichos bean variety released in 2022, probably by IIVR Varanasi and developed through inter-varietal breeding. Yield, maturity, adaptation and recommended states are not documented.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Stress tolerance is not demonstrated. The snippets that mention drought, heat, salt, and virus tolerance refer mainly to tomato or other bean varieties, and any link to this variety is unverified. The full IIVR climate-resilience paper should be consulted.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Kashi Bauni Sem-3 is a 2022-released Indian bean (dolichos bean) variety with first picking at 80-85 days. The search results are 19 duplicates of one tomato-focused review, which contain no stress, disease, pest, yield, genetic or commercial data for this variety. Evidence quality is low, and suitability for Gujarat cannot be assessed.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Indian bean variety released in 2022, with first picking at 80-85 days and peak fruiting afterward. Institution, parentage, yield, adaptation and recommended states are not specified.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No variety-specific evidence of drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, or of disease or pest resistance. Stress snippets in the source refer to tomato. The variety cannot be classified as stress tolerant on current evidence.

drought.details: HA 4 (Lablab purpureus cv. HA-4) has demonstrated tolerance to drought stress. It was subjected to drought stress for a period of eight days during its initial growth phase under strictly controlled conditions. The variety is noted in the context of drought stress tolerance and its adaptation to semi-arid, alfisol conditions, particularly relevant in regions like Bengaluru.

heat.details: HA 4 has been mentioned in the context of stress tolerance studies, including heat stress tolerance, alongside drought stress tolerance. Its adaptation to semi-arid conditions implies some degree of heat tolerance.

salinity.details: While HA-3 and HA-4 are mentioned in discussions related to salt stress studies, and research on mapping QTLs for salt tolerance in field beans is underway, a specific level of salinity tolerance for HA 4 is not detailed in the provided search results.

flood.details: No information regarding flood tolerance for HA 4 is available in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: No information regarding disease resistance for HA 4 is available in the provided search results.

pest_resistance.summary: No information regarding pest resistance for HA 4 is available in the provided search results.

agronomic_details.yield: Not specified in document
agronomic_details.stability: The photoperiod insensitivity of HA 4 enhances its adaptability, suggesting potential for cultivation across different seasons or regions, which can contribute to yield stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: HA 4 is described as photoperiod insensitive, a key characteristic for wider adaptation. It is adapted to semi-arid, alfisol conditions and has shown tolerance to a 15-day delay in onset of conditions, as observed in trials near Bengaluru (Karnataka).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Tirupati Field Bean-2 (CSC name) / Tirupati Field Bean-1 (Seednet name), field bean (Indian bean, Lablab purpureus var. lignosus), RARS Tirupati, code A0307020

Scope note: I ran four searches covering both names. None returned a page that mentions either "Tirupati Field Bean-1" or "Tirupati Field Bean-2" or the parentage "LOCAL (GP-18) x HA-3". Every heading below therefore reports either an institute-level fact or "No evidence found". Nothing here confirms the 2010 release, the parentage, or the variety code.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for either name. (Searched: "Tirupati Field Bean-2 field bean variety"; "Tirupati Field Bean-1 Indian bean RARS Tirupati developed by")

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for either name. Unrelated Indian bean varieties from other programmes report disease scores (for example, Gujarat Junagadh Indian Bean-2 had leaf spot and leaf blight intensities compared with a check) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00207.2 (not this variety).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for either name. The only trial-type result is for a different Indian bean (Gujarat Junagadh Indian Bean-2, green pod yield 112.46 q/ha vs check 89.56 q/ha) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00207.2 (not this variety).

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage LOCAL (GP-18) x HA-3 was not confirmed by any source. The HA-3 name appears only as a photo-insensitive vegetable type in an export listing -- https://bwellinternational.com/product/field-beans/ (not evidence of this cross).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Tirupati, under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU). RARS was established in 1979 and its stated mandate centres on groundnut and cropping systems, with pulses as a verification function -- https://www.angraurabitpt.org/who-are-we. No breeder or lead scientist name was found for Tirupati Field Bean-1 or -2 -- No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. Institute-level information only, as listed on the ANGRAU RARS page: "Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), S.V. Agricultural College campus, Chandragiri Road, Tirupati - 517502, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, India" -- https://www.angraurabitpt.org/who-are-we. This address is given for the RARS campus and a related incubator, not for the bean programme specifically. No official email, phone, or named contact person was found -- https://www.angraurabitpt.org/who-are-we.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for either name. Searches of ICAR and KrishiKosh-type sources (via general search) did not return any paper, report, or thesis on this variety. Sources that came up were on other Indian bean/lablab varieties and are not listed here as publications on this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for Tirupati Field Bean-1 or -2 from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, the SAU, or dealers. The only dealer results were generic seed-trader listings in Tirupati with no bean variety named -- https://www.tradeindia.com/tirupati/seeds-city-222733.html.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The raw field in the record is "Not specified", and no source names the states for this variety.

Recommended follow-up: check the Seednet portal entry for "Tirupati Field Bean-1" (variety code A0307020) directly, and search the ANGRAU/RARS Tirupati annual reports and the AICRP on MULLaRP (pulses) annual reports, which are the most likely places to record its release notification and trial data.

- Maturity of about 125-130 days, dark brown seed, plant height 160-180 cm, oil content 41-42%, and yield claimed at 12-15 quintals per acre. -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/seed/detail/5222-hybrid-mustard

salinity.details: CSSRI's technology listing states CS 60 is recommended for saline soils up to ECe 12.0 dS/m and alkali soils up to about pH 9.5, and is highly suitable for saline-sodic soils. CSSRI's varieties page gives lower limits (ECe about 9.0 dS/m, pH about 9.3, and 6-9 dS/m in another passage), so the tolerance ceiling differs between CSSRI sources and should be verified before use. A seedling-stage metabolomics study reports that CS 60 accumulated more differentially expressed metabolites than the sensitive line CS 245-2-80-7 under salt stress, with antioxidant-defence pathways protecting against osmotic and oxidative stress and more active photosynthesis. The reported trial performance in All India Salinity Alkalinity Tolerant Variety Trials could not be confirmed because the abstract is truncated. The level is rated high on the basis of the breeder-site recommendations and the mechanistic study; the discrepancy in stated limits lowers confidence in the precise ceiling.

It has been identified as contributing to drought tolerance, with its roots and F1 hybrid lines showing drought tolerance under stress conditions. It is also listed among varieties exhibiting drought stress tolerance in Indian mustard.

heat.details: The variety is relevant in the context of high temperature (heat) stress prevalence in India for rapeseed-mustard breeding, suggesting its adaptation to such conditions, though a specific tolerance level is not stated.

agronomic_details.stability: The proposed strain has resistance for lodging and shattering. It demonstrates a stable oil content across different locations.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for cultivation under after/relay cropping in paddy fields with come-up/full irrigation. It is advised in ICAR Rabi Agro-Advisories for farmers and explicitly recommended for 'Whole of Chhattisgarh'.
