search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in Pant Rai-20. The one trait tied to this variety is high-temperature tolerance at maturity. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf (AICRP table row for Pant Rai-20, spans 15-7 and 15-8; the URL is the gbpuat.res.in host as returned)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Results on Alternaria blight, white rust and aphid resistance concern other genotypes or programmes and were not attributed to Pant Rai-20. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf (search returned no variety-specific disease rating)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The AICRP rapeseed-mustard table lists Pant Rai-20 as a high-yielding, medium-maturity, bold-seeded line suited to irrigated and rainfed, timely-sown conditions, with a maturity of about 122-128 days and about 40% oil. The column headings are not fully legible in the extracted text, so the yield figure (25-30 in the same row) should be checked against the original table before use. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf
No variety-specific multi-location trial data found. The Pantnagar sowing-date and planting-geometry study used an unnamed Indian mustard variety and does not name Pant Rai-20. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/paperdetail.php?paper=1272

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: the AICRP table records Pant Rai-20 as a pure-line selection from Kranti. The seednet record says "Not specified", so this is a discrepancy to resolve, not a confirmed pedigree. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf
No QTL or marker study on Pant Rai-20 found. The yellow sarson QTL and SSR papers returned concern other Brassica rapa lines. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0209982

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Breeder name: not found. No Pant Rai-20 breeder or developing scientist is named in any result, so none is attributed here. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/08.06.2023_Varieties_Released.pdf (lists the variety among GBPUAT Genetics & Plant Breeding releases)
Institution: G. B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, which lists Pant Rai 20 among its mustard releases. The GBPUAT Pantnagar AICRP centre sits in the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/08.06.2023_Varieties_Released.pdf ; http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf
Station: Pantnagar, Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/paperdetail.php?paper=1272

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. No official email, phone or postal address for the GBPUAT Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding or the Pantnagar AICRP centre appeared in the results. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/DES/research_centre (Directorate of Research page; returned no contact fields)
Institute site URLs found: https://www.gbpuat.ac.in and https://www.gbpuat.res.in (contact pages not retrieved)

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Searches returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report entry, thesis or conference paper that names Pant Rai-20. Papers by GBPUAT authors on mustard (for example, Usha Pant's SSR and heat-stress work) do not name this variety, so they were not attributed. -- https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=hH8lAM0AAAAJ&hl=en (author profile only; not attributed)

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Results were retail sellers of rai (black mustard spice) and unrelated Indian oilseed stock; none refer to Pant Rai-20 seed. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or seednet seed-sale record was retrieved. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rai-seeds-15337203155.html (a spice seller, discarded as irrelevant)

RECOMMENDED STATES
Uttarakhand is the seednet recommended state. The GBPUAT and AICRP results confirm only that the release comes from a Uttarakhand university and that the Pantnagar centre targets plains of Uttarakhand. Neither source names Pant Rai-20 with a recommended state. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf

NAME AND SPECIES NOTES
variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Pant Rai-20". GBPUAT and AICRP write it "Pant Rai 20" or "Pant Rai-20". The release notification is given as SO.2680(E) with date 01.10.15 in the AICRP table, which differs from the year_of_release field (2015-06-25). The species is also unresolved. The seednet crop is yellow sarson (Brassica rapa), but the GBPUAT list places Pant Rai-20 under mustard (Rai), and the AICRP table is for rapeseed-mustard. Verify the species against the CSC minutes before relying on the record.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to this variety in the searched sources. The variety is described for irrigated conditions in the Rabi season (original variety data), so no drought claim is made.

heat.details: Described as tolerant to high temperature during the early crop stages, which is the basis for recommended September sowing. Two independent sources state this qualitatively: the GBPUAT AICRP-Rapeseed-Mustard listing and the Ministry of Agriculture (DAC) oilseeds characters table. Neither gives a quantitative score, so the level is set to medium rather than high.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to this variety.

flood.details: No evidence found for flooding tolerance specific to this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The disease-screening pages returned (ICAR-DRMR AICRP reports) name other entries, not Pant Rai-19. The original variety data (CSC) states that no disease or insect pest incidence is seen by the time the crop matures in early January, mainly due to escape mechanism. This is a CSC statement and was not verified by any searched source.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The original variety data (CSC) states that the variety escapes aphid infestation due to early maturity. This is an escape mechanism reported in the CSC data, not confirmed resistance, and was not verified by any searched source.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 20.50 q/ha under normal conditions (original variety data, CSC). The DAC table gives a yield potential of 1831 to 2511 kg/ha (18.3 to 25.1 q/ha) for PR 20061 (Pant rai 19).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The CSC data notes good adaptability to increasing doses of fertilizer, which is a response trait and not a stability measure.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated condition in the Rabi season (CSC). Suitable for early sowing, with September sowing supported by heat tolerance in the early stages (AICRP and DAC sources). Recommended for Punjab, Haryana and New Delhi in the DRMR report.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Medium early maturity group (99 to 133 days)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) DAC oilseeds table: yield potential 1831 to 2511 kg/ha and oil content 40.9 to 41.8% for PR 20061 (Pant rai 19). (2) AICRP-Rapeseed-Mustard listing: a row for Pant Rai-19 reads as roughly 20 to 25 q/ha yield, 110 to 115 days maturity and about 40% oil. The column mapping is inferred from a garbled table and must be verified against the original PDF. (3) DRMR Project Coordinator's report (2020-21): lists PR 2006-1 (Pant Rai 19) among releases from 2011 to 2020, but trial yield data were not visible in the snippet. No multi-location trial data specific to this variety were found beyond these.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Pant Rai-19 (PR 2006-1) searches: 4 web_search queries run. Name used in each finding is noted where it matters. The SeedNet portal itself was not returned by any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The AICRP-Rapeseed-Mustard listing for Pant Rai-19 (identified as Krishna-2-1 x HS-027-1, notification SO.1708(E)) describes it as suited to early-sown conditions with tolerance to high temperature during the early crop stages. Evidence refers to "Pant Rai-19" under the GBPUAT AICRP listing. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf
- The Ministry of Agriculture (DAC) oilseeds characters table lists "PR 20061 (Pant rai 19)" as tolerant to high temperature at the early stage. Evidence refers to "PR 20061 (Pant rai 19)". -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx
- No evidence found for drought, salinity, flooding or submergence tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. The disease-screening pages returned (ICAR-DRMR AICRP reports) name other entries (for example DRMR 2018-25, Rohini, Varuna), not Pant Rai-19. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- DAC table gives yield potential of 1831–2511 kg/ha and oil content of 40.9–41.8% for PR 20061 (Pant rai 19). -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx
- AICRP listing gives a row for Pant Rai-19 with values that read as roughly 20–25 q/ha yield, 110–115 days maturity and about 40% oil. The column mapping is inferred from a garbled table, so verify against the original PDF. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf
- The DRMR Project Coordinator's report (2020-21) lists PR 2006-1 (Pant Rai 19) among rapeseed-mustard releases during 2011–2020, identified for Punjab, Haryana and New Delhi. Trial yield data for this variety were not visible in the snippet. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- No multi-location trial data specific to Pant Rai-19 found beyond the above.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage recorded in the AICRP listing: Krishna-2-1 x HS-027-1. Evidence refers to "Pant Rai-19". -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf
- The parentage text supplied in the task (single cross, Krishna-2-1 x HS-027-1) matches the AICRP entry. The breeding method "single cross" comes from the task input and was not confirmed by a web page.
- Breeding-line code: PR 2006-1 (also written PR 20061 on the DAC page). Evidence refers to "PR 2006-1 (Pant Rai 19)". -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- No QTL, marker, gene or genome-resource evidence found. -- (no URL)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar. The Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding page lists "Pant Rai 19" among varieties it developed. Evidence refers to "Pant Rai 19". -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/genetics-ach.pdf
- The GBPUAT released-varieties list includes "Pant Rai-19" under oilseeds. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/Released_crop_varieties.pdf
- Station: Pantnagar, Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand (the station is named on the GBPUAT site, but no page links it to this variety beyond the department listing above).
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. Dr. Usha Pant (Senior Research Officer, Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, specialising in rapeseed-mustard breeding) appears on the GBPUAT profile page, but no page links her to Pant Rai-19. She is not attributed as breeder here. -- https://gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/usha_profile.html

CONTACT DETAILS
- No named breeder contact found.
- Institute-level only: Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, G.B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, Pantnagar, Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand. No email, phone or postal code was found in the returned pages. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/genetics-ach.pdf
- Institute contact page URL: No evidence found in these results. The GBPUAT main site is https://www.gbpuat.ac.in (the homepage was not checked in this session).
- Usha Pant profile page (no contact details on the snippet; not linked to this variety): https://gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/usha_profile.html

PUBLICATIONS
- AICRP-Rapeseed-Mustard, GBPUAT (year not stated). Varietal entry for Pant Rai-19 (Krishna-2-1 x HS-027-1), listed in the varieties-released table. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, conference paper or KrishiKosh record was found that names Pant Rai-19. The papers returned by search (for example Kumar, Pant & Pant 2016 on combining ability; Rai et al. 2017 on heterosis) do not mention this variety, so they are not listed.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned retail mustard-seed products (Rani, Deer and other US-based spice sellers) that are unrelated to this variety and were discarded. -- (no relevant URL)
- GBPUAT describes "Pantnagar Seeds" as a brand for its seed production in general, but no page confirms seed of Pant Rai-19 is produced or sold. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/genetics-ach.pdf
- Not searched in this session: NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale pages. The fourth search was used on retail sellers and returned nothing relevant.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- DAC oilseeds table: Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Jammu, Rajasthan. Evidence refers to "PR 20061 (Pant rai 19)". -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx
- DRMR Project Coordinator's report (2020-21): identified for Punjab, Haryana, New Delhi. Evidence refers to "PR 2006-1 (Pant Rai 19)". -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- The task input lists Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Haryana and New Delhi. Jammu & Kashmir is in the DAC list only as "Jammu" and is absent from the DRMR list. Jammu & Kashmir is not confirmed by a web page.

NAME AND CODE NOTE
- The evidence above refers to "Pant Rai-19" and "PR 2006-1 / PR 20061 (Pant Rai 19)". No SeedNet portal page was retrieved, so the name "Pant Rai-19 (PR-2006-1)" as shown on SeedNet is not confirmed by search.

agronomic_details.field_trials: 1) Sowing-date study (Bhuva and Detroja, Jagadhar/Jodhpur-area journal): Proagro 9444 recorded the highest grain yield, statistically comparable with GHB 538, and the highest calendar days, heat units and heat use efficiency among all varieties tested. 2) Rainfed Eastern India, KVK Munger (kharif 2013 and 2014): Proagro 9444 yielded 32.09 q/ha, comparable to the top-yielding hybrid Proagro 9450 (33.87 q/ha, a different variety reported only for context). 3) Summer irrigation study, Eastern UP plains: Proagro 9444 with irrigation scheduled at 100 mm CPE gave the best benefit-cost ratio and net return. No disease or pest trial results found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Marketed as withstanding heat and moisture stress, per the company's pearl millet product page (Bayer/Proagro, base 9444 entry) -- Highly adaptable and can withstand heat and moisture stress. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/Products-H/Brands/Seeds-and-Traits/Seed-ProAgro-Millet
- A distributor page for the hybrid reports tolerance to high temperature and moisture stress -- Tolerant to high temperature & moisture stress -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_9444
- The Proagro breeding head said the hybrid is widely adaptable to adverse conditions with high tillering (company statement, 2006 article) -- Proagro 9444 is widely adaptable to adverse conditions with high tillering capacity per plant. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/proagro-millet-gets-popular-in-rajasthan-106060201124_1.html
- A review of Indian pearl millet breeding names 9444 among hybrids with good seed set and high grain yield under high-temperature targeting -- 86M64 and Proagro 9444, which specifically target this environment for hybrid development, have been found having good seed set and high grain yield of the order of 4–5 t ha^−1. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40003-013-0089-z
- Drought, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for these specific stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Downy mildew resistance is claimed for the base hybrid -- Resistant to Downy mildew -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_9444
- Caution: the "Proagro 9444 Gold" variant is listed separately with downy mildew, rust and smut tolerance -- Matures in 75 days, good grain and fodder yield, excellent stay green, tolerant to downy mildew, rust aand smut. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/Products-H/Brands/Seeds-and-Traits/Seed-ProAgro-Millet (this applies to Gold, not confirmed for base 9444)
- Caution: the "Gaucho" variant is listed with termite tolerance -- Good tolerance against termite. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/Products-H/Brands/Seeds-and-Traits/Seed-ProAgro-Millet (variant only)
- Pest and disease reaction data from field trials: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity and use, per company page: Full maturity 80-85 days. High grain and fodder yield. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/Products-H/Brands/Seeds-and-Traits/Seed-ProAgro-Millet
- Distributor page gives maturity of 80-85 days in kharif and 85-90 days in summer -- in 80-85 days in Kharif and Summer season 85-90 days. -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_9444
- Sowing-date study (Jagadhar/Jodhpur-area journal, Bhuva and Detroja): Pearl millet variety 'Proagro 9444' recorded the highest grain yield which was statistically comparable with 'GHB 538' and took the highest calendar days, heat units and heat use efficiency as compared to all other varieties. -- https://journal.agrimetassociation.org/index.php/jam/article/download/577/479/522
- Rainfed Eastern India trial (KVK Munger, kharif 2013 and 2014): Significantly higher grain yield (33.87 q ha-1) was in hybrid 'Proagro 9450' which was comparable to 'Proagro 9444' (32.09 q ha-1) -- https://www.academia.edu/41689356/Evaluation_of_Pearl_millet_varieties_under_rainfed_region_of_Eastern_India
- Summer irrigation study, Eastern UP plains: The best benefit-cost ratio and net return were obtained when hybrid Proagro 9444 was planted with irrigation set at 100 mm CPE. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328600256_Productivity_and_Water_use_Efficiency_of_Summer_Pearlmillet_Pennisetum_glaucum_L_Hybrids_as_Influenced_by_Irrigation_Scheduling_in_Eastern_Uttar_Pradesh_Plains

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The search returned no QTL, marker or parentage studies naming this hybrid. The only nearby hits were general pearl millet heterotic-pool papers that do not name

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi
seednet_fields.Parentage: Bio-902 x ZEM-1 Bio-902 was developed at IARI, New Delhi (NRCPB) in 1993 for zone IV and is a leading variety of the country after Pusa Bold and Varuna. ZEM-1 is an exotic yellow seeded genotype which possesses low erucic acid content. It is late in maturity and poor performer for seed and oil yields in Indian subcontinent.
seednet_fields.Resemblence to Variety: Its plant is tall and compact type having profuse branching with high siliquae density and bold dark brown seeds resembles with Bio-902.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release & cultivation in the States of Uttar Pradesh, Uttrakhand, Madhya Pradesh and eastern Rajasthan  for timely sown irrigated conditions.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Tolerant to lodging and shattering. Responsive to higher doses on N (150% of recommended fertility). Recommended fertility level – 80 kg N, 40 kg P2O5, 40 kg K2O. Suitable for timely (October) sown irrigated conditions in zone III in the double cropping system.  Seed rate : 3 – 4 kg/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Plant height (cm) - 200 cm.	BOLD SEEDED with low erucic acid content (<2.0%). ii.	Very long main shoot (87cm) and other branches with high siliquae density. iii.	Compact plant type with profuse branching having five primary and 14 secondary branches. iv.	Light green leaves without hairiness. v.	Dark brown seed coat colour. vi.	Light yellow flowers. vii.	Small siliqua with undulated texture.   Tall, compact plant type II.	Leaf characters i.	Simple / Compound - Simple, - Shape of leaf pinae - Round and broad, - Colour -  Light green,- Pubescent/Glabrous - Pubescent, - Stem colour -  Light green, -  Flower colour -  Light yellow, - Siliqua - Small,- Seed - Bold, dark brown in colour
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress:
•	Tolerates salinity upto 12 dS/m and has lesser reduction in germination (%) and seedling dry weight. It recorded 10.3, 7.4 and 15.8 percent  reduction in germination percent at Kanpur, Hisar and S.K. Nagar, respectively, which was much lesser than salinity tolerant check CS 54. It was, therefore, rated as tolerant to salinity (<20%). At S.K. Nagar it has merely 15.7 % reduction in seedling dry weight. 
•	Variety was rated as moderately tolerant to terminal heat stress based on reduction in total dry weight at Hisar and Kanpur; 1000 seed weight and harvest index at Kanpur which is comparable to the tolerant check BPR 541-4 with respect to all the four parameters studied.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

drought.details: RB-50 is identified as drought tolerant and resistant to drought stress. It is listed among varieties specifically suited for rainfed conditions. It has been described as one of the most drought tolerant mustard genotypes.

heat.details: RB-50 is tolerant to terminal heat stress, which is a significant issue for Indian mustard at its terminal stage in India.

salinity.details: RB-50 is listed as a salinity tolerant variety of Indian mustard.

flood.details: RB-50 is listed as a variety suitable for ACZ-III-B Flood Prone Eastern Plains (Alwar, Rajasthan), implying some level of flood tolerance, grouped under general 'submergence tolerant varieties'.

disease_resistance.summary: RB-50 is resistant to lodging, all rusts, white rust, and yellow mosaic virus. It is also mentioned as a highly resistant mustard genotype for biotic stresses.

pest_resistance.summary: RB-50 is tolerant to aphids and jassids.

submergence.basis: Only the same ResearchGate review, which places RB-50 in a category grouping and states no direct submergence evidence. This is a category listing only.

drought.details: RGN 229 is identified as a climate-resilient variety demonstrating tolerance to drought. Moisture stress is known to cause significant yield reduction in Indian mustard, with RGN 229 specifically listed among varieties with drought tolerance.

heat.details: RGN 229 exhibits heat (high temperature) tolerance. It is listed as a climate-resilient variety for heat tolerance and specifically showed thermo tolerance in trials conducted at Kanpur. Indian mustard often faces high temperature stress at the terminal stage, and RGN 229 has been evaluated for its thermal requirements and heat use efficiency.

salinity.details: RGN 229 is identified as a climate-resilient variety with tolerance to salinity.

drought.details: Rainfed, timely-sown trial: seed yield fell by about 22.0% under stress, water loss was 4.2%, and harvest index fell 9.7%. The Drought Susceptibility Index (DSI) was 0.92, versus 1.21 for the check PM 25 (a lower DSI than the check indicates relatively better drought tolerance). The rating is medium because the evidence comes from a single trial reported in one paper (with the same figures repeated in a ResearchGate copy), and a 22% yield loss under stress is still substantial. The DAC source describes the variety as suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. The searches returned no evidence on heat tolerance for RH 761.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. The searches returned no evidence on salinity tolerance for RH 761.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. The searches returned no evidence on flood tolerance for RH 761.

disease_resistance.summary: White rust: severity low and decreasing across seasons. Alternaria leaf blight: moderate resistance, with 31.8% severity on leaves and 20.2% on pods (pods better than the check Rohini at 23.7%). Sclerotinia stem rot: moderate susceptibility, with severity falling from 34.0% (2015-16) to 26.8% (2017-18). Resistance to other diseases: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Aphid: infestation index improved from 2.93 (2015-16) to 1.19 (2017-18), indicating reduced infestation over seasons. Other pests: Not found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Recommended yield potential 2500-2600 kg/ha (DAC source); oil content 40%. Front-line demonstrations (Rajasthan): 15.59 q/ha for RH-761 recommended practice versus 12.30 q/ha for farmer practice (26.74% increase). Hisar rainfed trial: RH 761 was outyielded by RH 725 (RH 725 at 2583 kg/ha); the RH 761 figure for that trial was not given.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for yield stability across environments. The drought DSI and the Hisar and Rajasthan trial results are the only environment-specific yield evidence. Fertility-level seed yield data exist in the ResearchGate paper's tables but were not legible in the retrieved text.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions (DAC source). Recommended states as listed in the original data: Jammu, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan. Heat, salinity, flood and submergence adaptation: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Flowers at 43-47 days and matures in 140-149 days; average 141 days, comparable to checks.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Large leaves; main shoot 82-93 cm; 58-68 siliquae per plant; 14-16 seeds per siliqua. Morphological characteristics beyond these: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Drought, rainfed timely-sown trial: seed yield fell about 22.0% under stress; water loss 4.2%; harvest index fell 9.7%; DSI 0.92 versus 1.21 for PM 25. (2) Front-line demonstrations, Rajasthan/extension study: RH-761 averaged 15.59 q/ha versus 12.30 q/ha for farmer practice (26.74% increase). (3) Rainfed date-of-sowing trial at Hisar, rabi 2018-19 and 2019-20: RH 761 was outyielded by RH 725 (2583 kg/ha). (4) Agronomy coordinated trial: fertility-level seed yield data exist but the figures were not legible in the retrieved text. (5) Disease and pest monitoring across seasons (2015-16 to 2017-18) is summarised under disease and pest resistance above.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources (no QTL, SNP or SSR marker studies found). Variety code A040317621 and parentage were not confirmed: the Seednet portal was not returned by any search, and the parentage field is not found in the sources.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. Breeding-value evidence: RH 761 showed significant general combining ability (GCA) for thousand-seed weight and oil content across environments (Hisar timely and late sown, New Delhi). Hybrid evidence: RH 761 hybrids showed high heterobeltiosis for seed weight in some crosses (for example, NPJ 161 x RH 761 at 16.19%).
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. Metabolome evidence only: RH 761 and RH 725 differ in some leaf and stem metabolites (for example, malic acid is largely absent in RH 761 leaves). This describes metabolite differences and does not identify genes or pathways.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RH 761 / RH-761 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The release-minutes name "RH 761" and the Seednet name "RH-761" both appear in the sources, and the evidence below refers to the same variety under either spelling. The Seednet portal itself was not returned by any search, so nothing here confirms the Seednet record, variety code A040317621, or the parentage field.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Drought (rainfed, timely-sown trial): seed yield fell by about 22.0% under stress, water loss was 4.2%, harvest index fell 9.7%, and the Drought Susceptibility Index was 0.92, versus 1.21 for PM 25 -- https://www.agriculturaljournals.com/archives/2025.v7.i1.C.257/mustard-variety-rh-761-enhancing-biotic-and-abiotic-stress-resistance-for-superior-yield-and-stable-production
Drought (same paper, ResearchGate copy): same DSI and yield-reduction figures reported -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388388594_Mustard_variety-RH_761_Enhancing_biotic_and_abiotic_stress_resistance_for_superior_yield_and_stable_production
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. The searches returned nothing on these for RH 761.

DISEASE AND PEST
White rust: severity is low and decreasing across seasons -- https://www.agriculturaljournals.com/archives/2025.v7.i1.C.257/mustard-variety-rh-761-enhancing-biotic-and-abiotic-stress-resistance-for-superior-yield-and-stable-production
Alternaria leaf blight: moderate resistance, 31.8% severity on leaves and 20.2% on pods (pods better than the check Rohini at 23.7%) -- same URL
Sclerotinia stem rot: moderate susceptibility; severity fell from 34.0% (2015-16) to 26.8% (2017-18) -- same URL
Aphid: infestation index improved from 2.93 (2015-16) to 1.19 (2017-18) -- same URL
Other pests and resistance to other diseases: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Recommended yield potential 2500-2600 kg/ha, oil content 40%, release year 2019, suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx (retrieved through a Google Translate wrapper: https://translate.google.com/translate?u=https%3A%2F%2Foilseeds.dac.gov.in%2FRapeseed.aspx&hl=hi&sl=en&tl=hi&client=srp&prev=search)
Maturity: flowers at 43-47 days and matures in 140-149 days; average 141 days, comparable to checks -- https://www.agriculturaljournals.com/archives/2025.v7.i1.C.257/mustard-variety-rh-761-enhancing-biotic-and-abiotic-stress-resistance-for-superior-yield-and-stable-production
Plant type: large leaves, main shoot 82-93 cm, 58-68 siliquae per plant, 14-16 seeds per siliqua -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388388594_Mustard_variety-RH_761_Enhancing_biotic_and_abiotic_stress_resistance_for_superior_yield_and_stable_production
Front-line demonstrations (Rajasthan/extension study): RH-761 recommended-practice demonstrations averaged 15.59 q/ha against 12.30 q/ha for farmer practice, a 26.74% increase -- https://indianecologicalsociety.com/wp-content/themes/ecology/volume_pdfs/1681611840.pdf
Rainfed date-of-sowing trial at Hisar, rabi 2018-19 and 2019-20: RH 761 was outyielded by RH 725 (RH 725 seed yield 2583 kg/ha) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-5947
Agronomy coordinated trial: fertility-level seed yield data for RH 761 exist in the ResearchGate paper's tables, but the figures were not legible in the retrieved text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388388594_Mustard_variety-RH_761_Enhancing_biotic_and_abiotic_stress_resistance_for_superior_yield_and_stable_production

GENETICS AND QTL
Breeding value: RH 761 showed significant general combining ability for thousand-seed weight and oil content across environments (Hisar timely and late sown, New Delhi) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405844024165863
Hybrid performance: RH 761 hybrids gave high heterobeltiosis for seed weight in some crosses (for example, NPJ 161 x RH 761 at 16.19%) -- same URL
Metabolome: RH 761 and RH 725 differ in some leaf and stem metabolites (for example, malic acid is largely absent in RH 761 leaves) -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-69865-8
QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Lead breeders (per the 2025 RH 761 paper): Ram Avtar, Dalip Kumar, Rakesh Punia, Neeraj Malik, Nisha Kumari, Anita Kumari, Rajbir Singh Khedwal and Mahavir Bishnoi, Oilseeds Section, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar -- https://www.agriculturaljournals.com/archives/2025.v7.i1.C.257/mustard-variety-rh-761-enhancing-biotic-and-abiotic-stress-resistance-for-superior-yield-and-stable-production and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388388594_Mustard_variety-RH_761_Enhancing_biotic_and_abiotic_stress_resistance_for_superior_yield_and_stable_production
Developing institution: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar; its achievements page lists RH 761 as a national-level release -- https://hau.ac.in/page/achievements-32
Sole-breeder attribution: the sources name the oilseeds team as developers; a single named lead breeder was not confirmed.
Parentage: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Individual breeder email or phone: No evidence found.
Institute address, email or phone for CCS HAU Hisar Oilseeds Section or Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding: No evidence found. The sources contain no such contact details. Institute homepage for reference: https://hau.ac.in/ (the achievements page above is the only HAU page retrieved).
Corresponding author: the ResearchGate listing names Dalip Kumar (surname truncated in the text) at CCS HAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388388594_Mustard_variety-RH_761_Enhancing_biotic_and_abiotic_stress_resistance_for_superior_yield_and_stable_production
Seed-corporation address (not a breeder contact): National Seeds Corporation, Beej Bhawan, Pusa Complex, New Delhi-110012, as printed on a retailer listing whose title names RH-725 but whose body names RH-761 -- https://market.plantix.net/en/products/seeds/d56bdc79-ba82-44b2-af94-bbbb4d25d203/mustard-variety-rh725-certified-seed-2-kgg-pack/

PUBLICATIONS

drought.details: Two independent studies classed RH-749 as drought-sensitive. A greenhouse PGPR study ranked it the most drought-sensitive of four genotypes, behind RH-30, while RH-725 and RH-761 were more tolerant. A metabolomic study classed it as drought-sensitive relative to RH-725, with lower relative water content, chlorophyll and membrane stability under drought. Irrigation and anti-transpirant field trials (Bawal, 2017-18 and 2018-19) are not drought stress evidence and are not used to upgrade this rating.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance evidence was found for RH 0749. Only general Brassica juncea heat studies exist, which do not directly apply to this variety.

salinity.details: A single study reports that 100 mM NaCl applied for 20 days reduced chlorophyll content, net photosynthesis and stomatal conductance in RH-749 (listed as RH0-749). This documents a stress response but provides no comparative tolerance rating, so no tolerance level can be assigned.

flood.details: No evidence found for waterlogging or flood tolerance in RH 0749.

disease_resistance.summary: The Tribune report states the variety is resistant to major diseases but names no specific pathogens and gives no test data. The AICRP progeny trial used RH 0749 as a check for disease tolerance but reports no RH 0749 resistance scores. No specific disease resistance is confirmed for RH 0749 from the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance data were found. An avoidable-loss study on RH 0749 and other Brassica crops reports an insect-related loss of about 11.79% for RH 0749, which indicates susceptibility to insect damage rather than resistance. A pollinator foraging study used RH-0749 as a test variety but reports no pest resistance data.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported average yield of about 20-21 q/ha (approximately 2000-2100 kg/ha) with oil content of 39-40%.
agronomic_details.stability: No evidence found on stability across environments. The variety was identified at the All-India Rapeseed-Mustard group meet at Mathura, as reported by the Tribune, but no multi-environment stability data were provided.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Identified for timely-sown irrigated conditions in Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan (Zone 3, per the original variety data). The 2019-20 AICRP summary mentions RH 749 in Jammu and Kashmir under irrigated conditions, but the text is cut off and no result is available.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Long siliquae with bold seeds, as described by the Tribune report. No other morphological data were found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Irrigation and anti-transpirant trials (Bawal, 2017-18 and 2018-19) found RH-749 outperformed RH-725 on yield attributes and seed yield per plant. Used as a check in AICRP progeny row trials alongside RH 725 for seed yield and disease tolerance, with no result values reported for RH 0749. A 2019-20 AICRP summary mentions a Jammu and Kashmir irrigated trial without usable results.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No evidence found specific to RH 0749. An AICRP report mentions SSR markers for 154 genotypes, but RH 0749 is not named.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No evidence found for QTLs associated with RH 0749.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No evidence found for specific genes or pathways in RH 0749. The drought and salinity studies describe physiological responses (relative water content, chlorophyll, membrane stability, photosynthesis, stomatal conductance) but do not identify genes.

YIELD/TRIALS: Used as a check in AICRP progeny row trials alongside RH 725 for seed yield and disease tolerance -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
YIELD/TRIALS: 2019-20 AICRP summary mentions RH 749 in Jammu and Kashmir under irrigated conditions, but the text is cut off so no result is available -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf

DROUGHT: Greenhouse PGPR study ranked RH-749 as the most drought-sensitive of four genotypes, behind RH-30, while RH-725 and RH-761 were more tolerant -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00344-025-11887-1
DROUGHT: Metabolomic study classed RH-749 as drought-sensitive relative to RH-725, with lower relative water content, chlorophyll and membrane stability under drought -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12195340/
SALINITY: 100 mM NaCl for 20 days reduced chlorophyll content, net photosynthesis and stomatal conductance in RH-749 (listed as RH0-749) -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/85495

drought.details: Sources describe RH 1424 as suited to timely sowing under rainfed conditions, not as drought tolerant. The input record states it performs better under timely-sown rainfed conditions. No drought screening or trial data was found, so tolerance cannot be rated.

heat.details: A sowing-date trial found that delayed sowing reduced growth and yield in RH 1424, and canopy temperature rose with delay. This documents a sowing-date response, not heat-stress screening or tolerance. No heat-tolerance data was found.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. No salinity-tolerance screening data was found.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. Sources do not describe flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence of disease resistance specific to RH 1424 was found in the searches.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence of pest resistance specific to RH 1424 was found in the searches.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed trials averaged about 26 q/ha, reported as roughly 14% above RH 725. In a timely-sown trial, RH 1424 gave 26.13 q/ha versus 23.13 q/ha for RH 725, statistically at par. A seller listing gives 24-26 q/ha. Nitrogen at 100 kg/ha gave the highest seed yield in the timely-sown trial.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Only the rainfed and timely-sown trial results above are available; no multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions. Recommended for Jammu, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Rajasthan. A seller listing claims frost (pala) tolerance, which is a commercial claim and not trial data.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Oil content about 40.5% (apnikheti and seller listing). Seller listing reports flowering at 45-55 days, 17-18 seeds per pod and bold seed. Responsive to higher fertility doses (input record). Morphological characteristics beyond these were not specified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Rainfed trials: average about 26 q/ha, about 14% above RH 725 (apnikheti). (2) Timely-sown trial: RH 1424 gave 26.13 q/ha, at par with RH 725 at 23.13 q/ha; N at 100 kg/ha gave the highest seed yield; delayed sowing reduced growth and yield, and canopy temperature rose with delay (ICAR journal article). (3) Cultivar comparison of RH 1706, RH 1424, RH 725, RH 749 and Giriraj under sowing and INM treatments, rabi 2023-24 and 2024-25 (academia.edu source; results not summarised in the digest). (4) AICRP 2019-20 report lists RH 1424 among entries in the varietal trial programme (no yield data given in the digest). (5) Seller listing: 24-26 q/ha, 40.5% oil.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RH 1424 (mustard) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: the CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "RH 1424". The sources below refer to RH 1424 under that name. I found no Seednet portal page; the Seednet entry itself is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Sources describe RH 1424 as suited to timely sowing under rainfed conditions, not as a drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerant line -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/hr/updates-detaills/two-new-improved-mustard-varieties-have-been-introduced-by-ccs-hau-hisar/1173
- A seed-seller listing claims RH 1424 is tolerant to frost (pala); this is a commercial claim, not trial data -- https://www.mkdseeds.com/RH%201424%20Mustard%20seeds
- Sowing-date trial: delayed sowing reduced growth and yield in RH 1424, and canopy temperature rose with delay -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOB/article/view/166710
- No peer-reviewed or official stress-tolerance screening data found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to RH 1424 (searched within the variety and crop query; no hits).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rainfed trials averaged about 26 q/ha, reported as roughly 14% above RH 725 -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/hr/updates-detaills/two-new-improved-mustard-varieties-have-been-introduced-by-ccs-hau-hisar/1173
- Maturity is about 139 days; seed oil content about 40.5% -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/hr/updates-detaills/two-new-improved-mustard-varieties-have-been-introduced-by-ccs-hau-hisar/1173
- Seller listing gives 24-26 q/ha, flowering at 45-55 days, 17-18 seeds per pod, bold seed, 40.5% oil -- https://www.mkdseeds.com/RH%201424%20Mustard%20seeds
- Timely-sown RH 1424 gave 26.13 q/ha, statistically at par with RH 725 (23.13 q/ha); N at 100 kg/ha gave the highest seed yield in that trial -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOB/article/view/166710
- Cultivar comparison (RH 1706, RH 1424, RH 725, RH 749, Giriraj) under sowing and INM treatments, rabi 2023-24 and 2024-25 -- https://www.academia.edu/172118309/Effect_of_Different_Cultivars_and_INM_on_Physiological_Growth_Indices_of_Indian_Mustard_Brassica_juncea_L
- AICRP 2019-20 report lists RH 1424 among entries in the varietal/trial programme -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage RH-202 x RH-401B comes from the input record only; no search source confirmed it.
- No QTL, marker or genetic-mapping study for RH 1424 found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/chaudhary-charan-singh-haryana-agricultural-university-has-developed-two-improved-varieties-of-mustard
- Announced on 17 August 2022 by the university's oilseed team; the input's release date of 26 Oct 2022 is not confirmed by any source -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/hr/updates-detaills/two-new-improved-mustard-varieties-have-been-introduced-by-ccs-hau-hisar/1173
- Identified for cultivation at the AICRP (Mustard) meeting at RARI, Durgapur (Rajasthan) -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/chaudhary-charan-singh-haryana-agricultural-university-has-developed-two-improved-varieties-of-mustard
- Scientists named as developers of the RH 1424/RH 1706 pair (mustard team): Dr. Ram Avtar, Dr. Neeraj, Dr. Manjeet and Dr. Ashok Kumar (lead team); with Dr. Rakesh Poonia, Dr. Nisha Kumari, Dr. Vinod Goyal, Dr. Mahavir and Dr. Rajbir Singh -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/haryana-agricultural-university-developed-another-new-mustard-variety-rh1975 and https://www.farmingcosmos.com/hau-develops-new-mustard-variety-rh-1975-for-higher-yield-oil-content/
- Officials quoted at release: Vice Chancellor Prof. B.R. Kamboj; Director of Research Dr. Jeetram Sharma -- https://www.amarujala.com/haryana/hisar/haryana-agriculture-university-develops-rh-1424-and-rh-1706-varieties-of-mustard
- Station: Hisar (oilseed section); a specific station name was not found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contacts: no email, phone or address found for Dr. Ram Avtar, Dr. Neeraj, Dr. Manjeet, Dr. Ashok Kumar or others.
- Institute contacts: no official CCS HAU email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL found in the searches.
- Seed-dealer listing (not an institute contact): phone +91 8224917065, email mykisanagro@gmail.com -- https://www.mkdseeds.com/RH%201424%20Mustard%20seeds
- Action: check the CCS HAU Hisar oilseeds/mustard research division site and the AICRP Rapeseed-Mustard directorate page for official contacts.

PUBLICATIONS
- Keerthi, P., Neelam, Ram Avatar & Bhaskar, P. (year not shown in source). Optimizing yield and physiological performance of Indian mustard (Brassica juncea L.) varieties through sowing dates and nitrogen management. Journal of Oilseeds Research(?) (journal name truncated in source) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOB/article/view/166710
- Authors not confirmed (2026). Effect of Different Cultivars and INM on Physiological Growth Indices of Indian Mustard (Brassica juncea L.). Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology -- DOI 10.9734/JABB/2026/V29I94313 (https://doi.org/10.9734/JABB/2026/V29I94313); the source shows RH 1424 as one of five cultivars.
- AICRP on Rapeseed-Mustard Annual Report 2019-20 (Varietal Improvement, Crop Production) -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis, ICAR annual report entry specific to RH 1424 beyond the above, or QTL paper found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- IFFDC lists certified and TL seed of RH-1424 among mustard varieties available -- https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed
- NSC (Bharatpur) listing of RH-1424 T/L seed, 1 kg pouch -- https://www.mystore.in/en/product/nsc-farm-sona-mustard-rh-725-t-l (product suggestion list)
- Private dealer listing at about ₹450 per 1 kg pack -- https://www.mkdseeds.com/RH%201424%20Mustard%20seeds
- No SAU/KVK or Seednet availability record found; state seed corporation stock not verified.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, North Rajasthan and Jammu, identified at the AICRP Mustard meeting -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/chaudhary-charan-singh-haryana-agricultural-university-has-developed-two-improved-varieties-of-mustard
- The input lists "Jammu, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and northern Rajasthan"; this matches the sources.

Not yet verified: release notification number, Seednet listing, official HAU release notice.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CROP IDENTITY: RH 725 is a Brassica juncea (Indian mustard/raya) variety from CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar, not a wheat variety -- https://drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/varieties-developed-in-haryana-agricultural-university-will-benefit-other-states-as-well-1 ; https://hau.ac.in/page/achievements-11
INSTITUTION/BREEDER: Developed at CCS Haryana Agricultural University (HAU), Hisar; breeder named in popular press as Dr. Ramavtar Singh -- https://purvanchalfarms.com/rh-725-mustard-variety-details/ (secondary, non-official source)
RELEASE YEAR: Listed as released in 2018 with HAU as release institute -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/rh-725/ ; https://utkarsh.com/current-affairs/state/haryana/haryana-agricultural-university-developed-mustard-variety-rh-1975
YIELD: Average of about 10-12 quintals/acre with production potential of 14-15 quintals/acre (news report) -- https://utkarsh.com/current-affairs/state/haryana/haryana-agricultural-university-developed-mustard-variety-rh-1975 ; Commercial listing gives 10-13 quintals/acre -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/rh-725/
YIELD (commercial listing, unverified): Maximum yield quoted as 12 quintals/acre -- https://agrilcareer.com/product/rh-725-mustard-seed-buy-online/
AGRONOMY/QUALITY: Maturity 135-145 days; seed rate 2.5 kg/acre; spacing 12-18 inches; 15-22 seeds per siliqua; oil content 37-39%; oleic acid about 40% -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/rh-725/ (commercial listing, not an official trial report)
POPULARITY/ADOPTION: Described as the most popular mustard variety, grown on roughly 20-25% of the area in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Haryana -- https://drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/haryana-agricultural-university-developed-another-new-mustard-variety-rh1975 (news report, figures not from an official survey)
SEED AVAILABILITY: CCS HAU raw seed production in 2022-23 for raya included RH-725 (with RH-30 and RH-761) at 104.87 quintals total for the three varieties combined -- https://hau.ac.in/page/achievements-11
SEED AVAILABILITY (commercial): Sold through private online seed retailers; listed as out of stock at time of search -- https://agrilcareer.com/product/rh-725-mustard-seed-buy-online/ (no NSC, State Seed Corporation, or KVK availability evidence found)
RECOMMENDED STATES: The stated states (Jammu, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi) were not confirmed by any source found; sources mention Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Haryana as main areas of adoption -- https://drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/haryana-agricultural-university-developed-another-new-mustard-variety-rh1975
DROUGHT TOLERANCE: No evidence found
HEAT TOLERANCE: No evidence found
SALINITY TOLERANCE: No evidence found
FLOOD TOLERANCE: No evidence found
SUBMERGENCE TOLERANCE: No evidence found
DISEASE RESISTANCE (e.g., white rust, Alternaria, downy mildew, Sclerotinia): No evidence found
PEST RESISTANCE (e.g., aphid, painted bug): No evidence found
QTL/MARKERS: No evidence found
OFFICIAL TRIAL DATA (AICRP-Rapeseed & Mustard, zonal trials, notification gazette): No evidence found

agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data were returned.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRP-style multi-location trial (Ludhiana, Bharatpur, Hisar, Pantnagar and others) in the 2024 AICRP-RM workshop proceedings: RLC 3 is listed as a quality/canola-type entry, but no yield values are given. (2) ICAR-DRMR AICRP 2020 varietal improvement report: RLC 3 appears in a trial table row (Punjab / PAU Ludhiana / Indian mustard / 2016), but the table values are not legible in the snippet. No quantitative trial yield results were found. Full trial results in KrishiKosh theses or journal papers: Not found in searched sources.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: A KASP marker assay for erucic acid content in Indian mustard lists RLC 3 as low-erucic, with homozygous e1e1 e2e2 FAE1 alleles, and includes FAE1.1/FAE1.2 sequence comparison with PBR91. Marker names, SNP positions and chromosomal locations for RLC 3: Not found in searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. Marker or QTL mapping studies specific to RLC 3 yellow seed colour: No evidence found. RLC 3 is used as a parent in marker-assisted backcross lines PMAS 1602 and PMAS 1604 (PAU Ludhiana) and in pedigree lines PDZ-22 and PDZ-23 (IARI); these are use records, not QTL effects. Parentage of the variety itself is not stated.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Low erucic acid phenotype associated with homozygous e1e1 e2e2 FAE1 alleles, as reported in the KASP assay study. Other genes or pathways for RLC 3: Not found in searched sources.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Listed as white-rust tolerant (PAU College of Agriculture release list, 2015 date given there) -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewMatter&intDepTitleID=20
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Heat, drought, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no variety-specific statement on these traits.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Described as resistant to powdery mildew in a farm-advisory page (Apnikheti, "Features of RLC 3 variety of Mustard") -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/expert-advisory-details/features-of-rlc-3-variety-of-mustard/5241
DISEASE AND PEST -- White-rust tolerance, same PAU release list as above -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewMatter&intDepTitleID=20
DISEASE AND PEST -- RLC 3 was one of several B. juncea cultivars compared for tolerance to mustard aphid (Lipaphis erysimi), with biochemical responses reported per cultivar; the snippet does not give a resistance rating -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382868158_Induced_immune_defense_in_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_against_Lipaphis_erysimi_Kalt_via_altered_photosynthetic_and_enzymatic_levels
DISEASE AND PEST -- Sclerotinia, Alternaria, blackrot, and insect-pest resistance: No evidence found for RLC 3 specifically.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Tall plant type, maturity about 145 days, average yield about 7.3 quintal/acre, yellow seed colour -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/oilseeds/mustard (same figures also at https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/expert-advisory-details/features-of-rlc-3-variety-of-mustard/5241)
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Included as a quality/canola-type entry in a PAU AICRP-style multi-location trial (Ludhiana, Bharatpur, Hisar, Pantnagar and others); the snippet lists the entry but gives no yield values -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2024/Final_Proceeding_2024.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Appears in an ICAR-DRMR AICRP 2020 varietal improvement report with a Punjab / PAU Ludhiana / Indian mustard / RLC-3 / 2016 row in a trial table; the table values are not legible in the snippet -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- KASP marker assay for erucic acid content in Indian mustard, which lists RLC 3 as low-erucic with homozygous e1e1 e2e2 FAE1 alleles and includes FAE1.1/FAE1.2 sequence comparison with PBR91 -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.738805/full
GENETICS AND QTL -- RLC 3 is used as a parent in marker-assisted backcross lines PMAS 1602 and PMAS 1604 (PAU Ludhiana) and in pedigree lines PDZ-22 and PDZ-23 (IARI); the parentage recorded for the variety itself is not stated -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2024/Final_Proceeding_2024.pdf
GENETICS AND QTL -- Marker or QTL mapping studies specific to RLC 3 yellow seed colour: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developed by Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana, Punjab; described as the second institution in India to develop a canola-quality (double-low) Indian mustard variety, RLC 3 -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewMatter&intDepTitleID=20

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Seednet portal listing, National Seeds Corporation, Punjab State Seed Corporation, PAU seed sales, KVK or private-dealer stock for RLC 3: No evidence found. The search returned only retail yellow-sarson seed pages (Amazon, BigBasket, NY Spice Shop, Maya Bazaar, Urban Platter, House of Rasda) that are unrelated to this variety. These were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Punjab. Named in the PAU release list and in the ICAR-DRMR AICRP 2020 table row (Punjab, PAU Ludhiana) -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewMatter&intDepTitleID=20 and https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
RECOMMENDED STATES -- Zone-level notification details: No evidence found.

RECORD NOTES -- Release year: the PAU page gives 2015, while the Seednet record gives 2016-08-12. Both are shown here as found. Name variants: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "RLC 3"; sources also write "RLC-3" and "RLC3" (same variety by context). Seednet portal pages themselves were not returned, so the seednet crop label "Indian rapeseed and mustard (yellow sarson)" is not confirmed by a search hit. The PAU page's "canola-quality Indian mustard" description conflicts with the crop label "yellow sarson" in the Seednet record, since yellow sarson is normally Brassica rapa; the evidence points to Brassica juncea.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RGN-303 (mustard)

Scope note: Four searches were run. A fifth call to pull the full text of the Bikaner station PDF hit the tool's usage limit, so the findings below come from search snippets only. Several headings have little or no evidence. Name note: the CSC name is RGN-303 and the Seednet name is RNG-303. Every search used RGN-303, and no result mentioned RNG-303, so all evidence below refers to RGN-303.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found in the captured snippets. The snippets did not describe drought, heat, salinity, or other stress reactions for RGN-303.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found specific to RGN-303. A ResearchGate paper on Alternaria blight management in rapeseed-mustard mentions evaluating genotypes, but the snippet does not name RGN-303, so I am not attributing it to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/257076397_Management_of_alternaria_blight_of_rapeseed-mustard

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The Agriculture Research Station, Bikaner "at a glance" profile lists "RGN-303 (2014)" under mustard. Its snippet also mentions a fertilizer recommendation for the variety (half-dose fertilizer with vermicompost for mustard), but the snippet does not give the yield or maturity figures. -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The Bikaner Agriculture Research Station profile lists RGN-303 among mustard varieties, and the station also lists an AICRP on Rapeseed-Mustard project. No breeder name was found in the captured snippets. The record's institution is "Agriculture Research Station, S. K. Rajasthan Agricultural University." -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact was found. No email, phone, or postal address for the Bikaner station was captured in the snippets. The station profile PDF is the only institute source located, and it should be opened directly to retrieve the station's address and contact information.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or thesis specific to RGN-303 was identified. Not verified: the ResearchGate Alternaria paper above, which is not confirmed to involve RGN-303.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No seller, NSC, state corporation, or KVK listing was found. The Bikaner station profile mentions breeder seed production for mustard, but the snippet does not say RGN-303 seed is currently available. -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No state recommendation list was captured from the search results. The record lists Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Uttar Pradesh, but I could not verify these against a source.

Discrepancies to resolve:
- The release year is 2015 in the CSC record, but the Bikaner profile lists RGN-303 as 2014.
- The Seednet name RNG-303 has not been verified on any page.

Suggested next steps: open the Bikaner ARS PDF in full, check seednet.gov.in for RNG-303, and search KrishiKosh and the AICRP Rapeseed-Mustard annual reports for RGN-303 trial data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance specific to Sushree. A 2022 climate-resilient varieties newsletter lists Sushree among climate-resilient varieties, but the snippet gives no stress-specific data -- https://justagriculture.in/files/newsletter/2022/december/16.%20Climate%20Resilient%20Varieties%20and%20Genetic%20Stocks%20in.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches for disease or pest reaction of Sushree returned no page naming this variety with a resistance or susceptibility rating.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
On-farm participatory trial, rabi 2014-15, Bauligarh village, Angul district, mid-central table land zone of Odisha: Sushree gave 12.64 q/ha seed yield, about 45% above the local check Rai shoriso; plant height 153.78 cm; 173.19 siliquae/plant; 1000-seed weight 4.29 g; harvest index 22.98%; additional net return Rs 11,006.61/ha, benefit-cost ratio 1.80 -- https://www.allresearchjournal.com/archives/2015/vol1issue9/PartB/1-8-120-423.pdf
Same study, abstract summary page -- https://www.academia.edu/99448667/On_farm_assessment_of_toria_Brassica_campestris_L_variety_Sushree_under_mid_central_table_land_zone_of_Odisha
OUAT AICRP Rapeseed-Mustard centre (Ranital) reports Sushree as a released toria variety and the only one of its three released toria varieties still in the seed chain -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/
Sushree listed among varieties in a DRMR breeding table as a parent in fresh crosses (Tapeswari x Sushree) -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
Sushree mentioned in a DRMR AICRP summary with a low seed quantity note; no yield or agronomy data in the snippet -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Sushree is described as a mutant of TS-29 (designation ORT(m)-7-2) -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/
No QTL or marker study naming Sushree was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Odisha University of Agriculture & Technology (OUAT), via its AICRP on Rapeseed-Mustard, Ranital -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. No page named a breeder for Sushree.
Release date conflict: the OUAT page says Sushree was released in 2012, while the CSC record gives 2014-10-20. Both are recorded here; the evidence does not resolve the difference -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder name, role, email, phone: No evidence found.
Institute-level contact: No email, phone, or postal address for OUAT or its Ranital AICRP centre was found in the results. The only institute reference is the OUAT AICRP page -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/
Name tested: the evidence refers to "Sushree" for both variety_name and seednet_variety_name, since no separate Seednet name was found.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not identified in the results (2015). On farm assessment of toria (Brassica campestris L.) variety Sushree under mid central table land zone of Odisha. International Journal of Applied Research -- https://www.allresearchjournal.com/archives/2015/vol1issue9/PartB/1-8-120-423.pdf
Authors not identified (year not stated in result). On farm assessment of toria (Brassica campestris L.) variety Sushree under mid central table land zone of Odisha. Academia.edu record of the same study -- https://www.academia.edu/99448667/On_farm_assessment_of_toria_Brassica_campestris_L_variety_Sushree_under_mid_central_table_land_zone_of_Odisha
Authors not identified (2020). Indian Society of Oilseeds Research executive council report 2018-2020, mentioning Sushree in the toria seed-chain context. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344426080_THE_INDIAN_SOCIETY_OF_OILSEEDS_RESEARCH_EXECUTIVE_COUNCIL_FOR_2018-2020
No peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh), or AICRP annual report specifically on Sushree was found in the results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Sushree is in the seed chain per the OUAT AICRP page -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/
Seed-chain analysis lists Sushree among predominant toria varieties, contributing roughly 9.3%-40.6% in the cited seed-chain data (the range is across the listed varieties) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344668328_Analysis_of_seed_chain_and_its_implication_in_rapeseed-mustard_Brassica_spp_production_in_India
A private seed company product list includes SUSHREE among toria varieties. This is a commercial listing, not an NSC, state corporation, or SAU record -- https://www.indiaseeds.com/products.html
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or OUAT seed-sales listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Evidence is limited to Odisha's mid-central table land zone, from the on-farm trial above -- https://www.allresearchjournal.com/archives/2015/vol1issue9/PartB/1-8-120-423.pdf
No official notification or recommended-state list from the CSC or Seednet was found for this variety.

seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Less aphid infestation in comparison to check varieties.

heat.details: While heat tolerance in mustard introgression lines is mentioned in general contexts in ICAR reports, and SVJ-64 is listed among varieties when discussing abiotic stresses like heat, there is no explicit statement that SVJ-64 itself possesses high heat tolerance.

salinity.details: SVJ-64 is identified as tolerant to the combined stress of drought and salinity.

flood.details: No information specified.

disease_resistance.summary: SVJ-64 is listed as a variety that can control powdery mildew, implying resistance to this disease. Other general mentions of disease resistance in ICAR reports (e.g., Fusarium wilt, Alternaria leaf spot, white rust) are not explicitly attributed to SVJ-64.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. The PAU page above showed no TL 17 contact. Institute contact not verified from search results.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. No search returned state recommendation information for TL 17.

Limitations: The search tool's usage limit was reached during my checking pass, so I could not re-read the full text of the results for the exact string "TL 17" beyond the opening snippets I saw. The findings above are therefore based on visible snippets only. Before relying on this record, check the Seednet variety page (seednet.gov.in, Yellow Sarson/toria), the PAU Oilseeds section and its release notification, and KrishiKosh for TL 17 entries.

basic_info.institution: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya (BCKV), (West Bengal) and Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC)

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to TBM-143 in the searched sources. No mechanisms or tolerance rating were reported.

heat.details: A Zenodo study on salicylic acid and Indian mustard under terminal heat-stress conditions names TBM-143 as a studied genotype. The retrieved text reports only treatment effects on seed yield (seed yield was highest with 400 ppm salicylic acid under timely sowing), not TBM-143's heat tolerance level. No heat tolerance rating or mechanism was found.

salinity.details: The coastal trials at Kakdwip (a saline-zone station, BCKV Regional Research Station, Coastal Saline Zone) included TBM 143, but no salinity tolerance rating was reported. Yield performance in the coastal zone is recorded under agronomic_performance, not as a salinity tolerance result.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to TBM-143 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance evidence found for TBM-143 (searches for Alternaria blight, white rust, Sclerotinia and other diseases returned no record). Disease reaction field in the variety record: Not Specified.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistance to Plutella xylostella (diamondback moth): a reference cited in a ResearchGate paper on TBM-204 reports TBM 143 as superior in growth, yield components and seed yield, and as resistant to P. xylostella. This is secondhand. The retrieved text does not give the full Banerjee et al. (2023) citation, and the finding is not verified against a primary source. It is the only pest-related evidence found.

agronomic_details.yield: BCKV crop variety listing: seed yield of 14.0 q/ha (equivalent to 1,400 kg/ha). Coastal trial (Kakdwip, 2015-16): 1.80 t/ha, under a caveat that the 'TM 143' alias is unconfirmed. Coastal study (Kakdwip, 2018-2020): 1.29 t/ha. The variety record field 'average_yield' is given only as 'Kg/Ha' with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Only single-site coastal results (Kakdwip) and one multi-location BARC-BCKV trial, judged promising without reported stability statistics, were retrieved.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Coastal West Bengal (Kakdwip, Coastal Saline Zone) late-sown after paddy (early December sowing) in the 2015-16 trial, and the 2018-2020 coastal study. The digest recommends 150% RDF fertilizer for the coastal belt. Broader agro-climatic adaptation for West Bengal is not otherwise specified.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 152 cm; appressed two-chambered siliqua; yellow seed coat; bold seed; oil content 41.3% (BCKV crop variety listing). Coastal trial also reports highest test weight and seeds per siliqua for 'TM 143' (alias unconfirmed).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) BCKV crop variety listing: duration 104 days, plant height 152 cm, seed yield 14.0 q/ha, oil content 41.3%. (2) Coastal West Bengal, Kakdwip (BCKV Regional Research Station), 2015-16, late-sown after paddy: 'TM 143' gave the highest seed yield (1.80 t/ha) among eight cultivars, statistically at par with TM 204, and the highest test weight and seeds per siliqua. The page does not confirm that 'TM 143' is identical to TBM-143. (3) Kakdwip coastal study, 2018-2020: TBM 143 and Kranti were the top yielders at 1.29 and 1.28 t/ha respectively. (4) BARC-BCKV multi-location yield trial of Trombay Mustard in West Bengal: TM-204 and TM-143 judged promising; a release proposal was sent to the SVRC. (5) Terminal heat-stress study (salicylic acid, three sowing dates): TBM-143 included as a genotype; no tolerance rating reported.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under terminal heat-stress conditions, a Zenodo study on salicylic acid and Indian mustard names TBM-143 as a studied genotype, but the retrieved text reports only treatment effects on seed yield, not TBM-143's tolerance level. -- https://zenodo.org/records/18681400 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18681400)
- TBM 143 was reported as superior in growth, yield components and seed yield, and as resistant to the insect pest P. xylostella, in a reference cited in a ResearchGate paper on TBM-204. The retrieved text does not give the full Banerjee et al. (2023) citation, so this is secondhand. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- No evidence found for drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to TBM-143. The coastal trials at Kakdwip (a saline-zone station) included TBM 143, but no salinity tolerance rating was reported. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602

DISEASE AND PEST
- The P. xylostella (diamondback moth) resistance finding above is the only pest-related evidence found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- No evidence found for disease resistance (e.g., Alternaria blight, white rust, Sclerotinia) specific to TBM-143. Searches returned no such record.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- BCKV's crop variety listing gives TBM 143 a duration of 104 days, plant height of 152 cm, appressed two-chambered siliqua, yellow seed coat, bold seed, seed yield of 14.0 q/ha and oil content of 41.3%. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- Coastal West Bengal (Kakdwip, BCKV Regional Research Station, Coastal Saline Zone), 2015-16 trial: TM 143 gave the highest seed yield (1.80 t/ha) among eight cultivars, statistically at par with TM 204, under a late-sown (early December) schedule after paddy. The text also states TM 143 gave the highest test weight and seeds per siliqua. "TM 143" is a BARC gamma-mutant designation; the page does not state it is identical to TBM-143, so this is a likely alias to be confirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332653138_Selection_of_Rapeseed-mustard_Varieties_in_Coastal_Region_of_West_Bengal_A_Way_Forward_to_Rice-fallow_Intensification
- A 2018-2020 coastal study (Kakdwip) found TBM 143 and Kranti as the top yielders, at 1.29 and 1.28 t/ha respectively. The study recommends 150% RDF fertilizer for the coastal belt. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602
- BARC-BCKV multi-location yield trial of Trombay Mustard in West Bengal: TM-204 and TM-143 were judged promising, and a proposal was sent to the SVRC for release. -- https://bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/barc-bckv-programme-en
- Terminal heat stress: TBM-143 was used with salicylic acid treatments under three sowing dates; the paper reports seed yield was highest with 400 ppm under timely sowing. -- https://zenodo.org/records/18681400

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker, parentage or mutagenesis-lineage record specifically for TBM-143 was retrieved. The parentage field in the record is "Not specified", and the search did not resolve it. The BARC bulletin on Trombay crop varieties describes mutation and recombination breeding in general terms only. -- https://www.barc.gov.in/group/66_s246.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institutions for TBM-143, per the BCKV listing: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya (BCKV) with a BARC project, and the Department of Seed Science and Technology. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- BARC's Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division (NA&BTD) runs the Trombay crop-variety programme; mustard is one of its 12 crops. The bulletin does not name TBM-143 in the retrieved text. -- https://www.barc.gov.in/group/66_s246.pdf
- No breeder or scientist name for TBM-143 was found. Names appearing in TBM-204 literature (e.g., Dutta, A.; Rai, A.N.) belong to a different variety's paper and are not attributed here. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level only (no breeder contact found): Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal, PIN 741252. Phone and email not found in the retrieved text. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/Varieties-developed_nw.pdf
- Institute-level only: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), Trombay, Mumbai 400085, Maharashtra (postal code written with spaces in the source, "4 00 08 5"). Phone and email not found in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- BARC Director named in press coverage: Vivek Bhasin (institute head, not a breeder for this variety). -- https://www.deccanherald.com/india/maharashtra/barc-dedicates-8-new-trombay-crop-varieties-to-farmers-3308421
- No official email, phone, or contact page for the BCKV or BARC division was retrieved. -- (no URL)

PUBLICATIONS
- Dutta, A., Jambulkar, S.J., Rai, A.N., Bhujbal, S., Banerjee, H., Das, R., Dewanjee, S., Sarkar, S., Pramanik, M., and Mandal, S. (2019). Varietal and Fertilization Effects on Growth and Yield of Mustard under Coastal Environment. JISCAR (ICAR e-Journals) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not confirmed). Selection of Rapeseed-mustard Varieties in Coastal Region of West Bengal: A Way Forward to Rice-fallow Intensification. Journal not confirmed; BCKV Kakdwip trial 2015-16 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332653138_Selection_of_Rapeseed-mustard_Varieties_in_Coastal_Region_of_West_Bengal_A_Way_Forward

The only Srivilliputtur cotton pest note retrieved concerned cotton hybrid SVPR 1 (moderately resistant to jassid), which is a different variety and is discarded. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-srivilliputhur/varieties-released/

The Srivilliputtur station table retrieved lists other releases (SVPR 1 hybrid, 1991 SVPR 1 entry). Those rows are not TSH 387 and are discarded. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-srivilliputhur/varieties-released/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage, pedigree, or marker study for TSH 387 was retrieved. The parentage field is "Not specified" in the record and remains unverified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for TSH 387. The search confirmed only that Cotton Research Station, Srivilliputtur (TNAU) is the releasing centre for other cotton varieties, such as SVPR 4 and SVPR 6 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-srivilliputhur/varieties-released/. No breeder name was linked to TSH 387.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The retrieved text from the station's variety-release page contains no email, phone, or postal address. The station page is the only institute-level URL retrieved: https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-srivilliputhur/varieties-released/

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis naming TSH 387 was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. For the seednet name TS-38 under the crop heading "Indian Rapeseed and Mustard (Yellow Sarson)", the search returned a news item about a toria rapeseed variety TS-38 from Assam Agricultural University. This is a different crop and institution, so it is discarded -- https://ajmaliasacademy.in/ts-38-climate-resilient-rapeseed-variety/. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for TSH 387 or cotton TS-38 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The states listed in the record (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu) could not be confirmed from any retrieved page.

- Seednet name TS-38: the only hit is a rapeseed variety from Assam, so it is not this cotton variety.
