seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Medium tall, Narrow and dark green leaves, Tolerant to Head smut, sheath blight and brown spot, High grain yield.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The proposed culture TNAU 86, is tolerant to head smut, sheath blight and brown spot.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Tolerant to shoot fly

drought.details: A 2012-era summary table lists TNAU 86 as tolerant to drought. The digest gives no quantitative drought data, no degree of tolerance, and no mechanism. The level is medium because the tolerance is stated qualitatively only. The CSC adaptation record describes rainfed cultivation in both kharif and Rabi seasons, which is consistent with but does not prove drought tolerance.

heat.details: No evidence found in the digest for heat tolerance.

salinity.details: At seedling stage under imposed salinity at 50-200 mM, TNAU 86 gave the highest germination and salt-injury scores of five kodo millet varieties tested. It was one of two salinity-resistant entries. The level is high relative to the varieties tested; the digest gives no absolute threshold or mechanism.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest for flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Head smut: resistance listed in the small-millets summary table. Sheath blight: resistance listed in the same table. Brown spot: resistance listed in the same table. CSC ground-truth record also describes TNAU 86 as tolerant to head smut, sheath blight and brown spot. Leaf spot: No evidence found.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-specific resistance found for TNAU 86. Stem borer and leaf spot reactions: No evidence found. Shoot fly: the Recommended Package of Practices states that delayed sowing raises shoot fly incidence and advises timely sowing for the crop generally. This is a general crop management recommendation and is not evidence of TNAU 86 resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: grain 27.09 q/ha and fodder 56.00 q/ha. Small-millets summary table: 27-30 q/ha grain, which conflicts with a listed value of 1321 (units not stated, likely kg/ha) and needs checking against the original release notification. 2017-2020 multi-location trials: 3142 kg/ha grain yield (used as check for ATL 1).
agronomic_details.stability: Among the lowest MTSI scores across environments with CO 3, indicating relatively high stability in that comparison. Other stability measures: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed cultivation in both kharif and Rabi seasons (CSC record). Sowing before the second fortnight of July is recommended in the Package of Practices. Specific agro-climatic zones: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 95-110 days (summary source, units as given); 108-113 days in a trial table for TNAU 86
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium tall; narrow and dark green leaves (CSC record). Lodging absent and seed shattering present (PPV&FRA DUS descriptor scoring). DUS descriptor states for days to 50% flowering and panicle: details in the DUS source, values not given in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location trials 2017-2020: TNAU 86 recorded 3142 kg/ha grain yield and was used as the check for ATL 1. (2) Trial table: days to maturity 108-113 days. (3) Small-millets summary table: 27-30 q/ha grain yield, which conflicts with the 1321 value listed elsewhere. (4) Seedling salinity trial (50-200 mM): highest germination and salt-injury scores among five kodo varieties. (5) MTSI stability analysis: among the lowest scores across environments with CO 3. Trial site, season, and replication details: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE [name: TNAU 86 (CSC and Seednet both list TNAU 86)]
- Seedling salinity: TNAU 86 gave the highest germination and salt-injury scores of five kodo varieties at 50-200 mM, and it was one of two salinity-resistant entries -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389403775_PHYSIOLOGICAL_STUDY_OF_KODO_MILLET_UNDER_IMPOSED_SALINITY_STRESS_AT_SEEDLING_STAGE
- Drought: a 2012-era summary table lists TNAU 86 as tolerant to drought -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/367157080_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_ATL_1_A_high_yielding_Kodo_millet_variety (table entry also reproduced at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India)
- Heat, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST [name: TNAU 86]
- The same small-millets summary table lists resistance to head smut, sheath blight and brown spot -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Lodging is absent and seed shattering is present in the PPV&FRA DUS descriptor scoring for TNAU 86 -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/final-kodo-millet.pdf
- Shoot fly: delayed sowing raises shoot fly incidence, so timely sowing is advised for the crop generally -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf
- Stem borer, leaf spot, and other pest-specific reactions for TNAU 86: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS [name: TNAU 86]
- Maturity 95-110 days and grain yield listed as 1321 (units not stated; likely kg/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374549234_Revealing_the_biochemical_profile_and_antioxidant_activity_of_kodo_millet_Paspalum_scrobiculatum_L. The same kind of summary table gives 27-30 q/ha, which conflicts with 1321 kg/ha and needs checking against the original release notification -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Days to maturity in a trial table for TNAU 86 are 108-113 days -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/367157080_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_ATL_1_A_high_yielding_Kodo_millet_variety
- In 2017-2020 multi-location trials TNAU 86 recorded 3142 kg/ha grain yield, used as a check for ATL 1 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/367157080_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_ATL_1_A_high_yielding_Kodo_millet_variety
- Agronomy: seed rate 10 kg/ha for line sowing and 15 kg/ha for broadcasting; 40 kg N and 20 kg P2O5/ha -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf
- Sowing before the second fortnight of July is recommended -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf
- Stability: TNAU 86 had among the lowest MTSI scores across environments with CO 3 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13237-026-00680-4

GENETICS AND QTL [name: TNAU 86]
- Parentage: pure line selection from IPs 85 -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/02_Small_Millets.pdf
- DUS descriptor states for TNAU 86 (days to 50% flowering, panicle, lodging, shattering) -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/final-kodo-millet.pdf
- QTL or marker studies specific to TNAU 86: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION [name: TNAU 86]
- Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU). Named TNAU 86 breeder or lead scientist: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Lodging: the central/state release listing describes Bidhan Lentil 16 as erect and lodging resistant (name in evidence: "Bidhan Lentil 16") -- The listing marks the variety as erect with lodging resistance. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. The searches returned no page naming this variety for these stresses. The salinity-tolerance paper that came up (Frontiers, fgene.2026.1863296) is affiliated with BCKV but does not name Bidhan Lentil 16, so I excluded it.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The ICAR-IIPR MULLaRP rabi 2021-22 report has a Bidhan Lentil 16 entry that states the variety has resistance, but the extracted text cuts off before naming the disease. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No specific disease or pest resistance is confirmed. Several lentil disease-resistance pages were excluded because they do not name this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield and maturity: the central/state release listing gives 15-16 (yield unit not stated in the extract) and 109-132 days to maturity for Bidhan Lentil 16. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf ; the same figures appear in the MULLaRP report (Bidhan Lentil 16, BCKV, 2022, 15-16, 109-132, West Bengal, small seeded). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Suitability: the listing says it suits old and new alluvial zones. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Field trials of this variety: No evidence found. The BCKV trial pages that came up test Bidhan Lentil 15 and other genotypes, so I excluded them.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (from the supplied record, not verified by search): the cross is LL56 x L4710, with line C23E21 selected at F7. No search result names this cross for Bidhan Lentil 16.
- The MULLaRP report describes the variety as a small-seeded line developed from a cross, but the parent names are cut off. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya (BCKV), Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. A BCKV Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding paper (Roy et al.) on lentil disease resistance does not name this variety's breeder. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9896981/
- Note: C23E21 appears in a BCKV-ICARDA sowing-window paper as a pre-released genotype. That page does not name Bidhan Lentil 16, so I did not link them. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5086

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Institute contact: No email, phone, or postal address for BCKV or its Mohanpur station was found. The BCKV website domain appeared in results (https://bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/icarda-en), but the page showed no contact details.

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR-IIPR (2023). Progress report, MULLaRP rabi 2021-22 (All India Coordinated Research Project on MULLaRP). Report; author not stated. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Ministry of Agriculture, DPD (year not stated). Central released varieties of Lentil/Masoor in India. Government listing; author not stated. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming Bidhan Lentil 16 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The searches returned retail seed sellers and cover-crop sites for lentils generally, none naming Bidhan Lentil 16 or any NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, or BCKV seed sale. The MULLaRP report gives lentil breeder seed totals for all varieties, not this one.
- Seednet portal listing ("BIDHAN LENTIL-16", code A030917712): No evidence found. No Seednet page was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- West Bengal. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Year of release: the listing and the MULLaRP report both give 2022. The release date of 2022-06-17 in the record was not verified.

drought.details: A seed-priming study that sourced seed from ICAR-IARI describes IPL-316 as moderately tolerant to drought. The digest gives no field trial data for this claim, so the rating rests on a single secondary statement. Source-attribution discrepancy: the study's seed origin (ICAR-IARI, New Delhi) does not match the IIPR attribution. No mechanisms were reported.

heat.details: No evidence found. The searches returned nothing on heat tolerance for IPL-316.

salinity.details: The same seed-priming study describes IPL-316 as moderately tolerant to salinity. No field trial data are given, and no mechanisms were reported. The rating rests on a single secondary statement.

flood.details: No evidence found. The searches returned nothing on flood tolerance for IPL-316. A Pasighat (Arunachal Pradesh) foothill trial on residual moisture in rice fallows is reported under agronomic performance, but it does not address flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: tolerance reported by IIPR (potential yield and duration listing) and DPD (large-seed variety listing). Wilt-resistant/tolerant status is also listed in state advisory lists (Vikaspedia). Fusarium wilt: a Ratlam KVK demonstration promoted IPL-316 specifically for resistance to Fusarium wilt. Rust: tolerance reported by IIPR and DPD, and rust-resistant/tolerant status is listed in a crop protection advisory (Krishi Jagran) and a DPD disease control advisory. The sources state tolerance or resistance as a listing; no screening scores or resistance levels are given for either disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Aphid (Aphis craccivora): in a field screen, IPL-316 had the lowest mean population at 50% flowering (2.7 aphids/plant), against 13.5 aphids/plant on the highest-infested genotype. This indicates low aphid infestation relative to the screened genotypes, but the digest does not give the full genotype set or a formal resistance category. No other pest resistance was found.

agronomic_details.yield: IIPR listed potential yield of 18-20 q/ha. DPD listed 14-15 q/ha. Ratlam (Malwa, MP) cluster front-line demonstrations on 80 ha across 200 farms gave yield gains of 21.2% to 56.1% over farmers' practice. Bundelkhand (Lalitpur, UP) cluster demonstrations (2023-24) gave 1670 kg/ha under the package versus 1280 kg/ha under farmers' practice (31% gain). Prayagraj (SHUATS, UP) rabi 2019 trial gave a maximum seed yield of 1.52 t/ha under thiourea 1000 ppm plus iron 100 ppm. Pasighat (Arunachal Pradesh) 2015-17 gave 11.03 q/ha, the highest among nine varieties.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Results come from differing locations, years and management packages, so no cross-environment stability analysis is available.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended states (Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh) per the input record, with the qualifier 'parts of Rajasthan and Bundelkhand of Uttar Pradesh'. Input adaptation is under normal sown conditions. Field evidence includes the Malwa (MP), Bundelkhand (UP), Prayagraj (UP) and Pasighat (Arunachal Pradesh, foothill residual moisture in rice fallows) trials. A Nepal trial is outside India and is not used for Indian recommendations.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 102-112 days (IIPR listing). 110-115 days (DPD listing). 116 days to maturity (Pasighat trial, 2015-17). Input record: Not specified.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: DPD lists IPL-316 as a large-seeded variety, with 100-seed weight of 3.3 g in one table and 3.1 g in another. Herbicide response: IPL 316 showed high phytotoxicity (visual score about 6-7) to imazethapyr across 2020-21 to 2024-25 and is classed as susceptible to that post-emergence herbicide. Agroforestry study (Melia dubia, Bundelkhand): IPL 316 had higher seed N, K, Ca, Cu and Zn than L 4727. Input record: morphological characteristics Not specified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Ratlam (Malwa, MP) cluster front-line demonstrations, 80 ha, 200 farms: yield gains of 21.2% to 56.1% over farmers' practice. (2) Bundelkhand (Lalitpur, UP) cluster demonstrations, 2023-24: 1670 kg/ha versus 1280 kg/ha (31% gain). (3) Prayagraj (SHUATS, UP) bioregulator and micronutrient trial, rabi 2019: maximum seed yield 1.52 t/ha under thiourea 1000 ppm plus iron 100 ppm. (4) Pasighat (Arunachal Pradesh) foothill trial, 2015-17: 11.03 q/ha, highest of nine varieties, 116 days to maturity. (5) Kota genetic variability study (AICRP on MULLaRP): IPL-316 used as a check among 155 genotypes; no yield values captured. (6) Agroforestry study (Melia dubia, Bundelkhand): higher seed N, K, Ca, Cu and Zn than L 4727. (7) Imazethapyr post-emergence screen, 2020-21 to 2024-25: high phytotoxicity (score about 6-7), classed as susceptible. (8) Aphid field screen: lowest mean population of 2.7 aphids/plant at 50% flowering. (9) Nepal trial, IPL 316 as one of three genotypes with seed-rate and fertilizer factors: outside India, not used for Indian recommendations; no yield values captured in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: IPL-316 (lentil, Lens culinaris)

Name check: variety_name "IPL-316" and seednet_variety_name "IPL-316" were both searched. The IIPR and DPD sources write it as "IPL 316", and I treated these as the same name. No Seednet portal page for this variety was returned, so no Seednet evidence is listed. Release year: the input says NaT, but IIPR and DPD both record 2013 (CVRC). The CSC release minutes were not retrieved, so that year is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerance to wilt and rust; the listed potential yield is 18-20 q/ha and the duration is 102-112 days -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/
Tolerance to wilt and rust, large seed (3.3 g per 100 seeds in one table, 3.1 g in another), 110-115 days, 14-15 q/ha -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
Described as moderately tolerant to drought and salinity, as stated by a seed-priming study that sourced the seed from ICAR-IARI; no field trial data are given -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-39380-z
Imazethapyr (post-emergence herbicide) screening: IPL 316 showed high phytotoxicity (visual score about 6-7) across 2020-21 to 2024-25, so it is classed as susceptible to that herbicide -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/1712/1066/3828
Heat, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned nothing on these for IPL-316.

DISEASE AND PEST
Recommended as wilt-resistant/tolerant and as rust-resistant/tolerant in state advisory lists -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/lentil-rabi?lgn=en
Listed among wilt-resistant/tolerant and rust-resistant/tolerant varieties in a crop protection advisory -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/check-out-state-wise-suggested-varieties-of-lentil/
Listed as a tolerant/resistant variety in a disease control advisory -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF
Aphid (Aphis craccivora) field screen: IPL-316 had the lowest mean population (2.7 aphids/plant) at 50% flowering, against 13.5 on the highest genotype -- https://indianjournals.com/article/pa-18-1-023
Fusarium wilt: a Ratlam KVK demonstration promoted IPL-316 specifically for resistance to Fusarium wilt -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5482

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Ratlam (Malwa, MP) cluster front-line demonstrations on 80 ha across 200 farms: yield gains of 21.2% to 56.1% over farmers' practice -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5482
Bundelkhand (Lalitpur, UP) cluster demonstrations, 2023-24: 1670 kg/ha under the package versus 1280 kg/ha under farmers' practice, a 31% gain -- https://journaljsrr.com/index.php/JSRR/article/view/3984
Prayagraj (SHUATS, UP) bioregulator and micronutrient trial, rabi 2019: maximum seed yield of 1.52 t/ha under thiourea 1000 ppm plus iron 100 ppm -- http://www.ijcmas.com/9-12-2020/Pavan%20Ganesh,%20et%20al.pdf
Pasighat, Arunachal Pradesh (foothill, residual moisture in rice fallows), 2015-17: 11.03 q/ha, the highest yield among nine varieties, with 116 days to maturity -- https://www.academia.edu/87483011/Evaluation_of_lentil_varieties_under_foot_hill_of_north_east_agro_ecological_region_of_India
Kota genetic variability study (AICRP on MULLaRP, Kota): IPL-316 used as a check among 155 genotypes; no yield values captured -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=19277&vol=9-9-2020&SNo=259
Agroforestry (Melia dubia, Bundelkhand): IPL 316 had higher seed N, K, Ca, Cu and Zn than L 4727 -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/agronomy/articles/10.3389/fagro.2025.1675259/full
Nepal trial (IPL 316 as one of three genotypes with seed-rate and fertilizer factors): this is outside India, so it is not used for Indian recommendations -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364078647_Increasing_the_Productivity_of_Lentil_through_Agronomic_Interventions_in_Nepal

GENETICS AND QTL
QTL, marker or pedigree/parentage data for IPL-316: No evidence found. The only genetics-adjacent result was the imazethapyr tolerance screen (see Stress Tolerance). Parentage: not specified in the input, and no source gave it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur, which lists IPL 316 among its varieties, with release in 2013 (CVRC) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/
Institute mandate: development of high-yielding varieties and production of breeder seed; origin in the AICPIP at IARI in 1966 and restructuring in 1993 -- https://www.devex.com/organizations/indian-institute-of-pulses-research-155999
Discrepancy: a 2026 seed-priming study states that IPL-316 seed was obtained from ICAR-IARI, New Delhi, which does not match the IIPR attribution -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-39380-z
Lead breeder name: No evidence found for IPL-316. The IIPR "developed by" name found for IPL 225 (Dr Jitendra Kumar) and IPL 534 is for other varieties and is discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute address (institute-level, no breeder contact found): ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur 208 024 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
Institute contact page: https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/ (the page lists varieties only; no email or phone was captured)
Breeder email/phone for IPL-316: No evidence found.

stress_confirmation_note: The drought and salinity source study attributes IPL-316 to ICAR-IARI seed origin, which conflicts with the IIPR institution on record and should be verified before relying on those ratings.

drought.basis: Seed-priming study, nature.com s41598-026-39380-z, names IPL-316 as moderately drought tolerant. No official CSC/Seednet tolerance statement; CSC text concerns only a photograph.
drought.label: Single source

heat.basis: No heat tolerance evidence for IPL-316. Snippet on heat and drought stresses is generic, crop-level, and not attributed to this variety.
heat.label: Not confirmed

salinity.basis: Same seed-priming study (nature.com s41598-026-39380-z) names IPL-316 as moderately salinity tolerant. Counted once as the same document. No official tolerance statement.
salinity.label: Single source

flood.basis: No flood tolerance evidence. Pasighat residual-moisture trial does not address flood tolerance and is not counted.
flood.label: Not confirmed

submergence.basis: No submergence tolerance evidence found for IPL-316.
submergence.label: Not confirmed

disease_resistance.research_summary: Wilt: tolerance reported by IIPR (potential yield and duration listing) and DPD (large-seed variety listing). Wilt-resistant/tolerant status is also listed in state advisory lists (Vikaspedia). Fusarium wilt: a Ratlam KVK demonstration promoted IPL-316 specifically for resistance to Fusarium wilt. Rust: tolerance reported by IIPR and DPD, and rust-resistant/tolerant status is listed in a crop protection advisory (Krishi Jagran) and a DPD disease control advisory. The sources state tolerance or resistance as a listing; no screening scores or resistance levels are given for either disease.

drought.details: No evidence found for IPL 220 specifically. The digest cites lentil-wide QTL hotspot studies (a seedling/root-trait RIL study) that are not tied to this variety, so they do not establish drought tolerance for IPL 220.

heat.details: No evidence found for IPL 220 specifically. A general lentil drought/heat cross-tolerance study exists but does not include IPL 220.

salinity.details: No evidence found for IPL 220 specifically.

flood.details: No evidence found.

disease_resistance.summary: Rust: resistant (reported in the Dalhangyan Manch success story and the MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report). Fusarium wilt: resistant (DPD table and MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report; the release report describes resistance to wilt generally, so the specific Fusarium wilt claim is not fully confirmed). Stemphylium blight: high level of resistance, described as an emerging disease (Dalhangyan Manch success story).

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for IPL 220 specifically. No pest resistance is reported in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield reported as 13.8 q/ha (approximately 1,380 kg/ha). Potential yield reported as 15-20 q/ha (IIPR); the DPD table lists 14-18 q/ha. The original record's unit (Kg/Ha) is consistent with the converted average.
agronomic_details.stability: unknown. No multi-environment stability data are reported in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the North East Plain Zone (NEPZ): eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Assam and West Bengal. Pure-line variety.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 120-125 days per IIPR; 119-122 days per the DPD table.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Small seeded (2.4 g per 100 seeds); brown seed coat with orange cotyledons; reported high Zn and Fe. Protein 25.8%, comparable to checks PL 406 and HUL-57. Biofortification values conflict between sources (IIPR: Fe 94 mg/kg, Zn 57 mg/kg, Se 630 µg/kg; review: Fe 73 ppm, Zn 51 ppm) and are unverified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Yield superiority of 8.93% over the HUL 57 check and 11.13% over the KLS-218 check. Pedigree: three-way cross (DPL 44 x DPL 62) x DPL 58, developed by hybridization and pedigree selection.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No evidence found for IPL 220 specifically. The lentil-wide mapping studies cited under drought are for other populations.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No evidence found in the digest.

TOPIC: Breeder/institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur; released 2018 by CVRC -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/

TOPIC: Recommended states: Eastern UP, Bihar, Assam and West Bengal, listed under the North East Plain Zone (NEPZ) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf ; https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
TOPIC: Yield (average/trials): Average yield reported as 13.8 q/ha -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6366255/
TOPIC: Yield (potential/range): Potential yield 15-20 q/ha; DPD table lists 14-18 q/ha -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/ ; https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
TOPIC: Yield (comparison trials): Yield superiority of 8.93% over HUL 57 and 11.13% over KLS-218 checks -- https://dalhangyanmanch.res.in/eng/success_story.php
TOPIC: Maturity/duration: 120-125 days per IIPR; 119-122 days per DPD table -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/ ; https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
TOPIC: Seed traits: Small seeded (2.4 g/100 seeds), brown seed coat with orange cotyledons, high Zn and Fe -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/

disease_resistance.research_summary: Rust: resistant (reported in the Dalhangyan Manch success story and the MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report). Fusarium wilt: resistant (DPD table and MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report; the release report describes resistance to wilt generally, so the specific Fusarium wilt claim is not fully confirmed). Stemphylium blight: high level of resistance, described as an emerging disease (Dalhangyan Manch success story).

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur   (Uttar Pradesh)
seednet_fields.Parentage: (DPL 44 x DPL 62) x DPL-58. 1.	DPL 44: Derivative of Precoz, medium seeded, medium maturity, brown seeded with red cotyledon and resistant to rust. 2.	DPL 62: Large seeded, light green foliage, high yielding, resistant to rust and wilt. 3.	DPL 58: Large seeded, yellow cotyledons, dark green foliage, wilt resistance.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Large growing areas of Uttar Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Suitable for normal sown conditions with already recommended agronomic practices.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Semi-tall and semi spreading growth habit, large seeded, orange cotyledon, rudimentary tendril, rust and wilt resistance, violet flower, oval leaf shape, 2 pods/pedunmcle, 2 seeds/pod, brown dotted and globose or lens-shape (flattened-round) seed color and shape, orange cotyledon color, 2.1g/100 seed weight.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistance to rust and tolerance to wilt.

drought.details: No drought evidence found for IPL 225 in searched sources. Digest notes that only general lentil varieties were returned by searches, which were discarded as different varieties.

heat.details: No heat-tolerance evidence found for IPL 225. The digest mentions heat-tolerance specialisation only as a description of the lead breeder (Dr. Jitendra Kumar), which is not a varietal trait and is not used as evidence of variety tolerance.

salinity.details: No salinity evidence found for IPL 225 in searched sources.

flood.details: No flood evidence found for IPL 225 in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Rust: resistance recorded (MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report; DPD central/state release table lists rust and wilt tolerance; IIPR varieties page describes the variety as highly resistant to rust and Fusarium wilt). Fusarium wilt: resistance recorded (MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 breeder-seed/variety annexure table; IIPR varieties page; DPD table). The brief's Disease Reaction field reads 'Not Specified', which conflicts with these sources. Parent-level traits (DPL 44 rust resistance, DPL 62 rust and wilt resistance, DPL 58 wilt resistance) come from the brief and were not independently confirmed by a search result.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No insect pest resistance evidence (pod borer, aphid, leaf miner or other) was found for IPL 225. Brief states Pest Reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: 10-11 q/ha (MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report; DPD table; brief average yield '10-11 q/ha. Kg/Ha'). Potential yield 12-14 q/ha (iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/ and IIPR varieties page).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data for IPL 225 was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for timely-sown conditions (IIPR varieties page; DPD table) in Uttar Pradesh. Brief describes suitability for normal sown conditions with recommended agronomic practices and large growing areas of Uttar Pradesh. The sources do not give agro-climatic zone details beyond Uttar Pradesh.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 105 To 133Days (brief and DPD table). Other sources: 105-120 days (MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22) and 120-125 days (IIPR varieties page).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Small seeded (MULLaRP; IIPR varieties page); seed size 2.1 g/100 seeds; brown dotted seed coat; red cotyledons (iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/ and IIPR varieties page). Brief lists morphological characteristics as 'Na'. Brief lists dark green foliage and yellow cotyledons for DPL 58 parent only, not IPL 225.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location or on-farm trial results specific to IPL 225 were found. The MULLaRP report describes zonal trial data only in generic terms without IPL 225 figures. The ResearchGate/ICAR participatory-trial paper names JL-1, not IPL 225, and was discarded. The only yield values for IPL 225 are the variety-description figures listed under yield (10-11 q/ha and 12-14 q/ha), which are not trial summaries.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No SNP, SSR or other marker data for IPL 225 was found. Pedigree (not a marker): three-way cross (DPL 44 x DPL 62) x DPL 58.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL or effect data for IPL 225 was found.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. No genes or pathways were identified for IPL 225. Parent descriptions from the brief (unconfirmed by search): DPL 44 derivative of Precoz, medium seeded, medium maturity, brown seeded with red cotyledon, rust resistant; DPL 62 large seeded, light green foliage, high yielding, rust and wilt resistant; DPL 58 large seeded, yellow cotyledons, dark green foliage, wilt resistance.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistance to rust and wilt is recorded for IPL 225 (no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Highly resistant to rust and Fusarium wilt, with suitability for timely-sown conditions -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/research-achievements/ (search result, IIPR "Title of the Research & Technologies" table; URL as returned: https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/)
Rust and wilt tolerance listed in the central/state release table -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
Abiotic stress tolerance (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence): No evidence found for IPL 225. Searches returned only general lentil varieties (PSL 19 salt tolerance, Kota Masoor 1 drought/heat) which are different varieties and are discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to wilt and rust disease -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Resistant to Fusarium wilt and rust -- same URL (MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 breeder-seed/variety annexure table)
Insect pest resistance (pod borer, aphid, leaf miner, etc.): No evidence found for IPL 225. The pod-borer/aphid/leaf-miner data returned relates to LL 1373, which is a different variety and is discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity 105-120 days, average yield 10-11 q/ha, small seeded -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Maturity 105-133 days, yield 10-11 q/ha, timely sown, Uttar Pradesh -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
Potential yield 12-14 q/ha, duration 105-133 days, seed size 2.1 g/100 seeds, brown dotted seed coat, red cotyledons -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/
Maturity 120-125 days, yield 12-14 q/ha, small seeded, brown dotted seed coat, red cotyledons, timely-sown -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
Multi-location or on-farm trial results specific to IPL 225: No evidence found. The MULLaRP report describes zonal trial data generically without IPL 225 figures; the ResearchGate/ICAR participatory-trial paper names JL-1, not IPL 225 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309041977_Improving_lentil_Lens_culinaris_productivity_and_profitability_through_farmer_participatory_action_research_in_India (discarded)

GENETICS AND QTL
Pedigree: three-way cross (DPL 44 x DPL 62) x DPL 58 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Parent descriptions (DPL 44, DPL 62, DPL 58 traits) were supplied in the brief and not independently confirmed by a search result.
QTL, marker-assisted or genomic studies on IPL 225: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur, Crop Improvement Division -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
Lead breeder: Dr. Jitendra Kumar, Principal Scientist (Plant Breeding), listed as the developer of IPL 225 with lentil breeding and heat-tolerance specialisation -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/ and https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/
Institution history (formerly AICPIP at IARI, then Project Directorate (Pulses), then Directorate of Pulses Research, then IIPR in 1993) -- https://genetools.iari.res.in/iipr-page.html
Co-workers on the lentil programme (C.P. Nath, Narendra Kumar, G.P. Dixit) are named in a 2019 paper, but no source ties them to IPL 225 specifically -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/1712/1066/3828 (not attributed to this variety)

CONTACT DETAILS
Dr. Jitendra Kumar, Principal Scientist -- phone 9455510016, email jitendra73@gmail.com -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/ (this is a personal-domain address; no official ICAR email for this scientist was found)
Dr. Jitendra Kumar, Principal Scientist (Plant Breeding), email jitendra73@gmail.com -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/
Institute-level contact: director.iipr@icar.gov.in; phone 0512-2580986 -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/
Institute-level contact (older directory page): Director Dr. Bansa Singh, Kanpur; phone 91-512-2580995, 2580994, 2580986; fax 91-512-2580992; email director.iipr@icar.gov.in -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/icar-indian-institute-pulses-research
Note: a 2023 social-media post names Dr. Girish Prasad Dixit as Director from 22.02.2023, which conflicts with the older directory -- https://x.com/icar_iipr?lang=en
Postal address: Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh 208024 -- https://collegedunia.com/college/6642-indian-institute-of-pulses-research-iipr-kanpur (third-party aggregator; not an official page)
Institute website: https://iipr.icar.gov.in/ (also https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/)

PUBLICATIONS
No peer-reviewed paper on IPL 225 was found in the search results.
Authors not stated (2023). MULLaRP Project Coordinator's Report, Rabi 2021-22 (AICRP/ICAR annual report, which includes the IPL 225 variety description). Report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Authors not stated (2021). Central released varieties of lentil (Masoor) in India, DPD table (IPL 225 listed as 2021). Report -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
Nath, C.P., Kumar, N., Kumar, J., Dixit, G.P. (year not confirmed). Tolerant genotypes of lentil (Lens culinaris Medik.) identified for imazethapyr as a post-emergence application. Journal of Food Legumes -- DOI 10.53550/jfl.v38.i2.264 (the snippet does not name IPL 225; not attributed to this variety)
Breeder-seed production data for lentil (857.36 q produced against 547.44 q indent for 45 indented varieties in Rabi 2021-22) is reported in the MULLaRP report, but IPL 225 is not singled out -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for IPL 225 at National Seeds Corporation, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The search returned only non-Indian retail lentil sellers, which are discarded. The IIPR site references breeder-seed production in general terms -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/research-achievements/
No Seednet (seednet.gov.in) page for IPL 225 was returned by any search. The Seednet name and CSC name are the same ("IPL 225"), but this was not confirmed on Seednet.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Uttar Pradesh (whole state, timely-sown conditions) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/ and https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Uttar Pradesh, timely sown, listed under state-released varieties -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
Release year: 2020 (SVRC Uttar Pradesh, per https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/ and the MULLaRP report) versus 2021 (per the DPD table and the IIPR achievements page). The brief's 2020-11-09 date matches the 2020 sources; no CSC notification number was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Special characters listed for IPL 526 include tolerance to wilt and rust diseases -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/ (name and source checked; the same page is also indexed as icar-iipr.org.in/varity/)
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for IPL 526. The drought study on recombinant inbred lines (https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/view/2478) uses a cross of IPL 98/193 and EC 208362, not IPL 526. The salinity trial report (https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5681) concerns LH 17-19.

DISEASE AND PEST
Rust and wilt tolerance is reported in the DPD central-release table, which lists IPL 526 as tolerance to rust and wilt -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
The same DPD document also gives the rust and wilt entry in a second table -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
Pest resistance (pod borer, aphid, leaf miner): No evidence found for IPL 526.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Potential yield is given as 10-15 q/ha with duration of 105-112 days -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity/ (conflict: the DPD table lists 7-9 q/ha and 97-128 days -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf)
Seed quality: IPL 526 ranks second in thousand-seed mass among the varieties tested, behind IPL 534 -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2949824426000807
Economic impact: the IIPR outreach section lists IPL 526 among lentil varieties under an economic-impact study on climate-resilient agriculture, with an assumed adoption level of 3 percent -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/research-achievements/ (URL taken from search index as https://www-icar--iipr-org-in.translate.goog/research-achievements/?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc)
Field-trial or multi-location yield data specific to IPL 526: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Pedigree: the MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report lists IPL 526 with the cross DPL 62 x DPL 58 in a table row (this is a table layout reading, so the link to IPL 526 is by row) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Line x tester study: IPL 526 was one of fifteen lines, and the cross IPL 526 x Sehore 74-03 showed positive significant specific combining ability effects for several traits -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5681
QTL or marker studies on IPL 526: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur. The DPD table and the MULLaRP report both list IIPR, Kanpur as the originating centre -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Institute-level attribution: the ICAR-IIPR foundation-day report lists IPL 526 among lentil varieties the institute developed -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/10517
Lead breeder name: No evidence found for IPL 526. Institute-level sources only.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute email (ICAR portal listing): director.iipr@icar.gov.in, listed under Contact Address: Kanpur -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/icar-indian-institute-pulses-research (this page names Dr Bansa Singh as Director; the 2017 foundation-day report names Dr N.P. Singh as Director, so the listing may be outdated)
Institute website: iipr.icar.gov.in (per the Wikipedia entry -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Pulses_Research)
Postal address: only "Kanpur" appears in the retrieved text. No full postal address or breeder phone number was found.

PUBLICATIONS
Sharma, A.K.; Kumar, J.; Singh, P.K.; Sen Gupta, D.; Singh, M.; Dixit, G.P. (year not shown in retrieved text). Characterization of recombinant inbred lines for physiological and yield traits under drought conditions in lentil. Journal of Food Legumes -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/view/2478 (This paper does not concern IPL 526; it is listed only to record that it was excluded.)
Note: the Sharma paper above is excluded from the evidence for this variety and is not a publication on IPL 526.
Line x tester genetic analysis paper (authors and year not shown in the retrieved text; Legume Research listing) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5681
Screening of selected Indian lentil varieties for physical, nutritional and cooking characteristics (authors and year not shown in the retrieved text; ScienceDirect) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2949824426000807
Dixit, G.P.; Katiyar, P.K.; Singh, B.B. (2011). Characterization of lentil (Lens culinaris Medik.) varieties based on morphological traits. Agris record (journal not shown) -- https://agris.fao.org/search/ru/records/65df8e4db766d82b18025f9d (IPL 526 is not named in the retrieved text; excluded.)

drought.details: The 2020 Journal of Oilseeds Research paper reports tolerance to moisture stress for JLS-66 and states it was released for rainfed situations in Madhya Pradesh. The digest gives no graded scale, so 'medium' reflects a qualitative tolerance statement only, with no quantitative stress data. Rainfed adaptation is supported by the same paper.

heat.details: The 2020 Journal of Oilseeds Research paper reports tolerance to high temperature stress for JLS-66. The digest gives no graded scale or quantitative heat data, so the level reflects a qualitative statement only.

salinity.details: No evidence found for JLS-66 specifically. The PMC review lists the variety only in an irrigated/rainfed variety table with no stress data.

flood.details: No evidence found for JLS-66 specifically. The PMC review lists the variety only in an irrigated/rainfed variety table with no stress data.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistance to major diseases is stated in the 2020 paper (no named diseases). The DOD table lists resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew and wilt, with bud fly marked 'Mod.' (moderate). The AICRP page lists moderate resistance to powdery mildew and moderate susceptibility to Alternaria blight. This conflicts with the DOD row for Alternaria blight and is unresolved. Rust: No evidence found for JLS-66.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistance to bud fly, described as the most damaging pest, is stated in the 2020 paper. The DOD table lists bud fly as moderate ('Mod.'). The AICRP page lists moderate resistance to bud fly. Capsule borer: No evidence found for JLS-66.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed situations in Madhya Pradesh (2020 paper). Suitability for intercropping with pulses (AICRP page). Zone III (Bundelkhand in UP, Rajasthan and MP) was the trial zone; this is not confirmed as the notified recommendation. The PMC review lists the variety among irrigated-condition varieties with no yield data.

A castor-paper snippet reports rainfed Alfisol trial data for linseed varieties, but JLS-66 is not reported in those figures. No separate irrigated trial yield data found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JLS-66 (linseed)

Name note: The CSC release name is JLS-66 and the Seednet name is also JLS-66, with variety code SLS 66. Seednet's crop field says "LENTIL (MASUR)", but every linseed source found names JLS-66 as a linseed variety. I found no Seednet page for JLS-66 under any crop, so all findings below refer to the linseed variety. Release year conflicts across sources: the input says 2011-06-28, the AICRP page says 2018, and a DOD row says 2010 for "Jawahar Linseed-66 (SLS-66)" released at Hoshangabad.

STRESS TOLERANCE
-- The 2020 Journal of Oilseeds Research paper reports tolerance to moisture stress and high temperature stress for JLS-66 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- Rainfed adaptation is stated for the variety in the same paper, which says it was released for rainfed situations in Madhya Pradesh -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- Suitability for intercropping with pulses is listed on the AICRP linseed page -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
-- Flood, submergence, salinity and heat-specific tolerance: No evidence found for JLS-66 specifically (the PMC review lists it only in an irrigated/rainfed variety table, with no stress data) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

DISEASE AND PEST
-- Paper states resistance to major diseases and to bud fly, the most damaging pest -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- DOD table: resistant to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew, wilt and bud fly (marked "Mod.", i.e. moderate) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
-- AICRP page: moderately resistant to powdery mildew and bud fly, moderately susceptible to Alternaria blight. This conflicts with the DOD row for Alternaria blight -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
-- Rust and capsule borer: No evidence found for JLS-66

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
-- Maturity of about 114 days, seed yield about 1200 kg/ha, and 42.85% drying oil -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- A second set of figures in the search snippet (104 days, 849 kg/ha, 35.67% oil) is not clearly attributed to JLS-66 in the snippet, so I have not used it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378072674_Jawahar_Linseed_Sagar-66_JLS-66_Development_and_dissemination_of_newly_developed_linseed_variety_for_nutritional_security_of_India_SAGAR-66_JLS-66_DEVELOPMENT_OF_NEW_LINSEED_VARIETY_FOR_NUTRITIONAL_SE
-- All India coordinated trials (zone III, including Bundelkhand in UP, Rajasthan and MP): seed yield 10.8 to 20.97% above comparison varieties, and oil yield 16.03 to 37.80% above them. Comparators are JLS-67, NL-97, JLS-9 and T-397 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- Rainfed Madhya Pradesh trial trend: the castor-paper snippet reports rainfed Alfisol performance data for linseed varieties, but JLS-66 is not reported in trial figures there -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353769937_Performance_of_elite_castor_Ricinus_communis_L_hybrids_and_varieties_under_rainfed_Alfisols
-- Irrigated-condition performance: the PMC review lists JLS66 among irrigated-condition varieties, but gives no yield data -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

GENETICS AND QTL
-- No evidence found for QTL, marker, parentage or pedigree studies naming JLS-66. The PMC/MDPI review lists JLS66 only in variety tables -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4425/14/7/1461
-- Parentage: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
-- Developers named in the paper: Devendra K. Payasi and M. P. Dubey, AICRP on Linseed, Regional Agricultural Research Station, JNKVV, Sagar 470002, Madhya Pradesh -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- Developing institution: Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur, via the AICRP linseed centre at Sagar -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- Released centre listed as Sagar on the DOD table, and as Hoshangabad for the 2010 row -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
-- The ICAR-IIOR linseed breeder page and the Nagpur AICRP page are about other linseed programmes and are not linked to JLS-66, so I did not use them

CONTACT DETAILS
-- Devendra K. Payasi (AICRP Linseed, RARS Sagar): email dpayasi@gmail.com, as printed in an affiliation of a related review -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
-- M. P. Dubey (AICRP Linseed, RARS Sagar): no direct contact found for this person. A JNKVV telephone directory lists a Dr. M. P. Dubey, phone 9425620205, as Nodal Officer at Khurai, which is a different role. I have not attributed it to this breeder -- https://www.jnkvv.org/public/file/1756984461.TelephoneDirectory.pdf
-- Directorate of Farms, JNKVV (breeder seed production): Dr. V. K. Yadav, Director, mobile 8770867088, email seeds.jnkvv@gmail.com -- https://www.jnkvv.org/about-directorate-details/directorate-of-farms
-- JNKVV postal address: Krishinagar, Adhartal, Jabalpur 482004 (M.P.), India -- https://www.jnkvv.org/contact-us
-- Institute contact page (Vice Chancellor and office directory): https://www.jnkvv.org/contact-us
-- Postal address for RARS Sagar: Regional Agricultural Research Station, JNKVV, Sagar 470002, Madhya Pradesh -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376

PUBLICATIONS
-- Payasi, D. K. and Dubey, M. P. (2020). Jawahar Linseed Sagar-66 (JLS-66): Development and dissemination of newly developed linseed variety for nutritional security of India. Journal of Oilseeds Research 37(1) -- https://doi.org/10.56739/jor.v37i1.136376
-- Chauhan, S. and co-authors (2023). Molecular Advances to Combat Different Biotic and Abiotic Stresses in Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.): A Comprehensive Review. Genes 14(7) -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4425/14/7/1461 (JLS66 appears only in variety tables; full author list not retrieved, so I have not listed it as a study of JLS-66)
-- Conference papers, AICRP annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, and field-trial reports specific to JLS-66: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
-- In the 2020-21 breeder seed indent for linseed, JLS 66 is named as contributing about 7.5% of the indent -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353769937_Performance_of_elite_castor_Ricinus_communis_L_hybrids_and_varieties_under_rainfed_Alfisols (this is a castor paper that quotes seed-chain data for linseed; treat as indicative)
-- JNKVV Directorate of Farms handles breeder seed production under the national seed programme -- https://www.jnkvv.org/about-directorate-details/directorate-of-farms
-- Seednet listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU sales, or private dealers: No evidence found for JLS-66 in the search results

RECOMMENDED STATES
-- Madhya Pradesh, rainfed state release -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
-- Madhya Pradesh, rainfed areas (2010 row, Hoshangabad) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
-- Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, KNK and Odisha are listed against the JLS-66 row of a DOD table. This conflicts with the MP-only entries and needs checking against the gazette notification -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
-- Zone III (Bundelkhand, UP, Rajasthan, MP) appears as the trial zone, not confirmed as the notified recommendation -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Searches used: 4 of 4 allowed. The third search (research/publications) returned mostly off-topic hits, and the fourth (seed availability) returned only foreign retail listings, so several headings are thin. Both name fields are "LL 1613", so the evidence applies to the same name under both the CSC and Seednet headings. I did not query the Seednet portal directly, so no Seednet listing is confirmed.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE
No LL 1613-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found in the search results. -- No evidence found
Seed-size context: the ICAR-IIPR report lists LL 1613 as a small-seeded AVT-2 genotype alongside LL 1373, but the captured text is truncated before any stress data. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Unattributed disease note: the PAU 2022 annual report says a lentil variety is resistant to red leaf spot and moderately resistant to zonate leaf spot diseases. The captured text does not name the variety, so this may not refer to LL 1613. -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
The DPD release table lists LL 1613 under lentil release data with no disease entry in the captured row. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
LL 1613, released 2023, PAU Ludhiana, NWPZ (HR, PN, UP, UK, DL, RJ), irrigated condition; yield 16-17 and days 114-145 as shown in the table (the column order is ambiguous in the extraction, so verify before use). -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
Trial data: the ICAR-IIPR Rabi 2021-22 report lists LL 1613 among entries with numeric values (1653, 1792, 1467, 1617, 14.27, 23.72), but the captured text does not label these columns, so their meaning is unverified. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Agronomy: the same report mentions AVT-2 small-seeded genotypes LL 1373 and LL 1613 under sowing-date work, but the sowing-date results are cut off. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No LL 1613 QTL, marker or parentage-validation study found. The parentage "LL 1112 x PL 02-6" is from the input record only, not from any search result. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: PAU, Ludhiana per the DPD table. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
Release: LL 1613 is an open pollinated variety of lentil recommended for sale in Haryana, Punjab, Northern Rajasthan, Plains of Uttarakhand, Delhi, Western Uttar Pradesh and part of Jammu and Kashmir. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/lentil-variety-ll-1613/
Lead breeder name(s): not found in any result. -- No evidence found
Institute station: PAU Ludhiana is the developing institution; the specific breeding station is not stated in the results. -- No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder: none found. -- No evidence found
Institute-level: the PAU website is listed as www.pau.edu, Ludhiana, Punjab, with no email, phone or postal address in the results. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Agricultural_University
Verification needed: the official PAU email, phone and postal address, and the Department of Plant Breeding contact page, must be taken from the PAU site directly.

PUBLICATIONS
PAU Registrar (2022). Annual Report 2022, Punjab Agricultural University. Annual report -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
ICAR-IIPR (2023). Project Coordinator Report, MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22. Institutional report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Kailash Chandra et al. (2016). Lentil Breeding for Improving Productivity Using Classical and Molecular Approaches. Review (no LL 1613 content in captured text) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329609948_Lentil_Breeding_for_Improving_Productivity_Using_Classical_and_Molecular_Approaches
No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper on LL 1613 was found. -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, PAU seed-sales or Indian private-dealer listing for LL 1613 was found. The seed-related results were foreign retail sites, which I have excluded. -- No evidence found
Breeder seed context: ICAR-IIPR reports total lentil breeder seed production of 857.36 q against an indent of 547.44 q for 45 indented varieties in Rabi 2021-22, without naming LL 1613. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
Notified recommendation: Haryana, Punjab, Northern Rajasthan, Plains of Uttarakhand, Delhi, Western Uttar Pradesh and part of Jammu and Kashmir. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/lentil-variety-ll-1613/
Zone: the PAU report places LL 1613 in the Northwest Plains Zone (Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh, north Rajasthan and Jammu & Kashmir). -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
Release date and type: 25 September 2023 notification, open-pollinated, released by the Central Seed Committee process. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/lentil-variety-ll-1613/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: L 4727 (lentil, A0309083)

DROUGHT: No direct drought-tolerance evidence found for L 4727. A Bundelkhand trial describes it as a low-water-requirement variety, but that is a regional agronomic note, not a stress-tolerance test. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5491

HEAT: No evidence found. (The heat-tolerant entry in the DPD table is Kota Masoor-1, a different variety.) -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

SALINITY: No evidence found.

FLOOD: No evidence found.

SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found.

DISEASE RESISTANCE: Moderately resistant to wilt per the DPD central-release listing for L 4727 (2018, IARI). -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf ; https://www.dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
DISEASE RESISTANCE (corroboration): Its moderate resistance to wilt is also noted in a Legume Research paper. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5491
DISEASE RESISTANCE (rust/pests): No evidence found for rust, Ascochyta or pod-borer resistance in L 4727.

PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found.

QTL/MARKERS: No evidence found for L 4727 specifically.

PARENTAGE: The AICRP annexure lists L 4727 as Sehore 74-3 x (the cross is truncated in the source). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

YIELD AND TRIALS: The IARI best-practice note gives an average yield of 11.5 to 14.5 q / ha and exhibited yield superiority of 23.7 percent over the best check IPL 316. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
YIELD RANGE (central release listing): 11-15 q/ha, with 92-128 days to maturity. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
MATURITY/AGRONOMY: Developed by ICAR-IARI, New Delhi in 2018 and matures in 92-128 days. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5491
FLD DEMONSTRATIONS: L 4727 had 2,500 FLDs conducted in MP in 2018. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
SEED TRAITS: Early maturity and bold seed size are noted as its distinguishing features. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf

BREEDER/INSTITUTION: ICAR-IARI, New Delhi; notified and released in 2018. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf ; https://www.dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY: Breeder seed indent for L4727 is listed in the IARI note (values 7.0, 8.0, 10.0 and a total of 22.07 qtl, year not clearly stated). This is demand data, not a supply or NSC/State Seed Corporation listing. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
SEED AVAILABILITY (NSC/SSC/KVK): No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Central Zone, covering Madhya Pradesh, parts of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh, for timely planting under rainfed conditions in rabi. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
RECOMMENDED STATES (input check): The input lists Maharashtra as a recommended state. The IARI note does not include Maharashtra, while the DPD listing is for CZ/NWPZ (CG, ...). Verify Maharashtra against the official notification. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Lentil-14 (CSC name) / PANT LENTIL-4 (Seednet name), lentil (Lens culinaris), PL-320

Search status: four web_search calls were made. A fifth lookup hit the tool-call limit, so the gaps below could not be filled. The evidence is thin. Nothing found so far confirms the variety's own release notification, yield, or trial data.

Name mapping: The evidence does not confirm that Seednet's "PANT LENTIL-4" is the same entry as CSC "Pant Lentil-14". The only "PL4" reference I found is a ScienceDirect study that lists PL4 as a GBPUAT lentil variety, which may be an older line. Treat the two names as unreconciled until checked on seednet.gov.in.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Pant Lentil-14 or PANT LENTIL-4. The DPD listing gives tolerance notes for other Pant lentil varieties only (for example, Pant Lentil-9 is listed as resistant to rust) -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found specific to this variety. Related context only: the DPD listing includes rust resistance and wilt tolerance for some Pant lentil lines -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for this variety's maturity, yield, or trial results. The DPD table has maturity and yield columns for other entries, but I did not see a row for Pant Lentil-14 in the captured text -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage (UPL 175 x (Pant L 184 x P 288)) was supplied in the brief and was not independently verified. A MULLaRP report lists lentil crosses attempted in 2021-22 at GBPUAT Pantnagar (10 crosses) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUA&T), Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, under the ICAR-AICRP on Pulses. The GBPUAT Directorate of Research page lists "Pant Lentil 14" among its varieties -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/index.html?id=6. The AICRP centre at Pantnagar was established in 1966 in the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf. Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only, as no breeder contact was found:
- Dr. S.K. Verma, Director Research, GBPUA&T, Pantnagar – 263145, Uttarakhand, India -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/index.html?id=6
- Email: directorresearch@gbpuat.ac.in -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/index.html?id=6
- Phone: No evidence found.
- Breeder name, breeder email, and breeder phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report entry, or thesis specific to Pant Lentil-14 was found. Related item only: a study of Indian lentil varieties that includes PL4 and other GBPUAT lines, for physical, nutritional and cooking traits. Authors and year were not captured in the search output. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2949824426000807

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. This search was not run, as the tool-call limit was reached before it.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Per the brief (CSC minutes, not independently verified): Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, North-West & Central Rajasthan, Western Uttar Pradesh. No independent source found.

Recommended next steps: (1) Check the CSC release notification and the Seednet entry for the official name, notification year, and the PANT LENTIL-4 mapping. (2) Search KrishiKosh and the GBPUAT lentil breeding programme for the breeder's name and contact. (3) Look for the AICRP-MULLaRP annual report entries for the variety's multi-location trials. (4) Check seed sources with GBPUAT Seed Production, the Uttar Pradesh and Punjab state seed corporations, and the NSC.

disease_resistance.summary: Rust: Pant L 6 (CSC name) is listed as resistant to rust in a single-trait entry (DPD table), and Pant L-6 is described as rust-resistant/tolerant in a state-wise guide. Disease tolerance/resistance: Pant Lentil 5 (Seednet name) is named among tolerant/resistant varieties recommended for disease management, with no pathogen-specific data. Mapping of these entries to PL 02 is unconfirmed. Pod borer, wilt and ascochyta resistance were reported for other Pantnagar lines (Pant Lentil 9, Pant Lentil 12), not for PL 5 or PL 6, and are excluded here.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No pest data were found for PL 02, PL 5 or PL 6. Pod borer resistance was reported only for Pant Lentil 9 and Pant Lentil 12, so it is not attributed to this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Original CSC record: 1500.00 to 2000.00 Kg/Ha. DPD table (Pant L 6, CSC name): 16-18 q/ha (approximately 1600-1800 kg/ha). The two ranges are consistent in part but are reported from different sources and the name mapping is unconfirmed. No multi-location yield data were found.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location or across-environment yield stability data were found for PL 02 or PL 6.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: timely sown condition of Uttar Pradesh. Digest evidence: recommended for Uttarakhand (DPD table and state-wise guide). Digest reports Pant L 6 as small seeded, while ICAR-IIPR (Rabi 2021-22) lists Pant Lentil 5 among large-seeded lentils for central India. The seed-size and region statements conflict across sources and are not reconciled by the digest.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: SEMI ERECT ,STEM COLOUR IS DARK GREEN ;FLOWER IS BLUE IN COLOUR ;BOLD SEED SIZE ,GREY MOTTLED
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) A 2023 IJES fertilizer trial at Dehradun, Uttarakhand, used a 40 kg/ha seed rate and is attributed by the digest to the Seednet name (reported as Pant Masoor-5, a variant spelling); no yield result was reported in the digest. (2) ICAR-IIPR (Rabi 2021-22) lists Pant Lentil 5 among large-seeded lentils for central India; this is a listing, not a trial result. (3) DPD table records Pant L 6 at 16-18 q/ha, 125-145 days. No multi-location trial results were found for PL 02 or PL 6. Identity of PL 02 with either name is unconfirmed.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No SSR, SNP or marker data were found for PL 02 or PL 6. Parentage L4126 X LG 171 (from the original record) was not found in any search result.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL study was found for PL 02 or PL 6. Gene-action work was reported on biparental progenies (PL 6 x PL 8 and PL 6 x L 4147), with no QTL effects given in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. No genes or pathways were identified for this variety. The Pant L 406 gamma-ray multipodding mutant study (Laskar et al., 2018) concerns a different cultivar and is not evidence for PL 6.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Lentil 6 / PANT LENTIL-5 (PL 02), lentil (masoor)

Name note: The CSC name is "Pant Lentil 6" and the Seednet name is "PANT LENTIL-5". The evidence below refers to whichever name each source uses, and I label it. No source I found links "PL 02" to either name explicitly, so the identity of the variety is unconfirmed. Parentage "L4126 X LG 171" was not found in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pant L 6 (2009, GBPUA&T Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, small seeded) is listed as resistant to rust; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for it were found -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf and https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Lentil 5 is named among tolerant/resistant varieties recommended for disease management (ref. to "Pant Lentil 5" as tolerant/resistant to disease) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF
- Pant L-6 is listed as rust-resistant/tolerant in a state-wise guide -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/check-out-state-wise-suggested-varieties-of-lentil/
- No stress-tolerance evidence specific to PL 02 or to the Seednet name was found beyond the above.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pant L 6 (CSC name): resistant to rust (single-trait entry) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Lentil 5 (Seednet name): listed as tolerant/resistant for disease reduction; no pathogen-specific data -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF
- Pod borer, wilt and ascochyta resistance were reported for other Pantnagar lines (Pant Lentil 9, Pant Lentil 12), not for PL 5 or PL 6 -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- No pest data for PL 02 were found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pant L 6 (CSC name): yield 16-18 q/ha, 125-145 days, small seeded, Uttarakhand -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Lentil 5 (Seednet name): listed among large-seeded lentils for central India (ICAR-IIPR report, Rabi 2021-22) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- A 2023 IJES fertilizer trial used "Pant Masoor-5" at Dehradun, Uttarakhand (seed rate 40 kg/ha); this is the Seednet name's trial, reported under a variant spelling -- https://www.iaras.org/iaras/filedownloads/ijes/2023/008-0009(2023).pdf
- No multi-location yield data for PL 02 or PL 6 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Biparental progenies were developed from PL 6 x PL 8 and PL 6 x L 4147 crosses, with gene-action work, at Norman E. Borlaug Crop Research Centre, GBPUA&T -- https://isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/3421/3146
- No QTL or marker study for PL 02 or PL 6 was found.
- Note: the Pant L 406 mutant study (Laskar et al., 2018) concerns a different variety and is not evidence for PL 6 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328006648_Morphological_characterization_of_gamma_rays_induced_multipodding_mutant_mp_in_lentil_cultivar_Pant_L_406

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (inferred from the sponsoring state and the DPD listing): G.B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology (GBPUA&T), Pantnagar, Uttarakhand -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name for PL 6 or PL 5: No evidence found. Searches returned no breeder names for either variant.
- Station: Norman E. Borlaug Crop Research Centre, GBPUA&T (cited for the PL 6 crosses only) -- https://isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/3421/3146

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder name, role, email, phone: No evidence found.
- Institute email, phone, postal address, or contact-page URL for GBPUA&T Pantnagar: No evidence found in the results.
- Not an institute contact: a seed company site (https://www.pantnagarseeds.com/our-strength) and a state seed corporation page (https://www.indiamart.com/uttarakhand-seeds/aboutus.html) appeared, but neither gave contact details for this variety. Do not treat either as the breeding institute.

PUBLICATIONS
- Laskar, R.A. et al. (2018). Morphological characterization of gamma rays induced multipodding mutant (mp) in lentil cultivar Pant L 406. International Journal of Radiation Biology -- DOI 10.1080/09553002.2018.1511927 (different cultivar; background only)
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Generation of biparental progenies and dissection of gene action in lentil (PL 6 x PL 8; PL 6 x L 4147). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding -- https://isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/3421/3146
- Authors not shown (2026). Screening of Selected Indian Varieties of Lentils (Lens culinaris) for Physical, Nutritional and Cooking Characteristics (includes PL 5 and PL 6 from GBPUA&T). ScienceDirect -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2949824426000807
- Dikshit, H.K., Mishra, G.P., Aski, M.S., Singh, A., Tripathi, K., Bansal, R. (year not shown). Lentil Breeding. Springer chapter -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-16-9257-4_24 (general review; no PL 5 or PL 6 data)
- No AICRP/ICAR annual report entry or KrishiKosh thesis specific to PL 02, PL 5 or PL 6 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Pant L 6 / PL 5 / PL 6 specific seed sources: No evidence found.
- Uttarakhand Seeds and Tarai Development Corporation (UKS&TDC), originally the Tarai Development Corporation set up in 1969 and linked to GBPUA&T seed production -- https://www.indiamart.com/uttarakhand-seeds/aboutus.html
- A 2023 contingency plan lists seed supply through TDC/NSC/VPKAS for Dehradun -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/CP/Uttarkhand/UKD7-Dehradun-10.07.14.pdf
- NSC, KVK, SAU seed-sales listings for PL 5 or PL 6 were not found in the searches (the fourth search was not run).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttarakhand: PL-5 and PL-6 are listed among recommended lentil varieties -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF and https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/check-out-state-wise-suggested-varieties-of-lentil/
- Pant L 6 (CSC name): recommended area Uttarakhand -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- YEAR OF RELEASE: Pant L 6 is listed as 2009 in the DPD table (CSC name). Release year for PANT LENTIL-5 (Seednet name): not found. The record's "NaT" value should be replaced with 2009 only if the CSC name is confirmed as the same variety.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Lentil 7 (variety_name) / Pant Lentil-7 (PL-024) (seednet_variety_name), Lentil (Masoor)

Name note: The evidence below uses "Pant L 7" and "(PL 024)" (DPD table and review). The DPD table also has a "Pant Masoor 7" row with 2010 and Uttarakhand-area details, which may be the same variety under another name, but the page does not link the two, so I have flagged those findings. The Seednet name "Pant Lentil-7 (PL-024)" did not appear in any retrieved page.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. The searches returned only general lentil material or other varieties, and nothing that names this variety with these traits.
Rust resistance is the only stress trait recorded for this variety (see DISEASE AND PEST).

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to rust, large seed (DPD Pant L 7 row, 2009 table) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
Rust-resistant/tolerant varieties list includes "Pant L-7" -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/check-out-state-wise-suggested-varieties-of-lentil/
Pod borer: The DPD table records "Resistant to pod borer" under the "Pant Masoor 7" 2010 row (name is not confirmed as this variety) -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

drought.details: None of the search results mention Pant Lentil 16 (PL-366). The release data lists stress reaction as NONE. General crop-level evidence only: lentil is described as moderately tolerant to drought, with differences between cultivars, and tolerance to moisture stress is a key trait in rainfed production (CABI). Other released varieties such as Kota Masoor 2 are listed as tolerant to drought and high temperature, but this cannot be attributed to PL-366.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance data for PL-366. Heat tolerance is reported only for other varieties (for example Kota Masoor 2 and L 4727) in the central lentil varieties list.

salinity.details: No PL-366 data. CABI states lentil is generally very sensitive to salinity, and a review reports salt exposure can reduce plant growth or yield by 20% to 100%. Salinity tolerance for this variety is not documented.

flood.details: No PL-366 data. Lentil in general is intolerant of waterlogging and water stagnation (CABI, agriguru, CUTM notes).

drought.details: None of the search results mention Pant Lentil 16 (PL-366). The release data lists stress reaction as NONE. General crop-level evidence only: lentil is described as moderately tolerant to drought, with differences between cultivars, and tolerance to moisture stress is a key trait in rainfed production (CABI). Other released varieties such as Kota Masoor 2 are listed as tolerant to drought and high temperature, but this cannot be attributed to PL-366.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance data for PL-366. Heat tolerance is reported only for other varieties (for example Kota Masoor 2 and L 4727) in the central lentil varieties list.

salinity.details: No PL-366 data. CABI states lentil is generally very sensitive to salinity, and a review reports salt exposure can reduce plant growth or yield by 20% to 100%. Salinity tolerance for this variety is not documented.

flood.details: No PL-366 data. Lentil in general is intolerant of waterlogging and water stagnation (CABI, agriguru, CUTM notes).

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa - 6 (seednet name: Pusa -6 (IET 22290) (Pusa 1612-7-6-5)), Rice
