None of the results named this variety, its codes (IET 22290, Pusa 1612-7-6-5), or its parentage (Pusa Sugandh 5 lines). I checked all returned text for these strings and found no matches. The results were about other rice varieties, such as Pusa Basmati 1121, Pusa Basmati 1509 and Pusa Basmati 1718, and a Basmati QTL mapping study. I have excluded all of them as off-target.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety has government release-list citations (DPD) confirming rust resistance and moderate pod borer resistance, plus yield data of 12-13 q/ha. However, there is no peer-reviewed research and no abiotic stress evidence (drought, heat, salinity, flood). It is also a temperate Kashmir valley variety with a 204-day maturity, not recommended for Gujarat, so its suitability there is doubtful. The score sits at the 60 tier (citation present, weak stress evidence) and the biotic traits do not justify the 75 tier.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: SKUAST-K release; rust resistant; moderately resistant to pod borer; 12-13 q/ha; Kashmir valley
dashboard_data.seasons: Not explicitly stated; presumably rabi/autumn sowing in the Kashmir valley (inferred from the 204-day duration)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Shalimar Masoor-3 (SKUA-L-96) is a lentil variety released in 2019 by SKUAST-K for the Kashmir valley, with a yield of 12-13 q/ha and 204 days to maturity. It is resistant to rust and moderately resistant to pod borer, with no evidence of abiotic stress tolerance. Evidence comes only from government release lists, with no peer-reviewed or molecular data.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Kashmir valley lentil released in 2019 by SKUAST-K as SKUA-L-96. It yields 12-13 q/ha and matures in about 204 days. Parentage and plant traits are not specified.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Biotic resistance is documented for rust (resistant) and pod borer (moderately resistant). No evidence exists for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, since those snippet entries belong to other varieties. Suitability for Gujarat is unproven.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Masoor-3 (lentil)

Name note: The release-minute name and the Seednet name are both "Shalimar Masoor-3". Every finding below refers to that name. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so no Seednet-specific evidence exists in this digest. Several sources list the variety under other names: SKUA-L-96 in the DPD tables, and KLS 221 as a possible parent or selection in the ICAR-IIPR report.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as tolerant to frost and winter chilling, Kashmir valley bold-seeded type, released 2019 by SKUAST-K Srinagar (DPD state list; the same row also appears as SKUA-L-96) -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Same frost and winter-chill tolerance entry, with the year given as 2018 in a second DPD table -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Same frost and winter-chill tolerance entry in the ICAR-IIPR MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The DPD entry reading "resistant to rust, moderately resistant to pod borer" sits in the same table cell as the Shalimar Masoor-2 entry (it repeats under the -2 heading). It is not attributable to Shalimar Masoor-3 -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- The ICAR-IIPR report lists the -3 entry as bold seeded with no disease claim. Its row for the -2 variety carries the "moderately resistant to wilt and rust" claim -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to Shalimar Masoor-3.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield listed as 11-12 q/ha in one DPD table and 12-13 q/ha in another; maturity listed as 204 days -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Yield listed as 11.5-12.5 q/ha, maturity 204 days, in the ICAR-IIPR report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No multi-location trial results or agronomic packages specific to Shalimar Masoor-3 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage field in the ICAR-IIPR report reads "KLS 221 (Sel..." and is truncated; this is unverified and conflicts with the "Not specified" parentage in the record -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No QTL or marker studies specific to Shalimar Masoor-3 were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: SKUAST-K, Srinagar Centre (released 2019); the ICAR-IIPR report lists the same centre -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- No breeder or scientist name was found for Shalimar Masoor-3. The search returned a Shalimar Masoor-related Jammu paper (Singh et al. 2022), but it concerns other derivatives, so it is not attributed here -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9499259/
- Discarded: the SKUAST-K wheat article about the Shalimar wheat-3 (SW-3) variety names a breeder, but that is a different crop and variety -- https://brighterkashmir.com/shalimar-wheat-3-launched-in-gurez

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for a breeder email, phone or postal address for this variety.
- Institute-level only: SKUAST-K, Srinagar Centre (the release institution). No official contact page URL was returned by the search.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. The searches returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report entry or thesis that names Shalimar Masoor-3 as its subject. Items that name other Shalimar lentils (Masoor-1, Masoor-2, Jammu Lentil 71/144) were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The ICAR-IIPR MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report records breeder seed indents across 45 lentil varieties, but the line does not give a figure for Shalimar Masoor-3 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SKUAST seed sales or private dealers offering this variety. Results returned generic masoor dal sellers, which were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Jammu and Kashmir, Kashmir valley (state release, SKUAST-K). The DPD and ICAR-IIPR sources list the Kashmir valley region for this variety -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The central DPD lentil list gives VL Masoor 133 (VL 133), released 2011 by ICAR-VPKAS Almora, as tolerant to wilt, root rot and rust. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found for this variety. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf (the state-released table with the VL Masoor 133 row is in http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf)
- Evidence refers to: VL Masoor 133 (variety_name). No evidence found for the seednet name VL MASOOR-103 in this heading.

DISEASE AND PEST

- No pest-resistance evidence was found for VL Masoor 133. -- (no URL)

- VL MASOOR-103 (seednet name): the only VL 103 evidence found (a 2000 VPKAS release described as rust tolerant) is a different variety and was discarded. Evidence for VL MASOOR-103 under this heading: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Name matched: VL Masoor 514 (VL 514). The SEEDNET name "VL MASOOR-4" was not searched and nothing found links it to this variety.
- Resistant to powdery mildew and moderately resistant to rust in Uttarakhand hills (ICAR tribal/hill AR 2011-12) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/tribal-hill-region-AR-2011-12_3.pdf
- Moderately resistant to wilt and rust (DPD central/state lentil list) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to wilt and root rot, and tolerant to pod borer (compositional review table) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698673_COMPREHENSIVE_STUDY_OF_LENTIL_LENS_CULINARIS_MEDIK_SEED_AND_THEIR_NUTRITIONAL_PROFILE-A_REVIEW
- Moderately resistant to wilt and rust, listed as bold seeded (DPD state list) -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf (http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released 2011 by ICAR-VPKAS, Almora; yield 8-10 q/ha; maturity 155-160 days; bold seeded; Uttarakhand hills -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Protein content about 21.04%; 11.19% yield advantage over checks VL Masoor 507 and PL 05 in Uttarakhand hills under organic conditions -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/tribal-hill-region-AR-2011-12_3.pdf
- Listed among varieties used in an Indian pulse seed-system/technology demonstration paper -- https://www.isss-india.org/img/Bulletin31.pdf
- No evidence found for multi-location AICRP yield trial data specific to this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for QTL, marker or genetic-diversity studies on VL Masoor 514.
- Parentage as supplied in the input (pure line selection from hill collection VHC 6553, Sera village, Berinag, Pithoragarh) was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: ICAR-VPKAS (Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan), Almora, Uttarakhand -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for a named lead breeder or scientist.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for breeder email, phone or postal address, and no institute contact page was returned by the searches.
- Institute name only: ICAR-VPKAS, Almora (UK) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- The Seednet-style contact details and the official VPKAS address need to be checked directly on vpkas.icar.gov.in.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not identified (2020s compositional study of five lentil varieties including VL Masoor 514). Journal: PMC article on dehulling, germination and cooking effects on lentil nutrients, anti-nutrients and antioxidants -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5336446/
- Authors not identified. Compositional review of lentil seed listing VL Masoor 514 with stress notes. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698673_COMPREHENSIVE_STUDY_OF_LENTIL_LENS_CULINARIS_MEDIK_SEED_AND_THEIR_NUTRITIONAL_PROFILE-A_REVIEW
- Authors not identified. Current scenario of lentil production in Madhya Pradesh, listing VL-514 among varieties in breeder seed production. Bioinfo Publication -- https://www.bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0005193
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report with trial data, or DOI found for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Breeder seed production listed for VL-514 in Madhya Pradesh (not a sales listing) -- https://www.bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0005193
- ICAR-IIPR rabi 2021-22 PC report shows breeder seed indent of 1007 q for VL 514 in an indent table (cross-check needed) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- The VPKAS seed portal page returned only shows VL Masoor 514 as a related product on the VL Masoor 148 page, so it is not evidence of stock -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLMasoor148_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%B0148
- No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listings for VL Masoor 514. Indiamart results were generic masoor seed and not this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttarakhand (hill region) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Recommended states field recorded as "Not specified" in the input; no other state recommendation found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VL Masoor 129 (lentil)

Name note: the evidence below uses the spelling "VL Masoor 129" (dpd.gov.in). I did not see the Seednet listing "VL Masoor-129" in any result, so the Seednet-side evidence is absent, not confirmed.

Search budget note: four web_search calls were made. A fifth call was blocked by the tool limit, so the breeder, contact, and publication searches were not fully run. Gaps are marked below.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: the state-release table entry for VL Masoor 129 notes resistance against wilt and root rot. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: VL Masoor 129 is listed as resistant against wilt and root rot. No pod borer or other pest evidence specific to this variety found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: the table row for VL Masoor 129 contains the values "7-11" and "145-150" with no column headers in the snippet. These are most likely yield (q/ha) and days to maturity, but this is inferred and needs checking against the source. No multi-location trial data found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage "VL 101 x VL 1" comes only from the input record; no independent source was retrieved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: the release row names VPKAS, Almora as the developing institution (Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Almora). No individual breeder name was found in the results. Breeder search was not completed.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The breeder-contact search was not completed, so no official email, phone or address has been verified. The institute name VPKAS, Almora is the only institute-level identifier available.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for VL Masoor 129. The PMC article (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5336446/) studies VL Masoor 125, 133, 142, 507 and 514, not 129. No AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI was located.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned the release table but no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: listed as a state-released variety for Uttarakhand. A second source (dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF) lists Uttarakhand varieties, but the snippet I saw was truncated before the VL Masoor 129 entry.

RELEASE YEAR CONFLICT -- The input record says year of release is "NaT" (missing). dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf gives 2009. Treat 2009 as a source-supported value to verify, not as confirmed CSC minutes.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ratan (CG 5016), Wheat

Search status: Four searches ran in one batch. A fifth search, needed to re-check the snippets, was blocked by the tool's usage limit. Snippets were truncated in my output, so the findings below are partial. Only the slideshare page names this variety with its code, so it is the only page I can attribute to Ratan (CG 5016). Name search for "Ratan" alone returned a Brainly page about "Ratna" (not this variety), and the Raipur seed listing did not name Ratan in the portion I saw.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched, but no page in the results described stress tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Searched, but no page in the results described disease or pest resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Searched, but no page in the results gave yield, maturity, or trial data for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage recorded in the CSC input is HUW 325/DL-230-7. I did not find an independent source confirming it. No QTL, marker, or genome-resource evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Ratan (CG 5016) is listed among rabi crop varieties released or recommended by IGKV (Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya), with the entry stating it was developed at T.C.B. College of Agriculture & Research Station, Bilaspur. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/rabi-crop-varieties-release-or-recommended-by-igkv/247306068 (also https://slideshare.net/janhavimaurya/rabi-crop-varieties-release-or-recommended-by-igkv). Lead breeder name: not found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, or institute contact page was retrieved for this variety.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, thesis, or KrishiKosh record naming this variety was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for this variety. The only seed result was an IndiaMART listing for wheat seeds from Green Home, Raipur, Chhattisgarh (https://www.indiamart.com/green-home-raipur/wheat-seeds.html). It did not name Ratan in the text I saw, so I have not attributed it to this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The CSC record says "Not specified." The IGKV slideshare entry places the variety in Chhattisgarh context through IGKV and the Bilaspur station, but it does not state the recommended zone or states in the snippet I saw. Treat as unverified.

Gaps to close in a follow-up session: the Seednet portal entry for "Ratan (CG 5016)" (seednet.gov.in), the IGKV notification or release record, KrishiKosh, and the Ratan-specific rows of the AICRP wheat annual reports.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Lime VRM-1 (VRM-1, Agriculture Research Station, Vellore; release recorded as 2015-04-07)

RELEASE/BREEDER: No evidence found confirming the 2015 release date or the Vellore station as breeder. -- No source located
VARIETY IDENTITY: TNAU lists "VRM 1" among acid lime varieties, but another TNAU page calls it a "local variety" and elsewhere pairs it with "Tahithi lime," so its origin and identity need verification. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_fruits_acidlime.html
DROUGHT: No evidence found for VRM-1. A drought-tolerance claim exists only for a different, farmer-developed grafted acid lime selection, not VRM-1. -- https://nif.org.in/innovation/new_acid_lime_variety/292
HEAT: No evidence found.
SALINITY: No evidence found.
FLOOD/SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found. TNAU's general acid lime guidance says water stagnation should be avoided, which applies to the crop generally, not VRM-1 specifically. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_fruits_acidlime.html
DISEASE RESISTANCE: No evidence found for VRM-1. Canker tolerance is reported for other acid lime varieties (Pramalini, Sai Sarbati), not VRM-1. -- https://www.horticultureguruji.in/acid-lime/
PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found for VRM-1. Leaf miner and citrus butterfly tolerance is reported only for PKM 1. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_TNAU_varieties_fc_acidlime.html
QTL/MARKERS: No evidence found for VRM-1. -- No source located
YIELD: No VRM-1-specific yield found. The general acid lime yield guideline is about 25 t/ha/year. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf
TRIALS: TNAU Sankarankovil's 2017–2020 scheme included VRM 1 among four acid lime varieties in an evaluation of acid lime genotypes for year-round production; no results were reported. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-sankarankovil/ongoing-schemes/
PROPAGATION: TNAU recommends layering for VRM 1 (listed as Tahithi lime). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf
SEED AVAILABILITY (NSC/State Seed Corporations/KVKs): No evidence found. -- No source located
RECOMMENDED STATES: Not confirmed by a release notification. TNAU's crop guide lists VRM 1 among acid lime varieties and names Vellore among the growing districts, which indicates Tamil Nadu use only. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf ; https://mapmycrop.com/acid-lime-crop-guide/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
The search tool hit its usage limit after the first batch of four queries, so I could not run the second batch. The evidence below comes only from that first batch, and most headings have little or no support.

Name check: the CSC name "ARPITA" and the Seednet name "ARPITA(JBC-5)" refer to the same variety. The only evidence I found names it as "JBC 5 (Arpita)", so I treated the two names as one variety.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The ICAR 2010-11 report snippet I saw does not mention stress tolerance for Arpita. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. -- searched via the same ICAR and ResearchGate results; no disease or pest data for JBC-5 appeared in the text returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The ICAR 2010-11 Crop Improvement report refers to JBC 5 (Arpita) as a white jute variety that has shown yield (the surrounding text was truncated, so the yield figure and trial locations are unverified). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
Caution: the same snippet describes a variety with semi-dwarf plant type and flowering at 97 days, but the text is cut off, so I cannot confirm that this description belongs to Arpita rather than another variety. Do not attribute it to Arpita without checking the full report.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found for the parentage JRO-321 x THA/Y/086C or for any QTL or marker work. Neither parent code appeared in any result I retrieved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The ICAR report mentions the variety but does not name a breeder or station in the text I saw. Arpita is a Central release, so the institution field is blank in the record. The "JBC" prefix suggests a jute breeding line from the ICAR jute institutes, but that is inference, not sourced.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. I did not obtain a breeder, institute email, phone, or address for this variety. The search for the breeder and institute page did not run because of the tool limit.

PUBLICATIONS: 
- Scientific Cultivation of JUTE (year not shown in the snippet). Bangladesh Jute Research Institute, if the ResearchGate page's author attribution holds. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376269572_Scientific_Cultivation_of_JUTE
  This is a general cultivation document, not a study of Arpita. It lists JBC-5 (Arpita) only among varieties, and the author attribution to BJRI was not verified. I am not treating it as evidence about Arpita.
- No other publications on Arpita were found. Searches for peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, and KrishiKosh theses did not run.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The seed availability search did not return any seller, NSC, state seed corporation, or SAU listing for Arpita. The ResearchGate result again only listed the variety among others.

RECOMMENDED STATES: The supplied record lists West Bengal and Assam. I did not find independent confirmation of this in the search results. The ICAR snippet mentions white jute varieties in general, and it does not state the states for JBC-5.

Not run because of the tool limit: the Seednet portal check, KrishiKosh and AICRP searches, the breeder and institute page search, and the seed availability search with dealer and SAU sources. The Krishi Jagran result returned only general jute material and was excluded.

drought.details: The HPKV crop improvement document lists 'Tolerant to water stress conditions' near the KL 215 (Bhagsu) entry, but the snippet does not clearly tie this trait to Bhagsu rather than a neighbouring entry. The Seednet list gives 'drought tolerant' for other varieties. General textbook statements that linseed is fairly drought resistant are crop-level, not variety-specific. The HPKV Research Council agenda mentions a drought mapping population derived from DH 40 (tolerant) and a susceptible parent, with Bhagsu among eight varieties studied, but no Bhagsu drought rating is given.

heat.details: No Bhagsu-specific heat tolerance data. A symposium abstract mentions heat-tolerant genotypes, but Bhagsu is not identified as one of them.

salinity.details: No Bhagsu-specific salinity data. Salt tolerance screening with NaCl is mentioned in a symposium abstract, but Bhagsu's result is not given.

flood.details: No evidence found. Textbook sources note that oilseed crops, including linseed, do not tolerate waterlogging.

disease_resistance.summary: Bhagsu is described as resistant to rust (a Scribd summary lists 'resistant to rust (KL-215)', suited to utera sowing). The PMC release table also describes it as resistant to rust and powdery mildew, though the snippet wording is ambiguous. A symposium abstract lists Bhagsu among genotypes that were highly resistant (disease score 0) in a screening, but the disease is not named in the snippet.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance data found in the results.

agronomic_details.yield: The Scribd summary lists 4-5 q/ha, with 37.0 (likely oil content %). The HPKV document's 400-500 q/ha figure appears to belong to a forage crop entry, not Bhagsu.
agronomic_details.stability: In AMMI analysis, Bhagsu and Surbhi were the most unstable genotypes, although both had above-average oil content. A G x E study also reported a 11.69 percent difference for Bhagsu at Dhaula Kuan.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Bred and recommended for Himachal Pradesh, in hill conditions, with dual-purpose and utera use noted in one source.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 178-209 days per the Seednet list (180-185 days per the Scribd summary)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium height, blue flowers, small brown seeds. Pedigree RL-50-3 x Surbhi, developed by the pedigree method at Palampur.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Included in multi-environment G x E trials and in an eight-line genetic analysis of seed, fibre and dual-purpose traits.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No Bhagsu-specific markers, QTL or SNP data found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: None reported for Bhagsu. HPKV is developing a drought mapping population from DH 40 (tolerant) and a susceptible parent, and Bhagsu is used in other studies only as one of eight diverse lines.

disease_resistance.summary: A release table attributes resistance to rust and moderate resistance to wilt, powdery mildew and alternaria blight to Birsa Tisi-2 (BAU 14-09). Attribution is uncertain because the same block sits next to a tomato entry. A general BAU statement says released varieties resist major diseases and pests, but this has no variety-level scoring and is not measured in the sources. Resistance ratings for Birsa Tisi-1 (high rust and alternaria resistance) are a separate release and are excluded from this variety's profile.

pest_resistance.summary: Only a general BAU statement that released varieties resist major pests was found, with no variety-level scoring. Bud fly resistance is recorded for Birsa Tisi-1 only and is excluded from this variety's profile. No pest-specific resistance evidence for Birsa Tisi-2 was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Krishi Jagran reports a potential yield of 19.7 q/ha and 10.46% superiority over the national check T-397. The BAU release table gives conflicting values of 19-20 q/ha potential and 13-14 q/ha average. Average yield in CSC record: Not Available.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Described as suited to the drought-prone, dryland (rainfed) ecosystem of Jharkhand. A Punjab recommendation appears beside a Birsa Tisi-2 block but is unverified and excluded.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Open-pollinated (IAUA listing). Flowers blue and bold capsules (BAU release table). Oil content reported as 36.75% (Krishi Jagran) and 42-43% (BAU release table), which conflict.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Krishi Jagran: 19.7 q/ha potential yield, 36.75% oil, 128-130 days maturity, 10.46% superior to national check T-397. (2) BAU release table: 19-20 q/ha potential, 13-14 q/ha average, 42-43% oil, 128-129 days; values conflict with item 1. (3) BAU release set (not specific to Tisi-2): 15-20% yield advantage over traditional varieties. (4) Rabi 2024-25 trial of 30 linseed genotypes including BIRSA-TISI-2 (LC) at the Ranchi-6 research farm, BAU: genotypic correlations exceeded phenotypic correlations for yield traits; secondary branches, capsules per plant and seeds per capsule were the main direct contributors to yield; days to maturity had a negative direct effect. (5) Seed rate guidance of 25-30 kg/ha for linseed comes from an organic trial in which T-397 was the farmer-field variety, not Tisi-2.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTL/marker studies: No evidence found. A 30-genotype trial reported that genotypic correlations exceeded phenotypic correlations for yield traits, which indicates genetic control of those traits. This is a trait-level inference, not a mapped QTL.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Described as suited to the drought-prone, dryland ecosystem of Jharkhand, with resistance to major diseases and pests (general claim, not measured in the sources) -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/jharkhand-agri-research-institutes-release-16-high-yielding-crop-varieties-for-farmers/
Listed as an open-pollinated variety suited to rainfed conditions of Jharkhand -- https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistance to rust, moderate resistance to wilt, powdery mildew and alternaria blight are attributed to Birsa Tisi-2 (BAU 14-09) in a release table, but the same block sits next to a tomato entry, so attribution is uncertain -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
General statement that the released BAU varieties resist major diseases and pests (no variety-level scoring) -- https://www.bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/
Do not confuse with Birsa Tisi-1 (a separate, earlier BAU linseed release): high rust and alternaria resistance, moderate wilt and bud fly resistance -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_637852580202036105.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Potential yield 19.7 q/ha, 36.75% oil, 128-30 days maturity, 10.46% superior to national check T-397 -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/jharkhand-agri-research-institutes-release-16-high-yielding-crop-varieties-for-farmers/
Conflicting values in the BAU release table: 19-20 q/ha potential, 13-14 q/ha average, 42-43% oil, 128-129 days, flowers blue, bold capsules -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
Varieties were described as offering 15-20% yield advantage over traditional varieties (BAU release set, not specific to Tisi-2) -- https://www.bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/
Seed rate guidance of 25-30 kg/ha for linseed, with T-397 cited as the farmer-field variety in organic trials (not Tisi-2) -- https://icar.gov.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/Organic-linseed-Tisi-Farming.pdf
Field trial of 30 linseed genotypes including BIRSA-TISI-2 (LC), rabi 2024-25, Ranchi-6 research farm, BAU -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/209%20CORRELATION-AND-PATH-ANALYSIS-IN-LINSEED-(Linum-usitatissimum-L.)-FOR-SEED-YIELD-AND-YIELD-ATTRIBUTING-TRAITS.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Genotypic correlations exceeded phenotypic correlations for yield traits in the 30-genotype trial, indicating genetic control -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/209%20CORRELATION-AND-PATH-ANALYSIS-IN-LINSEED-(Linum-usitatissimum-L.)-FOR-SEED-YIELD-AND-YIELD-ATTRIBUTING-TRAITS.pdf
Secondary branches, capsules per plant and seeds per capsule were the main direct contributors to yield; days to maturity had a negative direct effect -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/209%20CORRELATION-AND-PATH-ANALYSIS-IN-LINSEED-(Linum-usitatissimum-L.)-FOR-SEED-YIELD-AND-YIELD-ATTRIBUTING-TRAITS.pdf
QTL/marker studies: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Birsa Tisi-2 was developed by BAU principal/chief scientist Sohan Ram -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/jharkhand-agri-research-institutes-release-16-high-yielding-crop-varieties-for-farmers/
Developing institution: Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, Jharkhand; code BAU 14-09 -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
Release was approved at an SVRC meeting on 24 March (year not stated in the page) with Director of Research A. Wadood -- https://lagatar24.com/ranchi-bau-scientists-develop-four-different-varieties-of-high-yielding-crops/
Release year conflict: the record says 26 Oct 2022 (CSC), while the news reports describe an SVRC release that appears to be from around 2021 -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/16-all-new-high-yielding-varieties-of-crops-developed-by-this-agri-research-institution/
Institution profile: Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, established 1981; the Wikipedia infobox lists a Vice-Chancellor that conflicts with the 2021 news (Onkar Nath Singh) -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birsa_Agricultural_University

CONTACT DETAILS
Lead breeder: Dr Sohan Ram, BAU principal/chief scientist. No email or phone found -- https://lagatar24.com/ranchi-bau-scientists-develop-four-different-varieties-of-high-yielding-crops/

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gobhi sarson (Brassica napus L.), PGSH 1699

Search budget note: four web_search calls were run, in one parallel batch. A fifth call was blocked by the tool's usage limit, so no further verification was possible. Several findings below come from truncated search snippets and need checking against the full documents.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page naming PGSH 1699 with disease or pest resistance was returned.

The variety has shown highly resistant reaction to rust and powdery mildew and resistant to wilt wheras national check was highly susceptible.
Highly resistant to rust under natural and artificial conditions. Resistant to Wilt under natural and artificial conditions.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Resistant to bud fly.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 60 kg N/ha. Method of application: Apply half dose of nitrogen after emergence of crop and rest half dose of nitrogen before flowering.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed as resistant to rust, powdery mildew and wilt -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Listed as moderately resistant to powdery mildew and moderately susceptible to Alternaria blight, under the name "JL 41 (Jawahar Alsi-41)" -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
No evidence found on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to rust, powdery mildew and wilt (DAC notified-varieties table) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Moderately resistant to powdery mildew, moderately susceptible to Alternaria blight (AICRP release table, "JL 41") -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
Named among linseed lines in an IIOR 2022 report where whitefly, leafhopper and aphid populations peaked in late December 2021. The sentence is garbled, so the link between this variety and those pest counts is uncertain -- https://www.scribd.com/document/738239893/56-Annual-Report-IIOR-AR-2022

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Release table: irrigated, Madhya Pradesh, State level, year 2011, listed range 1500-1600 with a value of 40, suitable for intercropping with sugarcane (units not stated in the snippet; the "40" may be a days or yield field) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
DAC table: year 2011, released at Hoshangabad, yield potential 40.00 and oil content 1600 (I) as listed; the columns look misaligned, so units are unverified -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
No evidence found for multi-location trial results or maturity days.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Parentage "(RL 102-7X0-7) X J-23" was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Released at Hoshangabad (DAC table); the developing institution is not confirmed as JNKVV or any named station -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
No evidence found naming the lead breeder(s). The breeder search did not complete (see note below).

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, address or institute contact page for this variety was returned.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Results were general linseed reviews and reports, not papers on this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Seed-dealer, NSC, SAU or KVK sale listings for this variety or for "Jawahar Linseed-9" were not returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Madhya Pradesh: listed among recommended linseed varieties for the state, with the note that the variety suits areas of Madhya Pradesh with limited irrigated facility -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Madhya Pradesh is also given as the release state with "Irrigated" and "State" categories in the AICRP release table -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

NAME NOTES
Variety name "Jawahar Linseed-41" was matched in DAC (also as "PKDL-41") and AICRP ("JL 41 / Jawahar Alsi-41"). Seednet name "JAWAHAR LINSEED-9" produced no evidence for this variety; the ICAR-CRIDA document mentions "JLS-9" and "J-23", which I discarded as different varieties. The ICAR 2024-25 report and the Jawahar Linseed Sagar (JLS 121) entry were also discarded.

NOTE: The search tool returned a usage-limit error partway through, so the breeder/contact search and the seed-availability search did not run successfully, and the publications search returned only general linseed material. Those headings should be re-run before the record is final.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Linseed-165 (seednet name: Jawahar Linseed-165 (PKDL-165); code PKDL-165; crop: Linseed)

Name matching: the evidence below refers to "Jawahar Alsi 165" (The Week/PTI, 2020), "JL 165" (AICRP-Linseed list and Grain Magazine), "Jawahar Linseed 165" (MDPI review) and "PKDL-165" (bud fly screening paper). I linked these to the CSC release because they share the JNKVV/Sagar institution, the 2020 year and the linseed crop. The Seednet portal name was not returned by any search, so no evidence is attributed to the Seednet record. Parentage "Meera X Polf-17" was not found in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety. The only related text is an ICAR 2024-25 report on other linseed varieties (not this one), so I did not use it. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- PKDL-165 was among genotypes in a preliminary natural-field bud fly screen, where it appears in a list alongside a "moderately susceptible" category; the page text is garbled, so the category assignment is not fully reliable and needs confirmation. Confirmation of resistance was called for in the paper. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376046405_Effect_of_Sowing_Dates_and_Preliminary_Screening_of_Linseed_Genotypes_for_Bud_Fly_Infestation
No rust, wilt, powdery mildew or Alternaria reaction was found for this variety. -- No evidence found (searched)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The 2020 PTI report gives a yield of 21 to 22 quintal/ha and a maturity of 160 to 170 days for "Jawahar Alsi 165." The 160 to 170 day maturity is unusually long for linseed and is unverified. The same report gives oil output of 454 kg/ha, 15 to 19 percent above earlier seed. -- https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/national/2020/08/16/bes7-mp-crops-varieties.html
A 2022 Seed Times newsletter lists JL 165 among varieties with high seed and oil yield and high omega-3 content. -- https://nsai.co.in/storage/app/media/Seed-Times-Sept-Dec-2022.pdf
No replicated multi-location trial data for this variety were found. -- No evidence found (searched)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage (Meera X Polf-17): No evidence found. Breeding method: No evidence found. Breeding-line code: the name appears only as "JL 165" and "PKDL-165." No QTL, marker or genome-resource data were found for this variety. The MDPI review (2023) lists "Jawahar Linseed 165" only as a name in a national genetic-resources table. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4425/14/7/1461

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The 2020 release was announced by Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (JNKVV), with recognition from the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards. The breeder's name was not given. -- https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/national/2020/08/16/bes7-mp-crops-varieties.html
Grain Magazine lists "JL 165" among varieties developed under the ICAR AICRP at RARS Sagar, Madhya Pradesh. -- https://www.grainmagazine.in/preview/645b17953640e00aea5643d2
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. Developing station: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Sagar, JNKVV (per the sources above; the Zonal Agricultural Research Station Powarkheda in the input record was not found in any result).

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level address (from MDPI affiliation): All India Coordinated Research Project on Linseed, Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya, Regional Agricultural Research Station, Sagar 470001, India. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4425/14/7/1461

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Name used: JLS-73 (variety code SLS-73). Seednet name JLS-79 has no evidence linking it to this entry; see the note under RECOMMENDED STATES.
- Directorate of Oilseeds Development characters table lists SLS-73 (JLS-73) as resistant to rust, powdery mildew and bud fly -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- A ResearchGate table of abiotic-stress-tolerant varieties lists JLS-73 (SLS-73) as "moderately resistant" to an unclear disease (text truncated in snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351224957_Abiotic_Stress_Tolerant_Crop_Varieties_Livestock_Breeds_and_Fish_Species
- Plant-disease reference lists SLS-73 (JLS-73) among rust-resistant linseed varieties, citing "Anonymous, 2022" -- https://www.plantsdiseases.com/p/diseases-of-linseed.html
- Drought, heat and salinity tolerance: No evidence found for JLS-73 specifically. The review found lists JLS73 in rainfed-condition tables without tolerance data -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini screening (2023–24 isolates) grades JLS-73 as susceptible, with wilt incidence of 30.1–50% -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
- Rust, powdery mildew and bud fly resistance: see STRESS TOLERANCE (DOD source).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Sowing-date trial comparing PKV-NL-260, PKV-NL-97 and JLS-73 in split-plot design; PKV-NL-260 sown in the 44th meteorological week outperformed PKV-NL-97 and JLS-73 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328336019_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Uptake_and_Quality_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_Varieties_as_Affected_by_Varying_Sowing_Dates
- Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi study in drought-prone area: JLS-73 among three cultivars, with 73.33% root colonisation at site three -- https://ijfans.org/uploads/paper/44d1a9b8e41cd079600968587e2df7a6.pdf
- Yield figure in the DOD table: 38.82 (units not stated; the oil-content column "1090 (R)" appears misaligned) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Excluded: Punjab "LS-73" trials and Nagaland "JLS-95" trials are different genotypes.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker-assisted or pedigree study for JLS-73 was returned. The Fusarium SSR study characterises the pathogen, not the variety's genetics.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Release centre: Sagar, year 2011 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Institution conflict: a ResearchGate table gives LNKVV Jabalpur for JLS-73 (SLS-73), 2011, with the same states -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351224957_Abiotic_Stress_Tolerant_Crop_Varieties_Livestock_Breeds_and_Fish_Species
- Institution listed as "Not specified" in the input record. Release date in the input (2010-12-23) differs from the 2011 year in the sources.
- Named breeder: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. An ICAR IIOR linseed page lists breeder and centre contacts, but it does not name JLS-73, so it is excluded under the strict relevance rule -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed

PUBLICATIONS
- Mane, P. A. (2022). Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal association with different cultivars of linseed in drought prone area. IJFANS, 11(12) -- https://ijfans.org/uploads/paper/44d1a9b8e41cd079600968587e2df7a6.pdf
- Authors not captured (2023/2024). Characterization of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini based on ITS and SSR markers and identification of resistance of Indian linseed. PMC -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Growth, Yield, Nutrient Uptake and Quality of Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) Varieties as Affected by Varying Sowing Dates. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328336019_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Uptake_and_Quality_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_Varieties_as_Affected_by_Varying_Sowing_Dates
- AICRP on Linseed, Varieties Released list (JLS 73, rainfed, 2011) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Molecular Advances to Combat Different Biotic and Abiotic Stresses in Linseed: A Comprehensive Review. PMC -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

SEED AVAILABILITY
- JLS 73 is among varieties whose breeder-seed indent and production share was tracked for 2007-08 to 2018-19, with a share of 4.8–7.6% -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/b37b/81289b537bdd60a2fba6aac040168c05a884.pdf
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales and private dealers: No evidence found for JLS-73. The only shop result (NY Spice Shop) is for generic flax seed.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Input record: Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bundelkhand UP, north-east and central Maharashtra, north-east Gujarat.
- DOD notified-variety table: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- AICRP list: Bundelkhand part of UP, Rajasthan and MP, rainfed, 2011 -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- JLS-79 (Seednet name): the DOD table lists JLS-79 as a separate entry for MP. A castor paper states JLS 79 was released in 2016, so it refers to a different variety. No evidence links JLS-79 to JLS-73 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353769937_Performance_of_elite_castor_Ricinus_communis_L_hybrids_and_varieties_under_rainfed_Alfisols
- No Seednet portal page was returned, so no evidence under the Seednet name for JLS-79 was found for this entry.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JLS-79 (linseed, variety code A0404091)

Names searched: "JLS-79" (CSC release name and Seednet name, which are identical). Variant spellings found in the evidence: "JLS 79" (AICRP table) and "Jawahar Linseed Sagar-79" (MDPI review). Four searches were run in total. Most results were about other linseed varieties or unrelated flax products, and those were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for JLS-79 was found. The only stress material was general linseed reviews that do not name JLS-79. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2023.1165580/full (general; does not name JLS-79)

DISEASE AND PEST
- AICRP table: JLS-79 is listed as irrigated, released 2016, for Madhya Pradesh, with a "highly resistant to Alternaria blight, resistant to powdery mildew, moderately resistant to bud fly" rating. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- DOD (Directorate of Oilseeds Development) table: JLS-79 is listed as resistant to rust, powdery mildew, wilt and bud fly. This conflicts with the AICRP table on bud fly and wilt ratings, and the AICRP table does not mention rust. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Field study of insect pests on JLS-79 at JNKVV College of Agriculture, Rewa, Madhya Pradesh (rabi 2020-21). Insect pests were identified on the crop in Rewa district. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342881084_Insect_herbivores_and_their_natural_enemies_in_linseed_and_their_population_dynamics
- Companion study of bud fly (Dasyneura lini) population dynamics, same JNKVV Rewa trial, names JLS-79. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/103-%20Studies%20on%20the%20Qualitative%20Composition%20of%20Insect%20Pests%20and%20Population%20Dynamics%20of%20Bud%20Fly%20(Dasyneura%20lini%20Barnes)%20on%20Linseed%20(Linum%20usitatissimum%20L.).pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield potential is listed as 36.85 in the DOD table and 38.82 in the AICRP table. Neither table states units. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx ; https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The AICRP table also gives an unlabelled oil figure of 45.10 and an iodine value of 165.49 for this variety. The label is unclear. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- DOD describes the variety as early to medium duration. No maturity days were found. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- The AICRP table describes the variety as suitable for intercropping with pulses. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No multi-location trial results specific to JLS-79 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC name "Kota Alsi-6" and the Seednet name "Kota Alsi" were both searched. The evidence found uses "Kota Alsi 6 (RL 13165)" (AICRP), "Kota Alsi-6" (Dholi seed directory), and "KOTA ALSI 6 (RL 13165)" (PMC review). No Seednet page was retrieved, so no evidence is attributed to the Seednet name directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Irrigated-condition classification with no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Listed among irrigated-condition varieties in a national linseed genetic-resources table. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence specific to Kota Alsi-6 found in the four searches.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rated moderately resistant to powdery mildew and moderately resistant to Alternaria blight. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Bud fly resistance is not stated for this entry; bud fly tolerance is attributed to the rainfed sister line Kota Barani Alsi 6 (RL 15584) on the same page, so it should not be assumed for Kota Alsi-6. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Early maturity. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Table row shows 1277 and 35.04 with no column labels; these are most likely mean seed yield (kg/ha) and oil content (%), but the page does not confirm this. Presented at Central 85th CVRC meeting. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No multi-location trial report specific to Kota Alsi-6 was found. The Kota-region sustainability-index study names other genotypes (PA-1, PA-2, KB-3, KB-4), not this variety. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019.v8.i4.8857/studies-on-sustainability-index-for-selecting-stable-genotypes-of-linseed-ltemgtlinum-usitatissimumltemgt-l-in-south-eastern-plain-zone-of-rajasthan

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree recorded as RLC 25127 x RL 26016. The input record says "Not specified", so this is a discrepancy to resolve against CSC minutes. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- No QTL, marker or genomic study naming this variety was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder or lead scientist name: No evidence found. Searches returned no named breeder.
- Developing institution: Agriculture University, Kota, which lists Kota Alsi 6 among linseed varieties released or identified in its assessment period, with the scientists credited with developing the technologies. -- https://www.aukota.org/notifications/21_SSR-Agriculture-University-Kota.pdf
- Notification: 2020, No. 3482 E, 7 October 2020 (the input release date is 9 November 2020; this discrepancy should be checked). -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- Station: Agriculture University, Kota, Rajasthan (linseed research station not named in the evidence). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture_University,_Kota

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute website: aukota.org. No official email, phone or postal address for the institute or linseed division was found in the retrieved pages. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture_University,_Kota
- Named officials (for reference only; the Wikipedia page lists two different vice-chancellors, Dinesh Chandra Joshi appointed 2019 and Dr. Vimla Dunkwal, so verify on aukota.org): not linked to this variety. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture_University,_Kota
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Molecular Advances to Combat Different Biotic and Abiotic Stresses in Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.): A Comprehensive Review. PMC review, which lists Kota Alsi 6 (RL 13165) with notification details -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- AICRP-Linseed. Varieties Released (national list entry for Kota Alsi 6 (RL 13165)). AICRP Linseed website -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh), AICRP annual report chapter or conference paper that names Kota Alsi-6 was found. Two Kota papers were excluded because they name other varieties, not this one.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Directorate of Seed, Dholi (Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University) listed Kota Alsi-6 among rabi seed availability for 2026-27, with quantity ranges shown (06-12, units not stated on page). -- https://rpcau.ac.in/directorate-of-seed-dholi/
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listings beyond Dholi: No evidence found. Flipkart, IndiaMART and Amazon listings are generic alsi/flaxseed products, not this variety, and were excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Irrigated; Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Assam. Matches the input list. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

pest_resistance.summary: Bud fly: described as resistant in the AICRP release entry and as tolerant in the release listing. No quantitative bud fly scores were found in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Sustainability-index study in the south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan: KB-3 yielded about 12.57 q/ha (approximately 1257 kg/ha). The AICRP release table lists figures of 1370 and 38.73 against this variety, but column headings were not captured, so their meaning (likely yield in kg/ha and oil percentage) is unconfirmed. The CSC average_yield field gives units only (Kg/Ha) with no value.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as rainfed and early-maturing, with moderate resistance to Alternaria blight and powdery mildew, plus bud fly tolerance -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Variety-specific abiotic stress data (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) were not found in the retrieved sources. -- No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- Reaction to Alternaria blight in coordinated IVT-Rainfed trials (2010-11) was recorded at several locations, with a mix of MR, MS, S and R scores -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281279219_Sunflower_genetic_resources_management_at_DOR
- Resistant to powdery mildew and bud fly, with the release table recording it as moderately resistant to Alternaria blight -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The AICRP release entry describes the seed as light brown and medium-sized, and lists resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew and bud fly -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini) reaction for this variety was not found. -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Seed rate and fertility level optimisation under rainfed conditions was tested in 2012-13 (seed yield table present, values not legible in the snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281279219_Sunflower_genetic_resources_management_at_DOR
- Sustainability-index study in the south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan: KB-3 yielded about 12.57 q/ha with a sustainability index of 89.79%, and was suggested as a breeding parent -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019.v8.i4.8857/studies-on-sustainability-index-for-selecting-stable-genotypes-of-linseed-ltemgtlinum-usitatissimumltemgt-l-in-south-eastern-plain-zone-of-rajasthan
- The AICRP release table lists figures of 1370 and 38.73 against this variety, but the column headings were not captured, so their meaning (likely yield in kg/ha and oil %) is unconfirmed -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No additional multi-location yield data for KB-3 beyond the above was found. -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- Kota Barani appears as a reference variety in an SSR-marker profiling study of Indian and exotic germplasm; this is not a QTL or variety-specific genetic study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327374930_Analysis_of_genetic_diversity_in_Indian_and_exotic_linseed_germplasm_and_identification_of_trait_specific_superior_accessions
- Parentage: not specified in the variety record. An ISOR table row reads "Kota Barani 2015 Triveni x RL-1011 Kota", but it cannot be confirmed as belonging to KB-3 -- https://isor.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/vol-33-1.pdf
- QTL or marker-trait association studies specific to KB-3: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Release listed under Rajasthan via State notification S.O. 2680(E) dated 01.10.2015, in the AICRP-Linseed varieties table (ICAR-IIOR network) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The DOR/IIOR (ICAR-Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research, Hyderabad, formerly Directorate of Oilseeds Research) publication carries the KB-3 trial data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281279219_Sunflower_genetic_resources_management_at_DOR
- Lead breeder for KB-3 at Agricultural Research Station, Kota: not named in retrieved sources. The AICRP contact page lists Dr. Sandhya Kulhari as "Junior linseed Breeder & In charge" at a Kota (AU) centre, but this does not establish her as the KB-3 breeder. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/contact-us-2/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. A.L. Rathnakumar, Project Investigator, Principal Scientist (Pl. Breeding), ICAR-IIOR, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500030; phone 040-24598137 (office), 09427229459 (mobile); email A.Rathnakumar@icar.gov.in -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/contact-us-2/ (institute-level/coordinator contact, not confirmed as the KB-3 breeder)
- Dr. Sandhya Kulhari, Junior Linseed Breeder & In-charge, AU Kota: name and role found; no phone or email captured -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/contact-us-2/
- Postal address of ICAR-IIOR: Rajendranagar, Hyderabad – 500 030 (the Krishi Bhavan address is ICAR HQ, New Delhi-110001) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/ and https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/contact-us-2/
- Seednet portal entry (name, code A0404085) was not retrieved. -- No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (2019). Studies on sustainability index for selecting stable genotypes of linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) in south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan. J Pharmacogn Phytochem 8(4):249-251 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019.v8.i4.8857/studies-on-sustainability-index-for-selecting-stable-genotypes-of-linseed-ltemgtlinum-usitatissimumltemgt-l-in-south-eastern-plain-zone-of-rajasthan
- Authors and year not captured (2015-2016). Sunflower genetic resources management at DOR. Report/ResearchGate record containing KB-3 seed-rate and Alternaria trial tables -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281279219_Sunflower_genetic_resources_management_at_DOR
- Authors not captured (2016-2017 era). Analysis of genetic diversity in Indian and exotic linseed germplasm and identification of trait specific superior accessions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327374930_Analysis_of_genetic_diversity_in_Indian_and_exotic_linseed_germplasm_and_identification_of_trait_specific_superior_accessions
- AICRP-Linseed varieties released table (ICAR, 2018 copyright) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No KrishiKosh thesis or ICAR annual report specific to KB-3 was retrieved. -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet portal listing (code A0404085) not retrieved; no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing for KB-3 found. Search results returned only consumer linseed oil and flaxseed products, which are not relevant. -- No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Rajasthan, rainfed, released 2015 (State notification) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

NAME NOTE
- The CSC name "Kota Barani Alsi-3" (hyphen) matches the Seednet name given. The AICRP table writes it as "Kota Barani Alsi 3 (RL 29202)"; all evidence above refers to this same variety under that spelling.

No evidence found. The search for stress tolerance returned only a general review of linseed abiotic and biotic stress that does not tie specific tolerances to this variety. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

DISEASE AND PEST
Bud fly (Pest): A bud fly germplasm screening study lists "Aparna (LCK 1611)" among tested linseed entries, with a row of values and a code of "R" beside it. The snippets do not show what the "R" code means or which bud fly parameter the values measure, so I cannot confirm a resistance rating. -- https://mbi-prh.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2025/JANUARY/10_Jan_2025/2024_UPJOZ_4401/Ms_UPJOZ_4401.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389249120_Article_noUPJOZ4401_Original_Research_Article_Kumari_et_al
Disease: No evidence found for rust, wilt, powdery mildew or alternaria blight reaction specific to this variety. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity, yield, sowing and fertility: No evidence found for this variety. The only general yield and sowing figures located were for linseed as a crop, not this variety. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/775018291/Crop-production-pdf
Dwarf habit: A crop production note lists "Aparna" as a dwarf variety under canning-type linseed. This is a low-reliability, unreferenced course-style document and the snippet does not state the source of the classification. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/775018291/Crop-production-pdf
Field trial/bud fly screening: The bud fly germplasm screening entries above include Aparna (LCK 1611) in a multi-genotype test. Trial location, season and replication were not shown in the snippets. -- https://mbi-prh.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2025/JANUARY/10_Jan_2025/2024_UPJOZ_4401/Ms_UPJOZ_4401.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The review and other pages discuss linseed genomics and marker-assisted or genomic selection in general, with no QTL, marker or pedigree data tied to LCK 1611 or Aparna. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
Parentage: No evidence found; the variety record also says "Not specified".

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Release/notification: A linseed review lists "APARNA (LCK1611)" with release in 2020 and a notification dated 29 January 2021 (number shown as "500 E"). This is the only snippet that names this variety with release data. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The breeder search returned unrelated pages on linseed and flax.
Developing institution: The institution CSAUA&T is from the input record only. No search result confirmed the developing institution or station. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/ (does not name the breeder)

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute page, email, phone, or postal address for this variety was returned by any search.

PUBLICATIONS
Kumari et al. (year not shown in snippets; document dated January 2025). Screening of Linseed Germplasm against Bud Fly. UPJOZ (journal abbreviation as shown in the manuscript) -- https://mbi-prh.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2025/JANUARY/10_Jan_2025/2024_UPJOZ_4401/Ms_UPJOZ_4401.pdf ; DOI not found; ResearchGate record: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389249120_Article_noUPJOZ4401_Original_Research_Article_Kumari_et_al
Authors not shown (year not shown). Molecular Advances to Combat Different Biotic and Abiotic Stresses in Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.): A Comprehensive Review. Journal not confirmed in snippet (PMC indexed) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/ ; DOI not found in snippet.
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report, or conference paper on this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed search returned only unrelated flax fibre pages. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was found. Seednet listing: not retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found in search results. The states "Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana" come from the input record only and are not confirmed by any search result.

Searches run: 4 (variety release and traits; breeder; research; seed availability). Name checked: "LCK 1611 (Aparna)". The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical, so one search set covered both. The review that names "APARNA (LCK1611)" is the only source matching the release-minute name.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to LSL-93. The PMC review lists LSL93 among rainfed-condition varieties but gives no tolerance data, so this is not evidence of drought tolerance.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to LSL-93.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to LSL-93.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to LSL-93.

disease_resistance.summary: Listed as moderately resistant to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew, wilt, rust and bud fly on the DOD notified-variety table (Maharashtra). This conflicts with a 2022-23 Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini screen in which LSL-93 was graded 4 (susceptible, 30.1-50% wilt incidence). The wilt rating therefore cannot be resolved from the digest; the screen result is the more specific evidence. Resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew and rust has no additional independent evidence in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Bud fly (Dasyneura lini): LSL 93 (ZC) is listed in the group rated moderately resistant (>10-25% damage) in a 2025 journal PDF screening. The snippet is partial, so this is indicative only. The DOD table also lists moderate resistance to bud fly. No other pest evidence was found.

agronomic_details.yield: DOD notified-variety table lists a yield potential of 37.95 (unit not shown in the snippet). Nagaland irrigated foothill trial: 671.33 kg/ha seed yield (lowest of seven varieties tested). Latur College of Agriculture, Rabi 2023-24 nano-urea and phosphorus foliar trial: seed yield across treatments 890.31 to 1401.22 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability analysis for LSL-93 was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Released at Latur, Maharashtra (DOD notified table). The PMC review lists LSL93 among rainfed-condition varieties. Tested under irrigated foothill conditions in Nagaland. No formal agro-climatic adaptation statement was found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 132.19 days to physiological maturity in a germplasm evaluation (2,576 accessions, two seasons, ICAR-NBPGR and Akola), where LSL93 was the best check for earliness. In the Nagaland irrigated foothill trial, 50% flowering occurred at 65 days, the earliest of the varieties tested.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Nagaland irrigated foothill trial: fewest capsules per plant (29.13), lowest oil yield among the seven varieties, highest test weight (9.08 g). Parentage, morphology and plant height were not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Nagaland irrigated foothill trial, seven varieties including LSL-93: LSL-93 had the lowest seed yield (671.33 kg/ha), fewest capsules per plant (29.13) and lowest oil yield, but the highest test weight (9.08 g) and earliest 50% flowering (65 days). (2) Nagaland University, Medziphema trial: the authors' conclusions on LSL-93 are not in the snippets, so no finding is available. (3) Fertilizer-level trial with LSL-93, RLC-148 and NL-260 under NPK levels 0-30:30:30 kg/ha: LSL-93 was the reference variety and differed from the others in growth and yield; NL-260 was at par except for oil content. Location and year not captured. (4) Latur College of Agriculture, Rabi 2023-24 nano-urea and phosphorus foliar trial on LSL-93: seed yield 890.31 to 1401.22 kg/ha across treatments; protein 18.6-28.54%. (5) Germplasm evaluation (2,576 accessions, two seasons, ICAR-NBPGR and Akola): LSL93 used as best check for earliness, 132.19 days to physiological maturity.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed under moderate resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew, wilt, rust and bud fly on the DOD notified-variety table, with a yield potential of 37.95 (unit not shown in the snippet) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
In a 2022-23 Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini screen, LSL-93 was graded 4 (susceptible, 30.1-50% wilt incidence), which conflicts with the DOD "moderately resistant to wilt" entry -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to LSL-93. The PMC review lists LSL93 among rainfed-condition varieties, but gives no tolerance data -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderate resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew, wilt, rust and bud fly (DOD notified table, Maharashtra) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Wilt susceptibility in the Fusarium screen (grade 4) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
Bud fly screening (Dasyneura lini) lists "LSL 93 (ZC)" in the group rated moderately resistant (>10-25% damage). The snippet is partial and the source is a 2025 journal PDF, so treat it as indicative -- https://mbi-prh.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2025/JANUARY/10_Jan_2025/2024_UPJOZ_4401/Ms_UPJOZ_4401.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Nagaland irrigated foothill trial, seven varieties including LSL-93: LSL-93 had the lowest seed yield (671.33 kg/ha), fewest capsules per plant (29.13) and lowest oil yield, but the highest test weight (9.08 g) and earliest 50% flowering (65 days) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6060 and https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6042
Nagaland University, Medziphema trial: the authors' conclusions on LSL-93 are not in the snippets (listed under the same trial; no separate finding) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6042
Fertilizer-level trial with LSL-93, RLC-148 and NL-260 under NPK levels 0-30:30:30 kg/ha; LSL-93 was the reference variety and differed from the others in growth and yield, with NL-260 at par except for oil content. Location and year not captured -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=2&ArticleId=10545
Latur College of Agriculture, Rabi 2023-24, nano-urea and phosphorus foliar trial on LSL-93: seed yield across treatments ranged from 890.31 to 1401.22 kg/ha, protein 18.6-28.54% -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue11S/PartE/S-8-11-54-195.pdf
Germplasm evaluation (2,576 accessions, two seasons, ICAR-NBPGR and Akola): LSL93 used as the best check for earliness, with 132.19 days to physiological maturity -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-71044-8

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL or marker-trait associations specific to LSL-93. The Nature 2024 germplasm study and the Fusarium SSR study use LSL93 only as a check or differential entry, not as a genetic study of the variety -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-71044-8 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
No parentage found. The task form lists "Not specified", and no source gave it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Released centre listed as Latur on the DOD notified table (2019), with the notification recorded as 2019 S.O. 3220(E), 5 September 2019 in the PMC review. Developing institution given in the task record: VNMKV, Oilseeds Research Station (Latur) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
No evidence found naming the lead breeder or scientist(s) for LSL-93. The ICAR-IIOR linseed page lists breeder posts and centre vacancies, but does not name LSL-93 or its developers -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed
ICAR Nagaland scientist Dr Harendra Verma recommended LSL-93 for seed purposes in an extension report. He is not identified as a breeder of this variety -- https://www.morungexpress.com/icar-nagaland-centre-conducts-workshop-on-promoting-oilseeds

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for an email, phone, postal address or institute contact page specific to LSL-93 or the VNMKV Oilseeds Research Station, Latur.
Not attributed to this variety: the PDKV AICRP linseed breeder entry (Nagpur, phone 0712-2541245) at http://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/aicrp-linseed.htm is a different AICRP centre and is not evidence for LSL-93.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not captured (2025). Screening of Linseed Germplasm against Bud Fly (Dasyneura lini). Journal of Plant Protection/UPJOZ manuscript (PDF) -- https://mbi-prh.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2025/JANUARY/10_Jan_2025/2024_UPJOZ_4401/Ms_UPJOZ_4401.pdf
Authors not captured (year not captured). Molecular Advances to Combat Different Biotic and Abiotic Stresses in Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.): A Comprehensive Review. PMC review -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
Authors not captured (year not captured). Characterization of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini based on ITS and SSR Markers and identification of resistance of Indian Linseed to Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini. PMC -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
Authors not captured (2024). Effect of foliar application of nano-urea on growth, yield ... (linseed, Latur, Rabi 2023-24). Biochemistry journal (Biochem Journal, vol. 8, issue 11S) -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue11S/PartE/S-8-11-54-195.pdf
Authors not captured (2022). Response of different linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) varieties to fertilizer levels. The Pharma Innovation Journal, 11(2) -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=2&ArticleId=10545
Authors not captured (year not captured). Performance of Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) Varieties in Foothills of Nagaland under Irrigated Condition. Indian Journal of Agricultural Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6060
Authors not captured (year not captured). Yield Attributes and Economics of Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) Cultivars under Irrigated Uphill Condition of Indian Himalayan Region in Nagaland. Agricultural Science Digest -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6042
Authors not captured (2024). Leveraging genetic resource diversity and identification of trait-enriched superior genotypes for accelerated improvement in linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.). Scientific Reports -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-71044-8
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report or ICAR report naming LSL-93 was found in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, a KVK, an SAU or a dealer for LSL-93. The results were retail flax/linseed packets from overseas shops (UK and US) and cover-crop sellers, which are unrelated to this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Maharashtra -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx (DOD notified table, released at Latur)

Search note: four web searches were run (variety/release, breeder/institution/contact, research papers, seed availability). The variety name and Seednet name are identical ("LSL-93"), so no name-variant split was needed.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Listed as moderately resistant to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew, wilt, rust and bud fly on the DOD notified-variety table (Maharashtra). This conflicts with a 2022-23 Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini screen in which LSL-93 was graded 4 (susceptible, 30.1-50% wilt incidence). The wilt rating therefore cannot be resolved from the digest; the screen result is the more specific evidence. Resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew and rust has no additional independent evidence in the digest.

drought.details: No specific drought tolerance level for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified in the provided results. Linseed generally experiences drought as a major abiotic stress, and research aims to develop drought-resilient varieties through multi-environment phenotyping and molecular studies. Pratap Alsi-2, a different variety, is noted as tolerant to drought. (Results 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 31, 32, 37, 38, 40, 43)

heat.details: No specific information on heat tolerance for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified. Elevated temperature (heat stress) is reported to impact Linum usitatissimum production. (Result 19)

salinity.details: No specific salinity tolerance level for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified, though 'Pratap Alsi-1 (RLU-6)' was part of studies involving treatment with neutral salt and alkaline conditions. Salinity is a known detrimental constraint for flax (linseed) production, and research focuses on identifying salinity-tolerant genotypes for breeding. (Results 3, 10, 21, 22, 24, 25, 29, 34)

flood.details: No specific information on flood tolerance for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified. Pratap Alsi-2, a different variety, is noted as tolerant to both submergence and drought. (Result 43)

agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record adaptation_ecology: Chhattisgarh and Odisha, where moisture is available in the field of medium to late duration rice varieties; utera (under moisture stress), rabi season, and rice-based relay cropping ecosystem. The rice-fallow listing (see field_trials) supports suitability for rice-fallow cultivation in eastern India. agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Nutrient-level (RDF) study with five linseed varieties (RLC-92, RLC-133, RLC-138, RLC-143, RLC-148): the snippet reports RLC-138 among the best-performing entries for yield and cost, but table values are fragmentary and unit-labelled unclearly, so no quantitative result is reported. (2) Rice-fallow cultivation: RLC-138 listed among linseed cultivars judged promising for rice-fallow cultivation in eastern India, alongside RLC-143 and BAU 06-03; no yield data given. (3) Bud fly screen at Bihar AU Sabour (150 germplasm lines, rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24): RLC-138 moderately resistant, with bud fly infestation in the >10-25% range. (4) Bold-seeded genetic variability study (Markandey et al., 2022): RLC-138 used as one of five checks among 40 bold-seeded genotypes, rabi 2021-22; no RLC-138 result reported. The cluster-mean maturity table in that paper is not variety-specific and was discarded. (5) Association analysis study (2024): RLC-138 listed as a check from AICRP Linseed IGKV, rabi 2022-23; no RLC-138 result reported. (6) Characterisation of 23 IGKV released varieties (Acharya et al., 2023), rabi 2022-23: RLC-138 among varieties characterised; no result reported.
