search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RLC 164 (linseed / ALSI)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "RLC 164". The AICRP page writes it as "RLC-164", and I treated that as the same variety. No search returned a Seednet portal page, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found. Four searches were run, one per topic plus one extra for seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The AICRP release table classes RLC-164 as rainfed, not irrigated or utera -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to RLC 164. A general statement that linseed is drought tolerant was found, but it is not about this variety, so I discarded it -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4912539/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Under artificial conditions it is moderately resistant to Alternaria blight and moderately susceptible to powdery mildew. Under natural conditions it is moderately resistant to Alternaria blight and to bud fly -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Same table text also contains "highly resistant to Alternaria blight, resistant to powdery mildew, moderately resistant to bud fly". The snippet does not clearly tie this to the RLC-164 row, so it is unverified -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Bud fly resistance is noted in the same source. No separate bud fly trial data for RLC 164 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The AICRP row gives RLC-164's release details (CVRC 2020) alongside two unlabelled numbers, 1161 and 32.6. The column headers are not visible in the snippet, so I cannot assign them to yield, maturity or oil content -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No evidence found for field-trial or multi-location yield results for RLC 164. The Chhattisgarh sowing-date trial tested RLC-92, not RLC 164, so I discarded it -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025.v8.i9.M.3881
- The IGKV 2023 genetic analysis study names RLC-92, RLC-133 and RLC-143 only, so I discarded it -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2023&vol=12&issue=6&ArticleId=21111

GENETICS AND QTL
- RLC 164 is listed among national linseed genetic resources in a seed-type table. This is a germplasm listing, not a genetic study -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- RLC-164 appears in a DUS descriptor context, with stigma-position and related trait groupings in the linseed variety characterisation -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue8/PartZ/12-7-733-170.pdf
- No QTL or marker study specific to RLC 164 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety is attributed to Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur. This comes from the input record. The AICRP release row retrieved does not show the institution name in the visible text -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The IGKV Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Raipur is the institute-level unit that works on linseed. No lead breeder name for RLC 164 was found -- https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301
- The Chhattisgarh linen-fibre paper lists RLC 164 among seven recent IGKV-linked varieties released after 2012, but it does not name a breeder -- https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder name, official email, phone or contact-page URL for RLC 164 was found.
- Institute-level address only: Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur-492 012 (Chhattisgarh), India -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-8-2-001

- Individual authors' names on other IGKV papers were not attributed to this variety.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not retrieved (2023). Title not retrieved. The Pharma Innovation Journal 12(8): 2203-2206. Mentions RLC-164 in a DUS descriptor context for IGKV-released linseed varieties -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue8/PartZ/12-7-733-170.pdf
- No DOI or full bibliographic record was retrieved for this item. Its author list must be confirmed from the journal before citing.
- No ICAR/AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or peer-reviewed field paper specific to RLC 164 was found. Other linseed papers and a KrishiKosh budfly thesis were retrieved but do not name RLC 164, so I discarded them.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for RLC 164.
- The results were non-Indian linseed sellers and a Scribd Rabi 2025-26 tentative seed availability document. The visible text of that document did not name RLC 164, so I discarded it -- https://www.scribd.com/document/902605334/Rabi-2025-26-Seed-Availability-Tentative

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for RLC 167 specifically. The four searches returned only generic linseed drought material and studies of other varieties (e.g., RLC-92, RLC-148, RLC-153), which I discarded. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

DISEASE AND PEST
- The AICRP-Linseed varieties-released table lists RLC-167 and attaches a rating that it is highly resistant to Alternaria blight, resistant to powdery mildew, and moderately resistant to bud fly. The rating text sits in a fragmented table, so it may not be cleanly tied to this row and should be checked against the source PDF. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found. The agronomy and trial papers retrieved (PGR foliar sprays, weed control at IGKV Raipur) do not name RLC 167. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137093 ; https://igkv.ac.in/__files/JAI/1/Journal_pub_1__uctfbwn0aq54uzg3dmwcx50h_202204051610516PM046.pdf
- No yield, maturity, or oil data specific to RLC 167 was found. The AICRP table has a fragment with "(45.10)" and "Iodine Value-165.49" that might belong to this row, but it cannot be confirmed. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The retrieved genetics studies used other crosses (e.g., RLC-95 x Indira alsi-32) and do not involve RLC 167. -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-8-2-001

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The retrieved sources give no named breeder or lead scientist for RLC 167. The variety is attributed to Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur, Chhattisgarh, as stated in the release record. Institute-level evidence: IGKV reports that it has released 16 linseed varieties, with RLC 161, RLC 164 and RLC 167 among the seven most recent (released after 2012). -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue3/PartK/8-4-8-452.pdf ; https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301
- IGKV's linseed work sits in the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Raipur, which hosts an AICRP on Linseed research farm. -- https://www.chemistryjournals.net/archives/2022/vol4issue2/PartA/4-2-50-637.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level only; no breeder contact found)
- Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Krishak Nagar, Raipur-492012 (C.G.). Telephone directory 2026: IPRO Office 0771-2443220, ipro@igkv.ac.in; Directorate of Extension Services des@igkv.ac.in. -- https://igkv.ac.in/images/Telephone_Directory2025.pdf
- Telephone directory 2021 (older listing): Office 0771-2443419, Fax 91-771-2442302, website www.igau.edu.in, email vcigkv@gmail.com, pa2vc.igkv@gmail.com. These may be superseded. -- https://igkv.ac.in/images/tp2021.pdf
- Journal of Agricultural Issues editorial office: jai@igkv.ac.in, Telefax 0771-2972070, website https://igkv.ac.in/ . -- https://igkv.ac.in/__files/JAI/1/Journal_pub_1__uctfbwn0aq54uzg3dmwcx50h_202204051610516PM046.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Pharma Innovation Journal 2023, 12(8): 2203-2206. Study of IGKV Raipur linseed genotypes in Rabi 2022-23, in which RLC-167 appears among the genotypes and in colour and seed-trait groupings. Authors not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue8/PartZ/12-7-733-170.pdf
- Indian Journal-style list (Biochem journal, IJABR 2024; 8(3): 968-970). Mentions RLC 167 only in a list of IGKV releases; not a trial on this variety. Authors not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue3/PartK/8-4-8-452.pdf
- International Journal of Fiber and Innovative Hybrid Materials (inence), charkha paper. Lists RLC 167 among IGKV releases only. Authors not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301
- Note: The Pharma Journal 2023 (12(6)) and IJCMAS 2022 papers name other IGKV genotypes but not RLC 167, so I excluded them. No peer-reviewed trial or thesis on RLC 167 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. Seednet and seed-dealer sources were not returned by the search. The results included a National Seed Project at IGKV Raipur (Badshahbhoge), but no page links it to RLC 167, so it is not listed as a source. -- https://cgcert.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/List-of-Individual-Producer.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The AICRP-Linseed table lists RLC-167 as irrigated, released by CVRC 2020 (85th CVRC), for Jammu, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Chhattisgarh. The source says "Jammu", not "Jammu & Kashmir" as recorded in the input. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

NAME CHECK
- variety_name ("RLC 167") and seednet_variety_name ("RLC 167") are identical. The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved, so all evidence above refers to the AICRP/IGKV name "RLC-167" or "RLC 167" and has not been checked against Seednet.

drought.details: A Patna Press article (BAU Best AICRP-Linseed award, 2024-25) describes Sabour Tisei-4 as drought-tolerant and suited to climate-change adaptation. The article uses the spelling 'Sabour Tisei-4' and gives no BRLS code, although the digest treats it as this variety. This is a press claim, not peer-reviewed data, and no quantitative drought trial data, physiological mechanism, or yield-under-stress result was found for Tisi-4.

heat.details: The same Patna Press article describes Sabour Tisei-4 as heat-tolerant. This is an unverified press claim, not peer-reviewed data. No quantitative heat trial data, sowing-date response, or physiological mechanism specific to Tisi-4 was found.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in the digest.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance is credited to Sabour Tisi-4 in any source in the digest. The Patna Press article attributes Alternaria blight and powdery mildew tolerance to Sabour Tisei-3, not Tisi-4. No evidence was found for resistance to any disease in BRLS 121 / Tisi-4.

pest_resistance.summary: Bud fly: Kumari et al. (2024) screened 150 linseed genotypes at BAU Sabour farm (rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24). BRLS 121 appears in a 28-entry list of germplasm, but the snippet does not state its reaction (resistant or susceptible). Status is unresolved. No other pest resistance evidence was found.

agronomic_details.yield: The original variety data lists an average yield of 13 quintal/ha. The digest does not independently confirm this value. It states that the BAU yield values in the sources refer to other entries. No Tisi-4-specific yield data was found in the digest.

SABOUR TISI-4 (BRLS 121) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The release-minutes name and the Seednet name are both given as "Sabour Tisi-4 (BRLS 121)". I did not reach the Seednet portal, so all evidence below is from the release-notification press coverage and BAU documents. Under "Sabour Tisei-4", the Patna Press article uses a spelling variant of the same name. Those mentions refer to this variety, but the article gives no BRLS code.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Patna Press article (BAU Best AICRP-Linseed award, 2024-25) describes Sabour Tisei-4 as drought- and heat-tolerant and suited to climate-change adaptation. This is a press claim, not peer-reviewed data. -- https://patnapress.com/bau-sabour-best-linseed-centre-award-2024-25/
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Salinity, flood, submergence, and waterlogging tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- The same Patna Press article attributes Alternaria blight and powdery mildew tolerance to Sabour Tisei-3, not Tisi-4. No disease resistance is credited to Tisi-4 in any source. -- https://patnapress.com/bau-sabour-best-linseed-centre-award-2024-25/
DISEASE AND PEST -- Bud fly: Kumari et al. (2024) screened 150 linseed genotypes at BAU Sabour farm (rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24) for bud fly reaction. BRLS 121 appears in a 28-entry list of germplasm, but the snippet does not state its reaction (resistant or susceptible). Treat as unresolved. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389249120_Article_noUPJOZ4401_Original_Research_Article_Kumari_et_al

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- BRLS 121 and BRLS 110-4 were promoted from IVT irrigated to AVT 1st year irrigated in AICRP trials (rabi 2019-20). -- https://bausabour.ac.in/album/File104_12_202311_41_57PIMG1.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maturity, grain yield, oil content, and sowing-date response for Tisi-4 specifically: No evidence found. The BAU yield values in the sources refer to other entries.

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage "(NL 260 x Shekhar) x PKDL 71" was not verified in any search result. Shekhar appears only as a zonal check in the Kumari et al. bud-fly trial. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389249120_Article_noUPJOZ4401_Original_Research_Article_Kumari_et_al
GENETICS AND QTL -- QTL, marker, or genomic-selection studies specific to BRLS 121: No evidence found. The Patna Press article mentions genomic selection in general terms for BAU varieties, not for this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Sabour Til-1 (BRT-04), Sesame

Name check: The CSC/release name is "Sabour Til-1" and the variety code is BRT-04. The Seednet name is unknown and was not found, so all evidence below refers to "Sabour Til-1" (BRT-04). Searches for "Sabour-1" returned a makhana variety and a different garlic variety; both were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Heat tolerant, and can be grown in summer season; the ICAR report lists it as suitable for irrigated rabi/summer conditions -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
- Drought, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The 2025 stability paper reports yield stability across Sabour, Purnea and Patna, but not stress tolerance -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/36

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to Macrophomina stem rot, root rot, Alternaria leaf spot, Cercospora leaf spot and phyllody -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average seed yield of about 9.9 q/ha and maturity of 84-90 days, with irrigated rabi/summer suitability -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
- In a 22-genotype stability trial at three sites in 2024 and 2025 (BAC Sabour, BPSAC Purnea, ARI Patna), this variety's seed yield per plant was above the population mean, and its regression coefficient exceeded 1 (indicating above-average response to environment) -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/36 (DOI 10.37992/2025.1603.038)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage, breeding method, and genome resources: No evidence found. The only code linked to the variety is BRT-04, from the ICAR report -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
- Release year: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The 2025 stability paper lists Dinkar, Sima Sinha, Mankesh Kumar, Ravi Ranjan Kumar, A.K. Singh, Fozia Homa and Namrata Dwivedi as authors of the trial that includes this variety. This is the closest evidence of who worked on it, but no page names them as its breeders -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/36
- The institution is Bihar Agricultural University (BAU), Sabour, which runs the AICRP on Sesame there. The 2022-23 BAU report lists the sesame AICRP at Sabour under Dr. Sima Sinha, but does not name this variety -- https://bausabour.ac.in/album/File117_04_202309_57_08PIMG1.pdf
- Lead breeder name specific to this variety: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level: Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour, Bhagalpur-813210, Bihar (postal address as printed on the BAU webinar publication) -- https://www.bausabour.ac.in/album/File111_05_202101_12_08PIMG1.pdf
- Official email, phone and breeder contact: No evidence found. Only the BAU domain (bausabour.ac.in) appeared in results; no contact page URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Dinkar, Sinha, S., Kumar, M., Kumar, R.R., Singh, A.K., Homa, F., & Dwivedi, N. (2025). Stability analysis for yield and its component traits in sesame (Sesamum indicum L.) genotypes. Ejplantbreeding (EJPB) -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/36 ; DOI: 10.37992/2025.1603.038
- Indian Council of Agricultural Research (2025). Annual Report 2024-25 (sesame variety table entry for Sabour Til-1, BRT-04) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
- Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour (2023). Annual Report 2022-23 (AICRP on Sesame entry, no variety named) -- https://bausabour.ac.in/album/File117_04_202309_57_08PIMG1.pdf
- Peer-reviewed field-trial papers, KrishiKosh theses, AICRP sesame reports naming this variety, and QTL/marker studies: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or dealer listings for Sabour Til-1: No evidence found. The search returned only retail white and black sesame (til) food products on Amazon.in and other shops, which are unrelated to this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh, per the ICAR 2024-25 report -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for irrigated condition of Zone-II of linseed growing area of India which includes states of Uttar Pradesh Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Assam and Nagaland.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: i.	Lodging/Shattering: Noon lodging and non Shattering. ii.	Fertilizer: Responsive to recommended doses of Fertilizers. iii.	Suitability: Suitable for timely sown (last week of October first week of November) RDF in irrigated condition. iv.	Spacing: 25-30 cm R-R
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Flower shape-Funnel, petel aestivation-Valvate, stamen-colorless, flower size-medium.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: TL 99 showed resistance to wilt & rust; whereas moderately susceptible to alternaria blight & powdery mildew under Unifom Disease Nursey Trial under natural condition.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Modertaely resisatnce to linseed bud fly in breeding trials.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Fertilizer with 40:20:20kg/ha, N,P&K receptively at the Basal application. *Phosphors should be applied through single phosphors. Foliar sprya of ura (2%) at pre flowering stage.

drought.details: TL 99 is identified as a drought tolerant linseed variety, showing moisture stress tolerance. It has been studied under rainfed moisture stress conditions to assess its drought tolerant morpho-physiological traits and is also noted for its tolerance to low moisture stress.

heat.details: The variety exhibits tolerance to heat stress, showing better stress tolerance indices. It is specifically mentioned to be tolerant to high temperature at the time of sowing and is generally resilient to environmental stresses including heat.

salinity.details: TL 99 shows good salinity tolerance, described as fairly tolerant to salinity. It is tolerant to salinity at the time of sowing and has been screened after treatment with neutral salt and alkaline conditions.

flood.details: Na

disease_resistance.summary: TL 99 exhibits tolerance to necrosis disease and is broadly described as resistant/tolerant to various diseases.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety shows resistance/tolerance to pests, consistent with attributes of recently released BARC varieties.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yield ranges from 1300-1400 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: While specific stability data is not provided, its recommendation across multiple states (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Assam, Nagaland) suggests adaptability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for timely sowing (last week of October to first week of November) with Recommended Dose of Fertilizers (RDF) under irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: TL 99 is non-lodging and non-shattering. It is responsive to recommended doses of fertilizers, with a recommended row-to-row spacing of 25-30 cm. It features a black seed coat and recorded high protein (27.72 g/100g) and total ash (4.55 g/100g) content.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been studied under rainfed moisture stress conditions. It is considered a promising edible quality linseed (LINOLA) and has been used in efforts to develop low ALA edible grade linseed oil.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Molecular analysis for identification of molecular markers, specifically involving FAD3A and FAD3B genes, has been conducted for TL 99.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs are identified in the provided search results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: TL 99 possesses a unique fatty acid composition, notably having very low linolenic acid (2-5%) and being recognized as the first low ALA (<5%) variety in India. It also has Linoleic Acid at 58.9%. Molecular analysis with FAD3A and FAD3B genes is linked to developing its low ALA edible grade linseed oil.

drought.details: No drought trial data specific to DHLM-28-4 was found. The only related evidence is species-level: little millet (Panicum sumatrense) as a species is reported to tolerate drought, salinity and waterlogging. This is not specific to DHLM-28-4 and cannot be attributed to the variety.

heat.details: No heat stress trial or evidence specific to DHLM-28-4 was found in the digest.

salinity.details: No salinity trial data specific to DHLM-28-4 was found. Species-level reports indicate little millet tolerates salinity; this is not variety-specific.

flood.details: No flood trial data specific to DHLM-28-4 was found. Species-level reports indicate little millet tolerates waterlogging; this is not variety-specific.

disease_resistance.summary: No specific disease is named as resisted by DHLM-28-4 in any source. A ResearchGate-hosted promotional page describes the variety as having pest and disease resilience, without field data. A popular-science article claims natural resistance to pests and diseases without naming pathogens. The same ResearchGate source mentions strong resistance to an unnamed pest or disease, but the text is truncated and the target is unverified.

pest_resistance.summary: Shoot fly (Atherigona species) is the only pest named. The ResearchGate source describes DHLM-28-4 as shoot-fly resistant and reports a shoot-fly tolerance figure of 19.42%, but the source does not clarify the scoring basis and is a promotional page without field data. An ICAR/AICRP proceedings report gives the peak shoot-fly timing in small millets (second half of August screening window); it does not provide resistance data for DHLM-28-4.

agronomic_details.yield: Input record gives 7.00 to 7.70 Kg/Ha. The ResearchGate-hosted source reports grain yield of 17.14 q/ha (about 1,714 kg/ha) and fodder yield of 6.5 t/ha. The input value and the reported grain yield differ by roughly two orders of magnitude and the input unit appears inconsistent with the source; this discrepancy is unresolved.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location or multi-year stability analysis was found. Evaluation years are given as 2013-2014 by one source.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Andhra Pradesh per the input record and the global-agriculture.com source. No agro-climatic analysis beyond these state listings was found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: Grain yield exceeded national checks OLM-203 and JK-8 by 9.59% and 11.21% respectively in one passage of the ResearchGate-hosted source. The same source gives 11.95% over OLM-203 in another passage, so the check margins are internally inconsistent. Evaluation years are given as 2013-2014. Maturity of 85-90 days is reported by the nutrichemsci.com article, which conflicts with the 114-116 day input value. The release year reported by the ResearchGate-hosted source is 2021, which conflicts with the 2023 input release year. No multi-location trial data beyond these summary figures was found.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL or mapping study specific to DHLM-28-4 was found. A chromosome-scale little millet genome paper reports species-level genomic resources and GWAS on micronutrient traits, not on this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DHLM-28-4 (LMV 513) -- little millet (Panicum sumatrense) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The CSC minutes name and the Seednet name are both "DHLM-28-4 (LMV 513)", so all evidence below refers to that name. No Seednet portal page was retrieved, so Seednet-specific fields (crop name, notification details) are unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Little millet as a species is reported to tolerate drought, salinity and waterlogging; this is species-level, not specific to DHLM-28-4 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12769566/
- A study reports the variety maintaining a shoot-fly tolerance figure of 19.42%; the source does not clarify the scoring basis -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence trial data specific to DHLM-28-4 was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The variety is described as shoot-fly resistant and as having pest and disease resilience, though the source is a promotional page without field data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- A popular-science article claims natural resistance to pests and diseases without naming pathogens or pests -- https://www.nutrichemsci.com/posts/lmv513-the-little-millet-revolutionizing-climateresilient-agriculture
- The same ResearchGate source mentions strong resistance to an unnamed pest/disease, but the text is truncated, so the target is unverified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- ICAR/AICRP reporting on shoot-fly peak timing in small millets (second half of August screening window) -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/AGM2022-AICRP_on_Sorghum_and_Small_millets-Proceedings.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity of 85-90 days is reported -- https://www.nutrichemsci.com/posts/lmv513-the-little-millet-revolutionizing-climateresilient-agriculture
- Grain yield 17.14 q/ha and fodder yield 6.5 t/ha are reported -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- Grain yield exceeded national checks OLM-203 and JK-8 by 9.59% and 11.21% respectively in one passage; the same source gives 11.95% over OLM-203 in another passage, so the check margins are inconsistent -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- Evaluation years are given as 2013-2014 for the variety; release/notification is said to be 2021 by this source, which conflicts with the 2023 CSC release -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- Multi-location trial data beyond the summary figures above was not found -- No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker-assisted or mapping study specific to DHLM-28-4 was found -- No evidence found.
- Parentage/pedigree of DHLM-28-4 is not given in any source (the input record also says "Not specified") -- No evidence found.
- A chromosome-scale little millet genome paper provides species-level genomic resources and GWAS on micronutrient traits, not on this variety -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-66716-6
- A little millet transcriptome database (LMTdb) exists, but it is based on a different genotype (RLM-37) -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10041709/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released as an open-pollinated variety by the Central Sub-committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties (CSC) (notified by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/little-millet-variety-dhlm-28-4-lmv-513/
- Developing institution: University of Agricultural Sciences, Dharwad, Agricultural Research Station, Hanumanamatti -- https://www.nutrichemsci.com/posts/lmv513-the-little-millet-revolutionizing-climateresilient-agriculture
- The ResearchGate page credits "Jakir Hussain K N" with the breeding text; this is a page credit, not a verified lead-breeder attribution -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- Nagappa Govankoppa, Small Millets Breeder & Head, Fodder Research & Production Unit, MARS, UAS Dharwad, is named as a small millet breeder but not as the DHLM-28-4 breeder -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue1/PartA/7-1-21-828.pdf
- Lead breeder for DHLM-28-4 (LMV 513): not verified -- No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email or phone was found -- No evidence found.
- Station address (institute-level): Agricultural Research Station, Hanumanamatti, Tq: Ranebennur, Dist: Haveri (Karnataka) -- https://uasd.edu/wp-content/uploads/telephonedirectory.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNV-3 (Little millet)

Name check: The CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "GNV-3". I did not find a Seednet portal page, so the Seednet crop name "LITTLE MILLET (SAMAI / KUTKI)" is unverified. All evidence below refers to the name GNV-3 (also written Gujarat Navsari Vari-3 in one source).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as tolerant to lodging and shattering, with palatable straw, in the NAU technology sheet for little millet (Vari) -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- Listed among varieties with non-lodging habit, resistance to grain smut and sheath blight, and multi-tillering, in an IIMR review of small millet varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Drought: no GNV-3-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found. A review says little millet as a crop is tolerant to moisture stress and drought, but this is not specific to GNV-3 -- https://renupublishers.com/images/article/ijbsv6n2i.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to grain smut and sheath blight -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- The NAU sheet lists "moderately resistant to blast and foot rot" in the same table block as Guj. Nagli-7 and Nagli-8; the layout is ambiguous, so I am not attributing it to GNV-3 -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- Insect pest resistance: no GNV-3-specific evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average grain yield 2864 kg/ha, 8.77% above GV-1, duration 120 days, early maturing and multi-tillering (NAU) -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- Same NAU sheet gives a farmer-table entry of 110-115 days, 1200 (kg/ha, not confirmed) yield, with "early maturity, high yielding" -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- IIMR table lists maturity 110-115 days and yield 28-29 (units as given; likely q/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Agronomic review: 2864 kg/ha versus local check GV-2 (2633 kg/ha) and national check CO-2 (1990 kg/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341195891_Agronomic_Management_in_Little_Millet_Panicum_sumatrense_L_for_Enhancement_of_Productivity_and_Sustainability
- Multi-location trial data for GNV 3 appear in a fodder and grain yield study (values not confirmed in the snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394843676_Fodder_and_Grain_Yield_Potential_of_Little_Millet_Panicum_sumatrense_race_robusta_and_trait-specific_genetic_resources_for_crop_improvement

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: pure line selection (NAU) -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- The input parentage text ("popular in South Bihar and parts of Orissa") is not supported by any source found. Bihar/Odisha popularity of GNV-3 was not found.
- Crosses using GNV-3 as a parent (GNV-3 x WV 126): 50-60% seed recovery with the SMUASB cold-water method, AICRP Small Millets Hill Millet Research Station, NAU Waghai -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1112117/full
- Crop-level: little millet is self-pollinated, tetraploid, 2n = 36 (applies to the crop, not GNV-3 alone) -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1112117/full
- QTL, marker, or genome resources specific to GNV-3: none found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Navsari Agricultural University (NAU), Gujarat, the source of the GNV (Navsari Vari) designation -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- Release-related citation: Patil et al. (2017) cited as reporting the GNV-3 release -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355465828_A_new_high_yielding_proso_millet_variety_Panicum_miliaceum_L_PMV_442
- Patil (2021) is cited for crossing work on GNV-3 at the AICRP Hill Millet Research Station, Waghai -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1112117/full
- Lead breeder name: not confirmed in any source. The "Patil" names are citation references only and I have not attributed breeding credit to a named individual.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found.
- Institute-level: Navsari Agricultural University website -- https://nau.in
- Official email, phone, and postal address for the NAU crop improvement unit or Hill Millet Research Station: not found in any result.

PUBLICATIONS
- Patil (2021). Hybridization technique work in little millet (cited in review; full reference not retrieved). Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1112117/full
- Patil et al. (2017). Release of little millet variety GNV-3 (as cited). Journal and full title not retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355465828_A_new_high_yielding_proso_millet_variety_Panicum_miliaceum_L_PMV_442
- Authors not retrieved (2020). Agronomic Management in Little Millet (Panicum sumatrense L.) for Enhancement of Productivity and Sustainability. IJBS (Renu Publishers) vol. 6, no. 2 -- https://renupublishers.com/images/article/ijbsv6n2i.pdf
- Lakhani et al. (2026). Nutritional and phytochemical profiling of little millet (Panicum sumatrense) genotypes, including GNV-3. Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture -- DOI 10.1002/jsfa.70216
- Hariprasanna K. (year not retrieved). High yielding varieties for enhancing the production of small millets in India. IIMR (ResearchGate) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Authors not retrieved. Fodder and grain yield potential of little millet, with GNV 3 in trial data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394843676_Fodder_and_Grain_Yield_Potential_of_Little_Millet_Panicum_sumatrense_race_robusta_and_trait-specific_genetic_resources_for_crop_improvement
- Authors not retrieved. Chapter 8: Millet, a climate-resilient alternative, which mentions GNV-3 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375924681_Chapter_-8_Millet_A_Climate-Resilient_Alternative_to_Conventional_Farming_for_a_Sustainable_Future_Ensuring_Food_Security
- KrishiKosh theses and ICAR AICRP annual reports: none found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned a retail listing for a different little millet product and a university seed portal (UAS-GKVK) with no GNV-3 entry -- https://uasgkvkseeds.org/
- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, NAU seed sales, and private dealer listings for GNV-3: not found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gujarat (CSC input). The IIMR table lists Gujarat Zone I, II and III -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- A 2026 ethnobotany review lists GNV-3 among reported high-yielding varieties, mentioning Tripura. This is a mention, not a recommendation, so I am not recording Tripura as a recommended state -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sustainable-food-systems/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2026.1725027/full

Searches run: 4 (variety and release; breeder and institution; research papers; seed availability). The Seednet portal was not surfaced by any search.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE (evidence refers to GV-2, the same name in both variety_name and seednet_variety_name; crop: little millet)
- NAU Waghai technology sheet describes GV-2 as resistant to lodging and shattering, and lists its panicles as long, semi-compact and well branched with bold grains, with more grains per earhead and productive tillers -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- The same NAU sheet lists GV-2 as a medium-duration, early-maturing, high-yielding type that is multi-tillering and non-lodging -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf (note: the sheet's table rows are garbled, and its lodging wording differs between entries, e.g. "moderately resistant" vs "resistant")
- No GV-2-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found. General little millet drought and waterlogging tolerance pages were discarded because they do not name GV-2.

DISEASE AND PEST (evidence refers to GV-2)
- A table of improved little millet varieties lists GV-2 (2016, 115-125 days, 26-28 q/ha, Gujarat) as resistant to pests and diseases, with white and bold seeds -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- A second listing of released little millet varieties also describes GV-2 as resistant to pests and diseases, though its text is garbled and the colour wording conflicts -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- No pathogen or pest species-level screening data for GV-2 were found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (evidence refers to GV-2)
- A little millet agronomy review uses GV-2 as the local check, reporting that the pure line WV-125 gave 2864 kg/ha, about 8.77 per cent above GV-2 at 2633 kg/ha -- https://renupublishers.com/images/article/ijbsv6n2i.pdf (GV-2 appears only as a comparator here)
- NAU advice for kharif GV-2 in South Gujarat heavy-rainfall zone (AES-I) recommends 40 kg N/ha and 20 kg P2O5/ha -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- GV-2 yield and duration figures conflict across sources: 1700 kg/ha with 32.6 per cent gain over GV-1 and 115-130 days (NAU sheet, GV-2 entry); 26-28 q/ha and 115-125 days (millets.res.in table); 1100 kg/ha and 120-125 days in a second NAU row -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- The NAU sheet also lists a separate older "Guj. Vari-2" (2006, 1700 kg/ha, medium duration). It is not the same entry as GV-2 and was not used for GV-2 traits -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (evidence refers to GV-2)
- A review of artificial hybridization in small millets records a GV-2 x WV 126 cross made with the SMUASB crossing method, reporting 50-60 per cent seed set at the AICRP-Small Millets centre, Hill Millet Research Station, NAU Waghai -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1112117/full
- No QTL, marker or genomic study naming GV-2 was found. Genome papers on little millet found do not name GV-2 and were discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (evidence refers to GV-2)
- The NAU sheet gives GV-2 as a mutant derived from GV-1 and says it was developed at the Waghai station of Navsari Agricultural University -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- The release table credits the GV-2 release to Waghai, NAU, 2016 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- The input record names "Pearl Millet Research Station, Navsari Agri. University", but every GV-2 source points to Hill Millet Research Station (HMRS), NAU, Waghai (The Dangs). The input institution appears to be wrong for this crop -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- No named lead breeder for GV-2 was found in any retrieved source.

CONTACT DETAILS (evidence refers to GV-2)
- No evidence found. No breeder

EVIDENCE DIGEST: GV-4 (Ambika), little millet

Name check: the release-minutes name ("GV-4 (Ambika)") and the Seednet name ("GV-4 (Ambika)") are identical. The Seednet portal did not appear in any search result, so every finding below refers to the variety name as written in the sources ("Gujarat Vari-4", "GV-4: Ambika", "Guj. Navsari Vari-4 (Ambika)"). No Seednet entry was confirmed.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No GV-4-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found. Species-level only: It can withstand both drought and waterlogging. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panicum_sumatrense
- Species-level: little millet is described as a hardy crop which can withstand drought better than most of other cereal crops and water logging to a certain extent. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-6-2018/Savankumar%20N.%20Patel2,%20et%20al.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No GV-4-specific disease or pest reaction was found. The compendium lists GV-4 only as Tolerant to shattering. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384431249_MILLET_CONCLAVE_COMPENDIUM_2023_-_FULL_BOOK
- Comparator only (GV-5, not GV-4): This genotype is resistant to diseases like leaf blast, neck blast and grain smut and also reported resistant reaction against shoot fly. -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Little millet variety Gujarat Vari 4 (GV 4: Ambika) is recommended for little millet growing regions of Gujarat. -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf (item 17.1.1.28, release proposal)
- This little millet variety produces average grain yield of 2933 kg/ha which is 13.78 % higher over local check GNV 3 -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
- Maturity and plant type: the compendium describes GV-4 as Medium duration and non lodging type with Long panicle with more number of grains and yellowish grains. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384431249_MILLET_CONCLAVE_COMPENDIUM_2023_-_FULL_BOOK

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Til-12 (variety_name) / JAWAHAR KUTKI-2 (seednet_variety_name)

Name mismatch: the evidence found is for Jawahar Til-12 (PKDS-12), a sesame variety. The Seednet name "JAWAHAR KUTKI-2" is listed under little millet, and no evidence for it turned up. The only Kutki-named release found is Jawahar Kutki-95 (JK-95 / DLM-95), a little millet variety notified in 2023. It is a different variety and is not treated as a match below.

STRESS TOLERANCE (Til-12 sesame)
Moderately resistant to Macrophomina stem/root rot is the only varietal stress-tolerance trait found; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or waterlogging data was found for this variety. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx ; https://mswt.in/nuts/sesame-seeds/
Seednet (JAWAHAR KUTKI-2): No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST (Til-12 sesame)
Macrophomina resistance: moderate, per DOD listing and trade pages. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx ; https://pisumfoods.com/oilseeds/sesame
Insect management: AICRP guidance is for insecticide spraying at bud initiation (imidacloprid, quinalphos, dimethoate). This is not variety-specific. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
Trade pages also claim capsule-borer tolerance, but this appears to be for TKG-308, not Til-12. -- https://mswt.in/nuts/sesame-seeds/
Seednet (JAWAHAR KUTKI-2): No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (Til-12 sesame)
Duration 82-85 days, white seed, 700-750 kg/ha yield potential, 48-52% oil content. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/ ; https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx
Compact plant architecture and uniform capsule distribution are reported in a Central India varieties article. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/grow-more-earn-more-improved-sesame-varieties-and-practices-for-mp-chhattisgarh-farmers/
Conflict: that article gives a 2006 release year, while DOD and AICRP give 2008.
Field-trial data from official multi-location trials: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (Til-12 sesame)
Parent use: PKDS-12 appears as a parent in a segregating-population study (Thilarani x PKDS-12) that reports heritability and genetic advance for yield-related traits. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Yengkhom-Devi-4/publication/364292115_VARIABILITY_AND_HERITABILITY_STUDIES_FOR_YIELD_AND_QUALITY_CONTRIBUTING_TRAITS_IN_SEGREGATING_GENERATIONS_OF_SESAME_Sesamum_indicum_L_Scientist_The_official_Journal_of_Scientist_R_Academy/links/6343b09c9cb4fe44f317bcc7/VARIABILITY-AND-HERITABILITY-STUDIES-FOR-YIELD-AND-QUALITY-CONTRIBUTING-TRAITS-IN-SEGREGATING-GENERATIONS-OF-SESAME-Sesamum-indicum-L-Scientist-The-official-Journal-of-Scientist-R-Academy.pdf
QTL/marker studies for PKDS-12: No evidence found.
Seednet (JAWAHAR KUTKI-2): No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (Til-12 sesame)
Release centre: ZARS, JNKVV, Powarkheda (MP), released 2008 per DOD. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx ; https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
Developing institution: JNKVV, Jabalpur, which has developed several sesame varieties by conventional breeding. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/seasame-breeding-crop-improvement-kharif/239907924
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. A JNKVV presenter (Dr. Pratibha Bisen, Plant Breeding and Genetics, College of Agriculture, Balaghat) is listed in a sesame breeding slide deck, but no link to PKDS-12 was found. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/seasame-breeding-crop-improvement-kharif/239907924
Parentage (Gariyaband local selection, from the input record): not verified by any search result.
Seednet (JAWAHAR KUTKI-2): No evidence found. Note that Jawahar Kutki-95 is linked to JNKVV-type naming, but this is unverified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kalinga Suan 18 (CSC release name) / Kalinga Suan 18 (CLMV-2) (Seednet name), little millet

Scope note: Four searches were run. The first included "CLMV-2" but no result mentioned that code. No search targeted the Seednet portal directly, so the Seednet-name evidence is absent rather than checked. Almost all evidence below is for the closely related variety Kalinga Suan 217 (OLM 217), not Kalinga Suan 18. Where a finding concerns 217, it is labelled as such.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Kalinga Suan 18. Searched under both names. The only related data is for Kalinga Suan 217, which an ICAR table lists as tolerant to shootfly and moderately resistant to sheath blight (not KS18) -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
General little millet context, not specific to KS18: the crop is described as withstanding both drought and waterlogging -- https://www.smartfood.org/smart-food-little-millet/

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for Kalinga Suan 18. Kalinga Suan 217 is listed as resistant to rust and grain smut (not KS18) -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
AICRP on Small Millets reports that grain smut in little millet has chemical control measures, and that shoot fly management technology has been developed for little millet -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicrp_small.php

Search budget note: The four permitted searches are used up. My first batch returned full results, but I printed only the first 300 characters of each, and my attempt to re-read the full pages hit the tool-call limit. Findings below are limited to those snippets. Items marked "not captured" may exist on the pages I could not re-open.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Arka Sweta. -- none

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data appeared in the captured text. -- none

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Listed as an F1 hybrid from a cross of IHR 3903 (a CGMS line) with IHR 3315. Reported yields are 28-30 t/ha fresh and 4.5 t/ha dry. Fruits are smooth and light green, turning red at maturity. -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
- Maturity, plant habit and multi-location trial results: not captured.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Conflict with the supplied record: the IIHR listing describes an F1 hybrid (IHR 3903 CGMS × IHR 3315), while the supplied parentage describes IIHR 3-1-1-1-5-1, a Lucknow collection developed by pure-line breeding. These cannot both be right for this variety. The supplied parentage is not supported by any evidence I found and should be checked against IIHR records. -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The IIHR page for Arka Sweta lists it under "Varieties / Technologies released by ICAR - IIHR." -- https://www.iihr.res.in/chilli-arka-sweta-0
- Lead breeder or scientist names: not captured. The supplied record names no breeder either.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. The only institute reference found is the IIHR website. Official email, phone and postal address were not captured. -- https://iihr.res.in
- Seednet contact details: not searched separately.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for Arka Sweta. A ResearchGate paper on hybrid chillies in Salem covers TNAU CO1 and Arka Meghana, not this variety, so I discarded it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354579998_Per_se_performance_of_hybrid_chillies_Capsicum_annuum_l_TNAU_

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Arka Sweta. A Gramik listing for "Sheetal Research Long Melon Seeds" is a private product for a different crop, so I discarded it. -- https://shop.gramik.in/product/Sheetal-Research-Long-Melon-Seeds-yOtUj
- Seednet name conflict: "ARKA SHEETAL" under "LONG MELON" does not match the chilli record. No Seednet listing was found under either name.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found. The supplied record says "Not specified," and no state recommendation appeared in the captured text.

Release year: the supplied date is 2015-04-07. This was not verified against any source.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: M/s. Khoja Habib Mamad, Near Gramin Bank, Post. Nagalpur, Tehsil. Anjar, Dist. Kutchh, (Gujarat) PIN- 370110.
seednet_fields.Parentage: Preliminary selection was made from the local material ‘Kutchhi Rajka’ and phenotypically similar elite plants were selected over several cycles and bulked.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: South Zone comprising states of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Resistant to lodging, medium to high fertilizer responsive, suitable to early sowing 15th October to 15th November. 1.	Seed rate: 15-18 kg for line sowing. 35-40 kg for broadcasting. 2.	30 cm between lines (mostly broadcasting). 3.	FYM: 20-25 t/ha. 4.	NPK: 25:50:50kg as basal dose. 2nd year, 0:50:50 kg. NPK in Number. 3rd year, 0:50:50 kg. NPK in Number.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Perennial for 3 years, long root system, suitable in high temperature ranges from 48 to 50 Co, dry and salt affected area. Tall variety having number or tillers per plant. More number of leaves per plant with oblong shape and tender shoot so high digestible protein. Seeds are yellowish kindly shaped.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Drought resistant due to long root system so suitable in warm condition.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Moderately Resistant to Downey Mildew.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: H. armigera and Lucerne weevil had low incidence and all entries showed non significant variations.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 1.	NPK: 25:50:50kg as basal dose. 2nd year, 0:50:50 kg. NPK in Number. 3rd year, 0:50:50 kg. NPK in Number.

drought.details: Specific drought tolerance for ADV 762 is not specified. However, maize is generally highly sensitive to drought, especially from pre-flowering to maturity, with critical periods during tasseling and grain-filling stages. Foliar calcium spray has been shown to confer drought stress tolerance in maize by modulating plant growth, water relations, proline content, and hydrogen peroxide activity. Calcium also regulates water status, proline, and H2O2 levels in maize plants under drought stress.

heat.details: Specific heat tolerance for ADV 762 is not specified. Rising temperatures due to greenhouse gas emissions cause heat stress in plants, including maize. Research indicates a calcium-dependent tolerant response of the cell wall in maize mesocotyl under heat stress.

salinity.details: Specific salinity tolerance for ADV 762 is not specified. Increased soil salinity reduces the availability of water and nutrients in the root zone, leading to water stress, oxidative stress, and ion toxicity in plants. Plants differ in their tolerance to soil salinity. Calcium plays a role in increasing the tolerance of corn (Zea mays L.) to salinity. Organic amendments have also been shown to mitigate salinity induced toxic effects in maize.

flood.details: Specific flood tolerance for ADV 762 is not specified. Maize is highly sensitive to waterlogging. Flooding influences maize plants.

disease_resistance.summary: Specific disease resistance for ADV 762 is not specified. However, diseases in maize are highly influenced by abiotic stress. Another Advanta maize product, PAC 741, is noted as tolerant to late wilt.

pest_resistance.summary: Specific pest resistance for ADV 762 is not specified. Pest issues in maize are highly influenced by abiotic stress.

drought.details: Specific tolerance for ADV 752 is unknown. General maize is prone to drought stress, especially during tasseling and grain-filling stages. However, some maize varieties are recognized as drought tolerant. Foliar calcium spray can confer drought stress tolerance in maize by modulating plant growth, water relations, proline content, and hydrogen peroxide activity. Calcium also regulates water status, proline, and H2O2 levels in maize plants under drought stress. Drought tolerance in maize can also be observed in varieties tolerant to both submergence and drought.

heat.details: Specific tolerance for ADV 752 is unknown. General maize adaptability to warm temperatures is noted. Physiological, biochemical, and molecular mechanisms of heat stress tolerance in maize, including calcium-dependent responses, have been observed. Heat stress is a significant factor influenced by temperature increases.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: BIO 9782 (seednet name: BIO 9782 (BIO 237)), Maize

Search note: I ran four web_search queries, all in one batch: "BIO 9782 maize variety", "BIO 9782 maize breeder institute", "BIO 9782 maize research paper", and "BIO 9782 maize seed availability". I did not run separate queries for the CSC minutes, Seednet, or KrishiKosh, so those sources are not checked. Only two pages in the results name this hybrid as "Bioseed 9782" in maize. Both are Nepal trials, not Indian evidence. Results naming "Bio 9682" and "Bioseed 9792" are different products and were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for this hybrid.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for this hybrid.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A Nepal trial at Bharatpur-15, Fulbari, Chitwan (Dec 2017 to May 2018) compared eight single-cross maize hybrids, including Bioseed 9782, in a three-replicate randomized design. Bioseed 9782 gave the highest grain yield in that trial, 15.96 t/ha, ahead of Gangakaveri at 14.26 t/ha and Shresta at 12.12 t/ha. It also had the highest standard heterosis, at 64.81%, and the longest cob, at 21.33 cm, with the widest cob diameter, at 17.67 cm -- f2ffoundation.org/faa/index.php/home/article/view/46 and doaj.org/article/af17e3c0b1c74b3f8fb6b32e6c4b8a15. This is a single-season, single-site Nepal trial, so it does not show Indian yield or recommended-state performance.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. Parentage and breeding-line codes are not in the results. The "Not specified" parentage in the record was not resolved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a named breeder or scientist. The only institutional link is the supplied record: Bioseed Research India, a division of DCM Shriram Ltd., Hyderabad. The searches did not confirm this from an independent source.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address, or institute contact page for Bioseed Research India or DCM Shriram was returned.

PUBLICATIONS --
Authors not stated in the retrieved snippets (year not stated). Performance evaluation of single-cross maize hybrids for flowering and yield traits. Journal not stated in retrieved text (Nepal, Chitwan trial, 2017-18 season) -- https://doaj.org/article/af17e3c0b1c74b3f8fb6b32e6c4b8a15 (the same paper is also listed at https://www.f2ffoundation.org/faa/index.php/home/article/view/46). DOI not shown in the retrieved text.

No AICRP, ICAR, KrishiKosh, or peer-reviewed Indian multi-location trial results for this variety were found. The Frontiers AICRP validation paper that appeared in the first search mentions only "Bio 9682," so it was discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for this variety. The seed listings returned (IndiaMart, AgriBegri, Gramik) are for "Bioseed 9792," a different product, so they were discarded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or Seednet listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Not verified by search. The states listed in the supplied record (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh) come from the input only. No CSC minutes or Seednet notification page was retrieved to confirm them.

Gaps for follow-up, since the four-search limit is used up: the CSC release minutes for 2015, the Seednet record for "BIO 9782 (BIO 237)", KrishiKosh, and Bioseed or DCM Shriram contact pages.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BL 45 (Seednet name: BML-45), berseem (Trifolium alexandrinum)
Searches run: 4 (release/traits; breeder/institution; research papers; Seednet name check). No search returned a page naming BL 45 or BML-45 together with berseem or maize.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The trait search returned only BL 44 and BL 42 pages (e.g., agrospectrumindia.com, PAU/Tribune notices). Those name other varieties, so I discarded them.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for BL 45.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Trial pages returned were about berseem in general or other varieties (e.g., researchgate.net herbicide and NPK trials, pub.isa-india.in PGR trial). None names BL 45.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The only genetics material was general berseem breeding history (PMC11336856, studocu.com), which does not mention BL 45.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The input lists Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) as institution. PAU pages found (pau.edu notices) concern seed production of BL 10, BL 42, BL 43 and BL 44, not BL 45, so no breeder or station is attributed to BL 45.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The pau.edu notice refers only to the "Office of the Director (Seeds), PAU, Ludhiana" with no email, phone or address, and it concerns other varieties. No breeder contact was found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. Papers returned name other berseem varieties or none (e.g., researchgate.net weed-management and herbicide papers, forageresearch.in comparison of notified varieties, Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry 2019 SP1:234-237). None names BL 45, so none is listed.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The PAU seed-production EOI (pau.edu) covers BL 10, BL 42, BL 43 and BL 44 only. The Seednet-name search for BML-45 returned only unrelated commercial maize products (agribegri.com, flipkart.com, amazon.in) and a Karimnagar Makka-1 hybrid paper (researchgate.net) that mentions an inbred "BML 7". These are name resemblances and were discarded. No berseem seed source for BL 45 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The input list (J&K, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) is unverified; no search result supports it for BL 45.

NOTES FOR THE RECORD
- Release year 2022-06-17 from the input is unverified; no release or notification evidence was found.
- Parentage is "Not specified" in the input; no evidence was found either way.
- Name check: "BL 45" is a berseem name, but the Seednet entry "BML-45" is listed under MAIZE (MAKKA) with variety code BM 12. The crop mismatch and the name difference should be checked against Seednet and the CSC release minutes before this record is used.
- Off-target pages seen (BL 42, BL 43, BL 44, BL 10, Karimnagar Makka-1, Siri 4555, CP 858, DKC 9081, GO-BER-10 clover patent, and others) were excluded under the strict relevance rule.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Seed ratea: 20 kg/ha Spacing: 30 x 10 cm Fertilizer: 25:50:25 kg NPK/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: (i)Plant height-Semi erect and determinate plant type with lanceolate leaflet. (ii)Flower colour-Yellow. (iii)Days to 50% flowering-40 days (30-53 days). (iv)Pod charcter-Pubescent, matured pod is black in colour. (v)Pod length-4.2 cm (4.0-4.5 cm).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The culture VBG 12-034 is resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus, Urdbean Leaf Crinkle Virus, Leaf Curl Virus diseases.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Modertaely resistant to pod borer complex Number of white flies per plant number of thrips per flowers and incidence of stem fly is very less when compared to the variety.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Apply fertilizers based on the soil testing or apply recommended dose of fertilizers of NPK @ 25:50:25 Kg/ha. Apply all the recommended dose of fertilizers as basal dose. Spray 2 per cent fertilizers

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BPCH-6 (variety_name) / BPCH-6 (seednet_variety_name), maize (MAKKA), code A0207854, ANGRAU, release 2015-06-25

Name note: Both names are "BPCH-6" and no Seednet page surfaced in my four searches, so every finding below refers to the name "BPCH 6"/"BPCH-6" as written in the source. Two results describe BPCH-6 as a popcorn hybrid; one describes it as a landrace. Treat the crop type as unresolved until the CSC minutes or Seednet entry is checked directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- A drought screen of Indian maize landraces reported that BPCH-6 had high relative water content and was selected as a drought-tolerant landrace for further study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371013636_Breeding_Drought-Tolerant_Maize_Zea_mays_Using_Molecular_Breeding_Tools_Recent_Advancements_and_Future_Prospective
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to BPCH-6.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for BPCH-6 resistance to any disease or pest. The only AICRP-style benchmarking slides I found list resistance for other hybrids, not BPCH-6 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A field experiment at the Maize Research Centre, Agricultural Research Institute (ARI), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, tested plant densities and nitrogen levels on the newly published popcorn hybrid BPCH-6 over two rabi seasons, reporting growth, yield and economics -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Popular-popcorn-varieties-in-India_tbl1_305145700
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A Andhra Pradesh/Telangana maize package of practices lists BPCH 6 as a recommended popcorn hybrid under speciality corn -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/package%20of%20practices/MaizePackage.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maturity, yield (t/ha) and plant population for BPCH-6: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for BPCH-6 parentage, marker studies or QTL. The parentage field in the input is "Not specified", and no source filled that gap.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution per the release record and the Rajendranagar paper: Acharya N. G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Lam, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh. The Rajendranagar paper names the variety's origin as Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University, previously ANGRAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Popular-popcorn-varieties-in-India_tbl1_305145700
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. No breeder name was attached to BPCH-6 in any source I retrieved.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The university's general description (headquarters at Lam, Guntur; established 1964 as Andhra Pradesh Agricultural University, renamed 1996) -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acharya_N._G._Ranga_Agricultural_University

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level contact (no breeder contact found): Acharya N G Ranga Agricultural University Administrative Office, Lam, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, 522 034; email registrar@angrau.ac.in -- https://angrau.ac.in/
CONTACT DETAILS -- Breeder email, direct phone, and division or maize-station postal address: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (Year not captured). Field experiment on plant density and nitrogen effects on the popcorn hybrid BPCH-6, Maize Research Centre, ARI Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. ResearchGate figure record -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Popular-popcorn-varieties-in-India_tbl1_305145700
- Authors not captured (Year not captured). "Breeding Drought-Tolerant Maize (Zea mays) Using Molecular Breeding Tools: Recent Advancements and Future Prospective." Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371013636_Breeding_Drought-Tolerant_Maize_Zea_mays_Using_Molecular_Breeding_Tools_Recent_Advancements_and_Future_Prospective
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report entry, or DOI specific to BPCH-6 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The Seednet portal was not reached in these searches, and the fourth search (seed availability) returned only non-Indian seed listings.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The input record states "All states (across the country)", which I could not verify. The only Indian listing found names BPCH 6 solely as a popcorn option in an Andhra Pradesh/Telangana package of practices -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/package%20of%20practices/MaizePackage.pdf

Open items for the reference record: confirm the crop type (hybrid vs. landrace), get the CSC minutes entry and Seednet record, and obtain the breeder's name and direct contact from ANGRAU or Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bajaura Makka-1 (maize)

Search note: The web_search budget ran out after four queries. My last call hit the limit, so I could not open the full pages. The findings below come only from the truncated result snippets I already captured, so several headings are incomplete. Treat this as a partial record.

Name note: The CSC name is "Bajaura Makka-1" and the Seednet name is "Bajaura Makka". The IIMR page gives "Bajaura Makka 1 (L173)" and the AICRP page gives "Bajaura Makka (L 201 Composite)". The variety code in the input is L-173, but the AICRP page lists L 201, so the code needs checking against the official notification.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found in the retrieved snippets. Drought, heat, salinity, flood, and submergence tolerance were not captured. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found in the retrieved snippets. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The IIMR page carries agrotechnique material, but only for the single-cross hybrid HQPM-1 (seed production with a 4:1 female-to-male row ratio). It does not describe Bajaura Makka-1, so it should not be attributed to this variety. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The Bajaura Makka-1 snippet shows only its registration and code, with no parentage or QTL data. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The variety is recorded as registered under Registration No. 41 of 2015 (PPV&FRA, notification dated 22 January 2015) and listed as Bajaura Makka 1 (L173). The developing institution is not named in the snippet. The Bajaura station is the CSKHPKV Hill Agricultural Research and Extension Centre (HAREC), which is an AICRP maize centre, so the station link is supported. No breeder name was found. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/ ; https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

CONTACT DETAILS: Institute-level only. The AICRP page lists the centre as CSKHPKV, HAREC, Bajaura, with coordinates given as roughly 31°8′N and 77°E (longitude is incomplete in the snippet). Its address begins "CSKHPKV, Hill..." and was truncated, so I could not record the full postal address, phone, or email. No breeder name, email, or phone was found. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. My searches returned no journal article, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI for this variety. A Karimnagar Makka-1 ResearchGate record appeared, but it is a different hybrid from a different state and is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No official source found. The only result was a retail listing for a "Makka" sweet-corn packet, which is not this variety and is excluded. Next steps: check Seednet (seednet.gov.in) for "Bajaura Makka" and the Himachal Pradesh SAU (CSKHPKV) seed unit.

RECOMMENDED STATES: The AICRP and IIMR pages place the variety at Bajaura, Himachal Pradesh, under CSKHPKV. The notified recommendation for states was not captured, so the input's "Not specified" stands. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/ ; https://iimr.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

Gaps to fill with a fresh search session: the full text of both Bajaura pages (breeder, parentage, yield, maturity, and contacts), the PPV&FRA gazette for Registration No. 41 of 2015, and KrishiKosh/CSKHPKV publications.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for Bisco X 5129 appeared in the results.

Another farming blog lists the same four states but places the crop in the Rabi season, which conflicts with the blog above -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-varieties-of-maize-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
Both blogs are secondary and unverified against CSC minutes or Seednet. Yield figures: No evidence found.
A 2016 Journal of Maize Research and Development paper evaluated 117 hybrids from 20 seed companies at three sites in Nepal, and its visible text names other Bisco hybrids (e.g., Bisco x 81) but no Bisco X 5129 data appeared in the excerpt -- https://www.nepjol.info/index.php/JMRD/article/download/16210/13147
A separate Nepal study found Bisco Gold 941 to be a top yielder; it is a different hybrid, not Bisco X 5129 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9674539/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No QTL or marker evidence found. The parentage BS 251 / (BSI 226 x BSI 252) comes only from the supplied variety record, not from an independent source. No search result confirmed it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution per the record: Bisco Bio-Sciences Pvt. Ltd. A company listing page names Bisco Bio-Sciences Pvt Ltd in its about text and carries the heading Limagrain India Private Limited -- https://www.indiamart.com/bisco-bio-sciences/
Breeder or scientist names: No evidence found. No station or institute page for this hybrid was located.
Note: Seednet name and CSC name are both "Bisco X 5129", so no separate Seednet-name search was needed. Seednet itself was not reached in these results.

No official institute contact page was found. No email or phone numbers were verified.

PUBLICATIONS -- No publication specific to Bisco X 5129 was found. Related but non-target items:
Authors not captured in the search excerpt (2016). Journal of Maize Research and Development, vol. 2(1), pp. 1-12: multi-hybrid evaluation in Nepal, Bisco X 5129 not confirmed in the excerpt -- https://www.nepjol.info/index.php/JMRD/article/download/16210/13147

KrishiKosh and AICRP/ICAR reports: No evidence found in these searches.

Related but non-target: a trade-data site lists Bisco maize seed export records under HS code 10051000, including a 2016 entry for a different Bisco variety -- https://www.seair.co.in/bisco-maize-seed-export-data/hs-code-10051000.aspx
