search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PMH 12 (JH 13347), Maize

Name note: The CSC name is "PMH 12" and the Seednet name is "PMH 12 (JH 13347)". The ICAR-IIMR cultivar list uses "PMH 12 (JH 13347)", so that list matches both names. I did not get a Seednet portal page in these searches, so no finding below comes from Seednet directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- The PAU maize team's account reports moderate tolerance or resistance to maydis leaf blight, turcicum leaf blight, banded leaf and sheath blight, brown stripe downy mildew and post-flowering stalk rot. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found. -- https://www.gleaf.in/news/pau-signs-moa-for-maize-hybrid-pmh-12

DISEASE AND PEST -- Same source as above: moderate tolerance to maydis leaf blight, turcicum leaf blight, banded leaf and sheath blight, brown stripe downy mildew and post-flowering stalk rot. No pest resistance data were found for PMH 12. -- https://www.gleaf.in/news/pau-signs-moa-for-maize-hybrid-pmh-12

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- PAU's Incharge of the maize research team describes PMH 12 as a uniform, stable, high-yielding medium-duration single-cross hybrid. It reportedly yields a mean of 71.06 q/ha in Zone III, is responsive to good management, and matures in about 90 days. -- https://www.gleaf.in/news/pau-signs-moa-for-maize-hybrid-pmh-12
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The ICAR-IIMR cultivar entry lists the release as a public cultivar from PAU, Ludhiana, notified 05.09.2019 (reference 3220(E)), with a "Normal" maturity class. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
No multi-location trial reports or agronomy papers specific to PMH 12 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage (LM 26 x LM 16; LM 26 = JCY 45-1-1-1-1-1-1; LM 16 = SE39 line code) was supplied in the request. It was not confirmed by any search result. No QTL, marker or genome-resource study for PMH 12 was found. The search also did not confirm the breeding method. Only the IIMR list supports the "JH 13347" code. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ (code only)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The developing institution is the Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, PAU, Ludhiana, per the ICAR-IIMR list. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Named in the PAU MoA report: Dr Surinder Sandhu (Incharge, maize research team, PAU); Dr Tosh Garg (maize breeder); Dr Dhatt and Dr VS Sohu (Head, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics); Dr Khushdeep Dharni (Associate Director, Technology Marketing and IPR Cell). The article does not give dates, so it is unclear whether these names apply to the original release team. -- https://www.gleaf.in/news/pau-signs-moa-for-maize-hybrid-pmh-12

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder email, phone or postal address for PMH 12 was found. No PAU Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics contact page was retrieved. The named people above are listed without contact details. -- No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The searches returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or conference paper that names PMH 12. Results for "PMH-11" and "PMH-1" are different varieties and were excluded. A Tribune article about PMH-13 was also excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No seller, NSC, State Seed Corporation or KVK listing for PMH 12 was found. The PAU MoA report says PAU signed an agreement to produce and supply PMH 12 seed to boost farmer access. It names no seed partner or price. -- https://www.gleaf.in/news/pau-signs-moa-for-maize-hybrid-pmh-12
The PAU seed-portal licensing page lists kharif maize hybrids PMH-1, PMH-3, PMH-4, PMH-5, PMH-6, Parkash and Megha, but does not list PMH 12. -- https://www.pau-seed.in/licensing.php

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The ICAR-IIMR list gives the zones as BH, JH, WB, OD, CHH and Eastern U.P. This expands to Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Eastern Uttar Pradesh. The request listed "parts of Uttar Pradesh and Odisha" and omitted Chhattisgarh, so the request's list should be checked against the official notification. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/

disease_resistance.research_summary: PAU maize team account (gleaf.in) reports moderate tolerance or resistance to maydis leaf blight, turcicum leaf blight, banded leaf and sheath blight, brown stripe downy mildew and post-flowering stalk rot. No numeric ratings are given in that source. Original variety data (CSC, not a digest URL) gives a proposed hybrid JH 13347 score on a 1-5 scale of 1.7 for maydis leaf blight, 3.1 for turcicum leaf blight, 3.0 for banded leaf and sheath blight, 4.4 on a 1-9 scale for charcoal rot, 2.6 on a 1-9 scale for Fusarium stalk rot, and 0.8 for curvularia leaf spot (1-5). Check varieties in the same table were HM 9, Bio 9637 and PMH 4. The table gives no separate PMH 12 score; it refers to the proposed hybrid JH 13347.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Composite-612 (variety_name) / Pusa Composite-612 (MP-480) (seednet_variety_name), Pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum)

Name note: Most pages cite "Pusa Composite 612" or "Pusa composite-612". The MP-480 code appears only in the millets.res.in notification table. Under each heading below, the evidence refers to the Pusa Composite-612 name unless stated otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought: a GT-biplot yield-stability study of 12 pearl millet genotypes in arid Rajasthan, grown at an ANGRAU station, found Pusa Comp. 612 stable and suggested it for rainfed cultivation over a wide range of conditions -- https://jeb.co.in./journal_issues/202303_mar23/paper_07.pdf ; http://www.jeb.co.in/journal_issues/202303_mar23/paper_07.pdf
- Rainfed/irrigated suitability: the Pusa Composite 612 entry is described as suitable for rainfed and irrigated conditions -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/pearlmillet-crop-production-technology/255075507
- Salinity/sodicity: Pusa composite-612 was one of five varieties grown under partially reclaimed sodic soil in Ayodhya; the retrieved abstract gives plant-height data only, with no stress-tolerance conclusion -- https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/issues/article_abstract.php?aid=16107&iid=426&jid=3
- Heat, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Downy mildew: the IARI ZTM & BPD page lists Pusa Composite 612 as resistant to downy mildew -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/pearl-millet/
- Downy mildew (IARI notification table): the notification summary for the MP 480 line mentions a downy-mildew-resistance feature for a different Pusa Composite (701) entry, so it is not attributed to 612 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf (discarded for this variety)
- Blast and other diseases: the IARI ZTM page's Pusa Composite 612 block does not mention blast; a blast statement on the same page belongs to a different entry, so it is discarded -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/pearl-millet/
- Insect pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: the IARI ZTM page gives 80-85 days, dual-purpose, suitable for normal and late sowing -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/pearl-millet/
- Yield (conflicting): one IARI ZTM page block gives 2.5 t/ha -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/pearl-millet/ ; the same site's later version gives 2.2-2.4 t/ha -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/pearl-millet/
- Grain and stover: a farming guide gives 2.5 t/ha grain for composite varieties under irrigation, without naming Pusa Composite 612 -- https://agriculturereview.com/pearlmillet-farming-guide/ (discarded for this variety; general composite figure)
- Multi-location and farmer trials: the AICPMIP 52nd Workshop proceedings mention Pusa Comp. 612 only in a seed-indent table, so no trial result is attributed -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2017.pdf
- Yield-stability trial: Pusa Comp. 612 was rated second-most stable behind 86M86 in the ANGRAU trial summary and recommended for large-scale assessment -- https://jeb.co.in./journal_issues/202303_mar23/paper_07.pdf
- Recommended agronomy: No evidence found for this variety beyond the above.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: the composite is said to derive from 9 elite inbred lines, highly resistant to downy mildew. This is taken from the input record. No search result confirmed it -- source: input record only (no URL)
- Breeding-line code: the millets.res.in notification table lists "Pusa Composite 612 (MP 480)" with S.O. 632(E), dated 25.03.11, and AICPMIP/IARI, New Delhi as the origin -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Breeding method: composite (open-pollinated) variety, per the Kehkashan page and the IARI page -- https://kehkashanco.com/en/insights/hybrid-pearl-millet-buyers-guide-2026
- QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found. The ICRISAT GWAS paper concerns other elite lines and is discarded -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11561417/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder: Dr. R.L. Kapoor is named as the breeder of Pusa Comp. 612 -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2017.pdf
- Institution: ICAR-IARI, New Delhi, through the AICPMIP pearl millet programme -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Release-year conflict: an IARI 2014 technology booklet gives "Year of release: 2008 (CVRC)" and a different recommended area (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana), which conflicts with the 2011 notification and the four-state list -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
- Station: the AICRP pearl millet success-story table lists Pusa Composite 612 in a 2011 row, but the extracted text is too garbled to confirm the year -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380432206_Recent_advances_in_the_production_technology_and_breeding_Of_pearl_millet

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute unit: ZTM & BPD Unit, ICAR-IARI, Pusa Campus, New Delhi-110012 (address on the Pearl Millet page). No email or phone was retrieved -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/pearl-millet/
- Breeder contact: No evidence found for R.L. Kapoor's email or phone.
- Seednet/CSC contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (2023). Yield stability analysis of pearl millet genotypes in arid regions (GT-biplot study, ANGRAU, Ananthapuramu). Journal of Experimental Biology/journal issue, March 2023 -- https://jeb.co.in./journal_issues/202303_mar23/paper_07.pdf
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Crop growth and yield parameters of five pearl millet varieties under partially reclaimed sodic soil, Ayodhya. Ecology, Environment and Conservation -- https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/issues/article_abstract.php?aid=16107&iid=426&jid=3
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Phenolic content, antioxidant potential and DNA damage protection of pearl millet cultivars of North Indian region (PC-612 included). Academia.edu record -- https://www.academia.edu/35517106/Phenolic_content_antioxidant_potential_and_DNA_damage_protection_of_pearl_millet_Pennisetum_glaucum_cultivars_of_North_Indian_region
- KrishiKosh theses, CSC release minutes, and AICRP annual reports specific to Pusa Composite-612: No evidence found in the search results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned state-level variety lists and foreign or retail seed pages, not a Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for Pusa Composite-612 -- https://nutricereals.dac.gov.in/pearlmillet.aspx

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu: the millets.res.in notification table and the IARI ZTM page both give this four-state list -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/pearl-millet/
- Conflicting entry: the IARI 2014 booklet names Rajasthan, Gujarat and Haryana -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for DFH-2 (seednet name "Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 -Female" and variety name "Pant Forage Maize Hybrid-1") returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this hybrid.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for DFH-2 turned up in the search results.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
DFH-2 is reported to have high green forage and dry matter yield, with advantages over national checks COHM-8, J-1006 and African Tall; no numeric yields were given -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Its multiple basal/lateral tillers and regrowth potential, combined with higher forage yield, are described as useful for dairy farmers; no trial numbers or locations given -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
No multi-location trial data or agronomic yield figures for DFH-2 were found beyond the above -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4

GENETICS AND QTL
DFH-2 is described as a single-cross inter-subspecies hybrid between maize (Zea mays) and its wild ancestor teosinte (Z. mays subsp. parviglumis) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
A 2026 Springer paper on wild relatives cites DFH-2 as an inter-subspecies hybrid with multi-cut, multi-ear and multi-tiller traits, but marks that source as "Unpublished" -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4 is not this page; the source is https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44372-026-00472-9
No QTL or marker studies for DFH-2 were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Shivam Yadav and N. K. Singh are the authors of the variety notification article -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
DFH-2 was developed at Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar, under AICRP on Maize, with no funding received during development -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Garhwal Post reports that the university's forage research programme received an ICAR best centre award, and that DFH-2 was the university's major achievement, notified and included in the seed chain -- https://garhwalpost.in/pantvarsitys-forage-research-programme-receives-icars-best-centre-award/
Name discrepancy: the Springer article names the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties; the Garhwal Post names the Central Variety Release Committee -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4 and https://garhwalpost.in/pantvarsitys-forage-research-programme-receives-icars-best-centre-award/

CONTACT DETAILS
Shivam Yadav, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, G. B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, 263145, India (author affiliation; no email or phone listed) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
N. K. Singh, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, G. B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, 263145, India (author affiliation; no email or phone listed) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Official email: No evidence found
Phone: No evidence found
Institute or AICRP contact page URL: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
Yadav, S., Singh, N.K. (2026). Pant Forage Maize Hybrid-1 (DFH-2). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding, 86, 258–259 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4 (DOI 10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4, taken from the URL; not separately printed in the results)
Authors not identified in the search snippet (2026). Wild relatives enhance genetic resources for maize (Zea mays ssp. mays) improvement through diversity analysis. Springer -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44372-026-00472-9 (lists DFH-2 only as an unpublished reference; not a DFH-2 study)
No KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports or conference papers on DFH-2 were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
The Garhwal Post states DFH-2 has been included in the seed chain -- https://garhwalpost.in/pantvarsitys-forage-research-programme-receives-icars-best-centre-award/
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sale or private dealer listing for DFH-2 was found.
Note: the seednet name "Pratap Hybrid Maize-1" returned only a different extra-early hybrid (EH-series, 2004 release, Rajasthan/Gujarat/MP) in the AICMIP list -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf. It is not this variety and was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Notified for cultivation in the Northern Western Zone (Uttarakhand plains, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) and Central Zone (Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Notification number S.O. 4388(E) is dated 08/10/2024 in the source, while the record's year_of_release is 2024-08-02. The notification date should be checked against the Gazette before the record is finalised -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (EH-number, 2004 release; this is NOT the -2 entry): reported as moderately resistant to stem borer -- Pratap Hybrid 1 (2004), pedigree EI-116 x EI-364, MPUA&T Udaipur, average yield 45 q/ha, moderate resistance to stem borer. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2 (EH-1389) drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (2004): moderate resistance to stem borer -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (AICMIP 2000+ hybrid table): listed as white semi flint, moderately resistant; the disease-rating text is truncated in the extract -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: extra early maturity, recommended for Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, in kharif -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: AICMIP table gives an average yield of 3.8 t/ha (2004 entry, extra early, kharif) -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: ResearchGate compilation gives 45 q/ha. This conflicts with the AICMIP 3.8 t/ha figure, and the two sources may not refer to the same trial basis -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No trial or yield evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 pedigree (EI-116 x EI-364) is the only parentage found; it is not verified for the -2 entry -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- QTL or marker studies for Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing centre for Pratap Hybrid 1 is listed as MPUA&T Udaipur (Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Institution for Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: not specified in the release record; the -1 centre above is the only institutional link found and is not confirmed for -2.
- Lead breeder names for either entry: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder names, roles, emails, phones, postal address for MPUA&T Udaipur maize division or any institute contact page: No evidence found. Searches did not return an institute contact page. No contact details were invented or inferred.

PUBLICATIONS
- Dass, S.; Karjagi, C. G.; Kumar, Bhupender; Jat, S. L.; Parihar, C. M.; Kumar, Ramesh; Kamboj, M. C. (2015). Single Cross Hybrid: A Potential Technology for Boosting Maize Production. Bibliographic record supplied by ICAR (journal not stated; general review, does not name Pratap Hybrid Maize-2) -- https://agris.fao.org/search/es/records/64747348bf943c8c79830277
- Author not given (year not given). Maize Hybrid and Composite Varieties Released in India (1961-2010). Compilation listing Pratap Hybrid 1 (2004); no -2 entry seen in the extract -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Author not given (2010). A Compendium of maize hybrids and composites of India under PPV & FRA, Technical Bulletin No. 2010/4, pp. 84. Extract names other Pratap entries; no -2 entry seen -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
- Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses, or DOIs specific to Pratap Hybrid Maize-2 (EH-1389): No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 or -2 from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales, or verified dealers: No evidence found. Dealer listings returned were generic hybrid maize sellers with no link to this variety, so they were excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh (kharif) -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: the ResearchGate compilation lists J&K, Uttarakhand, NE hills, HP and Assam, which conflicts with the AICMIP entry -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No evidence found. The CSC release record's "Not specified" is unresolved.

NAME AND SCOPE NOTES
- Every item above refers to Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (2004 release, EH-number not confirmed), not Pratap Hybrid Maize-2 (EH-1389, 2010). No source found for the -2 entry or for the code EH-1389.
- The Seednet name "Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 -Male" may be a labelling error. The evidence supports -1 but says nothing about a male parent line.
- Four searches were run. Coverage is limited: the AICMIP and ICAR-linked sources are the most authoritative results, and the remaining sources are secondary compilations. Verify against the Seednet portal, MPUA&T Udaipur, and the CSC minutes before relying on this record.

Days to 50% tasseling - 47-51 days, -Days to 50% silking - 49-53 day Anther colour  Present (Pink), - Tassel density Sparse, - Pollen shading - Good,- Fresh silk colour - Present (dark pink), - Seed colour - Yellow,- Seed size - Medium, - 100-seed weight - 27.17 g,-	Cob shape - Conico - cylindrical, - Number of leaf per plant- 12-16,-  Ear height (cm)- 78.8 cm, - leaves, - Cob placement - Medium to low, - Leaf texture - Normal, - Leaf edge - Smooth, - Brace root colour - Present, - Spikelet orientation - Semi erect, - Stem colour - Greenish

seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to PFSR, RDM, TLB and moderately resistant to BLSB, MLB and cyst nematode.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to this hybrid. The only trait noted in the PAU Kharif package is that it is male sterile and medium tall, so it needs no detasseling. This does not indicate drought tolerance.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to this hybrid.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to this hybrid.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to this hybrid. Dr Tosh Garg's PAU profile lists waterlogging tolerance as a breeding goal for maize in general, not for this hybrid.

disease_resistance.summary: No variety-specific evidence found for disease resistance. The PAU Kharif package lodging and stalk-rot note refers to a different, unnamed hybrid and is not attributed to Punjab Baby Corn 1. A Tribune article states that the husk protects baby corn ears from insects and diseases; this describes a property of the crop product, not a tested resistance in this hybrid.

pest_resistance.summary: No variety-specific evidence found for pest resistance. The only related statement is the crop-level Tribune note that the husk protects baby corn ears from insects, which is not a tested resistance for this hybrid.

agronomic_details.yield: PAU Kharif package: average of 8.4 quintals per acre of dehusked ears (approximately 20.8 q/ha by conversion at 2.471 acres per ha). This is close to the CSC-recorded average of 21.1 q/ha (CSC record is the ground truth). The PAU figure is for dehusked ears; the CSC basis is not specified. Fodder yield is about 128 quintals per acre after picking (Farming Cosmos).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Punjab (PAU and state variety approval committee). Agro-climatic detail beyond the state level is not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified in the CSC record. Crop duration for the baby corn crop is about 60-65 days (PAU Kharif package). Ear picking starts about 52 days after sowing.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Male sterile hybrid; medium tall; no detasseling needed; about three pickings per plant; higher yields of uniform, good-quality ears (Farming Cosmos). Spacing conflict not resolved by the digest: PAU package gives 60 x 15 cm; a Tribune article gives 30 cm rows with 20 cm plant spacing. The PAU package is the official package-of-practices source, but the conflict remains unresolved. Seed production: sow seed crops in the second fortnight of July to first week of August, and plant the female line 3-4 days after the male (PAU Kharif package).
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location or field trial results for this hybrid were found. The only performance statements are the PAU Kharif package average of 8.4 quintals per acre of dehusked ears and the Farming Cosmos description of higher yields of uniform, good-quality ears; neither reports trial data, sites, or replications.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Punjab Baby Corn 1 (CSC name) / Punjab baby corn 1 (JH 32434) (Seednet name)

Name note: None of the four searches returned a Seednet portal page, and no result mentioned the code JH 32434 or the CSC release minutes. All evidence below refers to the variety name "Punjab Baby Corn 1". The release date of 2022 and the Punjab recommendation are confirmed by PAU and press sources, not by Seednet or CSC minutes. The parentage (I 193 female × LM 13 male) came from your input and was not confirmed by any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE (Punjab Baby Corn 1): No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this hybrid. The only trait noted is that it is male sterile and medium tall, so it needs no detasseling -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Ancillary: Dr Tosh Garg's PAU profile lists waterlogging tolerance as a breeding goal for maize in general, not for this hybrid -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=564&intDepTitleID=&intLinkID=9

DISEASE AND PEST (Punjab Baby Corn 1): No variety-specific evidence found for disease or pest reaction. The PAU Kharif package's lodging and stalk-rot note refers to a different, unnamed hybrid in that section, so it is not attributed here -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Crop-level only: a Tribune article says the husk protects baby corn ears from insects and diseases, but this is a property of the crop product, not a tested resistance -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/amid-diversification-push-ludhiana-varsity-experts-vouch-for-baby-corn/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (Punjab Baby Corn 1): The PAU Kharif package gives an average of 8.4 quintals per acre of dehusked ears for this hybrid and says it is one of the suitable hybrids for baby corn -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Harvest timing: ear picking starts about 52 days after sowing, with about three pickings per plant, and fodder yield is about 128 quintals per acre after picking -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/pau-develops-recommends-8-new-varieties-for-general-cultivation-in-punjab/
Crop duration: the baby corn crop is completed in about 60-65 days -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Ear quality: the hybrid is described as giving higher yields of uniform, good-quality ears -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/pau-develops-recommends-8-new-varieties-for-general-cultivation-in-punjab/
Spacing (conflict to resolve): the PAU package gives 60 x 15 cm -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf ; a Tribune article gives 30 cm rows with 20 cm plant spacing -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/amid-diversification-push-ludhiana-varsity-experts-vouch-for-baby-corn/
Seed-production practice: sow seed crops in the second fortnight of July to first week of August, and plant the female line 3-4 days after the male -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Multi-location or field trial results for this hybrid: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No QTL, marker or genomic study on Punjab Baby Corn 1 appeared in any result. The pedigree I 193 × LM 13 is not verified by search.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Institution: Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana. The 2022 release was approved at the state variety approval committee meeting for field crops, chaired by the Punjab director of agriculture -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/pau-develops-recommends-8-new-varieties-for-general-cultivation-in-punjab/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
The search tool's quota ran out after the first four queries, so the digest below rests on those results only. The follow-up checks on the release notification, the seed sources and the breeder contacts could not be run.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: RCRMH-4 (Maize / MAIZE (MAKKA), variety code A020717328)

Name check: "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" are both RCRMH-4, so every heading below refers to that name. The only page found that names RCRMH-4 is a hybrid stability study, which is a maize context but not a release record.

STRESS TOLERANCE: The one page that names RCRMH-4 describes it as a stable, superior hybrid in a tropical maize stability study, with no stress-specific data for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392062482_Stability_of_Maize_Hybrids_Developed_Through_Integration_of_Rapid_Cycle_Genomic_Selection_and_Doubled_Haploid_Technology

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The search for RCRMH-4 returned no disease or pest resistance data.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The stability study (above) reports RCRMH-4 as stable and superior across environments. Maturity, yield values and trial locations were not visible in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392062482_Stability_of_Maize_Hybrids_Developed_Through_Integration_of_Rapid_Cycle_Genomic_Selection_and_Doubled_Haploid_Technology

GENETICS AND QTL: The same study ties RCRMH-4 to rapid-cycle genomic selection and doubled haploid technology in its development. Parentage, breeding-line codes and genome resources were not found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392062482_Stability_of_Maize_Hybrids_Developed_Through_Integration_of_Rapid_Cycle_Genomic_Selection_and_Doubled_Haploid_Technology

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No breeder name or developing station for RCRMH-4 appeared in the results. A page on quality protein maize short-duration hybrids was returned, but it does not name RCRMH-4 in the retrieved text, so it was discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No institute email, phone, address or contact page for RCRMH-4 was retrieved. The College of Agriculture, Bheemarayanagudi, Yadgiri (the institution in the variety record) was not confirmed by any retrieved page.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Pavani et al. (2019). Cited in the stability study as identifying RCRMH-12 and RCRMH-4 as stable and superior hybrids. Original journal and DOI not retrieved. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392062482_Stability_of_Maize_Hybrids_Developed_Through_Integration_of_Rapid_Cycle_Genomic_Selection_and_Doubled_Haploid_Technology
- Discarded: the phytojournal paper on heat-tolerant maize RCRMH-2 (a different variety), and the quality protein maize paper (does not name RCRMH-4).

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned only a paper on a different variety (RCRMH-2), which was discarded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for RCRMH-4 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The variety record lists Karnataka, but no retrieved page confirms this for RCRMH-4.

Open gaps for a follow-up session: the CSC release minutes and the Seednet entry for RCRMH-4, the original Pavani et al. (2019) citation, the institute's contact page, and the KrishiKosh and AICRP maize reports.

drought.details: No drought data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5, IMH-221 or H-64. The only related source (Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4, SMH4) describes cold tolerance and early maturity for high-altitude rainfed conditions, but does not report drought tolerance mechanisms or scores. Identity caveat: the digest does not establish that SMH4 findings apply to Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5.

heat.details: No heat stress data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5, IMH-221 or H-64. SMH4 is described as cold-tolerant (not heat-tolerant) and early-maturing for high-altitude rainfed temperate ecologies. Cold tolerance is not a heat-tolerance measure and is reported here only for context. Identity caveat applies to the SMH4 finding.

salinity.details: No salinity data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5, IMH-221 or H-64 (digest: searched in queries 1 and 3, no evidence found).

flood.details: No flood data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5, IMH-221 or H-64 (digest: searched in queries 1 and 3, no evidence found).

disease_resistance.summary: No disease reaction data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 itself. Reported findings for related entries, which should not be attributed to this record without verification: (1) SMH4 is reported as resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust. (2) IMH-221 is reported as tolerant of Turcicum leaf blight, maydis leaf blight and common rust. (3) Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1, a different SKUAST hybrid, is only moderately resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest reaction data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 itself. Reported findings for related entries, which should not be attributed to this record without verification: (1) SMH4 is reported as resistant to stem borers. (2) IMH-221 is reported as tolerant of Chilo partellus in AICRP and station trials.

agronomic_details.yield: No yield data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or H-64. Related entries: SMH4 has a potential yield of about 7.0 to 8.2 t/ha and a grain yield advantage of about 23.6% over Shalimar Maize Hybrid 1. IMH-221 has a stated yield of 7.5 t/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5. For SMH4, multi-location AICRP North Hill Zone trial data are reported (mean 5.56 t/ha, peak 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura), but no formal stability analysis is described in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: No adaptation data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5. Related entries: SMH4 is recommended for rainfed high-altitude temperate ecologies between 1800 and 2250 m amsl. IMH-221 is a short-duration kharif hybrid, responsive to nutrient inputs. The record's 'Kashmir Valley' recommendation is consistent with the SMH4 source per the digest, but this does not confirm the record's identity.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified in this table excerpt for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5. Related entry: SMH4 matures in about 135 to 140 days at 1800 to 2000 m amsl. IMH-221 is described as short-duration (no day count given).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5. Digest gives no morphological data for this record. Related entry: Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 agronomy (April sowing, 60 x 20 cm spacing, 90-60-40 kg/ha NPK) is for a different hybrid and is not applicable to Hybrid-5.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 field-trial results were found. All trial results in the digest relate to other entries: (1) SMH4 AICRP North Hill Zone multi-location trials averaged 5.56 t/ha, peaking at 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura (Himachal Pradesh). (2) SMH4 showed a grain yield advantage of about 23.6% over Shalimar Maize Hybrid 1. (3) IMH-221 tolerance to Chilo partellus, Turcicum leaf blight, maydis leaf blight and common rust was reported from AICRP and station trials. (4) Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 sowing and agronomy data are reported for high-altitude Kashmir, but the digest does not describe these as trial results.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or H-64. For SMH4, molecular marker work on the parents exists, with polymorphic markers separating SMH4 from SH-1. No marker names, SSR/SNP identifiers or positions were reported in the digest. For Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1, the parental inbreds are W3 and W5. For IMH-221, the parentage is IML 187 x BML 6.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 (CSC name) / Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4 (H-64) (Seednet name); code IMH-221 (DMRH-1417)

IDENTITY WARNING: The evidence does not establish that "Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5" and "IMH-221 (DMRH-1417)" are the same product. The IMH-221 evidence describes an ICAR-IIMR hybrid, and the Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 evidence is a single list entry. The Seednet name "Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4 (H-64)" also does not match any source. The SMH4 findings below refer to "Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4 (SMH4)", not to H-64 or Hybrid-5, and should not be attributed to this record without verification.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- SMH4 is described as cold-tolerant and early-maturing for high-altitude rainfed conditions. The development, dissemination and adoption of high yielding, early maturity, cold tolerant maize hybrids can serve as the most economical, effective and coherent approach to contribute significantly towards increasing maize production in Kashmir Valley. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found specifically for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5, IMH-221 or H-64. -- No evidence found (searched in queries 1 and 3)

DISEASE AND PEST
- SMH4 is reported as resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust, with resistance to stem borers. The variety is resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust, besides showing resistance to stem borers -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- IMH-221 is reported as tolerant of Turcicum leaf blight, maydis leaf blight and common rust, and of Chilo partellus in AICRP and station trials. It has shown tolerance to Turcicum leaf blight, maydis leaf blight and common rust diseases of maize. It has shown tolerance to Chilo partellus insect in the AICRP as well as station trials of maize. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 (a different SKUAST hybrid) is only moderately resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust. -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/HTML/03rather.htm
- No disease or pest data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 itself. -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- SMH4 matures in about 135 to 140 days at 1800 to 2000 m amsl. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH4 has a potential yield of about 7.0 to 8.2 t/ha and a grain yield advantage of about 23.6% over Shalimar Maize Hybrid 1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- In AICRP North Hill Zone multi-location trials, SMH4 averaged 5.56 t/ha, peaking at 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura (Himachal Pradesh). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- IMH-221 is a short-duration kharif hybrid with a stated yield of 7.5 t/ha and is responsive to nutrient inputs. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Sowing and agronomy data for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 (April sowing, 60 x 20 cm spacing, 90-60-40 kg/ha NPK) are reported for high-altitude Kashmir. These are not for Hybrid-5. -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/HTML/03rather.htm
- No Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 field-trial results were found. -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 was built from two inbreds, W3 and W5. -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/PDF/03rather.pdf
- SMH4 is a single-cross hybrid. Molecular marker work on SMH4 parents exists, with polymorphic markers separating SMH4 from SH-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- No pedigree or parentage was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or H-64. The IMH-221 parentage is IML 187 x BML 6. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 is listed among SKUAST-K maize hybrids released. -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuast-k-maize-improvement-programme-transforming-challenges-into-bountiful-harvests/
- SMH4 authors are M. Ashraf Ahangar, Asif B. Shikari, Showkat A. Waza, F. A. Sheikh, S. Najeeb, N. A. Teeli, Z. A. Dar and Ajaz A. Lone. Affiliations: Mountain Crop Research Station (Sagam/Khudwani) and Dryland Agriculture Research Station (Budgam), SKUAST-Kashmir. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH4 was developed by MCRS Sagam, not the Dryland (Karewa) station named in the record. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- IMH-221 was developed by ICAR-IIMR Ludhiana and its release date is listed as 06 March 2023. This conflicts with the record's release date of 26 October 2022 and with the SKUAST institution. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids ; https://icar.org.in/en/icar-iimrs-hybrids-reaching-unreached-strategically-diversifying-seeds-production-site-india-0
- Lead breeder for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or H-64: not found. -- No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or postal address was found for any of the names above, or for the Dryland (Karewa) station. -- No evidence found
- ICAR-IIMR Ludhiana is the institute for IMH-221; no contact details were extracted from the retrieved page. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Institute-level contact not verified. Please check SKUAST-Kashmir and ICAR-IIMR official contact pages directly.

PUBLICATIONS
- Ahangar, M. A. et al. (year not shown in source). Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4, a Most Promising Hybrid for High Altitude Ecologies of Kashmir Valley. ResearchGate record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- Rather, A. G. et al. (year not shown in source). Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 a high yielding maize hybrid under high altitude conditions of Kashmir valley. Maize Newsletter (MNL 84) -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/HTML/03rather.htm
- Kaul, J. and Dass, S. (2010). Maize Hybrid and Composite Varieties Released in India (1961-2010), 3rd ed. Directorate of Maize Research, New Delhi -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Thesis, SKUAST-Kashmir, Division of Genetics and Plant Breeding (Reg. No. 2011-371-D). Development of bulks in maize (Zea mays L.) for shorter breeding cycle as an approach to Participatory Plant Breeding. Author and year not confirmed from the retrieved text -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/c736fd1a-1af6-41ef-bead-80a6ff4bfec0/content
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report or DOI was found specifically for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or H-64.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No SKUAST, KVK, NSC or State Seed Corporation sales listing was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or SMH4. -- No evidence found
- ICAR-IIMR is dispatching IMH 221 consignments to Jammu & Kashmir and other states. -- https://icar.org.in/en/icar-iimrs-hybrids-reaching-unreached-strategically-diversifying-seeds-production-site-india-0
- Shalimar Hybrid Seeds Co. (Hyderabad) is a private trader that lists yellow maize seed. It is unrelated to SKUAST and no link to this variety was found. -- https://www.tradeindia.com/manufacturers/maize-seeds.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- SMH4 is recommended for rainfed high-altitude temperate ecologies between 1800 and 2250 m amsl. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- IMH-221 is recommended for Jammu & Kashmir. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- The record's "Kashmir Valley" recommendation is consistent with the SMH4 source. No gazette notification for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 was found. -- No evidence found

drought.details: No drought result for SMH-2 is in the digest. The 2021 Kharif drought phenology study reports large drops in canopy temperature, biomass and chlorophyll under drought stress, but it does not state which hybrids were tested. An irrigation-regime trial used SMH-2 and SMH-3, but the snippet gives no stress results for SMH-2. The only cold-tolerance statement in the digest concerns SMH4, not SMH-2. Name note: SMH-2 (CSC name) and SMH4 (Seednet name) are different hybrids in the sources found, and neither source confirms they are the same entry. The code H-17 and release date appear in no source found, and parentage is not confirmed for either name.

heat.details: No heat tolerance evidence found for SMH-2. The digest reports that SMH4 is cold tolerant and early maturing, which suits high-altitude Kashmir. Cold tolerance is not heat tolerance and is not attributed to SMH-2.

salinity.details: No evidence found for SMH-2 on salinity tolerance.

flood.details: No evidence found for SMH-2 on flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease reaction evidence found for SMH-2. SMH4 (Seednet name, a different hybrid in the sources) is reported resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust. SMH-1 is rated only moderately resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust (disease scores 2 against 3 for the check). Neither statement applies to SMH-2.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest reaction evidence found for SMH-2. SMH4 is reported resistant to stem borers and cutworms. This applies to SMH4 only and is not attributed to SMH-2.

agronomic_details.yield: SMH-2: pooled grain yield of 6.1 t/ha, with the highest growth and yield values among three hybrids in a nitrogen-management trial at SKUAST-K Wadura (2019-2020). SMH4 (different hybrid in the sources): averaged 5.56 t/ha in All India Coordinated trials in the North Hill Zone, top yield 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura, Himachal Pradesh, projected at 7.0-8.2 t/ha, and about 23.61% grain superiority over SMH-1. SMH-1: averaged 40.4 q/ha against 31.9 q/ha for the check C-15 (the text gives q/ha while the table gives kg/ha, so units are inconsistent). The original record states All India Coordinated Trial data is missing for approval.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: SMH-2 is listed among lower-belt varieties in SKUAST-K extension guidance. SMH-1 is listed for higher belts. SMH4 is described as suited to high-altitude Kashmir Valley and was evaluated in the North Hill Zone.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Nitrogen-management trial at SKUAST-K Wadura, 2019-2020: SMH-2 gave a pooled grain yield of 6.1 t/ha and the highest growth and yield values among three hybrids. (2) Irrigation-regime trial: SMH-2 and SMH-3 were the two hybrids used; the snippet gives no stress results for SMH-2. (3) 2021 Kharif drought phenology trial in Kashmir: large drops in canopy temperature, biomass and chlorophyll under drought; hybrids tested not clearly stated. (4) All India Coordinated trials, North Hill Zone: SMH4 averaged 5.56 t/ha, top 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura, Himachal Pradesh. (5) SMH4 versus SMH-1: about 23.61% grain superiority and projected 7.0-8.2 t/ha. (6) SMH-1 versus check C-15: 40.4 q/ha against 31.9 q/ha (unit inconsistency noted).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No SSR, SNP or QTL marker details for SMH-2 found in the digest. For SMH4, DNA fingerprinting was performed at the SKUAST Kashmir biotechnology lab. Molecular markers distinguished the SMI31 x SMI462 cross from SMH-1 and were monomorphic between the two inbred parents. No marker names or positions are given.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL studies found for SMH-2 or SMH4.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Maize Hybrid-2 (CSC name) / Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4 (H-64) (Seednet name), maize, SKUAST-K

Name note: The CSC name "Shalimar Maize Hybrid-2" and the Seednet name "Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4 (H-64)" are different hybrids in the sources I found. The SMH-2 evidence below refers to Shalimar Maize Hybrid-2. The SMH4 evidence refers to Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4, the Seednet name. Neither source confirms that these are the same entry. The code H-17 and the 2014-02-14 release date appear in no source I found. Parentage is not confirmed for either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- SMH4 is described as cold tolerant and early maturing, which suits high-altitude Kashmir. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- Drought effects on maize hybrids in Kashmir were studied in a 2021 Kharif phenology trial. The source reports large drops in canopy temperature, biomass and chlorophyll under drought stress. It does not clearly state which hybrids were tested. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Agro-morphological-traits-of-Shalimar-Maize-Hybrid-4_fig1_345204771
- An irrigation-regime trial used Shalimar Hybrid-2 and Shalimar Hybrid-3 as its two hybrids. The snippet gives no stress results for SMH-2. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- No evidence found for SMH-2 on flood, submergence, salinity or heat tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
- SMH4 is reported resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust, and to stem borers and cutworms. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH-1, the older hybrid, is rated only moderately resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust (disease scores 2 against 3 for the check). -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/PDF/03rather.pdf
- No evidence found for disease or pest reactions specific to SMH-2.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- SMH-2 gave a pooled grain yield of 6.1 t/ha and the highest growth and yield values among three hybrids in a nitrogen-management trial at SKUAST-K Wadura (2019–2020). -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39920262
- SMH-2 is listed among the lower-belt varieties in SKUAST-K extension guidance, while SMH-1 is listed for higher belts. -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=June03062024.pdf
- SMH4 averaged 5.56 t/ha in All India Coordinated trials in the North Hill Zone, with a top yield of 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura, Himachal Pradesh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH4 is projected at 7.0–8.2 t/ha and gave about 23.61% grain superiority over SMH-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH-1 averaged 40.4 q/ha against 31.9 for the check C-15 (text gives q/ha, the table gives kg/ha, so units are inconsistent). -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/HTML/03rather.htm
- Sowing guidance for Kashmir is April and hybrid seed rate is about 20 kg/ha at 60 x 20 cm. -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=April+02042025.pdf
- Recommended fertiliser for irrigated hybrids is N 150, P2O5 75, K2O 40 kg/ha plus ZnSO4 20 kg/ha. -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=June03062024.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- SMH4 was fingerprinted by DNA and characterised by protein profiling at the SKUAST Kashmir biotechnology lab. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- Molecular markers distinguished the SMI31 x SMI462 cross from SMH-1 and were monomorphic between the two inbred parents. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH-1 was developed from two inbred parents, W3 and W5. -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/HTML/03rather.htm
- No QTL studies found for SMH-2 or SMH4.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- SMH4 was developed by Mountain Crop Research Station (MCRS), Sagam, SKUAST-K. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH4 authors: M. Ashraf Ahangar, Asif B. Shikari, Showkat A. Waza, F. A. Sheikh, S. Najeeb, N. A. Teeli, Z. A. Dar, Ajaz A. Lone. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH-1 was released from the High Altitude Maize Research Sub-Station, Sagam. Its authors include

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VLQPM Hybrid 45 / VLQPM Hybrid 61 (maize, FQH165), evidence digest

Name note: the CSC name "VLQPM Hybrid 45" and the Seednet name "VLQPM Hybrid 61" are two different hybrids in the retrieved sources. Each finding below states which name it refers to. The parentage VBL 17 x VQL 1 appears in the source only for VLQPM Hybrid 61, not for Hybrid 45. Searches 1 to 4 were run; no separate seed-availability search was run within the query budget.

STRESS TOLERANCE

VLQPM Hybrid 45: Moderate resistance to turcicum leaf blight was observed, and the source describes the hybrid as tolerant to major diseases. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61: It also exhibited moderate resistance to turcicum and maydis leaf blight. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for either name in the retrieved text.

DISEASE AND PEST

VLQPM Hybrid 45: Moderate resistance to turcicum leaf blight (see Stress Tolerance above). No pest resistance evidence found. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61: Moderate resistance to turcicum and maydis leaf blight (see Stress Tolerance above). No pest resistance evidence found. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

VLQPM Hybrid 45 (maturity): Early maturing, with 90-95 days reported. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 45 (yield): Optimal performance of 7,805 kg/ha under 250:80:100 kg/ha NPK and a plant density of 83,000/ha, and the hybrid is described as responsive to nitrogen. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 45 (AICRP Zone I): Average yield of 6,673 kg/ha in AICRP trials during 2021-22, at par with the original hybrid VMH 45. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 45 (grain): Purple anthers, purple glume and silk; green husk; yellow, flint, round, medium-bold grain with a 1000-grain weight of about 300 g. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (maturity): Described as early maturing (85-90 days in mid-hills) and also as 95-100 days to maturity. The source is internally inconsistent; both values are reported. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (yield): Average of 4,435 kg/ha in state varietal trials in Uttarakhand hills during 2018-20, with 10.9% superiority over the QPM check Vivek QPM 9 under organic conditions. Optimal performance of 8,876 kg/ha under 150:60:60 kg/ha NPK. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (quality): 0.76% tryptophan, 3.30% lysine and 9.16% protein. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (grain and plant): Yellow, semi-flint, flat, medium-bold grain (1000-grain weight about 260 g); plant height 200-210 cm. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105

GENETICS AND QTL

VLQPM Hybrid 61 (parentage): Developed by crossing QPM lines VBL 17 (female) and VQL 1 (male). -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (line origin): VBL 17 and VQL 1 were developed by introgressing the opaque-2 allele using marker-assisted selection. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 45 (genetics): Developed by introgressing the opaque-2 allele using marker-assisted selection; the parental pedigree is not given in the retrieved text. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
QTL or marker mapping studies for either name: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

Developing institution (both names): ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, Uttarakhand. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
Named corresponding author (VLQPM Hybrid 45 and 61 variety bulletin): Rajesh Khulbe, ICAR-VPKAS, Almora. Full author list is not visible in the retrieved text. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
Almora AICRP maize directory: Dr. R.K. Khulbe is listed as Senior Scientist & I/C, Plant Breeding. Other breeders are also listed at the centre, but none is confirmed as a developer of this hybrid. -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Directory/Directory_2025.pdf
Institute profile: VPKAS is recognised as a pioneer maize breeding centre, and the centre reports 32 released varieties (9 composites and 23 hybrids). -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/almora-uttarakhand/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (maize) evidence digest

Name check: the CSC release minutes name and the Seednet name are identical ("VLQPM Hybrid 61"). The evidence below refers to that name, which the source also writes as "VLQPMH 61." No Seednet portal page was returned, so the Seednet record itself is unverified. Four searches were run: variety/release, breeder/institute, research papers, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this hybrid. The waterlogging and drought studies returned (e.g., the Asia AWDT multi-location trial and the waterlogging multi-environment trial) involve other hybrids, so I excluded them. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358285361_Multi-environment_field_testing_to_identify_better_performing_and_stable_genotypes_for_water_logging_stress_tolerance_in_tropical_maize (excluded, other hybrids); https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12554654/ (excluded, other hybrids)

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderate resistance to turcicum leaf blight and maydis leaf blight is reported for this hybrid. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
No pest-resistance data were found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Single-cross QPM hybrid, released and notified by the CSC on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties (S.O. 4065(E), dated 31.08.22) for Uttarakhand hills. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Maturity: the same source gives both 85-90 days in mid-hills and 95-100 days to maturity, which conflict; both are recorded here. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Average yield of 4,435 kg/ha in state varietal trials (2018-20, Uttarakhand hills), 10.9% above the QPM check Vivek QPM 9 under organic conditions. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Yield of about 8,876 kg/ha under 150:60:60 kg/ha NPK; the hybrid responds to nitrogen. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Plant height 200-210 cm. Grain is yellow, semi-flint, flat and medium-bold, with 1000-grain weight of about 260 g. Purple anthers, glume and silk; green husk with good cover. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Grain quality: 9.16% protein, 0.76% tryptophan, 3.30% lysine. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Parentage: the source says it was developed by crossing QPM lines including VBL 17; the second parent is truncated in the retrieved text, so VQL 1 could not be confirmed from the source. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL, marker or MAS studies specific to VLQPM Hybrid 61. The MAS-derived QPM work returned concerns Vivek QPM 9 and is excluded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263374947_Accelerated_development_of_quality_protein_maize_hybrid_through_marker-assisted_introgression_of_opaque-2_allele (excluded, other hybrid)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- The VPKAS maize listing gives the release as 2022 (SVRC), area Uttarakhand, which differs from the CSC notification route in the publication above. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize
- No lead breeder name for this variety was found in the retrieved text. Names on other VPKAS maize releases were not transferred to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute postal address: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Almora 263 601 (263601), Uttarakhand, India. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Institute website: https://vpkas.icar.gov.in (official ICAR-VPKAS site, from the maize listing page).
- No breeder name, email or phone number for this variety was found in the search results. Institute contact details were not visible beyond the address and website.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured in the retrieved text (year not confirmed). "Maize Variety VL VitA VLQPM Hybrid 45" (release notification compilation, includes a VLQPM Hybrid 61 entry). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding (IJGPB). -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Authors not captured (year not confirmed). "Vivek Maize hybrid 51 (FH 3554)" (release notification) lists VPKAS as developer, but does not mention VLQPM Hybrid 61 in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554 (excluded, other hybrid)
- No peer-reviewed field-trial papers, AICRP/ICAR reports or KrishiKosh theses specifically on VLQPM Hybrid 61 were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this hybrid was returned. The only related statement is that the publication expects the high-yielding parents to keep seed prices reasonable, which is a projection, not a seed-sale record. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105

RECOMMENDED STATES
Uttarakhand (hill regions). -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105 ; https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME CHECK
variety_name (CSC minutes) = "VLQPM Hybrid 63"; seednet_variety_name = "VLQPM Hybrid 63". Both names are identical, so all evidence below refers to both. The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved; the Seednet crop label was not checked against a live page.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderate resistance to turcicum leaf blight and maydis leaf blight, reported in the 2018-20 state trials -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data for this hybrid under those conditions.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate resistance to turcicum leaf blight and maydis leaf blight (same finding as above) -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Early maturing, 90-95 days in mid-hills; plant height 215-225 cm; 1000-grain weight about 280 g -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- State varietal trials in Uttarakhand hills, 2018-20: mean yield 4,675 kg/ha, 16.9% above the QPM check Vivek QPM 9 under organic conditions -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Responsive to nitrogen; 9,671 kg/ha at 150:60:60 kg/ha NPK -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Grain quality: 9.22% protein, 0.72% tryptophan, 3.20% lysine; semi-flint, yellow grain with purple anthers and glume -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Institute variety listing (SVRC, 2022, Uttarakhand) -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: VQL 398 (female) x V 467 (male). VQL 398 carries the opaque-2 allele introgressed by marker-assisted backcross breeding; V 467 is a high lysine and tryptophan line -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- QPM (quality protein maize) single-cross hybrid -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- QTL or marker-validation studies specific to this hybrid: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Named lead breeder or scientist for VLQPM Hybrid 63: No evidence found. The retrieved pages name only the institute. Names associated with other VPKAS QPM hybrids (Vivek QPM 9, Vivek Maize Hybrid 9) were found in other pages and were not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute name and postal address as printed: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Almora 263 601, Uttrakhand, India -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Institute website: https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize (official ICAR-VPKAS site)
- Official email: No evidence found
- Phone: No evidence found
- Breeder name, role, email or phone: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not confirmed in retrieved text (2022 variety notification compilation). Maize Variety VL VitA and VLQPM Hybrid 45 (includes VLQPM Hybrid 63 entry). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding (ISGPB) -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105 (Year: not confirmed in retrieved text; DOI: not found)
- The author names "H. Rajashekara" and "D. Mahanta" appear in the retrieved text near this entry, but their role for this variety is not confirmed, so they are not attributed here.
- Other QPM or VPKAS publications were found but do not name VLQPM Hybrid 63, so they are excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. Searches returned only generic seed-company, CIMMYT and seed-production pages, none naming this hybrid. Check the VPKAS Almora seed unit, the Uttarakhand State Seed Corporation or a KVK directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified for cultivation in Uttarakhand hills (S.O. 4065(E), dated 31.08.22) -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- VPKAS maize listing gives area of adaptation as Uttarakhand (SVRC, 2022) -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize
- Discrepancy: the notification text refers to the Central Sub-committee on Crop Standards (CSC). The VPKAS listing shows an SVRC (state) release. Verify the release body before citing it as a central release.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Vivek Maize Hybrid-27 (release-minutes name, variety_code FH 3288) and Vivek Hybrid Maize-53 (Seednet name, "Vivek Hybrid Maize - 53")

NAME NOTE: Every page that names "Vivek Maize Hybrid-27" or "Vivek Hybrid 27" points to the VPKAS Almora hybrid with pedigree V 335 x V 345. The Seednet name "Vivek Hybrid Maize - 53" points to a different hybrid, Vivek Maize Hybrid 53 (FH 3556), with parents V 407 x V 409. I found no page linking Vivek-53 to Vivek-27, so the Seednet-name findings are listed separately below and are not attributed to Vivek-27. The FH 3288 code appears on no page I retrieved. The input release year (2011-06-28) conflicts with the 2007 notification evidence (1703(E), 05/10/2007).

STRESS TOLERANCE
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: the 1961-2010 release compendium lists resistance to turcicum leaf blight (TLB) and common rust for Vivek 27 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was stated for this hybrid in any retrieved page. No evidence found for those stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: TLB and common rust resistance as listed in the 1961-2010 compendium -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: no pest-resistance data (stem borer, fall armyworm) was found. No evidence found for pests.
Seednet name (Vivek Hybrid Maize-53, not Vivek-27): tolerance to turcicum leaf blight, maydis leaf blight and a moderate rust reaction, reported over three years of multilocation trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: extra-early maturity and 5.0-5.5 t/ha yield in the 2000-era hybrid list -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: a yield of 85 q/ha is printed beside the Vivek 27 entry in the 1961-2010 compendium, but the layout is ambiguous and this conflicts with the 5.0-5.5 t/ha figure -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: the Vivek 27 entry in the 2010 compendium lists a leaf-angle trait score; no trial data was found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
Seednet name (Vivek-53, not Vivek-27): 12 multilocation trials in Zone I gave 7676 kg/ha, 26.08% above the Vivek QPM 9 check; plant height 185-195 cm; maturity 85-90 days in mid hills and 80-85 days in plains -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554
Seednet name (Vivek-53, not Vivek-27): a benchmarking table lists VMH 53 as a 7.6 t/ha, extra-early hybrid for Kharif in Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttarakhand and UP -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

GENETICS AND QTL
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: single cross with pedigree V 335 x V 345 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: no QTL, marker or molecular study naming this hybrid was found. No evidence found.
Seednet name (Vivek-53, not Vivek-27): parents V 407 (female) and V 409 (male) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: developed by ICAR-VPKAS, Almora (Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Uttarakhand), notified 2007 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: no named breeder or lead scientist was found on any page. No evidence found for breeder names.
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: release-year conflict. The input says 2011-06-28, but the compendium gives 05/10/2007 under notification 1703(E) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: FH 3288 code not found on any page. No evidence found for the variety code.
Seednet name (Vivek-53): developed by VPKAS Almora, identified by the Varietal Identification Committee -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554

CONTACT DETAILS
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: No evidence found. No breeder contact, email, phone or address appeared on a page that names this variety. The VPKAS Almora address seen on Gupta et al. pages concerns a different QPM hybrid (Vivek Maize Hybrid 9 / QPM 9), so it was excluded.
Seednet name (Vivek-53): the seed-portal page lists "VPKAS" as brand but gives no contact details -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VivekMaizeHybrid53_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%95%E0%A

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield of 6686 kg/ha across trials, with consistent superiority over checks Prakash (15.4-29.2%) and JH3459 (14.1-32.9%). Assam package lists a potential yield of 69 q/ha (about 6900 kg/ha); this is a package-level figure and its variety attribution is not explicit in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Consistent superiority over the checks Prakash and JH3459 across trials. The digest gives no further across-environment stability analysis.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to rainfed hill agro-ecosystems and the marginal Himalayan environment (mid hills). The digest lists the adaptation ecology as NEH Region in the original data, but no NEH-specific trial evidence was found in the digest. Hybrid seed should not be saved for resowing because of segregation (Assam package).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 90-95 days in mid hills; 80-90 days duration per Assam package
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height about 200-210 cm in the hills; semi-flint grain, yellow with purplish glume and brown anther. Assam package: yellow cob with white cap.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Station trials over three years under natural infection rated high tolerance to Turcicum and Maydis leaf blights (see disease_resistance). (2) Multi-trial average yield of 6686 kg/ha, with superiority over Prakash by 15.4-29.2% and over JH3459 by 14.1-32.9%. (3) Agronomy trials showed 21.8% yield superiority over JH3459 and 22.7% over Prakash. (4) Identified by the Varietal Identification Committee at the 56th Maize Workshop, ANGRAU Hyderabad, 6-8 April 2013. (5) A benchmarking table lists Hybrid 47 at 6.9 t/ha under a Uttar Pradesh Kharif row, but the digest marks this attribution as unverified and the table layout as ambiguous; it is excluded from the yield figures above. Fertilizer, seed rate and sowing schedule data specific to this hybrid were not found beyond the generic Assam package.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: "Vivek Maize Hybrid 47" (CSC name, code FH 3513) is the only name with matching evidence. No page was found under the Seednet name "Vivek Hybrid Maize - 53". Every Hybrid 53 page found refers to a different hybrid, so none is used below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Described as drought tolerant and suited to rainfed hill agro-ecosystems, with combined high grain yield and tolerance to major diseases and insects, for the marginal Himalayan environment -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554 (names Hybrid 47 in its section; the page title refers to Hybrid 51)
Listed as drought resistant in the Assam package-of-practice table -- https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/maize
Heat, salinity, flood, waterlogging, submergence: No evidence found for this variety (the search returned only general or other-variety content).

DISEASE AND PEST
High tolerance to Turcicum leaf blight (H. turcicum) and high tolerance to Maydis leaf blight (H. maydis) under natural infection over three years of station trials, with the parents also rated tolerant -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554
Generic statement that the listed hybrids are resistant to most diseases "to a fair degree" (the list includes Hybrid 47, but the statement is not specific to it) -- https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/maize
Insect pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Average yield of 6686 kg/ha across trials, with consistent superiority over checks Prakash (15.4-29.2%) and JH3459 (14.1-32.9%) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554

Maturity 90-95 days in mid hills; plant height about 200-210 cm in the hills; semi-flint grain, yellow with purplish glume and brown anther -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554
