seednet_fields.Parentage: TM102 X TM28 TM102 is Interspecific recombinants and TM28 is yellow and Bold seed coat mutant.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated condition during Rabi/winter season of W.B. and also suitable for irrigated eco-system of zone-V (Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Assam, Manipur).
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Resistant to lodging and seed shattering. Reponse well to recommended fertilizer @ 140: 70: 70 kg NPK/ha. With 30 cm. X 10cm. spacing: Seed rate: 7kg/ha.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: Waxy leaves and bold glossy seeds, Long main fru
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Leaves dark green, flower yellow colour, pods two locules with prominent constriction. Leaf suface rough.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Moderately resistant to alternaria leaf spot up 75 days after sowing.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Negligible to moderate aphid infestation.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): N: P2O5:K2O @ 140:70:70, N in three splits (50% as basal, 25% at 30 days after sowing and 25% at 45 days after sowing).

drought.details: No drought tolerance score for TBM-204 was found in the retrieved text. The variety is described as irrigated rabi/winter-season material in the adaptation evidence, which does not establish drought performance. Not found in searched sources.

heat.details: No TBM-204-specific heat trial or heat tolerance score was found. A zenodo heat-stress paper cites the TBM-204 notification but does not name TBM-204 as tested; that source was discarded as evidence for this variety.

salinity.details: Coastal (saline-zone) trials at BCKV Kakdwip with TBM-204 under late sowing were reported in a 2019 paper, but no salinity score was reported in the retrieved text. The backcross mapping population was developed at the RRS Coastal Saline Zone (2018-20) but no salinity result was retrieved.

flood.details: No flood tolerance score or evidence for TBM-204 was found in the retrieved text.

disease_resistance.summary: Field tolerance to Alternaria blight and white rust is reported for TBM-204 in the notification paper. No severity scores or disease levels were given in the retrieved text, so no resistance level is assigned. Note: the digest lists lodging and seed-shattering resistance (not a disease) as stated in the notification paper; the BCKV source records disease_reaction as 'Not Specified' in the original variety data.

pest_resistance.summary: Field tolerance to aphid (insect pest) is reported for TBM-204 in the notification paper. No other pest data was found. No severity scores were given, so no resistance level is assigned.

agronomic_details.yield: Average seed yield of 1336 kg/ha over 4 years of multi-location trials in West Bengal (notification paper), against Kranti (1211 kg/ha), Pusa Bold (1159 kg/ha) and B-9 (948 kg/ha). Attainable yield of 1500-1800 kg/ha under optimum sowing and management (notification paper). BCKV crop-variety table: seed yield 15.0 q/ha (equivalent to 1500 kg/ha). Oil content 41% (notification paper and BCKV table).
agronomic_details.stability: Over three years at 13 BCKV locations (2013-16), TM 204 showed a 10-15% yield advantage over Kranti and Pusa Bold. Coastal Kakdwip trial (2014-16): seed yield statistically at par with the best entry. Multi-location average across 4 years in West Bengal is reported in the notification paper. No formal stability statistic (e.g., AMMI or GGE) was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated rabi/winter season in West Bengal (digest adaptation evidence). Tested in the IVT (rabi 2016-17, Zone-V, timely-sown rainfed) and in coastal saline-zone trials at Kakdwip under late sowing. Zone-V state list (Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Assam, Manipur) appears in the ORIGINAL VARIETY DATA only and is not confirmed by the digest's trial evidence. Agronomy: fertilizer at 140:70:70 kg NPK/ha; spacing 30 cm x 10 cm; seed rate 7 kg/ha; resistant to lodging and seed shattering (original variety data and notification paper).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 110 To 95Days (duration conflict in the digest: 100 days per ResearchGate figure, 110 days per BCKV table, 115 days per notification paper; all three recorded, not resolved)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Waxy leaves and bold glossy seeds, Long main fru (original text is truncated in the source). BCKV table: plant height 155-160 cm; test weight 4.7 g. Yellow seed coat (notification paper). Resistant to lodging and seed shattering.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Notification paper IVT, rabi 2016-17, Zone-V, timely-sown rainfed: 23% yield gain over national check Kranti. (2) Notification paper, 4-year multi-location trials in West Bengal: mean 1336 kg/ha vs Kranti 1211, Pusa Bold 1159, B-9 948. (3) 2013-16 multi-location trial at 13 BCKV locations: TM 204 gave 10-15% yield advantage over Kranti and Pusa Bold over three years (no authors retrieved). (4) Coastal Kakdwip trial, 2014-16: TM 204 gave the highest siliqua count on the main axis and seed yield statistically at par with the best entry. (5) Coastal West Bengal fertilizer x variety trial included TBM 204 and TBM 143; no result for TBM-204 was retrieved. (6) Coastal late-sowing trials at Kakdwip (2019 paper): no salinity score reported. (7) Backcross mapping population (2018-20) linked to TBM-204; no yield or QTL result retrieved. No heat trial was found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: SSR marker analysis gives distinct alleles for TBM-204 versus Kranti and Pusa Bold. No marker names or positions were reported in the retrieved text. Pedigree: TM102 x TM28. TM102 is an interspecific recombinant; TM28 is a yellow-seeded, bold-seeded mutant.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: A backcross mapping population (2018-20, RRS Coastal Saline Zone) is linked to TBM-204 in the same paper, but no QTL result was retrieved. QTLs and effects: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: TBM-204 (CSC release-minute name) / TM-204 (Seednet name), mustard (Brassica juncea)

Name note: The journal paper and BCKV pages use "TBM-204" or "TBM 204". The BARC-BCKV programme page and the coastal trial paper use "TM-204" or "TM 204". The Seednet portal was not reachable through search, so no Seednet record was found. Under each heading below, the evidence refers to the name shown in the source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Field tolerance to aphids, Alternaria blight and white rust is reported for TBM-204 in the notification paper -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- The variety is reported as not lodging or shattering at maturity -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693
- Coastal (saline-zone) trials at BCKV Kakdwip with TBM-204 under late sowing were reported in a 2019 paper -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602 (no salinity score was reported in the retrieved text)
- No drought, flood, submergence or heat tolerance score for TBM-204 was found in the retrieved text. A 2025 seed-priming study on TBM-204 seed quality does not give a stress score -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-09325-z

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerance to aphid (insect pest) and to Alternaria blight and white rust under field conditions -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- No other pest or disease data for TBM-204 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Notification paper: 23% yield gain over national check Kranti in the IVT (rabi 2016-17, Zone-V, timely-sown rainfed) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693
- Notification paper: average seed yield of 1336 kg/ha over 4 years of multi-location trials in West Bengal, against Kranti (1211), Pusa Bold (1159) and B-9 (948) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693
- Notification paper: attainable yield 1500-1800 kg/ha under optimum sowing and management; harvest about 115 days after sowing; oil content 41% -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- BCKV crop-variety table: duration 110 days, plant height 155-160 cm, test weight 4.7 g, seed yield 15.0 q/ha, oil 41% -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- Note the duration conflict: 100 days (ResearchGate figure), 110 days (BCKV table), 115 days (notification paper). Record all three.
- 2013-16 multi-location trial at 13 BCKV locations: TM 204 showed 10-15% yield advantage over Kranti and Pusa Bold over three years -- https://cwss.in/Journal/Complete_jurnal/Vol.13-No.1__22.pdf (the year is 2013-16, the journal volume is 13; no author list was retrieved)
- Coastal Kakdwip trial (2014-16): TM 204 gave the highest siliqua count on the main axis and seed yield statistically at par with the best entry -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/89005
- Fertilizer x variety trial in coastal West Bengal included TBM 204 and TBM 143 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602
- Heat stress: no TBM-204-specific heat trial was found. A zenodo heat-stress paper cites the TBM-204 notification but does not name TBM-204 as tested -- https://zenodo.org/records/18681400 (discarded as evidence for this variety)

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree breeding: TM102 x TM28 cross made at BARC Trombay -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- TM102 is an interspecific recombinant; TM28 is a yellow-seeded, bold-seeded mutant -- same URL
- SSR marker analysis gives distinct alleles for TBM-204 versus Kranti and Pusa Bold -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693
- A backcross mapping population (2018-20, RRS Coastal Saline Zone) is linked to TBM-204 in the same paper; no QTL result was retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Flow-chart-showing-development-and-evaluation-of-backcross-mapping-population-used-in_fig1_344401463

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead authors (all Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, Mohanpur, Nadia): Amitava Dutta (first author), Sanjay J Jambhulkar, Archana N Rai, Shankar Bhujbal, H Banerjee, R Das, S Dewanjee, S Sarkar, M Pramanik, S Mandal -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136693
- Development was a collaboration between BARC (Trombay, Mumbai) and BCKV -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- BARC affiliation of the paper: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Trombay, Mumbai 400085 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- Applicant on the BCKV variety list: BCKV -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address (BCKV, Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal, PIN 741252) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/Varieties-developed_nw.pdf ; same address on the notification paper -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- No breeder email, phone or direct institute contact page was found in the retrieved results. Institute-level contact only: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, Mohanpur, Nadia 741252, West Bengal.
- BARC-BCKV programme page: https://bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/barc-bckv-programme-en (no contact details on the retrieved text)

PUBLICATIONS
- Dutta A, Jambhulkar SJ, Rai AN, Bhujbal S, Banerjee H, Das R, Dewanjee S, Sarkar S, Pramanik M, Mandal S (2019). Trombay Bidhan Mustard-204 (TBM-204): A high yielding yellow seed coat mustard [Brassica juncea (L.) Czern. & Coss.] variety notified for West Bengal. Journal of Oilseeds Research 36(4): 220-224 -- https://doi.org/10.56739/jor.v36i4.136693 (the ResearchGate page dates it September 2020; the journal volume is 36(4))
- Dutta A, Jambulkar SJ, Rai AN, Bhujbal S, Banerjee H, Das R, Dewanjee S, Sarkar S, Pramanik M, Mandal S (2019). Varietal and Fertilization Effects on Growth and Yield of Mustard under Coastal Environment. Journal of Interdisciplinary Sciences / JISCAR -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602
- Authors not retrieved (year not stated; journal Vol. 13 No. 1). Performance of yellow coated mustard (Brassica juncea L.) in West Bengal (2013-16 trials) -- https://cwss.in/Journal/Complete_jurnal/Vol.13-No.1__22.pdf
- Authors not retrieved (year not stated). Selection of Rapeseed-mustard Varieties in Coastal Region of West Bengal: A Way Forward to Rice-fallow Intensification. JISCAR -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/89005
- Authors not retrieved (2025). Physiological, biochemical and enzymatic quality parameters of primed seed of rapeseed-mustard genotypes. Scientific Reports -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-09325-z
- Not found: KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report entries, or a conference paper naming TBM-204 in the four searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The searches (run once on seed availability) returned only unrelated seed sellers (mustard greens, culinary seed, wheat "TAM 204", Sinapis alba) and a commodity exchange page. None names TBM-204 or TM-204.
- BCKV variety table lists the variety but gives no seed-sale information -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- No NSC, WB State Seed Corporation, KVK, BCKV seed sales or private dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Napier Grass Culture 21

Name note: The CSC name "Napier Grass Culture 21" and the Seednet name "Napier Grass Culture-21" both appeared in the searches, but neither exact string matched any result. Every finding below is about Napier grass (Pennisetum purpureum) in general, or about other named Napier varieties. None of it is confirmed as referring to this variety. Four searches were run, the maximum allowed.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No variety-specific evidence found. A general review says Napier grass growth and nutritive value are limited by low temperatures and drought, and that pearl millet x Napier hybrids were developed partly to improve drought tolerance -- https://gms.ctahr.hawaii.edu/gs/handler/getmedia.ashx?moid=3787&dt=3&g=12
Flood, submergence, salinity: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No variety-specific evidence found. The same Hawaii document describes Napier grass as generally resistant to most pests and diseases, with no variety named -- https://gms.ctahr.hawaii.edu/gs/handler/getmedia.ashx?moid=3787&dt=3&g=12

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No variety-specific evidence found. A 2017 MDPI review gives a general yield figure for Napier cultivars of about 60 t dry matter/ha/year -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/7/2/28 . A 2025 study titled "Growth-Stage dependent nutritional dynamics of super Napier grass" is listed on ResearchGate; it does not name Napier Grass Culture 21 in the retrieved text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/367817651_Lignocellulosic_Bioethanol_Production_of_Napier_Grass_Using_Trichoderma_reesei_and_Saccharomyces_cerevisiae_Co-Culture_Fermentation (related listing; the specific 2025 item was seen only as a title fragment).

GENETICS AND QTL -- No variety-specific evidence found. General Napier grass QTL and genotyping work exists, for example a 2024 whole-genome resequencing study of a global collection that mentions yield QTL -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12239605/ . Parentage for this variety is not known and was not found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder or developing institution found for Napier Grass Culture 21. A ResearchGate listing of Napier hybrids attributes NB 21, BN 2, CO 1, CO 2 and CO 3 to TNAU; these are other varieties, and no link to this one was found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366739789_Hybrid_napier_grass_a_potential_asset_for_livestock_production . Whether this variety was developed by TNAU or another institute is unverified.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, scientist, email, phone, address or institute contact page for this variety was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- No publication naming this variety was found. Related general items:
Authors not captured in search result (2017). Opportunities for Napier Grass (Pennisetum purpureum) Improvement Using Molecular Genetics. Agronomy 7(2):28. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/agronomy7020028
Garg, S.; Meel, M. S.; Gautam, L. (2025). Growth-Stage dependent nutritional dynamics of super Napier grass. Journal not confirmed from the search text (listed on ResearchGate, May 2025). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/367817651 (related listing; title and authors are partial)

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No seed source for Napier Grass Culture 21 was found. Retailers found sell generic or differently named Napier seed: Livingstone, Vattappara, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, sells "Super Napier Grass Seeds" -- https://www.indiamart.com/livingstone/lawn-grass-seeds.html ; RK Seeds sells Napier grass seed on IndiaMart -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rk-seeds-napier-grass-seeds-elephant-grass-seeds-pennisetum-purpureum-pack-of-1-kg-21502286688.html ; Farmson Biotech Napier seed on BigHaat -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/farmson-biotech-napier-grass-seeds . No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed sale was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found that this variety is recommended for Kerala or any other state. The only Kerala link is the Thiruvananthapuram seed retailer above, which does not establish a recommendation.

RELEASE AND METADATA -- Year of release (NaT) and parentage remain unknown. The crop label "millet" does not match the Seednet entry "Napier grass (elephant grass)"; Napier is a forage grass related to pearl millet, not a millet.

drought.details: Napier grass is described as drought tolerant and persistent, but this is generic to the species and not confirmed for CO-4 or for the Seednet/CSC entry. A Kerala water-stress study names CO-3, CO-5 and Super Napier, not CO-4. No CO-4 specific drought mechanism or trial data were found. The variety name is matched to CO-4 by inference only.

heat.details: No CO-4 specific heat tolerance data were found.

salinity.details: No CO-4 specific salinity tolerance data were found.

flood.details: No CO-4 specific flood tolerance data were found.

disease_resistance.summary: No CO-4 specific disease resistance evidence was found. Napier grass is described generically as vulnerable to disease and pest attacks, not CO-4 specific. The KVK Pathanamthitta page attributes pest and disease resistance to CO-3, not CO-4. No diseases with confirmed resistance in CO-4 are reported in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: No CO-4 specific pest resistance evidence was found. Napier grass is described generically as vulnerable to pest attacks. The KVK Pathanamthitta page attributes pest resistance to CO-3, not CO-4. No pests with confirmed resistance in CO-4 are reported in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: CO (CN) 4 gave a mean green fodder yield of 382 t/ha/year (reported in the MASU source), a 33 per cent increase over the check CO 3. The ICAR-IVRI Izatnagar trial of Co 4 recorded a maximum green fodder yield of 307.7 q/ha in 2015-16. Units differ between the two sources (t/ha versus q/ha) and both are reported as given. These are general CO-4 references, not confirmed for the Seednet/CSC entry.
agronomic_details.stability: The ICAR-IVRI trial (2013-14 to 2017-18, irrigated, UP) recorded a yield fall in the fourth year. Ratoon regrowth was good, and the crop was judged productive for 5-6 years. No multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CO (CN) 4 is described as well adapted to Tamil Nadu. Kerala is listed among major Cumbu Napier growing states. KVK Pathanamthitta (Kerala) offers CO-4 slips, which is use evidence and not an official recommendation. The ICAR-IVRI trial was conducted under irrigated conditions in UP. No Kerala-specific CO-4 trial data were found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified for CO-4. Generic Napier grass takes about 3-4 months after planting for first harvest, with cuts every 6-8 weeks (not CO-4 specific).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CO (CN) 4 is a triploid, so it is sterile and propagated vegetatively. Planting rate for Cumbu Napier seed/slip is 33,333 two-eye stem cuttings per hectare at 60 x 50 cm, and planting can be done year-round under irrigation. Ratoon regrowth was good in the ICAR-IVRI trial. Morphological characteristics were not found in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) MASU/TNAU release paper: mean green fodder yield of 382 t/ha/year, a 33 per cent increase over the check CO 3. (2) ICAR-IVRI Izatnagar trial of Co 4 (2013-14 to 2017-18, irrigated, UP): maximum green fodder yield of 307.7 q/ha in 2015-16, yield fell in the fourth year, ratoon regrowth was good, and the crop was judged productive for 5-6 years. (3) Hybrid CO-3, CO-5 and Super Napier were evaluated under water stress with irrigation in humid tropical Kerala; CO-4 is not named in that study. (4) The North Konkan Zone of Maharashtra study on Bajra Napier hybrid varieties is listed in the digest as a publication only, with no result data in the digest. No Kerala-specific CO-4 trial results were found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found for CO-4 in searched sources. A whole-genome resequencing study of a global Napier collection (ILRI-led) and a genetic study of Napier genotypes for biomass, water-use efficiency and feed quality are not CO-4 specific, and the digest gives no marker names or positions. A KAU Vellayani RAPD characterisation of 15 Napier accessions from AICRP centres is also not linked to CO-4 marker data in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not CO-4 specific. The ILRI-led whole-genome resequencing and QTL study reports QTL for yield and feed quality in a global Napier collection. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Napier Grass Culture 4 (variety_name) / Napier Grass Culture-4 (seednet_variety_name), crop: millet (Napier grass / elephant grass), variety code A062216651

Name mapping: No search result mentioned "Napier Grass Culture 4" or "Napier Grass Culture-4" as a named variety. The closest match is the TNAU hybrid CO (CN) 4 / CO-4 (Cumbu Napier), which is cited below. Every finding under the headings below refers to CO-4 by inference from the name, not to a confirmed record for the CSC or Seednet entry. The CSC release minutes, the release year, and the parentage for this exact entry were not found. Parentage is given only for CO-4 as a general reference.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Napier grass is described as drought tolerant and persistent, but this is generic to the species, not CO-4 specific -- https://ekishaan.com/napier-and-its-cultivation/
- Napier grass is described as drought tolerant and vulnerable to disease and pest attacks, again not CO-4 specific -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/igc/23/2-6-1/36
- Hybrid CO-3, CO-5 and Super Napier were evaluated under water stress with irrigation in humid tropical Kerala; CO-4 is not named in that title -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268381528_Hybrid_Napier_Pennisetum_perpureum_X_Pennisetum_americarnum_VAR_CO-3_a_resourceful_fodder_grass_for_dairy_development_in_Sri_Lanka (reference list entry)
- No CO-4 specific heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data were found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The KVK Pathanamthitta page attributes pest and disease resistance to CO-3, not CO-4 -- https://kvkcard.org//products.php
- No CO-4 specific disease or pest resistance evidence was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CO (CN) 4 is a triploid, so it is sterile and propagated vegetatively -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/96-7-12-291-292.pdf
- CO (CN) 4 gave a mean green fodder yield of 382 t/ha/year, a 33 per cent increase over the check CO 3 -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/96-7-12-291-292.pdf
- ICAR-IVRI Izatnagar trial of Co 4 (2013-14 to 2017-18, irrigated, UP): maximum green fodder yield of 307.7 q/ha in 2015-16; yield fell in the fourth year; ratoon regrowth was good and the crop was judged productive for 5-6 years -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=6529&context=igc
- Napier grass generally takes about 3-4 months after planting for first harvest, with cuts every 6-8 weeks -- https://ekishaan.com/napier-and-its-cultivation/
- Cumbu Napier seed/slip planting rate: 33,333 two-eye stem cuttings per hectare at 60 x 50 cm; can be planted year-round under irrigation -- https://kvknamakkalfodder.com/product/cumbu-napier-grass-slips/
- Kerala-specific CO-4 trial data were not found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- CO (CN) 4 came from a cross of Cumbu CO 8 with Napier FD 461 made in 2001 -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/96-7-12-291-292.pdf
- Another source describes CO-4 as a pearl millet x Napier cross made at TNAU Coimbatore -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374536154_A_High_Yielding_Cumbu_Napier_Hybrid_Grass_CO_CN_4
- Whole-genome resequencing and QTL study of a global Napier collection (ILRI-led): QTL for yield and feed quality, not CO-4 specific -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12239605/
- Genetic and QTL study of Napier genotypes for biomass, water-use efficiency and feed quality, not CO-4 specific -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8776657/
- KAU Vellayani RAPD characterisation of 15 Napier accessions from AICRP centres -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/communities/f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7?spc.page=1&spc.sf=dc.date.accessioned&spc.sd=DESC&scope=f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAMES SEARCHED: "Birsa Niger-3" (variety_name) and "Birsa Niger-3 (BNS-11)" (seednet_variety_name). Searches were run on both names. No Seednet portal page turned up in any search, so the Seednet name is attested only through the code BNS-11 on other sites. No CSC release minutes were found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought tolerance is listed for Birsa Niger-3 (BNS-11) in the Directorate of Oilseeds Development table, which also gives an 85-day early maturity -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx
- The biodiesel feedstock review's table gives an 85-day maturity and strong drought tolerance for the Birsa Niger-3 (BNS-11) row -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385299465_Fueling_the_future_Sustainable_Biodiesel_Production_Strategies_for_a_Cleaner_Tomorrow
- The NICRA (ICAR-ATARI Kolkata) 2012-13 report lists "Niger (Var. Birsa Niger-3)" among drought-tolerant varieties demonstrated in NICRA villages. The yield columns are not labelled in the extract, so no yield figure is recorded here -- http://www.atarikolkata.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/Annual-Report-NICRA-12-13.pdf
- No evidence found for salinity, flood, submergence or heat tolerance specific to this variety. The only drought-physiology study located (ResearchGate) used Niger cultivars IGPN 2004 and GA 10, not Birsa Niger-3 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313771436_Growth_and_Physiological_Alterations_in_Niger_Cultivars_under_Drought_Stress_1 (discarded for this record)

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found that names Birsa Niger-3 (BNS-11). The biodiesel review's disease note (powdery mildew and Alternaria resistance) sits in a table block that may belong to a different row, so it is not attributed here -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385299465_Fueling_the_future_Sustainable_Biodiesel_Production_Strategies_for_a_Cleaner_Tomorrow
- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The NICRA 2012-13 demonstration table (drought-tolerant variety demonstration, 5 demonstrations at 1.5 ha) lists Birsa Niger-3 -- http://www.atarikolkata.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/Annual-Report-NICRA-12-13.pdf
- Niger general agronomy (rainfed crop, average national yield 3.21 q/ha, low-yield causes including limited HYV choice and farm-saved seed) is not variety-specific -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/niger-oilseeds-1/niger-cultivation-practices (not attributed to this variety)
- Yield potential and oil content for Birsa Niger-3: blank in the DOD characters table -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx
- Multi-location trial results for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: "Local selection" is the value supplied in the request. No independent source confirmed it. No evidence found.
- Breeding-line code: BNS-11 is the variety code given in the DOD table -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx
- Breeding method: No evidence found for this variety.
- QTL/markers: No evidence found for this variety. A review states there are no global reports of trait mapping or marker-assisted breeding in Niger; it describes 554 KASP SNPs from transcriptome sequencing of two genotypes -- https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0472/15/3/350 (not attributed to this variety)
- Reproductive biology (crop-level): Niger is an outcrossing, self-incompatible species pollinated mainly by bees -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/niger-breedingcrop-improvement/245214403 (crop-level only)
- Genome resources specific to this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released centre: BAU (Birsa Agricultural University), Ranchi, Jharkhand -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx ; corroborated by https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385299465_Fueling_the_future_Sustainable_Biodiesel_Production_Strategies_for_a_Cleaner_Tomorrow
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. The BAU directors and scientists named in other pages are administrative or unrelated, so they are not attributed to this variety.
- Developing station: No specific station named for this variety. No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi - 834006, Jharkhand, India; phone +91-651-2450832; fax 0651-2450850 -- https://bauranchi.org/ (contact section) and https://www.indiacustomercare.com/birsa-agricultural-university-contact-no-0651-245-0832
- Institute website: https://bauranchi.org/
- Institute-level email (from an older BAU planning document, roughly 13 years old, so verify before use): vc@bauranchi.org (Vice Chancellor office); directorresearch@bauranchi.org (Director Research, Dr B.N. Singh, +91-651-2451055); dsf@bauranchi.org (Directorate of Seeds and Farms, Dr R.P. Singh, +91-651-2450850) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316853917_Business_Planning_and_Development_Unit_Birsa_Agricultural_University
- No breeder-specific contact found. Other contact numbers online (e.g., +91-651-2450500 and +91-651-2450832) are used on different pages and should be checked against the institute's contact page.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found that names Birsa Niger-3 (BNS-11) in a peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis. KrishiKosh Niger theses located (staggered sowing thesis, 2019) do not name this variety -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/dbc9f861-9dec-4ccd-b889-8c93db275eba/content (discarded)
- Authors not stated. (2012/2013). Annual Report, NICRA (ICAR-ATARI Kolkata), 2012-13 (drought-tolerant variety demonstration table listing Birsa Niger-3). Report -- http://www.atarikolkata.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/Annual-Report-NICRA-12-13.pdf
- Authors not stated. (Year not stated). Fueling the future: Sustainable Biodiesel Production Strategies for a Cleaner Tomorrow (variety table includes Birsa Niger-3 (BNS-11)). Journal/Report not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385299465_Fueling_the_future_Sustainable_Biodiesel_Production_Strategies_for_a_Cleaner_Tomorrow
- Authors not stated. (Year not stated). An overview of oilseeds and oil scenario, seed chain and strategy to energize seed production (notes Birsa Niger 3 as predominant in seed chain). Journal/Report not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350896370_An_overview_of_oilseeds_and_oil_scenario_seed_chain_and_strategy_to_energize_seed_production

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The seed chain overview states that Birsa Niger 3 was the predominant variety in the seed chain, and that breeder seed indents for niger were placed for 2014-15 to 2019-20 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350896370_An_overview_of_oilseeds_and_oil_scenario_seed_chain_and_strategy_to_energize_seed_production
- A niger presentation notes that non-availability of seed of promising varieties is a constraint (not specific to this variety) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/niger-breedingcrop-improvement/245214403
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales and private dealer listings: No evidence found. This search was the 4th and last permitted, and it returned only general niger trade and Seednet-unrelated pages.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified-variety state table (2008-2019) lists Birsa Niger-3 (BNS-11) for Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and West Bengal -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx
- The DOD characters table lists the recommended states as Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, MP, Odisha, Maharashtra, AP, WB and Kerala. This includes Kerala, which the state table does not -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx
- The request's list differs from this: it includes Orissa and Kerala but omits Andhra Pradesh and Bihar, which appear in the state table. The request's "Chattisgarh" and "Kerela" are spelling variants of Chhattisgarh and Kerala.
- Year of release 2010 is corroborated by the DOD table and the biodiesel review table -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385299465_Fueling_the_future_Sustainable_Biodiesel_Production_Strategies_for_a_Cleaner_Tomorrow

drought.details: No drought data for GNNIG-4 was found in any searched result. The research source describes the variety as suited to kharif rainfed conditions in Gujarat, but this is a recommended growing system, not a measured drought tolerance result.

heat.details: No heat tolerance data for GNNIG-4 was found in searched sources.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance data for GNNIG-4 was found in searched sources.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data for GNNIG-4 was found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Field resistance to Alternaria leaf spot and Cercospora leaf spot is reported in the research source (field conditions). In a natural-epiphytotic leaf spot screen of 21 niger cultivars, GNNIG-4 was among seven entries with a PDI of 12.42%, but the resistance category in the table was not legible in the snippet, so its reaction class is unconfirmed. The same screen classed GNNIG-3 (the Seednet name, a different earlier release) as resistant to Alternaria blight; this does not apply to GNNIG-4.

pest_resistance.summary: Reported resistance under field conditions to leaf-eating caterpillar and semilooper. No other pest reaction data was found. The Pest Reaction field in the original variety data is 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Station trials (2016-18): 543 kg/ha. AICRP trials over three years: 598 kg/ha grain yield. Oil content 37.77%; oil yield 205 kg/ha. Input data lists average_yield as Not Available.
agronomic_details.stability: Results are reported across station trials, three years of AICRP trials and 30 farmers' fields. No explicit stability statistic (for example, a GxE or stability index) was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Kharif or late kharif, as sole crop or intercrop; kharif rainfed conditions in Gujarat. No agro-climatic zone details beyond Gujarat were found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Bold seed of 4.08 g per 1000 seeds; greenish-purple stem. Input morphological_characteristics is 'Not specified'.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Station trials 2016-18 against checks GN-2, GNNIG-3 and IGPN-2004-1: GNNIG-4 averaged 543 kg/ha, which is 43.65%, 34.07% and 41.40% above those checks respectively. (2) AICRP trials over three years: 598 kg/ha grain yield, 27% above national check IGP-67. (3) Adaptive trials at 30 farmers' fields: the variety was favoured over checks GN-2 and IGPN-2004-1 (no yield figures given in the digest). (4) Leaf spot natural-epiphytotic screen of 21 niger cultivars: GNNIG-4 among seven entries with PDI 12.42%, reaction class unconfirmed. Note: the GNNIG-3 2016 AICRP entry (400-450 kg/ha, 32-35% oil, 110-115 days) refers to a different variety and is not GNNIG-4 data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Name check: the CSC name is GNNIG-4 (NMBP-1907). The Seednet name GNNIG-3 is a different, earlier release, so evidence about GNNIG-3 below does not describe GNNIG-4. I found no Seednet listing for GNNIG-4. Searches used: 4 (variety/release, breeder, research, and a combined contact/seed query).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Notified in 2021 as GNNIG-4 for kharif rainfed conditions in Gujarat (ex-NMBP-1907) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for GNNIG-4 was found in any result. -- No evidence found (searched; see the research and release sources above)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to Alternaria and Cercospora leaf spot and to leaf-eating caterpillar and semilooper under field conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- In a natural-epiphytotic leaf spot screen of 21 niger cultivars, GNNIG-4 was among seven entries with a PDI of 12.42%; the resistance category in the table was not legible in the snippet, so its reaction class is unconfirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393367222_Screening_of_Niger_Cultivars_Genotypes_for_Resistance_to_Leaf_Spot_Disease_Under_Natural_Conditions
- The same screen classed GNNIG-3 (the Seednet name) as resistant to Alternaria blight; this applies to GNNIG-3, not GNNIG-4. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393367222_Screening_of_Niger_Cultivars_Genotypes_for_Resistance_to_Leaf_Spot_Disease_Under_Natural_Conditions

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Medium maturity of 127 days; bold seed of 4.08 g per 1000 seeds; greenish-purple stem; suited to kharif or late kharif as sole or intercrop. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- Oil content 37.77% and oil yield 205 kg/ha. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- Station trials (2016–18) against GN-2, GNNIG-3 and IGPN-2004-1; the abstract reports 543 kg/ha, which is 43.65%, 34.07% and 41.40% above those checks respectively. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- In AICRP trials over three years, 598 kg/ha grain yield, 27% above national check IGP-67. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382945849_101_Niger_Guizotia_abyssinica_L-_An_Underutilized_Oilseed_Crop_with_High_Value (search result 20-3; the page is the same ResearchGate record: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State)
- Adaptive trials at 30 farmers' fields also favoured it over checks GN-2 and IGPN-2004-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- Seednet GNNIG-3 (a different, 2016 release): 400–450 kg/ha, 32–35% oil, 110–115 days, bold shining black seed. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/

GENETICS AND QTL
- Developed by mass selection from a mutated population of RCR-317 (15 kr). This conflicts with the input parentage ("selection from local cultivar"). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- No QTL or marker study for GNNIG-4 was found. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by Navsari Agricultural University (NAU) through the Niger Research Station, Vanarasi (Tal. Vansda), with the All India Coordinated Research Project on Niger at the same station. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- Lead author/scientist: Prashant Jagtap, NRS Vanarasi (listed as author; full author list not confirmed). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- P. M. Mistry is listed on a ResearchGate profile as an NAU, Surat scientist with this paper under Publications; his role in the breeding is not stated. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/P-Mistry
- Seednet GNNIG-3 breeder/institute: no separate source found; the 2016 AICRP entry is the only record. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Jagtap P., Niger Research Station, NAU, Vanarasi-396580, Gujarat; email listed as pacific7@rediffmail.com (a personal-domain address, not an official NAU domain; verify before use). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State
- Niger Research Station Vanarasi, Tal. Vansda, Distt. Navsari-396580, Gujarat (state government directory entry); the listed phone numbers (+91-11-26562122/25/33/44, 26567373, 26962819) are Delhi numbers from a national directory and are not confirmed as the station's. -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/allstinstitutions/niger-research-station-vanarasi-0
- NAU head office: Eru Char Rasta, Dandi Road, Navsari 396450, Gujarat; phone (02637) 283794; email registrar@nau.in. -- https://nau.in/index
- NAU IT cell contact: itcell@nau.in, 7359445544. -- https://nausagar.nau.in/contact
- NAU administration table (Registrar 02637-282823, registrar@nau.in). -- https://www.indiacustomercare.com/navsari-agricultural-university-contact-no

PUBLICATIONS
- Jagtap P. et al. (2023). Development of High Oil Yielding Niger Variety for Gujarat State. Journal of Oilseeds Research 40 (Special issue). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State (DOI not found; full author list not confirmed)
- Authors not confirmed (year not stated; ID suggests c. 2025). Screening of Niger Cultivars/Genotypes for Resistance to Leaf Spot Disease Under Natural Conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393367222_Screening_of_Niger_Cultivars_Genotypes_for_Resistance_to_Leaf_Spot_Disease_Under_Natural_Conditions
- Prashant et al. (year not confirmed). Alternaria and Cercospora Leaf Spot Diseases of Niger (Guizotia abyssinica Cass.) – A Traditional Tribal Crop of South Gujarat, India, with Cost Benefit Ratio in Relation to Different Fungicides. NAU, Navsari. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334730502_Alternaria_and_Cercospora_Leaf_Spot_Diseases_of_Niger_Guizotia_abyssinica_Cass_-_A_Traditional_Tribal_Crop_of_South_Gujarat_India_with_Cost_Benefit_Ratio_in_Relation_to_Different_Fungicides
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP annual report specific to GNNIG-4 was found. -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or NAU seed-sale listing for GNNIG-4 was found; the combined contact/seed query returned only institutional contact pages. A dedicated seed-availability search was not run, so this is not a full negative. -- No evidence found
- A Down to Earth article notes that formal seed production has been insufficient for niger generally and that government varieties seldom reach farmers. -- https://www.downtoearth.org.in/agriculture/illusive-oilseed-india-s-niger-seed-cultivation-is-declining-here-is-why-84380

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gujarat only, kharif rainfed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373992638_Development_of_High_Oil_Yielding_Niger_Variety_for_Gujarat_State

DISCREPANCIES TO RESOLVE
- Release year: input 2022-10-26; the paper says notified in 2021.
- Parentage: input says a selection from a local cultivar; the paper says mass selection from a mutagenised population of RCR-317 (15 kr).
- Seednet name GNNIG-3 refers to a different 2016 release; no Seednet record for GNNIG-4 was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JNS 2016-1413 (niger / Guizotia abyssinica)
Variety name checked: "JNS 2016-1413" (CSC release minutes). Seednet name: "JNS 2016-1413" (NIGER (RAMTIL), code A040517646). The two names are identical, so one set of searches covered both. No search result named this variety. Four searches were run (variety, breeder/institution, research/trials, seed availability). Results were about other niger varieties (JNS-28, JNS-30, JNS 9, Paiyur 1), unrelated sesame or azithromycin trials in Niger, and a Gondar niger oil study. Under the strict relevance rule, none of these are kept.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned only general niger and other-variety pages (for example JNS-28 and JNS-30 pages, which describe those varieties, not JNS 2016-1413).

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. Results mentioned amarbel resistance and leaf-spot tolerance only for JNS-28 and JNS-30, which are different varieties and are not attributed to JNS 2016-1413.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The AICRP-style and farmer-trial results that appeared were for JNS-28 and for a Bastar-zone germplasm study (IJCMAS, Baghel et al.), not this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The anther-culture double-haploid study (Springer, s11627-023-10391-z) used JNS 9 and JNS 28, not JNS 2016-1413.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The only institutional items named the Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur, as developer of three niger varieties notified by the Centre (Tribune India, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/schools/mp-agri-varsity-develops-new-varieties-of-oats-wheat-rice-361500; Krishi Jagran, https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/mp-agri-university-develops-new-varieties-of-oats-wheat-rice-niger-crops/). Neither page names JNS 2016-1413, so no breeder or institution is attributed to it. The CSC record's institution, the AICRP on Niger at Chhindwara, JNKVV, is taken from the input record only and is unverified.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found for a breeder or variety contact. Institute-level details appeared but are not attributed to this variety: JNKVV, Krishinagar, Adhartal, Madhya Pradesh (https://www.edarabia.com/27862/jawaharlal-nehru-krishi-vishwavidyalaya/), and the university site https://www.jnkvv.org/ (no contact details in the returned text). Verify both before use.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found for JNS 2016-1413. Papers returned concern other niger varieties or germplasm: JNS-28 (ResearchGate, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311431684_JNS-28_A_high_oil_and_seed_yielding_promising_genotype_of_Niger_Guizotia_Abyssinica_LF_Cass) and JNS-30 (ResearchGate, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316579454_JNS-30_A_new_released_niger_variety_for_Madhya_Pradesh_state_India). KrishiKosh anther-culture thesis on JNS 9 and JNS 28 (https://krishikosh.wordpress.com/2022/01/13/krishikosh-anther-culture-for-double-haploid-production-in-niger-guizotia-abyssinica-l-f-cass/).

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. A Down To Earth article (https://www.downtoearth.org.in/agriculture/illusive-oilseed-india-s-niger-seed-cultivation-is-declining-here-is-why-84380) reports that JNS 28 and JNS 30 seed is in short supply. Nothing names JNS 2016-1413. Seednet was not reachable from this environment, so the portal listing could not be checked.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Not verified. The only source is the input record ("Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand"). No search result confirmed it.

Next steps: check the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) directly for A040517646. Check the AICRP on Sesame and Niger annual reports (Chhindwara/JNKVV centre) and the CSC minutes for 2022, which may give the parentage, trial data and breeder names.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I ran the four searches, but the tool limit was reached during a fifth call, so this digest is built only from what the first searches returned. The searches returned one relevant source, an Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding article, and I could not read its full text, so the digest is incomplete.

Name discrepancy: The release minutes use "Bundel Jai 20122" with variety code "JHO 2012-2". The Seednet name is "Bundel Jai-2015-1". The EJPB article calls the entry "JHO-2015-1" and the variety "Bundel Jai-15-1". Its parentage (UPO 90 × IGO2-70) matches the record. The code and year differ, so the identity of the entry should be confirmed against the CSC notification and Seednet before the record is finalised.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found in the search results. The article abstract was truncated before any stress data appeared. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/932

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found in the search results. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/932

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The article reports fodder and seed yield evaluation of the entry in the hill zone of India (name given as Bundel Jai-15-1). The abstract notes the crop is ready for fodder harvest at an early stage, but the full figures were not retrieved. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/932

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found in the search results. The parentage cross UPO 90 × IGO2-70 is given in the same article (JHO-2015-1 derivative). -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/932

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The article describes the entry as a high-yielding forage oat derived from UPO 90 × IGO2-70, released as Bundel Jai-2015-1 in 2018 as an alternate variety for irrigated, timely-sown conditions in tropical and subtropical zones. Breeder names and developing station were not visible in the retrieved text. The institution named in the record is ICAR-Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute (Jhansi). -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/932

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder names, emails, phone numbers or addresses were found. The breeder-specific search returned only the same article. Institute-level contact should be taken from the ICAR-IGFRI official website (icar-igfri.res.in, not yet verified in this session).

PUBLICATIONS:
Authors not captured (2020s-era EJPB article; year not captured). Performance evaluation of oat variety Bundel Jai-15-1 for fodder and seed yield in hill zone of India. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/932

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Searches for Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU sales returned no seed source. Check seednet.gov.in directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES: The release record lists Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The EJPB article describes the target as irrigated, timely-sown tropical and subtropical conditions, which is consistent with these states but does not name them. The state list is from the record only, not independently confirmed. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/932

Gaps to close: full text of the EJPB article (authors, year, stress and yield data); CSC notification or Seednet entry for the variety code; IGFRI contact page; and a KrishiKosh search for theses on this entry.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to leaf blight and powdery mildew, per the five-year hill-zone trial paper (Ahmed et al., 2020, Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding).

agronomic_details.yield: Five-year mean green forage yield 292.65 q/ha, about 14-15% above check varieties; mean dry matter yield 96.6 q/ha, about 24-26% above checks (EJPB 2020). Input record gives approx. 250-255 q/ha GFY and approx. 50-60 q/ha DMY. Highest GFY at Srinagar (Kashmir) was 479.0 q/ha with 122.3 q/ha dry matter (DOI 10.37992/2020.1104.169).
agronomic_details.stability: Five-year hill-zone mean shows consistent advantage over checks; Srinagar result is a single-location figure. Stability across environments beyond these sites not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Input record: irrigated, timely-sown condition in tropical and subtropical areas during Rabi season. Trial evidence: hilly areas of Jammu, Himachal Pradesh and Srinagar (Kashmir). Released for hill areas and the forage programme. Responds positively to nitrogen fertilizer for green fodder and dry matter yield.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-erect stature, efficient tillering, medium grain size, suited to a single-cut system. Resistant to lodging and non-shattering (input record).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Five-year hill-zone trial (EJPB 2020): GFY 292.65 q/ha and DMY 96.6 q/ha, about 14-15% and 24-26% above checks; ready for fodder harvest at 50% flowering in about 110-120 days. (2) Srinagar (Kashmir): highest GFY 479.0 q/ha, DMY 122.3 q/ha. (3) Quality trial (DOAJ article): crude protein about 10.0%, IVDMD 54.8%, crude protein yield 3.9 q/ha; per-day productivity reported above Kent, OS-6 and SKO-90. (4) Nitrogen response trial: positive response to nitrogen for green fodder and dry matter yield. Note: release year is recorded as 2018 in the journal paper but 2019 in the IGFRI/MANAGE e-book table and input record; discrepancy unresolved.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Search note: the four searches returned no Seednet portal page for this variety, so the Seednet name could not be checked directly. All evidence below uses the names "Bundel Jai-2015-1" (release name) and "JHO-2015-1" (pre-release code), which the sources use interchangeably. No evidence was found for the Seednet variety code A0609050.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety. The only stress-related result was a general review saying conventional breeding has had limited success on drought and heat in oat, which does not name this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/397086699_Accelerated_Breeding_Approaches_for_Improved_Productivity_and_Quality_in_Dual-Purpose_Oats

DISEASE AND PEST -- Moderately resistant to leaf blight and powdery mildew, per the five-year hill-zone trial paper. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/932
DISEASE AND PEST -- No pest-resistance data for this variety was found. -- No evidence found

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance evidence found in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Green fodder: about 534 q/ha in the North West Zone, and 10-12% more than the national checks Kent and OS 6 across zones (trial data). Dry matter: about 108 q/ha. Seed yield: 18-20 q/ha. On-farm (KVK Nohar, Hanumangarh, Rajasthan): 411 q/ha green fodder versus 360 q/ha under farmers' practice (14.17% gain).
agronomic_details.stability: Superior to national checks Kent and OS 6 for green fodder and dry matter yield across multiple locations (7 locations: Bikaner, Jalore, Hisar, Ludhiana, Pantnagar, Udaipur, Meerut). No explicit stability statistics (e.g., GxE analysis) found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Digest title and sources reference the North East, South, and North West zones of India. A frontline demonstration study concludes OS 403 suits the semi-arid climate of Hanumangarh, Rajasthan. The digest's adaptation ecology field lists Eastern Uttar Pradesh.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Single-cut forage oat type. Bold-seeded grain. Described with better nutritional quality. Further morphological data not specified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Multi-location trials at 7 locations showed superiority over Kent and OS 6 for green fodder and dry matter yield, with the best qualifying variety also surpassed. KVK Nohar frontline demonstrations in Hanumangarh showed 14.17% gain in green fodder. Frontline demonstration economics: net return Rs 71,445/ha and benefit-cost ratio 4.10.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No OS 403-specific QTL, SNP, or SSR marker data found. A PLOS ONE germplasm study used DNA fingerprinting and placed OS-403 among high-grain-yield germplasm, but no marker positions are reported.

agronomic_performance.stability: Superior to national checks Kent and OS 6 for green fodder and dry matter yield across multiple locations (7 locations: Bikaner, Jalore, Hisar, Ludhiana, Pantnagar, Udaipur, Meerut). No explicit stability statistics (e.g., GxE analysis) found in the digest.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Digest title and sources reference the North East, South, and North West zones of India. A frontline demonstration study concludes OS 403 suits the semi-arid climate of Hanumangarh, Rajasthan. The digest's adaptation ecology field lists Eastern Uttar Pradesh.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Single-cut forage oat type. Bold-seeded grain. Described with better nutritional quality. Further morphological data not specified.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: Multi-location trials at 7 locations showed superiority over Kent and OS 6 for green fodder and dry matter yield, with the best qualifying variety also surpassed. KVK Nohar frontline demonstrations in Hanumangarh showed 14.17% gain in green fodder. Frontline demonstration economics: net return Rs 71,445/ha and benefit-cost ratio 4.10.

drought.details: The variety is explicitly stated to be tolerant against drought. It has been studied under varying levels of moisture stress, with research noting its characteristics in relation to chlorophyll and anthocyanin content under such conditions.

heat.details: While the variety is mentioned in documents discussing temperature stress, there is no direct evidence confirming HFO 529's specific level of heat tolerance. Studies on temperature stress in other crops like mustard and flax are noted in the same reports.

salinity.details: HFO 529 is listed among oat varieties tested under salt stress conditions. Oats are generally considered a moderately salt-tolerant crop, and HFO 529 is part of research efforts aimed at developing salt-tolerant varieties.

flood.details: No specific evidence regarding HFO 529's tolerance to flood stress was found. Mentions of water-logging tolerance refer to sugarcane clones in the provided results, not oats.

disease_resistance.summary: HFO 529 is reported to be resistant against Alternaria Leaf Spot and moderately resistant to Helminthosporium leaf blight disease.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety has been studied in contexts related to resistance against insect pests, though specific pests are not detailed for HFO 529.

agronomic_details.yield: HFO 529 recorded a maximum green fodder yield of 397 q/ha and dry matter yield of 79.24 q/ha in the Varietal Trial on IVT Oat (SC) in 2018-19. Earlier trials in 2017-18 reported a dry matter yield of 383 q/ha, where it outyielded other test entries like OS-6. Another report indicates a green fodder yield of 223 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Recommended for multiple states (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir) and tested under varying moisture and salt stress conditions, indicating adaptability across environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for timely-sown conditions with normal fertility. Adapted for cultivation in Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Jammu and Kashmir.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Found promising for green fodder yield per plant.
agronomic_details.field_trials: HFO 529 has been extensively tested in Varietal Trials on IVT Oat (SC) by Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University, Samastipur, as well as under varying levels of moisture and salt stress conditions by Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University and other institutions.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not specified for HFO 529. Physiological traits like chlorophyll and anthocyanin are mentioned in drought tolerance studies involving HFO 529.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
HFO 607 (fodder oat). Variety name in CSC minutes and Seednet name are both "HFO 607", so the evidence below applies to both headings.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Salinity screen (pot and screenhouse, 10 dS/m): HFO 607 had the lowest dry weight per plant (2.93 g) and the lowest relative water content (51.36%) among the genotypes tested, which points to comparatively poor salt tolerance. Source is a study by Devi, Singh and Goyal of CCS HAU, year not shown. Maximum dry weight (g) plant-1 was noticed in HJ-8 (6.20) followed by HFO 716 (5.37), HFO 529 (5.30) and minimum in HFO 607 (2.93) at 10 dS m-1 of salinity. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394327520_Effect_of_Salinity_on_Six_Genotypes_of_Avena_Sativa_during_Germination_and_Seedling_Growth
- No evidence found for drought, heat, flood or submergence tolerance specific to HFO 607. The search returned only general oat or other-variety pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The review table lists HFO-607 as a 2019 CCS HAU pedigree release, but the text in the snippet that mentions powdery mildew, leaf blight, aphid and armyworm resistance is not clearly attached to HFO-607 in the extracted text. I have not attributed any resistance to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365785271_Health_benefits_of_oat_Avena_sativa_and_nutritional_improvement_through_plant_breeding_interventions
- No variety-specific rust, smut or leaf blight rating for HFO 607 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release trial yield: average green fodder of 615.7 q/ha across North West Zone locations over three years. This variety gave 615.7 q/ha green fodder yield in North West Zone which was 11.9% and 17.4 % higher than the national checks Kent and OS 6, respectively. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- The same article reports 8.8% higher green fodder yield than the zonal check OL 125 in NWZ trials. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- AICRP on Forage Crops technology listing of HFO 607 as a single-cut variety, 2019-20, from CCS HAU Hisar, with a recommended area. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382887644_Fodder_Crops_Technologies_A_Five_Years_2019-2023_Journey_of_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization
- A field experiment at ICAR-NDRI Karnal (rabi 2021-22) evaluated HFO-607 under single cuts at 45, 55 and 65 days after sowing and no cut. Reported yield results were not extracted. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230132091_Prediction_of_fibre_components_in_oat_hulls_by_near_infrared_reflectance_spectroscopy
- Single-cut oat varieties generally: first cut at about 50–55 days. This is a general crop-level recommendation, not a HFO 607 trial result. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/166826/64546/507308
- Maturity and sowing-date data specific to HFO 607: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (from a review table, not from the release article): HJ-8 × UPO-04-1, developed by pedigree method, 2019, CCS HAU Hisar. This conflicts with the input field "Not specified", so it is recorded as a secondary-source finding. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365785271_Health_benefits_of_oat_Avena_sativa_and_nutritional_improvement_through_plant_breeding_interventions
- Breeding method: pedigree method. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- QTL or marker studies for HFO 607: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing team: Forage Section, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar. Named authors of the release article: D. S. Phogat, Yogesh Jindal, Minakshi Jattan, Naveen Kumar, Dalvinder Pal Singh, Jayanti Tokas. The individual lead breeder is not explicitly designated. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- Institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar-125 004 (Haryana). -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- Institution-level description (CCS HAU, Hisar): Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University is one of the biggest Agricultural University in Asia, established on February 2, 1970 and located at Hisar in the Indian state of Haryana. -- https://hau.ac.in/storage/app/uploads/VG6dQAaSUuipIFlVp92JI4OWkBCKQz7JZcEuxqgg.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Corresponding-author e-mail printed in the release article for the Forage Section team: jattanmina@gmail.com (Minakshi Jattan, listed as corresponding author). This is a personal address shown in the paper, not a verified official institute address. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- Postal address (institute-level, from the release article): Forage Section, Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar-125 004 (Haryana), India. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- Institute phone and official email: No evidence found in the search results. An institute contact page URL was not retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Phogat, D. S., Jindal, Y., Jattan, M., Kumar, N., Singh, D. P., Tokas, J. (year not shown; received 15 March 2021). HFO 607: A new single-cut oat variety for North West Zone of India. Forage Research -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- Dwivedi, R., Meena, V. K., Sharma, D., Singh, M., Chand, S. (2025). Oats (Avena sativa): A potential winter fodder crop for better livestock production. Indian Farming, September 2025 issue. Lists HFO 607 in its table of recent fodder oat varieties -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/166826/64546/507308
- Chand, S., et al. (2025). Analyzing trends and future projections in fodder oats (Avena sativa L.) for quality seed production in India. Frontiers in Plant Science. DOI 10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422. The variety-level text for HFO 607 was not visible in the retrieved extract, so this is recorded as a source only, not as HFO 607 evidence. -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422
- Devi, S., Singh, S., Goyal, V. (year not shown). Responses of oat (Avena sativa L.) genotypes under salt stress. Journal not identified in the extract. Contains the HFO 607 salinity data above. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394327520_Effect_of_Salinity_on_Six_Genotypes_of_Avena_Sativa_during_Germination_and_Seedling_Growth
- Field trial at ICAR-NDRI Karnal (rabi 2021-22), HFO-607 among four oat varieties. Authors, year and journal not extracted. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230132091_Prediction_of_fibre_components_in_oat_hulls_by_near_infrared_reflectance_spectroscopy
- KrishiKosh thesis search: not run, as the four allowed searches were used.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for HFO 607 seed. The searches returned general sources only: CCS HAU RDS Seed Farm sale counters for oat (no variety named) -- https://hau.ac.in/page/seed-sale-information ; Haryana certified oat seed statistics naming other varieties (HJ-8, OS-6, OS-377, OL-10, Kent) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368786506_STATUS_OF_CERTIFIED_SEED_PRODUCTION_OF_FORAGE_CROPS_IN_HARYANA ; a private hybrid oat seed trader in Hisar -- https://www.indiamart.com/evergreenseedco/oat-seeds.html. None of these names HFO 607, so none is recorded as evidence for it.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Released and notified for timely-sown, normal-fertility, irrigated conditions in the North West Zone: Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Terai region of Uttarakhand and Western Uttar Pradesh. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- The review table gives the same adoption area. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/166826/64546/507308
- Release-date discrepancy: input says 2020-11-09. Sources give identification 2019 (review table) and AICRP entry 2019-20. The notification date should be confirmed against the CSC minutes or the Gazette.

drought.details: HFO 611 is tolerant against drought and has been studied under varying levels of moisture stress. Research focuses on its drought tolerance, with keywords like chlorophyll and anthocyanin associated with these studies. Significant variation in performance was observed among oat varieties, including HFO 611, under moisture stress conditions.

heat.details: While not explicitly stated as heat tolerant, HFO 611 is included in studies focused on mitigating heat stress and minimizing production losses in fodder crops. Research shows enhancement in seed germination of hormo-primed HFO 611 seeds under heat stress conditions, suggesting it is susceptible to heat stress but can be managed.

salinity.details: Oat, including HFO 611, is generally considered a moderately salt tolerant crop. HFO 611 has been part of studies evaluating oat varieties under salt stress conditions, indicating its relevance for cultivation in saline environments.

flood.details: No information regarding flood tolerance was found in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: HFO 611 is resistant against Alternaria Leaf Spot, moderately resistant to Helminthosporium leaf blight disease, and moderately resistant against powdery mildew disease. Oats (Avena sativa) generally exhibit disease resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: Studies on oat varieties, including HFO 611, have examined resistance against insect pests. HFO 611 is noted in contexts related to insect pest resistance and management.

agronomic_details.yield: HFO 611 demonstrates a green fodder yield of 223 q/ha. Studies have also indicated potential enhancement in yield-related metrics (e.g., 7.45%) with the application of liquid bacterial inoculants.
agronomic_details.stability: HFO 611 has shown significant variation among varieties under moisture stress, implying its performance under such conditions is notable. It is described as widely adaptive.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The variety is recommended for cultivation in Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, and the Tarai Part of Uttarakhand.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Studies on HFO 611 in relation to stress tolerance have involved analyzing parameters like chlorophyll and anthocyanin content. Phenological and morphological traits are areas of study for oat varieties, including HFO 611, under stress conditions.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field studies on HFO 611 include two-year trials comparing 14 oat varieties under moisture stress conditions. It has also been part of trials conducted at fodder demonstration units (FDU) for mitigating heat stress. Further studies have been conducted on fresh and one-year-old seed lots of HFO 611 in the Department of Seed Science and Technology.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No specific molecular mechanisms or genes explicitly linked to HFO 611's stress tolerance were identified in the provided search results. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches for "HFO 707" with oat returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence).

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance record for HFO 707 was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for variety-level agronomy or multi-location trials. The ICAR Indian Farming oat article gives generic oat seed-rate and sowing advice (80–100 kg/ha) that is not tied to HFO 707, so I did not attribute it to this variety -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/166826/64546/507308

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Nothing on parentage or breeding method for HFO 707 was returned; the parentage field in the record is "Not specified", and I found nothing to fill it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar. The ICAR Indian Farming article lists CCS HAU Hisar among the major oat breeding institutions, and it lists HFO 707 as a CCS HAU, Hisar release -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/166826/64546/507308
Lead breeder or scientist name for HFO 707 -- No evidence found. The only oat paper returned with named CCS HAU authors (on HFO 607, a different variety) was excluded.
Station: CCS HAU Hisar main campus, with no station-level detail for HFO 707 found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. Institute-level contact only:
Institution: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University; address as listed: "CCS HAU NEAR MADUBAN PARK HISAR"; Pincode 125001; website http://www.hau.ernet.in -- https://hisar.gov.in/public-utility/chaudhary-charan-singh-haryana-agricultural-university/
Email: not found. Phone: not found. Divisional contact (Forage Section, Dept. of Genetics and Plant Breeding): not found for HFO 707. The email jattanmina@gmail.com appears only on the HFO 607 paper, so it was excluded.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, report or thesis naming HFO 707 was returned. Excluded: the HFO 607 single-cut paper (a different variety), and a CCS HAU biochemical study of 62 oat genotypes that does not name HFO 707 -- https://doi.org/10.3390/jcm13175126 is unrelated; the genotype study is at https://doi.org/ (DOAJ record) https://doaj.org/article/cfcd405fa03d455a86987e7909609c7a

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for HFO 707 at NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The only seed results were general or non-Indian retailers, which were excluded. A ResearchGate note on Haryana forage seed reports rising certified oat seed quantities, but it does not name HFO 707 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368786506_STATUS_OF_CERTIFIED_SEED_PRODUCTION_OF_FORAGE_CROPS_IN_HARYANA

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Terai part of Uttarakhand, Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan (multi-cut oat, CCS HAU Hisar), matching the input record -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/166826/64546/507308

NAME AND YEAR NOTES -- The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "HFO 707", and no separate Seednet page was found, so all evidence above refers to "HFO 707". The ICAR article gives 2021 as the release year, while the record gives 2022-06-17 (the CSC release minutes); the discrepancy is unresolved.
