search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search budget note: the search tool hit its use limit after four searches, so the remaining topics could not be searched. Findings below are limited to what the first four searches returned. Snippets were truncated in my output, so the wording below is paraphrased from partial text.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no page naming AAU-TTB-Dhan-40 with drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. Parentage in the input (Sub-1 background) is not verified by any source found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page found on this variety's blast, BLB, sheath blight, BPH or other resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Medium-duration paddy variety "Dholi (AAU-Dhan 40)" promoted in a rice-mustard cropping sequence by AAU-KVK Nalbari -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/159 (snippet only; no yield or maturity figures seen).

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. Parentage "Ranjit/Swarna Sub-1//Ranjit" comes only from the input record, not from a source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Listed as "AAU-TTB-Dhan-40 (Dholi)" with release date August 31, 2022, under the AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127 (Directorate of Research (Agriculture) page). No individual breeder name was linked to this variety. The AAU profile at https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Mr-Janardan-Das/323 credits Patkai (AAU-TTB-Dhan-42), Shatabdi (AAU-TTB-Dhan-43) and Prachur (AAU-TTB-Dhan-44) to a breeder, but does not mention Dholi, so it is not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only, from the AAU Directorate of Research page: AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar (https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127). No email, phone or postal address was captured in the snippet. No breeder contact found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for this variety. The search did not return any paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming AAU-TTB-Dhan-40 or Dholi.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned only the AAU-KVK Nalbari page, which mentions the variety in a cropping-sequence context, not in a seed-sale context. Seednet listing ("AAU-TTB-Dhan-40 (Dholi)", crop "PADDY (DHAN)") was not retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Assam. Release as "AAU-TTB-Dhan-40 (Dholi)" is recorded at https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127. The input's recommended state is consistent with this, but the page did not state the recommended-state wording itself in the snippet.

Name resolution: the evidence refers to "AAU-TTB-Dhan-40 (Dholi)" (AAU Directorate page) and "Dholi (AAU-Dhan 40)" (KVK page). Both match the seednet_variety_name; the CSC minute name ("AAU-TTB-Dhan-40") was not separately confirmed.

Gaps to fill in a follow-up session: Seednet portal record, CSC/ICAR release notification, AAU annual or Rice Research Institute reports, KrishiKosh theses, and the breeder contact on the AAU Titabar station page.

seednet_fields.Parentage: The proposed variety has been developed from a cross CN 1216 X CN 1131-4-4-1-4. Both the parents are pre-breeding materials developed under Shuttle Breeding programme of International Rice Research Institute (IRRI).
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: The variety may be recommended for Kharif season under rainfed low land condition.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Seed rate is 40 kg/ha (2-3 seedlings per hill)
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Disease infection was below the threshold level for the proposed variety AAU-KMJ Dhan-46 (Surma Dhan) at RARS, Karimganj, Assam during kharif 2018 and 2019. Under field screening without artificial inoculation the proposed variety showed Resistant to highly Resistant reaction in respect of False smut and Neck blast diseases, Resistant against Brown spot and Highly Resistant reaction in respect of False smut and Neck blast diseases, Resistant against Brown spot and Highly reaction against BLB
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Under field screening without artificial inoculation the proposed variety, AAU-KMJ Dhan-46 (Surma Dhan) showed White Ear Heads (WEH) to the extent of 0.6-0.8% panicles (Score-)) indicating its Highly Resistant reaction against Stem borer. Similarly, it showed neglible damage (Score-0) in respect of Leaf folder (HR) and very slight injury (Score-1) in respect to BPH and GLH indicating Highly Resistant reactions against these two pests
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha):
60:20:40 kg/ha of N:P2O5:K2O
Basal: ½ N+ Full P2O5+3/4K2O
1st topdressing: ¼ N + ¼ K2O at 30-35 DAT
2nd topdreesing: ¼ N at Panicle initiation stage

drought.details: None of the search results mention sesame variety AT-392. All results concern rice. The only parentage match is the rice variety ADT 39 (IR 8/IR 20), which is described as drought tolerant. That is a different crop and a different variety, and the match is coincidental, so it cannot be attributed to AT-392. The ADT 39 parentage resemblance suggests the 'IR 8 X IR 20' entry in the source data may be a rice parentage recorded in error for a sesame variety. No drought data for AT-392 can be drawn from these results.

heat.details: No heat tolerance evidence for AT-392 was found. The retrieved heat stress material is rice-specific (reproductive stage heat tolerance GWAS) and is not applicable.

drought.details: ADT 49 is identified as a drought tolerant variety. It is among the rice varieties listed as drought tolerant in various agricultural surveys and reports.

heat.details: ADT 49 is mentioned as a zonal check in the Southern region during Annual Rice Research Group Meetings where heat tolerance of rice varieties is discussed and screened. While not explicitly stated as 'heat tolerant,' its inclusion in such trials suggests a known performance or relevance in heat stress studies.

salinity.details: The variety grows well in saline soil and is well suited for it. It is also mentioned as a salt tolerant variety and included in evaluations of salt tolerant rice genotypes under saline conditions. It is suggested for YAAS affected saline lands.

flood.details: ADT 49 is tolerant to flood conditions and is recommended for flood-affected areas.

disease_resistance.summary: ADT 49 is reported to be resistant to blast and sheath rot.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety shows resistance to stem borer and brown plant hopper.

agronomic_details.yield: ADT 49 has an average yield of 6170 kg/ha. In comparative trials, another variety, ART (168), showed a yield of 5966 kg/ha, which was 10.5% higher than ADT 49, indicating ADT 49's yield serves as a benchmark.
agronomic_details.stability: The variety is recommended for irrigated conditions and grows well in sandy clay soil. It is considered ideal for the second season.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to irrigated conditions in Tamil Nadu. It is suitable as a Thaladi crop and for direct sowing.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to leaf folder. Brown Plant Hopper and Green Leaf Hopper are mentioned in general pest context, but specific resistance for ADT 50 is not stated.

drought.details: ADT 55 is a promising short duration rice variety developed through marker-assisted selection for drought tolerance. It possesses two drought-tolerant QTLs (qDTY1). Molecular breeding efforts have focused on developing varieties with inbuilt tolerance to drought. An abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_.Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar is relevant to this context, as ADT 55 is listed as a drought tolerant variety. It is also mentioned as tolerant to drought in distribution to farmers.

heat.details: ADT 55 has been screened for high temperature tolerance. Development of abiotic tolerant rice varieties, including those with high temperature tolerance, has been a breeding focus, with ADT 55 listed among them.

salinity.details: ADT 55 is explicitly stated as tolerant to salt. It is also noted that crosses are being attempted involving multiple stress tolerant donors, including those for salt tolerance, and ADT 55 has been used as a parent in such crosses. Salt tolerance has been directly correlated with various rice varieties.

flood.details: While submergence tolerance is noted, general flood tolerance (e.g., flash flood, standing water depth) is not specified beyond its suitability for semi-deep water conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: ADT 55 is resistant to leaf blast, neck blast, sheath rot, grain discoloration, and Rice Tungro Disease (RTD). It is also moderately resistant to blast, sheath rot, and brown spot. It is resistant to bacterial leaf blight (BLB). Its parentage includes IRBB 60, a known source of bacterial blight resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: ADT 55 is moderately resistant to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH 10) and moderately resistant to Stem Borer (SB). However, incidence of yellow stem borer has been noticed in ADT 55 paddy varieties in some areas.

agronomic_details.yield: Average reported yield is 59.3 q/ha. Another source indicates a yield of 65 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: ADT 55 is suitable for irrigated, wet conditions and also for semi-deep water, showing one-week submergence tolerance. It is classified as a short/early maturing variety and is non-Basmati type.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation in Tamil Nadu under irrigated, wet conditions, including Kar/Kuruvai and Summer seasons. It is an early maturing variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf (82 cm) plant height. Grains are Long Slender (LS), with soft gel consistency and good for cooking. It has intermediate amylase content and gelatinization temperature. It is also noted as a protein-rich paddy variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: ADT 55 has been produced and distributed to 74 farmers, indicating farmer acceptance and field performance. It has been screened at multiple centers for submergence and high temperature tolerance.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: ADT 55 was developed through Marker Assisted Selection (MAS). It possesses two drought-tolerant QTLs (qDTY1). A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_.Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar is associated with its stress tolerance profile.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: It carries two identified Quantitative Trait Loci (QTLs) for drought tolerance, referred to as qDTY1.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The variety is a result of molecular breeding for inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast. It is derived from MAS and is involved in new crosses with multiple stress tolerant donors. Its parentage is recorded as ADT 43/IRBB 60.

A 2014 ISSP South Zonal Seminar abstract (Agricultural College, Bapatla) reports that gamma-ray mutant lines of Akshaya were characterised for blast resistance; the digest gives no resistance level for these mutant lines. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE --
Akshaya (BPT 2231) is listed as moderately resistant to blast, but the snippet does not clearly tie that line to Akshaya rather than the neighbouring entry -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance -- searched, none in results.

DISEASE AND PEST --
Gamma-ray mutant lines of Akshaya were characterised for blast resistance, per a 2014 ISSP South Zonal Seminar abstract (Agricultural College, Bapatla) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259874628_Biofumigant_Activity_of_Brassica_Spp_Against_Soil_Borne_Plant_Pathogens
Blast reaction as "moderately resistant" -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf
Note: the KAU "Akshaya" (Kerala, released 2018: 130-140 days, moderately resistant to stem borer and leaf folder) is a different variety and must not be merged with this record -- https://kau.in/basic-page/varieties-released

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
Akshaya (BPT 2231) with parentage BPT 4358/IR64 appears in a multi-location/minikit trial table with yield values of 5.4, 2.02 and 2.67 (units not stated in snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287878106_Molecular_screening_for_fertility_restorer_genes_Rf3_Rf4_of_WA_-CMS_and_evaluation_of_F1_hybrids_in_rice_O_sativa_L_Arun_Kumar_Singh_P_Revathi_M_Pavani_R_M_Sundaram_P_Senguttuvel_K_B_KemparajuA_S_Hari_Prasad_C_N_Neeraja_N_Sravan_Raju_P_Kotewara_Rao_P_J_Suryendra_K.Jayaramulu_and_B.C._Viraktamath
Breeder-seed and cultivation-area data in the ARS Bapatla document refer to Sona Mahsuri, not Akshaya -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf
No evidence found for maturity days, yield ranges or season for Akshaya (BPT 2231) from a KVK or SAU source.

GENETICS AND QTL --
Parentage recorded as BPT 4358 / IR64 (matches the release record) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287878106_Molecular_screening_for_fertility_restorer_genes_Rf3_Rf4_of_WA_-CMS_and_evaluation_of_F1_hybrids_in_rice_O_sativa_L_Arun_Kumar_Singh_P_Revathi_M_Pavani_R_M_Sundaram_P_Senguttuvel_K_B_KemparajuA_S_Hari_Prasad_C_N_Neeraja_N_Sravan_Raju_P_Kotewara_Rao_P_J_Suryendra_K.Jayaramulu_and_B.C._Viraktamath
No QTL or marker study specific to Akshaya found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION --
Akshaya (BPT 2231) was developed at the Rice Research Unit, Bapatla -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapatla
Listed among Acharya N G Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) varieties -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-25/
Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
Gamma-ray mutant blast work credited to Dr G. Subbaiah, Associate Dean, Agricultural College Bapatla (ISSP 2014 abstract) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259874628_Biofumigant_Activity_of_Brassica_Spp_Against_Soil_Borne_Plant_Pathogens

CONTACT DETAILS --
Institute: Acharya N G Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), website angrau.ac.in -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-25/
Agricultural College, Bapatla postal code 522 101 (from ISSP 2014 abstract address) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259874628_Biofumigant_Activity_of_Brassica_Spp_Against_Soil_Borne_Plant_Pathogens
Breeder names, emails, phone numbers: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS --
Subbaiah G. et al. (2014). Characterization of the mutant lines of Akshaya rice variety for blast. ISSP South Zonal Seminar, Agricultural College Bapatla, 23 Jan 2014 (author list incomplete in snippet; title as printed in the ResearchGate attachment) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259874628_Biofumigant_Activity_of_Brassica_Spp_Against_Soil_Borne_Plant_Pathogens
Singh A.K. et al. (year not stated in snippet). Molecular screening for fertility restorer genes Rf3 & Rf4 of WA-CMS and evaluation of F1 hybrids in rice. Journal/report not identified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287878106_Molecular_screening_for_fertility_restorer_genes_Rf3_Rf4_of_WA_-CMS_and_evaluation_of_F1_hybrids_in_rice_O_sativa_L_Arun_Kumar_Singh_P_Revathi_M_Pavani_R_M_Sundaram_P_Senguttuvel_K_B_KemparajuA_S_Hari_Prasad_C_N_Neeraja_N_Sravan_Raju_P_Kotewara_Rao_P_J_Suryendra_K.Jayaramulu_and_B.C._Viraktamath
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report or DOI found for Akshaya.

SEED AVAILABILITY --
No evidence found on the Seednet portal under AKSHAYA or PADDY (DHAN); Seednet was not reached in the searches.
No official source (NSC, APSSC, KVK, ANGRAU seed sales) found.
Private traders listing "Akshaya" are unrelated to BPT 2231 (Akshaya Agencies, Akshaya Rice Industries, East Godavari) and were not used as evidence -- https://www.indiamart.com/sri-akshaya-rice-industries/paddy-seeds.html

RECOMMENDED STATES --
Recommended states: No evidence found (the release record says "Not specified"). Regional context only: ANGRAU Bapatla works on Andhra Pradesh conditions, and Akshaya was tested in the Krishna zone minikit trials -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf

NAME NOTE --
variety_name "Akshaya" and seednet_variety_name "AKSHAYA" are the same here; all evidence refers to Akshaya (BPT 2231) of ANGRAU Bapatla. No evidence found on the Seednet portal itself.

LIMITATIONS --
The web_search budget was used up after four queries, so the research was not finished. Breeder names, contacts, seed sources, KrishiKosh/AICRP records, and maturity and yield details remain open and should be checked directly on seednet.gov.in, angrau.ac.in and krishikosh.egranth.ac.in.

basic_info.institution: ICAR- Central Institute for subtropical Horticulture, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh

drought.details: No evidence found on drought tolerance. Searches returned only fruit-quality and yield descriptions. Evidence refers to Ambika mango (CISH, Lucknow); no Seednet record was found, and the Seednet crop PADDY (DHAN) conflicts with the mango crop.

heat.details: No evidence found on heat tolerance. Searches returned only fruit-quality and yield descriptions.

salinity.details: No evidence found on salinity tolerance. Searches returned only fruit-quality and yield descriptions.

flood.details: No evidence found on flood tolerance. Searches returned only fruit-quality and yield descriptions.

disease_resistance.summary: No evidence of varietal resistance or susceptibility to any disease was found. A post-harvest hot water treatment study on Ambika fruit at CISH, Lucknow, examined anthracnose and stem-end rot, but it reports treatment efficacy, not varietal resistance. No field disease resistance evidence was found.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found on varietal resistance or susceptibility to pests in the field.

agronomic_details.yield: About 80 kg per plant at about 10 years under improved cultural practices (ICAR-CISH information and secondary sources). No per-hectare yield found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data found; the east coast comparison is the only multi-site evidence and its figures are not clearly labelled.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to high-density planting (ICAR-CISH). A commercial-site claim gives 180-200 plants per acre, which is not peer-reviewed. Another source lists Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu as suitable and excludes areas with heavy rainfall; a further source lists Rajasthan in addition. These are secondary, non-CSC sources, so the CSC record of Uttar Pradesh is retained as ground truth.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 120-130 days from flowering to maturity (secondary source); late maturing (ICAR-CISH). Days from planting to maturity not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Regular bearer; 2-3 years to bearing (secondary source). Fruits 250-360 g, TSS 21 Brix, shelf life about 8 days. On ripening, fruit turns bright yellow with a dark red blush (CISH research farm postharvest study). Other morphological and plant architecture details: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: East coast of India performance comparison (Kishore 2015) compares Ambika with Amrapali, Arka Anmol and others; flowering intensity was noted as low; table figures are not clearly labelled in the available snippet, so no reliable quantitative ranking can be drawn. The about 80 kg per plant at 10 years figure is reported across several secondary sources. Commercial-site claims (200-400 g fruit, June-July fruiting, 180-200 plants per acre) are from nursery sites and are not peer-reviewed. Multi-location CSC or AICRP trial results: Not found in searched sources.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No marker or genomic study of Ambika was found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL study of Ambika was found.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: ICAR-CISH Nursery: Mango (CISH-Ambika), Rs 125, listed as available; requests accepted 1 January to 30 June each year. No Seednet (seednet.gov.in) or State Seed Corporation record found.
commercial_info.private_dealers: Hindustan Plantation, Lucknow, Rs 195 per plant (grafted, in stock); Al Habib Herbs & Seeds, Saharanpur, Rs 349 per plant (grafted, in stock); New Shadab Nursery, Lucknow, Rs 350 per plant (grafted). Amazon listing (Shibom Enterprise) is currently unavailable. Private listings are not verified.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: ANKIT (NDC-2008), Jute

Search status: The 4-search budget was used. A later attempt to read the full page text hit the tool-use limit, so the findings below come only from the truncated snippets of the first search batch. Several headings are thin for that reason.

Name note: The CSC minutes name (ANKIT) and the Seednet name (ANKIT (NDC-2008)) are the same variety. The only matching page found refers to it as "NDC 2008 (Ankit)", so the evidence applies to both names.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for ANKIT. Searched in the release and research queries.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The only related hit was a general jute cultivation guide (ResearchGate, "Scientific Cultivation of JUTE") that discusses anthracnose and fungicides for jute in general, with no mention of ANKIT. Not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376269572_Scientific_Cultivation_of_JUTE

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The cultivation guide above gives a seed rate for capsularis jute in general, not for ANKIT. Not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376269572_Scientific_Cultivation_of_JUTE

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found in the retrieved text. The parentage given in the release record, (71/20) X (JRC-321), was supplied by you and is not confirmed by any search result. No QTL or genome study was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution per the variety record: N.D. University of Agriculture & Technology, Kumarganj, Faizabad (U.P.). Breeder names were not found in any retrieved text. The "Ankit Saini" listed on the ResearchGate page is a name resemblance and has been discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376269572_Scientific_Cultivation_of_JUTE (discarded, not relevant)

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for NDU&T or the jute breeding programme was retrieved. The institute-level address from the ResearchGate page belongs to Bangladesh Jute Research Institute, which is a different institution and is not used here.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found specifically on ANKIT. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or trial result naming this variety was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for ANKIT was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Release and notification: 2009, U.P., S.O. 2187 (E) dated 27.08.2009, listed as "NDC 2008 (Ankit)". -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
Recommended states per the variety record (not verified by search): Bihar, Assam, Orissa, West Bengal, Eastern Part of U.P. The notification entry above names U.P. only, so the wider list should be checked against the official CSC or Seednet record.

drought.details: Tolerant to drought, with specific mention of tolerance during early vegetative stages. The variety is listed among drought-tolerant rice varieties demanded by farmers.

heat.details: Identified as heat tolerant and suitable for yield enhancement under heat stress conditions. Farmers have expressed a demand for more heat-tolerant varieties, and Ankur-7434 is listed among them.

salinity.details: No direct evidence states Ankur-7434 possesses salinity tolerance. While the development of salt-tolerant rice varieties and research on QTLs for salinity tolerance are mentioned in general contexts or as farmer demands, this is not specifically attributed to Ankur-7434.

flood.details: No direct evidence links Ankur-7434 to specific flood or waterlogging tolerance. General mentions of varieties with waterlogging tolerance or flash-flood tolerance are present in the same documents where Ankur-7434 is listed, but without a direct attribution.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to BS (likely Bacterial Sheath Blight) and moderately resistant to blast and Sh.R (likely Sheath Rot).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Farmer video testimonial (Hindi) claims healthy crop and good grain performance, unverified and not a trial -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M-cBYHVzBXM
- No official drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found -- searched, none found

DISEASE AND PEST
- Farmer video testimonial claims stem-borer-free rice, anecdotal and unverified -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K3O5YODG62Q
- No official blast, sheath blight, BPH or other resistance data found -- searched, none found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Hindi video describing it as a high-yield paddy variety, with a Jabalpur farmer, no yield figures verified -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tJTnnIsYhe0
- No maturity duration, yield trial, or multi-location trial results found -- searched, none found

GENETICS AND QTL
- No parentage, marker, or QTL information found; parentage is "Not specified" in the input -- searched, none found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution per input: Bayer Bioscience Pvt Ltd; a LinkedIn post describes the hybrid as launched by Bayer Crop Science -- https://www.linkedin.com/in/rohan-bisone-225a36284/
- No lead breeder name found -- searched, none found

CONTACT DETAILS
- No official breeder, institute, or Bayer contact found -- searched, none found
- Only commercial contact found: a territory sales manager profile at Seedworks International Pvt. Ltd. (name as shown: Rohan Bisone). This is a sales role, not an official contact, and no email or phone was found -- https://www.linkedin.com/in/rohan-bisone-225a36284/

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers found -- searched, none found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- A LinkedIn post says Bayer Crop Science launched two new hybrids, Arize 6677 and Arize 6555 ST -- https://www.linkedin.com/in/rohan-bisone-225a36284/
- Seednet listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU and dealer listings: not found -- searched, none found

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Gujarat -- from the input CSC record only; no search source confirmed this

SEARCH LOG AND LIMITS
- Four web_search queries were run, which was the maximum allowed. A fifth call was blocked by the tool limit, so the planned breeder/contact and publication searches were run only once each, and seednet.gov.in, ICAR and KrishiKosh were not directly searched.

- The evidence base is too thin for a reliable reference record. Recommended next steps: check the Seednet entry for "Arize-6555 (G)" directly, check the CSC minutes for the release notification, and contact Bayer Crop Science India for breeder and trial data.

One YouTube result is for "Arize AZ 8433 DT," a different product, so I excluded it from this record.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No source in the results mentions disease or pest resistance for either name.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for this variety. The only agronomy-related result is a Bayer article saying that its hybrid rice development adjusts seed traits to the needs of growers in the delta, with no variety-specific data -- https://www.bayer.com/en/about-us/explore-bayer/our-contributions/stories/climate-change-putting-rice-farmers-at-risk

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Parentage is listed as "Not specified" in the record, and no source gave a parent line.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder or institute contact found in the results. Not verified: no official email, phone, or postal address was found for Bayer BioScience's Indian rice breeding division. The Bayer global contributions page is the only institutional source and contains no contact details for this variety -- https://www.bayer.com/en/about-us/explore-bayer/our-contributions/stories/climate-change-putting-rice-farmers-at-risk

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or trial report on Arize Dhani or Arize Dhan DT appeared. disease_resistance.summary: Downy mildew: the AICPMIP entry describes Balwan (NBH 4903 (MH 1743)) as highly resistant. A Nuziveedu-linked seed listing describes NBH 4903 as tolerant to downy mildew; this is a secondary, less authoritative source. Blast: the AICPMIP entry describes Balwan as highly resistant. Major diseases: the AICPMIP entry describes tolerance, and a training manual describes resistance to major diseases. The training manual also describes Balwan as late maturing, which conflicts with the AICPMIP entry; the digest does not resolve this conflict. The original CSC record describes the variety as tolerant to disease at field level. Quantitative disease resistance figures: not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Major pests: the AICPMIP entry describes Balwan (NBH 4903 (MH 1743)) as highly resistant to major pests and tolerant to major pests. The training manual describes resistance to major pests, subject to the maturity conflict noted under disease resistance. The original CSC record describes the variety as tolerant to pests at field level. Pest-specific resistance figures: not found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Original CSC record: grain yield 16 q/acre to 18 q/acre (average over three years of coordinated trials); fodder yield 15 q/acre to 30 q/acre. Vantika Tech marketing page (unverified): 18 q/acre for Balwan 4903 and 12 q/acre for NHB 4903. Seed-retail listing: potential yield of 7-8 quintals/ha for NBH 4903. Rajasthan trial: 4536 kg/ha (see field trials).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources (no multi-environment stability analysis in the digest beyond the three-year average stated in the original record)
agronomic_details.adaptation: Original record: Zone B of AICPMIP, comprising Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. Recommended state per original record: Rajasthan. The digest does not confirm the Zone B adaptation or the Rajasthan recommendation independently.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: 1. Well exerted compact panicles. 2. Well exerted semicompact panicles. Non-lodging, non-shattering (AICPMIP entry). agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Randomised block trial with 3 replications in a Rajasthan-focused paper: NBH 4903 yielded 4536 kg/ha, statistically at par with the top entry Kaveri Super Boss (4667 kg/ha). The trial location text is ambiguous. (2) Character association and heritability study at Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh, kharif 2020, including NBH 4903 among 16 genotypes; table values are not labelled in the digest snippet and are not interpreted here. (3) Original CSC record: three-year average grain yield 16-18 q/acre in coordinated trials. No other trial results found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Balwan / NBH 4903 (MH 1743 / MH 2035), pearl millet

NAME CHECK: The CSC name "Balwan" and the Seednet name "NBH 4903 (Balwan) (MH 2035)" both appear in the AICPMIP notification table, and that table pairs Balwan with "NBH 4903 (MH 1743)". The Seednet-style code "MH 2035" appears in a separate NBH 4903 row. The two codes conflict, so each finding below says which name it refers to. No Seednet page was retrieved, so Seednet-specific fields are unverified. Four searches were run: release/agronomy, breeder/institution, research papers, and seed sources.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- The AICPMIP notification table describes Balwan as highly resistant to downy mildew, blast and major pests, and tolerant to major diseases and pests, with non-lodging and non-shattering habit (refers to Balwan / NBH 4903 (MH 1743)) -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- A training manual lists Balwan as resistant to major pests and diseases and non-lodging, but its entry for Balwan describes it as late maturing, which conflicts with the AICPMIP entry (refers to Balwan) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sangappa-Sangappa/publication/374087417_Training_manual_on_Millets_production_processing_and_value_addition_technologies_for_nutritional_security_for_Certified_farm_advisor_on_millets/links/650d3955d5293c106cd2d815/Training-manual-on-Millets-production-processing-and-value-addition-technologies-for-nutritional-security-for-Certified-farm-advisor-on-millets.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for this variety. Crop-level drought and heat tolerance statements exist but are not attributed to Balwan or NBH 4903 and are excluded.
DISEASE AND PEST -- Downy mildew and major pest tolerance are listed in the AICPMIP entry above. A Nuziveedu-linked seed listing also says NBH 4903 is tolerant to downy mildew (refers to NBH 4903) -- https://www.indianyellowpages.com/hyderabad/millets.htm
DISEASE AND PEST -- Pest and disease resistance figures beyond these qualitative statements: No evidence found.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maturity is given as 80-85 days (Nuziveedu field-crop page, NBH-4903) -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/ ; a Vantika Tech page gives 85-90 days for "Balwan 4903" and 80-85 days for "NHB 4903" -- https://www.vantikatech.com/2020/05/bajra-improved-high-yield-variety.html
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Plant height 220-225 cm, earhead 30-32 cm, 2-3 tillers, conical compact earhead, light grey grain, medium-bold globular grain (refers to NBH 4903) -- https://www.exportersindia.com/nuziveeduseeds/other-products.htm
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Yield claims: 18 q/acre for "Balwan 4903" and 12 q/acre for "NHB 4903" (Vantika Tech, unverified, marketing page) -- https://www.vantikatech.com/2020/05/bajra-improved-high-yield-variety.html ; potential yield of 7-8 quintals/ha stated on a seed-retail listing (refers to NBH 4903) -- https://agrosiaa.com/products/detail/nuziveedu-balwan-bajara-seeds-1-5-kg
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Randomised block trial (3 replications) in Rajasthan-focused paper: NBH 4903 gave 4536 kg/ha, statistically at par with the top entry (Kaveri Super Boss, 4667 kg/ha); the trial location text is ambiguous (refers to NBH 4903) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384258267_Market_Dynamics_and_Consumer_Insights_for_Value-added_Pearl_Millet_Products_Empirical_Evidence_from_Rajasthan_India
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Character association and heritability study at Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh, kharif 2020, including NBH 4903 among 16 genotypes; the table values are not labelled in the snippet and are not interpreted here -- https://www.ijcmas.com/special/11/N.%20Anuradha,%20et%20al.pdf
GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage NB 105A x NB 98R (refers to Balwan / NBH 4903 (MH 1743)) -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
GENETICS AND QTL -- Seed type recorded as hybrid (refers to NBH 4903) -- https://agrosiaa.com/products/detail/nuziveedu-balwan-bajara-seeds-1-5-kg ; the cytoplasmic male sterility system is not confirmed for this variety, so no breeding-method claim is made.
GENETICS AND QTL -- Breeding-line codes NB 105A / NB 98R are listed as parents but their own origin and sterility status are not documented here. No QTL, marker or genome-resource evidence found for this variety.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution / applicant: Nuziveedu Seeds Ltd., Hyderabad (refers to Balwan / NBH 4903) -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf ; company profile -- https://theorg.com/org/nuziveedu-seeds-ltd
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. The company R&D wing is described only generically -- https://www.exportersindia.com/nuziveeduseeds/seeds.htm
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Testing or release centre: The notification names Jodhpur AICRP-Pearl Millet as the release-table row context, but no station-level link to this variety was confirmed -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No lead breeder, developing station, or SKUAST page was returned. The stated institution (SKUAST) and parentage ("selection from local material") are unconfirmed by any source retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, or KrishiKosh theses mentioning Basmati 564 were returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The only seed result was a generic Etsy listing (https://www.etsy.com/market/basmati_rice_seed), which is not a valid source for this variety. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing was found.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bio 448 (CSC name) / BIO-434 (Seednet name), millet (pearl millet), code MH 1671

NAME AND CROP NOTE
- The CSC-side name "Bio 448" appears in the ICAR pearl millet hybrid list with code MH 1671. The list gives Bio 448 as a pearl millet hybrid. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- No search result mentioned "BIO-434" in connection with this variety, so the Seednet name is unverified. I did not retrieve a Seednet portal page.
- The input's Seednet crop field says "PADDY (DHAN)", which conflicts with the pearl millet evidence. Treat the Seednet crop mapping as unverified and possibly wrong.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The only trait listed for Bio 448 is tolerance to downy mildew, so drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance are not documented. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- No other stress-tolerance evidence was found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bio 448 is listed as tolerant to downy mildew. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- The ResearchGate blast-resistance paper concerns designated B-lines in ICRISAT's hybrid parent program, not Bio 448. It was discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316411091_Evaluation_of_designated_hybrid_seed_parents_of_pearl_millet_for_blast_resistance

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found. The search returned only general pearl millet hybrid or West African trial papers, none naming Bio 448 or MH 1671, so they were discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL or marker study naming Bio 448 or MH 1671 was returned.

drought.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

salinity.details: Described as susceptible, with significant yield loss under salinity. The only source is a non-official encyclopedia entry, so this is not an official evaluation. Level reflects tolerance as reported (low tolerance).

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight: sources conflict. A general encyclopedia entry describes the variety as resistant, while an ICAR-linked technology page describes it as extremely susceptible. Neither is an official evaluation. Sheath blight: susceptible; used as the susceptible parent in QTL mapping (BPT-5204 x ARC10531), so not reported as tolerant. EMS-derived sheath-blight-tolerant mutant lines of BPT-5204 were identified at ICAR-IIRR (mutant lines, not the original variety). Activation-tagged mutants were developed for sheath blight resistance in this line. Blast: a study title describes marker-assisted backcrossing to improve blast resistance of BPT 5204; the abstract was not retrieved, so no resistance outcome is reported.

pest_resistance.summary: Brown planthopper, stem borer, leaf folder and other pests: No evidence found for this variety in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Potential yield 6.0 t/ha (ANGRAU ARS Bapatla summary). Seed trade listing gives 45-50 quintals per hectare (non-official). In an SRI and seedling age trial at ARS (Paddy) Sirsi, a maximum grain yield of 5.1 t/ha was reported in one treatment, and a seed yield of 3.19 t/ha was reported from 12-day seedlings.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data were reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Listed for kharif and rabi seasons (ANGRAU summary). Seed trade listing describes medium-low land suitability (non-official). Samba-season demonstration data are described under field trials. Specific agro-climatic zones beyond Andhra Pradesh were not reported.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 140-145 days (ANGRAU ARS Bapatla summary and seed trade listing). A general encyclopedia entry gives 130-140 days. The sources differ.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Small, fine grain (seed trade listing, non-official). Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) SRI practice and seedling age trial, ARS (Paddy) Sirsi, kharif 2004-05: 12-day seedlings gave higher seed yield (3.19 t/ha), and one treatment gave maximum grain yield of 5.1 t/ha; trial focused on seed yield and quality. (2) Samba-season demonstration in which TKM 13 was evaluated as an alternative to the BPT 5204 control: TKM 13 matured about 7-10 days earlier and recorded lower disease incidence than the BPT 5204 control. This result concerns TKM 13 relative to BPT 5204, not the performance of BPT 5204 alone.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Sheath blight QTL mapping (BPT-5204 x ARC10531, F2 and BC1F2): SSR markers RM336 and RM205 are tied to major QTLs. Chromosome positions were not reported in the digest. Grain quality mapping (BPT 5204 x JAK 686, F2, 188 plants): positions not reported in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Sheath blight: nine QTLs on five chromosomes were mapped in BPT-5204 x ARC10531; qshb6.1 and related loci are summarised in a review. Grain protein and quality (BPT 5204 x JAK 686): four GPC QTLs, three amylose QTLs, and a major QTL qPC1.2 on chromosome 1. Effect sizes were not reported in the digest. Root architecture: MutMap QTL-seq on an EMS mutant of BPT-5204 (TI-128) mapped regions for root length and root volume; this is a mutant line, not the original variety.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Activation-tagged (Ac-Ds) mutants were generated for sheath blight resistance. Specific genes or pathways were not identified in the digest.

commercial_info.private_dealers: A seed trade listing for BPT-5204 exists at shivagroseeds.com. The digest does not confirm current stock or sale status.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
BPT-5204 (Samba Mahsuri), rice. Search performed on 4 queries; seednet.gov.in and ICAR/SAU sites were not reached directly, so seednet-portal evidence was not retrieved.

NAME CHECK: Both "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" are "BPT-5204". All evidence below refers to that name, which is also called Samba Mahsuri. No separate Seednet record was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bacterial blight: Sources conflict. One general encyclopedia entry says it is resistant to bacterial blight, but an ICAR-linked technology page says it is extremely susceptible to bacterial blight. Neither is an official evaluation. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_College,_Bapatla ; https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/institutes-wise.html?id=44
- Salinity: Described as susceptible, with significant yield loss under salinity. Non-official source. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_College,_Bapatla
- Sheath blight: Used as the susceptible parent in QTL mapping (BPT-5204 × ARC10531), so it is not reported as tolerant. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25977888/ ; https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/9/4/177
- Sheath blight mutants: EMS-derived sheath-blight-tolerant mutant lines of BPT-5204 were identified at ICAR-IIRR. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325178893_Identification_of_Agro-Morphological_characters_in_Sheath_Blight_Tolerant_mutant_lines_of_Samba_Mahsuri_BPT-5204_Rice_variety
- Drought, heat, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast: A study title describes marker-assisted backcrossing to improve blast resistance of BPT 5204. Its abstract was not retrieved in full. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/347309030_IMPROVING_RICE_BLAST_RESISTANCE_OF_BPT_5204_THROUGH_MOLECULAR_MARKER-ASSISTED_BACKCROSSING
- Sheath blight: Susceptible (see above). Activation-tagged mutants were developed for sheath blight resistance in this line. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38430361/
- Bacterial blight: See stress section (conflicting).
- Brown planthopper, stem borer, leaf folder, other pests: No evidence found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release and parentage: Samba Mahsuri (BPT 5204), parentage GEB 24/TN 1/Mahsuri, pedigree method, released 1986 through SVRC, crop duration 140-145 days, season kharif and rabi, potential yield 6.0 t/ha. This conflicts with the 2014 release year in the record. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf
- Duration: A general encyclopedia entry gives 130-140 days. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_College,_Bapatla
- Agronomy trial: At ARS (Paddy) Sirsi, kharif 2004-05, SRI practice and seedling age trials on seed yield and quality. Reported higher seed yield (3.19 t/ha) from 12-day seedlings and maximum grain yield of 5.1 t/ha in one treatment. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268302207_Evaluation_of_System_of_Rice_Intensification_Cultivation_Seedling_Age_and_Spacing_on_Seed_Yield_and_Quality_in_Samba_Masuhri_BPT-5204_Rice
- Replacement trial: In a samba-season demonstration, TKM 13 was evaluated as an alternative to BPT 5204. It matured about 7-10 days earlier and recorded lower disease incidence than the BPT 5204 control. -- https://www.bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0005401
- Plant traits from seed trade listings (non-official): duration 140-145 days; small fine grain; yield 45-50 quintals per hectare; medium-low land suitability. -- https://shivagroseeds.com/product/bpt-5204/

GENETICS AND QTL
- Sheath blight QTLs: From an F2 and BC1F2 population of BPT-5204 × ARC10531, nine QTLs on five chromosomes were mapped, with SSR markers RM336 and RM205 tied to major QTLs. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25977888/
- Sheath blight QTL overview: qshb6.1 and related loci from the same BPT-5204 × ARC10531 material are summarised in a review. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/9/4/177
- Grain protein and quality QTLs: An F2 population of BPT 5204 × JAK 686 (188 plants) was used. Four GPC QTLs, three amylose QTLs, and a major QTL qPC1.2 on chromosome 1 were identified. Done at ICAR-IIRR, Hyderabad. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11944466/
- Root architecture: An EMS mutant of BPT-5204 (TI-128) was used in MutMap QTL-seq to map root length and root volume regions. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38941724
- Sheath blight activation tagging: Ac-Ds activation-tagged mutants were generated for sheath blight resistance. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38430361/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Developed by Andhra Pradesh Agricultural Research Station, Bapatla (ANGRAU) in the 1980s. This is an encyclopedia and institutional summary; no named lead breeder for BPT-5204 was found. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/7.%20ARS,%20Bapatla%20Notable%20Achievements.pdf ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_College,_Bapatla ; https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/institutes-wise.html?id=44
- Station-level note: A non-official Bapatla college page lists former ARS and college heads (e.g., Dr. A. Adivi Reddy, Dr. G. Madhusudana Rao). None is linked to BPT-5204 in the source. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_College,_Bapatla
- Research authors (not breeders of the variety): Gandikota M. et al. (PJTSAU, ICAR-IIRR, ANGRAU Tirupati); Gopi P., Ballichatla S., Subba Rao L.V., Sonti R.V. (ICAR-IIRR Hyderabad; ICRISAT; CSIR-CCMB); Mandal N.P. et al. (NRRI/CRRI/ICAR). These are research team affiliations only. -- URLs in PUBLICATIONS.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Gandikota et al. corresponding author email as printed on the paper affiliation: vlnreddy@angrau.ac.in

disease_resistance.research_summary: Bacterial blight: sources conflict. A general encyclopedia entry describes the variety as resistant, while an ICAR-linked technology page describes it as extremely susceptible. Neither is an official evaluation. Sheath blight: susceptible; used as the susceptible parent in QTL mapping (BPT-5204 x ARC10531), so not reported as tolerant. EMS-derived sheath-blight-tolerant mutant lines of BPT-5204 were identified at ICAR-IIRR (mutant lines, not the original variety). Activation-tagged mutants were developed for sheath blight resistance in this line. Blast: a study title describes marker-assisted backcrossing to improve blast resistance of BPT 5204; the abstract was not retrieved, so no resistance outcome is reported.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BRG-4 (release minutes name) / BR-34 (Seednet name), crop field "chickpea" / Seednet crop "PADDY (DHAN)"

RECORD CONFLICT: The record is internally inconsistent. The crop field says chickpea, while the Seednet crop name, the parentage (pure-line selection from Dolangi rice, Monghyr) and the Seednet listing all point to paddy (rice). The evidence found below refers to BR-34 as a rice variety. No source found links "BRG-4" or "BRG 10-2" to chickpea or to any crop. The chickpea entry "BRG 2" (UAS Bangalore) in a DPD list is a different variety. Verify the crop field and variety code against CSC minutes before using this record.

STRESS TOLERANCE / DISEASE AND PEST (refers to BR-34, rice; no BRG-4 evidence): No evidence found. No source found on drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence, or disease/pest reaction for BR-34 or BRG-4. Searches on the BRG 10-2 rice query also returned nothing on this.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (refers to BR-34, rice): No evidence found. The only agronomic reference is a general list placing BR-34 under medium-land rice in Bihar with no yield, duration or trial data -- https://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/varieties-rice-bihar

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found for BRG-4, BRG 10-2 or BR-34. Parentage (pure-line selection from Dolangi rice) is taken from the record itself, not independently verified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (refers to BR-34 / institution named in record): No breeder or scientist name found for BRG-4, BRG 10-2 or BR-34. The institution in the record (Rajendra Agricultural University) is now Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University (RPCAU), Pusa, Samastipur; it was converted to a central university effective 07.10.2016 -- https://rpcau.ac.in/sri/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Rajendra_Prasad_Central_Agriculture_University . The record's "Bihar Agriculture Res. Institute, Patna" was not found in any source.

CONTACT DETAILS: No named breeder, email or phone found. Institute-level address found: Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University, Pusa, Samastipur – 848 125, Bihar, India (Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding) -- https://rpcau.ac.in/academics/departments/department-of-plant-breeding-and-genetics/ . No email or phone for this department was found in the search results. The Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding page is the best available starting point for an institute contact page.

PUBLICATIONS (refers to BR-34 / BRG-4 / BRG 10-2): No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI was found for these names. Unrelated items were excluded.

drought.details: General research indicates that drought is a major limiting factor in rice cultivation and efforts are ongoing to develop drought-tolerant rice varieties such as Sahbhagi Dhan and DRR dhan 42 (RESULT_4, RESULT_7, RESULT_17, RESULT_6). The variety BRRI 71 is also mentioned as drought-tolerant (RESULT_29). However, no specific information regarding the drought tolerance of BR-39 (or BR 34/BRRI dhan 34) was found in the provided search results.

heat.details: Rice cultivation can be affected by heat stress, particularly during the grain-filling stage (RESULT_11, RESULT_15, RESULT_19). Research is focused on breeding heat-tolerant rice varieties and identifying related QTLs/genes (RESULT_12, RESULT_15). No specific information regarding the heat tolerance of BR-39 (or BR 34/BRRI dhan 34) was found in the provided search results.

salinity.details: Salinity is a significant abiotic stress for rice, with various salt-tolerant varieties and landraces (e.g., BINA 8, BRRI dhan 55, CARI Dhan 5 from Pokkali) being developed or studied (RESULT_21, RESULT_22, RESULT_26, RESULT_27). QTLs for salinity-related traits like 'Saltol' have been identified (RESULT_12, RESULT_24). However, no specific information regarding the salinity tolerance of BR-39 (or BR 34/BRRI dhan 34) was found in the provided search results.

flood.details: Flooding events are frequent, necessitating flood-tolerant rice varieties. Varieties like CR Dhan 500 and BRRI dhan76 exhibit flood or tidal flood tolerance (RESULT_31, RESULT_33, RESULT_34, RESULT_35). The Sub1 QTL is noted for its mega effect on flood tolerance (RESULT_36). No specific information regarding the flood tolerance of BR-39 (or BR 34/BRRI dhan 34) was found in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: Not specified in the original variety data. While bacterial blight resistance has been enhanced in other salt-tolerant rice varieties (RESULT_22, RESULT_38), no specific disease resistance information for BR-39 (or BR 34/BRRI dhan 34) was found in the provided search results.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified in the original variety data or the provided search results.

agronomic_details.stability: Br 34 (2206 B) was tested in variety trials from 1956 to 1958, and its performance was reported as consistent. It also performed well in farmers' fields from 1955-1957.
agronomic_details.adaptation: This culture is suitable for transplanted conditions. It is a low input variety and responsive to low doses of fertilizers (40 N, 40 P3 O5, 20 K2O KG/HAC).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: TALL STATURE, LODGING TENDENCY AT MATURITY PENICLE EXSERTION IS COMPLETED AND TILLERING ABILITY IS GOOD. THE PLANT TYPE IS OPEN AND SENSITIVE TO PHOTOPERIOD. IT FLOWERS IN THE 2nd WEEK OF OCTOBER.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Br 34 (2206 B) was tested in variety trials from 1956 to 1958 and showed consistent performance. It also performed well in farmers' fields from 1955-1957. BR 34 (Chinigura) has been noted for its high vitamin levels (RESULT_13).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not specified for this variety. General information on marker-assisted breeding and pyramiding of target QTLs/genes for multiple stress tolerance in rice is available (RESULT_8, RESULT_18).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not specified for this variety. General QTLs for traits like salinity ('Saltol') and submergence ('Sub1') are mentioned in rice breeding efforts (RESULT_12, RESULT_24, RESULT_36).
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not specified for this variety. General molecular implications of abiotic stresses and genes/pathways involved in rice stress tolerance are areas of research (RESULT_12, RESULT_14, RESULT_31).

drought.details: The variety has been considered in the context of developing mutant varieties tolerant to abiotic stresses, including drought. It was evaluated for yield under abiotic stress conditions like drought. The breeding program for this variety involved efforts to develop drought-tolerant upland varieties.

heat.details: The variety has been identified as tolerant to heat stress and was part of a breeding program utilizing a controlled environment for heat tolerance. It was included in screening for high temperature tolerance in rice genotypes.

salinity.details: Badshabhog Selection-1 is described as salinity tolerant. It has been part of improved salt tolerant rice selections and evaluated under abiotic stresses including salinity.

flood.details: The variety is described as a yielding flood tolerant rice variety and was included in breeding for flood tolerance programs.

disease_resistance.summary: Badshabhog Selection-1 is resistant to blast, Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB), and is described as a general disease-resistant variety. It is also noted to be resistant to bacterial leaf blight and gall midge.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety is resistant to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH), Stem Borer (SB), and gall midge. It demonstrates tolerance to major insect pests, including Stem Borer and gall midge.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields vary: 65 quintals per hectare (q/ha) is stated for the protein-rich paddy variety, while another report indicates 35 quintals per hectare (Q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Unknown
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for irrigated conditions and suitable for semi-deep water. It shows a good response to late sown conditions. It is classified as a non-Basmati variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf (82 cm) with long slender grains. It is also noted as a protein-rich paddy variety. It is highly tolerant to cold stress.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Badshabhog Selection-1 has been widely evaluated in various All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (AICRIP) meetings and screenings, including those for submergence tolerance, high temperature tolerance, and general abiotic stress tolerance. It was part of approximately 500 on-farm trials.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
TOLERANCE (submergence): Bahadur-Sub1 is a Sub1-introgressed version of the Assam variety Bahadur, and screening ranked it among lines with higher submergence tolerance than the tolerant control Swarna-Sub1 -- https://academia.edu/Documents/in/Rice_Submergence_Tolerance
TOLERANCE (submergence, duration): The ICAR-NRRI table lists Bahadur-Sub1 as tolerating about two weeks of complete submergence -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf
TOLERANCE (submergence, mechanism): The Sub1 gene (from FR13A, chromosome 9) works by limiting underwater elongation, which conserves reserves for recovery; this mechanism is established for Sub1 lines generally, not verified specifically for Bahadur-Sub1 -- https://academic.oup.com/aobpla/article/doi/10.1093/aobpla/plu060/159405
TOLERANCE (submergence, field/phenotypic evaluation): Kharif 2015 phenotypic screening of 35 genotypes, including 8 BC2F3 lines from Bahadur x Swarna-Sub1, evaluated submergence tolerance and yield-related traits; high heritability and genetic advance were reported for key traits -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=9846&vol=7-9-2018&SNo=211
DROUGHT: No evidence found for Bahadur-Sub1 in the searched sources (a 2025 Assam seed-system chapter mentions "submergence and drought tolerance" varieties in general, but does not document drought tolerance for Bahadur-Sub1) -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-032-10879-1_13
HEAT: No evidence found -- none retrieved
SALINITY: No evidence found -- none retrieved
FLOOD (field/farmer level): Bahadur-Sub1 is reported as a flood-tolerant variety developed by Assam Agricultural University, adopted in flood-prone Assam -- https://dialogue.earth/en/food/flood-tolerant-rice-helps-farmers-in-assam/
DISEASE/PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found -- none retrieved
QTL/MARKERS: Sub1 QTL (major locus, LOD 36, about 69% R²) was introgressed into Bahadur via marker-assisted backcrossing using Swarna-Sub1 as donor parent; microsatellite markers were used for background selection -- https://researchgate.net/publication/23441677_Development_of_submergence-tolerant_rice_cultivars_The_Sub1_locus_and_beyond
YIELD (non-flooded): Sub1 varieties in Assam (including Bahadur-Sub1) showed a yield advantage of 1.0-1.2 t/ha over non-Sub1 counterparts in 2018-19 to 2022-23, including under non-flooded conditions -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-032-10879-1_13
YIELD (rainfed shallow lowland): Bahadur-155 Sub1 is listed with an average yield of 5.0 t/ha and recommended for Assam -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf
YIELD (general Sub1 trade-off): Sub1 introgressed lines showed no overall yield penalty under non-flooded conditions relative to their non-Sub1 counterparts (general, not Bahadur-specific) -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-27648-y
BREEDER/INSTITUTION: Developed by Assam Agricultural University (scientists quoted for the Sub1 varieties Ranjit-Sub1, Bahadur-Sub1, Swarna-Sub1); IRRI-supported backcrossing for Sub1 transfer -- https://dialogue.earth/en/food/flood-tolerant-rice-helps-farmers-in-assam/
RELEASE: Bahadur-Sub1 is reported in the Assam context alongside Ranjit-Sub1 (2018 notification); the exact 2018-01-20 release/notification date for Bahadur-Sub1 was not confirmed -- https://dialogue.earth/en/food/flood-tolerant-rice-helps-farmers-in-assam/
SEED AVAILABILITY (NSC/state corporations/KVKs): No official NSC, state seed corporation or KVK listing found. AAU produced over 102 tonnes of Ranjit-Sub1 seed in 2018 (Bahadur-Sub1 figure not found) -- https://dialogue.earth/en/food/flood-tolerant-rice-helps-farmers-in-assam/
SEED AVAILABILITY (commercial): A private seller in Dhemaji, Assam lists Bahadur Sub-1 seed at Rs 34/kg, claiming CSCB seed-certification standard; not an official source -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rice-seeds-bahadur-sub-1-20721268555.html
RECOMMENDED STATES: Assam (flood-prone areas; the ICAR-NRRI table and the Assam seed-system chapter both point to Assam) -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf

Search budget note: the search tool's limit was reached after the first batch of four queries. Two of those four queries returned the same Scribd document, so the record below is thin. Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Bhavapuri Sannalu," so no name-mismatch search was needed. The Seednet portal itself could not be queried (no internet access). The evidence below refers to the name "Bhavapuri Sannalu" as written in the record.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Not found in the retrieved snippets. The Scribd document was returned for the variety query but only its title and opening lines were visible. Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence data were not seen. Full text needed: https://www.scribd.com/doc/46993395/Bhavapuri-Sannalu-a-new-superfine-rice-variety-released-for-single-cropped-wetlands-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India

DISEASE AND PEST -- Not found in the retrieved snippets. Same source as above; resistance details not visible. Full text needed: https://www.scribd.com/doc/46993395/Bhavapuri-Sannalu-a-new-superfine-rice-variety-released-for-single-cropped-wetlands-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maturity, yield and trial results not found in the retrieved snippets. The Scribd document is described as a release note for a "superfine" rice variety; grain-quality and yield claims were not visible. Full text needed: https://www.scribd.com/doc/46993395/Bhavapuri-Sannalu-a-new-superfine-rice-variety-released-for-single-cropped-wetlands-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage from the input record only: PBT 5204 / CR 15 MR 1523 (no independent source checked). No QTL or marker study found in the retrieved results.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution from the input record: Rice Research Unit, Bapatla-522101 (Andhra Pradesh). Release year from the input record: 2010-10-10. The Scribd release note is the only variety-specific source retrieved; its visible text did not name a breeder. Breeder name not found. Institution page not retrieved.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder name, official email, phone or institute contact page found in the retrieved results. The institution address available from the input record is only "Rice Research Unit, Bapatla-522101." Acadmic contact should be sought from Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) or the Bapatla rice research station directly; I could not verify these details here.

PUBLICATIONS --
Scribd release note, title as given: "Bhavapuri Sannalu, a new superfine rice variety released for single-cropped wetlands of Andhra Pradesh, India." Author and year not visible in the retrieved text. Document type: release note or extension leaflet -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/46993395/Bhavapuri-Sannalu-a-new-superfine-rice-variety-released-for-single-cropped-wetlands-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India
Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, theses and KrishiKosh entries: No evidence found after searching. Not retrieved within the search budget.

The only related item retrieved is a CABI Digital Library article on breeder seed multiplication and certified seed distribution in India. Its list of inbred rice cultivars includes "Bhavapuri Sannalu," which confirms the variety has been in the Indian seed system but says nothing about current stock or sellers -- https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Input record says "Not specified." The Scribd release title refers to single-cropped wetlands of Andhra Pradesh, which suggests Andhra Pradesh as the target state, but this is from the title only and should be confirmed against the release notification or the Seednet entry.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The search for Bio 151 release and trait details returned only generic maize pages and unrelated hybrid or composite lists, none naming this variety for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for Bio 151 (BIO 9544) or Bio-501. The only corn-borer and QTL pages were about other maize materials.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for Bio 151 or Bio-501 was returned. The one IIMR cultivar-list snippet that mentions Bio 9544 (BIO151) gives no per-variety yield or maturity values that can be reliably tied to it. The record should not inherit yield or maturity values from neighbouring rows of that list. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The QTL results returned concern other maize populations and traits (protein/oil/starch, plant height, root traits, ear fasciation), and none name Bio 151 or Bio-501. Parentage is "Not specified" in the input, and no source supplied it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution (name-variant evidence): the ICAR-IIMR cultivar list records "Bio 9544 (BIO151)" as released by Bioseed Research India Pvt. Ltd., which is the "Bio Seeds Research India" in the input. The listing is a private release; no breeder name is given. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/
Institution profile: Bioseed Research India (BRI) is described as a Government of India-approved technology development company, 100% owned by DCM Shriram Consolidated Ltd, with R&D in corn among other crops. -- https://www.life-sciences-asia.com/organisation/bioseed-research-india-pvt-ltd-dcm-dscl-group-2001-28730.html
Lead breeder: No evidence found. No maize breeder is named for Bio 151. Breeder names on the RocketReach page are for tomato, pearl millet, and other crops, so none are attributed here. -- https://rocketreach.co/bioseed-research-india-pvt-ltd-profile_b45162d3fc700ebd
Bio-501 (Seednet name): No evidence found. The search returned no Seednet or other record for Bio-501. The Seednet crop is listed as "PADDY (DHAN)", which conflicts with maize and should be checked on the portal.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institution-level only; no breeder contact found.
Registered office of Bioseed Research India Limited (tofler.in record): 5th Floor, Kanchenjunga Building, 18 Barakhamba Road, New Delhi 110001; company email listed as blsachdeva@dscl.com. Note that this is a registry listing, not an institute page, and it is not verified as the developer's contact. -- https://www.tofler.in/bioseed-research-india-limited/company/U74899DL1992PLC050504
Bioseed brand (ZoomInfo page): headquarters given as plot no. 234 B, Block Phase II, Hyderabad; phone +91 4023555801; website www.bioseed.com. Brand-level and unverified against an official page. -- https://www.zoominfo.com/c/bioseed/356395513
ICAR-IIMR (cultivar list custodian, not the developer): email director.maize@icar.gov.in; phones +911612430038 and 9492430207; address PAU campus, Ludhiana 141004, Punjab. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/
Discarded: the Zauba Corp page for "BIOSEED INDIA LIMITED" (a different CIN and company) and the Biofresh Seeds (Ahmedabad) page, both of which are similarly named companies.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP or ICAR report, thesis, or KrishiKosh entry naming Bio 151 or Bio-501 was returned. The ResearchGate maize-release compilation mentions "CM 151" and other entries, but not Bio 151, so it was discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for Bio 151 or Bio-501 from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales, or dealers. The Bio 501 search returned only an unrelated Sri Lankan hybrid (SA 501) and US maize inbred patents, which were discarded. -- https://www.hayleysagriculture.com/sa-501/ (discarded, different product)

RECOMMENDED STATES
Input list (CSC release minutes, not web-verified): Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, A.P., Rajasthan, Gujarat, M.P., Chhattisgarh.
Web-derived: the IIMR cultivar-list snippet for Bio 9544 (BIO151) gives a different set (Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, ...), but the row boundaries in that snippet are unclear, so it cannot be confirmed as this variety's entry. Treat the states as unresolved until the CSC minutes are checked. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/

Name-variant note: "Bio 151" and "BIO 9544" both appear in the IIMR list, and that list also has a separate "151 · BH-40625 (DHM-117) · ANGRAU" entry, which is a different variety and was excluded.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: CB 06 535 was evaluated under SRI system of cultivation in Kharif 2010 11 at Coimbatore. The culture recorded higher yield under SRI than normal method. The culture recorded better agronomic efficiency (37.2 and 48.3% under normal and SRI respectively) than the check variety ADT 43 (30.5 and 33.5% under normal and SRI systems) (Table 3a). The culture possesses higher physiological efficiency by registering higher crop growth rate, leaf area Index, better light transmission ratio, spikelet fertility, Dry matter production and Harvest Index.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
1.	Erect long and Broad flag leaf
2.	Long slender grain (rough rice L/B ratio 3.87)
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress:
Abiotic – not tested
Biotic – reaction to pests and diseases furnished in para 8(e) and 8 (f).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
The culture CB 06 535 was screened against all the epidemic diseases viz., blast, bacterial blight, sheath rot, sheath blight, brown spot and rice tungro artificially inoculated conditions during 2009, 2010 and 2011. The culture CB 06 535 is found to be moderately resistant to Blast (scale 5), in 1 to 9 scale. The corresponding scores for ADT 43 are 7 or 9 scale for all the diseases in the order mentioned above. 
Under AICRIP, the culture was screened in NSN-1 and DSN-1, wherein CB 06 535 was found to be moderately resistant to blast.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests:
The culture CB 06535 was evaluated for three yea (2009, 10 & 11) at Coimbatore, Madurai and Aduthurai against the major pests and the culture CB 06 535 was moderately resistant to GLH (5) and BPH (3).

Under AICRIP, the culture was screened during 2010, CB 06 535 was found to be moderately resistant to WBPH, Leaf folder and stem borer.

Bred by marker-assisted backcrossing for multiple QTL improving root growth under drought. Out-yields its recurrent parent by 10% under rainfed conditions. The AICRIP table text is OCR-garbled, so the row alignment for 111 is uncertain. Level is medium because the evidence is descriptive and from a news release and a partly garbled table, with no quantified drought scoring. Evidence for the parent Kalinga III (weak stems, low inherent drought tolerance) was excluded because it applies to Birsa Vikas Dhan-110, not 111.

The parentage KALINGA III X IR 64 from the CSC record is not confirmed for 111 in the evidence, because the recurrent parent is not named in any retrieved page. The Kalinga III x IR 64 cross reported for Birsa Vikas Dhan-110 (Ashoka 228) was excluded as a different variety.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Marker-assisted selection for root growth QTL under drought. Specific genes and pathways were not reported in the evidence.
