search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Name match: Birsa Vikas Dhan-111 (PY 84), notified 2015. Described as early maturing, drought tolerant, and suited to direct-seeded uplands and transplanted medium lands of Eastern India -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2009/may/26018.htm
Named as a drought-tolerant variety with deep root traits; the AICRIP Ranchi table lists it as resistant to gall midge and moderately resistant to blast, BLB, false smut, stem borer and gundhi bug. The table text is OCR-garbled, so row alignment for 111 is uncertain -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
Seednet name Birsa Vikas Dhan-110: the AICRIP Ranchi table lists it as tolerant to blast, BLB, stem borer and drought, suited to rainfed upland (95 days) -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
Birsa Vikas Dhan-110 (Ashoka 228 line): earlier farmer-participatory trials identified Kalinga III as weak-stemmed and lodging-prone, with low inherent drought tolerance; this applies to the parent, not to 111 -- https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/57a08b72ed915d3cfd000d16/riu09impact1india-rice.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Birsa Vikas Dhan-111 (name match in AICRIP Ranchi table): resistant to gall midge, moderately resistant to blast, BLB, false smut, stem borer, gundhi bug -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
Birsa Vikas Dhan-110 (seednet name): tolerant to blast, BLB, stem borer and drought -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Birsa Vikas Dhan-111: matures in 120-125 days with yield potential of 18 to 20 q/acre; plant height 84-95 cm; deeply rooted, medium-tall (AICRIP table, OCR-garbled alignment) -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
Birsa Vikas Dhan-111: out-yields its recurrent parent by 10% under rainfed conditions; target-environment selection in farmers' fields in Jharkhand, Orissa and West Bengal from 2001 -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2009/may/26018.htm
Birsa Vikas Dhan-110 (seednet name): matures in 95 days, yield potential 10 to 12 q/acre, suited to rainfed upland -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
Birsa Vikas Dhan-110 (Ashoka 228): yielded significantly more than controls including Kalinga III in research and farmer-field trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/228682092_Collaborative_and_consultative_participatory_plant_breeding_of_rice_for_the_rainfed_uplands_of_eastern_India

GENETICS AND QTL
Birsa Vikas Dhan-111: bred by marker-assisted backcrossing with selection for multiple QTL for improved root growth under drought; first combined MAS and client-oriented breeding success for a quantitative trait -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2009/may/26018.htm
Birsa Vikas Dhan-111: background selection for Kalinga III alleles on target chromosomes, incomplete across all chromosomes; the largest introgressed segment was 40 cm on chromosome 2 -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2009/may/26018.htm
Target QTL first identified by Adam Price (then Bangor/Aberdeen work) and Birgitte Courtois (CIRAD/IRRI) -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2009/may/26018.htm
Birsa Vikas Dhan-110 (seednet name): Kalinga III x IR 64 cross, the source of Ashoka 228 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/228682092_Collaborative_and_consultative_participatory_plant_breeding_of_rice_for_the_rainfed_uplands_of_eastern_India
Parentage for 111: Kalinga III background is indicated by the background selection note, but the recurrent parent is not named in any retrieved page; the parentage "KALINGA III X IR 64" is not confirmed for 111 -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2009/may/26018.htm

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed in collaborative partnership between CAZS Natural Resources, Bangor University (UK), Gramin Vikas Trust (Ranchi, Jharkhand) and Birsa Agricultural University (BAU), Ranchi -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2009/may/26018.htm
Birsa Vikas Dhan-110 (Ashoka 228) came from consultative participatory breeding by the same partnership (GVT, BAU, CAZS-NR, with LI-BIRD in the EIRFP) -- https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/57a08b72ed915d3cfd000d16/riu09impact1india-rice.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist NAME(S) for Birsa Vikas Dhan-111: No evidence found. The search returned no named breeder for this variety. Wikipedia pages on Vijaipal Singh (Pusa Basmati 1121) were discarded as an unrelated variety.
Institution field "Not Available" in the CSC record: the evidence above names BAU Ranchi and GVT Ranchi.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder email, phone or postal address found for Birsa Vikas Dhan-111 or Birsa Vikas Dhan-110. Institute-level reference only: AICRIP centre at Kanke under Birsa Agricultural University, Ranchi, Jharkhand, started 1981 -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf (no contact details on that page as retrieved)

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not captured (year not shown). Collaborative and consultative participatory plant breeding of rice for the rainfed uplands of eastern India. Journal/report not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/228682092_Collaborative_and_consultative_participatory_plant_breeding_of_rice_for_the_rainfed_uplands_of_eastern_India (covers Ashoka 200F and Ashoka 228; Birsa Vikas Dhan-110 link, not 111)
Authors not captured (year not shown). New Upland Rice Varieties for India: Rainfed Agriculture Impact Study No. 1. Report -- https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/57a08b72ed915d3cfd000d16/riu09impact1india-rice.pdf (BVD 110 = Ashoka 228; the study does not name 111 in the retrieved text)
Authors not captured (2022). Impact of breeder seed multiplication and certified quality seed distribution on rice production in India. Journal: Agriculture & Food Security (DOI inferred from the URL) -- https://doi.org/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2 (lists Birsa Vikas Dhan 111 among cultivars with one year of breeder seed production)
Katherine Steele (2009). Novel upland rice variety bred using marker-assisted selection and client-oriented breeding released in Jharkhand, India. Plant Breeding News, Edition 200 (news item, not peer-reviewed) -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2009/may/26018.htm
No peer-reviewed paper specifically on Birsa Vikas Dhan-111 was found. Discarded: a BVD-109 nitrogen study and a Birsa dhan-104 DDSR review.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Retrieved listings were for Birsa Dhan-101 (Amazon, currently unavailable) and an unrelated IndiaMART dhan seed listing. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, BAU seed sales or dealer listing for Birsa Vikas Dhan-111 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Birsa Vikas Dhan-111: notified 2015 (S.O. 268(E), 28.01.2015) for Jharkhand -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
Birsa Vikas Dhan-111: released in Jharkhand; suited to direct-seeded uplands and transplanted medium lands of Eastern India -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2009/may/26018.htm
Birsa Vikas Dhan-110 (seednet name): Bihar notification list entry (S.O. 1177(E), 25/08/2005) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf (listed under a 2003 year; states not stated in the retrieved text)

RECORD NOTES
Name mapping: the CSC name Birsa Vikas Dhan-111 and the seednet name Birsa Vikas Dhan-110 refer to different varieties in the evidence. The 111 evidence is the 2015 Jharkhand notification and the 2009 MAS release. The 110 evidence is the 2005 notification and the Ashoka 228 line.
Year: the CSC year 2014-10-20 does not match the 2015 gazette notification (S.O. 268(E), 28.01.2015) in the evidence.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
BIRSA VIKAS DHAN-203 (rice) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC release-minute name "Birsa Vikas Dhan-203" and the Seednet name "Birsa Vikas Dhan - 203" both appear in the search results only as "Birsa Vikas Dhan 203" or "Birsa Vikash Dhan -203". No Seednet portal page was returned, so every finding below refers to the variety name, not a Seednet record. The 2014 release date and "Not Available" fields were not confirmed by any source.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Described as medium-tolerant to drought in the Ranchi AICRIP centre write-up, which says the variety may be cultivated transplanted in drought-prone medium; the drought-tolerance wording is not separately attributed to 203 -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- No flood, submergence, heat or salinity evidence found for this variety -- No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Listed as moderately resistant to blast, bacterial leaf blight (BLB), brown spot, stem borer and gundhi bug (the Ranchi PDF text for the 203 row is garbled, so this should be checked against the original PDF) -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- No gall midge, BPH or other pest-specific resistance data for 203 found -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Long slender grain, non-lodging, semi-dwarf plant type, with maturity of about 120-125 days and yield potential of 16 to 18 q/acre (Ranchi AICRIP centre table) -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- No multi-location trial or station-level yield data for 203 found in the search results -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL:
- No QTL, marker or pedigree evidence for Birsa Vikas Dhan-203 found. The IR 64/Kalinga III parentage in the record was not confirmed. The Birsa Vikas Dhan 111 (PY 84) marker-assisted QTL study belongs to a different variety and is excluded -- https://www.seedquest.com/News/releases/2009/may/26018.htm (excluded: other variety)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Notified in Jharkhand under the name Birsa Vikas Dhan 203 (IET 19896), via S.O. 268(E) dated 28.01.2015 -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- The Ranchi AICRIP centre, under Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, lists the variety in its rice table. This is the institutional link; the breeder names were not found -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- No lead breeder or scientist name found for this variety -- No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS:
- No breeder email, phone or personal contact found for this variety -- No evidence found
- Institute-level contact: none captured. The Ranchi AICRIP PDF gives the centre (Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, Jharkhand) but no email, phone or address -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf

PUBLICATIONS:
- Authors not captured; year and journal not captured. Title: "Impact of breeder seed multiplication and certified quality seed distribution on rice production in India" (Birsa Vikas Dhan 203 appears in its list of inbred cultivars; the paper is not specific to this variety) -- https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRIP annual report or KrishiKosh thesis specific to Birsa Vikas Dhan-203 found. The 2015 Singh et al. paper concerns Birsa Vikas Dhan-109, and the 2022 Zenodo note concerns Birsa Dhan 201/202 -- excluded as other varieties

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- Named in the cultivar list of the breeder-seed multiplication study, which covers breeder seed indents and certified seed distribution (not a current seller listing) -- https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, Birsa Agricultural University seed-sales or private dealer listing found. The Seednet portal was not returned -- No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Jharkhand (notification under the name Birsa Vikas Dhan 203, S.O. 268(E), 28.01.2015) -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Jharkhand (Ranchi AICRIP centre entry, rainfed upland and drought-prone transplanted medium) -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- Recommendation for other states not found. The Seednet "recommended_states_raw: Not Available" field was not confirmed

pest_resistance.summary: Moderate resistance to stem borer and gundhi bug (Leptocorisa spp.), per the AICRIP Ranchi centre table. The second AICRIP extract also lists BPH, but this cannot be confidently attributed to this variety. A 2018-2019 BAU Ranchi trial on gundhi bug in this aromatic variety tested insecticide sprays timed at 25, 55 and 85 days after transplanting; the lowest bug population came from the tipronil treatment. This trial reports insecticide control, not varietal resistance.

(3) 2018-2019 BAU Ranchi gundhi bug trial at BAU Rice Research Farm, Ranchi: insecticide sprays at 25, 55 and 85 days after transplanting; tipronil treatment gave the lowest bug population. This was an insecticide trial and does not measure variety yield.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME NOTE: The CSC-style name "Birsa Vikas Sugandha-1" and the Seednet name "Birsa Vikas Sugandha-1 (IET 18941)" are both used below. Sources also spell it "Birsa Vikash Sugandha-1", "Birsa Vikas Sugandh-1" and "Sugandha-1". No source I found uses the Seednet form or the code IET 18941, so no Seednet page was verified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The AICRIP Ranchi centre table gives a moderate-resistance profile for this line: moderately resistant to blast, bacterial leaf blight, brown spot, stem borer and gundhi bug. The same table's drought line is ambiguous in the extracted text, so drought tolerance is not confirmed for this variety. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- A second AICRIP extract attributes tolerance to blast, BLB, stem borer and BPH, but the row boundaries are garbled and cannot be tied to this variety with confidence. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- No evidence found for flood, submergence, salinity or heat tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate resistance to blast, bacterial leaf blight, brown spot, stem borer and gundhi bug, per the AICRIP Ranchi table. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- A 2018–2019 BAU Ranchi trial on gundhi bug in this aromatic variety tested insecticide sprays timed at 25, 55 and 85 days after transplanting, and the lowest bug population came from the tipronil treatment. -- https://www.acspublisher.com/journals/index.php/jefa/article/view/7884

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Plant type is long, slender and aromatic, with a length-to-breadth ratio of about 3.71. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- Maturity is about 120–125 days, with a yield potential of about 16–18 q/acre. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- The DFID programme report describes it as performing well in medium uplands in eastern India, and it was tested in participatory on-farm trials, state trials and AICRIP trials. -- https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/57a08c39e5274a27b200106f/R8099_FTR.pdf
- The same report lists it as a medium-land transplanted entry, and as a Nepal-programme variety. -- https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/57a08c39e5274a27b200106f/R8099_FTR.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Origin is recorded as a Nepal-programme product from LI-BIRD participatory plant breeding, which fits the parentage field. -- https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/57a08c39e5274a27b200106f/R8099_FTR.pdf
- A mutagenesis-impact paper lists this variety among rice cultivars released from induced mutant or mutagenesis-related work, which would support the gamma-irradiated parentage. The extract does not state which parent population was used. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365753595_Role_of_induced_mutagenesis_and_improved_crop_varieties_in_food_security_impact_in_the_Indian_context
- No QTL or marker study for this variety was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Birsa Agricultural University (BAU), Ranchi, Jharkhand. -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/2e7858a8-f76d-44fc-a056-a86e01190f6a
- A CGIAR record lists this variety among BAU releases for Jharkhand. -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/2e7858a8-f76d-44fc-a056-a86e01190f6a
- A researcher profile credits Daljit Singh Virk with contributing to development of this variety, alongside Birsa Vikas Dhan 203. This is a self-describing profile and not an official release record. -- https://livedna.net/?dna=44.11861
- Lead breeder name from an official notification: No evidence found.
- Station: BAU Rice Research Farm, Ranchi, is where the trial was run. -- https://www.acspublisher.com/journals/index.php/jefa/article/view/7884

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or direct contact was found.
- Institute-level address (from a 2022 author affiliation, Department of Entomology): Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi-834006. -- https://www.acspublisher.com/journals/index.php/jefa/article/view/7884
- No official BAU email, phone or contact-page URL was found in the search results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Jha, S. K.; Prasad, R. (2022). Integrated management of gundhi bug (Leptocorisa spp.) infesting aromatic rice. Journal (JEFA, per the URL) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/2582-2683.2022.00018.1
- Department for International Development Plant Sciences Research Programme (year and authors not stated). Final technical report, R8099. -- https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/57a08c39e5274a27b200106f/R8099_FTR.pdf
- Authors not stated (undated). Climate resilient strategies for rice production in Jharkhand towards fulfilling food security. CGIAR CGSpace record -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/2e7858a8-f76d-44fc-a056-a86e01190f6a
- Authors not stated (year not stated). Role of induced mutagenesis and improved crop varieties in food security: impact in the Indian context. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365753595_Role_of_induced_mutagenesis_and_improved_crop_varieties_in_food_security_impact_in_the_Indian_context
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRIP annual report entry or QTL paper was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or BAU seed-sales listing was found for this variety.
- DFID planning documents describe a large-scale seed production plan of 1–2 t for each of five transplanted varieties, including this one. This is a historical plan and does not confirm current stock. -- https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/57a08c39e5274a27b200106f/R8099_FTR.pdf
- An IndiaMART listing for "Sugandha" paddy seed is a generic product and is not linked to Birsa Vikas Sugandha-1, so it is not used. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sugandha-paddy-seed-20399096791.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Jharkhand: the variety is listed as a BAU release for Jharkhand, and the DFID report supports medium-upland and medium-land use in eastern India. -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/2e7858a8-f76d-44fc-a056-a86e01190f6a
- Release year 2015-06-25 and any CSC notification details: No evidence found in the searches.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CG Jawaphool Trombay (CSC name) / CG Jawaphool Trombay (RTR-31) (Seednet name), rice (paddy/dhan)

Searches run: 4 (variety and crop; breeder and institution; research papers; seed availability). Name tags: [CGJT] = "CG Jawaphool Trombay"; [RTR-31] = Seednet name. No result used the exact string "RTR-31" alongside CGJT. The IAEA record lists "Raipur Trombay Rice-31" among Jawaphool mutants, and Daily Pioneer names "Chhattisgarh Trombay Jawaphool (CTJ)-31". Both may refer to the same line, but neither page confirms that, so I have not treated them as the same variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
[CGJT] BARC's variety sheet describes the variety as semi-tall (120-125 cm) and lodging resistant, against a tall, lodging-susceptible Jawaphool parent -- https://www.barc.gov.in/div/66_209_h1251_2026.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no page giving these for CGJT.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No result on blast, bacterial leaf blight, sheath blight, brown planthopper, gall midge or stem borer for CGJT or RTR-31 was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
[CGJT] BARC sheet: duration 130-135 days, about 10-15 days earlier than local Jawaphool (145-150 days); mean grain yield 4034 kg/ha against 2871 kg/ha for local Jawaphool, reported as about 40% higher; slender aromatic grain -- https://www.barc.gov.in/div/66_209_h1251_2026.pdf
[CGJT] Kharif 2024 trial at IGKV Raipur Instructional Cum Research Farm (aromatic rice PCA study): CG Jawaphool Trombay was compared with Jawaphool parent and other lines, and the paper reports its tillering and milling/hulling traits -- http://www.plantarchives.org/article/196-%20Assessment%20of%20genetic%20diversity%20using%20PCA%20for%20yield%20attributing%20and%20grain%20quality%20traits%20in%20aromatic.pdf
[Jawaphool mutant, not confirmed as CGJT] Gamma-ray mutant trials on Jawaphool reported semi-tall, mid-late maturing lines -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333081136_Improvement_of_Traditional_Local_Rice_Varieties_through_Induced_Mutations_Using_Gamma_Radiations
Field yield trial data for RTR-31 or CGJT beyond the BARC sheet: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
[CGJT, origin] CGJT is a radiation-induced mutant of the traditional Jawaphool landrace of Chhattisgarh, produced in the IGKV-BARC mutation breeding programme (gamma irradiation, BARC Trombay) -- https://inis.iaea.org/records/bpw1z-37210
[CGJT, origin] Daily Pioneer reports that the variety was developed by gamma mutation of the traditional Jawaphool and Safri-17 landraces, with BARC -- https://www.dailypioneer.com/2020/state-editions/igau-develops-two-high-yielding-varieties-of-paddy.html
[Jawaphool mutant, not confirmed as CGJT] Gamma-ray dose of 300 Gy used on 1000 Jawaphool seeds for semi-dwarf and mid-late mutants -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353604993_Development_of_Semidwarf_and_Mid-Late_Maturing_Jawaphool_Mutant_Through_the_Use_of_Gamma_Radiation
QTL, marker or molecular study of CGJT: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
[CGJT] Developing institutions: Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur, with Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), Mumbai, in a BARC-IGKV collaboration released in 2020 for Chhattisgarh -- https://www.barc.gov.in/div/66_209_h1251_2026.pdf and https://www.dailypioneer.com/2020/state-editions/igau-develops-two-high-yielding-varieties-of-paddy.html
[CGJT] The IAEA record describes the joint IGKV-BARC mutation programme, run at IGKV's Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, Raipur, and lists CGJT among released mutant varieties -- https://inis.iaea.org/records/bpw1z-37210
Lead breeder or scientist name for CGJT: No evidence found. The Jawaphool mutant papers name IGKV Genetics and Plant Breeding authors, but none names CGJT itself, so I have not attributed them to this variety.
Station: IGKV Raipur (Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding) is the developing station according to the sources above.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder email, phone or direct contact found for CGJT.
Institute-level (from the sources, not verified against the institute's own contact page):

seednet_fields.Parentage: CO 32 is a hybrid derivative of the cross APK 1 x M35-1.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for both irrigated and rainfed condition.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: CO 32 is a tall growing non-lodging variety suitable for rainfed during kharif and rabi seasons and also during summer under irrigated condition.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: 1.	Glume colour: Greyed orange to Greyed yellow. 2.	Glume length: Medium (75% of grain covered). 3.	Caryopsis colour after threshing: Yellow white. 4.	Grain shape in dorsal view: Elliptic.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Medium.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: CO 32 is moderately resistant to shoot fly and stem borer.
seednet_fields.Average Yield (Kg/Ha): 1.	Mean grain yield:  2445 kg/ha. 2.	Dry fodder yield: 6490 kg/ha. 3.	Ranifed 3144 kg/ha and 11710 kg/ha under irrigation respectively. Kg/Ha
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): As basal, compost or Farm yard manure 12.5 t/ha + 2 kg of Azospirillum + 2 kg or Phospho bacterium + 45:45 kg of NPK/ha. TOP dressing (15th and 30th day) @ 22.5 kg N/ha (Irrigated).

drought.details: No drought tolerance evidence specific to CO 32 was found in the digest. The digest reports only rainfed and irrigated adaptation: rainfed grain yield of 2445 kg/ha and fodder of 6490 kg/ha (about 10.3% and 10% above CO 30), and irrigated grain yield averaging 2911 kg/ha and fodder 11710 kg/ha (12% and 10% above CO 30). These yields show adaptation to both conditions but do not measure drought tolerance. Generic sorghum drought text from unrelated pages was discarded.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to downy mildew and grain mold (ejplantbreeding article 843). The CSC variety data records the overall disease reaction as Medium. A TNAU-sourced summary reporting tolerance to leaf blight, downy mildew and stem borer was discarded because it does not name CO 32, so leaf blight resistance is not attributed to this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to shoot fly and stem borer (ejplantbreeding article 843); the CSC variety data gives the same moderate resistance for both pests.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed: mean grain yield 2445 kg/ha and dry fodder 6490 kg/ha (about 10.3% and 10% above CO 30). Irrigated: grain yield averaged 2911 kg/ha and fodder 11710 kg/ha (12% and 10% above CO 30). AICRP national testing (fifteen centres): mean grain 3100 kg/ha and fodder 11453 kg/ha. Discrepancy to check: the CSC data lists rainfed grain as 3144 kg/ha and 11710 kg/ha under irrigation, which does not match the digest's rainfed grain figure of 2445 kg/ha or its irrigated grain average of 2911 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Recommended for both rainfed and irrigated conditions. Gains over comparator varieties were reported across the multi-centre and TNAU station trials. No explicit stability statistics were found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for both irrigated and rainfed conditions in Tamil Nadu. Tall, non-lodging habit suited to rainfed kharif and rabi seasons and to summer irrigated cultivation (CSC data). The digest does not give agro-climatic zone details.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Grains yellowish-white, borne on medium semi-compact earheads (ejplantbreeding article 843). Tall growing and non-lodging per CSC data. Grain quality: protein 11.31-14.66% and fibre 5.8%, with better cooking-quality traits.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRP on Sorghum national testing, fifteen centres from 2010 onward: mean grain 3100 kg/ha and fodder 11453 kg/ha, exceeding CSV 17 by 6.11% (grain) and 29.99% (fodder). (2) Multi-centre trial table listing SPV 2369 (TNS 648) against CSV 17, CSV 20, CSV 23, CSV 27 and a local check; the digest gives no numeric values from this table. (3) Rainfed and irrigated trials at TNAU stations showing dual-purpose grain and fodder gains over CO 30 and K 12; the digest gives no numeric values. (4) Rainfed and irrigated yield comparisons against CO 30 as listed under Yield. No agronomic recommendations (seed rate, fertiliser, sowing window) specific to CO 32 were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CO 32 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: "variety_name" is CO 32 (sorghum, released 2020). "seednet_variety_name" is CO 32 (SPV 2369). The primary paper uses the culture name TNS 648 and links it to SPV 2369 in its trial tables. Each heading below states which name the evidence uses.

STRESS TOLERANCE (evidence uses CO 32 / TNS 648; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found)
- Recommended for both rainfed and irrigated conditions in Tamil Nadu, with rainfed grain yield of 2445 kg/ha and fodder of 6490 kg/ha, about 10.3% and 10% above CO 30 -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/843
- Irrigated grain yield averaged 2911 kg/ha and fodder 11710 kg/ha, a 12% and 10% gain over CO 30 -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/843
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to CO 32. The search returned only general sorghum drought-tolerance text from unrelated pages (e.g., https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/11212977), which I have discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST (evidence uses CO 32 / TNS 648)
- Moderately resistant to shoot fly and stem borer -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/843
- Moderately resistant to downy mildew and grain mold -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/843
- A TNAU-sourced summary reports tolerance to leaf blight, downy mildew and stem borer, but it does not name CO 32 explicitly and is not used as CO 32-specific evidence -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Book-2-VKA-Technology-Colour.pdf (discarded for attribution; listed for transparency only)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (evidence uses CO 32 / TNS 648 / SPV 2369)
- Maturity 105-110 days; grains yellowish-white, borne on medium semi-compact earheads -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/843
- AICRP on Sorghum national testing (fifteen centres, 2010 onward): mean grain 3100 kg/ha and fodder 11453 kg/ha, exceeding CSV 17 by 6.11% (grain) and 29.99% (fodder) -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/843
- Multi-centre trial table lists SPV 2369 (TNS 648) against CSV 17, CSV 20, CSV 23, CSV 27 and a local check -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350726321_A_new_high_yielding_dual_purpose_sorghum_variety_CO_32_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Dual-purpose grain and fodder yield gains over CO 30 and K 12 in rainfed and irrigated trials at TNAU stations -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350726321_A_new_high_yielding_dual_purpose_sorghum_variety_CO_32_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Grain quality: protein 11.31-14.66% and fibre 5.8%, with better cooking-quality traits -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/843
- No evidence found for agronomic recommendations (seed rate, fertiliser, sowing window) specific to CO 32.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: TNS 648 (APK 1 x M35-1), the culture released as CO 32 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350726321_A_new_high_yielding_dual_purpose_sorghum_variety_CO_32_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Breeding-line code TNS 648 and seed-portal code SPV 2369 are linked in the trial tables -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350726321_A_new_high_yielding_dual_purpose_sorghum_variety_CO_32_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Breeding method (pedigree, selection history): No evidence found beyond the cross and the statement that TNS 648 was proposed for release in 2020 -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/843
- QTL, markers, genes, genome resources: No evidence found for CO 32 or TNS 648. Shoot-fly QTL and KASP-marker work found in an institutional profile concerns other germplasm and was discarded -- https://tnau.irins.org/profile/157306

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (evidence uses CO 32 / TNS 648)
- Author metadata lists Ganesamurthy Kulandaivelu and Sivakumar Subbarayan, both at Tamil Nadu Agricultural University -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350726321_A_new_high_yielding_dual_purpose_sorghum_variety_CO_32_for_Tamil_Nadu
- The same record also lists Basil Selvi (Sheffield Hallam University) and Saravanakumar Venkatachalam (TNAU) as associated authors; their role for CO 32 is not confirmed by the article text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350726321_A_new_high_yielding_dual_purpose_sorghum_variety_CO_32_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University; trial and release work sits in the Department of Millets, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/843 (institution named); https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350726321_A_new_high_yielding_dual_purpose_sorghum_variety_CO_32_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Station: Coimbatore; the field trial record refers to the Department of Millets, TNAU, Coimbatore -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/TNAU%20-%20Seed%20stock%20position%20as%20on%2002.09.2022%20-%20English.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No named breeder contact (email or phone) for CO 32 was found. Breeder names above are from article metadata only.
- Institute-level: Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore - 641 003, Tamil Nadu, India -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2231 (journal contact block; postal address only)
- Department of Millets, TNAU, Coimbatore: telephone 0422-2450507 and email millets@tnau.ac.in, as printed in a seed-stock list. The layout does not clearly tie this line to CO 32, so treat it as the department contact, not a CO 32 breeder contact -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/TNAU%20-%20Seed%20stock%20position%20as%20on%2002.09.2022%20-%20English.pdf
- Institute web page: No evidence found for a dedicated TNAU contact URL for CO 32.

PUBLICATIONS (Authors (Year). Title. Journal/Report -- URL/DOI)
- Ganesamurthy K, Sivakumar S, et al. (2021). A new high yielding dual purpose sorghum variety CO 32 for Tamil Nadu. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/843 ; DOI https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.001 (year inferred from DOI; the page's "Published" date reads 23/12/25, which conflicts and should be checked)
- Kulandaivelu G, Subbarayan S, et al. (year not confirmed). A new high yielding dual purpose sorghum variety CO 32 for Tamil Nadu. ResearchGate version of the same paper -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350726321_A_new_high_yielding_dual_purpose_sorghum_variety_CO_32_for_Tamil_Nadu (duplicate of the item above, not a second publication)
- Institutional record: No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report or conference paper specific to CO 32 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY (evidence uses CO 32)
- TNAU Seed Centre stock position as on 02.09.2022 lists CO 32 with 37 kg available, at the Department of Millets, TNAU, Coimbatore -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/TNAU%20-%20Seed%20stock%20position%20as%20on%2002.09.2022%20-%20English.pdf
- The stock list states that availability depends on enquiry-time stock, so the 2022 quantity should be re-checked before use.
- NSC, State Seed Corporation/TANSEDA, KVK, and private dealer listings for CO 32: No evidence found. Dealer pages returned were for other sorghum products (e.g., CO (FS) 31 fodder), which I discarded.
- Seednet listing for CO 32 (SPV 2369): No evidence found (search did not return a Seednet page).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Released for general cultivation in Tamil Nadu under both rainfed and irrigated conditions -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/843
- Other states: No evidence found.

drought.details: CO52 is suitable for irrigated conditions as transplanted rice but is also described as drought tolerant. However, under stress, it may require protective life-saving measures. It is noted for escaping terminal drought stresses.

heat.details: The variety is noted for escaping terminal heat stresses.

salinity.details: CO52 is categorized as a salt susceptible elite cultivar. Studies indicate a low fold change (0.97) under salt stress compared to more tolerant varieties (6.88).

flood.details: While CO52 is used in breeding programs to develop stress-tolerant rice, including for submergence tolerance, direct evidence of its own flood tolerance is not provided.

disease_resistance.summary: CO52 is resistant to blast disease (including neck blast).

pest_resistance.summary: CO52 is resistant to gall midge. It is moderately susceptible to all hoppers, although one source specifies it is resistant to brown plant hoppers, and others generally note it as moderately resistant to insect pests.

agronomic_details.yield: CO52 has a mean grain yield of 6191 kg/ha (or 61.9 q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly specified, but it is a released variety for irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for irrigated conditions as transplanted rice in Tamil Nadu. It is a non-Basmati variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Dwarf (80-92 cm) plant height, with medium slender to fine grains.
agronomic_details.field_trials: CO52/PTB33 // CO52/AD(Bio)13066 crosses have been evaluated in station trials. The performance of purified CO52 nucleus seed has been recommended for further study.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: CO52 is utilized in marker-assisted breeding programs for pyramiding genes for biotic stress tolerance, specifically Xa4, xa5, xa13, and Pi54, and Bph2, Bph3, and Xa13. It is also used in marker-assisted introgression of genes/QTLs for herbicide tolerance and anaerobic conditions.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTLs linked to plant survival and submergence tolerance are studied in the context of breeding lines involving CO52.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not specified beyond gene and QTL mentions.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: CO52 is listed among eligible seed varieties for promotion of seed production under programs like the National Agricultural Development Programme.
commercial_info.availability_status: Readily available, inferred from its inclusion in government programs for seed production.

basic_info.institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (Department of Rice, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Coimbatore)

drought.details: No evidence found in the searches for drought tolerance in CO 51.

heat.details: A heat-escape study uses the CO 51 background as the target for an early-morning-flowering version, aimed at reducing heat-induced yield loss. The digest does not report a measured heat tolerance level for CO 51 itself, so no level is assigned.

salinity.details: A salinity study tested endophytic and rhizospheric microbes on CO51 and PB1 for salinity-stress alleviation. This is a microbe study, not a varietal salinity tolerance trial, so it is not used as evidence of tolerance.

flood.details: No evidence found in the searches for flood tolerance in CO 51.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: moderately resistant (TNAU 2013 release booklet; artificial screening reported in the 2019 EJPB paper). Blast: listed as resistant by TNAU technologies page and AICRIP Coimbatore centre report. Conflicting evidence: a marker-assisted study from a CO 51 x 562-4 cross reports CO 51 itself as susceptible on blast. Bacterial blight: listed as resistant on the TNAU technologies page (multiple resistance to blast, BPH and bacterial blight); no independent screening result for CO 51 in the digest. Brown Plant Hopper: listed under pest resistance below.

pest_resistance.summary: Brown Plant Hopper (BPH): moderately resistant under artificial screening (TNAU 2013 release booklet and EJPB 2019 paper); also listed as resistant on the TNAU technologies page and AICRIP Coimbatore report. Green Leaf Hopper (GLH): moderately resistant (TNAU 2013 release booklet and EJPB 2019 paper).

agronomic_details.yield: Mean yield over seven years of trials: 6623 kg/ha, 10.72% above ADT 43. Highest recorded yield: 11,377 kg/ha at Nallampalli, Dharmapuri district.
agronomic_details.stability: Tested over seven years of multi-location trials; the digest reports the mean yield advantage over ADT 43 but gives no separate stability statistic (e.g., GxE or stability index).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Tamil Nadu. Released as a Tamil Nadu paddy variety; farmer adoption reported in the Cauvery delta kuruvai season (see farmer adoption below). Other agro-climatic data not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf stature, efficient tillering, long droopy panicles. Grain: medium-slender white rice, milling about 69%, head rice recovery 63%, intermediate amylose (22%).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) MLT trials at TNAU stations, 2009 to 2012. (2) AICRIP IVT/AVT trials, 2009-2010. (3) Adaptive trials at 127 farmer locations in 17 districts, 2010-12. Results: seven-year mean yield 6623 kg/ha, 10.72% above ADT 43; highest recorded yield 11,377 kg/ha at Nallampalli, Dharmapuri district. Market quality: trader samples classed as a 'CO 51 type' carry a low premium; ADT 43 and TKM 15 are suggested as alternates (source: doaj.org article, authors not shown). Farmer adoption: an account reports about 40% of kuruvai-season area in the Cauvery delta under CO 51 within two years of release (citing Ramasamy 2015); this is a secondary account and is not independently verified in the digest.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources (no SNP or SSR marker names or positions for CO 51 in the digest). Marker-assisted backcrossing was used to develop early-morning-flowering NILs of CO 51.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: qEMF3 is carried by early-morning-flowering NILs of CO 51 developed by marker-assisted backcrossing; 19 BC3F2 progenies were homozygous for it. Effect size not reported in the digest. Pyramiding of Pi9, Pi54, xa13, Xa21, Gm1 and Gm4 into CO 51 backgrounds was carried out, with RILs and BILs screened for blast and bacterial blight; quantitative effects not reported in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources beyond the listed resistance genes (Pi9, Pi54, xa13, Xa21, Gm1, Gm4) and the qEMF3 locus.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The CSC name "CO 51" and the Seednet name "CO 51" are identical, so one set of searches covered both. The evidence refers to TNAU Rice CO 51 (IET 21605), also written CO(R) 51, a Tamil Nadu paddy variety. The input release date of 2014-10-20 does not match the sources, which give 2013 as the release year. Under this crop, the Seednet portal itself was not reached, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately resistant to Blast, Brown Plant Hopper and Green Leaf hopper (TNAU 2013 release booklet) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/variety_release_2013.pdf
- Under artificial screening, the line is moderately resistant to blast, BPH and GLH -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1227
- A heat-escape study reports the CO 51 background as a target for an early-morning-flowering version, aimed at reducing heat-induced yield loss -- https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0472/13/3/553
- A salinity study tested endophytic and rhizospheric microbes on CO51 and PB1 for salinity-stress alleviation; this is a microbe study, not a varietal tolerance trial -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Distinguishing-morphological-characters-of-TNAU-Rice-CO-51CB-06-535_tbl1_334196659
- Drought, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found in the searches.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Multiple resistance to blast, BPH and bacterial blight is listed for CO 51 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/cpbg/rice-technologies-developed/
- The AICRIP Coimbatore centre report describes CO 51 as resistant to blast and BPH -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/34%20Coimbatore.pdf
- Marker-assisted lines from a CO 51 × 562-4 cross were screened for bacterial blight and blast resistance, and CO 51 itself scored susceptible on blast in that study -- https://doi.org/10.3390/agriculture14050693

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration is 105–110 days, with semi-dwarf stature, efficient tillering and long droopy panicles -- https://www.scribd.com/document/490809354/3185-Article-Text-8180-1-10-20190617
- Mean yield over seven years of trials was 6623 kg/ha, 10.72% above ADT 43 -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1227
- Highest recorded yield was 11,377 kg/ha at Nallampalli, Dharmapuri district -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1227
- Testing covered MLT trials at TNAU stations from 2009 to 2012, AICRIP IVT/AVT trials in 2009–2010, and adaptive trials at 127 farmer locations in 17 districts in 2010–12 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334196659_TNAU_Rice_CO_51_IET_21605_-_A_high_yielding_short_duration_fine_grain_rice_variety_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Grain traits: medium-slender white rice, milling about 69%, head rice recovery 63%, intermediate amylose (22%) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/variety_release_2013.pdf
- Farmer adoption: an account reports about 40% of kuruvai-season area in the Cauvery delta under CO 51 within two years of release (citing Ramasamy 2015) -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Distinguishing-morphological-characters-of-TNAU-Rice-CO-51CB-06-535_tbl1_334196659
- Market quality: trader samples classed as a "CO 51 type" carry a low premium, and ADT 43 and TKM 15 are suggested as alternates -- https://doaj.org/article/ee3d7a719f024dc7b698aa3d5bd89f15

GENETICS AND QTL
- Early-morning-flowering NILs of CO 51 were developed by marker-assisted backcrossing, carrying qEMF3; 19 BC3F2 progenies were homozygous for it -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Distinguishing-morphological-characters-of-TNAU-Rice-CO-51CB-06-535_tbl1_334196659
- Pyramiding of Pi9, Pi54, xa13, Xa21, Gm1 and Gm4 into CO 51 backgrounds, with RILs and BILs screened for blast and BB -- https://doi.org/10.3390/agriculture14050693
- Pedigree: derived from ADT 43 / RR 272-1745 (CB 06 535 line, F5 stabilised Rabi 2005) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334196659_TNAU_Rice_CO_51_IET_21605_-_A_high_yielding_short_duration_fine_grain_rice_variety_for_Tamil_Nadu

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing department: Department of Rice, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1227
- Named developers in the 2019 paper: S. Robin, K. Mohanasundaram, S. Manonmani, S. Rajeswari, P. Jeyaprakash, R. Pushpam, K. Thiagarajan, R. Rabindran, S. Suresh, V. Ravichandran, S. Radhamani -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/2598/f8361d7e6dc3e8268a273066b5989323fe8b.pdf
- Department background: the rice section was formerly the Paddy Breeding Station, founded 1912 -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/cpbg/rice
- Early-morning-flowering work: Raveendran Muthurajan, Department of Plant Biotechnology, TNAU, Coimbatore -- https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0472/13/3/553

CONTACT DETAILS

- Institute-level: Department of Rice, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore - 641 003 (postal code from the 2019 paper's affiliation line) -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1227

disease_resistance.research_summary: Blast: moderately resistant (TNAU 2013 release booklet; artificial screening reported in the 2019 EJPB paper). Blast: listed as resistant by TNAU technologies page and AICRIP Coimbatore centre report. Conflicting evidence: a marker-assisted study from a CO 51 x 562-4 cross reports CO 51 itself as susceptible on blast. Bacterial blight: listed as resistant on the TNAU technologies page (multiple resistance to blast, BPH and bacterial blight); no independent screening result for CO 51 in the digest. Brown Plant Hopper: listed under pest resistance below.

pest_resistance.research_summary: Brown Plant Hopper (BPH): moderately resistant under artificial screening (TNAU 2013 release booklet and EJPB 2019 paper); also listed as resistant on the TNAU technologies page and AICRIP Coimbatore report. Green Leaf Hopper (GLH): moderately resistant (TNAU 2013 release booklet and EJPB 2019 paper).

drought.details: Described as an early duration, high-yielding drought tolerant rice variety for drought-prone districts of Tamil Nadu, derived from the cross PMK (R) 3 x Norungan. Listed under drought/moisture stress tolerant varieties in a Lok Sabha annex. TNAU 43rd Rice CSM (2024) records it as drought tolerant and suitable for direct seeding under rainfed and semi-dry conditions during the NEM period (September). A Journal of Rice Research study reported higher root length in CO 53 and Anna 4 under water stress, and it was identified as suitable for short-duration water stress conditions. The 2022 TNAU CSM proceedings note its drought tolerance in the context of induced drought stress evaluation at 55 DAS. Specific physiological mechanisms (e.g., root traits, osmotic adjustment) are only partly documented, mainly through the root-length observation.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance data for CO 53 found in the search results. Heat stress screening appears in the IIRR Annual Report 2020 and TNAU proceedings only as general program activity, not as CO 53 results.

salinity.details: No CO 53-specific salinity tolerance evidence found. A TNAU project on paddy diseases in saline soil is mentioned but not linked to CO 53 performance. Salinity is listed as a stress category in AICRIP proposals, without CO 53 results.

flood.details: The TNAU 41st CSM proceedings list CO 53 among varieties under observation for flood tolerance, but no tolerance rating or quantitative result is reported in the retrieved text.

disease_resistance.summary: Not specified for CO 53 in the retrieved results. Disease screening (stem rot, sheath rot) appears in IIRR program reports without variety-specific reaction data for CO 53.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified for CO 53 in the retrieved results.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No SSR, SNP, or QTL positions for CO 53 were found in the retrieved results. The PMC study on parental genetic diversity lists CO 53 among breeding parents but reports no marker details for it.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL effects specific to CO 53 were identified in the retrieved results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not specified. Drought tolerance is attributed to phenotypic evaluation and root traits rather than characterized genes or pathways.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to stem borer, gall midge, blast, bacterial leaf blight (BLB), brown spot, sheath rot, sheath blight, rice tungro disease (RTD) and glume discoloration (TNAU CO 56 page). TNAU release list (2023) reports moderate resistance to multiple diseases and to stem borer and gall midge. An AICRPR trial table row for CO 56 lists moderate resistance to MR-BL, BLB, RTD, BS and SB. Note: the digest's abbreviations MR-BL, BS and SB are recorded as given; the IRM/MS score of 6.3 is recorded in field trials.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to stem borer and gall midge (TNAU release list, 2023; also listed in the TNAU CO 56 page under the combined disease and pest list and in the AICRPR trial table as SB, and gall midge in the TNAU list). No quantitative pest score for CO 56 beyond the AICRPR notation was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Average grain yield 6372 kg/ha (TNAU CO 56 page and TNAU 2023 release list).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The 2020 agronomy trial showed better agronomic efficiency than CO 52 (more grains per panicle and higher grain yield), but multi-environment stability was not reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Tamil Nadu (adaptation_ecology in record). Season listed as Late Samba / Thaladi (TNAU CO 56 page). AICRPR trial entry notes rainfed condition.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 130 To 135Days (TNAU 2023 release list gives 130-135 days; TNAU CO 56 page gives 135-140 days; both recorded)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium slender white rice; milling 67%; head rice recovery 64.1%; over 350 grains per panicle; medium-tall; non-lodging; high tillering ability.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CO 56 (CB12132 / IET27408 / IET 25531), rice

NAME NOTE: No Seednet (seednet.gov.in) page was returned by any search, so the seednet_variety_name "CO 56 (CB12132(IET27408& IET 25531)" is unverified. The evidence below refers to the release-minute name as it appears in press coverage of the notification, and to "CO 56" on TNAU pages. Both are the same variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Moderately resistant to stem borer, gall midge, blast, bacterial leaf blight, brown spot, sheath rot, sheath blight, rice tungro disease and glume discoloration -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CO%2056.html
Non-lodging with high tillering ability (TNAU release list, 2023) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/New%20Varieties%20&%20Technologies%202023-15.02.2023%20-%20English-Final%20(1)%20(1).pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for CO 56 specifically. A TNAU release table contains "Drought tolerant; Non lodging", but the row is not clearly attributable to CO 56, so it is not recorded here -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/pdf/TNAU%20Variety%20release%20-%20Eng.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderately resistant to multiple diseases and to stem borer and gall midge (TNAU release list, 2023) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/New%20Varieties%20&%20Technologies%202023-15.02.2023%20-%20English-Final%20(1)%20(1).pdf
Moderate resistance to MR-BL, BLB, RTD, BS and SB is listed in an AICRPR trial table row for CO 56 -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Duration 135-140 days; season Late Samba / Thaladi; average grain yield 6372 kg/ha -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CO%2056.html
Duration 130-135 days; yield 6372 kg/ha; medium slender white rice, milling 67%, head rice recovery 64.1%; over 350 grains per panicle -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/New%20Varieties%20&%20Technologies%202023-15.02.2023%20-%20English-Final%20(1)%20(1).pdf
Medium-tall, non-lodging, high-yielding (TNAU technology list) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/cpbg/rice-technologies-developed/
Entry in AICRPR trial table, with the notes "rainfed condition" and IRM/MS scores of 6.3 -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf
Note: the TNAU lists give 135-140 days and 130-135 days; both are recorded above.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage per TNAU: CO (R)50 / CB 05501 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CO%2056.html
Parentage per the request record (CB 01001/CB 05501 derivative, Kharif 2007, F5 stabilised) is not confirmed by any source found; the TNAU parentage differs and should be reconciled.
CB12132 is a strong general combiner for filled grains per panicle and a useful donor for panicle traits; this is a study of the parent line, not of CO 56 -- https://www.mdpi.com/2223-7747/12/2/250
QTL/marker studies on CO 56: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), Coimbatore; the Department of Rice is the responsible unit -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/cpbg/rice-technologies-developed/
Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found in any source searched.
Release notification: Central Seed Committee, notified 25 September 2023 by Joint Secretary Pankaj Yadav, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-106-new-varieties-of-31-major-crops-for-farmers/
Open-pollinated variety, recommended for sale in Tamil Nadu -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/rice-variety-co-56-cb12132iet27408-iet-25531/
Date conflict: the record's year_of_release is 2023-05-02, but the notification date is 25 September 2023. The notification date is recorded here.

CONTACT DETAILS

Professor and Head, Department of Rice, TNAU, Coimbatore 641 003; phone 0422-2474967; email rice@tnau.ac.in -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/2014/Seed_stock_position_12.2.2015_eng.pdf and https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf

PUBLICATIONS

seednet_fields.Parentage: CO (R) 49 IS A HYBRID DERIVATIVE OF THE CROSS C 20/RNR 52147 EFFECTED DURING KHARIF 1996 AND STABILIZED IN F 4GENERATION DURING KHARIF 1999.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: IRRIGATED CONDITION AS A TRANSPLANTED CROP IN LATE SAMBA/ THALADI SEASON ( SEPT. - OCT. SOWING)
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: CO (R) 49 (CB 99019) WAS EVALUATED UNDER SRI SYSTEM OF RICE CULTIVATION IN RABI 2006--07 AT COIMBATORE. THE CULTURE RECORDED HIGHER GRAIN YIELD UNDER SRI THAN THE NORMAL METHOD AND ALSO OVER THE CHECK VARIETY, BPT 5204. NON LODGING NON SHATTERING HIGH TILLERING ABILITY SUITABLE FOR LATE SAMBA AND THALADI SEASON (SEP-OCT SOWING) AS TRANSPLANTED CROP IN TAMIL NADU. THE REICE VARIETY CO (R) 49 HAS MEDIUM SLENDER WHITE GRAIN TYPE WITH GOOD MILLING PERCENTAGE (72.3%) AND HEAD RICE. THIS VARIETY POSSESSES INTERMEDIATE AMYLOSE AND INTERMEDIATE GELATINIZATION TEMPERATURE WHICH ARE THE DESIRABLE TRAITS FOR GOOD COOKING QUALITY.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: 1. EXERTED DROOPY COMPACT PANICLES 2. MEDIUM SLENDER WHITE RICE
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 85-90 CM, GOOD EARLY PLANT VIGOUR : GREEN, COLEOPTILE : GREEN, BASAL LEAF SHEATH COLOUR : GREEN, LEAF BLADE COLOUR: GREEN, LEAF PUBESCENCE INTERMEDIATE, LEAF LENGTH : 45.0 CM (+ 5.0 MM) LEAF WIDTH : 1.50 CM  (+ 0.2 MM) DAYS TO 50% FLOWERING : 100-105 DAYS PANICLE EXERTION : WELL-EXERTED PANICLE  DAYS TO MATURITY (DAYS) : 135  DAYS SEED ACOAT (KERNEL ) COLOUR : WHITE 1000 GRAIN WEIGHT (G) 15.9, GRAIN MEDIUM SLENDER RICE GRADE : MEDIUM SLENDER MILLED RICE COLOUR : WHITE ABDOMINAL WHITE : OCCASIONALLY PRESENT
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: ABIOTIC -NOT TESTED BIOTIC- REACTION TO PESTS AND DISEASES FURNISHED IN PARA 12 (A) AND 12 (B)
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: THE CULTURE CB 99019 WAS SCREENED AGAINST ALL THE FIVE EPIDEMIC DISEASES VIZ., BLAST, BACTERIAL BLIGHT, SHEATH ROT, SHEATH LIGHT AND RICE TUNGRO DISEASE (RTD) UNDER ARTIFICIALLY INOCULATED CONDITIONS DURING 2004-05,2005-06 AND 2007 -08. THE CULTURE CB 99019 IS FOUND TO BE MODERATELY RESISTANT TO BLAST (5), BACTERIAL LEAF BLIGHT (5) AS AGAINST BPT 5204 (7&9)
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: THE CULTURE CB 99019 WAS EVALUATED FOR THREE YEARS (2005-08 ) AT COIMBATORE, MADURAI ANDADUTHURAI AGAINST THE MAJOR PESTS AND WAS FOUND TO BE MODERATELY RESISTANT TO YELLOW STEM BORER (3), GLH (3) AS AGAINST BT 5204 (7&9)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CO(R) 49 (Seednet name CO(R)49), Rice (Paddy)

NAME NOTE: Every finding below refers to the variety written "CO(R) 49" (Seednet spelling "CO(R)49"). Both spellings refer to the same release, and the retrieved sources also give the breeding line code CB 99019.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to CO(R) 49. -- No specific URL (search 1 and 3 returned none).

DISEASE AND PEST
- The MASU paper says the variety was screened against sheath rot, sheath blight and rice tungro disease, but the retrieved text does not give the resistance or susceptibility scores. -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-4-6-237-239.pdf
- No evidence found for blast, BPH or other pest reactions specific to CO(R) 49.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Described as a semi-dwarf, non-lodging, erect plant type that matures in about 135 days. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/280319446_COR_49_A_High_Yielding_Medium_Duration_Fine_Grain_Rice_Variety_for_Tamil_Nadu (abstract text also at https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-4-6-237-239.pdf)
- Grain quality: intermediate amylose (about 23.25%), soft gel consistency, moderate gelatinization temperature. -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-4-6-237-239.pdf
- Released as an alternative to BPT 5204 in 2008. -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-4-6-237-239.pdf
- Yield: no absolute kg/ha value for CO(R) 49 was retrieved. A comparator page reports that the TNAU hybrid CO 4 (7327 kg/ha) gave 14.5% more than CO(R) 49. Back-calculated, that implies about 6,400 kg/ha for CO(R) 49. This is my derivation, not a reported figure. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/394594784_TNAU_Rice_Hybrid_CO4_a_A_New_Fine_Grain_Rice_Hybrid
- Multi-location or AICRP trial data: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: derivative of the cross C 20 / RNR 52147. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/280319446_COR_49_A_High_Yielding_Medium_Duration_Fine_Grain_Rice_Variety_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Breeding line code: CB 99019 (medium duration culture). -- https://researchgate.net/publication/280319446_COR_49_A_High_Yielding_Medium_Duration_Fine_Grain_Rice_Variety_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Parentage and stabilisation timing (cross in kharif 1996, F4 stabilised in kharif 1999) come from the supplied record, not from a retrieved source. -- Input record only
- Breeding method (pedigree or single-seed descent) is not stated in the retrieved text.
- QTL, marker, gene and genome resource studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), Department of Rice, Coimbatore (Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics). -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/cpbg/rice-technologies-developed/ ; https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/cpbg/rice
- The TNAU Rice Technologies page lists CO (R)49 with parentage C20 x ... and notes it is protected under PPV&FRA. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/cpbg/rice-technologies-developed/
- Named authors of the release paper: R. Rabindran, S. Suresh, Subbalakshmi (the rest of the author list was not retrieved). Their specific roles as breeder are not stated in the retrieved text. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/280319446_COR_49_A_High_Yielding_Medium_Duration_Fine_Grain_Rice_Variety_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Breeder of record for CO(R) 49: No evidence found. The TNAU June 2012 newsletter names other rice staff (Dr. K. Nagarajan, Dr. S. Somasundaram), but it does not link them to this variety, so they are not attributed here. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/2012tnaupubln/june2012.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level only: Department of Rice / Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore. -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/cpbg/rice
- Email, phone and postal address: No evidence found in retrieved results.
- Named breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Rabindran R, Suresh S, Subbalakshmi et al. (year not shown in retrieved text). CO(R) 49: A High Yielding Medium Duration Fine Grain Rice Variety for Tamil Nadu. Madras Agricultural Journal (MASU archive, vol. 99, issues 4-6, pp. 237-239; year not confirmed) -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-4-6-237-239.pdf ; ResearchGate record: https://researchgate.net/publication/280319446_COR_49_A_High_Yielding_Medium_Duration_Fine_Grain_Rice_Variety_for_Tamil_Nadu
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR reports and other peer-reviewed papers on CO(R) 49: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet portal entry for CO(R)49: No evidence found (no Seednet page was retrieved).
- TNAU Seed Centre stock position reports exist (2015 and 2016), but the retrieved text did not show a CO(R) 49 line. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/2014/Seed_stock_position_12.2.2015_eng.pdf ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%20%2004.7.2016%20Final.pdf
- NSC, state corporation, KVK and private dealer listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Released for Tamil Nadu. The input record says "Not specified", so this is evidence the record should be updated. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/280319446_COR_49_A_High_Yielding_Medium_Duration_Fine_Grain_Rice_Variety_for_Tamil_Nadu

NOTES
- Searches run: four web searches returned results (CO(R) 49 variety; breeder/institute; research paper; Seednet/seed availability). A fifth search was blocked by the tool's usage limit, so the planned stress, contact and trial follow-ups were not run.
- Every finding above is from the release paper, TNAU pages, or the seed stock PDFs. Nothing was attributed to CO(R) 49 from a similarly named variety (CO 4, CO(R) 50, WGL 32100 or BPT 5204).

seednet_fields.Parentage: CB 01001 IS A DERIVATIVE OF THE CROSS CO 43/ADT 38, EFFECTED DURING KHARIF 1999 AND STABILIZED IN F4 GENERATION DURING KHARIF 2001
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: RECOMMENDED FOR RELEASE AND CULTIVATION IN THE STATES OF TAMIL NADU, KARNATAKA AND ANDHRA PRADESH UNDER IRRIGATED CONDITION AS A TRANSPLANTED CROP IN RABI SEASON. MATURITY 130-135 DAYS. AVERAGE YIELDS 5446 KGS/HA T
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: CB 01001 WAS EVALUATED UNDER AICRIP - IRRIGATED TRANSPLANTED LOW LAND RICE ECOSYSTEM. THE CULTURE RECORDED HIGHER GRAIN YIELD OF 8.06 T/HA WITH HIGHER NUMBER OF PANICLES /M2 (349) AND PANICLE WEIGHT OF 3.15 GRAM WHILE THE ALL INDIA CHECK JAYA RECORDED 4.36 T.HA GRAIN YIELD . 326 PANICLES/M2 AND PANICLE WEIGHT 2.67 GRAMS. NDR 359 (AN ALL INDIA CHECK VARIETY GIVEN AS COMPARISON FOR IET ENTRIES) ALSO RECORDED LOWER GRAIN YIELD OF 4.03 T/HA THE CULTURE IET 19321 HAD GOOD NITROGEN RESPONSE OF 15.10 (KGGRAIN/KG N ADDED) WHILE THE CHECKS JAYA AND NDR 359 RECORDED 2.83 AND 5.17 N RESPONSE RESPECTIVELY. CB 01001 WAS EVALUATED UNDER SRI SYSTEM OF CULTIVATION IN RABI 2006 -07 AT COIMBATORE. THE CULTURE RECORDED BETTER AGRONOMIC EFFICIENCY (37.3 AND 46.1% UNDER NORMAL AND SRI SYSTEMS) THE CULTURE CONFIRMS TO THE NEW PLANT TYPE ATTRIBUTES BY REGISTERING HIGHER CROP GROWTH RATE, LEAF AREA AND RELATEIV GROWTH RATE BETTER LIGHT TRANSMISSION RATIO, SPIKELET FERTILITY AND ABSOLUTE PRODUCTIVE TILLERS.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CR Dhan 206 (Gopinath) EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as an aerobic variety with tolerance to stem borer (dead heart and white ear), leaf folder, whorl maggot and rice hispa; moderately tolerant to gall midge biotype 1 -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- The 2019 NRRI list also records high tolerance to leaf folder, dead-heart stem borer and whorl maggot, and moderate tolerance to gall midge and white-ear stem borer -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- Named among 13 CRRI/NRRI varieties with high water-use efficiency -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRRI_Research-Bulletin-No-55.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for this variety. A salinity sentence on the released-varieties page is generic and not tied to this variety, so I did not attribute it.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Release list codes: "MR-LB, BS ShR, SB, LF" (3.95 t/ha). The abbreviations are not expanded on the page, so I have not interpreted them -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Specific blast or bacterial blight reaction for this variety: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release list: duration 115 days, plant height 105 cm, grain type SB -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- Yield is inconsistent across NRRI pages: 3.95 t/ha in one list, 5.0 t/ha and 5.4-6 t/ha in others. Treat as unresolved -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- An aerobic-system release summary (2015) lists CR Dhan 206 with yield around 4.2 t/ha; the figure is truncated in the snippet -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/daily_events/2015/english/Sept/14_sep_15_eng.pdf
- Field trial reports specific to this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree/variety code CR 2996-1-14-29-3-1 (IET 22731) given for CR Dhan 206 (Gopinath) in an NRRI analysis -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses
- Parentage: not stated in any source found.
- Variety-specific QTL or marker study: No evidence found. The CRRI Research Bulletin 58 covers QTLs generally and does not name this variety -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/CRRI-Research-Bulletin-58_compressed.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Rice Research Institute (now ICAR-National Rice Research Institute, NRRI), Bidyadharpur, Cuttack, Odisha -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ ; https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRRI_Research-Bulletin-No-55.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist names for this variety: No evidence found.
- Station: the variety is listed under the Cuttack headquarters, not a regional station -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level; no breeder contact found)
- Director, ICAR-Central Rice Research Institute, Cuttack 753006, Odisha. Phone +91-671-2367757/67; EPBX +91-671-2367768-783; Fax +91-671-2367663; Email directorcrricuttack@gmail.com -- https://icar-crri.in/contact-us/
- Email director.nrri@icar.org.in with phone +91 671 236 7768 and address Bidyadharpur, Cuttack, Odisha -- https://www.facebook.com/riceicar/ (third-party-hosted page)
- Email director.nrri@icar.gov.in is listed on a third-party directory with Director phone 0671-2367757 -- https://www.indiacustomercare.com/national-rice-research-institute-nrri-contact-no-0671-236-7757 (not an official ICAR page; verify before use)
- Postal address: Cuttack 753006, Odisha, India -- https://icar-crri.in/contact-us/

PUBLICATIONS
- Pathak, H.; Chidambaranathan, P. (2020). Rice Varieties of NRRI: Yield, Quality, Special Traits and Tolerance to Biotic and Abiotic Stresses. Journal/report not stated -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses
- Author not stated (2024). Recent Rice Varietal Innovations at ICAR-NRRI (2022-2024), NRRI Research Bulletin No. 55 -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRRI_Research-Bulletin-No-55.pdf
- Peer-reviewed paper, thesis or KrishiKosh record on this variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer sources for CR Dhan 206. The searches did not return a seed-sale page.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Odisha -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ ; https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf

SEEDNET NAME: CR DHAN-209
- The evidence found for "CR Dhan 209 (Priya)" refers to a different variety. It is an aerobic line released in 2016 for Odisha, with 112-115 days duration and 4.07 t/ha yield -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ . It is not CR Dhan 206 and I have not attributed any of its data to CR Dhan 206.
- No Seednet portal page for CR DHAN-209 or CR Dhan 206 was found.

NOTES
- Release year conflict: the CSC minutes date (2015-10-12) differs from the 2014 year in the ICAR-CRRI release lists. Verify against the CVRC/CSC notification.
- Name check: "Vl Dhan 206" (a Uttar Pradesh/Himalayan upland variety) and "CR Dhan 310/311" were excluded as different varieties.
- Search budget: four web searches were used, one per topic plus one extra for seed and contact.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CR Dhan 300 (CSC minutes name "CR Dhan 300"; Seednet name "CR DHAN-300")

Search coverage: 4 web_search queries were run (variety release/stress; breeder/institute/contact; research papers/QTL/trials; seed availability). No result returned under the Seednet name "CR DHAN-300", so all evidence below refers to "CR Dhan 300" (also listed as CR 2301-5, IET 19816).

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No variety-specific stress evidence found. The NRRI popular-varieties page has a stress block that appears to describe a different variety, so I did not attribute it to CR Dhan 300. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CR Dhan 203 (Sachala) -- evidence below refers to this entry. Seednet name CR DHAN-303 -- evidence below refers to a separately notified entry (see note under RECOMMENDED STATES).

STRESS TOLERANCE / DISEASE AND PEST
- Listed as an aerobic-type variety with the code CR2717-10-IR84899-B-185 (IET), tagged in the CRRI release table with moderate resistance (MR) to leaf blast and sheath-related and other listed diseases; drought/aerobic adaptation is the stated ecology -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- Highly tolerant to leaf folder, stem borer (dead heart) and whorl maggot; moderately tolerant to gall midge biotype 1 and stem borer (white ear heads) -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- The same pest reaction profile is restated in the NRRI/CRRI variety compilation, which also lists the variety under "Aerobic" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses
- Disease abbreviations in the listing (MR-LB, BS, ShR, SB) are not expanded in the source; I have not expanded them. Drought tolerance is not explicitly scored for CR Dhan 203 in the pages found -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 110 days, long slender (LS) grain, plant height 110 cm, listed yield 4.05 t/ha (release table) -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- A separate entry in the NRRI/CRRI yield table gives 5.4-6 t/ha for this line -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ (second listing in same page)
- Cluster-demonstration or on-farm trial data specific to CR Dhan 203: No evidence found. The Jharkhand field-day page covers CR Dhan 202 and CR Dhan 305 only -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/2904
- The 2021 AICRP rice research group proceedings list CR Dhan 201 and CR Dhan 202 as zonal entries, not CR Dhan 203 -- https://icar-iirr.org/56%20ARGM%20Draft%20Proceedings%202021-%202.08.2021.pdf
- Root-trait observation: one NRRI compilation records maximum root number in CR Dhan 203 (60 roots per ...), truncated in the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree as printed in the NRRI compilation: CR2717-10-IR84899-B-185 (IET IR78877/IRRI132). The pedigree string is fragmentary in the snippet; treat it as unverified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses
- Marker, QTL or MAS work on CR Dhan 203: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeder name for CR Dhan 203: No evidence found in any search result.
- Developing institution: Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI), Cuttack, Odisha, listed as the developer in the CRRI release table -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- Institutional naming: CRRI was renamed ICAR-National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) in 2015 per a secondary site; the CRRI release list is dated and the same varieties are credited to NRRI in other pages -- https://testbook.com/ias-preparation/central-rice-research-institute and https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- Institution history (founded 1946, Cuttack, ICAR) -- https://icar-crri.in/directors-message/
- Research stations: Central Rainfed Upland Rice Research Station, Hazaribagh (Jharkhand) and Regional Rainfed Lowland Rice Research Station, Gerua (Assam) -- https://arch-india.org/institution/central-rice-research-institute
- Industry demand: CR Dhan 203 was among the top ten indented varieties in 2022-23 -- https://icar-crri.in/major-achievements/

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found: No evidence found.
- Institute contact page, official email, phone or postal address for ICAR-CRRI/NRRI Cuttack: No evidence found in search results. The institute website appears as https://icar-crri.in/ (site pages returned; no contact page captured). The NRRI site is https://icar-nrri.in/.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not identified. (2020). Rice Varieties of NRRI: Yield, Quality, Special Traits and Tolerance to Biotic and Abiotic Stresses. Compilation/ResearchGate PDF (affiliation: Central Rice Research Institute) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339527323_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI_Yield_Quality_Special_Traits_and_Tolerance_to_Biotic_and_Abiotic_Stresses
- ICAR-CRRI, Cuttack (2025). CRRI varieties 1968-2024 (release list incl. CR Dhan 203). ICAR-CRRI report -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Peer-reviewed paper, thesis or KrishiKosh entry specific to CR Dhan 203: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No seed dealer, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU listing for CR Dhan 203 found: No evidence found.
- Seednet portal entry: No evidence found for CR DHAN-303 or CR Dhan 203 on seednet.gov.in in these searches.
- Search results for paddy seeds from dealers (IndiaMart, Flipkart, BigHaat, Krushidukan) were for other hybrid or basmati products and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Odisha, per the CRRI release list for CR Dhan 203 -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
- Release year: the release table lists 2014 for CR Dhan 203, which differs from the 2015-10-12 year in the CSC record. Not reconciled. No gazette notification for CR Dhan 203 was found; the 2014 gazette found is for CR Dhan 303.
- CR DHAN-303 (Seednet name) -- evidence refers to a different, separately notified entry, not CR Dhan 203: CR Dhan 303 (CR 2649-7, IET 21589), notified 2014 (S.O. 1146(E), 25.04.2014) for Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Odisha -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm. It is an irrigated, 125-day semi-dwarf variety from Udaya x IET 16611, with 5.0-6.0 t/ha yield and moderate resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, sheath rot and tungro -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/ and https://www.academia.edu/118613495/Production_Technology_for_rice_variety_CR_Dhan_303. These pages do not match the CR Dhan 203 (Sachala) code, parentage, ecology or duration, so they are not attributed to this record.
