search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CR Dhan 326 (Panchatatva) / CR Dhan 326  (Panchatatva)

Name note: The CSC release minute name is "CR Dhan 326 (Panchatatva)". The Seednet name is "CR Dhan 326  (Panchatatva)" with a double space. Every source below refers to the same variety under the single-space form. No source under either name gave a different variety.

Search coverage: 4 web_search queries were run: (1) variety/release/traits, (2) breeder/institution/contact, (3) research papers, (4) seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The CRRI variety table lists the line as irrigated, with an average yield of 6.2 t/ha and a duration of about 135–140 days. -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- A Springer paper reports that a non-lodging semi-tall recombinant line, carrying the Xa4, xa5, Xa7, xa13, Xa21 and SD1 combination, out-yielded both parents and the check genotypes in blind multilocation trials before release. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-026-01633-0
- The same paper notes that the Xa4 gene reduced lodging in the semi-dwarf and taller lines. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-026-01633-0
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The CRRI table lists bacterial blight resistance from the Xa4, xa5, Xa7, xa13 and Xa21 genes. -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- A pathotyping study reports that no tested Xoo isolates were virulent on IRBB66, which carries that five-gene set. This is background on the donor, not a field test of CR Dhan 326. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261440548_Pathotyping_and_genetic_screening_of_type_III_effectors_in_Indian_strains_of_Xanthomonas_oryzae_pv_oryzae_causing_bacterial_leaf_blight_of_rice
- No evidence found for blast, sheath blight, brown planthopper, gall midge or other pest resistance specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The release was notified for sale in Odisha as an open-pollinated variety. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/rice-variety-cr-dhan-326-panchatatva/
- The CRRI table gives an average yield of 6.2 t/ha. -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- The Springer paper reports blind multilocation trials as the basis for release. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-026-01633-0
- No evidence found for plot-level agronomic data (seed rate, fertiliser, transplanting date) or farmer-field trial numbers.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: five bacterial blight genes were pyramided into Naveen using IRBB66 as donor. The released line is a recombinant with the Xa4 + xa5 + Xa7 + xa13 + Xa21 + SD1 combination, not a simple Naveen/IRBB66 cross. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-026-01633-0
- The Springer paper confirms the SD1 allele by molecular profiling in Naveen and its lines. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-026-01633-0
- The same paper reports that Xa4 was the gene that improved lodging resistance in the lines. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-026-01633-0
- The Naveen/IRBB66 pyramiding also appears in a second record of the same work. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335183114_Assessing_area_production_and_return_with_rice_varieties_of_NRRI_Cuttack
- The Springer paper's acknowledgements list IRRI as the source of the IRBB66 seed. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-026-01633-0

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The CRRI variety table lists CR Dhan 326 among "Rice varieties developed by ICAR-CRRI, Cuttack." This conflicts with the institution in the record, which is ICAR-National Rice Research Institute. -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- The Springer paper's acknowledgements name S. K. Dash of CRRI for SNP genotyping support. This suggests a CRRI-led programme, but no breeder name is stated as lead. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-026-01633-0
- No evidence found for a named lead breeder, the developing station, or the institutional role of the breeder.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. None of the four searches retrieved a breeder name, official email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for ICAR-NRRI, Cuttack or ICAR-CRRI, Cuttack. The ICAR-CRRI variety PDF is the only institute-owned source retrieved, and it contains no contact details. Contact details should be taken from icar-nrri.in and icar-crri.in directly.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured in retrieved snippet (2026?). Multi-dimensional trait improvement of two unique semi-dwarf Indica rice varieties through combinatorial introgression of five bacterial blight resistance genes and sd1 alleles. Molecular Breeding -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-026-01633-0 ; DOI 10.1007/s11032-026-01633-0 ; PubMed mirror: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41658220/
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report entry, or conference paper specific to CR Dhan 326 was found in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for CR Dhan 326 seed stocks at the Odisha State Seeds Corporation (ORISEED). The OSSC availability page was retrieved, but its variety table did not appear in the search result. -- https://ossc.nic.in/Marketing/AvailabilityofSeeds
- No evidence found for Seednet, NSC, KVK or SAU seed sales or private dealers for this variety.
- Context only: a 2025 IRRI/Odisha article notes that seed availability for specialty varieties is scarce in the state. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/ag-tech-research-news/enhancing-decentralized-seed-production-of-healthier-rice-in-odisha/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Odisha. The notification was dated 25 September 2023 (Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, after Central Seed Committee consultation). -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/rice-variety-cr-dhan-326-panchatatva/
- Date discrepancy: the record's year_of_release is 2 May 2023, but the notification date is 25 September 2023. Please check the CSC minutes.
- The CRRI table lists the recommended state as Odisha. -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CR Dhan 701 (seednet name: CR DHAN 701 (IET 20852)(CRHR32); CSC name: CR Dhan 701)

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Search 1 ("CR Dhan 701 Rice variety") returned an ICAR page on a CRRI award (https://icar.org.in/index.php/en/node/8349) and no text naming this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No search result mentioned this variety's resistance profile.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Search 3 returned a 2024 paper on DRR Dhan 70 (IET 29415), an aerobic rice variety from ICAR-IIRR (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382618016_DRR_Dhan_70-_IET_29415_-_An_Aerobic_Rice_Variety). That is a different variety, so it is discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The only parentage in the record, CRMS 31A/CRL 22, is from the input record and was not confirmed by any search result. The breeding-line code IET 20852 and CRHR-32 also appeared only in the input record.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a named breeder. Search 2 returned a ResearchGate article on the National Rice Research Institute (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381732577_ROLE_OF_NATIONAL_RICE_RESEARCH_INSTITUTE_NRRI_IN_AGRICULTURAL_DEVELOPMENT). It lists CR Dhan 200 (Pyari) and CR Dhan 201 but not CR Dhan 701, so it is discarded for this variety. The institution named in the input record is Central Rice Research Institute, Cuttack, which I could not verify from search.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder or institute contact details were returned. I have not supplied any email, phone or address from memory.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming this variety was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The search returned an ICAR-CRRI MoU with Bioseed Research India (http://icar.org.in/en/node/7494). It concerns commercial licensing of CRRI technologies and does not name CR Dhan 701, so it is not counted.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Not verified by search. The input record gives Bihar and Gujarat. Treat this as unconfirmed input data.

NOTES ON METHOD
- I ran four searches, one per topic. I then attempted a fifth call to re-check the full page text for "701", "IET 20852" and "CRHR-32". The tool's usage limit stopped that call, so the full-page check was not completed.
- The findings above rest on the search snippets (roughly the first 300 characters of each result). A mention of this variety further down a page would not have been seen. Treat the "No evidence found" entries as provisional.
- The name CR Dhan 701 and the seednet name were searched in the same queries, so no separate evidence was found under either name.
- Recommended next steps: check the CSC release notification for CR Dhan 701, search the Seednet portal directly, and check KrishiKosh and the CRRI publications list for IET 20852 or CRHR 32.

drought.details: CR Dhan 801 is recognized as a multiple stress-tolerant variety, specifically tolerant to drought. It is listed among popular drought-tolerant rice varieties in India and exhibits resilience to water scarcity. Marker-aided qDTY pyramiding has been successfully applied in this variety for enhanced drought tolerance.

heat.details: While CR Dhan 801 is classified as a 'Climate Change-Ready' variety, and high temperature is mentioned as a general stress, there is no direct evidence specifying its inherent heat tolerance level in the provided search results.

salinity.details: CR Dhan 801 is listed as a climate change-ready rice variety with indicated tolerance to salinity stress.

flood.details: CR Dhan 801 is explicitly described as a flood-tolerant rice variety and a climate-smart variety tolerant to both drought and flooding stresses. It has been successfully adopted by farmers in flood-prone regions like Assam.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to brown spot and blast.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to yellow stem borer and leaf folder.

agronomic_details.yield: Performance studies indicate superiority in growth parameters, yield attributes, and economic viability. Marker-aided qDTY pyramiding in CR Dhan 801 has shown significantly improved performance.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly mentioned as 'stable' but its wide recommendation and popularity imply good performance across target environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for shallow lowland, submergence, and drought-prone areas. It is suitable for rainfed shallow lowland conditions and is categorized as a 'climate-smart' rice variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified in the provided search results.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials have been conducted in regions like Dibrugarh district of Assam, demonstrating good performance and resilience to water scarcity.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Drought tolerant QTLs: qDTY1.1, qDTY2.1, and qDTY3. Submergence tolerance conferred by Sub1 loci.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Marker-aided pyramiding of qDTY QTLs has been used to introduce drought tolerance into CR Dhan 801. The Sub1 loci, which provide submergence tolerance, have been introgressed into the variety through marker-assisted breeding. This breeding approach has also contributed to tolerance for anaerobic germination.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Introgression of specific genes/loci like Sub1 for submergence tolerance and unidentified genes/mechanisms associated with qDTY QTLs for drought tolerance.

drought.details: CR Dhan 802 is highly tolerant to drought and was developed to combat multiple stresses. Under drought stress conditions, it showed a 27.38% higher grain yield compared to other varieties and yielded 2344 kg/ha.

heat.details: The variety is explicitly described as heat resistant and possessing heat stress tolerance.

salinity.details: CR Dhan 802 is listed among salinity tolerant rice varieties.

flood.details: The variety is listed among flood tolerant rice varieties.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to leaf blast, glume discoloration, brown spot, and rice tungro virus disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant to stem borer.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield is 6508 kg/ha under normal conditions. Under drought stress, it yields 2344 kg/ha. It shows a higher grain yield under normal conditions (8.21% higher), submergence stress (3.06% higher), and significantly higher under drought stress (27.38% higher) compared to checks.
agronomic_details.stability: Described as a 'climate-smart' variety developed to combat multiple stresses, implying stability across varying environmental challenges.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for rainfed shallow lowland areas, particularly those prone to submergence and drought.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 140-145 days (specifically 142 days reported in multiple sources)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Weakly photosensitive with a late maturity duration. It possesses short bold grain with intermediate amylose content and a test weight of 19g. The base of the variety is purple in color and the seed is apiculous. It is non-lodging.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials have been conducted under normal, drought, and submergence stress conditions, including comparisons against Swarna Sub1 for submergence tolerance. Data from these trials supports its stress-tolerant performance.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: QTLs introgressed for improved traits include qSub1 for submergence tolerance, and qDTY1.1, qDTY2.1, and qDTY3.1 for drought tolerance/drought yield.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: The variety has been developed through genomic-assisted breeding, specifically through the introgression of identified QTLs for stress tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: QTL introgression for specific stress tolerance traits.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CR Dhan 802 (rice)

Search note: The four searches ran in one batch. A follow-up attempt to open the full pages hit the tool-use limit, so I could only review the truncated snippets. Any "No evidence found" line below means the snippets I saw had nothing on that topic, not that the full pages were checked.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Snippets list CR Dhan 802 under drought tolerance, alongside Sahbhagi Dhan, Swarna Shreya and CR Dhan 80 -- https://issca.icrisat.org/scalable-solutions/high-yielding-climate-resilient-and-nutritious-rice-varieties
STRESS TOLERANCE: Described as a climate-smart variety meant to address abiotic and biotic stresses; the page links these stresses to about half of India's rice area -- https://www.academia.edu/113528689/CR_Dhan_801_and_CR_Dhan_802_Climate_Smart_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI
STRESS TOLERANCE: Flood, salinity and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for CR Dhan 802 in the snippets reviewed (the ISSCA page names flood-tolerant varieties, but not CR Dhan 802).

DISEASE AND PEST: Reported resistance to stem borer, leaf folder, plant hoppers and case worm, with moderate resistance to bacterial blight -- https://www.academia.edu/113528689/CR_Dhan_801_and_CR_Dhan_802_Climate_Smart_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI
DISEASE AND PEST: Blast, sheath blight and other pathogens: No evidence found in the snippets reviewed.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Maturity duration, yield, plant height and trial data: No evidence found in the snippets reviewed. The academia.edu document appears to compare grain quality with its parent Swarna, but I did not see the full text.

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage is not specified in the CSC record. The academia.edu document appears to treat Swarna as the parent for comparison (a snippet asks about grain quality relative to Swarna), but this is not confirmed as parentage -- https://www.academia.edu/113528689/CR_Dhan_801_and_CR_Dhan_802_Climate_Smart_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI
GENETICS AND QTL: QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The document title attributes CR Dhan 801 and CR Dhan 802 to NRRI (National Rice Research Institute). Lead breeder names: No evidence found in the snippets reviewed -- https://www.academia.edu/113528689/CR_Dhan_801_and_CR_Dhan_802_Climate_Smart_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The CSC record says "ICAR-National Research Institute" without naming the station. Station and developing division: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder, email, phone or postal address found in the snippets reviewed. Institute contact page: not retrieved in this session.

PUBLICATIONS: Academia.edu (2023 or later, year not confirmed). CR Dhan 801 and CR Dhan 802 Climate-Smart Rice Varieties of NRRI. Authors: not seen in the snippet. Source: academia.edu -- https://www.academia.edu/113528689/CR_Dhan_801_and_CR_Dhan_802_Climate_Smart_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI
PUBLICATIONS: Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found in the searches run.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing appeared in the snippets. The Seednet portal was not returned by any search, so the Seednet name "CR Dhan 802" was not confirmed on that portal.

RECOMMENDED STATES: The CSC record gives Assam. No independent confirmation was found in the snippets reviewed.

Name check: Both the CSC name ("CR Dhan 802") and the Seednet name ("CR Dhan 802") were searched. The evidence above refers to "CR Dhan 802" as written; no page distinguished the two names.

Release year 2022 (CSC record): not confirmed by any snippet.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance evidence found for IET 29203 for blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight or gall midge. The Naveen-background bacterial blight, blast and gall midge work concerns parent Naveen, not this variety, and is not attributed to CR Dhan 805. The variety record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: Brown planthopper (BPH) resistance is the documented trait. The IIRR 2023 annual report lists the reaction as BPH resistant with the Odisha recommendation. The CRRI list tags the variety as BPH resistant. Antixenosis and tolerance were studied with CR-3006-8-2, CR-805 and Salkathi as entries, and BPH nymphs could not suck phloem sap from this variety. At a BPH hotspot, the BPH count was about 33 per 10 hills in IET 29203 versus 85 in Naveen. No evidence found for other pests.

agronomic_details.yield: Variety record gives an average yield of 5000.00 to 6000.00 kg/ha. The digest reports a farmer-trial range of 3.85 to 7.28 t/ha with a 5.45 t/ha average over 66 farmer trials, but attribution to this variety alone is unconfirmed. Naveen-background trial yield values are not legible in the extracted text and are not used as confirmed.
agronomic_details.stability: Yield was tested repeatedly only in Odisha. No multi-environment stability statistics found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated medium early situations (variety record). Recommended for Odisha. Ecology figures of 125 to 130 days are given in the CRRI list, though column labels are unclear in the extracted text.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf. Fertilizer responsive. Seed rate 40 kg/ha (variety record). Morphological characteristics: Not specified in variety record.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) BPH hotspot: BPH count about 33 per 10 hills in IET 29203 versus 85 in Naveen. (2) Salkathi donor hotspot: 23.80% higher yield than Naveen over two years. (3) Multi-location testing: IET 29203 was nominated into national blind multi-location AICRIP trials, but its yield was tested repeatedly only in Odisha. (4) Trial entry: IET 29203 was among NIL entries promoted for testing in 2021 (32 entries). (5) Farmer trials: 66 farmer trials with a 3.85 to 7.28 t/ha range and 5.45 t/ha average, attribution to this variety unconfirmed. (6) Naveen-background 2023 AICRPR trial summary in Odisha: values not legible, not used.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Pedigree: Naveen*3 / CR 3006-8-2. The variety is derived from a Naveen x CR-3006-8-2 cross (Salkathi-derived line). Marker positions for this variety: Not found in searched sources. Parent background only (Naveen, not attributed to this variety): Pi9, Xa21, Gm8, qDTY1.1, qDTY2.2 and qDTY4.1 introgressed by MAS.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: qBph4.3 and qBph4.4 are listed for CR Dhan 805 (BPH resistance). QTL effect sizes and positions for this variety: Not found in searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: BPH antixenosis and tolerance mechanisms were studied in this variety's background. Specific genes or pathways for IET 29203: Not found in searched sources.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not found in searched sources (no NSC or State Seed Corporation sales evidence for this variety). Breeder seed: NRRI breeder-seed indent for its varieties reported as 215 quintals for 2024 kharif, not broken down by variety.
commercial_info.private_dealers: Not found in searched sources. Seed-related hits such as 'Shakti seed Taj' are unrelated products and must not be attributed to this variety.

CR DHAN 805 (Naveen Shakti) [IET 29203] -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The CSC/notification list uses "CR Dhan 805 (Naveen Shakti)[IET 29203]", and the bracketed form appears in the same list. I did not retrieve a Seednet portal page, so the evidence below is for the CSC/notification name, with the Seednet name unverified. Release-year note: the record field says 2023-05-02, but the notification in the sources is dated 25 September 2023. Both are reported below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- BPH resistance is the documented trait. The ICAR-CRRI list tags the variety as BPH resistant and links it to QTLs qBph4.3 and qBph4.4 -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- BPH nymphs could not suck the phloem sap from this variety, and antixenosis and tolerance mechanisms were studied with CR-3006-8-2, CR-805 and Salkathi as entries. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383359418_BROWN_PLANTHOPPER_RESISTANT_RICE_A_JOURNEY_FROM_LANDRACES_TO_VARIETIES
- At the BPH hotspot, the BPH count was about 33 per 10 hills in IET 29203 versus 85 in Naveen -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391725005_Combining_host_plant_resistance_and_herbicide_tolerance_for_integrated_management_of_brown_planthopper_and_weed_complexes_in_direct_seeded_rice
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for this variety in the retrieved sources.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The IIRR 2023 annual report lists the variety's reaction as BPH resistant, with the Odisha recommendation -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf
- Blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight and gall midge reactions: No evidence found specific to IET 29203 (the Naveen-background BB/blast/gall midge work is on parent Naveen, see GENETICS).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Ecology and duration: The CRRI list gives irrigated ecology and duration figures of 125 and 130 days, but the column labels are not clear in the extracted text -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Yield: The 2023 Naveen-background trial summary reports Naveen Shakti means over three AICRPR years in Odisha, but the extracted table values are not legible. Do not use a yield figure from the retrieved text as confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391725005_Combining_host_plant_resistance_and_herbicide_tolerance_for_integrated_management_of_brown_planthopper_and_weed_complexes_in_direct_seeded_rice
- Farmer-trial range: One source reports 3.85 to 7.28 t/ha with a 5.45 t/ha average over 66 farmer trials, in a BPH-resistance paper that mentions CR Dhan 805. Attribution to this variety alone is unconfirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383359418_BROWN_PLANTHOPPER_RESISTANT_RICE_A_JOURNEY_FROM_LANDRACES_TO_VARIETIES
- Multi-location testing: IET 29203 was nominated into national blind multi-location AICRIP trials, and its yield was tested repeatedly only in Odisha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391725005_Combining_host_plant_resistance_and_herbicide_tolerance_for_integrated_management_of_brown_planthopper_and_weed_complexes_in_direct_seeded_rice
- Hotspot yield: The source reports 23.80% higher yield than Naveen over two years at the Salkathi donor hotspot -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391725005_Combining_host_plant_resistance_and_herbicide_tolerance_for_integrated_management_of_brown_planthopper_and_weed_complexes_in_direct_seeded_rice
- Trial entry: IET 29203 was among NIL entries promoted for testing in 2021 (32 entries) -- https://icar-iirr.org/56%20ARGM%20Draft%20Proceedings%202021-%202.08.2021.pdf
- Breeder-seed context: NRRI's biotic-stress varieties, which include CR Dhan 805, are notified for stress-prone zones -- https://icar-crri.in/major-achievements/

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: Naveen*3 / CR 3006-8-2 is listed in the IIRR 2023 annual report -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf
- Derivation: The variety is a derivative of a Naveen x CR-3006-8-2 cross (Salkathi-derived line) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383359418_BROWN_PLANTHOPPER_RESISTANT_RICE_A_JOURNEY_FROM_LANDRACES_TO_VARIETIES
- BPH QTLs: qBph4.3 and qBph4.4 are listed for CR Dhan 805 -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Parent background (Naveen, not this variety): Pi9, Xa21, Gm8, and qDTY1.1, qDTY2.2 and qDTY4.1 were introgressed into Naveen by MAS -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8412243/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder name(s): No evidence found in the retrieved sources.
- Developing institution: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack, Odisha -- https://icar-crri.in/major-achievements/ (NRRI listing, with the variety shown as released in the NRRI-developed table), and https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- Station: The variety is attributed to Cuttack; no separate station is named in the retrieved sources.
- Note: The CRRI list shows an "SVRC" release body and the notification is for Odisha only, with the Odisha state additionally releasing the popular name -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391725005_Combining_host_plant_resistance_and_herbicide_tolerance_for_integrated_management_of_brown_planthopper_and_weed_complexes_in_direct_seeded_rice

CONTACT DETAILS

- Institute contact: Director, ICAR-NRRI Cuttack, Dr. A.K. Nayak, appears in a 2024 NRRI event report -- https://icar-crri.in/nrri-rice-varieties-dedicated-to-the-nation-by-honble-prime-minister/
- Official email, phone and postal address of NRRI: No evidence found in the retrieved sources. Use the official site contact page for NRRI before recording any details.

PLoS ONE (parent-background paper; not on this variety) -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8412243/ or DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0256721

- Authors not identified (year not stated). Combining host plant resistance and herbicide tolerance for integrated management of brown planthopper and weed complexes in direct seeded rice. Journal article (ResearchGate record) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391725005_Combining_host_plant_resistance_and_herbicide_tolerance_for_integrated_management_of_brown_planthopper_and_weed_complexes_in_direct_seeded_rice
- ICAR-IIRR (2023). Annual Report 2023. ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf
- ICAR-CRRI (2025). Rice varieties/hybrids developed during 1968 to 2025 -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/CRRIs-varieties-1968-2024.pdf
- AICRP on Rice (2023-24). 59th Agronomy Technical Programme, lists IET 29203 -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/AICRIP%20Agronomy%20Technical%20Programme%202023-24%20on%2026-06-2023.pdf
- Not found: KrishiKosh theses, peer-reviewed papers specific to this variety, and KVK/SAU reports.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Notification list: CR Dhan 805 is listed for sale in Odisha as an Open Pollinated Variety -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/the-government-of-india-in-consultation-with-the-central-seed-committee-has-designated-106-varieties-of-31-crops-for-cultivation-in-india/
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales, or private dealers for this variety: No evidence found. The seed-related hits were unrelated products (e.g., "Shakti seed Taj") and must not be attributed to this variety.
- Breeder seed: NRRI's breeder-seed indent for its varieties is reported as 215 quintals for 2024 kharif, but the figure is not broken down by variety -- https://icar-crri.in/major-achievements/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Odisha only: CR Dhan 805 (Naveen Shakti)[IET 29203] is an Open Pollinated Variety of rice recommended for sale in Odisha. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/rice-variety-cr-dhan-805-naveen-shaktiiet-29203/
- Notification date: 25 September 2023, issued by the Joint Secretary, MoA&FW, after CSC consultation -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/rice-variety-cr-dhan-805-naveen-shaktiiet-29203/

genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: Basmati CSR 30 (Yamini) is a material used in seedling and reproductive stage QTL mapping studies for salt tolerance. Molecular markers are utilized in breeding efforts for this variety to enhance abiotic stress tolerance.
genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: Genetic improvement and marker-assisted breeding are employed for its stress tolerance traits, including salt resistance.

agronomic_performance.yield: Evaluated in various field trials, showing varying yields (e.g., 1.08-10.92 in one trial, 0.08-2.70 in another, 0.10-7.95 in a third, with units not specified in context, likely t/ha or similar experimental units). Reported superiority in grain yield on three years mean (15.02, possibly a percentage advantage).
agronomic_performance.stability: Not specified
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Well-adapted to sodic soil conditions (pH 8.8-9.5). Suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and semi-deep water environments.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf (82 cm plant height). Grains are long slender (LS), aromatic, and extra-long slender. Head Rice Recovery (HRR) is 57.9%. Flowering duration is approximately 96 days.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: Subjected to field trials by ICAR-CSSRI and other research institutes. Screened for salinity tolerance (germination frequency), heat stress tolerance, and submergence tolerance.

stress_confirmation_note: The salinity claim of 'Basmati' release conflicts with the CSC minutes, which record notification as an ordinary rice in 2001 with the Basmati renaming still pending and its GI implications unresolved.

drought.basis: Details describe drought tolerance only as a general stress mention and rainfed suitability. No CSC statement on drought. No cited URL counted because details call it generic.
drought.label: Not confirmed

heat.basis: Details say only that the variety was included in screening and is mentioned for adaptation to rising temperature. Screening inclusion is not a tolerance statement.
heat.label: Not confirmed

salinity.basis: 15 cited URLs (PMC8519845, ICAR/CSSRI reports, biosaline, USDA, others) plus snippets: Yamini article, 'Advances in breeding salt-tolerant rice', CSSRI 'Development of Salt-Tolerant Rice Varieties', ZnO nanoparticle paper. CSC minutes do not confirm tolerance.
salinity.label: Confirmed by 2+ sources

flood.basis: Only APN-GCR Final Training Manual lists the variety among flood-resistant varieties. No CSC or other confirmation.
flood.label: Single source

submergence.basis: Nine distinct cited documents: AICRIP 2023 and 2025 proceedings, IIRR ARGM 2021 and 2023 proceedings, rice-garud varieties page, biosaline Singh 2021, PMC8519845, APN manual, TNAU 41st CSM 2022. Details attribute one-week submergence tolerance.
submergence.label: Confirmed by 2+ sources

drought.details: Identified as a short duration, drought-tolerant rice variety. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), associated with drought tolerance, has been isolated from CSR 76.

heat.details: Screened for heat stress tolerance in annual rice group meetings.

salinity.details: Released as a salt-tolerant rice variety, specifically for sodic soils, capable of tolerating sodicity up to pH ~9.6. It is also tolerant to alkalinity and water logging stresses.

flood.details: Tolerant to water logging stresses.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot, and sheath spot. Also, cold tolerant.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified

agronomic_details.yield: 65 quintals per hectare
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, semi-deep water conditions, and irrigated areas. It is a non-Basmati, short-duration variety recommended for Uttar Pradesh.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf (82 cm height). Grains are 'LS' (Long Slender). Highly tolerant to cold stress.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been evaluated and discussed in proceedings of the Annual Rice Group Meetings (AICRIP), indicating its performance in trials.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Marker Assisted Breeding (MAS) is employed in the development of abiotic stress tolerant rice varieties. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), associated with drought tolerance, has been isolated from CSR 76.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTL names or positions are provided, but development involves molecular breeding for resistance/tolerance to stress, implying focus on major genes/QTLs.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The isolation of LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) from CSR 76 indicates a molecular mechanism contributing to its drought tolerance.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
The search tool hit its usage limit partway through, so this digest is incomplete. Only one search result names this variety, and it is a list page rather than a variety record.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: CSR-52 (CSC minutes name) / CSR 22 (Seednet name), rice (paddy)

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches did not return any page that describes salinity, drought, flood or other stress tolerance for CSR-52 or CSR 22. One CSSRI result (researchgate.net/publication/257650699) covers salt-tolerant crop varieties in general, but its snippet does not name CSR-52, so I have not attributed it.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The CSSRI highlights page lists CSR 52 among twelve rice varieties released through sustained breeding at CSSRI -- https://cssri.res.in/highlights/ (the snippet was truncated, so I could not confirm the full list or the breeders named). Institution per the input record: ICAR-Central Soil Salinity Research Institute.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone or address was returned. The CSSRI highlights URL (https://cssri.res.in/highlights/) is the only institute page identified; I did not retrieve its contact page. The institute contact page should be checked directly.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, report or thesis naming CSR-52 or CSR 22 was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The Seednet query for CSR 22 returned only unrelated basmati seed-image dataset results (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33204776).

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Only the input record gives "Uttar Pradesh"; no search result confirmed it.

Other results discarded as irrelevant: a researchgate page on CO 52 (IET 25487), a different Tamil Nadu rice variety, is not CSR-52.

Gaps to close manually: verify the release date (2019-06-01 in the input), parentage (not specified), and recommended states against the CSC release notification or the Seednet portal entry for CSR 22. Seed availability should be checked with the CSSRI Karnal division and Uttar Pradesh state seed agencies.

drought.details: CSR 22 is explicitly identified as a drought-tolerant and drought-resistant variety (RESULT_8, RESULT_9, RESULT_27). It performs well under multi-stress conditions, including drought and sodic soils (RESULT_6). It has been included in screening programs for drought tolerance (RESULT_25).

heat.details: The variety exhibits heat stress tolerance (RESULT_7, RESULT_16, RESULT_49). It shows performance under high temperature and low relative humidity conditions (34°C day / 25°C night at 50% RH) (RESULT_45, RESULT_48) and contributes to yield under multi-stress conditions including heat (RESULT_6).

salinity.details: CSR 22 is consistently described as a salinity-tolerant variety (RESULT_4, RESULT_14, RESULT_23, RESULT_47) and is specifically tolerant to sodic soils with a pH ranging from 9.6 to 10.0 (RESULT_9, RESULT_15, RESULT_19, RESULT_30). It is listed among salt-tolerant rice varieties for which breeder seed is produced (RESULT_10, RESULT_24, RESULT_41). It also shows tolerance to alkalinity (RESULT_33, RESULT_35) and is considered a source of salinity tolerance (RESULT_21). While multiple sources affirm its tolerance, one source (RESULT_26, RESULT_37) noted it as 'susceptible' in a specific context.

flood.details: CSR 22 is tolerant to water logging stress (RESULT_4, RESULT_33, RESULT_35) and is mentioned in contexts related to flood-prone areas (RESULT_36).

disease_resistance.summary: CSR 22 is included in screening for leaf blast and neck blast tolerance (RESULT_7, RESULT_16), suggesting some level of resistance or its use in breeding for resistance. It is generally noted among 'resistant / moderately resistant / tolerant' rice varieties (RESULT_47).

pest_resistance.summary: CSR 22 is stated to be pest tolerant (RESULT_9, RESULT_27).

agronomic_details.yield: CSR 22 is characterized as a 'high yielding' variety (RESULT_8, RESULT_47). It demonstrates yield under multi-stress conditions, including drought, frost, heat, and sodic soils (pH 9.78) (RESULT_6). It is also reported to yield under water and soil salinity risks in farmers' fields (RESULT_28, RESULT_29).
agronomic_details.stability: The variety shows stability under diverse abiotic stresses including drought, heat, salinity, alkalinity, water logging, and cold (RESULT_6, RESULT_33, RESULT_35). Its performance in multi-stress environments and saline/sodic soils suggests broad adaptation and stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSR 22 is well-adapted to areas with saline and sodic soils (RESULT_19, RESULT_30), as well as regions prone to drought, heat, water logging, and cold stresses. Its ability to grow in challenging soils where rice normally requires good-quality irrigation (RESULT_30) indicates strong adaptation.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: 1. PANICLE EXERTION: COMPLETE 2. GRAIN TYPE LONG SLENDER (Original Data). Confirmed as a 'long slender genotype' (RESULT_4, RESULT_14, RESULT_47).
agronomic_details.field_trials: CSR 22 has been evaluated for yield under multi-stress conditions in fields (RESULT_6) and for performance under water and soil salinity risks in farmers' fields (RESULT_28, RESULT_29). It has also been included in screenings for drought, heat, and submergence tolerance at multiple centers (RESULT_25, RESULT_40).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: QTLs have been mapped for salt tolerance, involving CSR 22 (RESULT_1, RESULT_2). The variety is also implicated in Marker Assisted Breeding for abiotic stress tolerance (RESULT_12) and submergence tolerance (RESULT_38).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTL mapping for salt tolerance has been conducted (RESULT_1, RESULT_2). Specific QTLs or their effects are not detailed in the provided results, but its use in marker-assisted breeding implies utilization of identified QTLs for stress tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Organ-specific gene expression in response to salt stress and drought has been studied in the context of CSR 22 (RESULT_2).

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Specific government corporations are not named, but the Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI) has been actively producing breeder seed of CSR 22, indicating its availability for further multiplication and distribution (RESULT_10, RESULT_24, RESULT_41).
commercial_info.availability_status: Available, as breeder seed production is ongoing for this salt-tolerant variety by the CSSRI.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Chhattisgarh Bhavya Dhan (IET-29523), rice

Name note: The CSC minutes name is "Chhattisgarh Bhavya Dhan" and the Seednet name is "Chhattisgarh Bhavya Dhan (IET-29523)". The evidence below refers to the same entry, identified by the code IET 29523 in ICAR and AICRIP material. I did not find separate CSC minutes text, so I cannot confirm which name the minutes use.

Institution note: The brief names "Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur". The sources I found call the university Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur. I have used the source wording where I cite it.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for this variety. Searches returned no variety-specific data on these traits. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
- Stated in the ICAR table only as suitable for rainfed and irrigated medium-duration ecologies. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to leaf blast and gall midge. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
- No evidence found for neck blast, bacterial blight, brown spot, sheath rot or other pest reactions specific to this variety. -- searched, same source

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average grain yield of 55 q/ha and maturity of 123-133 days, as listed for rainfed and irrigated medium-duration ecology. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
- AICRIP Progress Report 2022 (Vol. 1, Varietal Improvement) lists IET 29523 as promising in Chhattisgarh in the irrigated trials section. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Progress%20Report%202022%20Vol.1%20Final%2027.04.2023.pdf
- The 58th Annual Rice Group Meeting proceedings (2023) recommended repeating IET 29523 and IET 29536 in a medium-slender grain trial. -- https://icar-iirr.org/58%20ARGM%20Final%20Draft%20Proceedings15-09-2023.pdf
- Multi-location yield data for this entry: No evidence found in the sources I retrieved.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: Not specified in the brief, and no pedigree found in any source. No evidence found for QTL or marker studies.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The 2023 ARGM draft proceedings name Dr Deepak Sharma, Head, Plant Breeding, IGKV Raipur, as chairing a breeders' session. This does not identify him as the breeder of this variety. -- https://icar-iirr.org/58%20ARGM%20Final%20Draft%20Proceedings15-09-2023.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
- Developing institution: The ICAR annual report lists the variety under the ICAR-AICRP on Rice network, and the AICRIP progress report places IET 29523 in the ICAR-IIRR irrigated trials. The Raipur Rice Research Station page describes IGKV Raipur's rice breeding history. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf ; http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf
- Station: Rice Research Station, Raipur (IGKV) is the Raipur AICRIP centre. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder email, phone and postal address: No evidence found.
- Institute-level contact page: No contact page or address for IGKV Raipur Rice Research Station appeared in the results. The AICRIP coordinating unit is ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad. Its AICRIP page is https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/41-websitelinks/255-aicprp?Itemid=258 . I did not find an email, phone or street address for it in the retrieved text, so none is recorded here.

PUBLICATIONS
- AICRIP (2023). Progress Report 2022, Vol. 1: Varietal Improvement (Rice). AICRP on Rice, ICAR-IIRR -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Progress%20Report%202022%20Vol.1%20Final%2027.04.2023.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. I searched for drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence data for CG Madhuraj Dhan-55 (Seednet name: Chhattisgarh Madhuraj Dhaan-55). The pages returned were about DRR Dhan 55, a different ICAR-IIRR aerobic variety, so I excluded them. -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-research/institue-technologies-developed?id=202 (excluded)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No disease or pest reaction was found for CG Madhuraj Dhan-55. The disease and pest ratings returned for DRR Dhan 55 belong to a different variety and were excluded. -- https://sarr.co.in/2022/07/02/drr-dhan-55-iet-26194-a-high-yielding-early-maturing-aerobic-rice-variety/ (excluded)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CG Madhuraj 55 showed significantly higher total nitrogen uptake (66.95 kg/ha) and potassium uptake (119.39 kg/ha) than the other scented and quality varieties tested. (Name: Chhattisgarh Madhuraj 55, the spelling used in this paper.) -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue1/PartD/7-8-75-324.pdf
- Among the rice varieties in the organic-production study, CG Madhuraj-55 had the longest panicle, at 25.2 cm. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/225%20ASSESSING-YIELD-PERFORMANCE,-ECONOMIC-FEASIBILITY,-AND-SOIL-HEALTH-IMPACTS-OF-TRADITIONAL-AROMATIC,-HIGH-YIELDING,-AND-FORTIFIED-RICE-VARIETIES-IN-ORGANIC-PRODUCTION-SYSTEM.pdf
- CG Madhuraj 55 achieved the highest net return (Rs 35498/ha) among the fortified rice varieties in the organic-production study. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/225%20ASSESSING-YIELD-PERFORMANCE,-ECONOMIC-FEASIBILITY,-AND-SOIL-HEALTH-IMPACTS-OF-TRADITIONAL-AROMATIC,-HIGH-YIELDING,-AND-FORTIFIED-RICE-VARIETIES-IN-ORGANIC-PRODUCTION-SYSTEM.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- The P GI value of white grain of one of the tested rice landraces of Chhattisgarh named as CGMD-55 belonging to the Gurmatiya group was lowest. This supports the landrace origin given in the parentage field. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261952234_Glycaemic_index_GI_of_an_Indian_branded_thermally_treated_basmati_rice_variety_A_multi_centric_study
- The allele in the low-pGI genotype CGMD-55 is of intermediate size, about 110-115 bp, compared with 105-110 bp for Swarna and about 122-126 bp for IR64. This is a marker-size observation only, not a QTL mapping study. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261952234_Glycaemic_index_GI_of_an_Indian_branded_thermally_treated_basmati_rice_variety_A_multi_centric_study
- CG Madhuraj-55 is listed among high-yielding and nutritionally enriched rice varieties developed in India through traditional breeding strategies. No marker or QTL data specific to this variety was found. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7585584/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No evidence found for a named breeder or lead scientist of CG Madhuraj Dhan-55. The breeder name in the ICAR-IIRR pages refers to DRR Dhan 55 and was excluded. -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety is documented as a finger millet (ragi) variety (BR-36), although the record labels it PADDY, so the crop classification is questionable and should be checked. Evidence includes drought tolerance listing and moderate blast resistance, and a yield of 34-36 q/ha. All of it comes from secondary compilations (government lists, ICAR magazine, ResearchGate review), not primary peer-reviewed research, and there is no Gujarat-specific testing. This fits 'some stress trait, but no strong citation', so the score is 50 rather than 60 or 75. Score would be unreliable for paddy decisions.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Chhattisgarh Ragi-2 (BR-36) was released in 2018 for Chhattisgarh and appears to be a finger millet variety despite the PADDY label. It matures in 115-118 days, yields 34-36 q/ha, and is listed as drought tolerant and moderately resistant to neck and finger blast. Evidence comes only from secondary compilations, with no primary studies, markers or Gujarat data.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Finger millet variety BR-36 from IGKV Raipur, released in 2018 for Chhattisgarh. Matures in 115-118 days and yields 34-36 q/ha. Parentage and morphology are not specified.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Drought tolerance and moderate neck/finger blast resistance are reported in compilations. No evidence for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, and no molecular data. Evidence quality is low.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Chhattisgarh Zinc Rice-2 (CSC name) / Chhattisgarh Zinc Rice- 2 (CGZR-2) (IET 23829) (Seednet name). Rice (Paddy). Four searches were run. Where a line says "CGZR-2", the source names CGZR-2 directly. Where a source covers the biofortified group, the line says so.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found. The four searches returned no stress-tolerance data (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) for CGZR-2 specifically. A 2016 Business Standard piece headlined "drought" concerns the zinc rice programme but does not separate out CGZR-2 in the retrieved text. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/chhattisgarh-finds-rice-variety-to-fight-malnutrition-drought-116011500347_1.html

DISEASE AND PEST
- An IGKV-linked awareness article says the biofortified varieties, including Chhattisgarh Zinc Rice-2, show resistance to disease, and better adaptability. This is a general group claim with no resistance genes, scores or trial data for CGZR-2. -- https://agriarticles.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/E-05-04-139-516-518.pdf
- The same article's CGZR-2 section describes it as a protein-enriched variety from the Plant Molecular Biology department. That description matches the Protezin release, so it is likely a copy error and should not be relied on. -- https://agriarticles.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/E-05-04-139-516-518.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CGZR-2 is described as conventional breeding and biofortification techniques in its development. The article does not give any yield or trial data. -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/india/chhattisgarh-to-launch-immune-booster-fortified-zinc-rice-for-mass-production-soon
- CGZR-2 has a thin, small grain type, and CGZR-1 has a thicker grain type. Both were offered to farmers as alternatives. -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/india/chhattisgarh-to-launch-immune-booster-fortified-zinc-rice-for-mass-production-soon
- Grain zinc is reported at 22-24 ppm for CGZR-2. Another source gives 22 ppm for CGZR-2 in a package-of-practices listing for Eastern India. -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/india/chhattisgarh-to-launch-immune-booster-fortified-zinc-rice-for-mass-production-soon ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India
- CGZR-2 is listed among biofortified varieties in a heterosis and combining-ability study of irrigated and aerobic rice. The snippet gives no CGZR-2 results. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8134482
- No yield, multi-location or aerobic-trial data for CGZR-2 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage is recorded as R 1243-1224-578-1 and the release year as 2018. This is the only parentage found and it is not the "Not specified" value in the record. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1138408/full
- The release year conflicts with the 2019 CSC year. The Frontiers table is the only source that gives the 2018 date, so the conflict is unresolved.
- IET 23829 was not confirmed in any retrieved source. The NRRI bulletin gives IET 23824 for CGZR-1, and no IET or institute ID was found for CGZR-2. -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRRI_Research-Bulletin-No-48.pdf
- The NRRI bulletin states that the high-zinc varieties, including Chhattisgarh Zinc Rice-II, were developed through backcross, pedigree and bulk-pedigree methods. This is group-level, not CGZR-2 specific. -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRRI_Research-Bulletin-No-48.pdf
- No QTL, marker, or genome-resource study naming CGZR-2 was found. An IGKV nutritional-genomics page lists the release of CGZR-1, but it does not mention CGZR-2. -- https://igkv.ac.in/xenom/about.aspx

- Girish Chandel is also listed as Vice-Chancellor of Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya and leads its nutritional-genomics laboratory. This is an institutional role, not a named breeding-line credit. -- https://igkv.ac.in/xenom/about.aspx
- The developing institution is Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur. The varieties were developed on the university's agricultural fields. -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/india/chhattisgarh-to-launch-immune-booster-fortified-zinc-rice-for-mass-production-soon
- The breeding line is attributed to the Department of Plant Molecular Biology and Biotechnology in one article. That attribution is doubtful, as noted above. -- https://agriarticles.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/E-05-04-139-516-518.pdf

disease_resistance.summary: Listed as resistant to rust, Alternaria blight and wilt (DAC oilseeds linseed listing). The IAUA news and BAU release describe the variety as resistant to multiple diseases and pests without naming them. Disease reaction ratings from artificial or natural conditions: not found for Divya specifically.

pest_resistance.summary: Listed as resistant to bud fly (DAC oilseeds linseed listing). The IAUA news and BAU release describe multiple pest resistance without naming pests.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 15.4 q/ha; potential yield 21.15 q/ha (BAU release page and IAUA news, which repeat the same figures). The DOD record yield values (39.81 kg/ha) are garbled and were not used.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Multi-location trial results: no evidence found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended states per CSC ground truth: Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh. The DOD row for Divya also lists Uttarakhand, and a conflicting DOD row lists Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, KNK and Odisha; both are unverified. The BAU/Jharkhand release context points to Jharkhand as the releasing state, which does not match the CSC state list and needs verification against CSC minutes.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 127-130 days (BAU release page). An earlier paragraph on the same page (112-120 days, 14.9 q/ha) is not clearly tied to Divya and was not used.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Oil content 39.81% with about 60% omega-3 fatty acid (BAU release page). Morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location or formal trial results found for Divya. Reported figures are the average yield (15.4 q/ha) and potential yield (21.15 q/ha) from the BAU release page and IAUA news. The ambiguous 14.9 q/ha / 112-120 day figures on the same BAU page are not attributed to Divya.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME AND CROP CHECK
Variety name used: Divya (BAU-06-03). Seednet name: DIVYA. Crop: linseed. The Seednet crop field says "PADDY (DHAN)", and no source found links Divya to paddy. Paddy and other "Divya" results were discarded: Kalash Seeds paddy Divya -- https://www.kalashseeds.com/products/paddy/divya.php ; IIRR rice Divya (1989) -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf ; Divya F1 sponge gourd -- https://www.eastwestseed.com/variety/divya-f1/
Searches run: 4 of 4. The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved, so no Seednet record was found under either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed as resistant to rust, Alternaria blight, wilt and bud fly -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Described as resistant to multiple diseases and pests (IAUA news, BAU release) -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_637852580202036105.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found for this variety. Searches returned no variety-specific source.

DISEASE AND PEST
Rust, Alternaria blight, wilt, bud fly resistance (as listed above) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Multiple disease and pest resistance (as above) -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_637852580202036105.pdf
Disease reaction ratings from artificial and natural conditions: No evidence found for Divya specifically. The AICRP linseed release table covers other linseed varieties only in the retrieved text -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Oil content 39.81% with about 60% omega-3 fatty acid, average yield 15.4 q/ha, potential yield 21.15 q/ha, maturity 127-130 days -- https://bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/
Same release page also gives an earlier paragraph (14.9 q/ha, 112-120 days) that is not clearly tied to Divya; treat as ambiguous -- https://bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/
The IAUA news repeats 15.4 q/ha average and 21.15 q/ha potential -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_637852580202036105.pdf
DOD record gives yield potential as 39.81 kg/ha and oil as "1538 (I)" / "815 (R)". These values are garbled and conflict with the BAU figures; not used -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Multi-location trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage WGL 23022/SUREKHA: No evidence found. A "Surekha" hit (IIRR rice) was discarded.
QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.
Combining ability: A diallel study names a parent "Divya" (linseed). It is not shown to be this variety, so it is excluded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331542067_Diallel_Analysis_for_Estimation_of_Combining_Ability_for_Seed_Yield_and_It's_Component_Traits_in_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Birsa Agricultural University (BAU), Ranchi; release centre listed as Kanke -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
BAU released Divya (BAU-06-03) and Priyam (BAU-2012-1) as linseed varieties -- https://bauranchi.org/achievements/
Release by the Jharkhand State Variety Release Committee, with three linseed varieties in the batch (Divya is named on the BAU release page above) -- https://bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. Searches returned no breeder name for this variety.
Mismatch note: the central DOD record and the CSC metadata give 2016, while the BAU/Jharkhand state release coverage is dated around August 2021 -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/birsa-agricultural-university

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute: Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi - 834006, Jharkhand, India -- https://bauranchi.org/contact-us/
Institute phones: +91-651-2450832 and +91-651-2450850 -- https://bauranchi.org/contact-us/
Vice Chancellor's office email (VC office, institute-level): vc@bauranchi.org; VC phone 0651-2450500, 2450777 -- https://www.indiacustomercare.com/birsa-agricultural-university-contact-no-0651-245-0832 (third-party listing; check against the official site)
Dean, Faculty of Agriculture, Ranchi (institute-level, not a breeder): Dr. D. K. Shahi, phone 9431371709, email dksbau@gmail.com and deanagrilbau@gmail.com -- https://bauranchi.org/contact-us/
Breeder-level contact: No evidence found.
Aggregator email listings (registrar@bauranchi.org and others) are not from the official site and were not used.

PUBLICATIONS
Variety-specific peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR annual reports, theses, or conference papers naming Divya (BAU-06-03): No evidence found.
Excluded as crop-level only, with no confirmed mention of this variety: Rathnakumar AL, Divya A, Sujatha M (2023). Linseed varieties of India. ICAR-Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research, Hyderabad, p. P103 -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-84200-9_32
Excluded as a name match only: Mahto D. Diallel analysis for combining ability in linseed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331542067_Diallel_Analysis_for_Estimation_of_Combining_Ability_for_Seed_Yield_and_It's_Component_Traits_in_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L

SEED AVAILABILITY
BAU stated that its breeders, the Directorate of Seed and Farms, research stations, KVKs and seed villages will cooperate in seed production for the released varieties. This is a general statement for the batch, not specific to Divya -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/birsa-agricultural-university
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or dealer listings naming Divya: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand (DOD table row for Divya) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Uttarakhand also appears in the DOD state-wise table -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Conflict: another DOD row for the same yield and oil figures lists Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, KNK and Odisha. That row looks garbled and is unreliable -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
The BAU and Jharkhand release context points to Jharkhand as the releasing state, which does not match the CSC state list. Verify against the CSC minutes before relying on the recommended states -- https://bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/

drought.details: DRH 775 is recognized as a short-duration, drought-tolerant rice hybrid suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. It is tolerant to general water stress.

heat.details: This hybrid is identified as heat tolerant in nature and is suitable for yield enhancement under heat stress conditions. It has also shown a significant yield advantage in trials aimed at identifying heat-tolerant rice genotypes.

salinity.details: DRH 775 is listed among rice hybrids tolerant to abiotic stress conditions, which includes salinity. One source explicitly mentions it in the context of drought and salt tolerance in rice research.

flood.details: It exhibits tolerance to water logging and is listed among varieties tolerant to flash floods and stagnant flooding conditions, particularly relevant for direct-seeded rice (DSR).

disease_resistance.summary: DRH 775 is reported to be highly resistant to Gall Midge (GM).

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified beyond Gall Midge resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields vary, including 60-65 Quintals per hectare (6.0-6.5 t/ha), 7.7 tons per hectare in Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and 4.77 tons per hectare with a significant yield advantage over regional checks. In Nepal, yields of 5.6 t/ha have been noted.
agronomic_details.stability: DRH 775 has demonstrated a significant yield advantage over check varieties and is broadly adapted due to its tolerance to a wide range of abiotic stresses.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for irrigated areas, direct sown rainfed conditions, and aerobic cultivation. In Nepal, it is adapted to Tarai and inner Tarai regions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf (approximately 82 cm plant height) with long slender (LS) grains. It is also noted as non-lodging.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been included in monitoring reports for the 'Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India' program, indicating widespread evaluation and promotion. It has also shown significant yield advantage over checks in various trials and evaluations for stress tolerance.

STRESS TOLERANCE
[DRRH-4 / IET 27937] Released for aerobic (direct-seeded, water-limited) ecosystems, which is the only stress-related suitability stated for this hybrid; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence score for DRRH-4 was found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375060794_DRRH-4_IET_27937_-World's_First_Public_Bred_Aerobic_Rice_Hybrid
[DRRH-4 / IET 27937] Its aerobic-rice background is framed against abiotic stress: the authors note that most released rice hybrids are sensitive to high-temperature and drought stress, which motivated aerobic hybrid breeding (this is context, not a tested result for DRRH-4). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375060794_DRRH-4_IET_27937_-World's_First_Public_Bred_Aerobic_Rice_Hybrid
[DRR-44 / Seednet name] No evidence found for this heading. The DRR Dhan 44 (IET 22081) drought and water-limited results found belong to a different variety with the same "DRR 44" label and were discarded: https://www.icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/33-iirr-technologies/105-technology-3

DISEASE AND PEST
[DRRH-4 / IET 27937] Shows moderate resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, gall midge, rice stem borer and whorl maggot. -- https://sarr.co.in/2023/09/05/drrh-4-iet-27937-worlds-first-public-bred-aerobic-rice-hybrid/
[DRRH-4 / IET 27937] Listed by ICAR-IIRR as an aerobic rice hybrid with multiple resistance (no per-disease detail on that page). -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-research/institue-technologies-developed
[DRR-44 / Seednet name] No evidence found for this variety. The blast and bacterial leaf blight data found refer to DRR Dhan 44, a different variety: https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-research/institue-technologies-developed

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
[DRRH-4 / IET 27937] Maturity: about 120 days seed to seed; another copy of the paper gives 115-120 days versus transplanted rice. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/DRRH-4-IET-27937-Worlds-First-Public-13.pdf
[DRRH-4 / IET 27937] Yield: mean grain yield of 5030 kg/ha across the five states, 32%, 28%, 22% and 11% above national, zonal, local and hybrid checks; up to 5.5-6.0 t/ha reported under suitable conditions. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/DRRH-4-IET-27937-Worlds-First-Public-13.pdf
[DRRH-4 / IET 27937] State-wise weighted mean yield was 5306 kg/ha (14% above the best check) across Punjab, Odisha, Tripura, Chhattisgarh and Gujarat. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Yield-performance-of-DRRH-4-in-Punjab-Odisha-Tripura-Chhattisgarh-and-Gujarat-states_tbl1_375060794
[DRRH-4 / IET 27937] Grain and milling quality: hulling 79.2%, milling 71.3%, head rice recovery 62.8%; long bold grain (KL 6.5 mm, KB 2.4 mm). -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/DRRH-4-IET-27937-Worlds-First-Public-13.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Yield-performance-of-DRRH-4-in-Punjab-Odisha-Tripura-Chhattisgarh-and-Gujarat-states_tbl1_375060794
[DRRH-4 / IET 27937] Testing: evaluated in AICRIP multi-location aerobic trials in wet seasons 2018 to 2021, and nominated in the AICRIP aerobic trial of 2018. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375060794_DRRH-4_IET_27937_-World's_First_Public_Bred_Aerobic_Rice_Hybrid
[DRRH-4 / IET 27937] Release context: ICAR-IIRR reports DRRH 4 was among four hybrids released in kharif 2022-23 through CVRC, described as the world's first aerobic rice hybrid. -- https://icar-iirr.org/58%20ARGM%20Final%20Draft%20Proceedings15-09-2023.pdf

Resistance was pursued in the male parent (restorer RPHR-1005) by marker-assisted backcrossing with Xa21 (BB) and Pi54 (blast), giving BB and blast resistance in derived hybrids. Disease scores for DRRH-3 itself: Not found in searched sources. Earlier MABB work pyramided BB and gall midge resistance genes into RPHR-1005 (restorer line, not DRRH-3 directly).

No multi-location trial data, plot yields, or agronomic practice data were found. KrishiKosh theses, AICRIP reports, and field-trial reports: not searched separately.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: DRRH-3 (CSC name) / DRRH-1 (Seednet name), rice

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Parent DRRH3 is highly susceptible to bacterial blight and blast, which limit its productivity; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for DRRH-3 were found -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13562-016-0352-z
- Restorer line RPHR-1005 (male parent) was improved by marker-assisted backcrossing for bacterial blight and blast resistance; improved versions kept medium-slender grain and yield equal to or better than DRRH3 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13562-016-0352-z
- Seednet name (DRRH-1): no stress data found. The DRRH 1 record in the hybrid lists (1996, 7.30 t/ha, Andhra Pradesh) refers to a different hybrid -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm

DISEASE AND PEST
- DRRH3 is highly susceptible to bacterial blight (BB) and blast -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13562-016-0352-z
- Xa21 (BB) and Pi54 (blast) were introgressed into RPHR-1005, the male parent, by marker-assisted backcross breeding, giving BB and blast resistance in derived hybrids -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13562-016-0352-z
- Earlier MABB work pyramided BB and gall midge resistance genes into RPHR-1005 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12041-016-0711-5
- Insect pest and disease scores for DRRH-3 itself: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release record: DRRH-3 (IET 19543), year 2010, duration 131 days, yield 6.07 t/ha, developed by DRR Hyderabad -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Same hybrid listed as 2009 release with 6.07 t/ha and 131 days -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263920493_HYBRID_RICE_DEVELOPMENT_TWO_LINE_AND_THREE_LINE_SYSTEM
- DRRH3 is listed among early-duration hybrids and among medium-slender (MS) grain hybrids -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489
- Multi-location trial data, plot yields, and agronomic practices for DRRH-3: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage given in the input (IR 58025A/IR40750-82-2-2-3R): No evidence found. Parentage of the hybrid was not confirmed in any retrieved source.
- Male parent (restorer) is RPHR-1005, which carries fertility restoration genes Rf3 and Rf4 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13562-016-0352-z
- Xa21 + Pi54 introgression into RPHR-1005 by MABB; QTL/marker details listed in the Springer abstract -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13562-016-0352-z
- Earlier BB and gall midge gene pyramiding in RPHR-1005 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12041-016-0711-5
- Heterosis and SSR-based genetic purity for hybrids (general hybrid work, not DRRH-3-specific) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344590554_Hybrid_Rice_Research_Current_Status_and_Prospects

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Directorate of Rice Research (DRR), ICAR, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad (now ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, IIRR) -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://www.indiamart.com/directorate-rice-research/aboutus.html
- Lead breeder name for DRRH-3: No evidence found. E. A. Siddiq is credited with DRRH-1 (not DRRH-3) as Project Director of DRR -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._A._Siddiq
- Station: Rajendranagar, Hyderabad-500030 -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/contact-us

- Note: The Bihar notified-varieties list (2015) includes a PADDY (DHAN) notification table, but DRRH-3 does not appear in the retrieved excerpt -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh (central India) -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Same states listed in the 2009 table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263920493_HYBRID_RICE_DEVELOPMENT_TWO_LINE_AND_THREE_LINE_SYSTEM

NOTES ON RECORD
- Release year: sources give 2010 (drdpat) and 2009 (ResearchGate table). The input "NaT" should be replaced with 2009 or 2010 after checking the CSC/CSCS&NRV minutes.
- Variety code DRRH-44 (IET 19543): IET 19543 is confirmed for DRRH-3; DRRH-44 was not found in any source.
- Seednet name DRRH-1: the Seednet portal was not retrieved. The DRRH-1 evidence refers to a 1996 hybrid, so it should not be used as the DRRH-3 record.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Bacterial blight (BB): DRRH3 (parent) is highly susceptible to BB, which limits its productivity. Blast: DRRH3 (parent) is highly susceptible to blast, which limits its productivity. Resistance was pursued in the male parent (restorer RPHR-1005) by marker-assisted backcrossing with Xa21 (BB) and Pi54 (blast), giving BB and blast resistance in derived hybrids. Disease scores for DRRH-3 itself: Not found in searched sources. Earlier MABB work pyramided BB and gall midge resistance genes into RPHR-1005 (restorer line, not DRRH-3 directly).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: DRR-1 (CSC release name) / DRRH-1 (Seednet name)

Name note: No source I found uses "DRR-1" as a variety name. Every match for the parentage IR58025A/IR40750 and the public hybrid named DRRH-1 (IIRR, Hyderabad). The evidence below therefore refers to DRRH-1, the Seednet name. Its parentage matches the input record. The CSC release-minute name "DRR-1" is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no stress-tolerance data for DRRH-1 or its cross. Stress-tolerance results in the searches concerned other varieties (for example DRR Dhan 42 and DRR Dhan 58). -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-research/institue-technologies-developed?layout=edit&id=104 (drought data is for DRR Dhan 42, not DRRH-1)

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight or insect reaction data for DRRH-1 was returned. The parent IR58025A is described as a CMS line with stable sterility, not as a resistance source. -- https://www.fao.org/4/w8595t/w8595t02.htm

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- DRRH-1 was released in 1996 with a duration of 125-130 days. On-farm yield was 7.30 t/ha against a check of 5.50 t/ha, a 37.4% advantage (in West Bengal OFT table). A second table gives 32.7% over Tellahamsa, Andhra Pradesh. The two tables differ on the check and the state. -- https://www.fao.org/4/y3544e/y3544e04.htm ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/254371430_Rice_in_India_Present_Status_and_Strategies_to_Boost_Its_Production_Through_Hybrids ; https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm

GENETICS AND QTL -- Cross recorded as IR58025A/IR40750 (CMS female IR58025A, male restorer IR40750), per the public hybrid release table. IR58025A is an IRRI-bred CMS line, stable in sterility in tropical conditions. No QTL or marker study for DRRH-1 was found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/254371430_Rice_in_India_Present_Status_and_Strategies_to_Boost_Its_Production_Through_Hybrids ; https://www.fao.org/4/w8595t/w8595t02.htm

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: Directorate of Rice Research, Hyderabad, now ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. No lead breeder name for DRRH-1 was found in any source. A Wikipedia biography of E. A. Siddiq says he contributed to DRRH-1, but this is a single secondary claim and is unverified. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Rice_Research ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._A._Siddiq

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. No email, phone or postal address for ICAR-IIRR appeared in the results. Institute-level location only: Rajendranagar, near Hyderabad, Telangana. Contact page to verify: https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article?id=282&Itemid=258 (page content did not include contact details). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Rice_Research

PUBLICATIONS -- Hazra, C. R. Status of hybrid rice development in India (in FAO hybrid rice country reports; the table lists DRRH-1, 1996, 125-130 days, 7.30 t/ha). Year: not stated in the snippet (FAO 1999 volume, document w8595/y3544). -- https://www.fao.org/4/y3544e/y3544e04.htm
Authors not captured (2000s). Title: Rice in India: Present Status and Strategies to Boost Its Production Through Hybrids. Journal/report not confirmed in the snippet (DRR-based table; likely ResearchGate-hosted paper). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/254371430_Rice_in_India_Present_Status_and_Strategies_to_Boost_Its_Production_Through_Hybrids
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRIP report, or peer-reviewed DRRH-1 paper was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No current seed dealer, NSC, state corporation or KVK listing was found for DRRH-1. Public hybrid seed guidance lists DRRH-1 among public-sector hybrids and names Andhra Pradesh districts (Khammam, Warangal, Nizamabad, Kurnool, Nandyal) as potential seed-production areas in the rabi season. This is 1990s-era guidance and may be outdated. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/hybrid-rice-seed-production.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Input record says "Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh". Andhra Pradesh is supported by the 1996 release table and two other sources. Gujarat is not supported by any source found. One source lists Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal alongside Andhra Pradesh. The release record for DRRH-1 should be checked against the CSC or state SVRC notification before the state list is used. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm ; https://agriculture.institute/agriculture-fundamentals/recommended-rice-varieties-indian-states/
