search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DRR DHAN 41 (variety_name) / DRR DHAN-47 (seednet_variety_name), rice

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned pages on DRR Dhan 42, 44 and 58 (drought and salinity), but none names DRR Dhan 41 or DRR Dhan 47.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for DRR Dhan 41 or DRR Dhan 47. A search for the variety name returned a page on DRR Dhan 42 and 44 with blast and bacterial blight reactions, which I discarded as other varieties (https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/stress-tolerant-rice-varieties).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The only trial result returned concerns DRR Dhan 58, a different variety (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9385912/).

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for DRR Dhan 41 or DRR Dhan 47. The DRR Dhan 58 paper (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9385912/) describes Saltol and bacterial blight genes in a different variety, so I did not attribute it here.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The DRR prefix suggests ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad, but no page I retrieved links DRR Dhan 41 or 47 to IIRR or to any breeder. This is an unverified inference from the name, not a finding.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. Institute-level contact for ICAR-IIRR, which is not confirmed as this variety's developer:
- Dr. R. M. Sundaram, Director, ICAR-IIRR (publication contact) -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/Technologies/Innovative%20Technologies.pdf
- Email: director.iirr@icar.gov.in -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/Technologies/Innovative%20Technologies.pdf
- Tel: +91-40-24591218; Fax: +91-40-24591217 -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/Technologies/Innovative%20Technologies.pdf
- Address: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad – 500030, Telangana, India -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/Technologies/Innovative%20Technologies.pdf

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for DRR Dhan 41 or DRR Dhan 47. Unrelated items returned: a zinc-biofortification study on DRR Dhan-42 and DRR Dhan-48 (https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Unfortified-DRR-Dhan-42-and-zinc-biofortified-DRR-Dhan-48-rice-varieties-in-paddy_fig1_387106074) and the DRR Dhan 58 paper (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9385912/). Neither is about this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search was not run, because the search budget was reached. The seednet portal was not searched directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The variety's recommended states were not stated in any retrieved page. Recommendations for DRR Dhan 42 and others are not transferable.

Search log: three searches returned results (variety name, breeder/institute, exact name "DRR Dhan 41"). One parallel batch of five queries failed with a server tool-use limit, so the search budget may have been used up earlier than planned. Verify the variety name and its release notification on the CSC/seednet records, since no source confirmed that DRR Dhan 41 or DRR Dhan 47 exists.

disease_resistance.summary: IIRR release summary lists resistance to brown spot and neck blast for DRR Dhan 43. pest_resistance.summary: IIRR release summary lists resistance to brown planthopper (BPH) and field tolerance to stem borer for DRR Dhan 43. The same jumbled-text caveat applies and the block should be verified against the original slide. No other pest evidence was found.

DRR Dhan 43 (CSC name) -- evidence refers to DRR Dhan 43 unless marked "DRR Dhan 47 (Seednet name)".
Note: the Seednet name DRR DHAN-47 is a separate release record in the sources; findings under that name are kept separate and are not attributed to DRR Dhan 43.
Note: 4 searches were run (the limit). A separate seed-availability search was not run; the seed finding below came from the contact search.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- DRR Dhan 43: A secondary review says IIRR developed DRR Dhan 42, 43 and 44 as drought-tolerant cultivars and released them for field trials. This is not corroborated by an IIRR release sheet, so treat it as unverified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Drought-tolerant-rice-varieties-released-in-different-countries-of-South-Asia_tbl4_350592747
- DRR Dhan 47 (Seednet name): ICAR-IIRR lists it as heat tolerant among its high-yielding varieties. DRR Dhan 47 and DRR Dhan 52 high yielding varieties having heat tolerance. -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/?option=com_content&view=article&id=250
- DRR Dhan 47 (Seednet name): A climate-resilience overview also lists it under heat tolerance during critical growth stages. -- https://issca.icrisat.org/scalable-solutions/high-yielding-climate-resilient-and-nutritious-rice-varieties
- DRR Dhan 43: No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence beyond the item above was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- DRR Dhan 43: IIRR release summary lists resistance to brown spot, neck blast and BPH, with field tolerance to stem borer. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf (the PDF text is jumbled; the DRR Dhan 43 block sits between the DRR Dhan 42 and DRR Dhan 47 blocks, so verify against the original slide)
- DRR Dhan 47 (Seednet name): IIRR summary lists resistance to blast, moderate resistance to neck blast, sheath blight, brown spot and RTD, and resistance to sheath rot, BPH and WBPH in a block that may belong to a neighbouring variety. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- DRR Dhan 43: No other disease or pest evidence was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- DRR Dhan 43: Duration 110-115 days, long bold grain, yield potential 70-80 q/ha. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- DRR Dhan 43: Described as an early-duration, high-yielding variety suited to transplanted and direct-seeded aerobic cultivation with good weed competitiveness. This conflicts with the "long bold" grain type above, which should be checked against the official release notification. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Announcement_for_inviting_EXPRESSION_OF_INTENT_for_seedproduction_2022.pdf
- DRR Dhan 47 (Seednet name): Duration 115-120 days, short bold grain, yield about 60 q/ha transplanted and about 43 q/ha aerobic. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- No field-trial or multi-location yield data specific to DRR Dhan 43 was found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The only QTL-linked IIRR results (qDTY2.2 and qDTY4.1) refer to DRR Dhan 42, a different variety, and were discarded. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- Parentage: not found for either name.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- DRR Dhan 43: Developed by ICAR-IIRR (formerly DRR/AICRIP), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. The breeder's name was not found. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Announcement_for_inviting_EXPRESSION_OF_INTENT_for_seedproduction_2022.pdf
- DRR Dhan 47 (Seednet name): Institution-level attribution to IIRR only; no breeder name found. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- IIRR history: Originally the All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (1965), then the Directorate of Rice Research (1983), then IIRR (2014). -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/about-iirr/about-iirr

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad-500 030, India. -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/contact-us
- Director email: director.iirr@icar.gov.in. -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/contact-us
- Phone: Tel 91-40-24591285; Fax 91-40-24591217; PD Cell 91-40-24591218; Administration 91-40-24591257/256. -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/contact-us
- Institute general contact on the About page: 040-24591241, iirricar@gmail.com (a Gmail address, not an official ICAR domain). -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/about-iirr/about-iirr
- Director named as Dr. Raman Meenakshi Sundaram (Director/Project Coordinator). -- https://sarr.co.in/home/contact-us/ (Wikipedia also names him: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Rice_Research). The third-party listing (https://www.indiacustomercare.com/indian-institute-rice-research-icar-contact-no-040-24591281) gives a mobile number and other staff emails, but it is not an official source; verify before use.
- No breeder or scientist contact for DRR Dhan 43 was found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. Searches returned papers on DRR Dhan 58, Pusa 44 and other varieties, which were discarded. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9385912/

SEED AVAILABILITY
- DRR Dhan 43: IIRR invited registered seed growers and companies to produce its seed in 2022, listed as a 2015 release for irrigated early conditions. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Announcement_for_inviting_EXPRESSION_OF_INTENT_for_seedproduction_2022.pdf
- No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or dealer listings were found, because a dedicated seed search was not run.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- DRR Dhan 43: Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karnataka and Kerala. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- DRR Dhan 47 (Seednet name): Haryana, Gujarat and Odisha. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- Release year: the CSC record gives 2014-10-20, while the IIRR seed-production notice lists 2015 for DRR Dhan 43. The mismatch should be checked against the official gazette notification.

The ICAR listing gives no drought tolerance for DRR Dhan 45 and describes it for irrigated conditions. Drought statements found in the results concern DRR dhan 50, a different variety, and are excluded.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. The ICAR listing gives no heat tolerance for DRR Dhan 45.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. The ICAR listing gives no salinity tolerance for DRR Dhan 45.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. The ICAR listing gives no flood tolerance for DRR Dhan 45.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to blast, sheath rot and rice tungro virus (ICAR listing). Moderate resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot and bacterial blight, with sheath rot resistance noted (IIRR industry slide).

pest_resistance.summary: Resistance to brown planthopper (BPH) and whitebacked planthopper (WBPH) noted, and moderate resistance to plant hoppers (IIRR industry slide). Resistance to gall midge and rice thrips, and moderate resistance to plant hoppers, recorded in an IIRR seed-production table. This table row is ambiguous and may describe a neighbouring variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: DRR Dhan 45 (variety_name) / DRR DHAN 57 (seednet_variety_name), rice

Naming note: All evidence below refers to DRR Dhan 45 (IET 23832). The only DRR DHAN 57 hit was a list entry on the IIRR homepage, with no details, so no evidence on the Seednet name was found. Four searches were run (the maximum allowed), and the Seednet portal was not reached. Findings are paraphrased and attributed by URL.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as a semi-dwarf, non-lodging, long slender-grain variety for irrigated conditions; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance is listed for DRR Dhan 45 itself -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/8341
- The IIRR industry slide describes it as high yielding, early, and drought tolerant, but the same slide does not clearly tie that claim to a trial result -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- Drought-tolerance statements elsewhere in the results concern DRR dhan 50 (a different variety), so they are excluded here -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00037-w

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to blast, sheath rot and rice tungro virus -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/8341
- Moderate resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot and bacterial blight; sheath rot, BPH and WBPH resistance noted -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- Resistance to gall midge and rice thrips, and moderate resistance to plant hoppers, recorded in a seed-production table -- https://icar-iirr.org/Announcement_for_inviting_EXPRESSION_OF_INTENT_for_seedproduction_2022.pdf (this table row is ambiguous; it may describe a neighbouring variety)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration: 125 days (ICAR and IIRR slide) versus about 130 days (IIRR profile and Krishi Jagran); the two sources disagree -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/8341 ; https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-research/institue-technologies-developed/33-iirr-technologies/106-technology-4 ; https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/list-of-biofortified-rice-varieties-a-closer-look-at-nutrient-rich-options/
- Yield potential: 5-6 t/ha (IIRR profile), about 50 q/ha (IIRR slide), 50 q/ha (Krishi Jagran) -- same URLs as above
- AICRP biofortification multi-location trials in 2013-14 reported yield advantages over Samba Mahsuri (37.1%) and IR 64 (17.2%) in TN, KA and AP; in AP alone the margins were 8.3% and 15.5% -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-research/institue-technologies-developed/33-iirr-technologies/106-technology-4
- Grain zinc about 22.6 ppm overall (24.0 ppm in AP, KA and TN) in polished rice; amylose about 20.7% -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/8341
- Intermediate amylose (21.1%), intermediate ASV (3.5) and gel consistency 54 mm reported -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-research/institue-technologies-developed/33-iirr-technologies/106-technology-4
- Cost-of-cultivation comparison with Samba Mahsuri on sample farms in the 2017 rainy season found similar production cost per tonne -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Cost-of-cultivation-and-returns-from-Samba-Mahsuri-and-DRR-Dhan-45_tbl2_338280336

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: IR 73707-45-3-2-3 / IR 77080-B-34-3 -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-research/institue-technologies-developed/33-iirr-technologies/106-technology-4
- Developed by conventional breeding using HarvestPlus material; no marker or QTL study specific to DRR Dhan 45 was found -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/8341
- Parentage was "Not specified" in the input; the pedigree above comes from the IIRR profile
- Release-year discrepancy: 2015 (input, IIRR profile) versus 2016 (Krishi Jagran; IIRR seed announcement table) -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/list-of-biofortified-rice-varieties-a-closer-look-at-nutrient-rich-options/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/8341
- Breeder or scientist names: none found for DRR Dhan 45 in these results. A name appears in an IIRR slide URL (Dr L.V. Subba Rao), but the slide does not state he is the breeder, so it is not recorded as a breeder -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- Context: the institute was elevated from the Directorate of Rice Research to a national institute in December 2014 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351749037_Rice_breeding_in_India_eight_decades_of_journey_towards_enhancing_the_genetic_gain_for_yield_nutritional_quality_and_commodity_value

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad-500030 (Telangana) -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/8341
- Address variant: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad – 500 030 -- https://icar-iirr.org/Announcement_for_inviting_EXPRESSION_OF_INTENT_for_seedproduction_2022.pdf
- Official email, phone, or institute contact page URL: not found in these results. Institute homepage to check: https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR-IIRR (2023). 58th Annual Rice Group Meeting (ARGM) Final Draft Proceedings. ICAR-IIRR report (authors not listed in the extract) -- https://icar-iirr.org/58%20ARGM%20Final%20Draft%20Proceedings15-09-2023.pdf
- Authors not confirmed (year not confirmed). An economic analysis of biofortified rice varieties. ResearchGate entry (cost data for DRR Dhan 45 vs Samba Mahsuri, 2017 season) -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Cost-of-cultivation-and-returns-from-Samba-Mahsuri-and-DRR-Dhan-45_tbl2_338280336
- Abdul Fiyaz R et al. (year not confirmed). Rice breeding in India: eight decades of journey towards enhancing the genetic gain for yield, nutritional quality, and commodity value. Review that cites the release of DRR Dhan 45 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351749037_Rice_breeding_in_India_eight_decades_of_journey_towards_enhancing_the_genetic_gain_for_yield_nutritional_quality_and_commodity_value
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI specific to DRR Dhan 45 was found in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- IIRR seed-production call for expressions of intent (2022) lists DRR Dhan 45 among varieties for seed production -- https://icar-iirr.org/Announcement_for_inviting_EXPRESSION_OF_INTENT_for_seedproduction_2022.pdf
- Odisha farmer and FPO seed-training article (2025) mentions DRR dhan 45 as a specialty variety for seed production; it names no seed seller -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/ag-tech-research-news/enhancing-decentralized-seed-production-of-healthier-rice-in-odisha/
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing was found. Seednet was not reached, so the Seednet listing (under DRR DHAN 57) remains unverified.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh (ICAR listing) -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/8341 ; https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- Telangana added (Krishi Jagran; treated as secondary) -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/list-of-biofortified-rice-varieties-a-closer-look-at-nutrient-rich-options/
- Conflict: the IIRR seed-announcement table lists DRR Dhan 45 under Bihar (Zone III) and Chhattisgarh (Zone V), which may be a table-parsing error; this needs checking against the CSC notification -- https://icar-iirr.org/Announcement_for_inviting_EXPRESSION_OF_INTENT_for_seedproduction_2022.pdf

seednet_fields.Parentage: Considering the unlimited potential of wild species for identification of yield enhancing genes, interspecific population between Oryza sativa genotypes IR580325, KMR3 and Oryza rufipogon; was developed with a primary objective to identify yield QTLs. DRR Dhan 65 (IET 27641) is a wild introgression line developed by ICAR-IIRR using parental lines a) IR 58025A, a widely used CMS line having long grain type and early maturity along with good milling and eating quality, b)
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Maharashtra and regions with P deficit soil of India.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: It takes 130-135 days for maturity, Tolerance to P deficit soils compared to various check of early and late duration. Most suitable for irrigated, transplanted & also rainfed areas with P deficit soils of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Maharashtra under Late variety cultivation. It is also a multiple stress tolerance variety. Seed rate- 10kg/acre. It also showed significantly high response over various levels of Nitrogen.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Tall stature with complete panicle exertion (100% exertion), short grain type and late maturity.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The variety IET 27641 (RPBio4919-B-B NSR86), exhibited tolerant reaction to with SI of 4.3 (2018), 4.2 (2019) for leaf blast and 4 (2019) for neck blast. 5.3 (2021) for Sheath blight as compared to the Check in the trial. During 2020 (IET 27641 exhibited low over all disease score high promising index under NSN-1.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: The proposed variety, IET 27641 (RPBio4919-B-B NSR86) exhibited high tolerance low susceptibility index (SI) to insect pests like Plant hoppers SI of (2018 & 2019), stem borer SI of (2018), SI of 4 (2019), SI of 0.9 (2021) and leaf folder of SI of 3.6 (2018) & 0.5 (2019). During 2019 based on NSN, IET 27641 showed field tolerance to BPH at hot spot region Maruteru with a DS of 3.0.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Green manuring with daincha, which can be incorporated into soil at about 45 to 55 days after sowing and reduce the nitrogen dose by 20-25 kg/acre. 50:15:15 kg N, P2O5 and K2O/acre.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae): resistant. The variety carries Xa21, xa13, xa5 and Xa38 (per the release-notice and CSC-linked records). The IIRR slide deck describes it as highly resistant to bacterial blight, but the slide text is interleaved with other varieties, so this claim is treated with caution. The release notice and riceportal describe it as suited to bacterial blight endemic areas where susceptible Samba Mahsuri types are grown. No other disease scores were confirmed for DRR Dhan 53. Scores for leaf blast and neck blast belong to DRR Dhan 57 (IET 26171) and were excluded.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The digest states no separate pest or disease scores were confirmed for DRR Dhan 53 beyond bacterial blight. Pest resistance scores (planthoppers, whorl maggot, gall midge, rice thrips) belong to DRR Dhan 57 (IET 26171) and were excluded.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 5.50 t/ha (release notice); range 5.5-6 t/ha (seed-to-seed record). Units in the original data are listed as Kg/Ha; equivalent to 5,500 kg/ha on average.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to bacterial blight endemic areas where susceptible Samba Mahsuri types are grown. Recommended states: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Jharkhand, Odisha, Bihar, Gujarat. Ecology and agro-climatic detail beyond the state list: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf, non-lodging habit. Medium-slender grain. Long, fully exerted panicles with 100% exertion. Grain quality comparable to recurrent parent Improved Samba Mahsuri; the record is labelled 'low GI'. Head rice recovery conflicts between sources: 58.4% in the release notice and 78.7% on riceportal; the conflict is unresolved.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No trial-specific results for DRR Dhan 53 were found beyond the average yield of 5.50 t/ha reported in the release notice and the 5.5-6 t/ha range in the seed-to-seed record. Mean yield of 4782 kg/ha and 13-17% yield advantage over checks in Zones III and V belong to DRR Dhan 57 (IET 26171) and were excluded.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: DRR Dhan 53 (CSC release name; IET 27294) / DRR DHAN 57 (Seednet name)
Name note: The release-minute name "DRR Dhan 53" is the variety these findings describe. The Seednet name "DRR DHAN 57" matched a different entry, DRR Dhan 57 (IET 26171, an aerobic variety released for Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh). Those DRR Dhan 57 findings are labelled below and must not be attributed to DRR Dhan 53. No search result confirmed a Seednet listing for DRR Dhan 53.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- DRR Dhan 53 is a bacterial blight resistant variety carrying Xa21, xa13, xa5 and Xa38, with semi-dwarf, non-lodging habit -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/jspui/handle/123456789/71147 ; https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties
- The IIRR slide deck describes DRR Dhan 53 as highly resistant to bacterial blight. The slide text is interleaved with other varieties, so any other resistance claims there are unreliable -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in DRR Dhan 53. The salinity and drought results that came up belong to DRR Dhan 58, DRR Dhan 42/44 and other entries and were discarded.
- [DRR Dhan 57, IET 26171, Seednet-name entry] Aerobic variety with moderate resistance to leaf blast and neck blast -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382617803_DRR_Dhan_70-IET_29415_-_An_Aerobic_Rice_Variety

DISEASE AND PEST
- DRR Dhan 53 is described as resistant to bacterial blight; no separate pest or disease scores were confirmed beyond this -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/jspui/handle/123456789/71147
- [DRR Dhan 57, IET 26171] Moderate resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, planthoppers and whorl maggot, and resistance to gall midge and rice thrips -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382617803_DRR_Dhan_70-IET_29415_-_An_Aerobic_Rice_Variety

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Seed-to-seed maturity 130-135 days; average yield 5.5-6 t/ha -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/jspui/handle/123456789/71147
- Average yield 5.50 t/ha; medium-slender grain; long, fully exerted panicles; 100% exertion -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties
- Grain quality is comparable to recurrent parent Improved Samba Mahsuri, and the variety is suited to bacterial blight endemic areas where susceptible Samba Mahsuri types are grown -- http://www.riceportal.in/content/drr-dhan-53
- Head rice recovery is reported as 58.4% in the release notice and 78.7% on riceportal; the two sources conflict -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties ; http://www.riceportal.in/content/drr-dhan-53
- Its record is labelled "low GI" -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-research/institue-technologies-developed
- [DRR Dhan 57, IET 26171] Mean yield 4782 kg/ha, 13-17% above checks in Zones III and V; 120 days duration -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382617803_DRR_Dhan_70-IET_29415_-_An_Aerobic_Rice_Variety

GENETICS AND QTL
- Marker-assisted selection derivative of Improved Samba Mahsuri; cross Improved Samba Mahsuri*3/PAU 3554; parentage is therefore available and should replace "Not specified" -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/jspui/handle/123456789/71147 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365736796_DRR_Dhan_53_RP-6113-Patho-BB9_IET_27294_-_a_high_yielding_bacterial_blight_resistant_fine_grain_type_rice_variety
- Used as a parent in a cross ("DRR Dhan 53 x IRRI-162") in the IIRR 2023 annual report; the snippet is partial -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf
- [DRR Dhan 57, IET 26171] Developed from a BPT5204/Azucena cross -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382617803_DRR_Dhan_70-IET_29415_-_An_Aerobic_Rice_Variety

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead author per the Journal of Rice Research PDF: P. Senguttuvel, with Jyothi Badri, D. Ladhalakshmi, A. Yugander, S.K. Hajira Masood, T. Dilip and Kuldeep Singh (Director, ICAR-NBPGR) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365736796_DRR_Dhan_53_RP-6113-Patho-BB9_IET_27294_-_a_high_yielding_bacterial_blight_resistant_fine_grain_type_rice_variety
- The ResearchGate metadata lists G.S. Laha and Abdul Fiyaz R. as authors of the same paper. This conflicts with the PDF author list and was not resolved -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365736796_DRR_Dhan_53_RP-6113-Patho-BB9_IET_27294_-_a_high_yielding_bacterial_blight_resistant_fine_grain_type_rice_variety
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (formerly Directorate of Rice Research), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/jspui/handle/123456789/71147
- [DRR Dhan 57, IET 26171] Lead on the paper is P. Senguttuvel; Guntupalli Padmavathi (Principal Scientist, IIRR) is listed as a co-developer -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Guntupalli-Padmavathi

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or personal contact was found for DRR Dhan 53.
- Institute-level address as printed in the paper: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500030 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365736796_DRR_Dhan_53_RP-6113-Patho-BB9_IET_27294_-_a_high_yielding_bacterial_blight_resistant_fine_grain_type_rice_variety
- Institute website (homepage only; no contact page URL was found in results): https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/
- Director named on Wikipedia: Dr. Raman Meenakshi Sundaram. This is undated and was not verified against the institute site -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Rice_Research
- Email and phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Senguttuvel P, Badri J

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The release notice gives no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for DRR Dhan 56 (-- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties)

DISEASE AND PEST
DRR Dhan 56 is reported as resistant to leaf blast, neck blast, gall midge and rice thrips, and moderately resistant to planthoppers and stem borer (-- https://www.icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties?Itemid=101)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
DRR Dhan 56 (IET 26803) is an early-duration, tall, erect, non-lodging, non-shattering variety. It flowers in about 89 days, is about 102 cm tall, and has long panicles and good biomass (-- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties)
Head rice recovery is 64.1% and intermediate amylose is 23.15% (-- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties)
The notice does not give a yield figure for DRR Dhan 56. Its 5.50 t/ha average yield and 130–135 day maturity are for a different variety in the same notice, so they are not attributed here (-- https://www.icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties?Itemid=101)
Release: notified through the Central Sub-committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties, S.O. 500(E) (-- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties)
Name check: all DRR Dhan 56 evidence uses the CSC name. No page was found for the Seednet name "DRR Dhan 57", so the Seednet record could not be checked.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: the release notice gives the cross Huang-Hua-Zhan*2/Phalguna, which conflicts with the "Not specified" entry in the record. The variety was bred under the Green Super Rice (GSR) Phase III project with IRRI (-- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties)
No QTL or marker study naming DRR Dhan 56 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad, which announced the release (-- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties)
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The release notice names only the Director, Dr Raman Meenakshi Sundaram, and does not identify the breeder.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad (institute website: https://www.icar-iirr.org). No official email, phone or postal address was found in the search results. The institute home page was not opened, so its contact page was not verified.
Director named in the release notice: Dr Raman Meenakshi Sundaram, Director, ICAR-IIRR (-- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties)

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The searches returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper on DRR Dhan 56. A DRR Dhan 58 salinity paper (Rice journal, https://thericejournal.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s12284-022-00591-3) was excluded because it concerns a different variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for DRR Dhan 56 or DRR Dhan 57 was returned. The search limit was reached before a dedicated seed query could run.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found for Punjab or Haryana. The release notice gives zone-level recommendations only for DRR Dhan 54 and DRR Dhan 55, not for DRR Dhan 56 (-- https://www.icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article/11-news/147-icar-iirr-released-four-new-rice-varieties?Itemid=101)

LIMITATIONS
The web_search tool hit its usage limit during the run, so searches were not all completed as planned. Four searches ran: the first batch failed on the limit, and the later four covered variety, breeder/contact, research and parentage. No separate seed-availability search ran.

drought.details: No specific information regarding drought tolerance for DRR Dhan 46 was found in the provided search results. The search results primarily discuss drought tolerance for other DRR Dhan varieties, such as DRR Dhan 57 (RESULT_3, RESULT_5, RESULT_9, RESULT_19, RESULT_20, RESULT_45, RESULT_50) and DRR Dhan 42 (RESULT_1, RESULT_23).

heat.details: No specific information regarding heat tolerance for DRR Dhan 46 was found in the provided search results. The search results primarily discuss heat stress tolerance for other DRR Dhan varieties, such as DRR Dhan 57 (RESULT_6, RESULT_11, RESULT_13, RESULT_16, RESULT_47).

salinity.details: No specific information regarding salinity tolerance for DRR Dhan 46 was found in the provided search results. The search results primarily discuss salinity tolerance for other DRR Dhan varieties, such as DRR Dhan 58 (MAS derived salinity tolerant, RESULT_7, RESULT_21, RESULT_37) and DRR Dhan 57 in the context of general salinity tolerant varieties (RESULT_26, RESULT_27, RESULT_28, RESULT_29).

flood.details: No specific information regarding flood tolerance for DRR Dhan 46 was found in the provided search results. The search results discuss submergence tolerance for other DRR Dhan varieties like DRR Dhan 50 (RESULT_41) and DRR Dhan 57 (seedling stage submergence tolerance, RESULT_31, RESULT_32, RESULT_33, RESULT_34, RESULT_42, RESULT_44).

disease_resistance.summary: No specific information regarding disease resistance for DRR Dhan 46 was found in the provided search results. The search results mention disease resistance for other DRR Dhan varieties, such as DRR Dhan 57 (moderately resistant to major insect pests and diseases, RESULT_15) and DRR Dhan 58 (bacterial blight resistant, RESULT_7, RESULT_21, RESULT_37).

pest_resistance.summary: No specific information regarding pest resistance for DRR Dhan 46 was found in the provided search results. The search results mention pest resistance for other DRR Dhan varieties, such as DRR Dhan 57 (moderately resistant to major insect pests and diseases, RESULT_15).

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific information regarding QTLs for DRR Dhan 46 was found in the provided search results. The search results mention QTLs associated with low soil phosphorus tolerance (RESULT_38) and seedling and reproductive stage QTL mapping for salt tolerance (RESULT_25).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NOTE: Name conflict. The Seednet name "DRR DHAN 58" belongs to a separate, documented IIRR variety (a Samba Mahsuri near-isogenic line). Evidence under that name is listed separately and is not treated as evidence about DRR Dhan 68. Searches returned no seednet.gov.in page and no CSC minutes entry for either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
DRR Dhan 68: No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for DRR Dhan 68.
DRR Dhan 58 (Seednet name, different variety): Salinity tolerance at the seedling stage, from a Saltol QTL introgressed by marker-assisted backcrossing; the paper reports good performance in coastal saline multi-location trials in 2019 and 2020 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9385912/

DISEASE AND PEST
DRR Dhan 68: No evidence found.
DRR Dhan 58 (Seednet name): Carries three bacterial blight resistance genes (Xa21, xa13, xa5) in the Samba Mahsuri background -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9385912/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
DRR Dhan 68: The IIRR Annual Report 2022 lists DRR Dhan 68 in a release/recommendation table, with unlabelled columns (season BORO, grain type LS, a value of 6.56, and states AS, WB, TR). The yield value is not labelled, so it cannot be confirmed as yield -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
DRR Dhan 58 (Seednet name): Reported a 24% yield advantage over its recurrent parent under coastal saline conditions in multi-location trials -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9385912/
Maturity for DRR Dhan 68: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
DRR Dhan 68: The annual report table gives a parentage-like string, HHZ5-DT20-DT2-Huang-Hua-105, beside DRR Dhan 68. The column header is not recovered, so this cannot be confirmed as pedigree. Input parentage is "Not specified." -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
DRR Dhan 58 (Seednet name): Marker-assisted backcrossing with five Saltol markers and three bacterial blight genes; the selected line recovered 95.3% of the recurrent parent genome at BC3F2 -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35976520/
Not attributed: BRRI dhan99 (Bangladesh) salinity studies (e.g., https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0294573). The variety_code "BRRI Dhan 99" appears near DRR Dhan 68 in the IIRR table, but no source links the two, so these studies are excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
DRR Dhan 68: No lead breeder or scientist name found. The developing institution is ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (ICAR-IIRR), per the input record and the IIRR Annual Report 2022 table -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
DRR Dhan 58 (Seednet name): Developed at ICAR-IIRR, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, with the Department of Biotechnology as the affiliation of the lead team -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9385912/ Named authors include G. Rekha, V. Abhilash Kumar, P. Senguttuvel and R. M. Sundaram. These are authors of the DRR Dhan 58 paper, not confirmed breeders of DRR Dhan 68.

CONTACT DETAILS
DRR Dhan 68: No evidence found for an email, phone, breeder contact or institute contact page.
Institute-level (ICAR-IIRR): Director Dr. R M Sundaram (named as publisher of the 2022 annual report); postal location Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf and https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9385912/ No institute email or phone was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
DRR Dhan 68: No evidence found for a dedicated paper.
Rekha G, Abhilash Kumar V, Gokulan C. G., et al. (2022). DRR Dhan 58, a Seedling Stage Salinity Tolerant NIL of Improved Samba Mahsuri Shows Superior Performance in Multi-location Trials. Rice (Springer). -- https://thericejournal.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s12284-022-00591-3 / DOI 10.1186/s12284-022-00591-3 (Seednet name; not confirmed as DRR Dhan 68)
Sundaram R. M., et al. (2022). IIRR Annual Report 2022. ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRIP report entry, or QTL/marker study for DRR Dhan 68 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
DRR Dhan 68: No evidence found from NSC, state corporations, KVKs, SAU sales or private dealers.
DRR Dhan 58 (Seednet name): The IIRR seed portal lists a DRR Dhan 58 page marked out of stock, with a 135-day duration -- https://iirr-seedportal.in/ NRDC has invited seed companies to take a technology licence for DRR Dhan 58 -- https://www.nrdcindia.com/LatestDetail/130

RECOMMENDED STATES
DRR Dhan 68: Table entry reads "AS, WB, TR," which matches the input states Assam, West Bengal and Tripura -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf Gazette or CSC notification not found.
DRR Dhan 58 (Seednet name): The IIRR expression-of-intent document lists different states (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, Gujarat, Maharashtra). These do not match the DRR Dhan 68 record -- https://icar-iirr.org/Announcement_for_inviting_EXPRESSION_OF_INTENT_for_seedproduction_2022.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME NOTE: CSC name "DRR Dhan 69" appears only in the IIRR Annual Report 2022 table. Seednet name "DRR DHAN 59" matches a different IIRR entry (Xa33, BB resistant). I could not confirm they are the same variety, so the DRR Dhan 59 findings below are labelled as such. Four searches were run: variety, Seednet name, breeder/institute, and research. No separate seed-availability search was run because the 4-search cap was reached.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for DRR Dhan 69 (either name). The search returned pages on DRR Dhan 58, 65 and 55, which are other varieties and are excluded. -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/institute-research/institue-technologies-developed?id=243 (excluded, other variety)

DISEASE AND PEST
- DRR Dhan 59 (Seednet name; identity with DRR Dhan 69 unverified): DRR Dhan 59 is described as high-yielding, bacterial blight resistant, with a long bold grain type. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Announcement_for_inviting_EXPRESSION_OF_INTENT_for_seedproduction_2022.pdf
- DRR Dhan 59 (Seednet name): an IIRR presentation lists the entry as carrying Xa33 and moderate resistance to leaf blast and neck blast. The slide layout is ambiguous, so this line may belong to the neighbouring entry. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf
- DRR Dhan 69: No evidence found for disease or pest reaction.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- DRR Dhan 69: The IIRR Annual Report 2022 lists it in a table row reading "19 · DRR Dhan 69 · BR 8631-12-3-5-P2 · BR 7166-5B-5/ · 118 · BORO · LS · 6.85 · AS, WB, TR". The column labels are not printed, so the 118 (duration in days), Boro season, LS (long slender grain), 6.85 (yield, t/ha) and state codes are my reading, not confirmed. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
- DRR Dhan 69: No field-trial or multi-location result found beyond that table row.

GENETICS AND QTL
- DRR Dhan 69: No evidence found.
- DRR Dhan 59 (Seednet name): the Xa33 bacterial blight resistance gene is noted for this entry. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Industry_meet_ppt_Dr_LVSubbaRao.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- DRR Dhan 69: No breeder name found in any result. The only institutional link is the IIRR Annual Report 2022 table row. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
- Institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
- Excluded: the breeder named for DRR Dhan 100 (Kamla), a different variety, is not attributed to DRR Dhan 69. -- https://icar-iirr.org/index.php/en/component/content/article?id=282&Itemid=258

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address: ICAR - Indian Institute of Rice Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad – 500 030. -- https://icar-iirr.org/Announcement_for_inviting_EXPRESSION_OF_INTENT_for_seedproduction_2022.pdf
- Director named as publisher of the 2022 annual report: Dr. R M Sundaram, Director, ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
- Email and phone: No evidence found for DRR Dhan 69 or the institute in the results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Sundaram, R. M. (2022). ICAR-IIRR Annual Report

drought.details: DRR Dhan 59 is a drought tolerant rice variety that was developed to be suitable for irrigated conditions. It has been screened for drought stress tolerance and is associated with the abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2).

heat.details: The variety exhibits heat stress tolerance and was included in screenings for this trait. Candidate genes for heat tolerance have been identified in rice through combined GWAS and transcriptome analysis, which includes DRR Dhan 59.

salinity.details: DRR Dhan 59 is a salinity tolerant variety, specifically at the seedling stage, possessing the Saltol gene/QTL. Its salinity tolerance has been identified and quantified through salt stress studies.

seednet_fields.Parentage:
MTU 1010 *2/ Swarna
MTU 1010 also known as Cotton Dora Sannalu. It is an elite-mega rice variety of India released from Acharya NG Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) in 2000 and is developed from the cross Krishnaveni and IR-64. MTU 1010 is high yielding, semi dwarf (108 cm), short duration (120 days) rice variety possessing long slender grain type with resistance to blast and tolerance to BPH while highly sensitive to low soil P, when screened  in the low P plot of ICAR-IIRR.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: MTU 1010 growing regions of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana and in regions with P deficit soil of India in states especially in Eastern and North Eastern India for which the recurrent, MTU 1010 has been released.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Semi-dwarf stature with complete panicle exertion (100% exertion), long slender grain type and early maturity.

drought.details: DRR Dhan 60 is a drought-tolerant rice variety (Result 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 16, 18, 20, 32, 34, 44, 49). It is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions (Result 8, 20). It is an improved version of Improved Samba Mahsuri, showing tolerance to low soil (Result 3, 12, 44) and specifically low soil phosphorus (Result 18, 29, 36, 47). Its drought tolerance is associated with the introgression of the Pup1 QTL (Result 5, 11, 23, 33, 40, 47).

heat.details: DRR Dhan 60 is being screened and is associated with research on heat stress tolerance (Result 7, 13, 15, 17, 19, 25, 45). Scientists at ICAR-IIRR are involved in developing varieties with heat stress tolerance, including DRR Dhan 60 (Result 14).

salinity.details: DRR Dhan 60 has been developed with the introgression of the Saltol QTL for salinity tolerance (Result 11, 22, 25, 27, 30, 45), specifically demonstrating seedling stage salinity tolerance (Result 25, 45). It is suitable for salt-affected rice growing areas, such as those in Gujarat (Result 28), and is described as salinity tolerant (Result 14, 23, 26, 29, 30).

flood.details: While DRR Dhan 60 is mentioned in the context of developing 'Multiple Stress Tolerant Varieties for Flood' (Result 32) and 'submergence tolerance' (Result 7, 15, 33, 38, 50), direct and explicit information on its specific tolerance level to general flood conditions (e.g., stagnant water beyond submergence) is not detailed.

disease_resistance.summary: DRR Dhan 60 is resistant to bacterial blight (Result 4, 9, 10, 13, 18, 19, 23, 24, 25, 29, 35, 40, 43, 45, 47). This resistance is conferred by the introgression of the Xa21, xa13, and xa5 genes (Result 4, 5, 10, 13, 19, 23, 24, 25, 33, 35, 40, 43, 45, 47).

pest_resistance.summary: Not Specified

agronomic_details.yield: Described as a high yielding variety (Result 5, 21, 23).
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions (Result 8, 20) and medium-low soil (Result 1, 22, 34). It is also well-adapted to areas with low soil phosphorus (Result 3, 12, 18, 29, 36, 44, 47) and salt-affected areas (Result 28).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Non-Basmati (Result 8, 20, 28, 37).
agronomic_details.field_trials: DRR Dhan 60 has been evaluated in national programs, as indicated by its inclusion in the 'Draft proceedings of 59 Annual Rice Group Meetings' by AICRIP (Result 7, 15, 26, 38, 42).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Key genetic markers introgressed into DRR Dhan 60 include: Xa21, xa13, and xa5 for bacterial blight resistance (Result 4, 5, 10, 13, 19, 23, 24, 25, 33, 35, 40, 43, 45, 47); Pup1 (Phosphorus-uptake 1) for drought tolerance and high phosphorus use efficiency/tolerance to low soil phosphorus (Result 5, 6, 11, 16, 23, 33, 36, 39, 40, 41, 47); and Saltol QTL for salinity tolerance (Result 11, 22, 25, 27, 30, 45). The Sub1 gene is associated with its seedling stage submergence tolerance (Result 33, 50).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: The primary QTLs associated with DRR Dhan 60 are: Pup1 (drought tolerance, phosphorus use efficiency, low soil phosphorus tolerance), Saltol (salinity tolerance), and Xa21+xa13+xa5 (bacterial blight resistance). The Sub1 gene confers seedling stage submergence tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: DRR Dhan 60 has been developed using Marker Assisted Selection (MAS) and Marker Assisted Breeding (MABB) approaches (Result 9, 14, 32, 36, 43, 47), indicating precise introgression of target genes/QTLs for multiple stress tolerance.

drought.details: DRR Dhan 62 has been developed and released as a drought tolerant variety. It is suitable for irrigated conditions, indicating a general adaptability to controlled water environments, but its development explicitly addresses drought stress mitigation.

heat.details: The variety exhibits heat stress tolerance and is listed among varieties tolerant to heat stress. Research identified candidate genes for heat tolerance in rice, indicating a genetic basis for this trait.

salinity.details: DRR Dhan 62 is described as salinity tolerant and suitable for saline soils and salt-affected rice growing areas, including those in Gujarat.

flood.details: This variety has been developed for multiple stress tolerance, including flood, through Marker Assisted Breeding, specifically demonstrating submergence tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: DRR Dhan 62 is resistant to Bacterial blight (BB) and Blast diseases. This resistance is genetically engineered through the introgression of multiple resistance genes.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields from IIRR, Hyderabad trials include ranges such as 24.20-25.90 t/ha and 44.70-45.00 t/ha. It is generally described as a high-yielding variety, with yield performance evaluated under stress-prone conditions.
agronomic_details.stability: The variety's release for a wide range of states and its multi-stress tolerance traits suggest good adaptability across different environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: DRR Dhan 62 is suitable for irrigated and transplanted cultivation systems. It also shows adaptation to areas affected by low soil phosphorus and saline conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: It is a fine-grain type rice variety known for its excellent cooking quality. It is an improved version of Improved Samba Mahsuri.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Performance data for DRR Dhan 62 have been reported in the Draft Proceedings of the 58th and 59th Annual Rice Group Meetings (AICRIP-intranet.in), with trials conducted by ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: The variety carries multiple resistance genes: Xa21, xa13, and xa5 for Bacterial blight resistance, and Pi2 and Pi54 for Blast resistance. It also contains the Sub1 QTL for seedling stage submergence tolerance and qDTY2.1 and qDTY3.1 QTLs for reproductive stage submergence tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTLs introgressed include qSub1 for submergence tolerance and qDTY2.1 + qDTY3.1 for reproductive stage submergence tolerance. These were introduced via Marker Assisted Breeding (MAB) and Marker-Assisted Introgression (MAI).
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: DRR Dhan 62 is an improved version of 'Improved Samba Mahsuri', developed through Marker Assisted Selection (MAS) and Marker-Assisted Introgression to incorporate durable resistance genes and abiotic stress tolerance QTLs. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) from a drought tolerant rice cultivar is noted in connection to DRR Dhan 62's development.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: The variety carries multiple resistance genes: Xa21, xa13, and xa5 for Bacterial blight resistance, and Pi2 and Pi54 for Blast resistance. It also contains the Sub1 QTL for seedling stage submergence tolerance and qDTY2.1 and qDTY3.1 QTLs for reproductive stage submergence tolerance.
genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: QTLs introgressed include qSub1 for submergence tolerance and qDTY2.1 + qDTY3.1 for reproductive stage submergence tolerance. These were introduced via Marker Assisted Breeding (MAB) and Marker-Assisted Introgression (MAI).
genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: DRR Dhan 62 is an improved version of 'Improved Samba Mahsuri', developed through Marker Assisted Selection (MAS) and Marker-Assisted Introgression to incorporate durable resistance genes and abiotic stress tolerance QTLs. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) from a drought tolerant rice cultivar is noted in connection to DRR Dhan 62's development.

agronomic_performance.yield: Reported yields from IIRR, Hyderabad trials include ranges such as 24.20-25.90 t/ha and 44.70-45.00 t/ha. It is generally described as a high-yielding variety, with yield performance evaluated under stress-prone conditions.
agronomic_performance.stability: The variety's release for a wide range of states and its multi-stress tolerance traits suggest good adaptability across different environments.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: DRR Dhan 62 is suitable for irrigated and transplanted cultivation systems. It also shows adaptation to areas affected by low soil phosphorus and saline conditions.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: It is a fine-grain type rice variety known for its excellent cooking quality. It is an improved version of Improved Samba Mahsuri.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: Performance data for DRR Dhan 62 have been reported in the Draft Proceedings of the 58th and 59th Annual Rice Group Meetings (AICRIP-intranet.in), with trials conducted by ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad.

drought.details: Dubraj Selection 1 is a short duration drought tolerant rice variety suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and drought-prone areas. It exhibits tolerance to abiotic stresses including drought. It is listed among SS (Sugarcane Sett) and Drought tolerant varieties.

heat.details: The variety shows tolerance to abiotic stresses, specifically including heat. It has been included in screening trials for high temperature tolerance in rice genotypes.

salinity.details: Dubraj Selection 1 is reported to be tolerant to salinity. Its suitability for areas requiring saline water irrigation has been noted, and it has been a subject in studies related to yield and salinity tolerance in rice.

flood.details: While submergence tolerance is explicitly stated, general flood tolerance beyond submergence is not detailed in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: Dubraj Selection 1 is tolerant to leaf blast and neck blast.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety shows tolerance to White-backed Planthopper (WBPH).

agronomic_details.yield: The average yield for Dubraj Selection 1 is reported as 60-65 Quintals per hectare (Q/ha). Various trial results show varying yield contributions, indicating its performance across different experimental settings.
agronomic_details.stability: The variety's widespread evaluation in Annual Rice Group Meetings (ARGM) proceedings and IIRR Annual Reports across diverse agro-climatic conditions (irrigated, rainfed, semi-deep water, drought-prone, saline) suggests a degree of adaptability and stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Chhattisgarh, Dubraj Selection 1 is adapted to irrigated, direct sown rainfed conditions, short duration drought-prone areas, semi-deep water, and rainfed uplands. It is also suitable for rainfed lowland rice with medium water depth under anaerobic direct conditions and marginal lands.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Dubraj Selection 1 is a Non-Basmati variety. Its grains are described as Long Slender (LS) and aromatic.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Extensive field trials have been conducted for Dubraj Selection 1, as evidenced by its repeated inclusion and performance data in the draft proceedings of the 55th, 58th, and 59th Annual Rice Group Meetings and various annual reports of ICAR-IIRR (Indian Institute of Rice Research). These trials have assessed its performance under various stress conditions (drought, heat, submergence, salinity) and different planting systems.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (QTL, SNP, SSR) are detailed for Dubraj Selection 1 in the provided results. Stress tolerance traits are noted to be highly polygenic.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs or their effects are identified for Dubraj Selection 1.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS) is mentioned in the context of research for drought, heat, and submergence stress tolerance, implying its potential application or relevance to this variety. The SUB1A gene, known for submergence tolerance, is also mentioned in proximity to Dubraj Selection 1 in research contexts.

drought.details: No drought tolerance rating found. The Kaipad review describes the variety as suited to flood-prone and water-scarce environments, but this is an adaptation statement, not a tested drought-tolerance result. No drought mechanisms were reported.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources.

salinity.details: KAU varieties-released table states tolerance of medium salinity. The variety was designed for saline-prone Kaipad fields and is described as saline-tolerant in the Kaipad review. It is reported as suited to coastal saline and flooded areas. In a hydroponic NaCl seedling study of ten rice varieties (Ezhome-1 and Ezhome-2 from KAU Trissur), low Na+/K+ ratio and antioxidant activity were linked to tolerance; this study is included under the Ezhome-1 name in the digest. Landraces used as salinity donors in the breeding programme were reported to differ in salinity tolerance mechanism (molecular evidence). The digest notes that the Pokkali-differing mechanism applies to Ezhome-2 and is excluded here.

flood.details: KAU varieties-released table lists tolerance of flooding. The Kaipad review describes suitability for flood-prone environments. The Journal of Organics paper reports suitability for flooded areas. No degree of flood tolerance (e.g., duration of submergence or yield under flood) was found.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to sheath blight and bacterial leaf blight (KAU varieties-released table). A Kaipad farm-level observation reported no pest or disease incidence under Kaipad field conditions; this is not a formal resistance rating and applies only to the described field condition.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant to gall midge, leaf folder and case worm; moderately resistant to whorl maggot (KAU varieties-released table). Farm-level Kaipad observation reported no pest incidence under Kaipad field conditions; not a formal rating.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield of 3.5 t/ha under close-planted, no-management Kaipad conditions, about 70% above local cultivars (Wikipedia). The Journal of Organics paper describes high grain and straw yield, without figures in the digest.

drought.details: No drought tolerance rating found. The Kaipad review describes the variety as suited to flood-prone and water-scarce environments, but this is an adaptation statement, not a tested drought-tolerance result. No drought mechanisms were reported.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources.

salinity.details: KAU varieties-released table states tolerance of medium salinity. The variety was designed for saline-prone Kaipad fields and is described as saline-tolerant in the Kaipad review. It is reported as suited to coastal saline and flooded areas. In a hydroponic NaCl seedling study of ten rice varieties (Ezhome-1 and Ezhome-2 from KAU Trissur), low Na+/K+ ratio and antioxidant activity were linked to tolerance; this study is included under the Ezhome-1 name in the digest. Landraces used as salinity donors in the breeding programme were reported to differ in salinity tolerance mechanism (molecular evidence). The digest notes that the Pokkali-differing mechanism applies to Ezhome-2 and is excluded here.

flood.details: KAU varieties-released table lists tolerance of flooding. The Kaipad review describes suitability for flood-prone environments. The Journal of Organics paper reports suitability for flooded areas. No degree of flood tolerance (e.g., duration of submergence or yield under flood) was found.

submergence.details: Not found in searched sources. Flood tolerance evidence is not equivalent to submergence tolerance, and no submergence-specific trait or gene was reported.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: EZHOME 1 (Rice)

Name note: The CSC release name is "EZHOME 1" (written "Ezhome-1" in sources). The seednet_variety_name is Unknown, and I did not run a search on the Seednet portal, so no Seednet evidence was obtained. Every finding below refers to the name Ezhome-1 / EZHOME 1 in rice from Kerala Agricultural University (KAU). Searches returned no evidence for a separate Seednet name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerant of medium salinity and flooding, per the KAU varieties-released table -- https://rarsvni.kau.in/basic-page/varieties-released
Designed for saline-prone Kaipad fields in Kerala, with non-lodging, non-shattering, awnless grains -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezhome_Rice
Described as suited to flood-prone and water-scarce environments, and as saline-tolerant, in the Kaipad review -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/405801656_KAIPAD_-_Unique_Rice_Tract_of_Kerala_India
Reported as suited to coastal saline and flooded areas, with a shorter duration than the local land race -- https://jorganics.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/jo214.pdf
Included in a hydroponic NaCl seedling study of ten rice varieties (Ezhome-1 and Ezhome-2 from KAU Trissur), which linked low Na+/K+ ratio and antioxidant activity to tolerance -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/ARCC012
Non-lodging, which is a stated trait in several sources -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2025.1561280/full

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to gall midge, leaf folder and case worm; moderately resistant to whorl maggot, sheath blight and bacterial leaf blight -- https://rarsvni.kau.in/basic-page/varieties-released
Farm-level Kaipad observation: no pest or disease incidence reported under Kaipad field conditions -- https://farmextensionmanager.com/rice-variety-information-kaippad-tracts
Note: the no-incidence statement in the Kaipad field observation applies to the field condition described and is not a formal resistance rating.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Duration of 135-145 days, with release at PRS Panniyur, per Farm Extension Manager -- https://farmextensionmanager.com/rice-variety-information-kaippad-tracts
Duration of 130-135 days, with high grain and straw yield, per the Journal of Organics paper -- https://jorganics.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/jo214.pdf
Average yield of 3.5 t/ha under close-planted, no-management Kaipad conditions, about 70% above local cultivars -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezhome_Rice
Average of 18-20 tillers per plant and about 21 panicles per plant -- https://kerala-karshakan-e-journal (FIB Kerala KKE May 2025) -- https://fibkerala.gov.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/KKE%20MAY%202025.pdf
Entries from AICRP National Saline-Alkaline Screening trials are referenced in the Journal of Organics paper, but the trial figures are not visible in the retrieved text -- https://jorganics.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/jo214.pdf
Yield-gap study on farmers' fields comparing Ezhome-1 with and without shrimp rotation (21% of potential yield gap without shrimp) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342372967_Traditional_Rice_Cultivation_in_Kerala
Cooking quality described as non-sticky and palatable, and nutrient quality as higher than local check -- https://jorganics.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/jo214.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Hybrid-derived from a Jaya x Kuthiru cross -- https://fibkerala.gov.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/KKE%20MAY%202025.pdf
Alternative parentage description: Jaya as female parent crossed with a traditional land race as male parent -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/405801656_KAIPAD_-_Unique_Rice_Tract_of_Kerala_India
Breeding-line code JK 70 listed for Ezhome-1 (Ezhome-2 is Jo 345) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/405801656_KAIPAD_-_Unique_Rice_Tract_of_Kerala_India
Breeding method: combined conventional breeding with participatory plant breeding, carried out in farmers' fields; developed through organic plant breeding -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezhome_Rice
Landraces used as salinity donors in a breeding programme, with molecular evidence that the two donor landraces differ in salinity tolerance mechanism -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/405801656_KAIPAD_-_Unique_Rice_Tract_of_Kerala_India
Salinity tolerance mechanism in the Orkayama-derived line Ezhome-2 was reported to differ from Pokkali (this applies to Ezhome-2, not Ezhome-1) -- https://kau.in/people/vanaja-t-dr-0
No QTL, marker, or genome-resource study naming Ezhome-1 was found -- No evidence found after search.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Dr. T. Vanaja is listed by KAU as principal breeder and principal investigator for Ezhome-1 through Ezhome-4 and Mithila -- https://kau.in/people/vanaja-t-dr-0
Development led by Kerala Agricultural University, with farmer participation from Ezhome panchayat -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezhome_Rice
Breeding ran for about 20 years from 2000 at the Regional Agricultural Research Station, Pilicode, Kasaragod -- https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/projects/feedingcity/2023/09/25/exploring-the-unique-kaipad-ecosystem/
Wikipedia lists the Regional Agricultural Institute at Pilicode, Kasaragod as the Ezhome paddy site -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezhome_Rice
Farm Extension Manager lists station of release as PRS Panniyur (conflicts with the Pilicode attribution) -- https://farmextensionmanager.com/rice-variety-information-kaippad-tracts

CONTACT DETAILS
Dr. T. Vanaja, Principal Breeder and Principal Investigator, KAU people page; no email, phone, or postal address appears in the retrieved text -- https://kau.in/people/vanaja-t-dr-0
Institute-level contact: none found for KAU Pilicode RARS or KAU Directorate of Research in the retrieved results -- No evidence found after search.
The Malabar Kaipad Farmers' Society (Ezhome Grama Panchayat, Ezhome P.O, Kannur-670 334) is a farmers' body, not KAU, so I have not recorded it as a breeder contact -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338453176_Agricultural_Innovation_and_the_Protection_of_Traditional_Rice_Varieties_Kerala_a_Case_Study

PUBLICATIONS

Cited as sources for Ezhome-1 and Ezhome-2 in the Oryza review; full titles not retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/B-Mohan-Kumar-2/publication/352851690_Ecological_and_historical_perspectives_of_rice_cultivation_in_Kerala_a_synthesis/links/60e14521299bf1ea9ede0a6d/Ecological-and-historical-perspectives-of-rice-cultivation-in-Kerala-a-synthesis.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CNR-2 (CSC name) / GNR-2 (Seednet name), rice

Search budget: all 4 allowed web_search calls were used (3 for CNR-2, 1 for GNR-2 seed availability). None returned evidence about either name, so most headings below read "No evidence found." The GNR-2 release, breeder, and research topics were not searched, so their "No evidence found" entries mean only that the 4-call cap was reached. A follow-up run is needed for those.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searched "CNR-2 rice variety release recommended states maturity yield"; results were unrelated US and IRRI material.
DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. Same search as above; no CNR-2 or GNR-2 resistance data returned.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. Same search as above; no maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for CNR-2 or GNR-2.
GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The CNR-2 QTL search returned a 2020 Agronomy paper on grain-number QTL (https://doi.org/10.3390/agronomy10020180), but it does not mention CNR-2 or GNR-2, so it is not recorded as evidence.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. Searched "CNR-2 rice breeder developed by institute"; results were a hybrid rice breeding manual and nothing on this variety. No GNR-2 breeder search was run.
CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute, or contact page for either name was returned.
PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The CNR-2 research search returned no papers, AICRP reports, or KrishiKosh theses on this variety.
SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Searched "GNR-2 paddy variety seed availability"; the only Indian result was a Nuziveedu Seeds generic paddy catalogue page (https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/paddy-variety/), which does not name GNR-2 or CNR-2, so it is not recorded as evidence.
RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. No notification or release record for either name was returned. The input fields "Not specified" for institution, release year, states, and parentage remain unresolved.

Suggested next steps: search seednet.gov.in and the ICAR/CSC release notifications for "GNR-2" and "CNR-2" separately, and check KrishiKosh and the AICRP rice annual reports. Also verify whether "CNR" and "GNR" refer to the same variety, since the two names may be a transcription difference.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The GRH-2 pages returned only general descriptions. Searches also returned Ezhome and Golden Rice pages, which are unrelated. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/61ec6-annual-report-proof-2017-18.pdf (searched; GRH-2 named only as a new variety)

DISEASE AND PEST -- GRH-2 is moderately resistant against bacterial leaf blight, leaf blast, grain discolouration and sheath rot. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- The proposed hybrid is tolerant to insect pest like BPH, WBPH, leaf folder and stem borer. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- GNR-2 (Seednet name): No evidence found. The Main Rice Research Centre page lists GNR-2 only as one of seven improved varieties, with no resistance data. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- Green rice leafhopper (GRH) gene and QTL papers were returned. They concern a different pest and different rice lines, so they are discarded. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00122-006-0270-x

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Mid-late rice hybrid GRH-2 (6129 kg/ha) performed well in Gujarat state, where it exhibited overall 7.1% and 17.9% grain yield superiority over the best hybrid check US 312, and best variety GNR-3, respectively. (season 2017-18, as stated on the page) -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Grain quality: medium slender grain rice hybrid GRH-2 contains intermediate amylose and high head rice recovery. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Release timing conflict: the NAU 2017-18 annual report lists GRH-2 among two rice varieties developed that year, while the CSC release date is 2019-06-01. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/61ec6-annual-report-proof-2017-18.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- GNR-2 agronomy and trial data: No evidence found. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for GRH-2 or GNR-2 marker, QTL or parentage studies. Parentage is not specified in the record, and the searches did not establish it. Search returned only unrelated GRH resistance genes and Golden Rice work. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11769587/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: The NAU has released 105 high yielding good quality varieties of various crops including 18 varieties of cotton, 20 varieties of rice. -- https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Station: the Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari, which is the breeding station named on the GRH-2 information sheet. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Breeder name: No GRH-2-specific breeder name was found. The ResearchGate profile of Vipul P. Patel, Rice Breeder at NAU, does not mention GRH-2, so it is not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Staff at the GRH-2 seed MoU signing: Dr. T. R. Ahlawat (Director of Research), Dr. V. P. Patel (Associate Research Scientist, RRRS Vyara), Dr. P. B. Patel (Associate Research Scientist, MRRC Navsari) and Prof. Sheetal Patel (Assistant Research Scientist, RRRS Vyara). They are listed as present, not as breeders. -- https://nausagar.nau.in/the-first-of-its-kind-mou-between-navsari-agricultural-university-and-a-private-sector-seed-company-indo-us-biotech-ltd-ahmedabad-for-seed-production-and-marketing-of-high-yielding-and-medium-slender-grain-rice-hybrid-grh-2

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institution address: Navsari Agricultural University, Eru Char Rasta, Dandi Road, Navsari – 396 450 (Gujarat) INDIA. -- https://aems.nau.in/Main/view_experiment/1960
CONTACT DETAILS -- Vipulkumar Pranjivanbhai Patel, PI, Regional Rice Research Station (Vyara), email vppatel13@nau.in, mobile 8469417374. This is listed for an AVT-2 Aerobic rice trial (2023) and is not tied to GRH-2 on the page, so treat it as an unverified institutional contact. -- https://aems.nau.in/Main/view_experiment/1960

EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNR-3 (rice / PADDY (DHAN))
Variety name (CSC minutes) and Seednet name are both "GNR-3", so one name covers both. Only 4 web_search calls were allowed and all 4 ran, but I could only read ~400 characters of each result, so the findings below are partial. Seednet portal pages were not found.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for GNR-3.
DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page on GNR-3 blast, BLB, BPH or other resistance was returned.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found for field-trial, yield or maturity data. The one GNR-3 paper located (see PUBLICATIONS) appears to concern processing or value addition, not field performance.
GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage only. A GNR-3 record describes it as derived from the cross IR-28 x GR-4 -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/ohs-2.3.1/index.php/record/view/213880 (the Seednet "Not specified" parentage is therefore contradicted by this record, which should be checked). No QTL or marker study was found.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Navsari Agricultural University is the institution in the input record. No breeder or scientist name was found tied to GNR-3 in the snippets read. The Navsari Main Rice Research Centre document surfaced (https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf) but its visible text did not name GNR-3, so I have not attributed it to this variety. Treat it as an unverified lead.
CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No official email, phone, address or contact page for GNR-3 or its developing division was confirmed.
PUBLICATIONS:
Authors not captured (year not captured). A paddy variety GNR-3 suitable for value addition. ICAR KRISHI record -- https://krishi.icar.gov.in/ohs-2.3.1/index.php/record/view/213880
Authors not captured (year not captured). A paddy variety GNR-3 suitable for value addition. ResearchGate (PDF) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374419133_A_paddy_variety_GNR-3_suitable_for_value_addition
SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for GNR-3. A Kerala search result (kau.in, Pattambi paddy seed availability) concerns a different station and was discarded.
RECOMMENDED STATES: Gujarat, per the input record only (recommended_states_raw). No search page confirmed this.

Note: the search budget was exhausted during a further attempt to read full page text, so the gaps above are due to the tool limit, not confirmed absence. Next steps: open the two KRISHI/ResearchGate pages for authors, year and full text, and check seednet.gov.in directly for release notification and parentage.

disease_resistance.summary: No blast, brown planthopper (BPH) or bacterial blight reaction for GNR-4 was found in searched sources. Not found in searched sources for any disease resistance rating.

pest_resistance.summary: Stem borer: GNR-4 showed a moderately susceptible reaction under natural field conditions at the Main Rice Research Centre (MRRC), Navsari, alongside GR-4 and varieties 6, 9 and 103. No other pest reactions found.

agronomic_details.yield: Under irrigated transplanted conditions in South Gujarat, GNR-4 averaged 4409 kg/ha, which is 103% above Lal Kada and 11.2% above GR-11.
agronomic_details.stability: A location-wise comparison table (PET Kharif 2009, Navsari and other South Gujarat sites) against Lal Kada and GR-11 exists, but the values are not in the retrieved text. Stability across environments: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for transplanted rice in South Gujarat's heavy-rainfall zone (AES-III), according to the NAU Main Rice Research Centre. Adaptation outside South Gujarat: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources for plant morphology. Grain nutritional profile: iron about 91 ppm, dietary fibre about 2.87%, beta-carotene about 0.53 ppm. The NAU document advises spraying a 1% iron solution for bio-fortification.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Tested in kharif seasons 2009 to 2012 through the preliminary evaluation trial, small-scale and large-scale varietal trials, and district trials under transplanted conditions. (2) Under irrigated transplanted conditions in South Gujarat, mean yield of 4409 kg/ha, 103% above Lal Kada and 11.2% above GR-11. (3) Location-wise comparison in PET Kharif 2009 at Navsari and other South Gujarat sites against Lal Kada and GR-11 (table values not retrieved). (4) Stem borer natural-field screening at MRRC Navsari: moderately susceptible.
