EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNR-4 (rice, paddy)

Name note: The CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "GNR-4", so one search set covered both. No Seednet portal page for GNR-4 was retrieved. All evidence below refers to the name GNR-4 (Gujarat Navsari Rice-4).

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to GNR-4. The searches returned only a generic salinity meta-analysis and unrelated rice papers. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11003983/ (not GNR-4-specific)

DISEASE AND PEST
GNR-4 showed a moderately susceptible reaction to stem borer under natural field conditions at the Main Rice Research Centre, Navsari, alongside GR-4 and varieties 6, 9 and 103. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
The Mistry and Patel paper includes a table on GNR-4's reaction to major insect pests at MRRC Navsari, but the retrieved text does not show the scores. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
No blast, BPH or bacterial blight reaction for GNR-4 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Derived from NAUR-1 x Lal Kada, crossed at the Main Paddy Research Station, Navsari, in kharif 2005. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Bulked to F5 in summer 2009. Tested in the kharif seasons 2009 to 2012 through the preliminary evaluation trial, small-scale and large-scale varietal trials, and district trials under transplanted conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Under irrigated transplanted conditions in South Gujarat it averaged 4409 kg/ha, which is 103% above Lal Kada and 11.2% above GR-11. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Location-wise comparison table (PET Kharif 2009, Navsari and other South Gujarat sites) against Lal Kada and GR-11. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Nutritional profile: iron about 91 ppm, dietary fibre about 2.87%, beta-carotene about 0.53 ppm. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Maturity duration: not found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL, marker or molecular studies on GNR-4. The GNS4/DWARF11 and gsnl4 papers concern other rice lines and were excluded. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12284-017-0171-4 (excluded, different variety)
Pedigree information is in the AGRONOMY section above. Parentage field "Not specified" should be updated to NAUR-1 x Lal Kada. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by Navsari Agricultural University. The authors listed on the GNR-4 paper are Pramodkumar Mistry and Pathik Patel, both at Navsari Agricultural University, with Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari, given as the affiliation. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
The NAU crop-improvement listing names GNR-4 among the NAU-developed rice varieties. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
Vipul P. Patel (rice breeder, Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara) and P. B. Patel (Main Rice Research Centre) were excluded. Neither page links them to GNR-4.

CONTACT DETAILS
Names and roles as found: Pramodkumar Mistry (author, Navsari Agricultural University); Pathik Patel (author, Navsari Agricultural University; the paper identifies P. B. Patel as corresponding author). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Institution: Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari Agricultural University, Navsari 396 450, Gujarat, India. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
Institute page URL: https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676 (no email or phone retrieved).
Official email: not found. Phone: not found. Postal address of the MRRC division: not found beyond the city and postal code above.

PUBLICATIONS
Mistry, P. M. and Patel, P. B. (2014). Bio-fortified rice variety Gujarat Navsari Rice-4 (GNR-4). Journal not identified (ResearchGate listing dated January 2014) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4 (DOI not found)
Excluded: "A paddy variety GNR-3 suitable for value addition" (Mistry et al.). Its title and main cross concern GNR-3, although its abstract text mentions GNR-4. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374419133_A_paddy_variety_GNR-3_suitable_for_value_addition
No AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or peer-reviewed paper specific to GNR-4 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The searches returned seed listings for other varieties and firms: the Gujarat State Seeds Corporation (Gurabini) crop page lists GR4, GR11, GNR-3 and NAUR-1 for paddy, not GNR-4 (http://www.gurabini.com/cropDetails.aspx?id=1). The IFFDC and Nuziveedu paddy lists do not include GNR-4 (https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed; https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/paddy-variety/). The GSFC seeds page names paddy but no GNR-4 variety (https://www.gsfclimited.com/seeds).

RECOMMENDED STATES
Recommended for South Gujarat: the NAU Main Rice Research Centre advises transplanted-rice growers in South Gujarat's heavy-rainfall zone (AES-III) to grow GNR-4 for its higher net returns, and to spray a 1% iron solution for bio-fortification. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
Registration: the same NAU document says GNR-4 was registered with PPV&FRA, but it gives no registration number or date. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
Release notification date for 2016-08-12 (CSC minutes): not confirmed by any retrieved source.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GJ-103 (Seednet name GR-103), sorghum, NAU Main Sorghum Research Station, Surat

Searches run (4): "GJ-103 sorghum variety"; "GJ-103 sorghum breeder Navsari Agricultural University"; "GJ-103 sorghum GR-11 x Mahsuri research"; "GR-103 sorghum seed availability Gujarat". Neither GJ-103 nor GR-103 appeared in any result that names this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. The variety search returned only pages on other sorghum lines, such as GDJ 1 (Banas Surya), which is a different variety, and foreign or unrelated products.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. The GDJ 1 (Banas Surya) page reports disease and borer scores for that other variety, so it was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. Excluded as other varieties or crops: GDJ 1 (Banas Surya) multi-location yield data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358562511_A_novel_high_yielding_dual-purpose_sorghum_variety_GDJ_1Banas_Surya_for_semi-arid_region_of_Gujarat ; CoFS 29 fodder trial, Kheda -- https://www.gjoee.org/papers/1266.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. The parentage GR-11 x Mahsuri did not appear in any result. Excluded: a sorghum GWAS and an unrelated Ma/Dw gene paper, neither about this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No breeder name found under GJ-103 or GR-103. The NAU "About" page is institution-level and says The Navsari Zone of erstwhile GAU had attained the status of independent State Agricultural University (SAU) with the promulgation of Gujarat Agricultural Universities Act 2004; it does not name this variety. -- https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676
Excluded: a 2025 AGRESCO proceedings page lists NAU's endorsed sorghum variety GNJ-1, which is a different variety -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//18th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_773.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder or station contact found under GJ-103 or GR-103. Institute-level fallback only (this page does not name the variety): Navsari Agricultural University, Navsari – 396450, as printed on a KVK Navsari Scientific Advisory Committee report -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/d9016-14-th-sac-21-final-reoprt.pdf
No email or phone for the Main Sorghum Research Station, Athwa Farm, Surat was found.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report, or journal paper naming this variety appeared.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103. The results were general sorghum grain dealers in Ahmedabad (for example, https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sorghum-22836423391.html) and a state-wise seed supplier list that names the Gujarat State Seeds Corporation generically, not for this variety (https://nddb.coop/farmer/animal-nutrition/state-wise-list-of-seeds-producer-supplier). None are variety-specific, so none are recorded as seed sources.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found under GJ-103 or GR-103 in the search results. The only statement of Gujarat as the recommended state comes from the supplied variety record, not from a web source.

Gaps to close next: the CSC release minutes for GJ-103 (2025), the Seednet entry for GR-103, and the NAU Main Sorghum Research Station page. These were not reachable with the four searches allowed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GNR-6 / GR-6 (rice, Navsari Agricultural University) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: the search results name this variety as GNR-6 (variety code NVSR-2031). No result for the Seednet name GR-6 was relevant, so every finding below refers to GNR-6 unless marked otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to GNR-6. A NAU Main Rice Research Centre page lists GNR-6 among its released varieties but gives no stress data for it -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- The same NAU page has a row for GNR-6 that says it performed well across Gujarat. The surrounding text is fragmented, so the salt-affected-area statement nearby cannot be safely attributed to GNR-6 -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- The NAU Main Rice Research Centre page contains reaction descriptions (moderate resistance to bacterial leaf blight, grain discoloration and sheath rot; tolerance to BPH; moderate resistance to stem borer, leaf folder and sheath mite). The text is fragmented and the row layout does not confirm these apply to GNR-6, so treat them as unverified -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- GNR-6 is listed in the ICAR Annual Report 2019-20 as suitable for rainfed transplanted conditions in Gujarat -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/AR-2019-20.pdf
- A yield (65 to 70 q/ha) and maturity (120 to 125 days) entry appears in the same ICAR report, but the excerpt sits between the GNR-6 and GNR-7 rows and cannot be confidently assigned to GNR-6. Not recorded as a GNR-6 finding -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/AR-2019-20.pdf
- A field experiment at the Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara (2018 to 2020) compared GNR 6 with Purna, GR 5 and IR 28 under 100% and 50% recommended nitrogen with FYM. The results are truncated, so no yield values are recorded -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27
- The Scribd copy of an RRRS variety list names GNR-6 among notable varieties released since 2014, but gives no agronomic data in the excerpt. Its original source is unverified -- https://www.scribd.com/document/867808197/6c31c-Varities-English

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL or marker study for GNR-6 found.
- A heterosis study on GNR-4 (Mistry and Patel, NAU) reports that the cross NVSR-398 x GNR-6 was among the top three heterotic hybrids for grain yield per plant, evaluated at Main Rice Research Centre, Navsari in kharif 2018. This shows GNR-6 used as a parent; it is not a QTL study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Navsari Agricultural University. The NAU Main Rice Research Centre lists GNR-6 among its seven released varieties, and the centre is in SWMRU, Navsari -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Station: Main Rice Research Centre, Navsari (NAU) is named as the centre for paddy improvement, and the Regional Rice Research Station at Vyara is also a rice-breeding station -- https://nau.in/unithome/Regional%20Rice%20Research%20Station%20Vyara
- Breeder name: No evidence found that names the lead breeder of GNR-6. Vipul P. Patel's ResearchGate profile identifies him as a rice breeder at NAU's Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara, but no page links him to GNR-6's development. He is not attributed as breeder -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27
- No evidence found for the breeder or developer named on an NAU variety page for GNR-6.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Navsari Agricultural University. No official email or phone number for the rice programme was found in the results. Address details found: Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari (from the centre information page) -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara (Tapi district): the page gives the location (about 4 km from Gandevi town) but no postal address or phone -- https://nau.in/unithome/Regional%20Rice%20Research%20Station%20Vyara
- Institute contact page: No evidence found for an NAU contact-page URL in the results. The NAU about page is at https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676 but contains no contact details.
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Patel, V. P., and co-authors (years not shown in results). Field experiment at Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara, 2018 to 2020, comparing GNR 6 with Purna, GR 5 and IR 28. Journal/report not identified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27
- Mistry, P., and Patel, P. (year not shown in results). Bio-fortified rice variety Gujarat Navsari Rice-4 (GNR-4). Journal not identified. The paper names GNR-6 as a parent in a top heterotic cross. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report specific to GNR-6 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The Gujarat State Seeds Corporation crop-details page lists GNR-6 in a kharif paddy table with a price per 25 kg. The page is undated, so current availability is unconfirmed -- http://www.gurabini.com/cropDetails.aspx?id=1
- The Gujcomasol page lists paddy varieties GR-13, Gurjary, GNR-3 and Mahisagar but not GNR-6 -- https://www.gujcomasol.com/seeds.php
- No evidence found for GNR-6 at Seednet, KVKs, or private dealers. The GSFC and Nuziveedu paddy pages do not name GNR-6.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gujarat. The ICAR Annual Report 2019-20 lists GNR-6 with Gujarat as its state -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/AR-2019-20.pdf
- The NAU Main Rice Research Centre page says GNR-6 performed well across Gujarat -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf

Searches run: 4 (release and traits; breeder and institution; research and trials; seed availability). The Seednet portal was not reached directly, and the GR-6 name returned nothing relevant.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNR-7 (release/evidence name) / GR-7 (Seednet name), NVSR-6128, rice, Navsari Agricultural University

Search note: four web_search queries were run (variety, breeder/institution, research papers, seed availability). Most results were about other crops or varieties (for example Gamagora 7, Ratnagiri 7, Ghd7 gene papers) and were discarded. Unless stated otherwise, the findings below refer to GNR-7 (NVSR-6128), which the source names directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The variety search returned only unrelated pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
- GNR-7 is moderately resistant against bacterial leaf blight, grain discoloration and sheath rot. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- It showed tolerant to pest like BPH and moderate (the sentence is cut off in the source) -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Trial result: GNR-7 (5740 kg/ha) performed very well in South Gujarat, where it exhibited overall 13.0 %, 22.8% and 12.4 % grain yield superiority with easy threshability over the checks GNR-2, GR-11 and GAR-13, respectively. The source dates the trial to 2016-17. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Plant type: It has short slender grain, high productive tillers and number of grains per panicle with good quality characters. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Maturity, duration and parentage (GR-3 x Basmati-370): No evidence found in the search results.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The QTL and gene results returned were for Ghd7, GL7 and other genes in unrelated rice germplasm.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety is listed among the seven improved varieties released by the Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari Agricultural University. Seven improved varieties (NAUR-1, GNR-2, GNR-3, GNR-4, Purna, GNR-5, GNR-6, GNR-7 and GR-15) and two hybrids (GNRH-1 and GRH-2) of rice have been developed there. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- The same document links the code and name directly: Rice variety NVSR-6128 (GNR-7) recommended for normal rice growing areas of South Gujarat. -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. A ResearchGate profile for Vipul P. Patel lists a rice breeder at NAU's Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara. That page does not mention GNR-7, so it is not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27
- Release year: the 2018-08-10 date from the input could not be confirmed by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level address (from a publication address for the same centre, not a GNR-7 page): Main Rice Research Centre, SWMRU, Navsari Agricultural University, Navsari 396 450, Gujarat, India. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374418877_BIO-FORTIFIED_RICE_VARIETY_GUJARAT_NAVSARI_RICE-4_GNR-4
- Also listed as the Main Rice Research Centre in the centre information sheet: "SWMRU, Navsari Agricultural University, Navsari." -- https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/952d2-ic_mrrc_information.pdf
- Breeder email, phone and personal contact: No evidence found. A phone number found in the results (9426960246) belongs to a soil scientist at a different NAU unit and was discarded.

PUBLICATIONS
- No GNR-7-specific paper found.
- Ambiguous, not attributed to GNR-7: a paper on GNR-3 uses a check labelled "GR-7" (the Seednet name). It is unclear whether that check is the same variety. Authors and year not shown in the result. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374419133_A_paddy_variety_GNR-3_suitable_for_value_addition
- AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses and DOIs: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Gujarat State Seeds Corporation (GURABIN) lists "GR-7" among its kharif paddy varieties, with no price shown and only "Place Demand" as the availability note. The listing does not state that GR-7 is the same variety as GNR-7. -- http://www.gurabini.com/cropDetails.aspx?id=1

EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNR-9 (Seednet name GR-9; variety code Lalkada Gold), rice/paddy, Gujarat

Search budget note: I ran four web_search queries, one per required topic plus the optional seed-availability query. A further batch of name-check queries was blocked by the tool's usage limit, so no additional evidence was gathered.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The four searches returned no page naming GNR-9, GR-9 or Lalkada Gold with stress-tolerance data. The results were a general rice-types nutrition article, a BPH-resistant hybrid restorer-line paper (PMC5461369), a glutaredoxin review in rice (PMC10707574), and a rice seed supply article (farmprogress.com).

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The same search results apply; none named this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No page with maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The parentage (SATHI 34-36 x CR-544-1-2) did not appear in any result. The PMC5461369 hit concerns other restorer lines and is not attributed to this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No page named a breeder or scientist for GNR-9/GR-9. The institution (Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara, Navsari Agricultural University) did not appear in any result.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No official NAU, Vyara station, or ICAR contact page was returned.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis naming this variety was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. No Seednet listing, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer page for GNR-9, GR-9 or Lalkada Gold was returned. The seed-related hit (farmprogress.com) concerns a US rice seed market and is unrelated.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. Gujarat is the state given in the release record, but no retrieved page confirmed it.

Recommended next steps: check the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) directly for "GR-9" under PADDY (DHAN), check the CSC/ICAR release notification for the 17 June 2022 release, and query the Navsari Agricultural University Vyara rice station site and KrishiKosh for "GNR-9" or "Lalkada Gold". DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. Same search as above; no page on disease or pest resistance named this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. A ResearchGate profile of Vipul Patel (https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27) describes rainy-season trials in 2018–2020 at the Regional Rice Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University, Vyara, but the snippet names Purna, GR 5 and GNR 6 and does not mention GR 17 (Sardar). Discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The parentage in the request (Gurjari x Jaya, with Gurjari and Jaya lineage) came from the task input, not from any search result, so it is not cited here. No page on QTLs, markers or breeding-line codes was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found for this variety. The breeder query returned the Vipul Patel profile above, which shows an affiliation with the Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara, Navsari Agricultural University (https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vipul-Patel-27). That profile does not name GR 17 (Sardar) as a variety he developed, so it is not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for the Regional Rice Research Station, Vyara, was returned.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The research query returned a ResearchGate entry titled "Computer Vision Based Classification of Indian Gujarat-17 Rice Using Geometrical Features and Cart" (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281962240_Computer_Vision_Based_Classification_of_Indian_Gujarat-17_Rice_Using_Geometrical_Features_and_Cart). It concerns grain classification of a rice named "Gujarat-17", not the GR 17 (Sardar) variety or its release record, so it was discarded as a name resemblance. No authors, year or journal are recorded.

Next steps: check seednet.gov.in under PADDY (DHAN) for code A01022017, the CSC/Gujarat release notification for "GR 17 (Sardar)", and the Navsari Agricultural University Regional Rice Research Station page for breeder names, contacts and seed sales. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The searches returned two different names. The evidence for "Gujarat Anand Rice 22 (Swagat)" comes from AAU pages. The Seednet name "GUJARAT ANAND RICE-2 (IET-21614)" is attached to a different AAU variety, GAR-2 (released 2011). Pages about GAR-2 are therefore not attributed to GAR 22 below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as resistant to white-backed planthopper, yellow stem borer and leaf folder, and resistant to leaf blast and neck blast. Moderately resistant to bacterial leaf blight, sheath rot and grain discoloration -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The search returned no pages on these traits for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Insect resistance (planthopper, stem borer, leaf folder), blast resistance (leaf and neck), and moderate resistance to bacterial leaf blight, sheath rot and grain discoloration are as listed above -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average grain yield of 5613 kg/ha, reported as 22.6% above check GR 7 and 15.1% above check GAR 3 -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- Milling recovery of 72.08% and head rice recovery of 62.80%, at or above the checks -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- Medium maturity, medium plant height, more productive tillers, long slender kernel -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- No multi-location trial, AICRP or on-farm trial results found specifically for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for parentage (GURJARI IET-10750 x IET-14714/1-1-4-1-3-2) or for any QTL or marker study. The searches did not return any page naming this parentage.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Anand Agricultural University, Anand (listed as the source of the variety on the AAU site) -- https://aau.in/variety_released
- The AAU variety page lists the variety under the Department of Agricultural Research and Education and the Main Rice Research Station context, but no named breeder or scientist was found -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- No evidence found for a lead breeder's name.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for a breeder email, phone or personal contact for this variety.
- Institute-level page only: AAU main website -- https://www.aau.in (the search did not return a verified AAU contact page; the Main Vegetable Research Station contact found belongs to a different station and was discarded).

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming GAR 22 (Swagat) was returned. Pages on GAR-13, GAR-14, GAR-2, Gujarat Rice 21 and Gujarat Aerobic Rice 201 were discarded as other varieties.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales pages for this variety. The searches returned only unrelated rice traders and mill listings in Anand, which were discarded.
- Institute variety listing (not a seed-sales page) -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-29/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Recommended for the transplanted rice areas of middle Gujarat -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-rice-22-swagat
- The input record says "Gujarat". The AAU page is narrower (middle Gujarat), so the record should be checked.

RELEASE AND REGISTRATION (discrepancies to resolve)
- Year of release: AAU pages give 2021 (53rd SSSC) -- https://aau.in/variety_released. The input record gives 2022-06-17. These do not agree.
- Seednet name: No page found links "GUJARAT ANAND RICE-2 (IET-21614)" to GAR 22. The PPV&FR and Bihar notified-variety lists tie that name to GAR-2 (2011). The Seednet name in the input record should be checked against the portal. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumforextantnotified-nov-2021.pdf ; https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Variety code "GAR 22: Swagat": the AAU listing uses "Gujarat Anand Rice 22 (Swagat)", which supports the common name. No separate code source was found.

flood.details: Hasanta recorded a maximum reduction in agro-morphological and physiological traits under seven days of submergence stress, indicating low tolerance to submergence (a form of flood stress). Efforts are underway to pyramid submergence tolerance genes into this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Research is being conducted to pyramid three bacterial blight resistance genes into Hasanta through marker-assisted backcross breeding, suggesting the original variety may not possess sufficient resistance to bacterial blight.

pest_resistance.summary: Hasanta is mentioned as a paddy cultivar in studies evaluating resistance and susceptibility to rice root-knot nematode, but its specific reaction is not detailed.

agronomic_details.yield: Quantitative yield data for Hasanta is not specified, but it is studied in the context of optimizing resource use efficiency and weed management to mitigate yield loss.
agronomic_details.stability: Yield stability across environments using AMMI and GGE biplot tools has been evaluated for other lowland rice genotypes, but specific data for Hasanta is not provided.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Odisha. Hasanta has been a test variety in Raipur, Chhattisgarh, in studies evaluating optimum transplanting dates and thermal requirements, suggesting adaptability to different planting windows and regions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Hasanta's agro-morphological and physiological traits have been assessed under submergence stress. It is also subject to biochemical characterization for straw lignocellulose.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Hasanta has been used in field trials concerning integrated nutrient management (INM) practices (e.g., Green Manure + 50% STBNR through inorganics), weed dynamics and management under resource-conserving planting modules (e.g., direct-seeded rice, wet-direct seeded rice), and evaluation of thermal requirements across different transplanting windows.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Genetic markers are actively utilized in marker-assisted backcross breeding for pyramiding submergence tolerance and three bacterial blight resistance genes into the Hasanta variety. genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Gene pyramiding for submergence tolerance and bacterial blight resistance.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated paddy growing areas of Haryana, where the varieties like HKR 127 is grown for timely transplanting.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Resistant to lodging and shattering, responsive to fertilizer application. Seed rate 25 kg/ha for transplanting, fertilizer doses 150:60:60 kg NPK+25 kg ZnSo4/ha; Suitable for timely planting.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Compact plant with long flag leaf, yellow coloured long slender grain, internodes of light green colour, compact panicle.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: It is equally affected by bacterial blight in comparison to HKR 127 and HSD-1.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: It is less infested by plant hopper and equally by leaf folder and stem borer as compared to HKR 127 and HSD-1
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 150:60 kg NP + 25 ZnSo4 apply full dose of P and Zn as basal and N in three split at transplanting, 21 DAT and 42 DAT

agronomic_details.adaptation: Release record: recommended for low hills sub-tropical zone under transplanted irrigated conditions; suitable for early sown crop; tolerates water stress (CSC field, unverified in digest). agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: LONG SLENDER SEED WITH L/B TATIO OF 3.39 ; ONLY TOP PANICLES HAVE SMALL AWN ; EARLIER ANTHESIS DAYS WITH DARKER FOLIAGE THAN JAYA. Digest (AICRIP centre report): semi-dwarf, high-yielding, medium-duration variety with long flag leaf and long slender grain. Digest maturity figure of 145 days differs from the release record range of 135 to 140 days; both are reported here.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Transplanting date trial (academia.edu source, which names HKR-128): under late transplanting, HKR-128 showed about a 31% yield reduction compared with early transplanting on June 15, and it was statistically at par with HKR-127 in yield. (2) Hybrid rice IET/AICRIP-style trial table: HKR-128 appears only as a local check variety across Kaul (KUL) and other centres; check-variety role only, trial yield values not extracted. No other trial results found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
HKR 128 rice: evidence digest

Name note: the CSC/variety_name is HKR 128. The Seednet name is HKR-126, which is a different, separately released Kaul variety. Every search result that names HKR-126 was therefore discarded for HKR 128. The findings below refer to HKR 128 unless marked otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for HKR 128. The only stress-tolerance statements retrieved (10-day water-stress tolerance, salinity responses) concern HKR-126 or other genotypes and were excluded. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for HKR 128. The Kaul AICRIP centre report describes HKR 126 as resistant to stem rot and WBPH and moderately resistant to bacterial blight, but this is not attributed to HKR 128. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
Discarded: "HKR 95-128" is a separate bacterial-blight-resistant genetic stock maintained by NBPGR, not this variety. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- HKR 128 is a semi-dwarf, high-yielding medium-duration variety with long flag leaf and long slender grain, maturing in 145 days, and was described as tested in farmers' fields and likely for general cultivation in Haryana. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
Under late transplanting, HKR-128 showed about a 31% yield reduction versus early transplanting (June 15), and it was statistically at par with HKR-127 in yield. -- https://www.academia.edu/35376988/Effects_of_different_dates_of_transplanting_on_yield_attributes_yields_and_quality_of_non_scented_varieties_of_rice_Oryza_sativa
HKR-128 appears as a local check variety in an IET/AICRIP-style hybrid rice trial table, with yield data across Kaul (KUL) and other centres. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/HybridRiceProgressReport-2021.pdf (check-variety role only; trial yield values not extracted)

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for HKR 128. Parentage in the release record (NAMSAGNI 19 / IR-4215 / IR 5953 derived from IRRI F4 material, selected under artificial bacterial blight inoculation) was not corroborated by any retrieved page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- HKR 128 was developed at Rice Research Station, Kaul (district Kaithal, Haryana), under Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCSHAU), Hisar. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
The Hisar university page lists HKR 128 among seven non-scented varieties released by the Kaul station. -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-23
Lead breeder name for HKR 128: No evidence found. The retrieved pages name a "Rice Breeder & Head, RRS Kaul" without a name, and the names of other Kaul staff appear only in unrelated acknowledgments; none are attributed to HKR 128.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No individual breeder contact found. Institute-level information only:
Rice Research Station, Kaul, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Kaul 132021, India (address as printed on the Kaul station credit line). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8402606_Genetic_analysis_of_Indian_aromatic_and_quality_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_germplasm_using_panels_of_fluorescently-labeled_microsatellite_markers
Institute home page: https://hau.ac.in/page/home-23
Station information PDF (infrastructure, campus details): https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1716344337.pdf
Email and phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Lavanya, A. and Pinky, B. (2019). Physical and Nutritional Quality Evaluation of Different Rice varieties (includes HKR-128 from RRS Kaul). International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences, 8(6) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-6-2019/A.%20Lavanya%20and%20Boora%20Pinky.pdf
Author(s) not retrieved (year not retrieved). Effects of different dates of transplanting on yield attributes, yields and quality of non-scented varieties of rice (Oryza sativa L.). Journal not retrieved -- https://www.academia.edu/35376988/Effects_of_different_dates_of_transplanting_on_yield_attributes_yields_and_quality_of_non_scented_varieties_of_rice_Oryza_sativa
Author(s) not retrieved (year not retrieved). Kaul Rice Research Station centre report, AICRIP (HKR 128 release description). -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
Excluded: the HKR-126 callus regeneration paper (Callus induction and efficient regeneration from recalcitrant of indica rice varieties) concerns HKR-126 and HKR-120, not HKR 128. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316503793_Callus_induction_and_efficient_regeneration_from_recalcitrant_of_indica_rice_varieties

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for HKR 128 or HKR-126 from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or Seednet. The retrieved listings are for PR 126 (a PAU variety, different crop variety) or Hasco/Hari branded products and were discarded. Searched once with the HKR-126 and Haryana terms. Recommend checking the CCSHAU Rice Research Station seed sales and the Seednet portal directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Haryana, with an HAU statement that HKR 128 occupied substantial area in Haryana and other North Indian states. -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-23
Release status is unclear: the AICRIP centre report says HKR 128 was likely to be released for general cultivation in the state, and the release year in the record (2019) was not confirmed by any retrieved source. HKR-126 appears in a Haryana notified-paddy list (2022), but HKR 128 was not seen on that list. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-for-haryana/

drought.details: No drought data for HKR 127 found in the searches. The '10 days of water stress' result belongs to HKR 126 and is not applicable to HKR 127. The input record states that the variety tolerates water stress, but this is not corroborated by the evidence digest.

heat.details: No heat stress data for HKR 127 found in the searches.

salinity.details: In a salinity biplot analysis (MP, GMP, STI and yield), HKR 127 was among the genotypes favoured for salt tolerance. The text gives no salinity score, so no rating level can be assigned.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data for HKR 127 found in the searches.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae): HKR 127 is reported to show weak endurance against BB (low resistance), although farmers value its yield and cooking quality in Haryana. Breeding lines derived from an HKR-127 x IRBB-60 cross carrying Xa21, xa13 and xa5 showed lower lesion length, with the three-gene lines the most resistant; these are progeny lines, not HKR 127 itself. Blast and stem rot ratings for HKR 127 were not found. Stem rot and WBPH resistance in the Kaul station notes apply to HKR 126 only and are excluded here.

pest_resistance.summary: Brown planthopper, stem borer and other pest ratings for HKR 127 were not found in searched sources. Stem rot and WBPH resistance reported in the Kaul station notes apply to HKR 126 and are not attributed to HKR 127.

agronomic_details.yield: No yield figures (t/ha) for HKR 127 found in the searches. The input record gives 'Kg/Ha' as the average yield unit with no value. The digest notes that farmers value its yield in Haryana, without a quantity.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-location trial data found. Stability across environments not documented in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Input record states recommendation for low hills sub-tropical zone under transplanted irrigated conditions (not verified by the digest). Digest states HKR 127 is widely grown in Haryana and suited to early sowing (input record). Early maturity was presented as a way to shorten the gap before wheat sowing and reduce straw burning.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: LONG SLENDER SEED WITH L/B TATIO OF 3.39 ; ONLY TOP PANICLES HAVE SMALL AWN ; EARLIER ANTHESIS DAYS WITH DARKER FOLIAGE THAN JAYA.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Mehta 2019 evaluation of BB resistance in HKR-127 x IRBB-60 derived lines: lines carrying Xa21, xa13 and xa5 showed lower lesion length, with the three-gene lines most resistant. STRESS TOLERANCE
- HKR 127 is reported to show weak endurance against bacterial blight, though farmers value its yield and cooking quality in Haryana -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343049563_Evaluation_of_resistance_of_rice_genotypes_derived_from_the_cross_be-_tween_HKR-127_and_IRBB-60_against_bacterial_blight_caused_by_Xanthomonas_oryzae_pv_oryzae
- In a salinity biplot analysis, HKR 127 was among the genotypes favoured for salt tolerance (MP, GMP, STI and yield). The text does not give a salinity score. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361442656_Development_of_Salt-Tolerant_Rice_Varieties_to_Enhancing_Productivity_in_Salt-Affected_Environments
- No drought, heat, flood or submergence data for HKR 127 found in the searches. The "10 days of water stress" result refers to HKR 126, not HKR 127 -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf (not applicable to HKR 127)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial blight: HKR 127 has less endurance to BB. Breeding lines from an HKR-127 x IRBB-60 cross carrying Xa21, xa13 and xa5 showed lower lesion length, with the three-gene lines most resistant -- https://sajeb.org/index.php/sajeb/article/view/352
- Blast, brown planthopper, stem rot and stem borer ratings for HKR 127 were not found. Stem rot and WBPH resistance in the Kaul station notes apply to HKR 126 -- https://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf (HKR 126 only)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration: mid-early, 135-139 days, with long slender super-fine grain, stiff straw and disease resistance claimed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316503793_Callus_induction_and_efficient_regeneration_from_recalcitrant_of_indica_rice_varieties
- Morphology: semi-dwarf, high yielding, golden yellow grains, high milling recovery -- https://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
- Early maturity was presented as a way to shorten the gap before wheat sowing and reduce straw burning -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/comment/the-paddy-straw-challenge-613982
- No yield figures (t/ha) for HKR 127 found in the searches. No multi-location trial data found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (from the record supplied, not confirmed by search): NAMSAGNI 19/IR-4215-301-2-2-6 x IR 5953-162-1-2-3, selected from an F4 IRRI segregating population under artificial BB inoculation. No independent source found.
- Marker-assisted pyramiding of Xa21, xa13 and xa5 in HKR-127 backgrounds was reported at CCS HAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343049563_Evaluation_of_resistance_of_rice_genotypes_derived_from_the_cross_be-_tween_HKR-127_and_IRBB-60_against_bacterial_blight_caused_by_Xanthomonas_oryzae_pv_oryzae
- No QTL or marker-mapping study specific to HKR 127 found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: KAUL Rice Research Station, Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Kaul, Kaithal, Haryana. The station was established in 1974 -- https://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
- A GK source credits HKR 127 to the KAUL Rice Research Station, Haryana Agricultural University -- https://www.gktoday.in/question/terms-mtu1010-swarna-naveen-hkr127-pertain-to
- The HAU page lists HKR 127 among seven non-scented varieties released by the Haryana rice station -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-23
- Lead breeder name(s): not found in any retrieved source.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-23 (no email, phone or street address in the retrieved text)
- KAUL Rice Research Station, district Kaithal, Haryana. No email, phone or postal address found in the retrieved text -- https://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Mehta K (2019). Evaluation of resistance of rice genotypes (derived from the cross between HKR-127 and IRBB-60) against bacterial blight caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae. South Asian Journal of Experimental Biology 9(4):142-147 -- DOI 10.38150/sajeb.9(4).p142-147; https://sajeb.org/index.php/sajeb/article/view/352 (only first author visible in retrieved record)

- Prasad, G.S.V. et al. (2022). Impact of breeder seed multiplication and certified quality seed distribution on rice production in India. Journal not confirmed in retrieved record -- DOI 10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2; https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/full/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2 (HKR 127 listed among inbred cultivars; only one author confirmed)
- KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found (not searched directly; the search tool did not return KrishiKosh records).

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Notified in the list of notified rice varieties: HKR-127 (HKR-95-222), year 2009, notification 29/01/2010, S.O. 211(E) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Breeder seed multiplication for HKR 127 is covered in the national seed distribution study above. No current seed dealer, NSC, SSC or KVK listing for HKR 127 found. The Indiamart results are for PR 126 (a Punjab PAU variety), not HKR 127 -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/pr-126-paddy-seed-20406304873.html (not HKR 127)

drought.details: The digest reports HKR 49 achieved the highest water use efficiency (7.74 kg/ha/mm) under direct-seeded aerobic conditions at Kaul in 2019 and 2020. This is a water-use result under aerobic management, not a direct drought-tolerance rating, and no drought stress trial data were found. Tolerance level cannot be confirmed from the digest.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance in the digest.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in the digest.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: HKR 49: No evidence found for disease resistance in the digest. The digest contains HKR-47 (Seednet name, listed separately from HKR-49) disease information, which is not attributed to HKR 49 here: tolerant to false smut (Kaul source); susceptible to all ten presently prevalent pathotypes of bacterial blight in Punjab and prone to lodging (PAU source); minimum yield loss of 22.62% when inoculated at 30 DAT in Kaul plant pathology reports (pathogen not named in retrieved text); and a bacterial blight resistance study of HKR-47 x IRBB-60 derived genotypes (the source notes a weakness that the snippet does not state).

pest_resistance.summary: HKR 49: No evidence found for pest resistance in the digest. No HKR-47 pest resistance data were found in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: HKR 49: No yield figure (q/ha or kg/ha) found in the digest. Under direct-seeded aerobic conditions at Kaul it gave the highest net returns of Rs 84,963/ha in the trial reported. HKR-47 (not HKR-49): 29.5 quintals per acre average paddy yield (PAU source); 63.82 q/ha in a transplanting-date trial at Kaul.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for HKR 49. The digest gives no multi-environment stability data.
agronomic_details.adaptation: HKR 49: Suitable for direct-seeded aerobic conditions in the Kaul trial (2019 and 2020), where it was early duration. Recommended states per release data: Odisha, Bihar, Maharashtra, Gujarat. HKR-47 (not HKR-49): suitable for early and late planting (Kaul source); suitable for parboiling (PAU event page); among the most suitable genotypes under alternate wetting and drying in puddled direct-sown conditions (Kaul source); popular in Haryana for high yield and medium slender grains with excellent cooking and eating qualities.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: HKR 49: Not specified in the digest, though it is described as an early-duration cultivar under direct-seeded aerobic conditions. HKR-47 (not HKR-49): about 104 days to maturity after transplanting.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: HKR 49: Not specified in the digest, other than early duration. HKR-47 (not HKR-49): average plant height of 117 cm; medium slender grains; prone to lodging (PAU source).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) HKR 49, direct-seeded aerobic conditions at Kaul, 2019 and 2020: highest water use efficiency of 7.74 kg/ha/mm; early-duration cultivar; highest net returns of Rs 84,963/ha. (2) HKR-47, transplanting-date trial at Kaul: 63.82 q/ha, ranked behind HKR-128 and HKR-127; the source gives no HKR-49 data. (3) HKR-47, Kaul plant pathology reports: minimum yield loss of 22.62% when inoculated at 30 DAT (pathogen not named). (4) HKR-47, evaluation of duration genotypes under alternate wetting and drying in puddled direct-sown conditions: HKR 47 among the most suitable genotypes, along with hybrid HKR 1094 and hybrid Haryana Shankar Dhan 1.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- HKR-47 (Seednet name): It is tolerant to false smut and suitable for early and late planting. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf
- HKR-47: It is susceptible to all the ten presently prevalent pathotypes of bacterial blight pathogen in the Punjab state and is prone to lodging. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
- HKR-49 (variety_name): The highest water use efficiency (7.74 kg/ha/mm) was achieved with HKR 49. Tested under direct-seeded aerobic conditions at Kaul in 2019 and 2020 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/149739
- HKR-49: No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance beyond the water-use result above.

DISEASE AND PEST
- HKR-47: Kaul plant pathology reports the minimum yield loss of HKR 47 (22.62%) when inoculated at 30 DAT, with the pathogen not named in the retrieved text -- https://hau.academia.edu/Departments/Plant_Pathology_Rice_Research_Station_Kaul_136021_Haryana/Documents
- HKR-47: popular amongst rice farmers and consumers in Haryana because of its high yield, medium slender grains, and excellent cooking and eating qualities, though the source notes a weakness that the snippet does not state -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336317940_Evaluation_of_Resistance_of_Rice_Genotypes_Derived_from_the_Cross_between_HKR-47_and_IRBB-60_against_Bacterial_Blight_caused_by_Xanthomonas_oryzae_pv_oryzae
- HKR-49: No evidence found for disease or pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- HKR-49: Under direct-seeded aerobic conditions HKR 49 was an early-duration cultivar, and HKR 49 fetching the highest net returns (₹84,963/ha) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/149739
- HKR-47: HKR-47 (63.82 q/ha) ranked behind HKR-128 and HKR-127 in a transplanting-date trial at Kaul; the source gives no HKR-49 data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326605987_Effects_of_different_dates_of_transplanting_on_yield_attributes_yields_and_quality_of_non-scented_varieties_of_rice_Oryza_sativa
- HKR-47: It takes about 104 days to mature after transplanting with an average plant height of 117 cm. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
- HKR-47: Its' average paddy yield is 29.5 quintals per acre. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
- HKR-47: It is suitable for parboiling. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5025
- HKR-47: Evaluation of different duration genotypes under alternate wetting and drying in puddled direct sown conditions revealed that hybrid HKR 1094; inbred HKR 47 and hybrid Haryana Shankar Dhan 1 were found most suitable. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/09%20Kaul.pdf

disease_resistance.research_summary: Bacterial blight: moderately resistant, per the station description (AICRIP Kaul profile). Kaul epiphytotic screening trials (Kharif 2003-2009) list HKR 99-60 (HKR 48) among genotypes, but the retrieved text is truncated and gives no resistance rating. No evidence found for resistance to other diseases.

drought.details: The krishdoctor product page reports partial water-stress tolerance and good performance under moisture stress for Arize Tej Gold. The level is set to medium because the tolerance is described as partial and no trial data was found. A seller page (sandia-agric.com) makes drought claims only for 'Arize hybrids' in general; these are not variety-specific and were not used to set the level.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to HRI-180 or HRI-183.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bacterial leaf blight (BLB) resistance is listed for Arize Tej Gold, and the page also reports partial water-stress tolerance and good performance under moisture stress -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/2CAfsWZZ3p6JPLRRi2E1 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold / HRI-180)
- Bayer's Arize brand document lists Tej Gold among varieties with BLB tolerance, and says many Arize varieties tolerate biotic stress and suit direct seeding. Bayer's brand-level claim about flash-flood tolerance is not specific to Tej Gold -- https://www.bayer.in/sites/bayer_in/files/Bayer_25_Years_of_Arize_English_2019_0.pdf (name searched: Arize Tej Gold; the same brochure also lists Swift Gold, i.e. the Seednet name HRI-183)
- Drought, salinity and flood claims on a seller page are generic statements about "Arize hybrids", not trial data for this variety: temporary drought, moderate salinity, flash floods -- https://sandia-agric.com/product-818-1.html (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- No evidence found for heat, submergence, or formal drought/salinity screening data specific to HRI-180 or HRI-183.

DISEASE AND PEST
- BLB tolerance/resistance: the krishdoctor page calls it "resistant to BLB" in one place and "tolerant" in its description, so the strength of resistance is unclear -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/2CAfsWZZ3p6JPLRRi2E1 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- BLB tolerance listed in Bayer's brochure for Tej Gold and Swift Gold -- https://www.bayer.in/sites/bayer_in/files/Bayer_25_Years_of_Arize_English_2019_0.pdf (name searched: Arize Tej Gold / Swift Gold)
- Bayer's brochure also mentions a brown planthopper-tolerant hybrid, but that is Arize AZ 8433 DT, not this variety -- excluded.
- No evidence found for blast, sheath blight, brown planthopper or other pest resistance specific to HRI-180 or HRI-183.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 125-130 days -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/2CAfsWZZ3p6JPLRRi2E1 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Duration 125-130 days, with an unlabelled figure of 7.0 in the same row. The figure is likely yield in t/ha, but the column is not labelled -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/ (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- A seller page gives maturity of 110-120 days and yield of 8-9 t/ha. This is a marketing figure and conflicts with the 125-130 day figure above -- https://sandia-agric.com/product-818-1.html (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Bayer product page lists long slender grain, high yield, more productive tillers and fine grain with good eating quality -- https://www.bayercropscience.in/en/seed-products/arize-tej-gold/212799 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Milling recovery above 70% and long slender grain -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/2CAfsWZZ3p6JPLRRi2E1 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Nepal multi-hybrid trial (Lumbini Province) includes Arize tej Gold among hybrids compared under irrigated transplanting. The numeric columns are unlabelled in the snippet, so no yield is attributed here -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387415927_Evaluation_of_hybrid_rice_varieties_for_growth_and_yield_traits_under_irrigated_transplanted_conditions_in_Lumbini_Province_Nepal (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- No evidence found for AICRP/ICAR multi-location trial results or Indian yield data for HRI-180 or HRI-183.
- Excluded: a retailer page (mtolori.com) describing "Arize Tej Gold" as semi-dwarf and lodging-resistant, because its product title and listing refer to Arize 6444 Gold.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Parentage was not stated in the sources (matches the input "Not specified"). No QTL, marker, or CMS/restorer details were found for HRI-180 or HRI-183.
- Excluded: the IntechOpen rice-breeding chapter gives development details for Arize Tej (HRI 169), a different variety -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Notified by Government of India and marketed by Bayer Crop Science -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/2CAfsWZZ3p6JPLRRi2E1 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Bayer Crop Science listed as the company for the Tej Gold row in the hybrid list -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/ (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Bayer introduced hybrid rice in India in 1995 under the Arize brand. This is brand-level background, not variety-specific -- https://www.bayer.in/sites/bayer_in/files/Bayer_25_Years_of_Arize_English_2019_0.pdf
- No breeder or scientist name for HRI-180 or HRI-183 was found in any result. Excluded: a LinkedIn profile of a hybrid-rice consultant lists Arize products generically, not as breeder of this variety -- https://www.linkedin.com/in/ish-kumar-82449b16a/

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found.
- No email, phone or postal address for Bayer's rice seed division was found in the search results.
- Only institute-level product page found (not a contact page): Bayer Crop Science India, Arize Tej Gold product page -- https://www.bayercropscience.in/en/seed-products/arize-tej-gold/212799 (name searched: Arize Tej Gold)
- Seednet (seednet.gov.in) was not returned by any search, so no Seednet contact or variety record was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper specific to HRI-180 or HRI-183 was found.
- Only item found: Nepal hybrid evaluation that names Arize tej Gold. Authors and year were not captured from the snippet, and no journal is confirmed -- Authors not captured (Year not captured). Evaluation of hybrid rice varieties for growth and yield traits under irrigated transplanted conditions in Lumbini Province, Nepal. ResearchGate record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387415927_Evaluation_of_hybrid_rice_varieties_for_growth_and_yield_traits_under_irrigated_transplanted_conditions_in_Lumbini_Province_Nepal
- Excluded: Golden Rice and Arize Bigante papers (different varieties/products).

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Bayer product page lists Arize Tej Gold in 1 kg and 3 kg packs -

HUR-1309 (Malviya Sugandh Dhan-1309) rice: evidence digest

Name note: the sources spell the variety "HUR 1309 (Malviya Sugandhit Dhan 1309), IET 23873, IC 627082". I treat that as the same variety as both the CSC name and the Seednet name, which differ only by the variety code. Every finding below refers to that name unless stated otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for HUR-1309. Searches returned only HUR-917, HUR-105, HUR-4-3 and unrelated varieties. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280803337_HUR_917_Malviya_Sugandh_Dhan_917_IET_21838_A_New_Aromatic_Short_Grain_High_Yielding_Rice_Variety_Released_For_Cultivation_Of_Indo-Gangetic_Plain_Zone_Of_Uttar_Pradesh

DISEASE AND PEST
Listed as aromatic short grain, moderately resistant to rice neck blast, with a glume discolouration reaction noted. -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
No evidence found for bacterial leaf blight, stem borer, brown planthopper or other pest reactions specific to HUR-1309.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Listed as irrigated, medium duration of 115-120 days, with non-basmati yield of 50.0-55.0 q/ha. -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
Described as giving higher yield than Lalmati and Kalanamak across four zones of Uttar Pradesh, with short panicles, no awns, and grain distribution from base to tip of the panicle. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280803337_HUR_917_Malviya_Sugandh_Dhan_917_IET_21838_A_New_Aromatic_Short_Grain_High_Yielding_Rice_Variety_Released_For_Cultivation_Of_Indo-Gangetic_Plain_Zone_Of_Uttar_Pradesh
Grain quality is described as comparable to Kalanamak and Badshahbhog. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280803337_HUR_917_Malviya_Sugandh_Dhan_917_IET_21838_A_New_Aromatic_Short_Grain_High_Yielding_Rice_Variety_Released_For_Cultivation_Of_Indo-Gangetic_Plain_Zone_Of_Uttar_Pradesh
Discrepancy: the rice-garud record gives release year 2018, while the BHU document gives 2019 (see RECOMMENDED STATES).
Excluded: the Institute of Agricultural Sciences growth and fertility trial and the HUR-917 yield pages concern HUR-917, not HUR-1309.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for parentage, pedigree, breeding method, QTL, markers or genome resources for HUR-1309. The Seednet parentage field is "Not specified".
Breeding-line codes found: IET 23873 and IC 627082. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Mukesh-Kr-Singh
Excluded: the SSR and fragrance-marker gel study and the HUR-917 selection history concern HUR-917 (from DBS-13). The path-analysis paper uses HUR 3022, HUR 105 and Sarjoo 52 as parents, not HUR-1309.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Institute of Agricultural Sciences, Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi. -- https://www.bhu.ac.in/Content/FacultyCV/singhravi2005@gmail.com.pdf
Listed as a variety entry alongside Prakash Singh, Ravi P. Singh and Mukesh Kr Singh. The lead breeder is not explicitly confirmed by any source. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280803337_HUR_917_Malviya_Sugandh_Dhan_917_IET_21838_A_New_Aromatic_Short_Grain_High_Yielding_Rice_Variety_Released_For_Cultivation_Of_Indo-Gangetic_Plain_Zone_Of_Uttar_Pradesh
Department: Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, Institute of Agricultural Sciences, BHU, which is the likely breeding unit but not confirmed for this variety. -- https://www.bhu.ac.in/Images/files/Summerr%20School%20BHU_pdf%20Final(1).pdf
Excluded: Prof S.K. Singh and the IRRI-BHU Malviya Manila Sinchit Dhan-1 (MMSD-1) story concern a different variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder email or phone was found for HUR-1309.
Institute postal address: Institute of Agricultural Sciences, Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi-221005, with the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding named in the same document. -- https://www.bhu.ac.in/Images/files/Summerr%20School%20BHU_pdf%20Final(1).pdf
Institute-level contact document (director, dean and department contacts, no phone numbers in the excerpt): https://www.scribd.com/document/345837400/4-Institute-of-Agricultural-Science-1-doc
Unverified: an email address (singhravi2005@gmail.com) appears only inside the file name of a BHU CV PDF that lists HUR-1309. I have not confirmed it as a contact for this variety, so I have not recorded it as one.

PUBLICATIONS
Mukesh Kr Singh and co-authors (listed). Rice variety HUR 1309 (Malviya Sugandhit Dhan 1309), IET 23873, IC 627082. ResearchGate variety entry (year not shown) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Mukesh-Kr-Singh
Singh, P., Singh, R. P. and Singh, M. K. (2019, March). Patent listed on the same profile page. Patent title not confirmed as covering HUR-1309. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Mukesh-Kr-Singh
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or multi-location trial report specific to HUR-1309 was found. The Awasthi and Lal path-analysis paper (https://annalsofplantsciences.com/index.php/aps/article/view/158) and the HUR-917 publications were excluded as other varieties.

No evidence found. The search returned news about the IRRI-BHU MMSD-1 variety, which is a different variety, and no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for HUR-1309. -- https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/pakistan-farmer-seeks-newly-developed-rice-seeds-for-cultivation-from-bhu-123061500172_1.html (excluded as a different variety)

RECOMMENDED STATES
Uttar Pradesh. -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php

agronomic_details.yield: A cultivation-practices study reports that Him Palam Lal Dhan 1 (HPR 2795) produced significantly higher grain yield of rice and wheat compared with other varieties tested. A separate study reports that Him Palam Lal Dhan 1 and HPW 368 gave considerably greater grain yields for both rice and wheat. No quantitative yield values (t/ha) were given in the snippets.
agronomic_details.stability: Not established. The provided results do not report multi-environment or stability analyses.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Evaluated in wheat-rice cropping system studies, including trials on tillage and residue management. Specific agro-climatic fit is not stated in the provided results beyond the recommended states.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field and cropping-system studies include: (1) comparison of cultivation practices and varieties on productivity, profitability, and nutrient uptake of rice and wheat; (2) soil cultivation methods and genotypes on yield components and soil properties in rice and wheat; (3) a PhD thesis reporting HPR 2795 performance under conventional tillage within a wheat-rice system; (4) a study of genotype, sowing time, and rice residue management for wheat growth and yield. A separate thesis used HPR-2795 as a red rice variety with a reported seed germination of 92 percent.

disease_resistance.summary: Yellow mosaic virus (YMV/MYMV): resistant in the central release table (dpd.gov.in). pest_resistance.summary: Bruchid (pulse beetle, Callosobruchus maculatus): a study assessed IPU-2-43 for biochemical traits linked to resistance (sugars, protein, tannin, phenols, starch). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: IPU 02-43 (Black gram / urd bean)

Names: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "IPU 02-43". The evidence also uses the spellings "IPU 2-43", "IPU-2-43", "IPU 0243" and "IPU-02-43" for the same designation. No Seednet portal page was found, so every finding below comes from non-Seednet sources. Four searches were run. Breeder and contact searches returned partial results, and the findings are not full verification.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed among the drought-tolerant genotypes in a black gram genetics review (the text is truncated, so the exact trait wording is unconfirmed) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/ (DOI 10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363)
- No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Searches returned general black gram climate notes only, not variety-specific data.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to MYMV and powdery mildew (PM) in the central release table -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Listed as YMV and PM resistant -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/black-gram-ppt-black-gram-also-known-as-urad-or-urd-bean-is-an-important-pulse-crop-grown-in-india/271676749 (secondary compilation; not an official source)
- Listed as PM resistant in the Vikaspedia package of practices -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/blackgram-and-greengram?lgn=en
- Listed as MYMV-resistant in a breeding course page -- https://agridots.com/courses/bsc-agriculture/genetics-plant-breeding/crop-improvement-i-kharif/09-greengram-blackgram-breeding
- Bruchid (pulse beetle) study: IPU-2-43 was assessed for biochemical traits (sugars, protein, tannin, phenols, starch) linked to resistance to Callosobruchus maculatus. The page reports these values but does not state a resistance rating -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-LR-5225-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
- The same bruchid study gives IPU-2-43 protein of 20.56 percent and tannin of 13.53 mg/100 g (as shown in its table) -- same URL
- Listed as YMV tolerant in an AP seed-agency table (variety listed as released 2008) -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Blackgram.aspx (this release year conflicts with the 2009 CSC year; flagged)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Andhra Pradesh comparison of eight black gram varieties (kharif): IPU-2-43 seed yield reported as 980.67 kg/ha, with gross return Rs 59,288/ha and B:C ratio 1.86. The table is hard to read, and a separate figure of 2,359.33 kg/ha is also attributed to IPU-2-43, so the yield values need manual checking -- https://www.annalsofplantsciences.com/index.php/aps/article/download/900/pdf
- Odisha rabi trial (RRTTSS Kirei, Sundargarh, 2018-2020, three varieties and sowing dates): IPU 02-43 gave lower yield than PU 31. Its recorded yield was 557.4 kg/ha, and PU 31 gave the highest yield -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/Impact-of-different-Sowing-Dates-and-Cultivars-on-Yield-and-Economics-of-Blackgram-during-rabi-in-North-Western-Plateau-Zone-of-Odisha-Nirmala-Patel-26.pdf
- Madhya Pradesh kharif 2022 fertilizer trial (AKS University) compared IPU-2-43, PU-31 and Indira-1; Indira-1 performed best -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Performance-of-Different-Graded-Dose-of-Fertilizer-Manker-Chaturvedi/5b9aa556ffdd61fa62ef147f06536e15ee0dbf7c
- Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour (kharif 2018) herbicide trial on IPU 2-43 measured weed control, growth and yield -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/320/190/759
- Bihar herbicide study on IPU 2-43 is also cited as a reference in a 2017 weed-management paper -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Weed-Management-in-Black-Gram-(Vigna-mungo-L.)-and-Pankaj-Dewangan/6589bacbfec081c416a31747a8a8e55dc20bdbff (the 2017 paper itself is not confirmed to name this variety; the citing snippet does)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: No evidence found.
- Breeding method and pedigree: No evidence found.
- Used as a tester in a line x tester study with lines LBG-750, T-9, PU-31, LBG-685 and LBG-20 (combining ability for yield) -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue1/PartZ/12-1-33-403.pdf
- Iron (Fe) content of 86.3 ppm reported in a nutritional-quality genotype table -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/
- QTL, marker or genome-resource data specific to this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur, with 2009 central release -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf (also in http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf)
- A seed-vendor page also names IIPR Kanpur as developer (weaker, non-official source) -- https://blackgram.in/
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found.
- Station/institute page for this variety: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- IIPR, Kanpur: no official email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL was found in any result. No evidence found.
- Not a developer contact: "IRRI Odisha Hub Office, Plot No

official_quote.quote: Moderately resistant to MYMV and powder mildew

disease_resistance.research_summary: Yellow mosaic virus (YMV/MYMV): resistant in the central release table (dpd.gov.in). Also listed as YMV and PM resistant in a secondary SlideShare compilation (not an official source), and as MYMV-resistant in a breeding course page. An AP seed-agency table lists it as YMV tolerant, but gives a release year of 2008, which conflicts with the 2009 CSC year and is flagged. Powdery mildew (PM): resistant in the central release table and listed as PM resistant in the Vikaspedia package of practices.

basic_info.institution: Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya, Jabalpur

drought.details: Described as 'drought tolerant' and suitable for 'direct sown rainfed condition'. It is noted to be capable of 'escaping terminal drought'. However, under severe stress, it may require 'protective life saving'.

heat.details: Exhibits 'heat stress tolerance' and is 'tolerant to terminal heat stress', capable of 'escaping terminal heat stresses'.

salinity.details: Improved Chinnor has been identified as tolerant to salinity and included in screening for 'Salinity Tolerance in Rice'.

flood.details: Described as a 'flood tolerant rice variety' with 150 days duration.

disease_resistance.summary: Improved Chinnor exhibited tolerance to bacterial blight and false smut. It is also resistant to neck blast disease and rice tungro rice disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Improved Chinnor exhibited tolerance to Gall midge and is resistant to stem borer.

agronomic_details.yield: Various yield values have been reported in different trials, including: 2.40, 9.00, 6.60; 1.00, 9.52, 8.52; 7.60, 13.50, 5.90; and 2.75, 46.71, 43.96.
agronomic_details.stability: Its documented tolerance to multiple abiotic and biotic stresses (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence, gall midge, blast, bacterial blight, false smut, stem borer, tungro) suggests a degree of adaptability and stability across varying environmental conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Primarily suitable for irrigated conditions, but also mentioned as suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions due to its drought tolerance. It is classified as a Non-Basmati type.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: The variety is semi-dwarf, reaching a height of approximately 82 cm. It produces medium slender, aromatic grains (LS).
agronomic_details.field_trials: Agronomic performance data has been presented in Draft Proceedings of the Annual Rice Group Meetings (ARGM) and through Frontline Demonstrations (FLD).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jhankri (Taro)

Search status: Three searches ran and returned results. A fourth search was blocked by the tool's usage limit, so the seed-availability and breeder-contact checks are incomplete. Evidence is thin and comes from one ICAR-CTCRI annual report. The Seednet name is still unconfirmed. The report names the variety "Bhu Kripa (Jhankri)", so that is the likely Seednet name, but no Seednet page was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for Jhankri specifically. The CTCRI report mentions artificial screening of fifteen taro accessions with four showing moderate resistance, but it does not name Jhankri as one of them and does not state the stress or pathogen -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-02/ctcri-annual-report-2016-2017.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for Jhankri. The same CTCRI report's accession-screening result cannot be attributed to this variety -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-02/ctcri-annual-report-2016-2017.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Jhankri is listed as "Bhu Kripa (Jhankri)", released by the ICAR-CTCRI Regional Centre, Bhubaneswar, with good cooking quality. The snippet gives no yield, maturity, or trial data -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-02/ctcri-annual-report-2016-2017.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
No evidence found. Parentage, breeding-line code and breeding method were not found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: ICAR-CTCRI (Central Tuber Crops Research Institute), Regional Centre, Bhubaneswar, per the annual report -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-02/ctcri-annual-report-2016-2017.pdf
Breeder or lead scientist names: No evidence found.
Note: the Sree Hira paper (ResearchGate) concerns a different taro variety, so it was discarded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371013629_SREE_HIRA_A_new_elite_variety_of_taro_for_Odisha

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for a breeder, email, phone or postal address. The only institutional source identified is the CTCRI site domain, https://www.ctcri.org (from the report URL). Contact details were not verified.

PUBLICATIONS
ICAR-CTCRI (2017). Annual Report 2016-2017. ICAR-CTCRI Annual Report (author list not stated; year taken from report title) -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-02/ctcri-annual-report-2016-2017.pdf
No peer-reviewed papers, theses, or KrishiKosh entries were found for Jhankri.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The fourth search, covering NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs and dealers, was blocked by the tool's usage limit.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found for the states where Jhankri is recommended. The report links the variety to the Bhubaneswar regional centre, which is in Odisha, but it does not name the recommended states.

Field gaps: variety code, release year, parentage, breeder names, contact details, Seednet listing and seed sources remain unverified. Recommended next steps: search the CTCRI site and its Bhubaneswar regional centre page directly, check the Seednet portal for "Bhu Kripa", and consult the CSC release minutes for the official name and year.
