search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Chandragiri (OUAT Kalinga Rice 9), rice

Name note: The evidence below refers to "Chandragiri (OUAT Kalinga Rice 9)" and the code names in the record. No separate Seednet query was run, so every heading below applies to the name "Chandragiri" as it appears in OUAT and IRRI-NARES sources. Seednet variety name: Unknown, no evidence found. Search coverage: four web searches were run (general, breeder/institute, research/trials, seed). The general search returned mostly irrelevant results, so the release and stress findings came from the other queries.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- A 2024 field trial on Chandragiri describes it as a drought-tolerant rainfed upland variety, developed specifically for rainfed upland conditions, demonstrates remarkable adaptation to moisture stress conditions -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue3S/PartD/S-8-3-45-262.pdf
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The same 2025 article states that Chandragiri demonstrates resistance to major rice pathogens. Specific pathogens, resistance genes and scoring methods are not named in the retrieved text. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue3S/PartD/S-8-3-45-262.pdf
- Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Kharif 2024 on-farm trial: Chandragiri was conducted during the Kharif 2024 on farmer's field at Bagpur village, Narla Block, Kalahandi district, as part of the NICRA-TDC Project implemented through Krishi Vigyan -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue3S/PartD/S-8-3-45-262.pdf
- The trial compared Chandragiri with other varieties, and the article reports that Chandragiri provided the most favorable economic outcomes. Comparator varieties named in the table include Sahabhagi Dhan and Pragati. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue3S/PartD/S-8-3-45-262.pdf
- Maturity and yield (IRRI-NARES table, Chandragiri row): ecology listed as early transplanted, with a yield value of 4200 and a duration of 105. The table extract does not state units, so the units should be treated as unconfirmed. -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/eeb4bc62-10b4-4743-8ebf-f2e268afbdc2/content
- Multi-location trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line codes: IET 27880, ORJ 1336, and OUAT Kalinga Rice 9 appear in the record supplied with the query. The search did not independently confirm them. -- No URL (input record only)
- Parentage, breeding method, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Development credit: OUAT's OUAT Times newsletter says the Government of India notified two crop varieties of rice developed by OUAT, Bhubaneswar, namely Chandragiri (OUAT Kalinga Rice 9), and the Vice Chancellor congratulated the breeder & the team for their success. The breeder is not named in the text. -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Monthly-Newsletter-April-24OUAT-TIMES.pdf
- Station: OUAT's homepage says the variety is from RRTTSS, Jeypore, Koraput. The 2025 article describes it as developed by RRTTS, Jeypore under OUAT Bhubaneswar. -- https://ouat.ac.in/ ; https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue3S/PartD/S-8-3-45-262.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found (no name, email or phone).
- Institute-level address from the OUAT newsletter: Odisha University of Agriculture & Technology, Bhubaneswar – 751003. No email, phone or contact page URL was found for OUAT or RRTTS Jeypore. -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Monthly-Newsletter-April-24OUAT-TIMES.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2025). Chandragiri rice: a promising drought-tolerant variety (title fragment as retrieved; full title not confirmed). International Journal of Research in Agronomy 2025; SP-8(3): 299-303 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue3S/PartD/S-8-3-45-262.pdf
- IRRI-NARES varieties list, which includes Chandragiri (authors not stated; year not confirmed). -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/eeb4bc62-10b4-4743-8ebf-f2e268afbdc2/content
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports and DOI-indexed papers on this rice variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers for this rice variety: No evidence found. Results for "Chandragiri" were about unrelated products, so none were recorded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Odisha, Bihar and West Bengal. The IRRI-NARES table lists these states for Chandragiri (see Agronomy and Trials). The OUAT newsletter confirms only the Government of India notification. -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/eeb4bc62-10b4-4743-8ebf-f2e268afbdc2/content

EXCLUDED RESULTS (other products or places with the same name)
- Chandragiri arabica coffee (CCRI), Chandragiri Modern Rice Mill and Raktashali products, the Durakhal community seed bank, and the Chandragiri village in Andhra Pradesh are unrelated and were discarded.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: KHP-13 (CSC/release name) and KHP-10 (Seednet name), rice

Name note: Searches for KHP-13 and IET 21479 returned direct evidence for KHP-13. Searches for the Seednet name KHP-10 returned records for a different release year and notification. Under each heading I state which name the evidence refers to. Four web searches were run, one per topic.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Evidence for KHP-13 (IET 21479): a row in the IIRR 2018-19 report lists KHP 13 with IET 21479, with abbreviation codes that appear to cover blast, sheath blight and leaf folder reactions. The column legend is not visible in the retrieved text, so these codes are unconfirmed. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2018-19.pdf
- KHP-13 is named as one of the paddy varieties released for commercial cultivation in the hill zone around ZAHRS Mudigere. -- https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/
- No evidence found for submergence, drought, salinity or heat tolerance specific to KHP-13 or KHP-10.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Evidence for KHP-13: the IIRR row above is the only retrieved entry. Its codes appear to mark moderate reactions to blast and sheath blight (MR-BL, T-SB) and a leaf-folder code (LF). Confirm against the IIRR legend before use. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2018-19.pdf
- Evidence for KHP-10 (not KHP-13): a 2019-era study at Mudigere reports a reaction table of KHP-10 against major hill-zone pests, compared with checks. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290527694_A_new_red_rice_variety_for_Mid_Lands_in_Rainfed_ecosystem_of_Hill_zone_of_Karnataka
- No evidence found for KHP-13 resistance to bacterial leaf blight.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Evidence for KHP-13: the IIRR 2018-19 report lists KHP 13 with a duration figure of 135 in the same row. Whether this is days to maturity is not stated in the retrieved text. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2018-19.pdf
- Evidence for KHP-13 as a parent: the Tunga x KHP 13 cross population was evaluated in the 2023 wet season at ZAHRS Mudigere, with KHP 13 grain starch 79.96% and amylose 23.30% recorded. -- https://geneticsmr.com/index.php/gmr/article/download/3329/2090/8459
- Evidence for KHP-10: the ZAHRS Mudigere programme includes identification of dwarf mutants in KHP-10 after gamma irradiation. -- https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/
- No evidence found for KHP-13 yield levels, multi-location yield data, or maturity class beyond the row above.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (from user record): (M 03-83 x RP-79-5) x Rikuto Norin 21. No independent source in the retrieved results confirms it. No evidence found for QTL or marker studies on KHP-13.
- The Tunga x KHP 13 F4 population was screened with MGIDI-assisted selection for yield and grain traits. -- https://geneticsmr.com/index.php/gmr/article/download/3329/2090/8459

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Keladi Shivappa Nayaka University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences (KSNUAHS, formerly UAHS), Shivamogga, with ZAHRS Mudigere as the rice research station for the hill zone. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Agricultural_and_Horticultural_Sciences,_Shimoga
- Lead rice breeder found: Dr. B. M. Dushyantha Kumar, Senior Professor, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Navile; listed specialization is rice molecular breeding for biotic and abiotic stress. This is an institutional profile, not evidence that he bred KHP-13. -- https://uahs.edu.in/agricollege-shivamogga/
- Dushyantha Kumar is named as a developer of a different UAHS rice release (Sahyadri Kempumukthi), not KHP-13. -- https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/story/india/karnataka/red-rice-developed-in-shivamogga-takes-on-kerala-variety-1163988.html
- No evidence found naming the original breeder(s) of KHP-13 or IET 21479.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. B. M. Dushyantha Kumar, Senior Professor, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, UAHS. Email and phone: No evidence found in the retrieved results.
- Institute postal address: College of Agriculture, UAHS, Navile, Shivamogga – 577225. -- https://uahs.edu.in/agricollege-shivamogga/
- University address: Keladi Shivappa Nayaka UAHS, Iruvakki, Sagar Taluk, Shivamogga – 577412, Karnataka. -- https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/
- Institute contact page URL: https://uahs.edu.in (the site home page; a specific contact page was not retrieved). Email and phone numbers for the institute: No evidence found in the retrieved results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2026). Genetics and Molecular Research 25(13s), Tunga x KHP 13 cross, MGIDI-assisted selection, ZAHRS Mudigere. -- https://geneticsmr.com/index.php/gmr/article/download/3329/2090/8459
- Indian Institute of Rice Research (2019). Annual Report 2018-19, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. Multi-location trial table listing KHP 13 / IET 21479 with duration and reaction codes. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2018-19.pdf
- Kamaraddi, V. et al. (2015). Assessment of suitability of selected rice varieties for production of expanded rice (includes KHP-10, not KHP-13). Cogent Food & Agriculture 1(1). -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/23311932.2015.1112675
- Kumar, B. M. D. and Shadakshari, Y. G. A new red rice variety for mid lands in rainfed ecosystem of hill zone of Karnataka (includes KHP-10 pest reactions). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290527694_A_new_red_rice_variety_for_Mid_Lands_in_Rainfed_ecosystem_of_Hill_zone_of_Karnataka
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report specific to KHP-13 was retrieved. No DOI found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Evidence for KHP-10 in the national notified list: 2008 release, notified 27/08/2009 (S.O. 2187(E)). This is a notification record, not a seed source. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- No evidence found for KHP-13 or KHP-10 at NSC, Karnataka State Seed Corporation, KVKs, UAHS seed sales, or private dealers. The seed listings retrieved were for unrelated varieties.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Karnataka. Supported by the IIRR 2018-19 row (state code KA) and the UAHS statement that KHP-13 is released for commercial cultivation in the hill zone region. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2018-19.pdf ; https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/
- Seednet and CSC notification records for KHP-13 or KHP-10 were not retrieved, so the state list is not confirmed from an official notification.

CONFLICTS TO RESOLVE BEFORE USE
- The Seednet name KHP-10 is recorded in the notified list with a 2008 year of release and a 2009 notification. The user record gives a 2018 release for KHP-13. These do not match, so the Seednet entry and the CSC entry may refer to different varieties, or the Seednet name may be mislabelled.
- The IET 21479 and KHP 13 pairing and its alias "Indravathi" appear only in one IIRR table row. Verify against the CSC minutes.

heat.details: KHP-10 is listed in contexts discussing heat tolerance in rice varieties, and participatory validation trials consider heat stress at pollination.

salinity.details: As a red rice variety, KHP-10 exhibits resistance to salinity. It is mentioned in documents discussing salt tolerant rice varieties.

flood.details: Being a red rice variety, KHP-10 is resistant to flood.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
KKL (R) 2 / KKL(R) 2 (IET 28791), rice. Evidence below refers to the name "KKL(R) 2" as used in the CVRC-era press and AICRIP documents. The Seednet name "KKL (R) 2 (IET 28791)" appeared only in the IIRR and NRRI tables, where the code 28791 is shown next to "KKL (R) 2".

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerates flash floods and about 14 days of submergence during the tillering stage, per press reports (name: KKL(R)2) -- https://iebrain.com/industry-news/scientists-in-puducherry-create-flood-resistant-rice/; also https://www.businessinsider.in/science/news/puducherry-scientists-develop-flood-resistant-rice-variety/articleshow/97839013.cms
Under submergence, the reported yield is about 3,600 kg/ha, versus about 6,850 kg/ha under normal conditions -- https://www.businessinsider.in/science/news/puducherry-scientists-develop-flood-resistant-rice-variety/articleshow/97839013.cms
Its direct-seeded rice evaluation lists it among superior genotypes under wet direct-seeded rice (WDSR) -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/agronomy/articles/10.3389/fagro.2026.1955392/full (this paper names it only as KKL(R) 2 and does not report drought, heat, or salinity scores)

DISEASE AND PEST
Reported as moderately resistant to brown planthopper, whitebacked planthopper, blast and brown spot -- https://www.businessinsider.in/science/news/puducherry-scientists-develop-flood-resistant-rice-variety/articleshow/97839013.cms ; https://iebrain.com/industry-news/scientists-in-puducherry-create-flood-resistant-rice/
No sheath blight, bacterial blight, or gall midge data for this variety were found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Suited to Samba season, maturity about 135 days -- https://iebrain.com/industry-news/scientists-in-puducherry-create-flood-resistant-rice/
Average grain yield about 6,850 kg/ha under normal conditions -- https://www.businessinsider.in/science/news/puducherry-scientists-develop-flood-resistant-rice-variety/articleshow/97839013.cms
Cultivated in Samba season in Puducherry (Karaikal) in the AICRIP production survey, 2024 -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/2025/POS%202024.pdf
Included as a test genotype in a direct-seeded rice multi-trait study -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/agronomy/articles/10.3389/fagro.2026.1955392/full
No multi-location yield trial data (AICRP trial tables) were found for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Developed by crossing ADT 46 with Swarna Sub 1, using marker-assisted backcrossing three times -- https://www.businessinsider.in/science/news/puducherry-scientists-develop-flood-resistant-rice-variety/articleshow/97839013.cms ; https://iebrain.com/industry-news/scientists-in-puducherry-create-flood-resistant-rice/
Parentage as listed in the NRRI varietal table: ADT 46*3 x Swarna Sub 1 (2022, CVRC) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382209019_Translating_Science_for_the_Benefits_of_Society_The_Direct_and_Indirect_Impacts_of_NRRI
Breeding-line codes: IET 28791 and KR 16024 (IIRR Annual Report 2022 table entry; the snippet is partly garbled, so read it with caution) -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
Conflict: the IIRR table lists the pedigree as "ADT 46*3/105" with KR 16024 as the code, which differs from the Swarna Sub 1 cross above. Verify against the official CVRC notification.
No QTL, marker, or genome resource records specific to this variety were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by a team led by Dr. S. Thirumeni, Head, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru College of Agriculture and Research Institute, Karaikal -- https://www.preventionweb.net/news/puducherry-scientists-develop-flood-resistant-rice-variety
The institute is at Karaikal, Puducherry, and the work was supported by the Department of Biotechnology, Government of India -- https://www.preventionweb.net/news/puducherry-scientists-develop-flood-resistant-rice-variety ; https://iebrain.com/industry-news/scientists-in-puducherry-create-flood-resistant-rice/
Other team members were not named for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address, or institute contact page for PJN CARI Karaikal, or for Dr. S. Thirumeni, appeared in the search results. The institute name and town (Karaikal, Puducherry) are the only location details found.

PUBLICATIONS
Frontiers in Agronomy (2026). Direct-seeded rice as a promising approach for sustainable rice cultivation: multi-trait evaluation and selection of adapted genotypes. Frontiers in Agronomy -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/agronomy/articles/10.3389/fagro.2026.1955392/full (author list not captured in the search result)
No peer-reviewed paper dedicated to KKL(R) 2 was found. The KKL(R)-1 paper (Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding, 2015) and the KKL(R)-3 paper (Frontiers in Genetics, 2024) concern different varieties and are excluded.
IIRR Annual Report 2022 lists the variety in its release table -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf (not a standalone publication)
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP trial report, or DOI-linked paper specific to this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The Seednet portal, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales, and private dealer pages were not retrieved, because the search budget ran out before a seed-availability query could run. Only the AICRIP survey confirms that farmers grew it in Karaikal in 2024.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Puducherry -- https://www.businessinsider.in/science/news/puducherry-scientists-develop-flood-resistant-rice-variety/articleshow/97839013.cms (described as the first Puducherry rice variety recommended by the CVRC)
Tamil Nadu and Puducherry -- consistent with the input record and with the IIRR table entry "TN, PD" -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf

Note: three web searches succeeded. A fourth search was rejected by the tool's per-turn limit. The "No evidence found" entries for contacts and seed availability reflect that the search budget ran out, not an exhaustive search.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: KPH 272 (rice, PADDY (DHAN))
Name used: release minutes "KPH 272" and Seednet "KPH 272" are identical strings, so all evidence below refers to the same name. Parentage (KCMS 1090A/KRGOS-722) and release date (2016-08-12) come from the supplied record and were not confirmed by any search result.

STRESS TOLERANCE (name: KPH 272)
- Described in a company report as the first aerobic rice hybrid, with KPH 467 released in the medium-duration segment -- https://www.bseindia.com/bseplus/AnnualReport/532899/5328990317.pdf
- Company literature says its hybrids are bred for tolerance to biotic and abiotic stress in general, but no page ties a specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence score to KPH 272 -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/our-story/details-of-business/

DISEASE AND PEST (name: KPH 272)
- No evidence found. The Kaveri 2013-14 annual report mentions a bacterial leaf blight resistant rice hybrid, but the page does not name KPH 272 as that hybrid, so it is excluded -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/annual-reports/annual_report_2013_2014.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (name: KPH 272)
- In a multi-location comparison, KPH-272 (ME, mid-early) was one of five hybrids yielding 14-26% above the local check CARI Dhan-6 (3.1 t/ha); the trial's location is not stated in the excerpt -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-6-2019/B.%20Gangaiah.pdf
- A Kaveri annual report describes KPH 272 as "found promising" in rice trials (text truncated, no yield figures) -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/annual-reports/annual_report_2013_2014.pdf
- A variety listing gives KPH 272 with values 126-130 and 1.9 in unlabelled columns; the column meanings are not visible, so maturity and yield are not confirmed from this page -- https://www.asiafarming.com/high-yield-hybrid-paddy-rice-varieties-in-india-for-rabi-and-kharif-seasons

GENETICS AND QTL (name: KPH 272)
- No evidence found. Searches returned no QTL, marker or parentage study for KPH 272. The parentage in the record is unverified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (name: KPH 272)
- Developed by Kaveri Seed Company Limited (Hyderabad-based private company); no individual breeder name is linked to KPH 272 in any retrieved page -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/media/corporate-profile/
- Company founder listed as G.V. Bhaskar Rao (company history, not a breeder credit) -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/media/corporate-profile/
- No station or research-farm location is linked to KPH 272 specifically; the company reports over 600 acres of its own farm land -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/

CONTACT DETAILS (name: KPH 272)
- No breeder contact found. No official email, phone or postal address for the Kaveri research division was in the retrieved text. The only seller block is an IndiaMART listing for "Kaveri Seed Company Ltd." in Secunderabad with the contact fields not shown in the excerpt; it does not name KPH 272 -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/paddy-17710650830.html
- Institute contact page: not retrieved; the corporate site is https://www.kaveriseeds.in/

PUBLICATIONS (name: KPH 272)
- Gangaiah, B. (2019). Rice Hybrids and High Yielding Varieties for Augmenting [title truncated in source]. International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences (journal name inferred from URL; authors other than the first are not shown) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-6-2019/B.%20Gangaiah.pdf (no DOI shown)

- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, KrishiKosh record or AICRP/ICAR report naming KPH 272 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY (name: KPH 272)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No variety-specific stress data found for KPH-460 or KPH 467. Kaveri's company profile says its breeding aims at resistance to pests, diseases, drought and heat in general terms, not for this hybrid -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/our-story/details-of-business/
- AICRIP 2015 notes that a national three-tier trial system evaluates hybrids, but gives no stress-specific result for KPH 460 -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Kaveri's 2013-14 annual report mentions a bacterial leaf blight resistant rice hybrid with medium slender grain, but does not name KPH 460 as that hybrid, so the link is unverified -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/annual-reports/annual_report_2013_2014.pdf
- No other disease or pest resistance evidence found for KPH-460 or KPH 467.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- KPH 460 was released and notified for commercial cultivation in the 2015 kharif season, alongside ADV 8301 and KRH 4 -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf
- KPH 460 ranked first in AICRIP trials for two consecutive years, according to Kaveri's 2013-14 annual report (company-reported, no yield figures given) -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/annual-reports/annual_report_2013_2014.pdf
- A listing for KPH 467 (IET 24142, a different IET number from the IET 22938 in the release record) gives 126 days maturity and 6.7 t/ha yield -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- The AICRIP 2015 report states a general hybrid yield advantage of about 1.0 to 1.5 t/ha over high-yielding varieties; this is not specific to KPH 460 -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No parentage, marker or QTL study for KPH-460 or KPH 467 was found. Parentage is listed as "Not specified" in the input.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing company: Kaveri Seed Company Limited, Secunderabad, Telangana; its R&D includes research farms and a molecular breeding programme -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/sept20/Annual_Report_2019-20.pdf
- No lead breeder or scientist name found for KPH-460 or KPH 467. The company's founder and chairman, G. V. Bhaskar Rao, is named on the company profile, but he is not identified as a breeder -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/media/corporate-profile/
- No Seednet portal page was reached; the Seednet name (KPH 467) comes from the input only.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Registered office: # 513 B, 5th Floor, Minerva Complex, S.D. Road, Secunderabad 500 003, India; website www.kaveriseeds.in -- https://www.agropages.com/companydirectory/Detail-15619.htm
- Secunderabad office contact listed as "G Rao (Manager)"; no email or phone shown in the result -- https://www.indiamart.com/kaveri-seed-company-ltd/aboutus.html
- No official email or phone number found for Kaveri Seed Company, the institute, or any breeder.

PUBLICATIONS
- Muralidharan et al. (2022). Grain yield performance of hybrid rice in relation to inbred cultivars in long-term multi-environment tests in India. Crop Science -- https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/csc2.20747 (DOI 10.1002/csc2.20747; general hybrid-rice analysis, does not name KPH 460 in the retrieved text; full author list not retrieved)
- ICAR-IIRR/AICRIP (2015). Hybrid Rice, Kharif 2015 report. AICRIP annual report -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/AICRIP_Hybrid_Rice_Kharif_2015_Report.pdf (authors not stated in retrieved text)
- Kaveri Seed Company Ltd (2014). Annual Report 2013-2014: Growing the Future. Company report -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/annual-reports/annual_report_2013_2014.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh) or conference paper specific to KPH-460 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, a state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or a dealer listing for KPH-460 or KPH 467.
- Kaveri's corporate pages list KPH 460 and KPH 467 among its rice products, which shows company supply but not retail availability -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/media/corporate-profile/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Input record: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu (unverified against any notification).
- KPH 467 notification (S.O. 3540(E), dated 24.11.2016): Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- KPH 467 listing (IET 24142, 2016): Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm

NOTES ON CONFLICTS
- Release year: input says 2015-06-25; the Seednet-linked notification for KPH 467 is dated 2016 (S.O. 3540(E), 24.11.2016).
- IET: the input gives IET 22938 for KPH-460; the KPH 467 record gives IET 24142. These may be different entries; the evidence above does not confirm that KPH-460 and KPH 467 are the same hybrid.
- States: the input's recommended states do not match the notified states for KPH 467.

drought.details: No formal drought-tolerance rating for KRH-4 was found. In an aerobic (unpuddled) trial, KRH-4 showed higher water productivity than several comparison varieties. This is a water-use observation, not a stress-tolerance rating. The Mandya centre report mentions hybrids withstanding moisture stress but does not name KRH-4 as one of them.

heat.details: No heat-tolerance evidence for KRH-4 was found. Only maturity and yield-related evidence was located.

salinity.details: No salinity-tolerance evidence for KRH-4 was found.

flood.details: No flood-tolerance evidence for KRH-4 was found.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No KRH-4-specific disease resistance was found. The Mandya report describes BPH and blast resistance only for breeding lines in general. Its udbatta seed-treatment advice is general and not tied to KRH-4.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No KRH-4-specific pest resistance was found. BPH resistance is described only for breeding lines in general in the Mandya report.

agronomic_details.yield: Mandya centre report: average yield 7,500-8,000 kg/ha for KRH-4 versus 5,000-5,500 kg/ha for the 110-115 day check. The unit in the original variety data is recorded only as 'Kg/Ha'.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Southern dry zone of Karnataka, where farm survey evidence exists. Recommended-state and agro-climatic notification evidence was not found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 130-135 days (Mandya centre report, medium-duration hybrid). In the aerobic trial, 50% flowering was reached in about 92 days and maturity in about 138 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Male-sterile-line hybrid (Mandya report). In the aerobic trial, KRH-4 showed higher plant height and tillering and lower weed counts than several comparison varieties. Other morphological characteristics were not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Mandya centre report (AICRIP): KRH-4 medium duration of 130-135 days with average yield 7,500-8,000 kg/ha, against a 110-115 day check at 5,000-5,500 kg/ha. (2) Aerobic-rice trial: KRH-4 reached 50% flowering in about 92 days and maturity in about 138 days; it had higher plant height, tillering and water productivity and lower weed counts than several comparison varieties; no numeric values were given in the digest. (3) Farm survey, southern dry zone of Karnataka (100 respondents: 50 KRH-4 growers, 50 Meenakshi growers): KRH-4 growers reported higher yield and returns; no numeric values were given in the digest.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No marker study specific to KRH-4 was found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. The QTL study located returned to KRH-2, a different hybrid. The F2 genetic-parameter study reports high heritability for 1000-grain weight, flag leaf area and straw weight, and skewed distributions suggesting duplicate and non-additive gene action. No QTL effect sizes were given.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources for KRH-4 specifically. Parentage is CRMS 32A (female, a cold-tolerant CMS line from NRRI with Kalinga-I cytoplasm) x MSN36R (male). Gene action is described as duplicate and non-additive in the F2 population.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: KRH 4 (variety_name) / KRH-4 (seednet_variety_name), rice

Name note: both names refer to the same hybrid. Every source below uses "KRH-4" (a rice hybrid, not an inbred). No search returned a separate Seednet portal record, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found.

Search count: 4 web_search queries (variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Only maturity and yield-related evidence was found; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was documented for KRH-4 specifically. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf
- In an aerobic (unpuddled) trial, KRH-4 showed higher water productivity than several comparison varieties, which is a water-use observation rather than a formal stress-tolerance rating. -- https://www.omicsonline.org/open-access/studies-on-response-of-varieties-and-different-dates-of-sowing-onproductivity-of-aerobic-rice-2375-4338-1000142.php?aid=57976
- The Mandya centre report mentions that some hybrids were identified as withstanding moisture stress, but does not name KRH-4 as one of them. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No KRH-4-specific disease or pest resistance was found. The Mandya report describes BPH and blast resistance only for breeding lines in general. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf
- The Mandya report's udbatta disease seed-treatment advice is general and not tied to KRH-4. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The Mandya report describes KRH-4 as a medium-duration, male-sterile-line hybrid with 130-135 days duration and average yield of 7,500-8,000 kg/ha, compared with a 110-115 day check at 5,000-5,500 kg/ha. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf
- In an aerobic-rice trial, KRH-4 reached 50% flowering in about 92 days and maturity in about 138 days, with higher plant height, tillering and lower weed counts than several comparison varieties. -- https://www.omicsonline.org/open-access/studies-on-response-of-varieties-and-different-dates-of-sowing-onproductivity-of-aerobic-rice-2375-4338-1000142.php?aid=57976
- A farm survey in the southern dry zone of Karnataka (100 respondents: 50 KRH-4 growers, 50 Meenakshi growers) reported higher yield and returns for KRH-4 growers. -- https://www.mathsjournal.com/special-issue/2023/vol8/issue6S/S-8-6-31

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage is recorded as CRMS 32A (female) x MSN36R (male), from an F2 genetic-parameter study. -- https://www.academia.edu/27464972/ASSESSMENT_OF_GENETIC_PARAMETERS_FOR_YIELD_AND_ITS_RELATED_TRAITS_IN_F_2_POPULATION_OF_KRH_4_HYBRID_RICE_ORYZA_SATIVA_L
- The F2 study reports high heritability for 1000-grain weight, flag leaf area and straw weight, and skewed distributions suggesting duplicate and non-additive gene action. -- https://www.academia.edu/27464972/ASSESSMENT_OF_GENETIC_PARAMETERS_FOR_YIELD_AND_ITS_RELATED_TRAITS_IN_F_2_POPULATION_OF_KRH_4_HYBRID_RICE_ORYZA_SATIVA_L
- CRMS 32A is a cold-tolerant CMS line from NRRI (Kalinga-I cytoplasm), and the review lists KRH 4 among hybrids that used it as one of the parents. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489
- No QTL or marker study specific to KRH-4 was found. The QTL study located returned to KRH-2, a different hybrid. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7427098/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- KRH-4 was developed and released by UAS Bangalore, with ZARS Mandya (under UAS Bangalore) named as the working institute. -- https://www.mathsjournal.com/special-issue/2023/vol8/issue6S/S-8-6-31
- The Mandya centre report lists KRH-1, KRH-2 and KRH-4 among its released hybrids. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf
- A 2016 ResearchGate listing names C. Pushpa as an author on the KRH-4 identification paper. Her role as lead breeder is not confirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320709781_A_non-destructive_approach_for_identification_of_newly_released_rice_hybrid_KRH-4_and_its_parental_lines
- Release year: the Mandya report contains a "release in 1998" fragment that is ambiguous and may refer to another hybrid. The supplied year 2014-02-14 is unverified and conflicts with the 1998 fragment. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder name with email or phone was found.
- Institute-level: Zonal Agricultural Research Station (ZARS), V.C. Farm, Mandya, Karnataka. No email, phone or postal details appeared in the retrieved text. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf
- Institute-level: University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru (UAS Bangalore) is the releasing university. No contact page was retrieved. -- https://www.mathsjournal.com/special-issue/2023/vol8/issue6S/S-8-6-31

drought.details: The provided search results contain extensive information on drought tolerance for *rice* varieties named 'Krishna', 'Krishna Hamsa', or 'Satya Krishna (CR Dhan 10)'. These rice varieties are consistently described as drought tolerant or having introgression lines for drought tolerance, often showing yield advantages under reproductive drought stress. Research identifies superior haplotypes of key drought-responsive genes in 'Krishna' rice varieties and evaluates their performance under water stress. However, no information regarding the drought tolerance of the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) was found in the provided results.

heat.details: The provided search results indicate research on heat stress tolerance in *rice* involving scientists named 'Krishna' or 'Krishna Jagadish'. These studies focus on physiological and molecular implications of heat stress, including impacts on reproductive development and the role of brassinosteroids in protection against heat-shock. However, no information regarding the heat tolerance of the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) was found in the provided results.

salinity.details: The provided search results discuss salinity tolerance primarily in *rice* varieties. 'Satya Krishna (CR Dhan 10)' is noted as tolerant to coastal salinity. Research also identifies QTLs for reproductive stage salinity tolerance in rice, with 'Krishna H' involved in such studies. No information regarding the salinity tolerance of the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) was found in the provided results.

flood.details: The provided search results extensively describe flood and waterlogging tolerance in *rice* varieties. 'Satya Krishna (CR Dhan 10)' is described as having stiff straw for water logging situations and being tolerant to complete submergence for 15-17 days. Research involving 'Krishna RM' and 'Krishna T. Sundaram' focuses on combining drought and submergence tolerance in rice. No information regarding the flood tolerance of the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) was found in the provided results.

disease_resistance.summary: The provided search results indicate disease resistance for the *rice* variety 'Satya Krishna (CR Dhan 10)'. This variety shows resistance to Narrow Brown Leaf Spot (NBl) and Sheath Rot (ShR), and moderate resistance to Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB). No information regarding disease resistance for the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) was found in the provided results.

pest_resistance.summary: No information regarding pest resistance for the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) or any 'Krishna' named rice variety was found in the provided search results.

No yield data for the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) was found.
agronomic_details.stability: The locus `qDTY12.1` in rice is noted for its consistent effect on grain yield under drought stress. salinity.details: The provided search results discuss salinity tolerance primarily in *rice* varieties. 'Satya Krishna (CR Dhan 10)' is noted as tolerant to coastal salinity. drought.details: Identified as a drought tolerant rice variety, suitable for aerobic and irrigated medium land, and specifically for drought-prone areas of Subarnapur. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Kalinga Dhan 1204, indicating its genetic basis for drought tolerance. Molecular breeding efforts are focused on developing varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance, involving this variety.

heat.details: It exhibits heat stress tolerance, and molecular markers have been validated for high temperature stress tolerance in rice, with Kalinga Dhan 1204 being part of these studies.

salinity.details: It has been indicated as tolerant to salinity.

flood.details: Considered flood-tolerant and suitable for semi-deep water conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to sheath-rot and sheath blight.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance information for Kalinga Dhan 1204 was found in the provided results.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields include 43.2 q/ha (ICAR Annual Report) and 65 q/ha (Rice-Garud database). Field trials indicate that Kalinga Dhan 1204 performed better than Kalinga Dhan 1201.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly mentioned, but its recommendation for Odisha and involvement in multi-location trials (AICRIP proceedings) suggests general stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for aerobic and irrigated medium land, as well as semi-deep water conditions, particularly adapted to drought-prone areas.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Characterized by medium slender grain type.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been extensively used in experiments, including those designed as Randomized Block Design (RBD) for rice during Kharif, involving various fertilizer treatments. On-Farm Trials have been conducted by KVK Deogarh, where it showed superior performance compared to Kalinga Dhan 1201.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Molecular markers have been validated for high temperature stress tolerance using this variety. It is also involved in Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS) programs for stress tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not specifically mentioned as QTL, but a novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) was isolated from Kalinga Dhan 1204.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Isolation of gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) related to abiotic stress response and drought tolerance. Molecular breeding efforts are directed towards developing varieties with inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought and low soil P.

drought.details: Kalinga Dhan- 1401 is characterized as a short duration drought tolerant rice variety, suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and recommended for drought-prone areas like Subarnapur. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar, has been associated with this variety. Molecular breeding efforts have also been conducted for drought tolerance.

heat.details: The variety exhibits tolerance to heat stress and high temperatures. Molecular markers have been validated for high temperature stress tolerance in Kalinga Dhan- 1401.

salinity.details: Kalinga Dhan- 1401 is tolerant to salinity and osmotic stresses.

flood.details: The variety is suitable for semi-deep water conditions and shows tolerance to stagnant flooding.

disease_resistance.summary: Kalinga Dhan- 1401 possesses multiple disease resistance, including resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot, and bacterial leaf blast. Molecular breeding has been utilized for developing inbuilt resistance to blast.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety demonstrates tolerance to major insect pests, specifically resistance to stem borer (yellow stem borer) and gall midge.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields vary: 65 q/ha and 76.9 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly detailed.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for irrigated ecology, direct sown rainfed conditions, semi-deep water, and lowland environments. Demonstrated performance in drought-prone areas of Subarnapur.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Kalinga Dhan- 1401 is of medium slender grain type. It recorded high germination (77.33%) and maximum survival of seedlings (81.09%).
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been evaluated in various trials and discussed in the proceedings of the 57th, 58th, and 59th Annual Rice Group Meetings (ARGM).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Molecular markers have been validated for high temperature stress tolerance in rice. Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS) has been involved in developing stress-tolerant lines.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs are identified by name, but the development of varieties with inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast has been achieved through molecular breeding.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar, and its presence or role is linked with Kalinga Dhan-1401's drought tolerance. Molecular breeding efforts focus on developing resistance/tolerance to various abiotic and biotic stresses.

Molecular breeding has been applied for inbuilt resistance to blast.

pest_resistance.research_summary: This variety has tolerance to major insect pests. It is tolerant to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) and resistant to Gall Midge. It also shows moderate resistance to Stem Borer and Leaf folder.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Karjat 8 (Karjat - 8 in CSC minutes; Karjat 8 on Seednet, not verified)

NAME NOTE: Evidence refers to "Karjat-8", "Karjat 8", "KJT-13-4-53-19-12" (line/pedigree code) and "IET-19407" (IET code). Karjat-184 (IET-19265) is a different variety. Seednet's portal was not returned by any search, so no Seednet record was found under "Karjat 8" or "Karjat - 8".

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to neck blast and moderately resistant to bacterial blight and leaf blast. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334681259_Karjat-184_an_early_rice_variety_for_Konkan_region_of_Maharashtra_state (page is mainly about Karjat-184; the Karjat 8 text is on the same page)
- ICAR table lists Karjat 8 as a short-slender variety for rainfed, shallow lands, with moderate reaction coded MR-BL and GM. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2013-14.pdf (the abbreviations are not expanded on the page; BL and GM are read here as bacterial leaf blight and gall midge)
- Moderately resistant to leaf blast and neck blast. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/22%20Karjat.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast and bacterial blight reactions are listed under STRESS TOLERANCE above; the ICAR table and AICRIP centre report both support the blast reaction.
- Gall midge (GM): moderate reaction as coded in the ICAR table (see STRESS TOLERANCE). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2013-14.pdf
- Stem borer, brown planthopper, sheath blight, and tungro: No evidence found for Karjat 8 specifically.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Karjat-8 is listed with a 2012 release year, 140-145 days duration, 35-40 q/ha yield, and moderate blast tolerance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325103000_Technological_Interventions_Boon_for_Rice_production_in_Konkan_Region
- Duration of 140-145 days and short-slender grain: Karjat-8 released 2017 at 60 kg seed rate, 140 to 145 days, grain short slender with good cooking quality. -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/cereals?id=52
- Yield over checks: The variety exhibited about 12.6, 28.1 and 18.6 per cent higher yield over the checks in station, state and ada

disease_resistance.summary: SUGANDHA SAMBA: Not found in searched sources. MAHI SUGANDHA: listed as moderately susceptible (not resistant) to brown spot, sheath rot, tungro and bacterial leaf blight. These statements come from quiz and trade pages, not a breeder source, so they are unverified. The CSC record lists disease reaction as Not Specified. Blast tolerance in the 2015 IIRR newsletter table belongs to neighbouring varieties (Krishna, Shobhini), not SUGANDHA SAMBA.

pest_resistance.summary: SUGANDHA SAMBA: Not found in searched sources. MAHI SUGANDHA: listed as less susceptible to stem borer and gall midge (quiz/trade pages, unverified against a breeder source). CSC record lists pest reaction as Not Specified.

agronomic_details.yield: SUGANDHA SAMBA: about 6-7 t/ha reported under good management (Hans India article and Scribd document). CSC record average yield is 4500.00 to 6000.00 Kg/Ha (not corroborated by digest). MAHI SUGANDHA: 45-60 q/ha, best in irrigated areas (IndiaMART and Testbook). These figures belong to two different varieties and are not merged.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for either name. SUGANDHA SAMBA is reported as second-best variety for three consecutive kharif seasons (Scribd document), which is a multi-season ranking rather than a formal stability analysis.
agronomic_details.adaptation: SUGANDHA SAMBA: Not found in searched sources beyond the regional ranking noted in field trials. CSC record states the variety is recommended for transplanted conditions with assured irrigation and for areas where tall scented varieties (Basmati 370, Local Basmati types, Kamod, Kali Kamod) are grown; this is not corroborated by the digest. MAHI SUGANDHA: best in irrigated areas (trade listings).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: IT POSSESSES IDEAL PLANT TYPE CHARACTERS WITH COMPARATIVELY MEDIUM PLANT HEIGHT, UPRIGHT LEAVES, SYNCHRONISED TILLERING AND LATE LEAF SENESCENCE. THE PLANTS ARE STURDY. THE PANICLES ARE LONG, COMPACT AND FULLY EXSERTED WITH LONG SLENDER GRAINS WHICH ARE STRONGLY SCENTED. THE PLANT PARTS ARE NON PIGMENTED. THE GRAINS ARE AWNLESS AND SLIGHTLY BEAKED UNLIKE OTHER VARIETIES.
agronomic_details.field_trials: SUGANDHA SAMBA (digest evidence): (1) Ranked second in region IV (western region) in AICRIP kharif 2008 trials. (2) Farmer trials gave 11.1% higher average yield than Samba Mahsuri. (3) Reported as second-best variety for three consecutive kharif seasons. (4) Yield advantage over checks under late planting (no figures given). SUGANDHA SAMBA (CSC record, not in digest): no trial data given beyond the release record. MAHI SUGANDHA (CSC record, not in digest): highest grain yield when planted in the first week of July (60.33 q/ha), with a drastic yield reduction after July planting; yielded significantly higher than Basmati 370; responsive to nitrogen, with 100 kg N/ha increasing grain yield by 36.6% over 50 kg N/ha (34.2 q/ha); resistant to lodging whereas Basmati 370 is prone to lodging; no shattering observed. No trial results for MAHI SUGANDHA were found in the digest itself.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: SUGANDHA SAMBA (CSC name) / MAHI SUGANDHA (Seednet name), rice (paddy/dhan)

IDENTITY WARNING: The evidence points to two different varieties. The CSC name SUGANDHA SAMBA (RNR 2465) is an Andhra Pradesh variety from ANGRAU, released April 2010 by the state variety release committee, with parentage RNR-M7 x RNR 19994. The Seednet name MAHI SUGANDHA is a semi-dwarf basmati-type variety from Rajasthan (Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology, Udaipur, Regional Research Station Borwat Farm, Banswara). The CSC record's institution (Agriculture Research Station, Banswara) and the Seednet name fit the Mahi Sugandha line. The CSC parentage (BK 79 x Basmati 370) matches neither documented pedigree. Treat the two as unresolved until the CSC minutes and Seednet entry are checked against each other. Findings below are tagged by which name they support.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The only related note is a yield advantage over checks under late planting. -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India
- MAHI SUGANDHA: Listed as less susceptible to stem borer and gall midge, and moderately susceptible to brown spot, sheath rot, tungro and bacterial leaf blight. These are from quiz/trade pages, not a breeder source. -- https://testbook.com/question-answer/mahi-sugandha-is-a-variety-of-_______-cr--636d1127752fa37b569acd59 ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mahi-sugandh-basmati-rice-3420040688.html

DISEASE AND PEST
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: No evidence found for specific disease or pest reaction. Blast tolerance in the 2015 IIRR newsletter table belongs to neighbouring varieties (Krishna, Shobhini), not Sugandha Samba. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- MAHI SUGANDHA: See the stress entry above (stem borer, gall midge, brown spot, sheath rot, tungro, bacterial leaf blight). -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mahi-sugandh-basmati-rice-3014283673.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Semi-dwarf, aromatic, medium-slender, medium duration of 130–135 days, reported yield about 6–7 t/ha under good management. -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178 ; https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Ranked second in region IV (western region) in AICRIP kharif 2008 trials. Farmer trials gave 11.1% higher average yield than Samba Mahsuri. Reported as second-best variety for three consecutive kharif seasons. -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India ; https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178
- MAHI SUGANDHA: Semi-dwarf (87–98 cm), 129–135 days, yield 45–60 q/ha, best in irrigated areas. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mahi-sugandh-basmati-rice-3420040688.html ; https://testbook.com/question-answer/mahi-sugandha-is-a-variety-of-_______-cr--636d1127752fa37b569acd59
- Note: the 130–135 day and yield figures above are from two different varieties and must not be merged.

GENETICS AND QTL
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Pedigree method; female parent RNR-M7 (early samba), male parent RNR 19994. This conflicts with the CSC parentage BK 79 x Basmati 370. -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178 ; https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: No QTL, marker or genomic study found. -- No evidence found
- MAHI SUGANDHA: No QTL or marker study found. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Developed by the Rice Section, Agricultural Research Institute, Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. Named authors on the profile: Surender Raju, B.G. Reddy, R. Jagadeeswar, R.G. Verma, Y. Suryanarayana, L. Krishna, P. Raghava Reddy. Institute and station per the 2015 IIRR newsletter: Surender Raju is Principal Scientist (Rice) and Head of Genetics and Plant Breeding. -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India ; https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- MAHI SUGANDHA: Developed by the Regional Research Station, Borwat Farm, Banswara (Rajasthan), under Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology, Udaipur. No named breeder found. -- https://uttarpradesh.pscnotes.com/uppsc-upper-mains/mahi-sugandha-is-a-variety-of/

CONTACT DETAILS
- SUGANDHA SAMBA, names and roles: Surender Raju, Principal Scientist (Rice) and Head (G&PB), ANGRAU station as listed in the IIRR newsletter. Also Dr R. Jagadeeswar, Principal Scientist (Plant Pathology), and Dr N. Rama Gopala Varma, Senior Scientist (Entomology). -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- SUGANDHA SAMBA, address as found: Rice Section, Agricultural Research Institute, ANGRAU, P.O. Box 500030, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. No email or phone found. -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India
- SUGANDHA SAMBA, seed contact: A 2010-era forum post names a seed supplier (Sudarsana Reddy) and says to contact an email, but the address is not visible in the retrieved text. Not verified. -- https://www.agricultureinformation.com/forums/threads/sugandha-samba-rice.76294/
- MAHI SUGANDHA: No breeder or institute contact details found. Institute-level contact for MPUAT Udaipur or the Banswara RRS was not retrieved. -- No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Raju, S., Reddy, B.G., Jagadeeswar, R., Verma, R.G., Suryanarayana, Y., Krishna, L., Raghava Reddy, P. (year not shown). Sugandha Samba (RNR2465), first-ever high-yielding, aromatic, short-grained rice variety of Andhra Pradesh, India. Technical release document (uploaded copy) -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India
- Indian Institute of Rice Research (2015). Rice is Life, Vol. 13, No. 2 (IIRR newsletter, lists Sugandha Samba, RNR-M7 x RNR 19994, 135 days, released 2010). Newsletter -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Short and aromatic rice a big hit (2016). The Hans India news article. Newspaper -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP annual report specific to Sugandha Samba was found in the search results. -- No evidence found
- Mahi Sugandha: No peer-reviewed paper or KrishiKosh record was found in the search results. -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Trade listings for "Sugandha Paddy Seed" (Kota, Rajasthan, 50 kg packs) and a Sugandha-named product exist, but the listings do not confirm they are RNR 2465. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sugandha-paddy-seed-20399096791.html
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: The Scribd document and 2016 article describe distribution as mini-kit testing under AICRIP. No NSC, state seed corporation or SAU sales listing found. -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178
- MAHI SUGANDHA: Sold as a basmati variety by trade listings (Salem, New Delhi). No official seed-agency or SAU listing found. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mahi-sugandh-basmati-rice-3420040688.html
- Seednet portal: The Seednet entry itself was not reachable through search. -- No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Released in Andhra Pradesh (state variety release committee, April 2010). The CSC record's "Not specified" is unresolved. An Hans India article also lists West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Bihar and north-east states, but the context is cut off, so this is not confirmed as recommendation. -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178
- MAHI SUGANDHA: Rajasthan origin; declared as a basmati variety under the Seeds Act, 1966. Official recommended-state notification was not found. -- https://testbook.com/question-answer/mahi-sugandha-is-a-variety-of-_______-cr--636d1127752fa37b569acd59

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Malaviya Dhan 5-1 (CSC name) / MALVIYA DHAN-36 (Seednet name), rice

Searches run: 4. The CSC name "Malaviya Dhan 5-1" and code "HUR 5-1" returned no page that names this variety. All evidence below refers to the Seednet name "MALVIYA DHAN-36" unless stated otherwise. Its listing (year 1990, notified 1997) conflicts with the record's release year of 2011, so no link to HUR 5-1 is established.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed for medium and low lands in the agropedia notified-varieties table; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance is recorded -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- No other evidence found for Malviya Dhan-36 or HUR 5-1 under this heading.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Described as resistant to major diseases, with grain MS and white -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- The Bihar notified list confirms only the Seednet entry (MALVIYA DHAN-36, year 1990, notified 09/09/1997, S.O. 647(E)); it gives no resistance data -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- No specific pest or disease resistance evidence for HUR 5-1 found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield 42-45 q/ha, grain type and land type as listed -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- A duration value of 130-135 appears in the same row, but the column is not labelled, so maturity is unconfirmed -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- No multi-location, AICRPR or on-farm trial results naming this variety found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Parentage "EARLY MUTANT OF MAHSURI" from the record was not confirmed by any retrieved page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No breeder name or developing institution found for Malviya Dhan-36 or HUR 5-1. Searches surfaced Malaviya Manila Sinchit Dhan-1 (BHU/IRRI, different variety), HUR 917, HUR 156 and Malviya Dhan-2 (HUR-3022); these are discarded as other varieties.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No breeder or institute contact was retrieved that names this variety. Contact pages found (for example IIRR, Hyderabad) are not attributed because they do not name it.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (n.d.). Plant Growth Promotion Assessment in Rice Plant Enhanced by Inoculation of Rhizobacteria. Journal/report not shown; uses Malviya Dhan-36 as a test variety alongside Saryu-52 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274721649_Plant_Growth_Promotion_Assessment_in_Rice_Plant_Enhanced_by_Inoculation_of_Rhizobacteria
- No AICRPR/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or QTL paper naming this variety found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. Seed-dealer results (Ganga Seed Company, IndiaMART) do not name this variety. The Seednet page retrieved is an index and does not show the Malviya Dhan-36 entry -- https://seednet.gov.in/material/Agriculture_Variety.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttar Pradesh, per the agropedia notified-varieties table -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- The Bihar notified list records the Seednet entry but gives no state recommendation -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to Madhuramangala. Searches covered the variety name and its CPCRI release pages. The CPCRI page describes the variety only as high-yielding and suited to tender-nut and ripe-nut processing, with no abiotic-stress data. The Vittal drip irrigation fact sheet (100% pan evaporation; 45% yield increase, 44% water saving) is for arecanut in general and is not variety-specific.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to Madhuramangala. Searches covered the variety name and its CPCRI release pages.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to Madhuramangala. Searches covered the variety name and its CPCRI release pages.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to Madhuramangala. Searches covered the variety name and its CPCRI release pages.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No variety-specific disease resistance evidence was found for Madhuramangala. The only disease evidence is general arecanut fruit rot context from a 2012-2019 multi-location network meta-analysis of fungicide trials (Patil et al., 2022), which does not name Madhuramangala and makes no variety comparison. Fruit rot is described as present across most arecanut regions of India.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No variety-specific pest resistance evidence was found for Madhuramangala.

agronomic_details.yield: Official CPCRI page (earlier entry): 2.95 kg dry tender processed nuts per palm per year, or 3.54 kg dry kernel per palm per year. Later CPCRI page: 4.15 kg dry kernel per palm per year. ResearchGate CPCRI release summary: 4.15 kg chali per palm per year and about 5,600 kg dry kernel per ha per year. Indian-language summary of the same release, citing Ananda et al. (2015) for Madhuramangala (VTL-62): 3.53 kg dry kernel per palm per year, or 4.50-5.00 t dry kernel per ha per year. The sources conflict on units and values; the CSC record field 'average_yield' lists only the unit Kg/Ha without a value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data was found. The Scribd summary states that Madhuramangala yields above earlier varieties and gives marble-appearing split nuts with a higher market price, but this is not quantified or tied to environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Described by CPCRI as suited to tender-nut and ripe-nut processing. Recommended states conflict across sources: CPCRI variety page (earlier entry) lists Karnataka and Maharashtra; CPCRI variety page (newer entry, release recorded as 2014) lists Karnataka, West Bengal (North Bengal) and North East; ResearchGate CPCRI release summary lists Karnataka, West Bengal and the North Eastern region. The release year conflicts (record 2013-06-04; CPCRI says 2014) and should be verified against CSC minutes. No agro-climatic or soil data was found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Per ResearchGate CPCRI release summary: tall type with medium-thick stem, long internodes, partly drooping crown, homogeneous population and regular bearing. Quality note (Scribd summary): marble-appearing split nuts with higher market price.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) CPCRI yield data: 2.95 kg dry tender processed nuts or 3.54 kg dry kernel per palm per year (earlier CPCRI page); 4.15 kg dry kernel per palm per year (later CPCRI page); about 5,600 kg dry kernel per ha per year (ResearchGate CPCRI release summary). (2) Ananda et al. (2015) as cited in an Indian-language summary: 3.53 kg dry kernel per palm per year, or 4.50-5.00 t dry kernel per ha per year. (3) Malnad (Karnataka) cultivar trial: lists Mangala, Mohit Nagar, SAS-1 and Thirthalli local but does not include Madhuramangala, so it gives no comparison for this variety. (4) Vittal drip irrigation fact sheet: 45% yield increase and 44% water saving at 100% pan evaporation for arecanut in general; not variety-specific. No trial-specific design, location, or replication details were found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. CPCRI Vittal reports that arecanut germplasm was characterised with RAPD and SSR markers, and that markers were developed to separate tall and dwarf types. This is general and not specific to Madhuramangala; no marker positions are given.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL or marker-trait study for Madhuramangala found in searched sources.

commercial_info.kvk: Not found in searched sources. No KVK availability evidence found.

The VTL (Shriwardhan 1) code has no match; sources give Madhuramangala as VTL-62, which conflicts with the code in the record. Seed sources for arecanut were not searched directly.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Madhuramangala. Searches covered the variety name and its CPCRI release pages. -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Arecanut_Varieties
Madhuramangala is described only as high-yielding and suited to tender-nut and ripe-nut processing, with no abiotic-stress data. -- https://cpcri.icar.gov.in/page/article/Arecanut_Varieties

DISEASE AND PEST
No variety-specific disease or pest resistance evidence found. The only disease evidence is general arecanut fruit rot context from a 2012–2019 multi-location meta-analysis of fungicide trials, which does not name Madhuramangala. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9503749/
Fruit rot is described as having appeared across most arecanut regions of India, with no variety comparison. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9503749/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Official CPCRI page gives average yield of 2.95 kg dry tender processed nuts per palm per year, or 3.54 kg dry kernel per palm per year. -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Arecanut_Varieties
A later CPCRI page gives 4.15 kg dry kernel per palm per year. -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Arecanut_Varieties
ResearchGate CPCRI release summary gives 4.15 kg chali per palm per year and about 5,600 kg dry kernel per ha per year, and says the variety is a tall type with medium-thick stem, long internodes, partly drooping crown, homogeneous population and regular bearing. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316560015_New_arecanut_varieties_of_ICAR-CPCRI
Indian-language summary of the same release cites Ananda et al. (2015) for Madhuramangala (VTL-62) at 3.53 kg dry kernel per palm per year, or 4.50–5.00 t dry kernel per ha per year. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316560015_New_arecanut_varieties_of_ICAR-CPCRI
Scribd summary says Madhuramangala yields above earlier varieties and gives marble-appearing split nuts with higher market price. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/711066584/NewarecanutvarietiesofICAR-CPCRI
Vittal-station fact sheet gives drip irrigation at 100% pan evaporation for arecanut (45% yield increase, 44% water saving), but it is not variety-specific. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357955501_ICAR-CPCRI_Vittal_-in_the_service_of_farming_community
A Malnad (Karnataka) cultivar trial lists Mangala, Mohit Nagar, SAS-1 and Thirthalli local but not Madhuramangala, so it gives no comparison for this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351969454_Performance_of_different_Arecanut_Areca_catechu_L_cultivars_under_Malnad_region_of_Karnataka

GENETICS AND QTL
Madhuramangala is a selection from indigenous germplasm, not a hybrid, and its parentage is not recorded in the sources. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/production-technology-of-arecanut-areca-catechu-l-pdf/271842751
CPCRI Vittal reports that germplasm was characterised with RAPD and SSR markers, and that markers were developed to separate tall and dwarf arecanut types. This is general, not Madhuramangala-specific. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357955501_ICAR-CPCRI_Vittal_-in_the_service_of_farming_community
No QTL or marker-trait study for Madhuramangala found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357955501_ICAR-CPCRI_Vittal_-in_the_service_of_farming_community

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
MGD 101 Rice -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search log: 4 web_search queries run (variety/release, breeder, research, seed availability). Both names, "MGD 101" (variety_name and seednet_variety_name), returned the same evidence. Sources also write it as "MGD-101" and as "RF-55-198 (MGD-101)". No seednet.gov.in page surfaced, so no Seednet record was found. Many results were about other crops or products (rice-cooking guides, California Calrose lines, MGDG lipid-synthase genes, RiceTec patents) and were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Presenter slide lists MGD 101 as tolerant to drought and blast (rice, Karnataka extension material, 2013) -- https://slideshare.net/mprajanna2/recent-rice-varieties-and-hybrids-of-karnataka-by-mprajanna-2262013-final
- An acid-soil tolerance study names NIIL RF-55-198 (MGD-101) as a consistently superior line; the retrieved text does not explicitly rate MGD-101 as acid-soil tolerant, so treat this as unconfirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240773903_Studies_on_Acid_Soil_Tolerance_of_Rice_Plants_Oryza_sativa_L_I_Morphological_and_Physiological_Characteristics_of_Acid_Soil_Tolerant_Varieties_of_Rice_Plants_I_Morphological_and_Physiological_Characte
- No evidence found for salinity, submergence, flood or heat tolerance specific to MGD 101.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Same 2013 slide: blast tolerance (listed as a special feature) -- https://slideshare.net/mprajanna2/recent-rice-varieties-and-hybrids-of-karnataka-by-mprajanna-2262013-final
- No evidence found for specific pest or disease screening data, resistance genes, or pathotype reactions.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Slide gives duration 125-130 days, medium-bold grain, yield 3.8-4.5 t/ha, higher grain and fodder yield, and suitability for parboiling and flaking -- https://slideshare.net/mprajanna2/recent-rice-varieties-and-hybrids-of-karnataka-by-mprajanna-2262013-final
- Acid-soil study reports the line as grown on rainfed upland with about 2,500 ha area and potential for 10-12% of Karnataka's rainfed upland rice (around 22,000 ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240773903_Studies_on_Acid_Soil_Tolerance_of_Rice_Plants_Oryza_sativa_L_I_Morphological_and_Physiological_Characteristics_of_Acid_Soil_Tolerant_Varieties_of_Rice_Plants_I_Morphological_and_Physiological_Characte
- Multi-trait study on rice germplasm lists MGD-101 among top performers for panicle length, plant height and single-plant yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374349906_Multivariate_analysis_based_prediction_of_phenotypic_diversity_associated_with_yield_and_yield_component_traits_in_germplasm_lines_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- No evidence found for AICRP multi-location yield data for MGD 101.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line code: NIIL RF-55-198 is given as the line that became MGD-101 (acid-soil study) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240773903_Studies_on_Acid_Soil_Tolerance_of_Rice_Plants_Oryza_sativa_L_I_Morphological_and_Physiological_Characteristics_of_Acid_Soil_Tolerant_Varieties_of_Rice_Plants_I_Morphological_and_Physiological_Characte
- Molecular diversity: RAPD profiling of six rice varieties, including MGD-101, against Sahabagi Dhan, IR-64, BPT-5204, Azucena and Doddiga -- https://independent.academia.edu/ketakighatole
- Parentage ("((TEQING/BINAM//TEQING//TEQING") was not found in any retrieved source; it is unverified and the string appears malformed (unbalanced parentheses).
- Breeding method: No evidence found.
- QTL, markers, genome resources for MGD 101: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No breeder or developing institution is named for MGD 101 in any retrieved source. The acid-soil study ties RF-55-198 to the MGD-101 release, but the retrieved text does not name the institute or breeder.
- Karnataka rice material is attributed to UAS Bangalore on the 2013 slide, but that page does not say who developed MGD 101 -- https://slideshare.net/mprajanna2/recent-rice-varieties-and-hybrids-of-karnataka-by-mprajanna-2262013-final
- Institute attribution (e.g., UAS Bangalore, UAS GKVK) is therefore unconfirmed.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact is linked to MGD 101. The following belong to the slide's presenter and are not attributed to this variety: Dr. M.P. Rajanna, Senior Rice Breeder, University of Agricultural Sciences, Bangalore-560 065; email mprajanna@rocketmail.com; cell 099459 00893 -- https://slideshare.net/mprajanna2/recent-rice-varieties-and-hybrids-of-karnataka-by-mprajanna-2262013-final
- Institute contact page: not found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Studies on Acid Soil Tolerance of Rice Plants (Oryza sativa L.) I. Morphological and Physiological Characteristics of Acid Soil Tolerant Varieties of Rice Plants. Journal not stated -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240773903_Studies_on_Acid_Soil_Tolerance_of_Rice_Plants_Oryza_sativa_L_I_Morphological_and_Physiological_Characteristics_of_Acid_Soil_Tolerant_Varieties_of_Rice_Plants_I_Morphological_and_Physiological_Characte
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Multivariate analysis based prediction of phenotypic diversity associated with yield and yield component traits in germplasm lines of rice (Oryza sativa L.). Journal not stated -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374349906_Multivariate_analysis_based_prediction_of_phenotypic_diversity_associated_with_yield_and_yield_component_traits_in_germplasm_lines_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Ketaki Ghatole (year not stated). RAPD-based genetic diversity analysis of six rice varieties including MGD-101. Profile page; no journal or DOI shown -- https://independent.academia.edu/ketakighatole
- KrishiKosh theses, ICAR/AICRP reports, DOIs: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, UAS seed sales or private dealers. The seed-availability search returned only US and corporate rice seed news and patent deposits, none about MGD 101.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Karnataka. Named in the 2013 slide (rainfed/transitional ecosystems) and in the acid-soil study (rainfed upland in Karnataka) -- https://slideshare.net/mprajanna2/recent-rice-varieties-and-hybrids-of-karnataka-by-mprajanna-2262013-final ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240773903_Studies_on_Acid_Soil_Tolerance_of_Rice_Plants_Oryza_sativa_L_I_Morphological_and_Physiological_Characteristics_of_Acid_Soil_Tolerant_Varieties_of_Rice_Plants_I_Morphological_and_Physiological_Characte
- The input field "recommended_states_raw" is "Unknown"; the evidence above supports Karnataka only. Official gazette or CSC notification: not retrieved.

heat.details: MTU 1223 is listed in the 'tolerant' group (spikelet fertility above 65%, with yield and MTS above threshold) in a 2025 preprint screening, and it is named as a candidate for heat-tolerance breeding. disease_resistance.summary: Blast and bacterial leaf blight (BLB): sources conflict and the level must be confirmed before recording. The release description states tolerance to BLB and blast in one place. The trait table states resistance to blast and BLB, and also records moderate tolerance to bacterial leaf blight, leaf blast and neck blast. No further detail was found. Other diseases: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Stem borer: moderate tolerance recorded. Brown planthopper: no variety-specific resistance rating found. Rodents: no resistance rating found; the rodent study reports only compensation ability after damage (MTU-1223 was one of twelve varieties tested), not resistance.
