search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NK 5231 (rice)

Search note: I ran four web searches. The Seednet portal and CSC release minutes did not come up in any result, so every finding below is from Syngenta and reseller pages. Variety name: the CSC name is NK 5231 and the Seednet name is NK-5231. No search result showed the Seednet name, so all findings below refer to the NK 5231 name as used by Syngenta.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The Syngenta product page gives only general claims of suitability for rainfed or irrigated conditions and no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The Syngenta pages list no resistance ratings. The only related item is a pocket-insert leaflet PDF, which I could not open. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/nk-5231

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The Syngenta page lists the season as kharif, sowing between 15 May and 15 July, a crop duration of 120 to 125 days, a seed rate of 5 to 6 kg per acre, and spacing of 20 cm between rows and 15 cm between plants. It is described as mid-early duration with bold grain, more grains per panicle, and consistent adaptability. No multi-location trial data was found. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Parentage is not stated in any source, and no marker or QTL study was found. (The search results include a Syngenta NK 5251 page, which is a different variety.) -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developer: Syngenta India Pvt. Ltd., as given in the CSC record. The Syngenta product pages name no lead breeder, scientist or development station. The breeder-focused search returned only unrelated foreign patent and syndicated pages. No breeder name was found. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/nk-5231

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact was found. No email, phone or postal address for Syngenta India or its rice division appeared in the search results. The only location found is a reseller in Narayanpur, Assam (Nabarak Beej Bhandar), which is not an institute contact. Please check the Syngenta India contact page directly. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/syngenta-nk-5231-hybrid-rice-seed-2855772639455.html

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses or conference papers on NK 5231 were found. The ICAR 2024-25 annual report that came up in the trial search does not mention this variety in the extracts I could read. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- A reseller listing (Nabarak Beej Bhandar, Narayanpur, Assam) offers a 10 kg pack of the variety as in stock, with the listing ID 2855772639455. Availability and pricing were not checked with the seller. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or official seed-sales source was found. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/syngenta-nk-5231-hybrid-rice-seed-2855772639455.html

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The CSC raw record lists Assam. The Syngenta product page does not name any state. It gives only "major rice-growing areas" and says the variety suits rainfed or irrigated rice. Assam is therefore supported only by the CSC record and the reseller location, not by the company's own recommendation. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231

Release year -- The CSC record gives 2 August 2024. I could not find a notification gazette or Seednet entry to confirm it. Parentage is not specified in any source.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NK 16520 (rice / PADDY (DHAN), code A01022150)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "NK 16520", so all headings below refer to that single name.

Searches run (4 of 4 allowed): (1) "NK 16520 rice variety"; (2) "NK 16520 rice breeder developed by institute"; (3) "NK 16520 rice research paper trial"; (4) "NK 16520 paddy seed availability". None of the returned pages contained "NK 16520", "IR58025", or "Syngenta" in the text. The results were general rice-genetics material (an iconic-varieties special issue, IRRI's Rice Breeding Innovations department, a system-of-rice-intensification trial of unnamed varieties, and a seed-availability list of other paddy varieties). I discarded all of them as not about this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. No search result described drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for NK 16520.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No search result described blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight, BPH or other resistance for NK 16520.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for NK 16520 were returned. The only trial-type result was a sixteen-variety SRI trial that does not name NK 16520 in the retrieved text.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage in the supplied record (female IR58025A, maintainer IR58025B) was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No search result named a breeder or scientist for NK 16520. Syngenta India Limited is the institution in the supplied record only; no search result confirmed it as developer.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The only address on record is the supplied institution address (Syngenta India Limited, Amar Paradigm, S.No.110/11/3, Baner Road, Pune-411 045). It comes from the input, not from a search result, and no email, phone, or contact page was found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming NK 16520 was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned lists for other paddy varieties from a non-NK source; no NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for NK 16520 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found in search. The supplied record lists Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and Telangana, but no search result confirmed this. Treat it as unverified until checked against CSC release minutes or the Seednet portal.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) directly for code A01022150, obtain the CSC/ICAR release notification for 2019, and ask Syngenta India for breeder contact and trial data. These sources were not reachable with the search tool used here.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rainfed lowland thermal-indices study with three sowing dates (June, July, August) and four varieties including NLR-3041: NLR-3041 took the most days to 50% flowering (107.33, against 104.00 for BPT-5204) and had the highest accumulated growing degree days and photothermal units from sowing to harvest (2136.83 °C-day) -- https://sasapjas.org/influence-of-thermal-indices-on-phenology-of-rainfed-lowland-rice/
- On-farm trial (OFT) "Assessment of the performance of Paddy var. NLR-3041 in Nellore district (1st year)", 2018-19, trial no. 1/OFT/C.P/18-19/R/KVK/NLR. Its rationale was that NLR-3041 matches BPT 5204 in cooking quality -- https://www.kvknellore-angrau.org/technologies
- Yield data: No evidence found for NLR-3041 specifically.
- Maturity duration: the thermal-indices paper gives phenology only. Days to maturity: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- A KrishiKosh-hosted thesis (title on the page: "Morphological and molecular divergence for quantitative..."; author not in retrieved text) lists NLR-3041 with parentage BPT5204/NLR145 and institution ARS Nellore -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/f7451dec-427f-44b7-9ebe-c56b9d0458a5/content
- The same thesis also uses genotype panels that include NLR-3041 in marker profiling. Marker-trait associations for NLR-3041: No evidence found -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/f7451dec-427f-44b7-9ebe-c56b9d0458a5/content
- QTL or marker studies specific to NLR-3041: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (from the KrishiKosh listing above): ARS Nellore, ANGRAU (Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University) -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/f7451dec-427f-44b7-9ebe-c56b9d0458a5/content
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. The ARS Nellore rice papers in the results (C.P.D. Rajan, P. Rajasekhar, U. Vineetha) are about NLR 40054, not NLR-3041, so they are not attributed here -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Untitled16.pdf
- Release notification body and date: No evidence found in the results. The 2020-11-09 release date is from the input record only.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found.
- No ARS Nellore or ANGRAU contact page for this variety was found.
- The only address retrieved is for the KVK that ran the trial (not the breeding station): "NELLORE-524 004" -- https://www.kvknellore-angrau.org/technologies
- Email and phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Influence of thermal indices on phenology of rainfed lowland rice. Journal: SASA Journal of Agricultural Sciences (per URL; not confirmed in text) -- https://sasapjas.org/influence-of-thermal-indices-on-phenology-of-rainfed-lowland-rice/
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Morphological and molecular divergence for quantitative traits (thesis, title truncated in retrieval). Institution: IIRR, Hyderabad, per listing -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/f7451dec-427f-44b7-9ebe-c56b9d0458a5/content
- KVK Nellore OFT report, "Assessment of the performance of Paddy var. NLR-3041 in Nellore district (1st Year)", 2018-19. Not a peer-reviewed paper -- https://www.kvknellore-angrau.org/technologies
- AICRP/ICAR annual report entries: No evidence found.
- DOI: No evidence found for any item above.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK sale, SAU sale or dealer listing for NLR-3041. The IFFDC seed list names BPT-5204 but not NLR-3041 -- https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed
- Seednet general pages returned no variety-level data -- https://seednet.gov.in/GraphReport/SeedGraph.aspx

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Andhra Pradesh: supported only by the input record and by the Nellore district trial above, which tested the variety under local conditions -- https://www.kvknellore-angrau.org/technologies
- A press report (undated; its age is about 13 years, so it predates the 2020 release) says NLR 3041 was under trial and attracting farmer interest in Nellore, under the local name "Nellore Sona". The alias is not confirmed elsewhere, so it is not used as proof of the name match -- https://www.hyderabadfirst.in/?p=3434
- Official recommendation or notification for Andhra Pradesh: No evidence found.

Discarded: pages on NLR 40054, NLR 34449, NLR 4001, Molakolukulu, BPT 5204 alone, NLR-gene papers, and US/Louisiana rice patents. None names NLR 3041.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: resistance is reported. The RARS technical report describes NLR 40024 as blast tolerant and short duration. A Nellore trial report describes it as blast resistant. A blast-resistance marker study lists NLR 40024 among parents selected for blast resistance, yield and quality. No blast score, race spectrum or Pi resistance gene is named for this variety. Leaf blast, neck blast and other diseases: Not found in searched sources. The variety record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance is confirmed for NLR 40024. Leaf folder: incidence reported at 18.16% in NLR 40024, above the economic threshold level; this is a susceptibility finding, not resistance. Stem borer (Scirpophaga incertulas): a late-sown field test reported 0.11% white ears, scored highly resistant (scale 0), against 19.48% in susceptible check TN1. The digest lists this under NLR 40024 but the source text does not name the entry, so this attribution is not confirmed and is not reported as a resistance finding for this variety. The variety record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Variety record: 6.5 to 7.0 tons/ha. Organic-management trial: mean yield about 6064 kg/ha, reported as the highest of the entries tested (NLR 34242 at 5735 kg/ha). Record fertilizer response: yields well at 120 kg N/ha, 60 P2O5 and K2O; seed rate 50 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Variety record: early kharif and early rabi seasons in the southern zone of Andhra Pradesh. The Southern Zone 2015 recommendations list Swetha (NLR 40024) for early kharif planting. A Nellore report says it was developed for summer cultivation, which conflicts with the RARS early kharif listing. Digest describes it as suitable for machine harvesting (Nellore trial report, dating unclear).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Variety record: non-lodging, non-shattering, fertilizer responsive. The RARS report describes it as lodging tolerant and short duration. A Nellore report describes it as non-lodging (dating unclear). Morphological characteristics in the record: 'Na.' No further morphological evidence was found in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Organic-management trial: mean yield about 6064 kg/ha, highest of the entries tested, versus NLR 34242 at 5735 kg/ha (RARS technical report). (2) Late-sown puddled trial, North Coastal Zone of AP: 6164 kg/ha, reported as the most suitable variety there. The digest does not explicitly name NLR 40024 in this result, so attribution is not confirmed. (3) Late-sown stem borer test: highly resistant score for white ears (0.11%) versus TN1 (19.48%); attribution to NLR 40024 is not explicit in the source text. (4) Southern Zone 2015 recommendations list NLR 40024 (Swetha) for early kharif planting.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources for NLR 40024. Parentage recorded as WGL 14280-1 x NLR 30491 was not found in any search result and remains unverified. The digest reports no SSR, SNP or marker positions for this variety.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No evidence found. The blast-resistance marker study lists NLR 40024 as a parent and reports marker-trait co-segregation for other advanced lines, not for this variety.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. No gene or pathway is named for NLR 40024. The Pi resistance gene is not identified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as blast and lodging tolerant, short duration, suitable for early kharif -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- Described as blast resistant and non-lodging, with suitability for machine harvesting (Nellore trial report; the article's dating is unclear) -- https://www.hyderabadfirst.in/?p=3434
- Among parents selected for blast resistance, yield and quality in an Indian blast-resistance study -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-025-10279-8 (same study also indexed at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/273012781_Identification_and_validation_of_rice_blast_resistance_genes_in_Indian_rice_germplasm)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Stem borer (Scirpophaga incertulas), late-sown field test: 0.11% white ears, scored as highly resistant (scale 0), against 19.48% in susceptible check TN1 -- https://sasapjas.org/study-on-early-duration-rice-varieties-under-late-sown-situation-for-resistance-to-yellow-stem-borer-scirpophaga-incertulas-walker/
- Leaf folder: incidence reported at 18.16% in NLR 40024, above the economic threshold level, so this is not a resistance finding -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- Blast: resistance is reported in the sources above; no blast score, race spectrum or resistance gene (Pi) is named for this variety -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-025-10279-8

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Organic-management trial: mean yield about 6064 kg/ha, highest of the entries tested (NLR 34242 at 5735 kg/ha) -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- North Coastal Zone of AP, late-sown puddled conditions: 6164 kg/ha, named as the most suitable variety there -- https://sasapjas.org/study-on-early-duration-rice-varieties-under-late-sown-situation-for-resistance-to-yellow-stem-borer-scirpophaga-incertulas-walker/
- Southern zone 2015 recommendations list Swetha (NLR 40024) for early kharif planting -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/reports/Management%20practices%20for%20ZREAC%202015.pdf
- Season conflict: a Nellore report says it was developed for summer cultivation, whereas the RARS list says early kharif -- https://www.hyderabadfirst.in/?p=3434 ; https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- Maturity: described as short duration only; no day count was found for NLR 40024 -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The blast-resistance marker study lists NLR 40024 as a parent and reports marker-trait co-segregation for other advanced lines, not for this variety -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-025-10279-8
- Parentage WGL 14280-1 x NLR 30491 was not found in any search result. The pedigree in the record is unverified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released or listed under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) Nellore-line varieties; ANGRAU's Other-Institute page lists NLR 40024 Swetha -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-25/
- The RARS list (rarstpt.org) gives Swetha (NLR40024) with a 2012 year, which conflicts with the 2020-11-09 release date in the record -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- Breeder names: No evidence found. Principal scientist P. Ramesh Babu is quoted on NLR 34449 only, so he is not attributed to this variety -- https://www.hyderabadfirst.in/?p=3434
- Developing station: Nellore ARS/RRS is named in regional reports as the source of NLR-series varieties, and the Hans India report credits "scientists" with developing NLR 40024 (Swetha) -- https://www.thehansindia.com/andhra-pradesh/paddy-cultivation-area-drops-significantly-in-nellore-dist-785149

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME NOTE: Searches used "NMH-1242" and "NMH 1242". All hits matched the Seednet form "NMH - 1242" or the CSC form "NMH-1242", so the findings below apply to both names. None of the sources cite variety code A0207463 or the release year 2013.

STRESS TOLERANCE / DISEASE AND PEST
- Listed as "moderately tolerant to MLB" (maydis leaf blight) in an AICRP-based benchmarking table of Indian hybrids -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Included among Indian maize cultivars screened under PEG-induced simulated drought at the seedling stage (physiological traits measured 15 days after sowing). The snippet does not report NMH-1242's individual score or ranking -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342552203_Screening_of_Some_Selected_Indian_Maize_Cultivars_to_Simulated_Drought_Condition
- No evidence found for flood, submergence, heat, or salinity tolerance, or for pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Benchmarking table gives an average yield of 7.3 t/ha for NMH-1242 (Nuziveedu Seeds) under Kharif in the listed states; the grain is yellow and dent -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Multi-location trial of 117 commercial hybrids from 20 seed companies at three winter-season sites in Nepal (2011). NMH-1242 is listed among the entries. Its cluster is described as low-yielding and inconsistent, but the snippet does not clearly place NMH-1242 in that cluster. Treat as unconfirmed -- https://www.nepjol.info/index.php/JMRD/article/download/16210/13147
- Nepal Terai/inner-Terai varietal trials (2016/17–2018/19, NARC) include NMH-1242 as a commercial hybrid from Nuziveedu Seed Pvt. Ltd., Hyderabad. Yield values are not captured in the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311885729_Performance_evaluation_of_commercial_maize_hybrids_across_diverse_Terai_environments_during_the_winter_season_in_Nepal
- No evidence found for Indian multi-location AICRP yield data specific to NMH-1242 beyond the benchmarking table, or for maturity days.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- No evidence found for parentage NM-161 x NM-250. The only parent-line codes appearing in search results are unrelated US/Pioneer patent records.
- No evidence found for breeding method, QTL, markers, or genome resources for NMH-1242.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The developer is Nuziveedu Seeds Limited (Nuziveedu Seed Pvt. Ltd.), Hyderabad, India, as listed for NMH-1242 in a Nepal trial report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311885729_Performance_evaluation_of_commercial_maize_hybrids_across_diverse_Terai_environments_during_the_winter_season_in_Nepal
- The benchmarking table lists the centre/organisation as Nuziveedu Seeds Limited. Presentation authors are Jyoti Kaul, Bhupender Kumar, Chikkappa Karjagi and O P Yadav (IIMR/IARI). These are presenters, not confirmed breeders of NMH-1242 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- No evidence found for a named lead breeder or for a public-sector station.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No Nuziveedu Seeds email, phone, address, or contact page was returned for NMH-1242. The Nuziveedu maize product page that was found lists other hybrids (for example Bond NMH-007) and does not mention NMH-1242 -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/field-crop/maize-variety/
- Institute-level contact for the presenters' institute (IIMR, Pusa Campus, New Delhi 110012) appears in the presentation header, but it is not NMH-1242-specific -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NPH-242 (CSC release name) / NPH-4242 (Seednet name), rice (paddy), Nirmal Seeds Pvt. Ltd.

Search coverage: four web_search queries were run, the maximum allowed. Two used "NPH-242 rice" wording and one used "NPH-4242 paddy" with Assam. None returned a page about this variety. The results that came back were about other products (IR64, a US rice line M-206, the TAK-242 drug trial, and a Nuziveedu hybrid seed catalogue). Those are not evidence for NPH-242, so no finding below is drawn from them.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found (searched for NPH-242 and NPH-4242; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data)

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found (no blast, BLB, sheath blight, BPH or other resistance data located)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found (no maturity duration, yield, or multi-location trial data located)

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found (parentage is "Not specified" in the input record and no pedigree or marker data was located)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found (no lead breeder, developing station, or release notification identified; the institution in the record is Nirmal Seeds Pvt. Ltd., and no page confirming its role in developing this variety was found)

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found (no breeder, institute, or company email, phone, address or contact-page URL was located. Nothing has been inferred or filled in.)

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found (no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming NPH-242 or NPH-4242 was located)

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found (no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for NPH-242 or NPH-4242 was located. The Nuziveedu Seeds field-crop page that surfaced lists different products, including NP-7020 and the hybrid NPH-207, and is not evidence for this variety.)

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for Assam or any other state. The Assam value comes only from the input record and was not confirmed by any search result.

Suggested next steps, since the search budget is used up: check the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) for "NPH-4242" under PADDY (DHAN) and the CSC release minutes for the NPH-242 notification; contact Nirmal Seeds Pvt. Ltd. directly for breeder names and parentage; and search KrishiKosh and the Assam Agricultural University or AICRP rice trial reports for the variety name.

drought.details: This variety is described as drought tolerant and suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. Molecular breeding efforts are noted for developing rice varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance.

heat.details: While temperature stress is mentioned in a general context of research, specific heat tolerance for NPH-XI (IET 27332) is not explicitly stated in the provided results.

salinity.details: The variety is described as salinity tolerant.

flood.details: No explicit mention of flood tolerance. However, it is suitable for semi-deep water conditions and has submergence tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: This variety is highly resistant to Leaf Blight (LB) and neck infection. It is generally described as disease-resistant and moderately resistant, though specific diseases for the latter are not always detailed.

pest_resistance.summary: NPH-XI (IET 27332) is tolerant to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) and exhibits tolerance to major insect pests including Stem Borer and Gall Midge.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields for NPH-XI (IET 27332) are 65 q/ha and 63.5 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Stability across environments is not specified in the provided results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: This variety is suitable for irrigated, transplanted conditions, and also for direct sown rainfed conditions and semi-deep water. It is recommended for cultivation in Jharkhand and West Bengal.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Reported maturity periods are 130-133 days and 117 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: NPH-XI (IET 27332) is a semi-dwarf variety, approximately 82 cm in height. It produces Long Slender (LS) grains and is noted as a protein-rich paddy variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Details on specific field trials beyond general suitability statements are not provided.

Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) was isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar in a general context, but not explicitly attributed to NPH-XI (IET 27332). Molecular breeding efforts for drought, low soil P, and blast resistance are mentioned generally for rice varieties.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTL information for NPH-XI (IET 27332) is provided in the search results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) is noted in relation to drought tolerance in rice. Accession numbers MH469748 and MZ127288 are mentioned in a general report but are not directly linked to specific genetic mechanisms or genes of NPH-XI (IET 27332).

EVIDENCE DIGEST: OUAT Kalinga Rice 7 (Barunei), IET 23666, rice

Search status: The search tool hit its usage limit after the first batch of four queries, so I could not run the follow-up checks. Only one result contained the variety name with usable text. The Seednet name ("OUAT Kalinga Rice 7 (Barunei) (IET 23666)") was never returned by any search, so no evidence below is confirmed under that name. Everything below refers to the CSC/OUAT name "OUAT Kalinga Rice 7 (Barunei)." Snippet text was truncated, so the details should be checked against the full PDF.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The search returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety. Not searched in full.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Not searched in full.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The OUAT release list describes it as a medium-duration variety, but the snippet cut off before any maturity, yield, or trial figures. -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage from the request is Gouri / IR 65629-22-1. No independent source confirmed it. No QTL or marker evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology (OUAT), Bhubaneswar. The OUAT release list appears under the Directorate of Research. Lead breeder name: No evidence found. -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, or address was retrieved. The Directorate of Research, OUAT, Bhubaneswar is the only institutional contact source identified, but no contact details were extracted from it. Source: https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report entry, or thesis specific to this variety was confirmed. The IIRR Annual Report 2023 mentions "OUAT Kalinga" in its text, but the snippet does not clearly tie it to Barunei, so I have not listed it as a publication. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Not confirmed. The OUAT release list names the variety, but no seed-sale source was found. Not checked: Seednet, OUAT seed sales, Odisha State Seed Corporation, KVKs, or private dealers.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Odisha (matches the request). Source: https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

RECORD NOTES
- Release year conflict: the request gives 2023-05-02, but the OUAT list is titled "released during 2022-23." Confirm against the CSC minutes before using either date.
- Open items for a follow-up session: the Seednet entry for IET 23666, the CSC minutes, the full OUAT PDF (maturity, yield, and tolerance tables), the IIRR and AICRP rice reports, KrishiKosh theses, and OUAT contact pages.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PAC 801 (rice)

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "PAC 801" / "PAC-801". Searches 1 to 4 covered both spellings, and the Seednet/PADDY (DHAN) portal did not surface in any result. No result confirms a CSC release notification for this name. The "Uttar Pradesh" recommendation comes only from the input record. Several results are commercial or non-Indian and I have flagged them as such. Four searches were run, the maximum allowed.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Advanta's Philippines launch material says PAC 801 is adaptable to both wet and dry seasons. This is a company claim, not trial data. https://news.agropages.com/News/NewsDetail---18810.htm
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No independent drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence for PAC 801 was found. No result tests PAC 801 under these stresses. https://news.agropages.com/News/NewsDetail---18810.htm

DISEASE AND PEST -- No disease or pest resistance data specific to PAC 801 was found. The Ghana hybrid evaluation lists PAC 801 among the hybrids tested for disease reaction, but the snippet gives no PAC 801 scores. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331741636_Evaluation_of_Yield_Reaction_to_Diseases_and_Grain_Physical_Attributes_of_Some_Introduced_Rice_Hybrids_in_Ghana

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Advanta's Philippines material gives a potential yield of 11 t/ha and describes grains of about 7.33 mm, slender and long. These are company claims. https://news.agropages.com/News/NewsDetail---18810.htm
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A Ghana multi-location study lists PAC 801 as a hybrid entry from Advanta Seeds (2015 source) in a yield and disease trial. The snippet does not give PAC 801's yield figures. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331741636_Evaluation_of_Yield_Reaction_to_Diseases_and_Grain_Physical_Attributes_of_Some_Introduced_Rice_Hybrids_in_Ghana
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A retail-advisory table (Krishi Jagran, May 2020) classes PAC 801 as medium maturity, rainfed, and a better grain yielder. This is not an official ICAR or SAU record. https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/paddy-cultivation-advisory-amid-covid-19/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No AICRP, ICAR or SAU multi-location trial results for PAC 801 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No parentage, marker or QTL data for PAC 801 was found. Parentage is "Not specified" in the input record and no source supplied it.
GENETICS AND QTL -- Name collision: CR Dhan 801 (IET 25667) is a different NRRI release with a known pedigree (IR81896-B-B-195 / 2*Swarna-Sub1 // IR91659-54-35). It is not PAC 801 and should not be merged with it. https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/1.-leaflet_climatesmart_final.pdf

drought.details: PAC 807 is described as a short duration, drought-tolerant hybrid suitable for direct-sown rainfed conditions. It performs well even under water scarcity and has been noted for its drought tolerance as a stress-tolerant rice hybrid (part of the STRASA initiative).

heat.details: Farmers surveyed expressed a demand for more heat-tolerant varieties, and PAC 807 plus was listed in the same surveys. However, there is no direct explicit statement of heat tolerance for PAC 807 itself.

salinity.details: Demand for salt-tolerant rice varieties was noted in surveys where PAC 807 was also listed. PAC 807 plus was mentioned in the context of paddy fields under saline conditions, but no explicit salt tolerance is stated for the variety itself.

flood.details: PAC 807 is recommended in agriculture contingency plans for districts where transient water logging or partial inundation can occur, suggesting it may be suitable for such conditions. However, no explicit flood tolerance is mentioned.

disease_resistance.summary: PAC 807 Plus is described as blast tolerant.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified

agronomic_details.yield: In a rice-chickpea cropping system, PAC 807-chickpea sequence gave a rice crop equivalent yield (RCEY) of 7942 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: The hybrid has 'made its impact with farmers' in various states, suggesting good adoption and performance.
agronomic_details.adaptation: PAC 807 is adapted to direct-sown rainfed conditions and is recommended for hybrid rice cultivation in areas with deep, heavy clay soils, including those prone to transient water logging.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: PAC 807 has been included in several production-oriented surveys and annual reports from ICAR-IIRR and AICRIP, including surveys in 2019, 2022, and 2023. It is also mentioned in state agriculture contingency plans for Jharkhand (Palamau, Garhwa districts) and in a KVK Gumla trial.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: The variety is mentioned in the context of general research on 'Incorporating Drought and Submergence Tolerance QTL in Rice', but specific QTLs for PAC 807 are not provided.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PAC 837 Plus (rice, hybrid)

Name note: The release-minutes name is "PAC 837 Plus" and the Seednet name is "PAC 837 PLUS". They differ only in capitalisation, so they refer to the same variety. Seednet itself was not returned by any search, so no Seednet-portal evidence was found. Four searches were run: variety/release, breeder, research, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Described by a seller as tolerant to blast disease, but this listing is under a VNR Seeds product name ("Mahabali") and conflicts with the Advanta claim, so treat it as unverified -- https://www.somaniagro.com/collections/paddy
- Aerobic rice on-farm trials in Gorakhpur, Deoria and Kushinagar (2016 kharif) reported PAC 837 (not confirmed as "Plus") with better drought tolerance and higher grain yield -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/talk-on-aerobicrice-technology-onfarm-testing-and-dissemination/63214523
- No evidence found for flood, submergence, heat or salinity tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Marketed as resistant to bacterial leaf blight (BLB) -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/8VJZbuUtINjWiL0MyQ5a
- No peer-reviewed or official resistance-rating evidence found for BLB, blast or insect pests.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Marketed as medium duration of 130-135 days, 13-15 productive tillers per plant, and suitable for direct-seeded rice -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/8VJZbuUtINjWiL0MyQ5a
- Advanta lists yield data from field locations across India for the 2021/22 and 2022/23 harvests, with a caveat that results depend on weather and management -- https://in.advantaseeds.com/products/pac-837-plus
- Birsa Agricultural University (Ranchi), kharif 2012-2013: PAC-837 (not confirmed as "Plus") had significantly higher dry matter and a 5.2 t/ha grain yield at 35 kg seed/ha -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-11-2017/Md.%20Naiyar%20Ali,%20et%20al.pdf
- The same Birsa study covered DRRH-3, PAC-837, Arize Tej and Lalat, so it is not a trial of PAC 837 Plus specifically.

GENETICS AND QTL:
- No evidence found. Parentage given as 837A/837 R was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Manufacturer listed as Advanta Seeds (now UPL) -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/8VJZbuUtINjWiL0MyQ5a
- AICRIP hybrid rice report 2022-23 records PAC 837 Plus as released in 2022-23 by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, with a state release for Assam. It lists private-sector breeders as developers, but names no individual breeder -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Draft%20copy%20of%20Hybrid%20Rice%20progress%20report-2022.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- No breeder name, email, phone or postal address found.
- Institute-level contact: Advanta India product page (no contact details on the page) -- https://in.advantaseeds.com/products/pac-837-plus
- Parent company: UPL Limited (formerly Advanta Limited), per the variety record. No UPL contact page was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Naiyar Ali, Md. et al. (2017). Effect of seed rate and hybrid rice cultivars on growth and yield at Birsa Agricultural University, Ranchi (kharif 2012-2013). IJCMAS -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-11-2017/Md.%20Naiyar%20Ali,%20et%20al.pdf (uses PAC-837, not "Plus")
- Hybrid Rice progress report, AICRIP (2022). ICAR AICRIP annual report -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Draft%20copy%20of%20Hybrid%20Rice%20progress%20report-2022.pdf
- Aerobic rice on-farm testing and dissemination talk (2016). Presentation -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/talk-on-aerobicrice-technology-onfarm-testing-and-dissemination/63214523 (uses PAC 837)
- No KrishiKosh theses, DOIs or peer-reviewed papers specific to PAC 837 Plus were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- Sold online as hybrid paddy seed by KrishDoctor -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/8VJZbuUtINjWiL0MyQ5a
- Sold online by Agribiz (Advanta brand, 3 kg pack, listed as PAC 837) -- https://agribiz.farm/product/pac-837/
- Sold online by Somani Agro (under the VNR "Mahabali" name) -- https://www.somaniagro.com/collections/paddy
- Assam's notified-variety list includes PAC-837 under winter and summer paddy, but this may be the non-Plus variety -- https://asoca.assam.gov.in/frontimpotentdata/notified-recommended-varieties-of-different-crops
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Assam (state release, 2022-23) -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Draft%20copy%20of%20Hybrid%20Rice%20progress%20report-2022.pdf
- Assam ASOCA list shows PAC-837 for winter and summer paddy -- https://asoca.assam.gov.in/frontimpotentdata/notified-recommended-varieties-of-different-crops

drought.details: PAC 837 is identified as a drought-tolerant rice hybrid. It is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and has been studied for marker-trait association under drought stress. It is listed among rice hybrids tolerant to abiotic stress conditions.

heat.details: PAC 837 is listed among hybrids with adaptations to heat stress tolerance and is considered heat tolerant in nature. Efforts are also noted to incorporate heat tolerance in rice varieties.

salinity.details: PAC 837 is recognized as a rice hybrid tolerant to abiotic stress conditions, including salinity. It is mentioned in contexts where tolerance to stress conditions such as salinity is a desired trait for hybrids. Farmers have expressed a need for salt tolerant varieties, with PAC 837 being cultivated.

flood.details: PAC 837 is listed among varieties capable of adapting to excess water conditions. It is mentioned in the context of flash-flood tolerance and tolerance to water logging, which are important traits for rice cultivation.

disease_resistance.summary: PAC 837 shows moderate resistance (MR) to Rice Tungro Virus (RTV), Bacterial Sheath blight (BS), and Gall Midge (GLH). For PAC 837 Plus, it is tolerant against Blast (Leaf Blast Resistant, LB R-BL) and moderately resistant to Bacterial Sheath Blight (MR-BS). False Smut has become a major problem for PAC 837 in Barpeta district of Assam.

pest_resistance.summary: PAC 837 shows moderate resistance (MR) to Green Leaf Hopper (GLH).

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 6.32 tons/ha. Reported yields also include 5.62 t/ha and 6.30 t/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Its widespread recommendation and inclusion in various national reports and hybrid lists suggest reasonable stability across different environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to irrigated areas and suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. Cultivated during the boro season in Assam. Suitable for medium duration conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Non-lodging, fertilizer responsive, medium maturity hybrid. It is semi-dwarf, with reported heights ranging from 82 cm to 100 cm. Grains are Long Slender (LS).
agronomic_details.field_trials: PAC 837 has been part of field experiments, national level monitoring team reports (BGREI), production oriented surveys, and research bulletins focusing on hybrid rice seed production technology. It has shown impact with farmers in states like Bihar, Jharkhand, and Gujarat. It has been evaluated in comparison to other hybrids and local checks.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Research has been conducted on PAC 837 to access leaf shape dynamics through marker-trait association under drought stress. This indicates the use of genetic markers in studies involving the variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PAC 8744 RICE: EVIDENCE DIGEST

Names: the CSC record name is "PAC 8744" and the Seednet name is also "PAC 8744". No Seednet page was retrieved. Retail pages use "PAC 8744+", "PAC 8744 Plus" and "UPL Advanta 8744+" for what appears to be the same product, and I have treated them as this variety only where the page itself names PAC 8744. Four searches were run (the maximum). All of them returned retailer or trader pages. None returned Seednet, ICAR/CSC, institute, KrishiKosh, AICRP or journal material for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The retailer pages describe it only as suited to irrigated conditions. PAC 8744 Plus is a premium hybrid rice engineered for maximum productivity in irrigated environments. -- https://www.somaniagro.com/collections/paddy

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial leaf blight (BLB) tolerance is claimed by the seller and not supported by trial data. This medium-duration variety is specifically bred for high Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB) resistance, ensuring crop stability. -- https://www.somaniagro.com/collections/paddy
- A second retailer lists tolerance to BLB and no other disease resistance. Tolerance to BLB -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/pac-8744-advanta-hybrid-paddy-rice
- A 2020 advisory lists the PAC 8744+ name as fortified for BLB. PAC 8744+ · Medium maturity irrigated, fortified for BLB, high yielding -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/paddy-cultivation-advisory-amid-covid-19/
- Blast, insect and other pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration and growth habit, per retailer: Kharif Duration: 130 – 135 days, medium maturity, irrigated, with long slender grain and long panicles -- https://mydukaan.io/bumi7/products/pac-8744-advanta-hybrid-paddy-rice
- Yield claim, marketer only: 20% more than OP varieties of the same duration -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/pac-8744-advanta-hybrid-paddy-rice (no trial, station or season data behind it)
- Duration also listed on a second retailer page: Short Description : ONE OF THE BEST HYBRID SEED OF PADDY Duration : 130-135 DAYS. -- https://agribiz.farm/product/pac-8744/
- Multi-location or AICRP trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: No evidence found. The CSC record gives it as not specified, and no page names a parent line.
- QTL, marker or genomic study: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Named breeder or scientist, and developing station: No evidence found.
- Company as shown on retail pages: UPL Advanta 8744+ Seed (3 per packet) -- https://www.flipkart.com/upl-advanta-8744-seed/p/itmcda922e04c552 (the CSC record names Advanta Limited; the retail listing brands it under UPL Advanta.)

CONTACT DETAILS
- Advanta Limited, institute, or breeder email, phone or postal address: No evidence found.
- Third-party seller, Dharti Agro Chemicals Pvt. Ltd., Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh: Trader - Wholesaler / Distributor of Pac 8744 Hybrid Paddy Seed ... offered by Dharti Agro Chemicals Pvt. Ltd., Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. -- https://www.indiamart.com/ankur-seed-ltd/other-products.html (trader listing; no email or street address was shown; not the developer.)
- Third-party seller in Jammu, Vikas Basotra, Kathua: listed phone +91-8048977523 -- https://dir.indiamart.com/jammu/paddy-seeds.html (retailer contact, not the developer's.)
- Third-party seller in Jammu, Sharma Karyana Store, Mahanpur, Kathua: listed phone +91-8048247111 -- https://dir.indiamart.com/jammu/paddy-seeds.html (retailer contact, not the developer's.)

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. The search returned only unrelated rice papers (Pusa Basmati 1121, IR64, IR8 and genome studies). These were discarded under the relevance rule and are not attributed to this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Retail listing shows the variety as unavailable, with an out-of-stock marker. Currently Unavailable -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/pac-8744-advanta-hybrid-paddy-rice
- Another listing sells a 3 kg pack, with an out-of-stock marker on the page. Units: 3 kg -- https://agribiz.farm/product/pac-8744/ (the stock marker is ambiguous on this page.)

The release abstract reports leaf, neck and finger blast reactions as moderately resistant compared with the ruling strain GPU 28 and national check PR 202. A disease-management article (secondary source) lists Paiyur (RA)-2 among resistant varieties, so its resistance claim is less firm than the TNAU statement.

agronomic_details.stability: Station and farmers' field trials mean 2527 kg/ha. On-farm trials (kharif 2006, 40 locations) 2312 kg/ha. All India Coordinated Trials (2002-2004; 19/14/14 locations) mean 2535 kg/ha, ranking fourth, ninth and fourth. agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed; suitable for kharif rainfed conditions. Sowing windows under rainfed conditions: June-July (Adipattam) and September-October (Puratasipattam). Resistance to lodging and fertilizer responsive.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Station and farmers' field trials: 2527 kg/ha, 14.6% above GPU 28 and 6.6% above Paiyur 1. (2) On-farm trials, kharif 2006, 40 locations: 2312 kg/ha, 9.36% above GPU 28. (3) All India Coordinated Trials 2002-2004 (19/14/14 locations): mean 2535 kg/ha, 4.67% above national check PR 202, ranked fourth, ninth and fourth. (4) Rainfed average 2527 kg/ha grain, 4200 kg/ha straw. (5) TNAU page: grain yield about 3150 kg/ha. (6) Seed-drill sowing trial at RRS Paiyur (2017-2019) used Paiyur 2 as the sown variety; yield not reported in the digest. (7) Crop establishment study: Paiyur 2 gave 1668 kg/ha grain, the highest among tested varieties; SRI establishment gave 1797 kg/ha. (8) Sodic/saline field evaluation used Paiyur 2 only as a check; no tolerance result.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Paiyur (Ra) 2, Finger millet (Eleusine coracana)

Name handling: The CSC release name is "Paiyur" and the Seednet name is "Paiyur(Ra)2". The evidence below refers to the variety as "Paiyur (Ra) 2" or "Paiyur 2". The PPV&FR notification uses "Paiyur (Ra) 2" for finger millet. Searches for "Paiyur" alone also returned Paiyur 1 (a separate finger millet variety), horsegram "Paiyur 2" (a different crop), and a little millet release table listing "Paiyur 2" (a different crop). I discarded all of these. The Seednet portal itself did not appear in any search result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Leaf blast resistant; neck and finger blast moderately resistant (this is a disease trait, listed under DISEASE AND PEST). Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. The variety is described as a rainfed-adapted type, but no tolerance rating for those stresses appeared in the results. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/ragi/season_varieties.html
Its yield was measured under rainfed conditions in the release abstract, and it is described as non-lodging. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/46179332_A_high_yielding_new_ragi_variety_Paiyur_2

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to leaf blast & moderately resistant to neck and finger blast -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/ragi/season_varieties.html
A disease-management article lists Paiyur (RA)-2 among resistant varieties to plant in a cultural-control recommendation. It is a secondary source, so treat the resistance claim as less firm than the TNAU statement. -- https://www.khethari.com/blogs/news/disease-management-in-finger-millets
Pest resistance: No evidence found. Only general pest-management text on a different page was retrieved, and I did not attribute it to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Release year 2008 (state level), duration about 115 days (medium), and rainfed sowing windows of June-July (Adipattam) and September-October (Puratasipattam). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/ragi/season_varieties.html
Grain yield about 3150 kg/ha is listed on the same TNAU page. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/ragi/season_varieties.html
Rainfed average of 2527 kg/ha grain and 4200 kg/ha straw, with 1000-grain weight of 2.9 g against 2.71 g for GPU 28, compact incurved fingers and 7.2% protein. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/A-high-yielding-new-ragi-variety-Paiyur-2-Geetha-Suthamathi/7af46dd234afc1584200d10004b120363ca4363b
Station and farmers' field trials gave 2527 kg/ha, 14.6% above GPU 28 and 6.6% above Paiyur 1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/46179332_A_high_yielding_new_ragi_variety_Paiyur_2
On-farm trials (kharif 2006, 40 locations) gave 2312 kg/ha, 9.36% above GPU 28. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/46179332_A_high_yielding_new_ragi_variety_Paiyur_2
All India Coordinated Trials (2002-2004, 19/14/14 locations) gave mean 2535 kg/ha, 4.67% above the national check PR 202, ranking fourth, ninth and fourth. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/A-high-yielding-new-ragi-variety-Paiyur-2-Geetha-Suthamathi/7af46dd234afc1584200d10004b120363ca4363b
Seed-drill sowing trial at RRS Paiyur (2017-2019) used Paiyur 2 as the sown variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385543265_Comparative_Field_Assessment_of_Sowing_of_ragi_by_Seed_Cum_Fertilizer_Drill_and_Broadcasting_Techniques
Crop establishment study: Paiyur 2 gave 1668 kg/ha grain, the highest among tested varieties, with SRI establishment giving 1797 kg/ha. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321079384_Effect_of_Crop_Establishment_Methods_and_Varieties_on_Tillering_Habit_Growth_Rate_and_Yield_of_Finger-Millet
Sodic/saline soil performance: No evidence found. A sodic-field evaluation used Paiyur 2 only as a check, so it does not show tolerance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375029105_On-farm_evaluation_of_traditional_varieties_and_landraces_of_finger_millet_Eleusine_coracana_L_Gaertnr_using_morpho-biochemical_characters

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: derivative of VL 145 x Selection 10. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/A-high-yielding-new-ragi-variety-Paiyur-2-Geetha-Suthamathi/7af46dd234afc1584200d10004b120363ca4363b
Breeding line code DPI 20030 (culture name before release). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/46179332_A_high_yielding_new_ragi_variety_Paiyur_2
Parental sources: VL 145 from ICAR-VPKAS, Almora; Selection 10 from a local collection at Paiyur. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/finalpvjdec2020sign.pdf
Breeding method: a breeding programme at RRS Paiyur (2001-2006) produced the variety through yield trials. The method is described as hybridisation followed by selection. -- https://www.researchgate.net/topic/Finger-Millet/publications/44
QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The 2010 release paper names Konala Geetha, P. Suthamathi, A. K. Mani, M. Suresh and S. Vijayabaskaran as authors. The paper credits development to the Regional Research Station, Paiyur. Their formal role as lead breeder is not stated, so treat them as the paper's authors, not confirmed breeders. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/A-high-yielding-new-ragi-variety-Paiyur-2-Geetha-Suthamathi/7af46dd234afc1584200d10004b120363ca4363b
Developing institution: Regional Research Station, Paiyur, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), Paiyur-635112. -- https://indianjourn

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Palghar-2 (rice). Four searches were run. None returned a source describing the Palghar-2 variety itself, so most headings say "No evidence found."

Name note: The CSC release name is Palghar-2 and the Seednet name is PALGHAR-1. The searches used both names, and none of the results matched either one. The only hits were general Palghar district rice pages. Those pages do not refer to either variety name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched "Palghar-2 rice variety" and "PALGHAR-1 paddy seed availability".

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Searched "Palghar-2 rice variety".

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Searched "Palghar-2 rice variety" and "Palghar-2 rice research paper".

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Searched "Palghar-2 rice research paper". Parentage IR-22/PALGHAR-141-1 (from the variety record, not verified by search).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the breeder or the developing station. Only a general reference to Dr. Balasaheb Sawant Konkan Krishi Vidyapeeth, Dapoli (M.S.) appeared, in a ResearchGate paper on rice input availability in Palghar district -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333652002_Input_availability_sources_for_rice_growers_of_Palghar_district (this confirms the university exists but not that it developed Palghar-2).

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found for any breeder, email, phone, or address. Institution named in the record: Dr. Balasaheb Sawant Konkan Krishi Vidyapeeth, Dapoli. Its official site was not retrieved, so no contact details were verified.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for Palghar-2 or PALGHAR-1. The only item retrieved is not about the variety: Authors not captured (2019 indexing). Input availability sources for rice growers of Palghar district. ResearchGate preprint -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333652002_Input_availability_sources_for_rice_growers_of_Palghar_district

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for Palghar-2 or PALGHAR-1 from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales, or dealers. Searched "PALGHAR-1 paddy seed availability".

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The variety record lists "Not specified." Searches did not confirm a state recommendation.

Gaps and next steps (not run, since the 4-search limit was reached):
- Check seednet.gov.in directly for variety code A0102536 under PALGHAR-1.
- Check the CSC/ICAR release notification for Palghar-2 (2013) for state and parentage details.
- Search KrishiKosh and the Dapoli university site for Palghar-2 trial reports and the breeding station.

seednet_candidate_fields.Agronomic Features: PAN 2423 have shown an economic yield increment with increase in fertilizer dose application in both kharif and Boro season.
seednet_candidate_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: The flag leaf attitude is Semi erect.  Distinct Anthocyanin is present at the Coleoptile, Basal leaf sheath; leaf; Auricles; Collar and tip of Lemma.  Test weight was also found to be high as per DUS guidelines of PPV&FRA.
seednet_candidate_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: PAN 2423 (IET 21395) showed resistance to Grain discolouration and sheath rot and tolerant to sheath blight, BLB and Blast, when tested at Burdwan district in under natural condition.
seednet_candidate_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: PAN 2423 (IET 21395) showed tolerant to Stem Borer and Leaf Folder in Both Kharif and Boro season under natural field condition.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no stress-tolerance data for PBM 1 (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence). -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/top-10-green-gram-mung-bean-varieties-for-punjab/

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The pages on green gram disease resistance name other varieties (IPM 512-1, MH 1142, GAM 8, ML 2056, K-851) and were discarded. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Mungbean%20varieties.pdf ; https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/5%20GAM%208%20A%20New%20High%20yielding%20MYMV%20Virus%20Resistant%20Variety%20for%20Middle%20Gujarat%20M.P.%20Patel.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
PBM 1 is described as an erect, determinate, medium-statured plant with 9-11 seeds per pod and a maturity of about 75 days, with a stated yield potential of 4.2 quintal/acre (unit as given by source) and green grain with good cooking quality. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/top-10-green-gram-mung-bean-varieties-for-punjab/
Same agronomic description, repeated on a second site. -- https://coolbeanscharters.com/top-10-green-gram-mung-bean-varieties-for-the-punjab/
PAU compendium row for PBM 1 lists a 12.50 (yield unit not stated), bold grains, and 75-day maturity; the snippet is garbled. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf
No multi-location or AICRP trial data for PBM 1 found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Breeding method: the PAU compendium row gives "Induced mutation" as the origin of PBM 1. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf
Parentage: not confirmed. The same compendium row contains a fragment "...of ML 131" next to PBM 1, which may indicate ML 131 as the mutagenized parent, but the text is garbled and does not state it. Treat as unverified. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf
No QTL, marker, or genome-resource evidence found for PBM 1. The GWAS and Nepal studies returned were for other germplasm and were discarded. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7556912/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, as given in the compendium row for PBM 1. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf
Named breeder or scientist for PBM 1: No evidence found. Searches returned breeder details for PAU wheat, gram, and mung varieties that were not PBM 1 and were discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS
No PBM 1-specific breeder contact found.
Institute-level address only: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, Punjab – 141001 (PIN as stated in a PAU breeder-seed paper). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357701641_Breeder_seed_production_of_wheat_at_PAU_A_way_to_quality_seed_availability
No official PAU email or phone was found in the results. The PAU site pages returned concern other varieties and seed programmes, so no contact was taken from them. The Brar Seed Store listing (Ludhiana) shows a phone for generic "mung" seed, not PBM 1, and was discarded. -- https://www.brarseedstore.co.in/mung-seeds-4493405.html

PUBLICATIONS
Gosal, S. S. (publisher; year not stated). A Saga of Progress: Compendium of 50 Years of Achievements. Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis, or KrishiKosh record specifically on PBM 1 found. The KrishiKosh theses returned concern other green gram cultivars (ML-267, TM 96-2, PDM 11, CO 8, GMBL-1 and others) and were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for PBM 1. Search returned PAU seed sales for paddy (PR 126) and PAU's summer moong SML 1827, plus generic mung listings; none names PBM 1 and all were discarded. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageBanner&DO=viewBannerDetail&intID=4836 ; https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&dataE=datae&intID=8944
Seednet (seednet.gov.in) was not searched directly, so the Seednet name and status remain unverified.

RECOMMENDED STATES
PBM 1 is listed as released for the south-west districts of Punjab (state-level, not central). -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf

NOTES ON NAMES AND DATES
The name in the release minutes ("PBM-1") and the Seednet name ("Unknown") were both searched only under "PBM-1" and "PBM 1". Seednet was not queried, so no Seednet name is confirmed. The sources use "PBM 1" without a hyphen, and the evidence refers to that same name.
Release year conflicts: the compendium lists 1998, while Krishi Jagran gives 2000. Neither is confirmed by a notification record.
Central release of PBM 1 is not supported by any result found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PR 130 (rice)

Name note: The CSC release name is "PR 130" and the Seednet name is "PR-113". All evidence below refers to PR 130 (Punjab Agricultural University). None of the four searches returned a Seednet page for PR-113. The Punjab Package of Practices lists PR 113 as a separate, older variety released in 1998, so the Seednet record does not appear to be the same variety and should be checked against the portal.

Search budget: I used all four permitted web_search queries in one batch. The research and contact searches returned little that was specific to PR 130, so several headings below are gaps.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Lodging tolerant, per PAU's 2022 release statement and the Kharif Package of Practices. Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6506 ; https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- Described as bacterial blight resistant; the Package of Practices says it resists all ten bacterial blight pathotypes prevalent in Punjab. No evidence on blast, sheath blight, BPH or stem borer. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf ; https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6506

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maturity about 105 days after transplanting. Average plant height about 108 cm. Average paddy yield 30.0 quintals per acre (PAU release). Recommended nursery sowing is May 20-31 per the release, and May 25-31 per the Kharif Package of Practices. Grain is long, slender, translucent, with high total and head rice recovery. Multi-location trial data: No evidence found. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6506 ; https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf ; https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/updates-detaills/new-varieties-of-paddy-released-by-pau/1127

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage: PR 121 × HKR 47, per PAU's release statement. This corrects the "Not specified" entry in the input record. QTL or marker studies: No evidence found. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6506

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana (Department of Plant Breeding & Genetics per the input record). Named PAU scientists in the search results: Dr Gurjit Singh Mangat, Additional Director of Research (Crop Improvement), who is quoted on the release; and Dr Buta Singh Dhillon, Senior Rice Breeder, named in a later PAU advisory. Whether either is the lead breeder of PR 130 is not stated. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6506 ; https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intID=7614

CONTACT DETAILS -- Dr Gurjit Singh Mangat, Additional Director of Research (Crop Improvement), PAU -- email, phone and address: not found in search results. Dr Buta Singh Dhillon, Senior Rice Breeder, PAU -- email, phone and address: not found. Institute-level website: https://pau.edu (no email, phone or postal address appeared in the search content). drought_tolerance.technical_details: No source reports a drought tolerance rating for PR-114. The PAU package of practices mentions water stress from rainfall failure or canal closure only as a management risk. A genomic-breeding review lists drought QTL (qDTY2.2 + qDTY4.1) for IR64 Drt1 (DRR Dhan 42), not for PR-114. Wild-relative introgression work mentions PR 114 only as a genetic background.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The Heliyon review's heat-tolerance snippet appears next to a list of varieties (ADT 45, Gayatri, MTU 1010, PR 114), but the snippet does not show that PR 114 itself was tested or found heat tolerant. This is not valid evidence of tolerance.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: The Heliyon review lists PR 114 with ADT 45, Gayatri, MTU 1010, Pusa 44 and Sarjoo 52 in the context of qSALTOL + qSSISFH8.1 marker-assisted work (ref 92, apparently Singh et al. 2016). This suggests PR 114 was a recipient or background variety for Saltol introgression. It does not show that PR-114 itself is salt tolerant. The NRRI book says the goal is to transfer Sub1 + drought QTL + Saltol into popular varieties. The introgression status or outcome for PR 114 cannot be confirmed from the snippets.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No flood or waterlogging tolerance data for PR-114 were found. It was released for irrigated medium ecosystems.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence that PR-114 carries Sub1 or is submergence tolerant. Mentions of submergence in the ARGM proceedings concern screening trials in general. PR-114 appears in those documents only in seed indent/production tables.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB)
disease_resistance.technical_details: A ResearchGate figure on marker-assisted backcross breeding states PR 114 is resistant to BLB with an average yield of 6.7 t/ha. The NIPHM IPM package lists PR 114 among BLB-resistant varieties (with PR 111, PR 113, PR 115, PR 116, PR 118). The specific Xa genes are not stated in the snippets. Resistance to other diseases is not documented.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no
key_stress_attributes: BLB resistance (NIPHM IPM package; ResearchGate figure on marker-assisted backcross breeding)
Used as a background variety in Saltol/marker-assisted and wild-relative introgression work. This is not evidence of tolerance in PR-114 itself.

genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_markers: No markers are documented for PR-114 itself. The Heliyon review links PR 114 to qSALTOL + qSSISFH8.1 as a recipient or background variety. The wild-relative paper (Plant Breeding, doi:10.1111/pbr.12875) reports that PR 114 crossed with O. nivara accessions (CR100142A, IRGC100593) showed complete fertility restoration.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.qtl_information: Saltol-related QTL (qSALTOL, qSSISFH8.1) are associated with PR 114 in the introgression context. No confirmed introgression outcome or effect size is available.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.breeding_techniques: PR-114 was developed by conventional breeding at PAU. It has since been used as a recipient parent in marker-assisted backcross and wild-relative introgression work.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: PR-114 has citations: a Heliyon review, a Plant Breeding paper, ICAR proceedings and PAU documents. However, the stress evidence is weak. BLB resistance is documented, but that is a biotic trait and its sources are secondary. Salinity, drought and heat are not shown for PR-114 itself, since the review snippets only list it as a background variety. There is no evidence of suitability for Gujarat. Yield data exist (about 6-6.7 t/ha in Punjab), but their provenance is mixed. The score is therefore at the 50-60 level (some trait, weak citation support), and 50 is chosen because no abiotic stress trait is confirmed and the citations are mostly indirect.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Semi-dwarf PAU variety for irrigated medium lands; BLB resistant; yield about 6-6.7 t/ha in Punjab; popular in Punjab seed indents; used as a background in Saltol and wild-relative introgression studies.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: PR-114 is a semi-dwarf, BLB-resistant, high-yielding PAU rice variety (about 6-6.7 t/ha) released around 2000 for irrigated conditions in Punjab. No abiotic stress tolerance (drought, heat, salinity, submergence) is confirmed for the variety itself, since it appears in the literature mainly as a background for Saltol and wild-relative introgression work. Evidence quality is low to moderate and suitability for Gujarat is undocumented.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Semi-dwarf PAU variety with narrow, dark green erect leaves and a height of about 102 cm. Yield is about 6-6.7 t/ha under irrigated Punjab conditions. Maturity duration and parentage are not specified.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: BLB resistance is the only documented stress trait. No evidence confirms drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in PR-114 itself. Its mentions in genomic reviews concern use as a breeding background.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae): the source reports PR 123 as resistant to all 10 presently prevalent pathotypes of the BB pathogen in Punjab (ResearchGate figure). A PAU-linked summary at apnikheti.com describes it as only moderately resistant to bacterial blight, which conflicts with the first source; the conflict is unresolved. The research paper's disease reaction table (artificial inoculation at PAU) is referenced, but its values were not legible in the extracted text. Sheath blight: susceptible, with no genetic resistance available (ResearchGate figure). The AICRIP Ludhiana document lists PR 123 among bacterial blight variety entries, but gene assignments were not legible.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Fits the rice-wheat system in Punjab (ResearchGate figure). The digest notes a 2014 state approval reported in the research paper, which conflicts with the 2015-10-12 release date in the record.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Across 117 trials, 7333 kg/ha, about 8.75% above the check PR 111 (6743 kg/ha). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PR 123 (rice, Punjab Agricultural University, PAU code PAU 3842): evidence digest

Name note: "PR 123" (CSC minutes name) is used in all searches except the seed-availability query, which also used "PR-123" (Seednet name). No Seednet page was found under either spelling, so every finding below refers to the name "PR 123" unless stated otherwise. The 2015-10-12 release date in the record conflicts with the 2014 state approval reported in the research paper; both are noted under RECOMMENDED STATES.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to all 10 presently prevalent pathotypes of bacterial blight in Punjab -- PR 123 is resistant to all the presently prevalent 10 pathotypes of BB pathogen (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae) in the state of Punjab. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Conflicting bacterial blight description: a PAU-linked summary calls it only moderately resistant to bacterial blight -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/cereals/rice
- Sheath blight: susceptible, with no genetic resistance available -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. The search returned no PR 123-specific tolerance data for these stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial blight: see STRESS TOLERANCE above. The research paper's disease reaction table (artificial inoculation at PAU) is referenced but its values were not legible in the extracted text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005303_PR_123_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Superfine_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Insect pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Semi-dwarf, dark green erect leaves, average plant height about 105 cm -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Maturity about 143 days after seeding; fits the rice-wheat system in Punjab -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Yield components: about 338 panicles per square metre, about 136 spikelets per panicle, 88.0% fertility -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Across 117 trials, 7333 kg/ha, about 8.75% above the check PR 111 (6743 kg/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Farm yield about 29 quintal/acre -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/cereals/rice
- Average paddy yield about 2.0 quintal/acre above PR 111, with some farmers reporting 90-100 maunds/acre; this is a press account -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/features/rice-variety-pr-111-replaces-pr-123-84192
- Grain quality: extra-long slender, translucent grain, length/breadth ratio 3.98, head rice recovery 54.68% -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Tested in the AICRIP IVT-IME trial in Kharif 2013 as IET 23774 -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303

GENETICS AND QTL
- Designation PAU 3842-59-7-1-1, from the cross PR 116///PR 108/IRRI 76//PR 106-P2, by pedigree selection. This gives the parentage that the record lists as "Not specified" -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- QTL and marker studies: No evidence found. A PAU-AICRIP Ludhiana table lists PR 123 among bacterial blight variety entries, but gene assignments were not legible -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/31%20Ludhiana.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Authors: TS Bharaj, GS Mangat, Rupinder Kaur, Kuldeep Singh, Naveen Singh; Mangat is at PAU, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005303_PR_123_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Superfine_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Dr GS Mangat, described in a press report as senior rice breeder, PAU -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/features/rice-variety-pr-111-replaces-pr-123-84192
- Developing institution: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana; Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005303_PR_123_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Superfine_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr GS Mangat, corresponding author, email mangatgs@pau.edu -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005303_PR_123_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Superfine_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Institute postal address as given in the paper: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana - 141004 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005303_PR_123_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Superfine_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Dr Navjot Sidhu, Rice Breeder, PAU, office phone 91-0161-2401960 Ext. 423. This is a section-level contact and is not named for PR 123 specifically -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=449&intDepTitleID=21&intLinkID=9
- Official PAU email and phone for the rice section: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS

Journal not named in the extracted text (accepted 05.02.2015, "New Crop Variety" section) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005303_PR_123_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Superfine_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Journal DOI: not found in the search results
- AICRIP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper specific to PR 123: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Older PAU notice: PR 123 seed available at PAU Ludhiana, University Seed Farm Ladhowal, Bir Sikhan Wala, Naraingarh, and KVKs -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/education/director-assumes-charge-63825/
