search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pratibha (rice) -- variety_name "Pratibha" / seednet_variety_name "PRATIBHA" (OR 2172-7, IET 21582; SOWBHAGYA/ARC 6650; OUAT; released 2018-08-10)

Search budget: 4 web_search queries were run (one batch of four, covering variety/release, breeder/institution, research/trials, and seed availability). No query returned a page that names the rice variety Pratibha. Under each heading below, "No evidence found" means none of the four searches surfaced a relevant record. It does not mean the variety lacks such data. Seednet was not reached directly, so neither name was confirmed on that portal.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned only other OUAT rice releases (Kalinga Rice 1/Kolab, Kalinga Dhan 1205) with no Pratibha entry -- https://ouat.ac.in/regional-reaearch-and-technology-transfer-sub-station-jeypore-koraput/technologies-generated-jaypore/ ; https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found for Pratibha. The OUAT 2022-23 release list covers other rice varieties' resistance profiles only -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found for Pratibha (maturity, yield, plant height, or trial data not retrieved) -- https://ouat.ac.in/regional-reaearch-and-technology-transfer-sub-station-jeypore-koraput/technologies-generated-jaypore/

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found -- no Pratibha pedigree or marker study surfaced beyond the parentage supplied in the brief.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Institution is OUAT, Bhubaneswar (per the supplied record). No lead breeder name was found. A general source notes that Odisha's rice seed breeders are based at OUAT or at national institutes -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10460-024-10666-0

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder or named contact found. Institute-level domain only: OUAT website https://ouat.ac.in (Directorate of Research, Bhubaneswar, appears on the 2022-23 release PDF above). No email, phone, or postal address for the institute or Directorate was retrieved in these searches.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found for Pratibha. Only general rice-in-Odisha references surfaced, which do not cover this variety -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf (S.R. Das, IRRI Technical Bulletin 16, 2012, on Odisha rice and OUAT/CRRI releases; not specific to Pratibha).

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for Pratibha. The Odisha seed-distribution report notes seed supply gaps for some varieties but names no Pratibha seed source -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES: Supplied record says Odisha. No independent notification or state recommendation text for Pratibha was found in the searches.

Suggested next steps (outside this search budget): check the CSC/ICAR release notification for the 2018 Odisha entry, the seednet.gov.in variety page under PRATIBHA, the OUAT Directorate of Research variety list for 2018, and KrishiKosh for OUAT theses or papers.

drought.details: No evidence found. Searches returned no trial data on drought for PR 122.

heat.details: In a temperature-gradient tunnel study (kharif 2013-14, +4.5 to +5.8 C), PR 122 had the highest harvest index (33.0%) of six cultivars. The authors read this as the most heat-tolerant of the set. Grain number per panicle fell 30.6-46.7% under elevated temperature across cultivars, including PR 122. The level is medium because the evidence is a single study with a relative ranking and no mechanism data.

salinity.details: No evidence found. Searches returned no trial data on salinity for PR 122.

flood.details: No evidence found. Searches returned no trial data on flood for PR 122.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight: described as resistant to all ten pathotypes of bacterial blight prevalent in Punjab; carries resistance genes Xa4, xa13 and Xa21 (see genetics section). Rice blast (Pyricularia oryzae): in Talwandi Sabo, Malwa (2017-18), panicle blast incidence was lowest in PR 122 among the cultivars tested (PB 1121 was highest); the source text is partly garbled, so this finding is tentative and no resistance level is stated. Sheath blight: PR 122 is susceptible, with no genetic resistance available.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance evidence found. A 2013 pest-management table lists flubendamide for stem borer control under PR 122; this is a chemical control recommendation, not evidence of resistance. Other pests: no evidence found.

agronomic_details.yield: PAU trials (100 trials): average 7,965 kg/ha, 4.38% above check PR 118 (7,631 kg/ha). PAU extension figure: average 31.5 quintals per acre. AICRIP Ludhiana centre (2013): average 7,825 kg/ha. KVK Sri Muktsar Sahib (kharif 2013): grain yield 77.3 q/ha, not significantly different from the top entry.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Punjab. Tested in Ludhiana (AICRIP), Sri Muktsar Sahib district, Talwandi Sabo (Malwa) and central Punjab. Nursery sowing window May 20-25 (PAU kharif recommendation).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: About 147 days after seeding (release paper); 117 days after transplanting (PAU extension note). The two bases differ; both are reported as found. KVK Sri Muktsar Sahib (kharif 2013): 146.3 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf, dark green erect leaves, plant height about 108 cm, 316 panicles/m2, about 152 spikelets per panicle, fertility 93.8%. KVK Sri Muktsar Sahib (kharif 2013): 441.7 tillers/m2.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) PAU multi-location trials, 100 trials: average 7,965 kg/ha, 4.38% above PR 118 check (7,631 kg/ha). (2) PAU extension figure: average 31.5 quintals per acre. (3) AICRIP Ludhiana centre, 2013: average 7,825 kg/ha. (4) KVK Sri Muktsar Sahib, kharif 2013: maturity 146.3 days, 441.7 tillers/m2, grain yield 77.3 q/ha, not significantly different from the top entry. (5) Crop establishment study, kharif 2020-21, central Punjab: PR 122 compared with PR 126 and Pusa 44 under direct-seeded rice (DSR) and puddled transplanting, with tiller, height and yield-component data; numeric values for PR 122 are not given in the digest. (6) Talwandi Sabo, Malwa (2017-18): blast screening, PR 122 lowest panicle blast incidence (see disease section). (7) Temperature-gradient tunnel study, kharif 2013-14: highest harvest index (33.0%) among six cultivars (see heat section).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Gene-based bacterial blight resistance genes reported: Xa4, xa13 and Xa21. Chromosome positions and marker-trait associations: Not found in searched sources. Pedigree: PR 108/IRRI-76//PR 106-P1, pedigree selection; designation PAU 3761-26-3-1.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTL studies: No evidence found. No marker-trait mapping study found.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Resistance to bacterial blight conferred by Xa4, xa13 and Xa21 genes (gene-based, as reported in the release paper). No other pathway or gene-level evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PR 122 (rice, Oryza sativa)

Name check: The CSC minutes name and the Seednet name are both "PR 122". I did not reach the Seednet portal itself, so no Seednet-specific page was found. All findings below refer to the PR 122 rice variety, and none refers to PR 126, PR 121, PR 124, or other "PR" numbers.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bacterial blight: PR 122 is described as resistant to all ten pathotypes of bacterial blight prevalent in Punjab -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf (also https://foragenseeds.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/PAU-RICE-POP-DOWNLOADED-ON-30.05.2025.pdf)
- Heat: In a temperature-gradient tunnel study (kharif 2013-14, +4.5 to +5.8 °C), PR 122 had the highest harvest index (33.0%) of six cultivars, which the authors read as the most heat-tolerant of the set; grain number per panicle fell 30.6-46.7% under elevated temperature across cultivars -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353378154_Rice_yield_variability_in_Punjab_-_an_overview_of_five_decades_Paddy_and_Water_Environment_193
- Drought, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. Searches returned no trial data on these stresses for PR 122.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial blight: Three BB resistance genes (Xa4, xa13, Xa21) are reported -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Sheath blight: PR 122 is susceptible, with no genetic resistance available -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Rice blast (Talwandi Sabo, Malwa, 2017-18): Panicle blast incidence was lowest in PR 122 among the cultivars tested (PB 1121 was highest); text is partly garbled in the extract -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-8-2020/Nalini%20Singh%20and%20Jasvir%20Singh%20Brar.pdf
- Stem borer: A 2013 pest-management table lists PR 121 and PR 122 under flubendamide for stem borer -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353378154_Rice_yield_variability_in_Punjab_-_an_overview_of_five_decades_Paddy_and_Water_Environment_193
- Other pests and diseases: No evidence found beyond the above.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration: Matures about 147 days after seeding, and an 8-trial/extension note gives 117 days after transplanting -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L ; https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf (the two bases differ; both are reported as found)
- Morphology: Semi-dwarf, dark green erect leaves, plant height about 108 cm, 316 panicles/m², about 152 spikelets per panicle, fertility 93.8% -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Yield (PAU trials): Average 7,965 kg/ha over 100 trials, 4.38% above check PR 118 (7,631 kg/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Yield (PAU extension figure): Average 31.5 quintals per acre -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
- Yield (AICRIP Ludhiana centre, 2013): Average 7,825 kg/ha -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/31%20Ludhiana.pdf
- KVK Sri Muktsar Sahib (kharif 2013): Maturity 146.3 days, 441.7 tillers/m², grain yield 77.3 q/ha (not significantly different from the top entry) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/303775999_Comparative_Performance_of_Different_Varieties_of_Rice_in_Muktsar_District_of_Punjab
- Crop establishment (kharif 2020-21, central Punjab): PR 122 compared with PR 126 and Pusa 44 under DSR and puddled transplanting, with tiller, height and yield-component data -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/5839/5209
- Sowing window: Nursery May 20-25 (PAU kharif recommendation) -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: PR 108/IRRI-76//PR 106-P1, pedigree selection; designation PAU 3761-26-3-1 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Marker/gene content: Xa4, xa13 and Xa21 (gene-based, from the release paper; no QTL or marker-trait mapping study found) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- QTL studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana; Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Lead authors of the release paper: TS Bharaj, GS Mangat, Rupinder Kaur, Kuldeep Singh, Naveen Singh -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Principal rice breeder: GS Mangat, described in 2019 as principal rice breeder at PAU -- https://www.downtoearth.org.in/air/why-punjab-s-short-duration-paddy-varieties-have-not-solved-stubble-burning-80224
- Release year discrepancy: Release-paper and secondary sources give 2013 (State Variety Approval Committee, Punjab). The input record's year, 2015-10-12, is not supported by any retrieved source -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L ; https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf (not used for this year; see the table at http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/31%20Ludhiana.pdf, which lists 2013)
- Input parentage "Not specified": Parentage is available in the release paper (see GENETICS AND QTL).

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder/author: GS Mangat, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana. Corresponding-author email as printed: managatgs@pau.edu -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Institute address (from release paper): Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana - 141004 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005488_PR_122_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Institute phone and official institute contact page: No evidence found in these searches.
- Seller contacts are listed under SEED AVAILABILITY and are not institute contacts.

PUBLICATIONS

- Nalini Singh, Jasvir Singh Brar (2020). Screening of Disease Incidence in Rice Cultivars against Pyricularia oryzae in Talwandi Sabo, Punjab, India. Int J Curr Microbiol App Sci 9(8): 2198-2208 -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-8-2020/Nalini%20Singh%20and%20Jasvir%20Singh%20Brar.pdf ; DOI https://doi.org/10.20546/ijcmas.2020.908.251
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Rice yield variability in Punjab: an overview of five decades. Paddy and Water Environment 19(3) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353378154_Rice_yield_variability_in_Punjab_-_an_overview_of_five_decades_Paddy_and_Water_Environment_193
- Authors not captured (2013 kharif trial). Comparative Performance of Different Varieties of Rice in Muktsar District of Punjab. Report/conference item -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/303775999_Comparative_Performance_of_Different_Varieties_of_Rice_in_Muktsar_District_of_Punjab

disease_resistance.research_summary: Bacterial blight: described as resistant to all ten pathotypes of bacterial blight prevalent in Punjab; carries resistance genes Xa4, xa13 and Xa21 (see genetics section). Rice blast (Pyricularia oryzae): in Talwandi Sabo, Malwa (2017-18), panicle blast incidence was lowest in PR 122 among the cultivars tested (PB 1121 was highest); the source text is partly garbled, so this finding is tentative and no resistance level is stated. Sheath blight: PR 122 is susceptible, with no genetic resistance available.

drought.details: No direct drought-tolerance trial data found in the digest. Indirect evidence relates to water use and drought escape rather than tolerance: a short duration allows transplanting with the monsoon, and a farmer-participatory claim reports about 25% less water use than Pusa 44 and other long-duration types (unverified). PAU scientists state it can be sown near monsoon onset to conserve groundwater. These points indicate water-saving and escape potential, not measured drought tolerance.

drought.details: Identified as drought tolerant and suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. It is considered a short duration and drought tolerant variety.

heat.details: Described as heat tolerant and moderately resistant to terminal heat stress.

salinity.details: Shows tolerance to salinity, with some reports mentioning its performance under saline conditions. It is suitable for saline environments.

flood.details: Demonstrations of flood tolerant varieties in states like Bihar, West Bengal, and Odisha included PR 127, indicating its suitability for flood-prone areas.

disease_resistance.summary: PR 127 shows resistance to Bacterial Blight, is moderately resistant to White Rust, and mentions of general disease resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: Reported as tolerant to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) and generally resistant to major pests.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields vary: 50 Q/ha (50 quintals per hectare) according to rice-garud.icar-web.com, and an average paddy yield of 29.5 quintals per acre (approximately 72.8 Q/ha) according to Punjab Agricultural University.
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and direct seeding. It is adapted to lowland rice cultivation. Recommended for cultivation in Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat, Odisha, Bihar, and West Bengal.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 137 days. It is described as a medium maturing and short duration variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: PR 127 is a Non-Basmati variety. It is described as 'Dwarf' with an approximate height of 80 cm, though Punjab Agricultural University reports an average height of 104 cm. Its grains are long-slender (LS) and white.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Regularly included in annual rice group meetings and surveys (AICRIP, IIRR proceedings) for assessment of stress tolerance and agronomic parameters at various research centers including PAU, Ludhiana.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: The `xa45(t)` gene has been introgressed into PR 127 for Bacterial Blight resistance. The `qSub1` QTL is introgressed for submergence tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: The `qSub1` QTL has been introgressed to confer submergence tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Developed through molecular breeding, specifically by introgressing the `xa45(t)` gene into the popular variety Pusa 44 and introgressing the `qSub1` QTL for submergence tolerance. It is also noted to have 3 favorable alleles.

drought.details: No PR 128-specific evidence for drought tolerance was found. The only water-related statements concern its shorter duration and lower water requirement compared with Pusa 44. These describe water use, not drought tolerance mechanisms.

heat.details: No PR 128-specific heat tolerance evidence was found. The source describes early maturity (about 111 days after transplanting) as allowing the crop to avoid late-season abiotic stress, but this claim is made for the PR 121/126/128/131 group as a whole, not for PR 128 alone, so it is not attributed to PR 128.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. No PR 128-specific flood evidence in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight: PR 128 is reported as resistant to all 10 prevalent pathotypes of bacterial blight in Punjab (PAU sources). The PAU package of practices lists PR 128 among varieties resistant to most bacterial blight pathotypes. No PR 128-specific evidence was found for blast, false smut, sheath blight or other diseases.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No PR 128-specific evidence for brown planthopper, stem borer or other pests. The escape-from-pests statement in the source applies to the PR group generally and is not attributed to PR 128.

agronomic_details.yield: Average paddy yield 30.5 quintals per acre (PAU source). Fodder yield 234 quintals per acre against 214 for FBC 16, reported for fodder purpose.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location AICRP trial data specific to PR 128 were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Released for cultivation across Punjab. Nursery sowing recommended for May 20-25. Optimal yield is reported when transplanted after 20 June, which also leaves time for straw management without burning.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: About 111 days after transplanting, compared with about 130 days for Pusa 44
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Average plant height 110 cm. Grain long, slender and clear translucent. Milling: total and head rice recoveries were found at par with popular varieties; out-turn meets the 67% custom milling standard.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Paddy yield: average 30.5 quintals per acre. (2) Fodder purpose: 234 quintals per acre versus 214 quintals per acre for FBC 16. (3) Maturity: about 111 days after transplanting versus about 130 days for Pusa 44. (4) Milling trials run in 2019 and 2020: total and head rice recoveries at par with popular varieties; out-turn meets the 67% custom milling standard. (5) Transplanting date: optimal yield reported when transplanted after 20 June. No multi-location AICRP trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PR 128 (rice)
Name matching: "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" are both "PR 128". The search for the Seednet portal returned no Seednet page, so all evidence below refers to the name "PR 128". The variety code "(RYT 3437)" appeared in no result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Early maturity (about 111 days after transplanting) is described as letting the crop avoid late-season abiotic stress, but the source makes this claim for the PR 121/126/128/131 group as a whole, not for PR 128 alone. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&dataE=datae&intID=8996
- No PR 128-specific evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The only PR 128 water-related statements concern its shorter duration and lower water requirement compared with Pusa 44. -- https://www.aninews.in/news/national/general-news/punjab-farmers-advised-cultivating-pr-128-pr-129-varieties-of-non-basmati20200514174215/

DISEASE AND PEST
- PR 128 is reported as resistant to all 10 prevalent pathotypes of bacterial blight in Punjab. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf ; https://www.apnikheti.com/en/rj/updates-detaills/punjab-agricultural-university-has-developed-and-recommended-seven-new-varieties/1033
- The PAU package of practices lists PR 128 among varieties resistant to most bacterial blight pathotypes. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
- No PR 128-specific evidence found for blast, false smut, sheath blight, brown planthopper, stem borer or other pests. The escape-from-pests statement applies to the PR group generally. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&dataE=datae&intID=8996

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is about 111 days after transplanting, compared with about 130 days for Pusa 44. -- https://www.aninews.in/news/national/general-news/punjab-farmers-advised-cultivating-pr-128-pr-129-varieties-of-non-basmati20200514174215/
- Average plant height is 110 cm. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
- Average paddy yield is 30.5 quintals per acre. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5025
- Fodder yield was reported at 234 quintals per acre, against 214 for FBC 16 (fodder purpose). -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intEventID=5025
- Optimal yield is reported when transplanted after 20 June, which also leaves time for straw management without burning. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5117
- Nursery sowing is recommended for May 20-25. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
- Milling: total and head rice recoveries were found at par with popular varieties. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5117
- Milling trials were run in 2019 and 2020, and out-turn meets the 67% custom milling standard. -- https://www.diprpunjab.gov.in/?q=content/agriculture-department-advises-farmers-cultivation-pr-128-pr-129-varieties-non-basmati
- Grain is long, slender and clear translucent. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
- No multi-location AICRP trial data specific to PR 128 found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage/origin: described as an improved version of PAU 201. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&intEventID=5025 . The same source says PR 128 is distinct from PAU 201 (https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5117).
- Breeding line code, breeding method, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana, established 1962. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5025
- Lead breeder: Dr Mangat, Principal Rice Breeder and Head, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, PAU, Ludhiana (first name not given in the source). -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5117
- A PAU faculty profile says the scientist was involved in developing and releasing PR 128, PR 129, PR 130, PR 131 and PR 132. The faculty name is not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=449&intDepTitleID=21&intLinkID=9
- Release approval was given by the State Variety Approval Committee, chaired by Dr Suntantar Kumar Airi, Director of Agriculture, Punjab. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5025
- Director of Research Dr Navtej Singh Bains and Director of Extension Education Dr Jaskarn Singh Mahal commented on the variety. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/pau-develops-7-crop-varieties-45280

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder: Dr Mangat, Principal Rice Breeder and Head, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, PAU, Ludhiana. No email or phone found. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5117
- Institute: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, Punjab, India. No official email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL was retrieved. Institute site: https://www.pau.edu
- No contact details found for the faculty profile.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found naming PR 128 in a peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or conference paper. Two PAU faculty-profile papers (Lore et al. 2022, false smut donors; Jain et al. 2025, basmati neck blast) were discarded because they do not name PR 128. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=449&intDepTitleID=21&intLinkID=9
- Not searched: KrishiKosh (krishikosh.egranth.ac.in) and the AICRP rice site were not queried, because the four-search limit was reached.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Private dealer listing, Vignette Hi Tech Seed Company, Karnal, Haryana, "Natural Brown P.R.-128" at Rs 45/kg, minimum order 100 kg. -- https://indiamart.com/proddetail/p-r-128-new-paddy-seed-23372231955.html
- Private dealer listing, MK Natural Grains Exim (brand Yamuna Seeds), Indri, Haryana, "Natural PR-128" at Rs 45/kg, 10 kg and 30 kg. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/pr-128-paddy-seeds-23217033388.html
- Online retailer listing, Green World "Pusa PR-128", 1 kg and 10 kg. This is a third-party brand. -- https://www.amazon.in/Green-World-agriculture-Kg-pack/dp/B0BC26RDGB
- Caution: PAU advises farmers to buy only from authenticated sources. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5117
- Not found: Seednet listing, NSC or State Seed Corporation stock, KVK sales, and PAU seed-sale counter listings for PR 128.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Punjab. Released for cultivation across Punjab by the State Variety Approval Committee in February 2020. -- https://www.aninews.in/news/national/general-news/punjab-farmers-advised-cultivating-pr-128-pr-129-varieties-of-non-basmati20200514174215/
- PAU announcement dated 19 February 2020 covering PR 128, PR 129 and HKR 47. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5025

RELEASE YEAR (CSC field "Not specified")
- 2020, from the Punjab State Variety Approval Committee approval in February 2020. A Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards notification number was not found.

DISCARDED RESULTS
- The PR 126 hybrid controversy and PR 132 items concern other varieties. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/patiala/experts-at-kisan-mela-warn-farmers-against-fake-hybrid-seeds
- Pusa Basmati 1121 and PR 111 pages concern other varieties.
- The "PR Super 212" item concerns a private variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY RECORD: Pant Basmati 2 (CSC minutes name) / PUNJAB BASMATI-2 (Seednet name)

Name note: The evidence found refers to Pant Basmati 2 (IET 21953). It does not refer to PUNJAB BASMATI-2. Sources listing Punjab Basmati 2 show a separate notification (1708(E), 26.07.2012), so the Seednet name points to a different variety. Nothing found under the Seednet name was attributed to this record.

Parentage conflict: The supplied parentage (PAU 3030-29-2, Basmati 386/Super Basmati) names a PAU line. The AICRIP Pantnagar report gives the designation UPR 3506-7-1-1 for IET 21953. The record should not accept the supplied parentage without verification.

Year conflict: The supplied release year is 2014. Sources give 2016 (notification 112(E), 13.01.2016). The AICRIP Pantnagar report says release proposals were submitted in 2014.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Pant Basmati 2. The only stress-related items found concern other varieties (for example Pusa Basmati 1718 and Pusa Basmati 1847 for bacterial blight and blast), which were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found specific to Pant Basmati 2. An AICRIP Pantnagar report discusses bacterial blight pathotypes and insect date-of-planting effects in general terms, without naming this variety in those passages. Discarded as not specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Pant Basmati 2 is named as suitable for basmati-growing areas in an AICRIP Pantnagar centre report -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf
Pantnagar's AICRP rice document says the centre developed Pant Basmati 1 and Pant Basmati 2 and nominates entries to AICRP, SVT and INGER trials each year -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/2%20AICRP%20-RICE.pdf
No yield, maturity or plant-height data for Pant Basmati 2 were found. Two listings (airea.net and global-agriculture.com) give only the notification number and date.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The AICRIP Pantnagar report gives the line designation UPR 3506-7-1-1 but no pedigree or marker data.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, through the AICRIP rice centre in the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf and https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/2%20AICRP%20-RICE.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. The sources name no individual breeder for this variety. The Pusa Basmati breeder names found (Ashok Kumar Singh, IARI) relate to other varieties and were discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. Institute-level information only: GBPUAT Pantnagar, Udham Singh Nagar district, Uttarakhand 263145, and university website gbpuat.ac.in -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G._B._Pant_University_of_Agriculture_and_Technology (secondary source). No official email, phone or contact-page URL for the rice breeding programme was found. Verify directly with GBPUAT before use.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis or conference paper naming Pant Basmati 2 was found. Institutional reports found:
Author not stated (year not stated). AICRIP Pantnagar centre report, rice: IET 21953 named Pant Basmati 2, suitable for basmati-growing areas. Report -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf
Author not stated (year not stated). GBPUAT AICRP rice significant achievements: Pant Basmati 1 and Pant Basmati 2 developed at Pantnagar. Report -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/2%20AICRP%20-RICE.pdf
Items not verified: KrishiKosh and seednet.gov.in were not reached in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed listings returned were for Pakistani Punjab varieties (PK-1121, Super Basmati) and were discarded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, GBPUAT seed sales or dealer listing for Pant Basmati 2 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for a state list. The AICRIP Pantnagar report only says the variety suits basmati-growing areas -- https://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf
The Uttarakhand plains are the centre's mandate area, but no notification or recommendation text confirms which states this variety was released for.

Searches run: 4 (general variety; Seednet name; breeder/institute; IET 21953/GBPUAT trial). The Seednet portal itself was not reached, so the Seednet record for PUNJAB BASMATI-2 was not checked directly.

drought.details: Identified as tolerant against drought stress conditions, with significant improvement over Basmati 386. Evaluations for drought tolerance have utilized leaf rolling and senescence scores as selection criteria.

heat.details: Undergoing screening for high temperature tolerance in various research group meetings.

salinity.details: Demonstrates significant improvement in salt stress tolerance compared to Basmati 386. Included in general screenings for abiotic stresses like salinity.

flood.details: Not specified directly; however, it is screened for submergence tolerance, which is related to flood conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to White Backed Plant Hopper (BPH) and tolerant to Rice Tungro Virus (RTV). It is not identified as a diverse resistant/tolerant resource against bacterial blight.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to White Backed Plant Hopper (BPH). However, it is susceptible to Stem Borer and Leaf Folder insects.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield of 3156 kg/ha of paddy in different trials, with a potential yield of 5663 kg/ha. Reported yields also include 47 Q/ha (4700 kg/ha) and 4.0 t/ha (4000 kg/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly detailed, but trials indicate consistent performance within its adaptation zone.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Well-suited for the Basmati rice-wheat crop rotation prevalent in its recommended states. Primarily adapted to irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Intermediate tall / Semi tall (approximately 125 cm height) of medium maturity. Grains are described as Medium Slender (MS), white, and Aromatic White (AWA) by some sources, while others characterize them as Extra Long Slender (ELS), possessing excellent cooking and eating qualities.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Included in various yield assessment trials. Extensively screened for tolerance to abiotic stresses such as drought, heat, salinity, submergence, low temperature, and low-light conditions under AICRIP (All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project) group meetings. Also evaluated in genetic variability studies for yield and physiological traits.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Moderately resistant to White Backed Plant Hopper (BPH) and tolerant to Rice Tungro Virus (RTV). It is not identified as a diverse resistant/tolerant resource against bacterial blight.

pest_resistance.research_summary: Moderately resistant to White Backed Plant Hopper (BPH). However, it is susceptible to Stem Borer and Leaf Folder insects.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to bacterial blight (PAU-linked publication abstract; the variety is described as a bacterial blight resistant dwarf version of Basmati 386). The digest also records tolerance to lodging, which is not a disease finding and is noted here only for completeness: described as a semi-dwarf, photoperiod-sensitive aromatic line that is tolerant to lodging and resistant to bacterial blight. No evidence found for resistance to other diseases.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for resistance to blast, brown planthopper or stem borer for this variety. The digest notes a grain-tip awn feature said to deter birds; this is a bird-deterrent trait, not a pest-resistance finding.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Punjab Basmati 3 (rice)
Names searched: "Punjab Basmati 3" (CSC minutes name) and "PUNJAB BASMATI 3" (Seednet name). The search engine did not distinguish case, so both names are covered by the same results. Four searches were run: variety/traits, breeder/institution, research, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistant to bacterial blight and tolerant to lodging, per a PAU-linked publication abstract -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276391858_Punjab_Basmati_3-_A_Bacterial_Blight_Resistant_Dwarf_version_of_Basmati_Rice_Variety_Basmati_386
Described as a semi-dwarf, photoperiod-sensitive aromatic line that is tolerant to lodging and resistant to bacterial blight -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325384698_Basmati_Rice_in_the_Indian_Subcontinent_Strategies_to_Boost_Production_and_Quality_Traits
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
Bacterial blight resistance (see above); a grain-tip awn feature is noted as deterring birds -- https://www.academia.edu/30125861/Punjab_Basmati_3_A_Bacterial_Blight_Resistant_Dwarf_version_of_Basmati_Rice_Variety_Basmati_386
Blast, brown planthopper and stem borer resistance: No evidence found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Reported yield of about 4082 kg/ha, about 31% above Basmati 386, across 59 trials in Punjab -- https://www.academia.edu/30125861/Punjab_Basmati_3_A_Bacterial_Blight_Resistant_Dwarf_version_of_Basmati_Rice_Variety_Basmati_386
Maturity about 139 days and height about 105 cm; about 335 panicles per square metre and 67 spikelets per panicle -- https://www.academia.edu/30125861/Punjab_Basmati_3_A_Bacterial_Blight_Resistant_Dwarf_version_of_Basmati_Rice_Variety_Basmati_386
Nitrogen-source trial at PAU Ludhiana (2010–2011) on basmati rice, variety not named in the abstract, so not attributed to this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325384698_Basmati_Rice_in_the_Indian_Subcontinent_Strategies_to_Boost_Production_and_Quality_Traits (excluded from attribution; listed for transparency only)
Farm-level 2022–23 yield survey of ten basmati varieties in Punjab that includes Punjab Basmati 3; the table snippet lists yields for other varieties only, so no per-variety figure is attributed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389599197_Economics_of_Basmati_Rice_Cultivation_in_Punjab

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found (no QTL, marker or parentage study naming this variety was returned). Parentage is recorded as "Not specified" in the input; the only related statement is that it is an improved version of Basmati 386 -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/cereals/rice

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by PAU Ludhiana -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/cereals/rice
Co-authors of the 2014 PB3 paper are listed as Kuldeep Singh, Gurjit Mangat and Rupinder Kaur, with affiliations given as ICRISAT, Punjab Agricultural University and University of Wolverhampton respectively. Their roles in developing the variety are not stated in the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276391858_Punjab_Basmati_3-_A_Bacterial_Blight_Resistant_Dwarf_version_of_Basmati_Rice_Variety_Basmati_386
Lead breeder name for PB3: No evidence found. A PAU rice-breeding faculty profile was returned, but the snippet does not name it as PB3's breeder, so it is not attributed -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?DO=viewFacultyData&_act=manageDepartments&intDepTitleID=21&intFacultyID=151&intLinkID=9

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for an official email, phone or postal address for this variety or its breeder. Institute-level pages returned did not show contact text: Punjab Agricultural University home page -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?DO=viewFacultyData&_act=manageDepartments&intDepTitleID=21&intFacultyID=151&intLinkID=9 (faculty profile; no contact fields in snippet). Search again on the PAU site, the Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics page, or the PAU rice programme for contact details.

PUBLICATIONS
Singh, K., Mangat, G., Kaur, R., et al. (2014). Punjab Basmati 3 - A Bacterial Blight Resistant Dwarf version of Basmati Rice Variety Basmati 386. Journal of Agricultural Research 51(2) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276391858_Punjab_Basmati_3-_A_Bacterial_Blight_Resistant_Dwarf_version_of_Basmati_Rice_Variety_Basmati_386 (the author list shows only the first three names; the full author list was not checked)
Journal of Agricultural Research record from the same page (no separate DOI shown) -- https://www.academia.edu/30125861/Punjab_Basmati_3_A_Bacterial_Blight_Resistant_Dwarf_version_of_Basmati_Rice_Variety_Basmati_386
No AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis or seednet.gov.in record was returned in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, PAU seed sales or private dealers for Punjab Basmati 3 (PUNJAB BASMATI 3). Returned results were for other varieties or products: Pusa Basmati 1718, Pusa 1692, Pusa 1847 and Pusa Basmati 1121 packs, and Pakistani "Punjab Basmati" lines from Rice Research Institute, Kala Shah Kaku (a different product) -- https://www.flipkart.com/green-world-pusa-basmati-1718-variety-paddy-rice-3-kg-seeds-seed/p/itmfg2ajvwjmaxnp

RECOMMENDED STATES
Punjab (from the input record). The PB3 research pages describe trials across Punjab, but no notification or recommendation text was found -- https://www.academia.edu/30125861/Punjab_Basmati_3_A_Bacterial_Blight_Resistant_Dwarf_version_of_Basmati_Rice_Variety_Basmati_386
Notified basmati list: Punjab Basmati 3 appears among 45 basmati varieties notified under the Seeds Act, 1966 -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/45-notified-varieties-of-basmati-rice-in-india/
Official CSC/Seednet notification record and release year: No evidence found in these searches (input gives 2016-08-12).

seednet_fields.Parentage: Pusa Basmai 1/Nagina 22//Pusa Basmai 1*3 Pusa Basmati 1 is a first semi-dwarf, high yielding Basmati rice variety in the world with long slender grains developed at ICAR-IARI, New Delhi. Nagina 22 is an upland short duration drought tolerant aus rice possessing a QTL, qDTY1. 1 governing drought stress.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Basmati growing regions (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi western Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir) of India for which the recurrent parent Pusa Basmati 1 has been released.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Semi-dwarf stature and non-lodging habit, with long deflexed panicles which are completely exserted (100% exsertion), grains having awns with straw colored apiculi.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The drought NIL, Pusa 1882-12-111-20 (IET 28788) exhibits significant superiority of 101.5% with an average yield of 987.5 kg/ha over the recurrent parent (490 kg/ha) for reproductive stage drought stress under rainout shelter based on two years of testing while it also shows marginal superiority of 10.26% superior over the recurrent parent, Pusa Basmati 1 under normal irrigated condition.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: It exhibits similar reaction to major diseases and pests as compared to the recurrent parent, Pusa Basmati 1 in Basmati growing locations. The reaction of the NIL, Pusa 1882-12-111-20 (IET 28788) to the major diseases and peats was comparable to recurrent parent, Pusa Basmati 1. It showed comparatively lesser incidence of stem borer in Pantnagar, Kaul as compared to the recurrent parent during 2020.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight and blast resistance are reported. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bacterial blight and blast resistance are reported for Pusa Basmati 1885 (Seednet name PUSA BASMATI 1885), a line derived from PB 1121 that carries xa13 and Xa21 for blight and Pi54 and Pi2 for blast. Pusa Basmati 1885 is a dual disease resistant version of Pusa Basmati 1121 -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pusa_Basmati_1121 (secondary source)
- The APEDA notice describes the line as a MAS derived Near Isogenic Line of Pusa Basmati 1121 with inbuilt resistance to bacterial leaf blight and blast diseases -- https://apeda.gov.in/sites/default/files/product/NEWLY_RELEASED_BASMATI_VARIETIES.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no variety-specific abiotic stress data.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The IARI press release on three improved Basmati varieties says IARI added blight and blast resistance genes to Pusa Basmati 1121, Pusa Basmati 1509 and Pusa Basmati 6, producing lines including Pusa Basmati 1847, Pusa Basmati 1885 and a third line -- https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1863885&reg=48&lang=2 (the snippet does not give a 1885-specific susceptibility index, so none is attributed here)
- Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: the APEDA notice gives seed to seed maturity of 135-140 days similar to PB 1121 -- https://apeda.gov.in/sites/default/files/product/NEWLY_RELEASED_BASMATI_VARIETIES.pdf. A dealer page gives 145 days for this name (https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/pusa-basmati-paddy-seeds-1847-1885-1886-etc-27226558988.html), which conflicts and is treated as unreliable.
- Yield: Wikipedia reports 5.5% yield superiority over Pusa Basmati 1121 and an average yield of 4.68 t/ha -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pusa_Basmati_1121 (secondary; underlying trial source not identified)
- Multi-location trial data and grain-quality measurements for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Marker-assisted derivation: a MAS derived Near Isogenic Line of Pusa Basmati 1121 -- https://apeda.gov.in/sites/default/files/product/NEWLY_RELEASED_BASMATI_VARIETIES.pdf
- Gene combination: the Wikipedia entry lists xa13 and Xa21 for blight and Pi54 and Pi2 for blast -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pusa_Basmati_1121
- Conflict in parentage/method: the APEDA notice also says the line was developed through pedigree breeding method -- https://apeda.gov.in/sites/default/files/product/NEWLY_RELEASED_BASMATI_VARIETIES.pdf
- Parentage in the record is "Not specified". The closest supported parent is Pusa Basmati 1121, which is a donor-recurrent parent in the APEDA notice, not a verified pedigree.
- QTL or marker-validation studies specific to this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi -- https://apeda.gov.in/sites/default/files/product/NEWLY_RELEASED_BASMATI_VARIETIES.pdf ; https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1863885&reg=48&lang=2
- Lead breeder or scientist names for this variety: No evidence found. Names that surfaced (Vijaipal Singh, Ashok Kumar Singh and co-authors) are tied to Pusa Basmati 1121 and were excluded.
- Station: IARI campus at Pusa, New Delhi (the institute's name and campus are given in https://cropfarming.org/what-is-pusa-basmati-rice/ ; this

seednet_fields.Parentage: Pusa basmati 1509/Pusa 1601 1.	PB 1509 is a Basmati rice variety developed at ICAR-IARI, New Delhi and Pusa 1601 is an improved Basmati genotype developed from the cross, PRR78/Improved PB1. PRR78 is a Basmati rice restorer while Improved PB 1 is an improved Bacterial blight resistant Basmati rice variety.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Basmati GI areas of the states of Delhi, Haryana and Uttar Parades (Basmati GI area); Irrigated, Transplanted during Kharif season.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: 1.	Semi-dwarf, non-lodging. 2.	Early maturity. 3.	Non-shattering of grains at maturity. 4.	Responsive to 125 kg N. 5.	Most suitable for irrigated and late transplanting condition.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: 1.	Semi-dwarf, early maturity. 2.	Long panicles with Extra Long Slender grains. 3.	Non-shattering of grains at maturity.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Moderately resistant to blast, false smut and sheath blight diseases; moderately resistant to Brown Plant Hopper.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Pusa 1692-10-20-1-1-1 (IET 26995) exhibited moderately resistant reaction to blast disease with a mean SI of 5.0 as compared to highly susceptible reaction of Pusa Basmati 1121 (6.6) and Pusa Basmati 1 (6.4) in traditional Basmati growing location, Its reaction to other Major diseases and pests was comparable to PB 1121and PB 1 with lesser incidence of neck blast disease (SI-5.9) as against PB 1121 (SI-6.8), low incidence of false smut (SI-1.5) as compares to PB 1121 (SI-5.5) and PB 1 (S/-3.0), comparatively lesser sheath blight (SI-7.0) as compared to PB 1121 (SI-7.1) and PB 1 (SI-7.6).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Similar to other Basmati rice varieties but it can escape from Brown Plant Hopper incidence as it is early maturity.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Green manuring with daincha, which can be incorporated into soil at about 45 to 55 days after sowing and reduce the nitrogen dose by 20-25 kg/acre.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: The AHAS (Acetohydroxyacid Synthase) gene was introgressed into Pusa Basmati 1979, with SSR (Simple Sequence Repeat) markers used in the molecular breeding process.
genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: The AHAS QTL (Quantitative Trait Locus) was incorporated, conferring herbicide tolerance.
genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: Pusa Basmati 1979 is a non-genetically modified (non-GM) Basmati rice variety developed through genomic-assisted breeding and marker-assisted selection. It carries the AHAS gene, which provides complete resistance to Imazethapyr 10% SL herbicide. This variety is part of the RobiNOweed® brand, indicating its herbicide-tolerant characteristic.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for Pant Dhan 24 (IET 22096) and Pant Dhan-28 returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for either name. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for Pant Dhan 24 or Pant Dhan-28 resistance. The only pest study retrieved (brown planthopper life tables) used Pant Dhan-12, a different variety, so I have not attributed it here. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/337772606_Construction_of_stage_specific_life_table_of_rice_brown_plant_hopper_Nilaparvata_lugens_Stal_on_Pusa_Basamati-1_and_Pant_Dhan-12_under_natural_condition

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Pant Dhan 24 was among eight cultivars in a 2015–2016 establishment-method trial at Pantnagar, where it was compared with Pant Dhan 23, Pant Shankar Dhan 1 and 3, and others. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-6-2017/D.K.%20Singh,%20et%20al.pdf
Highest grain and straw yield was obtained with hybrid variety Pant Shankar Dhan 3 for both years except 2015 where Pant Dhan 24 recorded maximum straw yield. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-6-2017/D.K.%20Singh,%20et%20al.pdf
Pant Dhan 24 because it gave greater B: C. ratio. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-6-2017/D.K.%20Singh,%20et%20al.pdf
AICRP rice listing gives duration 130–135 days and yield 55–60 (units not stated in the table; likely q/ha). -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/2%20AICRP%20-RICE.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found (no parentage, marker, or QTL data; the source gives only the culture code UPR 3425-11-1-1 = IET 22096). -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, through the AICRIP rice centre. The AICRIP centre was set up in 1966 in the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Pantnagar. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf
Culture UPR 3425-11-1-1 (IET 22096) was named Pant Dhan 24 and found suitable for Bihar and Orissa. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf
No lead breeder name was found for Pant Dhan 24. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/2%20AICRP%20-RICE.pdf
Name discrepancy: the search turned up no source linking "Pant Dhan-28" (Seednet) to IET 22096. GBPUAT lists show Pant Dhan 28 as a separate released rice variety. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/21.02.2024_academia_industry_meet.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute contact (no breeder contact found): Dr. A.S. Jeena, Joint Director, Breeder Seed Production Centre, GBPUAT; PO Pantnagar, Distt. U.S. Nagar, Uttarakhand-263145; phone +91-7817005207. Email: not found. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/index.html?id=6

drought.details: Pant Dhan 28 is described as a short duration drought tolerant rice, suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. It exhibits tolerance to combined stress of drought and salinity, and other edaphic stresses.

heat.details: The variety is mentioned in contexts related to heat stress tolerance, including terminal heat tolerance, implying some level of resilience to high temperatures.

salinity.details: Pant Dhan 28 is described as tolerant to combined stress of drought and salinity. Its yield under salinity stress has been evaluated.

flood.details: The variety is listed as tolerant to water logging and is mentioned in the context of flood tolerant rice varieties.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Search limit reached: the tool stopped further searches after one batch of four. Topics 1 to 4 were covered only partly, so several headings below rest on thin or no evidence. Seednet was not reached, and the Parindra spelling was searched but returned nothing relevant.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The search returned no page giving drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Panindra.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No blast, BLB, sheath blight, BPH or other resistance data for Panindra was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A paper on Red Bao rice of Assam names Panindra among "water rice varieties" in a list, with no yield, maturity or trial data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/398435941_Red_Bao_Rice_of_Assam

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder name was found for Panindra. The only institutional link is the release record's Assam Agricultural University, Jorhat. A ResearchGate compilation, "Rice Varieties Developed by Assam Agricultural University", carries an AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute copyright line, but the excerpt I saw did not show Panindra, so I am not attributing it to this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found for Panindra-specific or institute contact details (no email, phone or postal address). The Red Bao page gives Sanjay Kumar Chetia, Director of Research (Agri.), AAU Jorhat, as an author affiliation. That is a role on a different paper, not a verified contact for this variety, and it needs checking against the current AAU website -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/398435941_Red_Bao_Rice_of_Assam

PUBLICATIONS -- Authors not fully visible (Year not visible). Red Bao Rice of Assam. ResearchGate (Panindra named only in a variety list) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/398435941_Red_Bao_Rice_of_Assam
No other paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI naming Panindra was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The "Parindra/Dhan" query returned only a Pune paddy-seed trader listing (https://www.indiamart.com/shreeraghavendra-agency/paddy-seed.html). It names generic "Dhan (Paddy)" seed and not this variety, so it is discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The "recommended_states_raw" field is "Not specified", and no notification or state recommendation was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Phule Raja (tomato) / Phule Radha (Seednet)

Name handling: "Phule Raja" (CSC name) and "Phule Radha" (Seednet name) are different records. The Seednet name points to a paddy variety, not a tomato variety. Searches ran as: (1) Phule Raja tomato variety; (2) Phule Raja breeder/institute; (3) Phule Raja research paper; (4) Phule Radha paddy Seednet and seed availability. The Phule Raja tomato evidence is thin, and I found nothing that confirms the release year, RTH-2 code, or parentage in the record.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for Phule Raja tomato. A Cameroon study on a "RAJA F1" hybrid is a different product and is not this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Different-production-parameters-of-the-RAJA-F1-hybrid-variety-in-the-dry-season_fig4_390407974
Seednet "Phule Radha" (paddy) stress data: No evidence found in the Seednet-linked results -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for Phule Raja. A listing of MPKV-released tomato varieties notes leaf curl and spotted wilt resistance for other MPKV lines (NTDR-1, Raiashree), but does not name Phule Raja -- https://agrigyan.in/tomato-variety-information-resistant-released-by/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A student-uploaded MPKV list names "Tomato- Phule Raja (Hybrid)" under the Tomato Improvement Project, with no data attached. This is a listing, not a trial report -- https://www.studocu.com/in/document/mahatma-phule-krishi-vidyapeeth/fundamentals-of-biochemistry/vegetable-variety-hhhfggg/72435476
No yield, maturity, or multi-location trial data found for Phule Raja -- (no URL)

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Parentage "T (N)-1 x Kolamba 540" was not verified in any source -- (no URL)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution is consistent with Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth (MPKV), Rahuri, Maharashtra -- https://studocu.com/in/document/mahatma-phule-krishi-vidyapeeth/fundamentals-of-biochemistry/vegetable-variety-hhhfggg/72435476
No breeder or lead scientist name found for Phule Raja -- (no URL)
Seednet "Phule Radha" is a paddy variety released in 2006 and notified in 2007 (S.O. 1178(E)), developed by MPKV per the same notification list; it is not the tomato variety -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder or division contact found. Institute website only: https://mpkv.ac.in (no email, phone, or postal address verified in the results) -- https://mpkv.ac.in/Uploads/Research/2024-English_20241017111319.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found for Phule Raja tomato. Results for "Phule Raja tomato research paper" were general tomato or unrelated cultivar studies (e.g., a heat-stress transcriptomics paper on other cultivars) and were excluded -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1278608/full

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for Phule Raja tomato from NSC, SAU, KVK, or dealers. The Seednet "Phule Radha" search returned only generic paddy dealers, not Phule Radha sellers -- https://seednet.gov.in/SeedGO/Index.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
Phule Raja: No evidence found. The 2014 release year and the Maharashtra recommendation in the input record are unverified by these searches.
Phule Radha (paddy): The Bihar notified-variety list confirms the entry and release year but does not give a recommended-state entry in the snippet reviewed -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

Open issues for follow-up: check the MPKV tomato release notification and the ICAR/CSC minutes directly for Phule Raja (RTH-2). Confirm whether the Seednet record should be linked to the paddy entry or removed.

agronomic_details.yield: Overall yield of 19.4 quintals per acre (48.58 q/ha), equivalent to the input record's 4858 kg/ha of paddy. Yield was 11.4% higher than Pusa Basmati 1121 and 6.1% higher than Pusa Basmati 1718.
agronomic_details.stability: Yielded consistently better than the check varieties in multi-locational trials. No further stability analysis across environments was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for commercial cultivation in the basmati growing regions of Punjab. Performs better when transplanted in the first fortnight of July. Also recommended for direct-seeded rice (DSR) based on trial results.

agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium plant height of 111 cm (farmingcosmos). Grain dimensions, milling quality and cooking quality are comparable to Pusa Basmati 1121. Possesses strong aroma like traditional basmati varieties. Input record morphological_characteristics is 'Not specified'.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-locational trials: yielded consistently better than check varieties. (2) Yield comparison: 11.4% more than Pusa Basmati 1121 and 6.1% more than Pusa Basmati 1718, with an overall yield of 19.4 quintals per acre (48.58 q/ha). (3) Direct-seeded (DSR) research trials: 17.7% higher yield than Pusa Basmati 1121, leading to a DSR recommendation. (4) Transplanting window: performs better when transplanted in the first fortnight of July. (5) PAU crop operations advice: complete transplanting of Punjab Basmati 7, Punjab Basmati 5, Pusa Basmati 1847, Pusa Basmati 1718 and Pusa Basmati 1121 in the first fortnight of July. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Punjab Basmati 7. The searches returned only a PAU rice-breeding profile that mentions drought and submergence as breeding targets for rice in general, not for this variety. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=449&intDepTitleID=21&intLinkID=9

DISEASE AND PEST
Bacterial blight: Dr RS Gill, a rice expert, said Punjab Basmati 7 is resistant to all 10 pathotypes of the bacterial blight pathogen prevalent in Punjab, while Pusa Basmati 1121 is susceptible to this disease. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5723
Bacterial blight (same statement, second source): Punjab Basmati 7 is resistant to all 10 pathotypes of bacterial blight pathogen prevalent in Punjab. -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/new-variety-punjab-basmati-7/
Insect and other pests: No evidence found for this variety. The only stem borer and planthopper resistance data found (Punjab Basmati, PK 8685-5-1-1-1-1) relate to a different Pakistani line of the same name. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377773191_EVOLUTION_OF_BREEDING_RESEARCH_IN_BASMATI_RICE_ORYZA_SATIVA_L_IN_PUNJAB_PAKISTAN (discarded from this heading as a different variety)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Multi-location yield: Punjab Basmati 7 yielded consistently better than the check varieties in the multi-locational trials. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5723
Yield advantage and average yield: the variety gave 11.4% more than Pusa Basmati 1121 and 6.1% more than Pusa Basmati 1718, with an overall yield of 19.4 quintals per acre (48.58 q/ha). -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5723 ; https://www.farmingcosmos.com/new-variety-punjab-basmati-7/
Direct-seeded (DSR) trials: In research trials under direct seeded conditions, Punjab Basmati 7 gave 17.7% higher yield than Pusa Basmati 1121, hence it has also been recommended for planting under DSR. -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/new-variety-punjab-basmati-7/
Duration and height: Punjab Basmati 7 matures in 101 days, about one week earlier than Pusa Basmati 1121 and Pusa Basmati 1718. It has a medium height of 111 cm. -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/new-variety-punjab-basmati-7/
Transplanting window: It performs better when transplanted in the first fortnight of July. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5723
Grain quality: Grain dimensions, milling quality and cooking quality are comparable to Pusa Basmati 1121. -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/new-variety-punjab-basmati-7/
Fragrance: Like traditional basmati varieties, it possesses strong aroma. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5723
PAU crop operations: Complete transplanting of Punjab Basmati 7, Punjab Basmati 5, Pusa Basmati 1847, Pusa Basmati 1718 and Pusa Basmati 1121 is recommended in the first fortnight of July. -- https://pau.edu/content/extserv/fo/7.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (PAU and press reports): The variant was created by crossing the standard basmati variety, Basmati 386, with Pusa Basmati 1121. -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/punjab-agricultural-university-launches-new-variety-of-basmati-rice/ ; The variety has been developed by involving the strongly scented traditional basmati variety 'Basmati 386' and the most popular basmati variety 'Pusa Basmati 1121'. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5723
Designation PAU 7555-1655-1-1-B and pedigree Bas 386/IET 1798//386*2///Pusa Bas: no evidence found in the searches (these come from the input record only).
QTL, marker and genomic studies: No evidence found for this variety. -- (searched; no relevant page returned)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5723
Lead scientist named as involved in the release: Dr Navjot Sidhu, Rice Breeder, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, College of Agriculture, PAU; her profile lists Punjab Basmati 7 among the varieties she helped develop and release. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=449&intDepTitleID=21&intLinkID=9
Department head quoted on the release: Dr GS Mangat, Head, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, PAU. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5723
Other scientists quoted on the variety (roles only): Dr RS Gill (rice expert) and Dr Buta Singh Dhillon (rice expert). -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5723
Release-year discrepancy: the input record says 2022-06-17, while PAU publicised the recommendation on 14-04-2021, and a notification list gives the gazette reference 4065(E) dated 31.08.2022. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5723 ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/45-notified-varieties-of-basmati-rice-in-india/

CONTACT DETAILS
Dr Navjot Sidhu, Rice Breeder, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, College of Agriculture, PAU Ludhiana. Office phone: 91-0161-2401960 Ext. 423. Email: not found. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=449&intDepTitleID=21&intLinkID=9
Institute portal: https://www.pau-seed.in/ (linked from a farming blog; not checked directly). -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/new-variety-punjab-basmati-7/
Postal address of PAU Ludhiana or the division: not found in the searches.
Note: the Lahore seller number (03004017349) and the KVK Shamsher Nagar comment appear in blog comments and are unverified; they are excluded.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Searches returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record for Punjab Basmati 7. The results that matched "Punjab Basmati" were a Pakistani line, an economics paper that mentions only Pusa 1509 and Pusa 1121, and a Food Chemistry paper on Pakistani rice. These are excluded as different varieties. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389599197_Economics_of_Basmati_Rice_Cultivation_in_Punjab

SEED AVAILABILITY
PAU seed production: PAU has produced sufficient seed of basmati varieties including Punjab Basmati 7 for the Kharif season. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&dataE=datae&intID=8944 (PAU press release, 04-04-2024)
Distribution points: Seed is available at Krishi Vigyan Kendras, Farm Advisory Service Centres, Regional Research Stations and University Seed Farms across the state. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&dataE=datae&intID=8944
Price notice (2023): Punjab Basmati 7 and Pusa Basmati 1121 (8 and 24 kg) are priced at Rs.600 and Rs.1800. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/updates-detaills/seeds-of-various-varieties-of-paddy-are-available-at-pau/1215
Retail listing: an Amazon listing for the seed (BASMATI PUNJAB-7, 8 kg) was marked currently unavailable. -- https://www.amazon.in/produced-Agricultural-University-Ludhiana-farmers/dp/B0F7GSPTDT
Seednet portal (DAC&FW): not checked; no evidence from seednet.gov.in was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Punjab only: Punjab Basmati 7 has been recommended for commercial cultivation in the basmati growing regions of the Punjab state. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=5723
Notification: listed as 45 Notified Varieties of basmati, gazette 4065(E) dated 31.08.2022. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/45-notified-varieties-of-basmati-rice-in-india/

NAME CHECK
The variety_name and seednet_variety_name in the record are both "Punjab Basmati 7", so the evidence above applies to both. The Amazon listing uses "BASMATI PUNJAB-7". No CSC minutes were retrieved to confirm the name there.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Bacterial blight: Punjab Basmati 7 is reported as resistant to all 10 pathotypes of the bacterial blight pathogen prevalent in Punjab. Dr RS Gill, a rice expert, made this statement, and the source also says Pusa Basmati 1121 is susceptible to this disease (comparator only). The same resistance statement appears in a second source (farmingcosmos). No other diseases were reported for this variety; input record disease_reaction is 'Not Specified'.

drought.details: While mentioned in lists concerning climate-resilient varieties, Pusa Basmati 1985 is not explicitly characterized as drought tolerant; its primary documented stress tolerance relates to herbicides. Other varieties are specifically identified for drought tolerance.

heat.details: It is mentioned alongside heat-tolerant varieties in general discussions of climate resilience but is not directly attributed with heat tolerance. Its primary documented trait is herbicide tolerance, distinct from heat tolerance found in other varieties like DRR Dhan 52.

salinity.details: No specific information indicates Pusa Basmati 1985 possesses salinity tolerance. Other varieties are identified for this trait.

flood.details: No specific information indicates Pusa Basmati 1985 possesses flood tolerance. It is noted for submergence tolerance in some broad lists but not explicitly characterized.

pest_resistance.summary: Pusa Basmati 1985 is listed with 'Pest' tolerance, though no specific pests or levels of resistance are detailed.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Delhi, Punjab, and Western Uttar Pradesh. Its herbicide tolerance and suitability for Direct Seeded Rice (DSR) address challenges like depleting water resources in north-western India by facilitating effective weed control in DSR systems.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: The AHAS (Acetolactate Synthase) gene, responsible for herbicide tolerance, was introgressed into Pusa Basmati 1985. SSR (Simple Sequence Repeats) molecular markers were used in its development.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: The Herbicide-tolerant QTL (AHAS) was incorporated.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Developed as a non-genetically modified (non-GM) variety through marker-assisted selection/backcross breeding, specifically for tolerance to the herbicide Imazethapyr. The herbicide tolerance is based on the AHAS gene.

drought.details: Pusa Basmati 1509 is identified as a drought-tolerant variety. IARI's Annual Report 2022 indicates it is highly tolerant to drought stress. It is considered suitable for drought-prone areas, with leaf rolling and senescence scores used as selection criteria.

heat.details: Pusa Basmati 1509 has shown improved tolerance to heat stress. It is included in screenings for heat stress tolerance and is mentioned in the context of breeding for combined heat and drought stress tolerance.

salinity.details: Pusa Basmati 1509 is an elite Basmati rice variety into which seedling stage salinity tolerance has been introgressed, specifically involving the 'Saltol' major QTL. This makes it a stress-tolerant variety for salinity.

flood.details: Pusa Basmati 1509 is mentioned among stress-tolerant varieties for flood-prone areas.

disease_resistance.summary: Pusa Basmati 1509 has resistance to Bacterial Blight and Blast. It is also mentioned as having Bakanae resistance (qBK1.1) through derived NILs.

pest_resistance.summary: Not Specified

agronomic_details.yield: Described as a high-yielding variety within the Basmati segment. Specific quantitative yield data is not provided in the search results.
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to irrigated transplanted conditions and suitable for general Basmati growing areas.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf (95-100 cm), reduced height, non-lodging.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Research and development efforts, including molecular breeding and introgression of various stress tolerance traits, imply extensive field trials. However, specific trial summaries are not detailed in the provided results.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: The 'Saltol' major QTL is introgressed for seedling stage salinity tolerance. The 'qSub1' (or Sub1) QTL is introgressed for submergence tolerance. The 'qBK1.1' QTL is associated with Bakanae resistance in derived NILs.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Saltol enhances seedling stage salt tolerance. qSub1 confers submergence tolerance. qBK1.1 contributes to Bakanae resistance.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Molecular breeding and Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS) have been extensively used to incorporate stress tolerance traits into Pusa Basmati 1509. The donor parent for specific traits is Pusa 1790.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa CRD KN2 (Pusa1638-07-171-1-81-1-2) (IET26213), rice

Name check: The CSC release minutes name and the Seednet name (with code IET26213) both appear in the search results only as the same listing. I found no Seednet portal page itself, so all evidence below refers to the release-list name "Pusa CRD KN2 (Pusa1638-07-171-1-81-1-2) (IET26213)."

Data conflicts to resolve:
- Release date: the record says 2023-05-02, but the notification reports date the release to 25 September 2023 (reported 3 October 2023).
- Parentage: the record says the BM68 mutant. One search result says the aromatic semi-dwarf Pusa 1176 was derived from BM34, and a different source describes BM68 with Pusa Basmati 1176 as parents of Kalanamak crosses. Confirm the mutant line before relying on this.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released as a high-yielding, semi-dwarf, non-lodging Kalanamak variety; lodging resistance is the only stress trait explicitly named -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety were found. Searched: yes. -- No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- A general (non-specific) statement says the Pusa Narendra KN1 and CRD KN2 pair has better pest and disease resistance than traditional Kalanamak, with no named pathogens or pests -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/paddy-farming-10-climate-smart-rice-varieties-for-high-and-profitable-yields/
- No race-specific or field-scored resistance data for CRD KN2 were found. Searched: yes. -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Three years of testing in the GI area of Uttar Pradesh gave an average yield of 31.6 q/ha for CRD KN2 -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- A separate note gives an average of around 4.5 t/ha for the newer dwarf varieties (KN1 and CRD Kalanamak 2) versus about 2.5 t/ha for traditional types; this figure is not split by variety -- https://hospitality lexis (URL below)
  Source: https://hospitalitylexis.com/kalanamak-rice-emerges-as-high-value-specialty-crop-as-cultivation-and-farmer-incomes-rise/
- Trial design, maturity days, plant height and seed-to-seed duration for CRD KN2 were not found. Searched: yes. -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- A recessive semi-dwarf allele, sd1-bm, comes from Bindli Mutant 34 and is present in the Pusa 1176 lineage -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395371592_Reviving_Kalanamak_Rice_A_Sustainable_Model_for_Enhancing_Farmers'_Income_in_Eastern_Uttar_Pradesh
- No marker, QTL or pedigree-confirmation study for CRD KN2 itself was found. Searched: yes. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi, per the release record and the IARI annual report -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- Lead breeder name(s) and station: not found in any source. The breeder names that appeared (Vijaipal Singh, Ashok Kumar Singh) are associated with Pusa Basmati 1121 and are not attributed to this variety. Searched: yes. -- No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder email, phone and postal address: not found. Institute-level contact page for IARI: not found in the search results. Searched: yes. -- No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Chaudhary R.K., Kumar R., Mishra S.B., Sahani A. (2022). Improvement of Local Speciality Rices as a Boon to Health, Wealth and Export Diversity: Case of Kalanamak Rice. Journal of Rice Research, Special Issue (Lead Lecture). -- https://doi.org/10.58297/IEYO2582 (covers the Kalanamak improvement programme generally; CRD KN2 is not confirmed as a subject)
- Singh D.P. et al. (2021). Evaluation of different Kalanamak rice genotypes for yield and yield related traits of eastern Uttar Pradesh. International Journal of Chemical Studies (author list truncated to "DP Singh and others" in the source; no DOI found). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349866561_Evaluation_of_different_Kalanamak_rice_genotypes_for_yield_and_yield_related_traits_of_eastern_Uttar_Pradesh
- IARI (2023). Annual Report 2023, ICAR-IARI, New Delhi (contains the CRD KN2 release description and yield figure; no individual authors). -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses and AICRP/ICAR rice trial reports specific to CRD KN2: none found. -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet listing for IET26213: not retrieved. -- No evidence found
- State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer stock of CRD KN2: not found. -- No evidence found
- Kalanamak-group seed: about 389.6 quintals of quality Kalanamak seed were produced and distributed during 2021-22 to 2025-26, and breeder seed is maintained at about 15-20 quintals a year. This is not specific to CRD KN2 -- https://hospitalitylexis.com/kalanamak-rice-emerges-as-high-value-specialty-crop-as-cultivation-and-farmer-incomes-rise/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttar Pradesh only, released for the eastern Uttar Pradesh Kalanamak Geographical Indication area -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- Listed as an Open Pollinated Variety for Uttar Pradesh in the 2023 central notification -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-31-new-varieties-of-14-crops-for-uttar-pradesh-farmers/
