search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: SAVA 127 (Rice)

Name note: The CSC minutes name ("SAVA 127") and the Seednet name ("SAVA 127") could not be checked. Seednet and CSC release-minute pages did not appear in any search, so every finding below refers to the trade name "Sava 127" / "Sava smart rice 127" from Savannah Seeds. Variety code SVH 005 appeared in no result.

Scope note: Savannah's own materials describe Sava 127 as a hybrid. It is not a publicly bred, notified variety, and I found no official ICAR or SAU record for it.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Strong lodging resistance, and a semi-dwarf stature of about 95-105 cm, per Savannah's product pages -- https://www.savannahseeds.com/product/smart-rice-portfolio/ ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sava-smart-rice-127-16879593433.html
- Lodging tolerance and higher nitrogen and water intake efficiency are claimed in the RiceTec seed product page -- https://ricetec-in.com/seed-products-india/
- Water savings of up to 40% were reported by farmers and in Savannah's trials, but this figure applies to the FullPage direct-seeded system generally, not to Sava 127 alone -- https://icrier.org/pdf/FDI-Innovations-and-Technology-in-Rice-Cultivation.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence test data for Sava 127 was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Claimed high tolerance to bacterial leaf blight (BLB) and blast resistance, described as a "superior disease package" -- https://www.savannahseeds.com/product/smart-rice-portfolio/ ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/savannahs-paddy-variety-sava-smart-rice-127/
- Same BLB and blast claims on the RiceTec seed page -- https://ricetec-in.com/seed-products-india/
- No independent screening or pest data (stem borer, BPH, etc.) was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is stated inconsistently across sources: "early medium" (Savannah portfolio, https://www.savannahseeds.com/product/smart-rice-portfolio/); 115-120 days (RiceTec, https://ricetec-in.com/seed-products-india/); 110-115 days (IndiaMART, https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sava-smart-rice-127-16879593433.html); 125-130 days (Hindi source, https://khetijankari.com/sawa-7301-paddy-seed/).
- Claimed field readiness for the next crop (potato, peas, wheat) and savings of 2-3 irrigations, chemical and fertilizer inputs -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/savannahs-paddy-variety-sava-smart-rice-127/
- Sava 127 was grown in an irrigated transplanted trial in Lumbini Province, Nepal (2022-2023, 25 hybrids, Arize 6444 as check). It was among the earliest to mature, and the table data are garbled, so no reliable yield figure is taken from it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387415927_Evaluation_of_hybrid_rice_varieties_for_growth_and_yield_traits_under_irrigated_transplanted_conditions_in_Lumbini_Province_Nepal
- Sava 127FP is offered for direct-seeded rice (no nursery, seed-drill sowing, weed control), with Vezir herbicide -- https://ricetec-in.com/seed-products-india/ ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/savannah-seeds-and-adama-india-launches-fullpage-rice-cropping-solution-for-paddy-farmers/
- Savannah reports nearly 500 demonstrations reaching over 17,000 farmers for the FullPage system (company figure) -- https://agriculturepost.com/farm-inputs/seeds/savannah-seeds-introduces-fullpage-technology-for-enhancing-rice-yield-and-saving-labour-costs/
- No AICRP or SAU multi-location trial results were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: No evidence found. Sava 127 is described as a hybrid, but no parent lines are named.
- Breeding-line code (SVH 005) and breeding method: No evidence found.
- Genome resources, markers and QTL: No evidence found.
- Trait mentions only: the FullPage variant carries an imidazolinone (IMI) herbicide-tolerance trait, and the products are described as "SmartRice genetics" -- https://ricetec-in.com/seed-products-india/ ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/savannah-seeds-and-adama-india-launches-fullpage-rice-cropping-solution-for-paddy-farmers/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder or lead scientist names: No evidence found.
- Developing institution: Savannah Seeds Private Limited, a subsidiary of RiceTec, which entered Indian rice seed business in 2010 -- https://ricetec-in.com/latest-news/ ; https://krishijagran.com/industry-news/savannah-seeds-acquires-rice-seed-assets-of-ganga-kaveri-spriha-seeds/
- Named CEO and Managing Director at the 2019 acquisition announcement: Ajai Rana (company statement, not a breeder) -- https://krishijagran.com/industry-news/savannah-seeds-acquires-rice-seed-assets-of-ganga-kaveri-spriha-seeds/
- Breeding station or research location: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Company: Savannah Seeds Private Limited, Gurugram/Gurgaon, Haryana (registered location as stated by the company); a listing also shows a Raipur, Chhattisgarh office -- https://www.indiamart.com/savannah-seeds/products.html ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sava-smart-rice-127-2851302590733.html
- Company website: https://www.savannahseeds.com/ (product portfolio page cited above)
- Official email, phone and full postal address: No evidence found. IndiaMART listings say contact details are shown only on request, and none appeared in the results.
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, KrishiKosh record, or ICAR/AICRP report naming Sava 127 was found.
- Nearest item: the Nepal hybrid-rice trial above (authors not captured in the search result; year 2024-2025 per the page's age metadata) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387415927_Evaluation_of_hybrid_rice_varieties_for_growth_and_yield_traits_under_irrigated_transplanted_conditions_in_Lumbini_Province_Nepal

SEED AVAILABILITY

SJR-5 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "SJR-5", so every search used the same name. Evidence below refers to SJR-5 (IET-19972) unless stated otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Four searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for SJR-5.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page describing blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight, BPH, stem borer or other resistance for SJR-5 was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No page gave maturity, plant height, yield, or multi-location trial data for SJR-5.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No page gave parentage (the input record also says "Not specified") or any marker or QTL study for SJR-5.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No page named a breeder, developing institute or station for SJR-5. A search for "SJR-5 rice breeder developed by institute" returned general IRRI, IR8 and ICAR-IIRR pages that do not mention SJR-5, so none were attributed to it.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute or station contact for SJR-5 was returned. The only ICAR-IIRR address seen (Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad 500030) appears as the affiliation of an author on an unrelated paper, so it is not attributed to SJR-5.

PUBLICATIONS:
Prasad, G. S. V. et al. (2022). Impact of breeder seed multiplication and certified quality seed distribution on rice production in India. Journal not visible in search snippet; SJR 5 appears only as one name in a cultivar table in the article -- https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/full/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2 (DOI 10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2). Note: the snippet shows only the first author's name, so the full author list and journal are unverified. The article does not describe SJR-5 itself.
No other publication, thesis, AICRP/ICAR report or KrishiKosh record for SJR-5 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for SJR-5 was returned. Results for other paddy varieties (Pusa Basmati, PB, IFFDC, OSSC lists) were discarded as not relevant.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Partial evidence only. A Bihar list of notified varieties gives "SJR-5(IET-19972) · 2011 · 10/10/2011 · S.O. 2326(E)" as a notification entry -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Drought: an ICAR-RCER Patna news report says farmers were advised to adopt short-duration, drought-tolerant varieties including Swarna Purvi Dhan-3 (name matches the release-minutes name; the Seednet name was not separately searched) -- https://patnapress.com/collective-rice-transplanting-icar-rcer-patna/
Submergence, flood, heat, salinity: No evidence found. The searches returned only Swarna Sukha, Swarna Shakti, Swarna Samriddhi and other varieties, which were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
Bacterial leaf blight: an IIRR Annual Report 2022 variety table row for Swarna Purvi Dhan 3 gives a "MR-BLB" entry, which appears to indicate moderate resistance to bacterial leaf blight; the column header was not fully legible in the extract, so treat this as unconfirmed -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
Other diseases and insects: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Duration and yield: the same IIRR 2022 table row lists a duration value of 87 (days, column unlabelled in extract) and a value of 5.53 (presumably t/ha, unlabelled) -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
Grain type: the same row codes the grain as LS (likely long slender), unlabelled -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
Suitability for direct-seeded or drought-prone systems: the ICAR-RCER news item above associates the variety with drought-tolerant short-duration cultivation -- https://patnapress.com/collective-rice-transplanting-icar-rcer-patna/
Multi-location trial results or yield data from peer-reviewed sources: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage/pedigree: the IIRR 2022 table row gives the pedigree as RCPR 60-IR 97073-26-1-1-3 and the cross as IR10L146/IR10L137. This conflicts with the input field "Not specified" and is taken from a table row whose columns were only partly readable -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
QTL or marker studies specific to this variety: No evidence found. Swarna-background marker work returned by the search (for example IIRR and NRRI Swarna-trait lines, and Swarna-Sub1) concerns other lines and was discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region (ICAR-RCER), Patna, Bihar. Support: the IRRI-NARES variety list shows ICAR-RCER Patna against a row whose name is truncated to "Swarna Purvi Dhan-" and whose number is not legible, so it was not attributed to this variety -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/eeb4bc62-10b4-4743-8ebf-f2e268afbdc2/content
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. A Lagatar report names Dr Santosh Kumar as developer of Swarna Purvi Dhan-1 and -2 only, so it was not attributed to Dhan-3 -- https://lagatar24.com/ranchi-bau-scientists-develop-four-different-varieties-of-high-yielding-crops/
Institute director (not a breeder): Dr Anup Das, Director, ICAR-RCER, as quoted in the news report -- https://patnapress.com/collective-rice-transplanting-icar-rcer-patna/

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute: ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region, Patna (institute contact page URL) -- https://icarrcer.icar.gov.in/variety-released-2/
Institute director: Dr Anup Das, Director, ICAR-RCER Patna (name only; no email, phone or address found) -- https://patnapress.com/collective-rice-transplanting-icar-rcer-patna/
Breeder email, phone, postal address: No evidence found.
Seednet portal helpdesk (portal-level, not variety-specific): support-seednet@gov.in -- https://seednet.gov.in/GraphReport/SeedGraph.aspx

PUBLICATIONS
ICAR-IIRR (2022). IIRR Annual Report 2022. Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad (Published by Dr R M Sundaram, Director) -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf
No peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh), conference papers or AICRP reports specific to Swarna Purvi Dhan 3 were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Seednet producer/marketer listing: No evidence found for this variety under either name. The search returned Swarna Seeds (UACI, Burdwan) pages, which are a company and product name resemblance and were discarded -- https://seednet.gov.in/material/Seed_Producers_Marketers.htm
NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed sale listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Haryana, Rajasthan, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra (abbreviated HR, RJ, BI, UP, CH, MH in the IIRR 2022 table row, matching the input) -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2022.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 (rice)

Scope note: Four searches were run (variety/release, breeder/institution, research, seed availability). Almost none of the results refer to Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 itself. Most hits concern other Swarna-derived lines (Swarna-Sub1, Swarna Sukha Dhan, Swarna Purvi Dhan 4/5), so they are not evidence for this variety. The Seednet name "SWARN PURBI DHAN" and the variety code "RCPR 19-IR 84899-B-179-13-1-1-1 / IET 24660" were not searched separately, because the four-search limit was reached. Results containing "Purvi"/"Purbi" or the code were checked, and the only matches are listed below. Where the evidence refers to a different name or line, that is stated.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
No evidence found for Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 specifically. Results on drought, flood and submergence tolerance concern Swarna-Sub1 or other varieties, not this one. -- https://ricetoday.irri.org/swarna-sub1-odishas-food-for-a-goddess/ (Swarna-Sub1 only, excluded)

DISEASE AND PEST:
Rice Package of Practices for Eastern India lists Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 under false smut (Ustilaginoidea virens) management as one of the "tolerant varieties" to select; the listing is a recommendation, not a tested resistance rating. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India
Matching name on Seednet ("SWARN PURBI DHAN"): not searched; no evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
No evidence found for maturity, yield or multi-location trial results for Swarna Purvi Dhan 1. The Package of Practices lists it among varieties for eastern India, but no duration or yield is given for it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India

GENETICS AND QTL:
No evidence found. Parentage is "Not specified" in the record, and no source gives a pedigree. -- (no URL with evidence)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
No evidence found that names a lead breeder or scientist for Swarna Purvi Dhan 1 or confirms its developing institution (ICAR-RCER, per the record). The ICAR-NRRI and IRRI pages found concern other varieties and are not evidence for this one. -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/RB-34.pdf (other varieties, excluded)

CONTACT DETAILS:
No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, address or ICAR-RCER contact page was returned by any search.

PUBLICATIONS:
No evidence found for peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, theses or KrishiKosh entries on Swarna Purvi Dhan 1. The Package of Practices (Kumar et al. listed as an author in the search snippet, year not confirmed) mentions the variety but is a general extension guide, not a variety study. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India

SEED AVAILABILITY:
No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU sources for Swarna Purvi Dhan 1. The IRRI news page lists Swarna Purvi Dhan-5 (not this variety) as available for direct-seeded rice. -- https://www.irri.org/news-and-events/news/31-high-impact-irri-nares-developed-rice-varieties-now-available-across-india (Purvi Dhan-5, excluded)

RECOMMENDED STATES:
The only state on record is Jharkhand, taken from the release record (recommended_states_raw). No external source confirms it. -- (release record, no URL)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Swarna Purvi Dhan 2 specifically. The ICAR-RCER release notice names it only among three climate-resilient releases, with no trait data (https://icarrcer.icar.gov.in/variety-released-2/). A tolerance-trait listing for eastern India does not include Purvi Dhan 2 (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India). The IIRR 2023 annual report has an AICRP table row for "Swarna Purvi Dhan-2" (RCPR 46-IR93827-29-1-1-2, IET 26767), with trait codes that are garbled in the extracted text. The row includes "MR-BLB" next to the codes, but I could not decode the columns reliably (https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf).

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for Swarna Purvi Dhan 2 specifically. The IIRR 2023 table row above is the only trait-coded reference, and it is not decoded. Disease-tolerant variety lists in the eastern India package of practices do not name Purvi Dhan 2 (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Listed as a short-duration (about 115-125 days) irrigated-ecology variety in the eastern India package of practices (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India). A Ranchi news report gives a 110-120 day maturity for Swarna Purvi Dhan-2 together with Swarna Sukha Dhan and Swarna Purvi Dhan-1, attributed to Dr Santosh Kumar of ICAR-RCER (https://lagatar24.com/ranchi-bau-scientists-develop-four-different-varieties-of-high-yielding-crops/). The IIRR 2023 report describes the AICRP testing system and lists the variety's row in a trial table, but yield data for Purvi Dhan 2 was not extracted (https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf). No evidence found for a yield value specific to this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for Swarna Purvi Dhan 2. The marker-assisted work on Swarna (Sub1, xa5/Xa21, OsSPL14, SCM2) concerns the parent cultivar Swarna, not this variety (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8353458/). Parentage is not specified in the input and no source gave it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developed at ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region (ICAR-RCER), Patna. Lead breeder named as Dr Santosh Kumar, Senior Scientist, ICAR-RCER Patna (https://lagatar24.com/ranchi-bau-scientists-develop-four-different-varieties-of-high-yielding-crops/). The institute's variety-release page lists the Purvi Dhan series among ICAR-RCER releases (https://icarrcer.icar.gov.in/variety-released-2/). Co-authors on related RCER work are Rakesh Kumar and Sanjeev Kumar, though they are not confirmed as Purvi Dhan 2 breeders (https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/143280/53178/391485).

CONTACT DETAILS -- Dr Santosh Kumar, Senior Scientist, ICAR-RCER, Patna. No email or phone found. Institute address as printed in a related RCER paper: ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region, Patna, Bihar 800 014 (https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/143280/53178/391485). Institute web page: https://icarrcer.icar.gov.in/variety-released-2/ (an alternative domain, https://icarrcer.org.in, also appears). No official email or phone number was found in the results.

PUBLICATIONS --
Kumar, S. et al. (2025). Rice: Package of Practices for Eastern India. In: Crop Production in Changing Climate: Package of Practices for Eastern India, pp. 07-20. ICAR-RCER, Patna -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India (author list from the ResearchGate record; publisher is the Director, ICAR-RCER)
Indian Hub for Rice Research (ICAR-IIRR) (2023). Annual Report 2023 (AICRP on Rice variety table row for Swarna Purvi Dhan-2). ICAR-IIRR, Hyderabad -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf (author list not extracted)
No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI specific to Swarna Purvi Dhan 2 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for Swarna Purvi Dhan 2 seed from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales, or dealers. Results for "Swarna" seed were for other varieties (Swarna MTU 7029, Swarna Dhan IET-5656) and were not used. The Seednet name "SWARN PURBI DHAN" was not searched separately because the search budget was used; no evidence was gathered under that name.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The input lists Jharkhand. No source found in the searches confirmed this for Swarna Purvi Dhan 2. The package of practices lists the variety under irrigated ecology without a state (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India). The input release date of 2022-10-26 was also not confirmed by any source; the ICAR-RCER release page gives no date (https://icarrcer.icar.gov.in/variety-released-2/).

drought.details: Sahyadri Megha is a drought-tolerant rice variety, described as short-duration and suitable for direct-sown rainfed conditions. It is also referred to as moderately drought tolerant. A novel abiotic stress-responsive gene, LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from a drought-tolerant rice cultivar, Sahyadri Megha, indicating its genetic basis for this trait. Molecular breeding efforts aim for inbuilt drought resistance/tolerance.

heat.details: The variety exhibits heat stress tolerance and has been included in screenings for high temperature tolerance in rice genotypes.

salinity.details: Sahyadri Megha is tolerant to salinity, and its yield and salinity tolerance in rice have been subjects of study.

flood.details: Information specifically on flood tolerance (beyond submergence) is not provided.

disease_resistance.summary: Sahyadri Megha is resistant to blast disease (a fungal disease) and highly tolerant to blast. It is also resistant to Helminthosporium spot and gall midge. Molecular breeding aims for inbuilt blast resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety is resistant to gall midge.

agronomic_details.stability: Suitable for both irrigated and direct-sown rainfed conditions. Recommended for the Kharif season.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Primarily adapted for cultivation in Karnataka.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Sahyadri Megha is a non-Basmati, new red variety of paddy. It is noted for being protein-rich and high in nutrients.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has undergone and been reported in various trials, including those for drought stress tolerance, heat stress tolerance, salinity tolerance, and submergence tolerance as part of the All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (AICRIP) and IIRR annual reports. Performance scores are reported in these proceedings, indicating its participation in multi-location evaluations.

drought.details: Sava 200 is identified as a short duration drought tolerant rice hybrid suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. Molecular breeding efforts have aimed to develop varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar, and Sava 200 is listed in this context.

heat.details: The variety is tolerant to temperature stress, and high temperature tolerance has been a focus in developing abiotic tolerant rice varieties.

salinity.details: While salinity and osmotic stress tolerance trials are conducted within the research context, specific tolerance levels for Sava 200 are not provided in the search results.

flood.details: Sava 200 is suitable for semi-deep water conditions and exhibits tolerance to one week of submergence.

disease_resistance.summary: Sava 200 is highly resistant to Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB/LB) and neck infection. It is also tolerant/resistant to blast, rice bunt, Rice Tungro Disease (RTD), and Sheath Blight (ShBl).

pest_resistance.summary: Sava 200 is moderately resistant/tolerant to Stem Borer (SB). It also shows tolerance to gall midge, Brown Planthopper (BPH), and Green Leafhopper (GLH).

agronomic_details.yield: Sava 200 is described as a high yielding hybrid with reported yields of 65 q/ha and 76.5 q/ha in different contexts.
agronomic_details.stability: Based on two years of evaluation, Sava 200 was found suitable for cultivation in Zone-II. It has been included in All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (AICRIP) trials and multi-location testing.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Sava 200 is a Non-Basmati hybrid suitable for both rainfed and irrigated ecology, including early rainfed and irrigated conditions. It is also suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and semi-deep water environments. It has been identified as suitable for cultivation in Zone-II.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Sava 200 is a semi-dwarf variety (82 cm) with long slender (LS) grains. It is also noted to be lodging tolerant.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Sava 200 has been an entry in All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (AICRIP) trials, including Soil stress tolerant trials and AVT 1-E TP Zone -2 & 3 Kharif 2016. It was evaluated for two years for its suitability in Zone-II and included in multi-location testing for grain yield performance.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar, and Sava 200 is associated with this research context for drought tolerance.

drought.details: Sava 300 is a drought tolerant rice hybrid suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and irrigated early stress conditions. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Sava 300, indicating its genetic basis for drought tolerance. Molecular breeding efforts have also focused on developing rice varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance.

heat.details: It is suitable for irrigated early stress conditions, which can include temperature stress. Research on high temperature tolerance has contributed to the development of abiotic tolerant rice varieties, within which Sava 300 is categorized.

Molecular breeding for blast resistance has been conducted.

pest_resistance.summary: Sava 300 shows tolerance to major insect pests. It is tolerant to Green Leaf Hopper (T-GLH), Brown Plant Hopper (BPH), leaf folder, gundhi bug, stem-borer, and gall midge.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Sava 300 exhibits enhanced disease tolerance and resistance. It is highly resistant to Leaf Blight (LB), neck infection, and Sheath-rot. It shows moderate resistance (MR-BL) to Blast (including leaf blast and bacterial leaf blast), and resistance to brown spot and false smut. Molecular breeding for blast resistance has been conducted.

pest_resistance.research_summary: Sava 300 shows tolerance to major insect pests. It is tolerant to Green Leaf Hopper (T-GLH), Brown Plant Hopper (BPH), leaf folder, gundhi bug, stem-borer, and gall midge.

heat.details: Described as a cold-tolerant, early-maturing indica (SDIOPR paper). A farmer reported good crop health through a heatwave and flood-like conditions; this is anecdotal and not trial data, so no heat tolerance level is assigned.

flood.details: A farmer reported crop health under flood-like conditions and good performance across weather conditions at high altitude. This is anecdotal, not trial data, so no level is assigned.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: moderate resistance reported in the SDIOPR paper. A 2025 news report describes it as resistant to blast (named 'Shalimar-4', alongside Shalimar-5); this conflicts with the 'moderate' rating. A KVK Kupwara paper describes SR-4 as high-yielding and disease-resistant without naming the disease. No other diseases found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found in searched sources for insect pest resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: Budgam FLD mean seed yield 85 q/ha (about 8.5 t/ha) over four years versus 50.5 q/ha for local check China-1039. Yield potential 7.5-8.0 t/ha (SDIOPR paper). Kupwara FLD mean 83.33 q/ha versus 51.66 q/ha farmer practice. The developer claims about 10 t/ha (interview, not trial data). A 2025 report gives about 17 q/ha, which conflicts with the 7.5-8.0 t/ha figure.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Consistent FLD advantage is reported across Budgam and Kupwara, but no stability analysis across environments was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Valley plains (SDIOPR paper); high-altitude performance reported anecdotally by a farmer. Sown second fortnight of April and transplanted second fortnight of May (SDIOPR paper). Budgam FLD table gives sowing from 1st week April to 1st fortnight May.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 135-140 days (SDIOPR paper). CSC record states 'Not specified'.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Early-maturing indica; cold-tolerant (SDIOPR paper). Spacing 20 x 20 cm. Seed rate 50-60 kg/ha (SDIOPR paper) conflicts with 60-80 kg/ha in the Budgam FLD table. No further morphological data found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Budgam FLD (2018-2021): mean seed yield 85 q/ha versus 50.5 q/ha for local check China-1039 over four years; BCR 2.22 versus 1.38; seed rate 60-80 kg/ha and sowing 1st week April to 1st fortnight May. (2) Kupwara FLD (2021-22 to 2023-24, 180 demonstrations): mean 83.33 q/ha versus 51.66 q/ha farmer practice. (3) Irrigation and nitrogen schedule study on SKUA-408 measuring PAR interception: a study exists, but its results are not given in the digest. (4) Developer's claim of about 10 t/ha and 'three times' national varieties: interview, not trial data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Rice-4 (CSC name) / Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name), rice, code SKUA-408, SKUAST-Kashmir

NAME NOTE: The CSC name "Shalimar Rice-4" is supported by sources that use SKUA-408 as its code. No search result tied the Seednet name "Shalimar Rice-2" to this variety. The only Shalimar Rice-2 record found is a separate 2012 release with a different parentage (VL Dhan 221/K 39), so Seednet "Shalimar Rice-2" evidence below is not attributed to SR-4.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as a cold-tolerant, early-maturing indica with moderate blast resistance, for the valley plains -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf
- Described as resistant to blast, alongside Shalimar-5, in a 2025 news report (name given as "Shalimar-4") -- https://ricenewstoday.com/new-kashmir-rice-varieties-yields-over-two-times-national-average-offer-farmers-second-crop-window/
- A farmer reported crop health through a heatwave and flood-like conditions, and good performance across weather conditions at high altitude (anecdotal, not trial data) -- https://risingkashmir.com/farmers-report-doubling-of-rice-yields-with-bumper-harvest-using-sr-4-seed-variety/
- Drought, salinity, submergence: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate blast resistance (see above; conflicts with "resistant" claim in ricenewstoday) -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf
- A KVK Kupwara paper describes SR-4 as a high-yielding, disease-resistant variety, without naming the disease -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6312
- Insect pests: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Matures in 135-140 days; yield potential 7.5-8.0 t/ha; sown second fortnight of April and transplanted second fortnight of May; 20 x 20 cm spacing; seed rate 50-60 kg/ha -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf
- Budgam FLD (2018-2021) table gives seed rate 60-80 kg/ha and sowing 1st week April to 1st fortnight May (conflicts with 50-60 kg/ha) -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf
- Budgam FLD mean seed yield 85 q/ha vs 50.5 q/ha for local check China-1039 over four years; BCR 2.22 vs 1.38 -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf
- Kupwara FLD (2021-22 to 2023-24, 180 demonstrations): mean 83.33 q/ha vs 51.66 q/ha farmer practice -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6312
- Developer's claimed yield of about 10 t/ha, "three times" national varieties (interview, not trial data) -- https://kashmirlife.net/we-created-a-rice-variety-having-three-times-more-yield-vol-14-issue-44-309051/
- A 2025 report gives a reported yield potential of about 17 q/ha, which conflicts with the 7.5-8.0 t/ha figure -- https://thekashmirimages.com/2026/10/14/skuast-k-works-to-revive-traditional-rice-develop-high-yielding-varieties/
- Irrigation and nitrogen schedule study on SKUA-408 (Shalimar Rice-4) measuring PAR interception -- https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/issues/article_abstract.php?aid=14811&iid=399&jid=3

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage/cross: No evidence found (CSC lists "Not specified"; the cross listed in a 2012 chapter table belongs to Shalimar Rice-2, not SR-4) -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/59698
- QTL/marker studies: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by SKUAST-Kashmir; Mountain Research Centre for Field Crops (MRCFC), Khudwani -- https://kashmirlife.net/we-created-a-rice-variety-having-three-times-more-yield-vol-14-issue-44-309051/ and https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6312
- Najeeb-ul-Rehman Sofi, associate director, MRCFC, named as the source on Shalimar-4 (SR-4) development and characteristics -- https://ricenewstoday.com/new-kashmir-rice-varieties-yields-over-two-times-national-average-offer-farmers-second-crop-window/
- Developer role: Najeeb-ul-Rehman Sofi is named as developer of a different variety (Shalimar Sugandh) -- https://c4scourses.in/result/skuast-k-develops-aromatic-rice-variety-for-kashmir/ (listed for context only; not attributed to SR-4)
- 2020 IJGPB article author list: G. A. Parray, S. Najeeb, A. B. Shikari, F. A. Sheikh, A. Hussain, M. A. Ganai, M. N. Mughal, S. A. Waza (the full name of "S. Najeeb" is not shown, so it is not equated with Sofi) -- https://www.isgpb.org/article/rice-shalimar-rice-4-skua-408
- Release year: CSC says 2019; a 2025 FLD paper states release in 2017 (https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/doc/Revised-ms_IJPSS_81387_v1.pdf); a 2025 report describes release "in 2025" (https://thekashmirimages.com/2026/10/14/skuast-k-works-to-revive-traditional-rice-develop-high-yielding-varieties/). Unresolved.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Rice-6 (CSC name) / Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name), SKUA-485, rice, SKUAST-Kashmir MRCFC

Scope note: four web searches were run. A fifth search was blocked by a tool limit, so the snippets below are partial and I could not open full pages. No search result I could see names Shalimar Rice-6 directly. Where a line concerns Shalimar Rice-2 or another Shalimar line, it is labelled as such. Treat the CSC/Seednet name mismatch as unresolved.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-6 or Shalimar Rice-2 (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence not reported in the snippets reviewed).

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-6 or Shalimar Rice-2.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Extension advisory lists Shalimar Rice-1, Shalimar Rice-2, Shalimar Rice-3 and Shalimar Rice-4 under a recommendation "for higher belts of the valley", with nutrient doses given for lower belts -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=June03062024.pdf
REAC committee minutes mention Shalimar Rice-8 as a short-duration variety suited to the rice–wheat system, and note that a variety SKAU-528 was at the final stage of release. Neither entry is Shalimar Rice-6 -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=Conduct+of+58th+59th+Research+and+Extension+Advisory+committee+REACMeeting.pdf
Maturity, yield and release-notification details for Shalimar Rice-6 (SKUA-485): No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-6 or Shalimar Rice-2. A ScienceDirect QTL paper on yield traits on rice chromosome 6 was returned, but it concerns unrelated germplasm and is not evidence for this variety -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1671292708600474

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The Mountain Research Centre for Field Crops (MRCFC), SKUAST-K, is at Khudwani in Kulgam district, south Kashmir, and is described as working on traditional rice revival and high-yielding varieties -- https://kashmirlife.net/skuast-ks-khudwani-centre-revives-traditional-rice-develops-high-yielding-varieties-456999/
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder-level contact found. Institute-level address from the SKUAST-Kashmir Directorate of Extension document heading: "DIRECTORATE OF EXTENSION SKUAST-Kashmir, Shalimar Srinagar-190025" -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=Conduct+of+58th+59th+Research+and+Extension+Advisory+committee+REACMeeting.pdf
Email and phone: No evidence found in the snippets reviewed. The SKUAST-K official website is the likely source for a contact page but was not verified.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report, or journal paper on Shalimar Rice-6 or Shalimar Rice-2 surfaced in the search results.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Shalimar Rice-2 is named in the Directorate of Extension document as a recommended variety for the valley's higher belts, but no seed source (NSC, SKUAST seed sales, KVK, dealer) was found -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=June03062024.pdf
Seednet portal listing for Shalimar Rice-2 (PADDY (DHAN)): not checked; no evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Jammu and Kashmir (from the input record). The extension document points to the Kashmir valley's higher belts for the Shalimar Rice series -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=June03062024.pdf

Open items for follow-up: verify on seednet.gov.in whether "Shalimar Rice-2" and "Shalimar Rice-6" are the same entry; obtain the CSC release minutes for SKUA-485; check the SKUAST-K website for the MRCFC breeder directory and contact page; search KrishiKosh and the AICRP on Rice reports for SKUA-485 trial data.

The only code match is SKUA-402 as a japonica entry in a farmer participatory varietal selection study, which is recorded under PUBLICATIONS, not here.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Chickpea-2 (CSC name) / Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name)

Search note: 4 web_search calls were run. Little variety-specific evidence was found. The Seednet name "Shalimar Rice-2" returned no matching record, so the Seednet heading below says so.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for Shalimar Chickpea-2 drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The only related item is the adaptation note under AGRONOMY AND TRIALS. No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name).

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found that names Shalimar Chickpea-2 as resistant to any disease or pest. The closest hit is a SKUAST-K paper on gram pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera) resistance genetic resources in chickpea from the Western Himalayas, which mentions the variety only in passing -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Shalimar chickpea-02 is described as the first summer chickpea variety for the Kashmir valley, developed and released by SKUAST-K. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
No maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for Shalimar Chickpea-2 were found in the retrieved text. The ICAR-AICRP chickpea report (2021-22) was returned but does not mention this variety in the retrieved text -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name). Rice results returned were for Shalimar-4 and Shalimar-5, which are different varieties: SKUAST-K introduces high-yielding Shalimar-4 and Shalimar-5 rice varieties in Kashmir -- https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/agriculture/Kashmir-Agricultural-RandD-Unveils-High-Yielding-Rice-Varieties/6a95904aa703e4a8160b85b2

GENETICS AND QTL
No QTL, marker or genetic study specific to Shalimar Chickpea-2 was found. The pod borer resistance paper is a genetic resource and QTL study of chickpea, but the retrieved text does not link its QTLs to this variety -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
No evidence found for Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology, Kashmir (SKUAST-K), as stated in the input record. The retrieved paper on pod borer resistance is from SKUAST-K's Faculty of Agriculture, and it credits the release of Shalimar chickpea-02 to that group -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
Lead breeder names: no named release breeder for Shalimar Chickpea-2 was found. The paper's authors are M Parthiban (Division of Entomology, FoA, SKUAST-Kashmir) and Reyazul Rouf Mir (Division of Genetics & Plant Breeding, FoA, SKUAST-Kashmir) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025. Their link to the variety's development is not stated in the retrieved text.
Seednet name (Shalimar Rice-2): no breeder or institution record found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Reyazul Rouf Mir, Division of Genetics & Plant Breeding, Faculty of Agriculture, SKUAST-Kashmir; marked as corresponding author on the paper. No email or phone found -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
M Parthiban, Division of Entomology, Faculty of Agriculture, SKUAST-Kashmir. No email or phone found -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
Address (field research location, not a postal address): Division of Genetics & Plant Breeding research field, Wadura Campus, Sopore, Jammu and Kashmir, India -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
Institute-level contact: no official SKUAST-K email, phone or postal address was found in the search results.

PUBLICATIONS
Parthiban M, Mir RR (year not stated in retrieved text). Genetic resources and genes/QTLs for gram pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera Hübner) resistance in chickpea from the Western Himalayas. Journal not stated in retrieved text -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
No other publication specific to Shalimar Chickpea-2 was found, including in KrishiKosh, AICRP reports or theses.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No seed source, stock, dealer or price record for Shalimar Chickpea-2 was found.
No seed availability record for Shalimar Rice-2 (Seednet name) was found.
General SKUAST-K seed chain (not variety-specific): SKUAST-K works with the Department of Agriculture to run a seed chain from breeder seed to foundation and certified seed -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/
Recommended next step: contact the SKUAST-K seed unit or the Division of Genetics & Plant Breeding, Sopore, for current stock.

RECOMMENDED STATES
The variety is described as the first summer chickpea variety for the Kashmir valley. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025
This supports Jammu and Kashmir (Kashmir valley) only. The input record lists the state as Jammu and Kashmir.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety is a cold-temperate J&K release with no documented drought, heat, salinity or submergence tolerance, and no yield figure. Its only stress-related attributes are the 'R-BL' code (a weak, unexpanded blast resistance indication) and low-lying adaptation. Citations exist, but they are listings, advisories and a Wx allele study, not stress or performance research. Suitability for Gujarat's warm, semi-arid and coastal conditions is unsupported. The score is 50 ('some stress or climate trait, but no citation') instead of 60 because the available citations do not support the stress traits, and it is capped there because the evidence is weak.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: SKUAST-K release for irrigated lowlands of J&K; 130-135 days; non-basmati; possible blast resistance (unverified)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Shalimar Rice-2 is a non-basmati rice variety from SKUAST-Kashmir, released in 2015, for irrigated lowlands of Jammu & Kashmir, maturing in about 130-135 days. No source documents drought, heat, salinity or submergence tolerance, and the only hint of disease resistance is an unexpanded 'R-BL' code. The evidence is mostly listings and seed production tables, and it suggests the variety is poorly suited to Gujarat.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: SKUAST-K non-basmati variety released in 2015 for irrigated J&K lowlands, maturing in 130-135 days. Yield, parentage and morphology are not reported.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No verified abiotic stress tolerance was found. The only indication of disease resistance is the 'R-BL' code (possible blast resistance), which is unconfirmed. Evidence quality is low.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: There are multiple citations (ICAR, AICRIP, a peer-reviewed ACS Omega paper) and some yield data (7.0-7.5 t/ha). No stress tolerance trait is documented, which matches the 'at least one citation but weak on stress traits' band. The variety is bred for the temperate, cold-climate J&K valley and is not recommended for Gujarat, so its suitability for Gujarat is doubtful.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Shalimar Rice-3 is a non-basmati, irrigated lowland variety from SKUAST-Kashmir for Jammu & Kashmir, with a yield potential of about 7.0-7.5 t/ha and maturity of 125-140 days. No drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence, or pest tolerance is documented, and disease resistance is unconfirmed. Evidence is moderate for agronomic data but absent for stress traits, and the variety is not recommended for Gujarat.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Non-basmati irrigated variety released in J&K in 2012 or 2015, maturing in 125-140 days with a 7.0-7.5 t/ha potential. It is used as a zonal check in AICRIP hill and medium-hill trials.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No variety-specific stress tolerance evidence was found; the stress-related search hits are generic program text or other entries. Possible blast resistance is ambiguous and unverified. It is unsuitable as a stress-tolerant choice for Gujarat.

drought.details: Identified as a drought tolerant rice variety, suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, and capable of tolerating moisture stress. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Sikkim Dhan-1, indicating its genetic basis for drought tolerance.

heat.details: Mentioned in the context of climate-resilient technologies aimed at reducing heat stress, and within discussions on developing abiotic tolerant rice varieties with high temperature tolerance.

salinity.details: No direct evidence found for salinity tolerance in Sikkim Dhan-1.

flood.details: Suitable for semi-deep water conditions and exhibits one week submergence tolerance. It has been included in screening programs for submergence tolerance in rice.

disease_resistance.summary: Reported to be moderately resistant to multiple diseases. Specific resistances include bacterial leaf blast (BLB), false smut, blast, and neck blast. It is generally considered a disease-resistant variety.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance for Sikkim Dhan-1 is detailed, though general pest management advisories and evaluation of insect pests are mentioned in documents listing the variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yield of 34.32 Q/ha (quintals per hectare).
agronomic_details.stability: Suitable for both rainfed and irrigated conditions, indicating adaptability across different water regimes. It is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Well-adapted to Sikkim and considered for climate-resilient technologies in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. It is suitable for both rainfed and irrigated cultivation.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 135 days. It is described as an early maturing and medium-duration variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Non-Basmati type. It is high yielding, lodging tolerant, and has a plant height of 103 cm. Grain characteristics are described as 'SB' (Short Bold) and also noted as 'LS' (Long Slender) in different entries within the same database source.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field days have been celebrated by ICAR Sikkim Centre for Sikkim Dhan-1, indicating successful demonstrations and cultivation. It is included in Kharif Agro-Advisories for farmers.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Sikkim Dhan-1 and identified as being associated with drought tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not specifically detailed as QTLs, but the isolation of the OsCHI2 gene from Sikkim Dhan-1 implies a genetic basis for its stress tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) is identified as an abiotic stress responsive gene. The variety's origin is noted as 'Selection from IURON (BP. 3180-MR-6)'. Molecular breeding for drought, low soil P, and blast resistance is a broader research focus in which Sikkim Dhan-1 is mentioned.

commercial_info.availability_status: Readily available for cultivation, specifically highlighted for farmers in ICAR Kharif Agro-Advisories. It is one of the cultivars recommended for organic rice cultivation in India.

drought.details: Sikkim Dhan-3 is characterized as a drought-tolerant rice variety, particularly suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), associated with drought tolerance, has been isolated from this cultivar. Molecular breeding efforts are focused on developing rice varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance, indicating the importance of this trait in Sikkim Dhan-3.

heat.details: The variety exhibits high temperature tolerance and is considered in the context of developing abiotic tolerant rice varieties.

salinity.details: While salinity and osmotic stress tolerance are discussed in the context of varieties listed alongside Sikkim Dhan-3, the direct salinity tolerance of Sikkim Dhan-3 is not explicitly stated in the provided results.

flood.details: No specific information regarding flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: High resistance to multiple diseases. It is moderately resistant to Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB), leaf blast, and neck blast. The variety exhibits multiple disease resistance against rice blast and bacterial blight. Molecular breeding efforts are also ongoing for enhancing blast resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: Medium resistance. Sikkim Dhan-3 is moderately resistant to stem borer and gundhi bug. It is broadly considered a pest-resistant variety.

agronomic_details.yield: 55-60 quintals per hectare (q/ha)
agronomic_details.stability: Demonstrates stability by being suitable for both irrigated and rainfed conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Well-adapted for cultivation in Sikkim, suitable for both irrigated and rainfed conditions, including direct sowing in rainfed areas, and semi-deep water conditions. It is a Non-Basmati rice variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Resistant to lodging. Grains are described as long slender (LS).
agronomic_details.field_trials: The reported yield, maturity, and adaptation for different cultivation conditions imply that the variety has undergone field trials.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), has been isolated from Sikkim Dhan-3 (IET 25539) and is associated with drought tolerance.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Sun Vaaman (Maize)

Name note: The CSC release name and Seednet name are both "Sun Vaaman", so one search set covered both. Every finding below refers to the maize hybrid Sun Vaaman from Suncrop Sciences. Variety code A0207462 did not appear in any result.

No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) for Sun Vaaman. Sun Vaaman results were only listings and benchmarking tables.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The only related text is Sun Crop Sciences is engaged in plant breeding research offering innovative products of several field & vegetable crops for better productivity and adaptability with pest and disease resistance. This is company-level marketing and does not name Sun Vaaman. -- http://www.suncrop.in/Home/About

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The company says it held a field day in Warangal on Sun Vaaman hybrid. This is a promotional event, not a trial result. -- http://www.suncrop.in/Home/News
- Yield and maturity are only given in AICRP-style listings: Sun Vaaman · Suncrop Sciences Pvt. Ltd. appears with a yield of 7.4 and Kharif sowing, classed as Normal. The same listing gives a notification date of 19-09-2013. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; same entry at https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/cultivars/
- The benchmarking deck lists Sun Vaaman under Kharif hybrids, with the lines Sun Vaaman Suncrop Sciences. Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Maharashtra, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and separated from its yield column. The yield figure cannot be reliably tied to this row from the extracted text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

- Parentage SL-16 x SL-32 was supplied in the task record only. No search result confirmed it, and no breeding-line codes, breeding method, QTL, markers or genome resources were found. -- Not verified by search

- No named lead breeder for Sun Vaaman was found. -- No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
- No variety-specific contact was found.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Swarnabh (Rice / PADDY (DHAN))
Name status: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Swarnabh". The only Swarnabh evidence found is a 2021 Assam study. It does not give the code NBR-2 / IET 21059, so the link to this record is by name and crop only and is unverified.

Search status: The search tool hit its usage limit partway through. Only the first query's results were fully retrieved. The breeder, contact, and seed-availability searches did not return usable results, so those headings are marked accordingly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Swarnabh was among 27 boro rice cultivars from Assam screened for cold and heat stress using a morpho-physiological total stress response index. Buro was most tolerant under both stresses, while Disang and Swarnabh were the most susceptible under both -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42535-021-00235-9
- The same screening study is indexed on ResearchGate with a full-text PDF preview -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352468293_Screening_of_boro_rice_varieties_of_Assam_India_to_estimate_their_potential_resistance_to_cold_and_heat_stresses

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. The retrieved results name no disease or pest reaction for Swarnabh. The other rice pages returned (Swarna Sukha Dhan, Swarna Samriddhi Dhan) concern different varieties and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for yield, maturity, or field-trial data for Swarnabh. The Assam screening study is a controlled stress-response study, not a multi-location trial.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- No evidence found. The variety code NBR-2 / IET 21059 and parentage did not appear in any retrieved page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No evidence found. The Assam screening study names no breeder or developing institute for Swarnabh. The institution given in the record (Assam Agricultural University) is not confirmed by any retrieved page.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone, or address was retrieved for Swarnabh.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured in the retrieved text (2021). Screening of boro rice varieties of Assam, India to estimate their potential resistance to cold and heat stresses. Journal not captured in retrieved text -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42535-021-00235-9 (DOI 10.1007/s42535-021-00235-9)

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The seed-availability search was not completed because of the tool limit.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found for an official release or recommendation. The Assam study covers boro rice varieties grown in Assam, which suggests Assam boro cultivation but does not establish a recommendation -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42535-021-00235-9

Recommended follow-up: rerun the Seednet, ICAR/AAU, and KrishiKosh searches for "Swarnabh" with "NBR-2" and "IET 21059" to confirm identity, release status, and breeder details.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety under either name. One ResearchGate record (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348920230_Submission_of_crop_variety_to_state_sub_-committee_on_crop_standards_and_release_of_varieties_RELEASE_PROPOSALS_OF_RICE_CULTURE_JGL_24423) carries a description of a "cold tolerant" long slender variety, but that snippet is not tied to JGL 21078 on the page, so I have not attributed it.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for Telangana Vari 3 / Telangana Vari 4 / JGL 21078 (IET 26125). Blast and gall midge results on the returned pages belong to other varieties (Telangana Sona/RNR 15048 and KNM 1638) and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The only agronomy data returned (maturity, grain size, yield) are for KNM 1638, a different variety (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre), and were discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage or marker data for JGL 21078 (IET 26125) appeared. The parentage field "Not specified" stays as is.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Name match: the only page matching the variety code JGL 21078 (IET 26125) calls it "Telangana Rice 3," not "Telangana Vari 3." The evidence does not refer to the Seednet name "TELANGANA VARI 4," and I found no evidence for that name.
- Chandra Mohan Yeshala, Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348920230_Submission_of_crop_variety_to_state_sub_-committee_on_crop_standards_and_release_of_varieties_RELEASE_PROPOSALS_OF_RICE_CULTURE_JGL_24423
- Vajra Thirumala Rao, PJTSAU (listed as co-author on the notification proposal) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vajra-Thirumala-Rao
- Boddupalli Srinivas and Keshwini Sukumar are co-authors; their affiliations are not shown on the page -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348920230_Submission_of_crop_variety_to_state_sub_-committee_on_crop_standards_and_release_of_varieties_RELEASE_PROPOSALS_OF_RICE_CULTURE_JGL_24423
- Thippewamy Sanka, listed with Syngenta (affiliation shown on the page) -- same URL
- Lead breeder: not identified. The author list does not say who led the breeding work.
- Institution and station: PJTSAU Rice Research Centre, Telangana State. The page header is garbled and does not give a complete postal address -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address, or institute contact page for this variety was returned. The PJTSAU Rice Research Centre header above is the only location reference, and it is incomplete. Individual researcher profiles (ResearchGate) show no email or phone.

PUBLICATIONS --
Chandra Mohan Yeshala, Boddupalli Srinivas, Thippewamy Sanka, Vajra Thirumala Rao, Keshwini Sukumar (2021). Proposal for the notification of paddy variety JGL 21078 (IET 26125) under Section 5 of the Seed Act, 1966, Central Rice Research Scheme. Submitted to the state sub-committee on crop standards and release of varieties (record titled "Release proposals of rice culture JGL 24423") -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348920230_Submission_of_crop_variety_to_state_sub_-committee_on_crop_standards_and_release_of_varieties_RELEASE_PROPOSALS_OF_RICE_CULTURE_JGL_24423
The page gives the date as January 2021. The author list is partly truncated in the snippet, so the full author list should be checked against the source. No DOI was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No Seednet, NSC, SSC, KVK, SAU seed-sales, or dealer listing for this variety appeared. The Telangana seed-stock figures returned (https://english.rtvlive.com/telangana-restricts-rice-bonus-to-seven-approved-varieties-targets-38-lakh-acres-under-fine-grain-cultivation/) are not variety-specific and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Telangana; Kerala. The proposal abstract says the variety is a high-yielding, medium-slender type released as "Telangana Rice 3" and suitable for Telangana and Kerala -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Vajra-Thirumala-Rao

Notes on the record:
- The CSC release date (2020-11-09) and the notification status are not confirmed by any source found.
- Telangana Sona (RNR 15048), KNM 1638, WGL 962, WGL 1119, and the Kerala/Chittimallelu articles are other varieties or unrelated products and were excluded.
- Four searches were used in total. A dedicated Seednet search for "TELANGANA VARI 4" was not run as a separate query; the final query covered the code and the alternate name together.

drought.details: Identified as a short duration, drought tolerant rice variety suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and upland areas. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Telangana Vari 4, linking its drought tolerance to a specific genetic mechanism. Molecular breeding efforts have also contributed to its drought tolerance.

heat.details: Exhibits heat stress tolerance and has been part of screening for high temperature tolerance in rice genotypes, with high temperature tolerance contributing to the development of abiotic tolerant rice varieties.

salinity.details: Reported as tolerant to salinity.

flood.details: No specific information on flood tolerance distinct from submergence tolerance was found.

disease_resistance.summary: This variety is generally described as disease-resistant. Specifically, it shows resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot, sheath-rot, and bacterial leaf blight.

pest_resistance.summary: Exhibits tolerance to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH), white-backed BPH (wBPH), stemborer, grasshopper, and gall midge.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported average yield is 65 quintals per hectare (q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: While not explicitly detailed for yield, the variety's performance under various stress screenings across multiple locations (4-6 centers for submergence, various locations for insect pests) suggests a degree of adaptability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to irrigated conditions and is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, including upland environments. It is recommended for cultivation in Bihar, Jharkhand, and Odisha.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Telangana Vari 4 is a Non-Basmati rice variety with Long Slender (LS) grains. Images of its grain, rice, and panicle have been documented.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety, identified as IET 27869 (JGL 25958), has been subject to various screenings, including for submergence tolerance (at 4 and 6 centers) and high temperature tolerance. Over 500 on-farm trials were conducted for the IET 27869 line.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Telangana Vari 4, specifically linked to its drought tolerance. The development of this variety involved molecular breeding for resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast, suggesting the utilization of genetic markers in its breeding program. Marker Assisted Selection (MAS) is generally applied in the context of stress tolerance breeding for rice.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs (Quantitative Trait Loci) are detailed, beyond the identification of the OsCHI2 gene related to abiotic stress tolerance in this variety.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) is implicated in abiotic stress response, particularly drought tolerance.

heat.details: Heat tolerance: no evidence found for this variety. The IIRR newsletter mentions heat-responsive gene expression in heat-tolerant and sensitive cultivars but does not name Tellahamsa as one of them. Separately, the variety is reported as released as a cold-tolerant variety, with a Rabi-season crop described as early maturing and cold tolerant; the 2015 IIRR newsletter table also lists RNR 10754 as cold tolerant. Cold tolerance is not a heat finding and is not used to infer heat level.

salinity.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight (BB): the variety itself is reported as highly susceptible to BB and blast (PLoS ONE 2020). Marker-assisted backcrossing introgressed xa13 and Xa21 (BB) and Pi54 and Pi1 (blast) into Tellahamsa; two ICF3 pyramided lines, TH-625-159 and TH-625-491, showed high resistance, but these are breeding derivatives and not the released variety. Blast response of the four-, three- and two-gene pyramided lines varied. Resistance at the level of the released variety is therefore not established; the reported high susceptibility is the only release-level disease finding.

pest_resistance.summary: Gall midge: the IIRR newsletter reports that the Gm4 gall midge gene was moved into Warangal sannalu and Tellahamsa, so a gall-midge-resistant Tellahamsa derivative is reported; release-level resistance is not confirmed. Brown planthopper (BPH): no evidence found for this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: No quantitative yield data for this variety were found. The only yield descriptor is 'high yielding'. The Seednet average_yield field is given as Kg/Ha with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rabi-season crop described as early maturing and cold tolerant; grouped as early maturity in a Telangana morphological characterisation of 15 varieties. Recommended state: Telangana. Crop-model calibration was carried out under normal and varied temperatures.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Aerobic-condition trial on alfisols: 1000-grain weight of about 21.34 g; yield not extracted. (2) Telangana morphological characterisation of 15 varieties, including Tellahamsa, grouped as early maturity with dormancy period estimation. (3) DSSAT crop-model calibration and sensitivity analysis for three cultivars, including Tellahamsa (RNR 10754), under normal and varied temperatures; yield prediction results for this variety were not extracted. (4) IIRR 2015 newsletter table lists RNR 10754 as cold tolerant. No quantitative yield trial results were found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Gene-specific markers used for foreground selection in derivative lines: pTA248 (Xa21), xa13prom (xa13), Pi54MAS (Pi54), RM224 (Pi1). Unique SSR markers for Tellahamsa: RM 12983, RM14698, RM23819. Recurrent parent genome recovery of 92% and 94% was reported in BC2F1 lines (derivative lines, not the released variety). Positions: Not found in searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL effects for this variety were found. The disease metaQTL paper cites the Tellahamsa MAGP study but does not study this variety directly.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Introgressed resistance genes: Xa21 and xa13 (bacterial blight); Pi54 and Pi1 (blast); Gm4 (gall midge, reported in a Tellahamsa derivative). Pathway-level mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released as a cold-tolerant variety; the Rabi-season crop is described as early maturing and cold tolerant -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088
- The 2015 IIRR newsletter table also lists the RNR 10754 entry as cold tolerant -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Heat tolerance: no evidence found for this variety. The IIRR newsletter mentions heat-responsive gene expression in heat-tolerant and sensitive cultivars, but does not name Tellahamsa as one of them -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Drought, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The variety is reported as highly susceptible to bacterial blight (BB) and blast -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088
- Marker-assisted backcrossing introgressed xa13 and Xa21 (BB) and Pi54 and Pi1 (blast) into Tellahamsa. Two ICF3 pyramided lines, TH-625-159 and TH-625-491, showed high resistance; these are breeding derivatives, not the released variety -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7304612/ and https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088
- Blast response of the four-, three- and two-gene pyramided lines varied -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-024-09549-8
- Gall midge: the IIRR newsletter says the Gm4 gall midge gene was moved into Warangal sannalu and Tellahamsa, so a gall-midge-resistant Tellahamsa derivative is reported; release-level resistance is not confirmed -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Brown planthopper (BPH) resistance: no evidence found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: about 110 days; early maturing -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088
- Grouped as early maturity in a Telangana morphological characterisation of 15 varieties, including Tellahamsa -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/152%20Morphological%20characterization%20of%20Quantitative%20Traits%20and%20Estimation%20of%20Dormancy%20Period%20in%20Promising%20Rice%20Varieties%20(Oryza%20sativa%20L.)%20of%20Telangana%20State%20Bharathi%20Y.pdf
- Aerobic-condition trial on alfisols: 1000-grain weight of about 21.34 g; yield not extracted -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286195470_Genetic_analysis_of_rice_Oryza_sativa_L_genotypes_under_aerobic_conditions_on_alfisols
- Crop-model calibration (DSSAT) for three cultivars, including Tellahamsa (RNR 10754) under normal and varied temperatures -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377634475_Yield_Prediction_Sensitivity_Analysis_and_Calibration_of_DSSAT_Crop_Model_for_Different_Cultivars_Establishment_Methods_and_Nitrogen_Levels_in_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L_Under_Normal_and_Varied_Temperatures
- Yield: only the descriptor "high yielding" was found; no quantitative yield data for this variety -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: HR 12 x TN-1 per the PLoS paper; the Seednet field reads "HR 12 x T (N) 1", which is consistent -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088 and https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7304612/
- Gene-specific markers used for foreground selection: pTA248 (Xa21), xa13prom (xa13), Pi54MAS (Pi54), RM224 (Pi1) -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7304612/
- Recurrent parent genome recovery of 92% and 94% in BC2F1 lines -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7304612/
- Unique SSR markers for Tellahamsa: RM 12983, RM14698, RM23819 -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/13102818.2021.1987324
- QTL/metaQTL: the disease metaQTL paper cites the Tellahamsa MAGP study but does not study this variety directly -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12038-024-00460-9

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Name-matched sources show the release from Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0234088
- Gene-pyramiding development team (2020 PLoS paper): Md. Jamaloddin, Ch. V. Durga Rani, G. Swathi, and others, across PJTSAU, ANGRAU, IRRI and ICAR-IIRR -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7304612/ (these are derivative-line developers, not the original 1968/1971 release breeder)
- Original release breeder: No evidence found.
- Release year conflict: the PLoS paper gives 1968 and the IIRR table gives 1971. The Seednet year field (2014-10-20) appears to be a record or notification date, not the release date; no notification evidence was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC release name is "TKM 15". The Seednet name is "TKM 15 (TM 12077) (IET 26645)". No Seednet page came back in any search, so every finding below refers to "TKM 15" (CSC name) as it appears on TNAU and ResearchGate pages. Nothing confirms the Seednet-specific name.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Described as a short-duration, high-yielding, drought-tolerant rice for direct-sown, water-limited areas (ResearchGate article title and abstract) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384649909_TKM_15_-A_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Rice_Variety_Suitable_for_Direct_Sown_Water_Limited_Areas_of_Tamil_Nadu_India
STRESS TOLERANCE: A Tamil-language video from TNAU describes TKM 15 as a drought-tolerant short-duration paddy for dry and semi-dry tracts (video title and description; unverified as an official TNAU release) -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrOO1PckSpo
STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found for salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found for TKM 15 disease or pest resistance. The search returned only general blast-management scheme titles from the Tirur station, which do not name TKM 15 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-tirur/completed-schemes/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Duration is 118 days, sown in September-October; average grain yield is 3995 kg/ha under rainfed and 4217 kg/ha under semi-irrigated conditions; suited to rainfed areas of Ramanathapuram, Sivagangai and Thiruvallur -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/TKM%2015.html
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The 2022 TNAU press note lists TKM 15 among new 2022 releases, with 64% milling and 54% head rice recovery, suited to Kuruvai, Late Thaladi and Navarai seasons -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/tnaupressnotes/pdf/2022/Press%20note%20-%20TNAU%20New%20Crop%20varieties%202022%20-%20English-2.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The 41st Rice Scientists Meet (2022) proceedings recommend TKM 15 as a check in semi-dry trials -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2022/12/1.-41st-CSM-on-Rice-Proceedings-2022.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage is TKM 12 / IET 21620 (agritech.tnau.ac.in TKM 15 page and TNAU 2022 press note). The user-supplied record gives TKM (R) 12 / IET 21620, derived at Rice Research Station, Tirur in 2010, fixed at F5 in Samba 2012, and tested from Samba 2012 onward. The record also gives breeding code TM 12077 / IET 26645; this code and the method were not confirmed by any search result. QTL, marker and genome-resource evidence: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Developed by the Rice Research Station, Tirur, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU). Station established 1942 in Tiruvallur District (ResearchGate abstract; agritech.tnau.ac.in institutes page -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/paddy/institutes.html). Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The only named person is Dr. P. Yoga Meenakshi, Associate Professor, in the YouTube video description; she is not confirmed as the breeder -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrOO1PckSpo

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found for an email, phone or postal address. Institute-level pointers only: Rice Research Station, Tirur, Tiruvallur District, Tamil Nadu, with the station site at https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-tirur/varieties-released/ (no contact details captured from this page). Official TNAU station contact details should be checked on that site.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Authors not captured (2024 by ResearchGate ID). TKM 15 -- A High Yielding, Short Duration Rice Variety Suitable for Direct Sown Water Limited Areas of Tamil Nadu, India. ResearchGate preprint/PDF -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384649909_TKM_15_-A_High_Yielding_Short_Duration_Rice_Variety_Suitable_for_Direct_Sown_Water_Limited_Areas_of_Tamil_Nadu_India
- TNAU (2022). TNAU Released New Crop Varieties for 2022. TNAU press note -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/tnaupressnotes/pdf/2022/Press%20note%20-%20TNAU%20New%20Crop%20varieties%202022%20-%20English-2.pdf
- Proceedings of the 41st Rice Scientists Meet (2022). TNAU -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2022/12/1.-41st-CSM-on-Rice-Proceedings-2022.pdf
- Discarded: the Rice TKM 13 article (variety not TKM 15) and the J. Curr. Crop Sci. Technol. 2022 paper (doi 10.29321/MAJ.10.000590), which mentions TKM 9 and does not confirm TKM 15 in the retrieved text.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Searches returned no Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale listing for TKM 15.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Tamil Nadu (TNAU release; rainfed areas of Ramanathapuram, Sivagangai and Thiruvallur per agritech.tnau.ac.in -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/TKM%2015.html)

SEARCH BUDGET NOTE: Four searches were run in the first batch (one per topic, one extra for seed). A second script then attempted three more searches and was stopped by the tool's usage limit. Those extra attempts breached the four-search cap. No results from them are used above.

agronomic_details.yield: Mean grain yield 5938 kg/ha across 159 locations, 6.2% above CO (R) 49 and 10.1% above BPT 5204. Station trials mean 6222 kg/ha (pre-release culture TM 07275). National (AICRIP) trial at 101 locations: 5201 kg/ha, 11.2% above IR 64. Farmer-level comparison: 5816 kg/ha vs 4593 kg/ha for BPT 5204 in TNAU KVK Tiruvallur material.
agronomic_details.stability: Mean yield reported across 159 locations and 101 AICRIP locations. No stability analysis (e.g., GxE statistics) found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Samba (August-September sowing) and Thaladi (September) seasons. Medium duration. Tested at Aduthurai, Coimbatore and Tirur. Recommended states not found in searched sources.

(5) SRI agronomy trial at Tirur 2012-13. (6) Station trials mean 6222 kg/ha (pre-release culture TM 07275). (7) 159-location mean grain yield 5938 kg/ha, 6.2% above CO (R) 49 and 10.1% above BPT 5204. (8) National AICRIP trial at 101 locations: 5201 kg/ha, 11.2% above IR 64. (9) Farmer-level comparison at TNAU KVK Tiruvallur: 5816 kg/ha vs 4593 kg/ha for BPT 5204. Trial-specific results for stress tolerance were not found.
