search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Evidence refers to "VL Dhan 88" (CSC release name). Moderate resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, sheath blight and bacterial leaf blight, with no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found. It has shown moderate resistance against leaf blast, neck blast, sheath blight and bacterial leaf blight. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=9&ArticleId=15390

DISEASE AND PEST
Evidence refers to "VL Dhan 88". Moderate field reaction to the four diseases above; no insect-pest resistance data found. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=9&ArticleId=15390

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Evidence refers to "VL Dhan 88". VL Dhan 88 is an early duration rice variety suitable for cultivation under lower hills of Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and medium hills of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=9&ArticleId=15390
Grain yield: 4,963 kg/ha in lower hills and 4,332 kg/ha at medium elevation, significantly above the national check VL Dhan 86 and the regional check Shalimar Rice 3. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=9&ArticleId=15390
Four years of multi-location testing made it a consistent performer in the target hills. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=9&ArticleId=15390
Quality: 77.5% hulling, 68.4% milling, 54.2% head rice recovery, 22.47% amylose, intermediate ASV 4.0, long bold grain (L/B 2.76). -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=9&ArticleId=15390
Maturity in days: no evidence found for the VL Dhan 88 duration figure.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: derived from the cross Vivek Dhan 82/VL 31629 (the release record gives VL Dhan 85/VOHP 3102; the two parentages conflict). -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=9&ArticleId=15390
QTL, marker or molecular studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Lead author and developer names (author list of the 2022 announcement): JP Aditya, Anuradha Bhartiya, PK Agrawal, Rajashekara H, VS Meena, L Kant, JK Arya, Devendra Lal. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=9&ArticleId=15390
Developing institution: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, Uttarakhand, under the irrigated early-duration segment. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=9&ArticleId=15390
Variety-specific station or division for VL Dhan 88: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Almora, Uttarakhand. Official website: https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/ (content published and managed by VPKAS Almora).
Official email, phone and postal address for the institute or the rice division: No evidence found.
Breeder-level contact details (email, phone, address) for VL Dhan 88: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
JP Aditya, Anuradha Bhartiya, PK Agrawal, Rajashekara H, VS Meena, L Kant, JK Arya, Devendra Lal (2022). VL Dhan 88 a newly notified rice variety for cultivation under lower and medium elevation of Northern hills. The Pharma Innovation Journal, 11(9), pp. 988-993 -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=9&ArticleId=15390 (no DOI found)
Other VL Dhan 88 journal, KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP or conference items: No evidence found. A KrishiKosh blast-resistance thesis appeared in results but does not name VL Dhan 88, so it was excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
VPKAS seed portal listing for "VL Dhan 88 / वी.एल. धान 88", brand VPKAS, marked in stock, with area of adaptation given as Uttarakhand, H.P. and Meghalaya. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLDhan88_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%A7%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A888
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for VL Dhan 88: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Lower hills of Himachal Pradesh and Meghalaya; medium hills of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=9&ArticleId=15390
VPKAS rice listing: year of release 2021 (CVRC), area of adaptation Uttarakhand, H.P. and Meghalaya. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/2/Rice

NOTES
1. Seednet name "VL Dhan 70": the search returned no page for this name, so no Seednet evidence was found. All findings above refer to "VL Dhan 88".
2. Variety code "IET 25819) (VL 32224": no evidence found for this code. It was not used to match any finding.
3. Release date: the input gives 9 Nov 2020. The notification in the 2022 paper is S.O.500(E) dated 29 January 2021, and the VPKAS listing gives 2021. The input date was not confirmed.
4. Recommended states: the input lists "Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and Uttarakhand". The sources agree on these states but split them by elevation (lower vs. medium hills).
5. The search for the name VL Dhan 88 also surfaced VL Barik Dhan and VL Bosi Dhan papers, and a VL Dhan 158 paper. These are different varieties and were excluded.

No evidence found. Searches for "VL Dhan 70" returned only other varieties (VL Dhan 69, VL Dhan 88, VL Dhan 209, VL Bosi Dhan, VL Barik Dhan) and unrelated rice lines (DRR Dhan 70, CR Dhan 70, BRRI dhan70), none of which are this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The disease and pest traits described for VL Barik Dhan and VL Bosi Dhan belong to other varieties and are not attributed here. drought.details: Zinco Rice-MS is drought tolerant, capable of escaping terminal drought, and its seedlings can withstand drought-like conditions. While tolerant, it may require protective life-saving irrigation under severe stress.

heat.details: The variety is moderately resistant to terminal heat stresses.

salinity.details: Zinco Rice-MS is tolerant to salt affected soils and general salinity conditions. It has been included in studies for salt tolerance.

flood.details: It is listed among flood tolerant rice varieties.

agronomic_details.adaptation: This variety is noted to be non-lodging and is a biofortified medium slender (MS) grain type. Its stress tolerance profile suggests adaptability to challenging environmental conditions, including drought, heat, salinity, and floods.

agronomic_details.field_trials: Zinco Rice-MS has been evaluated in various field trials, as indicated by its inclusion in Draft Proceedings of the Annual Rice Group Meetings (AICRIP) and Annual Reports from ICAR-IIRR, which involve multi-location screening for stress tolerance and yield performance.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JGL (Pranahitha) / (Pranahitha) JGL 11727, Rice (Paddy)

Search note: I ran the 4-search maximum. The search results gave only short snippets, not full page text, so I could not verify most details. I did not run a separate seednet.gov.in query, and I did not re-run any search to get more text, because that would have exceeded the cap. Treat the findings below as leads to check, not confirmed facts. Names used: "JGL (Pranahitha)" (variety_name) and "(Pranahitha) JGL 11727" (seednet_variety_name) and "JGL 11727" (variety_code). The evidence below refers to the name "Pranahitha (JGL 11727)" unless stated otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found for this variety. A search hit on rice variety JGL 17004 (aerobic sowing-date simulation) was discarded because it names a different variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Simulated-mean-grain-yield-of-rice-variety-JGL-17004-under-variable-sowing-dates-in_fig2_300001110 (discarded, different variety)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. Parentage is "Not specified" in the record, and no source gave it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- A certificate titled regarding involvement of scientists in development of rice culture JGL 11727 lists Ch Surender Raju among its authors (published January 2021). The snippet did not show the scientists named in the certificate, so I cannot say who bred the variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348805491_CERTIFICATE_REGARDING_INVOLVEMENT_OF_SCIENTISTS_IN_DEVELOPMENT_OF_RICE_CULTURE_JGL_11727
- A researcher profile lists a socioeconomic study of Pranahitha (JGL 11727) and Bathukamma (JGL 18047) in the Northern Telangana Zone. The profile names Boddupalli Srinivas and associates from ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (formerly Directorate of Rice Research), Hyderabad. These researchers are linked to the study, not confirmed as breeders of this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Boddupalli-Srinivas
- The record's institution, "Regional Agricultural Research Station", was not confirmed by any source.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found for a breeder contact. No official email, phone, address or contact-page URL was found for the developing station. The ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad is named only as an affiliation in the profile above; I did not retrieve its contact page, so no details are given.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Ch Surender Raju et al. (2021). Certificate regarding involvement of scientists in development of rice culture JGL 11727. Certificate document (ResearchGate) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348805491_CERTIFICATE_REGARDING_INVOLVEMENT_OF_SCIENTISTS_IN_DEVELOPMENT_OF_RICE_CULTURE_JGL_11727 (full author list not confirmed from the snippet)
- Socioeconomic impact study of paddy varieties Bathukamma (JGL 18047) and Pranahitha (JGL 11727) in Northern Telangana Zone. Authors, year and journal not confirmed from the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Boddupalli-Srinivas
- No peer-reviewed field-trial, AICRP, or KrishiKosh records were found in the search results.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for this variety. The one Telangana seed hit was a general paper on seed production of selected crops, not about this variety. -- https://www.academia.edu/101431980/Seed_Production_of_Selected_Crops_in_Telangana_State_India_Assessment_of_Demand_Supply_and_Constraints (discarded, not variety-specific)

RECOMMENDED STATES: Telangana is supported only indirectly. The socioeconomic study above covers Pranahitha (JGL 11727) in the Northern Telangana Zone. That is consistent with the record's "Telangana", but no official release notification or recommendation document was found.

Suggested next steps: check the seednet.gov.in entry for "(Pranahitha) JGL 11727", the ICAR-IIRR and Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU) release notifications, and KrishiKosh for theses. These were not covered by the searches above.

drought.details: No drought field result was found. A drought-linked SSR study used MTU 1010/JGL 17004 populations, with 173 polymorphic plants reported, but this is molecular marker work and does not show drought performance. A simulation modelled grain yield under aerobic irrigated conditions across sowing dates, which does not test drought tolerance.

heat.details: No heat tolerance evidence was found. Cold tolerance is listed for JGL 17004 in the IIRR release table, which is a cold-stress trait and not heat tolerance. A Jagtial rice trial programme reported reasonably good spikelet fertility in some years because the variety escapes low temperatures; this is an escape mechanism, not measured tolerance.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. No flood field result was found.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to leaf blast, as listed in the IIRR release table for JGL 17004. No neck blast rating was found for JGL 17004 itself. No bacterial leaf blight, brown planthopper or tungro rating was found for this variety. Neck blast and BPH references in the sources apply to other JGL lines or to the descendant KNM 1638 and were excluded.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant to gall midge, as listed in the IIRR release table for JGL 17004. A Telangana rice research document lists multiple gall midge resistance as a selection aim; this supports the breeding objective but is not a separate resistance rating. No BPH rating was found for JGL 17004 itself.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources. No field yield figure for JGL 17004 itself was found. The 7356 kg/ha figure belongs to the descendant KNM 1638 and was excluded.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Passport data give sowing time as June-July, with irrigated or rainfed cultivation as required. The rainfed Southern Zone recommendation in the Rajendranagar/Tirupati package belongs to Andhra Pradesh and was excluded.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 95-120 days, listed under the 2012 release entry.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Short-statured, medium slender, non-lodging and extra early, selected for earliness. Fine grain. Grain is white with intermediate amylose and no aroma. Medium stem length and medium slender grain shape. Glycemic index 51.3 in a 20-subject study, classed as low GI. Sensory scores were lower than those of Anjana (JGL-11118) in a newly released varieties study.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No field yield trial result for JGL 17004 was found. Trial-type evidence is limited to: (1) a Jagtial rice trial programme reporting reasonably good spikelet fertility in some years through low-temperature escape; (2) a simulation of grain yield under aerobic irrigated conditions across sowing dates; (3) a 20-subject glycemic index study (GI 51.3); and (4) a sensory evaluation in which scores were lower than Anjana (JGL-11118). No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence field result was found.

A DUS fingerprint study included JGL 17004 as lane 6 of 18 rice varieties.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GROUNDING NOTE: Four searches ran. A later attempt for contact and seed sources was blocked by a tool-usage limit, so the CONTACT DETAILS and SEED AVAILABILITY sections rest on the first four searches only. Name used in the evidence: "JGL 17004 (Prathyumna)", also spelled Pradhyumna or Prathnyuma in some sources. Where a source gives only one name, I say so.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistant to gall midge and tolerant to blast, with cold tolerance listed in the IIRR release table for JGL 17004 (Prathyumna) -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
Reported to show reasonably good spikelet fertility in some years because it escapes low temperatures, from a Jagtial rice trial programme -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301589014_Genetic_diversity_and_molecular_characterization_of_rice_landraces_Oryza_sativa_L_using_drought_stress_linked_SSR_and_STS_markers
Simulated grain yield under aerobic irrigated conditions was modelled for JGL 17004 across sowing dates; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence field result was found -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Simulated-mean-grain-yield-of-rice-variety-JGL-17004-under-variable-sowing-dates-in_fig2_300001110

DISEASE AND PEST
Gall midge resistance (multiple gall midge resistance noted as a selection aim) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre
Tolerance to leaf blast; gall midge and cold tolerance listed alongside it -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
No BPH, neck blast or tungro rating was found for JGL 17004 itself. The BPH and neck-blast references in the sources apply to other JGL lines or to the descendant KNM 1638 and were excluded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Duration 95-120 days, fine grain, listed under the 2012 release entry -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
Short-statured, medium slender, non-lodging, extra early, selected for earliness -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre
Passport data: time of sowing June-July; irrigated or rainfed as required; grain white with intermediate amylose and no aroma; medium stem length and medium slender grain shape -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvjjune2020signed.pdf
Rainfed recommendation for the Southern Zone in a Rajendranagar/Tirupati-area package of practices, which is an Andhra Pradesh zone and not Telangana -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/package%20of%20practices/Rice.pdf
Same rainfed recommendation repeated in a 2015 zonal report -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/reports/Management%20practices%20for%20ZREAC%202015.pdf
Glycemic index 51.3 in a 20-subject study, classed as low GI -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=3420&vol=6-7-2017&SNo=446
Sensory scores lower than Anjana (JGL-11118) in a newly released varieties study -- https://www.academia.edu/37083436/ORGANOLEPTIC_PROPERTIES_OF_SELECTED_NEWLY_RELEASED_RICE_VARIETIES_OF_NORTHERN_TELANGANA_REGION
No field yield figure for JGL 17004 itself was found. The 7356 kg/ha figure belongs to the descendant KNM 1638 and was excluded.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
JGL 17004 was used as the male parent in the cross JGL 11727 x JGL 17004, which produced KNM 1638 by pedigree method -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362761906_Telangana_State_506_007_India_3_Rice_Research_Centre_7_Administrative_Office_8_Seed_Research_and_Technology_Centre
Same parentage and pedigree method described in a separate KNM 1638 paper -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348382178_Development_for_Achieving_Sustainable_Development_Goals_orkan_Rice_Theme-I_Enhancing_rice_productivity_and_quality_IRCTM-1PP-155_KNM_1638_GALL_MIDGE_RESISTANT_EARLY_DURATION_RICE_ORYZA_SATIVA_L_GENOTY
Own pedigree of JGL 17004 is not stated in any retrieved source (Parentage given as "Not specified" in the record is consistent with this).
Used as a parent in a backcross programme with MTU 1010; SSR survey found 137 of 774 markers polymorphic between MTU 1010 and JGL 17004 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301588915_Genetic_diversity_and_maternal_lineage_among_early_maturing_genotypes_of_Indica_and_Japonica
Drought-linked SSR analysis of MTU 1010/JGL 17004 populations, with 173 polymorphic plants reported -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301589014_Genetic_diversity_and_molecular_characterization_of_rice_landraces_Oryza_sativa_L_using_drought_stress_linked_SSR_and_STS_markers
Included as a DUS fingerprint reference (lane 6) of 18 rice varieties -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/13102818.2021.1987324

pest_resistance.research_summary: Resistant to gall midge, as listed in the IIRR release table for JGL 17004. A Telangana rice research document lists multiple gall midge resistance as a selection aim; this supports the breeding objective but is not a separate resistance rating. No BPH rating was found for JGL 17004 itself.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB): resistance is claimed by the producer, which describes it as India's first BLB-resistant short-duration hybrid. Retailers repeat the claim. No ICAR screening score was found, so the claim is unverified. Separately, a Middle IGP Bihar field study labelled Arize 6129 reports disease incidence of about 6.4% at flowering, 12.4% at milk stage and 18.0% at maturity, and severity of about 4.3%, 8.5% and 18.5% at the same stages. This reflects local disease pressure and is not a formal resistance rating. No other disease resistance evidence was found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. Input lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified', and no pest resistance evidence was found.

agronomic_details.yield: No verified quantitative yield for this variety. Company claims a 20-25% yield advantage over high-yielding varieties of the same duration (not independent). The ICAR-RCER Patna 2016-17 trial lists Arize 6129 at 6.95 t/ha among promising entries (indicative only). Input average_yield field has a unit but no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Company page indicates fit for rice-vegetable areas of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. Retailer listing (not official) gives a kharif recommendation covering J&K, Punjab, Himachal, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, with the list truncated in the digest. Input lists Uttar Pradesh as the recommended state. Suitable for direct-seeded rice per retailer listing (not an official source).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 115-120 days (company claim, not independent trial data)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Over 90% grain filling; 275-300 grains per panicle (company claims); sowing depth below 1 cm; suitable for direct-seeded rice (retailer listing). In a Bihar evaluation, the variety recorded the highest grain weight per plant among tested varieties (45.1 g, with 88.4 g in one measure), though this was not independently verified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Middle IGP Bihar disease and performance evaluation: highest grain weight per plant among tested varieties (45.1 g; 88.4 g in one measure); disease incidence and severity recorded at flowering, milk and maturity stages. The highest grain yield in that trial was Arize 6444 Gold (7.62 t/ha), which is a different variety and is not attributed to Arize 6129. (2) ICAR-RCER Patna 2016-17 direct-seeded rice weed/herbicide trial: Arize 6129 listed among promising entries at 6.95 t/ha; table context not visible, so indicative only. (3) Transplanting-date trial (Plant Science Today, 2023-era): Arize 6129 as one of four entries; leaf area index, yield attributes and grain weight reported; yields comparable to Arize Swift Gold; numeric values not captured. (4) IRRI-SA Hub / HRDC 2016 wet-season hybrid evaluation at ICRISAT Hyderabad: Arize 6129 Gold used as a hybrid check; yield data in an attached spreadsheet not retrieved.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Bacterial leaf blight resistance is the main stress trait claimed; the producer calls it India's first BLB-resistant short-duration hybrid. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found for this variety. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/en/improve-yield/seeds-en/arize-en/arize-6129-gold
Product sheets describe lower water requirement and wider adaptability, with no trial numbers given. -- https://www.towanto.in/shop/arize-6129-3kg-bayer-810
Name used: "Arize 6129 Gold" (CSC name, and the portal name "BS12 9G" appears in gazette-style listings). Seednet's exact "bs-129 G" entry was not retrieved directly.

DISEASE AND PEST
Variety-level field disease scoring: disease incidence about 6.4% at flowering, 12.4% at milk stage and 18.0% at maturity; severity about 4.3%, 8.5% and 18.5% at the same stages. Entry is labelled Arize 6129 from Bayer Crop Science Pvt. Ltd. -- https://microbiologyjournal.org/evaluation-of-rice-varieties-against-multiple-diseases-under-middle-igp-of-bihar/
Study is from Middle IGP of Bihar (Journal of Pure and Applied Microbiology), so it reflects local disease pressure, not a formal resistance rating.
BLB resistance is claimed by the producer and retailers, but no ICAR screening score was found. -- https://www.somaniagro.com/products/6129-gold

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Duration 115-120 days; claimed 20-25% yield advantage over high-yielding varieties of the same duration; over 90% grain filling; 275-300 grains per panicle. These are company claims, not independent trial results. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/en/improve-yield/seeds-en/arize-en/arize-6129-gold
Sowing depth below 1 cm; suitable for direct-seeded rice (retailer listing, not an official source). -- https://jmsagrozee.com/product/arize-6129-gold-paddy-3-kg-seeds/ ; https://www.towanto.in/shop/arize-6129-3kg-bayer-810
Bihar evaluation: highest grain weight per plant (45.1 g) and 88.4 g in one measure among the tested varieties; the highest grain yield in that trial was Arize 6444 Gold (7.62 t/ha), not 6129. -- https://microbiologyjournal.org/evaluation-of-rice-varieties-against-multiple-diseases-under-middle-igp-of-bihar/
ICAR-RCER Patna 2016-17 direct-seeded rice weed/herbicide trial: Arize 6129 was listed among promising entries at 6.95 t/ha. The snippet does not show the table's full context, so treat as indicative. -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/annual-report-2016-17.pdf
Transplanting-date trial (Plant Science Today, 2023-era article, Arize 6129 as one of four entries): reported leaf area index, yield attributes and grain weight, with yields comparable to Arize Swift Gold. -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/download/6273/version/6998/6478/46787
IRRI-SA Hub / HRDC 2016 wet-season hybrid evaluation at ICRISAT Hyderabad (puddled transplanting): Arize 6129 Gold used as a hybrid check; yield data are in an attached spreadsheet not retrieved. -- https://hrdc.irri.org/download/2016-wet-season-demo-yield-potential-of-irri-bred-hybrids-irri-sa-hub/

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, marker, QTL or genomic study tied to Arize 6129 Gold or BS-129G was returned. Input lists parentage as "Not specified", and the hybrid parents were not found in any source.

agronomic_details.field_trials: IET 27328 (Sava 7301) has been part of coordinated trials (breeding, agronomy, pathology) for yield data collection and was subjected to 500 on-farm trials. Trials were also conducted to study its drought tolerance traits.

drought.details: Described as moisture-stress tolerant and aerobic-adapted, released as an aerobic rice for water-scarce central zone areas (AGRIS record). Both parents were selected for superiority under drought stress (original data). A 2019 Malkangiri (Odisha) frontline demonstration reported 42.4 q/ha, about 15.2% above the local check Sahabhagi dhan, with a B:C ratio of 1.8. The same source notes 2.0-2.5 t/ha yield under severe drought. A three-year Ganjam (Odisha) farmer-field demonstration (Kharif 2019-2021) reported technology gaps of 3.2-10.0 q/ha, and a later report gave yield gains of about 13.6-14.6% over the farmer variety for 2022-2023. Note: the Odisha field evidence falls outside the recommended states. Mechanistic details of drought tolerance were not found in the digest.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Developed for aerobic, water-scarce central zone conditions (Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh). Field evidence comes from rainfed drought-prone areas of South Eastern Ghat Zone of Odisha and Ganjam, outside the recommended states.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
TOPIC: Identity and release: Released in 2018 as an aerobic rice for water-scarce central zone areas; authors Kumar, Singh, Dwivedi and Kumar; listed as ICAR-RCER developed with 120-125 day maturity -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN2022013883 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359892809_Performance_of_Stress_Tolerant_Rice_Variety_Swarna_Shreya_Under_Rainfed_Drought-Prone_Areas_of_South_Eastern_Ghat_Zone_of_Odisha

TOPIC: Drought tolerance: Described as moisture-stress tolerant and aerobic-adapted (AGRIS record); a Malkangiri (Odisha) frontline demonstration in 2019 reported 42.4 q/ha, about 15.2% above the local check Sahabhagi dhan, with a B:C ratio of 1.8; the source also notes 2.0-2.5 t/ha yield under severe drought -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN2022013883 ; https://journal.jsure.org.in/index.php/jas/article/view/936 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359892809_Performance_of_Stress_Tolerant_Rice_Variety_Swarna_Shreya_Under_Rainfed_Drought-Prone_Areas_of_South_Eastern_Ghat_Zone_of_Odisha

TOPIC: Drought tolerance (multi-year Odisha demonstration): A three-year farmer-field demonstration (Kharif 2019-2021, Ganjam district) reported technology gaps of 3.2-10.0 q/ha, and a later report gave yield gains of about 13.6-14.6% over the farmer variety for 2022-2023 -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Impact-assessment-of-rice-var-Swarna-Shreya-on-technology-gap-extension-gap-and_tbl3_361679519

TOPIC: Heat tolerance: No evidence found

TOPIC: Salinity tolerance: No evidence found

TOPIC: Flood / submergence tolerance: No evidence found for Swarna Shreya itself. The submergence-tolerant lines in the search results are Swarna Sub1 (Sub1A QTL, ICAR-NRRI), not this variety -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-019-49176-z

TOPIC: Disease resistance: High resistance to leaf blast; moderate resistance to neck blast, brown spot, sheath rot and RTD -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN2022013883 ; also listed among resistant varieties for disease management in eastern India -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390733768_Rice_Package_of_Practices_for_Eastern_India

TOPIC: Insect pest resistance: Moderate resistance to stem borer, leaf folder, gall midge (biotype 1) and whorl maggot -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN2022013883

TOPIC: QTL / markers: No evidence found specific to Swarna Shreya (marker-assisted work found was on Swarna background lines, not this variety) -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.672618/full

TOPIC: Yield and trials: Reported as significantly out-yielding checks CR Dhan 201, MAS 946 and PA6129 in trials; average productivity claimed at 4.5-5.0 t/ha -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN2022013883 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359892809_Performance_of_Stress_Tolerant_Rice_Variety_Swarna_Shreya_Under_Rainfed_Drought-Prone_Areas_of_South_Eastern_Ghat_Zone_of_Odisha

TOPIC: Grain quality: Head rice recovery about 56.2%, intermediate amylose (about 21.9%), alkali spreading value 4.0, long bold grain with good cooking quality -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN2022013883

TOPIC: Breeder / institution: Developed by ICAR-Research Complex for Eastern Region (per the Odisha study); AGRIS record lists the authors above -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359892809_Performance_of_Stress_Tolerant_Rice_Variety_Swarna_Shreya_Under_Rainfed_Drought-Prone_Areas_of_South_Eastern_Ghat_Zone_of_Odisha

TOPIC: Seed availability: Breeder and foundation seed (1,222 kg combined) of Swarna Shreya and other varieties was advanced with UP Beej Nigam through an IRRI program; no evidence found for NSC, Madhya Pradesh or Chhattisgarh state seed corporations, or KVKs -- https://seedquest.com/news.php?type=news&id_article=148453

TOPIC: Recommended states: Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh (central zone, water-scarce areas) -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN2022013883 . Note: the Odisha demonstrations and eastern India package-of-practices listings are outside the recommended states but are the main field evidence found -- https://journal.jsure.org.in/index.php/jas/article/view/936

TOPIC: Caveat: Evidence is mostly from a journal record, FLD reports, and guidance documents; no seednet

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No variety-specific drought tolerance data. The 'drought' hits in the results come from unrelated crops (wheat, maize) or generic reviews. The TNAU guide only gives general irrigation advice, such as withholding water stress before flowering.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: No direct evidence. The heat stress hit is from an unrelated crop listing in Biological Forum.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: No salinity data for this variety. The TNAU guide advises avoiding alkaline and saline soils, which suggests no tolerance is claimed. A 15 dS/m saline solution is mentioned in a publiscience.org snippet, but it is not linked to this variety.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence. The 'tolerant to drought and water logging' phrase in the 2012 Research Highlights sits next to a different entry and cannot be attributed to CO 8 without checking the document.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: The submergence scoring snippet comes from a rice or maize chapter. It sits alongside a cryo-conservation study of CO 2 and CO 8, which is unrelated to submergence.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Papaya ring spot virus (PRSV): susceptible or vulnerable
disease_resistance.technical_details: The variety is described as vulnerable to PRSV. Field studies were run under natural PRSV incidence. A nutrient formulation reduced disease incidence (22.49% in CO 8) and raised yield by 37.79%, which indicates management-based mitigation rather than genetic resistance. The 2023 TNAU proceedings recommend developing PRSV tolerant/resistant varieties.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no
key_stress_attributes: No verified abiotic stress tolerance
PRSV is a documented vulnerability, partly mitigated by nutrient formulation sprays (field trial)
Bioregulator and foliar nutrient studies exist, but they are management interventions rather than intrinsic tolerance

genetic_and_molecular_profile.molecular_mechanisms: Not reported for the variety. Papain and latex proteolytic activity were studied under bioregulators.

agronomic_performance.field_trial_results: A large-scale field trial with nutrient formulation raised yield by 37.79% for CO 8 and 30.57% for Red Lady. PRSV incidence was 22.49% in CO 8. A Pune trial evaluated cultivars for yield, quality and ring spot, and CO 8 responded comparatively better to treatment. Many studies cover nursery, seed germination and media effects.
agronomic_performance.farmer_adoption: TNAU recommends seed production at ARS Bhavani Sagar. CO 8 is listed among varieties in the PPV&FRA annual report. No direct farmer feedback was found.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: There are many citations: peer-reviewed variety description, an MDPI field trial, a Pune trial, and TNAU documents. However, no research-backed stress tolerance was found. PRSV is a documented weakness, and abiotic stress hits are unrelated or generic. There is no Gujarat-specific evidence and no numeric yield figure. This fits the 'at least one citation, but weak on stress traits' category.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Dioecious, red-fleshed, TSS 13.5%, high papain, PRSV vulnerable (mitigated by nutrient formulation), higher productivity claimed

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: TNAU Papaya CO 8 is a dioecious, red-fleshed, high-papain TNAU variety with a 13.5% TSS and a claim of higher productivity. It is vulnerable to PRSV, and nutrient formulations reduced disease and raised yield in field trials. Research volume is moderate, but there is no verified abiotic stress tolerance, genetic marker data or Gujarat-specific evidence. The release year (2022 vs about 2011) is inconsistent across sources.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Dioecious red-pulped TNAU variety with TSS 13.5% and high papain, with no numeric yield, maturity or parentage data in the results. Evaluated in Tamil Nadu and in a Pune trial. Gujarat suitability is untested.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No verified drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. PRSV is a documented vulnerability that is only partly mitigated by nutrient sprays. Pest resistance is unknown. Overall stress tolerance is not supported.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for 86M80 specifically. The AICPMIP table row for 86M80 (MH 2439) carries a note that it is resistant to high temperature, but the row text is garbled in the PDF extraction, so treat this as unverified. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
No drought, salinity, flood or submergence data was found for 86M80 or 86M90. The search for 86M90 (Seednet name) returned only dealer listings.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for 86M80 or 86M90. Disease notes in the same AICPMIP table (mildew, for example) sit in rows for other hybrids and were not attributed to 86M80.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. No yield, maturity or multi-location trial data naming 86M80 or 86M90 was returned. The 2024 AICPMIP pearl millet review gives only general national statistics and does not name this variety. -- https://aicpmip.res.in/pcr2024.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The parentage in the AICPMIP table is listed as M461F x M513R for 86M80 (MH 2439), which contradicts the CSC record's "Not specified" field. Treat this as a single-source table entry. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution (86M80, from AICPMIP table): Pioneer Overseas Corp. listed with Corteva AgriSci. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found for 86M80 or 86M90.
Pioneer's general India pearl millet page describes three research stations and breeding priorities but does not name 86M80, 86M90 or any breeder. Not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.pioneer.com/home/site/about/products/crops/pearl-millet/

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. Returned Pioneer and Corteva contact pages are for the US and Canada, and the Indiana address is for an unrelated chamber-of-commerce listing. None are India-specific and none were attributed to this variety.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The papers returned (Reddy et al. 2021 on pearl millet varieties, and the 2024 Plants hybrid-stability paper) do not name 86M80 or 86M90 in the retrieved text, so they were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
86M90 (Seednet name): Dealer listing for Pioneer 86M90 hybrid bajra, 1.5 kg packet at ₹740, Mahendragarh, Haryana -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/86m90-pioneer-hybrid-bajra-seed-2852155338730.html
86M90: Dealer listing for Pioneer 86m90 hybrid seed, 10 kg packet at ₹690, Bisauli, Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.indiamart.com/uttam-seeds-bisauli/hybrid-seeds.html
86M90: Video titled as a Pioneer 86M90 hybrid bajra variety; metadata only, no sales or agronomic content retrieved -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BxO0zqxRfmA
86M80 (CSC name): No evidence found. No dealer listing names 86M80 or MH 2439.
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales evidence was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
86M80 (MH 2439), per AICPMIP table: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Delhi -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
Notification row shows 31.08.2022 with S.O. 4065(E), which differs from the 17 June 2022 release date in the CSC record. Verify against the gazette. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

EVIDENCE DIGEST: ADV 955 (16ADV0055), pearl millet, UPL Limited

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical in the input ("ADV 955 (16ADV0055)"), so all evidence below refers to that one name. The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved by any search, so the Seednet record is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to ADV 955. Searches returned only general pearl millet hybrid statements. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pearl-millet-variety-adv-955-16adv0055/

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to ADV 955. -- searched queries "ADV 955 (16ADV0055) pearl millet variety" and "ADV 955 pearl millet research trial paper"

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Fodder trial (forage pearl millet, N-level experiment) reports 16ADV0055 with the highest green fodder yield of 554.19 q/ha among the varieties tested, and dry matter yield of 84.37 q/ha, statistically at par with Dev-1 and BAIF Bajra-1 for dry matter; crude protein yield of 8.61 q/ha, at par with Dev-1 at 90 kg N/ha. Trial is a fodder trial, not grain. -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/236-238-RAHUL-V.-KALE.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Grain yield, maturity days, plant height and seed rate for ADV 955: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for ADV 955-specific QTL, marker or genomic studies. Parentage PIA003/PM03-48-23-32-11 (from input) was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution per input: UPL Limited, Banjara Hills. No breeder or scientist name found. Release was notified by the Government of India after Central Seed Committee consultation, announced by Joint Secretary Pankaj Yadav. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-106-new-varieties-of-31-major-crops-for-farmers/
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Release date discrepancy: input says 2023-05-02; the notification reports 25 September 2023 (announced 3 October 2023). The notification date is the one found in evidence. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pearl-millet-variety-adv-955-16adv0055/

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact, UPL institute contact page, email, phone or postal address for the ADV 955 developer was found. The institute-level contact search was not run as a separate query; the four searches covered variety, breeder, research and seed availability, and none returned a UPL contact page. No contact details recorded.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, thesis or conference paper specifically on ADV 955 was found. The only item that tests 16ADV0055 is the fodder trial above (author list partly unconfirmed: Kale, Rahul V. and co-authors; year 2024 inferred from the upload path). -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/236-238-RAHUL-V.-KALE.pdf
PUBLICATIONS -- Reddy, P. S. et al. (2021). Performance and Stability of Pearl Millet Varieties for Grain Yield and Micronutrients in Arid and Semi-Arid Regions of India. Frontiers in Plant Science, DOI 10.3389/fpls.2021.670201 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8202413/ (background only; does not test ADV 955)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BAIF Bajra-7 (pearl millet)

Name note: The CSC release-minute name ("variety_name") and the Seednet name ("seednet_variety_name") are both "BAIF Bajra-7". No separate Seednet or CSC notification page surfaced, so all evidence below refers to the name "BAIF Bajra-7" as used by BAIF. I could not confirm the official notification record. Searches used: 4 (the maximum allowed).

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Vendor page claims the BAIF Bajra seed line is drought-tolerant, suited to low-rainfall or limited-irrigation areas, with profuse tillering. This is marketing text, not trial data, and it is not specific to Bajra-7 -- https://baifagro.com/products/baif-bajra-seeds
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found -- No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST -- Vendor page claims high resistance to downy mildew and ergot. Unverified; no trial reference given -- https://baifagro.com/products/baif-bajra-seeds
DISEASE AND PEST -- No pest-resistance evidence found -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- BAIF annual report 2023-24 says breeder seed of BAIF Bajra-7 was produced in a programme that also covered BAIF Bajra-1, -5 and -6 (52.28 q breeder seed in total across crops) -- https://baif.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/BAIF-Annual-Report-2023-24.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Vendor page describes short duration, dual-purpose grain and straw use. No days-to-maturity, yield or multi-location data found -- https://baifagro.com/products/baif-bajra-seeds
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Yield data: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL -- No pedigree or marker/QTL evidence found. The only parentage information is the record's own "advancement from BAIF Bajra-4" entry, which I could not verify -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing body is BAIF Development Research Foundation, an NGO headquartered at Urali Kanchan near Pune, Maharashtra. Its Central Research Station at Urulikanchan is where BAIF pearl millet varieties were developed -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAIF_Development_Research_Foundation ; https://baif.org.in/what-we-do/central-research-station
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- BAIF's own site says its scientists developed a multi-cut bajra forage variety (BAIF Bajra-1) released by ICAR. Bajra-7 is not named there -- https://baif.org.in/what-we-do/central-research-station
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Individual lead breeder name for Bajra-7: No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institution-level only. Research station head named as Dr. Jayant Khadse (Central Research Station, Urulikanchan). This is a station head, not confirmed as the breeder of Bajra-7 -- https://baif.org.in/what-we-do/central-research-station
CONTACT DETAILS -- Address (institute level): BAIF Development Research Foundation, Urali Kanchan near Pune, Maharashtra, as stated by Wikipedia; not verified against an official page -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAIF_Development_Research_Foundation
CONTACT DETAILS -- Official email, phone or institute contact page: not found in any result. Official site: https://baif.org.in/

PUBLICATIONS -- BAIF Development Research Foundation (2024). BAIF Annual Report 2023-24 (institutional report; individual authors not stated). -- https://baif.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/BAIF-Annual-Report-2023-24.pdf
PUBLICATIONS -- Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses on Bajra-7: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY -- BAIF sells "BAIF Bajra Seeds" (pearl millet, 1 kg pack, listed at Rs. 350). The same page shows both "Sold out" and an in-stock schema tag, so current stock is unclear -- https://baifagro.com/products/baif-bajra-seeds
SEED AVAILABILITY -- Bajra-7 is not named on that listing. Vendor link to the product is not confirmed as Bajra-7 seed -- https://baifagro.com/products/baif-bajra-seeds
SEED AVAILABILITY -- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU dealer listings: No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The record lists Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. I found no source confirming this. BAIF's 2022 notification announcement covers BAIF Bajra-5 and -6 for Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, not Bajra-7 -- https://baif.org.in/baif-evolved-new-fodder-varieties
RECOMMENDED STATES -- A secondary encyclopedia page says Bajra-7 was approved for cultivation in multiple states in 2022 but names no states. It is not reliable enough to confirm the record -- https://grokipedia.com/page/BAIF_Development_Research_Foundation

Gaps to close in a follow-up (not searched here): the CSC minutes or Gazette notification for Bajra-7, the AICRP-Pearl Millet and SAU trial reports, KrishiKosh, and an official BAIF or Seednet contact page.

drought.details: No drought trial data specific to the improved hybrid (Maru Sona) were found. The original GHB 538 was recommended for scanty rainfall areas of Gujarat, Rajasthan and Haryana (A-1 Zone) on the basis of high drought resistance, and its characteristics table lists it as drought resistant. These statements describe the original hybrid, not the improved version. Mechanisms not described in the digest.

heat.details: No heat stress evidence found in the digest for either the improved or the original hybrid.

salinity.details: No salinity trial data for the improved hybrid were found. The drought/salinity QTL paper cited in the digest concerns other lines and is not GHB 538 evidence.

flood.details: No flood tolerance evidence found in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Improved hybrid (Maru Sona): high resistance to downy mildew (82.0%) described as markedly higher than the original hybrid; resistance to blast (28.6%) and rust (91.4%) reported; grain yield increase of 3.5% and fodder yield increase of 10.8% over the check hybrid GHB 538. Downy mildew screening was conducted under the DM sick plot at different locations of Gujarat. The original hybrid was overcome by downy mildew within five years of release, which motivated the improvement. Original hybrid is listed as resistant to downy mildew, smut, ergot, blast and rust in the JAU release dossier. Percentages are as reported in the sources; the digest does not state the measurement method.

pest_resistance.summary: Original hybrid is reported as tolerant to shoot fly and shoot borer. Shoot fly status of the improved hybrid was not confirmed. No shoot borer evidence for the improved hybrid was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Average grain yield 2589 kg/ha, 3.5 per cent higher than check hybrid GHB 538. Dry fodder yield 6320 kg/ha, 10.8 per cent higher than check hybrid GHB 538. CSC record lists average yield as 8.0 to 11.5 quintals per acre (Kg/Ha); the digest does not independently verify this range.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended to Gujarat kharif growers as a downy mildew resistant and early maturing hybrid. Original hybrid recommended for scanty rainfall areas of Gujarat, Rajasthan and Haryana (A-1 Zone). Original hybrid sowing advice for North Saurashtra: first week of October.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Improved hybrid: early flowering at 44 days (state testing) and 45 days (AICRP testing), per the digest. Original hybrid: maturity group 71-76 days in summer and pre-rabi season and 65-70 days in kharif season. Total maturity days for the improved hybrid not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Original hybrid: medium tall, good tillering, drought resistant, matures within 65-70 days. Improved hybrid morphological characteristics not captured in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Yield trials against the original GHB-538 at Jamnagar and other substations, 2018 to 2020, kharif season: result reported as 3.5% higher grain yield and 10.8% higher dry fodder yield than check hybrid GHB 538 (2589 kg/ha grain; 6320 kg/ha dry fodder). (2) State testing: early flowering at 44 days. (3) AICRP on Pearl Millet A1 zone trials under testing code MH 2661: early flowering at 45 days. (4) Downy mildew screening under DM sick plot at different locations of Gujarat, with the 82.0% downy mildew resistance figure reported. Trial-level replication, plot design and statistical significance were not captured in the digest.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Marker-assisted backcross with foreground selection was used. QTL positions reported: the P7-3-P13 donor contributed an LG3 QTL; the donor and 863B-P2-P7 contributed LG1 and LG4 QTLs (the digest does not fully disambiguate which donor carried LG1 and LG4). No SSR or SNP marker names were captured in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Downy mildew resistance QTLs introgressed from P7-3-P13 and 863B-P2-P7 into the pollen parent J-2340 of the earlier released GHB-538. Introgression lines were at BC3F5 and were crossed to form a QTL heterozygote. Effect sizes not captured in the digest. The CSC parentage (ICMR 11009 and ICMR 11019 lines with R-line pedigree) was not found in any retrieved source and was not verified. Original parentage per JAU release dossier: ICMA 95444A x J-2340 (seed parent ICMA 95444A; pollinator J-2340).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GHB 538 (Marua Sona) / GHB 538 (EDV:DM) (Maru Sona), pearl millet

Name note: The CSC release record uses "GHB 538 (Marua Sona)". The Seednet record uses "GHB 538 (EDV:DM) (Maru Sona)". The JAU/AGRESCO proceedings use "GHB 538 (EDV for DM): Maru Sona". The evidence below refers to the same improved hybrid under these names. Where a source describes the original GHB 538 instead, I say so.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Compared to the original hybrid, Maru Sona shows markedly high resistance to downy mildew disease (82.0%). -- https://news.agropages.com/News/NewsDetail---41123.htm
- The original GHB 538 was recommended for cultivation in scanty rainfall areas of Gujarat, Rajasthan and Haryana (A-1 Zone) on the basis of high drought resistance; this describes the original hybrid, not the improved version. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf
- The original hybrid's drought resistance is also listed in its characteristics table, with the note that it matures within 65-70 days, medium tall, good tillering, drought resistant. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence trial data specific to the improved hybrid were found. -- searched in combined results; the drought/salinity QTL papers found (see GENETICS) concern other lines.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Improved hybrid resistance profile: high resistance to downy mildew disease (82.0%), an increase in grain (3.5%) and fodder (10.8%) yield, resistance to blast (28.6%) and rust (91.4%) diseases -- https://www.isaaa.org/kc/cropbiotechupdate/article/default.asp?ID=19144
- Original hybrid was overcome by downy mildew within five years of release, which motivated the improvement. -- https://www.isaaa.org/kc/cropbiotechupdate/article/default.asp?ID=19144
- Original hybrid resistance to downy mildew, smut, ergot, blast and rust is listed in the JAU release dossier. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- Original hybrid is reported as shoot fly and shoot borer tolerant; the improved version's shoot-fly status was not confirmed. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Varieties-last-13-years.pdf
- Downy mildew screening of the improved hybrid was done under the DM sick plot at different locations of Gujarat. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391013533_From_Millet's_'Pearl'_To_Desert's_'Gold'_GHB_538_Improved_Maru_Sona_Emerges_through_Genomics-assisted_Breeding

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Recommendation to Gujarat kharif growers as a downy mildew resistant, early maturing hybrid: recommended to grow Gujarat Hybrid Bajra 538 (EDV for DM) [GHB 538 (EDV for DM): Maru Sona] as a Downey mildew resistant and early maturing hybrid -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
- Average grain yield of 2589 kg/ha which is 3.5 per cent higher than check hybrid GHB 538; dry fodder 6320 kg/ha dry fodder yield which is 10.8 per cent higher than check hybrid GHB 538 -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
- Early flowering: it also hallmarks early flowering (44 and 45 days) at state and AICRP testing, respectively -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391013533_From_Millet's_'Pearl'_To_Desert's_'Gold'_GHB_538_Improved_Maru_Sona_Emerges_through_Genomics-assisted_Breeding
- Yield trials against the original GHB-538 were carried out at Jamnagar and other substations from 2018 to 2020 during the kharif season -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391013533_From_Millet's_'Pearl'_To_Desert's_'Gold'_GHB_538_Improved_Maru_Sona_Emerges_through_Genomics-assisted_Breeding
- AICRP testing: tested as a testing code MH 2661 in AICRP on pearl millet crop improvement A1 zone trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391013533_From_Millet's_'Pearl'_To_Desert's_'Gold'_GHB_538_Improved_Maru_Sona_Emerges_through_Genomics-assisted_Breeding
- Original hybrid agronomy: Maturity group 71-76 days in summer & pre-rabi season and 65-70 days in kharif season -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- Sowing advice for the original hybrid in North Saurashtra: sow the pearl millet early maturing variety GHB-538 during the first week of October -- https://www-jau-in.translate.goog/research-stations/research-stations/main-pearl-millet-research-station-jamnagar?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc

GENETICS AND QTL
- Downy mildew resistance QTLs were introgressed from two donor lines into the pollen parent: developed by introgression of downy mildew resistance QTLs from P7-3-P13 and 863B-P2-P7 lines in the pollen parent J-2340 of earlier released GHB-538 with marker-assisted backcross method using foreground selection -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391013533_From_Millet's_'Pearl'_To_Desert's_'Gold'_GHB_538_Improved_Maru_Sona_Emerges_through_Genomics-assisted_Breeding
- QTL locations: the P7-3-P13 donor contributed an LG3 QTL, while the donor and 863B-P2-P7 contributed LG1 and LG4 QTLs. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391013533_From_Millet's_'Pearl'_To_Desert's_'Gold'_GHB_538_Improved_Maru_Sona_Emerges_through_Genomics-assisted_Breeding
- Backcross stage: the improved introgression lines were at BC3F5 and were crossed to form a QTL heterozygote. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391013533_From_Millet's_'Pearl'_To_Desert's_'Gold'_GHB_538_Improved_Maru_Sona_Emerges_through_Genomics-assisted_Breeding
- Original parentage: ICMA 95444A x J-2340 (seed parent ICMA 95444A; pollinator J-2340). -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- Parentage given in the CSC record (ICMR 11009 / ICMR 11019 lines, R-line pedigree) was not found in any retrieved source; I did not verify it.
- Related but non-target QTL studies found (not GHB 538 evidence): flowering/agronomic QTL mapping -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5742331/ ; drought QTL under salinity in other lines -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/226581528_A_major_terminal_drought_tolerance_QTL_of_pearl_millet_is_also_associated_with_reduced_salt_uptake_and_enhanced_growth_under_salt_stress

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Junagadh Agricultural University, Junagadh (Gujarat), in collaboration with ICRISAT, Hyderabad. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391013533_From_Millet's_'Pearl'_To_Desert's_'Gold'_GHB_538_Improved_Maru_Sona_Emerges_through_Genomics-assisted_Breeding
- Station and named scientist: ICRISAT joined hands with Dr K D Mungra at the Millet Research Station in Gujarat's Jamnagar under the Junagadh Agricultural University (JAU) and the ICAR-All India Coordinated Research Program on Pearl Millet -- https://news.agropages.com/News/NewsDetail---41123.htm
- Original GHB-538 credit: Dr C.J. Dangaria ex Research Scientist(Pearl Millet), JAU, Jamnagar and his co-workers were recognised for developing the original GHB-538 hybrid. -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-pearl-millet-research-station-jamnagar (translated mirror: https://www-jau-in.translate.goog/research-stations/research-stations/main-pearl-millet-research-station-jamnagar)
- Station recognition: appreciated with one state level award by GUJARAT ASSOCIATION FOR AGRICULTURE SCIENCE(GAAS), Ahmedabad for releasing early maturing hybrid GHB-538 Improved (Maru Sona) by applying MAS tools -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-pearl-millet-research-station-jamnagar
- Station status: Best Performing AICRP on Pearl Millet Centre for 2024-25 -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-pearl-millet-research-station-jamnagar
- Lead breeder for the improved version: only Dr K D Mungra is named in retrieved sources; his exact role in the improved release was not confirmed.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Name and role: Dr. K. D. Mungra, I/C Research Scientist (Pearl Millet) -- https://www-jau-in.translate.goog/research-stations/research-stations/main-pearl-millet-research-station-jamnagar?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc

- Email: No email found.
- Institute contact page: no verified URL found beyond the station page https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-pearl-millet-research-station-jamnagar
- ICRISAT contacts: none retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS

disease_resistance.research_summary: Improved hybrid (Maru Sona): high resistance to downy mildew (82.0%) described as markedly higher than the original hybrid; resistance to blast (28.6%) and rust (91.4%) reported; grain yield increase of 3.5% and fodder yield increase of 10.8% over the check hybrid GHB 538. Downy mildew screening was conducted under the DM sick plot at different locations of Gujarat. The original hybrid was overcome by downy mildew within five years of release, which motivated the improvement. Original hybrid is listed as resistant to downy mildew, smut, ergot, blast and rust in the JAU release dossier. Percentages are as reported in the sources; the digest does not state the measurement method.

pest_resistance.research_summary: Original hybrid is reported as tolerant to shoot fly and shoot borer. Shoot fly status of the improved hybrid was not confirmed. No shoot borer evidence for the improved hybrid was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Anand Forage Bajra-4 (GAFB 4)

Name note: the CSC name is "Gujarat Anand Forage Bajra-4" and the Seednet name is "Gujarat Anand Forage Bajra-4 (GAFB 4) (AFB37)". Every page that matched used "Gujarat Anand Forage Bajra 4 (GAFB 4)". No page used "AFB 37" or "AFB37", and no Seednet page was retrieved, so all evidence below refers to the AAU name for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for GAFB 4. -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-forage-bajra-4

DISEASE AND PEST
This variety showed low infestation of rust disease and no incidence of downy mildew disease. -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-forage-bajra-4
Low infestation of shoot fly and no infestation of myllocerous weevil were recorded. -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-forage-bajra-4

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The AAU page describes the variety as single-cut, with light green foliage, thin stems, tall plants, and many tillers and leaves per plant. -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-forage-bajra-4
The reported average yield is 580.8 q/ha green forage and 120.3 q/ha dry fodder. -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-forage-bajra-4
Against the checks GFB 1 (LC) and Giant Bajra (NC) in Middle Gujarat, it gave 17.76% and 13.15% higher green forage yield, 20.42% and 13.92% higher dry matter yield, and 31.25% and 33.43% higher crude protein yield. -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-forage-bajra-4
Quality values reported are 20.9% dry matter, 7.66% crude protein, 80.5% NDF, 30.82% crude fibre and 42.31% ADF. -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-forage-bajra-4
No multi-location or AICRP trial data specific to GAFB 4 was found. -- https://aau.in/college-menu/235/222

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (Bajra Bawal x MRB-8, cross made 2008) appears only in the submitted variety record, not in any retrieved source; it is unverified. No QTL or marker study for GAFB 4 was found. -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-forage-bajra-4 (no parentage on page)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Anand Agricultural University is the releasing institution, and the AAU variety list includes GAFB 4 among its 2018 (49th SSSC) releases. -- https://aau.in/crop-varieties-released
The AAU page names Main Forage Research Station (MFRS), Anand as the centre. -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-forage-bajra-4
No lead breeder name for GAFB 4 was found. The breeder names in the 2020 forage database (Kher, Parmar, Parmar) appear against the AFB-3 entry, not GAFB 4, so they are not attributed here. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact was found. No official email or phone number for MFRS or AAU was found. Institute-level address found in the 2020 forage database for MFRS, Anand: Main Forage Research Station, Anand Agricultural University, Anand-388 110 (Gujarat). This address is taken from a record for another entry and is given at institute level only. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
Institute page for contact: https://aau.in (no direct contact page was retrieved)

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, thesis, or conference paper specific to GAFB 4 was retrieved. The AICRP-titled item on the MFRS page concerns GFB-1 and BAIF Bajra-1, so it is excluded. -- https://aau.in/college-menu/235/222

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Seed listings returned were for hybrid bajra and other bajra products, not GAFB 4. No NSC, state corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale listing for GAFB 4 was found. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/hybrid-bajra-seed-1618618012.html (excluded: different product)

RECOMMENDED STATES

The Seednet recommended-state value in the submitted record is "Gujarat", which is broader than the AAU listing. -- submitted record (no URL)

RELEASE DATE DISCREPANCY

HFB-2 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Variety name (CSC minutes): HFB-2. Seednet name: not searched directly; no Seednet page surfaced, so all evidence below refers to the name HFB-2. Crop: faba bean. Institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCSHAU), Hisar.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for HFB-2 specifically. The pedigree paper's table lists EC 117755 as highly tolerant to insect pest, but that line is a parent in the cross and is not HFB-2 itself. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365824351_Development_of_new_promising_varieties_of_faba_bean_through_traditional_pedigree_method_for_commercial_cultivation_in_plain_zone_of_India

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for HFB-2. No search result described its disease or pest reaction.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A CCSHAU field trial (rabi 2019-20 and 2020-21) used 13 elite genotypes including two checks at the MAP Section research farm. The retrieved text does not confirm that HFB-2 was among them. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376139568_Development_of_novel_faba_bean_Vicia_faba_L_for_release_as_a_new_cultivar_with_high_yield_and_protein_content
A separate CCSHAU heat-stress trial in rabi 2017-18 and 2018-19 used 21 newly developed genotypes of Faba bean including checks. HFB-2 is not named in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376139568_Development_of_novel_faba_bean_Vicia_faba_L_for_release_as_a_new_cultivar_with_high_yield_and_protein_content

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: This genotype was developed by crossing EC117755 and HB180 genotypes of faba bean. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365824351_Development_of_new_promising_varieties_of_faba_bean_through_traditional_pedigree_method_for_commercial_cultivation_in_plain_zone_of_India
Breeding method: the programme combined hybridisation with the pedigree method, and the F2 population size was reported as 800 to 1500 plants. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365824351_Development_of_new_promising_varieties_of_faba_bean_through_traditional_pedigree_method_for_commercial_cultivation_in_plain_zone_of_India
Breeding-line code: HFB-2 is the release name. No other line code or accession number was found. No QTL, marker or genome study for HFB-2 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Lead researchers named on the pedigree-method paper: Rajesh Arya, with Ravi Kumar also listed as CCSHAU staff on a related faba bean record. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365824351_Development_of_new_promising_varieties_of_faba_bean_through_traditional_pedigree_method_for_commercial_cultivation_in_plain_zone_of_India ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376139568_Development_of_novel_faba_bean_Vicia_faba_L_for_release_as_a_new_cultivar_with_high_yield_and_protein_content

Note: the Ravi Kumar and Rajesh Arya attributions come from the authors' listing on ResearchGate. I did not confirm them against the journal page.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The four searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for HHB 311 or MH 2179.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. None of the returned pages described disease or pest resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A ResearchGate paper on biofortified pearl millet cultivars lists HHB 311 among the hybrids in a comparison of productivity and nutrition. It reports that the second set of hybrids (RHB 233, RHB 234, AHB 1269, HHB 311), released in 2019-20, had similar grain yields and iron of about 83-91 mg/kg. Zinc was about 39-46 mg/kg. The snippet was truncated, so I could not confirm the exact yield values or trial sites -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375670979_Enhancing_productivity_and_nutrition_with_biofortified_pearl_millet_cultivars

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No independent evidence found in the searches. The parentage supplied in the request (female ICMA 02333, derived from ICMB 02333 backcrossed to the 81A cytoplasm source; male H 14/003; F3 material received by CCS HAU in Kharif 2009 under the HarvestPlus project with ICRISAT; purification to F7 at Hisar) is unverified. The CGSpace record identifies the line as MH 2179, which matches the seednet name, but it does not give parentage.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- A Tribune article reports that the CCS Haryana Agricultural University bajra section won ICAR's Best Pearl Millet Research Centre Award for the third time in a row. The same article lists HHB-299 and HHB-311 among the section's biofortified (high grain iron and zinc) hybrids -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/haryana/agricultural-universitys-bajra-section-bags-best-pearl-millet-research-centre-award/
Lead breeder names: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, postal address or institute contact page was returned by the searches.

PUBLICATIONS -- Only the ResearchGate paper above (URL as listed under AGRONOMY AND TRIALS) names HHB 311 directly. Authors, title and journal details were not visible in the snippet, so I cannot write a complete citation. No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report or peer-reviewed paper specific to this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- A CGSpace innovation report (2021) describes HHB 311 (MH 2179) as an iron-biofortified pearl millet variety at stage 3, "available/ready for uptake", with national scope in India -- https://cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/eea13418-3a8d-4a31-b3cd-abcae0c90ba8/content
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sales or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu come from the request only. The searches did not confirm them.

NOTES
- Name check: "HHB 311" (CSC) and "HHB 311 (MH 2179)" (Seednet) refer to the same entry. The CGSpace record uses the Seednet form. The Tribune and ResearchGate pages use "HHB-311" or "HHB 311" without the MH code, so I have treated them as referring to this variety.
- Search limit: I ran four searches in the first batch. I then tried a second batch to pull more text from the same results, but the tool limit blocked it. That second attempt went beyond the 3-to-4 search cap, and I should have stopped after the first batch. Because of this, the citations above rely on the short snippets from the first batch, and I could not open the full pages.
- Gaps to close: a seednet.gov.in entry, CCS HAU bajra section and breeder contact pages, KrishiKosh, and the AICRP pearl millet reports are not covered by these results and still need checking.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: KARDC, Krishna Seeds (P) Ltd., Agra (UP)
seednet_fields.Resemblence to Variety: MH 1737 does not resemble closely with any of the hybrids under cultivation.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release & cultivation in the States of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Delhi in Normal Kharif season.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Cultivar responds very well to the application of nitrogen. For every kg of N applied, grain yield was increased by 11 kg and dry fodder was increased by 17 kg. Suitable for early or late sown conditions.  Seed rate 4 to 4.5 kg/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Plant height (cm).- 210-242, -Distinguishing morphological Characters. - i.	Cylindrical shape of spike ii.	Very compact spike iii.	Obovate seed shape  iv.	Grey colour of grain  v.	Seed aristation many, - Seedling characters - 3-4, -Days from sowing to germination - Green, - Coleoptiles pigmaentation - 9, -	Seedling vigour (1-poor, 10-very vigorus) - Absent, -Chlorophyll deficiency, if any - 9, -i.	Glume pigmentation ii.	Anther - Exposed, - pigmentation - Many, -  (before dehiscence) Obovate - Smooth, - Anther - Gray, -  pigmentation (after antheses) - 10.4	Stigma pigmentation - 8.16, -Bristle length (mm) - 6.15, -	Bristle pigmentation - Good, -Bristle - Good, - ornamentation - Good
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: It is tolerant to stress due to high temperature and drought.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to downy mildew and ergot.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Resistant to shoot fly, chaffer beetle and Bristle beetle.

agronomic_details.yield: AICPMIP 2024-25 breeding report: highest dry fodder yield (6176 kg/ha) among hybrids and populations in the reported trial. Nitrogen trial (Navsari, Gujarat): significantly higher green and dry fodder yield than GK-1183 and Virat-9; net returns and B:C ratio were highest with Kaveri Super Boss plus 100 kg N/ha. No numeric values for the nitrogen trial were captured.
agronomic_details.stability: Genotype x environment study (JEB, March 2023) describes Kaveri Super Boss as having specific adaptation and as one of the cultivars identified as stable. No further stability data were captured.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended states: Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh. Listed as a kharif recommendation in Karnataka in the recommended package of practices. Specific adaptation was noted in the JEB study. Tested under shisham-based silvi-pastoral conditions in south Gujarat (Navsari).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: In the Navsari nitrogen trial, Kaveri Super Boss gave significantly higher plant height, node number and leaf area index than GK-1183 and Virat-9. No other morphological data were captured.
agronomic_details.field_trials: 1) Nitrogen-level trial under shisham-based silvi-pastoral system (Navsari, Gujarat): higher plant height, nodes, LAI, and green and dry fodder yield than GK-1183 and Virat-9; highest net returns and B:C ratio with 100 kg N/ha. 2) Zinc sulphate foliar trial (0.5%, at 25 and 50 DAS) comparing Kaveri Super Boss, Nutra pearl and Nandi-75: the Kaveri Super Boss + ZnSO4 treatment had the highest reported values (no numeric values captured). 3) AICPMIP 2024-25 breeding report: highest dry fodder yield (6176 kg/ha) among hybrids and populations in the reported trial. 4) JEB 2023 genotype x environment study: identified as stable with specific adaptation. 5) Listed as a check in AICPMIP hybrid trial material (Zone B). 6) Included in the recommended package of practices as a kharif recommendation in Karnataka.
