search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Arpan (IPFD 19-3), field pea (Pisum sativum)

Name check: The release-minute name and the Seednet name both appear as "Arpan (IPFD 19-3)" in the sources I found. I did not retrieve a Seednet portal page, so the Seednet entry below is inferred from the notification lists, not confirmed on the portal.

Release date check: The supplied year_of_release is 2023-05-02. The sources show a notification on 25 September 2023, so the supplied date should be verified against the CSC/Gazette record.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Both varieties exhibit resistance to powdery mildew and ascochyta blight, with moderate resistance to rust, offering improved grain quality. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/148571
- Suitability for rainfed and irrigated conditions is stated, but no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence trial data specific to Arpan was found. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/148571 (and https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to powdery mildew and ascochyta blight, moderately resistant to rust, per the IIPR release note. -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/
- Resistant to powdery mildew and resistance to rust are listed in the ICAR annual report table for Arpan (IPFD 19-3). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf
- No pest (aphid, pod borer, etc.) resistance data specific to Arpan was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Grain yield: 17.67 q/ha seed yield in the ICAR table; the IIPR note cites a yield potential of 26 q/ha. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf ; https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/
- Maturity: about 122 days, with medium-bold seeds of about 18.55 g per 100 seeds. -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/
- Plant type: dwarf and leafy, creamy-white seeded. -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/
- Quality: protein 20–22%, Fe 91.5 ppm, Zn 50.5 ppm. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf
- Multi-location trial: the IIPR progress report (Rabi 2021-22) lists IPFD 19-3 with a mean of 1767 kg/ha over 15 entries in an AVT table; the zone label is not legible in the extract. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No peer-reviewed sowing-date or agronomy trial on Arpan specifically was found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker, or genomic study on Arpan (IPFD 19-3) was found. The parentage (IPFD 1-10 x IPFD 10-13) was supplied in the brief and not verified by a source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeders: A. K. Parihar (Pigeonpea and Field Pea Breeder) is listed as having developed Arpan (IPFD 19-3). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/team/ak_parihar/
- Co-author: G. P. Dixit (ICAR-IIPR) on the NEPZ release article. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/148571
- Institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur, UP. The developing-station detail is at institute level; the NEPZ release was recommended by the 90th CVRC. -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/
- Release listing: 106-variety national notification, Arpan under Eastern UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, Assam and West Bengal. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-106-new-varieties-of-31-major-crops-for-farmers/

CONTACT DETAILS
- A. K. Parihar, Pigeonpea and Field Pea Breeder, ICAR-IIPR. No email or phone found in the page extracts. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/team/ak_parihar/
- G. P. Dixit, ICAR-IIPR. Address as printed in the author line: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh 208 024. No email or phone found. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/148571
- Institute-level contact page on the IIPR site; no official email or phone was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Parihar, A. K., & Dixit, G. P. (2024). High-yielding and multiple stress resistance field pea varieties suitable for cultivation in north-eastern plains of India. Indian Farming, 74(2), 09–11. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/148571
- Scientific article title and DOI for the Indian Farming item were not found; the citation is taken from the journal's "How to Cite" block.
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper specifically on Arpan was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or private-dealer stock of Arpan. The IIPR-linked MULLaRP report shows national breeder-seed production for field pea (940.45 q against an indent of 782 q for 25 indented varieties), but that is not variety-specific. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- A 2025 KVK-linked item lists Arpan among varieties given to women farmers. This is a distribution event, not a sales channel. -- https://highlandpost.com/farming-knowledge-resilience-celebrated-on-national-women-farmers-day/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Assam and West Bengal. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-31-new-varieties-of-14-crops-for-uttar-pradesh-farmers/
- Recommended for the North Eastern Plain Zone (NEPZ) by the 90th CVRC. -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
The search budget ran out partway through, so this digest is thin. My first code block ran all four searches, and a second attempt to read full result text was blocked by the tool limit. I worked only from the short snippets returned, so most headings have no evidence.

Variety name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "HFP 1426", so one set of evidence applies to both.

Parentage field: the value "VBN 1 x VCP 10 - 001" contains corrupted characters. The intended parentage is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned nothing on drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance for HFP 1426.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The Frontiers snippet discusses rust screening at ICAR-IIPR Kanpur (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2019.00825/xml), but it does not mention HFP 1426 in the text I saw, so I cannot link it to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Partial. A heterosis and combining-ability study on field pea used HFP 1426 as a parent in crosses (RFPG 79 x HFP 1426 and IPF 14-13 x HFP 1426). The snippet notes these crosses involved tall parents, with plant height as a trait examined. Yield values for HFP 1426 were not visible. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/horticulturae9020256

GENETICS AND QTL -- Partial, indirect. The same heterosis/combining-ability study (above) treats HFP 1426 as a parent for yield and plant height traits. No QTL or marker study naming HFP 1426 was found. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/horticulturae9020256

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No breeder name, developing station, or CCS Haryana Agricultural University page for HFP 1426 appeared in the results. The Frontiers result mentions ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur, but only in connection with other genotypes, not as the developer of this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute-level email, phone, or address for HFP 1426 was returned. I did not search for a CCS HAU or ICAR-IIPR contact page specifically, so these are unverified.

PUBLICATIONS --
- Horticulturae study on heterosis and combining ability for yield and yield attributes in field pea using PCA and GGE biplots. Authors not visible in snippet (year likely 2023, from volume 9 of the journal, not confirmed). Horticulturae 9(2). -- https://doi.org/10.3390/horticulturae9020256
- Frontiers in Plant Science article, DOI 10.3389/fpls.2019.00825. Authors and title not visible in snippet; it covers rust screening of field pea genotypes and does not clearly involve HFP 1426. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2019.00825/xml

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed search returned only unrelated commercial cover-crop seed listings. No Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for HFP 1426 appeared.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for the states listed in the record (Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Assam). The search did not confirm any notification or recommendation. Release date (2023-05-02 in the record) and the CSC notification were also not confirmed.

Not yet searched: the CSC release minutes and Seednet portal entry, the CCS HAU variety-release page, and KrishiKosh theses. A follow-up search with a fresh budget should target these first.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: North West Plain Zone of India comprising of Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, part of J&K and western Uttar Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Resistant to lodging because of dwarfness. Resistant to shattering. Suitable for normal sown irrigated conditions during rabi season with recommended agronomic practices.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Dwarf variety with leaflets, green foliage, white flower, earlier in maturity than existing ones, medium bold slightly wrinkled and cylindrical cream coloured seeds.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to Powdery mildew, Ascochyta blight and Root rot and moderately resistant to Rust.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Pod damage and aphid population was found very less in HFP 1428 in comparison to checks.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Kg N: acre; 16kg P2O5/acre as basal dose P @ 35kg per acre.

disease_resistance.summary: Reported resistant to powdery mildew, Ascochyta blight and root rot, and moderately resistant to rust (MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report). The same resistance profile is reported in the 2024 release paper. The original CSC record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod damage and aphid population were very low compared with checks (2024 release paper). Listed with less incidence of pod borer and aphids in the national MULLaRP table. A ResearchGate figure entry on reaction to insect pests (mean of three years) exists, but its text was not retrieved, so no further detail is available. The original CSC record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Grain yield potential 25-26 q/ha (MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22). Average yield of 39 q/ha recorded in the original CSC variety data. Averaged over three years in All India Coordinated trials in the NWPZ, seed yield was 2603 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Entered the top-three yield group in 88.88% of pooled trials, against 44.4% for Pant P 74 and 22.2% for HFP 529. Performed well at both lower and normal seed rates. Multi-environment stability beyond these pooled results was not found in the searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: North Western Plain Zone of India: irrigated areas under normal sown rabi conditions with recommended agronomic practices. Resistant to lodging because of dwarfness and resistant to shattering (original CSC variety data).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Dwarf type (MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22). Resistant to lodging because of dwarfness and resistant to shattering (original CSC variety data). Protein content 22.47% and nitrogenase activity 72.81 nmoles C2H4/plant/h (2024 release paper).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) All India Coordinated trials in the NWPZ, three-year average: seed yield 2603 kg/ha, 23.59% above Pant P 74, 31.46% above HFP 529, 55.49% above KPMR 22 and 27.78% above the tall check HFP 9907B. (2) Pooled trials: top-three yield group in 88.88% of trials, versus 44.4% for Pant P 74 and 22.2% for HFP 529. (3) 2019-20 seed-rate trial at 80 and 100 kg/ha: performed well at both rates. (4) MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22: grain yield potential 25-26 q/ha, maturity 120-125 days. (5) Pod damage and aphid population very low compared with checks. (6) Insect-pest reaction figure (mean of three years) listed on ResearchGate; text not retrieved. (7) Summary yield data in Coordinated Varietal Trials is listed on ResearchGate as a title only; no data retrieved. A crop-level national average of about 913 kg/ha was discarded as not specific to this variety.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. QTL or marker studies: no evidence found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. A combining-ability study reported that HFP 1428 was a good general combiner for harvest index, and that HFP 529 and HFP 1428 were good general combiners for early maturity and flowering. The cross HFP 9426 x HFP 1428 showed significant positive specific combining ability for biological and seed yield.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. The variety was developed by the pedigree method of breeding. Parentage is HFP 529 x Pant P 25 (original CSC record and MULLaRP report).

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not found in searched sources. The ICAR-IIPR report (Rabi 2021-22) states that breeder seed production of field pea was 940.45 q against an indent of 782 q for 25 indented varieties, and lists HFP 1428 among field-pea entries, but does not confirm it was in that indent.
commercial_info.private_dealers: Not found in searched sources. The seed-availability search returned only unrelated commercial pea-seed retailers.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: HFP 1428 (fieldpea, Pisum sativum)

Name note: The CSC release minutes name and the Seednet portal name are both "HFP 1428". Sources also write it as "HFP-1428". The variety code A0311122 and the Seednet listing did not appear in any result, so every finding below refers to the HFP 1428 name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Reported resistant to powdery mildew, Ascochyta blight and root rot, and moderately resistant to rust. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Same resistance profile (powdery mildew, Ascochyta blight, root rot resistant; rust moderately resistant) reported in the 2024 release paper. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024.v7.i12.E.2182
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: no evidence found for this variety in the searched sources. Abiotic-stress wording in the 2024 paper is general to the crop, not specific to HFP 1428. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue12/PartE/7-12-33-809.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Pod damage and aphid population were very low compared with checks. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024.v7.i12.E.2182
Listed with less incidence of pod borer and aphids in the national MULLaRP table. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Reaction to diseases and insect pests has a ResearchGate figure entry (mean of three years), but the figure text itself was not retrieved. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Reaction-of-fieldpea-variety-HFP-1428-and-checks-against-insect-pests-Mean-of-three_tbl3_387086545

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Dwarf type, grain yield potential 25-26 q/ha, maturity 120-125 days. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Averaged over three years in All India Coordinated trials in the NWPZ, seed yield 2603 kg/ha. This was 23.59% above Pant P 74, 31.46% above HFP 529, 55.49% above KPMR 22 and 27.78% above the tall check HFP 9907B. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024.v7.i12.E.2182
Entered the top-three yield group in 88.88% of pooled trials, against 44.4% for Pant P 74 and 22.2% for HFP 529. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024.v7.i12.E.2182
Performed well at both lower and normal seed rates, with seed rates of 80 and 100 kg/ha tested in 2019-20. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue12/PartE/7-12-33-809.pdf
Field-pea variety with a crop-level yield note (not HFP 1428-specific): the national average is about 913 kg/ha. Discarded as not specific to this variety. -- (not used)
Protein content 22.47% and nitrogenase activity 72.81 nmoles C2H4/plant/h. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024.v7.i12.E.2182

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage HFP 529 x Pant P 25, release year 2020. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Developed by pedigree method of breeding. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024.v7.i12.E.2182
Combining-ability study: HFP 1428 was a good general combiner for harvest index, and HFP 529 and HFP 1428 were good general combiners for early maturity and flowering. The cross HFP 9426 x HFP 1428 showed significant positive specific combining ability for biological and seed yield. -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/view/1867
QTL or marker studies: no evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by the Pulses Section, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024.v7.i12.E.2182
Development team named in the university announcement: Dr. Rajesh Yadav, Dr. Ravika, Dr. Naresh Kumar, Dr. A.K. Chhabra, Dr. Ramdhan Jat, Dr. Tarun Verma and Dr. Promil Kapoor. -- http://www.newsnsahit.com/2020/12/22/haryana-agricultural-university-hisar-has-developed-disease-resistant-variety-of-pea-hfp-1428-for-grain/
Announcement quotes Director of Research Dr. S.K. Sehrawat. Notified by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Approval, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. -- http://www.newsnsahit.com/2020/12/22/haryana-agricultural-university-hisar-has-developed-disease-resistant-variety-of-pea-hfp-1428-for-grain/
Identified under the AICRP on MULLaRP. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024.v7.i12.E.2182

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for the breeders or for the CCS HAU Pulses Section appeared in the results. The Hisar institution is named in the sources above, but no institute contact details were retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
Devi, U., Kumawat, P., Yadav, R. K., Kumar, P., Choudhary, L., Kumar, S. and Kasniya, P. K. (2024). HFP-1428: A new high-yielding fieldpea variety released for India. International Journal of Research in Agronomy 7(12): 391-394. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024.v7.i12.E.2182 / DOI 10.33545/2618060X.2024.v7.i12e.2182
Authors not visible in result (2024?). Assessment of combining ability and gene actions for seed yield and quality traits in field pea [Pisum sativum L.]. Journal of Food Legumes (isprd). -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/view/1867
ICAR-IIPR (2022). Progress report, AICRP on MULLaRP, Rabi 2021-22 (annual report entry for HFP 1428). Report. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Related ResearchGate-listed items (titled "Protein content and nitrogenase activity in fieldpea variety HFP 1428" and "Summary yield data of fieldpea variety HFP 1428 in Coordinated Varietal Trials") were found only as titles, with no authors, journal or DOI. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Reaction-of-fieldpea-variety-HFP-1428-and-checks-against-insect-pests-Mean-of-three_tbl3_387086545
Theses on KrishiKosh: no evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned only unrelated commercial pea-seed retailers. A specific Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing for HFP 1428 was not retrieved.
ICAR-IIPR report (Rabi 2021-22) states that breeder seed production of field pea was 940.45 q against an indent of 782 q for 25 indented varieties. It lists HFP 1428 among field-pea entries but does not confirm it was in that indent. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
Irrigated areas of the North Western Plain Zone: Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, parts of J&K and western Uttar Pradesh, rabi season. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024.v7.i12.E.2182
Same zone and states in the national MULLaRP report. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Same states in the 2020 university press announcement. -- http://www.newsnsahit.com/2020/12/22/haryana-agricultural-university-hisar-has-developed-disease-resistant-variety-of-pea-hfp-1428-for-grain/

drought.details: HFP 529 is identified as a multi-stress tolerant variety with specific tolerance to drought and water stress conditions. Management practices for moisture stresses suggest that one irrigation at 60-70 days after sowing may be sufficient.

heat.details: While general research on breeding legume crops mentions the identification of major QTLs and potential candidate genes for heat stress tolerance, specific heat tolerance for HFP 529 itself is not detailed in the provided results. A new variety, HFP 529 x Pant P 31, is noted as heat tolerant, but this refers to the cross, not HFP 529 directly.

salinity.details: HFP 529 is reported to be fairly tolerant to salt conditions.

flood.details: HFP 529 is mentioned in the context of tolerance to waterlogging and multi-stress conditions, including floods.

disease_resistance.summary: HFP 529 is resistant to wilt, rust, powdery mildew, Ascochyta blight, Leaf Blight (LC), and Common Root Rot (CR).

pest_resistance.summary: HFP 529 is moderately resistant to Pod Borer (PB).

seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Almost comparable pod damage percentage to check variety Prakash.

disease_resistance.summary: Powdery mildew: resistant. Listed as resistant to powdery mildew in an ICAR-IIPR (MULLaRP) report and in a 2019 field-pea variety list. Rust: multi-location trials (six locations, 2014-16) recorded mean rust scores for HFP-715, and the paper states that rust reaction varied by location and year. These scores are not presented as a tolerance rating, so rust resistance or tolerance is not confirmed. The rust tolerance row in the MULLaRP table is garbled in the retrieved text, so it cannot be attributed to HFP 715 with confidence.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence found for pest resistance in HFP 715.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 6.0-6.5 q/acre (recorded in the CSC data as 'q/acre Kg/Ha'). Digest table: 15-16 q/ha for HFP 715 (dwarf type). Manipur-based paper: yield potential of about 2 t/ha in the NEH region. These figures are not harmonised and differ in units and conditions. Heterosis study: HFP 715 was a good general combiner for seed yield-related traits, and the cross HFP 715 x GP02/1108 showed the highest heterobeltiosis for seed yield.
agronomic_details.stability: Rust reaction varied by location and year across six locations (2014-16), according to the Frontiers paper. No stability index or formal GxE statistic for HFP 715 was found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: North Hill Zone (Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand) per the Central and State release list. NEH region (Assam, Manipur, Mizoram, Meghalaya, Tripura, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim) per the CSC record and supported by one Manipur-based paper. Sub-tropical NEH conditions are referenced in the Bhuvaneswari publication.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Erect and dwarf type, so lodging is not a problem (CSC record and digest). Recommended dose of fertilizers is sufficient for good yield (CSC record). Morphological characteristics beyond habit: Unknown. Maturity conflict: the digest's agronomy table gives 115-120 days, and the 2019 rust trial table gives 72 days to 50% flowering and 136 days to maturity. These conflict with the CSC value of 200-210 days, which is retained in this profile.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location rust trial, six locations, 2014-16 (Frontiers in Plant Science, 2019): mean rust scores recorded for HFP-715, with reaction varying by location and year; scores not presented as a tolerance rating. Trial table also gives 72 days to 50% flowering and 136 days to maturity. (2) Heterosis and combining ability study (Horticulturae, 2023): HFP 715 was a good general combiner for days to maturity, plant height, 100-seed weight, pods per plant and harvest index; the cross HFP 715 x GP02/1108 gave the highest heterobeltiosis for seed yield. No other trial results for HFP 715 were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: HFP 715 (fieldpea, Pisum sativum)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "HFP 715", so one name was searched. The Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) did not come up in any result, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Powdery mildew resistance is listed for HFP 715 in an ICAR-IIPR (MULLaRP) report, and a 2019 field-pea list also records it as resistant to powdery mildew. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf ; https://www.dpd.gov.in/vi)%20Fieldpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no variety-specific data for these stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rust: Multi-location trials (six locations, 2014-16) recorded mean rust scores for HFP-715 in a table, and the paper says rust reaction varied by location and year. The scores are not presented as a tolerance rating. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2019.00825/xml
- Rust tolerance is also mentioned in the MULLaRP table, but the row is garbled in the retrieved text, so I cannot confirm which variety it refers to. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity and yield: One table gives 115-120 days and 15-16 q/ha for HFP 715 (dwarf type). -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/vi)%20Fieldpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Conflicting maturity: In a 2019 rust trial table, HFP-715 had 72 days to 50% flowering and 136 days to maturity. This conflicts with the 115-120 day figure above, probably because the trial used different conditions or a different definition of maturity. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2019.00825/xml
- Combining ability: HFP 715 was a good general combiner for days to maturity, plant height, 100-seed weight, pods per plant and harvest index in a heterosis study. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/horticulturae9020256
- Trial results: No evidence found beyond the rust and heterosis trials above.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: DMR 50 × HFP 9948. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2019.00825/full
- Hybrid performance: The cross HFP 715 × GP02/1108 showed the highest heterobeltiosis for seed yield in the heterosis study. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/horticulturae9020256
- QTL or marker studies specific to HFP 715: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2019.00825/xml ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. The searches did not name a breeder for HFP 715. A LinkedIn profile that came up is about a different person and a different crop, so I have discarded it.
- Station: No evidence found beyond the university at Hisar.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute location: The university is located at Hisar in Haryana. -- https://hau.ac.in/storage/app/uploads/VG6dQAaSUuipIFlVp92JI4OWkBCKQz7JZcEuxqgg.pdf
- Official email, phone and postal address for the university or the breeding division: No evidence found in the retrieved results. Please check the university website (hau.ac.in) directly.
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Bhuvaneswari et al. (year not stated in retrieved text). Breeding for improved yield and powdery mildew, rust resistance in fieldpea (Pisum sativum L. ssp. arvense) adapted for sub-tropical condition of NEH region of India. Journal of Food Legumes (ISPRD) -- DOI 10.59797/jfl.v37.i4.222 ; https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/1348/907/2855
- Authors not retrieved (2019). Deciphering Genotype-by-Environment Interaction for Targeting Test Environments and Rust Resistant Genotypes in Field Pea (Pisum sativum L.). Frontiers in Plant Science 10 -- DOI 10.3389/fpls.2019.00825 ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2019.00825/full
- Authors not retrieved (year not stated in retrieved text). Estimation of Heterosis and the Combining Ability Effect for Yield and Its Attributes in Field Pea (Pisum sativum L.) Using PCA and GGE Biplots. Horticulturae 9(2) -- DOI 10.3390/horticulturae9020256
- ICAR-IIPR (2021-22). Progress report, MULLaRP, Rabi 2021-22. ICAR-IIPR -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP-specific report on HFP 715 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- A seed-chain list for fieldpea names HFP 715 among varieties; the list is undated and older than the other sources. -- https://www.isss-india.org/img/Bulletin31.pdf
- The ICAR-IIPR report says 25 fieldpea varieties were in the seed chain, but HFP 715 is not confirmed on that list. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealer listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The Central and State release list gives HFP 715 as a 2014 CCS HAU release for the North Hill Zone (J&K, HP, UK). -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/vi)%20Fieldpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The NEH recommendation (Assam, Manipur, Mizoram, Meghalaya, Tripura, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim) is supported by a Manipur-based paper, which lists HFP 715 among varieties recommended for the NEH region with yield potential of about 2 t/ha. -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/1348/907/2855 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/303916984_Evaluation_of_morphological_diversity_of_field_pea_Pisum_sativum_subsp_Arvense_L_germplasm_under_sub-tropical_climate_of_Manipur
- Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir: Covered by the North Hill Zone listing above.
- Uttarakhand, Assam, Manipur, Mizoram, Meghalaya, Tripura, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim: The NEH recommendation is supported by one source. The other states on the requested list are not confirmed by any retrieved source.
- Release year: 2014, per the CCS HAU notification list. -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1550223744.pdf

drought.details: No IPFD 11-5-specific drought evidence found. The water-deficit pilot study (doi 10.3390/ijpb15040080) used other accessions and cannot be attributed to IPFD 11-5.

heat.details: A GGE biplot study on heat-stressed field pea identified IPFD 11-5 as a superior genotype for producing viable seed under high-temperature conditions. It was also among the promising genotypes for germination under normal conditions. The level reflects relative superiority among the genotypes in that study; the digest does not report absolute seed-set or yield values, nor the mechanisms behind the response.

salinity.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Powdery mildew: described as resistant by IIPR (official variety profile). Rust and Ascochyta blight: No evidence found for IPFD 11-5 specifically. IIPR notes rust and powdery mildew as breeding targets in field pea generally, which is not variety-specific evidence.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod borer: described as moderately tolerant by IIPR (official variety profile). Aphid and leaf miner: No evidence found for IPFD 11-5 specifically.

agronomic_details.yield: IIPR official profile gives potential yield of 22-23 q/ha, equivalent to approximately 2200-2300 kg/ha. Record unit is Kg/Ha. In a West Bengal KVK trial (rabi 2021-22), IPFD 11-5 yielded 716.8 kg/ha, the lowest of four varieties tested.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources as a formal multi-environment stability analysis. Observed yields differ widely between the West Bengal KVK trial (716.8 kg/ha, lowest of four) and the IIPR potential yield (22-23 q/ha). The Sikkim NEH trial ranked it second to Vikas at one site.
agronomic_details.adaptation: IIPR lists the recommended area as Central Zone. The digest's Central Zone description (Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, parts of Rajasthan) refers to IPFD 2014-2, not IPFD 11-5. Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh recommendations for IPFD 11-5: no evidence found. The MULLaRP report says IPFD 11-5 is suited to short-duration cultivation in Eastern India, which conflicts with the record's state list. The record's adaptation ecology (Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh and South Rajasthan) is not confirmed by the digest. The record's state list is retained as the CSC ground truth, but the conflicts above should be resolved before use. Release year: IIPR lists 2016 (CVRC), versus the record's 2015-06-25.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Creamy white, round seed (IIPR official profile). Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) GGE biplot heat-stress study: IPFD 11-5 identified as superior for viable seed production under high-temperature conditions and among promising genotypes for germination under normal conditions. (2) West Bengal KVK trial, Purba Medinipur, rabi 2021-22, two sowing dates: 716.8 kg/ha, lowest of four varieties tested. (3) NEH organic rice-fallow trial, Sikkim mid-hills, 2015-16: one of eight varieties tested; the NEH annual report ranks it second to Vikas at one site. The Sikkim-specific table link is titled as a Pasighat, Arunachal performance figure (Vikas and HUDP 15); no IPFD 11-5 result was extracted from it. (4) MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report lists duration of 105-110 days and yield data for the variety. KrishiKosh theses and AICRP field-trial reports naming IPFD 11-5: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
IPFD 11-5 fieldpea -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: the CSC release name ("variety_name") and the Seednet name ("seednet_variety_name") are both "IPFD 11-5" in every source I found, so all evidence below refers to the same name. The Seednet portal itself did not appear in any search result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Heat stress: a GGE biplot study on heat-stressed field pea identified IPFD 11-5 as a superior genotype for producing viable seed under high-temperature conditions, and it was also among the promising genotypes for germination under normal conditions -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.635868/full
Drought: no IPFD 11-5-specific drought evidence found (the water-deficit pilot study at doi 10.3390/ijpb15040080 used other accessions) -- No evidence found
Salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
Powdery mildew: described as resistant -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
Pod borer: described as moderately tolerant -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
Rust, Ascochyta blight, aphid, leaf miner for IPFD 11-5 specifically: No evidence found (IIPR notes rust and powdery mildew are breeding targets in field pea generally -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Official profile: potential yield 22-23 q/ha, duration 105-110 days, creamy white round seed, recommended for Central Zone -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
Duration and yield in the MULLaRP report also list 105-110 days -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
West Bengal KVK trial, rabi 2021-22 (Purba Medinipur, two sowing dates): IPFD 11-5 gave 716.8 kg/ha, lowest of four varieties tested -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/6568/5336/9002
NEH organic rice-fallow trial, Sikkim mid-hills 2015-16: IPFD 11-5 was one of eight varieties tested; the NEH annual report ranks it second to Vikas at one site -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308680263_Annual_Report_2015-16_on_Promotion_of_Pulses_in_NEH_Region
Sikkim trial detail (Sikkim-specific table): https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Performance-of-Fieldpea-Vikas-left-and-HUDP-15-right-at-Pasighat-Arunachal_fig6_308680263

GENETICS AND QTL
Pedigree: the MULLaRP report gives the cross as DDR 16 x HUDP 7 in one entry and "CZ Dwarf type x DDR 16" in the same line, so the parentage is ambiguous; the record's "Not specified" should be replaced with this note -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
QTL/marker studies naming IPFD 11-5: No evidence found (the GWAS and Fusarium QTL papers found do not include it as a studied line -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6888555/)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Lead breeder: A.K. Parihar (Pigeonpea and Field pea breeder), credited with IPFD 11-5 among his varieties -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/team/ak_parihar/
Co-authors of the release note and of the Field Pea Breeding chapter: Girish Prasad Dixit, N.P. Singh; Ashok K. Parihar, Abhishek Bohra, Shailesh Tripathi -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-96-7838-9_8
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh -- https://icar.org.in/index.php/en/node/10517
Station/division: IIPR headquarters, Kanpur; the release is credited to the Institute (no division name found) -- https://www-icar--iipr-org-in.translate.goog/research-achievements/?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc
Release year discrepancy: IIPR lists 2016 (CVRC); the record says 2015-06-25 -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder email, phone, personal address: No evidence found
Institute address: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur 208 024, Uttar Pradesh, India -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Institute email, phone, contact page URL: No evidence found in the retrieved results (the team profile page is https://iipr.icar.gov.in/team/ak_parihar/)

PUBLICATIONS
Dixit GP, Parihar AK, Singh NP (2017). "Variety central fieldpea IPFD 11-5" notification of crop varieties and registration of germplasm. Indian Journal of Genetics 77(3):438-439 -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-96-7838-9_8 (cited there; the journal page itself was not retrieved)
Lamichaney A, Parihar AK, Hazra KK, Dixit GP, Katiyar PK, Singh D, Singh AK, Kumar N, Singh NP (2021). Untangling the Influence of Heat Stress on Crop Phenology, Seed Set, Seed Weight, and Germination in Field Pea (Pisum sativum L.). Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2021.635868
Authors not shown (2025). Effect of sowing dates on phenology and yield of field pea varieties including IPFD 11-5, Purba Medinipur, West Bengal. Indian Journal of Agronomy 70(2):245-248 -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/6568/5336/9002
Authors not shown (2016). Annual Report (2015-16) on Promotion of Pulses in NEH Region. ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308680263_Annual_Report_2015-16_on_Promotion_of_Pulses_in_NEH_Region
Authors not shown (2021-22). Project Coordinator's Report, MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22. ICAR-IIPR -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
KrishiKosh theses and AICRP field-trial reports naming IPFD 11-5: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
Seednet listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer for IPFD 11-5: No evidence found
General: 25 fieldpea varieties are reported as in the seed chain, without naming IPFD 11-5 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
General: IIPR maintains nucleus and breeder seed as per DAC indent -- https://www-icar--iipr-org-in.translate.goog/research-achievements/?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc

RECOMMENDED STATES
IIPR lists the recommended area as Central Zone -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
The Central Zone is described as including Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and parts of Rajasthan, but this text refers to IPFD 2014-2, not IPFD 11-5 -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh for IPFD 11-5: No evidence found
IIPR's MULLaRP report says IPFD 11-5 is suited to short-duration cultivation in Eastern India, which conflicts with the record's state list -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: IPFD 13-2 (Anant), Pea (Pisum sativum)

Name note: The CSC release name is "IPFD 13-2" and the Seednet name is "IPFD 13-2". No Seednet page for this variety was returned, so the evidence below refers to the IIPR name "IPFD 13-2 (Anant)". Where the IIPR page uses the same name, the evidence applies to both names.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Resistant to powdery mildew, downy mildew and rust, per the IIPR variety table -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The search returned no such data.

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Resistant to powdery mildew, downy mildew and rust disease, per the IIPR variety entry -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
- Listed among pea varieties resistant to powdery mildew, rust and pod borer in a handbook chapter -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383409346_pea_A_Handbook_of_Temperate_Vegetables
- Pea weevil (Bruchus pisorum) study classes IPFD 13-2 as moderately to highly susceptible to the insect, and the study also places it among moderately susceptible cultivars -- https://zenodo.org/records/23726411

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Average grain yield of 17-18 q/ha across locations in Uttar Pradesh -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
- Potential yield 20-22 q/ha, duration 115-125 days, recommended area Uttar Pradesh -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
- Medium-sized, round, smooth, white seed with yellow cotyledon -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
- Maize-paper note that IPFD 13-2 out-yielded best checks in preliminary station trials of a different crop context is not usable as pea evidence and is discarded.
- No multi-location pea trial report or AICRP annual report entry beyond the IIPR summary was found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources):
- No evidence found for parentage, pedigree, QTL, markers or genome resources specific to IPFD 13-2. The search returned only general pea genomics resources (GenoPea SNP array), which do not name this variety. Discarded as not variety-specific: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26590015/
- The breeding-line code "IPFD 13-2" is the designation itself; no breeding method was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur, Crop Improvement Division -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
- Lead breeder credited: A. K. Parihar (Pigeonpea and Field pea breeder, IIPR). His page lists IPFD 13-2 among eight field pea varieties he developed -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/Ak_Parihar.html
- Parihar's team page lists other field pea varieties but does not list IPFD 13-2 -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/team/ak_parihar/ (not used for attribution)
- Institution's variety record gives release year 2020 by SVRC (UP), not by CSC -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/

CONTACT DETAILS:
- Breeder: A. K. Parihar, Principal Investigator (Plant Breeding), AICRP on MULLaRP, IIPR Kanpur -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/Ak_Parihar.html
- Breeder email and phone: No evidence found in the retrieved page content.
- Institute postal address (Crop Improvement Division, ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur 208 024, Uttar Pradesh, India), stated in a different paper's affiliation line; institute-level only -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359278789_Maize_Hybrid_Karimnagar_Makka-1
- Institute website: https://iipr.icar.gov.in/ (institute-level contact page URL; the contact page itself was not retrieved)

PUBLICATIONS:
- Zenodo record on pea weevil incubation, hatchability and larval period across pea cultivars, including IPFD 13-2 (author list not captured in retrieved content). Year not captured. -- https://zenodo.org/records/23726411
- Handbook chapter "Pea (A Handbook of Temperate Vegetables)" mentioning IPFD 13-2 (Anant) as a resistant cultivar (authors and year not captured) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383409346_pea_A_Handbook_of_Temperate_Vegetables
- Advances in Production Technology of Garden Pea, listing IPFD 13-2 (Anant) as a resistant cultivar (authors and year not captured) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374113634_Advances_in_Production_Technology_of_Garden_Pea
- Dixit G.P., Parihar A.K., Bohra A. and Singh N.P. (2016). Achievements and prospects of grass pea improvement. Not verified as relating to IPFD 13-2 -- discarded for this variety.
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report specifically on IPFD 13-2 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- Breeder seed indent for IPFD 13-2 increased from 5.0 to 34.0 quintals over three years, per IIPR -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
- No evidence found for Seednet listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer availability.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Uttar Pradesh (released and notified for the whole state) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/

pest_resistance.research_summary: Listed as resistant to pod borer in a handbook chapter. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
IPFD 9-2
Crop: Pea (field pea)
Variety name and Seednet name are both "IPFD 9-2", so the evidence below refers to that name. I did not retrieve a seednet.gov.in page, so Seednet-specific fields (variety code A0311109, crop name, parentage) are unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistant to powdery mildew and tolerant to rust (IIPR varieties listing) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity.html
Resistant to powdery mildew and tolerant to rust (MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report table) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to IPFD 9-2. The Parihar et al. 2023 heat-stress paper and other IIPR heat/abiotic pages name no variety in the retrieved text, so they were excluded.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to powdery mildew (IIPR technology listing) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
Pea weevil (Bruchus pisorum) trial: IPFD 9-2 was slightly less resistant than Rachna, which was highly resistant; Malviya pea-15 was highly susceptible -- https://zenodo.org/records/23726411
Rust: tolerant (see Stress Tolerance above).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Potential yield 20-22 q/ha; duration 125-130 days; semidwarf, tendril, white-seeded (IIPR varieties page) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
Yield 15-16 q/ha and maturity 105-110 days (IIPR varieties listing and MULLaRP report table) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varity.html ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Conflict: duration 125-130 days (IIPR varieties page, IIPR crop-improvement page) vs 105-110 days (MULLaRP report, Krishak Jagat Hindi article). Yield 20-22 q/ha (IIPR variety page) vs 15-16 q/ha (IIPR varieties listing; Krishak Jagat). Record both and verify against the CSC/SVRC notification.
Seed weight: HSW 17.80 g (IIPR crop-improvement page) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/cimprovment/
Seed traits: round, smooth, white/creamish-white, medium size, yellow cotyledon -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
Seed-trait and yield trial data from IPFD 6-3 and IPFD 10-12 papers were excluded (other varieties).

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (not in Seednet record): IPFD 98-1 x HUDP 2018 (MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report table, listed as the pedigree column for IPFD 9-2) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
Powdery mildew resistance is reported for IPF 4-9 (name as written on the IIPR list, "IPF 04-9"), and it is described as tolerant to rust. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varity/
A separate central/state release table lists IPF 4-9 (2011, IIPR) as resistant to powdery mildew and moderately resistant to rust, with moderate resistance to pod borer and stem fly. Table columns are garbled in the extract, so treat the exact wording with caution. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/vi)%20Fieldpea%20Varieties.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for IPF 4-9 in these searches. Only the abiotic-stress hits found were for other varieties or generic pea pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
Powdery mildew resistance and rust tolerance (IIPR listing, IPF 04-9). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varity/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Oat-2 (CSC name) / JAWAHAR MATAR-2 (Seednet name)

Name note: Searches for "Jawahar Oat-2", "JO 2000-61" and oat-specific terms returned no page that names this oat variety. The Seednet name "JAWAHAR MATAR-2" is a field/garden pea variety (crop: PEAS). Pea findings below refer to the Seednet name in pea, not to the oat. Do not read them as oat evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Oat (Jawahar Oat-2): No evidence found. Searches returned only general oat drought/salt bibliometrics and unrelated oat genotype studies, none naming this variety. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11279746/ (discarded as not this variety)
Pea (JAWAHAR MATAR-2): No evidence found for abiotic stress tolerance (heat, drought, salinity, flood, submergence). A generic pea page notes field peas are sensitive to heat at flowering, which applies to pea in general, not this variety. -- https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/7425668 (generic, not this variety; discarded)

DISEASE AND PEST
Oat: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Kashi Sudha: The only IIVR page found describes it as a cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) with golden mosaic virus and Pseudocercospora cruenta tolerance, not as a field pea. -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/kashi-sudha
Kashi Udai (seednet name Kashi Udhay): Vegetable pea genotypes were screened for high-temperature tolerance, and Kashi Udai was among genotypes showing high-temperature tolerance and high pod yield under both stress and non-stress conditions. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304423824010677
No evidence found for drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in either name.

DISEASE AND PEST
Kashi Sudha: Golden mosaic virus and Pseudocercospora cruenta tolerant (cowpea record, not field pea). -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/kashi-sudha
Kashi Udai: No variety-specific disease rating found. The IIVR pea page lists general pea diseases (powdery mildew, rust, Fusarium wilt, downy mildew) without attributing resistance to Kashi Udai. -- https://icariivr.org.in/pea-2/
Kashi Udai: A consumer-oriented listing says it has good tolerance to diseases and pests, but gives no source or rating. -- https://www.indiainputs.com/pea-varieties-in-india/20027/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Kashi Udai (vegetable/garden pea): Early variety; IIVR page gives 8-10 pods per plant, pod length 9-10 cm, 8-9 bold seeds per pod, and about 48% shelling, with green pod yield of 100-110 q/ha. -- https://icariivr.org.in/pea-2/
Kashi Udai: One farmer-level account reports first flowering at 35-37 days after sowing, plant height 58-62 cm, and yields of 10-11 t/ha. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/success_stories/pdf/horti/2013/h_ss4_2013.pdf
Kashi Udai: In a 2006-07 IIVR sowing-date trial, the best seed yield was about 10.6 q/ha, obtained from late-October sowing. -- https://www.isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/697/519
Kashi Sudha: The only agronomic data found is cowpea-based, and it cannot be applied to field pea. -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/kashi-sudha

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for Kashi Sudha or Kashi Udai specifically. A genotype panel including Kashi Udai was listed as carrying genes for various economic traits, but no marker or QTL study was identified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373286659_Kashi_Purvi_A_newly_developed_high-yielding_early_variety_of_vegetable_pea_Pisum_sativum_var_hortense_L

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Kashi Sudha: Listed as an IIVR (ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research, Varanasi) variety, with a legume vegetable/cowpea classification. -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/iivr-varieties/by-crop?shs_term_node_tid_depth=63
Kashi Udai: Developed by ICAR-IIVR, Varanasi, with Kashi Nandini and Kashi Mukti described as early vegetable pea releases from that institute. -- https://www.isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/697/519
No individual breeder or scientist name was found for either variety. The 2006-07 IIVR sowing-date trial lists Rameshwar Singh and P.M. Singh as authors of the study, not as breeders.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact was found for either variety.
Institute-level: ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research, Varanasi. Institute website: https://icariivr.org.in/ and https://iivr.icar.gov.in/. No official email, phone or postal address was retrieved from these pages in this search. Verify on the institute's contact page before use.

PUBLICATIONS
Singh, R. & Singh, P.M. (year not captured). Effect of sowing dates and varieties on yield and quality of garden pea seed. Indian Journal of Vegetable Science (ISVS) -- https://www.isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/697/519
Pal et al. (year not captured). Assessing area, production and impact of vegetable varieties from ICAR-IIVR, Varanasi. Journal of the ISVS -- https://isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/395/326
Devi et al. (year not captured). Kashi Purvi: A newly developed high-yielding early variety of vegetable pea (Pisum sativum var. hortense L.). Journal publication -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373286659_Kashi_Purvi_A_newly_developed_high-yielding_early_variety_of_vegetable_pea_Pisum_sativum_var_hortense_L
Authors not captured (year not captured). Phenotypic, stability and adaptation analysis of vegetable pea genotypes for high-temperature stress tolerance. ScienceDirect -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304423824010677
No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP-VC annual report for either name was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Kashi Udai (pea): ICAR-IIVR signed a breeder-seed transfer MoU with Shriram Farm Solutions covering pea, among five vegetable crops. -- https://businessnewsforprofit.com/news/shriram-farm-solutions-inks-mou-with-icar-iivr-to-access-breeder-seeds-for-five-vegetable-crops/
Kashi Udai (pea): A Jalaun, UP trader lists "Natural Kashi Uday Green Pea Seed" at ₹90/kg, but the listing is a trade item and not verified seed. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/kashi-uday-green-pea-seed-25598767255.html
Kashi Udai (name mismatch): A Lucknow dealer lists "kashi Uday Pigeon Pea Seeds," which refers to a different crop and should not be used as evidence for pea seed. -- https://www.porwalhybridseeds.com/pea-seeds.html
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU listing was found.
Kashi Sudha: No seed source for field pea was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Kashi Sudha: The IIVR record lists Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Orissa, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, but this is a cowpea record. -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/iivr-varieties/by-crop?shs_term_node_tid_depth=63
Kashi Udai: The IIVR page gives Uttar Pradesh as the notified state, with notification in 2006 under SVRC-UP (S.O. 597(E), 25.04.2006). -- https://icariivr.org.in/pea-2/
Kashi Udai: Its suitability is described for the pea-wheat system in eastern Uttar Pradesh. -- https://www.isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/697/519

RECORD CONFLICTS TO RESOLVE
1. Crop: The record says fieldpea, but every Kashi Sudha source identifies it as cowpea. The pea evidence refers to Kashi Udai, which is a different variety.
2. Name: The seednet name Kashi Udhay appears as Kashi Udai in the sources. Spelling differences are likely but unconfirmed.
3. Release year: The record says 2008, but Kashi Udai is recorded as notified in 2006.
4. Institution, states, parentage: The record fields "Not specified" are supported by IIVR sources for Kashi Sudha and Kashi Udai.

disease_resistance.research_summary: Kashi Sudha: tolerance to golden mosaic virus and Pseudocercospora cruenta, recorded only on an IIVR cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) page. This is not a field pea record and cannot be applied to field pea. Kashi Udai: no variety-specific disease rating found. The IIVR pea page lists general pea diseases (powdery mildew, rust, Fusarium wilt, downy mildew) without attributing resistance to Kashi Udai. A consumer listing claims good tolerance to diseases and pests for Kashi Udai, but it gives no source or rating and is treated as unverified.

drought.details: None of the search results mention Pant Pea 517. General pea literature notes drought and terminal heat tolerance as breeding targets, and one thesis evaluated 13 pea genotypes for yield and drought tolerance under rainfed conditions. No variety-specific data was found.

heat.details: No variety-specific evidence was found. A review on heat stress tolerance in peas (Devi et al. 2023, Front. Plant Sci. 13:1108276) is cited in the search results but does not mention this variety.

salinity.details: No data on this variety. The results contain only general mentions of salt tolerance in other crops and in field pea.

flood.details: No variety-specific data. General sources state that pea is sensitive to waterlogging and that even one day of waterlogging causes damage, so well-drained soils are recommended.

drought.details: No search result reports drought tolerance for Pant Pea 509. General crop context only: the Krishi Sandesh garden pea production guide states that green peas are most sensitive to moisture stress at the flowering stage. The Directorate of Pulses Ready Reckoner advises timely sowing to avoid post-flowering drought and heat stress, which aggravate root rot. These statements describe the crop generally and do not establish this variety's response.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat data found. The Krishi Sandesh guide notes frost damage during flowering in pea. The Ready Reckoner links post-flowering heat stress to disease aggravation in pulses. Neither source tests Pant Pea 509.

salinity.details: No search result addresses salinity tolerance in Pant Pea 509 or in field pea. The PAU vegetable package notes that alkaline soils with high salt concentration are unsuitable for peas, which is general guidance and not variety evidence.

flood.details: No variety-specific flood data found. The Krishi Sandesh guide states that waterlogging in a pea field, even for one day, causes injury. This is crop-level context and does not evaluate Pant Pea 509. Relevant because the recommended states include eastern rice-belt areas with high rainfall and flooding risk.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease reaction data for Pant Pea 509 was found. General pulse disease context: the Ready Reckoner lists dry root rot and wilt as pulse diseases and recommends crop rotation and timely sowing. The NIPHM AESA IPM package for pea advises avoiding sowing adjacent to last season's stubble, controlling volunteer peas that harbour disease, and adopting the bower system. The Krishi Sandesh guide states high humidity favours pea disease incidence. None of these sources report resistance in Pant Pea 509.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest reaction data for Pant Pea 509 was found. The NIPHM AESA pea package provides general IPM guidance only.

agronomic_details.yield: Not specified in table. No yield data for Pant Pea 509 was found.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-environment stability data found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Assam (per the original variety data). The ICAR Rabi Agro-Advisory notes that field pea is generally sown from mid-October to mid-November in the plains, but it does not mention Pant Pea 509.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: No trial data for Pant Pea 509 was found. The ICAR Rabi Agro-Advisory names other Pant varieties (Pant Matar 155, Pant Matar 250) that are sown in the same window, but these are not evidence for Pant Pea 509.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No SSR, SNP, or QTL information for Pant Pea 509 was found in the search results. Parentage is not specified.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL data found for this variety.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No genes or pathways associated with Pant Pea 509 were identified. The PMC review on genomics-enabled breeding for biotic stresses in pea is general background and does not describe this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for Pant P 462 specifically. The one ICAR-IIPR report mentions a rust/powdery mildew breeding objective for field pea and aphid screening, but does not name this line as tolerant or resistant -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
General field pea background only (not this variety): heat stress at flowering reduces pod set and seed set -- https://s3.wp.wsu.edu/uploads/sites/2063/2013/12/FieldPeaProduction_NDExtension_a1166.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No variety-specific evidence for Pant P 462 was found. A DPD table lists "Powdery mildew resistant varieties" that include "Pant P -", but the entry is truncated, so it cannot be confirmed which Pant P line is meant -- http://dpd.gov.in/Pea.pdf
The ICAR-IIPR report says field pea breeding targets rust and powdery mildew, and that aphid screening was done at Ranchi, Pantnagar and Varanasi; Pant P 462 is not named as resistant -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
[Pant P 462] Multi-location AICRP-MULLaRP table, Rabi 2021-22, Field Pea (Tall) entry "Pant P 462" with four numeric columns (2265, 1641, 1674, 1860 kg/ha, probably by zone or location) and CV values 21.01 and 25.00. The column headings are not legible in the extracted text, so the numbers should be checked against the original PDF before use -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
[Pant P 462] Maturity, plant type and specific yield potential: no evidence found in the searches.
[Field pea, general] Sowing window 15 October to 15 November; seed rate 70-80 kg/ha for tall and 100 kg/ha for dwarf types -- http://dpd.gov.in/Pea.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
[Pant P 462] Parentage HFP 529 x Pant P 31 was supplied in the request and was not confirmed by any search result -- no URL.
No QTL, marker or genomic study naming Pant P 462 was found. A general field pea GWAS covering Indian accessions exists but does not include this line -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6888555/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUA&T), Pantnagar, Uttarakhand -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/
Department: Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Pantnagar. Faculty names listed there include Dr. J.P. Jaiswal (Head), Dr. R.K. Panwar, Dr. S.K. Verma, Dr. Anju Arora and others. This listing is an older page and does not show who bred Pant P 462 -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/index.html
No lead breeder for Pant P 462 was found in the searches. Dr. Panwar, Dr. Verma and Dr. Arora are named as breeders of Pant Urd 12, a different crop -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/26.07.2021_Issue-13_COA_Pantnagar_Newsletter.pdf
Station: the Crop Research Centre, Pantnagar is named as the source of Pant Pea varieties in one study, but not specifically for Pant P 462 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020.v9.i1.10470/field-pea-pisum-sativum-varieties-shelf-life-evaluation-and-product-development

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, Pantnagar, Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand 263145, India. Telephone: 05944–233349 / 233350. Email as shown: registrar[at]gbpuat[dot]ac[dot]in -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/
Directorate of Research: Dr. S.K. Verma, Director Research, Pantnagar 263145. Contacts +91-9411324848 (O), directorresearch@gbpuat.ac.in -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/index.html?id=9
Genetics and Plant Breeding Department (older page): Dr. J.P. Jaiswal, Head, +91-5944-233879, 233242 (O), +91-7579145670 (M), jpj[dot]gbpu[at]gmail[dot]com. Dr. R.K. Panwar, +91-9411159751. Dr. S.K. Verma, +91-9412141008, sk_pantvarsity[at]yahoo[dot]co[dot]in. Dr. Anju Arora, +91-9456768397, aroraanjudua[at]gmail[dot]com -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/index.html
Note: these contacts were retrieved from pages whose dates are not clear, so they should be verified before use. No breeder-specific contact for Pant P 462 was found.

PUBLICATIONS
No peer-reviewed paper, thesis or conference paper specific to Pant P 462 was found in the searches. The following were checked and do not cover this variety.
Vinay Kumar, Baudh B., Shiva N., Pratap J., Prasad S., Dharmendra K. (2025). Genetic Divergence, Variability and Association Analysis for Seed Yield and its Contributing Traits in Selected Germplasm of Field Pea (Pisum sativum L.). Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5413 (Pant P 462 not in the listed genotypes)
Goswami K., Shukla P. (2020). Field pea (Pisum sativum) varieties: Shelf life evaluation and product development. J Pharmacogn Phytochem 9(1):45-50 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020.v9.i1.10470/field-pea-pisum-sativum-varieties-shelf-life-evaluation-and-product-development (uses Pant Pea-13, 14, 25, 42, 74 only)
Das A., Parihar A.K., Saxena D. et al. (2019). Deciphering Genotype-by-Environment Interaction for Targeting Test Environments and Rust Resistant Genotypes in Field Pea. Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2019.00825/xml (rust screening; Pant P 462 not confirmed)
ICAR-IIPR, AICRP on MULLaRP (2022). Progress Report, Rabi 2021-22 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf (the only source that names Pant P 462 with trial data)

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for Pant P 462 from Seednet, a state seed corporation, KVK or dealer. The Seednet search returned only Australian Seednet products, which are unrelated. Checking seednet.gov.in and the GBPUA&T seed production unit is still needed -- no verified URL.
The ICAR-IIPR report records breeder seed production for field pea of 940.45 q against an indent of 782 q across 25 varieties, but it does not break this down by variety -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found for Pant P 462's recommended states. The request lists Jharkhand, Bihar, West Bengal, Assam, West Bengal (duplicated) and eastern Uttar Pradesh; this is unverified input. The DPD state table lists other varieties, such as Pant Pea-14 and Pant Pea-25 for Uttarakhand -- http://dpd.gov.in/Pea.pdf
Release/notification: no notification or CSC minute for Pant P 462 was found. The 2023 release date in the request is unverified.

NAME CHECK
Searches used both "Pant Pea 462 (Pant P 462)" and "Pant P 462". The only variety-specific evidence (the ICAR-IIPR table) uses "Pant P 462". No Seednet portal page under "Pant Pea 462" was found, so the Seednet name is unverified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shikhar (IPFD 19-1), field pea

Name note: The CSC release minutes and the Seednet portal both use "Shikhar (IPFD 19-1)". No separate Seednet-specific page turned up, so all evidence below refers to the same name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to powdery mildew and moderately resistant to rust; the release-notice wording is that it is "resistant to powdery mildew" and "moderately resistance to rust" -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/
- Resistant to powdery mildew and ascochyta blight, with moderate rust resistance, and described as suited to both irrigated and rainfed fields -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/148571
- Listed as suitable for rainfed and irrigated conditions, with moderate rust resistance and powdery mildew resistance -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf
- No Shikhar-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found. Heat-stress work on field pea (Lamichaney et al. 2021) used the parent line IPF 5-19 only as a check, so it does not establish Shikhar's heat tolerance -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.635868/full

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to powdery mildew, ascochyta blight, and moderately resistant to rust -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/
- No Shikhar-specific insect or pest data found. Pest and disease text found on the IPF 5-19 figure page (ResearchGate) concerns the parent region's general pest problems and is not variety-specific -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/High-yielding-field-pea-variety-AMAN-IPF-5-19_fig2_367362519

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Dwarf, semi-leafless plant type with creamish-white seed -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/
- Grain yield potential given as 27 q/ha in one IIPR notice, while the ICAR Annual Report 2023-24 gives 19.17 q/ha seed yield; the two figures are not reconciled in the sources -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/ ; https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf
- Maturity 120-125 days (IIPR notice) and 121 days (ICAR AR) -- same URLs
- Seed size medium bold, about 18.0 g per 100 seeds -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/
- Multi-location trial data for Shikhar not found beyond the notices above

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage IPF 5-19 x MDP 2 is taken from the supplied record; no independent source confirmed it
- No QTL, marker, or GWAS study on Shikhar found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur, for the North Eastern Plain Zone -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/148571
- Dr. A. K. Parihar (Pigeonpea and Field pea Breeder) lists IPFD 19-1 (Shikhar) among varieties developed -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/team/ak_parihar/
- Co-authors on the NEPZ paper: A. K. Parihar and G. P. Dixit, both at ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur 208 024 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/148571
- Dr. Amrit Lamichaney is credited with contributing to IPFD 19-1 and IPFD 19-3 development; he is now at Sikkim University -- https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-96-0506-4
- Release listed under the 90th CVRC identification; notification issued 25 September 2023 -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/ ; https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/fieldpea-variety-shikhar-ipfd-19-1/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. A. K. Parihar, Pigeonpea and Field pea Breeder, ICAR-IIPR -- no email or phone found -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/team/ak_parihar/
- Dr. Amrit Lamichaney, now Associate Professor, Department of Horticulture, Sikkim University, Gangtok -- no contact details found -- https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-96-0506-4
- Institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh 208 024 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/Pulses-as-a-condidate-crops.pdf
- Institute website: iipr.icar.gov.in -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Pulses_Research
- Institute email and phone not found in the searches; the official site contact page should be checked directly

PUBLICATIONS
- Parihar, A.K., Hazra, K.K., Lamichaney, A., Dixit, G.P., Singh, D., Singh, A.K., Singh, N.P. (2022). Characterizing plant trait(s) for improved heat tolerance in field pea (Pisum sativum L.) under subtropical climate. International Journal of Biometeorology, pp. 1-15. -- DOI not found; cited from https://iipr.icar.gov.in/team/ak_parihar/ (general field pea, not Shikhar-specific)
- Lamichaney, A., Parihar, A.K., Hazra, K.K., Dixit, G.P., Katiyar, P.K., Singh, D., Singh, A.K., Kumar, N., Singh, N.P. (2021). Untangling the Influence of Heat Stress on Crop Phenology, Seed Set, Seed Weight, and Germination in Field Pea (Pisum sativum L.). Frontiers in Plant Science. -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2021.635868 (uses IPF 5-19 as check; not Shikhar-specific)
- Das, A., Parihar, A.K., Saxena, D. (2019). Deciphering Genotype-by-Environment Interaction for Targeting Test Environments and Rust Resistant Genotypes in Field Pea (Pisum sativum L.). Frontiers in Plant Science. -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2019.00825 (rust screening of 250 genotypes under AICRP on MULLaRP; Shikhar not confirmed among them)
- Parihar, A.K., Dixit, G.P. (year not shown). High-yielding and multiple stress resistance field pea varieties suitable for cultivation in north-eastern plains of India. Indian Farming (ICAR). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/148571
- Parihar, A.K., Bohra, A., Lamichaney, A., Singh, S.N. et al. (ed. Hybrid Seed Production for Boosting Crop Yields, Springer, 2025). -- https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-96-0506-4 (book; not a Shikhar study)
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP annual report entry specific to Shikhar found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. Searches returned no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing for Shikhar (IPFD 19-1). The one "Shikhar" seed listing found was a hybrid bajra product, which is unrelated -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/hybrid-bajra-seed-shikhar-24416439588.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Bihar, Jharkhand, Assam, West Bengal, and central and eastern parts of Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/fieldpea-variety-shikhar-ipfd-19-1/
- Listed as an open pollinated variety in the 2023 notification for Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-31-new-varieties-of-14-crops-for-uttar-pradesh-farmers/
- Recommended for the North Eastern Plain Zone by the 90th CVRC -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/events/identified-new-varieties-of-urdbean-and-fieldpea/

disease_resistance.summary: TRCP 9 showed multiple resistance to powdery mildew, Ascochyta blight and root rot at all locations (PC Report MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22). The same report lists TRCP 9 as resistant to rust. Source wording is 'multiple resistance' without a numeric rating or severity scale.

pest_resistance.summary: TRCP 9 is listed as resistant to root knot nematode (PC Report MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22, table row '15. TRCP 9 ICAR Res. Complex Agartala'). Pod borer and stem fly: Not found in searched sources. The pest-resistance text found in the krishisewa.com page applies to the variety Aman and was excluded.

agronomic_details.yield: Seven-centre mean: 1604 kg/ha for TRCP 9, reported as superior to all compared cultivars at Shillongani and Tripura (TRCP 8: 1494 kg/ha; Aman: 1260 kg/ha). NEH multi-location trial table: 1471 kg/ha, the highest yield in that table. 2014-15 twelve-variety NEH trial: 1737 kg/ha, reported as following the top entry (source text garbled, so sentence order is unclear).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the multi-location results summarised under field_trials. The seven-centre mean is the only cross-location summary reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: TRCP 9 was reported as better adapted to Assam and Tripura conditions (Raising productivity of pulses in diverse agro-ecologies of North East Hill region of India). Reported as sub-tropical NEH region adaptation in the Bhuvaneswari et al. publication, but that text is a comparison against other lines and is not a TRCP 9 study.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not found in searched sources. An unlabelled value of 85-90 appears in the ICAR table row for TRCP 9, but it cannot be confirmed as days to maturity. The text reports only a 112 to 122 day range across other varieties, with TRCP 9 not named in that span.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Habit: described as a new tall field pea variety. Pods: 19.9 pods per plant in the NEH trial table, with relatively more seeds per pod and higher 100-seed weight (qualitative comparison; no numeric values given for seeds per pod or 100-seed weight). Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) NEH multi-location trial, 2014-15, twelve varieties: TRCP 9 gave 1737 kg/ha, after the top entry; sentence order unclear in source. (2) Seven-centre mean: TRCP 9 gave 1604 kg/ha and was superior to all compared cultivars at Shillongani and Tripura; TRCP 8 gave 1494 kg/ha and Aman gave 1260 kg/ha. (3) NEH trial table: TRCP 9 yielded the highest at 1471 kg/ha, with 19.9 pods per plant and higher 100-seed weight. Disease and pest scoring from the same ICAR report is described under stress_tolerance.
