search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: TRCP 9 (CSC name) / TRCP-9 (Seednet name), field pea (Pisum sativum ssp. arvense)

Name check: every relevant page uses "TRCP 9" with a space. No page with the hyphenated "TRCP-9" form was found, and the Seednet-targeted search returned nothing about this variety. Discarded: Progress No. 9 pea seed listings from US vendors (a different variety), and fisheries and museum pages (unrelated).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- TRCP 9 showed multiple resistance to powdery mildew, Ascochyta blight and root rot at all locations. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no page reporting these traits for TRCP 9. The only abiotic-stress context was general field pea literature (e.g., drought is a significant production challenge for field pea), which does not name this variety. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/ijpb15040080 (not TRCP 9-specific; excluded from the evidence count)

DISEASE AND PEST
- TRCP 9 is listed as resistant to rust and root knot nematode. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf (table row, "15. TRCP 9 ICAR Res. Complex Agartala")
- TRCP 9 showed multiple resistance to powdery mildew, Ascochyta blight and root rot at all locations. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Pod borer and stem fly: No evidence found for TRCP 9. The pest-resistance text found applies to the variety Aman, not TRCP 9. -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-varietes/368-fieldpea-variety.html (excluded)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Habit: A new tall field pea variety TRCP 9 has been released and notified for Tripura state. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Yield, NEH multi-location trial (2014-15, twelve varieties): TRCP 9 gave 1737 kg/ha, after the top entry. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/308680263_Annual_Report_2015-16_on_Promotion_of_Pulses_in_NEH_Region (Note: the source text is garbled; the entry for AMAN sits above it, so the sentence order is unclear.)
- Yield, seven-centre mean: TRCP 9 (1604 kg/ha) was superior to all these cultivars at Shillongani and Tripura, with TRCP 8 (1494 kg/ha) and Aman (1260 kg/ha) ranked below it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336115227_Raising_productivity_of_pulses_in_diverse_agro-ecologies_of_North_East_Hill_region_of_India_-_A_case_study
- Yield and pods, NEH trial table: TRCP 9 yielded the highest (1471 kg/ha) and had 19.9 pods per plant, with relatively more seeds per pod and higher 100-seed weight. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308680263_Annual_Report_2015-16_on_Promotion_of_Pulses_in_NEH_Region
- Adaptation: TRCP 9 was better adapted to Assam and Tripura conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336115227_Raising_productivity_of_pulses_in_diverse_agro-ecologies_of_North_East_Hill_region_of_India_-_A_case_study
- Maturity: The ICAR table row for TRCP 9 includes a value of 85-90 in an unlabelled column; it cannot be confirmed as days to maturity. The text reports only a range across varieties (112 days (IPFD 6-3) to 122 days (Vikas) to attain 80% maturity), with TRCP 9 not named in that span. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308680263_Annual_Report_2015-16_on_Promotion_of_Pulses_in_NEH_Region

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The searches returned genome-wide association and genetic-diversity studies of field pea, but none names TRCP 9 or reports its parentage or markers. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6888555/ (excluded)
- Parentage: The Parentage field was "Not specified." The ICAR table row for TRCP 9 reads "BMR 7 x P 163," which may be a parentage entry, but this is unverified because the table layout is ambiguous. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: The ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region, Tripura Centre is the Tripura centre's mandate page; no page names TRCP 9 under this profile. -- https://icarneh.icar.gov.in/Profile/Tripura.html
- Breeder name: No evidence found that names the breeder of TRCP 9 specifically. Dr S.P. Das is identified as Principal Scientist (Plant Breeding) and I/C AICRP (Tripura) in a 2016 pulses meeting report. This is an institutional role, not a stated breeder of TRCP 9. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/308680263_Annual_Report_2015-16_on_Promotion_of_Pulses_in_NEH_Region
- Lembucherra station: ICAR Research Complex for NEH region, Tripura Centre (Lembucherra) is the location cited for the NEH pulses trials. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/308680263_Annual_Report_2015-16_on_Promotion_of_Pulses_in_NEH_Region

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level only; no breeder contact found for TRCP 9)
- Dr S.P. Das, Principal Scientist (Plant Breeding), I/C AICRP (Tripura); phone 9436450747; ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region, Tripura Centre, Lembucherra-799210, West Tripura, India. Source: a seed-chain table in a pulses report, which does not tie this contact to TRCP 9. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324031547_Seed_A_vital_component_for_enhancing_pulses_productivity
- Agartala address (third-party listing, not an official page): V/3, Agartala Capital Complex, Agartala, Pin 799 006, West Tripura; phones 91 381-2865201, 91 381-2917883. -- https://www.indcareer.com/tripura/agartala/icar-research-complex-neh-region-tripura

Choudhury, Principal Scientist and Head, Burhan.Choudhury@icar.org.in, 8131074848; Rahul Kumar, Scientist (Genetics & Plant Breeding), Rahul.Kumar5@icar.org.in, 8958626086. -- http://www.icarneh.ernet.in/Staff/Tripura.html
- Email for TRCP 9 breeder: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS

disease_resistance.summary: Powdery mildew: resistant (IIPR PC report, Rabi 2021-22 and Journal of Food Legumes entry, 2016, IIPR Kanpur). Rust: moderately resistant per the IIPR PC report, but described as tolerant in the Journal of Food Legumes entry. The two sources conflict on the rust rating. Source conflict on rust should be reviewed before use.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: IIPR table (Rabi 2021-22 PC report) lists 19-20 q/ha for IPFD 6-3 (approximately 1900-2000 kg/ha). The West Bengal KVK trial recorded 818.0 kg/ha (see field_trials).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Listed for Uttar Pradesh in the IIPR release table. The West Bengal KVK trial used IPFD 6-3 as a trial entry only and does not establish a recommendation for West Bengal.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 110-115 days per the IIPR release table (PC report, Rabi 2021-22). The Journal of Food Legumes source gives 115-120 days for the same variety. The duration figures are inconsistent across sources.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Tendril type (IIPR PC report). Round, creamy white seed (Journal of Food Legumes entry). 1000-seed weight 168.3 g, the highest among the trial varieties in the West Bengal KVK trial (range 159.4-168.3 g). Plant height 66.04 cm and 16.50 branches per plant at 80 DAS, the highest among the trial varieties in the same trial. Parentage per IIPR table: KPMRD 389 x HUDP 7 (the brief lists parentage as 'Not specified', so this should be reviewed).
agronomic_details.field_trials: West Bengal KVK trial, rabi 2021-22, two sowing dates, four varieties (Purba Medinipur KVK): IPFD 6-3 yielded 818.0 kg/ha, ahead of IPFD 12-2 at 787.5 kg/ha and IPFD 10-12 at 731.5 kg/ha. IPFD 6-3 also had the highest 1000-seed weight (168.3 g), plant height at 80 DAS (66.04 cm) and branches per plant at 80 DAS (16.50). No other trial results for IPFD 6-3 were found in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE / DISEASE AND PEST
(Evidence refers to IPFD 6-3, the CSC name "Fieldpea" and Seednet name "Field pea" both checked, no Seednet page retrieved)
- IPFD 6-3 at IIPR Kanpur, from KPMRD 389 x HUDP 7, is resistant to powdery mildew, moderately resistant to rust, and has a tendril type -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- IPFD6-3 (2016, IIPR Kanpur) has round, creamy white seed, is resistant to powdery mildew, and is tolerant to rust -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/2496/1531
- Abiotic stress (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence): No evidence found. The searches returned only disease and general agronomy data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration and yield in the IIPR table: 2016 release, 19-20 (q/ha), 110-115 days -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf. A second table gives 115-120 days for the same variety, so the duration figure is inconsistent across sources -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/2496/1531
- West Bengal KVK trial (rabi 2021-22, two sowing dates, four varieties): IPFD 6-3 yielded 818.0 kg/ha, ahead of IPFD 12-2 at 787.5 kg/ha and IPFD 10-12 at 731.5 kg/ha -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/6568/5336/9002
- Same trial, agronomic traits: 1000-seed weight ranged 159.4–168.3 g across the varieties, with the highest value for IPFD 6-3 at 168.3 g -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/6568/5336/9002
- Same trial, IPFD 6-3 plant vigour: IPFD 6-3 had the highest plant height (66.04 cm) and number of branches per plant (16.50) at 80 DAS -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/6568/5336/9002

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL or marker study naming IPFD 6-3 was found. The parentage KPMRD 389 x HUDP 7 appears only in the IIPR variety table (not in a genetics paper) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developer: Dr. Girish Prasad Dixit, Scientist (Plant Breeding), who has developed high-yielding pulse varieties including IPFD 6-3 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/overview-present-director/
- Institution and station: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur 208 024 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Institution listed for IPFD 6-3 in the release table: IIPR, Kanpur -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Release announcement: IIPR listed 4 fieldpea varieties, including IPFD 6-3, among the 15 most promising pulse varieties developed in the last couple of years -- https://icar.org.in/node/10517

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. Girish Prasad Dixit (breeder): no email, phone or personal contact found. The director's profile page gives biography only -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/overview-present-director/
- Institute: ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur 208 024 (postal address as found). Location: situated on Grand Trunk Road, about twelve kilometres from Kanpur Central Railway Station towards New Delhi -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Pulses_Research (Wikipedia, not an official source)
- Official email, phone and institute contact page URL: No evidence found in retrieved results. The only contact details retrieved (Dr. Yogesh Kumar, chickpea breeder) belong to a different crop and were discarded -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not retrieved (2025). Field pea sowing-date study, Purba Medinipur KVK, West Bengal, rabi 2021-22 (title not fully retrieved). Indian Journal of Agronomy 70(2): 245-248 -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/6568/5336/9002
- Authors not retrieved (2026). Field pea seed-production research paper, Journal of Food Legumes 39(1), which includes IPFD 6-3 among varieties taken up for seed production (title not retrieved) -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/2496/1531
- Authors not retrieved (2022-23). Project Coordinator's report, AICRP on MULLaRP, Rabi 2021-22 (ICAR-IIPR), includes IPFD 6-3 in its release table and seed-chain data -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper specific to IPFD 6-3 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- 25 fieldpea varieties were in the seed chain, and IPFD 6-3 is among the popular fieldpea varieties of the decade -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- IPFD 6-3 was among the varieties taken up for seed production to meet demand -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/2496/1531
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for IPFD 6-3: No evidence found. The fourth search returned only unrelated cover-crop and microgreen seed listings, which were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttar Pradesh: IPFD 6-3 is listed for U.P. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf (the same table gives 2016 release year and 110-115 days, see AGRONOMY AND TRIALS)
- The West Bengal study used IPFD 6-3 as a trial entry and does not establish a recommendation for that state -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/6568/5336/9002

NOTES
- Name mapping: the CSC name "Fieldpea" and the Seednet name "Field pea" were both searched. All evidence refers to the variety code IPFD 6-3. No Seednet page for this variety was retrieved, so Seednet-specific details are unverified.
- Parentage: the tables give KPMRD 389 x HUDP 7. The brief lists it as "Not specified", so this should be reviewed before use.
- Searches run: 4 (Search 1: release and traits; Search 2: breeder and contacts; Search 3: research papers; Search 4: seed availability).

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to powdery mildew and rust, per the ICAR-IIPR MULLaRP rabi 2021-22 report table listing RFP 2009-1 (Indira Matar 1) with IGKV Raipur as developer. pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for pod borer, aphid, Ascochyta, or wilt resistance in Indira Matar 1. Pest and disease statements for other varieties (for example IPFD 2014-2, IPF 16-13) were not applied to this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: No quantified grain yield (q/ha) for Indira Matar 1 was found in the retrieved text. The table snippets did not give a usable value. Variety record average_yield field reads 'Kg/Ha' with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Described as suited to utera cultivation in eastern India (BCKV AICRP page). The ICAR-IIPR report lists it as suitable for rice fallow cultivation. The same report names Chhattisgarh, Bihar, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Assam as candidate rice-fallow pea states.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Sources conflict: 105-110 days (BCKV AICRP on MULLaRP page); 100-105 days (ICAR-IIPR MULLaRP rabi 2021-22 report table).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Seed priming (1% KNO3) and seed rate trial on Indira Matar-1 as a utera crop at IGKV Research cum Instructional Farm, rabi 2020-21; the digest gives no quantitative results. (2) Biomass and yield comparison of Indira Matar with VL 42 and Rachana in the New Alluvial Zone of West Bengal, 2018-19 and 2019-20; the table snippets did not yield a usable value for Indira Matar, so no quantified result is reported. (3) Chopkar R. et al. used Indira Matar-1 as a parent in intergeneric crosses with grasspea (research 2017-18), which is a breeding use rather than a yield trial. No quantified grain yield was found in any trial.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerant to powdery mildew and rust, per the ICAR-IIPR MULLaRP rabi 2021-22 report table that lists RFP 2009-1 (Indira Matar 1) with IGKV Raipur as developer -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Powdery mildew tolerance is also stated for this variety in the AICRP on MULLaRP (BCKV) page -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-mullarp-en
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Indira Matar 1.
- Context only, not specific to this variety: a 20-location study of tall-type breeding lines found that high maximum temperature during flowering, and high minimum temperature during flowering and the reproductive period, were linked to lower yields -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pce.15450

DISEASE AND PEST
- Powdery mildew tolerance and rust tolerance, as listed above -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No evidence found for pod borer, aphid, Ascochyta, or wilt resistance in Indira Matar 1. Pest and disease statements found for other varieties (for example IPFD 2014-2, IPF 16-13) were not applied to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Short duration: matures in 105-110 days and is described as suited to utera cultivation in eastern India -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-mullarp-en
- A different ICAR table gives 100-105 days for the same line. The two sources disagree on duration -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Seed priming (1% KNO3) and seed rate trial on Indira Matar-1 as a utera crop, IGKV Research cum Instructional Farm, rabi 2020-21 -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue7/PartAE/12-7-277-229.pdf
- Biomass and yield comparison of Indira Matar with VL 42 and Rachana, New Alluvial Zone of West Bengal, 2018-19 and 2019-20 -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Yield-and-plant-biomass-at-maturity-achieved-by-VL-42-Indira-Matar-and-Rachana-varieties_tbl1_378688781
- No quantified grain yield (q/ha) for Indira Matar 1 was found in the retrieved text. The table snippets did not give a usable value.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage shown as Rachna x EC (EC accession 334160-1) in the ICAR-IIPR MULLaRP report table. This conflicts with the "Not specified" parentage in the record -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No evidence found for QTL or marker studies on this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Field pea". The evidence refers to the variety code "Indira Matar 1 (RFP 2009-1)", not to the generic crop name -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Developing institution: IGKV, Raipur (Chhattisgarh), in the ICAR-IIPR MULLaRP report table -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Field pea work at IGKV Raipur sits within the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, IGKV Raipur 492 012 -- https://igkv.ac.in/_Attachment/web/Research/Publication/2016/Publication_4_20210902011103509.pdf
- No lead breeder name found for Indira Matar 1.
- Release year conflict: the CSC record gives 2015-06-25, while the DPD annual report and the ICAR table give 2016 -- https://dpd.gov.in/Annual%20Report%20%202023-24%2014.01.2025.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email or phone found for Indira Matar 1.
- Institute address as found: Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur, 492012, India (affiliation line) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00484-024-02720-7
- Institute address as found: Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding / College of Agriculture, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur 492 012 (CG), India -- https://igkv.ac.in/_Attachment/web/Research/Publication/2016/Publication_4_20210902011103509.pdf
- Journal office address as found: Journal of Agricultural Issues, University Technical Cell, College of Agriculture, IGKV, Raipur (C.G.) 492 012 -- https://igkv.ac.in/_Attachment/web/Research/Publication/2016/Publication_4_20210902011103509.pdf
- Official email and phone numbers for IGKV or its Genetics and Plant Breeding department: No evidence found in the retrieved results.

PUBLICATIONS

Multi-location evaluation of field pea in Indian climates: eco-phenological dynamics, crop-environment relationships, and identification of mega-environments. Does not report on Indira Matar 1 specifically -- https://doi.org/10.1007/s00484-024-02720-7 ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38922422

- Chopkar R. et al. (year not confirmed, research 2017-18). Use of plant growth regulators to enhance pod setting in wide hybridization between grasspea and pea. Biological Forum. Indira Matar-1 used as a parent in intergeneric crosses -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/88%20Use%20of%20Plant%20Growth%20Regulators%20to%20Enhance%20the%20Pod%20Setting%20in%20Wide%20Hybridization%20Between%20Grasspea%20and%20Pea%20Rita%20Chopkara.pdf

Uses Indira Matar among three varieties in West Bengal. - No KrishiKosh thesis specific to Indira Matar 1 was found. The KrishiKosh hits were unrelated (hoary pea, chickpea, INM).

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or dealer listings of Indira Matar 1.
- Pulse seed programme status: the DPD annual reports list the 2016 release of Indira Matar 1 (RFP 2009-1) in the pea variety list, but do not give seed quantities or sellers -- https://dpd.gov.in/Final%20%20Annual%20Report%20(2022-23)%20with%20Preface%20(As%20on%2020.02.2024).pdf
- Retail pea seed listings found in search were generic pea seeds, not this variety, and were excluded -- https://www.alkarty.com/peas-seeds

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Chhattisgarh and Bihar, as stated in the record. The ICAR-IIPR report lists it as suitable for rice fallow cultivation, with Chhattisgarh listed in the state column -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- The same report names Chhattisgarh, Bihar, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Assam as candidate rice-fallow pea states -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- The BCKV AICRP page recommends it for utera cultivation in eastern India -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-mullarp-en

heat.details: Listed as heat tolerant in a review table citing Dhall and Brar (2015). The table spells the name 'Mater Ageta-7'; the digest treats this as the same variety. The degree of tolerance and the mechanisms are not stated in the digest.

Keywords include rust and pea wilt, but the digest cannot confirm which disease the resistance refers to. No other disease evidence found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources (no pest resistance evidence found).

agronomic_details.yield: Average green pod yield of 32 q/acre (source reports q/acre; CSC record lists average yield in Kg/Ha without a value).
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location and adaptive trial yields are described in the 2015 paper, but the snippets are fragmentary and no reliable percentages or stability values can be reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Identified for national-level cultivation in zone IV (Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand) per PAU. No agro-climatic detail found beyond this.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Sources conflict: first picking about 65-70 days after sowing (Seed Production of Garden Pea), versus first picking within 60 days of sowing (PAU event page, which also notes clearing fields for wheat). The CSC record lists maturity as not specified.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plants are vigorous with 15-18 well-filled pods, 7-9 seeds per pod, and shelling out-turn of 48%. Early-maturing.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location and adaptive trials described in the 2015 Dhall and Brar paper, with comparison against Matar Ageta-6 and Arkel; snippets do not allow reliable yield figures. (2) Sowing-time study: Matar Ageta 7 covered about 2% of surveyed area, indicating a minor variety in that sample; this is a survey result, not a yield trial. (3) Flowering and pod-picking evaluation in the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh with comparison against other early varieties; the digest does not report this variety's specific result. (4) Aluminium-toxicity soil study: yield reduced by added Al (see drought field). Yield figures for other crops on the PAU College of Horticulture page were discarded.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Matar Ageta-7 (Pea, Pisum sativum)
Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Matar Ageta-7", so every finding below refers to that one name. I ran 4 searches. The Seednet portal was not searched separately, and no Seednet page surfaced.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as heat tolerant in a review table that cites Dhall and Brar (2015); the table spells it "Mater Ageta-7" -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2026.1762081/full
- Grouped with susceptible genotypes (alongside AP-3) in an aluminium-toxicity soil study, where added Al reduced its yield; this is a sensitivity finding, not a tolerance one -- https://www.academia.edu/91366932/Impact_of_Aluminium_on_Nutrient_Profile_of_Soil_under_Various_Genotypes_of_Garden_Pea
- Salinity, drought, flood and submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The 2015 Dhall and Brar paper reports a moderately resistant reaction for this variety under some test conditions; the snippet does not name the disease. Its keyword list includes rust and pea wilt, but I cannot confirm which of these the resistance refers to -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/285383933_Matar_AGETA-7_An_early_maturing_variety_of_pea
- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Early-maturing; first picking about 65-70 days after sowing, with average green pod yield of 32 q/acre -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313770085_Seed_Production_of_Garden_Pea
- Pedigree-derived early variety; plants are vigorous with 15-18 well-filled pods, 7-9 seeds per pod, shelling out-turn 48% -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325662909_Pea_Cultivation
- Multi-location and adaptive trial yields, and the comparison with Matar Ageta-6 and Arkel, are described in the 2015 paper, but the snippets are fragmentary and no percentages can be reliably reported -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/285383933_Matar_AGETA-7_An_early_maturing_variety_of_pea
- Sowing-time study: Matar Ageta 7 was on about 2% of surveyed area, so it was a minor variety in that sample -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327836097_Profitability_of_Pea_Cultivation_under_Different_Sowing_Times
- Flowering and pod-picking evaluation in Malwa region, Madhya Pradesh; comparison with other early varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365946870_Evaluation_of_Garden_Pea_Pisum_sativum_L_varieties_for_Growth_and_Flowering_Attributes_under_Malwa_Region_of_Madhya_Pradesh
- Note: a PAU College of Horticulture page mixes pea text with other crops; its yield figures for other crops were discarded, and only the pea-specific figures above were kept -- https://pau.edu/cohf/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewMatter&intDepTitleID=337&intLinkID=5

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: cross between Matar Ageta-6 and AP-3; developed by pedigree method -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325662909_Pea_Cultivation
- Breeding-line code: No evidence found.
- Genome resources, QTL or markers specific to this variety: No evidence found. The Frontiers review discusses pea abiotic-stress genomics generally, not this variety.
- Caution: "VL Ageti Matar-7" (VL-7, VPKAS Almora) is a different variety and was excluded -- https://www.biologydiscussion.com/vegetable-breeding/pea-origin-varieties-and-future-prospects-india/68547

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana; the 2015 paper is from the Department of Vegetable Science -- https://www.indianjournals.com/ijor.aspx?target=ijor%3Ajre&volume=52&issue=4&article=027
- Lead breeder names: R. K. Dhall and P. S. Brar appear as authors of the release paper, but their roles as breeder of this variety are not explicitly stated in the snippet -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Matar-AGETA-7:-An-early-maturing-variety-of-pea-Dhall-Brar/bb37b4aad6ec56782ff0248b09dccd747afce482
- Release year: sources say 2015 (Pea Cultivation; the PAU 2019 report notes earlier state-level release), which conflicts with the 2021 year in the input -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325662909_Pea_Cultivation ; https://pau.edu/content/research/ra/ra_2019.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Sabji Matar-3 (CSC name) / Pant Sabji Matar-3 (PM-5) (Seednet name)

Naming note: The CSC record gives "Pant Sabji Matar-3" and Seednet gives "Pant Sabji Matar-3 (PM-5)". The PPV&FRA registry compendium lists "Pant Sabji Matar-3 (PM-5)", so the PM-5 code is tied to this variety there. Crop note: the CSC record says field pea, but every source I found describes it as a garden/vegetable pea (Pisum sativum var. hortense) and Seednet lists it as PEA (VEGETABLE). Evidence below refers to the same variety under both names unless stated.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. Its only described tolerance is a general suitability for rainfed and irrigated conditions -- https://www.indiainputs.com/pea-varieties-in-india/20027/

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to Pant Sabji Matar-3. Sources for Pant Sabji Matar 5, Pant Sabji Matar 6 and other Pant pea lines describe powdery mildew resistance, but those are different varieties and should not be attributed to this one -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/13%20AICRP%20-%20VEGETABLE%20CROPS.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Plants are dwarf with dark green foliage; pods are long, curved and well filled; seeds are wrinkled with a green seed coat; first picking at 60-65 days; yield potential stated as 90 q/ha -- https://www.pantnagarseeds.com/kitchen-seeds
-- Maturity given as medium duration, 65-70 days, with medium smooth pods and sweet flavour -- https://www.indiainputs.com/pea-varieties-in-india/20027/
-- An older Pantnagar-era table lists picking starting 60-75 days after sowing and yield of 9 t/ha for "Pant Sabji Matar 3", though the row layout is ambiguous -- https://www.eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/pdf/lec17.pdf
-- A 2004 trial at Partapur, Nubra valley (Ladakh) included Pant Sabji Matar 3 among 8 cultivars; the abstract text found does not report its yield or the author list -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324230190_Performance_of_garden_pea_varieties_for_their_growth_and_yield_characteristics_in_Vidharbha_region_of_Maharashtra_India
-- Described as prominent early variety in Uttarakhand Tarai, alongside Arkel and VL-7 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329028508_Scientific_Cultivation_of_Vegetable_Pea

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage conflict: one source gives Arkel x Early Badger for Pant Sabji Matar-3 -- https://www.horticultureguruji.in/pea-cultivation/
-- An older table gives T 19 x Early Badger, but places it under the Jawahar Matar-3 entry, so it may not belong to this variety -- https://www.eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/pdf/lec17.pdf
-- The CSC parentage field says "Not specified". No QTL or marker study found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUA&T), Pantnagar, Uttarakhand -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/Released_crop_varieties.pdf
-- Station/programme context: AICRP centre established 1966 in the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Pantnagar -- https://www.icar-iirr.org.in/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf
-- No individual lead breeder name found for this variety. No evidence found for the lead breeder.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Breeder Seed Production Centre, GBPUA&T; officer in charge Dr. A.S. Jeena, Joint Director; mailing address PO Pantnagar, Distt. U.S. Nagar, Uttarakhand-263145; phone +91-7817005207 -- https://gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/
-- Institute website: gbpuat.ac.in. No official email address found. No breeder-specific contact found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report entry, thesis or KrishiKosh record specific to Pant Sabji Matar-3 was found.
-- Singh et al. (2012) and Parihar et al. (2022) are cited for the Tarai varieties in a review, but full references were not retrievable -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329028508_Scientific_Cultivation_of_Vegetable_Pea
-- The Ladakh 2004 trial appears in a ResearchGate record with an unrelated title; author and journal details were not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324230190_Performance_of_garden_pea_varieties_for_their_growth_and_yield_characteristics_in_Vidharbha_region_of_Maharashtra_India

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Pantnagar seeds listing for Pant Sabji Matar-3 -- https://www.pantnagarseeds.com/kitchen-seeds
-- GBPUA&T's Directorate of Research lists breeder seed production of desired seed classes among its functions, and the AICRP report cites about 150 q of breeder seed produced each year, but this figure is not specific to this variety -- https://gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/ and https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/13%20AICRP%20-%20VEGETABLE%20CROPS.pdf
-- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales listing found for this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Uttar Pradesh (CSC record) -- https://www.indiainputs.com/pea-varieties-in-india/20027/ lists Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh as its regions
-- An AICRP vegetable report links the variety with Uttarakhand and Madhya Pradesh, where it reportedly covered about 40% of the area during 2011-2017 -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/13%20AICRP%20-%20VEGETABLE%20CROPS.pdf
-- Release year 2014-01-13 (CSC record): no evidence found in the sources.

drought.details: Recognized as a drought-resistant vegetable. Evaluation under irrigated and rainfed conditions in West Bengal indicated it could be selected as drought-tolerant, exhibiting a high drought tolerance index. Water stress should be avoided during flowering and seed formation for the crop in general.

heat.details: Studies have explored heat stress tolerance in peas, and Punjab-89 has been noted in contexts related to developing varieties with terminal heat tolerance. It is suited for different seasons, but peas generally are cool-weather crops.

salinity.details: It is mentioned as tolerant to salt stress, particularly when field tested with PGPR (Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria) strains like Priestia megaterium IHB B 7164, which promotes plant growth under stress conditions including salt. It is also listed among varieties classified as resistant or tolerant to salt conditions, and suitable for main season cultivation in areas affected by saline lands.

flood.details: It has shown some ability to germinate under anaerobic conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Punjab-89 is resistant to rust and tolerant to powdery mildew and wilt. It has been studied in the context of gene-based resistance to Erysiphe species causing powdery mildew.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified

agronomic_details.yield: Quantitative yield is not specified. However, Punjab-89 has been observed to record the highest number of branches per plant in performance studies in the North-Western Himalayan Region, which may correlate with higher yield potential. It is noted that the legumes give 55% seeds.
agronomic_details.stability: It has been evaluated under both irrigated and rainfed conditions, suggesting adaptability to varying moisture availability. Its suitability for different seasons implies environmental stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Well-adapted for cultivation in Punjab, being developed by PAU. It has been evaluated in the foothills of the Terai Agro-ecological Region of West Bengal, the North-Western Himalayan Region, and Bihar. It is suited for different seasons and can be grown as a winter crop. While generally adaptable to various soil types, alkaline soils with high salt concentration are not suitable for pea cultivation. It cannot tolerate frost.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium dwarf, vigorous plants with a pant height of 92 cm. It produces a high number (28-30) of well-filled pods per plant. The pods are dark green and long, typically containing 9-10 wrinkle seeds.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials have been conducted in West Bengal under irrigated and rainfed conditions. Performance studies were also carried out in the North-Western Himalayan Region. It was also used in field testing for PGPR strains and in randomized block designs for cultivation studies, including optimal sowing dates (e.g., November 5th) and spacing (20 x 7.5 cm).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (QTL, SNP, SSR) are detailed for Punjab-89 in the provided results. General pea QTLs for heat stress tolerance are mentioned but not linked directly to this variety.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs identified for Punjab-89. General research on QTLs for heat stress tolerance in pea is noted.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Punjab-89 has been used in field testing to understand the molecular mechanisms of Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPR) strains in promoting plant growth under abiotic stress conditions, including salt stress.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: Vivekanand Parvatiya Krishi Ansandhan Sansthan (ICAR), Almora - 263 601, Uttarakhand.
seednet_fields.Parentage: Indigenous collection, the seed sample was collected from Srirampur village, Agra.
seednet_fields.Resemblence to Variety: Resemble in pod shape with Azad Pea 1
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release and cultivation in the States of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu Kashmir under both irrigated and rainfed condition. Resistant against powdery mildew, wilt, white rot and leaf blight.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Like other garden pea varieties, the cultural and fertilizer requirements are similar. Under organic conditions, 20 T/ha FYM are recommended for its cultivation in hills whereas 10-20 T/ha FYM and 20 kgN, 60 kg P2O5 adn K2) ha-1 are recommended for cultivation under inorganic.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: xi. Pod shape: Curved/sickle, xii. Pods/peduncle: Mostly double, xiii. No. of pods/Plant: 10-15, xiv. No. of pods/kg: 190-120, xv. Av. Pod length: 8.1 cm, xvi. No. of seeds/pod: 7-8, xvii. 100 green grain weight: 35-40 gms, xviii. Shelling%: 46, xix. Sweetness: Sweet, xx. Seed colour: Greenish wrinkled, xxi. 100 seed weight: 21 gms.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: a) Plant Height: 56.4 cm, b) Distinguishing morphological characters: Plants are dwarf, vigorous in growth with green foliage. Pods are long, dark green and curved. Seed is wrinkled and greenish in colour. i. Growth habit: Dwarf, ii. 50% flowering: 90-100 days (in mid hills), iii. Maturity days: Medium 132-135 days, iv. Number of branch: 1-2, v. Node of first flower: 7-10, vi. Foliage colour: Green, vii. Leaf type: Normal, viii. Flower colour: White, ix. No. of flowers/peduncle: Two, x. Pod colour: Dark green
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Powdery mildew is a serious problem in valleys, low and mid hills during spring season. Under natural conditions, this variety possesses high degree of resistance against powdery mildew and resistance against wilt (5-8%), white rot (2-3%) and leaf blight resulting in less economic loss.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Less incidence of pests like pod borer has been observed in this variety under mid hills conditions.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to Uttarakhand hills under irrigated and rainfed conditions. It is listed as a recommended vegetable pea variety for districts like Pauri Garhwal in Uttarakhand.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: 1. PLANTS ARE DWARF, VIGOROUS IN GROWTH WITH DARK GREEN FOLIAGE. 2. PODS ARE LONG, DARK GREEN AND SLIGHTLY CURVED. 3. THE PROXIMAL END IS SLIGHTLY NARROW THAN DISTAL END. 4. SEED IS GREENISH SEMI- WRINKLED.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Vivek Matar-11, along with Vivek Matar-9 and Vivek Matar-10, is included in the vegetable pea varieties recommended in the Agriculture Contingency Plan for Pauri Garhwal district in Uttarakhand, indicating its suitability for cultivation in this region. The variety was also listed among vegetable pea varieties collected by the Plant Authority of India.

csc_fields.special_traits: Resembles in pod shape and maturity duration with Azad Pea 1. Plant height: 56.4 cm. Growth habit: Dwarf. 50% flowering: 90-100 days (in mid hills). Maturity days: Medium, 132-135 days. Number of branch: 1-2. Node of First flower: 7-10. Foliage colour: Green. Leaf type: Normal. Flower colour: White. No. of flowers/peduncle: Two. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I could not complete the required research. The search tool returned usable results for only one query, and then the tool reported that its use limit was exceeded, so the breeder, publication and seed-availability searches never ran. No source I found mentions VL Matar 64 (VL 64) at all. The one result set I got refers to VL Matar-42, the seednet name, which is a different variety. Treat everything below as evidence for VL Matar-42 unless stated otherwise.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: CSC name "VL Matar 64" / variety code VL 64 has no hits in any result. Seednet name "VL Matar-42" has hits. Findings below under the Seednet name refer to VL Matar-42, not VL 64.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- VL Matar-42 is listed as resistant to powdery mildew and moderately resistant to rust in a central/state fieldpea variety table -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/vi)%20Fieldpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for VL 64 or VL Matar-42 was found -- No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- VL Matar-42 is named among powdery-mildew-resistant fieldpea varieties in a DPD crop note -- http://dpd.gov.in/Pea.pdf
- No pod borer, stem fly or other pest data for VL 64 or VL Matar-42 was found -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The VPKAS fieldpea table lists VL Matar 42 as released in 2006 by CVRC and SVRC for timely-sown conditions in the NEPZ, including Uttarakhand hills -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/12/Field%20Pea
- The same DPD table gives VL-42 a maturity range of 108-155 days -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/vi)%20Fieldpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The DPD crop note gives a fieldpea sowing window of 15 October to 15 November -- http://dpd.gov.in/Pea.pdf
- No multi-location trial data for VL 64 was found -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker or pedigree-verification evidence found for VL 64 -- No evidence found
- The VPKAS table lists VL Matar 1 as an earlier release (1978) for Uttarakhand hills, which is consistent with it being a parent, but the cross "VL Matar 1 x P 388" was not confirmed -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/12/Field%20Pea

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The VPKAS fieldpea release list does not include VL Matar 64 in the snapshot retrieved -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/12/Field%20Pea
- No breeder or lead scientist name for VL 64 or VL Matar-42 was found -- No evidence found

Search note: The search tool's usage limit was reached after 4 queries (all 4 were run in the first batch; the follow-up batch was rejected). Several headings therefore rest on little or no evidence. Only pages that name VL Matar 42/47 or the "VL 42" short form in a field pea context are kept below. Name mismatches are flagged under each heading.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for either name.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Powdery mildew resistance is reported for "VL matar-42" and "VL matar-47" in a list of resistant varieties. This refers to the Seednet name (VL Matar-42) and the CSC name (VL Matar 47) respectively. -- http://dpd.gov.in/Pea.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A research figure lists yield and plant biomass at maturity for "VL 42" alongside Indira Matar and Rachana. "VL 42" is taken here as the short form of VL Matar-42 (Seednet name). The figure gives no independent yield values in the retrieved text, and no VL Matar 47 trial data was found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Yield-and-plant-biomass-at-maturity-achieved-by-VL-42-Indira-Matar-and-Rachana-varieties_tbl1_378688781

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No QTL, marker or genetic study naming either variety was retrieved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The ICAR Vegetable/Pulses variety compendium lists "VL Matar 42" as a field pea variety released in 2006 by CVRC and SVRC for timely-sown conditions. This refers to the Seednet name (VL Matar-42). The page does not name a breeder or developing station for it. No record for VL Matar 47 was found. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/12/Field%20Pea

Discrepancy: the compendium gives a 2006 release for VL Matar 42, while the record gives 2011-06-28 for VL 47. The two entries may be different varieties or the record may be wrong. This has not been resolved.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, institute email, phone or address for VL Matar 47 or VL Matar-42 was retrieved. The VPKAS page above is the only official source and has no contact details in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming VL Matar 47 or VL Matar-42 was retrieved. The only item is the research figure above, which has no authors, year or journal in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Yield-and-plant-biomass-at-maturity-achieved-by-VL-42-Indira-Matar-and-Rachana-varieties_tbl1_378688781

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The only seed-related results were consumer retail listings for unrelated pea seed products (e.g., Amazon), which were discarded as not naming this variety. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The compendium lists VL Matar 42 for timely-sown conditions with area of adaptation as the field "Uttarakhand Hills" for the earlier VL Matar 1 entry only; no recommended-state entry for VL Matar 42 or VL Matar 47 was clearly retrieved. The recorded value "Not specified" is therefore left unchanged. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/12/Field%20Pea

Suggested follow-up (not run, since the search limit was reached): search seednet.gov.in and the VPKAS/CVRC notification for "VL Matar 47" and "VL Matar 42" separately; check the Uttarakhand (VPKAS, Almora/Ranichauri) institute pages for the breeder and contact; and search KrishiKosh for theses on VL Matar 42/47.

disease_resistance.summary: No evidence found in the digest for DSH-6 resistance to grain mould, rust, leaf blight, anthracnose or downy mildew. The variety record (CSC ground truth) states the variety is highly resistant to stem rot disease, which is not corroborated by the digest. Stem rot resistance is therefore recorded as a claim from the variety record only.

pest_resistance.summary: Stem borer: SPH 1943 (variety code in the record, treated as a hybrid in the evidence) was on par with the resistant check IS 2205 for deadhearts at Palem, Dharwad and Parbhani; across locations deadhearts averaged 14.5% for SPH 1943 and other entries, statistically on par with the resistant check. Shoot fly: SPH 1943 showed better resistance than other entries in the multi-location trial. No pest resistance evidence was found for DSH-6 itself.

agronomic_details.yield: No DSH-6 yield data found. For SPH 1943 (variety code in the record): about 4411 kg/ha grain in Zone I as the early hybrid, ahead of the best early check; about 3424 kg/ha versus 3152 kg/ha for the early hybrid check CSH 30 (about 9% higher). The record's average_yield is not specified.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for DSH-6. SPH 1943 reached three years of AICRP testing; stability across environments beyond these reported trials was not assessed in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Not found in searched sources for DSH-6. SPH 1943 trial centres included Dharwad, Chamarajanagara and Hagari (Karnataka), Palem, Dharwad and Parbhani. The record's adaptation_ecology is not specified in fragment.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: ITS PLANTS ARE LEAFY HAVING LONG STALK. ITS LEAFLETS ARE ROUNDISH IN SHAPE AND FLOWERS ARE LIGHT PINK IN COLOUR. IT IS HIGHLY RESISTANT TO STEM ROT DISEASE AND IS THUS PARTICULARLY SUITABLE FOR DISEASE IN FESTED FIELDS. IT SUPPLIES GREEN FODDER UPTO MIDDLE OF MAY. ITS SEEDS ARE SMALL IN SIZE.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Zone I early hybrid trial: SPH 1943 gave about 4411 kg/ha grain, ahead of the best early check (kharif grain breeding report). (2) Second trial: SPH 1943 about 9% above early hybrid check CSH 30 (3424 vs 3152 kg/ha). (3) Kharif entomology trial, stem borer: SPH 1943 on par with resistant check IS 2205 at Palem, Dharwad and Parbhani; trial average deadhearts 14.5%. (4) Multi-location shoot fly trial: SPH 1943 had better resistance than other entries. (5) Entomology kharif trial maturity: trial mean 71.8 days (range 64.7 to 78.1); one entry was the earliest but the text is truncated and SPH 1943 maturity is not confirmed. (6) SPH 1943 completed three years of AICRP testing; SPV 2773 was top-ranked at Dharwad (this does not concern DSH-6). No trial results were found for DSH-6.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for DSH-6 or SH-69 on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence. The searches returned only generic sorghum and US seed-catalogue pages. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/3-Sorghum-Kharif-Grain-Breeding-Report-agm23.pdf (no DSH-6 content)
- SPH 1943 (variety code in the record, which the evidence treats as a hybrid) was on par with the resistant check IS 2205 for stem borer deadhearts at Palem, Dharwad and Parbhani in the kharif entomology trial. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/7-Sorghum-Entomology%20Kharif%20%20Report-agm23.pdf
- SPH 1943 had better shoot fly resistance than other entries in the multi-location trial. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/AGM2022-AICRP_on_Sorghum_and_Small_millets-Proceedings.pdf (https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/AGM2022-AICRP_on_Sorghum_and_Small_millets-Proceedings.pdf)

DISEASE AND PEST
- The same entomology report says that across locations stem borer deadhearts averaged 14.5% for SPH 1943 and other entries, with the test entries statistically on par with the resistant check. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/7-Sorghum-Entomology%20Kharif%20%20Report-agm23.pdf
- No evidence found for DSH-6 disease resistance (grain mould, rust, leaf blight, anthracnose or downy mildew).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- SPH 1943 was the early hybrid in Zone I, giving about 4411 kg/ha grain, ahead of the best early check. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/3-Sorghum-Kharif-Grain-Breeding-Report-agm23.pdf
- In another trial the same hybrid was about 9% above the early hybrid check CSH 30 (3424 vs 3152 kg/ha). -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/3-Sorghum-Kharif-Grain-Breeding-Report-agm23.pdf
- The SPH 1943 report reached three years of AICRP testing, and the variety SPV 2773 was top-ranked at Dharwad. This does not concern DSH-6. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/3-Sorghum-Kharif-Grain-Breeding-Report-agm23.pdf
- The entomology trial reports a trial mean maturity of 71.8 days (range 64.7 to 78.1), with one entry the earliest. The text is truncated and does not name the entry, so the maturity of SPH 1943 is not confirmed. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/kh/7-Sorghum-Entomology-Kharif-Report-agm22.pdf
- No evidence found for DSH-6 yield, maturity or fodder data in any search.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for DSH-6, CSH-49 or SH-69 (pedigree, marker or QTL studies). The record's parentage "INDIGENOUS MATERIAL" could not be checked.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No breeder or scientist name was found for DSH-6. The name "DSH-6" appears in none of the four searches.
- Name check: the SeedNet name SH-69 under "PERSIAN CLOVER" returned only Persian clover (Trifolium resupinatum) fodder pages. None concern sorghum, so the SeedNet crop/variety entry looks mis-assigned. The evidence does not refer to DSH-6 under either name. -- https://www.feedipedia.org/node/244
- The AICRP on Sorghum (Hyderabad) reports cover the SPH 1943 hybrid code, and the institution named in the record is the AICRP on Sorghum and Millets. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/3-Sorghum-Kharif-Grain-Breeding-Report-agm23.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for any breeder email, phone or postal address. Institute-level page only: the AICRP sorghum/millets web domain. -- https://millets.res.in
- No evidence found for the Main Agricultural Research Station or SAU contact page in the search results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in indexed snippet (2023). Sorghum Kharif Grain Breeding Report, AICRP on Sorghum, Hyderabad (agm23). -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/3-Sorghum-Kharif-Grain-Breeding-Report-agm23.pdf
- Authors not stated in indexed snippet (2023). Sorghum Kharif Entomology Report, AICRP on Sorghum, Hyderabad (agm23). -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/7-Sorghum-Entomology%20Kharif%20%20Report-agm23.pdf
- Authors not stated in indexed snippet (2022). Proceedings of the AGM 2022, AICRP on Sorghum and Small Millets. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/AGM2022-AICRP_on_Sorghum_and_Small_millets-Proceedings.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh) or DSH-6-specific conference paper found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The seed pages returned were US retail sites unrelated to this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found that DSH-6 is recommended for Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Gujarat or Rajasthan. The only Karnataka link is that the AICRP trial centres in Dharwad, Chamarajanagara and Hagari tested SPH 1943. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip22/Sorghum/reports22/kh/3-Sorghum-Kharif-Grain-Breeding-Report-agm23.pdf
- The ICRISAT paper lists Karnataka and Rajasthan among main sorghum states, but this is general context and not a DSH-6 recommendation. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/5452/7/Sorghum-paper-final-ASAE.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Searches run: 4 (release/recommendation, breeder/institution, research/parentage, seed availability). Both names were searched. "Anand Grain Tur-2" is the CSC/minutes name; "Anand Grain Tur-2 (AGT-2)" is the Seednet name. The evidence below mostly uses the Gujarat-state listing names, "AGT 2" or "Anand Grain Tur-2 (AGT-2)".

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found for AGT-2 specifically. The DPD pigeonpea table has text about wilt resistance and seed traits near the AGT 2 row, but the layout splits rows across columns, so I could not confidently attribute resistance to this variety. Treat as unverified. -- https://dpd.gov.in/ii)%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found that ties resistance traits specifically to AGT-2. The same DPD table lists wilt and sterility-mosaic resistance for other varieties in adjacent rows, which I have not attributed to AGT-2. -- https://dpd.gov.in/ii)%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: AGT 2 is listed as an indeterminate, semi-spreading, medium-maturity, white, bold-seeded type, with a duration of about 170-180 days, yield of about 15-16 q/ha, and a Moel Farm Vadodara origin. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
Multi-location or field-trial results specific to AGT-2: No evidence found. -- search 3 returned no AGT-2 trial pages.

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage (GAUT 87-20 x GAUT 85-21, cross made Kharif 1988) was supplied in the input record only. No web source confirmed it. No breeding-line codes, breeding method, QTL, marker, or genome-resource evidence found. -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Anand Agricultural University, Anand, lists AGT-2 among its state-released varieties, with the release entry dated 2009 (39th SSSC). -- https://aau.in/variety_released
The Vadodara Model Farm / Pulses Research Station is the listed development site. No breeder name was found for AGT-2. The one AAU pigeonpea paper that surfaced (Deepak Patil, CROPGRO model, Pulse Research Station Vadodara) is a modelling study. I have not attributed it to this variety, because it names a different station-level dataset and no link to AGT-2 is stated. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329416338_Effect_of_intra-seasonal_variation_in_temperature_and_rainfall_on_seed_yield_of_pigeon_pea_cultivars_using_CROPGRO_model (not AGT-2 evidence)

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder contact found. Institute-level: Anand Agricultural University, Anand, Gujarat; the release record names the Associate Research Scientist, Pulses Research Station, Model Farm, Vadodara-3 (Gujarat). No email, phone, or contact-page URL found in the results. -- https://aau.in/variety_released

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found for any paper, AICRP report, thesis, or KrishiKosh entry specific to AGT-2. The AAU proceedings result (Thirteenth AGRESCO) concerns a different pigeonpea vegetable line, so it is excluded. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Thirteenth_AGRESCO.pdf (excluded)

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for seed sales from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed units, or dealers. -- search 4 returned only the DPD listing.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Gujarat (Central Zone, CZ/Gujarat), per the DPD central-release table and the AAU record. -- https://dpd.gov.in/ii)%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf

Discrepancy to note: the release year is 2009 (AAU 39th SSSC), but the DPD table lists the notification year as 2011.

drought.details: The variety is described as drought-escaping and short-duration (150-155 days), which allows it to escape terminal drought. A review of its adoption in Marathwada describes it as drought-escaping and short-duration, with a semi-spreading habit. A study titled 'Performance and economic impact of Pigeaon pea-(BDN-711) under drought condition' reports that BDN 711 performed well under drought conditions in a NICRA village in Marathwada, Maharashtra. The full study text was not retrieved, so the level rests on the escape mechanism and the summary of that study, not on quantitative yield data. Escape is not the same as tolerance, so the level reflects the evidence available, not a measured tolerance score.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NOTE: The crop field says "fieldpea", but BRG-3 is a pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan) line. The Seednet crop name is PIGEON PEA (RED GRAM/ARHAR). All findings below are for pigeonpea. Both names, BRG-3 and BRG-3 on Seednet, are the same string, so no name conflict arose. The "fieldpea" searches returned only Pisum sativum releases, which I discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- UAS(B) pigeonpea page lists BRG-3 as resistant to wilt and sterility mosaic (no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found) -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/pigeonpea-zars-gkvk-bengaluru/

DISEASE AND PEST -- UAS(B) ZARS GKVK page lists BRG-3 as resistant to wilt and sterility mosaic disease -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/pigeonpea-zars-gkvk-bengaluru/
DISEASE AND PEST -- Sterility mosaic screening paper (Environment and Ecology 36(2): 430-436, 2018) includes BRG-3 in a genotype table with a disease incidence of 29.97 and a reaction code of MR (moderately resistant), and a second column of R, and the text names BRG-3 among three genotypes singled out in the screen; the extract does not state the final category clearly, and the text says BRG-3 was previously reported resistant by other workers -- https://environmentandecology.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/MS12-1.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for insect pest (pod borer, etc.) resistance specific to BRG-3. The search returned transgenic Cry2Aa pigeonpea work, which does not name BRG-3 and was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- UAS(B) lists frontline demonstrations of BRG-3 (with BRG-5) under the AICRP on Pigeonpea at ZARS GKVK, Bengaluru (start year 2001) -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/pigeonpea-zars-gkvk-bengaluru/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No yield figures for BRG-3 found. The yield figures on the same page (16-18 q dry seed/ha) belong to BRG 1 and were discarded.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Release-year check: UAS(B) list of releases over the last ten years places BRG-3 in the 2016-17 row, not 2018 as in the CSC record -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/list-of-crop-varieties-hybrids-released-by-uasb-during-last-ten-years/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Generic pigeonpea genomics and SSR/SNP reviews do not name BRG-3 and were discarded -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2015.00050/full

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: University of Agricultural Sciences, Bangalore (UAS(B)), through its ZARS, GKVK, Bengaluru pigeonpea programme, which runs the AICRP on Pigeonpea -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/pigeonpea-zars-gkvk-bengaluru/
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No lead breeder or scientist name found for BRG-3 in any result.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute station page: ZARS, GKVK, Bengaluru (UAS(B)) -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/pigeonpea-zars-gkvk-bengaluru/
CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder name, email, phone or postal address appears in the extracted text of that page. No breeder contact found.

PUBLICATIONS -- Environment and Ecology 36(2): 430-436 (2018). Sterility mosaic screening of pigeonpea genotypes including BRG-3. Authors: not shown in the extract. Journal: Environment and Ecology. -- https://environmentandecology.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/MS12-1.pdf
PUBLICATIONS -- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report or peer-reviewed paper specifically on BRG-3 found in the search results.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The search returned only US retail sellers of unrelated pigeon pea (gandules) seed, which were discarded. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, UAS(B) seed sales or dealer listing for BRG-3 was found. Check the UAS(B) seed unit and the Seednet portal directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Karnataka, as given in the CSC record. No state recommendation list for BRG-3 was found in the search results. The UAS(B) release list confirms the release came from UAS(B), but it does not name the states.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: described as resistant by the UAS Bangalore pigeonpea programme page (which also describes BRG 5 as suitable for both dhal and vegetable use) and as totally resistant to wilt in a seed-production presentation. Sterility mosaic disease: rated resistant in a 2018 Kharif screening at Latur, alongside other BRG entries (Dethe et al., 2024, abstract). The degree of resistance (level) is not stated in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod-borer or other insect resistance: Not found in searched sources. UAS pages list BRG 5 only in frontline demonstrations and general pest-screening programmes, without a resistance rating.

agronomic_details.yield: 10-12 q/ha (CSC table). In an intercropping trial, pigeonpea intercropped with black gram gave a pigeonpea yield of 1.85 t/ha, higher than sole pigeonpea; sole BRG-5 yield value not separately reported in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data for BRG 5 were returned.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Karnataka, southern zone (SZ-Karnataka), per CSC table; suitable for southern Karnataka per seed-production presentation. Also suitable for dhal and vegetable use (bold green seed) per UAS page.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 160-170 days (CSC table and UAS page); sole BRG-5 matured in 170-180 days in an intercropping trial at 120 cm row spacing
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Indeterminate, semi-spreading, red flowers, brown seed (CSC table); red flowers, dark brown seed, bold green seed suitable as vegetable (UAS page)
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Intercropping trial: sole BRG-5 at 120 cm row spacing matured in 170-180 days; pigeonpea + black gram gave higher pigeonpea yield (1.85 t/ha) than sole pigeonpea. (2) UAS GKVK dryland programme: included as a promising pulse variety compared with local cultivars (BRG-1, BRG-2, BRG-5 grouped together); no BRG 5-only yield data reported. (3) Frontline demonstrations and general pest-screening programmes list BRG 5, without results specific to the variety. (4) 2018 Kharif screening at Latur rated BRG 5 resistant to sterility mosaic disease, alongside other BRG entries.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

Results about field pea varieties (Pant Marter, Rachna, etc.) were discarded. The evidence below refers to BRG 5 under the Seednet/CSC name "BRG 5" in pigeonpea -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf

EVIDENCE DIGEST: BS 158 (CSC release name) / BS - 1 (Seednet name), rice (CSC) / pigeon pea (Seednet), Bayer BioScience Pvt. Ltd, released 2016-08-12, recommended state Madhya Pradesh

Search budget: all 4 allowed web_search queries were used. No search returned a page that names BS 158 or BS - 1 in a rice or pigeon pea context, so every heading below is "No evidence found" unless noted.

Name and crop check: The CSC record says crop "rice" and Seednet says "PIGEON PEA (RED GRAM/ARHAR)". The two records disagree on crop, and I found no source to settle it. Searches on "BS 158" returned unrelated rice items (IRRI 158, NSIC RC 158, Hashemi rice, Mississippi trial entries). Searches on "BS 1" with pigeon pea returned unrelated products and reviews. None of these is attributed to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searched "BS 158 rice variety" and "BS 158 pigeon pea research". Returned only brown spot (Bipolaris oryzae) resistance papers on other rice lines, which I discarded because they name other varieties.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. Same searches as above. Brown spot and pod borer material was not linked to BS 158 or BS - 1 and was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. Searched "BS 158 pigeon pea research". Returned general pigeon pea agronomy and Kenyan vegetable pigeon pea trials, which are other cultivars.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. Returned QTL work on rice brown spot resistance (bsr1) in other lines, and a pigeon pea SSR diversity study on accessions that do not include BS 158 or BS - 1.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. Searched "BS 158 Bayer BioScience developed by". Returned only Bayer corporate and unrelated Bayer pages. Bayer India's profile lists "Bayer BioScience Private Limited" as a Bayer Group legal entity (https://www.bayer.in/en-in/about-us/bayer-in-india), but no page links that entity to this variety, so I do not attribute any breeder to it.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. Only the Bayer India corporate profile was returned (https://www.bayer.in/en-in/about-us/bayer-in-india), and it gives no contact details for a variety or breeding team. No email, phone, or address was found for this variety.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, thesis, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh record naming BS 158 or BS - 1 was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Searched "BS 1 pigeon pea seed availability Madhya Pradesh". Returned Agrostar's listing for Bombay Super 20 pigeon pea (https://agrostar.in/product/bombay-super-20-pigeon-pea-1-kg-seeds/AGS-S-4234?language=en&state=madhya-pradesh), which is a different variety, and generic trader listings, which I discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found for this variety. The DPD list of centrally released pigeon pea varieties was returned (http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf). It covers Madhya Pradesh entries, but the excerpts I saw do not include BS 158 or BS - 1, so it does not support the Madhya Pradesh recommendation. The full PDF should be checked directly for either name before this field is filled.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNS-11 (Navya), Sugarcane

Name mapping: The evidence refers to CoN 13072, which NAU lists as "Gujarat Navsari Sugarcane – 11", also called Navya. The Seednet name "GNS-11 (Navya) (CoN 13072)" and the variety_name "GNS-11" both match this entry. No Seednet portal page was retrieved, so no Seednet-specific evidence is reported. Release year: the NAU document gives 2018, not the 2021 in the record. No CSC release minute for CoN 13072 was retrieved. The 2023 notification list in the results does not include it.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- CoN 13072 was among varieties found moderately resistant to red rot in the NAU technology report, a finding stated for the variety set rather than a field-trial measurement. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/43d3d-technologies-developed-2025.pdf
- A separate NAU item grades the same variety as moderately resistant to whip smut. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/43d3d-technologies-developed-2025.pdf
- Salinity: a Navsari (Main Sugarcane Research Station) study screened CoN-13072 against NaCl levels, using rhizobacteria, in tissue-culture conditions. Root length, shoot-root ratio, leaf area and chlorophyll index were recorded, and the variety showed the highest values in several of these traits. This is a laboratory/tissue-culture screen, not a field result, and the page's date is unclear. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368327160_Sugarcane_plant_growth_promoting_rhizo_bacterial_interaction_for_enhanced_salinity_tolerance
- Drought, heat, flood and submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Red rot: moderately resistant (MR) in the NAU table. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/43d3d-technologies-developed-2025.pdf
- Wilt: MR in the NAU table. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/43d3d-technologies-developed-2025.pdf
- Whip smut: moderately resistant per the NAU technology report. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/43d3d-technologies-developed-2025.pdf
- Insect pests and nematodes: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Cane yield 132.53 t/ha, sugar yield 17.86 t/ha, juice sucrose 19.11%, as tabulated for CoN 13072 by NAU. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/43d3d-technologies-developed-2025.pdf
- Maturity: the variety is described as early maturing, taking about 10 to 12 months, in a newspaper report on "Navya". The report is not an official source. -- https://allgujaratnews.in/en/gujarat-new-sugarcane-variety-which-produces-more-than-any-other-variety-in-india/
- A later trial of clones used CoN 13072 as the standard check. It was surpassed for stalk length, several sucrose and CCS traits, and germination. The trial's location and authors were not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://www.agriculturaljournals.com/archives/2025/vol7issue9/PartB/7-9-24-487.pdf
- An evaluation of CON 13072 reported plant height of 270.60 cm, Brix 18.47% and purity 79.33%. The table extraction is garbled and the trial site and season are not confirmed. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue10/PartL/11-9-344-797.pdf
- Ratooning, tillering, and germination for this variety specifically: No evidence found beyond the check comparisons above.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: the NAU table names Co 86032 G.C. as a parent. The record's statement that the male parent is unknown (general cross) was not verified by any retrieved page. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/43d3d-technologies-developed-2025.pdf
- Breeding method: the NAU table gives the breeding-line code CoN 13072 and a Navsari origin, but the breeding method is not stated. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/43d3d-technologies-developed-2025.pdf
- QTL, marker, or genome studies: No evidence found.
- Tissue culture: the Navsari station produces tissue-culture plantlets at scale, but no source ties CoN 13072 specifically to that programme. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/navsari.htm

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder names: No evidence found. The retrieved pages name no individual breeder for CoN 13072.
- Developing institution: Navasari Agricultural University (NAU), Main Sugarcane Research Station (MSRS), Navsari. The variety is listed among NAU-released sugarcane varieties. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/43d3d-technologies-developed-2025.pdf
- The station's own page lists earlier NAU releases (CoN 07072 and CoN 09072), not CoN 13072, but describes the station's role in breeder seed production. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/navsari.htm
- NAU reports 9 sugarcane varieties released and a research history at Navsari from the 1960s. -- https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or personal contact was found.
- Institute-level: Navsari Agricultural University website, https://nau.in (no phone, email or postal address was retrieved from the search results). The NAU "NAU Varieties" page links to the station's own website. -- https://nau.in/nauvariety
- Main Sugarcane Research Station address and phone: No evidence found beyond the name "Main Sugarcane Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University, Navsari".
- ICAR Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore (institution-level, not the variety's developer): www.sugarcane.res.in. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/ICAR-SBIVision2050.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown (2025). Multi-cycle clone evaluation with CoN 13072 as check. Agricultural Journals (vol 7, issue 9, Part B), pp. 117 ff. -- https://www.agriculturaljournals.com/archives/2025/vol7issue9/PartB/7-9-24-487.pdf
- Authors not shown (2022). Evaluation of sugarcane genotypes including CON 13072. The Pharma Innovation Journal 11(10): 1020-1024. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue10/PartL/11-9-344-797.pdf
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Sugarcane plant growth promoting rhizobacterial interaction for enhanced salinity tolerance, on CoN-13072 and CoN-13073, from MSRS Navsari tissue-culture laboratories. ResearchGate. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368327160_Sugarcane_plant_growth_promoting_rhizo_bacterial_interaction_for_enhanced_salinity_tolerance
- Not found: KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports, DOI-indexed papers specifically on CoN 13072.
- Discarded: the Journal of Sugarcane Research deep-learning paper (181 genotypes, no CoN 13072 named in the retrieved text). Other items were unrelated crops or other varieties.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet: No evidence found; no Seednet page was retrieved.
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales, private dealers: No evidence found for CoN 13072. The "Navya" hits were okra and bhindi products and are discarded.
- General context only: MSRS reports producing about 500 tonnes of breeder seed a year for improved varieties in general. This is not variety-specific. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/navsari.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gujarat. The NAU report lists CoN 13072 under varieties released for general cultivation in Gujarat, through the State Seed Sub Committee. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/43d3d-technologies-developed-2025.pdf
- It was not in the 2023 CSC notification list of ten varieties, so the notification route for national release is unconfirmed. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-10-new-varieties-of-sugarcane-for-farmers/

Broader agro-climatic fit beyond these trial conditions: Not found in searched sources.

GT 102 under drip irrigation with sugarcane-trash mulch at 0.8 PEF; drip with mulch saved about 49% irrigation water relative to surface irrigation; no yield value reported in the digest. STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in GT-102. The search returned general pigeonpea and field pea material only. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Listed as resistant to sterility mosaic disease (SMD) and as tolerant of pod borer. Indeterminate, spreading plant with white, bold seed; state-released 2007 by SVRC, Navsari Agricultural University, Gujarat. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Same DPD table gives SMD resistance and a wilt/tolerance note for the neighbouring GT 103/GT 104 entries, not GT-102. Do not transfer those to GT-102. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for wilt or Phytophthora resistance specific to GT-102. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- DPD table lists maturity of about 100-110 days and yield of about 15-16 q/ha for GT 102. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Drip irrigation and mulching trial with cv. GT-102 (CV. GT-102) as the test variety; the paper reports a maximum yield of about 3318 kg/ha and recommends it for rabi sowing in the trial conditions. Sown 21 November, row spacing 60 x 20 cm (paired rows) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-2-2019/M.A.%20Solanki,%20et%20al.pdf
- NAU rabi pigeonpea report: cv. GT 102 used for drip irrigation with sugarcane-trash mulch and scheduling at 0.8 PEF; drip with mulch saved about 49% irrigation water relative to surface irrigation. -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/6a8db-pfdc_published-paper.pdf
- No evidence found for multi-location AICRP trial results for GT-102 in the retrieved pages. -- (searched)

GENETICS AND QTL
- Combining ability study: GT 102 identified as a superior parent for early flowering, with significant negative general combining ability (GCA) effects, and as a good general combiner for seed yield. Authors, year and journal not shown in retrieved text. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6012
- Genome-wide association study of antioxidant activity and anti-nutritional factors lists GT-102 among the pigeonpea varieties tested. No QTL or marker result specific to GT-102 was found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383525328_Genome_wide_association_study_of_antioxidant_activity_in_pigeonpea_germplasm
- Parentage: No evidence found. The input record says "Not specified", and no source gave a cross.

- Station: The Pulses and Castor Research Station, Mega Seed Project, NAU, is acknowledged as supplying GT-102 seed for an amino acid study. The input's "Pulse Research Station" name was not found. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42535-025-01557-8

The Seednet crop name "PIGEON PEA (RED GRAM/ARHAR)" matches the evidence. The year of release conflicts: DPD lists 2007 (SVRC), while the input says 2016-08-12. Seednet itself was not retrieved.
