search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GUJARAT TUR 108 (BANAS UJJWAL) / SEEDNET NAME GT 108: BANAS UJJWAL -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name and crop check: the record lists the crop as "fieldpea", but every source found is for pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan, tur/arhar/red gram). The evidence below treats the variety as pigeonpea. The Seednet crop name (PIGEON PEA) agrees with the sources.
Name check: the release proposal uses "Gujarat Tur 108 (GT 108 : Banas Ujjwal)", which matches the variety_name field. No Seednet portal page was retrieved, so the seednet_variety_name is not independently confirmed. The code SKNP 1614 appeared in no retrieved source.
Release date: the only dated source is the 17th Combined AGRESCO meeting (2021), which proposed the variety for release. The 2022-10-26 release date in the record could not be verified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistant reaction to sterility mosaic disease (SMD) reported in the release proposal -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
No drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence evidence found for GT 108 (searched) -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
SMD resistance is the only disease or pest reaction recorded for GT 108 -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
No Fusarium wilt, pod borer, pod fly, or Phytophthora data for GT 108 found (searched) -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Average seed yield of 2400 kg/ha, reported as 36.27, 12.82, 13.15, 12.19 and 21.40 per cent above the checks BDN 2, GJP 1 and others (the check list is truncated in the source) -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
Maturity of about 174 days, within the 166-185 day medium group -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
Plant type: semi-spreading, yellow flowers, straight green pods with brown streaks, creamy-white seed -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
Seed-rate and fertilizer edits (2.5-3 kg/ha seed; NPKS 50:25:40:20 kg/ha) were requested by the meeting -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
No field-trial or multi-location data for GT 108 beyond the release table found -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No parentage, pedigree, marker, or QTL study for GT 108 found. Parentage is not specified in the record, and no source gave it -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
Pigeonpea combining-ability and heterosis studies at the Pulses Research Station, SDAU (2019-2020) used Banas, GT 102, GT 103, GT 100, GT 1 and SKNP lines, but GT 108 is not among the named parents -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6012 and https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6013

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: S.D. Agricultural University (SDAU), Pulses Research Station, Sardarkrushinagar, Gujarat. The release proposal was assigned to the Research Scientist (Pulses), PRS, SDAU, Sardarkrushinagar -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
Named lead breeder: not found in any source (searched) -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
Meeting action points for the proposal: state that breeder seed availability must be mentioned; verify phenolic-compound data; restrict recommendation to north Gujarat and rename accordingly (outcome not found) -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
Institute context: the PRS at Sardarkrushinagar is listed as a centre for pulses seed production -- https://icar-iipr.org.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php

CONTACT DETAILS
Centre: Pulses Research Station, SKNagar. Address: S.D. Agricultural University, Sardarkrushinagar (Gujarat). Centre incharge: Dr. M. P. Patel. Email: rspulses@sdau.edu.in (assembled from a line-split listing). Mobile: 9428137237 -- https://icar-iipr.org.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php
Note: this is a station-level contact from a seed listing, not a breeder contact. No breeder email or phone was found.
Other SDAU names found (not confirmed as GT 108 breeders): Dr. P. T. Patel, Research Scientist (Seed), SDAU, Sardarkrushinagar -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
Not stated (2021). Proceedings of the Seventeenth Meeting of Combined AGRESCO of SAUs and Kamdhenu University (release proposal for GT 108, item 17.1.1.35). Combined AGRESCO report -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
Peer-reviewed or thesis papers on GT 108 itself: no evidence found (searched) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6012

SEED AVAILABILITY
Breeder seed availability was requested in the proposal but no quantity was found -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
The ICAR-IIPR pulses seed hub listing did not show GT 108 in the retrieved portion; the Pulses Research Station SKNagar entry shows only other varieties -- https://icar-iipr.org.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php
GSFC markets Tur seed under the Sardar brand, but the variety is not named -- https://www.gsfclimited.com/seeds
Private listing of "Research Tur & Arhar Seeds" (variety not named) -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/research-tur-arhar-seeds-3092076612.html
No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sale record for GT 108 found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Proposal text: farmers of Gujarat state growing pigeonpea in kharif season -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
Meeting action: propose the variety for north Gujarat instead of the whole state, with a matching name change; final decision not found -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf

NAME AND CROP CHECK: The retrieved sources name IPA 15-2 (Sharada) as a pigeonpea (red gram/arhar) variety, which matches the Seednet crop name "PIGEON PEA (RED GRAM/ARHAR)". They do not support the "fieldpea" crop in the record. The IIPR fieldpea listing names IPF 99-25 (Adarsh), not IPA 15-2. Findings below are therefore for the pigeonpea entry. Variety-name matches were searched under "IPA 15-2" and "IPA 15-2 (Sharada)"; no source used "IPA 15-2" as a fieldpea. Searches: 4 of 4 used.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
The variety is reported as resistant to Fusarium wilt and sterility mosaic disease (SMD). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The searches returned no such claims for IPA 15-2.

DISEASE AND PEST:
Wilt resistance was recorded at 15.11% and sterility mosaic disease resistance at 15.62%. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jfl-34-1-010
Parental resistance: the female parent NDA 1 shows resistance to SMD, and the male parent MAL 13 shows resistance to wilt. -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/297/174/701
Insect pest reaction: a table of IPA 15-2 reaction to insect pests is cited, but its values were not retrieved. -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/297/174/701

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
Maturity: duration is given as 240-255 days. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varity/
Potential yield: 28-33 q/ha. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varity/
Average grain yield of 28 q/ha across NEPZ locations. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
AICRP testing 2017-18 to 2019-20 gave a weighted mean of 2266 kg/ha over six locations. -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/view/297
Highest single-location yield of 2998 kg/ha, at Varanasi. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jfl-34-1-010
Yield superiority of 23.47% over the national check Bahar and 24.38% over the zonal check IPA 203 (Prakash). -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jfl-34-1-010
Breeder seed indent of about 26 qt over the last three years. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
Release: listed as released in 2020 by CVRC. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varity/

GENETICS AND QTL:
Parentage: developed by crossing NDA 1 and MAL 13, via pedigree breeding. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jfl-34-1-010 (the record's "Not specified" parentage should be updated)
NDA 1 was selected from a Faizabad local landrace. -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/297/174/701
No evidence found for QTL, marker or molecular studies specific to IPA 15-2.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: IPA 206 (variety_name, CSC minutes) / IPA 206 (seednet_variety_name, Seednet portal), Pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan). Both names were searched. The results use "IPA 206" and "IPA 206 (Ganga)", and no page gave a Seednet listing or variety code A0312198.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Resistant to wilt and sterility mosaic disease (SMD), per the IIPR variety table for IPA 206 (Ganga) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Apnikheti describes IPA 206 as resistant to wilt, as a long-duration variety -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/pigeon-pea-tur
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to IPA 206. The search returned general pigeonpea pages and an ICRISAT heat-tolerant pigeonpea story, which concerns a different cultivar -- https://newsarenaindia.com/states/heat-tolerant-pigeon-pea-indian-scientists-crack-the-code/47136

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Wilt (Fusarium udum) and SMD resistance are listed for IPA 206 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/
- No pod-borer or pod-fly resistance evidence for IPA 206 was found. Pest pages retrieved concerned the cultivar Bahar and UPAS-120 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327270198_Pigeonpea_and_Integrated_Pest_Management (excluded, different variety)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Duration 245-250 days; potential yield 25-26 q/ha; recommended area Uttar Pradesh; year of release recorded as 2019 by SVRC (UP) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/ and https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Discrepancy: the input gives release year 2020. The IIPR source says 2019. Treat 2019 as the source-backed value and flag the conflict.
- Average yield about 10 q/acre, long duration, for UP -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/pigeon-pea-tur (consistent with 25-26 q/ha)
- A consumer blog gives 245-250 days and 10 q/acre. It is secondary and low-reliability -- https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/tur-crop-cultivation-in-india
- No multi-location AICRP trial data for IPA 206 was found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources):
- Parentage (Bahar x AC 314-314), breeding method, and gene/QTL data: No evidence found for IPA 206. The only Bahar x AC 314-314 pedigree retrieved is for IPA 203, a different variety, so it is excluded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369745589_IPA_203_A_Promising_Variety_of_long-duration_pigeonpea
- The parentage in the input is therefore unverified.
- Morphology from the IIPR table: purple seed coat, golden-yellow cotyledon, medium seed of 10-11 g per 100 seeds -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Genome resources and QTL: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Developing institution: ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur, Crop Improvement Division -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Lead scientist: Dr.SatheeshNaik SJ, Scientist Senior Scale -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- The breeder listed is ICAR-IIPR; no separate SAU or other institution was found for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- Dr.SatheeshNaik SJ, Scientist Senior Scale, ICAR-IIPR Kanpur (Crop Improvement Division), phone 9743149596, email Satheesh.SJ@icar.gov.in -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Institute postal address: No evidence found for the IIPR address. Institute site: https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/

PUBLICATIONS:
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper specifically on IPA 206 was found. Excluded: IPA 203 paper (different variety) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369745589_IPA_203_A_Promising_Variety_of_long-duration_pigeonpea ; a generic pigeonpea breeding chapter that does not name IPA 206 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309136303_Breeding_Improved_Cultivars_of_Pigeonpea_in_India
- No KrishiKosh search could be run in the four-search budget.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- Breeder-seed indent: IIPR reports an average of 7 quintals of breeder seed indented over three years for IPA 206 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Seednet listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer stock for IPA 206: No evidence found. The IndiaMart and other dealer listings returned were for IPA 15-6 or unnamed arhar and were excluded -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/pigeon-pea-seeds-pusa-ipa-15-6-arher-seeds-toor-2854226780048.html

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/ and https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/pigeon-pea-tur

Note: Seednet was not searched separately, so the Seednet name and variety code A0312198 are unverified.

disease_resistance.summary: IIPR's variety entry for the pigeon pea hybrid IPH 09-5 reports resistance to Fusarium wilt and sterility mosaic disease (SMD). The genetic enhancement page describes IPH 15-03 and IPH 09-5 as multiple disease-resistant hybrids for the NWPZ, without naming specific diseases. A pigeon pea pest/disease guidance page lists wilt and SMD resistance as a selection criterion for IPH 09-5; this supports the criterion but is not independent confirmation. The IIPR entry is the primary basis for this claim. The record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified', so the record and IIPR sources do not agree in detail. IPH 15-03 is described as resistant to common pests and diseases with no specifics, and it is listed under the Seednet name, so it is not treated as confirmed for this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'. The only pest-related statement concerns IPH 15-03 (Seednet name) as resistant to common pests and diseases, with no specifics, and it is not attributed to IPH 09-5.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NOTE: The evidence shows IPH 09-5 and IPH 15-03 are pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan) hybrids, not fieldpea. The fieldpea-related pages returned were about other varieties (IPFD, IPF, Aman) and were discarded. The Seednet name IPH 15-03 is also a pigeonpea hybrid. The recommended-states list in the record differs from the IIPR text.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistant to Fusarium wilt and sterility mosaic disease (SMD), per IIPR's variety entry for the pigeonpea hybrid IPH 09-5 -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/ (also https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/)
IIPR's genetic enhancement page describes IPH15-03 and IPH 09-5 as short-duration, high-yielding, multiple disease-resistant pigeonpea hybrids for the NWPZ -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/research-achievements/ (translate.goog mirror: https://www-icar--iipr-org-in.translate.goog/research-achievements/)
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to IPH 09-5 or IPH 15-03.

DISEASE AND PEST
Wilt and SMD resistance for IPH 09-5 (see STRESS TOLERANCE) -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
IPH 15-03 described as resistant to common pests and diseases, with no specifics -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-hybrid-pigeonpea-iph-15-03-recommended-for-punjab-delhi-haryana-and-uttar-pradesh/
Wilt and SMD resistance listed as a selection criterion for IPH 09-5 in pigeonpea pest/disease guidance -- https://wikifarmer.com/library/en/article/principles-of-selecting-the-best-varieties-and-hybrids-for-pigeon-pea-cultivation

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
IPH 09-5 averages about 20 q/ha across NWPZ locations -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/
IPH 09-5 described as an early-duration pigeonpea hybrid -- https://www.icar.org.in/index.php/en/node/10517 (also https://icar.org.in/en/node/10517)
IPH 15-03 (Seednet name): released 2020, matures in 153-155 days, productivity 16.0 q/ha -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-hybrid-pigeonpea-iph-15-03-recommended-for-punjab-delhi-haryana-and-uttar-pradesh/ (source is a secondary news page; no primary trial report found)
IPH 09-5 listed among release-year entries as 2021 in IIPR's 2014-2025 table; the record says 2020-11-09 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/research-achievements/ (translate.goog mirror above)

GENETICS AND QTL
IPH 09-5 and IPH 15-03 are CMS-based (cytoplasmic male sterility) hybrids within the hybrid system developed by ICAR-NARS and ICRISAT -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/view/169
Parentage given in the record ("PA 163 A x AK 250189R") was not found in any source. No QTL or marker study for either name was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed at ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur, Crop Improvement Division -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/

disease_resistance.research_summary: IIPR's variety entry for the pigeon pea hybrid IPH 09-5 reports resistance to Fusarium wilt and sterility mosaic disease (SMD). The genetic enhancement page describes IPH 15-03 and IPH 09-5 as multiple disease-resistant hybrids for the NWPZ, without naming specific diseases. A pigeon pea pest/disease guidance page lists wilt and SMD resistance as a selection criterion for IPH 09-5; this supports the criterion but is not independent confirmation. The IIPR entry is the primary basis for this claim. The record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified', so the record and IIPR sources do not agree in detail. IPH 15-03 is described as resistant to common pests and diseases with no specifics, and it is listed under the Seednet name, so it is not treated as confirmed for this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
IPH 15-03 (CSC/CVRC minute name) and IPH 15-03 (Seednet name) are the same string, so all evidence below refers to the same name. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so no finding is attributed to Seednet. Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as a hybrid with resistance to wilt (Fusarium udum), brown seed and medium seed size (8–8.54 g per 100 seeds) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Same ICAR-IIPR listing gives a potential yield of 24–25 q/ha, duration 150–155 days, recommended area North West Plain Zone, and "timely sown and rainfed" ecology -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/cimprovment/
- Described as early maturing and resistant to wilt in a general agronomy course page -- https://indianagriexam.com/courses/general-agriculture-course-for-for-competitive-exams/lesson/cultivation-of-pigeon-pea-cajanus-cajan-module-17/
- Heat, drought, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The sources name wilt resistance only.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Fusarium wilt resistance is stated for IPH 15-03 on the ICAR-IIPR pages above (https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/ ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/cimprovment/).
- A news article calls it resistant to common pests and diseases, with no named pest or disease -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-hybrid-pigeonpea-iph-15-03-recommended-for-punjab-delhi-haryana-and-uttar-pradesh/ (generic, low weight)
- Sterility mosaic resistance: No evidence found for IPH 15-03. The sterility-mosaic wording on the IIPR cimprovment page sits beside a different entry.
- Pod borer or other insect resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released 2020 (CVRC). Duration 150–155 days; potential yield 24–25 q/ha -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/
- Average productivity of 16.0 q/ha and maturity of 153–155 days in a 2025 news report. This conflicts with the 24–25 q/ha IIPR figure; both are reported -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-hybrid-pigeonpea-iph-15-03-recommended-for-punjab-delhi-haryana-and-uttar-pradesh/
- Pigeonpea hybrid review: IPH 15-03 is suited to pigeonpea–wheat rotation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/46194379_Prospects_of_Pigeonpea_Hybrids_in_Indian_Agriculture
- Multi-location or field-trial yield data: No evidence found beyond the figures above.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage PA 163 A x AK 250189R: user-supplied. No search result confirmed it. The AK 250189R line appears in a different population in the Frontiers study below, which is not attributed to IPH 15-03.
- Breeding method: first cytoplasmic male sterility (CMS)-based pigeonpea hybrid in the series; the review names it as the first CMS-based hybrid -- https://era.dpi.qld.gov.au/id/eprint/15166/1/1.+Review+paper_50+Yr_R.pdf
- Listed among four CMS-based hybrids (ICPH 2671, ICPH 2740, IPH 15-03, IPH 09-5) released for cultivation -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/view/169
- Marker study: ten SSR markers were tested on IPH 15-03 and its A, B and R parents; marker CcGM17648 gave the IPH 15-03 profile -- https://public-pages-files-2025.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2017.00377/xml/nlm
- Breeding-line codes for A and R parents: No evidence found.
- Genome resources (genome assembly, reference data): No evidence found for IPH 15-03.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (ICAR-IIPR), Kanpur -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Crop Improvement Division lists IPH 15-03 among its releases -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/
- Lead breeder name for IPH 15-03: No evidence found. The Division's pigeonpea breeder (Ashok Kumar Parihar) is named on the Division page and authored a hybrid-breeding review that covers IPH 15-03. That link is inferred, not stated -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/ ; https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/view/169
- Station: Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/view/169

CONTACT DETAILS
- Ashok Kumar Parihar, Pigeonpea and Field pea Breeder (Division of Crop Improvement, ICAR-IIPR): ashoka.parihar@gmail.com; ashok.parihar@icar.gov.in -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/ (the first address is a personal Gmail; treat it with caution)
- Institute postal address: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur – 208 024, Uttar Pradesh, India -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/view/169
- Institute phone and official institute email: No evidence found in the sources retrieved.
- Institute contact page URL: https://iipr.icar.gov.in/cimprovment/ (Division page; a full contact page was not retrieved)

PUBLICATIONS
- Parihar, A. K. (year not retrieved). Pigeonpea hybrid breeding in India. Journal of Food Legumes -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/view/169 (discusses the four CMS hybrids including IPH 15-03)
- Saxena et al. (year not retrieved). Hybrid pigeonpea: The gains and hiccups. Review paper (50-year review) -- https://era.dpi.qld.gov.au/id/eprint/15166/1/1.+Review+paper_50+Yr_R.pdf (describes IPH 15-03 as the first CMS-based hybrid)
- Authors not retrieved (2017). Frontiers in Plant Science, DOI 10.3389/fpls.2017.00377 -- https://public-pages-files-2025.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2017.00377/xml/nlm (SSR marker study including IPH 15-03; title not retrieved)
- Book chapter (year not retrieved). Springer, DOI 10.1007/978-981-96-0506-4_7 -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-96-0506-4_7 (mentions IPH 15-03 as a CMS-based hybrid suited to pigeonpea–wheat rotation)
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports, peer-reviewed field-trial papers: No evidence found in the searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- National Seeds Corporation, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales, private dealers: No evidence found.
- ICAR-IIPR notes that its breeder seed indent for the parental lines averaged about 2 q over three years -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/ (this is a parental-line indent, not hybrid seed sales)
- Seednet portal listing (variety code A0312185): No evidence found; no Seednet page was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Punjab, Delhi, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-hybrid-pigeonpea-iph-15-03-recommended-for-punjab-delhi-haryana-and-uttar-pradesh/
- ICAR-IIPR lists the recommended area as the North West Plain Zone, which covers these states -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- A groundnut water-stress review states that JAL 42, described as an advance breeding line, was an ideal plant type under irrigated summer conditions, linked to higher branch number and leaf area index. This is not evidence of a released variety's drought tolerance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262456369_Water_deficit_stress_and_its_management_in_groundnut

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The "JAL-42 groundnut variety release notification stress tolerance" search returned only generic groundnut disease and drought pages that do not name JAL-42.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The same review lists JAL 42 among the plant-type comparisons used for summer irrigated groundnut, with the trial details not given on the page. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262456369_Water_deficit_stress_and_its_management_in_groundnut
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Other results from the search (KVK on-farm trials in Ariyalur and Dindigul, ICRISAT ICGV 91114, JAU high-oleic line) name other groundnut varieties and do not mention JAL-42, so they were discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The ICRISAT genomic-tools review is about groundnut breeding in general and does not name JAL-42. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4794498/ (discarded, not linked to this variety)
GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage ("selection from cross No. 148 x C11; cross made 1971; selection from F2 in 1975") comes from the input record, not from any search result. No independent source was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No search result names a breeder or developing institution for JAL-42. The "Orissa" institution value in the input record is not confirmed by any source. The ICRISAT and JAU pages found are about other varieties and were discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute, or contact page for JAL-42 was returned.

PUBLICATIONS -- Authors not stated (year not stated). Water deficit stress and its management in groundnut. ResearchGate PDF (a compilation that names JAL 42 but does not identify it as a paper about the variety) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262456369_Water_deficit_stress_and_its_management_in_groundnut
PUBLICATIONS -- No other paper naming JAL-42 was found. The KrishiKosh, AICRP and journal search was run through the "JAL-42 groundnut research paper trial" query, which returned no other matching item.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The "JAL 42 groundnut seed availability" search returned generic seed sellers (an IndiaMART Jalgaon listing, a US seed company) and an Andhra Pradesh village seed-bank case study, none of which names JAL-42. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The input record says "Not specified", and no search result gives a notified state or zone for JAL-42.

Name check: The Seednet name "JA-4" is listed under pigeon pea (red gram/arhar), which is a different crop. No search was run for "JA-4" on its own, because the four-query limit was used on the groundnut name. No JA-4 evidence was collected, and any finding for pigeon pea would be excluded under the crop-match rule. A separate JA-4 search is needed to confirm whether the Seednet record is a mislabelled groundnut entry or a separate pigeon pea variety.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: LRG 133-33 (variety_name "LRG 133-33"; seednet_variety_name "LRG 133-33", which is identical, so no separate Seednet evidence was found). Crop: pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan, red gram/arhar). The ANGRAU sheet also gives the alias "LRG 133-33 (Sowbhagya)". Searches run: 4 of 4. No Seednet portal page was returned, so no Seednet-specific finding is recorded.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Terminal drought escape, and resistance to wilt and sterility mosaic disease, are listed in the same DPD table row as LRG 133-33 (2021 entry, RARS Lam). The snippet is ambiguous about whether these traits belong to this row or the adjacent one, so treat them as unconfirmed -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No submergence, flood, salinity or heat tolerance evidence found for this variety. Searches were run for drought, not for these other stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Disease reaction under natural field conditions is noted for LRG 133-33 in the DPD table, but the specific disease scores are not in the retrieved text -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Wilt and sterility mosaic resistance: the DPD row is the only source. No separate pest-resistance evidence found.

- ANGRAU variety sheet: crop duration 165-170 days, kharif season, release 2020 via CVRC -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Redgram.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Phule 11082 (CSC variety code CoM 11082) / Seednet name PHULE-12

Search budget: four web_search queries were run in one batch. A fifth query failed with a server tool-use limit, so the contact, research, and stress checks are incomplete. Only the first 300 characters of each result were reviewed, so the findings below may miss detail in the full pages.

Name and crop mismatch: the CSC evidence refers to sugarcane under "Phule 11082" / "CoM 11082". The Seednet name "PHULE-12" is listed under pigeon pea (red gram/arhar). The PHULE-12 search returned only unrelated pigeon pea seed listings, so no evidence links PHULE-12 to sugarcane or to the CSC variety. Treat the Seednet entry as unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found in the retrieved snippets. The Padegaon page and the search results did not show drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for this variety. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found in the retrieved snippets. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Early-maturing sugarcane variety CoM 11082 (Phule 11082) is described as pre-released in Maharashtra for suru and preseason planting in 2018-19 and identified for the peninsular zone. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm
Note: this pre-release date (2018-19) differs from the year of release in the record (2022-10-26). Both should be checked against CSC release minutes.
A snippet on the same page lists "high sugar, high yield" and "spines on cane" with broad yellowish-green leaves. The snippet does not state which variety these traits belong to, so they are not attributed to Phule 11082 here. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The search did not target this topic.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Central Sugarcane Research Station, Padegaon is the developing station. The page describes it as having about eight decades of varietal work and says its earlier varieties Co 86032 and CoM 0265 cover more than 90% of Maharashtra's cane area. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm
Lead breeder name: not found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute page found: Central Sugarcane Research Station, Padegaon (AICRP on Sugarcane page, ICAR-IISR). -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm
No breeder name, email, phone, or postal address was captured. The station's contact details were not extracted, so the contact page should be checked directly.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The search did not return peer-reviewed papers, AICRP annual reports, theses, or KrishiKosh records for Phule 11082 / CoM 11082. Research-specific searches were not completed because the tool limit was reached.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The Seednet-name search for PHULE-12 returned only unrelated commercial pigeon pea listings. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer source was identified for the sugarcane variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Maharashtra, per the record and the CSC/AICRP page noting pre-release there for suru and preseason. The same page identifies the variety for the peninsular zone. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PNPH-24 (Seednet name: PNPH 24, IET 21406), Rice

Name check: The CSC name "PNPH-24" and the Seednet name "PNPH 24 (IET 21406)" refer to the same entry in the notification lists. The retrieved evidence covers a hybrid rice variety. The CSC release year (2007) and institution (Prabhat Agri Biotech Ltd.) were not found in any retrieved source. Searches did not return a Seednet portal page directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under the PNPH 24 name (hybrid), the variety is listed as a medium-early hybrid suited to drought situations -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356605148_ADVANCED_BREEDING_STRATEGIES_FOR_RICE_IMPROVEMENT
- Same source group: PNPH 24 is classed as mid-early and able to sustain yield under drought situations -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489
- PNPH 24 is listed among mid-early maturing hybrids suitable for water-scarce situations -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/360464100_Irrigated_Rice_Breeding
- No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. The retrieved disease-scenario paper names PNPH 24 only in a list of varieties grown in Bihar and Jharkhand, with no resistance data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281737890_Public-private_partnership_for_hybrid_rice_Proceedings_of_the_6th_International_Hybrid_Rice_Symposium_The_disease_scenario_in_Jharkhand_Bihar_and_Uttar_Pradesh_India_with_reference_to_hybrid_rice

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 120-130 days, yield 5.8 to 6.9 t/ha (listed under the notified hybrid rice table) -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Same figures in the hybrid rice list of 1994-2021 -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/
- Super Hybrid Rice review table: 120-130 days, yield not given, Nuziveedu Seeds listed -- https://www.academia.edu/68324607/Super_Hybrid_Rice_in_China_and_India_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- Advisory listing: Vijay PNPH 24 for kharif/rabi in irrigated areas of Bihar, West Bengal, Odisha -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/paddy-cultivation-advisory-amid-covid-19/
- No multi-location trial data, no yield-trial results and no agronomy beyond the table entries were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, QTL or genome resources for PNPH 24 in the retrieved sources. The parentage string supplied in the request (PRN 1 A / IR 58025 CMS line; PRN 24 R restorer) could not be verified from any retrieved page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The notified entry names Nuziveedu Seeds Limited as the applicant/developer, not Prabhat Agri Biotech Ltd. -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Individual breeder or scientist names: No evidence found.
- Prabhat Agri Biotech Ltd.: No evidence found in any retrieved source.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level (only contact-type information found): Nuziveedu Seeds Limited, Medchal Mandal, Ranga Reddy-501401 (A.P.) -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Hybrid-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Email, phone, and institute contact page URL: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in the retrieved text (Rout D, Jena D, Singh V, Kumar M, Arsode P, Singh P, Katara JK, Samantaray S, Verma RL appear in a reference fragment, not confirmed as this paper's authors) (year not stated). Advanced Breeding Strategies for Rice Improvement. ResearchGate preprint, PNPH 24 named as a drought-suitable mid-early hybrid -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356605148_ADVANCED_BREEDING_STRATEGIES_FOR_RICE_IMPROVEMENT
- Authors not stated (year not stated). Irrigated Rice Breeding. ResearchGate, lists PNPH 24 as mid-early -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/360464100_Irrigated_Rice_Breeding
- Authors not stated (year not stated). Hybrid Rice Research: Current Status and Prospects. IntechOpen chapter 73489, lists PNPH 24 in the mid-early group -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489
- Authors not stated (year not stated). Super Hybrid Rice in China and India: Current Status and Future Prospects. Academia.edu, reference table entry for PNPH 24 -- https://www.academia.edu/68324607/Super_Hybrid_Rice_in_China_and_India_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- Authors not stated (year not stated). Rice breeding in India: eight decades of journey towards enhancing the genetic gain for yield, nutritional quality, and commodity value. ResearchGate, mentions PNPH 24 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351749037_Rice_breeding_in_India_eight_decades_of_journey_towards_enhancing_the_genetic_gain_for_yield_nutritional_quality_and_commodity_value
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI specific to PNPH 24 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Assam Seed Corporation supply tenders included PNPH-24 among hybrid paddy varieties (undated news item, date unverified) -- https://assamtribune.com/anomalies-in-paddy-seed-supply-alleged
- Vijay PNPH 24 appears as a brand-named product in an advisory list. Whether this is the same product was not confirmed -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/paddy-cultivation-advisory-amid-covid-19/
- No NSC, KVK, SAU or current dealer listing for PNPH 24 was found. The Ajinkya R-24 product from agroshopy.com was discarded as a different variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified 10.09.2012, S.O. 2125(E), for Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
- Assam: an entry "PNPH24" in the 2011-2021 notified paddy list, S.O. 500(E) dated 29.01.2021, Assam. The name is written without the space or hyphen, so this link to PNPH 24 (IET 21406) is probable but not certain -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- The CSC release year of 2007 was not found in any source. The earliest evidence is the 2012 notification.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage "Brazil-1 x NP-60" from the CSC record was not confirmed by any search result. Note: the IARI page's parentage text (Amrapali x Sensation) refers to mango Pusa Peetamber and must not be attributed to papaya Pusa Peet. -- https://iari.res.in/en/fht-achievements.php

Acta Horticulturae 851: 81-88 -- DOI 10.17660/ActaHortic.2010.851.9 (https://www.actahort.org/books/851/851_9.htm). This paper covers older IARI papaya varieties and does not mention Pusa Peet.

drought.details: No drought data specific to PA 291 found in the digest. The 2023-24 Pantnagar study is a general pigeonpea diversity paper and does not provide PA 291 drought evidence.

heat.details: No heat-stress data specific to PA 291 found in the digest.

salinity.details: No salinity data specific to PA 291 found in the digest.

flood.details: No flood data specific to PA 291 found in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Verified: tolerance to Phytophthora stem blight (CSC centrally released pigeonpea table, listed as PA 291). Unverified: wilt resistance and good grain quality (secondary blog, no source given; the digest marks this as unverified). Not verified for PA 291: mosaic virus and powdery mildew resistance, which the blog credits to Pant Arhar 7 (Seednet name); identity with PA 291 is not confirmed. No specific PA 291 sterility mosaic disease (SMD) data found (general SMD review only).

pest_resistance.summary: Verified: tolerance to pod borer (CSC centrally released pigeonpea table, listed as PA 291). Insect-pest screening of 27 elite pigeonpea genotypes at Pantnagar (Kharif 2021-22) was found, but inclusion of PA 291 is not confirmed in the retrieved text. No other PA 291 pest data found.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC table (listed as PA 291): 16-18 q/ha (approximately 1600-1800 kg/ha, converted from q/ha). Blog-reported 18-23 q/acre (unverified, secondary source). Blog-reported 22-27 q/acre for Pant Arhar 7 (Seednet name); identity with PA 291 unconfirmed.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data for PA 291 found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for kharif sowing in the plains and hills of Uttarakhand, with sowing till mid-June in the plains (GBPUAT advisory). Listed as NWPZ in the CSC table, covering Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, West UP and the plains of Uttarakhand. A 2022 advisory lists PA 291 with Pant Arhar 3, UPAS 120, VL Arhar 1 and Pant Arhar 6 for plains and hills.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 140-150 days (CSC centrally released pigeonpea table, listed as PA 291)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. Early-maturing classification per Saxena (2019). The 2023-24 Pantnagar trial flagged PA-291 as promising for branches per plant (see field trials); no morphological description was found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Pantnagar 2023-24 trial (155 genotypes, randomised block design, 3 replications): PA-291 was flagged as promising among 11 genotypes for branches per plant, pods per plant, test weight and seed yield per plant. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pant Arhar-291 (CSC name, also written PA 291): listed as tolerant to Phytophthora stem blight and to pod borer in the centrally released pigeonpea table -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Arhar-291: a secondary blog describes it as wilt-resistant with good grain quality; this is unverified and lacks a source -- https://upaj.ag/blogs/articles/pigeon-pea-arhar-farming-nutrition-pest-and-disease-management
- Pant Arhar 7 (Seednet name): the same blog credits resistance to mosaic virus and powdery mildew. Evidence for this name is not confirmed as the same line as PA 291 -- https://upaj.ag/blogs/articles/pigeon-pea-arhar-farming-nutrition-pest-and-disease-management
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data specific to PA 291 found (the 2023-24 Pantnagar study is a general pigeonpea diversity paper) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/400706374_GENETIC_VARIABILITY_CORRELATION_PATH_ANALYSIS_AND_GENETIC_DIVERSITY_STUDIES_IN_PIGEON_PEA_CAJANUS_CAJAN_L_MILLSP

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pant Arhar-291 (CSC name): tolerance to Phytophthora stem blight and pod borer per the centrally released list -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Arhar-291 (CSC name): the blog's wilt-resistance claim is unverified -- https://upaj.ag/blogs/articles/pigeon-pea-arhar-farming-nutrition-pest-and-disease-management
- Pant Arhar 7 (Seednet name): blog reports mosaic and powdery mildew resistance; not verified for PA 291 -- https://upaj.ag/blogs/articles/pigeon-pea-arhar-farming-nutrition-pest-and-disease-management
- Insect-pest screening of 27 elite pigeonpea genotypes at Pantnagar (Kharif 2021-22). Inclusion of PA 291 not confirmed in the retrieved text -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42690-026-01944-x
- No specific PA 291 sterility mosaic data found (general SMD review only) -- https://www.ijltemas.in/submission/online/article/view/3713

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pant Arhar-291 (CSC name): 2008 release, 140-150 days maturity, 16-18 q/ha yield (listed as PA 291) -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Arhar-291 (CSC name): recommended for kharif sowing in plains and hills of Uttarakhand, with sowing till mid-June in plains -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/Extension_Edu/02.05.2020_Kharif_season_Advisory.pdf
- Pant Arhar-291: a 2022 advisory lists it with Pant Arhar 3, UPAS 120, VL Arhar 1 and Pant Arhar 6 for plains and hills -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/arhar-varieties-suitable-for-growing-in-kharif-in-uttarakhand-plains-and-hill/
- Pant Arhar-291: blog-reported yield of 18-23 q/acre (unverified, secondary source) -- https://upaj.ag/blogs/articles/pigeon-pea-arhar-farming-nutrition-pest-and-disease-management
- Pant Arhar 7 (Seednet name): blog-reported yield of 22-27 q/acre; identity with PA 291 unconfirmed -- https://upaj.ag/blogs/articles/pigeon-pea-arhar-farming-nutrition-pest-and-disease-management
- Pantnagar 2023-24 trial (155 genotypes, RBD, 3 reps): PA-291 flagged as promising for branches, pods per plant, test weight and seed yield per plant among 11 genotypes -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/400706374_GENETIC_VARIABILITY_CORRELATION_PATH_ANALYSIS_AND_GENETIC_DIVERSITY_STUDIES_IN_PIGEON_PEA_CAJANUS_CAJAN_L_MILLSP

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker or pedigree study for PA 291 found. Parentage is not stated in any source retrieved.
- Saxena (2019) groups PA 291 (2009) among early-maturing cultivars bred by hybridisation and selection -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbr.12696
- Pant Arhar 7 (Seednet name): no genetic record found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Pant Arhar-291 (CSC name): developing institution is G. B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar, per the centrally released list -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder for PA 291: no name found. The Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, GBPUAT, lists Dr. R.K. Panwar and Dr. S.K. Verma as PIs of the AICRP on Pigeonpea at Pantnagar. Their link to PA 291 is not confirmed -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/index.html
- Pant Arhar 7 (Seednet name): no institution or breeder linked to this name found.
- Institutional context: AICRP centre at GBPUAT Pantnagar, established 1966, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf
- Station: Norman E. Borlaug Crop Research Centre, Pantnagar (where pigeonpea screening trials were run) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42690-026-01944-x

- Naidu, G.R., Patnaik, H. & Hiranmayee, B.S.S. (2025). Early Detection of Sterility Mosaic Disease in Pigeon Pea Using Machine Learning and Regional Data Sources: A Review. IJLTEMAS -- DOI 10.51583/IJLTEMAS.2025.1412000020 (not specific to PA 291)
- Technical bulletin on pigeonpea cultivation, KVK Reasi (Jammu) -- https://kvkreasi.in/arhar.pdf (no PA 291 data)
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report or PA 291 field trial report found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Pant Arhar-291: GBPUAT advisory recommends it for Kharif sowing, but no seed source or price was found -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/Extension_Edu/02.05.2020_Kharif_season_Advisory.pdf

- Pantnagar Seeds (private brand, marketing offices in Uttarakhand): no arhar listing found -- https://www.pantnagarseeds.com/our-strength
- Seednet portal listing for "Pant Arhar 7": not retrieved (no search of seednet.gov.in returned results)

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Pant Arhar-291 (CSC name): listed as NWPZ, covering Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, West UP and the plains of Uttarakhand, not Uttarakhand alone -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Uttarakhand plains and hills per the GBPUAT kharif advisory -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/Extension_Edu/02.05.2020_Kharif_season_Advisory.pdf

NOTES FOR THE RECORD
- Crop mismatch: the input says "fieldpea", but all evidence refers to pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan, arhar). Field pea is a different crop. Please confirm the crop before using this record.
- Name mismatch: PA 291 and Pant Arhar-291 are treated as the same line. Pant Arhar 7 on Seednet is not confirmed as the same line.
- Release year: the CSC table gives 2008; Saxena (2019) gives 2009. Year of release is recorded as 2008 pending confirmation.

disease_resistance.summary: Listed as resistant to wilt and sterility mosaic disease in the central release table (dpd.gov.in, listed as 'Rev Lochan'/'Rajeev Lochan'). This evidence is recorded for pigeonpea, not chickpea, and is included with a crop-mismatch caveat. Input CSC data lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: An IGKV Raipur Entomology screening of local pigeonpea germplasm (pod borer complex work) reportedly placed Rajeevlochan third-least susceptible. The digest's ranking description is internally inconsistent (it names three entries ahead of Rajeevlochan while describing it as third-least susceptible), so this is not a confirmed resistance rating. This is pigeonpea evidence, not chickpea. Input CSC data lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Dpd.gov.in lists a yield of 18-19 q/ha (approximately 1800-1900 kg/ha) for Rajeevlochan (pigeonpea evidence). The input CSC average_yield field is blank ('Kg/Ha' with no value).

agronomic_details.adaptation: Per CSC input data: rainfed in dosa and kanhar soils (vertisols); irrigated (1-2 irrigations) in light soils and under late planting; grown on rice bunds (dorsa and kanhar soils); suitable for intercropping with soybean; suitable for normal to late sowing up to the first week of August; responsive to recommended fertilizer doses (20:40:20 kg NPK/ha); seed rate 20 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: INTERMEDIATE PLANT WITH GREEN AND MEDIUM LEAVES; GREEN STEM WITH PIGMENTATION AT BASE; MEDIUM BOLD SEED WITH ROUND, SMOOTH AND MAROON COLOURED SEED COAT.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) 2013-14 rabi trial at IGKV Raipur comparing six genotypes: Asha gave the highest seed yield; Rajeevlochan was statistically comparable to Laxmi and RPS-2007-106 (pigeonpea). (2) 2016-17 rabi trial of 20 genotypes at IGKV Raipur: Rajeevlochan recorded the most primary branches per plant (7.6) (pigeonpea). (3) Kharif 2017-18 plot trial at the IGKV Raipur research farm: Rajeevlochan used as the variety, sown 30 June 2017 at 20 kg/ha seed rate (pigeonpea). (4) Used as the check variety in a diallel study at the IGKV Raipur Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding (pigeonpea). Trial results are pigeonpea findings and should not be applied to chickpea without verification.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed as resistant to wilt and sterility mosaic disease, with maturity around 178 days and yield of 18-19 q/ha (evidence refers to "Rev Lochan"/"Rajeev Lochan", seednet name Rajeevlochan, pigeonpea) -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
Rajeevlochan is named as an IGKV Raipur pigeonpea genotype with a 2011 year-of-release entry; the release year differs from the 2010-12-23 date in the input -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Rajeevlochan.

DISEASE AND PEST
Rajeevlochan ranked as the third-least susceptible entry (after ICP 6999, ICP 7391 and ICP 7374 are named ahead of it in the ranking order, ICPL 87119 follows) in an IGKV Raipur Entomology screening of local pigeonpea germplasm; the thesis text relates to pod borer complex work -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/13fa8dec-a599-4374-8b0b-cadc63b8b2dd/content
Wilt and sterility mosaic resistance is listed for "Rajeev Lochan" in the central release table -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
In a 2013-14 rabi trial at IGKV Raipur comparing six genotypes, Asha gave the highest seed yield; Rajeevlochan was listed alongside Laxmi and RPS-2007-106 as statistically comparable -- http://www.ijcmas.com/6-3-2017/Birendra%20Tigga,%20et%20al.pdf
A 2016-17 rabi trial of 20 genotypes at IGKV Raipur recorded the most primary branches per plant in Rajeevlochan (7.6) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355928518_CROP_IMPROVEMENT_AND_ITS_YIELD_ATTRIBUTES_IN_RABI_PIGEONPEA_CajanuscajanL_Millsp
A kharif 2017-18 plot trial at the IGKV Raipur research farm used Rajeevlochan as the variety (sown 30 June 2017, 20 kg/ha seed rate) -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/13fa8dec-a599-4374-8b0b-cadc63b8b2dd/content
Rajeevlochan was used as the check variety in a diallel study at the IGKV Raipur Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/List-of-15-selected-superior-cultivars-of-pigeonpea-on-the-basis-of-yield-and-yield_tbl2_257410510

GENETICS AND QTL
Rajeevlochan appeared in a genetic divergence (D2-type clustering) analysis of pigeonpea accessions from Ambikapur, Chhattisgarh, where it fell in a single-member cluster and was suggested for future breeding -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue9/PartW/10-10-497-879.pdf
No evidence found for QTL, marker-trait association or molecular mapping studies on Rajeevlochan. Parentage (ICPL 92060 selection, ICP 7667 x (ICP 7118 x ICP 6997)) was not verified by any retrieved page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Rajeevlochan is recorded as originating at IGKV (Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya), Raipur, Chhattisgarh -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355928518_CROP_IMPROVEMENT_AND_ITS_YIELD_ATTRIBUTES_IN_RABI_PIGEONPEA_CajanuscajanL_Millsp
Release credited to IGKVV, Raipur, central zone Chhattisgarh -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
No evidence found for a lead breeder or scientist name for Rajeevlochan. Station: Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, IGKV, Raipur (research-cum-instructional farm) -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/List-of-15-selected-superior-cultivars-of-pigeonpea-on-the-basis-of-yield-and-yield_tbl2_257410510

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder email, phone or postal address was retrieved for Rajeevlochan. An IGKV Raipur institute contact page was not retrieved in the search; the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding is the best institute-level lead, but no contact details were found for it.

PUBLICATIONS
Tigga, B., Chandraker, D.K., Banjara, T.R., Bhagat, S.K., Dev, M. (2017). Effect of Different Genotype and Planting Geometry on Growth and Productivity of Rabi Season Pigeon Pea (Cajanus cajan L.). International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences -- http://www.ijcmas.com/6-3-2017/Birendra%20Tigga,%20et%20al.pdf / DOI 10.20546/ijcmas.2017.603.249
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2020). Crop Improvement and its Yield Attributes in Rabi Pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan L. Millsp.). International Journal of Modern Agriculture, Vol. 9, No. 4 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355928518_CROP_IMPROVEMENT_AND_ITS_YIELD_ATTRIBUTES_IN_RABI_PIGEONPEA_CajanuscajanL_Millsp
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2023). Genetic diversity analysis in pigeonpea [Cajanus cajan (L.) Millsp.] (Pharma Innovation Journal, Vol. 12, Issue 9 per URL) -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue9/PartW/10-10-497-879.pdf
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2017-18). Screening of local pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan L.) at IGKV Raipur, Department of Entomology (KrishiKosh thesis/report) -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/13fa8dec-a599-4374-8b0b-cadc63b8b2dd/content

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, Chhattisgarh state seed corporation, KVK, IGKV seed sales or private dealer listing for Rajeevlochan was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Chhattisgarh (central zone, CG) -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf

NOTES ON NAMES AND CROP
Crop mismatch: the input lists chickpea, but Seednet lists pigeonpea (red gram/arhar). Every page found refers to pigeonpea, so all findings above are for pigeonpea. No chickpea evidence was found.
Name: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Rajeevlochan". The dpd.gov.in table uses "Rajeev Lochan". Both spellings were treated as the same variety.
Institution: the input "Chattisgarh" is a state name. The developer is IGKV Raipur.
Release year: input says 2010-12-23; dpd.gov.in says 2011. Verify against the CSC minutes and Seednet.
Breeder and contact searches were limited to one query each, so the gaps above may be filled by a targeted IGKV Raipur search.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Proposed variety has superior quality. It contains average sucrose in juice of 18.17%.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: The variety is characterized by slightly zig-zag to straight green stalk turns green on exposure to light, tumescent to cylindrical with medium to long internode, constricted node with small round bud and very shallow to indicated bud groove, staggered two rows root eyes, green leaves, green leaf sheath with purple blotches, one bigger and other small and transitional auricles.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Proposed Variety can be growth in moisture stress condition also.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
1.	Red Rot- Resistant.
2.	Wilt- Moderately resistant.
3.	Smut- Moderately resistant.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests:
1.	Shoot and rootborer- Low incidence.
2.	Top borer- Low incidence.
3.	Stalk borer- Low incidence.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): N-150 Kg, P2O5- 85 Kg, K2O-60 Kg/ha.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Stress data are thin. The Assam package of practices lists this line's disease reaction as moderately resistant to root rot, with phyllody and bacterial wilt also named in its row, though the table text is garbled in the extraction. All the varieties are susceptible to Phytophthora blight and bacterial wilt to varying degrees. -- https://kvkchirang.aau.ac.in/pdf/package_of_practice/kharif/Sesamum.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. -- (no URL returned)

DISEASE AND PEST
Reaction to root rot, phyllody and bacterial wilt appears in the Assam tables listed under STRESS TOLERANCE. Pest reaction: No evidence found. -- https://kvkchirang.aau.ac.in/pdf/package_of_practice/kharif/Sesamum.pdf ; https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The 2021 Assam kharif package gives a duration of 80-90 days, a yield of 8-10 q/ha, 46% oil and black seed for this line, with sowing from June to the first fortnight of August. -- https://kvkchirang.aau.ac.in/pdf/package_of_practice/kharif/Sesamum.pdf
The 2015 Assam kharif package reports the same 80-90 day duration, 8-10 q/ha yield, 46% oil and 0.3 seed-coat colour entry for AST-1 (AAUDT 9304-14-4, IC 551415), with Hills Zone adaptation and black seed. -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf
Field-trial or multi-location data: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Breeding-line code AAUDT 9304-14-4 appears as a parent in a crossing study on physiological traits, with its crosses rated for oil yield. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10681-008-9871-6
Parentage ("Local x ST 1683") and breeding method: No evidence found. The ST 1683 entry in the Assam table is a separate variety row and does not confirm parentage. -- https://kvkchirang.aau.ac.in/pdf/package_of_practice/kharif/Sesamum.pdf
QTL, marker, or genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Lead breeder or scientist names and station: No evidence found. The name "Regional Research Station, Diphu" was not confirmed by any retrieved page.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute, division or contact-page entry for this variety was returned.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not stated (Year not stated). Analysis of genetic architecture for some physiological characters in sesame (Sesamum indicum L.). Journal not confirmed in retrieved text (Springer, DOI prefix 10.1007/s10681) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10681-008-9871-6
Assam State Department of Agriculture (2015). Package of Practices for Kharif Crops of Assam. Published jointly by the Assam state agriculture department -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf
Assam Agricultural University, KVK Chirang (2021). Package of Practices for Kharif Crops of Assam, 2021 -- https://kvkchirang.aau.ac.in/pdf/package_of_practice/kharif/Sesamum.pdf
KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR reports, peer-reviewed papers on AST-1 itself: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for AST-1 seed from NSC, the Assam state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales, or a named dealer. The search returned generic sesame commodity traders in Assam (e.g., Morigaon, Darrang, Barpeta Road) that do not name this variety, and these were discarded. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sesame-seeds-17992790497.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
Assam only. The Assam kharif package lists this line for Assam, with Hills Zone adaptation in the 2015 table. -- https://kvkchirang.aau.ac.in/pdf/package_of_practice/kharif/Sesamum.pdf ; https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION (not a required heading; recorded for reference)
No CSC release minutes or 2020 notification for AST-1 were found. The one notification result returned concerns a different sesame variety (Ashrit, OUAT Kalinga Sesame-1, Odisha, 2023), which was discarded. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/sesame-variety-ashrit-ouat-kalinga-sesame-1/

NAME NOTE
Evidence for both the variety_name "AST-1" and the seednet_variety_name "AST-1 (AAUDR 9304-14-4-1)" was found only under the forms "AST-1 (AAUDT 9304-14-4-1)" and "AAUDT 9304-14-4". The Seednet portal was not returned by any search, so no Seednet-specific evidence exists. The "AAUDR" spelling did not appear in any retrieved result.

drought.details: TJT 501 is widely considered a drought-tolerant variety of pigeonpea, which itself is known as the most drought-tolerant pulse crop. It is listed among drought-tolerant varieties and has been studied in contexts of water stress quantification. However, one study also identified it as a 'drought sensitive genotype'.

heat.details: TJT 501 is noted as tolerant to heat.

salinity.details: TJT 501 is listed among popular varieties for cultivation in saline regions, suggesting some adaptation to salt stress.

flood.details: TJT 501 is tolerant to waterlogging.

disease_resistance.summary: TJT 501 is resistant to wilt and tolerant to Phytophthora blight. For Sterility Mosaic Disease (SMD), it is described as tolerant or resistant in multiple sources, but one source indicates susceptibility.

pest_resistance.summary: TJT 501 is tolerant to Helicoverpa Armigera (H. Armigera), Pod Borers, and Pod Fly.

disease_resistance.summary: Fusarium wilt: resistant (dpd.gov.in table lists TS-3R as resistant to Fusarium wilt; the input record states RESISTANT TO FUSARIUM WILT). The Vijayapur paper describes the variety as early and resistant to wilt, with early maturity and wilt resistance cited as reasons for a yield increase of up to 25% in Vijayapur district. Sterility mosaic disease: no evidence found for TS-3R (the dpd.gov.in table lists this trait for other varieties only).

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The input record lists pest_reaction as Not specified. Pod borer resistance: no evidence found for TS-3R (the dpd.gov.in table lists this trait for other varieties only).

agronomic_details.yield: Input record: average yield 1100.00 to 1700.00 Kg/Ha. Vijayapur cluster front-line demonstration: 11.91 q/ha (approximately 1191 kg/ha) for TS-3R versus 9.33 q/ha for local Gulyal. The dpd.gov.in yield column reads 12-16 but the units are not stated on the page (likely q/ha, not confirmed). Note: the dpd.gov.in table lists 100-seed weight as 10.5 g, whereas the input record lists 11.5 g.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for stability across environments. The Vijayapur demonstration (2018-19 to 2020-21) reported a yield advantage over local Gulyal in one district, and the Ethiopia on-station trial reported higher dry matter for TS-3R, but no formal stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Input record: recommended to Zone II of Karnataka, suitable for medium to deep black soil, under rainfed as well as protective irrigation conditions. Suitable for kharif and late sown cropping systems. The Vijayapur demonstration was conducted in a dry zone of Karnataka. The dpd.gov.in table places the area of adoption in Karnataka (southern zone).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: DARK PURPLE COLOUR STRIPS ON THE OUTER SURFACE WING PETAL OF THE FLOWER ; YELLOW COLOUR ON THE INNER SURFACE OF ALL THE PETALS ; SEED COLOUR IS RED AND BOLD SIZE, 100 SEED WT. :11.5 G.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Cluster front-line demonstration, Vijayapur district, 2018-19 to 2020-21 (two seasons), 105 ha, 217 farmers: TS-3R yielded 11.91 q/ha versus 9.33 q/ha for local Gulyal; gross return Rs. 88,308.5/ha; B:C ratio 3.42; yield increase of up to 25% reported. (2) On-station trial, Jinka Agricultural Research Center, South Omo, Ethiopia: TS-3R, GRG-152 and GRG-811 compared under two sowing dates; TS-3R had higher dry matter in reproductive parts (63.68 g/plant) and higher total dry matter at early growth; June sowing gave the highest dry matter overall. Grain yield from this trial was not stated in the digest. (3) Farmer preference and adoption study, Kalyana-Karnataka, TS-3R versus GRG-811, 120 farmers: farmers reported non-availability and high cost of improved seed as constraints. No yield value was reported in the digest for this study.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: TS-3R (pigeon pea, *Cajanus cajan*)

Searches run: 4 web_search queries, covering variety/release, breeder/institution, research publications, and seed availability. Both name fields (variety_name and seednet_variety_name) are "TS-3R", so all evidence below refers to that name. No Seednet portal page appeared in the results, so Seednet-specific fields are not verified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as early and resistant to wilt, with the early maturity and wilt resistance cited as reasons for a yield increase of up to 25% in Vijayapur district -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue4/PartR/9-4-134-425.pdf
- Listed as resistant to Fusarium wilt, with 100-seed weight of 10.5 g -- https://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Drought or heat tolerance, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. The Vijayapur paper mentions a dry zone of Karnataka but does not state a drought-tolerance rating for TS-3R -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue4/PartR/9-4-134-425.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wilt resistance (Fusarium) as above -- https://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Sterility mosaic disease and pod borer resistance: No evidence found for TS-3R. Those traits appear in the dpd.gov.in table for other varieties only.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Cluster front-line demonstration in Vijayapur (2018-19 to 2020-21 two-season trial, 105 ha, 217 farmers): TS-3R yielded 11.91 q/ha against 9.33 q/ha for local Gulyal; gross return Rs. 88,308.5/ha; B:C ratio 3.42 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020.v9.i4.11932/impact-of-large-scale-demonstration-of-pigeon-pea-variety-ts-3r-cfld-programme-in-vijayapur-district
- Jinka, South Omo, Ethiopia on-station trial: TS-3R, GRG-152 and GRG-811 compared under two sowing dates; TS-3R had higher dry matter in reproductive parts (63.68 g/plant) and higher total dry matter at early growth, with June sowing giving the highest dry matter -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350721608_Evaluation_of_Pigeon_pea_Cajanus_cajan_for_Dry_Matter_Yield_and_Chemical_Composition_on_Station_of_Jinka_Agricultural_Research_Center_South_Omo_South-Western_Ethiopia
- Maturity 150-155 days, indeterminate, semi-spreading, white and bold seeded; yield column reads 12-16 (units not stated on the page) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- A second national table lists TS 3R as released in 2011 by ARS Gulbarga (conflicts with the 2010 release year in the other table) -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Farmer preference and adoption study (Kalyana-Karnataka, TS-3R vs GRG-811, 120 farmers): farmers reported non-availability and high cost of improved seed as constraints -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381409361_International_Journal_of_Agriculture_Extension_and_Social_Development_Extent_of_adoption_of_pigeonpea_technologies_and_production_challenges_of_pigeonpea_farming_in_Kalyana-Karnataka_region

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage TS-3 x MARUTI (from the input record): No evidence found in any search result.
- Breeding line code, breeding method, QTL/marker and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released through the State Variety Release Committee (SVRC) in 2010 (per dpd.gov.in table), with source institution ARS Gulbarga, Karnataka -- https://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. The Vijayapur paper authors (BC Kolhar, SA Biradar, Vivek S Devarnavadagi, Shivalingappa Hotkar) are extension/KVK staff who evaluated the variety, not identified as its breeders -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue4/PartR/9-4-134-425.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email or phone found. Institute-level address from the Vijayapur paper: ICAR-Krishi Vigyana Kendra, Hitnalli farm, Vijayapur-586101, Karnataka, India (corresponding author Vivek S Devarnavadagi). Email and phone: not found -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue4/PartR/9-4-134-425.pdf
- ARS Gulbarga (developing station) email, phone or contact page: No evidence found in the search results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Kolhar, B. C., Biradar, S. A., Devarnavadagi, V. S., & Hotkar, S. (2020). Impact of large scale demonstration of pigeon pea variety TS-3R CFLD programme in Vijayapur district. Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry, 9(4), 1336-1338 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020.v9.i4.11932/impact-of-large-scale-demonstration-of-pigeon-pea-variety-ts-3r-cfld-programme-in-vijayapur-district
- Authors (year), title and journal for the Jinka, Ethiopia trial (TS-3R, GRG-152, GRG-811): listed on ResearchGate; author names and year were not confirmed in the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350721608_Evaluation_of_Pigeon_pea_Cajanus_cajan_for_Dry_Matter_Yield_and_Chemical_Composition_on_Station_of_Jinka_Agricultural_Research_Center_South_Omo_South-Western_Ethiopia
- Preference analysis of pigeonpea varietal attributes, Kalyana-Karnataka (TS-3R vs GRG-811): authors and year not confirmed in the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381409187_Preference_Analysis_of_Pigeonpea_Varietal_Attributes_among_Farmers_and_Traders_in_Kalyana_Karnataka_Region_A_Conjoint_Analysis_Approach
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports, and ICAR/SVRC proceedings on TS-3R: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Certified seed of TS-3R was supplied by ICAR-KVK Vijayapur for the demonstration -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue4/PartR/9-4-134-425.pdf
- Private dealer listings: Karnataka Agro Seeds, 5 kg pack, listed at Rs. 975 (MRP Rs. 1,080) -- https://agroshopy.com/index.php?product_id=771&route=product%2Fproduct
- Private dealer listing: Varada Seeds, TS-3R red gram -- https://agroshopy.com/index.php?product_id=771&route=product%2Fproduct
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, SAU seed sales, Seednet listing: No evidence found in the search results.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Karnataka (dpd.gov.in table: source ARS Gulbarga, area of adoption Karnataka, southern zone) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Other states: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of RTS-43. The one relevant page describes a stay-green habit, which is a trait some breeders link to drought tolerance, but the page does not rate tolerance. -- https://barc.gov.in/div/66_209.html
Early and synchronized flowering, stay green type, white lustrous, round and bold seeds with good roti making quality, early maturing, suitable for deep black soils (BARC release note for RTS-43; name matches this variety; crop is sorghum). -- https://barc.gov.in/div/66_209.html

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The search returned no page naming RTS-43 with disease or pest reaction data. -- searched "RTS-43 sorghum variety" and "RTS-43 sorghum research paper trial"

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Early maturity and suitability for deep black soils are reported in the BARC release note, but no yield, trial or multi-location data were found. -- https://barc.gov.in/div/66_209.html
Maturity-day counts, yield figures and seeding recommendations: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for RTS-43 in any genetic or marker study. The parentage given in the record (a selection from ICP-87051 x PT-221) was not confirmed by any retrieved page. -- searched "RTS-43 sorghum research paper trial"

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), Trombay, Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India. The BARC page states the variety was developed in collaboration with the University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur. No individual breeder is named. -- https://barc.gov.in/div/66_209.html
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
Rejected as name resemblances: Gujarat Jowar 43 (GJ 43), a different sorghum variety from Gujarat -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370048172_A_new_sorghum_variety_Gujarat_Jowar_43_GJ_43_for_feed_and_fodder_security_of_milch_animals_in_Gujarat ; CSH 43 MF, a fodder hybrid -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=171 ; N.G.P. Rao (Wikipedia), a biography not linked to RTS-43 -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neelamraju_Ganga_Prasada_Rao

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for a BARC or UAS Raichur contact (email, phone, postal address or contact page) tied to RTS-43. The only institute-linked page retrieved is the BARC division page above, and its retrieved text contains no contact details. -- https://barc.gov.in/div/66_209.html

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Searches for RTS-43 papers, AICRP or ICAR reports, theses (KrishiKosh) and conference papers returned no matching item.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for RTS-43 seed from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, a KVK, UAS Raichur or a private dealer.
Seednet name TS-3: the Seednet name is listed under pigeon pea, not sorghum, so it cannot be evidence for this sorghum variety. Pigeon pea pages that name TS-3 or TS-3R were excluded as a different crop. The Seednet entry TS-3 appears in a pigeon pea list -- https://dpd.gov.in/Pigeonpea.pdf (excluded from the RTS-43 record). Seller pages for TS-3R pigeon pea seed (Varada, Sagar, Mrityunjaya) were also excluded -- https://agroshopy.in/product/varada-redgram-seeds-ts-3r-tur-5-kg/

RECOMMENDED STATES
Karnataka is not confirmed by any retrieved page. The only link found is the BARC note that RTS-43 was developed with UAS Raichur, which is in Karnataka. No recommendation notification for any state was found. -- https://barc.gov.in/div/66_209.html
Release date: the record gives 13 March 2025, but the BARC page is dated 10/2024. The discrepancy is unresolved.

disease_resistance.summary: Fusarium wilt: reported as moderately resistant in the EJPB release paper (Sandhya Kishore et al., 2022). Sterility mosaic, Phytophthora and Alternaria: not found in searched sources. The generic pigeonpea trait table did not name this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod fly (Melanagromyza obtusa): reported as tolerant in the EJPB release paper. Helicoverpa: not found in searched sources. The generic pigeonpea trait table did not name this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 1677 kg/ha, which is 30.71% above PT0012 (national check), 28.50% above TS-3R (zonal check) and 10.60% above PRG-176 (local check). Maximum 3082 kg/ha recorded at Gulbarga, Karnataka.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the maximum yield location noted above. No multi-environment stability statistics were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Mid-early duration, described as suitable for kharif sowing. Suitable for the southern zone of India. A rabi-season (2023-24) sowing-date trial found 30 September to be the best sowing date among the varieties tested, with WRGE-121 and WRGE-182 performing better for growth and yield.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: 100-seed weight 9.0-10.0 g; protein content 23.05%. Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) EJPB release paper: average yield 1677 kg/ha, 30.71%, 28.50% and 10.60% above PT0012, TS-3R and PRG-176 respectively; maximum 3082 kg/ha at Gulbarga, Karnataka. (2) Grain yield from AICRP and IVT trials was reported, but only titles were retrieved; no result values found. (3) Rabi-season sowing-date trial, 2023-24 season: WRGE-121 and WRGE-182 performed better than WRGE-93 and WRGE-97 for growth and yield; sowing on 30 September was best. (4) Nitrogen uptake and nitrogen use efficiency (72) were comparable to WRGE-182; the authors linked this to its longer growth duration. (5) Front-line demonstration at Kothapeta village (Warangal) on 21.07.2023, with WRGE 121 distributed alongside WRGE 97 and PRG 176 for farmer evaluation. (6) Quality parameters and mineral content versus PRG-176: title only, no results retrieved.
