EVIDENCE DIGEST: PKV Pink (AKS 311), safflower

Name note: "variety_name" is PKV Pink and "seednet_variety_name" is PKV-PINK. All four searches returned evidence under "PKV Pink" or "AKS 311". No result came from the Seednet portal itself, so no Seednet listing is confirmed. Searches used: 4 of 4 allowed.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Success-stories table lists PKV-Pink (AKS 311) as moderately tolerant to wilt -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to PKV Pink in the retrieved sources.
DISEASE AND PEST -- Moderate wilt tolerance is the only disease or pest trait recorded for PKV Pink (see above). No Alternaria or aphid rating for this variety was found; the AICRP achievements page mentions only general breeding objectives for Alternaria, wilt and aphid -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/major-achievements/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Yield potential is given as 1576 kg/ha (AICRP achievements) and 1500 kg/ha (success-stories table), with 135-140 days to maturity and 30% oil content in the table -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/major-achievements/ ; https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Akola centre reports seed yield of 15-21 q/ha and oil content of 32-33% for PKV Pink -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/major-achievements/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- PKV Pink served as the high-yielding check in the Preliminary Hybrid Trial of 2012-13 under dryland Vertisol conditions -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/pkv_journal/pkv-res-journal%2038(1).pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Agronomy notes from Akola: N raised from 25 to 40 kg/ha gave higher seed yield; PSB plus 5 t FYM/ha can replace 100% P in the green gram-safflower system -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/major-achievements/

drought.details: No evidence found. Drought tolerance was not reported for this line in any retrieved source. The digest notes that the release-date and parentage fields could not be confirmed from retrieved text. The variety record describes suitability for rainfed and irrigated sown conditions, but this is a suitability statement, not a measured drought-tolerance finding.

heat.details: No evidence found. Heat tolerance was not reported in any retrieved source.

salinity.details: No evidence found. Salinity tolerance was not reported in any retrieved source.

flood.details: No evidence found. Flood tolerance was not reported in any retrieved source.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance recorded for RVSAF 18-1. The CSC committee noted that the line behaved on par with the check varieties for pests and diseases, so it showed no special resistance advantage. No Alternaria, wilt or other disease resistance was recorded for this line. The Alternaria and wilt tolerance in the source belongs to a different line, RVSAF 14-1, and was excluded (http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf was not used as evidence for RVSAF 18-1).

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance recorded for RVSAF 18-1. The CSC committee noted that the line behaved on par with the check varieties for pests, so it showed no special resistance advantage. The variety record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Committee minutes report an 18% yield advantage over the zonal check and a 4% advantage over local checks. Press coverage reports an average oil yield of 676 kg/ha across national trials, about 31% above the checks A-1 and PBNS 12. The variety record's average_yield field is given only as 'Kg/Ha' with no value, so no official seed-yield figure in kg/ha was found.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The line was tested for three consecutive rabi seasons (2018, 2019 and 2020) in AICRP safflower multilocation trials, but no stability analysis across environments was reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Release recommendation in the Central zone for rainfed conditions, per the CSC minutes (Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, South Rajasthan and Odisha). The variety record lists Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, and the variety record's adaptation_ecology field also lists Madhya Pradesh. The notification list (October 2023) includes Madhya Pradesh. The CSC minutes list a different zone. This discrepancy should be checked against the official gazette notification.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 127 To 131Days (from the variety record). Maturity days from official trial tables were not found in the searched sources.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Spiny, yellow-flowered type that turns orange at maturity (press coverage). Other morphological characteristics: Not specified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: CSC 87th meeting minutes: 18% yield advantage over the zonal check and 4% over local checks. Press coverage: average oil yield of 676 kg/ha across national trials, about 31% above checks A-1 and PBNS 12. Tested for three consecutive rabi seasons (2018, 2019, 2020) in AICRP safflower multilocation trials. Reported oil content close to 40%; about 3 to 3.5 kg of seed needed per litre of oil (press coverage). Official trial tables with maturity days, seed yield (kg/ha) and seed-oil percentage were not found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No QTL, marker or genomic study covering RVSAF 18-1 was found. Pedigree (MS-6 x NARI-57) could not be confirmed in any retrieved text.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. The QTL papers retrieved concern other safflower populations (Mex.22-191 x Goldasht; Hashemi et al. 2024; Mex.22-191 x IL.111 drought QTL) and were not used as evidence for RVSAF 18-1.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RVSAF-18-1 (Raj Vijay Safflower 18-1), safflower

Name note: The CSC minutes and the notification lists use "RVSAF 18-1 (Raj Vijay Safflower 18-1)". The Seednet name is "RVSAF-18-1 ( Raj Vijay Safflower 18-1)". I found no Seednet portal page in these searches, so every finding below refers to the same variety under the CSC/press name. The release-date field (2023-05-02) and parentage (MS-6 x NARI-57) could not be confirmed from any retrieved text.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance were not reported for this line in any retrieved source. No evidence found for these traits. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/356664896 (CSC 87th minutes, the only official-style source located)

DISEASE AND PEST
The CSC committee noted that the line behaved on par with the check varieties for pests and diseases, so it showed no special resistance advantage. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356664896_Minutes_of_the_87_th_meeting_of_Central_Sub-Committee_on_Crop_Standards_Notification_and_Release_of_Varieties_for_Agricultural_Crops_held_through_Video_Conferencing_on_22
No Alternaria, wilt or other disease resistance was recorded for RVSAF 18-1 itself. The Alternaria and wilt tolerance found in the source belongs to a different line, RVSAF 14-1. -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf (not used as evidence for RVSAF 18-1)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The committee minutes report an 18% yield advantage over the zonal check and a 4% advantage over local checks. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356664896_Minutes_of_the_87_th_meeting_of_Central_Sub-Committee_on_Crop_Standards_Notification_and_Release_of_Varieties_for_Agricultural_Crops_held_through_Video_Conferencing_on_22
Press coverage reports an average oil yield of 676 kg/ha across national trials, about 31% above the checks A-1 and PBNS 12. -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/indore/indore-new-safflower-seed-variety-boosts-farmers-income-by-30
The line was bred by hybridization followed by pedigree selection and was tested for three consecutive rabi seasons (2018, 2019 and 2020) in AICRP safflower multilocation trials. -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/indore/indore-new-safflower-seed-variety-boosts-farmers-income-by-30
Reported oil content is close to 40%, and the press piece says only about 3–3.5 kg of seed is needed per litre of oil. -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/indore/indore-new-safflower-seed-variety-boosts-farmers-income-by-30
It is a spiny, yellow-flowered type that turns orange at maturity. -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/indore/indore-new-safflower-seed-variety-boosts-farmers-income-by-30
Maturity days, seed yield in kg/ha and seed-oil percentage from official trial tables were not found for this line. No evidence found for maturity. -- (no URL)

GENETICS AND QTL
No QTL, marker or genomic study covering RVSAF 18-1 was found. The QTL papers retrieved concern other safflower populations (e.g., Mex.22-191 x Goldasht; Hashemi et al. 2024; Mex.22-191 x IL.111 drought QTL). -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10681-024-03408-0 (not used as evidence for RVSAF 18-1)
Pedigree (MS-6 x NARI-57) could not be confirmed in any retrieved text. No evidence found. -- (no URL)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The press report names Dr Usha Saxena and Dr Mukesh Saxena of the College of Agriculture, Indore as the developers. -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/indore/indore-new-safflower-seed-variety-boosts-farmers-income-by-30
The CSC minutes list the proposing institution as the College of Agriculture, Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (RVSKVV), Indore, Madhya Pradesh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356664896_Minutes_of_the_87_th_meeting_of_Central_Sub-Committee_on_Crop_Standards_Notification_and_Release_of_Varieties_for_Agricultural_Crops_held_through_Video_Conferencing_on_22
The line is linked to the AICRP on Safflower centre at the College of Agriculture, Indore. -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
Names: Dr Usha Saxena and Dr Mukesh Saxena (developers, per press report). -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/indore/indore-new-safflower-seed-variety-boosts-farmers-income-by-30
Institution: College of Agriculture, RVSKVV, Indore (Madhya Pradesh). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356664896_Minutes_of_the_87_th_meeting_of_Central_Sub-Committee_on_Crop_Standards_Notification_and_Release_of_Varieties_for_Agricultural_Crops_held_through_Video_Conferencing_on_22
Official email, phone, postal address and institute contact-page URL for RVSKVV or the Indore AICRP safflower centre: No evidence found in these searches. The NARI safflower contact found on the AICRP success-stories page belongs to a different safflower line and was not used. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/ (not used as evidence for this variety)

PUBLICATIONS
Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties (2021 meeting minutes, 87th). Minutes of the 87th meeting of CSCCSNRVAC. Report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356664896_Minutes_of_the_87_th_meeting_of_Central_Sub-Committee_on_Crop_Standards_Notification_and_Release_of_Varieties_for_Agricultural_Crops_held_through_Video_Conferencing_on_22
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper specifically on RVSAF 18-1 was found. -- (no URL)

SEED AVAILABILITY
Press coverage says the variety is used by farmers across eight states. -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/indore/indore-new-safflower-seed-variety-boosts-farmers-income-by-30
No seed dealer, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sales listing was found. Seednet, KVK and SAU seed-sales pages were not reachable through these searches. No evidence found. -- (no URL)

RECOMMENDED STATES
Release recommendation in the Central zone for rainfed conditions, per the CSC minutes: Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, South Rajasthan and Odisha. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356664896_Minutes_of_the_87_th_meeting_of_Central_Sub-Committee_on_Crop_Standards_Notification_and_Release_of_Varieties_for_Agricultural_Crops_held_through_Video_Conferencing_on_22
Notification list (October 2023): Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-106-new-varieties-of-31-major-crops-for-farmers/
Press coverage names eight states including Odisha. -- https://www.freepressjournal.in/indore/indore-new-safflower-seed-variety-boosts-farmers-income-by-30
Discrepancy: the variety record lists Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, with no Madhya Pradesh. The notification list includes MP, and the CSC minutes list a different zone (Central, including MP, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Odisha). The record should be checked against the official gazette notification.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: SSF-708 (safflower)

Search limit note: the search tool hit its usage cap during my fourth call, so I could not run a separate Seednet name check or open full pages. Findings below come from search snippets (roughly the first 300 characters of each result). Treat them as partial. The CSC release-minute name and the Seednet name were both "SSF-708," so no name mismatch was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The snippets I saw do not mention drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance for SSF-708. The AICRP success-stories page may contain this, but I could not read it in full.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Partial. The AICRP success-stories snippet describes SSF-708 as moderately to (text cut off, likely "moderately tolerant" to a disease or pest), but the snippet ends before naming the trait. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No yield, maturity, or trial data appeared in the snippets I could read.

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage only. The AICRP success-stories page lists SSF-708 as a 2012 entry with parentage NARI-2 X JSI-99. No QTL or marker study was found. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partial. The AICRP success-stories page links a safflower breeder to Nimbkar Agricultural Research Institute (NARI), Phaltan, Satara district, Maharashtra, in the same entry that names SSF-708. The snippet does not state explicitly that this breeder developed SSF-708, so treat that link as unconfirmed. The ICAR-IIOR page (node/576), which carries an SSF-708 entry, is a variety information page from the Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research, Hyderabad. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/ ; https://www.icar-iior.org.in/node/576

CONTACT DETAILS -- Partial, institute-level only. IIOR, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500 030. Phone 040-2459844 (listed under the Director; this number was truncated in the snippet, so verify it). No breeder email or direct phone was found. No individual breeder name was confirmed for SSF-708. -- https://www.icar-iior.org.in/node/576

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, thesis, or AICRP report specific to SSF-708 appeared in the results I could read.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The ICAR-IIOR page carries an SSF-708 entry, but the snippet did not show seed source details. Not searched separately for NSC, state corporations, KVKs, SAU sales, or private dealers.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Maharashtra. The ICAR-IIOR page lists the recommended region as safflower growing areas of Maharashtra. -- https://www.icar-iior.org.in/node/576 ; the DOD safflower page also lists SSF-708 among recommended varieties, without a state breakdown in the snippet. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Safflower.aspx

RELEASE YEAR -- Recorded as NaT in the input. The AICRP page gives 2012 as the year of release, which conflicts with the input. Verify against the CSC minutes or the Seednet entry before using it.

PKM(Sa) 5 / PKM(Sa)5 sapota: EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: the CSC name is "PKM(Sa) 5" and the Seednet name is "PKM(Sa)5". The sources use "PKM (Sa) 5", "PKM(Sa)-5", "PKM-5" and, in one retail listing, "PKM Sapota". I treated these as the same variety only where the description matches. No search returned a seednet.gov.in page for either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: HBL-113 (Barley, variety code A0101003)

Name check: the CSC name (HBL-113) and the Seednet name (HBL-113) are the same string, so all evidence below refers to the same name. Search returned variant spellings "HBL 113" and "HBL-113". The search budget ran out after four queries, so the follow-up stress, KrishiKosh, and Seednet searches were not run. Findings are limited accordingly.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page giving drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for HBL-113. Yellow rust resistance is stated only in the supplied variety record, not in a search result.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No independent evidence found. Yellow rust resistance and aphid/insect resistance appear only in the supplied variety record ("HBL-113 is a selection for yellow rust resistant from Zephyre... also resistant to aphids and other insect pests"). This is unverified by search.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A 2000s-era ICAR journal article on hulled and hulless barley genetic variability used HBL 113 as one of three check varieties (with BHS 400 and VLB 118) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/83717/35348 (Wheat and Barley Research 10(3): 185-189). The snippet gives no yield, maturity, or sowing data for HBL-113 itself. Sowing window (mid-October to mid-November, low and mid hills, rainfed and timely sown) comes only from the supplied record.

GENETICS AND QTL -- HBL-113 is described as a feed barley selection from Zyphee (spelled "Zephyre" in the supplied record) -- https://mel.cgiar.org/reporting/download/hash/2d77f88a1028dce2d3b5551740f42a8c (spatio-temporal genetic diversity in Indian barley, listing it with HPKV Bajaura as source). No breeding-line code, breeding method, QTL, or marker data was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution per the supplied record and the CGIAR diversity report: HPKV (Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya), Barley Breeder, Regional Research Station, Bajaura. The lead breeder's name was not found in any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found for a named breeder, email, or phone number. The only address on record is the supplied institution string: "BARLEY BREEDER, HPKV, REGIONAL RESEARCH STATION, BAJAURA, DISTRICT KULU (HP)-175 125." No official email, phone, or institute contact-page URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS --
- Verma and Sarkar (2010). Diversity for malting quality in barley (Hordeum vulgare) varieties released in India. Cited in the ResearchGate record; the snippet reports HBL 113 clustering with Alfa 93, NB 1, and NB 3 for malting traits. Authors of the cited study beyond Verma and Sarkar, journal, and volume were not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286841821_Diversity_for_malting_quality_in_barley_Hordeum_vulgare_varieties_released_in_India
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Genetic variability and association study in some hulled and hulless barley. Wheat and Barley Research 10(3): 185-189 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/83717/35348
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Spatio-temporal genetic diversity in Indian barley (report). Indian barley diversity report, CGIAR MEL -- https://mel.cgiar.org/reporting/download/hash/2d77f88a1028dce2d3b5551740f42a8c
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report was retrieved (search not run).

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-sales search returned only unrelated pages (a game wiki entry for "barley seed"). Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, and SAU sources were not checked.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The supplied record gives "Unknown." The search results name no state, but do state that the variety is a feed barley from HPKV Bajaura. Its record describes low and mid hill zones, which points to Himachal Pradesh, but that is an inference and not confirmed by any retrieved source.

RELEASE YEAR (not a requested heading, recorded for reference) -- 1995, from the supplied record only; not confirmed by search.

drought.details: No variety-specific drought evidence found. The digest notes general barley drought tolerance only for the crop, not for RD-2552. Stability data (Jammu plains, normal and late sown) show above-mean yield with bi = 0.92 and S2di = 0.58, but these are not drought-specific.

heat.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

salinity.details: CSC record: recommended for timely-sown irrigated conditions and salinity/alkalinity conditions of plain zones. Listed as salt tolerant (irrigated) in the IIWBR pocket guide. RARI Durgapura describes wide adaptability and suitability for saline conditions. A 1999 release entry describes it as a high-yielding feed barley under normal and saline soils. A Journal of Cereal Research review lists it as salinity tolerant. In a 64-variety trial under partially reclaimed saline-sodic soil (pH 8.6-8.9, EC 4-4.2 dS/m) it ranked among the higher grain-yield varieties. No physiological or genetic mechanism is described in the digest.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Yellow rusts and leaf blights: described as resistant in a 1999 release entry (ResearchGate). Recommended as a resistant/tolerant variety, grouped with DWRUB52, DWRB73 and DWRUB64, in a disease management section of the IIWBR pocket guide. Brown rust: CSC record states susceptible to moderately susceptible. This conflicts with the resistance claims above and is unresolved in the digest. Loose smut, covered smut, net blotch and spot blotch: no evidence found.

pest_resistance.summary: CSC record: moderately susceptible to common pests. Aphid resistance: the pocket guide names RD2052, RD2035 and RD2592 for aphid-prone areas but does not name RD-2552, so no aphid resistance is attributed to this variety. No other pest-specific evidence found.

agronomic_details.yield: Two-year precision nutrient trial: 10.64% higher pooled grain yield than RD 2035 and 4.83% higher than RD 2786. Dual-purpose trial: highest grain yield (3.01 t/ha) and straw yield (5.80 t/ha) among varieties tested, with 318.2 effective tillers/m2. Dual-purpose review: highest straw yield (68 q/ha) in the regenerated crop; RD 2035 had the highest seed yield (46.20 q/ha). Recommended dual-purpose yield of about 200 q/ha green fodder and 2.5-3.0 t/ha grain in northern plains (IIWBR perspective plan). Pocket-guide entries of 46.10 and 38.37 for irrigated, timely-sown trials; units and conditions not stated. CSC average_yield: Unknown.
agronomic_details.stability: Jammu plains, normal and late sown: above-mean yield, bi = 0.92, S2di = 0.58. Not characterised across other environments in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: timely-sown irrigated conditions and salinity/alkalinity conditions of plain zones. Dual-purpose suitability in northern plains (IIWBR). Saline and saline-sodic soils (RARI; 64-variety trial).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RD-2552 (Barley, JAU), EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The CSC minute name (RD-2552) and the Seednet name (RD-2552) are the same in the input. The sources write it as "RD 2552", "RD2552" or "RD-2552". I did not retrieve a Seednet portal page for this variety, so no evidence below is from Seednet. Searches used: 4 of 4 allowed.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Salt tolerant (irrigated), listed in the IIWBR cultivation pocket guide -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
Described as having wide adaptability and suitability for saline conditions, per RARI Durgapura -- https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm
Described as a high-yielding feed barley under normal and saline soils (1999 release entry) -- https://researchgate.net/publication/297538956_Barley_Hordeum_vulgare_L (Sarkar et al., 2013 chapter)
Listed as salinity-tolerant in a Journal of Cereal Research review on barley breeding in India -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/177379/66211/527923
Ranked among the higher grain-yield varieties under partially reclaimed saline-sodic soil (pH 8.6-8.9, EC 4-4.2 dS/m) in a 64-variety trial -- https://www.academia.edu/49057781/Variability_for_yield_and_yield_contributing_traits_in_released_varieties_of_barley_Hordeum_vulgare_L
Drought: no variety-specific drought evidence found. General barley drought tolerance is noted only for the crop, not for RD-2552 -- https://phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue5/PartM/8-5-44-299.pdf
Heat, flood, submergence: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to yellow rusts and leaf blights (1999 release entry) -- https://researchgate.net/publication/297538956_Barley_Hordeum_vulgare_L
Recommended as a resistant/tolerant variety, grouped with DWRUB52, DWRB73 and DWRUB64, in a disease management section -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
Aphid resistance: the pocket guide names RD2052, RD2035 and RD2592 for aphid-prone areas, but not RD-2552 -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf (not attributed to RD-2552)
Loose smut, covered smut, net blotch, spot blotch: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity: RD 2035 reached 50% heading and maturity 8 and 2 days earlier than RD 2552 in a two-year precision nutrient trial, so RD 2552 is later -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336666211_Growth_Quality_and_Yield_of_Barley_Hordeum_vulgare_L_as_Influenced_by_Varieties_and_Precision_nutrient_Management_Practices
Grain yield: RD 2552 gave 10.64% higher pooled grain yield than RD 2035 and 4.83% higher than RD 2786 in that trial -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336666211_Growth_Quality_and_Yield_of_Barley_Hordeum_vulgare_L_as_Influenced_by_Varieties_and_Precision_nutrient_Management_Practices
Dual-purpose trial (cutting schedules): RD 2552 gave the highest grain (3.01 t/ha) and straw (5.80 t/ha) yields among the varieties tested, with 318.2 effective tillers/m2 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286941050_Evaluation_of_dual_purpose_barley_for_fodder_and_grain_under_different_cutting_schedules
Dual-purpose review: RD 2552 had the highest straw yield (68 q/ha) in the regenerated crop, while RD 2035 had the highest seed yield (46.20 q/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/317565561_Dual_purpose_barley_as_affected_by_date_of_sowing_varieties_and_stage_of_harvesting-A_review
Recommended for dual-purpose use with about 200 q/ha green fodder and 2.5-3.0 t/ha grain in northern plains, alongside RD 2035 -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Perspective-Plan-Vision-2025.pdf
Irrigated, timely-sown trial entries give RD 2552 yields of 46.10 and 38.37 in a pocket-guide table, but the units and trial conditions are not stated -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
Seed rate 100 kg/ha and sowing depth 5-7 cm were given for barley generally, not for RD 2552 specifically -- https://iiwbr.org.in/barley-network/
Stability (Jammu plains, normal and late sown): RD 2552 had above-mean yield, bi = 0.92, S2di = 0.58 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue5/PartM/8-5-44-299.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: RD2035/DL472 -- https://researchgate.net/publication/297539975_Barley_Hordeum_vulgare_L (Kumar, 2012 chapter)
Parentage RD2035/DL472 with release year 1999, NWPZ and NEPZ -- https://researchgate.net/publication/297538956_Barley_Hordeum_vulgare_L
Used as a parent: RD 2552 was a parent in crosses with DWRB 91, DWRB 64, RD 2715 and RD 2786, in combining-ability studies -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-12-2019/Deepak%20Panwar%20and%20Hemlata%20Sharma.pdf
Cross listed: RD 2053 x RD 2552 was among the best F1 crosses for grain yield in a genetic analysis of six-rowed barley (gene effects, heterosis) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijpgr-16-2-014
Breeding method, QTL, marker and genome data for RD 2552: No evidence found
Note: "BH495/RD2552" in the IIWBR compendium is the parentage of BH 902, not of RD-2552, and was excluded -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-48-Barley-Varieties-and-Genetic-Stocks-A-Compendium.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. None of the retrieved pages names a breeder for RD 2552.
Developing institution: Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute (RARI), Durgapura -- https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm
RARI's page calls itself a constituent of Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University, Jobner. The input names Rajasthan Agriculture University. This discrepancy is unresolved -- https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm
RARI's page credits the institute with RD 2035 and RD 2552, both described as high-yielding and suited to saline conditions -- https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm
Released through the AICRP on barley (1966 onward), now run by IIWBR Karnal. Attribution of RD

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RD 2660 (Barley, Hordeum vulgare)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "RD 2660", so every search used that name. No Seednet portal page was returned. Searches were run for variety/release, breeder/institute, research/AICRP, and seed availability. The seed search returned mostly unrelated RuneScape and US seed-shop pages, which were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Described as developed for rainfed conditions, with rainfed timely-sown recommendation; no specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence test data for RD 2660 found -- https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Rainfed timely-sown placement in the NWPZ table (RD 2660, 24.30 q/ha) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Other "rainfed" malt variety reference (RD 2624 and RD 2660 named together as rainfed-adapted) -- https://www.tourism.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/agriculture/Rajasthan%20Agricultural%20Competitiveness%20Project/valuechainreport/RACP_VC_Barley.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for RD 2660 specifically. Rust-resistance and aphid-resistance statements in the search results apply to other named varieties (e.g., RD 2786, RD 2794, RD 2899, RD 2907, RD 2052, RD 2035, RD 2592) and were discarded.

disease_resistance.summary: Original CSC record states RD-2668 has resistance to major rusts and is tolerant to leaf blight diseases; the digest does not confirm this with test data, pathogen, or rating. No evidence found for rust, loose smut, or other specific resistance ratings for RD-2668 in the digest. The RARI page credits rust resistance to RD 2786, RD 2794, RD 2899 and RD 2907, not RD-2668, so those ratings are excluded.

(3) A 2026 journal paper reports RD 2668 with the highest total sugar content (2.69%) among the tested genotypes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed as moderately resistant to sheath blight, sheath rot and narrow brown leaf spot (name appears as "Jal-Lahri"; rainfed low-land ecosystem) -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2007.htm
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in the searches.

DISEASE AND PEST
Described as resistant to major diseases, with moderate resistance to sheath blight, sheath rot and narrow brown leaf spot (name "Jal-Lahri") -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2007.htm
No evidence found for insect-pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity 110-180 days, tall plant height of 110-140 cm, medium-slender grain, yield 25-50 q/ha (name "Jal-Lahri") -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2007.htm
No evidence found for multi-location trial results or AICRP data for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage recorded as Pankaj x Mahsuri x TKM-6 (name "Jal-Lahri") -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2007.htm
No evidence found for breeding-line codes, breeding method, QTL, markers or genome resources.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. Searches returned only general rice-institute pages (CRRI, NRRI, IIRR, IRRI) and unrelated breeder biographies, none naming the developers of JAL Lahri. The institution given in the record (Dept. of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, N.D. University of Agriculture and Technology, Faizabad) was not confirmed by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, address or contact page for JAL Lahri was returned.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No journal, AICRP, KrishiKosh or conference record for JAL Lahri was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found on Seednet, NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales or dealers. The IFFDC seed availability page lists paddy varieties, but JAL Lahri is not among them -- https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed
Dealer pages returned for paddy seed do not name JAL Lahri and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Listed in a Bihar notified-varieties PDF with serial 352, release year 1994, notification date 02/09/1994 and notification number 636(E). This shows notification, not a recommended-state list -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
Included in the notified rice varieties list for Uttar Pradesh and Uttaranchal (page dated September 2022) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-uttar-pradesh-uttaranchal/
The Bihar DRDPAT annexure also includes an entry for this variety with the state label "Uttar Pradesh" (the "317" in that entry appears to be a serial number, not a verified field) -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2007.htm

Name check: the CSC release name "JAL LAHRI" and the Seednet name "JAL LAHRI" were both searched. The evidence above uses the name "Jal-Lahri" or "JAL LAHRI", and no Seednet portal page was returned for either name.

drought.details: The digest reports no evidence for drought tolerance specific to this variety. The CSC record states the variety has better tolerance to drought at the physiological level than Kranti and matures 4-5 days earlier than Jaya and 10-12 days earlier than Surekha and Phalguna, which the record says enables drought evasion and tolerance. These are CSC record statements only and were not corroborated by the digest. The digest describes the variety under irrigated ecosystem conditions. No quantitative drought data were found.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: resistant, per the Bihar rice varieties table (digest). The CSC record additionally states tolerance to blast, sheath rot, brown spot and bacterial blight. These CSC statements are not corroborated by the digest, and the CSC disease text refers to a proposed variety designation R320-298, which is not the IET-10749 code and has not been reconciled with this variety. Sheath rot, brown spot and bacterial blight: not confirmed by the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Gall midge (biotype-1): the CSC record states complete resistance. Stem borer and leaf folder: the CSC record states tolerance. The digest does not confirm these. The digest lists Mahamaya among IGKV paddy pest-complex management packages, which indicates a pest-management reference only and does not establish resistance. The Gujarat PVS report describes a name-match variety as more resistant to pests and diseases, but its identity with IET-10749 is not confirmed, so it is not attributed here.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Bihar table and bioinfopublication source: about 40 q/ha and 45-55 q/ha respectively, 125-day duration, irrigated, long bold grain. Name match only; identity with IET-10749 not confirmed, so this result is not attributed to this variety. (3) Kharif 2021-2022 line x tester combining-ability study at IGKV Raipur: Mahamaya was among three superior varieties. No yield values were reported in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Birsa Dhan-106 (Rice)

Name check: variety_name "Birsa Dhan-106" and seednet_variety_name "BIRSA DHAN-106" are the same variety. Every finding below refers to that name, and the sources spell it either way.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as resistant to drought in the national varietal table (IET-12052, 1996, rainfed, Bihar) -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Dwarf, short bold white grain; described as resistant to blast, BLB and stem borer in the notification-era summary -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- Ranchi AICRIP centre lists it as tolerant to blast, BLB and stem borer, maturing in 90-95 days -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- ICAR-CRIDA Bihar contingency plans recommend it as a drought-tolerant, short-duration option for direct seeding into moisture-limited upland conditions -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/CP/Bihar/BR34_Siwan_28.12.2013.pdf (the document names the variety among early options; the drought-tolerance wording applies to the medium-duration direct-seeded group, so treat this as indirect support)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerant to blast, BLB and stem borer; yield potential 10-12 q/acre -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- Resistant to blast, BLB and Helminthosporium (moderately resistant to blast and BLB in one source) -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php ; http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- No evidence found for gall midge, brown planthopper or sheath blight resistance specific to this variety. Other Birsa Dhan lines are listed with gall midge tolerance, but those are different varieties and are not attributed here.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 90-95 days -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0 ; http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- Yield 35-40 q/ha (rainfed uplands) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0 ; https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Ranchi AICRIP yield potential 10-12 q/acre -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/13%20Ranchi.pdf
- Plant type: dwarf, 75-80 cm -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Multi-location trial data, yield-trial series or AICRIP station-wise results: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line code IET-12052 -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php ; http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- CONFLICT IN PARENTAGE: The supplied record gives Fine Gora x IET 2832 (IET 2832 being a DRR Hyderabad line). The national varietal table gives "Bala x Black Gora x OS-36 x CH-1039" -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php . The two cannot be reconciled from the sources found; the supplied parentage is not confirmed by any source found.
- Breeding method, QTL/marker studies, genome resources: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released in 1996 for Bihar; the varietal table credits no named breeder -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php
- Birsa Agricultural University (Ranchi) is the institution named in the supplied record; no source found names a lead breeder for this variety. Breeder names: No evidence found
- Institute-level confirmation that BAU developed this line: No evidence found beyond the supplied record. A news item discusses BAU releasing a set of varieties but does not name Birsa Dhan-106 -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/birsa-agricultural-university

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for any named breeder, email, phone or postal address specific to this variety.
- Institute-level page for Birsa Agricultural University (Kanke, Ranchi): not retrieved in this session. The supplied record gives "Rice Breeder, Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi-834 006 (Bihar)" as the institution address, but this could not be verified from a search result.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, conference paper or AICRP annual-report entry specific to Birsa Dhan-106 was found. Items found for "Birsa Dhan-107" (IRRN, 1999, https://zenodo.org/records/6948009) are a different variety and are excluded.
- No evidence found for KrishiKosh theses or DOIs on this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Birsa Dhan-106 from NSC, Bihar or Jharkhand State Seed Corporation, KVK, BAU seed sales or private dealers. The only seed listing retrieved is for Birsa Dhan-101 (Amazon) and is excluded.
- Notification record: Bihar DBT variety list shows BIRSA DHAN-106 under notified varieties dated 01/01/1996 -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) entry for variety code A0102048: not retrieved in this session.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Bihar, per the national varietal table -- https://rice-garud.icar-web.com/varieties.php ; http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- Bihar DBT list also records notification in 1996 -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Jharkhand: the supplied record names Bihar only; no source found for Jharkhand recommendation.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jitendra (IET-10526), Rice

Name note: The release-minute name "Jitendra (IET-10526)" and the Seednet name "JITENDRA (IET-10526)" refer to the same entry in the sources I found. Seednet itself did not come up in any search, so every item below comes from third-party pages that use the first form or its uppercase variant.

Searches run: 4 (release/traits; breeder/institute; research papers; seed availability). The breeder, institute and seed searches returned mostly unrelated pages, so several headings below say "No evidence found."

STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed as rainfed deep-water ecosystem, late duration, tall (160-170 cm) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Listed as moderately resistant to gall midge (GM) and leaf folder (LF), with the same tall, late, rainfed deep-water profile -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-variety-recommended-cultivation-uttar-pradesh
No explicit drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance rating found; the only stress-related information is the deep-water ecosystem classification. -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-variety-recommended-cultivation-uttar-pradesh

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to neck blast (Pyricularia) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Resistant to brown planthopper (BPH) and white-backed planthopper (WBPH) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Moderately resistant to gall midge and leaf folder -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-variety-recommended-cultivation-uttar-pradesh
Same disease/pest profile repeated in the Rice Development Status Paper table, Directorate of Rice Development, Patna -- https://www.scribd.com/document/805668781/Status-Paper-on-Rice

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity: late duration -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Ecosystem: rainfed deep water -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Plant height: 160-170 cm, tall -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Grain: long slender, white -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-variety-recommended-cultivation-uttar-pradesh
Yield: 50 q/ha (as stated in the notification table; no trial data, locations or seasons given) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
No multi-location trial or AICRP report naming this variety was found. -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: selection from land races (no named parents) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-variety-recommended-cultivation-uttar-pradesh
Breeding-line code: IET-10526 (IET number is the only breeding-line code in the sources) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
Breeding method: selection (from land races), per the parentage entry above; no pedigree or method detail beyond that.
QTL, marker, or genome-resource studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution and station (Rice Research Station, Chinsurah, West Bengal, as given in the brief): No evidence found. No source I retrieved names the Chinsurah station or any institution for this variety.
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. Results with similar names (lentil breeder Jitendra Kumar, Tiwari, Khurana, Tomar, and a Raipur engineer named Jitendra) concern other people and were discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder contact: No evidence found.
Institute contact (email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for Rice Research Station, Chinsurah, or the Directorate of Rice Development): No evidence found in the retrieved pages.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Results with the name Jitendra (rice-lentil, rice-drought, ResearchGate profiles, Zenodo Uttar Pradesh conference paper) concerned other varieties, crops or people and were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Seed dealer, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed listing for this variety was not retrieved. Results on seed supply were generic (Indonesia, US, UP seed-chain articles) and do not name this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh (release record lists both) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0 and https://www.scribd.com/document/805668781/Status-Paper-on-Rice
Uttar Pradesh and Uttaranchal notified rice list includes this variety (entry 40 in 2022 lists) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-uttar-pradesh-uttaranchal/ and https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-uttar-pradesh-and-uttaranchal-2/
Tripura state list also includes this variety -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in//State-Tripura.htm
Uttarakhand list in a hybrid-rice thesis mentions Jitendra (IET-10526) with a numeric code of 108 in an unclear context; not verified -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/a55e1a4b-a29e-474e-b6b8-f0c932d24134/content

RELEASE RECORD (for reference)
Year of release: 1997 -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
Notification date and number in Bihar list: 01/05/1997, 360(E) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Purnendu (IET-10029), Rice

Name note: "variety_name" is Purnendu (IET-10029), the name in the CSC/notification lists. "seednet_variety_name" is PURNENDU (IET-10029). The Seednet search did not return a Seednet page, so no evidence below comes from seednet.gov.in. All findings below refer to the variety name Purnendu (IET-10029) unless stated otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as resistant to sheath blight, sheath rot, leaf folder and stem borer, and moderately resistant to gall midge; rainfed semi-deep, tall (140-150 cm), 150-160 days, about 53 q/ha -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2008.htm
- The same resistance profile appears in a notified-varieties table (1996-2007) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- The IRRI Rice Research Note describes it as a deepwater variety suited to 50-100 cm water depth, which conflicts with the "rainfed semi-deep" classification above -- https://zenodo.org/records/7006233
- No flood, submergence, drought, heat or salinity tolerance data specific to Purnendu were found (a drought/salinity mention on a traditional-variety page names Patnai-23 only, not Purnendu, so it is excluded).

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistance to sheath blight (Sh B), sheath rot (Sh.R), leaf folder (LF), stem borer (SB); moderate resistance to gall midge (GM) -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2008.htm
- Same entries -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- Purnendu is cited as a regional check in a Rajdeep insect screening context only; no Purnendu pest data were found on that page -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352769397_Rajdeep_IET_17713_A_New_Rainfed_Lowland_High_Yielding_Rice_Variety_for_Semideep_Situation

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Purnendu served as the regional check in AICRIP-type trials for a semi-deep entry, where the new entry out-yielded it by about 13.28% in 2002; these are the comparator data for Rajdeep, not Purnendu's own trial yield -- https://www.academia.edu/49399451/Rajdeep_IET_17713_A_New_Rainfed_Lowland_High_Yielding_Rice_Variety_for_Semideep_Situation
- Purnendu appears in an AICRIP-style comparison among rainfed semi-deep and lowland checks (mean yield table, 1995-2013 period) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331502365_Genetic_Gain_for_Yield_in_Rice_Breeding_and_Rice_Production_in_India_to_Meet_with_the_Demand_from_Increased_Human_Population
- Listed among station-trial checks in a CRRI annual report, 2011-12 -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/2011-12.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage Patnai 23 / Jaladhi 2 -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2008.htm
- Same parentage with the same IET code, listed in a microsatellite diversity table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262002249_L_Behera_S_Mohanty_S_K_Pradhan_S_Singh_O_N_Singh_R_K_Sahu_S_C_Sahu_S_K_Dash_and_T_Mohapatra_2013_Assessment_of_genetic_diversity_of_rainfed_lowland_rice_genotypes_using_microsatellite_markers_Indian_J
- Microsatellite study shows Purnendu closely similar to Sabita (similarity 0.88) and grouped with semi-deep genotypes; no QTL or gene-level data for Purnendu were found -- same URL as above
- Listed with pedigree Patnai 23/Jaladhi 2 among genotypes screened for fertility restorer (Rf) genes in an Assam study; the snippet does not state Purnendu's restorer result -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/294108386_Identification_of_fertility_restorers_among_Assam_rice_cultivars_by_phenotyping_and_molecular_screening_approaches
- Pedigree and a year of 1994 appear in a variety table with a 1995-2013 yield window; the table does not explain the year -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331502365_Genetic_Gain_for_Yield_in_Rice_Breeding_and_Rice_Production_in_India_to_Meet_with_the_Demand_from_Increased_Human_Population
- Breeding method, breeding-line code beyond IET-10029, and genome resources: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution is the Rice Research Station, Chinsurah (Government of West Bengal, Hooghly) -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2008.htm (institution given in the record and consistent with the station listings)
- Lead breeder or scientist for Purnendu: No evidence found. The breeder names that surfaced (for example, Sitesh Chatterjee) are on pages about other varieties (Rajdeep IET 17713) or the station lab, and are NOT attributed to Purnendu here -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352769397_Rajdeep_IET_17713_A_New_Rainfed_Lowland_High_Yielding_Rice_Variety_for_Semideep_Situation

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level only; no breeder contact found)
- Rice Research Station-Chinsurah (GLIS record): Address PO Chinsurah RS, 712102, Hooghly, India; Telephone 91-33-26862484; Fax 91-33-26861149; Email field present but obfuscated in the record (not legible, so not transcribed) -- https://glis.fao.org/glis/wiews/detail?wiewsCode=IND559
- Station address also appears as Hooghly-712102, West Bengal -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404181532_INVENTORY-OF-AROMATIC-FOLK-RICE-VARIETIES-OF-WEST-BENGAL
- Breeder-level contact for Purnendu: No evidence found. A personal lab contact page (phone and email) belongs to a different scientist's lab and is excluded -- https://www.researchgate.net/lab/Sitesh-Chatterjee-Lab-Rice-Research-Station-Chuchura-Sitesh-Chatterjee

PUBLICATIONS
- Anonymous (1995). Purnendu, a New Deepwater (50-100 Cm) Rice Variety in Eastern India. International Rice Research Notes 20(4):12-13 -- https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7006233 (author not shown in the source record)
- Behera L, Mohanty S, Pradhan SK, Singh S, Singh ON, Sahu RK, Sahu SC, Dash SK, Mohapatra T (2013). Assessment of genetic diversity of rainfed lowland rice genotypes using microsatellite markers. Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding 73(2):142-152 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262002249_L_Behera_S_Mohanty_S_K_Pradhan_S_Singh_O_N_Singh_R_K_Sahu_S_C_Sahu_S_K_Dash_and_T_Mohapatra_2013_Assessment_of_genetic_diversity_of_rainfed_lowland_rice_genotypes_using_microsatellite_markers_Indian_J
- Authors not shown (2019 approx.). Genetic Gain for Yield in Rice Breeding and Rice Production in India (ICAR-IIRR affiliation) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331502365_Genetic_Gain_for_Yield_in_Rice_Breeding_and_Rice_Production_in_India_to_Meet_with_the_Demand_from_Increased_Human_Population
- Authors not shown (2011-12). ICAR-CRRI Annual Report 2011-12 (station trial listing Purnendu as a check) -- https://icar-crri.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/2011-12.pdf
- Authors not shown (2015 list). Notified varieties list entry for Purnendu (IET-10029), notified 01/05/1997, Notification 360(E) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses, SAU papers and the 2011-12 CRRI annual report: no Purnendu-specific theses found on KrishiKosh in these searches

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. Searches returned only unrelated retail "dhan/paddy" seed listings (pooja seed, generic paddy traders) that do not name Purnendu, so they are excluded. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for Purnendu was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- West Bengal (listed under the state column for this variety) -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2008.htm and http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- Notified in the 1996-2007 national notification list; the Bihar DBT copy of the list shows notification 360(E) without naming a recommended state for the variety -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- The "recommended_states_raw" field in the input record ("Unknown") should be updated to West Bengal, based on these two sources.

RELEASE RECORD SUMMARY
- Release year 1997 -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2008.ht

seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: IT IS AN INDUCED MUTANT OF MAHSURI. IT FITS WELL UNDER RICE-WHEAT ROTATION WHERE MAHSURI IS A POPULAR VARIETY. BECAUSE OF EARLINESS THERE IS NO PROBLEM OF PANICLE EMERGENCE DUE TO EARLY ONSET OF COLD WHETHER EVEN UNDER DELAYED TRANSPLANTING. PADDY GRAINS HAVE DORMANCY. RICE GRAINS ARE MEDIUM SLENDER, SOMEWHAT LONGER THAN MAHSURI WHAT SHINING HAVING GOOD COOKING QUALITY.

salinity.details: Described as a salt-tolerant rice from CSSRI Karnal with alkalinity tolerance, adapted to irrigated saline-alkaline soils. Tolerant to alkalinity at about pH 9.9, with a reported tolerance threshold of pH 9.2-9.9 and EC 9.0 in one table row. Listed among salt-tolerant varieties released for salinity tolerance, and named among successful salt-tolerant cultivars from India in a mechanisms review. Grain quality under salinity and alkalinity stress was assessed for a tolerant group that included CSR 13 (lysimeter study). Institute CSR-13 description (CSC record, not verified in digest): under very high salt stress, less than 25% sterile spikelets, mainly on tips; growth nearly normal with some reduction in tillering and plant height, some leaves discoloured and rolled, slight tip burning. Excellent under normal and moderately deteriorated salt-affected soils.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources for flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: resistant per digest sources (agropedia pages describe it as resistant to blast). Rice tungro virus (RTV): digest found no evidence; CSC record states moderately tolerant to RTV (not verified in digest). BPH and GB resistance: no evidence found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest evidence found in the digest sources. CSC record (not verified in digest): tolerant of leaf folder, and shows very low incidence of stem borer with white ears even after 95 days of transplanting.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CSR-13 (IET-10348), Rice/Paddy

Searches run: 4 (variety and release; breeder and institute; research papers and parentage; seed availability). No result came from seednet.gov.in, so the Seednet-side name (A0102105, "PADDY (DHAN)") has no direct evidence. Both names refer to the same variety. The CSC-style name and the Seednet name are identical in every source found, so all findings below apply to both.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Salt-tolerant rice from CSSRI Karnal, with alkalinity tolerance; described as irrigated saline-alkaline soil adapted -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-variety-recommended-cultivation-uttar-pradesh
- Tolerant to alkalinity at about pH 9.9, with a reported tolerance threshold of pH 9.2-9.9 and EC 9.0 in one table row (CSR 13, CSR1/Bas.370//CSR5) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh
- Listed among salt-tolerant varieties released for salinity tolerance in a review of rice salinity tolerance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281317520_Rice_breeding_for_salt_tolerance
- Grain quality under salinity and alkalinity stress was assessed for a group of tolerant genotypes that included CSR 13 (lysimeter study) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259164184_Effects_of_Soil_Salinity_and_Alkalinity_on_Grain_Quality_of_Tolerant_Semi-Tolerant_and_Sensitive_Rice_Genotypes
- Salt-tolerance mechanisms review that names CSR13 among successful salt-tolerant cultivars from India -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-5760
- Drought, heat, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to blast (grain: long slender) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-variety-recommended-cultivation-uttar-pradesh
- Resistant to blast (grain: LS) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- BLB, BPH, GB resistance: No evidence found (the only nearby resistance entries on the page were for other varieties)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 115-130 days; irrigated saline-alkaline ecosystem; grain long slender (rated for UP recommendation) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-variety-recommended-cultivation-uttar-pradesh
- Duration 115-130 days (rice varieties notified 1996-2007 table) -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- Significantly higher grain yield than the non-salt-tolerant check Pant 4 in a trial reported in a review -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh
- Included as a new check (with CSR 27) in the salt-tolerance trial series in 2000 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh
- Demonstrated on farmers' fields as a salt-tolerant rice variety (institute demonstration list, not a trial dataset) -- https://cssri.res.in/technology-evaluation-and-transfer/
- Yield figures for this variety: No evidence found (the 35-50 q/ha entry on the agropedia page was not clearly attributed to CSR-13 and was discarded)

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: CSR 1/Basmati 370//CSR 5 (three-way cross) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh
- Parentage given as CSR 1 x Basmati 370 x CSR 5 -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-variety-recommended-cultivation-uttar-pradesh
- Breeding line code 80-H-3-13; IET No. 10348; breeding method: pedigree selection -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh and https://researchsquare.com/article/rs-213648/v1
- QTL or marker data specific to CSR-13: No evidence found (QTL and genome pages returned concerned other lines, such as CSR27 and Pusa Basmati 1, and were discarded)
- Genome resources: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI), Karnal, ICAR -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379529917_Recent_Approaches_in_Breeding_for_Salt_Tolerance_in_Rice_in_Bangladesh
- Released by CVRC (CSSRI is the developer). Developed through conventional breeding, not transgenic -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/257650699_tolerant_crop_varieties_developed_at_CSSRI_Karnal_India_a_success_story
- Notified or released within CSSRI's Crop Improvement division's rice list, with a release year of 1998 on that page (the Bihar notification list gives 1999) -- https://cssri.res.in/crop-improvement/
- Named lead breeder or scientist: No evidence found (the review only lists the breeder designation "rice breeder at ICAR-CSSRI" without names)

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Central Soil Salinity Research Institute, Zarifa Farm, Kachawa Road, Karnal – 132001 (India); phone 91-184-2290501; phone 91-184-2291156; email cssridirector@gmail.com -- https://cssri.res.in/technology-evaluation-and-transfer/
- Institute website (crop improvement page): https://cssri.res.in/crop-improvement/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- The NDUAT publication describes this variety as submergence tolerant. -- https://www.nduat.org/pdf/anduat.pdf
- A popular article on the "Samba sub 1" name puts its submergence tolerance at about 15 days of standing water. -- https://krishiscience.co.in/storage/app/finalpdf/K3toD2HFbD9NYOLUhd2T6eUkR5XCDt6KuNPAqNuI.pdf
- The sources give no drought, heat, salinity or flood-trial figures for this variety. Generic Sub1 material (Swarna-Sub1, Sambha Mahsuri-Sub1, Nepal's Sambha Masuli Sub-1) was excluded because it does not name this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- NDUAT lists resistance to brown spot, neck blast, leaf folder, blue beetle, GMB-1 and plant hopper. -- https://www.nduat.org/pdf/anduat.pdf
- A popular article on the "Samba sub 1" name reports susceptibility to some fungal diseases, and its title includes blast management. -- https://krishiscience.co.in/storage/app/finalpdf/K3toD2HFbD9NYOLUhd2T6eUkR5XCDt6KuNPAqNuI.pdf
- The ResearchGate version of the same article is titled around blast management of this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364994093_SAMBA-SUB1_IMPROVED_VARIETY_OF_RICE_AND_MANAGEMENT_OF_BLAST_OF_RICE

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- NDUAT gives maturity of 150-155 days and yield of 50-55 q/ha. -- https://www.nduat.org/pdf/anduat.pdf
- The popular article gives a crop duration of 135 days, which conflicts with NDUAT. -- https://krishiscience.co.in/storage/app/finalpdf/K3toD2HFbD9NYOLUhd2T6eUkR5XCDt6KuNPAqNuI.pdf
- The same article gives a nursery sowing window and a direct-seeding window, and a seed rate for direct seeding. -- https://krishiscience.co.in/storage/app/finalpdf/K3toD2HFbD9NYOLUhd2T6eUkR5XCDt6KuNPAqNuI.pdf
- NDUAT reports about 40,000 ha of cultivation in eastern Uttar Pradesh. -- https://www.nduat.org/pdf/anduat.pdf
- No multi-location or AICRP trial data specific to this variety was found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage "Sambha Mahsuri*3/IR 49830-7-1-2-3" and the breeding line code IET 21248 come from the supplied record. The IET code is confirmed by the notification list (see RECOMMENDED STATES). No search source confirmed the parentage.
- The sources on Sub1 introgression into Sambha Mahsuri describe a different product, Sambha Mahsuri-Sub1 (IRIS/IR07F287 codes). They were not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265298680_Submergence_risks_and_farmers'_preferences_Implications_for_breeding_Sub1_rice_in_Southeast_Asia
- No QTL, marker or genome-resource study naming this variety was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- NDUAT's crop-variety table lists "Sambha Sub-1" among varieties it developed. -- https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf
- The NDUAT research highlights list the same variety in the same table. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/skteditedResearchAchievementsfoNet-2014.pdf
- The Directorate of Research at NDUAT is headquartered at Kumarganj. -- https://www.nduat.org/pdf/anduat.pdf
- No breeder name was found in any source. The supplied "Rice Breeder, Deptt. of Crop Physiology" wording is not confirmed by search.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or personal contact was found.
- No NDUAT institute email, phone or contact page URL was found in the results.
- The only address evidence is institute-level: the Directorate of Research HQ at Kumarganj, Faizabad (https://www.nduat.org/pdf/anduat.pdf). The postal code 224229 comes from the supplied record, not from search.

PUBLICATIONS
- Singh, S. K.; Patel, A. K. (2022). SAMBA-SUB1: Improved variety of rice and management of blast of rice. Popular article (ResearchGate; krishiscience.co.in); no journal or DOI identified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364994093_SAMBA-SUB1_IMPROVED_VARIETY_OF_RICE_AND_MANAGEMENT_OF_BLAST_OF_RICE ; https://krishiscience.co.in/storage/app/finalpdf/K3toD2HFbD9NYOLUhd2T6eUkR5XCDt6KuNPAqNuI.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper on this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No NSC, UP Beej Nigam, KVK or SAU seed sale listing for this variety was found.
- The IRRI–UP Beej Nigam partnership reports seed distribution, but its variety list does not name Sambha Sub-1. -- https://news.irri.org/2023/08/irri-partnership-in-uttar-pradesh-to.html
- An Odisha seed corporation availability page lists "Sambha-sub-1". This is name-only and unverified: it does not confirm the IET 21248 line or the NDUAT release. -- https://osscltd.in/cms/marketing/availability-of-seeds
- The Nepal seed-system pages refer to Sambha Masuli Sub-1, a different product, and were excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The notified name is "Samba sub 1 (IET 21248)", notified in 2015 under S.O. 268(E) dated 28.01.2015 for Uttar Pradesh. -- http://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm ; also https://www.krishakjagat.org/national-news/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- The popular article recommends it for Uttar Pradesh, Assam, West Bengal and Tripura. This is not in the gazette and is a secondary claim. -- https://krishiscience.co.in/storage/app/finalpdf/K3toD2HFbD9NYOLUhd2T6eUkR5XCDt6KuNPAqNuI.pdf
- Year of release: 2015 (notification). The CSC release minutes are not located.

NAME NOTE
- Evidence refers to "Sambha Sub-1" (NDUAT), "Samba sub 1 (IET 21248)" (notification) and "Sambha Sub 1" (popular article). The Seednet name "Sambha Sub - 1 (IET 21248)" was not separately found on Seednet, so the Seednet portal was not checked directly.
